title: Anthony Joshua Welcomes Baby Girl, Says 'I Can't Believe I'm A Girl Dad'
description: Anthony Joshua has announced the birth of his daughter, his second child with former childhood sweetheart Nicole Osbourne - three weeks before his heavyweight fight with Tyson Fury in Cardiff.
content:
Anthony Joshua has become a father again – and this time he is a "girl dad". The British heavyweight announced that he and his former childhood sweetheart, Nicole Osbourne, have welcomed a baby girl, three weeks before he steps into the ring with Tyson Fury in Cardiff.

The 37-year-old broke the news in an interview published on 18 November 2026, and the timing caught almost everyone off guard: he had kept the pregnancy entirely out of the public eye while preparing for the biggest domestic fight of his career.

"I can't believe I'm a girl dad"

"It's been amazing, a big blessing, and I can't believe I'm a girl dad. I didn't want to find the sex out during the pregnancy."

Joshua said he deliberately asked not to be told the baby's sex. When he found out it was a girl, his whole plan for fatherhood changed on the spot.

"I love boys but as soon as I found out we had a little girl I said, 'No more FIFA, no more motorbiking, no more PlayStation!'"

He went further, describing the kind of father he intends to be:

"I'm going to do it all, so you might see me with some eyeshadow on, some nail polish on, drinking some tea in a doll's playhouse and just trying to do the right thing by her. I will change nappies – I've gotta go through all that stinky bum time again!"

The mother, and the name

The baby is Joshua's second child with Nicole Osbourne. The pair are not in a romantic relationship, but they came together to extend their family. Their son, Joseph Bayley Temiloluwa Prince Joshua, is 11 and has been kept largely out of the public eye.

Joshua said the baby girl does not have a name yet – but she already has one from her father.

"We haven't given her a name yet, but she's my Princess."

He also spoke about what raising a daughter means to him personally:

"Now I've got a daughter, I will get an insight and a bit more understanding of what it means to be a woman, and how I can be supportive. My daughter will give me a first-hand experience of the power of a woman – I've spoken to all the women in my family, and it's amazing the amount of support that women give each other."

Why the news lands hard

The announcement comes 11 months after the car crash in Nigeria that killed two of Joshua's closest friends and left him injured. He has spoken since about wanting another child to "give back to the world" – a line that reads differently now that the baby is here.

It also lands in the middle of a fight camp. Joshua faces Tyson Fury on Friday, 11 December 2026 at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff – a bout British boxing has chased for years, and one that will define the final chapter of both careers.

What it means for the Fury fight

Nothing, technically. A newborn does not change a jab. But fighters have long spoken about how fatherhood reshapes the way they approach the sport – less risk-taking, more purpose. Joshua, who has spent most of the past year rebuilding after the crash, now has a second reason to walk out of that ring on his feet.

Whether it sharpens him or softens him is the question Cardiff will answer on 11 December.

Bottom line: Anthony Joshua is a father again – a daughter, still unnamed, already called "Princess" – and he will fight Tyson Fury three weeks after her birth. The heavyweight division's biggest storyline just got a human one attached to it.

title: Musk regrets spending $500m on Republicans after US midterms
description:
Billionaire entrepreneur Elon Musk has said he felt “foolish” for spending nearly $500m on Republican candidates during the 2026 midterm elections after Democrats made significant gains and reclaimed control of Congress.
Musk made the admission during a virtual interview at the New York Times DealBo
content:
Billionaire entrepreneur Elon Musk has said he felt “foolish” for spending nearly $500m on Republican candidates during the 2026 midterm elections after Democrats made significant gains and reclaimed control of Congress.

Musk made the admission during a virtual interview at the New York Times DealBook Summit on Wednesday, saying he would have spent less if he could go back.

“I feel pretty foolish about having spent so much money and not seeing much for it, or maybe it would have been much worse without that,” he said.

The Tesla chief executive added that the outcome showed that money alone could not determine the results of American elections.

“But it certainly shows that, you know, American elections are not just about money. You know, obviously you can put a lot of money into election and have an effect that is relatively minor, and I think that that was the case here. So probably I could rewind the clock. I would have spent less money,” Musk said.

According to ABC News, Musk spent heavily on key Republican races during the election cycle, hoping to help the party retain its Senate majority. However, Democrats won several contests across the country and regained control of both chambers of Congress.

During the interview, Musk also sought to distance himself from the Make America Great Again movement associated with President Donald Trump, describing his political views as moderate.

“So, you know, I think I’m ideologically quite moderate, although, you know, I don’t think I have like, you know, any kind of extreme political views,” he said.

Asked about his association with MAGA, Musk said he did not identify with what he described as blind loyalty to Republican Party policies.

“I’m not MAGA. Well, at least I’m not like, I’m not sure what MAGA means … If that means sort of blind adherence to a set of policies by the Republican Party, then I certainly don’t have that. I think there are positives and negatives in both parties,” he said.

Musk has been a prominent supporter of Trump and Republican candidates, including during the 2024 presidential election, when he described himself as “dark gothic MAGA” at a Trump rally in New York City.

His relationship with Trump, however, later came under strain over the Republican tax and spending legislation promoted by the White House, following Musk’s involvement in the administration’s efforts to reduce government spending.

Despite the disagreement, Musk continued to support Republican candidates ahead of the 2026 midterms, including through substantial financial contributions.

He also commented on the election of Democrat Gina Hinojosa as Texas governor, expressing confidence that she would govern moderately.

“I don’t think she’s sort of a far-left governor, and based on everything I’ve heard about her, I think things will be fine in Texas with Gina as governor,” Musk said.

The 2026 midterm elections saw Democrats make significant gains, winning control of both chambers of Congress and ending the Republicans’ hold on the Senate and House of Representatives.

The post Musk regrets spending $500m on Republicans after US midterms appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: NAFDAC intercepts unregistered beverages, skin-lightening injections at Kano airport
description:
The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control has intercepted 17 cartons of suspected unregistered beverages and skin-lightening and anti-ageing injections at the Mallam Aminu Kano International Airport, Kano.
According to a statement shared by the agency on Thursday, the intercep
content:
The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control has intercepted 17 cartons of suspected unregistered beverages and skin-lightening and anti-ageing injections at the Mallam Aminu Kano International Airport, Kano.

According to a statement shared by the agency on Thursday, the interception followed a joint examination conducted at the Skyway Aviation Handling Company Plc Shed.

The products were discovered concealed within a 33-carton consignment declared as “personal effects” and transported aboard an Ethiopian Airlines flight that arrived the previous day.

NAFDAC said a physical examination revealed that “the products bore no NAFDAC registration numbers, while the consignment lacked the requisite import documentation.”

It added that “the entire consignment was placed on hold in the custody of the Nigeria Customs Service.”

The agency said the importer was subsequently invited for questioning and “a statement was obtained as part of the investigation.”

NAFDAC noted that the products remained on hold pending further regulatory directives, adding that “their quality and authenticity have not yet been established.”

The agency said it continued to strengthen surveillance and enforcement at Nigeria’s entry points “to prevent the unlawful importation and circulation of unregistered, substandard and falsified regulated products and protect public health.”

In a related development, the House of Representatives had summoned NAFDAC and other security agencies over concerns about fake drugs and sought tougher penalties for offenders.

The post NAFDAC intercepts unregistered beverages, skin-lightening injections at Kano airport appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Keeping my father’s succession video was a mistake – Jimmy Odukoya
description: The embattled Senior Pastor of The Fountain of Life Church, Jimmy Odukoya, has explained why he retained a 2021 video in which his late father, Pastor Taiwo Odukoya, named Pastor Kunle Areogun as his preferred successor, despite allegedly being instructed to delete the recording after recovering fro
content:
The embattled Senior Pastor of The Fountain of Life Church, Jimmy Odukoya, has explained why he retained a 2021 video in which his late father, Pastor Taiwo Odukoya, named Pastor Kunle Areogun as his preferred successor, despite allegedly being instructed to delete the recording after recovering from surgery.

Odukoya gave the explanation while addressing workers of the church on Wednesday, amid the leadership crisis that has resulted in a faction of its Board of Trustees withdrawing recognition of him as Senior Pastor, according to Church Times.

The publication reported that its correspondent was present at the meeting, where Jimmy addressed about 300 church workers.

Jimmy said the video was recorded in 2021 when his father was preparing to undergo surgery in the United States and feared he might not survive the procedure.

He said, “That was when he asked me to record him where he made the statements about succession. I was the one who recorded the video,” adding that his father’s elder brother, Pastor John Odukoya, was also aware of the recording.

Explaining what happened after the operation, Church Times quoted him as saying, “He said, however, that after the surgery turned out successful, his father asked him to delete the video as it was no longer valid. Rather than delete the video, Jimmy kept it, admitting that it was a grave mistake on his part.”

The publication further reported that he said, “He added that only a handful of people were privy to the video, including his sisters, whom he alleged released it to the public.”

Giving further insight into the leadership dispute, Jimmy said the disagreement with the board started about a year after he assumed office, when members allegedly asked him to relinquish his position as Chairman of the Board of Trustees and concentrate on his pastoral responsibilities.

According to Church Times, he said, “That was a hard pill for him to swallow. He said he sensed that what the board wanted to do was to control him, insisting that he would not allow that to happen.”

The report also quoted him as alleging that his sister, Pastor Tolu Odukoya-Ijogun, had approached him and asked him to step down so she could become the board’s chairman.

Jimmy said the dispute was taken before the General Overseer of the Redeemed Christian Church of God, Pastor Enoch Adeboye, following interventions by Bishop Mike Okonkwo.

Recounting the meeting, he said, “When we got to Pastor Adeboye, I was there, and I watched every board member lie against me to my face.”

According to the report, Adeboye allowed him to explain his side of the disagreement before advising the parties to resolve their differences. He also reportedly reminded Jimmy that he had been called to preach the gospel and not to be chairman of the board, warning that if they failed to resolve the disagreement, “it will not be goodbye, it will be bye-bye.”

He further stated that the board, which included Pastors Kunle Areogun and Rotimi Okpaise, presented him with a seven-point demand, but he only agreed to four of the conditions.

On allegations of financial misconduct, Jimmy denied claims that he embezzled N250m donated to the church for a project.

According to Church Times, he told the workers that the money remained intact, explaining that the project had been delayed because of the economic situation and rising costs, which made its execution difficult.

The report added that he said he had restricted access to church funds and argued that if there had been financial wrongdoing, members of the accounts department would also be culpable.

Jimmy maintained that he remained the Senior Pastor of the church, although he expressed uncertainty about how the next Sunday service would proceed. He also said an advertised church programme would not hold because he did not want the crisis to escalate.

The development comes after a faction of the church’s Board of Trustees announced on Tuesday, November 17, that it had withdrawn recognition of Jimmy as Senior Pastor with immediate effect and appointed Pastor Rotimi Okpaise as interim spiritual and administrative leader.

The faction cited a December 2021 succession video in which Taiwo named Areogun as his preferred successor.

In the recording, the late founder said, “In case of my demise, which I don’t expect to happen soon, or a situation where I cannot write or talk, please, the next pastor of the church should be Kunle Areogun.”

He also designated Jimmy as Areogun’s immediate administrative assistant and head of the youth church.

PUNCH Online had reported that the trustees claimed they only became aware of the video in late December 2025, more than two years after Taiwo’s death, and that it was not presented during Jimmy’s appointment in September 2023.

However, a statement from Jimmy’s camp rejected the board faction’s decision as constitutionally invalid, insisting that he remained the duly appointed Senior Pastor and Chairman of the Board of Trustees.

Taiwo founded The Fountain of Life Church in 1992 with his first wife, Pastor Bimbo Odukoya. Following his death on August 7, 2023, Jimmy was announced as Senior Pastor in September and formally installed on September 30, 2023, while his sister, Tolu, was named Associate Senior Pastor.

The competing claims have left the church embroiled in a leadership crisis, with both factions insisting on the legitimacy of their positions.

The post Keeping my father’s succession video was a mistake – Jimmy Odukoya appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: UNN to introduce random drug tests after deaths of four students
description:
The University of Nigeria, Nsukka, said it will introduce random drug testing for students, including those living off campus, following the deaths of four students at an off-campus house party.
According to a statement posted on the school’s Facebook page on Wednesday, the Vice-Chancellor, Prof Sim
content:
The University of Nigeria, Nsukka, said it will introduce random drug testing for students, including those living off campus, following the deaths of four students at an off-campus house party.

According to a statement posted on the school’s Facebook page on Wednesday, the Vice-Chancellor, Prof Simon Ortuanya, disclosed this on Tuesday when he received a condolence delegation of traditional rulers led by the Chairman of the Enugu State Traditional Rulers Council, HRM Igwe Samuel Ikechukwu Asadu.

The university said the proposed measure would be implemented in partnership with the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency, while its recently established Directorate of Community Relations would coordinate engagement with landlords and other community stakeholders.

Ortuanya said the university was also strengthening its existing safety measures and regulatory framework to protect students, regardless of where they lived.

He explained that the tests would be conducted randomly, without following a predictable pattern.

“Students of a particular department or faculty could be randomly selected for the test,” he said.

The Vice-Chancellor said the university recognised the challenges of monitoring students living outside its campuses but expressed optimism that drug testing and closer collaboration with landlords would help address misconduct among students.

He urged students to learn from the tragedy, recalling that the university had prohibited formal sign-out celebrations and similar activities on its campuses in Nsukka, Enugu and Ituku-Ozalla since 2025.

“It is our collective responsibility to protect the lives and welfare of our students and preserve the sanity, sanctity and integrity of the University as a centre of learning,” he said.

Ortuanya also said the university was cooperating with relevant government and security agencies investigating the house party incident and was awaiting the outcome of their investigations.

He expressed condolences to the families of the deceased students and assured them of the university’s continued concern and support.

The traditional rulers, who visited the university to commiserate with its management and community, described the deaths as a major loss to the institution, the bereaved families and society.

Asadu said the council considered it important to identify with the university in its moment of grief and offer support.

“On behalf of the Traditional Rulers Council in Enugu State, we express our deep sympathy to the University management, the bereaved families and the entire University community over this painful loss.

“The loss of young lives, particularly at a time when their parents had invested so much in their upbringing and education, is heartbreaking,” he said.

He commended the Vice-Chancellor for his response to the incident and the steps taken to support affected students.

The traditional rulers also pledged to work with the university and other stakeholders to prevent a recurrence.

The proposed drug-testing policy follows an incident on November 11, when four students died and six others were hospitalised after a gathering at an off-campus lodge in the Hilltop area of Nsukka.

The party, held at Praise Lord Lodge, was reportedly organised to celebrate a friend who had completed his final-year examinations. The university said 10 students were involved.

The Vice-Chancellor had earlier said preliminary findings suggested possible alcohol and drug abuse but stressed that the university had not reached a conclusive determination on the cause of death.

He said the institution was working with security agencies to establish what happened.

The Enugu State Police Command also opened an investigation into the deaths. Its spokesperson, SP Daniel Ndukwe, said the four victims, comprising two males and two females, reportedly took ill after consuming alcoholic beverages at the gathering.

Six others were taken to hospital, while the four bodies were deposited in a mortuary for autopsy.

The police said the investigation was intended to establish the circumstances surrounding the deaths.

The incident came despite the university’s existing restrictions on sign-out celebrations.

Ortuanya said UNN had prohibited formal sign-out activities and similar celebrations on its campuses in Nsukka, Enugu and Ituku-Ozalla since 2025.

The latest incident, however, occurred at a private facility outside the university campus.

The post UNN to introduce random drug tests after deaths of four students appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Anthony Joshua announces arrival of baby girl with longtime partner Osbourne
description:
British boxing champion Anthony Joshua has announced his excitement over becoming a father to a baby girl, saying her arrival has given him a fresh perspective on fatherhood.
Joshua and his childhood sweetheart, Nicole Osbourne, welcomed their daughter on November 14, 2026.
The former two-time unifi
content:
British boxing champion Anthony Joshua has announced his excitement over becoming a father to a baby girl, saying her arrival has given him a fresh perspective on fatherhood.

Joshua and his childhood sweetheart, Nicole Osbourne, welcomed their daughter on November 14, 2026.

The former two-time unified heavyweight champion and Osbourne are also parents to an 11-year-old son, Joseph.

Speaking in an interview with Very Nigerian, which began trending on Thursday, Joshua said having a daughter would help him develop a deeper understanding of women and how best to support them.

The boxer expressed enthusiasm about the new experience, noting that raising a girl would offer him a different perspective on parenting and his responsibilities as a father.

“Now I’ve got a daughter, I will get an insight and a bit more understanding of what it means to be a woman, and how I can be supportive. My daughter will give me firsthand experience of a woman’s power.

“I’ve spoken to all the women in my family, and it’s amazing the amount of support that women give each other. We haven’t given her a name yet, but she’s my Princess,” he said.

Describing the birth as a huge blessing, Joshua said he was delighted to become a girl dad, adding that he had chosen not to find out the baby’s sex during the pregnancy.

“It’s been amazing, a big blessing and I can’t believe I’m a girl dad. I didn’t want to find the sex out during the pregnancy.

“I love boys but as soon as I found out we had a little girl I said, ‘No more Fifa, no more motorbiking, no more PlayStation!’” he said.

The boxer also expressed his willingness to take an active role in his daughter’s upbringing, including taking part in activities such as dressing up and playing with dolls.

“I’m going to do it all, so you might see me with some eyeshadow on, some nail polish on, drinking some tea in a doll’s playhouse and just trying to do the right thing by her, you know?

“I will change nappies, I’ve gotta go through all that stinky bum time again!” he added.

The development comes ahead of Joshua’s reported December 11 showdown with fellow British heavyweight boxer Tyson Fury.

The post Anthony Joshua announces arrival of baby girl with longtime partner Osbourne appeared first on Very Nigerian.

title: Why Premier League big six clubs keep getting richer — Report
description:
The financial gap between the Premier League’s traditional Big Six and the rest of the division continues to widen, with new figures highlighting how England’s wealthiest clubs are strengthening their dominance through commercial revenue, broadcasting deals and increased spending power.
Manchester U
content:
The financial gap between the Premier League’s traditional Big Six and the rest of the division continues to widen, with new figures highlighting how England’s wealthiest clubs are strengthening their dominance through commercial revenue, broadcasting deals and increased spending power.

Manchester United, Liverpool, Manchester City, Arsenal, Tottenham Hotspur and Chelsea have established themselves as the league’s financial heavyweights, generating hundreds of millions of pounds more than their domestic rivals.

A report by BBC Sport on Thursday highlights how the growing financial advantage is making it increasingly difficult for other Premier League clubs to compete with the established elite.

The scale of the divide is reflected in the figures involving Everton, the only club outside the Big Six to have remained in the Premier League since its formation in 1992.

In 2009-10, the average revenue gap between the Big Six and Everton stood at £120 million. By 2024-25, that figure had increased to £442 million.

The growth has largely been driven by the expansion of international broadcasting rights and the commercial appeal of clubs with huge global fanbases.

According to University of Liverpool football finance professor Kieran Maguire, the biggest clubs have become particularly attractive to international sponsors because of their worldwide following and the Premier League’s global television reach.

The report revealed that commercial deals account for 45 per cent of the Big Six’s revenue, compared with just 10 per cent for Everton. Smaller clubs consequently depend more heavily on broadcasting income, which accounts for 66 per cent of Everton’s revenue.

Champions League participation has also contributed to the widening financial divide, with clubs benefiting from the substantial financial rewards of competing in Europe’s premier club competition.

UEFA’s value pillar, introduced as part of its Champions League financial distribution system, reserves 35 per cent of competition revenue for clubs based on their historical performance and commercial value.

This has further strengthened the financial position of established European giants, with Manchester City earning an estimated £37.9 million from the value pillar last season, compared with Newcastle United’s £13.6 million.

Aston Villa and Newcastle have both improved their financial positions through European qualification, but the distribution system continues to favour clubs with stronger historical records.

Meanwhile, Chelsea are beginning to fall behind their traditional rivals financially, with Stamford Bridge’s limited capacity identified as a major obstacle to increasing matchday revenue.

The report noted that Chelsea recorded the lowest revenue among the Big Six over the past two seasons, finishing £74 million behind Tottenham and £200 million below Liverpool and Manchester City.

Despite generating an average of £80 per supporter in matchday spending during 2024-25, Chelsea’s 40,000-capacity stadium leaves them at a disadvantage against rivals whose grounds hold at least 60,000 spectators.

Their matchday revenue has increased by only £16 million over the past decade, compared with £69 million for Manchester United and £85 million for Tottenham following the opening of their new stadium.

The introduction of the Premier League’s squad-cost ratio (SCR) rules could further strengthen the spending advantage of wealthier clubs.

Unlike the previous profit and sustainability rules, SCR allows clubs to spend a percentage of their revenue on squad costs, giving clubs with higher earnings greater financial flexibility in the transfer market.

Although the new system offers clubs such as Aston Villa and Newcastle more room to invest, Maguire believes the structure still favours the Big Six because of their significantly greater revenue.

The financial consequences are already becoming evident in the transfer market.

Premier League clubs spent a record £3.5 billion during the summer transfer window, while 13 clubs broke their transfer records.

Brentford, Brighton, Crystal Palace, Leeds United and Nottingham Forest were among the clubs to spend more than £40 million on individual players, highlighting how transfer spending is spreading across the division.

However, the growing financial power of the biggest clubs means they remain better positioned to compete for elite players and offer more attractive wages.

While clubs such as Brighton have demonstrated that intelligent recruitment, player development and effective financial management can challenge the established order, sustaining that success remains difficult.

The report suggests that the Premier League’s financial structure is increasingly reinforcing the position of its wealthiest clubs, raising further questions about the long-term competitiveness of the division.

The article is based on the BBC Sport report, with the financial figures and explanations retained. Deloitte’s latest figures also show that Premier League clubs generated £6.8bn collectively in 2024-25, with the Big Six accounting for almost three-quarters of commercial revenue.

The post Why Premier League big six clubs keep getting richer — Report appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Why I rejected European country posting for South Africa — Fani-Kayode
description:
Nigeria’s High Commissioner to South Africa, Femi Fani-Kayode, has disclosed that he appealed to President Bola Tinubu to be reassigned to South Africa after he was initially posted to a European country.



He made the disclosure at a dinner and reception organised by the Nigerian High Commission a
content:
Nigeria’s High Commissioner to South Africa, Femi Fani-Kayode, has disclosed that he appealed to President Bola Tinubu to be reassigned to South Africa after he was initially posted to a European country.

He made the disclosure at a dinner and reception organised by the Nigerian High Commission and Consular Office in Pretoria following the presentation of his letters of credence to South African President Cyril Ramaphosa on November 13.

“I was sent here by our president, President Bola Ahmed, president of the Federal Republic of Nigeria — 250 million strong, a massive country, resilient people with rich history, very proud people, hard-working people that love life and love their country passionately, and I’ve been sent to represent those people and our government in a country which is equally resilient, hard-working, decent, civilised, with an equally rich history and heritage, as we have,” he said.

Explaining his choice of South Africa, the envoy said the two countries could work together to advance the interests of the continent.

“And that’s why I chose this country. I was initially posted to a European country, and I made an appeal to our president that I preferred to go to South Africa, which he graciously agreed to. So I find myself here,” he added.

Fani-Kayode was initially posted as Nigeria’s ambassador to Germany before he was reassigned to South Africa in May.

At the time, he said he had formally approached the then Minister of Foreign Affairs, Yusuf Tuggar, to express his reservations about the Germany posting.

The former minister said he was uncomfortable with the appointment for “a number of personal reasons” and because he had spent most of his life in Europe. He also said he preferred South Africa, a country he had never visited but had considerable interest in.

Ita Enang, who was initially posted to South Africa, was subsequently reassigned to Germany in Fani-Kayode’s place.

Speaking about his priorities in South Africa, Fani-Kayode said he had begun addressing issues affecting Nigerians in the country since his arrival. He also described those behind xenophobic attacks as a “tiny minority”, arguing that they did not represent the majority of South Africans, whom he described as decent and accommodating.

The post Why I rejected European country posting for South Africa — Fani-Kayode appeared first on Vanguard News.

It disclosed that the entire consignment was placed on hold in the custody of the Nigeria Customs Service, while the importer was subsequently invited for questioning, and a statement was obtained as part of the investigation.

NAFDAC said the products remain on hold pending further regulatory directives, adding that their quality and authenticity have not yet been established.

The agency said it continues to strengthen surveillance and enforcement at Nigeria’s entry points to prevent the unlawful importation and circulation of unregistered, substandard and falsified regulated products and protect public health.

The interception comes amid a renewed crackdown by NAFDAC in Kano.

On November 12, the agency uncovered nearly 11,400 cartons of banned and unregistered agrochemicals during an intelligence-led operation across 23 warehouses in the state, including paraquat-based products valued at about N200 million.

title: Xi, Trump and Putin begin unprecedented summit in China
description:
The leaders of China, the United States and Russia kicked off their first trilateral talks on Thursday, aimed according to Beijing as “safeguarding world peace” but sparking alarm and derision elsewhere.



The meeting between Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen, which analysts e
content:
The leaders of China, the United States and Russia kicked off their first trilateral talks on Thursday, aimed according to Beijing as “safeguarding world peace” but sparking alarm and derision elsewhere.

The meeting between Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen, which analysts expect to be heavier in symbolism than breakthroughs, comes with Russia’s Ukraine offensive approaching the five-year mark.

Trump is bogged down by his war with Iran that has choked oil supplies and pushed up consumer prices worldwide, while an ascendant China is looking to strengthen its hand in East Asia.

The Kylin Villa summit has stoked fears that the three powerful men want to divide the globe into spheres of influence, for example by making decisions impacting Ukraine over the heads of Kyiv or Europe.

Earlier Thursday, Trump and Putin held a meeting — their first since August 2025 — with the 80-year-old US president calling the Russian his “friend”, who responded in English: “Nice to meet you.”

Trump and Xi then came together — for the third time this year — for one-on-one discussions, with the US leader highlighting their “very special relationship”.

The two men’s talks were expected to touch on trade and potentially common rules for artificial intelligence, under the cloud of the Nvidia spy scandal.

“During this period, China-US relations have remained generally stable and improved, bringing tangible benefits to the people of both countries and injecting stability and certainty into the world,” Xi said.

Putin, 74, and Xi, 73, held talks on Wednesday — their 50th meeting, the Chinese president said.

Beijing, Washington and Moscow have given different accounts of the agenda for the three-way meeting on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum.

Washington initially signalled that Ukraine was off the table, before Trump said the war would feature. Xi does not view the conflict as China’s problem to solve.

Trump said in his meeting with Xi however that both China and the United States were “looking to both help with respect to the war with Russia and Ukraine.”

The Kremlin has said that the agenda had not been finalised, but it would be hard to avoid discussing Ukraine at the meeting, which is set to last “no more than an hour”.

Germany was also due to host Ukraine’s allies for a “Coalition of the Willing” meeting on Thursday involving envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff.

China has said only that the trio will hold “in-depth exchanges on safeguarding world peace and promoting strategic stability in major-power relations”.

Critics warned that the optics from the meeting will be damaging for the US president — but a fillip to Xi and Putin.

The meeting “gives Putin a platform to legitimise his war of aggression over Ukraine with seemingly little repercussions,” said Lyle Morris at the Asia Society Policy Institute.

“Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin are playing Donald Trump like a cheap violin,” Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer said.

– Nuclear disarmament –

Also up for discussion are the Iran war and nuclear disarmament, according to Washington, after a US-Russia bilateral treaty on atomic weapons expired in February.

Beijing has long maintained that the United States and Russia must reduce their giant nuclear arsenals before it agrees to talks on its smaller stockpile.

“Look, we have 4,000 nuclear weapons. Russia has 3,800 nuclear weapons. China now has four or five hundred, but they’re going to catch (up),” Trump told Fox News from Shenzhen.

Trump has also that North Korean leader Kim Jong Un “would like” to come to China to see him. The two met three times in Trump’s first term.

Pyongyang — which has drawn closer to Russia in recent years — has not officially responded, with state media showing Kim visiting on Wednesday a naval university.

Beijing on Thursday repeated that it had no information on any Kim visit.

– Airport welcome –

Breaking with decades of diplomatic protocol, Xi received Trump at the airport, with the men briefly hugging before a red-carpet greeting complete with cheering children and an air-force flyover.

This reciprocated the airport greeting Trump gave Xi at Joint Base Andrews in September.

“It’s a friendship relationship. It’s a respect relationship,” Trump told Fox News.

The airport welcome showed “great respect, and I appreciate that. That’s a big win for us. It’s a big win for China too,” Trump said.

Other world leaders at the APEC meeting include Japan’s Sanae Takaichi, South Korea’s Lee Jae Myung, Canada’s Mark Carney and Australia’s Anthony Albanese.

Takaichi, on her first visit since angering Beijing a year ago with comments about Taiwan, met Putin — relations are also tense — on Wednesday, Tokyo said.

Takaichi, who by Thursday afternoon had not held any formal meeting with Xi, said Thursday she wanted a “constructive and stable relationship” with China.

Despite their differences, all the leaders — including Putin — posed for the APEC “family photo” on Thursday in special scarves.

Xi opened the APEC leaders’ meeting on Thursday with a call to “reduce barriers to trade and investment”.

Trump said he opposed “any form of globalist regulation or anything to control and stifle” AI.

title: MREIF mortgage: What you need for the ₦100m FG-backed housing loan
description:
Nigerians seeking to access the Federal Government-backed MOFI Real Estate Investment Fund mortgage of up to ₦100m must be at least 21 years old, have a satisfactory credit score and contribute at least 20 per cent of the property’s value as equity, according to the fund’s guidelines.
The Ministry o
content:
Nigerians seeking to access the Federal Government-backed MOFI Real Estate Investment Fund mortgage of up to ₦100m must be at least 21 years old, have a satisfactory credit score and contribute at least 20 per cent of the property’s value as equity, according to the fund’s guidelines.

The Ministry of Finance Incorporated Real Estate Investment Fund, established to address housing affordability and expand access to mortgage financing, also requires applicants to meet specific documentation and income verification conditions before they can access the facility.

According to the Frequently Asked Questions section on the MREIF website, borrowers must be at least 21 years old but not older than 60 years at the expiration of the loan.

“The person should have a satisfactory credit score. Borrowers must contribute at least 20% of the value of the housing unit,” the fund stated.

The requirements apply to prospective homebuyers seeking financing under the scheme, which has a maximum loan limit of ₦100m under its pension-backed mortgage arrangement.

The fund, established by the Ministry of Finance Incorporated, the investment arm of the Federal Government, is designed to address challenges in Nigeria’s housing sector by tackling both supply and demand constraints.

Explaining its objectives, MREIF said it was established to provide affordable mortgage financing, support housing development, generate employment and deepen local manufacturing of building materials.

It also aims to create up to two million jobs, generate up to $10bn in mortgage assets and contribute up to $20bn to economic growth.

Requirements for employed applicants

Employed Nigerians seeking to access the mortgage facility are required to submit personal, employment and financial documents as part of the application process.

According to the fund’s application requirements, applicants must provide the following:

Personal documents

* Loan application letter.

* Completed application form.

* Bank Verification Number (BVN) printout.

* Recent utility bill not older than three months.

* Signed sales or provisional offer letter.

* Passport photograph.

Employment and financial documents

* Appointment or employment letter, or last promotion letter.

* Curriculum vitae.

* Staff identity card.

* Salary account statement covering one year.

* Payslips covering one year.

* Tax clearance card or Tax Identification Number (TIN).

* PENCOM statement (optional).

Additional requirements for joint applications

Employed applicants submitting joint applications with their spouses must also provide:

* Spouse’s consent letter for the joint application.

* Valid means of identification.

* BVN printout.

* Passport photograph.

* Salary or business account statement.

* Tax clearance card or TIN.

* Spouse’s appointment or employment letter, or last promotion letter.

* Spouse’s CV and staff identity card.

* One-year salary account statement and payslips.

* PENCOM account statement (optional for Retirement Savings Account holders).

The fund also lists the following additional documents for applicants to upload after submitting their initial applications:

* Letter of introduction from the applicant’s human resources department.

* Two reference forms completed by current account holders with commercial banks. The accounts must be at least six months old and must not be salary accounts.

* Preferred Primary Mortgage Bank (PMB) account opening form.

* Evidence of equity contribution.

Requirements for self-employed applicants

Self-employed Nigerians are also eligible to apply but must provide additional documents to establish their business operations and demonstrate their financial capacity.

The requirements include:

Personal documents

* Completed loan application form.

* Loan application letter.

* Signed sales or provisional offer letter.

* Recent utility bill, such as an electricity or water bill.

* Passport photograph.

* Three years’ personal bank account statements.

* CV.

* PENCOM account statement (optional).

Business documents

* Copy of Corporate Affairs Commission (CAC) registration documents.

* Three years’ company bank account statements.

* Company profile, including a list of clients.

* Evidence of trade association payment and endorsement.

* Tax certificate or TIN.

Additional requirements for joint applications

Self-employed applicants submitting joint applications with their spouses must provide:

* Spouse’s consent letter.

* Copy of CAC documents.

* Valid means of identification.

* BVN printout.

* Passport photograph.

* Three years’ company bank account statements.

* Evidence of trade association payment and endorsement.

* Tax certificate or TIN.

* Spouse’s CV.

* PENCOM account statement (optional).

Other documents required include:

* Two references.

* Board resolution authorising the borrowing and guaranteeing of the facility.

* Evidence of running contracts and contract renewals.

* Preferred PMB account opening form.

* Three years’ audited or management accounts.

* Evidence of equity contribution payment.

Diaspora applicants’ requirements

Nigerians living abroad can also access the mortgage facility, although they are required to make a higher initial contribution.

According to MREIF, diaspora applicants must provide evidence of an equity contribution of at least 40 per cent of the property’s value.

Other application requirements include:

Personal and residence documents

* Completed loan application form.

* Loan application letter.

* Signed sales or provisional offer letter.

* Passport photograph.

* CV.

* Copy of residence permit and work permit.

* Utility bill not older than three months.

* Evidence of tax payment.

* Evidence of equity contribution of at least 40 per cent.

Income verification documents

* Bank account statements covering 12 months.

* Payslips covering 12 months.

* Employment letter or letter of last promotion.

Additional documents

* Two Nigerian references.

* PENCOM statement (optional).

* At least two credit search reports from the country of residence.

* Letter of introduction from the employer.

One property per borrower under mortgage scheme

Although MREIF allows Nigerians to purchase multiple houses with their personal resources, the fund limits the number of properties an individual can acquire through its mortgage financing.

“Home buyers can buy multiple houses with their own resources, but can only buy one unit through MREIF mortgage financing,” it stated.

The fund also said its housing projects would cover states across Nigeria where there were available homebuyers.

On the mortgage products available, MREIF listed its pension-backed mortgage and a non-interest mortgage option, which it said was coming soon.

The fund explained that its intervention was designed to address Nigeria’s housing deficit, limited access to affordable mortgage financing and the need to provide offtake guarantees for qualified housing developers.

It said it intended to improve housing affordability by offering mortgage financing to homebuyers and offtake guarantees to housing delivery partners through a technology-driven platform.

According to the fund, the platform would allow Nigerians to view available housing units and complete purchase transactions.

MREIF also said it would employ due diligence, active asset management and a dedicated risk management team to mitigate market, liquidity, operational and regulatory risks.

The post MREIF mortgage: What you need for the ₦100m FG-backed housing loan appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Kenyan world marathon champion Peres Jepchirchir banned for three years over doping
description:
Reigning world marathon champion Peres Jepchirchir has been handed a three-year ban for doping, the Athletics Integrity Unit (AIU) has announced.
The suspension marks another setback for the reputation of Kenyan athletics, following the doping case involving the highly decorated 33-year-old athlete.
content:
Reigning world marathon champion Peres Jepchirchir has been handed a three-year ban for doping, the Athletics Integrity Unit (AIU) has announced.

The suspension marks another setback for the reputation of Kenyan athletics, following the doping case involving the highly decorated 33-year-old athlete.

Jepchirchir, who won Olympic gold at the Tokyo Games in 2021 after the event was postponed due to the COVID-19 pandemic, was suspended after an out-of-competition sample revealed traces of erythropoietin (EPO), a banned substance used to boost blood performance.

The AIU confirmed on Thursday that the Kenyan athlete had received a three-year suspension, effective from October 20.

Veronica Loleo, half marathon silver medallist at the World Road Running Championships in 2026, was given three years for the same offence.

And Ronald Korir, a fourth-place finisher in the 2023 Berlin Marathon, received a six-year ban after he was unable to explain abnormalities in his Athlete Biological Passport.

They join more than 140 Kenyan athletes, including current women’s marathon world record-holder Ruth Chepngetich, who have been suspended or banned by the AIU since 2017.

“The Kenyan authorities have made a lot of progress in the fight against doping in the last five years, but these cases highlight that there is still a long way to go,” AIU chief executive Brett Clothier said in a statement.

“The Kenyan government is aware of the current situation and has committed to further strengthen the Anti-Doping Agency of Kenya and take action to address the criminal networks that facilitate doping within the country,” he added.

The AIU said Jepchirchir’s out-of-competition sample had been collected in Kenya prior to her victory in the Sydney Marathon in August.

Jepchirchir’s lauded career has also seen her as a former world record-holder in the half-marathon while she is a four-time World Marathon Major winner having also captured titles in the London Marathon in 2024, the Boston Marathon (2022) and the New York Marathon (2021).

The decision of World Athletics to award Nairobi the 2029 world championships is likely to increase the scrutiny of the east African nation’s anti-doping policies.

Kenya hosted a three-day visit from the World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA) last month, the body’s chief Witold Banka telling the country that it had to strive for zero tolerance on doping.

“Kenya proudly calls itself the Home of Champions. But for that home to remain respected and credible, it must also be clean,” Banka said.

title: Anthony Joshua welcomes baby girl
description:
British boxing champion Anthony Joshua has spoken about his excitement over becoming a father to a baby girl, saying the arrival of his daughter has given him a new perspective on fatherhood.
Joshua and his childhood sweetheart, Nicole Osbourne, welcomed their daughter on November 14, 2026.
The form
content:
British boxing champion Anthony Joshua has spoken about his excitement over becoming a father to a baby girl, saying the arrival of his daughter has given him a new perspective on fatherhood.

Joshua and his childhood sweetheart, Nicole Osbourne, welcomed their daughter on November 14, 2026.

The former two-time unified heavyweight champion and Osbourne, also share an 11-year-old son, Joseph.

Speaking in an interview with The Sun which started trending on Thursday, Joshua said having a daughter would give him a better understanding of women and how to support them.

“Now I’ve got a daughter, I will get an insight and a bit more understanding of what it means to be a woman, and how I can be supportive. My daughter will give me firsthand experience of a woman’s power.

“I’ve spoken to all the women in my family, and it’s amazing the amount of support that women give each other. We haven’t given her a name yet, but she’s my Princess,” he said.

Describing the birth as a huge blessing, Joshua said he was delighted to become a girl dad, adding that he had chosen not to find out the baby’s sex during the pregnancy.

“It’s been amazing, a big blessing and I can’t believe I’m a girl dad. I didn’t want to find the sex out during the pregnancy.

“I love boys but as soon as I found out we had a little girl I said, ‘No more Fifa, no more motorbiking, no more PlayStation!’” he said.

The boxer also expressed his willingness to take an active role in his daughter’s upbringing, including taking part in activities such as dressing up and playing with dolls.

“I’m going to do it all, so you might see me with some eyeshadow on, some nail polish on, drinking some tea in a doll’s playhouse and just trying to do the right thing by her, you know?

“I will change nappies, I’ve gotta go through all that stinky bum time again!” he added.

The development comes ahead of Joshua’s reported December 11 showdown with fellow British heavyweight boxer Tyson Fury.

title: Commonwealth Games gold medallist loses arm in motorcycle crash
description:
Commonwealth Games gold medallist weightlifter Mohd Hafizuddin Roslin had his right arm amputated after a serious motorcycle accident in his native Malaysia.
The 21-year-old was conscious and in a stable condition in hospital on Thursday, three days after the crash, the country’s top weightlifting o
content:
Commonwealth Games gold medallist weightlifter Mohd Hafizuddin Roslin had his right arm amputated after a serious motorcycle accident in his native Malaysia.

The 21-year-old was conscious and in a stable condition in hospital on Thursday, three days after the crash, the country’s top weightlifting official said.

Hafizuddin won Commonwealth gold in the 88kg event in Glasgow in July and was a prospect for the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics.

“He is awake and smiling,” Malaysia Weightlifting Federation president Ayub Rahmat told AFP.

“Physically his condition is improving but this incident has had a great impact on his future.”

He called it “a shock and a huge loss” for weightlifting in the country.

Doctors amputated Hafizuddin’s arm above the elbow, local media reports said.

The Malaysian government said it would cover all his treatment and medical costs.

“We are already looking at how he can be integrated into the sport, including a future coaching role in weightlifting,” Ayub added.

AFP

title: Learn to grow; stop running your mouth all over – Lamido tells Shettima
description:
By Muhammad Inuwa, Dutse



‎Former Jigawa State Governor and Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) founding member, Dr Sule Lamido, has called on Vice President Kashim Shettima to exercise greater caution in his public comments, urging him to demonstrate the maturity and seriousness expected of someone ho
content:
By Muhammad Inuwa, Dutse

‎Former Jigawa State Governor and Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) founding member, Dr Sule Lamido, has called on Vice President Kashim Shettima to exercise greater caution in his public comments, urging him to demonstrate the maturity and seriousness expected of someone holding such a high office.

‎Lamido made the remarks while speaking with journalists shortly after the PDP campaign flag-off in Dutse on Wednesday.

‎He acknowledged Shettima’s intelligence, eloquence and personal qualities but argued that effective leadership requires more than these attributes.

According to him, the Vice President must recognise the importance of his position and appreciate the responsibility that comes with being the country’s second-highest political office holder and a leading figure in Northern Nigeria.

‎”Let him understand that he is number one in the North. Whatever he says must be taken seriously. He needs to move away from jokes because I think he does not fully appreciate the responsibilities attached to the office he occupies,” Lamido said.

He further challenged Shettima to use his position to advance the interests of Northern Nigeria rather than engage in public exchanges that could undermine the dignity of his office.

‎Lamido also expressed displeasure over some of the Vice President’s previous remarks about prominent political figures, including former Vice President Yemi Osinbajo, former Vice President Atiku Abubakar and former Senate President Ahmad Lawan.

He recalled that Shettima had previously referred to Osinbajo as an ice-cream seller and Atiku as a sanitation inspector, describing such remarks as disrespectful to individuals who had occupied important positions in the country.

‎The former governor maintained that Shettima should be more conscious of how his statements are received and interpreted by the public.

‎”He needs to be more serious and go beyond making jokes. He should consider what he says, how people perceive him and the meaning they attach to his statements instead of speaking carelessly,” he said.

Lamido stressed that the Vice Presidency demands a high level of responsibility and decorum, urging Shettima to improve his conduct and demonstrate greater respect for the institution he represents.

‎He added that the position carries responsibilities that should not be treated lightly, insisting that the Vice President must rise to the expectations of his office.

‎Speaking at the event , Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) chairman in Jigawa State Hon. Babandi Ibrahim Gumel says the momouth crowd shows the people of the state are tired with the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) and are ready to votes it out coming 2027 governorship election, insisting that incumbency will not guarantee its victory.

‎The party said the growing dissatisfaction among residents over their current condition would pave the way for the PDP’s return to power in the state.

Speaking on behalf of the candidates, the PDP governorship candidate, Mustapha Sule Lamido, thanked the party leadership and members for giving them the mandate to contest the forthcoming elections.

He assured residents that all PDP candidates would conduct peaceful and violence-free campaigns while seeking the support of voters across the state.

title: NIS Bans Unauthorised Sports Coaching Programmes In Nigeria
description: The management of the National Institute for Sports has issued a directive banning sports federations, associations, and other organisations from running coaching courses without the Institute’s prior approval.The NIS is the sole legally recognised professional institute responsible for traini
content:
The management of the National Institute for Sports has issued a directive banning sports federations, associations, and other organisations from running coaching courses without the Institute’s prior approval.

The NIS is the sole legally recognised professional institute responsible for training coaches and regulating coaching education across all sports in Nigeria.

The measure, according to a statement by the Service, is aimed at protecting the integrity, credibility, and uniform standards of sports coaching nationwide in line with global best practices.

It noted that the Sports Federations and relevant bodies have been directed to seek formal approval from NIS before launching any coaching education initiatives.

The management emphasised that the ban was necessary in line with the renewed agenda of the institution to protect the integrity, standards and credibility of coaching education in the country, ensuring that individuals who present themselves as professionally trained coaches meet the required standards.

The management further maintained that all stakeholders in the Nigerian sports sector must recognise the statutory responsibility of the NIS and work within the established regulatory framework before embarking on any coaching education initiative.

The ban, the NIS noted, reinforces its commitment to maintaining professional standards in coach education and strengthening the development of sports through properly regulated training programmes.

title: Police foil plot to abduct Kwara businessman, arrest seven suspects
description:
The Intelligence Response Team (IRT) of the Nigeria Police Force has foiled a suspected plot to abduct an unnamed businessman in Bode Saadu area of Kwara State.
The team also arrested seven suspects and recovered a firearm and ammunition.
Police Public Relations Officer (PPRO) in Kwara, SP Adetoun E
content:
The Intelligence Response Team (IRT) of the Nigeria Police Force has foiled a suspected plot to abduct an unnamed businessman in Bode Saadu area of Kwara State.

The team also arrested seven suspects and recovered a firearm and ammunition.

Police Public Relations Officer (PPRO) in Kwara, SP Adetoun Ejire-Adeyemi, disclosed this in a Thursday statement on behalf of the state Commissioner of Police.

Ejire-Adeyemi disclosed that while acting on credible intelligence, IRT personnel raided a hideout in Bode Saadu at about 8:30pm on Monday, November 16.

According to the statement, preliminary investigations indicate that the suspects were planning the abduction at the location when they were apprehended.

The suspects were identified as Shehu Tijani, 20, alias Malami; Abubakar Ali, 19, alias Bodo; Abubakar Garba Mohammed, 20; Bello Mohammadu Haruna, 25; Dahiru Abdullahi, alias Dogo; Abubakar Mohammadu, 30, alias Siddi; and Buba Alhaji Umar, 20, alias Hambunle.

The police spokesperson further disclosed that the operation led to the recovery of one locally fabricated revolver and 30 rounds of 7.62mm ammunition.

The statement reads, “During questioning, the suspects admitted involvement in previous kidnapping incidents in Bode Saadu and neighboring communities.

“They also provided information on suspected accomplices still at large.

“The investigation has now widened to trace and apprehend those accomplices and recover weapons in their possession.”

The Kwara State Commissioner of Police, CP Ojo Adekimi, reassured residents of Bode Saadu and neighbouring communities that their safety remains a priority.

He emphasised that the command would continue to use intelligence to identify emerging threats and intervene before lives and livelihoods are put at risk.

Chinese President Xi Jinping has said that relations between China and the United States have remained generally stable and improved.
Xi made this known on Thursday during a meeting with his US counterpart, Donald Trump, in Shenzhen, marking their third face-to-face meeting this year.
“During this p
content:
Chinese President Xi Jinping has said that relations between China and the United States have remained generally stable and improved.

Xi made this known on Thursday during a meeting with his US counterpart, Donald Trump, in Shenzhen, marking their third face-to-face meeting this year.

“During this period, China-US relations have remained generally stable and improved, bringing tangible benefits to the people of both countries and injecting stability and certainty into the world,” Xi said.

His remarks came ahead of the leaders’ trilateral talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin.

Also speaking, Trump said the United States and China were willing to work together to help end the war between Russia and Ukraine.

“We’re looking to both help with respect to the war with Russia and Ukraine. I’d like to see it ended; I think I can speak for both of us, very much,” Trump said.

title: Nollywood star Nancy Isime opens up on juggling acting, TV presenting
description:
Nollywood actress and television presenter Nancy Isime has opened up on how she managed the demands of acting and television presenting when she began her acting career, describing the experience as hectic but manageable.
The 34-year-old actress spoke during a recent interview on the Nollywood On Ra
content:
Nollywood actress and television presenter Nancy Isime has opened up on how she managed the demands of acting and television presenting when she began her acting career, describing the experience as hectic but manageable.

The 34-year-old actress spoke during a recent interview on the Nollywood On Radio podcast, where she was asked how she balanced her television presenting duties with her growing acting career.

Isime said she relied on a well-planned schedule to manage both professions, taking on one responsibility after another despite the demanding nature of the jobs.

“It wasn’t bad. I just had a schedule. I did one after the other. It was hectic, but it wasn’t bad. It wasn’t easy, but I did my best,” she said.

Asked how she had changed from the woman she was at the beginning of her career, the actress said she had become more experienced, skilled and better equipped to handle different situations.

“I will just say I’m more experienced, I’m more skilled at life. I understand how to handle certain situations better, certain tasks better, and of course, with age comes some more wisdom,” she said.

In 2024, Isime disclosed that she had never daydreamed about getting married.

She said her priority had always been building her career and attaining financial independence rather than walking down the aisle.

title: Kenyan world marathon champion gets three-year ban for doping
description:
Reigning marathon world champion Peres Jepchirchir has been banned for three years for doping, the Athletics Integrity Unit said on Thursday, in the latest blow to the reputation of Kenyan athletics.
The highly decorated 33-year-old Jepchirchir, who also won Olympic gold in the COVID-delayed Tokyo G
content:
Reigning marathon world champion Peres Jepchirchir has been banned for three years for doping, the Athletics Integrity Unit said on Thursday, in the latest blow to the reputation of Kenyan athletics.

The highly decorated 33-year-old Jepchirchir, who also won Olympic gold in the COVID-delayed Tokyo Games in 2021, was suspended after an out-of-competition sample showed traces of the banned blood booster EPO.

The AIU confirmed she had been given a full ban for three years from October 20.

Two other Kenyan runners were banned.

Veronica Loleo, half marathon silver medallist at the World Road Running Championships in 2026, was given three years for the same offence.

And Ronald Korir, a fourth-place finisher in the 2023 Berlin Marathon, received a six-year ban after he was unable to explain abnormalities in his Athlete Biological Passport.

They join more than 140 Kenyan athletes, including current women’s marathon world record-holder Ruth Chepngetich, who have been suspended or banned by the AIU since 2017.

“The Kenyan authorities have made a lot of progress in the fight against doping in the last five years, but these cases highlight that there is still a long way to go,” AIU chief executive Brett Clothier said in a statement.

“The Kenyan government is aware of the current situation and has committed to further strengthen the Anti-Doping Agency of Kenya and take action to address the criminal networks that facilitate doping within the country,” he added.

The AIU said Jepchirchir’s out-of-competition sample had been collected in Kenya prior to her victory in the Sydney Marathon in August.

Jepchirchir’s lauded career has also seen her as a former world record-holder in the half-marathon, while she is a four-time World Marathon Major winner, having also captured titles in the London Marathon in 2024, the Boston Marathon (2022) and the New York Marathon (2021).

The decision of World Athletics to award Nairobi the 2029 world championships is likely to increase the scrutiny of the East African nation’s anti-doping policies.

Kenya hosted a three-day visit from the World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA) last month, with the body’s chief Witold Banka telling the country that it had to strive for zero tolerance on doping.

“Kenya proudly calls itself the Home of Champions. But for that home to remain respected and credible, it must also be clean,” Banka said.

AFP

title: Musk says he feels ‘pretty foolish’ for failed US election spending
description:
World’s richest man Elon Musk said Wednesday he felt “pretty foolish” for donating nearly half a billion dollars to failed campaigns in recent US midterm elections, backing right-wing Republicans in races that were largely won by Democrats.



“I feel pretty foolish about having spent so much money
content:
World’s richest man Elon Musk said Wednesday he felt “pretty foolish” for donating nearly half a billion dollars to failed campaigns in recent US midterm elections, backing right-wing Republicans in races that were largely won by Democrats.

“I feel pretty foolish about having spent so much money and not seeing much for it, or maybe it would have been much worse without that,” Musk said via videolink at the New York Times Dealbook conference.

Musk said his goal was “either the presidency, the House or the Senate be of the other party. That was my actual goal here, which failed by the way.”

The Tesla and SpaceX boss sought to extract a lesson from the folly, telling the audience: “It certainly shows that American elections are not just about money.”

“Obviously you can put a lot of money into election and have an effect that is relatively minor, and I think that was the case here,” he continued.

The midterms weren’t the South Africa-born tech tycoon’s first foray into American elections.

Musk spent more than $250 million to help US President Donald Trump return to the White House for his second term and briefly led the 80-year-old Republican’s Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE), before they had a public falling out.

They’ve since reconciled and instead of souring on Republican politics, Musk has continued to back Republicans who the president champions.

Among the candidates he backed most strongly was Texas Senate candidate Ken Paxton, with Musk contributing an estimated $220 million to the Republican, only for the race to be won by James Talarico, a 37-year-old Democrat.

The headquarters of several of Musk’s companies, including SpaceX and Tesla, are in Austin, Texas.

“If I could rewind the clock, I would have spent less money,” Musk said of the elections, adding: “I didn’t put a lot of personal attention into it because I’m focused on building SpaceX, Tesla.”

title: 2027: INEC deploys 186,277 BVAS machines to states
description:
The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has disclosed that it has deployed between 75 and 80 per cent of its Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) devices to states ahead of the 2027 general elections.
The deployment represents about 186,277 BVAS devices, with some states still wait
content:
The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has disclosed that it has deployed between 75 and 80 per cent of its Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) devices to states ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The deployment represents about 186,277 BVAS devices, with some states still waiting to receive their complete allocations.

INEC National Commissioner, Mohammed Haruna, disclosed this in an exclusive interview with Very Nigerian in Abuja, explaining that while most states had received their equipment, others were yet to collect all the devices allocated to them.

Haruna assured that all outstanding equipment and non-sensitive election materials would be delivered before the end of November.

He said, “About 75 to 80 per cent of the BVAs have been deployed to states. Most states have received them, though not the full complement. Some have received the full complement of the materials, but some have a few numbers left to collect”.

He, however, identified Kano, the Federal Capital Territory and Kaduna as among the states that have received full deployment of non-sensitive election materials.

“Almost all the states have received their materials. But the ones that are complete, I know FCT, for instance, Kano and Kaduna too.”

INEC had disclosed Thursday last week that it had begun the distribution of non-sensitive materials to some states ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The commission, while hosting a delegation from Kenya’s Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission, further disclosed that it has completed nine scheduled activities and was stepping up preparations following an assessment of its readiness across the six geopolitical zones.

The Commission said, “We have six zones in Nigeria. The purpose is to go around the zones to see how prepared we are, assess what the zones have put in place, the challenges and what to do.

“Right now, all non-sensitive materials are almost ready. In fact, today as we speak here, the non-sensitive materials have been lifted to some zones now.”

In 2023, INEC deployed a total of 175,856 BVAs machines to 176,846 polling units nationwide. However, in October, the INEC chairman, Professor Joash Amupitan (SAN), announced that INEC has procured an additional 57,000 BVAs devices in addition to its existing inventory to strengthen its technological capacity ahead of the 2027 polls.

With its additional procurement, The PUNCH projected a total of 232,846 BVAs devices for the 2027 elections, representing an increase of approximately 32.4 per cent over the 2023 deployment.

Amupitan also said that the maximum number of registered voters assigned to one BVAs has been reduced from 1,250 to 850.

He added that polling units with more than 850 registered voters will receive multiple BVAs. Meanwhile, in 2023, the standard operational arrangement was one BVAS device per polling unit.

Additionally, INEC has created 453 additional polling units, which brings the total number of polling units nationwide for the 2027 elections to 177,299.

Speaking further with our correspondent, Haruna stressed that the commission expects all states to receive their outstanding materials before the end of November.

“So, I’m sure by the end of the month, before the end of the month, all the states will receive the full complement,” he said.

On the distribution of sensitive election materials, the national commissioner explained that the commission had adopted a centralised arrangement involving the Central Bank of Nigeria to safeguard the materials until the week of the elections.

He said the sensitive materials had already been delivered to CBN offices across the country, where they would remain in custody until they were due for distribution.

“Of course, sensitive materials, those, we won’t start distributing them now. We take them straight to the CBN for custody until the week of the election,” he said.

Haruna added that the distribution would be conducted at the CBN premises in the presence of political party agents, the media and civil society organisations to ensure transparency.

“And, you know, we distribute them from CBN. All the agents from political parties will be there. The media is there, civil society organisations are there at the CBN premises.

“That’s where we are going to distribute them. But they have been delivered already to CBN offices around the country,” he stated.

On the deployment and configuration of the BVAS, the INEC commission explained that the commission would undertake the configuration exercise close to the elections rather than at this stage of preparation for the Mock accreditation fixed for November 28.

He pointed out that each device was customised to a particular polling unit to ensure accountability and prevent misuse.

“The BVAs, we’ll configure them close to the election. We’ll not configure them now. You know, each one is customised to each polling unit. Each BVA is for its own area, so that at least you can hold somebody responsible,” he said.

On measures being introduced to strengthen electoral transparency and improve the credibility of the voting process, the commissioner disclosed that INEC had strengthened its electronic transmission and verification procedures through the electronic version of Form EC8A.

He explained that the electronic form would provide an additional layer of verification by ensuring that results uploaded by presiding officers corresponded with the results agreed upon and signed by polling officials, party agents and security personnel.

According to him, the system would reject results where discrepancies existed between the electronically entered figures and the agreed polling unit results.

He said, “But the main thing we have done is this EC8A. There’s an e-version of it. So once the presiding officer, once they agree, they have updated, they have looked at the results, they have agreed that that is the accurate result, the polling agent signs, security signs.

“He tries to upload it onto the app. Suppose he doesn’t agree, because the one that has been entered before, you know, if there’s a discrepancy, it will not be uploaded. It will not be the same content.”

Haruna, however, said the commission was introducing additional measures to strengthen the electoral process but would not disclose all the details publicly, citing security considerations.

“There are so many things that we’re doing. But there are certain things, of course, we cannot reveal. Because if you do, it’s actually harmful for security reasons,” he said.

He added that while INEC remained committed to improving the transparency and integrity of elections, some of its operational safeguards would remain undisclosed to prevent possible exploitation.

Following the enactment of the Electoral Act 2026, the Independent National Electoral Commission has revised the timetable for the 2027 general elections, fixing January 16, 2027, for the presidential and National Assembly elections.

The commission also scheduled the governorship and State Houses of Assembly elections for February 6, 2027.

The post 2027: INEC deploys 186,277 BVAS machines to states appeared first on Very Nigerian.
