title: GOKA BET Strengthens Brand Strategy, Signs Obafemi Martins As Brand Ambassador
description: Sports betting and gaming company GOKA BET has strengthened its brand positioning with the unveiling of former Super Eagles striker Obafemi Martins as its official brand ambassador, in a strategic move aimed at deepening its connection with sports and entertainment audiences across Nigeria and Afric
content:
Sports betting and gaming company GOKA BET has strengthened its brand positioning with the unveiling of former Super Eagles striker Obafemi Martins as its official brand ambassador, in a strategic move aimed at deepening its connection with sports and entertainment audiences across Nigeria and Africa.

The partnership, announced at a press conference held in Lagos, Nigeria, represents a significant step in the company’s efforts to build a distinctive entertainment brand and expand its reach within the African market.

Speaking at the event, GOKA BET’s Marketing Manager and Partnership Specialist, Titilayo Ismail Adebanjo, described Martins’ appointment as an important milestone in the company’s growth journey.

He said that the former Nigerian international’s remarkable football career, international experience and longstanding relationship with football fans made him a valuable addition to the brand.

According to him, the partnership goes beyond securing a familiar face for the company, as it is designed to create meaningful connections with football supporters and entertainment audiences through engaging campaigns, memorable brand experiences and other initiatives.

Adebanjo said GOKA BET was committed to building a trusted and distinctive platform anchored on accessibility, reliability, transparency and customer satisfaction.

He added that the company recognised the expectations of Nigerian customers and would continue to pursue innovation and improved customer experiences to strengthen public confidence in its services.

Speaking on his appointment, Martins expressed excitement about joining the GOKA BET family, describing football as a powerful force that connects people, creates unforgettable moments and brings millions of fans together.

The former striker said his experiences playing professional football in different countries had given him a deeper appreciation of the passion the game generates among Nigerian and African supporters.

He described the partnership as an opportunity to connect with sports and casino fans in a new and exciting way while contributing to the growth of a brand making its mark in the Nigerian and African markets.

“I have played and scored goals across some of the biggest stages in world football, and now I’m bringing that same passion and winning mentality with me on a new journey with GOKA BET,” Martins said.

He added that he looked forward to working with the company to develop exciting experiences and engaging campaigns that would strengthen its relationship with football fans across the continent.

Martins also called on his supporters and football lovers across Nigeria and Africa to join him on the new journey, expressing optimism about the opportunities ahead.

On responsible gaming, both Martins and Adebanjo emphasised the importance of ensuring that betting and casino gaming remained forms of entertainment rather than a guaranteed source of income.

Martins encouraged customers to participate responsibly and within their financial means, while Adebanjo urged players to understand their limits and make informed decisions.

He said that the company’s long-term ambition was to build a sustainable brand founded on trust, transparency, respect for customers and consistent service delivery.

Adebanjo added that the partnership reinforced GOKA BET’s determination to establish a lasting presence in Nigeria, with opportunities to extend its reach into other African markets.

The GOKA BET’s platform brings sports betting and online casino together in a single, seamless experience. On the sportsbook side, players get competitive odds across football, basketball, tennis, esports, horse racing, greyhound racing and virtual sports; and on the casino side, it offers a constantly refreshed library of games powered by certified Random Number Generator technology, including online slots, live blackjack, live roulette, baccarat, poker variants, crash games, Keno, Mines, Plinko and Lucky Wheel.

title: Port Harcourt Int’I Airport Conducts Emergency Response Exercise To Enhance Preparedness
description: The Port Harcourt International Airport has conducted an emergency response exercise to assess its preparedness and response capacity in handling aircraft emergencies in line with regulatory requirements of the Nigerian Civil Aviation Authority (NCAA).The full-scale exercise, held on Wednesday, invo
content:
The Port Harcourt International Airport has conducted an emergency response exercise to assess its preparedness and response capacity in handling aircraft emergencies in line with regulatory requirements of the Nigerian Civil Aviation Authority (NCAA).

The full-scale exercise, held on Wednesday, involved emergency responders, including firefighters, security personnel, medical teams and the airport control unit.

The simulation featured an aircraft emergency that triggered an alarm, prompting responders to evacuate victims, extinguish the simulated fire, secure the affected area and transport injured persons to the airport hospital for treatment.

Speaking during the exercise, Lydia Ezike, Regional Manager, South South, Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria (FAAN), said the exercise was designed to test the adequacy of the airport’s emergency plan, response capabilities and coordination among relevant agencies.

“We are conducting a full-scale emergency mock exercise in compliance with the regulatory requirements as stipulated by NCAA to test the adequacy of the airport emergency plan and procedures.

“We are testing the response capability of the primary emergency responders, as well as the communication and coordination with stakeholders,” she said.

Ezike added that the exercise would be followed by an evaluation by regulators and further simulations to equip personnel with the technical knowledge required to respond effectively to emergencies involving aircraft within the airport and its eight-kilometre radius.

She advised passengers and airport users to observe safety signs and comply with instructions from airlines and airport authorities to ensure safe flights and a positive travel experience.

Also speaking, the Airport Chief of Security, Ukaegbu Stephen, said the essence of the exercise was to prepare them to respond effectively in the event of an emergency.

He said the emergency responders demonstrated promptness in responding to the simulated incident.

He explained that firefighters arrived promptly, while aviation security personnel secured the area and controlled access to ensure an orderly response.

General Manager in the Nigerian Civil Aviation Authority, Chukwu Emmanuel, who observed the exercise, described emergency preparedness as essential to airport safety.

He said accidents could occur without warning, stressing the need for continuous training and preparedness among airport personnel.

“The thing about accidents is that it doesn’t announce itself. What we do is to make sure that we get the personnel ready as to how they will respond in a situation where there is an emergency occurrence, which is either an incident or an accident,” he said.

Emmanuel added that emergency preparedness should not be limited to any particular period or season, noting that the airport must maintain the highest safety standards at all times.

He said regular training, emergency preparedness meetings and other safety programmes were necessary to ensure personnel understood their responsibilities during emergencies.

title: Odukoya succession: What Adeboye, Kumuyi, Oyedepo said about their successors
description: The leadership crisis at The Fountain of Life Church, following the disputed removal of Pastor Jimmy Odukoya as Senior Pastor, has brought renewed attention to the question of succession in Nigeria’s major Christian denominations led by Pastor Enoch Adeboye, Pastor WF Kumuyi and Bishop David Oyedepo
content:
The leadership crisis at The Fountain of Life Church, following the disputed removal of Pastor Jimmy Odukoya as Senior Pastor, has brought renewed attention to the question of succession in Nigeria’s major Christian denominations led by Pastor Enoch Adeboye, Pastor WF Kumuyi and Bishop David Oyedepo.

A section of the church’s Board of Trustees announced that it no longer recognised Jimmy Odukoya as Senior Pastor and appointed Pastor Rotimi Okpaise as interim spiritual and administrative leader. The trustees cited governance concerns and information about the late founder, Pastor Taiwo Odukoya’s succession preference.

However, Jimmy Odukoya and his supporters rejected the announcement, insisting that he remained the duly appointed Senior Pastor and Chairman of the Board of Trustees. They described the trustees behind the decision as a group acting outside the church’s constitutional framework.

The disagreement has renewed discussions about how leadership should pass from one generation to another in churches built around influential founders and long-serving spiritual leaders.

Three prominent Nigerian clerics, the General Overseer of the Redeemed Christian Church of God, Pastor Enoch Adeboye; the General Superintendent of the Deeper Christian Life Ministry, Pastor William Kumuyi; and the Presiding Bishop of the Living Faith Church Worldwide, also known as Winners’ Chapel, Bishop David Oyedepo, have previously spoken about succession in their respective ministries.

While Adeboye has said he is waiting for God to reveal his successor, Kumuyi has rejected the idea of handing the ministry to any of his biological children, insisting that the church belongs to Jesus Christ. Oyedepo, on his part, has described a formal succession procedure contained in his church’s governing document, ‘The Mandate’.

God will reveal successor — Adeboye

Adeboye, who has led the RCCG since 1981, addressed speculation about his successor during the church’s ministers’ conference at the Redemption Camp, Ogun State, in August 2018.

At the time, reports had circulated that he might hand over the leadership of the church to Oyedepo, Pastor Joe Olaiya or one of his sons.

According to Tribune in 2017, the RCCG leader dismissed the speculation, saying he had not received any revelation from God about who would succeed him.

He explained that, based on his understanding of biblical succession, God would inform him before revealing the person to others.

“Elijah knew before Elisha knew that he would succeed him; Moses also knew that Joshua would succeed him and likewise Eli knew before Samuel and not the other way round and therefore, God will tell me first before any other person about who will become my successor as a general overseer,” he said.

Adeboye also addressed claims that Oyedepo, Pastor Joe Olaiya or one of his sons would take over from him.

“Some even said I would hand over to Bishop David Oyedepo, some said to Pastor Joe Olaiya because the two are very close to me and they do minister during our major events such as the conventions, Holy Ghost congresses and yet another quarter said one of my sons is the one succeeding me,” he said.

He urged members and the public to stop spreading speculation about the matter, insisting that no successor had been revealed to him.

“So, let me say it loud and clear again that God has not told me who my successor is.

“What God had told me several years ago was that He would tell me who my successor would be at least five years before I would be called home, and as at this now, He had not told me anything as regards that, which means He is not ready to call me home in the next five years,” Adeboye said.

He also acknowledged the demands that would come with leading the church, saying whoever eventually succeeded him would have to make significant sacrifices.

“Because I know how many hours I pray a day and I can count how many days I eat in a year too.

“So, whoever that will take over from me, such person will have to surpass me and God will have mercy on the person,” he said.

Adeboye’s comments followed an earlier leadership transition in January 2017, when he stepped down as General Overseer of the RCCG in Nigeria and Pastor Joseph Obayemi was appointed National Overseer. Adeboye, however, retained his position as General Overseer of RCCG Worldwide.

Church is not family inheritance — Kumuyi

Kumuyi has also repeatedly rejected the idea that leadership of the Deeper Christian Life Ministry should be transferred to one of his children.

In June 2026, PUNCH Online reported that the cleric addressed speculation that one of his biological sons could eventually succeed him, stressing that the church was not his personal property to be handed over to a family member.

During a church service, he said the ministry belonged to Jesus Christ and that its next leader should emerge through divine direction.

“Our attention has been drawn to the fact that some people are saying, ‘Is he going to hand over the church to his son?’ It’s the church of the Lord Jesus Christ and nobody has the right to hand it over to his son,” he said.

Kumuyi also cited biblical figures, arguing that the early leaders of the Christian faith did not transfer the church to their biological children.

“Peter did not hand over the church to his son. Paul did not have any son or wife, but Paul did not hand over the church to his son. And John did not hand over the church to his son,” he said.

The cleric had addressed the succession question earlier, in August 2025, when he expressed displeasure over what he described as subtle agitations within the church about his successor.

Speaking during a Bible study programme, PUNCH Online reported that Kumuyi questioned whether some members were already tired of his leadership and warned against attempts to pressure him into stepping aside.

“Are you tired of me?” he asked, prompting a response from members of the congregation.

The cleric was particularly concerned about comments by an unnamed young preacher who, according to him, had repeatedly said there was no leadership without a successor.

“The brother who taught the other Tuesday kept saying there is no leadership without a successor.

“He said it twice. I felt that was too much, more so since your father is still here. God will give a successor at His own time,” Kumuyi said.

He maintained that members should not attempt to dictate when he should leave office, adding that the issue of his successor was in God’s hands.

“You are not going to fight your shepherd, your pilot. I reject any member of the church, whether you are a worker, choir member, or security person, who tries to control me,” he said.

He further warned against attempts to undermine his conviction.

“Don’t try to kill my conviction. It will only make me resist you so that when you get to the other side, you won’t say I did not tell you.

“I will keep on telling you that under your resistance until I go,” he added.

Kumuyi, however, acknowledged that the ministry would eventually have a successor, but insisted that the choice would not be dictated by pressure from members.

“When the time comes, God will choose a man after His own heart. Don’t try to drive me away, even though I know you cannot,” he said.

Winners’ Chapel has succession procedure — Oyedepo

Unlike Adeboye and Kumuyi, who have publicly emphasised divine direction in the choice of their successors, Oyedepo has spoken about a formal procedure for leadership transition in the Living Faith Church Worldwide.

In a sermon reported by Daily Times Nigeria in June 2020, the bishop said the succession process was contained in The Mandate, a document he described as the church’s governing guide.

According to him, the procedure requires the presiding bishop to submit three names to the Council of Priests upon attaining the age of 70.

The candidates are then examined by the church’s secretariat to determine whether they meet the required qualifications.

Oyedepo explained that if none of the nominees qualified, the names would be returned to the presiding bishop, who would have another opportunity to submit a fresh list. If the second submission also failed, the Council of Priests would take over the process, with the Board ratifying the eventual decision.

He described the arrangement as a defined process designed to prevent uncertainty when a church leader leaves office.

“When you are 70 as leader of this Church, you present 3 names to the Council of Priests for them to see if any of them is qualified by the Secretariat. If they are not qualified, throw it back to you, you have one more chance to make another presentation and after that, you are out of it. The Council takes it, the Board goes to rectify. It is a process, not that somebody dies and then we don’t know what to do,” he said.

The cleric also said the procedure was documented and available to members of the church.

“If you read the book ‘The Mandate’ you will see the succession procedure of apostleship in this ministry. Open, it’s in the hand of everybody,” he said.

Oyedepo further explained that the transition was expected to take place within a specified period, saying the process was designed to ensure that the church would not be left without a clear leadership direction.

He also warned against treating churches as personal or family property, arguing that such an approach undermined the purpose of the ministry.

“If you want to leave a church as an inheritance for your family, the Church has died,” he said.

He reinforced the position by warning that a church should not become an enterprise owned by its founder.

“If church becomes your personal property, you have lost it, if it becomes a family property, it is dead,” Oyedepo said.

He also cautioned founders against compelling their children to take up ministry roles, saying they should be allowed to pursue the paths for which they were suited.

“Don’t call your sons and daughters to ministry, you may frustrate their destiny, don’t,” he said.

Although the three clerics have expressed their views in different ways and at different times, their public comments indicate opposition to the automatic transfer of church leadership to biological children.

Adeboye has maintained that God would reveal his successor to him at the appropriate time, while Kumuyi has insisted that the church belongs to Jesus Christ and should not be treated as family property.

Oyedepo, meanwhile, has outlined a succession process involving the submission and assessment of nominees by designated church bodies, while warning against turning a ministry into a family inheritance.

Their positions highlight different approaches to succession planning in large religious organisations: divine revelation, the rejection of hereditary leadership and a documented institutional procedure.

In the case of the Fountain of Life Church, the trustees who announced Jimmy Odukoya’s removal maintain that their decision stands, while the pastor and his supporters insist that the process was not constitutionally valid. Both sides have presented competing claims about who has the authority to determine the church’s leadership.

The post Odukoya succession: What Adeboye, Kumuyi, Oyedepo said about their successors appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Police rescue 15 kidnap victims in Kogi
description:
The Kogi State Police Command has successfully rescued 15 kidnapped victims following an intelligence-led search and rescue operation conducted in the early hours of Wednesday at Magaru Forest, Kakun-Kabba, Kogi State.
A statement issued in the early hours of Thursday by the state police Command’s s
content:
The Kogi State Police Command has successfully rescued 15 kidnapped victims following an intelligence-led search and rescue operation conducted in the early hours of Wednesday at Magaru Forest, Kakun-Kabba, Kogi State.

A statement issued in the early hours of Thursday by the state police Command’s spokesperson, ASP Salisu Afusat stated that the operation was executed pursuant to the directive of the Commissioner of Police, Kogi State Command, Commissioner of Police Naziru Kankarofi.

“It  involved a joint security team comprising personnel of the Kabba Area Command, Kabba ‘A’ Division, Iyara Division, Ekerin-Adde Division, Ayetoro-Gbede Division, Violent Crime Response Unit (VCRU), 70 Police Mobile Force (PMF), the Nigerian Army’s 251 Tank Battalion, Forest Guards, Kogi State Vigilante Services, Agbekoya and Kabba Security Outfit.” ASP Afusat noted.

She said that during the operation, the joint team advanced into the forest and engaged the kidnappers in a fierce gun battle.

“The superior firepower of the security operatives forced the criminals to retreat, with some sustaining varying degrees of gunshot injuries.

The rescued victims include:

1. Okuma Terlum – Male, 47 years
2. Ojo Deborah – Female, 23 years
3. Samuel Danjuma – Male, 3 years
4. Faith Raphael – Female, 21 years
5. Emmanuella Raphael – Female, 3 years
6. Donald Tor – Male, 31 years
7. Joseph Jonathan – Male, 20 years
8. Tergu Joseph – Male, 15 years
9. Samuel Joseph – Male, 8 years
10. Engr. Joseph Adebija – Male, 58 years
11. Lois Abiodun – Female, 50 years
12. Chuks Obiakor – Male, 45 years
13. Ola Olufemi – Male, 58 years
14. Ankpe Godwin – Male, 23 years
15. Kuhwa Solomon – Male, 25 years.

She said that two other female victims, identified only as Joy and Nwakan, escaped from their abductors during the initial encounter where the victims were taken captive.

“While conveying the rescued victims out of the forest, the joint security team came under another ambush by members of the criminal gang in a desperate attempt to frustrate the rescue mission. However, the operatives successfully repelled the attack through superior firepower and safely brought all fifteen victims out of the forest.”

She said that the victims were debriefed and immediately conveyed to St. John’s Catholic Hospital, Kabba, for medical attention, having endured considerable physical and psychological distress during their captivity.

Afusat, however, said, “Although no suspects have been arrested, actionable intelligence has been generated, and an intelligence-led investigation is ongoing to track down and apprehend the fleeing members of the kidnapping syndicate, as well as identify and bring their sponsors to justice”.

The commissioner of police commended the courage, resilience and effective collaboration demonstrated by all participating security agencies and local security outfits.

He reiterated the command’s unwavering commitment to sustaining coordinated operations against kidnapping and other violent crimes across the state.

The command appreciated the support and cooperation of members of the public and urges residents to continue providing credible and timely information to assist security agencies in the ongoing efforts to rid Kogi State of criminal elements.

The post Police rescue 15 kidnap victims in Kogi appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Lagos-Ibadan gridlock: Tinubu’s aide spends five hours in traffic, faults contractor
description:
President Bola Tinubu’s Special Adviser on Media and Communications, Sunday Dare, has faulted the timing of ongoing construction on the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway after being caught in traffic for more than five hours on his way to Ibadan, Oyo State.



Dare lamented that the congestion had left thousa
content:
President Bola Tinubu’s Special Adviser on Media and Communications, Sunday Dare, has faulted the timing of ongoing construction on the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway after being caught in traffic for more than five hours on his way to Ibadan, Oyo State.

Dare lamented that the congestion had left thousands of travellers stranded, forcing some to abandon their vehicles and walk long distances to their destinations.

In a Facebook post on Wednesday night, he questioned why the Chinese firm handling the project chose to carry out the work during peak traffic periods instead of at night when fewer vehicles use the road.

“It beats me why a Chinese Contractor would choose the busiest hours of vehicular traffic to construct the bridge and road around this exit point. Stranded cars, thousands of people trekking to get home,” he wrote.

He added, “What happened to doing construction work during the obituary hours when traffic is lean? This is unnecessary pain. It needs to be corrected.”

The traffic disruption followed the recommencement of work on a pedestrian bridge around the Aseese section of the expressway on Wednesday, affecting motorists travelling in both directions.

title: Ibom Air records over N5b profit in 1 year, appoints 2 executive directors
description:
Ibom Airlines Limited (Ibom Air) has declared  profit of ₦5.485 billion for the financial year ended 31 December 2025, sustaining its profitability despite the unfavourable aviation environment. 
The results were presented at the airline’s Annual General Meeting (AGM), held on 17 November 2026 at it
content:
Ibom Airlines Limited (Ibom Air) has declared  profit of ₦5.485 billion for the financial year ended 31 December 2025, sustaining its profitability despite the unfavourable aviation environment. 

The results were presented at the airline’s Annual General Meeting (AGM), held on 17 November 2026 at its Corporate Office, Victor Attah International Airport, Uyo.

A statement  signed  by Ibom Air’s Group  Manager, Marketing & Communications  Aniekan Essienette stated that the AGM brought together shareholders, directors, management, and key stakeholders to review the Company’s financial performance and strategic direction.

Essienette said the Chsirman of Ibom Air Mr Mfon Udom while Presenting the audited financial results explained that the airline delivered record passenger numbers, record number of flights and record revenue in 2025, with revenue growing by 52% from N96.53B in 2024, to N147.03B in 2025.

She said Udom  attributed the sustained profitability to the Company’s operational discipline, prudent financial management, and commitment to safety and excellent customer service.

Essienette  added that Udom  emphasized the need for the Shareholder to invest further equity in the airline in 2026 to help shore up its balance sheet and position the airline for the next phase of its growth.

She said senator Effiong Bob who represented the shareholders  commended the Board, management, and workforce of Ibom Airline for their dedication to operational excellence and service.

A key outcome of the AGM was the formal ratification of the appointments of Dr. Eno Udoma-Eniang as Executive Director, Legal and Corporate Affairs, and Mr. Mfon Udomah as Executive Director, Finance.

Both Executive Directors bring decades of professional experience and leadership expertise to their roles and are expected to support the airline’s next phase of growth and corporate development.

” We  would further strengthen the Company’s governance structure and executive capacity, positioning Ibom Air for sustained success in an increasingly competitive industry

“Akwa Ibom State Government would  continue to support  the airline . We commend  the Board and management for upholding strong corporate governance standards and delivering value to stakeholders” .

According to Essienette,  stakeholders in attendance were  Senator Emmanuel Ibok Essien, Senator Aloysius Etok, Hon. Owoidighe Ekpotai, Barr. Emmanuel Enoidem, and Chief Okon Osung.

The AGM concluded with a renewed commitment to Ibom Air’s vision of becoming a world-class African regional airline, supported by financial sustainability, service innovation, and operational excellence.

The post Ibom Air records over N5b profit in 1 year, appoints 2 executive directors appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: 2027: Anambra APC inaugurates 350-member campaign council
description:
The All Progressives Congress in Anambra State has inaugurated a 350-member campaign council to coordinate its mobilisation efforts ahead of the 2027 general elections.
The council, inaugurated at the party’s secretariat in Awka on Wednesday, will be led by Chief Azuka Okwusa as Director-General, wh
content:
The All Progressives Congress in Anambra State has inaugurated a 350-member campaign council to coordinate its mobilisation efforts ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The council, inaugurated at the party’s secretariat in Awka on Wednesday, will be led by Chief Azuka Okwusa as Director-General, while the state chairman, Senator Emmanuel Anosike, will serve as its chairman.

Other members include Obiora Okpara as secretary; Dr Valentine Ilobi, Chairman of the Media Directorate; Mark Okoye of the All Progressives Grand Alliance; Emeka Agbasi; and Dr Pascal Candle, among others.

A former Minister of Labour and Employment, Dr Chris Ngige, and the party’s candidate in the 2025 Anambra governorship election, Prince Nicholas Ukachukwu, were named patrons of the council.

Speaking at the inauguration, Anosike urged members to mobilise support for President Bola Tinubu and other APC candidates in the 2027 elections.

He said the party should base its campaign on the achievements and performance of the Tinubu administration rather than sentiments.

Anosike said, “The major purpose of the inauguration is to commence in earnest door-to-door mobilisation campaign across the 5,526 polling units that constitue Anambra State.
The Campaign Council is made up of 350 members.

“The party under my watch is fully prepared to welcome President Tinubu to Anambra State for his re-election campaign rally scheduled for November 19 at the Alex Ekwueme Square, Awka.

“We urged the council members to engage in grassroots campaigns and we charge them to remain in their polling units and not travel until the elections are conducted next year.”

In his acceptance speech, Okwusa called on members to demonstrate discipline, commitment and a willingness to make sacrifices in carrying out their responsibilities.

He described the inauguration as the beginning of a major assignment for the party in the state, warning members against treating their roles as merely ceremonial.

He said, “The 2027 elections will demand discipline, organisation, sacrifice, and absolute commitment for every one of us.

“No one should assume that the task ahead will be easy, and no members of this council should consider this our assignment or role as ceremonial.”

Okwusa also urged members to set aside personal disagreements and work for the collective interest of the party ahead of January 16, 2027.

The event was attended by party candidates, including Senator Uche Ekwunife, Kingsley Ezekwelu and Ambassador Elijah Onyeagba, as well as other party members and journalists.

The APC is seeking to strengthen its political foothold in Anambra following its defeat in the November 8, 2025 governorship election.

The party’s candidate, Nicholas Ukachukwu, polled 99,445 votes to finish second behind incumbent Governor Charles Soludo of the All Progressives Grand Alliance, who secured 422,664 votes to win a second term.

The Independent National Electoral Commission has fixed January 16, 2027, for the presidential and National Assembly elections, while the governorship and State Houses of Assembly elections are scheduled for February 6, 2027.

The post 2027: Anambra APC inaugurates 350-member campaign council appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Youth group hails Tinubu, Umahi over South-East road projects
description:
Youths under the Renewed Hope Youth Infrastructure Tour have embarked on an inspection tour of major road projects in the South-East region, commending President Bola Tinubu and the Minister of Works, David Umahi, for their role in driving critical infrastructural interventions across the region
The
content:
Youths under the Renewed Hope Youth Infrastructure Tour have embarked on an inspection tour of major road projects in the South-East region, commending President Bola Tinubu and the Minister of Works, David Umahi, for their role in driving critical infrastructural interventions across the region

The tour, organised by the Office of the Senior Special Assistant on Youth Mobilisation to the National Chairman of the All Progressives Congress, Juliet Obinta, was aimed at offering young Nigerians an opportunity to observe ongoing and completed Federal Government infrastructure projects, understand their economic importance and engage in conversations about national development.

The exercise, which covered the Eke Obinagu Flyover, Enugu–Onitsha Expressway, Ugwu Onyeama axis and the New Artisan Bridge along the Enugu–Port Harcourt Expressway, among others, highlighted the Federal Government’s infrastructure interventions under the administration of President Bola Tinubu and the implementation efforts of the Ministry of Works under Senator Umahi.

The group said the projects are strategically important to traffic management and connectivity around the busy corridor, with expected benefits for motorists, businesses and residents.

Speaking during the tour on Wednesday, the Senior Special Assistant on Youth Mobilisation to the National Chairman of the All Progressives Congress, Juliet Obinta, commended President Tinubu for prioritising infrastructure development as a major component of his administration’s economic agenda. 

She equally acknowledged Umahi’s leadership of the Ministry of Works and his role in driving the implementation of critical road projects across the country.

She said, “The Renewed Hope Youth Infrastructure Tour is conceived to take young people beyond political conversations and provide them with an opportunity to witness government interventions, understand their impact and communicate their observations to the public.

“We appreciate Mr President and the Minister of Works for supporting the initiative, including the provision of a bus to our office, which facilitated the mobilisation and participation of young people in the exercise.

“Youth participation in governance should extend beyond election periods and social media conversations to include policy awareness, project monitoring, constructive engagement and national development.”

The delegation also visited sections of the Enugu–Onitsha Expressway, including the Ugwu Onyeama axis, where attention was drawn to the importance of sustained road rehabilitation, improved transportation, engineering solutions and road safety.

At the New Artisan Bridge along the Enugu–Port Harcourt Expressway, the delegation highlighted the Federal Government’s intervention following the collapse of the old bridge, which had severely disrupted transportation and forced motorists to navigate alternative routes through different streets within Enugu.

Also at the Peenoks Junction along the expressway, Obinta identified a traffic management challenge involving motorists attempting to access an adjoining road from the opposite carriageway.

She explained that motorists currently have to travel a considerable distance towards the 82 Division axis before making a U-turn to access the connecting road, a situation that reportedly encourages some commercial drivers to engage in dangerous one-way driving to avoid the longer route.

She consequently appealed to the Minister of Works to consider directing the relevant technical department to assess the junction and explore the possibility of providing a properly engineered median opening, dedicated turning bay or another suitable traffic management arrangement.

She stressed that infrastructure development should go beyond road construction to include practical interventions that improve motorists’ safety, accessibility and convenience.

Addressing the media, the Enugu State APC Youth Leader, Basil Ojengwa, expressed appreciation to President Bola Tinubu, for approving and prioritising major infrastructure projects in the South-East, particularly the Eke Obinagu Flyover and the reconstruction of the New Artisan Bridge.

Ojengwa recalled the difficulties motorists experienced following the collapse of the bridge, explaining that the incident disrupted transportation and forced road users to seek alternative routes through adjoining streets within Enugu metropolis.

He particularly commended the Minister of Works, Senator David Umahi, for his prompt intervention following the incident, noting that the Minister’s visit to the affected location and subsequent commencement of work helped address a major transportation challenge confronting residents and commuters.

He described the intervention as significant to the restoration of movement along the strategic corridor and appreciated the Minister for his efforts in ensuring that the bridge received the necessary attention.

Also speaking, during the exercise, the Deputy Chairman of Awgu Local Government Area, Uchenna Ezediuto, commended the Federal Government’s infrastructure interventions in Enugu State and acknowledged the complementary role of the Enugu State Government under Governor Peter Mbah.

Ezediuto noted that the Governor had consistently complemented Federal Government infrastructure interventions through corresponding projects within the state.

“While the Federal Government is undertaking major infrastructure projects, including the flyover around the Eke Obinagu axis, the state government was also addressing connecting roads and other infrastructure around Enugu metropolis to improve accessibility and ensure that residents benefited from the interventions,” he added. 

He equally recalled the intervention of both the Federal and Enugu State Governments following the collapse of the New Artisan Bridge, noting that the state government provided alternative routes for motorists while the Federal Government undertook the reconstruction of the affected bridge.

Ezediuto, however, commended President Tinubu and Governor Mbah for the interventions, stressing the importance of collaboration between the two levels of government in addressing infrastructure challenges and improving the lives of residents.

He further applauded Obinta for initiating the ‘Renewed Hope Youth Infrastructure Tour’, describing it as an opportunity for young people, particularly those in the South-East, to gain firsthand knowledge of Federal Government projects and understand their significance to the region’s economic development.

He observed that such engagements could deepen young people’s understanding of public policies and ongoing infrastructure investments, while encouraging informed participation in national conversations about development and continuity of public projects.

The ‘Renewed Hope Youth Infrastructure Tour’ provided an opportunity for participating youths to observe the projects, interact with stakeholders and identify areas requiring further attention.

In her closing remarks, Obinta reiterated her appreciation to President Bola Tinubu for his administration’s infrastructure agenda and to the Honourable Minister of Works, Senator David Umahi, for his role in driving the Ministry’s interventions and supporting the youth engagement initiative.

She maintained that young Nigerians must become informed stakeholders in governance by understanding government policies, appreciating development efforts and making constructive contributions towards addressing challenges in their communities.

The exercise ended with a call for sustained attention to infrastructure development, effective project delivery, road safety and stronger youth participation in national development.

The ‘Renewed Hope Youth Infrastructure Tour’ underscores the importance of connecting governance with public awareness, infrastructure development and active youth participation.

title: Anthony Joshua welcomes baby girl, speaks on fatherhood
description:
British boxing champion Anthony Joshua has spoken about how the arrival of his baby girl with his childhood sweetheart, Nicole Osbourne, is changing his perspective on fatherhood.
The former two-time unified heavyweight champion joked that he was ready to give up video games and motorbiking to devot
content:
British boxing champion Anthony Joshua has spoken about how the arrival of his baby girl with his childhood sweetheart, Nicole Osbourne, is changing his perspective on fatherhood.

The former two-time unified heavyweight champion joked that he was ready to give up video games and motorbiking to devote more attention to his little princess.

Joshua and Osbourne welcomed their daughter on November 14, 2026.

The pair, who are no longer romantically involved, also share an 11-year-old son, Joseph.

Speaking in an interview with The Sun, Joshua said becoming a father to a girl would give him a deeper understanding of women and how best to support them.

“Now I’ve got a daughter, I will get an insight and a bit more understanding of what it means to be a woman, and how I can be supportive,” he said, describing the newborn as his “Princess”.

Joshua also expressed excitement about being actively involved in his daughter’s upbringing, saying he was prepared to take on everything from dressing up to changing nappies.

“I’m going to do it all, so you might see me with some eyeshadow on, some nail polish on, drinking some tea in a doll’s playhouse,” he added.

He described the birth as “a big blessing” and joked that having a daughter meant no more FIFA, motorbiking or PlayStation.

title: Africa’s instant payment transactions hit $1.8trn in 2025 as Nigeria leads – Report
description:
…AfricaNenda warns trust, consumer protection gaps could slow adoption
By Chinenye Anuforo from Mauritius
Nigeria’s instant payment system has earned the highest inclusivity rating in Africa, even as the continent recorded 71.4 billion instant payment transactions valued at $1.8 trillion in 2025, ac
content:
…AfricaNenda warns trust, consumer protection gaps could slow adoption

By Chinenye Anuforo from Mauritius

Nigeria’s instant payment system has earned the highest inclusivity rating in Africa, even as the continent recorded 71.4 billion instant payment transactions valued at $1.8 trillion in 2025, according to the 2026 State of Inclusive Instant Payment Systems (SIIPS) in Africa report.

The fifth edition of the report, released today, Thursday, November 19, 2026, in Mauritius by AfricaNenda Foundation in partnership with the United Nations Economic Commission for Africa (UNECA) and the World Bank Group, identifies Nigeria’s NIBSS Instant Payment (NIP) system as the only one on the continent to have attained the mature level of inclusivity, the highest category on the report’s inclusivity spectrum.

The report’s assessment highlighted the country’s progress in developing an instant payment infrastructure that supports transactions across different financial service providers, including banks and mobile money operators.

It also noted that NIP is helping to reduce the cost of digital payments for Nigeria’s largely informal micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) by eliminating some of the expenses associated with holding funds in advance and reconciling transactions.

The continental figures reflect the rapid expansion of instant payment infrastructure across Africa. According to the report, the 71.4 billion transactions recorded in 2025 represent almost three times the volume processed in 2021, with a total transaction value of $1.8 trillion.

As of July 2026, Africa had 39 live instant payment systems, comprising 35 domestic and four regional systems, providing instant payment functionality across 43 countries.

However, despite the impressive growth, the report warns that persistent trust and consumer protection challenges could undermine the continent’s efforts to move more people and businesses away from cash.

Findings from a survey of 1,403 individuals and MSME digital payment users across 15 African markets between March and April 2026 showed that 55 per cent of respondents still relied on cash for about half of their transactions, while only 33 per cent used digital payment methods most of the time.

More than half of the respondents had experienced payment problems, including delayed transactions and transfers to wrong recipients. Yet, one in three users who encountered such problems did not report them, largely because they did not know how to seek redress.

The report further found that 43 per cent of users who lost money in digital payment transactions reduced their use of digital payment services.

It said the experience of failed transactions and unresolved complaints could weaken confidence in digital financial services, even where the underlying payment infrastructure was efficient.

According to the report, trust is influenced by the speed of transactions, clear payment confirmation messages and the ability of users to verify recipients before sending money.

Deputy Chief Executive Officer of AfricaNenda Foundation and lead author of the report, Sabine F. Mensah, said the continent had made significant progress in expanding instant payment infrastructure, but the next phase must focus on building public confidence.

“Five years ago, our first report mapped 29 instant payment systems. Today, there are 39, and one in two African adults live in a country served by an inclusive instant payment system,” she said.

Mensah said the priority had shifted from simply making instant payments available to ensuring that people trusted the systems enough to use them instead of cash.

“The question has changed. It is no longer whether Africans can pay instantly, but whether they trust the system enough to stop reaching for cash,” she said.

She added that confidence depended on transactions going through instantly, preventive safeguards such as recipient name validation, real-time payment confirmation and timely resolution of complaints when something went wrong.

Chief Executive Officer of AfricaNenda Foundation, Dr Robert Ochola, said Africa had developed inclusive instant payment infrastructure at a remarkable pace, driven by the expertise of its local technology professionals.

“Africa has built inclusive instant payment infrastructure at remarkable speed, drawing on the talent of its own software engineers and designers,” he said.

He stressed that the next five years should focus on making the systems affordable, safe and sustainable.

The report called for stronger consumer protection measures, including recipient verification, real-time transaction confirmation and accessible complaint-resolution mechanisms.

It also recommended clearer frameworks for determining liability in cases of authorised push payment fraud, alongside stronger use of artificial intelligence to detect and prevent fraudulent transactions.

For Nigeria, the findings underline the importance of building on the NIP system’s strong inclusivity rating by strengthening safeguards that protect users when digital transactions fail or funds are lost.

The report’s broader assessment suggests that the success of instant payment systems should not be measured only by the number or value of transactions processed, but also by whether users can transact confidently and obtain timely redress when problems occur.

It also found that countries with instant payment systems recorded about seven percentage points higher active account usage than countries without such systems, although the report described the finding as an early, directional association rather than proof of a direct causal relationship.

With Nigeria already recognised for the maturity of its instant payment infrastructure, the next challenge is ensuring that reliability, affordability and consumer protection keep pace with the growth of digital transactions.

The post Africa’s instant payment transactions hit $1.8trn in 2025 as Nigeria leads – Report appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Taiwo Obe pays tribute to late Vanguard Online Editor, Femi Ajasa
description:
Founder of The Journalism Clinic, Taiwo Obe, has paid tribute to the late Online Editor of Vanguard Media Limited, Olufemi Ajasa, recalling their professional relationship and describing his death as a painful loss.







Obe, in a tribute shared on social media, recounted how Ajasa participated in
content:
Founder of The Journalism Clinic, Taiwo Obe, has paid tribute to the late Online Editor of Vanguard Media Limited, Olufemi Ajasa, recalling their professional relationship and describing his death as a painful loss.

Obe, in a tribute shared on social media, recounted how Ajasa participated in one of the first paid journalism training programmes organised at The Hub, the training facility of The Journalism Clinic, in Anifowose, Lagos.

He said the training, held around 2015, had three participants from Vanguard’s Online Desk, including then Online Editor, John Abayomi, Adekunle Aliyu and Ajasa.

Obe recalled that Vanguard’s Chairman, Sam Amuka-Pemu, had earlier visited the facility and promised that the newspaper would send its staff to training programmes organised there.

According to him, Amuka-Pemu fulfilled the promise by ensuring that Vanguard staff participated in the training.

Obe traced his relationship with Amuka-Pemu to around 1997, when his company, TaijoWonukabe Limited, moved from an office provided by late columnist Pini Jason Onyegbadue to a three-bedroom bungalow on Bassie Ogamba Street, off Adeniran Ogunsanya, Surulere, Lagos.

He said the property belonged to Madam Pemu, a relation of Amuka-Pemu, who lived in a separate bungalow within the same premises.

Obe recalled that when Amuka-Pemu visited Madam Pemu shortly after the company moved in, he approached the veteran journalist to introduce himself.

“Money is good. See how you boys have changed this building,” Amuka-Pemu reportedly told him after their exchange of pleasantries.

Obe said the encounter marked the beginning of a relationship that continued over the years.

He added that when Amuka-Pemu visited The Hub shortly after its establishment around 2015, the veteran journalist promised that Vanguard would participate in the facility’s training programmes.

Recalling his encounters with Ajasa after the training, Obe described the late journalist as respectful, ambitious and consistently well-dressed.

“Since that training, I had encountered Femi in various places and positions. He remained as respectful as ever; always go-getting and consistently impeccably-dressed,” he wrote.

Vanguard had reported that Ajasa died at the age of 44 after a brief illness.

Expressing grief over his death, Obe concluded his tribute with the Yoruba expression, “Sùn re ò, Femooo,” meaning farewell and rest well.

The post Taiwo Obe pays tribute to late Vanguard Online Editor, Femi Ajasa appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Mineral wealth: WiM-Africa demands Industrial Revolution
description:
Women in Mining Africa (WiM-Africa) has challenged West African governments to stop relying on mineral export revenues and turn the region’s vast mineral wealth into industries, jobs and economic prosperity.
The organisation said mineral resources would remain a wasted opportunity unless investments
content:
Women in Mining Africa (WiM-Africa) has challenged West African governments to stop relying on mineral export revenues and turn the region’s vast mineral wealth into industries, jobs and economic prosperity.

The organisation said mineral resources would remain a wasted opportunity unless investments translated into functional industries, stronger local businesses and improved living conditions for mining communities.

Executive Director of WiM-Africa, Dr Comfort Asokoro-Ogaji, stated this in a position paper presented at the 2026 West Africa Integration and Investment Summit (WAIIS) held in Sierra Leone.

She said the region must move beyond investment announcements to focus on building productive capacity through industrialisation, regional cooperation, responsible mining and inclusive economic opportunities.

According to her, the success of mineral investments should be measured by projects that secure financing, commence operations, develop local businesses and improve the livelihoods of people in mining communities.

She stressed that mineral deposits alone could not guarantee economic transformation without credible geological information, adequate financing, reliable infrastructure, clear regulatory frameworks and access to markets.

The WiM-Africa boss urged governments and development partners to prioritise project preparation, including environmental and social assessments, community engagement, commercial studies and appropriate financing arrangements.

On regional industrialisation, she called for stronger cooperation among West African countries to develop competitive mineral value chains, noting that processing facilities require reliable electricity, water, transportation, technical expertise and ready markets.

She said countries could maximise opportunities by jointly developing infrastructure, harmonising standards and facilitating cross-border trade.

Asokoro-Ogaji also warned that responsible mining must go beyond tracing the origin of minerals to ensuring workers’ safety, environmental protection and fair treatment of host communities.

She called for stronger regulatory oversight, regular inspections and the formalisation of artisanal and small-scale mining to provide operators with legal access to markets, technical support and safer equipment.

On community development, she insisted that host communities must be treated as partners through transparent compensation arrangements, employment opportunities and local procurement.

She further called for greater economic participation by women and young people, stressing the need to provide women-owned businesses with access to finance, technical certification, procurement contracts and ownership opportunities.

According to her, women’s participation in mining must go beyond representation to include ownership and decision-making positions, particularly in the control of budgets, contracts and investments.

To ensure implementation of the summit’s resolutions, Asokoro-Ogaji proposed a 90-day post-summit action plan with clearly defined responsibilities, project-preparation requirements, financing pathways and measurable targets.

She urged participating institutions to regularly report progress on investment commitments, funds disbursed, infrastructure delivered, operational facilities, local business growth, employment and women’s ownership.

She maintained that West Africa could transform its mineral wealth into lasting industrial capacity if governments embraced disciplined project preparation, regional cooperation and accountability.

“The measure of success will be what remains in the region: productive enterprises, skilled people, functioning infrastructure and communities with a meaningful stake in development,” she said.

title: Customs target faster cargo clearance
description:
The Nigeria Customs Service has concluded plans to upgrade its B’Odogwu Unified Customs Management System to address cargo clearance bottlenecks, strengthen the tracking of goods in transit and improve revenue collection.
The resolutions followed a three-day review workshop, where the service and it
content:
The Nigeria Customs Service has concluded plans to upgrade its B’Odogwu Unified Customs Management System to address cargo clearance bottlenecks, strengthen the tracking of goods in transit and improve revenue collection.

The resolutions followed a three-day review workshop, where the service and its technology partners identified operational gaps and agreed on technical improvements to make the platform more efficient.

A major outcome of the meeting was the plan to replace 200 obsolete electronic cargo tracking seals with 2,000 newly procured units, alongside the integration of an upgraded Electronic Cargo Tracking System with the B’Odogwu platform.

The measures are expected to strengthen the monitoring of bonded cargo, reduce the risk of diversion and improve the accountability of goods moving through Nigeria’s customs-controlled transit corridors.

The workshop, held between November 9 and 11, 2026, brought together NCS management and officers, Trade Modernisation Project Limited and CB-XP representatives to assess the implementation of the system and agree on measures to address identified challenges.

In a statement issued by the service on Wednesday, the NCS said the discussions focused on improving the platform’s operational efficiency, strengthening customs processes and developing a roadmap for its future development.

The statement read, “The Nigeria Customs Service has concluded a three-day review of its B’Odogwu Unified Customs Management System in Lisbon, Portugal, with resolutions aimed at addressing operational challenges, accelerating cargo clearance, strengthening cargo tracking and improving revenue collection. The workshop, held from 9 to 11 November 2026 at the Corinthia Hotel, brought together NCS management and officers, Trade Modernisation Project Limited and CB-XP representatives to assess the system’s implementation and agree on technical and operational improvements.”

Speaking at the opening ceremony, the Deputy Comptroller-General of Customs in charge of ICT Modernisation, Oluyomi Adebakin, commended the Comptroller-General of Customs, Adewale Adeniyi, for his support for technological innovation and capacity development within the service.

The Managing Director of Trade Modernisation Project Limited, Jummai Umar-Ajijola, who represented the company’s Chairman, Saleh Ahmadu, said the B’Odogwu platform had attracted interest from the African Continental Free Trade Area Secretariat.

She said improvements to the system had contributed to higher revenue generation and strengthened the country’s revenue collection framework.

Umar-Ajijola said the review was an opportunity to assess the platform’s performance since its implementation and develop a clear direction for further improvements.

“We are to work to find a concrete plan not only to consolidate but to build a change roadmap going forward at the assessment of the three years so far,” she said.

She also commended the NCS Public Relations Unit for its consistent reporting on the project.

The workshop also identified several areas requiring improvement, including the automation of customs procedure code approvals and the processing of import, export, re-importation and transit declarations.

Participants also agreed on the need to harmonise procedure code nomenclature across customs operations to promote consistency, efficiency and accountability.

Under the proposed cargo tracking improvements, individual containers covered by relevant transit declarations will be monitored more effectively, while bond registration and validation processes will be strengthened.

The measures are also expected to improve controls over bonded cargo movements and minimise cases of diversion, a persistent concern in customs transit operations.

The meeting further examined plans to integrate the B’Odogwu platform with the Nigeria Export Processing Zones Authority to improve the processing and monitoring of transactions involving export processing zones.

Participants also considered improvements to the Transire Processing System, including upgrades to the platform’s reporting dashboard, search filters and Harmonised System Code search functionality.

Other proposed changes include allowing officers to access previously processed declarations, improving the monitoring of procedure code applications and introducing system alerts to reduce processing errors.

The workshop also agreed on incorporating Time Release Study requirements into the platform to help the service monitor how long cargo takes to move through customs clearance procedures.

The Time Release Study is an international customs assessment tool used to identify delays and measure the efficiency of cargo clearance processes.

In addition, participants reviewed the Standard Operating Procedures for Bond Management, Transire Commands and Export Commands to ensure that customs operations comply with the Nigeria Customs Service Act 2023.

They resolved that all requests for modifications to the B’Odogwu platform must be reviewed and approved by the Officer in Charge of the Project Management Office before deployment. The decision is aimed at strengthening oversight and ensuring that system changes are properly assessed before implementation.

At the closing ceremony on November 11, the Deputy Comptroller-General of Customs in charge of Finance, Administration and Technical Services, Kikelomo Adeola, stressed the importance of translating the workshop’s resolutions into practical improvements.

The ceremony also featured a presentation by the Customs Area Controller, Comptroller Murtala Mu’azu, and goodwill remarks by the CB-XP Chairman, Edward Bowen.

The service said specific responsibilities had been assigned to relevant NCS and TMPL units to ensure the implementation of the agreed resolutions.

The development comes as Nigeria continues to pursue the modernisation of its customs administration through technology, with faster cargo clearance, improved trade facilitation, tighter border controls and increased revenue generation among the major objectives of the reforms.

title: Gov Idris flags off over N8b community investment fund for women affinity groups
description:
From Ola Muhammad Birnin Kebbi
Kebbi State Governor,  Dr. Nasir Idris, Kauran Gwandu, on Wednesday officially flagged off the disbursement of over ₦8 billion Community Investment Fund (CIF) to Women Affinity Groups (WAGs) across the state under the Nigeria for Women Programme Scale-Up Project.
The c
content:
From Ola Muhammad Birnin Kebbi

Kebbi State Governor,  Dr. Nasir Idris, Kauran Gwandu, on Wednesday officially flagged off the disbursement of over ₦8 billion Community Investment Fund (CIF) to Women Affinity Groups (WAGs) across the state under the Nigeria for Women Programme Scale-Up Project.

The ceremony, held at the Haliru Abdu Stadium, Birnin Kebbi, was attended by the Minister of Women Affairs, Imaan Sulaiman-Ibrahim; Minister of Budget and Economic Planning, Senator Abubakar Atiku Bagudu; representatives of the World Bank; government officials; traditional rulers; and thousands of women beneficiaries.

The fund is being disbursed to over 3,000 Women Affinity Groups across Kebbi State to strengthen their financial capacity, promote entrepreneurship, expand small-scale businesses and improve the economic well-being of women, particularly those in rural communities.

Speaking at the event, Governor Idris reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to sustaining and expanding women empowerment initiatives, assuring that the programme would be extended to cover every local government area in the state.

He emphasised that women remain critical partners in family development, community advancement and the overall economic growth of Kebbi State.

The Governor stressed that his administration would continue to create opportunities for women to achieve financial independence, noting that the initiative aligns with its broader commitment to wealth creation, poverty reduction and inclusive economic development.

He assured that every necessary measure would be taken to ensure that women across the state benefit from the programme.

Governor Idris further disclosed that his administration had made additional financial provisions to support participating local governments, with ₦250 million earmarked for each benefiting local government to strengthen the implementation and impact of the initiative.

He urged the beneficiaries to utilise the funds judiciously, invest in productive ventures and embrace the spirit of collective responsibility that underpins the Women Affinity Groups. He also called on them to sustain their commitment to peace, unity and the development policies of the government.

In her remarks, the Minister of Women Affairs, Imaan Sulaiman-Ibrahim, commended Governor Idris for his commitment to women’s economic empowerment, describing Kebbi State as a model in the implementation of the Nigeria for Women Programme.

She disclosed that the programme had mobilised over 80,000 women in Kebbi State into organised affinity groups, which had collectively saved more than ₦1.1 billion and accessed loans exceeding their initial savings, demonstrating the effectiveness of the group-based empowerment model.

The Minister explained that the Community Investment Fund was not a handout but a collective financial resource designed to strengthen women’s economic activities through organised groups. She urged beneficiaries to protect the funds, maintain proper financial records and invest in productive ventures, particularly agriculture, rice processing, livestock production, food processing and other businesses capable of generating sustainable income.

Also speaking, the Minister of Budget and Economic Planning, Senator Abubakar Atiku Bagudu, praised the Kebbi State Government for prioritising women’s empowerment and providing the necessary support for the successful implementation of the programme.

He observed that women in Kebbi had demonstrated remarkable commitment to entrepreneurship, savings and community development, urging them to maximise the opportunities provided by the initiative to improve their livelihoods and contribute more significantly to the state’s economic growth.

The World Bank representative, Mr. Michael Ilesanmi, described the flag-off as a significant milestone for Kebbi State and Nigeria, noting that the state had remained one of the leading participants in the Nigeria for Women Programme since its commencement in 2018.

He disclosed that Kebbi had recorded impressive achievements through the programme, with thousands of women organised into affinity groups and substantial savings generated through their collective efforts. He also commended Governor Idris for his commitment to expanding the programme to additional local government areas.

Earlier, the Kebbi State Commissioner for Women Affairs, Hajiya Halima Hassan Kamba, disclosed that during the pilot phase of the programme, approximately 80,000 women benefited from financial literacy training, business management and other capacity-building initiatives, while ₦3.2 billion was disbursed as individual livelihood grants.

She further revealed that under the scale-up phase, over 83,000 women had been mobilised into 3,506 affinity groups, collectively generating savings of ₦4.11 billion and providing loans amounting to ₦1.31 billion among members.

The Commissioner commended Governor Idris, the Federal Government and the World Bank for their sustained partnership and commitment to advancing women’s economic opportunities in the state.

The post Gov Idris flags off over N8b community investment fund for women affinity groups appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Northern leaders have failed the people, need collective agenda — Uba Sani
description:
By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo



Kaduna State Governor, Senator Uba Sani, has challenged past and present political leaders from Northern Nigeria to acknowledge their failures and unite around a common development agenda for the region.







He also cautioned politicians against exploiting ethnic and reg
content:
By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo

Kaduna State Governor, Senator Uba Sani, has challenged past and present political leaders from Northern Nigeria to acknowledge their failures and unite around a common development agenda for the region.

He also cautioned politicians against exploiting ethnic and regional sentiments to seek political power ahead of the 2027 general elections without presenting concrete records of their contributions to the development of the North.

Uba Sani spoke on Wednesday at a summit on Good Governance, Inclusivity and Sustainable Development organised by the Sir Ahmadu Bello Memorial Foundation.

The governor said northern leaders had strayed from the development vision of the late Premier of Northern Nigeria, Sir Ahmadu Bello, who he said envisaged a united, peaceful and self-sufficient region.

He called on the foundation to convene a meeting of past and present political leaders from the North to develop a common blueprint for the region’s development.

He urged political leaders to engage in honest self-assessment and acknowledge their collective shortcomings.

“We must look ourselves in the mirror and tell ourselves some home truths. All of us, including myself, have failed the people,” he said.

The governor also warned politicians seeking electoral support on the basis of their northern identity to demonstrate what they had done for the region while occupying positions of public responsibility.

According to him, appeals to regional sentiments without verifiable records of service would not address the development challenges confronting the North.

However, Uba Sani commended President Bola Tinubu for supporting critical infrastructure projects in Kaduna State, saying some of his administration’s achievements were made possible by the President’s interventions.

“I want to seize this opportunity to thank the President for all that he has done for Kaduna State in the last three and a half years,” he said.

He recalled approaching Tinubu over the completion of the Abuja-Kaduna-Kano highway, describing it as a major economic corridor linking northern and southern Nigeria.

He said the President had released billions of naira towards completing the project, which had previously been abandoned, adding that work on the highway was almost 95 per cent complete.

The governor also disclosed that he and the Speaker of the House of Representatives, Tajudeen Abbas, had approached the President over the proposed Kaduna Light Rail Project.

He said Tinubu had approved $865 million for the project, adding that the contract had been signed and arrangements were underway for the President to perform its groundbreaking ceremony in Kaduna within two weeks.

“I am happy to say that President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, knowing the history of Kaduna, decided to approve $865 million for the Kaduna Light Rail Project. The contract has been signed. By the grace of God, in the next two weeks, he will be coming to Kaduna to do the groundbreaking,” he said.

Uba Sani, who assumed office on May 29, 2023, also highlighted his administration’s achievements in pension payments, transportation, agriculture and security.

He said his government inherited pension liabilities of about N24 billion but had so far paid more than N21 billion to 9,683 state and local government retirees, as well as families of deceased public servants.

On transportation, he said the administration had deployed 100 buses under its free Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) bus service, recording 5.2 million passenger trips and saving commuters more than N5 billion.

The governor said insecurity had previously prevented residents of some communities from accessing schools and farmlands, but the Kaduna Peace Model had helped restore access to more than 500,000 hectares of previously inaccessible farmland.

He further declared that no school in the state was currently closed because of insecurity.

On agriculture, Uba Sani said his administration had increased the sector’s annual budgetary allocation from N1.48 billion to more than N100 billion since assuming office.

He added that more than 69,000 smallholder farmers had received improved agricultural inputs, while over 1,400 truckloads of fertiliser had been distributed to more than 500,000 farmers across the state’s 23 local government areas.

According to him, the government had also facilitated access to more than 200 tractors through partnerships and enrolled over 100,000 farmers in crop insurance schemes.

He disclosed that 5,000 livestock farmers had equally received equipment and production inputs.

The governor said his administration was also implementing the Special Agro-Industrial Processing Zones and the Rural Access and Agricultural Marketing Project to link farmers with processors and markets, reduce post-harvest losses and improve agricultural returns.

The post Northern leaders have failed the people, need collective agenda — Uba Sani appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: PA Fasoranti: Ondo Govt Releases 8-Day Burial Programme
description: The Ondo State Government has released an eight-day programme of burial activities for the late elder statesman and Afenifere leader, Pa Reuben Famuyide Fasoranti, with his funeral service and interment scheduled for Thursday, December 17, 2026.The programme, signed by the Chairman and Secretary of
content:
The Ondo State Government has released an eight-day programme of burial activities for the late elder statesman and Afenifere leader, Pa Reuben Famuyide Fasoranti, with his funeral service and interment scheduled for Thursday, December 17, 2026.

The programme, signed by the Chairman and Secretary of the State Burial Committee, Dr Kayode Ajulo (SAN) and Apostle Eniola Olushola, Esq, respectively, shows that the ceremonies will begin on Sunday, December 13, with a cultural heritage day in honour of the deceased, who was born on May 11, 1926 and died on October 20, 2026.

The opening ceremony, scheduled for 12 noon, will feature a showcase of Ondo State’s cultural heritage at the Dr Olusegun Mimiko International Centre for Culture and Events (The Dome), Akure.

A commendation service will hold at Anglican Grammar School, Iju-Itaogbolu, at 9.00 am on Monday, December 14, followed by a novelty football match in Fasoranti’s honour at the Akure Township Stadium.

The football fixtures will see Anglican Grammar School, Iju-Itaogbolu, take on St Frances, Akure, at 2.00 pm, while Akure High School will face Ondo Boys High School at 4.00 pm.

Activities on Tuesday, December 15, will feature a symposium, a national tribute, and an academic award at The Dome, Akure.

The symposium, themed “A Selfless Cradle Light That The Yoruba Race Can’t Forget In A Hurry”, will be organised by Afenifere, the DAWN Commission and the Ondo State Government. It is scheduled for 10.00 am and will be followed by a national tribute and academic award.

A lying-in-state and Christian wake-keep will take place at the deceased’s country home, Omolere Close, Akure, at 4.00 pm on Wednesday, December 16.

The funeral service will hold at St David’s Anglican Cathedral, Ijomu, Akure, at 10.00 am prompt on Thursday, December 17, with interment to follow immediately at the church cemetery.

A reception and entertainment of guests will subsequently be held at designated venues for the different categories of guests.

The programme will continue on Friday, December 18, with a thanksgiving service at Akure Central Mosque at 1.00 pm, while Saturday, December 19, has been set aside for family visits to Baba’s residence.

The final activity, an outing and thanksgiving service, will be held at St David’s Anglican Cathedral, Ijomu, Akure, at 10.00 am prompt on Sunday, December 20.

The post PA Fasoranti: Ondo Govt Releases 8-Day Burial Programme appeared first on Channels Television.

title: FULL LIST: Fake documents that could earn applicants five-year Canada ban
description:
Canadian authorities have warned prospective visa applicants against the falsification of required documents to gain entry into the country.
According to a tweet via the X handle of the Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada on Thursday, it noted that submitting falsified or altered documents
content:
Canadian authorities have warned prospective visa applicants against the falsification of required documents to gain entry into the country.

According to a tweet via the X handle of the Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada on Thursday, it noted that submitting falsified or altered documents during visa applications can stop an applicant from entering Canada for a minimum of five years.

Such documents range from marriage certificates to language results, entry and exit stamps, visas, transcripts and divorce documents, among others.

The IRCC also warned that one could face legal consequences in their home country if found guilty of any related criminal activity.

Information obtained from the IRCC website noted that providing false information about one’s medical conditions to the panel physician during a person’s medical exam is also considered fraud.

Below is the full list of documents whose falsification is considered fraud in Canada:

1. Passports and travel documents

2. Visas, exit and entry stamps

3. Language results

4. Proof of employment or job offers

5. Letters of acceptance from learning institutions, tuition receipts and transcripts

6. Diplomas, degrees and apprenticeship or trade papers

7. Proof of relationship, including certificates of birth, adoption, marriage, final divorce, annulment, separation, death or custodianship

8. Police certificates or court documents

9. DNA testing

The IRCC noted that while it’s not bent on punishing people affected by fraud, it’s determined to identify “those who are responsible for fraud.”

“Lying about how long you or someone else has been physically present in Canada while applying for a permanent residency (PR) renewal or citizenship is also considered fraud. Learn more about PR card residency obligations and physical presence,” the information added.

It highlighted consequences of immigration and citizenship fraud to include application refusal, a minimum of a five-year ban from Canada, a permanent fraud record with the IRCC, and the removal of one’s temporary or permanent residency status, or Canadian citizenship.

Others include a five-year ban from citizenship application and an outright expulsion from Canada.

The IRCC further warned that Canadian citizens or permanent residents who are in a relationship of convenience for immigration reasons may be charged with a crime.

A relationship of convenience is a marriage, a common-law or conjugal relationship whose main goal is to immigrate to another country.

The IRCC warned that its officers are well-trained to detect false marriages and common-law or conjugal relationships, via document checks, visits to people’s homes, and interviews with both sponsors and applicants.

“Our officers are trained to recognise genuine immigration applications. They know how to detect false marriages and common-law or conjugal relationships.

“They have many ways to spot marriage fraud, including document checks, visits to people’s homes and interviews with both sponsors and applicants,” the information read partly.

Authorities also warned that in the case of credit card payment reversals, it could cause one’s visa application to be cancelled or delayed.

This, it said, could also attract a 10-year entry ban.

“If the fee paid with a credit card is reversed, your visa application could be cancelled or delayed. Your visa application could also be denied and you could potentially be banned from travelling to Canada for up to 10 years. Applications you submit in the future can also be impacted,” it added.

The post FULL LIST: Fake documents that could earn applicants five-year Canada ban appeared first on Punch Newspapers.
