title: Tinubu’s aide spends five hours in Lagos-Ibadan gridlock, faults contractor
description:
The Special Adviser to President Bola Tinubu on Media and Communications, Sunday Dare, has criticised the timing of construction work on the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway after spending more than five hours in traffic while travelling to Ibadan, Oyo State.
Dare said the prolonged gridlock had left thousan
content:
The Special Adviser to President Bola Tinubu on Media and Communications, Sunday Dare, has criticised the timing of construction work on the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway after spending more than five hours in traffic while travelling to Ibadan, Oyo State.

Dare said the prolonged gridlock had left thousands of commuters stranded, with many forced to abandon their vehicles and trek to their destinations.

He made this known in a post on his Facebook account on Wednesday night, while expressing frustration over the decision to carry out construction work around the busy exit point during peak traffic hours.

Dare, who was travelling to Ibadan ahead of the All Progressives Congress presidential rally scheduled for Saturday, said he was on his way to the city for several radio and television appearances.

He questioned why the Chinese contractor handling the construction chose to work during the busiest hours of vehicular movement rather than at night when traffic was lighter.

He wrote, “Tonight – Lagos -Ibadan Expressway. I have been in a traffic gridlock for over five hours trying to get out of Lagos to Ibadan for multiple radio and television appearances ahead of the APC Presidential Rally coming up on Saturday in Ibadan.

“It beats me why a Chinese Contractor would choose the busiest hours of vehicular traffic to construct the bridge and road around this exit point. Stranded cars, thousands of people trekking to get home.

“What happened to doing construction work during the obituary hours when traffic is lean? This is unnecessary pain. It needs to be corrected.”

The gridlock followed the resumption of construction work on a pedestrian bridge around the Aseese area of the expressway, which disrupted vehicular movement in both directions on Wednesday.

PUNCH Metro reported that the traffic congestion stretched from the Redemption Camp area to Aseese bus stop for motorists heading towards Lagos, while those travelling towards Ogun State were held up from the Long Bridge area to Aseese.

A PUNCH correspondent who boarded a commercial vehicle from Ibadan shortly after 11am arrived in Magboro, Ogun State, at about 5.30pm.

Another motorist reportedly spent eight hours travelling from Mowe to Magboro.

The congestion also forced several commuters to abandon their vehicles and trek several kilometres, while commercial motorcyclists took advantage of the situation to increase their fares.

In September, motorists and commuters on the expressway were also trapped in gridlock for more than 14 hours following a multiple-vehicle crash around Kara Bridge, which compounded ongoing repair works.

Meanwhile, the Ogun State Traffic Compliance and Enforcement Agency had said the latest traffic diversion was expected to last four days, from Wednesday, November 18, to Sunday, November 22.

The agency’s spokesperson, Babatunde Akinbiyi, said the Federal Ministry of Works, in collaboration with CBC Construction Company, was carrying out the temporary diversion to facilitate the installation of the pedestrian bridge.

The agency said the Traffic Compliance and Enforcement Agency and the Federal Road Safety Corps would deploy personnel to the affected section to manage traffic and minimise delays.

The post Tinubu’s aide spends five hours in Lagos-Ibadan gridlock, faults contractor appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Mudryk blames Ukraine national team for failed drug test
description:
Tottenham winger Mykhailo Mudryk has blamed the administration of the Ukrainian national team for his failed drugs test and subsequent suspension from football.
The 25-year-old, who joined Tottenham on a season-long loan from Chelsea, was suspended from November 2024 until July 2026 after testing po
content:
Tottenham winger Mykhailo Mudryk has blamed the administration of the Ukrainian national team for his failed drugs test and subsequent suspension from football.

The 25-year-old, who joined Tottenham on a season-long loan from Chelsea, was suspended from November 2024 until July 2026 after testing positive for meldonium, a banned substance.

Mudryk believes the substance entered his system while he was on international duty with Ukraine, insisting that he could only have been exposed to the drug in his home country.

Speaking in an interview with Ukrainian YouTube channel Guest of Gordon, on Wednesday, the winger said he had never heard of meldonium before the positive test.

“The environment, the situation in the Ukrainian national team. It should never have existed. I probably haven’t said it publicly yet, but I’m saying it now.

“I had never heard of a drug like meldonium. It is a drug you can only get in Eastern Europe. It could only have got into my body in Ukraine. There is no such drug in England,” Mudryk said.

Asked whether he directly blamed the national team, Mudryk replied: “Yes, exactly.”

He explained that his only visits to Ukraine during the period were for national team commitments, suggesting that the substance could have entered his system while he was at the national team camp.

Mudryk also criticised the Ukrainian Association of Football (UAF), accusing the organisation of failing to support him adequately during the case.

He claimed that UAF president Andriy Shevchenko offered little assistance and alleged that the association was responsible for leaks surrounding the investigation.

The winger further argued that the association’s handling of the matter contributed to delays in his return to professional football.

Mudryk initially faced a possible four-year ban from the Football Association (FA), but successfully appealed to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS).

He eventually accepted that he had breached anti-doping regulations and agreed to a suspension equivalent to the period he had already served, allowing him to return to football in July 2026.

The former Shakhtar Donetsk player also revealed that he spent millions of pounds on legal expenses, personal coaching, pitch hire and private physiotherapy while serving his suspension.

He said the positive test came as a devastating shock and had a significant impact on him mentally.

“It was a bolt from the blue. I couldn’t believe it was true,” he said.

“It was like falling off a skyscraper. In a dream you would hit the ground. In life, I just kept on falling. It hit me very hard, mentally.”

Mudryk admitted that he cried and turned to alcohol following his initial suspension but maintained that he never lost confidence in his ability to return to top-level football.

After making an appearance for Chelsea during their pre-season tour of Asia, he completed a deadline-day loan move to Tottenham, where he reunited with former Shakhtar Donetsk manager Roberto De Zerbi.

The Ukrainian Association of Football has yet to respond to Mudryk’s latest allegations. BBC Sport reported that it had contacted the association for comment.

Last year, a UAF spokesperson told BBC Sport that the organisation was in close contact with Mudryk’s lawyers but had not received any communication from the FA regarding the case.

The post Mudryk blames Ukraine national team for failed drug test appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Airstrike Kills 21 ISWAP Fighters In Borno — Army
description: Precision air strikes conducted by the Air Assets of Joint Task Force (North East), Operation HADIN KAI (OPHK), have neutralised 21 Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP) fighters and severely injured 10 others in separate operations around Monguno and the South Lake Chad area of Borno State.Cap
content:
Precision air strikes conducted by the Air Assets of Joint Task Force (North East), Operation HADIN KAI (OPHK), have neutralised 21 Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP) fighters and severely injured 10 others in separate operations around Monguno and the South Lake Chad area of Borno State.

Captain Mohammed Goni, Acting Media Information Officer, Headquarters Joint Task Force (North East) Operation HADIN KAI, in a press statement Wednesday night, revealed the operation was conducted between November 16 and 17, 2026.

“The first operation followed intelligence reports of ISWAP fighters advancing towards Monguno. Acting on the intelligence, an Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) established surveillance over the area and identified terrorists moving along a bush path northeast of Monguno

“The subsequent precision strike neutralised seven fighters, including members of the terrorist group’s Improvised Explosive Device (IED) network. Further confirmation revealed that Abba Bomma identified as a key IED team expert, was incapacitated, while four other fighters sustained severe injuries,” the statement reads in part.

Goni further revealed that, in a separate operation at Arinna in the South Lake Chad area, precision air strikes dealt a significant blow to ISWAP’s leadership and operational structure.

Among those neutralised was Mallam Sharki, a prominent member of the group’s Shura Council and Amirul Amniya (Provost Commander). Also neutralised was Abu Sa’ad, the Qaid of Sabon Tumbu.

Twelve additional fighters were eliminated, while five others sustained severe injuries. Several terrorist motorcycles were also destroyed during the operation.

According to the Theatre Command, the two operations accounted for 21 ISWAP fighters neutralised and 10 severely injured, degrading the group’s leadership structure, disrupting its IED network and weakening its operational capabilities.

The post Airstrike Kills 21 ISWAP Fighters In Borno — Army appeared first on Channels Television.

title: Tinubu interview: Diana London breaks silence on alleged $4.5m payment
description:
American political strategist and media personality Diana London has rejected claims that she received $4.5 million from the Nigerian government in connection with her recent interview with President Bola Tinubu.
London addressed the allegation in a post on X on Wednesday night, describing it as an
content:
American political strategist and media personality Diana London has rejected claims that she received $4.5 million from the Nigerian government in connection with her recent interview with President Bola Tinubu.

London addressed the allegation in a post on X on Wednesday night, describing it as an attempt to discredit her. She maintained that her trip to Nigeria was primarily to conduct an interview with the president for a documentary and experience the country personally.

“I unequivocally deny the claim that Nigeria’s government nor anyone else in Nigeria paid me $4.5 million. I went to Nigeria to interview President Tinubu @officialABAT for parts of a documentary and see Nigeria for myself,” she wrote.

She also dismissed the allegation as a smear campaign, insisting that it would not affect her willingness to speak about the issues.

“This SMEAR CAMPAIGN can make noise, but can’t change the facts or stop me from speaking the truth,” she added.

The denial comes after questions were raised about London’s interview with Tinubu at the Presidential Villa in Abuja on Tuesday, amid reports of a $4.5 million lobbying arrangement involving the Nigerian government and a United States-based firm.

Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar called on the Presidency to explain whether the interview was connected to the reported lobbying engagement.

Atiku conveyed his position in a statement released Wednesday by his Director of Strategic Communication, Phrank Shaibu.

The former vice-president cited US filings which, according to him, listed London as a consultant to DCI Group AZ, a firm reportedly retained by the Nigerian government through Aster Legal.

He said the documents indicated that DCI Group received a $4.5 million retainer and urged the government to clarify the nature of London’s involvement and whether the interview was part of the arrangement.

Atiku also asked the Presidency to make the contract public, provide details of the payment and release the complete, unedited recording of the interview.

He argued that Nigerians deserved to know whether the meeting was an independent media engagement or a publicity exercise funded by the government.

He further sought clarification on the identity of the person who approved the reported payment, the source of the money and whether taxpayers’ funds were used.

The controversy gained further attention after London published posts on social media commending the security cooperation between Nigeria and the United States under Tinubu and US President Donald Trump.

She had described Nigeria as America’s greatest ally in Africa and praised the security partnership, suggesting that it could also strengthen economic and trade relations between the two countries.

London also acknowledged the opportunity to work with people involved in improving relations between the Nigerian government and the Trump administration.

The posts were later deleted, while access to the comment section of her X account was restricted following reactions from Nigerian social media users.

Her latest statement marks her direct response to the reported $4.5 million payment allegation.

However, the Presidency had not publicly addressed Atiku’s questions or clarified whether London’s interview with Tinubu was connected to the reported lobbying arrangement as of the time of filing this report.

The post Tinubu interview: Diana London breaks silence on alleged $4.5m payment appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Offa Bank Robbery: Saraki, Ahmed Can’t Be Arraigned Without Proper Service — Kwara Court
description: Justice Osuolale Ajayi of the Kwara State High Court in Ilorin said that the first and second defendants in the ongoing Offa robbery case, former Senate President, Dr. Abubakar Bukola Saraki, and former Governor of Kwara State, Alhaji Abdulfatah Ahmed, cannot be arraigned until they are properly ser
content:
Justice Osuolale Ajayi of the Kwara State High Court in Ilorin said that the first and second defendants in the ongoing Offa robbery case, former Senate President, Dr. Abubakar Bukola Saraki, and former Governor of Kwara State, Alhaji Abdulfatah Ahmed, cannot be arraigned until they are properly served with the charges.

The presiding judge, Justice Ajayi, delivered the court’s ruling on the pending issues, having reserved judgment at the previous sitting after hearing arguments from both the prosecution and defence.

At the resumed hearing, the judge read the court’s decisions and directed that the charges be served on the defendants by November 20 while fixing December 3, 2026, for the arraignment to proceed.

The prosecution had argued for the immediate commencement of the trial with the arraignment of the four defendants.

The court ruling follows the defence team’s earlier objection that the defendants had not been personally served with the charges, arguing that service on their lawyers alone did not satisfy the requirements of due process and a fair hearing.

At the previous sitting, counsel to Saraki, Adebayo Adelodun (SAN) drew the court’s attention to the improper service and questioned the urgency of the proceedings, asking, “My Lord, why the hurry?”

He had also reminded the court of the pending appeal before the Court of Appeal concerning issues of jurisdiction and the competence of the trial court to entertain the matter.

The defence had urged the court to take cognisance of the pending appellate proceedings and the legal objections already raised before taking further steps in the case.

The judge, however, said he would not suspend hearing because there was no indication as to when the Court of Appeal would give its ruling on the application of the defence for an order on all parties to maintain status quo ante bellum.

The latest directive now gives the parties a timeline for completion of service of the charges, with December 3 fixed for the next stage of proceedings.

Also, the Court of Appeal sitting in Ilorin had reserved its ruling on the application of the applicants (Saraki and Ahmed) on whether an order to maintain status quo ante bellum should be given to the parties and the trial court.

The development is connected to the April 5, 2018, robbery in Offa, when armed men launched coordinated attacks on several commercial banks and the police divisional headquarters, killing more than 30 people, including police officers and civilians.

The attackers targeted branches of Guaranty Trust Bank, First Bank, Ecobank, Zenith Bank and Union Bank, as well as Ibolo Microfinance Bank, during the operation.

They reportedly stormed the banks with sophisticated weapons and explosives, engaging police personnel in gun battles and overpowering security operatives at the divisional headquarters.

The attack resulted in the deaths of over 30 people, including 12 police officers and a pregnant woman, according to widely reported accounts of the incident.

The robbers also reportedly carted away millions of naira and 21 AK-47 rifles from the police armoury.

The scale of the attack generated nationwide outrage and prompted the then Inspector-General of Police, Ibrahim Idris, to deploy the Police Intelligence Response Team, led by then Deputy Commissioner of Police, Abba Kyari, to investigate the incident.

The police subsequently arrested several suspects, including Ayoade Akinnibosun, Ibukunle Ogunleye, Adeola Abraham, Salahudeen Azeez and Niyi Ogundiran, who were later prosecuted for their involvement in the robbery.

The state government recently reduced the original 20 charges against Saraki, Ahmed and two former aides, Yusuf Abdulwahab and Alabi Olalekan, to four counts.

Reacting to the development, Saraki accused the Kwara State Government of abusing the judicial process and using the robbery case to persecute him and former Governor Ahmed.

Saraki, through his media office, described the development as an indication that the allegations linking him to the deadly robbery lacked credible evidence.

He accused Governor AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq’s administration of deploying the criminal proceedings to damage his reputation ahead of the 2027 general elections.

In a statement issued on Monday by the Head of the Abubakar Bukola Saraki Media Office, Yusuph Olaniyonu, in Abuja, the former Senate President said the government had abandoned all the allegations relating to armed robbery, the killing of police officers and illegal possession of firearms.

The statement read, “The amendment to the charge sheet only reveals that there was no case against these gentlemen from the beginning, and what the state government is indulging in is abuse of power, a travesty of the justice system, and mockery of the prosecutorial powers of the state.

“The government has retained allegations that the four defendants conspired to belong to a gang of thieves and actually belonged to such a gang, alongside two counts relating to the alleged concealment or disappearance of a vehicle used for an unlawful purpose.”

The development came amid renewed political controversy over the robbery after a former chieftain of the All Progressives Congress in Kwara State, Saheed Popoola, admitted that he played a leading role in the campaign linking Saraki to the incident during the political struggle that culminated in the defeat of the former governor’s political structure in 2019.

Popoola, who is now the Peoples Democratic Party senatorial candidate for Kwara South, made the disclosure on Sunday at the palace of the Olofa of Offa, Oba Mufutau Gbadamosi, during Saraki’s political tour of the district.

He said the robbery allegations were deliberately revived and politicised by some APC members to undermine Saraki’s political influence in the state during the “O to ge” movement.

He said, “I was a leading member of the APC then that started the politicisation and revival of the issue of Offa robbery just to get to Saraki. But after we finished and won, it was I who was being persecuted.

“This includes the use of songs and slogans to associate Saraki with the incident just because of politics. However, God has intervened, and the reality is that Saraki is back in Kwara.”

Popoola, who expressed regret over his participation in the political struggle against Saraki, challenged those who continued to politicise the tragedy to demonstrate genuine concern for the victims and their families.

He alleged that many of the individuals who repeatedly raised the robbery allegations had neither visited the affected families nor offered them meaningful assistance since the incident.

Dismissing suggestions that Saraki could have been motivated by financial considerations to sponsor the robbery, Popoola said the former governor had resources far beyond the amount that could have been stolen from the banks.

“All the money in the entire banks in Offa, Ilorin, Patigi and the entire Kwara State put together is not enough for Saraki to spend in three days,” he declared.

However, the Kwara State chapter of the All Progressives Congress defended the evidence presented during the trial of the convicted robbers, insisting that it linked Saraki to members of the gang.

The state APC Publicity Secretary, Abdulwaheed Babatunde, stated this on Monday while addressing a press conference in Ilorin, following Popoola’s admission.

Babatunde maintained that Popoola’s confession could not erase evidence presented during the trial of the five convicted robbers, alleging that gang leader Ayoade Akinnibosun and other members implicated Saraki in their statements and testimonies.

He said, “Whether Saraki likes it or not, he is an accessory before and after the fact. The vehicles and arms were given at his instance, without which they couldn’t have attempted a robbery.”

The APC spokesman also alleged that a vehicle used in the operation was initially concealed at the Government House in Ilorin before being moved to the Ministry of Environment, adding that the suspects had links with Saraki and his family.

The post Offa Bank Robbery: Saraki, Ahmed Can’t Be Arraigned Without Proper Service — Kwara Court appeared first on Channels Television.

title: Fountain of Life crisis: Jimmy Odukoya alleges conspiracy
description:
By Ebunoluwa Sessou



The leadership crisis rocking The Fountain of Life Church has taken a fresh turn, with its Senior Pastor, Pastor Jimmy Odukoya, breaking his silence on allegations surrounding his leadership, the controversial succession video involving his late father and claims of financial
content:
By Ebunoluwa Sessou

The leadership crisis rocking The Fountain of Life Church has taken a fresh turn, with its Senior Pastor, Pastor Jimmy Odukoya, breaking his silence on allegations surrounding his leadership, the controversial succession video involving his late father and claims of financial impropriety.

Addressing church workers on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, Odukoya gave his account of the prolonged disagreements between him, members of the church’s Board of Trustees (BOT) and his sisters, insisting that he remains the Senior Pastor despite the controversy.

The meeting, which reportedly attracted about 300 workers, provided an opportunity for the embattled cleric to explain his position following the circulation of a video in which his late father, Pastor Taiwo Odukoya, allegedly indicated a succession preference involving Pastor Kunle Areogun.

Odukoya, who arrived at the church premises in a convoy of about five vehicles accompanied by security personnel, entered the auditorium at about 6.45 p.m. and was received with applause by the workers.

Speaking emotionally, he said he had endured considerable distress over the crisis but initially chose to remain silent in the hope that the disagreements would be resolved internally.

He said the decision by some board members to make his late father’s succession video public compelled him to address the workers and clarify issues surrounding the leadership dispute.

Succession video and father’s instruction

One of the major issues addressed by Odukoya was the video in which his late father reportedly expressed a preference for Areogun to take over the church’s leadership after his death.

He said the recording was made around 2021, shortly before his father travelled to the United States for surgery.

According to him, his father, uncertain about the outcome of the medical procedure, decided to document his thoughts on the future leadership of the church.

Odukoya said he personally recorded the video, while his late father’s elder brother, John Odukoya, was also aware of the exercise.

He, however, admitted that he retained the recording despite his father’s subsequent instruction to delete it after the surgery was successful.

“Following my father’s successful surgery, he instructed me to delete the recording because the circumstances that prompted its creation had changed, but I chose to retain the video against my father’s instruction and this I admit as a grave mistake,” he said.

He added that only a few people, including his sisters, knew about the recording.

The disclosure raises questions about the circumstances surrounding the recording, its intended status after the surgery and the decision to make it public several years later.

It also brings into focus the distinction between a succession preference expressed by the late founder and the formal governance processes through which leadership of the church is determined.

How leadership disagreement started

Tracing the origins of the crisis, Odukoya said the disagreements began about a year after he assumed leadership of the church following his father’s death.

He said concerns were raised about his administration, prompting the BOT to propose that he relinquish his position as chairman of the board and concentrate exclusively on his pastoral responsibilities.

Odukoya said he found the proposal difficult to accept, interpreting it as an attempt by the board to control his leadership.

He also alleged that his two sisters supported the board’s position and repeatedly pressured him to step down as chairman.

He specifically claimed that one of his sisters, Tolu, approached him and expressed interest in taking over the chairmanship.

The disagreement reportedly deepened as efforts to resolve the matter failed.

He said Bishop Mike Okonkwo intervened at a point and appealed to him to relinquish the BOT chairmanship, but he rejected the suggestion.

The dispute, therefore, appears to extend beyond who occupies the pulpit to the broader relationship between pastoral authority and institutional governance within the church.

Adeboye’s intervention

The crisis eventually attracted the attention of Pastor Enoch Adeboye, General Overseer of the Redeemed Christian Church of God, who was reportedly approached by members of the board to intervene.

Recounting the meeting, Odukoya alleged that some board members made false allegations against him in Adeboye’s presence.

He said Adeboye, however, gave him an opportunity to present his side of the disagreement.

According to him, after listening to both parties, Adeboye advised them to return and resolve their differences.

Odukoya said Adeboye told him that his primary calling was to preach the gospel rather than occupy the position of BOT chairman.

He also recalled that the RCCG leader warned that failure to resolve the disagreement could have serious consequences, telling the parties that it would not be goodbye but “bye-bye”.

The intervention, however, did not end the disagreement.

Odukoya disclosed that the BOT, comprising Pastor Kunle Areogun and Pastor Rotimi Okpaise, presented a seven-point demand to him.

He said he agreed to four of the demands but rejected the proposal that he relinquish his position as BOT chairman.

The disagreement over the chairmanship subsequently became one of the defining issues in the church’s leadership crisis.

N250m controversy: Odukoya denies embezzlement

Beyond the leadership dispute, Odukoya also addressed allegations of financial impropriety, including claims that he misappropriated church funds.

He said the allegations had been particularly distressing, disclosing that he was threatened with possible involvement of the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC).

One of the allegations, according to him, concerned N250 million reportedly donated by an individual to the church for a particular project.

Odukoya denied embezzling the money, insisting that the funds remained intact.

He explained that the project had experienced delays because of prevailing economic conditions and rising costs, which made its execution difficult.

He also disclosed that he had restricted access to church funds, while questioning why allegations of financial misconduct should be directed at him alone if there were irregularities within the church’s financial management system.

He argued that personnel in the accounts department would also have responsibilities in the event of any financial wrongdoing.

However, his account represents his response to the allegations. Independent clarification from the church’s financial administrators, the BOT and the donor would be necessary to establish the status of the N250 million and the circumstances surrounding the delayed project.

Family ties strained by crisis

Perhaps the most emotional aspect of Odukoya’s account was his admission that the disagreement had severely damaged his relationship with his sisters.

He lamented that the crisis had placed him in opposition to members of his immediate family, making an already difficult leadership challenge more painful.

He also said he had asked members of the BOT, including his elder sister, to resign as part of efforts to give the church a fresh start.

According to him, he was willing to have his sister return to the board in the future but believed the institution needed a clean slate to move forward.

His sisters, however, were reportedly unconvinced, while the board maintained its position.

The situation highlights the intersection of family relationships, church administration, succession arrangements and institutional authority underpinning the dispute.

Prayer, fasting and spiritual reassurance

Explaining why he remained firm despite the pressure, Odukoya said he resorted to fasting and prayer, seeking divine direction on how to handle the crisis.

He disclosed that he asked God to speak to him through a dream or send someone he did not know to provide clarity.

According to him, his late father subsequently appeared to him in a dream, assuring him that he would overcome attempts to discredit him.

He also recounted meeting a pastor who allegedly advised him that unless he removed the BOT members, they would continue to create difficulties for his administration.

Odukoya said the experiences strengthened his resolve not to yield to the board’s demands.

Insists he remains Senior Pastor

Despite the controversy and a statement reportedly circulated by the board on Tuesday, Odukoya maintained that he remains the Senior Pastor of The Fountain of Life Church.

He also expressed uncertainty about how the church’s Sunday service would proceed, suggesting that an advertised programme would not hold because he did not want the disagreement to escalate further.

He hinted that his late father had previously approached Areogun about taking over the church after his demise.

According to Odukoya, Areogun declined the offer, explaining that his calling to ministry was to support Pastor Taiwo Odukoya and that he would not remain in the church if the founder was no longer there.

He said this was why Areogun eventually resigned his membership of the BOT when asked.

Odukoya also defended his stewardship, arguing that the church had recorded increased attendance and other achievements since he assumed leadership.

He, however, acknowledged that a large congregation was not necessarily proof of being right with God.

What next for Fountain of Life?

The meeting ended at about 8 p.m., although some workers and members reportedly remained behind to encourage reconciliation between Odukoya and his sisters.

Some of those present were said to have stressed that the church could not make meaningful progress without peace among the three family members.

The leadership dispute remains unresolved, with questions surrounding the board’s position, the church’s succession arrangements and the allegations against Odukoya still requiring clarification from the other parties involved.

The post Fountain of Life crisis: Jimmy Odukoya alleges conspiracy appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Anthropic valued at $1.5tn ahead of stock market debut
description:
Artificial intelligence company Anthropic has priced its initial public offering at 1.5tn ahead of its planned stock market debut.
The final price, announced on Wednesday, November 18, exceeded the company’s earlier target range of $70 to $78 per share, following strong investor demand during its IP
content:
Artificial intelligence company Anthropic has priced its initial public offering at 1.5tn ahead of its planned stock market debut.

The final price, announced on Wednesday, November 18, exceeded the company’s earlier target range of $70 to $78 per share, following strong investor demand during its IPO roadshow.

Reuters, in a report, said, “the pricing was disclosed by a person familiar with the matter, adding that the size of the offering had also increased.”

The news agency reported that demand during the roadshow exceeded several times the number of shares available, despite concerns about the company’s growth prospects and the rising cost of developing and operating artificial intelligence models.

Anthropic declined to comment on the pricing, Reuters reported, while noting that Bloomberg first reported the development.

According to the Associated Press, “The company had initially planned to offer 825 million shares, with its stock expected to trade on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol ANT.

The IPO is one of the biggest stock market offerings on record and marks a major milestone for the artificial intelligence industry, as investors seek exposure to companies developing advanced AI models.

Anthropic was founded in 2021 by former OpenAI executives, including its Chief Executive Officer, Dario Amodei, and his sister, Daniela Amodei.

It has since become a major competitor in the AI industry through its Claude family of models.

Explaining the scale of the undertaking, Anthropic said in its earlier IPO filing, as reported by ABC News, on Wednesday, that “building and scaling frontier intelligence is one of the most important and capital-intensive endeavors in history.”

The company also disclosed plans for a separate $26bn private placement involving major technology companies, including Google, Microsoft, Nvidia, AMD, Broadcom, Micron and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company.

The IPO comes amid growing investor interest in artificial intelligence businesses, although concerns remain over the enormous infrastructure costs associated with developing and operating advanced AI systems.

title: ‘It will be a miracle if Tinubu wins two or three states in the North’ – Hakeem Baba-Ahmed
description:
The National Chairman of the Peoples Redemption Party (PRP), Dr Hakeem Baba-Ahmed, has expressed doubts about the All Progressives Congress’ chances in the 2027 general elections, predicting that it could struggle to secure victories in Northern Nigeria.
Baba-Ahmed made the remarks during an intervi
content:
The National Chairman of the Peoples Redemption Party (PRP), Dr Hakeem Baba-Ahmed, has expressed doubts about the All Progressives Congress’ chances in the 2027 general elections, predicting that it could struggle to secure victories in Northern Nigeria.

Baba-Ahmed made the remarks during an interview on Trust TV’s Daily Politics, hosted by Hamza Idris, while assessing the political climate ahead of the next general elections.

According to him, the level of public dissatisfaction with the ruling party could make it difficult for the APC to win even two or three states in the North.

“On the basis of the current disposition of the public towards APC at all levels, it will be a miracle if they genuinely win two or three states in the North,” he said.

The PRP chairman also predicted that the APC could face electoral setbacks in other parts of the country, saying he would not be surprised if the party lost all five states in the South-East, two or three states in the South-South and possibly two states in the South-West, as well as most of the North-Central region.

He also questioned promises by some APC governors that they could deliver millions of votes for President Bola Tinubu in 2027, asking where such votes would come from amid growing public dissatisfaction.

Baba-Ahmed argued that the President should not rely solely on assurances from governors but should pay attention to the reactions of ordinary Nigerians during public engagements.

He cited the APC’s recent rally in Jos, Plateau State, claiming that the stadium appeared empty or half-filled, which he said raised questions about the level of public support for the ruling party.

The former presidential aide also criticised the disruption of worshippers during President Tinubu’s visit to a mosque in Abuja, expressing concern over reports that people were prevented from accessing the mosque because of the President’s arrival.

His comments come as political parties intensify preparations for the 2027 general elections, with competing claims over the ruling party’s popularity and its prospects across the country.

The post ‘It will be a miracle if Tinubu wins two or three states in the North’ – Hakeem Baba-Ahmed appeared first on Very Nigerian.

content:
Barcelona winger, Anthony Gordon has revealed just how obsessed his teammate, Lamine Yamal is with football.

In a light-hearted Q&A with LaLiga’s official social media channel, the England international was asked who talks about football the most every day among the Barcelona squad.

Gordon did not hesitate.

“Lamine Yamal could talk about football 24 hours a day,” he said.

The 25-year-old, who joined Barcelona from Newcastle United in the summer, has settled quickly at the Camp Nou and offered a glimpse into life inside Hansi Flick’s dressing room during the chat.

Gordon answered a series of questions about his teammates, including who arrives earliest for training and who he thinks could become the best coach in the future.

He named Andreas Christensen as always the first player to arrive at the Ciutat Esportiva training ground.

He equally tipped Dutchman, Frenkie de Jong to make the best coach thanks to his “smart vision on the pitch.”

But it was his answer on Yamal that stood out, highlighting the 19-year-old’s love for the game beyond matches and training.

Gordon has previously praised Yamal, describing what he has achieved at such a young age as “ridiculous” and saying he is “on a whole other level.”

title: DisCo Staff Allegedly Killed For Disconnecting Building Over Debt In Delta
description: The management of Benin Electricity Distribution Company (BEDC) has called on the Delta State Government to strengthen the protection of electricity workers following the alleged killing of one of its staff members, 38-year-old Oscar Uduka Eze, in Umunede, Ika North East Local Government Area of Del
content:
The management of Benin Electricity Distribution Company (BEDC) has called on the Delta State Government to strengthen the protection of electricity workers following the alleged killing of one of its staff members, 38-year-old Oscar Uduka Eze, in Umunede, Ika North East Local Government Area of Delta State.

The company made the call on Wednesday during a press briefing by its Acting Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer, Jonathan Lawani, at the BEDC headquarters in Benin City.

BEDC said Eze was allegedly stabbed to death on Monday, November 16, 2026, while carrying out his official duties in the community, following the disconnection of electricity supply to a property over an outstanding bill of nearly N300,000.

According to the company, the deceased was performing an authorised assignment within the regulatory framework of the electricity distribution sector when some persons allegedly traced him to another location in the community and stabbed him repeatedly.

Describing the incident as a painful loss, Lawani said the killing of the staff member was an attack on the company’s workforce and called for justice for the deceased and his family.

“Some hoodlums, some men who claim to be more powerful than God, traced him to a house within the same community and stabbed him with knives until he died on the spot,” he said.

The BEDC management explained that disconnection remained an approved regulatory mechanism for addressing non-payment of electricity bills, insisting that Eze had acted within the scope of his official responsibilities.

The company also disclosed that some suspects had been arrested in connection with the incident, expressing confidence that the relevant authorities would ensure a thorough investigation and prosecution of those involved.

“Sad as it is, we cannot recover his life. We can never bring his life back to his people. But one thing is certain: we must bring justice to his family,” Lawani stated.

BEDC further expressed concern that the incident could threaten its operations in Delta State, urging the state government to provide a safe working environment for personnel in the electricity sector.

The company warned that failure to address the security concerns could compel its management to consult with the board on the next steps regarding its operations in the state.

It stressed that the safety of its workforce remained essential to the delivery of electricity services and called on government and well-meaning Nigerians to condemn attacks on personnel carrying out legitimate official assignments.

The post DisCo Staff Allegedly Killed For Disconnecting Building Over Debt In Delta appeared first on Channels Television.

description:
By Emem Idio







Yenagoa—A Bayelsa State High Court sitting in Yenagoa has sentenced a 39-year-old driver, Perelayefa Nelson, to five years’ imprisonment for his complicity in the theft of a Toyota Hilux utility vehicle valued at over N22 million.



Nelson was arrested in 2024 by operatives of t
content:
By Emem Idio

Yenagoa—A Bayelsa State High Court sitting in Yenagoa has sentenced a 39-year-old driver, Perelayefa Nelson, to five years’ imprisonment for his complicity in the theft of a Toyota Hilux utility vehicle valued at over N22 million.


Nelson was arrested in 2024 by operatives of the then Operation Puff Adder, now the Violence Crime Response Unit.


The prosecution told the court that the defendant acted contrary to the express instruction of his employer, Eddy Brayei, a politician and businessman, by parking the white Hilux, with registration number KSF 522 CY, at a location other than the designated Monalisa Hotel.


According to the prosecution, Brayei had specifically directed Nelson to park the vehicle at the hotel for security reasons. However, the defendant allegedly parked it by the fence of the Federal Medical Centre, FMC, Yenagoa, where it subsequently went missing.


The defendant was subsequently charged to court over his alleged involvement in the theft.


Delivering judgment, Justice Patience Zuofa, sentenced Nelson to five years’ imprisonment after reviewing the evidence presented by the police prosecution.


The conviction followed the prosecution’s presentation of evidence linking the defendant to the circumstances surrounding the disappearance of the vehicle.

title: Fani-Kayode reveals why he requested South Africa posting instead of Europe
description:
Femi Fani-Kayode, Nigeria’s High Commissioner to South Africa, has disclosed that he was initially assigned to a European country but later appealed to be posted to South Africa.
Fani-Kayode made this revelation during a dinner and reception hosted by the Nigerian High Commission and Consular Office
content:
Femi Fani-Kayode, Nigeria’s High Commissioner to South Africa, has disclosed that he was initially assigned to a European country but later appealed to be posted to South Africa.

Fani-Kayode made this revelation during a dinner and reception hosted by the Nigerian High Commission and Consular Office in Pretoria.

The event followed the presentation of his letters of credence to South African President Cyril Ramaphosa on November 13, marking the formal commencement of his diplomatic assignment in the country.

“I was sent here by our president, President Bola Ahmed, president of the Federal Republic of Nigeria — 250 million strong, a massive country, resilient people with rich history, very proud people, hardworking people that love life and love their country passionately, and I’ve been sent to represent those people and our government in a country which is equally resilient, hardworking, decent, civilised, with an equally rich history and heritage, as we have,” he said.

“And we’ve all been through so much. And what’s important is this: it is important that we recognise the fact that together, South Africa and Nigeria can actually help to move sub-Saharan and Africa, in general, forward. We must not allow any division, we must not allow any misunderstanding, we must not allow even any slight to put us apart.

“And that’s why I chose this country. I was initially posted to a European country, and I made an appeal to our president that I preferred to go to South Africa which he graciously agreed to. So I find myself here.”

Fani-Kayode did not name the European nation to which he was initially posted. However, media reports had identified Germany as his proposed posting, although neither the Nigerian nor German government has confirmed the reported rejection of the appointment.

Fani-Kayode said from the time he arrived in South Africa, he began to look into some of the things that concerned the Nigerian community.

He described those responsible for xenophobic attacks in South Africa as a “tiny minority”, saying they do not represent the majority of South Africans, whom he characterised as decent and accommodating people.

The envoy reiterated that Nigeria would not sever economic ties with South Africa despite the clamour from Nigerians.

He said he would work to rebuild ties between the countries.

title: I Feel ‘Pretty Foolish’ For Failed US Election Spending — Musk
description: World’s richest man Elon Musk said Wednesday he felt “pretty foolish” for donating nearly half a billion dollars to failed campaigns in recent US midterm elections, backing right-wing Republicans in races that were largely won by Democrats.“I feel pretty foolish about having
content:
World’s richest man Elon Musk said Wednesday he felt “pretty foolish” for donating nearly half a billion dollars to failed campaigns in recent US midterm elections, backing right-wing Republicans in races that were largely won by Democrats.

“I feel pretty foolish about having spent so much money and not seeing much for it, or maybe it would have been much worse without that,” Musk said via videolink at the New York Times Dealbook conference.

Musk said his goal was “either the presidency, the House or the Senate be of the other party. That was my actual goal here, which failed by the way.”

The Tesla and SpaceX boss sought to extract a lesson from the folly, telling the audience: “It certainly shows that American elections are not just about money.”

“Obviously you can put a lot of money into election and have an effect that is relatively minor, and I think that was the case here,” he continued.

The midterms weren’t the South Africa-born tech tycoon’s first foray into American elections.

Musk spent more than $250 million to help US President Donald Trump return to the White House for his second term and briefly led the 80-year-old Republican’s Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE), before they had a public falling out.

They’ve since reconciled, and instead of souring on Republican politics, Musk has continued to back Republicans whom the president champions.

Among the candidates he backed most strongly was Texas Senate candidate Ken Paxton, with Musk contributing an estimated $220 million to the Republican, only for the race to be won by James Talarico, a 37-year-old Democrat.

The headquarters of several of Musk’s companies, including SpaceX and Tesla, are in Austin, Texas.

“If I could rewind the clock, I would have spent less money,” Musk said of the elections, adding: “I didn’t put a lot of personal attention into it because I’m focused on building SpaceX, Tesla.”

title: Soldiers captured in viral video inside Kwara bush not fraternising with enemies – Army
description:
The Headquarters of the Joint Task Force Operation Savannah Shield (JTF OPSS) has clarified that the soldiers captured alongside Department of State Services (DSS) operatives in a viral video interacting with armed bandits in a bush in Kwara State were not fraternising with enemies.
In a statement i
content:
The Headquarters of the Joint Task Force Operation Savannah Shield (JTF OPSS) has clarified that the soldiers captured alongside Department of State Services (DSS) operatives in a viral video interacting with armed bandits in a bush in Kwara State were not fraternising with enemies.

In a statement issued on Wednesday, by the Acting Deputy Director, Army Public Relations, 9 Division/Operation Savannah Shield, Lieutenant Colonel Ibrahim Shittu, the JTF said the video has generated misleading narratives and interpretations suggesting an inappropriate relationship between troops and the armed elements.

It noted that the engagement captured in the video was a deliberate security initiative involving troops and armed bandits who had indicated their willingness to surrender their weapons and facilitate the release of kidnapped victims.

“It was an outcome of successful military strangulation operations that left no room for the terrorists aside surrender or neutralisation. The video in circulation captures part of an engagement undertaken in this light,” the statement reads in part.

The military disclosed that during the engagement, a total of 12 AK-47 rifles were recovered, while 10 kidnapped victims were released.

It described the development as a significant outcome of the non-kinetic approach being employed alongside sustained military operations to address security challenges and encourage the voluntary surrender of armed elements.

“Contrary to the misleading interpretations accompanying the video, the interaction was neither an act of fraternisation nor an abandonment of the military’s constitutional responsibilities. Rather, it was a calculated engagement aimed at achieving tangible security outcomes, particularly the recovery of weapons and the safe release of innocent citizens held hostage,” JTF OPSS said.

The task force said it remains committed to employing a comprehensive approach that combines robust kinetic operations with intelligence-led engagements and other non-kinetic measures to address terrorism, banditry and other security threats.

Such initiatives, it said, are intended to provide opportunities for those willing to surrender to do so.

“Any individual or group that chooses to surrender will be subjected to the necessary security screening and applicable legal procedures. It should be noted that surrendered combatants are not to be harmed at the point of surrender in line with law of armed conflict, international best practices and operational rules of engagement. In the same vein, acceptance of surrender is an acceptable outcome of conflict resolution,” the statement further reads.

JTF OPSS reassured Nigerians that the Armed Forces remain resolute, professional and focused on their constitutional mandate of protecting the territorial integrity of the country and safeguarding lives and property.

Members of the public were urged to disregard misleading interpretations of the circulating video and avoid sharing unverified narratives capable of undermining ongoing security efforts.

title: Ban sign-out ceremonies at all levels of education, say parents, student leaders
description:
By Adesina  Wahab



In recent years, a fad has taken root in Nigeria’s education system, the practice of signing out of school when students conclude their examinations, even without being sure of what the results would look like. It is especially rampant at secondary school and tertiary education
content:
By Adesina  Wahab

In recent years, a fad has taken root in Nigeria’s education system, the practice of signing out of school when students conclude their examinations, even without being sure of what the results would look like. It is especially rampant at secondary school and tertiary education levels. Out of what many have labelled youthful exuberance, the graduating students do engage in various activities, including holding wild parties.

Read Also: (Video) UNN Party Tragedy: How I regained consciousness, found friends lying lifeless – Survivor

In May this year, many parents, guardians and even teachers were left bewildered when the social media was full of videos of some male secondary school students fondling their female counterparts in broad daylight. Some male students were also seen signing on the uniforms of their female colleagues in their private areas. The students were traced to a particular school in Ondo State and punishment meted out to them. 

But at tertiary education level, wild parties and binge drinking have led to unnecessary deaths. Only in April this year, after the second convocation ceremony of Bamidele Olumilua University of Education, Science and Technology (BOUESTI) in Ikere-Ekiti, Ekiti State, three persons, two of whom were graduating students of the university, died in a stampede that resulted from a fight at a party thrown by some students of the university. A member of staff of the hotel where the party was held was the third casualty.

Investigations by the Police revealed that a fight broke out during the party and that sharp objects were freely used, leading to people scampering for safety and many people being trampled upon. Scores of people sustained varying degrees of injuries.

Just few days ago, the news broke that some students of the University of Nigeria, Nsukka, died as a result of what they consumed at a sign-out party organised by some graduating students. The figure initially given was eight but in the end, four students were confirmed dead. Even if it was one person that died, human life is too valuable to be toyed with.

Reacting to the development, the Governor of Enugu State, Peter Mbah, described the deaths as a grievous loss, not only to the immediate families of the deceased and the university, but also to Enugu State as a whole. He called for a ban on sign-out parties among undergraduates, noting that the practice had brought too much sorrow to families and tertiary institutions across the country.

“I received with rude shock and deep sense of loss the news of the off-campus sing-out party leading to the death of four students of the University of Nigeria Nsukka, and hospitalisation of six others.

“This is a grievous loss not only to the immediate families of the deceased and the university, but also to us as a state. Losing them in their prime and along with their promising future cuts as deeply as a sharp knife. We, therefore share in this grief and pray God to grant their families, friends, and the UNN community the equanimity to bear the heartbreaking loss.

“Our hearts go out to their parents in particular, who sacrificed personal comforts to sponsor their children through the university, but only to face this sad turn of events.

“As a government, we have ordered a thorough investigation into the circumstances surrounding their deaths and will work closely with the university authorities and security agencies to get to the roots of the sad development and forestall a recurrence.

“Going forward, we will work with the authorities of tertiary institutions to enforce a full ban on sign-out parties and other excessive celebrations, a trend that has cost more lives and brought more sorrows than joy to families and higher institutions of learning,” the governor stated.

Students go overboard at such parties — NAPTAN boss

Speaking with Vanguard on the matter, the Chairman of the Board of Trustees of the National Parent Teacher Association of Nigeria, Chief Adeolu Ogunbanjo, blamed excesses on the part of students for the calamities resulting from sign-out ceremonies.

“Nobody is saying that people should not celebrate their accomplishments. But excess of everything is bad. Due to youthful exuberance, people do tend to go overboard during such parties. They are not like the graduation ceremonies and the attendant receptions family members organise for their children and wards. Those ones do have family members, friends and elderly people in attendance and any move to go overboard would be checked.

“What should be done is that sign-out ceremonies should be banned at all levels. We cannot afford to continue losing our young ones to things we can prevent. Unfortunately, most of the time, such wild celebrations are held outside school premises, where school authorities would not have the opportunity of stopping such events. It is the duty of parents and guardians now to impress it on their wards that such events are no longer acceptable and tolerated, “ he stated.

There is need for moderation — NANS 

Also speaking on the matter, the National Public Relations Officer of the National Association of Nigerian Students, NANS, Obidah David, said there is need for moderation in everything.

“We can only sympathise with the families of the victims. We cannot hold the school authorities responsible as it happened outside the campus. What I want to say is that there is need for moderation in whatever we do. We must also be careful. Juvenile delinquencies shown by college students who would be signing and defacing their uniforms are not acceptable. Also, wild parties are not what graduating university students should engage in too. There is more to life than such things.

“As student leaders, we will sensitise other students on the need to be careful. Regarding the UNN incident, there are conflicting reports on what could have been the cause of the tragic incident. At any rate, we should not put ourselves in harm’s way by our conduct. Such sign-out ceremonies must be outlawed,” he submitted.

Vanguard News

title: 2027: Ndume warns political violence could threaten Nigeria’s elections
description:
Senator Ali Ndume has warned that rising political violence and intolerance could threaten the credibility and peaceful conduct of Nigeria’s 2027 general elections if authorities fail to address the situation early.
The APC lawmaker representing Borno South said attacks on political leaders and thei
content:
Senator Ali Ndume has warned that rising political violence and intolerance could threaten the credibility and peaceful conduct of Nigeria’s 2027 general elections if authorities fail to address the situation early.

The APC lawmaker representing Borno South said attacks on political leaders and their supporters could spread if those responsible were not identified and prosecuted.

Ndume spoke during an interview with ARISE News on Wednesday, after the Senate considered a motion sponsored by Senator Abdul Ningi calling for investigations into electoral violence and prosecution of perpetrators.

Ndume, who seconded the motion, said lawmakers were concerned about reported attacks involving President Bola Tinubu’s convoy, former Labour Party presidential candidate Peter Obi and former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar.

He stressed the need for authorities to intervene before political violence becomes difficult to contain.

“So that we may nip it in the bud,” he said.

He likened the situation to a fire that could spread beyond control if not tackled immediately.

“The problem is like fire. If it catches, you don’t know why it will stop, and you may have problem putting it off,” he added.

The senator insisted that responsibility for political violence should not be limited to those who physically carry out attacks, arguing that individuals who finance or sponsor such activities should also face the consequences.

“If, for example, I sponsored, confirmed, evidently sponsored that group to carry out that kind of criminality, then I should be held responsible too,” he said.

Ndume also called for the establishment of special courts to handle electoral violence cases, noting that delays in the justice system often weaken accountability.

“The problem with our judicial system is justice has been excessively delayed,” he said.

He further advocated a ban on weapons such as knives and sticks during political campaigns, urging security agencies to ensure that offenders are prosecuted.

On the security response to the reported attack on Tinubu’s convoy, Ndume commended security agencies but noted that the protection available to the president could not be compared with that of ordinary Nigerians.

“You cannot compare that with the security of Mr President,” he said.

However, he emphasised the government’s constitutional responsibility to protect citizens, citing Section 14(2)(b) of the 1999 Constitution.

The senator also linked the growing involvement of young people in political violence to unemployment and widespread frustration.

“Violence, by youth and children, is trying to take over the political scene,” he said.

He added that there was “a high level of frustration, anger among our youth, especially with the high level of unemployment.”

Ndume’s warning comes amid increasing political activities ahead of the 2027 elections, with concerns over attacks on political figures and restrictions on opposition parties.

title: Dollar to Naira exchange rate today, November 19, 2026
description:
The Nigerian naira opened early morning trading on Thursday, November 19, 2026, with diverging trends across the official and informal currency segments, as the official interbank spot market showed mild appreciation while the parallel market maintained pressure above the ₦1,440 threshold.



Offici
content:
The Nigerian naira opened early morning trading on Thursday, November 19, 2026, with diverging trends across the official and informal currency segments, as the official interbank spot market showed mild appreciation while the parallel market maintained pressure above the ₦1,440 threshold.

Official Market Performance

Real-time interbank spot tracking at the Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM) placed the US dollar at ₦1,350.50 as of early Thursday morning, reflecting a slight gain of 0.10 percent for the local currency from its early session opening of ₦1,351.81. This follows Wednesday’s official volume-weighted closing benchmark of ₦1,363.23 per dollar published by the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN).

Parallel Market Rates

In the parallel market, also referred to as the black market, Bureau de Change (BDC) operators and street dealers in Lagos and Abuja quoted the US dollar within a selling band of ₦1,445 to ₦1,468, with buying rates hovering between ₦1,435 and ₦1,455 depending on transaction volume and location. Following Wednesday’s late trading close where street rates climbed as high as ₦1,453 to ₦1,468, the spread between the official NFEM benchmark and the informal market stands between ₦90 and ₦105 per dollar.

Market Drivers and Reserve Outlook

Currency analysts attribute the persistent divergence between both windows to moderating autonomous foreign exchange inflows alongside heightened seasonal import demand and corporate obligations. Market data indicates that weekly inflows into the foreign exchange market recently moderated to $807.6 million as offshore portfolio investors adopted a cautious stance.

Despite recent liquidity interventions by the apex bank—which have trimmed Nigeria’s external reserves by approximately $390 million from their late-October peak of $55.26 billion—the country’s reserve buffer remains over 26 percent higher than the $43.54 billion recorded during the corresponding period in 2025. Financial institutions expect the Central Bank of Nigeria to sustain targeted liquidity support to keep official NFEM rates anchored within the ₦1,350 to ₦1,365 band, even as unfulfilled retail demand continues to drive premiums in the parallel segment.

title: Canada suspends cadet training over budget cuts
description:
Canada’s military has suspended most weekend training activities and competitions for cadets in parts of the country until March 2027.
It cited budget constraints despite the government’s commitment to billions of dollars in additional defence spending.
The restrictions, which affect cadet programme
content:
Canada’s military has suspended most weekend training activities and competitions for cadets in parts of the country until March 2027.

It cited budget constraints despite the government’s commitment to billions of dollars in additional defence spending.

The restrictions, which affect cadet programmes in Ontario and British Columbia, will remain in place until the end of the current fiscal year on March 31, 2027.

However, weekly parade nights are allowed to continue for now.

According to CBC News, which reported the development on Wednesday, internal emails obtained by the broadcaster showed that the Department of National Defence was struggling to manage operational and support funding cuts.

An email quoting the commander of Ontario’s Regional Cadet Support Unit (Central), Lt.-Col. Raphael MacKenzie, said all cadet activities had been suspended for the remainder of the fiscal year, except weekly parade nights.

The restrictions took immediate effect in Ontario, while similar measures are scheduled to begin in British Columbia on November 21.

In a statement, Canada’s Department of National Defence said funding for the cadet and junior Canadian ranger programmes was being reviewed, adding that their combined allocation had increased to $`265m.

The department said some planned activities would have to be adjusted to align spending with available resources, while efforts would be made to protect experiences considered important to young participants.

It added that it was too early to determine the full extent of the changes and their impact.

The development comes as the government of Prime Minister Mark Carney commits billions of dollars in additional funding to strengthen Canada’s military capabilities, including the acquisition of combat equipment.

However, the department is also required to identify $459m in operational savings during the current fiscal year and another $459m in the following year, following spending reduction measures announced by the previous government in 2023 and implemented through the 2024 federal budget.

Conservative defence critic James Bezan said reservists and cadets were bearing the consequences of the spending restrictions.

“Mark Carney and the Liberals can’t be talking out of both sides of their mouths, saying that they’re investing in the armed forces and then cutting operations,” Bezan said.

“That reduces our readiness. The Carney cuts are having real impacts on the day-to-day operations of the Canadian Armed Forces.”

A separate internal email concerning British Columbia acknowledged that the restrictions would disappoint cadets, families and personnel who had spent time planning activities.

The email said regional leadership was prioritising activities directly supporting weekly training at cadet corps and squadrons.
