title: South-South: Incumbents, heavyweights in make or mar gov battles
description:
By Jimitota Onoyume



WITH the 2027 general elections approaching, the battle for four governorship seats across the South-South is gathering momentum, with incumbents, political heavyweights and emerging contenders positioning themselves for control of the region’s political landscape.



In Akwa
content:
By Jimitota Onoyume

WITH the 2027 general elections approaching, the battle for four governorship seats across the South-South is gathering momentum, with incumbents, political heavyweights and emerging contenders positioning themselves for control of the region’s political landscape.

In Akwa Ibom, Governor Umo Eno is banking on his performance, incumbency and the mass defection of Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, members to the All Progressives Congress, APC, to secure a second term.

In Cross River, Governor Bassey Otu enjoys the advantages of incumbency, federal backing and expanding political alliances, but faces a determined challenge from PDP’s Arthur Jarvis Archibong.

Rivers presents a more complicated contest, with the influence of FCT Minister Nyesom Wike, the political grievances arising from the protracted power struggle in the state and the growing appeal of opposition parties shaping the calculations.

In Delta, Governor Sheriff Oborevwori appears to enjoy an advantageous position following his defection to the APC and the support of influential political leaders, while opposition candidates seek to exploit the changing political alignments.

Across the four states, the contests will test the strength of incumbency, party structures, political alliances, grassroots mobilisation and the capacity of opposition candidates to convert public support into electoral victories. There will be no governorship polls in Bayelsa and Edo.

Eno holds ace as opposition plots upset in Akwa Ibom

Governor Umo Eno of the APC appears to have the upper hand in the battle for Akwa Ibom Government House, facing former senator and minister, John Akpanudoedehe of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, and former House of Representatives member, Michael Enyong of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC.

Eno, who hails from Akwa Ibom North-East Senatorial District, Uyo, enjoys the advantage of incumbency and the political boost arising from the defection of several PDP members to the APC.

His performance in office over the last three and a half years is also being projected as a major selling point as he seeks another four years.

Although Akpanudoedehe commands considerable political recognition in the state, and Enyong brings legislative experience to the contest, observers believe the incumbent’s political machinery and expanding support base could prove difficult to dislodge.

A public affairs analyst, Mr Ben Ikoriko, believes Eno’s empowerment programmes, particularly for people at the lower end of the state’s economy, could secure him substantial electoral support.

He said: “Umo Eno will win. Yes, there are two other contenders; Akpanudoedehe and Enyong, the governor has done well and deserves a second term. Again, the PDP crossed to the APC. I can tell you that 80 per cent of the people are with Umo Eno.”

Ikoriko said the governor had empowered beneficiaries with cash, sewing machines, fishing equipment and other tools to establish businesses.

“My in-law, wife and mother benefitted from the largesse. People were given cash, sewing machines and many other things, including modern fishing equipment for fishermen,” he added.

Another public affairs stakeholder, Andy Eyo, also predicted Eno’s victory, arguing that zoning considerations and the governor’s political acceptance were working in his favour.

However, the NDC has dismissed the argument that incumbency gives Eno an insurmountable advantage.

The party’s State Publicity Secretary, Edidiong Umoetor, expressed confidence that Enyong would defeat the governor, citing his legislative experience and capacity to deliver good governance.

He said: “When you have a good candidate, the party sells beyond expectation. At the national level, we have Peter Obi, who even the blind, the deaf know about him. Then coming to Akwa Ibom State, we are not afraid of the power of incumbency.”

Describing Enyong as an experienced legislator, Umoetor said: “Enyong is a two-time representative of his constituency in the National Assembly. He was chairman of the Committee on Mining and Mineral Resources twice. So, the experience and capacity are there.”

He added: “We are 100 per cent sure of winning. Our strategies are with us and we are moving forward by God’s grace.”

The APC, however, insists that Eno’s achievements have put him in a commanding position.

Its spokesman, Chief Patryk Edeke, said the administration had paid more than N91 billion out of over N120 billion in inherited gratuity arrears.

He also cited the provision of ambulances to all 31 local government areas, improvements in primary healthcare, compassionate homes for vulnerable people and the construction of about 1,550 kilometres of roads.

According to him, these projects have strengthened public confidence in the administration.

With the incumbent’s political structure, performance claims and the opposition’s determination to make an impact, Akwa Ibom’s contest promises to be a test of whether Eno’s popularity can withstand a coordinated challenge.

Otu’s commanding lead faces Archibong’s grassroots challenge in C-River

In Cross River, the central question is whether Governor Bassey Otu can consolidate his political advantage or whether the opposition can mobilise enough support to dislodge him in the February 6, 2027 governorship election.

Four major contenders dominate the race: Otu of the APC, Sir Arthur Jarvis Archibong of the PDP, Ambassador Nkoyo Toyo of the ADC and John Odey Jr. of the NDC.

Otu appears to be the frontrunner, buoyed by incumbency, party machinery, political alliances and federal backing.

He emerged as the APC’s sole aspirant and secured the party’s ticket, with 160,038 votes reportedly recorded across the state’s 18 local government areas.

His position has been strengthened by defections from opposition parties, endorsements by traditional rulers, religious organisations and support groups, as well as political engagements across the state.

Federal backing is another advantage. Vice-President Kashim Shettima, representing President Bola Tinubu at the groundbreaking ceremony of the Bakassi Deep Seaport, urged Cross River residents to support the governor for continuity.

Otu’s supporters also point to his agricultural initiatives and economic programmes, including the payment of the first N10 billion tranche of retirees’ gratuities.

However, critics argue that increased Federation Account Allocation Committee, FAAC, inflows and internally generated revenue have not translated into commensurate visible infrastructure and development.

Some also contend that his political advantage rests more on incumbency than widespread public enthusiasm.

Archibong, proprietor of Arthur Jarvis University, has emerged as Otu’s most visible challenger.

The PDP candidate has reportedly toured all 18 local government areas, consulting political stakeholders and community leaders. His rallies and town hall meetings have also attracted sizeable crowds.

His challenge to Otu to participate in a public debate is part of an effort to project himself as accessible and ready to subject his ideas to public scrutiny.

Archibong is also believed to enjoy some goodwill from FCT Minister Nyesom Wike through Prof. Sandy Onor, who reportedly led PDP candidates to Abuja to meet the minister.

However, his lack of experience in public office could become a campaign issue. His opposition to the ‘Back to South’ arrangement, despite supporting Onor in 2023, has also attracted criticism.

The PDP’s internal difficulties constitute another challenge. The resignation and defection of former state chairman, Venatius Ikem, to the APC weakened the party’s structure. His replacement, Chief Francis Bullem, faces the task of rebuilding the party and restoring confidence.

For Archibong, the challenge is not merely attracting crowds but converting enthusiasm into votes through effective polling-unit mobilisation.

Toyo, a lawyer and former member of the House of Representatives representing Calabar Municipality/Odukpani Federal Constituency, brings considerable political experience to the contest.

She is arguably the most politically experienced among the opposition challengers. Her candidacy offers voters an alternative to the dominant APC and PDP.

Toyo and her running mate, Dr Dino Magam, are on INEC’s final list. She was also scheduled to unveil her manifesto and launch her campaign fund on November 16.

Her major disadvantage, however, is the late start to the campaign. Archibong has already established considerable visibility, while ADC’s organisational reach remains limited compared with the APC and PDP.

Reported defections from the ADC, including a chieftain who launched a movement supporting Otu’s re-election, further expose its difficulties.

For Odey, the NDC candidate, the challenge is more fundamental: establishing a visible campaign structure.

There have been few indications of statewide consultations, rallies or grassroots mobilisation. His deputy, Stella Archibong, has reportedly withdrawn from the ticket and aligned with the Otu administration, dealing another blow to his ambition.

Unless he changes strategy and intensifies mobilisation, Odey risks remaining a distant contender.

Ultimately, Otu’s political alliances and federal backing give him a commanding advantage, but Cross River’s electoral history suggests that the opposition should not be written off.

Wike factor, Fubara’s political fate shape four-way battle in Rivers

The Rivers governorship contest presents one of the most intriguing political battles in the South-South, with four candidates positioning themselves to control the state’s political machinery.

The candidates are Hon. Kingsley Chinda of the APC, Dumo Lulu-Briggs of the NDC, Dr Gabriel Pidomson of the ADC and Pastor Nature Dumale Kieghe of the Peoples Redemption Party, PRP.

Chinda’s greatest advantage is his position as candidate of the ruling APC and his membership of the Rainbow Coalition, a political group with influence across the state’s 23 local government areas.

More significantly, he enjoys the backing of Wike, who has considerable influence in the state’s political calculations and enjoys the support of President Bola Tinubu.

Chinda is also reportedly the preferred successor of Governor Siminalayi Fubara, who has been effectively shut out of seeking a second term. Fubara has pledged to ensure that Chinda succeeds him in 2027.

The candidate is therefore expected to benefit from considerable political and financial resources, as well as the backing of influential political actors at the state and federal levels.

But these advantages could also become his biggest liability.

Wike’s role in the political crisis that engulfed Rivers, culminating in President Tinubu’s declaration of a state of emergency in March 2025, remains a contentious issue.

Many Rivers people, particularly in the Ijaw-speaking areas, remain aggrieved over the treatment of Fubara. Some view the political developments as denying the Ijaw ethnic nationality the opportunity to govern the state for eight years, as other groups had done in the past.

Consequently, Chinda could face a protest vote from voters opposed to Wike’s influence and the political circumstances surrounding Fubara’s exit.

He also has to contend with a legal challenge instituted by one of the governorship candidates over the implication of the recent Supreme Court judgment for his defection from the PDP to the APC.

For NDC’s Dumo Lulu-Briggs, the greatest attraction is the political appeal of the party’s presidential candidate, Peter Obi, whose support cuts across party, ethnic and religious boundaries.

A wealthy businessman, Dumo also has the financial capacity to fund his campaign without depending entirely on party resources.

His Ijaw and riverine roots could further attract support from voters opposed to Wike’s political influence, particularly those sympathetic to Fubara.

However, questions have been raised about his commitment and campaign energy. Some political observers regard him as a perennial governorship contestant whose repeated appearances in the race have yet to translate into a decisive political breakthrough.

ADC’s Pidomson has a different advantage. He belongs to the same party as former Rivers Governor Rotimi Amaechi, who is Atiku Abubakar’s running mate in the 2027 presidential contest.

The Atiku-Amaechi ticket could provide a national political platform and visibility for Pidomson, particularly if the opposition makes significant electoral gains.

His major weakness, however, is inadequate funding. Politics in Rivers requires substantial financial resources, and Pidomson is not believed to enjoy the financial muscle available to some of his rivals.

The internal divisions within Ogoni land, particularly disagreements over resumption of oil exploration and the agitation for Bori State, could also complicate his political calculations.

Kieghe of the PRP is perhaps the least established of the four contenders.

His supporters could market him as a fresh face without the baggage of previous political office. His religious background may also provide a limited support base.

However, he lacks the financial resources, political experience, popularity and organisational structure required to mount a formidable statewide campaign.

The Rivers contest is therefore likely to revolve around the Wike factor, the political grievances surrounding Fubara, the appeal of Obi and the ability of opposition candidates to translate sympathy into votes.

As it is, Wike’s backing gives Chinda a formidable structure, but resentment over Fubara’s political ordeal could fuel a protest vote for Dumo and other opposition candidates.

Oborevwori’s political coalition puts APC in pole position in Delta

In Delta State, Governor Sheriff Oborevwori appears to enjoy a significant political advantage following his defection from the PDP to the APC and the support of influential political figures across the state.

All four major governorship candidates hail from Delta Central Senatorial District, reflecting the state’s established zoning arrangement.

They are Oborevwori of the APC, Peter Mrakpor of the PDP, Deacon Chris Iyovwaye of the NDC and Chief Great Ogboru of the ADC.

Oborevwori’s strongest asset is his expanding political coalition and grassroots support base.

His defection to the APC has strengthened the party’s presence across the state’s wards, local government areas and senatorial districts.

He also enjoys the backing of influential political leaders, including former governors James Ibori and Ifeanyi Okowa, Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, Senators Ede Dafinone and Joel-Onowakpo Thomas, and former Senator James Manager.

The support cuts across different political tendencies and is expected to strengthen the governor’s re-election machinery.

The state’s zoning arrangement may also work in his favour. With Delta Central currently occupying the governorship, the understanding that Delta South would have its turn after the Central’s tenure expires in 2031, followed by Delta North in 2039, could discourage serious opposition from those districts against another Central candidate in 2027.

These factors place Oborevwori in an advantageous position, although his eventual victory will depend on the electorate.

NDC’s Iyovwaye, who also hails from Okpe Local Government Area, is hoping to benefit from the growing national profile of Peter Obi and the party’s increasing visibility.

The NDC is gradually attracting political attention in Delta, with its mobilisation efforts making inroads into Delta Central and Delta North.

Iyovwaye also enjoys the backing of prominent political figures, including former Deputy President of the Senate, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, and former Speaker of the Delta State House of Assembly, Rt. Hon. Victor Ochei.

Both men are pursuing senatorial ambitions in Delta Central and Delta North respectively. Their political structures, established followership and grassroots networks could provide the NDC with a platform to expand its influence.

However, Iyovwaye’s prospects will depend on how effectively he can harness these alliances, strengthen the party’s structures and convert growing visibility into votes.

For ADC’s Great Ogboru, the 2027 contest represents another attempt to capture the state’s top political office.

Popularly known as the People’s General, Ogboru is one of Delta’s most familiar opposition figures. An indigene of Ethiope East Local Government Area, he has contested the governorship in successive election cycles since 2007 under different political platforms.

His political persistence and loyal followership remain important assets. His personal popularity also gives him an identity that transcends party affiliations.

However, the ADC is facing organisational challenges ahead of the election.

The Obedient Movement, which previously provided considerable support to the party, has shifted allegiance to the NDC, where Obi is pursuing his presidential ambition.

Leadership disputes and court cases surrounding the ADC’s national leadership have also raised questions about its internal stability.

At the grassroots, the party is yet to demonstrate a formidable presence across the state’s wards and local government areas.

Ogboru will therefore have to rely heavily on his personal political profile to overcome ADC’s structural weaknesses.

PDP’s Mrakpor, a former Attorney-General and Commissioner for Justice in the state, is seeking to revive the party’s fortunes after its major political setback.

His experience in public service and familiarity with Delta’s political landscape are among his strongest assets.

However, the defection of Oborevwori to the APC on April 28, 2025, dealt a major blow to the PDP, triggering a significant realignment of political forces.

The party has also been weakened by prolonged leadership disputes at the national level, internal divisions and multiple litigations, all of which have complicated efforts to rebuild its structures.

Nevertheless, the PDP retains a longstanding political identity and grassroots presence in Delta, having governed the state for several years.

Mrakpor hopes to leverage that legacy, his experience in government and the party’s remaining support base to mount a credible challenge.

With Oborevwori’s political coalition, zoning considerations and APC’s expanding structure, the governor appears to have the advantage. But the opposition candidates will be seeking to exploit any cracks in the ruling party’s alliance.

Big picture

Across the South-South, the 2027 governorship contests are shaping up as battles between incumbency and opposition mobilisation, established political structures and emerging alliances.

Eno, Otu and Oborevwori appear to enjoy varying degrees of political advantage, while Rivers presents a more complicated contest in which Wike’s influence and the political fallout from the Fubara crisis could prove decisive.

For the opposition, the challenge is to move beyond endorsements, political alliances and campaign rallies to establish effective grassroots structures capable of delivering votes.

Ultimately, political influence, money, party organisation, candidate credibility and the electorate’s assessment of government performance will determine who occupies the four Government Houses after the 2027 elections.

Egufe Yafugborhi, Ochuko Akuopha, Dan Abia, Chidi Ndaa, Ike Uchechukwu & Emmanuel Una also contributed to this report.

title: VIDEO: Putin’s nuclear briefcase caught on camera in China
description:
The nuclear briefcase of Russian President Vladimir Putin was spotted on camera in a rare appearance on Wednesday ahead of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen, China.
The summit marks a historic formal trilateral meeting to be held among Putin, his US counterpart Donald Trump an
content:
The nuclear briefcase of Russian President Vladimir Putin was spotted on camera in a rare appearance on Wednesday ahead of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen, China.

The summit marks a historic formal trilateral meeting to be held among Putin, his US counterpart Donald Trump and China’s Xi Jinping.

In footage released by Russian state TV and posted by CBS News on its Facebook page late Wednesday, a Russian journalist was seen approaching a Russian naval officer who confirmed the briefcase’s identity.

Before approaching the officer, the journalist said, while the camera was focused on the officer and some unknown men, “Look, that’s the famous nuclear briefcase right behind us.”

He then walked up to the officer and asked, “Hello, is this the nuclear briefcase you’ve got there?”

The officer replied, with a smile on his face, “Yes.”

In what looked like a further confirmation, the journalist queried further, “Yes? The one?”

“The one,” the officer affirmed, while walking in a direction that was not shown on camera.

Showing an element of surprise after the brief interview, the journalist said, “Unbelievable!”

Known as the “Cheget,” CBS News reports that the briefcase allows Putin to “maintain unbroken command and control over Russia’s nuclear arsenal at all times, regardless of his physical location.”

Fox News said the briefcase “reportedly travels with Putin at all times, but it’s rarely seen on camera,” while Al Jazeera stated that the briefcase can be used to “authorise a nuclear strike.”

Beijing has long maintained that the US and Russia should reduce their giant nuclear arsenals before it agrees to talks on its smaller stockpile, PUNCH Online reports Wednesday.

The report noted that the summit is expected to include discussions of the Iran war and nuclear disarmament, according to Washington, after a US-Russia bilateral treaty on atomic weapons expired in February.

Putin has been largely shunned by the West since his 2022 offensive in Ukraine began.

Earlier, the Russian leader informed the APEC gathering that what’s needed is “unity rather than division… and dialogue rather than ultimatums,” at a time when military and political tensions are “on the rise.”

Ukraine’s Foreign Minister Andriy Sybiga, speaking to reporters in Kyiv, said he hoped Xi and Trump would put “pressure on Russia to end the war.”

In his remarks, according to Chinese state news agency Xinhua. Xi told Trump that he looks forward to an “in-depth exchange of views with you on major issues concerning China-US relations, Asia-Pacific cooperation, and the global landscape, with the aim of advancing a constructive, strategically stable relationship between our two nations.”

title: Govt of the day serving interests of few – Ndume
description:
By Dickson Omobola



Senator representing Borno South Senatorial District, Ali Ndume, Wednesday, admitted being part of the country’s political failure, saying government of the day is a government of some people, by some people and for some people.



Ndume also lamented rising political violence
content:
By Dickson Omobola

Senator representing Borno South Senatorial District, Ali Ndume, Wednesday, admitted being part of the country’s political failure, saying government of the day is a government of some people, by some people and for some people.

Ndume also lamented rising political violence in the country, saying anyone found sponsoring such acts should be held responsible.

Speaking on Prime Time, an Arise Television programme, he expressed dissatisfaction with the manner in which public office holders were amassing wealth, saying many of them were gluttons.

He said: “I am part of the failure, I cannot deny that. I am not going to claim to be the best or better than anybody. But if I had known that this is how this politics is going to turn out to be, I wouldn’t have joined it. You can compare politics to AIDS. Once you catch it, you can’t say you don’t have AIDS. I’m telling you. It’s a dangerous game, especially in Nigeria. You can’t get cured.

“It’s true that government of the day has been a government of some people, by some people and for some people. If it were a government of all, this complaint and all that would not be happening. It did not start with this government. It started with the previous government. It has become a practice that you must be within the cycle. Even within the cycle, there are cabals running the government.”

On violence as a tool for political competition, he said: “In fact, that is why I am happy that everybody is concerned, so that we may nip it in the bud. My friend and colleague, Ningi, moved the motion after we spoke, and I seconded the motion. Then you can see how our colleagues showed concern, and Nigerians generally. It is one of the motions that was apolitical because the problem is like fire. If it catches, you don’t know when it will stop, and you may have a problem putting it off.

“It has also happened in a few countries where things got out of hand and, in extreme cases, reached a stage where the country’s government collapsed. You could see what happened in Bangladesh. Some years back, you could hear what happened in the Middle East.

“When people easily take the law into their own hands to express their hunger and use whatever is available that can be regarded as a weapon or tool, then it becomes a dangerous thing.”

title: Anchor  Borrowers Scheme: Reps divided over calls to write off farmers’ N1trn loans waiver
description:
By Gift ChapiOdekina



Abuja — A motion seeking the cancellation of outstanding loans obtained by farmers under various government-backed agricultural intervention programmes yesterday divided members of the House of Representatives.



Lawmakers disagreed over whether distressed farmers should be
content:
By Gift ChapiOdekina

Abuja — A motion seeking the cancellation of outstanding loans obtained by farmers under various government-backed agricultural intervention programmes yesterday divided members of the House of Representatives.

Lawmakers disagreed over whether distressed farmers should be granted debt relief or subjected to an investigation.

The motion, sponsored by Inuwa Garba, representing Yamaltu/Deba federal constituency of Gombe State, was predicated on the economic difficulties confronting farmers, particularly the impact of insecurity, climate change, natural disasters and other challenges that had disrupted agricultural production across the country.

The federal government had, in recent years, introduced several agricultural financing initiatives, including the Anchor Borrowers’ Programme, Commercial Agriculture Credit Scheme and NIRSAL-supported facilities, to boost food production, empower farmers and strengthen national food security.

Leading debate on the motion, Garba said insecurity, banditry, insurgency, farmer-herder clashes, flooding, drought and other environmental challenges had significantly undermined agricultural activities, resulting in crop failures, loss of investments and reduced farm incomes.

He argued that many beneficiaries of government-sponsored agricultural loans were unable to meet their repayment obligations, not because they were unwilling to repay, but because circumstances beyond their control had severely affected their productive capacity and financial stability.

According to him, continued accumulation and enforcement of outstanding debts, including principal, interest and penalties, can push already struggling farmers further into poverty, expose them to asset seizures and discourage participation in future agricultural activities.

However, opposing the proposed debt cancellation, Bamidele Salam, representing Ede South/Ede North/Ejigbo/Egbedore federal constituency of Osun State, questioned the justification for a blanket waiver, citing findings in the Auditor-General for the Federation’s report before the House.

Salam, who chairs the House Committee on Public Accounts, alleged that some beneficiaries of agricultural intervention loans running into over N1tn diverted the funds to businesses and personal investments.

unrelated to farming.

He said some beneficiaries who approached the Central Bank of Nigeria and commercial banks for agricultural loans allegedly channelled the funds into real estate acquisitions in Abuja, Lagos and even Dubai.

He also expressed concern over the state of the Bank of Agriculture which, he said, had been rendered virtually immobile by N795billion in loans owed by beneficiaries, many of whom allegedly diverted the funds.

Salam warned that approving a blanket waiver without establishing how the loans were utilised would set a dangerous precedent for future government intervention programmes.

He said: “If we come as a parliament and recommend a holistic waiving of all loans given out to persons who are purportedly to be farmers, we will be setting a very, very dangerous precedent for people to come, access government facilities, some of them interest-free, some of them single-digit interest, only for them to go and use those monies for other things.”

Similarly, Isiaka Ibrahim, a lawmaker from Ogun State, aligned with Salam’s position, alleging that some people had accessed government loans only to divert the funds to personal pursuits, including marrying additional wives.

He, however, acknowledged that a comprehensive investigation could identify genuine farmers whose businesses had been affected by economic hardship and who were consequently unable to repay their loans.

Also contributing, Paul Kalejaiye, an All Progressives Congress lawmaker from Lagos State, urged the House to exercise caution, stressing the need to investigate the utilisation of funds disbursed under the various agricultural intervention schemes before taking a decision on debt forgiveness.

Following the disagreement among lawmakers and their inability to reach a consensus, the House adjourned further consideration of the motion until Tuesday, November 24, for additional legislative scrutiny.

title: FAAC disburses N2.4trn to FG, states, LGs in October
description:
By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief   



ABUJA — THE Federation Account Allocation Committee, FAAC, yesterday, shared the sum of N2.441 trillion among the three tiers of government.



The amount was from the October 2026 Federation Account Revenue, which was shared at the FAAC meeting held in Abuja o
content:
By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief   

ABUJA — THE Federation Account Allocation Committee, FAAC, yesterday, shared the sum of N2.441 trillion among the three tiers of government.

The amount was from the October 2026 Federation Account Revenue, which was shared at the FAAC meeting held in Abuja on Wednesday.

The N2.441 trillion comprised distributable statutory revenue of N1.688 trillion and Value Added Tax (VAT) revenue of N752.488 billion.

A communiqué issued by the Federation Account Allocation Committee, FAAC, indicated that gross revenue of N3.811 trillion was available in the month of October 2026.

Total deduction for cost of collection was N128.797 billion while total transfers, refunds and savings stood at N1.241 trillion.

According to the communiqué sent by Director of Press of the Office of the Accountant-General of the Federation, Bawa Mokwa, gross statutory revenue of N2.999 trillion was received for the month of October 2026.

This was lower than the sum of N3.096 trillion received in the preceding month by N97.323 billion.

Gross revenue of N812.446 billion was available from the Value Added Tax (VAT) in October 2026. This was lower than the N816.872 billion available in the month of September 2026 by N4.426 billion.

The communiqué stated that from the N2.441 trillion total distributable revenue, the Federal Government received a total sum of N856.065 billion and the state governments received a total sum of N809.909 billion.

The Local Government Councils received N568.701 billion, while the sum of N206.384 billion (13% of mineral revenue) was shared to the benefiting State as derivation revenue.

On the N1.688 trillion distributable statutory revenue, the Federal Government received N780.816 billion and the State Governments received N396.040 billion.

The Local Government Councils received N305.331 billion and the sum of N206.384 billion (13% of mineral revenue) was shared to the benefiting States as derivation revenue.

From the N752.488 billion distributable Value Added Tax (VAT) revenue, the Federal Government received N75.249 billion, the State Governments received N413.868 billion and the Local Government Councils received N263.371 billion.

In October 2026, Excise Duty and CET Levies increased marginally, while Petroleum Profit Tax (PPT), Hydrocarbon Tax (HT), Petroleum Royalties, Import Duty, Companies Income Tax (CIT), CGT & SDT, Value Added Tax (VTA), Mineral Royalties, and Gas Flared Penalty, Rental Gas Flared Fee and Misc. Oil Revenue all decreased.

title: State police on verge of reality; operational guidelines bill submitted to Justice Ministry
description:
By Henry Umoru & Johnbosco Agbakwuru



ABUJA — Operation of State police in Nigeria is at the verge of being realised. The National Assembly yesterday transmitted the bill ratified by the 36 state houses of Assembly to President Bola Tinubu yesterday for assent. The lawmakers asked the president to
content:
By Henry Umoru & Johnbosco Agbakwuru

ABUJA — Operation of State police in Nigeria is at the verge of being realised. The National Assembly yesterday transmitted the bill ratified by the 36 state houses of Assembly to President Bola Tinubu yesterday for assent. The lawmakers asked the president to send a bill on the operational guidelines for state police for passage.

Chief of Staff to president, Femi Gbajabiamila disclosed yesterday that the operational guidelines bill has been forwarded to the Ministry of Justice for validation.

To quicken the process, the Senate asked President Tinubu to forward to the National Assembly the National Policing Bill which would provide for the operationlisation of state police across the 36 states of the federation for legislative scrutiny and expeditious passage.

It also mandated the clerk to the National Assembly, CNA, Kamoru Ogunlana to transmit the constitutional amendment bill that seeks to establish State Police Services in Nigeria to the President for assent, having satisfied all the constitutional requirements, in line with the Acts Authentication Act, 2004.

President Tinubu, however, received the State Police Bill later yesterday, with the Chief of Staff to the President, Mr, Femi Gbajabiamila, saying the bill requested by the Senate had been submitted to the Federal Ministry of Justice for legislative drafting validation.

According to him, upon receipt of the validated version, the President Working Group, which he chairs, will review and present it, alongside its report to the President for consideration.

Resolutions of the Senate were sequel to a motion, titled “Passage of Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria (Sixth Alteration) Bill, 2026 and sponsored by the Senate Leader, Senator Opeyemi Bamidele.

Bamidele, who urged the President to forward to the Senate expeditiously the National Policing Bill, said in his presentation: “The Senate: Recall that pursuant to Section 9(1) of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999, the National Assembly processed an Executive Bill seeking to alter the provisions of the Constitution to establish State Police as part of the national policing structure.

“Also recall that the Senate and the House of Representatives on June 24 and July, 23, 2026, respectively, overwhelmingly supported the bill with over 2/3 majority votes, thereby meeting the constitutional threshold for the passage of the bill by the National Assembly;

“Aware that the National Assembly transmitted the bill to the 36 State Houses of Assembly for the mandatory approval by resolution of not less than 2/3 majority of the State Houses of Assembly as provided by Section 9(2) of the Constitution before the Bill can be passed;

The states…

“Also aware that the 36 State Houses of Assembly have transmitted their resolution of the bill to the National Assembly, namely Abia, Adamawa, Anambra, Akwa-Ibom, Bauchi, Bayelsa, Benue, Borno, Cross-River, Delta, Ebonyi, Edo, Ekiti, Enugu, Gombe, Imo, Jigawa, Kaduna, Kano, Katsina, Kebbi, Kogi, Kwara, Lagos, Nasarawa, Niger, Ogun, Ondo, Osun, Oyo, Plateau, Rivers, Sokoto, Taraba, Yobe and Zamfara;

“Convinced that the bill has fulfilled the conditions set out in Sections 9(1) and (2) of the Constitution for a Constitutional amendment of this nature to be passed.”

Speaking further, he said the prayers in the motion were to “mandate the Clerk to the National Assembly, to transmit “A Bill for an Act to Alter the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria 1999, to Provide for the Establishment of State Police Services, and for Related Matters (Sixth Alteration) 2026, to the president for his assent, in line with the Acts Authentication Act, 2004;

“We thank Mr. President for taking ownership and boldly supporting the bill throughout the process; and also urge him to forward the National Policing Bill that will enable the operationalisation of subnational policing, for legislative scrutiny and expeditious passage by the National Assembly,”

The Senate, accordingly, adopted the prayers and congratulated itself and the National Assembly for the historic feat on the State Police Bill .

The State Police Bill is a bill for an Act to alter the 1999 Constitution to provide for the establishment of State Police Services, and for Related Matters (Sixth Alteration) 2026.

The bill, titled “A Bill for an Act to Alter the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 to Provide for the Establishment of State Police Services and for Related Matters,” seeks to create the constitutional framework for the establishment of state police across the federation.

In his remarks, President of the Senate, Godswill Akpabio, said the executive was expected to send the modalities for the implementation of State Police Services to the National Assembly because they do not want to give unnecessary timelines, but noted that time was of the essence.

Akpabio, who noted that establishment of state police would solve the problem of insecurity in the country by 70%, said: “ This is a legislation that will not be forgotten . It is a major achievement of the 10th National Assembly .

“The next step is to address the operationalisation of the system and ensure that there is no conflict between the state police and the federal police .”

Recall that the presidency had couple of weeks ago, engaged critical stakeholders in the polity on National Policing Bill which it intended to forward to National Assembly for consideration and enactment of laws that would guide operations of policing in the country .

In his remarks after the adoption of the prayers, Deputy President of the Senate, Barau Jibrin, who commended President Tinubu and legislators at both the federal and state levels for making state police a reality, said: “I wish to express my profound appreciation to every member of the committee on the review of the constitution under my chairmanship, other members of the Senate and, indeed, all members of the National Assembly for their invaluable contributions to the legislative process that has brought us to this historic moment in our collective pursuit of the establishment of State Police in Nigeria. We have all played a part in making this history.

“This is a remarkable achievement for the present administration and the current National Assembly. As we all know, the issue of state police has been under consideration in Nigeria for a very long time. ‘’Successive governments and administrations have engaged in discussions and explored various options towards establishing this system in our country,” he said.

Jibrin, who is the Chairman, Senate Committee on Constitution Review, said further: “However, despite these efforts, the process encountered several setbacks until the emergence of this administration.

‘’We must, therefore, acknowledge and commend the unwavering commitment of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu to ensuring the passage of this bill and the integration of state police into our country’s policing architecture.

“This is, indeed, a significant milestone, and we thank Almighty God for allowing us to be part of a historic process that will form an important part of the legacy we are leaving for our nation.

“It is against this background that I strongly support the motion and urge this distinguished Senate to pass it without delay. All the necessary legislative processes have been undertaken and concluded. The remaining step is to transmit the bill to Mr President for his assent.

“This is a collective achievement that deserves to be celebrated. The proposed state police system is designed to complement the operations of the Nigeria Police Force, strengthen our overall policing structure and enhance our capacity to address security challenges across the country.’’

Tinubu receives state police bill for assent

Meanwhile, President Tinubu yesterday received the Constitution (Sixth Alteration) Bill, which seeks to establish State Police in Nigeria.

The bill was formally transmitted to him by his Special Advisers on Senate and House of Representatives Matters, Senator Basheer Lado and Dr. Wasiu Olanrewaju-Smart.

The Chief of Staff to the President and Chairman, Presidential Working Group on State Police, Femi Gbajabiamila, disclosed this in a statement

”All 36 State Houses of Assembly have approved the bill, exceeding the constitutional requirement of at least 24 states, representing two-thirds of the 36 states, as stipulated in Section 9(2) of the Constitution,” the statement read.

It stated further that President Tinubu would review the Constitution Alteration Bill in consultation with the Attorney-General of the Federation, AGF.

”He will assent to the bill at a formal signing ceremony,” the statement added.

Gbajabiamila said the Presidential Working Group on State Police, which he chairs, with the support of the Policy Advisory Committee, had undertaken extensive stakeholder engagement and nationwide consultations towards developing a draft National Policing Bill.

”The draft bill has been submitted to the Federal Ministry of Justice for legislative drafting validation. Upon receipt of the validated version, the Working Group will review it and present it, alongside its report, to Mr President for consideration.

”President Tinubu expresses his appreciation to the President of the Senate, speaker of the House of Representatives, members of the National Assembly, the Clerk to the National Assembly, the 36 state governors, the State Houses of Assembly, and all Nigerians who have demonstrated a shared commitment to addressing the nation’s security challenges,’’ Gbajabiamila said.

title: Group urges ECOWAS court to deliver ruling on detained activist
description: The Take It Back Movement Nigeria, Delta State Chapter, has urged the President of the Community Court of Justice of the Economic Community of West African States to give administrative attention to an outstanding ruling on an application for interim measures filed by detained activist, Ighorhiohwun
content:
The Take It Back Movement Nigeria, Delta State Chapter, has urged the President of the Community Court of Justice of the Economic Community of West African States to give administrative attention to an outstanding ruling on an application for interim measures filed by detained activist, Ighorhiohwunu Aghogho.

The group said the ruling in Suit No. ECW/CCJ/APP/28/25, instituted by Aghogho against the Federal Republic of Nigeria, had remained pending for about nine months after the application was adjourned for ruling on January 29, 2026.

In a letter dated November 16, 2026, and addressed to the ECOWAS Court President in Abuja, the organisation expressed concern over the delay, noting that Aghogho had reportedly remained in detention at the Nigerian Correctional Service’s Warri Custodial Centre, Okere-Warri, Delta State, since June 16, 2025.

The letter, signed by the group’s state coordinator, Ochuko Etu, and state secretary, Efafe Okemute, noted the prolonged detention and the outstanding application for interim protection, raising concerns about the urgency of the relief sought and the effectiveness of interim judicial protection.

It stated, “Interim measures serve an important protective purpose. They are intended to preserve the rights of parties, prevent irreparable harm and safeguard the effectiveness of judicial proceedings pending the final determination of substantive claims.”

The organisation acknowledged that filing an application for interim measures did not automatically entitle an applicant to the relief sought but maintained that such applications required timely judicial consideration, particularly where the alleged circumstances giving rise to the request for protection were continuing.

It said, “The purpose of such an application underscores the importance of timely judicial consideration, particularly where delay may affect the practical value of the protection being requested.”

The group, however, stressed that its letter was not intended to interfere with the court’s independence or impartiality or influence the outcome of the pending application.

It said it was not a party to the suit and was neither seeking to intervene in the proceedings nor introduce additional evidence or legal arguments.

“Our intervention is, therefore, strictly limited to an institutional expression of concern and a respectful request for administrative attention to the status and timely communication of the outstanding ruling,” the letter stated.

Citing Articles 79 and 80 of the ECOWAS Court’s Rules of Procedure, alongside the applicable Instructions to the Chief Registrar, the organisation said the procedural framework provided arrangements for handling applications for interim measures, including their submission for the President’s consideration and prioritisation of translation where necessary.

It urged the court president to determine whether any administrative or procedural issues caused the delay and, where appropriate, facilitate the delivery and formal communication of the ruling.

The group also requested that if the ruling had already been delivered, information on its status should be communicated through the court’s recognised channels.

It further asked that any additional procedural steps required from the parties be promptly communicated to them.

The organisation said its appeal was motivated by the need to strengthen public confidence in judicial institutions, adding that the credibility of the judiciary depended not only on the independence and fairness of its decisions but also on the timely administration of justice.

It added that it acted in good faith and in the public interest, without prejudice to the rights of either party or the merits of the substantive proceedings.

title: Pinheiro unveils six books on key areas of Nigerian law
description:
After nearly four decades in legal practice, Senior Advocate of Nigeria, Dr ‘Kemi Pinheiro, will on Friday, November 20, 2026, unveil six books examining different aspects of Nigerian law and documenting his professional experiences.
The presentation, organised by Pinheiro LP, will be chaired by the
content:
After nearly four decades in legal practice, Senior Advocate of Nigeria, Dr ‘Kemi Pinheiro, will on Friday, November 20, 2026, unveil six books examining different aspects of Nigerian law and documenting his professional experiences.

The presentation, organised by Pinheiro LP, will be chaired by the Chief Justice of Nigeria, Justice Kudirat Motonmori Olatokunbo Kekere-Ekun, and is expected to attract members of the judiciary, the Bar, academia and other stakeholders in the justice sector.

The six publications are “Strategies in Criminal Trial: A Practitioner’s Guide”; “Insolvency Law in Nigeria: Practice and Procedure”; “Arbitration Law and Practice in Nigeria; Defining Moments: Chronicles of a Silk (Volume One)”; “The Compendium; and MULAN Legal: Trending Issues of Law and Faith – Essays in Honour of ‘Kemi Pinheiro, SAN”.

The books cover criminal litigation, corporate insolvency, arbitration, legal practice, professional experiences and the intersection of law and faith.

In Defining Moments: Chronicles of a Silk (Volume One), Pinheiro documents aspects of his professional journey, reflecting on experiences and defining moments from nearly four decades at the Bar.

His Strategies in Criminal Trial: A Practitioner’s Guide examines the practical demands of criminal litigation, including procedural and evidential issues confronting legal practitioners. It also addresses the treatment and admissibility of electronic evidence in criminal proceedings.

The publication on insolvency, Insolvency Law in Nigeria: Practice and Procedure, examines the legal framework for corporate rescue, restructuring and insolvency under the Companies and Allied Matters Act 2020.

Similarly, Arbitration Law and Practice in Nigeria explores the country’s arbitration framework under the Arbitration and Mediation Act 2023, with particular attention to enforcing arbitral awards and the growing role of alternative dispute resolution in commercial disputes.

The collection also features contributions from other legal practitioners and academics.

The Compendium brings together scholarly essays examining various legal issues and developments, while MULAN Legal: Trending Issues of Law and Faith – Essays in Honour of ‘Kemi Pinheiro, SAN explores the relationship between law, faith and Nigeria’s plural legal system.

Together, the publications combine practical legal guidance, academic contributions and personal reflections on the legal profession.

The presentation is expected to give members of the judiciary, legal practitioners, academics and other stakeholders an opportunity to engage with the legal issues addressed in the books.

title: ICYMI: US strategist denies $4.5m payment for Tinubu interview
description:
American political strategist and media personality, Diana London, has denied receiving $4.5m from the Nigerian government or anyone else in the country, following controversy over her interview with President Bola Tinubu.
London, who is the Chief Executive Officer of London Global Strategies, said
content:
American political strategist and media personality, Diana London, has denied receiving $4.5m from the Nigerian government or anyone else in the country, following controversy over her interview with President Bola Tinubu.

London, who is the Chief Executive Officer of London Global Strategies, said she travelled to Nigeria to interview Tinubu for parts of a documentary and to see the country herself.

In a post on her X account on Wednesday, she described the allegation as a smear campaign and insisted that neither the Nigerian government nor any other individual in the country paid her $4.5m.

“I unequivocally deny the claim that Nigeria’s government nor anyone else in Nigeria paid me $4.5 million. I went to Nigeria to interview President Tinubu @officialABAT for parts of a documentary and see Nigeria for myself.

“This SMEAR CAMPAIGN can make noise, but can’t change the facts or stop me from speaking the truth,” she wrote.

Her response comes amid public criticism following her interview with Tinubu at the Presidential Villa, Abuja, on Tuesday.

The controversy intensified after London deleted earlier posts in which she praised the security partnership between Nigeria and the United States and described Nigeria as America’s greatest ally in Africa.

She subsequently restricted access to the comment section of her X account, limiting responses to selected users.

PUNCH had earlier reported that the development followed a report by Peoples Gazette alleging that London received $4.5m for the assignment.

However, details in documents filed under the United States Foreign Agents Registration Act showed that London Global Strategies received payments of 375,000 from DCI Group, a US-based lobbying firm engaged by the Nigerian government through Aster Legal.

The payments were described as retainers for services rendered under the lobbying arrangement.

London has now expressly denied receiving the $4.5m from Nigeria, while maintaining that her visit was for a documentary interview.

The interview has also raised questions about the relationship between her media engagement and her company’s involvement in the lobbying arrangement.

Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar had called on the Presidency to publish the lobbying contract, disclose the payments and invoices, and release the full, unedited recording of Tinubu’s interview.

He also asked the Presidency to clarify whether the interview formed part of the $4.5m lobbying arrangement.

The Presidency had yet to publicly clarify the relationship between the interview and the lobbying contract as of the time of filing this report.

The post ICYMI: US strategist denies $4.5m payment for Tinubu interview appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: US Democrats nominate Jeffries to be first Black House speaker
description:
Hakeem Jeffries is on the cusp of becoming the first Black speaker of the US House of Representatives after Democrats elected him their leader Wednesday following a sweeping midterm election triumph.



The 56-year-old New Yorker secured 251 votes in a closed-door, secret ballot, with 11 cast agains
content:
Hakeem Jeffries is on the cusp of becoming the first Black speaker of the US House of Representatives after Democrats elected him their leader Wednesday following a sweeping midterm election triumph.

The 56-year-old New Yorker secured 251 votes in a closed-door, secret ballot, with 11 cast against his nomination, according to US media.

Jeffries faced no declared challenger, although opposition from some newly elected progressives had exposed divisions over how Democrats should wield their newfound power.

His nomination puts him on course to preside over a commanding Democratic majority during the final two years of President Donald Trump’s term, as his party prepares to reverse Republican policies and investigate the administration.

Jeffries must still win a formal vote of the full House when the new Congress convenes on January 3, when he would become the first Black politician to hold the powerful post. With a large Democratic majority, this is seen as something of a formality.

Both returning Democrats and incoming lawmakers participated in Wednesday’s election, including progressives who had sought concessions on issues ranging from US military support for Israel to the influence of money in politics.

Jeffries had requested a recorded vote rather than a nomination “by acclamation” — without a formal ballot — as some allies had hoped.

He argued that every Democrat should have an opportunity to weigh his experience, record and vision, citing the precedent set when the party last took control of the House in 2018.

The ballot remained secret, with the overall tally made public but individual votes kept anonymous.

Ahead of the election, Jeffries met progressive lawmakers to discuss issues including Israel and healthcare, with proposals to lower the Medicare eligibility age and expand coverage among the topics discussed.

The Democratic leader has also sought to shift attention to the party’s plans for governing after voters handed Republicans a crushing defeat amid anger over the Iran war and soaring fuel costs.

“Folks are drowning in this Republican economy, and House Democrats are committed to turning that situation around, beginning on day one,” he told reporters Tuesday.

“We’re going to relentlessly fight for an affordable America.”

– Brooklyn roots –

Raised in Brooklyn’s working-class Crown Heights neighborhood, Jeffries trained as a lawyer before entering the New York state legislature in 2007 and winning election to Congress in 2012.

Known for his measured manner, sharp rhetoric and penchant for quoting hip-hop artists, he became the first Black politician to lead a party in either chamber of Congress when Democrats chose him to succeed Nancy Pelosi in 2022.

He also served as a House prosecutor during Trump’s first impeachment trial in 2020.

As speaker, Jeffries would preside over one of Washington’s most powerful institutions and stand second in line to the presidency behind the vice president.

But he would face a formidable task in managing a Democratic coalition spanning centrists and an increasingly assertive left flank.

His party has promised investigations into Trump and his administration, while lawmakers remain divided over Israel, healthcare and how aggressively to pursue their agenda against a president who retains veto power.

Jeffries’s nomination contrasts with a more competitive leadership contest among Senate Democrats, where veteran party chief Chuck Schumer faces a challenge from progressive Maryland Senator Chris Van Hollen.

Van Hollen has attracted support from prominent left-wing figures, including Bernie Sanders, but acknowledges he is the underdog. Senate Democrats will elect their leader in early December.

Republicans chose their own congressional leaders last week, elevating Trump ally Jim Jordan in the House and retaining John Thune in the Senate.

title: SIFAX boss advocates adequate storage to boost food production
description:
By Kafayat Kokumo



Chairman of SIFAX Group, Dr Taiwo Afolabi, has called for adequate infrastructure for storage and distribution in order to increase the economic benefits of increased food production.



He made this call at the 2026 Annual Strategy Retreat of the Odu’a Investment Company Limite
content:
By Kafayat Kokumo

Chairman of SIFAX Group, Dr Taiwo Afolabi, has called for adequate infrastructure for storage and distribution in order to increase the economic benefits of increased food production.


He made this call at the 2026 Annual Strategy Retreat of the Odu’a Investment Company Limited held at the International Institute of Tropical Agriculture (IITA), Ibadan.


Represented by the Deputy Director, Strategy and Operations, Oliver Omajuwa, SIFAX Group, Afolabi said that investments in agricultural logistics were critical to connecting production centres with processing facilities, retail markets and export channels.
He said: “Increased production would yield limited economic benefits without adequate infrastructure for aggregation, preservation, storage and distribution.


“Cold rooms, temperature-controlled transportation and strategically located warehouses are critical investments capable of connecting agricultural production to processing facilities, retail markets and export channels.”


The SIFAX boss identified warehousing, transportation, agricultural aggregation, cold-chain services, technology and specialised logistics as viable investment opportunities, urging investors to identify gaps across the value chain before committing resources.
He also advised Odu’a Investment Company Limited to assess the transportation, storage and distribution needs of its portfolio companies, noting that their combined requirements could provide a foundation for a shared logistics platform.


On port logistics, Afolabi said investment opportunities extended beyond terminal operations to cargo handling, freight forwarding, customs clearing, equipment maintenance, storage and export consolidation.
He said: “Integrating these services would improve cargo movement, reduce operational complexities and enable customers to access multiple logistics solutions without engaging several service providers.”
He further urged investors to explore greenfield developments, acquisitions and strategic partnerships with established operators, depending on their financial capacity, technical expertise and market opportunities.
Afolabi also highlighted the importance of technology-driven solutions, including cargo tracking, inventory management and operational monitoring systems, in improving efficiency, visibility and service delivery across the logistics value chain.
However, he cautioned investors against making decisions based primarily on asset ownership, stressing that acquiring trucks, constructing warehouses or purchasing equipment did not automatically guarantee profitability.

title: Unilorin student seeks N43m for kidney transplant
description:
… Family spends over N20m, sells property to sustain treatmentBy Chioma Obinna



The family of Olajide Victor, a 200-level student of the University of Ilorin, Kwara State, has appealed for N43 million to fund a kidney transplant for him after he was diagnosed with Stage V end-stage renal disease.
content:
… Family spends over N20m, sells property to sustain treatment
By Chioma Obinna

The family of Olajide Victor, a 200-level student of the University of Ilorin, Kwara State, has appealed for N43 million to fund a kidney transplant for him after he was diagnosed with Stage V end-stage renal disease.


Victor is expected to undergo the life-saving procedure at Newhaven Specialist Hospital, Lagos, as his family struggles to meet the cost of his treatment.


He said his health challenges began in November 2025 after he sustained a minor fracture in his left leg while playing football at the university’s sports complex. Weeks later, his face and legs became swollen, prompting medical examinations.


Following several tests, including kidney function investigations, he was diagnosed with Stage V kidney disease at Taiwo Hospital, Ilorin.


A medical report signed by Dr S. Alagbe, Consultant Nephrologist, indicated that Victor requires continued haemodialysis twice weekly.


His mother, Comfort Adesanya, said the family had spent over N20 million on his treatment and sold their land, house and other valuables to keep him alive.


She appealed to individuals, corporate organisations and well-meaning Nigerians to help raise the N43 million required for the transplant, saying the family could no longer cope with the rising cost of treatment.


Donations can be made to Victor Adekunle Olajide, UBA, Account Number: 2458216260 or call Victor on 09018866426.

title: Food security: Nigerian farmers risk wasting billions on fertilisers without soil testing, experts warn
description:
By Adeola Badru & Cynthia Alo



Nigeria’s quest for food security may continue to suffer setbacks unless farmers move away from indiscriminate fertiliser application and embrace soil testing and crop-specific nutrient management, agricultural experts have warned.







The experts, who spoke at th
content:
By Adeola Badru & Cynthia Alo

Nigeria’s quest for food security may continue to suffer setbacks unless farmers move away from indiscriminate fertiliser application and embrace soil testing and crop-specific nutrient management, agricultural experts have warned.

The experts, who spoke at the 2026 South-West Nigeria Fertiliser and Soil Health Summit in Ibadan, Oyo State, cautioned that increasing fertiliser consumption without understanding the specific nutrient requirements of farmland could undermine agricultural productivity, weaken farmers’ incomes and worsen soil degradation.

They argued that the country’s approach to fertiliser management must go beyond distributing inputs to farmers and focus on ensuring that the right fertiliser is applied to the right soil, for the right crop and at the appropriate time.

The position formed a major highlight of the communiqué issued at the end of the summit, organised by the Institute of Agricultural Research and Training (IAR&T), Obafemi Awolowo University, Moor Plantation, Ibadan, on Tuesday.

With the theme, “Fertilisers and Food Security in South-West Nigeria: The Journey So Far,” the summit brought together more than 150 scientists, farmers, policymakers, fertiliser manufacturers and distributors, agricultural extension professionals and development partners to examine the challenges confronting fertiliser utilisation and soil health in the region.

The participants expressed concern that the continued reliance on blanket fertiliser recommendations failed to address significant differences in soil fertility, acidity, phosphorus fixation, nutrient depletion and other soil-related challenges across different agroecological zones.

According to the communiqué, “The predominance of blanket fertiliser recommendations does not adequately address the variations in soil fertility, soil acidity, phosphorus fixation, nutrient depletion and other soil constraints across different agroecological zones in the region.”

The experts maintained that fertiliser recommendations should increasingly be based on soil testing, crop requirements, prevailing agroecological conditions and economically viable nutrient management practices.

They also identified high fertiliser prices, inadequate distribution networks, limited access to credit and inconsistent availability as major constraints preventing smallholder farmers from accessing and effectively utilising the agricultural input.

The summit further warned that declining soil organic matter, nutrient imbalance, erosion and other forms of soil degradation continued to undermine fertiliser-use efficiency and agricultural productivity.

To address the situation, it called on research institutions to strengthen soil fertility mapping and develop crop-, soil- and location-specific fertiliser recommendations for major crops cultivated across South-West Nigeria.

It also urged governments and relevant agricultural institutions to facilitate affordable and accessible soil testing services to enable farmers to understand the condition of their farmland before applying fertilisers.

The participants advocated integrated soil fertility management, involving the combination of mineral fertilisers with organic resources, crop residues, compost, animal manure and biological inputs, as a more sustainable approach to improving soil health and agricultural productivity.

The summit also called for stronger collaboration between fertiliser manufacturers and research institutions to develop formulations capable of addressing specific soil deficiencies, including phosphorus fixation and shortages of secondary and micronutrients.

On the impact of climate change, the experts noted that irregular rainfall patterns and increasing incidences of drought required farmers to adopt climate-smart fertiliser management strategies.

They recommended that fertiliser application guidelines should take rainfall variability, planting dates, crop water requirements and appropriate application methods into consideration.

The communiqué also raised concerns over the circulation of adulterated and substandard fertiliser products, calling on regulatory institutions to intensify inspections, product certification, market surveillance and enforcement of existing standards.

It further recommended greater investment in digital soil maps, fertiliser recommendation platforms, mobile advisory services and precision nutrient management technologies to improve fertiliser distribution, application and monitoring.

The summit stressed that sustainable fertiliser management should not be measured solely by increased crop yields but should also take account of environmental protection, farmers’ economic returns and the long-term preservation of soil health.

It called for a coordinated monitoring framework to assess the impact of fertiliser interventions on crop productivity, farmers’ income, fertiliser-use efficiency and soil health.

The summit acknowledged previous interventions by regional governments, research institutions and development partners to strengthen fertiliser and soil health systems but maintained that significant gaps remained in ensuring that fertilisers were affordable, accessible, appropriate, balanced and efficiently utilised.

It warned that increased fertiliser use alone could not guarantee food security, insisting that sustainable agricultural production required sound soil health management, scientifically informed recommendations, effective extension services, quality assurance and supportive government policies.

Earlier in his address, the chairman of the occasion and the Vice-Chancellor of Obafemi Awolowo University, Ile-Ife, Prof. Simeon Bamire, who was represented by the Dean of the Faculty of Agriculture, Prof. A.O. Ajayi, emphasised the need to redirect attention from fertiliser distribution to fertiliser-use efficiency, describing it as a critical pathway to achieving food security.

In his remarks, the Director of IAR&T, Prof. Gabriel Oluwatosin, noted that one of the key resolutions reached at the summit was the need to organise zonal fertiliser summits across the country, adding that without proper soil health management and fertilizer use, as the population is growing, farmers would not be able to secure their food food security.
