title: State police won’t be used to hound political opponents –C’River govt
description:
From Aniekan Aniekan, Calabar
The Cross River State Government has moved to allay fears that governors could turn state police into instruments of political repression, declaring that the proposed security outfit would not be used to intimidate opposition politicians or settle political scores.
Comm
content:
From Aniekan Aniekan, Calabar

The Cross River State Government has moved to allay fears that governors could turn state police into instruments of political repression, declaring that the proposed security outfit would not be used to intimidate opposition politicians or settle political scores.

Commissioner for Information and Orientation, Ekpenyong Cobham, dismissed concerns over possible abuse of state police powers, insisting that worsening insecurity demanded decentralised policing and that the state’s experience with its Homeland Security Services had demonstrated the benefits of locally managed security operations.

Cobham maintained that the protection of lives and property must take precedence over fears of political interference, arguing that the establishment of state police would strengthen security operations by bringing law enforcement closer to communities.

He cited the state’s existing Homeland Security Services as evidence that a locally managed security outfit could operate without being deployed against political opponents.

“Cross River State already has a security system, which is the Homeland Security Services. From it, we have so far gathered the requisite experience in running a localised security apparatus,” he said.

The commissioner explained that the proposed state police system would require appropriate legislation and administrative structures before becoming operational, adding that states would need to establish recruitment procedures and provide adequate training for personnel.

According to him, each state would be expected to domesticate the relevant legislation through its House of Assembly, establish the necessary administrative framework and recruit qualified personnel for training at new or existing police facilities.

Cobham expressed confidence in Cross River’s preparedness, suggesting that the Attorney-General and Commissioner for Justice might already be considering the legal and administrative requirements for establishing the proposed police service.

He argued that decentralised policing would improve intelligence gathering and response to security threats because officers familiar with the language, culture and terrain of their communities would be better positioned to identify criminal activities and respond promptly.

Citing Calabar South, where he resides, Cobham said the area had become considerably more peaceful following the deployment of Homeland Security personnel, despite its previous reputation for insecurity.

He maintained that the experience demonstrated the advantages of community-based security arrangements and the need to strengthen local capacity to protect residents.

The commissioner insisted that the growing security challenges confronting the country made the establishment of state police imperative, stressing that concerns about possible political interference should not overshadow the need for effective policing.

His assurance comes amid renewed debate over the potential abuse of state police by governors, particularly fears that locally controlled security personnel could be deployed to intimidate opposition politicians, restrict political activities or settle political disputes.

The Senate has consequently demanded a comprehensive operational law to define the powers and responsibilities of federal and state police authorities and establish safeguards against jurisdictional conflicts.

Senate President Godswill Akpabio, while commenting on the proposed policing arrangement, stressed the importance of preventing operational clashes between the two security structures.

“The next step is to address the operationalisation of the system and ensure that there is no conflict between the State Police and the Federal Police,” Akpabio said.

The demand followed the approval of the Constitution (Sixth Alteration) Bill, 2026, by all 36 state Houses of Assembly and its transmission to President Bola Tinubu for assent.

The proposed National Policing Bill, which is expected to provide the legal and administrative framework for the decentralised policing system, is undergoing executive consideration.

title: Tinubu unveils first University of Public Relations and Leadership
description:
From Juliana Taiwo-Obalonye, Abuja
President Bola Tinubu has unveiled Nigeria’s first University of Public Relations and Leadership, approving the specialised institution to advance professional training, research and leadership development amid growing concerns over misinformation, disinformation a
content:
From Juliana Taiwo-Obalonye, Abuja

President Bola Tinubu has unveiled Nigeria’s first University of Public Relations and Leadership, approving the specialised institution to advance professional training, research and leadership development amid growing concerns over misinformation, disinformation and declining public trust.

Tinubu, represented by Vice-President Kashim Shettima at the opening of the 38th World Public Relations Forum (WPRF) and fifth African Public Relations Association Conference in Abuja on Wednesday, said the institution would equip communication professionals to confront the challenges of artificial intelligence and rapidly changing digital technologies.

Tinubu described the university, located in Nasarawa State, as a lasting legacy of Nigeria’s hosting of the global forum and an investment in the future of responsible communication.

“I am pleased to formally approve and support the establishment of the University of Public Relations and Leadership, a pioneering initiative designed to advance specialised education, research, professional development and leadership training in public relations, strategic communications and related disciplines.”

He commended the Nigerian Institute of Public Relations (NIPR), Federal Ministry of Information and National Orientation and Nasarawa State Government for collaborating on the initiative, particularly acknowledging Governor Abdullahi Sule’s commitment to the project.

Speaking on the forum’s theme, “Responsible Communication: The Voice of the World,” Tinubu challenged practitioners to move beyond image and reputation management to promote truth, accountability, transparency and constructive engagement between governments and citizens.

He said responsible communication was essential to democratic governance, economic development and public confidence in institutions, urging practitioners to uphold the highest ethical and professional standards.

The President also highlighted Nigeria’s economic and demographic potential, projecting that its population would reach 440 million by 2050, making it the world’s third most populous country.

He said six of Africa’s 10 unicorn companies were Nigerian, citing Flutterwave, OPay, Interswitch, Andela, Moniepoint and Moove as examples of the country’s growing technology ecosystem.

Tinubu urged international delegates to explore investment opportunities in Nigeria’s technology, creative industries, tourism and other sectors.

“Nigeria welcomes you. Nigeria is open for partnership, and Nigeria is ready to engage with the world,” he said.

Kenyan President William Ruto, represented at the forum, urged African governments to make communication central to policymaking, warning that public trust could not be manufactured through publicity but must be earned through honesty, transparency and accountability.

He disclosed that Kenya adopted a National Communication Policy in August 2026 to ensure that government institutions provided citizens with timely, accurate and accessible information.

Minister of Information and National Orientation, Mohammed Idris, called for stronger professional ethics and international cooperation against misinformation, warning that the misuse of digital platforms could deepen divisions and threaten security.

“Our communication should build bridges, not walls,” he said, urging governments to communicate openly, journalists to uphold professional standards and public relations practitioners to embrace transparency.

NIPR President, Ike Neliaku, disclosed that 2,837 delegates had attended the forum as of yesterday, describing it as the largest gathering in the event’s history.

He said the conference would address professional development, youth participation, women’s leadership, community relations and peacebuilding, alongside a cultural festival and a social responsibility initiative to feed 10,000 people.

“Public relations is not propaganda. Public relations is a business of trust,” Neliaku declared.

President of the Global Alliance for Public Relations and Communication Management, Justin Green, commended Nigeria for securing the hosting rights, saying the country’s determination had attracted delegates from 126 countries.

Green also described the University of Public Relations and Leadership as the world’s first university dedicated to the profession and praised the Nasarawa State Government for supporting the initiative.

African Public Relations Association President, Arik Karani, commended Nigeria’s leadership in professional regulation, noting that its public relations legislation had provided a model for other African countries.

“Nigeria is the table when we are discussing public relations,” he said, urging Africa to take a more active role in shaping global communication standards.

The post Tinubu unveils first University of Public Relations and Leadership appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Kogi youths demand power shift
description:
From Romanus Ugwu, Abuja
A coalition of youths drawn from Kogi State’s three senatorial districts has rejected Governor Usman Ododo’s bid for a second term in the 2027 governorship election, warning that his re-election would extend the hold of one zone on the governorship to 16 consecutive years, c
content:
From Romanus Ugwu, Abuja

A coalition of youths drawn from Kogi State’s three senatorial districts has rejected Governor Usman Ododo’s bid for a second term in the 2027 governorship election, warning that his re-election would extend the hold of one zone on the governorship to 16 consecutive years, contrary to their demand for equitable power rotation.

The youths, comprising representatives of Igala, Ebira, Okun and other ethnic groups, insisted that the governorship should shift to another zone after the eight-year tenure of former Governor Yahaya Bello and the current administration of Ododo, both from Kogi Central.

They also accused the state government of favouritism in appointments and contracts, failure to promote civil servants with corresponding salary increases, inadequate employment opportunities and lack of accountability in the management of public funds.

Addressing a press conference in Abuja yesterday under the auspices of De Group, in collaboration with the Igala Youth Council and other socio-cultural and political organisations, the coalition described the proposed 16-year zonal arrangement as unjust and unacceptable.

In a statement jointly signed by spokesperson of De Group, retired Colonel Kabiru Ndamadu, and National President of the Igala Youth Council Worldwide, Onogu Collins Monday, the youths argued that allowing Ododo to complete another four-year term would consolidate the dominance of one senatorial zone in the state’s political leadership.

“Governor Ahmed Usman Ododo assumed office January 27, 2024, succeeding former Governor Yahaya Bello, who ruled for eight years from the same zone.

“That means one zone has already held power for eight years, and is now in its third year under Governor Ododo. Any plan to extend that hold to 16 continuous years for one zone is unjust, undemocratic and unacceptable to the people of Kogi State.

“No zone is superior to another. No zone was created to rule forever while others only watch. Power must rotate. Power must shift now — in the interest of justice, equity and fairness for all Kogites,” the coalition declared.

Beyond the power rotation controversy, the youths questioned the state’s development record, alleging that substantial revenues received by the government had not translated into improved welfare, employment opportunities and infrastructure.

They claimed that Kogi had received more than N385 billion in Federation Account Allocation Committee (FAAC) disbursements and N71.67 billion in internally generated revenue within two years, figures they said should have supported better public services and workers’ welfare.

“With over N385 billion FAAC plus N71.67 billion IGR in two years, Kogi has no excuse to be poor, no excuse not to promote workers, no excuse not to employ our youths, and no excuse to persecute its own leaders,” they stated.

The coalition accused the administration of concentrating government appointments, contracts and empowerment opportunities among a small circle of political associates, describing the situation as a betrayal of the broader population.

“What we have in Kogi State today is not a government for all Kogites. It is a paddy-paddy government — government for friends, for family, for loyalists, for a small cabal.

“Contracts go to the same few people. Appointments go to the same few people. Empowerment goes to the same few people. Money circulates among the same few people.

“While the masses — the workers, the farmers, the market women, the students, the pensioners — suffer and beg to survive. Kogi State belongs to all of us, not to a few paddy-paddy friends,” the statement alleged.

On workers’ welfare, the coalition accused successive administrations of failing to implement promotions with corresponding salary increases, claiming that some civil servants had remained on the same salary grades for years despite rising living costs.

“For over nine years, civil servants in Kogi State have been denied real promotion with corresponding increase in salary. Workers are stagnated on the same level, doing the same work, with no growth, no motivation, no reward for service.

“A worker who joined service in 2016 is still suffering on the same salary grade in 2026, while cost of living has multiplied by five times,” the youths claimed.

They also alleged that successive administrations had failed to undertake meaningful recruitment of teachers, health workers and other categories of public servants, leaving thousands of graduates without employment.

“From Bello till date, there has been no meaningful mass employment for our youths. Thousands of graduates in Kogi East, Central and West are roaming the streets. No teachers recruited to fill our empty schools. No health workers recruited to fill our empty hospitals. No jobs for our graduates,” they said.

The coalition demanded an immediate end to what it described as political exclusion and victimisation of advocates of power rotation, specifically mentioning Senators Jibrin Isah Echocho and Sunday Karimi.

It also called for the implementation of outstanding civil service promotions with full salary benefits, mass recruitment of qualified youths, teachers and health workers, and equitable distribution of government appointments, contracts and empowerment opportunities.

The youths further demanded a forensic audit of local government allocations received since January 27, 2024, urging the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) to investigate the expenditure of public funds at both state and local government levels.

“We specifically call on the EFCC to investigate the former council chairmen from all the local governments in Kogi State. Let every former chairman come and account for the billions that entered his local government during his tenure.

“No former chairman should be allowed to walk away with the money of the people. They must explain what they did with FAAC, what they did with IGR, and what they did with every kobo that was meant for the grassroots.

“If they are innocent, the investigation will clear them. If they are guilty, they must face the law. Kogi people deserve to know where their local government money went,” the coalition said.

The youths maintained that their agitation was directed at what they considered inequitable political arrangements and governance practices rather than any individual.

“We are not fighting any individual. We are fighting injustice. We are fighting bad governance. We are fighting a paddy-paddy system that enriches a few and impoverishes millions. We are fighting a system that wants to silence all opposition so that it can keep power forever,” they declared.

The state government’s response to the allegations was not contained in the statement.

title: 2027: Reject corrupt candidates, end imposition, Maho tells parties
description:
By Favour Ulebor, Abuja



Ahead of the 2027 general elections, political analyst and lecturer at the International Institute of Journalists, Dr Austin Maho, has urged political parties to reject corrupt candidates, end the imposition of party leaders and introduce strict disciplinary measures to st
content:
By Favour Ulebor, Abuja

Ahead of the 2027 general elections, political analyst and lecturer at the International Institute of Journalists, Dr Austin Maho, has urged political parties to reject corrupt candidates, end the imposition of party leaders and introduce strict disciplinary measures to strengthen Nigeria’s democracy.

Maho made the call on Wednesday in Abuja at the International Stakeholders Engagement Forum on Anti-Corruption, Party Building and Democratic Governance, organised by the Diplomatic Correspondents Association of Nigeria (DICAN).

The forum had as its theme, “Nigeria’s 2027 Poll: Promoting Party Organisation, Discipline and Anti-Corruption Reforms: Lessons from Xi Jinping Thought.”

Presenting a paper at the event, Maho called on political parties to introduce anti-corruption agreements for candidates, establish independent disciplinary committees and maintain credible membership registers to promote transparency and accountability.

He warned that Nigerian political parties had increasingly become platforms for winning elections rather than institutions founded on ideology, discipline and national development.

Maho also faulted the high cost of nomination forms, saying it was shutting out credible Nigerians from elective positions and encouraging money-driven politics.

He said, “In China, the Party is an organization first, an election machine second.

“In Nigeria, our parties are election machines first, and organizations almost never.

“When we sell forms at that price, we are telling thieves to come and buy the ticket, because only thieves can afford it.”

He urged Nigerian political parties to draw lessons from China’s approach to party organisation, discipline and anti-corruption while preserving the country’s multiparty democratic system.

According to him, parties must strengthen their grassroots structures, ensure transparent congresses and sanction members found guilty of corruption, irrespective of their political influence.

Also speaking, the Counsellor at the Chinese Embassy in Nigeria, Dong Hairong, said China remained committed to its anti-corruption campaign, disclosing that 8.1 million cases had been filed since 2012.

She said 7.92 million officials had received disciplinary and administrative penalties, including more than 900 officials at vice-ministerial level and above.

Dong explained that China’s anti-corruption drive was aimed at strengthening public trust, improving governance and ensuring accountability among government officials.

She reaffirmed China’s willingness to share its governance experience with Nigeria and deepen cooperation between both countries.

In his goodwill message, the Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, Ambassador Sola Enikanolaiye, said strong political parties and effective anti-corruption measures were essential to democratic development.

Represented by the Assistant Director, Administration, in the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Mahmud Aliyu, the minister said democracy should go beyond periodic elections to encompass transparency, accountability and respect for the rule of law.

He urged political parties, civil society organisations and government institutions to strengthen democratic values and promote responsible leadership.

Similarly, the Executive Chairman of the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission, Ola Olukoyede, called for greater public participation in the fight against corruption.

Represented by the commission’s Head of Media and Publicity, Dele Oyewale, Olukoyede described corruption as a major challenge undermining Nigeria’s development, security and democratic institutions.

He disclosed that the commission had secured 10,872 convictions and recovered N1.23 trillion within the 34 months of his leadership.

He said, “The best diplomatic statement that we can make to the rest of the world is our commitment to the fight against corruption.”

Earlier, DICAN Chairman, Idehai Frederick, said the forum was organised to stimulate discussions on strengthening political parties, tackling corruption and improving democratic governance ahead of the 2027 elections.

He said Nigeria could draw lessons from China’s experience in party discipline and institutional development without abandoning its multiparty democratic system.

Frederick urged stakeholders to develop practical recommendations for strengthening democratic institutions and promoting accountability in governance.

The post 2027: Reject corrupt candidates, end imposition, Maho tells parties appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Diplomatic row: Nigeria, South Africa move to resolve differences
description:
• Abuja reviews Fani-Kayode’s engagement with Pretoria
Federal Government has called for renewed diplomatic engagement with South Africa to resolve outstanding differences between the two countries following a disagreement over the treatment of Nigeria’s High Commissioner, Femi Fani-Kayode, during t
content:
• Abuja reviews Fani-Kayode’s engagement with Pretoria

Federal Government has called for renewed diplomatic engagement with South Africa to resolve outstanding differences between the two countries following a disagreement over the treatment of Nigeria’s High Commissioner, Femi Fani-Kayode, during the presentation of his credentials to President Cyril Ramaphosa.

Ministry of Foreign Affairs disclosed yesterday that it was reviewing a comprehensive report on recent developments, including Tuesday’s meeting between Fani-Kayode and the Director-General of South Africa’s Department of International Relations and Cooperation (DIRCO), Zane Dangor.

The intervention followed a diplomatic controversy triggered by Fani-Kayode’s allegation that his introduction and speech were deliberately excluded from the live broadcast of the credentials presentation ceremony in Pretoria, although those of other ambassadors were aired.

South African authorities disputed the allegation of deliberate exclusion, describing the incident as a broadcasting issue rather than an intentional slight against Nigeria.

The disagreement subsequently escalated into exchanges between the Nigerian High Commission and South African presidential officials, prompting DIRCO to invite the Nigerian envoy for discussions.

In a statement issued after Tuesday’s meeting, DIRCO said Dangor expressed South Africa’s concern over the events surrounding the credentials ceremony and the envoy’s subsequent remarks on social media.

The South African official also reminded Fani-Kayode of Article 41 of the Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations, which requires diplomatic representatives to conduct official business with their host governments through established diplomatic channels.

However, the Nigerian High Commission rejected suggestions that Fani-Kayode had been reprimanded, describing the meeting as cordial and constructive and insisting that both sides had exchanged views on matters of mutual concern.

The envoy also raised concerns about the safety and treatment of Nigerians living in South Africa, an issue that has repeatedly strained relations between the two countries.

Against this background, spokesperson for Nigeria’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Oluwafemi Adeniyi, said the Federal Government was closely monitoring developments and reviewing reports of the discussions between its envoy and South African authorities.

Adeniyi stressed that both countries must deepen engagement to resolve outstanding issues while preserving their longstanding relationship founded on African solidarity, friendship and mutual respect.

“Particularly, as we both work assiduously to revitalise our longstanding bilateral relations, such is a relationship founded on African solidarity, friendship, and mutual respect.

“In this regard, the ministry reiterates commitment to sustained diplomatic engagement, while reviewing comprehensive report on the events that transpired in recent days,” he said.

The latest disagreement comes against a history of diplomatic tensions between Africa’s two major economies, particularly over attacks on foreign nationals, including Nigerians, in South Africa.

Relations between Abuja and Pretoria have periodically been strained by xenophobic violence, immigration disputes and concerns over the protection of Nigerian citizens and businesses.

In 2019, attacks targeting foreign nationals and their businesses in South Africa triggered diplomatic protests from Nigeria and retaliatory attacks on some South African-linked businesses in Nigeria.

Fresh concerns over attacks on foreigners in South Africa resurfaced in 2026, renewing demands for stronger protection of Nigerians and more effective bilateral cooperation.

Despite these differences, both countries have maintained significant diplomatic, economic and political ties, with cooperation extending to trade, investment and regional affairs.

South Africa’s foreign affairs department reaffirmed its commitment to strengthening the strategic partnership with Nigeria, stressing that the relationship should continue to be guided by mutual respect, cooperation and African solidarity.

The Nigerian Foreign Affairs Ministry did not specify the outcome of its review or announce further diplomatic measures, but maintained that sustained engagement remained the preferred approach to resolving the outstanding issues.

title: Ex-labour leaders broker peace between Ajaero, Osifo
description:
From Adanna Nnamani, Abuja
Presidents of the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC), Joe Ajaero, and the Trade Union Congress of Nigeria (TUC), Festus Osifo, have resolved their differences and agreed to work together following the intervention of former leaders of the two labour centres.
The reconciliation
content:
From Adanna Nnamani, Abuja

Presidents of the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC), Joe Ajaero, and the Trade Union Congress of Nigeria (TUC), Festus Osifo, have resolved their differences and agreed to work together following the intervention of former leaders of the two labour centres.

The reconciliation was announced on Wednesday at a joint press conference in Abuja, after meetings convened by the former presidents ended late on Tuesday night.

The disagreement centred on the Federal Government’s N70,000 monthly transport allowance for public sector workers. While Ajaero defended the NLC’s engagement with the government, Osifo faulted the process, arguing that the TUC was not adequately carried along. The dispute subsequently degenerated into public accusations and counter-accusations.

Speaking on behalf of the former presidents, Peter Esele said they intervened because they were uncomfortable with the public exchanges and concerned about their implications for the unity of the labour movement.

He listed those involved in the intervention as Hassan Sunmonu, Peace Obiajulu, Ayuba Wabba, Bobboi Bala Kaigama, Quadri Olaleye and himself.

“Certain things happen in the labour movement; we disagree. There’s nothing wrong with that. But what played out in the open was something that the past presidents were not comfortable with.

“So, the past presidents of NLC and TUC met with the leadership. We had meetings here yesterday that finished late in the night,” Esele said.

He explained that the resolutions would be communicated to state councils of both organisations to strengthen cooperation across the labour movement, adding that Ajaero and Osifo had endorsed the agreement.

In a joint statement signed by both leaders, the NLC and TUC confirmed that the misunderstanding had been amicably resolved and pledged to conduct their affairs with mutual respect, trust and cooperation.

“It is no longer news that a family misunderstanding arose between the two Labour Centers, which unfortunately played out in the public domain. However, in the true spirit of labour solidari ty, maturity and collective responsibility, distinguished former presidents of NLC and TUC intervened and worked tirelessly to resolve the disagreements. We are pleased to announce that their intervention has yielded the desired results, and the misunderstanding has been amicably resolved,” they stated.

The two organisations said their responsibility to defend workers’ rights must take precedence over disagreements between their leaders.

“We wish to place it on record that the unity of the Nigerian working class is far greater than any disagreement between its leadership. Our common struggle, shared history and collective responsibility to defend workers’ rights must never be sacrificed on the altar of misunderstanding or institutional differences.

“Consequently, the leadership of both Labour Centers has unanimously resolved to work together in an atmosphere of mutual respect, trust and cooperation in the defense of the interests of Nigerian workers, pensioners and the downtrodden. We recognize that the challenges confronting the working people are enormous, and this is certainly not the time for division, needless rivalry or distractions.”

Both labour centres reaffirmed their commitment to the welfare, dignity and material wellbeing of their members, stressing that solidarity and collective action remained essential to protecting workers’ interests.

They warned that disagreements within organised labour must not create opportunities for forces seeking to weaken the movement or reverse gains secured through years of struggle.

“We are determined to ensure that our differences do not provide an opportunity for anti-worker forces to weaken the labour movement or undermine the gains achieved through decades of collective struggle. Our responsibility is to confront the forces of exploitation, defend decent work, demand economic justice and resist every policy that impoverishes workers and pensioners,” they said.

To sustain the reconciliation, the organisations agreed to strengthen cooperation and establish mechanisms for addressing future disagreements before they escalate.

“To consolidate this renewed commitment, both Labour Centers have agreed to institute appropriate measures that will strengthen mutual respect, promote harmonious working relations, establish clear and effective mechanisms for resolving future disagreements, and prevent a recurrence of such misunderstandings.”

They thanked the former presidents for their intervention and urged affiliates, state councils, industrial unions, workers and pensioners to remain united.

“The temporary misunderstanding between our Centers must not be allowed to weaken the confidence of Nigerian workers in their organizations.

“The NLC and TUC are united in purpose, resolute in commitment and unwavering in the struggle for social and economic justice,” they stated.

The post Ex-labour leaders broker peace between Ajaero, Osifo appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: UTME: JAMB introduces home-based change of institution, course
description:
From Fred Ezeh, Abuja
Candidates seeking to change their preferred institutions or courses in the Unified Tertiary Matriculation Examination (UTME) can now do so from the comfort of their homes without visiting offices of the Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board (JAMB) or its accredited centres.
content:
From Fred Ezeh, Abuja

Candidates seeking to change their preferred institutions or courses in the Unified Tertiary Matriculation Examination (UTME) can now do so from the comfort of their homes without visiting offices of the Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board (JAMB) or its accredited centres.

The Board, which announced the introduction of the new service in Abuja, said the initiative would eliminate the stress, transportation costs and long waiting periods associated with physical visits to its offices, while making its services more accessible and convenient for candidates across the country.

It explained that candidates could now effect changes to their institutions and courses from any location with internet access through their registered JAMB profiles, describing the development as another milestone in its ongoing digital transformation.

In a statement issued by its Acting Director, Public Affairs and Protocol, Fabian Benjamin, JAMB said the initiative was part of efforts by its Registrar, Segun Aina, to reposition the Board as a service-oriented and digitally driven institution.

The Board said the arrangement aligned with the Federal Government’s Ease of Doing Business policy and global best practices in digital public service delivery, adding that it would significantly reduce congestion at JAMB offices and accredited facilities nationwide.

Explaining the procedure, JAMB said candidates were required to log into its e-Facility portal using their registered email addresses and passwords, select the Corrections and Uploads option on the sidebar menu and click on Change of Programme/Institution.

“Under the arrangement, candidates can process changes to their institutions and/or programmes directly through the JAMB e-Facility portal using their registered email addresses and passwords.

“To access the service, candidates are required to log into the portal, select the Corrections and Uploads option on the sidebar menu and click on Change of Programme/Institution.

“They are also required to select UTME, choose the relevant examination year and initiate payment for the service,” the statement explained.

JAMB said candidates would thereafter be redirected to the CREDO payment platform to complete their transactions using debit cards or bank transfers.

It advised candidates to return to their payment pages after completing the transactions to ensure that their payment status reflected “PAID (Not Used)” before proceeding with the changes.

“Thereafter, candidates can return to the Change of Institution/Course page, enter their preferred institution and/or programme details and validate the transaction using a One-Time Password (OTP) sent to their registered email addresses. Upon successful OTP validation, candidates can submit their changes by clicking the SAVE button,” the Board stated.

It explained that a confirmation message would appear once the change of institution or course had been successfully processed, after which candidates were expected to print their Change of Programme/Institution slips.

The Board also directed candidates to log into the Central Admission Processing System (CAPS) to confirm that their new institution and course selections had been updated.

JAMB, however, cautioned candidates against making errors in their selections, advising them to carefully review their preferred institutions and courses before submitting their requests.

It stressed the need for candidates to ensure that their payments had been confirmed and that their registered email accounts remained accessible for OTP authentication.

The Board also warned candidates against engaging intermediaries or paying individuals to undertake the exercise on their behalf, insisting that the process was designed to be completed personally through their individual profiles.

It urged candidates to protect their login credentials and OTPs against unauthorised access to prevent fraud and manipulation of their admission records.

Aina reiterated the Board’s commitment to deploying technology to simplify administrative procedures and ensure that candidates, irrespective of their locations, could access essential services without unnecessary difficulties.

He said the ultimate objective was to build a more responsive and efficient institution where candidates would spend less time seeking administrative services and devote more attention to pursuing their educational aspirations.

The post UTME: JAMB introduces home-based change of institution, course appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

content:
Plateau United technical adviser Gbenga Ogunbote has warned his players against complacency after their 3-0 victory over Kun Khalifat ended a four-match winless run in the Nigeria Premier Football League.

The Peace Boys returned to winning ways on Tuesday at the New Jos Stadium, with Ogunbote expressing satisfaction with the response of his players following their recent struggles.

“It was a good comeback for us after four games without a win. We needed a lot to psych the players up. Thank God we had one of the best moments, coming back to start winning. We hope and pray that we will be able to manage it,” Ogunbote told the media.

The coach, however, insisted that his side must build on the victory rather than allow the result to make them complacent.

“We will leverage on it. We will not relax like we had before. We had a slip; I did say before that it was a temporary setback,” he added.

Plateau United took the lead in the 12th minute through Victor Tchadienne before Victor Dawa doubled their advantage shortly before half-time.

Dawa completed his brace seven minutes into the second half to seal an emphatic victory for the hosts.

The result ended a difficult spell for the Jos-based side and lifted them to eighth position on the league table.

Ogunbote also expressed concern about officiating in away matches, saying he hoped his team would receive the same standard of refereeing on the road.

“We still hope and pray that we will have the type of officiating that we get here in our away games. I can tell that we will go out and play very well,” he said.

Plateau United will now seek to maintain their momentum when they face Ranchers Bees in their next league fixture.

The post Ogunbote vows Plateau United won’t lose focus appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: 2027 countdown: Tinubu approves establishment of Kebbi inland dry port

By Omeiza Ajayi



ABUJA — President Bola Tinubu has appealed to Kebbi State voters to give him a second term to complete his eight-year tenure, promising that it would be their turn to produ
content:
…Tells Kebbi voters allow me complete 8 years

..North firmly represented in decision-making — Shettima

By Omeiza Ajayi

ABUJA — President Bola Tinubu has appealed to Kebbi State voters to give him a second term to complete his eight-year tenure, promising that it would be their turn to produce the president thereafter.


“This time, I am before you to seek your support for the second time to complete what I have started. It will be your turn next time,” Tinubu told supporters at the All Progressives Congress, APC, presidential campaign rally at Haliru Abdu Stadium, Birnin Kebbi, yesterday.


The President said he returned to the state to thank the people for supporting him and other APC candidates in the 2023 elections.
“You voted for me, you voted for Kaura Gwandu, you voted for our senators. Now I have come back to say thank you. May God bless you and answer your prayers,” he said.


Seeking assurances of their support in 2027, Tinubu asked the crowd whether they had their Permanent Voter Cards, PVCs, and were ready to vote.


“Are you ready to vote? Do you have your PVC? Raise your hand if you have your PVC. Are you going to come out and vote? Thank you very much. I can go home comfortably and sleep. I know you will come out to vote from top to bottom,” he said.
Tinubu also announced approval of a long-awaited inland dry port for the state.


“I understand your request on the inland dry port. That is a given. Kebbi needs it and it is approved,” he declared.
He said requests by Governor Nasir Idris, including road projects and the reconstruction of a road damaged by flooding, were receiving attention.


“All the requests of the governor are before me here. I have listed them carefully. We are working together,” he added.


North at decision-making table


Vice President Kashim Shettima, in his remarks, said the North was adequately represented in the Tinubu administration, citing key appointments in the security and defence architecture.


He named the Minister of Defence, General Christopher Musa; Minister of State for Defence, Bello Matawalle; National Security Adviser, Nuhu Ribadu; and Chief of Naval Staff, Vice Admiral Idi Abbas.


“The North sits comfortably at the table where decisions are made,” Shettima declared, adding that “a vote for His Excellency President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and for me as your Vice President is a vote for the preservation of the North.”


He recalled Tinubu’s support for the North during the APC presidential primary, saying the President stood by the late former President Muhammadu Buhari’s preferred candidate.


“He stood by the man who told delegates that he would never buy their votes with dollars. He made sure that the favourite of the North, the late General Muhammadu Buhari, became our party’s choice,” he said.


Shettima said the North rewarded Tinubu in 2023 with 60.2 per cent of its votes and expressed confidence that the region would repeat the gesture in the 2027 election.


On security, he said Tinubu had approved an increase of up to 80 per cent in the salaries of armed forces personnel. He also disclosed that the President had assigned him to chair a committee for the procurement of N200 billion worth of fertiliser for distribution to farmers during the dry season.


Listing federal projects in Kebbi, Shettima cited the Sokoto-Badagry highway, with 258 kilometres passing through the state, describing it as the longest stretch in any state. Others include a 3.5-megawatt solar project in Ambursa and the upgrade of the Federal Medical Centre, Birnin Kebbi, to a teaching hospital.


He said the College of Nursing and Midwifery, Ambursa, had been commissioned, while Kebbi State University, Aliero, received N693 million in student loan funding through the Nigerian Education Loan Fund, NELFUND.


Shettima urged residents to vote for Tinubu on January 16 and return Governor Idris for a second term on February 6.
APC leaders rally support
Minister of Budget and Economic Planning and former Kebbi governor, Atiku Bagudu, said the APC was entering the 2027 election with greater unity than in 2023.
“We are a more united Kebbi State here today, and we are facing the 2027 election more united than we did in 2023 under the able leadership of our governor,” he said.
Bagudu credited Tinubu with bringing party leaders together, saying the President encouraged them to work together because the coming political task required “more hands rather than less”.
The Director-General of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Abdulaziz Yari, urged opposition parties to learn from the large turnout, claiming that no previous administration had invested as much in Kebbi and the North as the Tinubu government.
APC National Chairman, Professor Nentawe Yilwatda, said Tinubu deserved another term to consolidate his development projects across the country. The Speaker of the House of Representatives, Tajudeen Abbas, and Deputy Senate President, Barau Jibrin, also canvassed support for Tinubu and Idris.
Former Governor Adamu Aliero praised Tinubu for approving the deployment of an armoured brigade to strengthen security in the state. Yobe State Governor, Mai Mala Buni, and former Kebbi governor, Usman Saidu Dakingari, also urged support for the President.
Tinubu arrived at about 1.35pm, accompanied by Shettima, Yilwatda, Yari and serving and former governors. Thousands of supporters from the state’s 21 local government areas attended the rally, where northern pro-Tinubu singer, Adamu Dauda Kahutu, popularly known as Rarara, entertained the crowd.
The rally followed an empowerment programme organised at the instance of the First Lady, Senator Oluremi Tinubu, which benefited at least 2,000 women in the state.

The post 2027 countdown: Tinubu approves establishment of Kebbi inland dry port appeared first on Vanguard News.

description:

The Governor gave the a
content:
Lagos State Governor, Babajide Sanwo-Olu, has reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to youth sports development, pledging support for the growth of young table tennis talents through initiatives such as the Daniel Ford International Elite Youth Table Tennis Championship.

The Governor gave the assurance while receiving a delegation led by the Managing Director of Daniel Ford International, Yemi Edun, alongside the President of ITTF Africa and Executive Vice President of the International Table Tennis Federation, Wahid Oshodi, and two emerging table tennis players, Matthew Kuti and Emmanuella Shaibu.

The delegation formally invited Governor Sanwo-Olu to the grand finale of the fourth edition of the championship, scheduled to hold on December 20, 2026, at the historic Rowe Park Sports Centre, Yaba, Lagos.

Recalling his attendance at the previous edition of the tournament, Governor Sanwo-Olu expressed delight at the championship’s progress and enquired about the development of the young athletes. He encouraged the players to remain focused on their goals and commended the organisers for creating opportunities that enable young Nigerians to pursue excellence through sport.

“Young people need platforms that allow them to develop their talents and realise their potential,” the Governor said.

“Initiatives such as this championship play a vital role in identifying future champions and inspiring the next generation of athletes.”

His remarks underscored the importance of strategic partnerships between government, the private sector and sporting institutions in creating pathways for youth participation and success in competitive sports.

The visit also provided an opportunity for the delegation to interact with members of the Flamingos, Nigeria’s national women’s U-17 football team, whose achievements continue to bring pride and recognition to the country.

Speaking on the vision behind the championship, Edun said the initiative was designed to go beyond an annual tournament and serve as a sustainable platform for discovering, nurturing and preparing Nigerian players for international competition.

“Our objective is to build a clear pathway for young talents to progress from grassroots development to the global stage,” Edun said. “We want every young Nigerian who watches these players compete internationally to believe that they too can achieve similar success through dedication, hard work and opportunity.”

According to Edun, the championship also seeks to inspire more children to embrace table tennis, build confidence through sport and develop the mindset needed to compete at the highest levels.

title: Govts must stop imposing projects on citizens – Uzodimma, Sule
description:
From Juliana Taiwo-Obalonye, Abuja
Imo State Governor, Hope Uzodimma, and his Nasarawa State counterpart, Abdullahi Sule, have warned against imposing development projects and policies on citizens without their input, insisting that governments must involve communities in identifying their needs, se
content:
From Juliana Taiwo-Obalonye, Abuja

Imo State Governor, Hope Uzodimma, and his Nasarawa State counterpart, Abdullahi Sule, have warned against imposing development projects and policies on citizens without their input, insisting that governments must involve communities in identifying their needs, setting priorities and determining how public resources are deployed.

The governors said winning and sustaining public trust remained one of the greatest challenges of leadership, particularly when governments introduced difficult economic policies that imposed hardship on citizens, stressing that transparency, effective communication and inclusive decision-making were essential to securing public confidence.

Speaking at the 2026 World Public Relations Forum (WPRF) in Abuja, the governors also defended President Bola Tinubu’s removal of petrol subsidy and foreign exchange reforms, arguing that although the policies had increased economic pressure on households, they had provided state governments with additional resources to undertake development projects.

While Uzodimma described subsidy removal as a difficult but necessary decision taken in Nigeria’s overall interest, Sule disclosed that the increased allocations accruing to Nasarawa State following the reforms had made it possible for his administration to commit resources to the proposed world’s first University of Public Relations and Leadership.

The governors spoke during a high-level panel on “Responsible Governance and Communication: Building Trust through Community Engagement, Stakeholder Relations and Inclusive Impact,” where they maintained that public trust could not be secured through government pronouncements alone but must be earned through citizens’ participation and measurable improvements in their living conditions.

Uzodimma said his administration had adopted a governance model that involved stakeholders from the conception of policies and projects through planning, implementation and evaluation, rather than presenting communities with decisions already taken on their behalf.

According to him, citizens, including women, young people, persons with disabilities, students, traditional rulers, security agencies and political stakeholders, must be given opportunities to contribute to decisions affecting their lives.

He explained that his administration established an agency for persons with disabilities to ensure that their concerns were accommodated in government programmes, stressing that meaningful participation required citizens to see how their suggestions translated into concrete projects.

“The toughest thing on leadership is winning the trust of the people and keeping the trust, especially when you want to accept a decision that will hurt people first,” Uzodimma said.

Citing the removal of petrol subsidy, the governor acknowledged that the policy had imposed financial difficulties on many households but argued that it had also increased resources available to the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory for infrastructure and socioeconomic development.

He maintained that difficult reforms could only achieve their intended objectives when governments explained their necessity, recognised the concerns of affected groups and demonstrated that the sacrifices demanded of citizens would produce tangible benefits.

Illustrating the dilemma confronting policymakers, Uzodimma said the introduction of affordable government buses could reduce transportation costs for workers, traders and students but might adversely affect commercial transport operators whose livelihoods depended on existing arrangements.

He argued that responsible leadership required governments to balance such competing interests, engage those likely to be affected and communicate alternative opportunities available to them.

The governor said his administration had institutionalised public engagement through quarterly stakeholders’ meetings introduced in June 2020, less than six months after he assumed office, providing platforms for citizens to question government officials, criticise policies and demand explanations on matters affecting their communities.

He disclosed that the state had also introduced a radio town hall programme involving more than 20 stations across the South-East, through which residents and Nigerians in the diaspora could interact directly with government officials and receive responses to their concerns.

Uzodimma added that an elders’ council had been established to advise the government and provide insights into the expectations and grievances of communities, while an agency for persons with disabilities ensured that vulnerable groups were not excluded from decision-making.

According to him, the engagement platforms had enabled his administration to identify problems early, address grievances and strengthen public confidence, particularly in an era when misinformation could spread rapidly through social media and influence public perceptions of government.

He listed his administration’s interventions to include digital skills training for more than 75,000 young people, programmes which he said had created over 85,000 jobs and learning opportunities, and the One Kindred One Business initiative, under which more than 600 businesses had been registered by the end of 2025.

The governor said the Federal Government was adopting the business initiative for national application, describing it as an example of how community-based participation could stimulate economic activities and create opportunities at the grassroots.

“For us in Imo, the voice that matters most is the voice of our people. We engage with them, we communicate, we listen to the feedback they share with us. We work with that feedback and they see through our delivery that we have been listening,” he said.

Uzodimma also challenged public relations practitioners to encourage genuine dialogue between governments and citizens rather than concentrate exclusively on projecting government achievements.

“If you tell a government to listen to its people, help make sure that the people also listen to government,” he said.

Corroborating the need for participatory governance, Sule said development planning in Nasarawa State was driven by consultations with communities to identify gaps and establish priorities in infrastructure, education, youth development and other critical sectors.

He maintained that citizens should not be treated merely as recipients of government projects but as active participants in determining what should be provided and how such interventions should be implemented.

“They are part of the planning. They are part of the design,” Sule said, stressing that involving communities from the outset helped governments avoid spending scarce resources on projects that failed to address the people’s immediate needs.

The Nasarawa governor said transparency and honesty were indispensable to public confidence, adding that citizens should be able to assess government performance by comparing their circumstances and the level of development over time.

Turning to the economic reforms of the Tinubu administration, Sule said the removal of petrol subsidy and unification of foreign exchange rates had significantly improved the financial capacity of state governments, making it possible for Nasarawa to undertake projects that would previously have been beyond its resources.

He cited the proposed University of Public Relations and Leadership, an initiative of the Global Alliance for Public Relations and Communication Management, as one of the projects made possible by the additional resources available to his administration.

According to him, the institution would have remained an aspiration if Nasarawa had continued receiving monthly allocations of between N4 billion and N5 billion, as was the case before the reforms.

“If not for the removal of subsidy by President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, if not for the unification and the floating of the naira, if it was a period when Nasarawa State was just receiving somewhere around N4 billion to N5 billion a month, it would remain a dream for Nasarawa State.”

Sule explained that the proposed institution would be a specialised centre for research, learning and leadership development rather than a conventional university devoted primarily to undergraduate education.

He said Nasarawa emerged as the preferred location despite initial expectations that the university would be established in Abuja or another major Nigerian city, citing the state’s proximity to the Federal Capital Territory, availability of land, natural resources and investment potential.

Highlighting the state’s economic prospects, the governor identified commercially viable deposits of lithium, titanium, barite, lead, zinc and tin, alongside agricultural and industrial investments, including what he described as Africa’s largest medium-density fibreboard processing plant, with a daily capacity of 6,000 metric tonnes.

He said the combination of land, natural resources, human capital and security made Nasarawa suitable for the institution, which he hoped would eventually attract international scholars, researchers and public relations professionals.

Drawing comparisons with Harvard University in the United States, Sule said the proposed university should aspire to build an international reputation through sustained investment in research, leadership development and academic excellence.

He welcomed delegates from 126 countries attending the forum and urged them to return to Nigeria when the institution became operational.

Earlier, the panel moderator, Shreya Krishnan, Managing Director of AnitaB.org India and Chair of the Policy Advocacy Committee of UNESCO’s Women for Ethical AI in South Asia, challenged the governors to demonstrate how their administrations translated public communication into responsible decisions and measurable improvements in citizens’ lives.

“Public trust is shaped by more than what governments say. It is built by what citizens experience.”

Krishnan maintained that citizens judged governments not merely by the frequency of official announcements but by whether their concerns were heard, decisions explained, public services improved and neglected communities reached.

She stressed that effective public relations could not compensate for poor governance, warning that public confidence could neither be manufactured through publicity campaigns nor sustained without accountability and tangible results.

According to her, responsible communication must be reflected in how governments listen, make decisions, engage stakeholders and deliver outcomes that citizens can see and experience.

She concluded that public trust was built through consistent action rather than isolated announcements, stressing that governments must demonstrate through their policies, projects and service delivery that citizens’ voices genuinely mattered.

The post Govts must stop imposing projects on citizens – Uzodimma, Sule appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Innovator develops machine to reduce drudgery in post-harvest cleaning of farm
description:
By Cynthia Alo







The use of manual methods to sort and wash agricultural produce, including tigernuts, ginger, potatoes and grains, may become less demanding with the development of a locally made machine designed to integrate sorting, washing and drying operations.







The innovation, devel
content:
By Cynthia Alo

The use of manual methods to sort and wash agricultural produce, including tigernuts, ginger, potatoes and grains, may become less demanding with the development of a locally made machine designed to integrate sorting, washing and drying operations.

The innovation, developed by a Kogi State-born physicist and innovator, Kabir Umar, is aimed at addressing the labour-intensive and often unhygienic methods used by smallholder farmers, cleaning artisans and agro-processors to prepare agricultural commodities for local consumption and processing.


Umar said the absence of affordable integrated cleaning equipment had left many small-scale operators dependent on manual sorting and washing, while those seeking mechanised alternatives often had to acquire expensive imported specialised equipment.
He identified tigernuts as one of the commodities particularly affected by the challenge, explaining that some cleaning artisans still use their legs to wash the nuts before sorting them by hand.


According to him, similar challenges affect the handling of other agricultural commodities, including ginger, potatoes, millet, beans and hibiscus flowers, popularly known as zobo.


Umar said the idea for the machine emerged in 2020 after he ventured into agro-processing and encountered difficulties with the cleaning and drying of raw agricultural materials, which he identified as an important first step in value addition.


He subsequently developed a multipurpose post-harvest sorting and washing machine, with an additional drying capability, designed to provide an integrated cleaning solution for different agricultural commodities.


The innovator said he had mainly used the machine to sort and wash tigernuts for further processing into tigernut flour, adding that demonstrations to tigernut cleaning artisans showed its potential to reduce manual labour and improve productivity.
He, however, disclosed that the machine was still at an advanced prototype stage and had yet to be deployed sustainably to support farmers and other operators across the agricultural value chain.
According to him, wider adoption of the machine could improve the quality of agricultural produce entering local markets, support value addition, create jobs and strengthen the export potential of Nigerian commodities by improving their post-harvest handling.
On the challenges facing the development, Umar identified inadequate funding as a major constraint that had slowed the transition from prototype development to commercial production.
He expressed optimism that intervention through the National Agency for Science and Engineering Infrastructure’s (NASENI) Innovate Naija Challenge would help accelerate the commercialisation process.

title: Youth Olympics: NSC rewards gold medallists with $20k
description:
The National Sports Commission has rewarded Nigeria’s three Youth Olympic gold medallists with $20,000 each, following their historic performance at the Games in Dakar, Senegal.
The beneficiaries are Bright Gift, who won the men’s 100m in a Games record of 10.28 seconds, Rosemary Chigozie Nwankwo, w
content:
The National Sports Commission has rewarded Nigeria’s three Youth Olympic gold medallists with $20,000 each, following their historic performance at the Games in Dakar, Senegal.

The beneficiaries are Bright Gift, who won the men’s 100m in a Games record of 10.28 seconds, Rosemary Chigozie Nwankwo, who won the women’s 100m in 11.16 seconds, and Praise Tejiri Ugoh, who won the women’s 400m in a personal best of 52.76 seconds.

The NSC announced the reward in a statement signed by the Special Assistant on Media to the Director General, Kola Daniel, on Wednesday. It follows the N100m reward given by President Bola Tinubu to the Flamingos, and the NSC said the athletes had not been left out of the celebrations.

The Commission described the gesture as part of its commitment to reward excellence, motivate young athletes and ensure that no category of Nigerian champions is left behind in the ongoing sports reforms.

They added that the reward reflects the recognition of their dedication and patriotism on the global stage, and aligns with the Renewed Hope Agenda for sports, which prioritises athlete welfare, grassroots development, early discovery of talent and a sustainable reward system for podium performances.

The NSC said more structured incentive packages were being put in place for athletes who win medals at continental and global competitions, including the African Games, the Commonwealth Games, the World Championships and the Olympic Games.

The Nigeria Olympic Committee had earlier rewarded the three athletes with $1,000 each at the airport reception on the team’s return from Dakar.

The three golds were Nigeria’s best-ever outing at the Youth Olympics, surpassing the previous best of two at the inaugural edition in Singapore in 2010. The Commission praised the athletes for their resilience, focus and conduct, and urged them to remain disciplined and serve as role models to millions of young Nigerians.

They also thanked President Tinubu for his support for sports development, describing his leadership as a turning point for the sector.

title: Summit to examine financing, market access for farmers, agribusinesses
description:
By Cynthia Alo







Farm financing, market access and innovative solutions for farmers and agribusiness operators will take centre stage at the fifth edition of the Wealth Creation Summit scheduled for November 28, 2026, in Abuja.The summit, organised by Golden Harvest Acres Ventures, is expected
content:
By Cynthia Alo

Farm financing, market access and innovative solutions for farmers and agribusiness operators will take centre stage at the fifth edition of the Wealth Creation Summit scheduled for November 28, 2026, in Abuja.
The summit, organised by Golden Harvest Acres Ventures, is expected to bring together more than 1,000 farmers, agribusiness owners, investors, entrepreneurs and young Nigerians to explore opportunities for improving agricultural productivity and building sustainable businesses.
The event, themed, “Unlocking Opportunities for Wealth Creation, Innovation and Sustainable Agricultural Development,” will focus on connecting agricultural producers and entrepreneurs with financing opportunities, markets, investors and business development support.
A major feature of the summit will be the launch of the Wealth Creation Network, an agribusiness and entrepreneurship cooperative designed to support farmers, women and young entrepreneurs through training, access to agricultural inputs, produce aggregation, market linkages and business development services.
The network is also expected to provide members with opportunities for bulk produce sales, export linkages and investment-readiness training.
Speaking ahead of the event, Convener of the summit and Founder of Golden Harvest Acres Ventures, Uzua Brainz, said the initiative was intended to provide participants with practical opportunities beyond conference discussions.
“We do not want people to attend Wealth Creation Summit 5.0, listen to speeches and return home exactly as they came. We want them to leave with clarity, structure, connections and practical opportunities for wealth creation,” he said.

title: Whyte predicts early knockout for Joshua vs Fury
description:
Former heavyweight contender, Dillian Whyte, has predicted that the fight between British-Nigerian, Anthony Joshua, and Tyson Fury will end in an early knockout, and says it may not last beyond the first round.
Whyte, who has fought both men, told Sky Sports Boxing that he would be surprised if the
content:
Former heavyweight contender, Dillian Whyte, has predicted that the fight between British-Nigerian, Anthony Joshua, and Tyson Fury will end in an early knockout, and says it may not last beyond the first round.

Whyte, who has fought both men, told Sky Sports Boxing that he would be surprised if the contest on December 11 went beyond five rounds. The fight takes place at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff, with three heavyweight bouts confirmed for the undercard.

He said the rivals had changed since the fight was first talked about six years ago.

“It might be an even better fight now than it would have been. Six years ago, the guys were more cagey; they had better defence, better feet. If you asked me six years ago, I would have said either AJ by KO or Fury by points,” he said.

“Now, they are both showing vulnerability. Fury could knock him out in a round. AJ could knock out Fury in a round.”

He added that Fury’s speed had dropped, saying, “Tyson’s feet have slowed down; he is not as fast as he was, not as reactive as he was. AJ has shown a lot of vulnerability, and he has been through a lot of things, mentally, as well. So, I think that it is going to be a great fight. I would be surprised if it lasts five rounds.”

Whyte beat Joshua as an amateur, but was stopped by him in 2015 when they fought for the British title. Joshua went on to win a world title in his next fight.

Whyte’s first world title challenge came against Fury in 2022, when he was knocked out as the Briton defended his belt at home for the first time in his career.

title: Morocco matches Nigeria’s No.5 best FIFA rankings
description:
Morocco have climbed two places to fifth in the latest FIFA Men’s World Rankings, matching the highest position Nigeria has ever held in the standings.
The Atlas Lions have 1,809.37 points in the rankings released on Wednesday. They are the first African nation to enter the top five since Nigeria re
content:
Morocco have climbed two places to fifth in the latest FIFA Men’s World Rankings, matching the highest position Nigeria has ever held in the standings.

The Atlas Lions have 1,809.37 points in the rankings released on Wednesday. They are the first African nation to enter the top five since Nigeria reached the same position in April 1994, a gap of 32 years.

Their rise followed two wins over Niger in the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers during the November international break. Morocco won the first game 5-1 and the return fixture 1-0 on Tuesday.

The 17-year-old Abdellah Ouazane scored the only goal in the second match, handing Morocco their fourth straight win in Group A and confirming their place at the 2027 AFCON. They have taken all 12 points from their four qualifiers, with two games left.

Spain remain on top of the rankings, followed by Argentina, France and England. Portugal and Brazil have dropped to sixth and seventh, respectively.

Morocco are among nine countries that have secured places at the 2027 AFCON after the fourth round of qualifiers. They are joined by Senegal, Mali, Burkina Faso, Benin and Cameroon, while co-hosts Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda qualified automatically. Burkina Faso beat Mauritania 3-1, Mali won 2-0 against Rwanda, and Cameroon went through after Comoros defeated Congo 1-0. Senegal’s qualification was confirmed by results elsewhere.

The tournament will run from June 19 to July 17, 2027, with the remaining 15 places to be decided when qualifying ends in March 2027.

The Super Eagles moved up one place to 29th globally and are fifth in Africa with 1,564.18 points. Eric Chelle’s men beat Tanzania 3-1 in Uyo last Friday but drew 0-0 in Zanzibar on Tuesday. The result lifted them above Algeria, who dropped four places to 32nd and sixth in Africa.

Senegal are second in Africa and 18th in the world, followed by Egypt (26th) and Côte d’Ivoire (28th).

title: Abua survives scare, Quadre reaches Da-Silva tennis semis
description:
Top seed Canice Abua battled back from a set down to defeat Ayomide Folorunsho and reach the quarter-finals of the men’s singles at the maiden Destiny Da-Silva Tennis Open Championship in Lagos.
Abua, who lost the opening set 5-7, recovered to win the next two 6-2, 6-3 in their third-round encounter
content:
Top seed Canice Abua battled back from a set down to defeat Ayomide Folorunsho and reach the quarter-finals of the men’s singles at the maiden Destiny Da-Silva Tennis Open Championship in Lagos.

Abua, who lost the opening set 5-7, recovered to win the next two 6-2, 6-3 in their third-round encounter, setting up a last-eight meeting with 15th-seed David Edward.

Edward secured his quarter-final place after seeing off Chima Michael at 7-6(9), 1-0 in their encounter.

In the women’s singles, Nigeria’s number one, Oyinlomo Quadre, continued her impressive run with a 6-3, 6-0 demolition of Ohunene Yakubu to book a semi-final date with Bright Emmanuel.

Emmanuel caused a major upset on Wednesday, defeating third-seed Nenrot Suwa 6-2, 6-1 to reach the last four.

The other women’s semi-final will feature second-seed Khadijat Mohammed and fifth-seed Success Ogunjobi.

Mohammed defeated Godwin Mary 6-1, 6-1, while Ogunjobi recovered from a set down to stun fourth-seed Etoro Bassey 6-2, 3-6, 6-1.

Elsewhere in the men’s singles, Michael Emmanuel defeated Musa Mamud 6-1, 6-2 to set up a quarter-final clash with seventh-seed Yahaya Sani-Inabo, who beat Joseph Jimoh 3-6, 6-3, 6-3.

Sylvanus Ajang also advanced after dispatching Iyanuoluwa Taiwo 6-2, 6-0 and will face Dahiru Muhammed, who edged Musa Mohammed 3-6, 6-2, 7-6(5).

Lucky Danjuma and Yusuf Abubakar complete the men’s singles quarter-final line-up.

The competition, organised by the Destiny Da-Silva Foundation, features a N30 million prize purse and provides a platform for both able-bodied and wheelchair tennis players.

Men’s and women’s doubles matches, alongside wheelchair men’s and women’s singles and doubles fixtures, are also scheduled for Thursday, November 19, 2026.

title: Akpe proud to lead Olympic Eagles to victory
description:
Basel defender Victory Akpe has expressed his delight at captaining the Olympic Eagles to a commanding victory over the Democratic Republic of Congo, which secured Nigeria’s place in the final qualifying round of next year’s U-23 Africa Cup of Nations, PUNCH Sports Extra reports.
The Olympic Eagles
content:
Basel defender Victory Akpe has expressed his delight at captaining the Olympic Eagles to a commanding victory over the Democratic Republic of Congo, which secured Nigeria’s place in the final qualifying round of next year’s U-23 Africa Cup of Nations, PUNCH Sports Extra reports.

The Olympic Eagles overturned a first-leg deficit with a convincing 4-0 win over DR Congo at the Remo Stars Stadium in Ikenne-Remo, four days after losing the first leg in Lubumbashi.

Akpe led the side as Alex Oweilayefa, Peter Osayande, Victor Samuel and Abdulmuiz Adeleke all got on the scoresheet to complete the comeback.

The 20-year-old had been called up to the senior national team during the September international break but was withdrawn from the squad before being handed the responsibility of captaining the Olympic Eagles.

“Great feeling to represent this country and put on that amazing jersey,” Akpe told PUNCH Sports Extra.

Reflecting on the pressure to overturn the first-leg defeat, the defender said the team needed time to build an understanding, having had little opportunity to play together before the tie.

“Most of us played together for the first time, so we needed at least one game to understand one another. When we came back, we decided to learn fast from our mistakes and improve as fast as possible so we can play better than the first leg,” he said.

At club level, Akpe has scored one goal and provided one assist in 13 league appearances for Basel this season.

Nigeria will face Zambia in the final qualifying round for next year’s U-23 Africa Cup of Nations in Egypt. The tournament will determine Africa’s representatives in the men’s football event at the Los Angeles 2028 Olympic Games.

title: Konga shows tech-enabled retail platforms can complement conventional healthcare delivery
description:
By Prince Osuagwu



The growing intersection of technology, healthcare and e-commerce is opening new opportunities for mobile health delivery in Nigeria.



This is as one of Nigeria’s composite e-commerce companies Konga attracted the partnership of global skincare brand, La Roche-Posay, to expand
content:
By Prince Osuagwu

The growing intersection of technology, healthcare and e-commerce is opening new opportunities for mobile health delivery in Nigeria.


This is as one of Nigeria’s composite e-commerce companies Konga attracted the partnership of global skincare brand, La Roche-Posay, to expand access to dermatological expertise and authentic skincare products in the country.


The partnership, leverages Konga Health’s retail and e-commerce network to connect consumers with genuine dermatological products, professional skincare advice and health education.


The partnership sealed in Lagos recently, demonstrated how technology-enabled retail platforms could complement conventional healthcare delivery by making specialist skincare products and information more accessible to consumers.


La Roche-Posay, a brand under L’Oréal Dermatological Beauty, partnered with Konga Health, its official distributor in Nigeria, to promote dermatological science, product authenticity and informed skincare choices.
A major attraction was the interactive skin science experience, which allowed visitors to explore common skin conditions, including hyperpigmentation, acne, damaged skin barriers, dryness and the effects of ultraviolet radiation.
The programme also featured free consultations with certified dermatologists and members of the L’Oréal Dermatological Beauty MedSquad, who provided professional skin analysis, guidance and practical recommendations.
Among the participating specialists were Dr Ayesha Akinkugbe, dermatologist and Vice-President of the Nigerian Association of Dermatologists, and Dr Folakemi Cole-Adeife.
The event showcased five major La Roche-Posay product franchises: Cicaplast for skin repair, Mela B3 for hyperpigmentation, Anthelios for sun protection, Lipikar for dry and atopic-prone skin, and Effaclar for acne-prone skin.
Speaking at the event, Leo Stan Ekeh, Chairman of Zinox Group, said the commercial opportunities in Nigeria’s beauty and personal-care market, was enormous.
He added that the importance of bringing globally recognised brands and quality products closer to Nigerian consumers can never be overemphasised.
For Anaïs Routhiau, Business Development Manager, LID LDB SSA, the Living Lab provided an opportunity to bring La Roche-Posay’s commitment to dermatological science closer to consumers, helping them better understand their skin and the science behind the products they use.
Beyond the medical engagements, the partnership addresses a growing challenge in Nigeria’s skincare market: access to genuine products and reliable health information.
Through Konga Health’s distribution and e-commerce infrastructure, consumers can access authentic L’Oréal Dermatological Beauty products through an authorised channel, reducing exposure to counterfeit products and unreliable sellers.
The initiative underscores the growing role of digital commerce in mobile health, particularly in connecting consumers to specialised healthcare products and professional guidance beyond conventional hospital settings.
Other personalities at the event included Prince Nnamdi Ekeh, CEO of Konga Group; Mrs Chioma Ekeh, Group CEO of TD Africa; Yvonne Enwerem, Vice-President of Konga Health; and representatives of L’Oréal Dermatological Beauty.
Also present were actor Osas Ighodaro, who served as Chief Living Lab Officer; health educator Dr Chinonso Egemba, popularly known as Aproko Doctor; media personality Mimi Onalaja; and beauty entrepreneur Subuola Oyeleye.
The collaboration highlights how the convergence of digital retail, medical expertise and consumer education can strengthen access to dermatological healthcare while building trust in Nigeria’s expanding beauty and personal-care market.
