title: FG plans grain release to crash food prices
description:
The Federal Government has announced plans to release grains purchased and stored under the Bank of Agriculture’s Guaranteed Minimum Price programme into the market to increase food supply and prevent excessive increases in commodity prices.
The government also disclosed plans to distribute three mi
content:
The Federal Government has announced plans to release grains purchased and stored under the Bank of Agriculture’s Guaranteed Minimum Price programme into the market to increase food supply and prevent excessive increases in commodity prices.

The government also disclosed plans to distribute three million bags of fertiliser within the next month as part of measures to reduce farmers’ production costs and improve food availability across the country.

The Minister of Agriculture and Food Security, Abubakar Kyari, announced the measures on Wednesday during the presentation of the 2026 Wet Season Agricultural Performance Survey Report in Abuja.

According to a statement issued by the ministry, Kyari said the release of stored agricultural produce would form part of the government’s strategy to stabilise food prices while protecting farmers’ incomes.

“The same crops that we have that were stored under the guaranteed minimum price programme under the Bank of Agriculture will be released very soon to stabilise the market prices,” the minister said.

He disclosed that the government would announce the modalities for distributing the commodities, although he did not specify the quantity of grains available for release or the proposed distribution date.

Kyari explained that increased agricultural productivity, expanded cultivated land and improved access to farming inputs were expected to ease pressure on food prices.

He said a comparison of commodity prices between 2025 and 2026 indicated reductions in the prices of some agricultural products, particularly maize and dairy products.

“Just within the one year, we have seen a drop in dairy, maize and so forth that has come down,” he said.

The minister disclosed that the Presidential Fertiliser Initiative was preparing to release three million bags of fertiliser within the next month, following an intervention announced by Vice President Kashim Shettima.

He explained that the initiative would help reduce production costs and encourage farmers to expand cultivation.

Kyari also highlighted the National Agricultural Development Fund and the recapitalisation of the Bank of Agriculture as measures intended to improve farmers’ access to financing.

He said the Guaranteed Minimum Price programme provided farmers with a market for their produce, encouraging agricultural production while supporting price stability.

The minister attributed the expansion of cultivated farmland partly to improved security, explaining that military operations had enabled farmers to return to previously inaccessible agricultural areas.

On mechanisation, Kyari disclosed that the government had deployed 2,000 tractors, while deliveries under the second phase of the programme were expected within two to three months.

He also announced growing investment interest in agricultural processing, including cocoa, sesame, cassava and cashew nuts.

According to him, the government had signed a $33m investment agreement with a Turkish company for greenhouse projects within Nigeria’s Special Agro-Industrial Processing Zones.

Meanwhile, the Executive Director of the National Agricultural Extension and Research Liaison Services, Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria, Yusuf Sani, disclosed that production of 13 out of 17 major crops assessed was projected to increase in 2026.

“Nineteen multi disciplinary teams conducted field assessments across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory between August 31 and September 6, 2026, in collaboration with state ministries of agriculture, agricultural research institutes, Agricultural Development Programmes and development partners,” Sani said.

He identified Niger as the leading rice-producing state, Kano as the largest producer of sorghum and Yobe as the leading millet-producing state.

Sani called for stronger storage facilities, improved post-harvest handling and better market access to prevent agricultural losses.

Kyari clarified that the assessment covered only wet-season production, adding that a separate dry-season survey had been commissioned to determine Nigeria’s overall agricultural output for 2026.

The announcement comes amid easing monthly food prices, although annual food inflation remains elevated.

According to the National Bureau of Statistics’ October 2026 Consumer Price Index report, released on Monday, food inflation stood at 19.13 per cent, compared with 19.59 per cent in September and 16.30 per cent in October 2025.

The post FG plans grain release to crash food prices appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Abia man arrested for allegedly killing brother
description:
The Abia State Police Command has arrested a man, Iheanyi Nwosu, for allegedly shooting his biological brother, Eze Nwosu, dead in the Amaiyi Mgbogho community, Isiala Ngwa North Local Government Area of the state.
The Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Maureen Chinaka, confirmed the arrest on Wed
content:
The Abia State Police Command has arrested a man, Iheanyi Nwosu, for allegedly shooting his biological brother, Eze Nwosu, dead in the Amaiyi Mgbogho community, Isiala Ngwa North Local Government Area of the state.

The Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Maureen Chinaka, confirmed the arrest on Wednesday, saying the suspect was apprehended on Tuesday by operatives of the Umuoba Police Division, in collaboration with community vigilantes.

“Our attention was called to it, and we rapidly responded on Tuesday as officers from the Umuoba Police Division in the Isiala Ngwa North Local Government Area of Abia State, in collaboration with community vigilantes, apprehended the suspect. Investigation is ongoing,” Chinaka said.

Community sources said the incident followed a disagreement involving the suspect’s wife and the deceased’s wife.

According to reports, Eze Nwosu, a youth leader in the community, reportedly saw his wife fleeing from the family compound and attempted to find out what had happened.

However, his brother allegedly emerged from his room with a short gun and shot him at close range in the neck, killing him instantly.

The suspect reportedly fled into the bush after realising that his brother had died, as villagers began gathering at the scene.

However, members of the community’s local security outfit, alongside other residents, reportedly combed the surrounding bushes and apprehended him at his hiding place.

He was subsequently handed over to the Umuoba Police Division for further investigation.

The community expressed grief over the incident, describing the deceased as a peaceful member of the community.

The post Abia man arrested for allegedly killing brother appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Troops kill 21 suspected ISWAP fighters in Borno
description:
… As terrorists kill five, abduct 11 in Askira-Uba



By Ndahi Marama, Maiduguri



Troops of the Joint Task Force, North East, Operation HADIN KAI, have neutralised 21 suspected Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP) fighters and injured 10 others in separate air operations around Monguno and t
content:
… As terrorists kill five, abduct 11 in Askira-Uba

By Ndahi Marama, Maiduguri

Troops of the Joint Task Force, North East, Operation HADIN KAI, have neutralised 21 suspected Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP) fighters and injured 10 others in separate air operations around Monguno and the South Lake Chad area of Borno State.

The military operations, conducted between November 16 and 17, 2026, came amid renewed attacks by insurgents in parts of the state.

In a separate incident, suspected terrorists on Tuesday invaded Pubaku village in Rumirgo Ward, Askira-Uba Local Government Area of Southern Borno, killing five residents and abducting 11 others, including 10 women.

The attackers were also said to have set several residential buildings and shops ablaze, forcing residents to flee into the bush for safety.

In a statement issued on Wednesday, Acting Media Information Officer, Headquarters Joint Task Force North East, Operation HADIN KAI, Captain Mohammed Goni, said the military air strikes followed intelligence reports of terrorist movements around Monguno and the South Lake Chad area.

He said the first operation was launched after intelligence indicated that ISWAP fighters were advancing towards Monguno.

According to him, an unmanned aerial vehicle deployed for surveillance identified the fighters moving along a bush path northeast of Monguno, prompting a precision air strike that neutralised seven insurgents, including members of the group’s Improvised Explosive Device network.

Goni said further assessment of the operation showed that ABBA BOMMA, identified as a key IED team expert, was incapacitated, while four other fighters sustained severe injuries.

He disclosed that a second operation at Arinna, in the South Lake Chad area, dealt a significant blow to the group’s leadership and operational structure.

Among those killed, according to the military, was MALLAM SHARKI, a member of the group’s Shura Council and Amirul Amniya (Provost Commander).

Also neutralised was ABU SAAD, identified as the Qaid of Sabon Tumbu, alongside 12 other fighters, while five insurgents sustained severe injuries.

Several motorcycles belonging to the terrorists were also destroyed during the operation.

Goni said the two operations resulted in the neutralisation of 21 ISWAP fighters and injuries to 10 others, adding that the strikes had weakened the group’s leadership structure, disrupted its IED network and degraded its operational capabilities.

He reaffirmed the Theatre Command’s commitment to sustaining military operations against terrorists until lasting peace and normalcy were restored across the North-East.

The military also urged residents to continue providing security agencies with credible and timely information.

Meanwhile, residents of Pubaku confirmed the attack on their community, saying the assailants operated without resistance before fleeing after killing five people, abducting 11 residents and destroying property.

A resident, Yakubu Pubagu, who spoke with our correspondent on Wednesday, described the incident as devastating.

“Yes, there was a devastating attack on our community (Pubagu) on Tuesday, where five of our people were killed, 10 women and one man abducted after destroying many houses,” he said.

The attack left the community largely deserted as residents fled to nearby bushes for safety.

The incident came barely 48 hours after suspected insurgents reportedly fired several mortar rounds targeting the Senate Chief Whip, Senator Mohammed Tahir Monguno, former Borno State Governor, Maina Maaji Lawan, and other stakeholders during a political mobilisation visit to Kukawa Local Government Area in support of All Progressives Congress candidates.

The post Troops kill 21 suspected ISWAP fighters in Borno appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: School records success in WAEC, NECO exams
description: ST Columbanus Secondary School, Ikwen in Obot Akara Local Government Area of Akwa Ibom State, has recorded 100 per cent success in the West African Senior School Certificate Examination and the National Examinations Council examination, consolidating its reputation as one of the leading schools in t
content:
ST Columbanus Secondary School, Ikwen in Obot Akara Local Government Area of Akwa Ibom State, has recorded 100 per cent success in the West African Senior School Certificate Examination and the National Examinations Council examination, consolidating its reputation as one of the leading schools in the state.

The school management said all the candidates presented for the examinations obtained the required credits, including English Language and Mathematics, qualifying them for admission into tertiary institutions.

Speakng to journalists on Tuesday in Uyo, The School Principal, Rev. Fr. Emem Umoren, attributed the feat to disciplined academic programmes, dedicated teachers, regular assessments and effective monitoring of students from SS1 to SS3.

He said, “Preparation for external examinations begins on the first day students enter the school. It started with intensive revision, mock examinations and exposure to examination techniques to build confidence and competence.”

He said the 100 per cent record was not accidental, but the outcome of strategic planning, teamwork and a culture that demands hard work, integrity and intellectual curiosity from both staff and students.

”In a society where quality education remains essential for national development, St. Columbanus Secondary School, Ikwen, stands out as a shining example of what commitment, discipline and effective leadership can achieve.

”The school’s sustained excellence in WAEC, NECO and JAMB examinations serves as evidence that quality education can flourish when visionary leadership, dedicated teachers, disciplined students and supportive parents work together towards a common goal”, he explained.

He added that students of the school have also continued to record impressive performances in the Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board examination, with many securing admission into competitive courses in universities across the country.

‎‎Umoren also added that the school has organised special JAMB preparatory classes, computer-based test training and intensive tutorials to ensure that students are familiar with the CBT format and the demands of the examination.

‎‎”We train our students to be confident in the CBT environment. Many students fail JAMB not because they are not intelligent, but because they are not familiar with the system. In St. Columbanus, we address that early,” he said.

‎‎A recent graduate, Ubong Essien, who scored over 280 in JAMB, said the school’s early exposure to JAMB questions and computer-based test training made the examination easy for him and his classmates.

‎‎”St. Columbanus is a school where you don’t just pass, you excel. The teachers push you, the principal monitors you, and the environment compels you to take your studies seriously.

‎‎”From SS1, we were already being exposed to JAMB questions. By SS3, it was easy. The teachers were always there to guide us. I am grateful to St. Columbanus,” he said.

‎‎Parents have described the results as a justification of their confidence in the school, with Mrs. Aniedi Akpan saying her first child passed WAEC with excellent grades and is now studying medicine at the university.

‎‎A community leader, Chief Monday Udoh, said the school’s emphasis on discipline had helped to check truancy, cultism and examination malpractice, making it a model for other schools in Obot Akara.

The post School records success in WAEC, NECO exams appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Local renewable energy financing hits N450bn, says REA
description:
Nigeria’s local financing for renewable energy projects has reached N450bn following a N100bn financing agreement between the Rural Electrification Agency and Jaiz Bank to expand electricity access in underserved communities.
The agreement, sealed through a Memorandum of Understanding at the REA hea
content:
Nigeria’s local financing for renewable energy projects has reached N450bn following a N100bn financing agreement between the Rural Electrification Agency and Jaiz Bank to expand electricity access in underserved communities.

The agreement, sealed through a Memorandum of Understanding at the REA headquarters and announced in a statement issued on Wednesday, is expected to provide additional funding for renewable energy developers and help accelerate the delivery of electricity projects across the country.

The partnership brings Jaiz Bank into a growing pool of local financial institutions supporting the agency’s renewable energy financing drive, which already includes Lotus Bank, FCMB, Stanbic IBTC and Alpha Morgan.

The statement read, “Nigeria’s local financing for renewable energy projects has reached N450 billion following the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding between the Rural Electrification Agenc and Jaiz Bank for a N100 billion financing facility aimed at accelerating electricity access in underserved communities across the country.”

Speaking at the signing ceremony, the Managing Director of REA, Abba Aliyu, said access to domestic capital was essential to sustaining the growth of Nigeria’s renewable energy sector and achieving the country’s electricity access targets.

He welcomed Jaiz Bank’s participation, noting that the partnership would strengthen the agency’s efforts to mobilise local financing for renewable energy projects.

“I would like to say that you joined at the right time, even though we already have local financing arrangements with Lotus Bank, FCMB, Stanbic IBTC and Alpha Morgan. We are happy to have Jaiz Bank on board, as access to financing is key to reaching this N450bn milestone,” Aliyu said.

He said the global transition towards cleaner energy, reinforced by international climate commitments, was creating greater opportunities for renewable energy investments, particularly solar power.

Aliyu noted that from the Paris Agreement to COP30, countries had continued to accelerate efforts towards carbon neutrality, with renewable energy increasingly becoming a competitive source of electricity.

He said electricity was also assuming a more strategic role in the global economy, moving beyond its traditional function as a basic utility to become the foundation of technological advancement and intelligence.

Citing rising electricity demand in the United States, China, India and South Africa, the REA chief said global electricity demand was projected to reach 18 petawatt-hours by 2050.

Against this background, he said Nigeria needed to expand its electricity infrastructure and attract more investments into decentralised renewable energy solutions to close its access gap.

Aliyu said the agency had identified seven key areas requiring attention to bridge the country’s electricity access divide.

He also commended President Bola Tinubu for approving the Distributed Access through Renewable Energy Scale-up project, describing it as the world’s largest publicly funded renewable energy initiative, supported by the World Bank.

According to him, the programme reflects the Federal Government’s commitment to extending reliable electricity to communities that remain underserved by the national grid.

Aliyu stressed that the agency’s work went beyond mobilising financing, saying it was also delivering electricity infrastructure in different parts of the country.

He cited recently commissioned projects at the Federal University of Lafia, which has a 1.6-megawatt interconnected mini-grid; Oke-Oyi, with a 581-kilowatt-peak system; and Ballagaza and Marayar Rogo in Warawa Local Government Area of Kano State, with a combined 265kWp capacity.

The projects were recently commissioned by the Minister of Power, Joseph Tegbe.

In his remarks, the Managing Director of Jaiz Bank, Haruna Musa, commended President Tinubu and the REA management for their efforts to expand electricity access through renewable energy.

The post Local renewable energy financing hits N450bn, says REA appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: CBN, NNPC move to tighten oil revenues oversight
description:
The Central Bank of Nigeria and the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited have signed a Memorandum of Understanding to strengthen oversight of oil and gas revenues, improve foreign exchange inflows and ensure transparent remittances into government accounts.
The agreement, signed on Wednesday
content:
The Central Bank of Nigeria and the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited have signed a Memorandum of Understanding to strengthen oversight of oil and gas revenues, improve foreign exchange inflows and ensure transparent remittances into government accounts.

The agreement, signed on Wednesday at the CBN headquarters in Abuja, will also facilitate energy financing, automate payment systems and strengthen regulatory compliance between the two institutions.

Speaking at the ceremony, CBN Governor, Olayemi Cardoso, said the partnership would improve the management and settlement of oil proceeds, which remain critical to Nigeria’s fiscal revenue and foreign exchange stability.

“As custodian of NNPC Limited’s key operational foreign currency accounts, the Central Bank of Nigeria plays a critical role in ensuring the timely, secure and transparent settlement of oil and gas proceeds into the Federation Account and other designated government accounts,” Cardoso said.

He explained that predictable oil revenue inflows were essential to maintaining monetary stability, particularly during periods of economic volatility.

“Our continued collaboration in efficient account management, funds transfer and liquidity support directly contributes to macroeconomic stability by ensuring the availability of revenue to achieve fiscal mandates and predictable inflows into the foreign exchange markets,” he added.

Cardoso disclosed that the agreement would cover the monetisation of hydrocarbon assets, faster operational approvals, payment automation, cybersecurity, regulatory alignment and information sharing.

He also announced plans to attract international financial institutions to support Nigeria’s gas development through appropriate financing arrangements.

“The CBN is well positioned to collaborate with NNPC Limited by exercising its convening power to attract global institutions with financial structures that can help develop Nigeria’s vast natural gas resources,” he said.

The governor clarified that the agreement formalised an existing relationship, noting that the CBN, NNPC and other oil-sector institutions had been meeting regularly to resolve operational challenges.

In her welcome remarks, the CBN Deputy Governor, Operations, Emem Usoro, disclosed that Nigeria’s gross external reserves had exceeded $55bn, supported by higher oil production and sustained diaspora remittances.

“Today, while our gross external reserves exceed $55bn, supported by higher oil production and sustained diaspora remittances, we are confident that this MoU will help preserve and strengthen our reserves through improved export earnings and foreign exchange inflows,” she said.

Usoro explained that the agreement would establish clearer governance arrangements for international trade, energy financing, liquidity support and risk management.

The Group Chief Executive Officer of NNPC Limited, Bayo Ojulari, said the partnership would strengthen financial discipline and help the company raise capital using its assets and balance sheet.

Ojulari also revealed that NNPC faced severe financial difficulties when he assumed office in April 2025, including weak liquidity, troubled projects, substantial loans and refinery challenges.

“At the starting point, NNPC was in a very challenging situation. Our liquidity position was extremely weak, and the majority of our projects were heavily challenged,” he disclosed.

He explained that management subsequently reviewed proposed asset divestments and existing loans to address the company’s financial difficulties.

According to him, the agreement will establish joint steering and working committees to monitor implementation against agreed performance indicators.

“We are here not just for the optics. We are here to build a working partnership that delivers results,” Ojulari said.

Also speaking, NNPC’s Group Chief Financial Officer, Adedapo Segun, said the agreement would replace the previous practice of handling financial issues through irregular, transaction-specific arrangements.

“For too long, NNPC Limited and the CBN have cooperated on an ad hoc basis, transaction by transaction and crisis by crisis. That model will no longer serve Nigeria,” he said.

Segun explained that improved coordination would help attract the investment needed to increase Nigeria’s crude oil production from 1.8 million barrels per day to three million barrels per day.

The post CBN, NNPC move to tighten oil revenues oversight appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Eight-hour gridlock paralyses Lagos-Ibadan Expressway
description:
Motorists and commuters were stranded for several hours on Wednesday as the resumption of construction work on a pedestrian bridge at the Aseese area of the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway triggered a massive traffic gridlock.
PUNCH Metro correspondents monitoring the situation gathered that the traffic str
content:
Motorists and commuters were stranded for several hours on Wednesday as the resumption of construction work on a pedestrian bridge at the Aseese area of the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway triggered a massive traffic gridlock.

PUNCH Metro correspondents monitoring the situation gathered that the traffic stretched from the Redemption Camp area to Asese bus stop for motorists heading towards Lagos, while those travelling from Lagos towards Ogun State were held up from the Long Bridge area to Aseese.

One of our correspondents, who boarded a commercial vehicle from Ibadan shortly after 11 am, did not arrive in Magboro until about 5.30 pm. Another motorist lamented spending eight hours travelling from Mowe to Magboro.

The congestion began building up shortly after the Redeemed Christian Church of God camp area, where the correspondent encountered an almost complete standstill.

The gridlock was attributed to ongoing construction work around the Asese axis of the expressway.

Frustrated by the prolonged delay, several commuters abandoned their vehicles and trekked several kilometres to their destinations.

Commercial motorcycle operators also took advantage of the situation to increase their fares, with one rider demanding as much as N6,000 from a passenger travelling from Mowe to Ibafo.

Our correspondents also observed that some motorists resorted to driving against the flow of traffic, while an armed security officer was seen leading a convoy of new vehicles through the wrong lane around The PUNCH Place area of the expressway.

Speaking with one of our correspondents, a motorist, Ifeanyi Chukwuebuka, expressed frustration over the decision to carry out the bridge construction during the day, saying it had worsened traffic congestion.

He noted that the gridlock had disrupted movement for motorists and pedestrians, particularly as travel activities were increasing ahead of the festive season.

Chukwuebuka added that the prolonged traffic had significantly affected his daily income and his ability to provide for his family.

He said, “The money that I am supposed to make today has been reduced because I have to park and stop work due to the traffic. This will affect me as a family man.

“They are not supposed to be constructing a bridge at this time when people are going home, and the movement is high.”

He urged the government to ensure that such construction works were scheduled for nighttime, after most commuters had returned home, rather than during peak travel periods.

Another motorist, who identified himself as Mr Kabiru, lamented spending several hours in the gridlock.

“I have been in the traffic for more than two hours. It is unfortunate that we have to go through this every time,” he said.

He called on the government to address the recurring traffic congestion on the expressway, adding, “Something should be done about this recurring traffic anytime there is construction work on this expressway.”

A pedestrian, who identified himself as Confidence, said he resorted to trekking because of the traffic.

“I had to trek because of the traffic situation. I am coming from the Warrwa side and heading to Magboro,” he said.

When contacted on possible alternative measures to minimise the gridlock while the construction lasted, the acting Controller of the Federal Ministry of Works in Ogun State, Adeleye Olajide, said the installation of the bridge could not be avoided.

“There’s no two ways about it now; they have to launch the bridge,” he said.

He explained that the government was working towards completing the bridges before the festive period.

“This is better done now than waiting for the festive period,” he added.

Meanwhile, the spokesperson for the Ogun State Traffic Compliance and Enforcement Agency, Babatunde Akinbiyi, urged motorists to exercise caution, noting that the temporary traffic diversion would last four days.

Akinbiyi said in a statement on Wednesday that the Federal Ministry of Works, in collaboration with CBC Construction Company, would carry out the pedestrian bridge installation.

He explained that vehicles inbound to Lagos would be temporarily diverted towards the Lagos carriageway at Asese before rejoining their normal route at a designated exit point opposite Christ Embassy.

He stated, “The general public, particularly the motoring public, plying the Lagos–Ibadan Expressway, are hereby informed that the Federal Ministry of Works, in collaboration with CBC Construction Company, will undertake a temporary traffic diversion at Asese, opposite Christ Embassy, to facilitate the installation of a pedestrian bridge across the expressway, from Wednesday, November 18, 2026, through Sunday, November 22, 2026.”

Akinbiyi advised motorists to approach the construction zone with caution, exercise patience and obey traffic instructions from officials.

He added that TRACE and the Federal Road Safety Corps would deploy personnel to the affected section to manage traffic, minimise delays and ensure the safety of road users.

“The motoring public is hereby urged to cooperate with the traffic management agencies and bear with the temporary inconvenience occasioned by this essential infrastructure development,” he added.

The post Eight-hour gridlock paralyses Lagos-Ibadan Expressway appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: ‘NECA awards help firms identify operational gaps’
description:
The Nigeria Employers’ Consultative Association has stated that the NECA’s Employers’ Excellence Award helps companies assess their operations with a view to knowing which areas need attention.
The Director-General of NECA, Adewale-Smatt Oyerinde, stated this on Wednesday in Lagos while speaking dur
content:
The Nigeria Employers’ Consultative Association has stated that the NECA’s Employers’ Excellence Award helps companies assess their operations with a view to knowing which areas need attention.

The Director-General of NECA, Adewale-Smatt Oyerinde, stated this on Wednesday in Lagos while speaking during a press conference ahead of the 2026 NECA’s Employers’ Excellence Award, billed for next week.

Oyerinde, who was represented at the event by the Director, Social and Labour Affairs at NECA, Mrs Adenike Ajala, stressed that the award helps companies assess even their internal processes and governance structures, and then benchmark against what is happening in the economy.

Oyerinde stated that NECA would continue to advocate for an environment that enables businesses to carry out their operations. “And that is one of the reasons why we have been able to sustain this initiative. Because businesses have been able to survive due to the advocacy that we do, the interventions that we make on their behalf, whatever business issue that they have.”

“One of the things that we also want companies to take away is for them to be able to see the gaps in their processes. And for them to be able to address those gaps so that when they apply, they are able to meet that. And that is one of the things that encourage companies to apply every year. Because it allows them to assess even their internal processes, their governance structures, and then benchmark against what is happening in the economy,” Oyerinde said.

According to him, some companies apply just to be able to check what they are doing well and what they are not doing well. “Some people will tell you, I have seen it, I am not doing well, I have to go back, I have to check my internal processes and then I will come back to apply. So it is an assessment for what you do as an organisation and you also get the reports.”

He added that out of about 200 applications received for this year’s award, only 128 had been able to scale through to the point where they were now being assessed.

Speaking on the award, Oyerinde emphasised that over the years, the NECA Employers’ Excellence Awards had evolved into a distinguished platform for celebrating organisations and employers on merit, whose leadership, enterprise, innovation and workplace practices contribute meaningfully to national development.

He reiterated that the awards reflect NECA’s enduring commitment to promoting a business environment in which enterprise success is matched by responsible employment practices, investment in people, respect for workers’ rights, innovation and corporate responsibility.

The post ‘NECA awards help firms identify operational gaps’ appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: NSChE advocates private sector-led revival of Ajaokuta Steel Company
description:
The Nigerian Society of Chemical Engineers, a subsidiary of the Nigerian Society of Engineers has called for a private sector-led revival of the Ajaokuta Steel Company Limited in order to save the country from further revenue losses.
The NSChE said a transparent, competitive and commercially discipl
content:
The Nigerian Society of Chemical Engineers, a subsidiary of the Nigerian Society of Engineers has called for a private sector-led revival of the Ajaokuta Steel Company Limited in order to save the country from further revenue losses.

The NSChE said a transparent, competitive and commercially disciplined revival of Ajaokuta Steel Company Limited would strengthen domestic manufacturing, infrastructure, engineering capability and employment.

The society said Nigeria loses $4 billion annually to steel imports, pointing out that the revival of the Ajaokuta Steel Company would bridge the gap and cater for her annual steel demand estimated at about 10 million tonnes.

National President of NSChE, Engr. Bayo Olarewaju-Alo, disclosed this during a news briefing in Port Harcout as part of activities marking the body’s 56th International Conference and Annual General Meeting and Exhibition with the theme ‘Advancing Nigeria’s Industrial Revolution Through Gas Valorisation And Ai-Driven Engineering Imperatives’.

Olarewaju-Alo noted that while private ownership can restore Ajaokuta, ownership change alone would not deliver a viable steel industry, insisting on a credible investment framework that secures raw materials, energy, logistics, financing and markets.

He stated, “The Nigerian Society of Chemical Engineers (NSChE) calls for a transparent, competitive and commercially disciplined revival of Ajaokuta Steel Company Limited. Our position is clear: private ownership can restore Ajaokuta, but ownership change alone will not deliver a viable steel industry.

“Success requires a credible investment framework that secures raw materials, energy, logistics, financing and markets. A Strategic Industrial Imperative Nigeria’s annual steel demand is estimated at about 10 million tonnes, against local production of roughly 1.2 million tonnes, largely from scrap-based operations.

“The shortfall contributes to an estimated US$4 billion annual steel import bill. Reviving Ajaokuta would strengthen domestic manufacturing, infrastructure, engineering capability and employment while conserving foreign exchange.

While noting that technical assessments suggest that the complex’s core structures remain viable despite ageing equipment and prolonged neglect, the NSChE national president said: “Domestic iron ore, natural gas and flux materials provide a strong resource base.

“However, imported coking coal, ferroalloys and specialised refractories expose the project to foreign exchange risks. Inadequate power, ports and transport infrastructure remain major constraints.”

“The NSChE supports majority ownership by a Nigerian consortium or conglomerate—not a foreign majority owner—with strategic technical partners and a minority federal government stake.

“This structure should align investment with operational performance while safeguarding national interests. Restructuring must prioritise steel supply to Nigeria’s industrial economy,”

While calling for urgent action, Olarewaju-Alo said: “A successful revival would reduce steel imports, conserve foreign exchange, create direct and indirect jobs, stimulate mining, power, transport and engineering services, and strengthen local manufacturing and technical skills.

“NSChE urges policymakers, investors, financial institutions and industry stakeholders to move from debate to disciplined execution: privatize transparently; establish a clean investment vehicle; secure ore, gas, power and logistics through enforceable contracts; finance for the long term; and keep technology choice open.

“Ajaokuta must become a productive industrial asset whose output serves Nigeria’s development. The time for a private sector-led revival is now.

Recall that the Ajaokuta Steel Company Limited is Nigeria’s largest steel mill, located on a 24,000-hectare site in Ajaokuta, Kogi State; established in 1979 under President Shehu Shagari with Russian/Soviet backing as a foundational industrialization project.

Although the complex reached advanced stage of technical completion by 1994, it has remained largely moribund and incomplete for decades due to management challenges, funding hurdles, and infrastructure delays.

title: Farmers’ quest for quick weed control sustains illegal use of banned agrochemicals — NAFDAC
description:
…Warns of health risks from chemical residuesBy Cynthia Alo



Farmers’ preference for fast-acting agrochemicals is sustaining the illegal importation and use of banned chemicals in Nigeria, the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control, NAFDAC, has said.The agency said some farme
content:
…Warns of health risks from chemical residues
By Cynthia Alo

Farmers’ preference for fast-acting agrochemicals is sustaining the illegal importation and use of banned chemicals in Nigeria, the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control, NAFDAC, has said.
The agency said some farmers continued to patronise prohibited products because of their effectiveness in killing weeds within a short period, despite the potential health risks to human life associated with those chemicals.
Director, North West Zone, NAFDAC, Dadi Nantim Mullah, disclosed this in an exclusive interview with Vanguard Agrobiz in Lagos.
Mullah explained that the increasing demand for food, driven by population growth and the expansion of food businesses, had heightened the need to produce and preserve food on a larger scale, leading to greater reliance on agrochemicals.
He said the need to store food for longer periods, particularly as restaurants and other food businesses catered to more consumers, had made preservation increasingly important.
According to him, the expansion of farm sizes had also increased farmers’ need for chemicals to support production process.
He stated: “Because of explosion in population, people need to have food stored longer than they normally would.
“For instance, if before, we can buy tomatoes, cook it and eat same day, but now, we have restaurants wanting to have much more tomatoes to cook for many more people. So, people need to grind it, preserve it, and then reach more people.
“That process looks simple, but it requires a lot of efforts which has to be supported by some conventional or unconventional applications.
‘‘The farmer who was using half an acre, but has suddenly expanded to 10 acres, would need increased aid to meet the increased production demand.
“So, chemicals came in to help, whether they are pesticides, herbicides, or whatsoever it is that can help to produce more, preserve more.”
However, he warned that the increased use of agrochemicals could expose consumers to harmful chemical residues when farmers and other users applied inappropriate products or exceeded prescribed quantities.
Mullah specifically identified paraquat-containing products among the banned chemicals still being brought into Nigeria illegally, despite the agency’s prohibition.
He said farmers continued to favour the chemical because of its rapid weed-killing effect, with a single application reportedly drying grass within 24 hours.
He said: “If you don’t use the correct quantity, or you don’t use the chemical that is appropriate for the type of food that you want to preserve, it will eventually affect the consumer. We have what we call pesticide residues.
“Some of them are banned already by NAFDAC, so that we will not use them. I’ll give you an example with paraquat-containing pesticides.
“They are brought in. Farmers love that chemical because if you spray it on your farm, within 24 hours grass is dried, but it retains and it causes cancer. And that impact is not good for the health of the consumer.”
According to him, NAFDAC banned the chemical about two years ago, but illegal importation has continued because of its demand.
He also listed atrazine among chemicals banned by the agency, urging farmers not to select agrochemicals simply because they appear more effective or are being used by other farmers.
He said: “NAFDAC banned those type of chemicals two years ago, but people are still bringing them in illegally.
“Don’t use any chemical you don’t know what it is meant for. Don’t apply it simply because it looks good, or somebody else used it. Ensure you follow NAFDAC-approved guidelines in using these chemicals to preserve food for the public.”
Mullah explained that NAFDAC has maintained daily inspections at borders and facilities to check the importation of prohibited chemicals and ensure that approved agrochemicals are used according to prescribed guidelines.
He said: “First, those that are impacting on our health, cancer-causing, NAFDAC has banned, and one of them I mentioned is paraquat. There are others—atrazine and all those ones that have been banned by NAFDAC so that we will not use them in the country.
“We conduct inspections at the borders and in facilities to ensure those who are using or importing the ones that are approved, they are using it in appropriate prescribed guidelines.”
He added that the agency conducts daily market inspections, withdrawing and destroying products found to be expired or improperly stored.
“We go out every day in NAFDAC. Every single day we go out. We mop out the ones we see in the markets or in the stores or sales outlets,” he said.
Mullah urged farmers to follow approved guidelines in selecting and applying agrochemicals, stressing that the drive to increase food production and preserve supplies should not compromise food safety and consumers’ health.

The post Farmers’ quest for quick weed control sustains illegal use of banned agrochemicals — NAFDAC appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Delta kingdom seeks Oborevwori’s intervention over disputed land
description: Idjerhe Kingdom in Ethiope West Local Government Area of Delta State has appealed to the Governor of Delta State, Sheriff Oborevwori, to urgently facilitate an impartial investigation into claims between the kingdom and its neighbouring Mosogar over the rightful ownership of the site of the 1998 Jes
content:
Idjerhe Kingdom in Ethiope West Local Government Area of Delta State has appealed to the Governor of Delta State, Sheriff Oborevwori, to urgently facilitate an impartial investigation into claims between the kingdom and its neighbouring Mosogar over the rightful ownership of the site of the 1998 Jesse fire disaster incident.

In a statement signed by its Crown Otota (Iyasere), Chief Uzzi Onosia James Obriki, and made available to journalist on Monday, he said that the intervention would help establish the facts, prevent unnecessary communal tension and preserve the longstanding relationship between the two kingdoms.

Idjerhe also urged traditional rulers, community leaders, families and youths in both kingdoms to “exercise restraint”, warning against unilateral actions and inflammatory statements capable of worsening the disagreement.

”Our desire is to see the truth established, justice served and the good relationship between our communities preserved”, Idjerhe Kingdom stated.

The development followed a press briefing addressed on October 30, 2026, by the Otota of Mosogar Kingdom, Chief Napoleon Emefe, insisting that the location of the 1998 Jesse fire disaster belongs to its ancestral families.

Emefe had stated that the identification of the disaster location as Atiwor during Idjerhe’s October 17 memorial ceremony was “a misrepresentation of historical identity”.

‎It would be recalled that the Jesse Fire Disaster occurred on October 17, 1998 when a pipeline explosion resulted in the deaths of more than 1,000 people. The tragedy has remained a major historical scar on the affected communities, with surviving relatives and residents continuing to seek justice and proper recognition for the victims.

‎A memorial ceremony was held on October 17, 2026, by the Ovie of Idjerhe Kingdom, His Majesty, King Monday Obukowho Whiskey, Udurhie I, alongside other indigenes and stakeholders at the disaster site where participants remembered the victims, offered prayers and made renewed calls for government support and a national monument in their honour.

‎Mosogar maintained that the disputed land belonged to its ancestral families, arguing that the historical administrative relationship between the two kingdoms did not automatically establish Idjerhe’s ownership of every parcel of land within the former Idjerhe clan.

‎Idjerhe Kingdom, in a swift reaction, however rejected Mosogar Kingdom’s claim to ownership of the site, insisting that the location falls within its ancestral territory and demanding an impartial examination of historical land records to resolve the dispute.

‎According to Idjerhe Kingdom in the statement signed by its Crown Otota (Iyasere), Chief Uzzi Onosia James Obriki, “the disaster occurred at Atiwor Community in Great Idjerhe Kingdom”, challenging Mosogar’s position that the land belongs to the Origheyegha-Omene family of Orokpokpor-Akpobome community.

‎Chief Obriki, responding on behalf of the Idjerhe Traditional Council, maintained that “the historical ownership of the land could not be determined by geographical proximity or the existence of a neighbouring settlement”.

‎Obriki declared that “the disputed territory forms part of the ancestral holdings of the Ekpah family of Odokpor, one of the eight recognised quarters of Idjerhe Central”.

‎”The family had owned and occupied an extensive area of farmland historically known as Enasoh in Atiwor for more than 200 years, long before the emergence of Orokpokpor settlement”, Obriki added.

‎He argued that the settlement of Orokpokpor emerged less than 60 years ago, particularly around the period of the construction of Garmon Bridge, maintaining that its historical development should be examined alongside the ancestral records of the Ekpah family.

The post Delta kingdom seeks Oborevwori’s intervention over disputed land appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Enugu guard to die by hanging for murder
description:
An Enugu State High Court has sentenced a security guard, Shuibu Mohammed, to death by hanging for stabbing a man, Njoku Nwabueze, to death with a dagger at Soil Plaza, Emene, Enugu.
Justice Kenneth Ikechukwu Okpe, in a judgment delivered on Wednesday in Charge No. E/66C/2022, convicted Mohammed of
content:
An Enugu State High Court has sentenced a security guard, Shuibu Mohammed, to death by hanging for stabbing a man, Njoku Nwabueze, to death with a dagger at Soil Plaza, Emene, Enugu.

Justice Kenneth Ikechukwu Okpe, in a judgment delivered on Wednesday in Charge No. E/66C/2022, convicted Mohammed of murder, contrary to Section 274(1) of the Criminal Code, Cap 30, Vol. II, Laws of Enugu State, 2004.

“I hold that the prosecution proved beyond reasonable doubt that the defendant intentionally killed the deceased, Njoku Nwabueze. Accordingly, the defendant, Shuibu Mohammed, is hereby convicted on this charge of murder,” the judge held.

He subsequently sentenced the defendant to death by hanging, adding, “May God have mercy on his soul.”

The charge stated that Mohammed murdered Nwabueze on or about October 1, 2021, at Soil Plaza, Emene, by stabbing him with a dagger.

The information was filed on April 14, 2022, by Nnaemeka Ngene, then a legal officer with the Enugu State Ministry of Justice. However, the case was prosecuted from the outset by C. N. Avah, a director in the ministry.

Following several adjournments, the defendant took his plea on April 24, 2024, while the trial commenced on July 17, 2024.

The prosecution called two police witnesses, Inspectors Amorha Nnaemeka and Chidi Opara, and tendered photographs of the deceased, the defendant’s statements to the police and a statement by the deceased’s brother, Njoku Onyekachi.

The defence called only Mohammed, who denied killing or quarrelling with the deceased.

In his judgment, Justice Okpe held that the prosecution had established the death of Nwabueze, dismissing the defence’s argument that an autopsy report was necessary to prove the cause of death.

“There are instances where the cause of death is so obvious that the requirement for a medical report to prove the offence of murder will be dispensed with,” he held, citing Oladapo v. State [2020] 7 NWLR (Pt. 1723) 238.

The judge also dismissed the defence’s objection to the evidence of the two police witnesses, who testified that they saw the deceased’s lifeless body, photographed it, observed a bleeding injury and later identified the corpse at the mortuary.

“Contrary to the submission of counsel for the defendant, these are not hearsay evidence. Rather, they are evidence of what PW1 and PW2 saw in the course of their investigation,” he held.

On the confessional statements, Justice Okpe noted that although they were recorded at different locations and on different dates, they were essentially consistent.

“At no point, not even in open court, did the defendant raise any issue on the voluntariness of his confessional statements. So, the statements were voluntarily made,” he held, adding that the confessions were direct and positive on the killing.

The court also relied on circumstantial evidence, particularly the defendant’s disappearance from his duty post after the incident and his subsequent concealment at Eke Obinagu until he was lured out.

“If the defendant did not kill the deceased and did not even fight with him, why did he go into hiding?” the judge queried.

Defence counsel, C. C. Azubuike, had argued that the court could not rely on the confessional statements because they were obtained without compliance with Section 17(1), (2), (3) and (4) of the Administration of Criminal Justice Law of Enugu State, 2017, which provides for video recording or the presence of a lawyer during the recording of confessional statements.

Counsel cited Charles v. The State of Lagos (2023) 13 NWLR (Pt. 1901) 213.

However, Justice Okpe dismissed the argument, holding that where there was no allegation of oppression or involuntariness, non-compliance with the ACJL provision would not automatically render a confession inadmissible. He relied on Iwah v. State (2026) LPELR-83365 (SC).

The judge also rejected the defence’s argument on an illiterate jurat, noting that the defendant testified in English without an interpreter. He equally dismissed the claim that the statements were unsigned, holding that they bore the defendant’s thumbprints, which he did not deny.

On the issue of intent, Justice Okpe held that the use of a dagger to stab the deceased in the heart region demonstrated that the defendant knew, or ought to have known, that death or grievous bodily harm was a probable consequence.

“The defendant intentionally pierced the deceased at his heart region and offered no help and no assistance,” he held.

Although the defendant did not raise the defences of provocation and self-defence, the court considered both on its own motion because of the capital nature of the charge.

On provocation, the judge held that even if the defendant had been provoked, “his mode of resentment was not proportionate to the provocation occasioned.”

He also rejected self-defence, noting that the deceased was stabbed in the back, indicating that he was not attacking the defendant at the time.

“The evidence showed that the deceased was no longer attacking the defendant when the defendant stabbed him, and, therefore, the defence of self-defence will also not avail the defendant,” he held.

During his allocutus, Azubuike pleaded for mercy, arguing that the defendant was the breadwinner of his family. The prosecution, however, informed the court that there was no previous record of conviction against him.

But Justice Okpe said the defendant had shown no remorse throughout the trial.

“From the commencement of this trial up to today, when the case came up for judgment, the defendant showed no remorse for his actions. He carried on as if the trial was a waste of his time,” the judge said.

He further held that the offence carried a mandatory death sentence and that the court had no discretion in imposing a lesser punishment, citing Lucky v. State (2016) LPELR-40541.

Avah appeared for the prosecution, while Azubuike represented the defendant.

The post Enugu guard to die by hanging for murder appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Economies lose 80% of disaster costs to insurance gaps – W’Bank
description: More than 80 per cent of financial losses caused by natural disasters have gone uninsured in parts of Africa, Asia and Latin America over the past decade, exposing developing economies to significant financial risks and highlighting the need for more affordable insurance coverage, the World Bank Gro
content:
More than 80 per cent of financial losses caused by natural disasters have gone uninsured in parts of Africa, Asia and Latin America over the past decade, exposing developing economies to significant financial risks and highlighting the need for more affordable insurance coverage, the World Bank Group has said.

The finding was contained in the World Bank Group’s Finance and Prosperity 2026 report, released on Wednesday, which examined financial sector performance across emerging market and developing economies and highlighted the growing insurance protection gap against natural disasters.

The report said the scale of uninsured losses underscored the vulnerability of developing economies to climate-related disasters, particularly where insurance markets were unable to provide sufficient protection against financial damage.

It recommended that governments prioritise measures to reduce disaster risks and improve the availability and affordability of natural disaster insurance.

The bank said strengthening insurance protection was important to limiting the financial consequences of disasters, which can place additional pressure on households, businesses and public finances when losses are not covered.

Beyond insurance, the report examined broader vulnerabilities in emerging market and developing economies, warning that financial stability risks were increasing in some countries amid volatile global economic conditions.

It said the conflict in the Middle East had contributed to rising commodity prices, tighter financial conditions and increased market volatility, creating additional risks for vulnerable developing economies.

Financial markets had demonstrated uneven resilience across countries, while the outlook remained uncertain, with significant downside risks ahead, according to the report.

The financier also warned that banks’ substantial holdings of fragile sovereign debt could expose financial systems to significant risks in some countries.

It said most countries facing high financial sector risks lacked sufficient institutional capacity to manage financial stability challenges, calling for urgent improvements in prudential supervision and financial sector safety nets.

The recommendations include strengthening the regulatory oversight of financial institutions and improving the mechanisms available to authorities to respond to financial sector vulnerabilities.

In a separate report released on Tuesday, the World Bank also highlighted the constraints facing micro, small and medium-sized enterprises in developing countries, particularly their limited access to financing.

The MSME Finance Gap report said the financing shortfall reached $4tn between 2019 and 2023, identifying barriers that prevent small businesses from accessing credit and equity investment.

MSMEs account for 90 per cent of businesses and 75 per cent of workers in emerging market and developing economies, yet many remain underserved by financial institutions.

The lender said access to formal loans could raise employment in individual firms by an average of 12 per cent and increase sales and profits by about 18 per cent.

title: 2027: Stakeholders plan Tinubu re election campaign in Bayelsa
description:
The Managing Director of the Niger Delta Development Commission, Dr Samuel Ogbuku, has declared that political leaders and stakeholders in Bayelsa East Senatorial District have resolved to deliver their votes to President Bola Tinubu and the All Progressives Congress in the 2027 general elections.
O
content:
The Managing Director of the Niger Delta Development Commission, Dr Samuel Ogbuku, has declared that political leaders and stakeholders in Bayelsa East Senatorial District have resolved to deliver their votes to President Bola Tinubu and the All Progressives Congress in the 2027 general elections.

Ogbuku said leaders, women, youths and other stakeholders from Brass, Nembe and Ogbia Local Government Areas had agreed to bury their political differences and work together to secure victory for the APC at the polls.

He spoke during a political stakeholders’ engagement involving supporters and leaders of the party from the three local government areas at the Government House, Yenagoa.

The NDDC managing director said the gathering was part of efforts to appreciate Tinubu for his administration’s infrastructure interventions in the district and mobilise support for the President’s re-election bid.

He explained that the organisers deliberately brought together traditional leaders, women, youths, parents and children to demonstrate their appreciation beyond newspaper publications and courtesy visits.

Ogbuku said, “That was why we said we were going to come out en masse for the world to see us, not only doing paper publications thanking you or coming to pay courtesy visits, but bringing out our mothers, our fathers, our youths and the children for the world to see and tell you thank you.”

He added that the people were prepared to translate their appreciation into electoral support for the President and other APC candidates.

“And the final thank you these people want to give is committing their votes to APC for the president and all other candidates of the party,” he said.

Ogbuku urged the people of the district to ensure that their commitment was reflected in the actual election results, saying Bayelsa must demonstrate its support through votes rather than mere political declarations.

He said the outcome would also strengthen the political standing of Governor Douye Diri among his colleagues at the national level.

“Whatever we are doing, we are going to support the government to ensure that when the governor sits amongst governors in Abuja, the result he is going to present will also be worthwhile,”  Ogbuku said.

The NDDC boss, who made reference to a statement credited to the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, cautioned against claiming electoral victory without actively participating in the political process.

According to him, Bayelsa East would not make claims of victory without working to achieve it. He also said that political leaders from the district had visited former President Goodluck Jonathan to seek his permission and blessings before embarking on their political mobilisation exercise.

He said Jonathan, who hails from Bayelsa East, blessed the movement and the candidates, including those seeking elective positions at the presidential and other levels.

The NDDC managing director said the visit demonstrated the importance the leaders attached to Jonathan’s influence and leadership in the state.

He further declared that the political differences that had divided leaders in the district had been set aside in the interest of a common political objective.

“For the first time, we have all buried our differences and we have decided to stand together. All the leaders in Bayelsa East are together,” he said.

On Tinubu’s infrastructure interventions, Ogbuku commended the President for the Ogbia access road, which he said had significantly improved transportation and connectivity in the area.

He described the approximately 46-kilometre road as a major intervention, recalling the difficulties commuters previously encountered in accessing Ogbia town.

He also listed solar-powered streetlights in communities and the second phase of the Nembe-Brass Road as other projects expected to improve the economic fortunes of the district.

According to him, the completion of the Nembe-Brass Road would end years of isolation for several communities and open up opportunities in the blue economy.

Ogbuku, however, acknowledged concerns raised by women over the absence of female candidates among those being presented for elective positions, describing the issue as sensitive.

He also described his appointment as NDDC managing director as a landmark achievement for Bayelsa East, noting that it was the first time someone from the senatorial district had occupied the position.

Meanwhile, the Bayelsa State Chairman of the APC, Warman Ogoriba, announced plans by the party to commence grassroots campaigns across the state as part of its preparations for the 2027 general elections.

Ogoriba said the ongoing engagements with stakeholders and supporters in Bayelsa East were preliminary consultations aimed at strengthening the party’s mobilisation structures ahead of the elections.

He clarified that the gathering was not the formal campaign but an opportunity for the party to interact with its members, appreciate their commitment and consolidate support for Tinubu and other APC candidates.

“This is not the main campaign. This is just our pre-campaign, and we are meeting the people. Wait for us very soon. We will start campaigning across all the wards,” the APC chairman said.

Ogoriba expressed confidence that Bayelsa Central and Bayelsa West would also participate in the mobilisation exercise, stressing that the party was determined to reach supporters across the three senatorial districts.

He thanked party members and stakeholders in Bayelsa East for their participation, describing the district as important to the APC’s preparations for the 2027 presidential election.

The APC chairman’s declaration signals the party’s intention to intensify its grassroots mobilisation and expand its political engagement across communities and wards in Bayelsa State ahead of the 2027 polls.

The post 2027: Stakeholders plan Tinubu re election campaign in Bayelsa appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Suspected power surge sparks Kwara fire, destroys 10 shops
description:
Traders in the Opomolu area of Ilorin, Kwara State, have lost their shops and goods after a midnight fire swept through a shopping area, destroying eight shops and two container shops.
PUNCH Metro gathered that the incident occurred at Ile Hausa in the Ilorin East Local Government Area in the early
content:
Traders in the Opomolu area of Ilorin, Kwara State, have lost their shops and goods after a midnight fire swept through a shopping area, destroying eight shops and two container shops.

PUNCH Metro gathered that the incident occurred at Ile Hausa in the Ilorin East Local Government Area in the early hours of Wednesday.

The Kwara State Fire Service said its personnel arrived at the scene at 12:35 am after receiving a distress call and immediately began efforts to contain the blaze and prevent it from spreading to neighbouring properties.

In a statement signed by its Public Relations Officer, Hassan Adekunle, the agency said preliminary findings indicated that a power surge might have triggered the fire, although investigations were ongoing to establish the actual cause.

“Preliminary information gathered at the scene suggests that the fire may have been triggered by a power surge.

“However, investigations are still ongoing, as other possible factors are also being examined to establish the actual cause of the incident,” the statement read.

Reacting to the incident, the Chief Fire Officer, Alabi Muhammed, urged traders to adopt stricter fire safety measures, warning that negligence involving electrical appliances and cooking materials could expose business premises to fire outbreaks.

He particularly cautioned operators of local restaurants and food businesses using charcoal and firewood to ensure that their cooking materials and other sources of heat were completely extinguished before leaving their premises.

Muhammed also advised business owners to engage qualified professionals for electrical installations, switch off appliances and isolate power sources at closing time, and keep combustible materials away from sources of ignition.

He added that traders should equip their shops with functional fire extinguishers and immediately report unusual smoke, sparks or other signs of fire to the emergency service.

He described fire prevention as a collective responsibility, stressing that prompt reporting of emergencies could help minimise damage.

“Fire prevention is a collective responsibility, and early reporting remains essential in reducing the extent of damage during fire emergencies,” the Chief Fire Officer was quoted as saying.

The incident came three days after firefighters prevented a potential disaster involving a petrol tanker loaded with about 55,000 litres of Premium Motor Spirit during a fuel transfer operation at a filling station in Moro Local Government Area of the state.

The post Suspected power surge sparks Kwara fire, destroys 10 shops appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Flutterwave marks decade with $50bn transaction milestone
description:
Flutterwave has processed more than one billion transactions valued at over $50 billion since its establishment in 2016, as the fintech company won the Africa’s Best Payments Infrastructure Provider award at the Euromoney Transaction Banking Awards 2026.
The recognition comes as the company marks it
content:
Flutterwave has processed more than one billion transactions valued at over $50 billion since its establishment in 2016, as the fintech company won the Africa’s Best Payments Infrastructure Provider award at the Euromoney Transaction Banking Awards 2026.

The recognition comes as the company marks its 10th anniversary and expands its operations beyond payments into banking, multicurrency services and stablecoin-powered financial infrastructure.

Presented by Euromoney, an international financial publication, the Transaction Banking Awards recognise performance across the global transaction banking and payments industry.

Since its establishment, Flutterwave has focused on connecting local payment methods, banking networks and international payment systems through a single platform to enable businesses to accept payments, reach customers and expand across borders.

The company said its platform was trusted by approximately four million individuals and businesses, ranging from small and medium-sized enterprises to global organisations.

Its Founder and Chief Executive Officer, Olugbenga ‘GB’ Agboola, said the award was an acknowledgement of the company’s work over the past decade.

“Being recognised by Euromoney as Africa’s Best Payments Infrastructure Provider is a proud moment for everyone at Flutterwave, particularly as we celebrate our tenth anniversary. When we started Flutterwave in 2016, our ambition was to make it easier for African businesses to move money and participate in the global economy,” he said.

He added, “Ten years on, we have built infrastructure that supports millions of businesses and connects African markets to the rest of the world. This award recognises the dedication of our team, the trust of our customers, and the partnerships that have helped us grow. It also reinforces why we started this journey.

“There is still significant work to be done to make payments across Africa simpler, faster, and more accessible. This is why we are continuing to evolve beyond payments, building a more comprehensive financial infrastructure that brings together payments, banking, stablecoin capabilities and other financial services to help businesses and individuals move, manage and access money more efficiently. We remain committed to building the infrastructure that will support the continent’s next phase of economic growth.”

As part of its expansion, Flutterwave acquired open banking company Mono and secured a Nigerian Microfinance Banking Licence, steps aimed at integrating payments, banking and financial data capabilities into its operations.

The company is also developing stablecoin-powered payment and settlement infrastructure, with strategic investments from Ripple and Circle supporting its expansion into digital asset infrastructure.

The capabilities are designed to facilitate cross-border money transfers and settlements, complementing existing payment networks used by businesses.

Flutterwave is also expanding its multicurrency services to help businesses manage international collections and payments while serving customers across different markets.

The company’s broader financial services strategy is aimed at bringing payments, banking, multicurrency capabilities and stablecoin-powered infrastructure together to enable businesses and individuals to manage funds and move money across borders.

Earlier this year, Flutterwave was recognised by CNBC and Statista as one of the world’s top 250 fintech companies, while its Founder and CEO, Olugbenga Agboola, was named among the Top 100 Fintech Leaders by Fintech Magazine.

The post Flutterwave marks decade with $50bn transaction milestone appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Tinubu expands 2027 campaign itinerary to 19 states
description:
President Bola Tinubu has expanded his campaign itinerary for the 2027 presidential election, increasing the number of states he plans to visit from 12 to 19, with the Federal Capital Territory also included.
The PUNCH gathered that the revised timetable shows that Tinubu is expected to attend 20 ra
content:
President Bola Tinubu has expanded his campaign itinerary for the 2027 presidential election, increasing the number of states he plans to visit from 12 to 19, with the Federal Capital Territory also included.

The PUNCH gathered that the revised timetable shows that Tinubu is expected to attend 20 rallies organised by the All Progressives Congress across the country between October 24, 2026, and January 13, 2027.

President Tinubu had disclosed during the inauguration of the APC Presidential Campaign Council on October 14 that he would be unable to attend all campaign rallies.

The new additions to the itinerary include Katsina, Taraba, Zamfara, Imo and Kwara, while Akwa Ibom, Jigawa and Kebbi have also been included following Tinubu’s recent campaign appearances in the states.

Tinubu had already attended rallies in Uyo, Akwa Ibom State, on November 6; Port Harcourt, Rivers State, on November 7; Dutse, Jigawa State, on November 10; and Birnin Kebbi, Kebbi State, on November 17.

Under the revised timetable, Tinubu is expected to visit Katsina on December 2, Kano on December 17, Jalingo, Taraba State, on December 19, and Abuja on December 21. Other engagements include Gusau, Zamfara State, on December 28, and Owerri, Imo State, on December 30.

The President is also scheduled to resume campaigning in the New Year with rallies in Yola, Adamawa State, on January 4; Sokoto on January 5; and Ilorin, Kwara State, on January 8.

He will subsequently visit Asaba, Delta State, on January 11, before concluding the campaign with a rally in Lagos on January 13.

The APC calendar also features changes to the original timetable, including the postponement of the Sokoto rally from December 5 to January 5 and the movement of the Lagos campaign finale from January 9 to January 13.

The revised campaign schedule places the North-West ahead of other geopolitical zones, with Tinubu expected to visit seven states: Kaduna, Jigawa, Kebbi, Katsina, Kano, Zamfara and Sokoto.

The North-East and South-South have three states each on the itinerary, while the North-Central, South-West and South-East have two states apiece.

title: Onitsha monarch is now the law against gender-based violence
description:
The Obi of Onitsha has put the weight of a 700-year-old throne behind one message: no custom justifies violence against a woman. Now GBV is no longer a private matter. It is a palace matter.
Nigeria does not have a GBV law problem. It has a culture problem.
We have the Violence Against Persons Prohi
content:
The Obi of Onitsha has put the weight of a 700-year-old throne behind one message: no custom justifies violence against a woman. Now GBV is no longer a private matter. It is a palace matter.

Nigeria does not have a GBV law problem. It has a culture problem.

We have the Violence Against Persons Prohibition Act. We have state laws. We have campaigns. Yet a woman beaten in her home is still told to “go and settle it as family”. A girl abused is still told to keep quiet to protect the family name. The law speaks, but culture whispers louder, and culture usually wins.

That is why what is happening in Onitsha matters.

The Obi of Onitsha, Igwe Nnaemeka Alfred Achebe, has decided that the throne will no longer be neutral. He has put the full weight of a 700-year-old monarchy behind one simple message: there is no custom, no tradition, and no proverb that justifies violence against a woman.

In Onitsha today, GBV is no longer a private matter. It is a public matter.

It did not start as a GBV project.

In 2014, the Obi-in-Council set up the Onitsha Advancement Foundation to push education, skills, and the preservation of Onitsha values. But a serious institution cannot preserve values while ignoring violence in the home. So, OnAF became the engine.

First, the Obi changed what ‘royal power’ means. He did not just condemn GBV in a speech. He got traditional rulers across Anambra to sign a collective royal mandate, a public commitment to protect women and vulnerable people. That is no small thing in a culture where a ruler is expected to protect custom, not question it.

Then he did something even rarer for a palace: he asked for data.

OnAF carried out participatory research across all the villages in Onitsha. 841 people spoke. They were asked what they know about GBV, what forms it takes, why it happens, what it does to women and girls, and why survivors do not report.

The answer was uncomfortable but useful. People knew what GBV was. They just did not trust the system to protect them if they spoke.

So, Onitsha built a system they would trust.

That research produced two tools: a data-driven GBV awareness curriculum for people who live and work in Onitsha, and an Onitsha GBV Prevention Strategy, with monitoring built in to track progress toward zero tolerance.

Then came the law, Onitsha style.

The Obi-in-Council moved to formally incorporate a GBV prevention and response framework into Onitsha’s customary guidelines. Alongside it, the Council is developing a compendium of rules to penalise domestic abuse, verbal and emotional violence, and discriminatory inheritance practices.

Those rules will guide the Ime Obi Traditional Court.

This is the genius of the model. The formal court is far, expensive, slow and intimidating. The Ime Obi court is near, trusted, fast and transparent. A survivor does not need a lawyer and transport fare to Lagos or Awka to be heard. She can be heard at home, by a court her community respects.

And to make sure it is not just the palace talking to itself, OnAF has been holding strategic dialogues with Ndi Diopka, the kindred head. When the kindred heads buy in, the message reaches every compound, every umunna meeting, and every family dispute.

That is how you change culture. Not by press release. By palace, by data, by court, and by kindred.

On October 16, 2026, the Obi took it one step further. He launched the OnAF GBV Centre, Africa’s first palace-connected GBV centre. It is not just a building. It is a statement: survivors do not have to run away from the community to get help. Help is now inside the community, with the blessing of the King.

According to the OnAF Programme Coordinator and Onitsha GBV Project Lead, Dr Rita Melifonwu, the centre will serve as a one-stop shop for all GBV work in the kingdom, with confidential counselling, crisis intervention and support, supported by the Ford Foundation. The Obi described it as a safe environment for the Rapid Response Team to work with stakeholders and support survivors.

This is the lesson for Nigeria.

We have spent years trying to fight GBV by fighting culture. Onitsha is showing us a smarter way: fight GBV by reclaiming culture.

When a 700-year-old stool says culture must serve people, not punish them, the silence breaks. And when the silence breaks in Onitsha, it will be harder for it to hold anywhere else.

The Bottom Line is that laws can punish a man after he beats his wife. Only a changed culture can stop him before he raises his hand. In Onitsha, the King has chosen to change the culture.

The post Onitsha monarch is now the law against gender-based violence appeared first on Punch Newspapers.
