title: Edo community leader calls for govt intervention in land dispute
description: THE Ohen Obao of Aduwawa in Ikpoba-Okha local government area of Edo State, Chief Priest Nosakhare Odumore, has appealed to the Oba of Benin, the governor of the state Senator Monday Okpebholo, and security agencies to intervene in a lingering land dispute in the community, expressing fears that it
content:
THE Ohen Obao of Aduwawa in Ikpoba-Okha local government area of Edo State, Chief Priest Nosakhare Odumore, has appealed to the Oba of Benin, the governor of the state Senator Monday Okpebholo, and security agencies to intervene in a lingering land dispute in the community, expressing fears that it could threaten public peace.

 He said the disputed land is between two businessmen in the state who have contributed immensely to the development of the community.

In his statement made available to SOUTH SOUTH PUNCH on Tuesday, Odumore said he had invited the parties for dialogue and amicable resolution of the issue but that one of the parties has failed to show up for meetings.

“The reason  for issuing a press statement is not to promote division, take sides or undermine anybody’s legitimate interest, but to make the public aware of the efforts I have made to resolve a lingering land dispute and prevent a situation that could threaten the peace, security and unity of our community.

“The land in question has become a subject of dispute between two individuals. One is an Igbo businessman who has, for many years, claimed ownership of the property and used it as a parking space for his hotel.

“The other claimant is a Benin-based businessman and owner who runs a transport company and recently come forward to lay claim to the same property.

“In my determination to prevent this disagreement from escalating, I initiated efforts to bring both parties before the traditional authority so that each could present his claims, provide relevant information and be given a fair opportunity to be heard.

“I extended several invitations through the appropriate traditional channels, expecting both parties to honour the process and allow us to resolve the matter amicably.

“However, I wish to express my disappointment that while the Igbo businessman has consistently honoured the invitations and appeared before me, the other person has failed to appear despite repeated efforts to secure his attendance.

“So, I am using this opportunity to appeal to the Oba of Benin, the governor of the state, Monday Okpebholo, and security agencies to intervene in the lingering land dispute in the community and I am  that the situation can threaten public peace.

While declaring that he has not ruled on the matter  in favour of any of the parties, Odumore said he has barricaded the disputed land with the traditional palm frond and gave a fresh seven days for the parties to appear before him.

title: ADC, candidates rally supporters, allay disqualification fear
description:
Party officials and candidates of the African Democratic Congress in the January 16 general election in the South South have dismissed the  fear of being disqualified, rallying their supporters and residents  for votes.
While they have accepted that the David Mark-led exco have been sacked, they not
content:
Party officials and candidates of the African Democratic Congress in the January 16 general election in the South South have dismissed the  fear of being disqualified, rallying their supporters and residents  for votes.

While they have accepted that the David Mark-led exco have been sacked, they noted that they remain candidates and expressed hope that the court would reinstate the national exco of the party.

In Rivers State, most of the party’s campaign remains in the social and electronic media.

The state ADC governorship candidate, Dr Gabriel Pidomson has been appearing on various radio stations in Port Harcourt selling his programmes. Also recently he appeared on a national TV where he expressed confidence that the party will be on the ballot despite the court ruling.

Dr Pidomson described the ruling as a temporary setback, noting that he is talking to his support groups in the state to win voters.

“For sure, the ruling is a temporary setback for the party but I am still campaigning in order to get the needed votes to win the election,” he added.

In Edo State, the South South PUNCH checks revealed that the campaign activities of the ADC and its candidates were visible in the past one week with the Edo South Senatorial candidate, Matthew Iduoriyekemwen leading the way.

He has met with various groups and stakeholders and sold his manifesto to them. Iduoriyekemwen’s media aide, Paul Okojie, said his principal has been busy on the campaign trail, noting that the court judgement has not slowed him down.

He said, “Yes, he is still campaigning and the court judgement has not slowed him down. We are sure that the national leadership issue will be sorted out soon.

“He has continued to meet with different groups and stakeholders. He is doing everything possible to attract votes from all the local government in the senatorial districts.”

The Spokesman of the party in the state, Chris Ojeikere, said the party is campaigning, noting that the party’s presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar has also been busy on the campaign train.

He noted that the party is also active in Edo while its candidates were meeting with groups to secure votes in the coming election.

“No, the court judgement has not halted our campaign both at the national and state levels. There is no ban on campaigns so we have continued. The case is about leadership not ban on campaigns.

For us, the ruling is unethical but it will be sorted out soon.”

He added that all other candidates in other parts of the state were also campaigning.

In Delta, the party said its campaign activities have not been suspended despite the court ruling. The state Publicity Secretary, Fred Akpevwe, in an interview, dismissed suggestions that the legal dispute had affected the party’s political activities in the state.

Akpevwe said the court case concerned the party’s leadership and did not prevent members from continuing their political engagements.

He said, “It has nothing to do with our campaigns. Our campaigns are still on course. The dispute is centred on the question of who is the party’s recognised chairman, and that is separate from the party’s campaign activities.”

Akpevwe maintained that the party remained active in the state despite the leadership dispute.

In Akwa Ibom, the state Publicity Secretary, Solomon Johnny, said the party is focused, undeterred, strong, united and fully on the campaign trail.

‎‎He noted that the judgement has not weakened the party structure, nor has it stopped its candidates from meeting voters ahead of the elections.

‎‎‎He said, “For us in ADC in Akwa Ibom State, we are strong and still campaigning. The court judgement has not slowed us down. We are sure that the leadership issue will be sorted out soon.

‎‎He said campaign activities were visible across the three senatorial districts in the past one week, with candidates meeting youths, women, stakeholders and party members to sell their manifestos.

‎‎“Our candidates have continued to meet with different groups and we are doing everything possible to attract votes from all the local government areas in the state. Last week, we had stakeholders’ engagement in Uyo and we are building a formidable team for 2027,” he added.

In Bayelsa State, the party vowed to soon launch a statewide campaign as part of efforts to strengthen its political structures and mobilise support ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The State Chairman, Hon. Johnny Derek, said the party had not suspended its campaign activities but was currently concentrating on grassroots mobilisation and engagements at the ward level across the state.

He explained that the party would soon intensify its activities with a full-scale statewide campaign to reach more residents and communicate its political programmes.

“We are campaigning. We have not stopped. Very soon, we will come out with full force. Our activities have been in the media and very soon, we are coming out with full force to launch a statewide campaign.

“But for now, as a party, we are conducting our various campaigns at the ward level,” he added.

The post ADC, candidates rally supporters, allay disqualification fear appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

By Joseph Erunke











Abuja—Nigeria has expanded its presence in the global university rankings, recording its highest-ever number of institutions in the Times Higher Education, THE, Interdisciplinary Science Rankings, even as the country struggles to push more universities into the world’s to
content:
By Joseph Erunke

Abuja—Nigeria has expanded its presence in the global university rankings, recording its highest-ever number of institutions in the Times Higher Education, THE, Interdisciplinary Science Rankings, even as the country struggles to push more universities into the world’s top 500.


The latest 2027 ranking saw 27 Nigerian universities make the global list, a 50 per cent increase from the 18 institutions ranked in 2026.


However, the country’s growing numerical presence has not translated into stronger representation among the world’s leading institutions.
While the number of Nigerian universities participating in the exercise continued to rise, only two made it into the global top 300, against five in the previous editio
Similarly, seven Nigerian institutions featured in the top 500, compared with eight in 2026.
Amid the mixed performance, Covenant University, Ota, Ogun State, retained its position as Africa’s leading institution in interdisciplinary science, placing joint 49th globally to remain the continent’s only university among the world’s top 50 for the second consecutive year.
The private university also maintained its lead over Egypt’s Cairo University, which placed joint 52nd globally, reinforcing Nigeria’s capacity to produce globally competitive institutions, despite persistent funding and research infrastructure challenges.
Chairman of the Nigerian Tertiary Education Ranking Advisory Committee, NiTERAC, Professor Emeritus Peter Okebukola, who disclosed the results in a statement issued in Abuja yesterday, described the growing participation of Nigerian universities as encouraging but warned that the country must move beyond increasing its numbers to improving its actual performance.
The 2027 ranking, released on November 18, assessed 1,058 universities across 102 countries and territories.
It measured institutions’ capacity to fund, support and deliver research cutting across scientific disciplines.
According to Okebukola, Nigeria’s performance represents a significant expansion from the 19 universities ranked in the maiden 2025 edition, while another seven institutions were accorded Reporter status after submitting data.
This brings the total number of Nigerian universities participating in the 2027 exercise to 34, compared with 30 in 2026 and 27 in 2025.
He said Nigeria had climbed from 16th to 11th position globally in terms of the number of ranked universities, retaining its second position in Africa behind Egypt, which has 37 institutions.
Despite the progress, the ranking exposed the difficulty Nigerian universities face in translating increased participation into improved research competitiveness.
Under the latest assessment, Covenant University emerged as Nigeria’s highest-ranked institution, followed by Landmark University, Omu-Aran, which occupied the 251–300 global band.
Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria, and the University of Ilorin were placed in the 351–400 band, while the University of Calabar, University of Lagos and University of Nigeria, Nsukka, occupied the 401–500 category.
Ladoke Akintola University of Technology, Obafemi Awolowo University and the University of Benin completed Nigeria’s top 10, placing within the 501–600 band.
Okebukola, former Executive Secretary of the National Universities Commission,NUC, particularly applauded Ahmadu Bello University and the University of Calabar for their remarkable improvement.
ABU moved from the 601–800 band in 2026 to the 351–400 category in the latest ranking.
, while the University of Calabar climbed from the 601–800 band to the 401–500 category.
Eight Nigerian universities also made their debut in the global ranking. They are the Federal University of Technology, Minna; Michael Okpara University of Agriculture, Umudike; Joseph Sarwuan Tarka University, Makurdi; University of Jos; Rivers State University; Babcock University; Bells University of Technology; and Nile University of Nigeria. Osun State University equally returned to the ranking after a year’s absence.
Of the 27 Nigerian universities ranked, 14 are federal institutions, seven state-owned, while six are privately-owned.
Explaining the factors behind Nigeria’s relatively weak showing in the upper brackets, Okebukola identified inadequate funding for interdisciplinary science research, insufficient dedicated research facilities, weak administrative support and the absence of institutional policies encouraging collaboration across scientific disciplines as major constraints.
He explained that the THE ranking uses 11 performance indicators grouped into three broad pillars: inputs, processes and outputs.
While inputs account for 19 per cent of the assessment and processes 16 per cent, outputs carry the highest weight at 65 per cent.
According to him, many Nigerian universities recorded poor scores in the inputs and processes categories, particularly in research funding and the institutional structures required to promote collaboration across disciplines.
Okebukola commended the Minister of Education, Dr Tunji Alausa, for prioritising the global competitiveness of Nigerian tertiary institutions and establishing NiTERAC to coordinate efforts towards improving the international standing of the country’s universities.

The post More Nigerian varsities make global list, few break into top 500 appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Foursquare G.O. tasks graduands on integrity, national development
description:
By Olayinka Latona



The General Overseer of the Foursquare Gospel Church in Nigeria, Rev. Sam Aboyeji, has charged graduating students of LIFE Theological Seminary, Ikorodu, Lagos, to uphold integrity and sound biblical doctrine as they prepare to preach the Gospel and contribute to society.



Ab
content:
By Olayinka Latona

The General Overseer of the Foursquare Gospel Church in Nigeria, Rev. Sam Aboyeji, has charged graduating students of LIFE Theological Seminary, Ikorodu, Lagos, to uphold integrity and sound biblical doctrine as they prepare to preach the Gospel and contribute to society.

Aboyeji gave the charge at the institution’s 2026 graduation ceremony, where he urged the graduands to see their graduation not as an end but as a stepping stone to greater responsibilities in God’s service.

Speaking on the theme of the ceremony, “Trailblazers,” and drawing from Titus 2:7-8, the cleric said the credibility of their future ministries would depend largely on the integrity of their personal lives.

He said: “You have been equipped with knowledge and skills that must now find expression in faithful service to God and humanity. I charge you to distinguish yourselves as trailblazers whose lives exemplify the sound doctrine you have received.”

Quoting Apostle Paul’s admonition to Titus, Aboyeji urged the graduates to be examples of good works, demonstrating integrity in doctrine, reverence, incorruptible speech and soundness of character.

He warned against compromising biblical truths in the face of challenges, urging them to remain courageous, steadfast and diligent in their ministerial responsibilities.

“Be courageous in breaking new ground, steadfast in the face of challenges, uncompromising in matters of biblical truth, and diligent in the discharge of your ministerial responsibilities,” he said.

Reminding the graduands that service to God was a sacred responsibility requiring accountability to the Creator, the General Overseer urged them to remain worthy ambassadors of LIFE Theological Seminary and vessels of honour in their respective fields of assignment.

Also speaking, the Chairman of the Governing Council of LIFE Theological Seminary, Rev. Joe Ameh, urged the graduating class to distinguish themselves as trailblazers and uncompromising ambassadors of Christ in a society increasingly challenged by moral decay and corruption.

Ameh said the graduates were expected to demonstrate the values of Christianity and apply their theological training in addressing contemporary issues in a rapidly changing society.

He said: “As trailblazers, those of you graduating today are expected to be ardent and passionate in distinguishing yourselves before a world characterised by normlessness and anomie. You are expected to be pathfinders in blazing the trail that should characterise the essence of being Christians with a fair measure of theological education in responding to contemporary issues in a fast-evolving setting.”

The seminary council chairman also decried what he described as pervasive corrupt practices threatening the nation’s God-given assets and resources.

He, however, urged the new ministers to remain steadfast and uphold Christian values despite pressures to compromise their standards.

“Despite these pervasive corruptive tendencies, you are to be different in words and conduct and indeed be zealous to propagate sound Christian values irrespective of pressures to compromise our Christian standards,” he said.

The post Foursquare G.O. tasks graduands on integrity, national development appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: FAAC allocation rises to N2.44tn despite revenue decline
description:
The Federal Government, 36 states and 774 local government councils shared N2.441tn from the Federation Account in November 2026, representing an increase of N13bn, or 0.54 per cent, from the N2.428tn distributed in October, despite a decline in gross revenue collections.
The increase marked the sec
content:
The Federal Government, 36 states and 774 local government councils shared N2.441tn from the Federation Account in November 2026, representing an increase of N13bn, or 0.54 per cent, from the N2.428tn distributed in October, despite a decline in gross revenue collections.

The increase marked the second consecutive monthly rise in Federation Account Allocation Committee disbursements, following the sharp decline recorded in September, when allocations fell by 22.2 per cent from the record N3.007tn shared in August.

The latest allocation, which represents revenue generated in October, was approved at the November FAAC meeting held in Abuja.

The Office of the Accountant-General of the Federation disclosed this in a statement issued on Wednesday by its Director of Press and Public Relations, Bawa Mokwa.

According to the statement, “A total sum of N2.441tn, being October 2026 Federation Account Revenue, has been shared to the Federal Government, States and the Local Government Councils.”

An analysis by The PUNCH showed that the N2.441tn distributed in November was N13bn higher than the previous month’s allocation but remained N566bn, or 18.8 per cent, below the record N3.007tn shared in August.

The November distribution also exceeded the N2.338tn shared in September by N103bn, or 4.4 per cent, although it remained N109bn below the N2.550tn distributed in July.

The latest figures indicate that allocations to the three tiers of government have continued to recover gradually from September’s decline, despite weakening revenue collections.

According to the FAAC communiqué, total gross revenue fell by N102bn, or 2.6 per cent, from N3.913tn in September to N3.811tn in October.

Gross statutory revenue declined by N97.323bn, or 3.1 per cent, to N2.999tn in October from N3.096tn in September.

The statement said, “According to the communiqué, gross statutory revenue of N2.999tn was received for the month of October 2026. This was lower than the sum of N3.096tn received in the preceding month by N97.323bn.”

The decline reversed the recovery recorded in September, when gross statutory revenue increased by N246.384bn from N2.850tn in August.

Similarly, gross Value Added Tax collections declined for the second consecutive month, falling by N4.426bn, or 0.54 per cent, from N816.872bn in September to N812.446bn in October.

VAT collections had previously declined by N17.972bn in September, following an increase of N40.875bn in August.

The statement read, “Gross revenue of N812.446bn was available from the Value Added Tax in October 2026. This was lower than the N816.872bn available in the month of September 2026 by N4.426bn.”

Despite the decline in gross collections, the amount available for distribution increased because deductions, transfers, refunds and savings fell during the month.

According to the communiqué, N128.797bn was deducted as cost of collection in October, compared with N131.758bn in September, representing a reduction of N2.961bn.

Similarly, transfers, refunds and savings declined by N111bn, or 8.2 per cent, from N1.352tn in September to N1.241tn in October.

The combined reduction of approximately N114bn in these two categories helped offset the N102bn decline in gross revenue, allowing distributable revenue to increase by N13bn.

The N2.441tn available for distribution comprised N1.688tn in statutory revenue and N752.488bn from VAT.

Distributable statutory revenue increased by N16bn, or approximately 0.96 per cent, from N1.672tn in September, while distributable VAT declined by N4.099bn, or 0.54 per cent, from N756.587bn.

A breakdown of the allocation showed that the Federal Government received N856.065bn, compared with N832.242bn in October, representing an increase of N23.823bn, or 2.9 per cent.

The 36 state governments received N809.909bn, up by N10.037bn, or 1.25 per cent, from N799.872bn in the previous month.

Similarly, the 774 local government councils received N568.701bn, representing an increase of N8.041bn, or 1.43 per cent, from N560.660bn.

The post FAAC allocation rises to N2.44tn despite revenue decline appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Akwa Ibom urges students to embrace science, technology
description:

The call was made at the 2026 grand finale of the Igniting Minds through Science programme held on Tuesday in Uyo, where secondary school st
content:
The Akwa Ibom State Government has urged students to embrace science and technology and apply their knowledge to solve practical problems in their communities.

The call was made at the 2026 grand finale of the Igniting Minds through Science programme held on Tuesday in Uyo, where secondary school students showcased innovative solutions to everyday challenges.

The programme, organised by Vcare for Development Foundation, with support from Sterling Oil Exploration and Energy Production Company Limited, was implemented in partnership with the Akwa Ibom State Ministry of Education.

Speaking at the event, the Permanent Secretary, Akwa Ibom State Ministry of Education, Okon Effiong, expressed delight at the programme’s growth and expanding reach across the state.

He commended Sterling Oil and Vcare for Development Foundation, for encouraging students to develop an interest in science and, more importantly, apply their knowledge practically.

He said, “I want to sincerely thank Sterling Oil and Vcare for Development Foundation because you have encouraged our students to be interested in science subjects, not just to be interested but to take a step further by being practical.”

He reaffirmed the importance of the partnership and encouraged VCDF to further expand the Igniting Minds through Science programme across Akwa Ibom State.

‎‎Effiong said the exercise showcased innovative student projects addressing water distribution, renewable energy, flood monitoring and alternative heating systems.

‎‎”Since its introduction in 2024, IMS has provided secondary school students with opportunities to move beyond classroom theories and apply science, technology, engineering and mathematics knowledge to challenges within their communities.

‎‎”The 2026 edition reached 4,186 students across 141 secondary and technical schools in Akwa Ibom State”, he said.

‎‎Following STEM workshops and teacher orientation sessions, students worked in teams under the guidance of their coordinating science teachers to identify challenges in their communities, examine their possible causes and develop practical, technology-driven solutions with 14 selected schools, out of 75 funded projects, presented their innovations.

‎‎Government Technical College, Ewet, Uyo, emerged overall winner with Sharepump, an automatic water pump and power-switching prototype designed to regulate water supply and improve water distribution in homes and multi-storey buildings.

‎‎Secondary Grammar School, Ibeno, secured second place with its Footstep Energy Harvester, a prototype that converts the mechanical energy generated by footsteps into electrical energy, demonstrating the possibilities of alternative and renewable energy sources.

‎‎Afaha Inang Secondary School, Onna, came third with Community FloodGuard, a flood-monitoring and protection prototype designed to help communities detect potential flooding, strengthen early-warning systems and respond more effectively to flood risks.

‎‎On his part, Ubong Ukpo, Coordinating teacher of the winning team from Government Technical College, Ewet in Uyo LGA, said the journey involved challenges that required teamwork, collaboration and determination to overcome.

‎‎Similarly, Imaobong David of Adiahaobong Girls Secondary School, Ikot Imo, Nsit Ubium LGA, expressed appreciation for the opportunity to participate and showcase her school’s creativity.

‎The participants and relevant stakeholders hailed Sterling Oil, stressing that through its corporate social responsibility investments, Sterling Oil Group continues to strengthen education, build capacity and expand opportunities for communities across Nigeria, reinforcing the role of private-sector partnerships in advancing educational development and youth empowerment.

The post Akwa Ibom urges students to embrace science, technology appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Oyo, Kwara raise student bursaries
description:
The Oyo and Kwara State governments have increased financial support for tertiary institution students through higher bursary payments, with Oyo approving awards of up to N500,000 for 5,000 final-year students and Kwara raising its annual allowance from N20,000 to N50,000.
In Oyo State, the governme
content:
The Oyo and Kwara State governments have increased financial support for tertiary institution students through higher bursary payments, with Oyo approving awards of up to N500,000 for 5,000 final-year students and Kwara raising its annual allowance from N20,000 to N50,000.

In Oyo State, the government has commenced the implementation of its 2025/2026 bursary scheme for final-year students of the state studying in tertiary institutions across Nigeria.

The screening exercise, coordinated by the Federation of Oyo State Students’ Union National, is underway for eligible students in universities, polytechnics, colleges of education and other specialised institutions.

The development was contained in a statement released by the Special Adviser (Media), Dr. Sulaimon Olanrewaju, and made available to journalists in Ibadan on Wednesday.

Speaking during the screening exercise at the Oyo State Ministry of Education, Science and Technology, the 10th National President of FOSSU, Distinguished Senator Yekinni Sodiq, said the bursary programme reflected Governor Seyi Makinde’s commitment to supporting students and easing the financial burden of higher education.

According to him, 5,000 final-year students across the country successfully registered for the scheme.

Sodiq explained that the programme was open to final-year students of Oyo State origin studying in accredited tertiary institutions, provided they met the stipulated requirements.

He urged beneficiaries to make judicious use of the funds, noting that the bursary would support their academic pursuits and assist students engaged in small-scale businesses and other productive ventures.

Also speaking, the Head of Government to the FOSSU National President, Hon. Kamil-Bello Umar-Farouk, commended Makinde for sustaining the bursary scheme since assuming office and expanding opportunities for Oyo State students.

Farouk disclosed that students enrolled in Nigeria Certificate in Education programmes, who were excluded from the previous edition, had been included following appeals to the governor.

“Last year, NCE students were not captured under the bursary scheme. We appealed to the Governor because they are also stakeholders in the education sector and deserving beneficiaries. We are grateful that His Excellency approved their inclusion this year, and they will now benefit from the programme,” he said.

He further disclosed that Makinde had approved an increase in the bursary awards following requests from student representatives.

According to him, while beneficiaries received a flat bursary of N100,000 in the previous edition, the revised structure provides different amounts across categories of students.

“NCE students will receive N100,000 each, while polytechnic students will receive N150,000. Students in universities and other tertiary institutions will benefit from N200,000 each. Medical and clinical students, law graduates in Law School, as well as aviation students, will receive N500,000 each,” Farouk stated.

He appreciated the Senior Special Assistant to the Governor on Student Affairs, Hon. Victor Olojede, for his efforts towards the implementation of the programme, and commended the FOSSU leadership for advancing the interests of Oyo State students.

“On behalf of Oyo State students across Nigeria and beyond, we express our profound appreciation to Governor Seyi Makinde for this intervention. We remain grateful for his unwavering commitment to the welfare and educational development of students in the state,” he added.

In Kwara State, Governor AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq has announced an increase in the annual bursary for students from N20,000 to N50,000.

The governor made the announcement on Wednesday during a meeting with the leadership of the National Association of Nigerian Students, Joint Campus Committee, at the Government House in Ilorin.

He said payment of the new amount would begin before the end of November.

In a 52-second video obtained by The PUNCH, AbdulRazaq said his administration had reconsidered the existing amount after further discussions on providing more financial support for students.

“The fund is just to support the students. We approved N20,000 in bursary for each student. We’ve had discussions among ourselves and resolved that we must give our students N50,000,” the governor said.

“Payment will start before the end of this month,” he added.

The increase represents a 150 per cent rise from the previous N20,000 allocation and brings the state’s bursary to ten times the N5,000 paid to students in 2019.

The announcement came on the same day that the National Association of Kwara State Students pledged the support of its more than 50,000 members for the governor, citing his administration’s interventions in education and student welfare.

The association’s National President, Muhammed Issa, disclosed this during a radio programme monitored by our correspondent, where he identified the increase in bursary payments and the provision of two new buses for the association as some of the administration’s notable interventions.

Issa, who appeared on the programme alongside the association’s Public Relations Officer, Muhammed Baba, and Senate President, Yahaya Oladimeji, said the students’ endorsement followed a recent gathering at the Kwara State House of Assembly.

According to him, students drawn from across the country unanimously passed a vote of confidence in AbdulRazaq in recognition of his administration’s contributions to their welfare.

“The increase in bursary from N5,000 in 2019 to N20,000 and the provision of two new buses for our association are some of the interventions we appreciate this administration for,” Issa said.

He, however, urged the government to extend more assistance to Kwara indigenes studying outside the state, particularly those in the northern and southern parts of the country, who he said were struggling to meet their tuition obligations.

“We want the government to do more for our students studying outside Kwara State, especially those in the northern and southern parts of the country, who are finding it difficult to meet their tuition obligations,” he said.

The NAKSS president also called for sustained investment in education, describing AbdulRazaq as a youth-friendly governor.

He insisted that the association’s position was based on its assessment of student welfare rather than political affiliation.

The post Oyo, Kwara raise student bursaries appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

content:
By Islamiyyah Adekanbi

Engr. Goodluck Idele’s decades of engineering work, including his involvement in building and delivering vessels for the Nigerian Navy and oil and gas companies, have earned him a Fellowship Award from the Nigeria Association of Technologists in Engineering, NATE.


Idele was inducted as a Fellow at a ceremony held on Thursday, November 12, at the Dr. Obi Wali International Conference Centre, Port Harcourt, Rivers State.
The award recognises his professional achievements and contributions to engineering. His work on vessels for clients in Nigeria and abroad reflects the technical expertise and commitment to quality that NATE cited in honouring him.
NATE is an affiliate member of the Council for the Regulation of Engineering in Nigeria, COREN.
The ceremony brought together guests from academia, government, the engineering profession and the oil and gas industry.
Idele’s fellowship marks a milestone in a career spanning several decades and recognises his service to engineering practice.

title: Reps to summon NAFDAC, DSS over fake drugs, deaths
description: The House of Representatives has resolved to invite the heads of the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control, the Department of State Services and the Nigeria Police Force to brief its relevant committees on measures being taken to tackle the growing circulation of fake drugs an
content:
The House of Representatives has resolved to invite the heads of the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control, the Department of State Services and the Nigeria Police Force to brief its relevant committees on measures being taken to tackle the growing circulation of fake drugs and adulterated drinks across the country.

The resolution followed the adoption of a motion of urgent public importance moved on Wednesday by the member representing Obi/Oju Federal Constituency of Benue State, Mr David Agada, following reports that the consumption of a suspected poisonous herbal medicine had claimed four lives in the constituency.

The motion, titled “Urgent need to investigate the alleged distribution and administration of suspected poisonous, unregistered/substandard herbal medicinal products in Obi/Oju Federal Constituency, Benue State to prevent further loss of lives,” called for urgent intervention to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident and prevent further casualties.

Moving the motion, Agada reminded lawmakers of their responsibility to protect the lives and welfare of their constituents.

He noted that the NAFDAC Act empowers the agency to regulate and control the manufacture, distribution, sale and use of drugs, herbal medicinal products and other regulated health-related products in Nigeria.

He also cited the Food and Drugs Act and the Counterfeit and Fake Drugs and Unwholesome Processed Foods (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act, which prohibit the manufacture, distribution and sale of unsafe, adulterated, counterfeit or unwholesome drugs and related products.

Speaking on the incident, Agada said, “The House is concerned that on October 31 2026, three individuals identified as Muhammad Sani Adamu, Musa Alhaji Kala who claim to come from Sokoto State and Alhaji Muhammad Sule from Bauchi States allegedly introduced and distributed a herbal medicinal product in Oju/Obi Federal Constituency, Benue State, claiming that the product could cure typhoid fever, waist pain and other ailments.

“We are concerned that several residents reportedly purchased and consumed the said product, after which a number of them developed severe symptoms within hours and were rushed to different hospitals for emergency medical attention.

“The House is disturbed that the incident has reportedly resulted in the deaths of four persons, namely-Awugo Joseph Oyije, who died on 2nd November, 2026; James Ogah Onma, who died on 4th November, 2026, following referral for further medical treatment; Ode Friday Ogah died on November 5, 2026; and Mr Agi Edugbeke who died on the 11th day of November, 2026.”

He added that 11 other persons were reportedly affected and were receiving medical attention, with two referred to hospitals in Makurdi, the Benue State capital.

The affected persons were identified as Otumala Ochele, Binta Sule, Onu Oboh, Adoga Onu, Upa James, Igbo Pius, Ochele Genesis, Otumala Amos, Uwa Baku, Ate Vivian Okpune and Roman Ehile.

Agada further warned that other residents might have consumed the suspected product without being identified or could be receiving treatment outside recognised health facilities, raising the risk of additional casualties.

According to him, “The House is worried that other residents within the affected communities may have consumed the suspected product without being identified or may be receiving treatment outside recognised health facilities, thereby increasing the possibility of further casualties.

“The House is further worried that the composition, source, manufacturing conditions, NAFDAC registration status, safety, dosage and possible adverse effects of the product remain unverified, raising serious concerns about the possible circulation of poisonous, adulterated, unregistered or substandard herbal medicinal products.”

He said the incident constituted a serious public health concern requiring immediate intervention by relevant federal and state authorities to establish the circumstances surrounding the deaths, prevent further exposure and ensure that those responsible, where culpability was established, were brought to justice.

Contributing to the debate, the House Leader, Prof. Julius Ihonvbere, said the proliferation of fake drugs and drinks had become a national challenge requiring a broader response beyond NAFDAC’s current capacity.

He said the agency was struggling with inadequate personnel, noting that its workforce of about 2,000 was insufficient to effectively police the country’s drug distribution network.

“This issue has gone beyond NAFDAC which has only a staff strength of about 2,000 people. The agency requires at least 10,000 staff members to be able to execute its mandate. NAFDAC does not have a presence everywhere; it is not in my village in Edo State.

“I think we need to have a holistic conversation about this problem because it is getting out of hand. If we do not do something quickly, more Nigerians will continue to die of fake drugs and drinks.”

Ihonvbere urged the House to recommend stiffer penalties for manufacturers and distributors of fake and contaminated products.

“Mr Speaker, I think we can suggest life imprisonment or even the death penalty for those involved in this criminal enterprise and may bring the DG of NAFDAC to come and tell us where they are on this matter,” he added.

Similarly, Ali Shettima (APC, Yobe) urged lawmakers to look beyond the Benue incident and address the nationwide consequences of the circulation of fake drugs.

“Let us look beyond Benue and focus on what the issue of fake drugs is doing throughout the country. NAFDAC needs to intensify its work in regulating the activities of herbal medicine producers. Selling fake products to innocent citizens in the name of drugs and drinks is very unfortunate. An enabling law should be enacted to ensure that those involved in this are penalised if they are found guilty,” he said.

Another Yobe lawmaker, Fatima Talba, however, urged caution, arguing that many Nigerians patronised unregulated herbal medicine sellers partly because of limited access to affordable and reliable healthcare alternatives.

She said, “Some of the people who patronise these do not have any other place to go to. It is not as if these people are forced to buy these products because even in the hospitals, there are fake drugs. We cannot tell these people not to patronise these fake herbal drug sellers because we have not given then alternatives.”

Peter Uzoekwe (NDC, Anambra) proposed holding market leadership accountable for the sale and distribution of counterfeit drugs, suggesting that the executives of markets where such products were manufactured or sold should be removed.

“Let us make it a duty that any market where fake drugs are manufactured or sold, we will depose the executives. If we do this, you will see that those executives would act as taskforce,” he said.

Also contributing, Ismaila Haruna, who represents Toro Federal Constituency of Bauchi State, called for an investigation into deaths allegedly linked to the use of sexual performance-enhancing drugs.

“There are existing laws in place guiding the regulation of herbal medicine. What is left is enforcement. Is NAFDAC doing its job? Again, we need to investigate why men are dying in their numbers because many times, we hear of men dying in hotel rooms and what have you,” he said.

At the end of the debate, the House resolved to invite NAFDAC, the Nigeria Police Force and the DSS to brief its relevant committees on measures being taken to curb the circulation of fake herbal medicines and adulterated drinks across the country.

The post Reps to summon NAFDAC, DSS over fake drugs, deaths appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Eyesan seeks more opportunities for women in petroleum sector
description:
By Obas Esiedesa, Abuja



The Commission Chief Executive, Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission (NUPRC), Mrs. Oritsemeyiwa Eyesan, has called for greater opportunities for women in the petroleum sector.







Eyesan made the call on Wednesday while speaking on the topic, “Breaking Barr
content:
By Obas Esiedesa, Abuja

The Commission Chief Executive, Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission (NUPRC), Mrs. Oritsemeyiwa Eyesan, has called for greater opportunities for women in the petroleum sector.

Eyesan made the call on Wednesday while speaking on the topic, “Breaking Barriers,” at the 2026 Women in NNPC Limited (WIN) in Abuja, under the theme, “Powered by Her.”

She asked women to also prioritise competence, resilience and continuous learning as critical tools for breaking barriers.

A statement by the Commission said Eyesan urged women not to be discouraged by delayed promotions, stressing that professional growth requires patience, perseverance and commitment to excellence.

Sharing her personal experience, Eyesan disclosed that she spent eight years in the same position without promotion but remained committed to her career.

Eyesan also emphasised the importance of involving men in conversations about gender inclusion and women’s advancement, noting that some of the major milestones in her career were made possible by men who recognised her competence and provided opportunities.

“I was appointed the first female Head of Strategy, not by a woman, but by a man who believed in my competence. I was also appointed as the first female EVP Upstream, NNPCL, by a man who believed in my competence, and today I stand as the first female CCE of NUPRC by Mr President, who is a man who believes that I will deliver,” she said.

Acknowledging the gradual increase in opportunities for women in the industry, the NUPRC boss called for more deliberate efforts to achieve meaningful representation, advocating at least 25 per cent participation of women in leadership and decision-making positions.

“Is it happening at the scale we want? Not quite, we need more. At least one in four. Not just because we want to make up the numbers but because we think we bring value to the table,” she said.

The NUPRC boss also commended the Group Chief Executive Officer of NNPC Limited, Mr Bayo Ojulari, for the WIN initiative, describing it as a valuable platform for positioning young women for greater opportunities and leadership roles in the oil and gas industry.

She noted that the Nigerian oil and gas industry was recording significant progress through collaboration between the regulator, NNPC Limited and other industry operators.

title: FG monitors Starlink, crypto use by terrorists, bandits
description:
The Federal Government is monitoring the use of satellite internet service Starlink, cryptocurrencies and commercial drones by terrorists and other armed groups as part of efforts to disrupt their operations and financing networks.
Starlink is a satellite-based internet service operated by Elon Musk
content:
The Federal Government is monitoring the use of satellite internet service Starlink, cryptocurrencies and commercial drones by terrorists and other armed groups as part of efforts to disrupt their operations and financing networks.

Starlink is a satellite-based internet service operated by Elon Musk’s SpaceX.

Unlike conventional internet services that depend heavily on fibre-optic cables and ground-based infrastructure, Starlink uses satellites orbiting the Earth to provide internet connectivity.

Speaking during an interview with Reuters, the Minister of Defence, Christopher Musa, disclosed that Nigeria was working with United States authorities to dismantle financial networks supporting militant activities.

“Authorities are monitoring militant groups’ use of Starlink, cryptocurrencies and commercial drones, and they are working with US authorities to disrupt financing networks,” the report stated.

Musa said the government was concerned about the growing use of emerging technologies by armed groups to coordinate operations, evade security forces and finance their activities.

He also raised concerns over attempts by Islamic State Sahel to recruit criminal gangs in northwestern Nigeria, warning that the development could transform largely profit-driven bandit groups into ideologically driven insurgents.

The minister said such a development could produce groups similar to the Islamic State West Africa Province, which operates mainly in the North-East.

Musa said terrorists and bandits were exploiting dense forests and porous borders with Niger and Benin to escape security forces after carrying out attacks.

However, he said improvements in military surveillance had enhanced the ability of security forces to track armed groups through difficult terrain, thereby restricting their freedom of movement.

The minister added that Nigeria was collaborating with neighbouring countries to disrupt cross-border movements, logistics and recruitment networks connecting armed groups across the Sahel.

“We don’t want them to develop that capacity,” Musa said, adding, “We’re blocking the logistics and taking them out from within Nigeria.”

He further disclosed that Nigeria had reached a five-kilometre cross-border right-of-pursuit arrangement with Cameroon, Niger and Chad, allowing troops to pursue terrorists and bandits across border areas.

“Musa said Nigeria has agreed a 5-kilometre (3-mile) cross-border right of pursuit arrangement with neighbouring Cameroon, Niger and Chad, allowing troops to pursue militants and bandits across border areas,” the report said.

The post FG monitors Starlink, crypto use by terrorists, bandits appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: 2027: Adebayo promises N200 petrol, end Boko Haram
description:
The Social Democratic Party presidential candidate, Prince Adewole Adebayo, has promised to end the Boko Haram insurgency within three months of assuming office if elected President in 2027.
Adebayo made the pledge on Wednesday at the party’s presidential campaign rally in Yola, Adamawa State, where
content:
The Social Democratic Party presidential candidate, Prince Adewole Adebayo, has promised to end the Boko Haram insurgency within three months of assuming office if elected President in 2027.

Adebayo made the pledge on Wednesday at the party’s presidential campaign rally in Yola, Adamawa State, where he urged residents to vote out the ruling All Progressives Congress in the next general election.

This was disclosed in a statement issued in Abuja by the SDP Campaign Spokesman, Mark Adebayo.

Speaking alongside the party’s governorship candidate, Dr Christopher Nathaniel, Adebayo blamed poor governance for the persistent insecurity in the North-East, lamenting the human cost of the insurgency and the prolonged displacement of communities.

The SDP presidential candidate recalled the military operations to reclaim communities, including Mubi, Madagali, Michika, Gwoza and Bama, from insurgents, saying successive governments had failed to provide lasting solutions to the humanitarian crisis.

He said, “We will, within three months of getting into government, put an end to Boko Haram insurgency. Between Usman Bugaje, my running mate, and I have no business with them.

“Do you know how many people lost their lives in the battle to recover Mubi, Madagali, Michika, Gwoza and Bama? That is why I salute the Nigerian Legion for coming here.

“If you don’t know, there are children who were born and grew up inside IDP camps. Yet, no single politician can explain that. So when we get to government, it will be our priority. We will end Boko Haram immediately.”

The legal practitioner said his proposed administration would prioritise security, affordable food, free education, accessible healthcare and employment, insisting that public resources should be deployed to improve the living conditions of Nigerians.

He also promised to reduce the price of petrol to N200 per litre and expand the adoption of Compressed Natural Gas-powered vehicles as part of efforts to reduce transportation costs.

“Secondly, we will force the price of petrol to N200 per litre. And I believe Christopher Nathaniel and other governors like him will convert most of the vehicles in Nigeria to CNG,” he said.

Adebayo also faulted President Bola Tinubu’s request for more time to address the country’s economic and security challenges, arguing that Nigerians needed a change of leadership and a government accountable to the people.

Earlier in his speech, the SDP governorship candidate promised to reform education, strengthen public healthcare and create employment through industrialisation if elected governor.

Nathaniel, who spoke at the rally, welcomed Adebayo and described the SDP presidential ticket as a credible alternative ahead of the 2027 general election.

He said, “My administration will restore the quality of public education in Adamawa State and ensure that children from less privileged backgrounds have access to affordable and quality learning.”

The governorship candidate also pledged to revive the state’s public healthcare system, recalling that he was born at the Jimeta General Hospital and lamenting the decline in the quality of services at public health facilities.

He said his proposed reforms would include better welfare for healthcare workers and the provision of accommodation for doctors and nurses within hospital premises, as was previously the practice.

Nathaniel also advised voters to look beyond party affiliations and assess the policy programmes and capacity of candidates seeking their mandate.

Meanwhile, the SDP National Chairman, Prof Sadiq Gombe, urged Nigerians to make informed political choices ahead of the 2027 elections, arguing that poverty and insecurity could only be addressed through purposeful leadership and people-oriented policies.

Gombe, who also spoke at the Yola rally, called on residents to support Adebayo and his running mate, Prof Usman Bugaje.

He said, “Poverty is one of the major factors contributing to insecurity, insurgency, kidnapping, and other criminal activities. Addressing the economic hardship facing Nigerians is critical to restoring peace and stability across the country.

“Therefore, our SDP presidential ticket is committed to tackling these challenges through policies that promote economic opportunities, improve living conditions and restore public confidence in governance.”

The post 2027: Adebayo promises N200 petrol, end Boko Haram appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Senate seeks compensation, sanctions over 37 artisans’ deaths
description:
The Senate on Wednesday called on the Federal Government to prosecute or appropriately punish officers found culpable in the deaths of 37 young artisans who died in the custody of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps in Minna, Niger State.
It also urged the government to pay compensation to
content:
The Senate on Wednesday called on the Federal Government to prosecute or appropriately punish officers found culpable in the deaths of 37 young artisans who died in the custody of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps in Minna, Niger State.

It also urged the government to pay compensation to the bereaved families and implement the recommendations of the independent investigative committee set up to probe the incident.

The resolutions followed a motion sponsored by Senator Mohammed Sani Musa (Niger East), who raised concerns over the circumstances surrounding the deaths of the artisans on September 17, 2026, after their arrest during an operation against suspected illegal mining activities.

Presenting the motion, Musa described the incident as a serious human rights concern, saying it raised questions about the treatment of detainees and accountability within security agencies.

He said, “The incident should not be treated as an ordinary tragedy but as a serious matter requiring transparency, accountability and institutional reforms to prevent a recurrence.”

The senator told the chamber that the Federal Government had constituted a 10-member independent investigative committee to establish the circumstances surrounding the deaths.

He said the committee had completed its assignment and submitted a report that reportedly identified serious lapses and recommended sanctions, institutional reforms and compensation for the victims’ families.

Musa urged the Senate to intervene by demanding the immediate implementation of the recommendations, particularly those concerning officers found culpable and reforms within the NSCDC.

The deaths sparked public outrage, mourning and protests in Niger State, prompting calls for an independent investigation into the treatment of the young men while in detention.

The Senate, during Wednesday’s plenary, observed a minute of silence in honour of the deceased and commended President Bola Tinubu, the Federal Government and Niger State Governor, Mohammed Umaru Bago, for facilitating the establishment of the investigative committee.

It also resolved to constitute a delegation led by the Senate President to pay a condolence visit to the families of the deceased in Niger State.

The chamber directed its committees on Interior, Human Rights, Police Affairs and Judiciary to monitor the implementation of the investigative committee’s recommendations and report back.

The Acting Chief Whip, Senator Diket Plang (Plateau Central), moved an amendment to include the Senate Committee on Solid Minerals among the committees overseeing the implementation process.

The amendment was seconded by Senator Abdul Ningi (Bauchi Central) and adopted.

Contributing to the debate, former Edo State Governor, Senator Adams Oshiomhole (Edo North), called on the Senate to condemn illegal mining, arguing that it should be treated with the same seriousness as illegal oil bunkering.

He said, “The illegal mining should be treated with the same seriousness as illegal oil bunkering, given its implications for national revenue, economic stability and the exploitation of the country’s natural resources.”

Oshiomhole urged traditional rulers, state governments and local government authorities to intensify public enlightenment campaigns against illegal mining.

He described the activity as an economic crime, arguing that it deprived the government of legitimate revenue while allowing individuals and criminal networks to exploit the country’s mineral resources for personal gain.

He also called for stringent penalties for those involved in illegal mining but cautioned against interpreting the Senate’s position as an endorsement of the deaths of the 37 artisans.

He stressed that the need to tackle illegal mining should be separated from the circumstances surrounding the deaths, particularly as the victims’ involvement in the activity had not been conclusively established.

His additional prayer was seconded by Senator Simon Lalong (Plateau South).

Lalong also urged the Senate to commend state governors and the 36 State Houses of Assembly for supporting the constitutional amendment on state police.

He described the approval of the State Police Bill as a significant achievement, noting that the proposal had generated controversy over the years before securing unanimous support from the states.

The Senate President welcomed the additional prayers but cautioned lawmakers against assuming that the deceased were illegal miners.

He said the victims were in NSCDC custody when they died, adding, “The Senate must be careful not to make assumptions about their guilt or innocence.”

His clarification reinforced the need to establish the circumstances of the deaths and determine the responsibility of those involved in the detention of the artisans.

However, Ningi raised a point of order under Order 56, questioning the relevance of Oshiomhole’s additional prayer on illegal mining to the substantive motion.

He argued that the motion concerned the deaths of 37 Nigerians in the custody of a government security agency and that the Senate should focus on justice, human rights and compassion for the bereaved families.

Ningi maintained that although illegal mining was a serious national concern, it should not distract from the immediate issue of the deaths and the need to hold those responsible accountable.

The Senate subsequently adopted the prayers, including the demand for the implementation of the investigative committee’s recommendations, sanctions against culpable officers, compensation for the families and reforms within the NSCDC.

The PUNCH reported in September 2026 that 37 artisanal miners died in the custody of the NSCDC in Minna, Niger State, triggering public outrage, mourning and protests.

A presidential investigative panel subsequently concluded that the deaths resulted from severe overcrowding, extreme heat, dehydration and neglect, rather than a disease outbreak initially claimed by the NSCDC.

The incident raised concerns over the treatment of detainees and the accountability of security agencies, with families and rights advocates demanding justice for the victims.

The post Senate seeks compensation, sanctions over 37 artisans’ deaths appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Troops neutralise 21 ISWAP fighters in Borno airstrikes
description:
Troops of the Joint Task Force, Operation Hadin Kai, have neutralised 21 terrorists around Monguno Local Government Area and the southern part of the Lake Chad area of Borno State.
The Army said the terrorists were neutralised in precision airstrikes conducted by the air assets of the Joint Task For
content:
Troops of the Joint Task Force, Operation Hadin Kai, have neutralised 21 terrorists around Monguno Local Government Area and the southern part of the Lake Chad area of Borno State.

The Army said the terrorists were neutralised in precision airstrikes conducted by the air assets of the Joint Task Force between November 16 and 17, 2026.

In a statement on Wednesday, the Acting Military Information Officer of the North-East Joint Task Force, Operation Hadin Kai, Captain Mohammed Goni, said 10 other terrorist fighters were severely injured in the operations.

The statement read, “In a significant operational success, precision air strikes conducted by the Air Assets of Joint Task Force (North East), Operation HADIN KAI (OPHK), between 16 and 17 November 2026, have neutralised 21 Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP) fighters and severely injured 10 others in separate operations around Monguno and the South Lake Chad area of Borno State.

Goni said the first operation followed intelligence reports of ISWAP fighters advancing towards Monguno.

Acting on the intelligence, he said an Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) established surveillance over the area and identified terrorists moving along a bush path northeast of Monguno.

“The subsequent precision strike neutralised seven fighters, including members of the terrorist group’s Improvised Explosive Device (IED) network. Further confirmation revealed that ABBA BOMMA, identified as a key IED team expert, was incapacitated, while four other fighters sustained severe injuries,” he said.

In a separate operation at Arinna in the South Lake Chad area, the Army spokesman noted that precision airstrikes dealt a significant blow to ISWAP’s leadership and operational structure.

“Among those neutralised was MALLAM SHARKI, a prominent member of the group’s Shura Council and Amirul Amniya (Provost Commander).

“Also neutralised was ABU SAAD, the Qaid of Sabon Tumbu. Twelve additional fighters were eliminated, while five others sustained severe injuries. Several terrorist motorcycles were also destroyed during the operation. Altogether, the two operations accounted for 21 ISWAP fighters neutralised and 10 severely injured,” the statement said.

The post Troops neutralise 21 ISWAP fighters in Borno airstrikes appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Jaiz Bank, REA seal N100bn renewable energy deal
description:
Jaiz Bank Plc has signed a N100bn financing agreement with the Rural Electrification Agency to support renewable energy infrastructure development and expand electricity access across Nigeria.
The agreement brings the agency’s total local commercial financing commitments for renewable energy project
content:
Jaiz Bank Plc has signed a N100bn financing agreement with the Rural Electrification Agency to support renewable energy infrastructure development and expand electricity access across Nigeria.

The agreement brings the agency’s total local commercial financing commitments for renewable energy projects to N450bn, as the Federal Government seeks greater private sector participation in addressing the country’s electricity access deficit.

According to a statement issued by the bank on Wednesday, the Memorandum of Understanding was signed in Abuja on 17 November, 2026, as part of efforts to attract domestic financing for sustainable electricity infrastructure.

The statement read, “Jaiz Bank Plc, Nigeria’s pioneer non-interest bank, has reaffirmed its commitment to Nigeria’s infrastructure development and improved quality of life through a N100bn financing Memorandum of Understanding signed with the Rural Electrification Agency to support renewable energy development and expand electricity access across the country.”

Speaking at the signing ceremony, the Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Jaiz Bank, Haruna Musa, said the bank’s commitment to infrastructure financing was driven by the need to support critical development projects and improve the lives of Nigerians.

He explained that investments in energy infrastructure had significant implications for economic development, business expansion, employment generation and the wellbeing of communities.

Musa noted that the bank considered infrastructure financing an important means of creating economic opportunities and supporting sustainable development.

He added that Jaiz Bank would continue to support projects capable of delivering measurable economic and social benefits, particularly in communities facing electricity access challenges.

The agreement was signed with the Managing Director of the Rural Electrification Agency, Abba Aliyu, and is expected to support the deployment of renewable energy solutions across the country.

The statement added, “The N100bn MoU, signed on November 17, 2026, further strengthens Jaiz Bank’s commitment to sustainable infrastructure financing and the deployment of renewable energy solutions as part of efforts to bridge Nigeria’s electricity access gap.

“The agreement also raises local commercial financing commitments mobilised by the Rural Electrification Agency for renewable energy projects to N450bn, representing a significant boost to domestic funding for electricity infrastructure and energy access initiatives.”

The post Jaiz Bank, REA seal N100bn renewable energy deal appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

content:
By Peter Egwuatu

UAC of Nigeria Plc has completed the sale of its 43 per cent equity interest in DP World Logistics Limited, formerly known as MDS Logistics Limited, to 22 Plus Invest Limited, a member of the Tropical General Investments (TGI) Group.

Ayomipo Wey, Company Secretary and Group General Counsel of UACN, disclosed this in a statement sent to the Nigerian Exchange Limited (NGX) on Wednesday.

The transaction, which was completed on November 18, 2026, followed approval by the Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission (FCCPC).

The company said the development followed its earlier announcement on September 24, 2026, of an agreement to sell its shareholding in DP World Logistics as part of its divestment plans.

Commenting on the completion of the transaction, UAC Group Managing Director, Fola Aiyesimoju, expressed satisfaction with the successful conclusion of the divestment.

He also appreciated the DP World team for its contributions to the UAC Group over the years, while wishing DP World and 22 Plus Invest a successful partnership and continued progress in their future business operations.

Similarly, Vice Chairman of TGI Group, Farouk Gumel, welcomed the completion of the acquisition, expressing optimism about the partnership with DP World.

Gumel said the partnership would focus on advancing a shared vision for Africa’s trade and logistics sector, particularly by strengthening supply chains, improving regional connectivity and creating long-term value for customers and economies across the continent.

He added that the acquisition marked a new phase for DP World Logistics under its new ownership and was expected to support efforts to strengthen logistics operations and trade connectivity across Africa.

title: Reps probe naira deductions from students’ fees
description: The House of Representatives has resolved to investigate the cancellation of the 2026 admission exercise of the National Teachers’ Institute, Kaduna, by the Federal Ministry of Education, as well as alleged deductions of students’ fees as operating surplus for remittance into the Federation Account.
content:
The House of Representatives has resolved to investigate the cancellation of the 2026 admission exercise of the National Teachers’ Institute, Kaduna, by the Federal Ministry of Education, as well as alleged deductions of students’ fees as operating surplus for remittance into the Federation Account.

The House also called for the suspension of further action on the cancellation of admissions into the institute’s Nigeria Certificate in Education and degree programmes pending a comprehensive review and the conclusion of the legislative process to clarify its academic mandate.

The resolutions followed the consideration of a motion of urgent public importance sponsored by Niger lawmaker, Mr Saidu Abdullahi on Wednesday.

Presenting his concerns, Abdullahi drew attention to a November 7, 2026 press release by the Federal Ministry of Education announcing the cancellation of 2026 admissions into NTI’s NCE and degree programmes, alongside the termination of all university affiliations and degree-awarding arrangements.

The lawmaker noted that the directive came while the National Teachers’ Institute Act (Amendment) Bill, 2025 which seeks to expressly empower the institute to award NCEs, undergraduate and postgraduate degrees, was still undergoing legislative consideration.

He recalled that the bill was transmitted to the Senate for concurrence on July 1, 2025, raising concerns over the timing of the ministerial directive and the uncertainty it had created for the institution and prospective students.

“The House notes that the development could expose thousands of applicants to financial losses, psychological distress and disruption of their educational aspirations.

“The House is concerned that the cancellation of programmes serving underserved communities and teachers in rural areas, particularly in Northern Nigeria, could undermine efforts to strengthen teacher education and lead to the underutilisation of public infrastructure developed over five decades,” Abdullahi said.

Beyond the admissions controversy, the motion raised questions about the financial management of the institute, particularly deductions made from gross student-fee receipts as operating surplus and subsequent remittances into the Federation Account.

“The House is concerned that the deductions had allegedly depleted NTI’s operational funds, leaving the institute struggling to pay facilitators, produce essential learning materials and conduct examinations effectively,” he added.

It also noted that the NTI Staff Union, in a statement issued on November 9, 2026, raised concerns about the implications of the directive for job security and called for a fair administrative process that would protect the interests of students already enrolled.

Following the abduction of the motion, the lawmakers urged the Federal Ministry of Education to stay further action on the cancellation of the 2026 NCE and degree admissions pending the outcome of a comprehensive review and the conclusion of the legislative process on the NTI Amendment Bill.

They also called on the Federal Ministry of Finance and the Office of the Accountant-General of the Federation to suspend deductions of operating surpluses from student-fee receipts and refund any unlawful deductions made from March 2026 to date.

The House said the intervention would enable the institute to meet its obligations to students and facilitators and sustain its academic operations.

In another resolution, the lawmakers urged the Senate to expedite consideration of the NTI Amendment Bill to establish a clear legal framework for the institute’s academic mandate.

To ensure accountability, the House mandated its Committees on Federal Colleges of Education and Finance to investigate the legality and implications of the Education Ministry’s directive.

The committees are to engage the Federal Ministry of Education, National Universities Commission, National Commission for Colleges of Education, Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board and NTI management as part of the investigation.

They are also to establish the legal basis for treating student-fee receipts as operating surplus, examine the deductions and recommend measures to protect the institute’s operational funds.

The committees are expected to submit their findings within four weeks for further legislative action, while the Committee on Legislative Compliance was mandated to monitor the implementation of the resolutions.

Established to promote teacher education and professional development through distance learning and collaboration with tertiary institutions, NTI has played an important role in expanding access to teacher training, particularly for serving teachers and learners in communities with limited access to conventional institutions.

The controversy has raised wider questions about the institute’s statutory powers, the authority of the executive to discontinue its academic programmes while an amendment to its enabling law is before the National Assembly, and the financial arrangements governing the institution’s operations.

The outcome of the House investigation is expected to clarify these issues and determine the implications of the admissions cancellation for prospective students, existing learners, staff and the future of teacher education through the institute.

In another development, a motion seeking the cancellation of outstanding loans obtained by Nigerian farmers under government-backed agricultural intervention programmes has divided members of the House of Representatives, with lawmakers disagreeing over whether debt forgiveness would offer relief to struggling farmers or reward beneficiaries who diverted the funds.

The motion, moved on Tuesday by the member representing Yamaltu/Deba Federal Constituency, Gombe State, Inuwa Garba, sought a waiver of outstanding agricultural loans, citing insecurity, climate-related disasters and prevailing economic hardship that have undermined farmers’ ability to repay their debts.

Garba argued that many beneficiaries were unable to meet their repayment obligations because circumstances beyond their control had severely affected their farming activities, investments and incomes.

Over the years, the Federal Government, through the Central Bank of Nigeria and other financial institutions, introduced several agricultural financing initiatives, including the Anchor Borrowers’ Programme, the Commercial Agriculture Credit Scheme and NIRSAL-supported facilities, to boost food production, empower farmers and strengthen national food security.

Leading the debate on the motion, Garba said, “The House is concerned that widespread insecurity, banditry, insurgency, farmer-herder conflicts, flooding, drought, climate change and other natural and human-induced disasters like soil degradation, poor soil fertility, poor irrigation infrastructure and inadequate veterinary and disease control services have severely disrupted agricultural activities, resulting in substantial crop failures, food insufficiency, loss of investments and diminished farm incomes.

“The House is concerned that many beneficiaries of government-sponsored agricultural loans have been unable to meet their repayment obligations, not necessarily due to unwillingness to repay, but because circumstances beyond their control have substantially undermined their productive capacity and financial stability.

“We are worried that the continued accumulation and enforcement of outstanding agricultural debts, including principal, interest and penalties, could push already distressed farmers into deeper poverty, expose them to asset seizures and discourage their participation in future agriculturAl activities.”

He further argued that compelling financially distressed farmers to repay the loans under prevailing economic conditions could undermine the objectives of the intervention programmes.

According to him, such pressure could worsen food insecurity, unemployment and poverty in rural communities rather than strengthen agricultural production.

However, opposing the proposed blanket waiver, the member representing Ede South/Ede North/Ejigbo/Egbedore Federal Constituency, Osun State, Bamidele Salam, said an audit report by the Auditor-General for the Federation before the House had exposed widespread abuse of the agricultural financing schemes.

Salam alleged that some beneficiaries who accessed more than N1tn under the Anchor Borrowers’ Programme diverted the funds into businesses and investments unrelated to agriculture, including real estate acquisitions.

He called for a comprehensive investigation into the intervention programmes to establish how the loans were utilised and identify beneficiaries who genuinely invested the funds in farming.

The post Reps probe naira deductions from students’ fees appeared first on Punch Newspapers.
