title: NLC, TUC end public disagreement over workers’ allowance
description:
The Nigeria Labour Congress and the Trade Union Congress of Nigeria have resolved their disagreement over the Federal Government’s N70,000 six-month transport allowance for workers.
The unions announced the resolution on Wednesday during a joint press conference in Abuja, saying they had agreed to p
content:
The Nigeria Labour Congress and the Trade Union Congress of Nigeria have resolved their disagreement over the Federal Government’s N70,000 six-month transport allowance for workers.

The unions announced the resolution on Wednesday during a joint press conference in Abuja, saying they had agreed to put their differences behind them in the interest of Nigerian workers.

In a joint statement signed by NLC President, Joe Ajaero, and TUC President-General, Festus Osifo, the organisations acknowledged that their disagreement had played out publicly but stressed that their shared history and responsibility to workers were more important than institutional differences.

They described the dispute as a family misunderstanding, which was resolved amicably through the intervention of former leaders of both labour centres.

The statement read, “The unity of the Nigerian working class is far greater than any disagreement between leaderships. Our common struggle, shared history, and collective responsibility to defend workers’ rights must never be sacrificed on the altar of misunderstanding or institutional differences.”

The disagreement centred on the N70,000 transport allowance approved by President Bola Tinubu for workers across different levels of government for six months.

The dispute became public after Ajaero and Osifo separately appeared on Channels Television’s The Morning Brief, where they disagreed over which labour centre had the authority to negotiate with the Federal Government on behalf of workers.

Ajaero argued that the NLC could negotiate independently, relying on the principle of representation under the International Labour Organisation.

“TUC can negotiate along with NLC, but NLC can negotiate alone based on the principle of most workers’ representatives of the ILO”, the NLC President noted.

Osifo, however, described the N70,000 agreement announced by Ajaero as an aberration, arguing that the TUC was not involved in the negotiations.

He challenged the NLC president to produce the ILO regulation that permitted one labour centre to negotiate on behalf of the other.

He stated, “He should show me in the ILO Regulations where it says one party is going to negotiate without the other one being there or consulted. He should show me! He should show Nigerians!

“ILO doctrine is that when you have more affiliates, and you are going for one of their events, it is not correct that the most represented will go and negotiate on behalf of the other one when the unions have their own umbrella.

“There is nowhere in ILO regulations that says a trade centre cannot negotiate for its members. It is not there! It is just that if you are going to the ILO, it is tripartite- the labour, government and the employers.”

Osifo also argued that the NLC could not negotiate on behalf of workers represented by the TUC simply because it had more affiliated unions.

He added, “But what we are saying is that you have about 60 affiliates while we have about 40. You cannot! You cannot negotiate for a body that is represented, for a body that has a trade union.

“You cannot negotiate on their behalf! It is not there anywhere! Yes, if we go to negotiations- I sit down, you sit down, and we agree”.

Ajaero, in his response, argued that the Trade Union Amendment Act 2005 made union membership voluntary and allowed workers to choose the organisations they wished to join.

“The 2005 Trade Union Amendment Act made membership of trade unions voluntary. It is the worker who determines the union he belongs to.

“Section 40 of the Nigerian 1999 Constitution, as amended, was clear that every Nigerian worker has the right to belong to any trade union, political or religious institution of his choice, which gives every worker the latitude to belong to any union of their choice,” Ajaero stated.

He also questioned Osifo’s claim of having a substantial number of workers in the federal civil service, arguing that only one TUC-affiliated union belonged to the Joint National Public Service Negotiating Council.

According to Ajaero, the council comprises eight union bodies, seven of which are affiliated with the NLC. He further argued that the TUC-affiliated union had subjected its negotiating authority to the joint body.

Osifo maintained that the two labour centres needed to participate in negotiations where their respective members were concerned.

He stated, “In that case, the two bodies must come together. We are not contesting the fact that NLC has more affiliates.

“But what we are saying is that you have about 60 affiliates while we have about 40. You cannot! You cannot negotiate for a body that is represented, for a body that has a trade union.

“You cannot negotiate on their behalf! It is not there anywhere! Yes, if we go to negotiations- I sit down, you sit down, and we agree.”

The TUC leader also questioned the legitimacy of the meeting at which the transport allowance was agreed, saying it was not a meeting of the Joint National Public Service Negotiating Council.

“But that meeting that took place was not the Council meeting. The Minister is not a member of the Council. Ajaero is not a member of the Council. The Council even has a quorum and the number of persons that must be seated to form a quorum. But at the end of the day, that meeting was not a JNC meeting. The members of JNC were not there!

“Again, if you see the release that was sent out by those three bodies, you will discover that after the last minimum wage, we got about a 33 per cent increment, and how does that work? Because from N30,000, we got N70,000.

“What you are supposed to do is that JNC will have to sit down and apply consequential adjustments,” he asked.

Ajaero, on his part, said the NLC had engaged the Federal Government after issuing an ultimatum over the workers’ demands.

“We gave the government an ultimatum; we were supposed to start an action. The government asked for four days to meet with us, and we met, and they resumed sitting after four days.

“After the meeting, the 70k allowance came up.”

He added that demands for a new minimum wage could not be negotiated without the establishment of a formal negotiation committee and wider consultations involving labour, government and employers.

The resolution of the disagreement comes amid renewed discussions over workers’ pay, following the Federal Government’s approval of a committee to examine concerns raised by the TUC over a new national minimum wage.

The TUC Secretary-General, Comrade General N.A. Toro, disclosed the development in a statement on Tuesday after a meeting between the union and the Federal Government.

The meeting followed a letter dated October 8, 2026, titled “Request for an Urgent Meeting to Address Critical National Economic, Security and Labour Challenges,” submitted by the TUC.

The Secretary to the Government of the Federation, Senator George Akume, chaired the meeting, while the TUC delegation was led by Osifo.

Other members of the delegation included Toro, Deputy President Shehu Mohammed, Trustee Akintola Benjamin and Auditor II Kamal Ibrahim.

The Head of the Civil Service of the Federation and the Permanent Secretary in the Office of the Secretary to the Government of the Federation, Ibrahim Kana, also attended.

The TUC said it had rejected the proposed six-month transport allowance, insisting that workers should receive a salary increase while discussions on a new national minimum wage were being concluded.

“In the course of the deliberations, the TUC made its position unequivocally clear on the proposed ₦70,000 transport intervention for a period of six months, which it rejected, preferring instead a salary increase pending the commencement and conclusion of discussions on a new National Minimum Wage.

“This position, alongside the other demands and concerns raised by Congress, will form part of the issues to be thoroughly interrogated by the High-Powered Committee,” the statement read in part.

The union said the committee would assess the issues raised, examine steps already taken by the government and make recommendations on outstanding matters.

“The Committee will therefore undertake a comprehensive review and reconciliation of the issues, establish the extent of actions already taken by the Government, identify outstanding matters and make appropriate findings and recommendations,” the statement said in part.

The committee comprises three TUC representatives, alongside officials from the Office of the Secretary to the Government of the Federation, the Office of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation, the National Salaries, Incomes and Wages Commission, and the Federal Ministry of Labour and Employment.

It is expected to begin work immediately and submit its report to the Secretary to the Government of the Federation within two weeks.

title: 2027: INEC dispatches 186,277 BVAS to states
description:
The Independent National Electoral Commission has said that about 75 to 80 per cent of its Bimodal Voter Accreditation Systems, which amounts to186,277 devices, has already been deployed to states ahead of the 2027 general elections.
INEC National Commissioner, Mohammed Haruna, disclosed this in an
content:
The Independent National Electoral Commission has said that about 75 to 80 per cent of its Bimodal Voter Accreditation Systems, which amounts to186,277 devices, has already been deployed to states ahead of the 2027 general elections.

INEC National Commissioner, Mohammed Haruna, disclosed this in an exclusive chat with The PUNCH in Abuja, explaining that although most states had received their materials, some were yet to collect their full allocations.

He added that all outstanding equipment and non-sensitive materials will be delivered before the end of November.

Haruna said, “About 75 to 80 per cent of the BVAs have been deployed to states. Most states have received them, though not the full complement. Some have received the full complement of the materials, but some have a few numbers left to collect”.

He, however, identified Kano, the Federal Capital Territory and Kaduna as among the states that have received full deployment of non-sensitive election materials.

“Almost all the states have received their materials. But the ones that are complete, I know FCT, for instance, Kano and Kaduna too.”

INEC had disclosed Thursday last week that it had begun the distribution of non-sensitive materials to some states ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The commission, while hosting a delegation from Kenya’s Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission, further disclosed that it has completed nine scheduled activities and was stepping up preparations following an assessment of its readiness across the six geopolitical zones.

The Commission said, “We have six zones in Nigeria. The purpose is to go around the zones to see how prepared we are, assess what the zones have put in place, the challenges and what to do.

“Right now, all non-sensitive materials are almost ready. In fact, today as we speak here, the non-sensitive materials have been lifted to some zones now.”

In 2023, INEC deployed a total of 175,856 BVAs machines to 176,846 polling units nationwide. However, in October, the INEC chairman, Professor Joash Amupitan (SAN), announced that INEC has procured an additional 57,000 BVAs devices in addition to its existing inventory to strengthen its technological capacity ahead of the 2027 polls.

With its additional procurement, The PUNCH projected a total of 232,846 BVAs devices for the 2027 elections, representing an increase of approximately 32.4 per cent over the 2023 deployment.

Amupitan also said that the maximum number of registered voters assigned to one BVAs has been reduced from 1,250 to 850.

He added that polling units with more than 850 registered voters will receive multiple BVAs. Meanwhile, in 2023, the standard operational arrangement was one BVAS device per polling unit.

Additionally, INEC has created 453 additional polling units, which brings the total number of polling units nationwide for the 2027 elections to 177,299.

Speaking further with our correspondent, Haruna stressed that the commission expects all states to receive their outstanding materials before the end of November.

“So, I’m sure by the end of the month, before the end of the month, all the states will receive the full complement,” he said.

On the distribution of sensitive election materials, the national commissioner explained that the commission had adopted a centralised arrangement involving the Central Bank of Nigeria to safeguard the materials until the week of the elections.

He said the sensitive materials had already been delivered to CBN offices across the country, where they would remain in custody until they were due for distribution.

“Of course, sensitive materials, those, we won’t start distributing them now. We take them straight to the CBN for custody until the week of the election,” he said.

Haruna added that the distribution would be conducted at the CBN premises in the presence of political party agents, the media and civil society organisations to ensure transparency.

“And, you know, we distribute them from CBN. All the agents from political parties will be there. The media is there, civil society organisations are there at the CBN premises.

“That’s where we are going to distribute them. But they have been delivered already to CBN offices around the country,” he stated.

On the deployment and configuration of the BVAS, the INEC commission explained that the commission would undertake the configuration exercise close to the elections rather than at this stage of preparation for the Mock accreditation fixed for November 28.

He pointed out that each device was customised to a particular polling unit to ensure accountability and prevent misuse.

“The BVAs, we’ll configure them close to the election. We’ll not configure them now. You know, each one is customised to each polling unit. Each BVA is for its own area, so that at least you can hold somebody responsible,” he said.

On measures being introduced to strengthen electoral transparency and improve the credibility of the voting process, the commissioner disclosed that INEC had strengthened its electronic transmission and verification procedures through the electronic version of Form EC8A.

He explained that the electronic form would provide an additional layer of verification by ensuring that results uploaded by presiding officers corresponded with the results agreed upon and signed by polling officials, party agents and security personnel.

According to him, the system would reject results where discrepancies existed between the electronically entered figures and the agreed polling unit results.

He said, “But the main thing we have done is this EC8A. There’s an e-version of it. So once the presiding officer, once they agree, they have updated, they have looked at the results, they have agreed that that is the accurate result, the polling agent signs, security signs.

“He tries to upload it onto the app. Suppose he doesn’t agree, because the one that has been entered before, you know, if there’s a discrepancy, it will not be uploaded. It will not be the same content.”

Haruna, however, said the commission was introducing additional measures to strengthen the electoral process but would not disclose all the details publicly, citing security considerations.

“There are so many things that we’re doing. But there are certain things, of course, we cannot reveal. Because if you do, it’s actually harmful for security reasons,” he said.

He added that while INEC remained committed to improving the transparency and integrity of elections, some of its operational safeguards would remain undisclosed to prevent possible exploitation.

Following the enactment of the Electoral Act 2026, the Independent National Electoral Commission has revised the timetable for the 2027 general elections, fixing January 16, 2027, for the presidential and National Assembly elections.

The commission also scheduled the governorship and State Houses of Assembly elections for February 6, 2027.

The post 2027: INEC dispatches 186,277 BVAS to states appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Fake agency: ICPC opposes Adeyemi’s bail, cites safety
description:
The Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission has urged a Federal Capital Territory High Court to reject the bail application of a suspected fraudster, Adeniyi Adeyemi, arguing that his continued detention is necessary for his personal safety.
The ICPC argued that Adeyemi c
content:
The Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission has urged a Federal Capital Territory High Court to reject the bail application of a suspected fraudster, Adeniyi Adeyemi, arguing that his continued detention is necessary for his personal safety.

The ICPC argued that Adeyemi could be physically harmed by people to whom he allegedly owed some money.

Prosecution counsel, Sylvanus Tahir (SAN), made the submission on Wednesday while opposing the bail applications filed by Adeyemi and four civil servants charged alongside him over an alleged N27bn fraud involving the purported Presidential Foreign Investment Promotion Council.

“My lord, there are many petitions against him, and the people who lodged those petitions are after him,” Tahir told the court.

He cited the case of a petitioner from Ibadan who allegedly lost money to the defendant and had been searching for him.

“We believe that it will be in his own best interest to remain in custody for safekeeping,” the prosecution counsel said.

The ICPC also described Adeyemi as a flight risk, alleging that he had access to substantial funds and could interfere with some of the proposed witnesses.

However, Adeyemi, through his counsel, Ibrahim Angulu (SAN), objected to the prosecution’s argument, insisting that he lacked the financial capacity to flee or influence witnesses because his bank accounts, including those belonging to his wives, had been frozen.

“My lord, the accounts of the defendant were frozen, including those of his wives. They have all been frozen. So he does not have the means to escape or to influence the witnesses,” Angulu said.

Adeyemi and the four other defendants, Aminu Abdullahi, Ogaba Harry, Florence Omameh and Patricia Akhigbe, had pleaded not guilty to a 36-count amended charge bordering on obtaining money by false pretence, forgery and corruption.

The defendants, through their respective lawyers, urged the court to admit them to bail, citing their constitutional rights to personal liberty and presumption of innocence, as well as provisions of the Administration of Criminal Justice Act.

They also pleaded ill health and promised to attend subsequent proceedings.

The prosecution, however, urged the court to reject the applications and order an accelerated hearing of the case.

Justice Halilu Yusuf adjourned proceedings until November 30 for a ruling on the bail applications and commencement of trial.

The judge ordered that the male defendants be remanded at the Kuje Correctional Centre, while the two female defendants were taken to the Suleja Correctional Centre.

The ICPC had alleged that Adeyemi fraudulently presented himself as the Director-General of the Presidential Foreign Investment Promotion Council, which it described as a non-existent government agency, and obtained more than N27bn under the guise of establishing the organisation.

He was also accused of obtaining another N3.8bn purportedly for the agency’s personnel costs.

According to the commission, Adeyemi allegedly forged documents bearing the purported signature of the Chief of Staff to the President, Femi Gbajabiamila, to portray himself as the agency’s director-general and secure government office facilities at the Federal Secretariat Complex, Phase III, Abuja.

Four civil servants were allegedly involved in facilitating his activities.

They are named as Abdullahi, an Assistant Chief Technical Officer in the Office of the Secretary to the Government of the Federation, accused of receiving N210,000 from Adeyemi to facilitate the allocation of office space.

Harry, an official in the Office of the Chief Economic Adviser to the President, was also accused of receiving N300,000 to facilitate the release of two official vehicles — a Prado SUV and a Land Cruiser SUV — to the defendant.

In another count, Adeyemi was accused of obtaining N20m on July 29, 2025, from Oyekunle Gbenga, Managing Director of Divine Dopacy Nigeria Limited, under the guise of a project facilitation loan for a purported N2.8bn contract awarded by the fictitious agency.

The contract was allegedly for the procurement of furniture and renovation of the official residence of the agency’s purported director-general.

The commission said the alleged offences were committed between 2024 and 2026.

Adeyemi has been in detention since July 14 and was first arraigned on October 29. His re-arraignment on Wednesday followed an amendment of the charge to include the four civil servants.

title: 179 Lagos public servants win performance awards
description:
The Lagos State Government has selected 179 public servants for outstanding performance awards, while 13 other officers and three government agencies will receive productivity honours, in a recognition exercise the state says is aimed at driving efficiency in the public service.
The Head of Service,
content:
The Lagos State Government has selected 179 public servants for outstanding performance awards, while 13 other officers and three government agencies will receive productivity honours, in a recognition exercise the state says is aimed at driving efficiency in the public service.

The Head of Service, Bode Agoro, announced the figures on Tuesday at the 2026 Outstanding Public Servants and State Productivity Order of Merit awards held at the Adeyemi Bero Auditorium, Alausa, Ikeja.

The awards, organised as part of the state’s Public Service Week, cover two categories: the Outstanding Public Servants Award and the State Productivity Order of Merit Award.

Giving a breakdown, Agoro said the 179 officers recognised for outstanding service comprised 103 senior and 76 junior officers. The senior category had 53 men and 50 women, while the junior category had an equal 38 men and 38 women.

Another 13 officers and three ministries, departments and agencies were selected for the State Productivity Order of Merit Award.

The recognition came as Agoro challenged public servants to abandon routine approaches to administration and adopt professional standards, digital skills and innovation to meet growing demands for efficient and accountable governance.

Speaking at a public lecture themed “The Public Servants of the 21st Century: Professionalism, Competence, and Mindset for a Changing Government”, he said the modern public service required more than years of experience, stressing that officers must demonstrate competence, integrity, adaptability and the ability to deliver measurable results.

He said technological changes and rising expectations from citizens had made it necessary for public servants to continually upgrade their skills and embrace digital transformation.

Agoro argued that productivity should not be measured merely by the completion of official assignments, but by the extent to which workers improved government processes, created value and translated policies into tangible benefits for residents.

He described the awards as a means of reinforcing a culture of excellence and accountability, urging recipients to regard their recognition as an obligation to sustain their performance rather than an end in itself.

He also urged unsuccessful nominees and other public servants to remain committed to professional development, discipline and innovation, insisting that improved service delivery should be a collective responsibility across government institutions.

Agoro said the quality and commitment of public servants would remain central to the state’s ability to meet residents’ expectations and achieve sustainable development

title: FG backs eight startups with N1.07bn equity funding
description: The Growth Lab programme of the Investment in Digital and Creative Enterprises (iDICE) Startup Bridge initiative has officially commenced, welcoming eight carefully selected Nigerian startups into a structured growth journey designed to strengthen their businesses, deepen their investment readiness,
content:
The Growth Lab programme of the Investment in Digital and Creative Enterprises (iDICE) Startup Bridge initiative has officially commenced, welcoming eight carefully selected Nigerian startups into a structured growth journey designed to strengthen their businesses, deepen their investment readiness, and position them for their next phase of growth.

This is the second arm of the iDICE Startup Bridge, the first being the Founders Lab, an initiative of the Federal Government of Nigeria, implemented by the Bank of Industry (BOI) and co-financed by the African Development Bank (AfDB), Agence Française de Développement (AFD), and the Islamic Development Bank (IsDB), with the aim of supporting entrepreneurs at different stages of the startup journey, providing opportunities for capacity development, access to industry expertise, and pathways to financing.

Applicants underwent a rigorous, multi-stage selection process involving assessment, evaluation, and due diligence exercises to identify startups with the potential, readiness, and capacity to benefit from the programme. The process was designed to ensure that the final eight represent startups with a clear growth ambition and the potential to contribute meaningfully to Nigeria’s digital and creative economy.

With the selection process concluded, the commencement of Growth Lab marks another significant milestone for iDICE Startup Bridge, moving from identifying high-potential businesses to actively supporting their growth. Through Growth Lab, each participating startup will access $100,000 (approx. N134m) in equity investment, alongside structured growth support, access to industry experts, investment readiness support, and preparation for future opportunities.

The selected startups for this cohort of Growth Lab are: GoDash (Last-mile Logistics, Northwest), Telios (Energy, Southeast), Vantrace (Regtech, Southwest), KrosAI (AI, South-South), Leaflet (Agritech, Southeast), Lenol (Mobility, South-South), 360gadgetsafrica (Ecommerce, North Central), and SavvyBee (Fintech, Southwest).

As part of the programme launch, the founders of the selected startups recently participated in a series of in-person onboarding sessions, held in Lagos, which brought them together with key stakeholders, peers, and ecosystem enablers, providing an opportunity to build connections, gain insights into the support available to them, and develop a clear understanding of the programme’s expectations, structure, and growth objectives.

Commenting on the launch of Growth Lab, the National Coordinator of the iDICE Programme, Ife Adebayo, said: “Each of these founders has earned their place through a rigorous and transparent process that tested not just their ideas, but how they run their businesses. Growth Lab is the Federal Government’s commitment to backing that discipline with real capital and real support. Through the Bank of Industry and our development partners, we are investing in these companies because we believe they can create jobs, attract further investment, and show what Nigeria’s digital and creative economy is capable of. Beyond funding, we will stand with them on the institutional and regulatory side, so that the next stage of their growth is not held back by barriers we can help remove.”

Over the coming weeks, the eight startups will participate in programme activities focused on strengthening their business models, improving operational capacity, navigating growth challenges, and preparing for future investment opportunities.

title: Lagos bets on jobs, businesses for $1tn economy
description:
The Lagos State Government says it is targeting a $1tn economy by 2052, banking on small businesses, employment generation, infrastructure investment and private sector growth to transform the state into one of the world’s leading subnational economies.
Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu disclosed the targ
content:
The Lagos State Government says it is targeting a $1tn economy by 2052, banking on small businesses, employment generation, infrastructure investment and private sector growth to transform the state into one of the world’s leading subnational economies.

Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu disclosed the target at the fourth Lagos State Employment Trust Fund Summit, where he said the state had expanded its budget from less than N700bn in 2019 to N4.2tn, with increased spending directed at economic development, empowerment and job creation.

The governor said the $1tn ambition was achievable but would require sustained investment in infrastructure, stronger institutions and partnerships with the private sector.

“As the second-largest economy in Africa, Lagos is charting an ambitious yet achievable course towards a $1 trillion GDP by 2052. Achieving this milestone will position Lagos among the leading economic subnationals globally, and the foundational work required to reach that destination has already begun,” he said.

Sanwo-Olu spoke at the summit, themed “Lagos Works: Building Africa’s Most Productive City”, where he presented the Lagos State Employment Trust Fund as one of the institutions expected to drive the state’s economic ambitions.

He said the fund had disbursed loans to more than 20,000 small businesses, created over 320,000 jobs and helped preserve another 173,000 jobs, with a repayment rate of 95 per cent.

“Guided by our T.H.E.M.E.S. Plus agenda, we have systematically scaled our financial capacity to accelerate this prosperity. From an operating budget below N700 billion when we assumed office, we are currently running a N4.2 trillion budget dedicated entirely to shared prosperity, strategic empowerment and aggressively reducing unemployment through enablers like the LSETF,” the governor said.

The fund’s Executive Secretary, Feyisayo Alayande, said it had disbursed more than N15bn in loans to over 20,000 beneficiaries in its 10 years of operation, describing its repayment performance as evidence that public financing could support businesses while maintaining financial discipline.

“Every N100 entrusted to our entrepreneurs is repaid and redeployed to fuel the next business venture,” she said.

Alayande said the revolving loan model had helped the fund create more than 320,000 jobs directly and indirectly and safeguard about 173,000 others that could have been lost to economic pressures.

She added that the fund had trained or connected more than 30,000 young people to employment opportunities and supported over 1,200 technology start-ups through its Lagos Innovates programme.

The Commissioner for Wealth Creation and Employment, Akinyemi Ajigbotafe, said the state had reached more than 6,500 graduates and generated over 200,000 jobs through its employment and wealth creation initiatives since 2023.

He identified the Graduate Internship Placement Programme as a major intervention for helping graduates acquire workplace experience and improve their chances of securing employment.

Ajigbotafe also said the Lagos State Job Fair had brought together more than 300 organisations and thousands of job seekers across the 2025 and subsequent editions.

On support for small businesses and informal sector workers, the commissioner disclosed that the state had equipped 800 artisans and 400 tradesmen across 60 trade associations with modern tools.

He added that the ministry had distributed 1,425 point-of-sale machines in partnership with Wema Bank to expand digital financial inclusion and support small businesses.

Sanwo-Olu said the state’s economic ambition depended on building a productive economy in which workers generated greater value, businesses expanded their markets and households enjoyed improved disposable incomes.

He also stressed the need for continuity in government programmes, citing the LSETF, established before his administration, as an example of an institution strengthened rather than abandoned by successive administrations.

title: ‘Politicians must emulate Jonathan’s 2015 election concession’
description:
Ahead of the 2027 general elections, politicians seeking elective offices have been urged to emulate former President Goodluck Jonathan by accepting the outcome of the polls in the interest of peace and democratic stability.
The Journalists Monitoring Performance for Democratic Governance, led by it
content:
Ahead of the 2027 general elections, politicians seeking elective offices have been urged to emulate former President Goodluck Jonathan by accepting the outcome of the polls in the interest of peace and democratic stability.

The Journalists Monitoring Performance for Democratic Governance, led by its President, Vincent Akpomefure, made the call at a press conference held in Maryland, Lagos, on Wednesday.

Jonathan, who contested the 2015 presidential election on the platform of the Peoples Democratic Party, conceded defeat to the candidate of the All Progressives Congress, Muhammadu Buhari, after the poll.

His decision to accept the outcome paved the way for Nigeria’s first transfer of power from an incumbent ruling party to an opposition party through the ballot box.

Speaking, Akpomefure urged political actors across the country to learn from Jonathan’s decision to concede defeat in the 2015 presidential election and facilitate a peaceful transfer of power to the opposition.

The concerns come amid recent attacks on political gatherings and leaders ahead of the 2027 elections.

On November 12, suspected political thugs disrupted a town hall meeting organised by the Nigeria Democratic Congress for its presidential candidate, Peter Obi, in Oregun, Lagos, attacking supporters and damaging vehicles.

In a separate incident on November 13, President Bola Tinubu’s motorcade was attacked with stones and other dangerous objects shortly after he observed Friday prayers at a mosque in the Garki area of Abuja.

Also, the Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission, Prof. Joash Amupitan, was confronted by Nigerian protesters in London on November 12, 2026, who blocked his movement and demanded his resignation over allegations of irregularities in the preliminary voters’ register and fears about the neutrality of the commission ahead of the elections.

Akpomefure said the warning was prompted by growing political intolerance, attacks and threats of violence ahead of the elections, which could undermine the country’s stability.

He said the government and opposition must understand that they had a responsibility to protect democracy.

Akpomefure said, “A few months ahead of this all-important election, we have seen evidence of intolerance, violent attacks and threats of even greater violence.

“We are calling on politicians to learn from Dr Jonathan in the sense that they need to accept the outcome of the 2027 elections at the local, state and federal levels.”

He, however, pointed out that the appeal was not a call on President Bola Tinubu to hand over power to the opposition but a reminder that both winners and losers in the 2027 elections should respect the people’s choice.

He urged Nigerians to defend free and fair elections, stressing that the group was not advocating a situation in which the ruling party must lose power but one in which all political parties would respect a credible electoral outcome.

He said, “The important point is not that a ruling party must hand over to the opposition only to prove a free and fair election. No. What we seek is a free and fair election that Nigerians need to accept. If the ruling party wins, let the opposition respect the outcome of the election; if the opposition wins, let the ruling party respect the outcome.”

Akpomefure said the group was using the 2027 elections to draw attention to Jonathan’s decision to concede defeat in 2015, describing it as an example of humility and personal sacrifice for democratic stability.

He said the former President’s action demonstrated that the country’s interest should take precedence over the desire to retain political power, regardless of the ethnic background of the incumbent.

Akpomefure stressed, “We want an election that will leave us with confidence, peace, trust and stability, without which we can neither speak of democracy, liberty nor press freedom.

“As journalists, we need to insist on peaceful campaigns devoid of threats and violence, and devoid of religious and ethnic sentiments. We need to remember what the civil war cost us as a nation. We do not want to see a repeat of that ugly history.”

He said the 2027 elections would be significant because they would take place 60 years after the first military coup in Nigeria, which occurred on January 15, 1966, and warned against a repeat of the events that plunged the country into the civil war.

“The January election is significant in many ways. It will be taking place exactly 60 years after the first military coup,” he said.

He recalled that the 1964 general election contributed to the crisis that preceded the coup and the civil war, which lasted 30 months and claimed more than one million lives.

The media conference also marked the commencement of activities towards Jonathan’s 70th birthday celebration, during which the group announced plans to unveil a book titled “Goodluck Jonathan: The President Who Ruled With Golden Fingers.”

Akpomefure said the book would examine Jonathan’s political journey, presidency and contribution to Nigeria’s democratic development, with particular attention to the 2015 elections and the peaceful transfer of power that followed.

He said the publication would also explore the former President’s background, rise to power, electoral reforms, education policies and commitment to democratic values.

He added that the public presentation of the book would take place in 2027, after the general elections, as part of activities marking Jonathan’s 70th birthday.

The group also announced that the Ibenanawei of Bomo Kingdom in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State, King Joshua Igbugburu, would serve as the royal father of the occasion.

The monarch, who ascended the throne in 1958 at the age of 20, was described by the group as a longstanding traditional ruler with a place in the history of Bayelsa State and Nigeria.

The post ‘Politicians must emulate Jonathan’s 2015 election concession’ appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: FG, NIM push leadership development for young professionals
description:
The Federal Government and the Nigerian Institute of Management have called for stronger investment in professional training, digital skills and leadership development to prepare young Nigerians for management positions and opportunities in international markets.
The call was made on Wednesday at th
content:
The Federal Government and the Nigerian Institute of Management have called for stronger investment in professional training, digital skills and leadership development to prepare young Nigerians for management positions and opportunities in international markets.

The call was made on Wednesday at the third Young Managers’ Summit and the grand finale of the 2026 Young Managers’ Competition, organised by the institute at the Chris Abebe Auditorium, Management House, Victoria Island, Lagos.

Representing the Minister of Youth Development, Comrade Ayodele Olawande, and the Ministry’s Permanent Secretary, Dr Maryam Kashinro, said professional qualifications alone were no longer sufficient to prepare young people for the demands of an increasingly connected global economy.

Her presentation identified innovative thinking, adaptability, digital fluency and cross-cultural competence as essential capabilities for professionals seeking to compete beyond their domestic markets.

The ministry said technological connectivity had expanded opportunities for international collaboration and cross-border business, requiring Nigerian professionals to develop the ability to work with people from different cultural and professional backgrounds.

It also highlighted the Federal Government’s Nigerian Youth Academy, which operates around the principle of one youth, two skills, as a flagship initiative for developing employability and enterprise capabilities among young Nigerians.

The programme focuses on practical vocational and entrepreneurial training, digital learning and structured mentorship, with the objective of improving productivity and equipping young people with market-relevant skills.

The ministry said Nigeria’s large and talented youth population represented an important resource for national development but identified access to relevant skills and institutional support as critical challenges.

It called for a shift from preparing young people primarily to seek employment towards developing founders, executives and professionals capable of creating enterprises and competing internationally.

The presentation also identified integrity, discipline, communication, sound judgment and teamwork as five essential qualities that should complement technical knowledge in developing effective managers.

It said professional institutions such as NIM had an important responsibility to cultivate these qualities through structured leadership development and professional training.

President and Chairman of Council of the institute, Dr Umar Mustapha, said the Young Managers’ Summit was designed to strengthen the management capabilities of emerging professionals and provide opportunities for them to engage with experienced industry leaders.

“The Young Managers’ Summit stands as a flagship youth development programme and a vital corporate social responsibility initiative designed to cultivate world-class leadership,” Mustapha said.

He described the summit as a platform that combines intellectual development with leadership training, enabling young professionals to demonstrate creativity, strategic thinking and problem-solving capabilities.

The 2026 edition was held under the theme, “Global Competitiveness and Cross-Cultural Management: Preparing Young Managers for Success in International Markets”.

Mustapha said the institute had expanded the scope of its Young Managers’ Competition to make it more intellectually demanding and relevant to contemporary management challenges.

title: Bayelsa seeks Lagos expertise on AI pricing, e-procurement
description:
Lagos State’s electronic procurement system and proposed use of artificial intelligence to track prices of goods and services are attracting interest from Bayelsa State, which is seeking to improve how public contracts are priced, awarded and monitored.
The Bayelsa State Government is particularly i
content:
Lagos State’s electronic procurement system and proposed use of artificial intelligence to track prices of goods and services are attracting interest from Bayelsa State, which is seeking to improve how public contracts are priced, awarded and monitored.

The Bayelsa State Government is particularly interested in how Lagos uses technology to strengthen procurement transparency and assess costs, including the additional expenses associated with transporting materials and executing projects in riverine communities.

The interest emerged during a two-day working visit by a Bayelsa delegation to the Lagos State Public Procurement Agency. The delegation was led by the state’s Head of Service, Wisdom Sawyer, and the Director-General of its Due Process Bureau, Aaron Timiye.

Receiving the delegation on Tuesday, the Director-General of the Lagos agency, Fatai Onafowote, said the state’s procurement reforms had evolved from a centralised tendering arrangement to a decentralised regulatory system in which ministries, departments and agencies conduct procurement within established legal guidelines.

He traced the reforms to the Lagos State Public Procurement Law, enacted in 2011 and amended in 2015 and 2021, while identifying the introduction of a comprehensive electronic procurement system in 2019 as a major step in the process.

Onafowote also highlighted the establishment of a dedicated procurement career cadre for officers on Grade Levels 08 to 17 and the development of a simplified procurement lifecycle flowchart as measures aimed at strengthening professional standards and compliance across government institutions.

The Bayelsa delegation’s interest in Lagos was partly driven by similarities in the geographical challenges confronting both states, particularly the cost implications of delivering infrastructure and public services in coastal and riverine communities.

Sawyer cited Southern Ijaw and Brass in Bayelsa and the Ojo Local Government Area in Lagos as examples of communities where transportation and logistics can significantly affect the cost of public projects.

He said the delegation was keen to understand Lagos’ electronic procurement platform and explore the application of artificial intelligence in developing reliable price intelligence systems for procurement planning and cost evaluation.

Such systems, if adopted, could help procurement authorities establish more dependable cost estimates and assess whether prices quoted for public contracts reflect prevailing market conditions and the peculiar costs of project locations.

Sawyer said the experience gained from the visit would assist Bayelsa in strengthening its procurement framework and improving the capacity of procurement officers across its ministries, departments and agencies.

The delegation received practical presentations on the Lagos procurement lifecycle and the operation of its digital platform.

Timiye described the engagement as fruitful, noting that it followed an earlier benchmarking visit to Lagos in 2022. He said the delegation also hoped to inspect selected infrastructure projects in the state to understand how procurement regulations translate into project execution and service delivery.

The team also paid a courtesy visit to the Lagos State Head of Service, Olabode Agoro, and participated in activities marking the state’s Public Service Week.

Sawyer commended the Lagos State Government for its investment in public servants’ welfare and capacity development, citing housing opportunities, car support and training initiatives.

title: ADC accuses INEC of bias, demands mock exercise postponement
description: The African Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council has accused the Independent National Electoral Commission of bias over the timing of its invitation to political parties for the November 28 mock accreditation and results collation exercise, demanding its postponement to allow adequate p
content:
The African Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council has accused the Independent National Electoral Commission of bias over the timing of its invitation to political parties for the November 28 mock accreditation and results collation exercise, demanding its postponement to allow adequate preparation.

The council also faulted the Commission’s reported position that results from Ward, Local Government and State collation levels would not be electronically transmitted and uploaded to its Result Viewing Portal (IReV) during the 2027 general elections.

In a statement issued in Abuja on Wednesday, the ADC-PCC Director of Media and Publicity, Kola Ologbondiyan, described INEC’s notice as hasty and unfair, alleging that the Commission deliberately delayed notifying the party until November 18, the final day for submitting the names of participating agents.

According to the council, INEC’s letter, dated November 16, gave political parties barely two days to meet the deadline for submitting agents’ names for an exercise scheduled to cover all 774 local government areas and two polling units in each of the country’s 8,838 Registration Areas.

It argued that the timeframe was inadequate for political parties to mobilise, train and deploy agents for an exercise intended to test the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System ahead of the 2027 elections.

“How does INEC expect political parties to adequately prepare, mobilise, train and submit their agents for an exercise of this magnitude within such a short time? This is not preparation; it is an ambush,” the council said.

It added that a mock exercise designed to test the credibility of the electoral system could not achieve its purpose if critical stakeholders were effectively excluded through an unreasonable timeline.

“INEC cannot test electoral credibility through an incredible process,” it declared, urging the Commission to postpone the exercise and provide political parties with sufficient time to participate.

The ADC-PCC’s demand comes amid growing political attention to INEC’s preparations for the 2027 general elections, particularly the deployment of technology in voter accreditation, results management and the electronic transmission of election results.

On electronic transmission, the council expressed concern over comments reportedly made on Tuesday by INEC’s Director of Information and Communication Technology, Lawrence Bayode, that the Commission had neither developed nor tested the necessary system for uploading results from Ward, Local Government and State collation levels.

It said the position contradicted previous assurances by the Commission’s former Chairman, Professor Mahmood Yakubu, and his successor, Professor Joash Amupitan, SAN, on extending electronic publication of results beyond the polling unit level.

The council maintained that Nigerians had consistently demanded real-time electronic transmission and public access to results to reduce opportunities for manipulation during the collation process.

“Nigerians fought for and demanded real-time electronic transmission of election results precisely to eliminate the manipulation that often occurs between the Polling Unit and subsequent collation levels,” it added.

It specifically questioned why Forms EC8B, EC8C and EC8D, which contain results at the Ward, Local Government and State collation levels, respectively, would not be uploaded to IReV when polling unit results recorded in Form EC8A could be electronically captured and published.

“If Form EC8A, the polling unit result, can be captured and uploaded to IReV, there is no convincing reason why the corresponding results at subsequent collation levels cannot also be made publicly accessible,” the council said.

It warned that limiting public access to polling unit results would leave gaps in the transparency of the collation process and could undermine confidence in the 2027 elections.

The campaign council further urged INEC to demonstrate its independence and impartiality, cautioning against policies that could give the ruling All Progressives Congress an undue advantage.

“INEC is not an extension of the ruling party. It is an independent electoral umpire, and it must act like one. Its credibility rests on its ability to treat all political parties fairly and transparently,” it said.

The council also appealed to Amupitan to ensure that the Commission’s actions matched its assurances, warning that the credibility of the 2027 elections would be a major test of his leadership.

“The world is watching the INEC Chairman, Professor Joash Amupitan. He must be mindful of the weight of responsibility before him. His name, his legacy and the peace of this country are at stake. History will judge him not by assurances, but by the credibility of the elections he conducts,” it added.

The campaign council reaffirmed its commitment to peaceful democratic engagement but insisted that it would continue to demand transparency and accountability in the electoral process.

“We will not be intimidated. We will not be silenced. We will continue to insist that every Nigerian’s vote must count,” the statement further read.

The post ADC accuses INEC of bias, demands mock exercise postponement appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Army defends Kwara bandit engagement, recovers 12 AK-47 rifles
description: The Nigerian Army has explained that a viral video showing troops of the Armed Forces of Nigeria and personnel of the Department of State Services interacting with armed bandits in Kwara State was part of a security operation that led to the recovery of 12 AK-47 rifles and the release of 10 kidnappe
content:
The Nigerian Army has explained that a viral video showing troops of the Armed Forces of Nigeria and personnel of the Department of State Services interacting with armed bandits in Kwara State was part of a security operation that led to the recovery of 12 AK-47 rifles and the release of 10 kidnapped victims.

The Army said the engagement was a deliberate security initiative involving bandits who had indicated their willingness to surrender their weapons and facilitate the release of their captives.

It dismissed insinuations that the interaction suggested an inappropriate relationship between the security operatives and the armed groups.

The clarification was contained in a statement issued on Wednesday by the Acting Deputy Director, Army Public Relations, 9 Division/Operation Savannah Shield, Lieutenant Colonel Ibrahim Shittu.

According to the statement, the engagement followed sustained military operations that had put pressure on the armed groups, leaving them with the options of surrendering or being neutralised.

It explained that the video circulating on social media captured only part of the engagement, which was undertaken to secure the surrender of weapons and the release of kidnapped persons.

“During the engagement, a total of 12 AK-47 rifles were recovered, while 10 kidnapped victims were released,” the statement said.

The task force described the development as a significant outcome of its non-kinetic approach, which it said was being deployed alongside sustained military operations to tackle insecurity and encourage armed elements to surrender voluntarily.

It noted that the outcome had earlier been made public through a report announcing the recovery of the rifles and the release of the kidnapped victims.

The Army also rejected suggestions that the interaction amounted to fraternisation with bandits or an abandonment of its constitutional responsibilities, insisting that it was a calculated security engagement aimed at achieving tangible results.

“Contrary to the misleading interpretations accompanying the video, the interaction was neither an act of fraternisation nor an abandonment of the military’s constitutional responsibilities,” the statement added.

The task force said it would continue to combine military offensives with intelligence-led engagements and other non-kinetic measures to address terrorism, banditry and other security threats.

It added that armed individuals or groups willing to surrender would be subjected to security screening and applicable legal procedures.

On the treatment of surrendering combatants, the Army said security personnel were required to respect the provisions of the law of armed conflict, international best practices and operational rules of engagement.

“It should be noted that surrendered combatants are not to be harmed at the point of surrender in line with the law of armed conflict, international best practices and operational rules of engagement,” the statement said.

The task force maintained that accepting surrender was a legitimate outcome of conflict resolution, particularly where it could lead to the recovery of weapons and the protection of innocent citizens.

It reassured Nigerians that the Armed Forces remained committed to protecting the country’s territorial integrity and safeguarding lives and property.

The Army urged members of the public to disregard misleading interpretations of the video and avoid circulating unverified information capable of undermining ongoing security operations.

The post Army defends Kwara bandit engagement, recovers 12 AK-47 rifles appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Mental Health: 300,000 UK youths to participate in social media ban study
description:
More than 300,000 young people in the United Kingdom will participate in what researchers describe as the country’s largest study into how a planned social media ban for under-16s could affect their mental health.
The research will examine the habits of children and teenagers, including whether they
content:
More than 300,000 young people in the United Kingdom will participate in what researchers describe as the country’s largest study into how a planned social media ban for under-16s could affect their mental health.

The research will examine the habits of children and teenagers, including whether they spend less time on their phones and what activities they turn to instead of scrolling through social media.

According to the BBC on Wednesday, 10 research projects have been commissioned across England, Wales and Scotland to reflect the experiences of teenagers from diverse backgrounds.

The study comes ahead of the UK government’s planned restrictions, due to begin in spring 2027, which will prevent under-16s from accessing several social media platforms, including Instagram, TikTok and Snapchat.

The projects are funded by health charity, The Wellcome Trust, and are expected to help shape future online safety policies in the UK and internationally. Some preliminary findings are expected before the restrictions take effect.

Researchers will use wearable technology, smartphones, digital diaries and surveys to collect data on how young people respond to the restrictions, both physically and mentally.

They will also examine whether teenagers find ways to circumvent the restrictions.

Dr Camilla Iannone, research lead at Wellcome, described the study as a once-in-a-generation opportunity to examine the relationship between social media restrictions and young people’s mental health.

“We really don’t think that this is a simple binary question of whether social media is good or bad, or whether restrictions work or don’t work.

“Instead, the teams will study whether changing young people’s digital environment leads to meaningful changes in their mental health and wellbeing.”

The participants are being recruited to reflect a diverse range of young people, including different genders and sexual orientations.

The study will also include people with existing mental health conditions, such as anxiety and depression, as well as young people who are neurodivergent.

Research groups have been established at Cardiff University, the University of Oxford, the University of Birmingham, King’s College London, the University of Edinburgh, the University of Manchester, the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine, and University College London.

The UK’s planned restrictions follow a similar model introduced in Australia in December 2025 to prevent children from accessing social media platforms.

However, the Australian ban is yet to produce clear results, according to the BBC. While supporters say it is protecting young people from harmful content, critics argue that the restrictions have been too harsh.

Online forum Reddit and a digital rights group are also involved in a legal challenge at Australia’s High Court, arguing that the law is unconstitutional.

There have also been reports of Australian teenagers finding ways to circumvent the restrictions, while the UK government has promised to introduce tougher blocks.

The post Mental Health: 300,000 UK youths to participate in social media ban study appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Borno gov builds 500-seat auditorium for Cameroon varsity
description:
Borno State Governor, Babagana Zulum, has constructed a 500-seat auditorium for the University of Maroua in Cameroon.
The governor’s spokesman, Dauda Illiya, said in a statement on Wednesday that Zulum, during the unveiling, stated that the project was undertaken in appreciation of the country’s sup
content:
Borno State Governor, Babagana Zulum, has constructed a 500-seat auditorium for the University of Maroua in Cameroon.

The governor’s spokesman, Dauda Illiya, said in a statement on Wednesday that Zulum, during the unveiling, stated that the project was undertaken in appreciation of the country’s support in sheltering thousands of Borno residents displaced by insurgency.

According to Illiya, the governor also said the project fulfilled a pledge he made at the fifth Lake Chad Basin Governors’ Forum in Maiduguri in January 2025 to undertake projects in Cameroon’s Far North Region, Niger’s Diffa Region and Chad’s Lac Region in appreciation of their support for displaced Borno residents.

The statement read, “Borno State governor, Babagana Umar Zulum, said his administration constructed a 500-seat auditorium at the University of Maroua to appreciate the Republic of Cameroon for sheltering thousands of Borno residents displaced by insurgency and to strengthen ties between Borno State and Cameroon’s Far North Region.

“This facility is a token of our profound appreciation for the hospitality and solidarity extended to our people during the years of displacement,” Zulum said.

According to Zulum, many displaced residents spent more than a decade in Cameroon, particularly at the Minawao Refugee Camp, where they received shelter, healthcare, education and access to farmland.

He thanked the Cameroonian authorities, the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees, the United Nations Development Programme and other partners for supporting them.

Zulum said the voluntary and dignified return of displaced residents became a priority for his administration after his first official visit to the Far North Region in September 2019.

“Through our collective efforts and sustained collaboration with the Cameroonian authorities and our development partners, we have facilitated the voluntary repatriation of our citizens,” he said.

He also thanked Cameroonian President Paul Biya, his wife, Chantal Biya, and the Governor of the Far North Region, Midjiyawa Bakari, for their support.

Illiya further said Zulum announced that the Borno State Government would sponsor 50 students from the state to study French at the University of Maroua.

“The governor also pledged to provide a bus to the university and announced financial support for the institution” Illiya said.

According to the governor’s spokesman, the Governor of the Far North Region, Midjiyawa Bakari, thanked Zulum for building the 500-seat auditorium at the University of Maroua.

“Your Excellency, by building this auditorium, you are telling the world that solidarity is never forgotten,” Bakari said.

Bakari pledged to protect and maintain the auditorium and said he hoped it would bring students and researchers from Cameroon, Chad and Nigeria together to work on shared challenges, including climate change, cross-border trade and security.

The post Borno gov builds 500-seat auditorium for Cameroon varsity appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: American strategist denies receiving $4.5m for Tinubu interview
description:
By Nwafor Sunday Polycarp, Online News Editor







American political strategist and media personality, Diana London, has denied receiving $4.5 million from the Nigerian government for her recent interview with President Bola Tinubu.







London, in a post on her X account on Wednesday night, de
content:
By Nwafor Sunday Polycarp, Online News Editor

American political strategist and media personality, Diana London, has denied receiving $4.5 million from the Nigerian government for her recent interview with President Bola Tinubu.

London, in a post on her X account on Wednesday night, described the allegation as a smear campaign, insisting that neither the Nigerian government nor anyone else in the country paid her the reported sum.

She said her visit to Nigeria was to interview Tinubu for a documentary and to see the country for herself.

“I unequivocally deny the claim that Nigeria’s government nor anyone else in Nigeria paid me $4.5 million. I went to Nigeria to interview President Tinubu @officialABAT for parts of a documentary and see Nigeria for myself.

“This SMEAR CAMPAIGN can make noise, but can’t change the facts or stop me from speaking the truth,” she wrote.

The denial comes amid controversy surrounding her interview with Tinubu at the Presidential Villa, Abuja, on Tuesday, and reports alleging that she was linked to a $4.5 million lobbying arrangement involving the Nigerian government in the United States.

Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar had called on the Presidency to clarify whether the interview was connected to the reported lobbying contract and disclose the details of the arrangement.

In a statement issued on Wednesday by his Director of Strategic Communication, Phrank Shaibu, Atiku said US filings identified London as a consultant to DCI Group AZ, a firm reportedly engaged by the Nigerian government through Aster Legal.

He said the filings indicated that DCI Group received a $4.5 million retainer but maintained that the Presidency should clarify whether the interview formed part of the contract.

Atiku demanded the publication of the contract, details of the payment and the release of the full, unedited recording of the interview.

He also questioned the nature of the engagement, arguing that the Presidency should establish whether the encounter was an independent journalistic exercise or part of a government-funded publicity arrangement.

The former vice president further asked the government to disclose who authorised the payment, the source of the funds and whether public money was involved.

The controversy followed London’s earlier social media posts praising the security partnership between Nigeria and the United States under Tinubu and US President Donald Trump.

In one of the posts, she described Nigeria as the United States’ greatest ally in Africa, saying the security cooperation between both countries was producing results and could create further economic and trade opportunities.

She also expressed appreciation for the opportunity to work with individuals representing Nigeria in efforts to strengthen relations between the Trump administration and the Nigerian government.

However, the posts were subsequently deleted, while London restricted access to the comment section of her X account following criticism from Nigerian social media users.

The development prompted further questions about her engagement with the Tinubu administration and the reported $4.5 million lobbying arrangement.

London’s latest statement is her first direct public response to the allegation that she received the money.

Meanwhile, the Presidency has yet to publicly clarify whether her interview with Tinubu was connected to the reported lobbying contract.

The post American strategist denies receiving $4.5m for Tinubu interview appeared first on Vanguard News.

content:
…as AFLCA 2026 honours excellence

By Bianca Iboma-Emefu

Lagos is set to welcome some of Africa’s most influential political, academic and business figures this Friday as the city hosts the 11th edition of the Africa Future Leadership Conference and Awards (AFLCA 2026).

The prestigious gathering will take place on November 20, 2026, at the Oriental Hotel in Lekki. Expected at the high-profile event are Benue State Governor Rev. Fr. Dr. Hyacinth Alia, Kogi State Governor Alhaji Ahmed Usman Ododo, Anambra State First Lady Dr. Mrs. Nonye Soludo, renowned Kenyan Pan-Africanist scholar Prof. P.L.O. Lumumba, and a host of public officials, business executives and distinguished African personalities.

Organised under the vision of Ambassador Mark Isimenmen Idiahi, Publisher of ‘The Africa Future Leadership Magazine and Convener of the awards, AFLCA has grown beyond a traditional award ceremony. It has become a strategic platform where leadership, ideas, impact and legacy converge.

The credibility of the platform is further strengthened by an accomplished advisory board that includes Prof. Rotimi Olokodana of Central Christian University, Maryland; Dr. Lucy Surhyel Newman, CEO of the African Summit; Amb. Kingsley Nwanze, Director General of the Centre for Leadership and Creative Entrepreneurs in Africa; and Chief Dr. Joy Ehiagwine Patrick, Group Managing Director of the PATJEDA Group.

Previous editions have recognised outstanding figures who have shaped the continent, among them EFCC Executive Chairman Mr. Olanipekun Olukoyede, 2027 Accord Party presidential candidate Prof. Christopher Imumolen, industrialist and flautist Dr. Tee Mac Omatshola Iseli, Amb. Obukome Elaine Ibru-Mukoro, Chief Maximus Ogbonna, Dr. Ubon Udoh of ASR Africa, and Mountain of Fire and Miracles Ministries founder Dr. Daniel Kolawole Olukoya.

This year’s confirmed and expected honourees and key participants include Prof. P.L.O. Lumumba, Governors Alia and Ododo, former Kogi Governor Captain Idris Ichalla Wada, Anambra First Lady Dr. Mrs. Nonye Soludo, Lagos State House of Assembly Speaker Rt. Hon. Dr. Mudashiru Obasa, NIMC Director General Engr. Dr. Abisoye Coker-Odusote, Barr. Mrs. Ngozi Ekeoma of Nepal Energies, Engr. Matthew Tonlagha of Maton Engineering, Prof. Duke Okoro, Hon. Ezehi M.D. Igbas, Hon. Moyosore Adebanjo, and Dr. Victor Okolobah.

Organisers say the philosophy driving AFLCA remains clear: Africa’s future will be shaped by individuals who dare to lead, institutions that champion excellence, and businesses that create lasting opportunities. The conference offers a premier stage for leadership conversations, cross-border collaboration and the inspiration of the next generation of African leaders.

Members of the press, stakeholders and the public are invited to witness what promises to be one of the most significant leadership gatherings on the continent this year.

title: Otti woos global investors to Abia, as AfrICANDO 2026 opens in Umuahia
description:
From Okey Sampson, Umuahia
Abia State Governor, Dr. Alex Otti has invited the global investment community to Abia, to explore the vast economic opportunities in the State, with the assurance to prospective investors that all investment opportunities in Abia are not only promising, but offer prospect
content:
From Okey Sampson, Umuahia

Abia State Governor, Dr. Alex Otti has invited the global investment community to Abia, to explore the vast economic opportunities in the State, with the assurance to prospective investors that all investment opportunities in Abia are not only promising, but offer prospects for long-term value creation.

Governor Otti gave the invitation while declaring open the US-Africa Trade and Investment Conference and Expo, AfrICANDO 2026, at Umuahia, the state capital.

In his speech titled, “Access, Opportunities and Prosperity,” Otti said Abia has witnessed significant developments across its 17 local government areas and various sectors of the economy, creating an enabling environment for investment and business partnerships.

“There is so much going on in Abia, across the local government areas, and in all the sectors of our economic and social expressions.

“All the investment opportunities in the State are promising and have been consciously set up to create long-term value for interested investors seeking to partner with our community of resilient entrepreneurs.”

Otti identified the African Growth and Opportunity Act (AGOA), enacted by the United States Congress in 2000, and the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), established through the African Union in 2018 and adopted by 54 member States, as important frameworks for promoting sustainable economic growth.

He told the participants that his deliberate investments in public infrastructure, security and social services have repositioned Abia, particularly Aba, as an emerging investment destination.

The Governor lauded the Foundation for Democracy in Africa (FDA) and the Abia Global Chamber of Commerce for bringing the first AfrICANDO event to be hosted on the African continent to Abia State.

Otti said the conference was of great importance to artisans, small business owners, industrialists, investors and multilateral development partners.

He informed that local government areas, government ministries and departments, manufacturers, agricultural entrepreneurs and other business interests were participating in the exhibition to showcase investment opportunities to facilitate partnerships.

He urged participants to take advantage of the conference to establish business relationships and conclude investment agreements.

The President of the Foundation for Democracy in Africa, Dr. Fred Oladeinde; the Mayor of Miami-Dade County, United States of America, Hon. Daniella Levine Cava; the representative of the Democratic Republic of Congo, Dr. Milenge Mwenelwata; and the Head of Sub-Office, Lagos, of the International Organization for Migration (IOM), Mr. Ali Ibrahim Ali, in their speeches, commended Governor Otti for his visionary leadership and commitment to economic development.

While appreciating the State for hosting the international conference, they highlighted the importance of international partnerships and intra-African trade.

Dr. Oladeinde in particular, announced plans to collaborate with the Abia State Government and other partners to establish an Africa Trade Development Centre in the State.

In the same vein, Hon. Levine Cava spoke of the readiness of Miami-Dade County to strengthen its partnership with Abia State through the Miami-Dade Gateway to Africa initiative, with emphasis in expanding trade, attracting investment and promoting innovation.

The Chairman of the Local Organising Committee (LOC) of AfrICANDO 2026 and Chief of Staff to the Governor, Caleb Ajagba, had earlier in his address described the 27th Annual US-Africa Trade and Investment Conference as a strategic platform for unlocking Africa’s economic potential, attracting investments and accelerating industrial development.

Ajagba noted that Abia hosting of the international event reflects Governor Otti’s commitment to creating an enabling business environment and positioning the State as an attractive investment destination.

Equally, the Chairman of the Abia State Diaspora Commission, Dr. Okey Agbara, and the Chairman, Abia Global Chamber of Commerce, Mr. James Umekwe, said AfrICANDO 2026 is a practical economic opportunity for connecting local manufacturers, agricultural processors and service providers with international buyers, investors and technical partners.

They said the conference would promote export opportunities, boost local production, create jobs and strengthen Nigeria’s access to regional and global markets through AfCFTA and AGOA.

Similarly, the former Chief of Army Staff, Lt. Gen. Azubuike Ihejirika (retd) and Mazi Sam Ohuabunwa lauded Governor Otti for attracting AfrICANDO 2026 to Abia.

AfrICANDO 2026, which is ongoing in Abia, attracted participants from all parts of the world.

The post Otti woos global investors to Abia, as AfrICANDO 2026 opens in Umuahia appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.
