title: Ghana Publishes Official Cost Of Residence Permit For Foreigners
description: Ghana Immigration Service has published what foreigners must pay for residence and work permits in 2026 - from GH¢259 for a student permit to US$18,000 for indefinite residence. Here is the full breakdown, including what Nigerians pay under the ECOWAS rate.
content:
Ghana has published the official cost of residence permits for foreigners, and the figures are now sitting on the website of the Ghana Immigration Service (GIS) for anyone to check. The schedule runs from GH¢259 for a student residence permit to US$18,000 for an indefinite residence permit taken by a non-ECOWAS national.

The story matters in Nigeria because thousands of Nigerians live, trade and work in Ghana under the ECOWAS protocol – and while the protocol gives free entry, it does not give a free residence permit.

What Ghana actually published

The GIS fee schedule is grouped by three categories of applicant: Ghanaians holding foreign passports, ECOWAS citizens, and other nationals. Every permit type has its own line, and the currency differs – some items are quoted in Ghana cedis, others in US dollars. Dollar-denominated fees are paid at the prevailing exchange rate on the day of payment.

The main fees at a glance

PermitECOWAS citizensOther nationals
Work and residence permit (company-sponsored)US$647US$1,293
Residence permit – missionaries, NGOsUS$388US$388
Residence permit – GIPC automatic quotaUS$388US$500
Residence permit – immigrant quotaUS$500US$647
Residence permit – dependantGH¢259GH¢388
Residence permit – studentGH¢194GH¢259
Residence permit – shareholdersGH¢2,000—
Indefinite residence permitGH¢10,000US$18,000
Indefinite status – spouse of a GhanaianGH¢5,000GH¢5,000
Right of abodeGH¢1,940GH¢3,879
Aliens identity cardUS$40US$40
Expired residence permit (penalty, per month)GH¢200GH¢300
Extension of visitors permit (per month)GH¢39GH¢65
Rotator permit (up to 6 months / 6–12 months)US$647 / US$1,000US$647 / US$1,000
Re-entry permit (single / multiple)US$100 / US$194US$100 / US$194
E-gate feeUS$50US$50

Source: Ghana Immigration Service, Immigration Service Fees and Charges (LI 2228 review).

What Nigerians pay

Nigeria is an ECOWAS member state, so Nigerians fall in the ECOWAS column, which is consistently cheaper than the rate charged to other nationals:

  • Company-sponsored work and residence permit: US$647, against US$1,293 for a non-ECOWAS national – a saving of US$646.
  • Dependant residence permit: GH¢259, against GH¢388.
  • Student residence permit: GH¢194, against GH¢259.
  • Expired residence permit penalty: GH¢200 per month, against GH¢300.
  • Right of abode: GH¢1,940, against GH¢3,879.

Free movement under ECOWAS covers entry for up to 90 days. Staying longer, working, or setting up a business still requires a residence permit, and that permit still costs money.

Where the real cost hides

The government fee is rarely the whole bill. A work and residence permit in Ghana normally needs an employer that holds an immigrant quota or GIPC automatic quota position, plus a Ghana Card, a medical report and police clearance. Companies usually pay the quota fee on top of the permit fee, and that is the part agents quote separately.

The penalties are also steep. Overstaying a residence permit attracts GH¢200 per month for ECOWAS nationals and GH¢300 for other nationals. An expired visitors permit carries the same monthly penalty, and renewing a visitors permit costs GH¢39 per month for ECOWAS citizens.

How to apply without being scammed

  1. Apply only through the Ghana Immigration Service – gis.gov.gh – or its regional commands. The full fee schedule is published there.
  2. Pay into the official GIS account and insist on an official receipt. A receipt from an individual is not a permit.
  3. Check the exchange rate used on the day. Dollar fees converted at a friendly rate can quietly add hundreds of cedis.
  4. Keep your permit valid. The monthly penalty for a lapsed permit is cheaper to avoid than to settle.

Bottom line

Ghana has not invented a new charge – it has published an existing schedule openly. For Nigerians the headline number is US$647 for a company-sponsored work and residence permit, and GH¢259 for a dependant. Anything quoted far above that deserves a second look before money changes hands.

content:
Lionel Messi, Cristiano Ronaldo, Kylian Mbappe, Ousmane Dembele and Lamine Yamal are among the high-profile footballers nominated for the 2026 Beyond Developments Globe Soccer Awards.

The nominees for the 17th edition of the awards were unveiled on Wednesday through the organisers’ official website, with Paris Saint-Germain and Spain among the prominent names following their successes in the UEFA Champions League and 2026 FIFA World Cup.

Dembele, who won the Best Men’s Player award last year, has been shortlisted again alongside 25 other players for the individual prize.

Meanwhile, Ronaldo will be seeking to retain the Best Middle East Player award after making the 2026 shortlist.

The awards ceremony is billed for December 28 in the United Arab Emirates, while public voting across 12 categories commenced on Wednesday and will end on November 30.

The organisers disclosed that fans would determine the first round of voting, with their votes combined with those of the Globe Soccer Jury during the second round.

The jury features several prominent former football figures, including Marcello Lippi, Antonio Conte, Iker Casillas and Luis Figo.

The previous edition attracted more than 30 million votes from over 200 countries and territories.

According to the organisers, supporters can cast their votes through the official website, vote.globesoccer.com, or the Globe Soccer mobile application.

title: 2027: Babangida Aliyu endorses Uba Sani for second term
description:
By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo



Former Niger State Governor, Mu’azu Babangida Aliyu, has endorsed Kaduna State Governor, Senator Uba Sani, for a second term, citing his administration’s efforts in restoring peace and promoting development across the state.







Aliyu, who is Chairman of the Board of Tru
content:
By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo

Former Niger State Governor, Mu’azu Babangida Aliyu, has endorsed Kaduna State Governor, Senator Uba Sani, for a second term, citing his administration’s efforts in restoring peace and promoting development across the state.

Aliyu, who is Chairman of the Board of Trustees of the Sir Ahmadu Bello Memorial Foundation (SABMF), gave the endorsement on Wednesday while delivering the keynote address at the Kaduna Summit on Inclusivity, Good Governance and Sustainable Development organised by the foundation.

He said Sani deserved another term to consolidate the gains recorded by his administration, particularly in addressing insecurity and rebuilding harmony in a state previously troubled by ethno-religious crises.

According to him, the improved security situation has enabled farmers to return to their farms, while some schools previously shut down because of insecurity have reopened.

The former governor also commended Sani’s inclusive approach to governance, noting that his engagement with traditional rulers, religious leaders, women, youths, civil society organisations and non-indigenes had helped strengthen public confidence and rebuild trust between the government and residents.

He observed that Muslims and Christians were increasingly living together peacefully across the state, attributing the development to what he described as Sani’s purposeful leadership and commitment to inclusivity.

Aliyu urged Kaduna residents to support and vote for the governor in the 2027 governorship election, arguing that continuity was necessary to sustain peace, stability and development.

“Let us not gamble with peace. Let us not abandon progress midway,” he said.

Also calling for continuity, the Director-General of SABMF, Engr. Abubakar Gambo Umar, said Kaduna needed leadership that united its diverse population rather than divided it.

In his welcome address, Umar said the state required leadership that judged people by their character, ideas and contributions rather than stereotypes or inherited suspicion.

He expressed satisfaction with what he described as Sani’s efforts in institution-building, expanding opportunities and promoting peace and inclusivity.

Umar noted that Kaduna remained the headquarters of Northern Nigeria, adding that positive developments in the state could have beneficial effects across the region.

He said Sani deserved a second term to consolidate the achievements of his administration.

Meanwhile, the Speaker of the House of Representatives, Tajudeen Abbas, has urged stakeholders to ensure that the summit translated commendations into accountability, constructive criticism and practical recommendations for improved governance.

Abbas, who chaired the occasion, was represented by the Deputy Leader of the House, Rep. Ado Doguwa.

He commended the foundation for providing a platform for constructive engagement on security, good governance and sustainable development, describing Kaduna as strategically important to Nigeria’s political, economic and social development.

The Speaker said good governance should be measured by leadership quality, institutional integrity and responsible management of public resources, stressing that transparency, accountability, responsiveness and respect for the rule of law were essential.

He also commended Sani for allowing his administration’s programmes and projects since 2023 to undergo constructive scrutiny, describing such openness as important to democratic accountability and improved service delivery.

Abbas highlighted the governor’s engagement with traditional rulers, religious leaders, women, youths and civil society organisations, as well as peace-building initiatives, including the establishment of the Disarmament, Demobilisation and Reintegration Peace and Security Committee.

He said lasting peace required more than security operations, noting that dialogue, trust and reconciliation were equally important.

However, he acknowledged continuing security challenges in parts of Kaduna, particularly recent attacks in Southern Kaduna, and expressed sympathy with families affected by the incidents.

The Speaker identified intelligence sharing, inter-agency cooperation and community engagement as important components of the Kaduna Peace Model.

He also highlighted collaboration with federal security agencies, the establishment of the Kaduna Vigilance Service and the State Security Trust Fund as part of efforts to address insecurity.

On development, Abbas called for sustained investment in education, healthcare, agriculture, infrastructure and skills acquisition, urging stronger partnerships among government, the private sector, development institutions and local communities.

He urged participants to approach the summit with openness and objectivity, stressing the need to identify both achievements and areas requiring improvement.

Abbas also reaffirmed the National Assembly’s commitment to responsible legislation and effective oversight to ensure that public resources translated into tangible benefits for citizens.

He called for stronger collaboration among the federal, state and local governments, describing traditional institutions as indispensable partners in promoting social cohesion, resolving disputes and mobilising communities for development.

The summit, held in Kaduna on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, brought together government officials, traditional rulers, religious leaders, civil society organisations, development partners and other stakeholders to discuss inclusivity, good governance and sustainable development.

title: Xi, Trump, Putin Exchange Greetings Before Historic China Summit
description: The leaders of China, the United States and Russia exchanged greetings as they met in Shenzhen on Wednesday, a day before their history-making first formal trilateral summit in the Chinese city.The agenda for Thursday’s meeting between presidents Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin &md
content:
The leaders of China, the United States and Russia exchanged greetings as they met in Shenzhen on Wednesday, a day before their history-making first formal trilateral summit in the Chinese city.

The agenda for Thursday’s meeting between presidents Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin — which has raised fears of a carve-up into new “spheres of influence” — was unclear, however.

And the three-way meeting was set to last “no more than an hour”, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told Russian state media Wednesday.

When Trump touched down in Shenzhen, Xi became the first Chinese paramount leader in decades to welcome a foreign leader as he arrived, mirroring the US president’s gesture at Joint Base Andrews in September.

Trump descended the stairs from his plane to be met by Xi, as well as renditions of both countries’ national anthems and fighter jets that flew overhead and left colourful vapour trails.

The pair strolled down a red carpet lined with people waving pom-poms, brandishing Chinese and US national flags, and shouting: “A warm welcome to you!”

A motorcade of dark limousines later carried Trump into the city, where the streets had been cleared of traffic, an AFP reporter observed.

Xi, Trump, Putin and other leaders attending the broader Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit then gathered for a welcome dinner, and the three briefly exchanged greetings before a group photo.

“I look forward to an in-depth exchange of views with you on major issues concerning China-US relations, Asia-Pacific cooperation, and the global landscape, with the aim of advancing a constructive, strategically stable relationship between our two nations,” Xi told Trump, according to Chinese state news agency Xinhua.

Sanctions ‘Failed’: Putin

Washington had signalled that the Ukraine war — something Xi vehemently sees as not China’s problem — was not expected to be addressed in the trilateral meeting, before Trump said that it would.

The summit is expected to include discussions of the Iran war and nuclear disarmament, according to Washington, after a US-Russia bilateral treaty on atomic weapons expired in February.

Beijing has long maintained that the US and Russia should reduce their giant nuclear arsenals before it agrees to talks on its smaller stockpile.

Earlier on Wednesday, Putin struck a defiant tone on his war in Ukraine, saying Western sanctions provoked by the 2022 invasion had “failed”.

Addressing the APEC gathering, the Russian leader said he expected the trilateral summit to be “highly useful”.

“At a time when military-political risks are on the rise, what is desperately needed is unity rather than division… and dialogue rather than ultimatums,” Putin said.

The Russian leader has been largely shunned by the West since his 2022 offensive in Ukraine began, but has found an audience with Trump.

However, “full-scale” talks solely between Putin and Trump are unlikely to take place during their visits to China, Moscow said, according to Russian state media.

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, also in Shenzhen, said sanctions would “continue to increase as long as this war goes on”.

Ukraine’s Foreign Minister Andriy Sybiga, speaking to reporters in Kyiv, said he hoped Xi and Trump would put “pressure on Russia to end the war”.

Kim Incoming?

Putin and Xi met, their fifth tete-a-tete this year, including one by video link. The two men have long touted their strong personal friendship.

Xi urged closer ties with Moscow, saying the nations should “leverage the mechanisms for exchanges between the two countries’ governments, legislative bodies, militaries and political parties”.

Trump came to China from the Philippines, where a day earlier he met fellow leaders of the Quad — Australia, Japan and India — for the first time in his second term.

The grouping is broadly aimed at counterbalancing China’s regional influence.

Trump has also floated the possibility of meeting Kim Jong Un in China, saying the North Korean leader “would like” to meet, although there has been no confirmation from Pyongyang.

Trump was in the Philippines for a summit of the 11-member Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) where there were protests against a US supply chain initiative.

The spectre of Trump’s ongoing tariff blitz has loomed large over his recent travels.

Chinese Premier Li Qiang on Monday slammed what he called a “countercurrent of unilateralism and protectionism” while touting Beijing’s own expanding trade with ASEAN.

On Tuesday, a combative Trump doubled down, saying the United States would catch China in rare-earths production “within 10 months”.

AFP

The post Xi, Trump, Putin Exchange Greetings Before Historic China Summit appeared first on Channels Television.

content:
…Promises N200 petrol, affordable housing, jobs

By Henry Umoru

ABUJA — The Social Democratic Party (SDP) has pledged to tackle poverty, insecurity, unemployment and other socio-economic challenges facing Nigerians if elected into power in the 2027 general elections.

The party said addressing poverty and economic hardship was critical to tackling insecurity, insurgency, kidnapping and other criminal activities across the country.

Speaking on Wednesday at the SDP presidential campaign rally in Yola, Adamawa State, the party’s National Chairman, Professor Sadiq Gombe, urged Nigerians to make informed political choices ahead of the 2027 elections, saying poverty and insecurity required purposeful leadership and people-oriented policies.

Gombe urged residents to support the party’s presidential candidate, Prince Adewole Adebayo, and his running mate, Professor Usman Bugaje, saying the ticket was committed to addressing the country’s challenges through policies that would create economic opportunities, improve living conditions and restore public confidence in governance.

In a statement issued on Wednesday by the National Coordinator of the SDP Presidential Campaign Council, Dr Yunusa Tanko, the party chairman urged Adamawa residents to assess the records, character and policy proposals of candidates before deciding whom to support in the 2027 elections.

In his remarks, the presidential candidate, Adebayo, said an SDP-led administration would redefine governance by ensuring that public resources were deployed for the benefit of Nigerians, with priority given to security, education, healthcare, housing, food security and employment.

Describing the SDP as a party founded on democratic values and social justice, he said its philosophy was anchored on the belief that political power belonged to the people and that government resources must be used to improve their welfare.

He said his proposed administration would focus on implementing the fundamental objectives and directive principles of state policy contained in Chapter Two of the Constitution, particularly provisions relating to poverty reduction and citizens’ welfare.

“Government is the organisation selected by you through your votes. Government must provide security, accountability, good food, affordable housing, quality education and accessible healthcare. It must work for the people who elected it,” he said.

On security, Adebayo identified terrorism, banditry and kidnapping as some of Nigeria’s most pressing challenges, promising decisive measures to address them through improved security management and better support for security personnel.

He also pledged to strengthen the welfare and operational capacity of the armed forces and other security agencies, saying personnel responsible for protecting the country would receive the necessary equipment, funding and support to discharge their duties.

On economic recovery, the SDP candidate said his administration would pursue policies that encouraged production, investment and job creation rather than relying excessively on taxation and borrowing.

He argued that Nigeria’s wealth should be invested in developing human capital through education, healthcare, agriculture, technology and industrialisation, describing these sectors as critical drivers of national prosperity.

On education, Adebayo promised compulsory, qualitative and free education from primary to tertiary levels, alongside vocational and adult education programmes to provide opportunities for Nigerians who could not access formal schooling.

He also pledged improved access to healthcare, affordable food and decent housing, promising policies that would enable workers to meet their basic needs and save from their earnings.

The presidential candidate further promised to reduce transportation costs by promoting the conversion of vehicles to Compressed Natural Gas (CNG), while pledging that petrol would sell for N200 per litre under his proposed administration.

He also outlined plans for a railway corridor linking the Lake Chad region through Borno, Adamawa, Taraba and Benue to Kogi and parts of the South-East and South-South, saying the project would boost transportation, trade and economic integration.

Describing Adamawa as a major agricultural and agro-industrial hub, Adebayo said the state’s natural resources, fertile land and livestock potential could be harnessed through investments in food production, processing and manufacturing.

He urged Nigerians to protect the integrity of the 2027 elections by refusing to sell their voter cards, checking their polling units and participating actively in the electoral process.

He also called on security personnel to remain loyal to the Constitution and protect the rights of citizens irrespective of their political affiliations.

Meanwhile, the SDP governorship candidate in Adamawa State, Dr Christopher Nathaniel, outlined his development agenda, promising reforms in education, healthcare, transportation, agriculture and industrialisation if elected.

Nathaniel said his administration would restore the quality of public education and ensure that children from less privileged backgrounds had access to affordable and quality learning opportunities.

Recalling that he was born at Jimeta General Hospital, he expressed concern over the decline in public healthcare services and promised to improve hospital facilities and the welfare of medical personnel, including providing accommodation for doctors and nurses within hospital premises.

On transportation, the governorship candidate said the state had commenced investments in CNG-powered transportation, with about 1,000 tricycle operators already benefiting from the initiative.

He claimed that participating operators were earning an additional N10,000 daily, representing an estimated N10 million injected into the local economy every day, adding that the programme would be expanded to create more economic opportunities.

Nathaniel also identified Adamawa’s livestock and agricultural resources as major opportunities for industrial growth, proposing the establishment of industries for processing animal hides and skins, manufacturing products from cattle horns and producing organic fertiliser from animal waste.

He said his administration would establish agro-processing industries for groundnuts, beans and soya beans to encourage local production, reduce dependence on raw material exports and create jobs for young people.

Also speaking, Tanko said the party’s presidential ticket would prioritise the fight against poverty and insecurity, describing the two challenges as central to Nigeria’s development concerns.

He urged supporters to take ownership of the campaign, claiming that the SDP was the first political party to present a documented manifesto for its 2027 presidential campaign.

According to him, the manifesto would provide Nigerians with a basis for assessing the candidates’ promises and holding them accountable.

Tanko urged Adamawa residents to spread the party’s message across their communities, saying the 2027 elections offered Nigerians an opportunity to demand accountable leadership and a government committed to addressing their everyday challenges.

The rally, held in Yola, attracted SDP leaders, candidates, party supporters and other stakeholders as the party intensified its mobilisation ahead of the 2027 general elections.

title: ‎Tinubu receives state police bill for assent

‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru, Abuja



President Bola Tinubu has received the Constitution (Sixth Alteration) Bill, which seeks to establish state police in Nigeria.



‎The bill was formally transmitted to him today by his Special Advisers on Senate and House of Representatives Matters, Senator Basheer
content:
‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru, Abuja

President Bola Tinubu has received the Constitution (Sixth Alteration) Bill, which seeks to establish state police in Nigeria.

‎The bill was formally transmitted to him today by his Special Advisers on Senate and House of Representatives Matters, Senator Basheer Lado and Dr Wasiu Olanrewaju-Smart.

‎This was disclosed via a statement by the Chief of Staff to the PresPolice and Chairman, Presidential Working Group on State Police, Rt. Hon. Femi Gbajabiamila.

‎According to the statement, “All 36 State Houses of Assembly have approved the Bill, exceeding the constitutional requirement of at least 24 States, representing two-thirds of the 36 States, as stipulated in Section 9(2) of the Constitution.”

‎It further stated that President Tinubu will review the Constitution Alteration Bill in consultation with the Attorney-General of the Federation.

‎”He will assent to the bill at a formal signing ceremony,” it added.

‎Meanwhile, Honourable Gbajabiamila, has said that the Presidential Working Group on State Police, which he chairs, with the support of the Policy Advisory Committee, has undertaken extensive stakeholder engagement and nationwide consultations towards developing a draft National Policing Bill.

‎”The draft bill has been submitted to the Federal Ministry of Justice for legislative drafting validation. Upon receipt of the validated version, the Working Group will review it and present it, alongside its report, to Mr President for consideration,” he said.

‎The former Speaker of the House of Representatives stated, “President Tinubu expresses his appreciation to the President of the Senate, the Speaker of the House of Representatives, members of the National Assembly, the Clerk to the National Assembly, the 36 State Governors, the State Houses of Assembly, and all Nigerians who have demonstrated a shared commitment to addressing the nation’s security challenges.”

title: ADC leaders lazy, entitled politicians – NDC campaign DG
description:
By Dickson Omobola



Director-General of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, National Campaign Council, Ibrahim Abdulkareem, Wednesday, said some leaders of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, as lazy and entitled politicians.



Abdulkareem also said they had failed to establish clear terms fo
content:
By Dickson Omobola

Director-General of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, National Campaign Council, Ibrahim Abdulkareem, Wednesday, said some leaders of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, as lazy and entitled politicians.

Abdulkareem also said they had failed to establish clear terms for the coalition they were seeking to build.

He faulted the ADC leaders for failing to agree on power-sharing arrangements and a presidential candidate before bringing politicians into the coalition, saying the North should not continue to dominate the country’s leadership.

Speaking on Prime Time, an Arise Television programme, he said: “I used to term some of the people I see in ADC as lazy politicians. Right from time, even when they are constructing this coalition that they talk about, instead of them finding a way of doing what the All Progressives Congress, APC, had done, put everything in black and white that we want to come for a coalition. And this coalition, this is the person that we want to be the president, or we are zoning this part of what we are going to do to this part of the country.

“At that time, everybody that is coming into that coalition knows exactly why he’s coming, so it’s not going to be any problem in trying to see who becomes what. Immediately we started this thing they started to say Peter Obi is a vice-presidential candidate to Atiku. What kind of coalition is that? The entitlement from the elite, I find it very annoying sometimes.

“You just decide the North. Which North? You talk like you own something that you. There is no right given to Atiku, for example, to say everybody must surrender. We have been ruling from Gen Ibrahim Babangida (retd) to the late Muhammadu Buhari. But look at where we are.

“Go and see our streets. Go and see our villages. Look at how we have been ravaged. But since somebody is still coming today, trying to play this northern card at this level, it’s time to start thinking how can we hire somebody, irrespective of where he’s coming from, irrespective of religion or tribe, somebody that we know he has this integrity, somebody that can make these public funds to be used for public good, somebody that can be accountable, not people that are old and full of entitlement.”

title: Lagos-Ibadan Expressway gridlock leaves commuters stranded for hours
description:
Motorists and commuters were stranded for several hours on Wednesday following the resumption of construction work on a pedestrian bridge around the Aseese area of the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway, which triggered a massive traffic gridlock.







The congestion paralysed movement on both sides of the e
content:
Motorists and commuters were stranded for several hours on Wednesday following the resumption of construction work on a pedestrian bridge around the Aseese area of the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway, which triggered a massive traffic gridlock.

The congestion paralysed movement on both sides of the expressway, with motorists travelling towards Lagos held up from the Redemption Camp area to Aseese bus stop, while those heading towards Ogun State were trapped from the Long Bridge area to Aseese.

The scale of the gridlock left commuters spending unusually long hours on journeys that would ordinarily take a fraction of the time.

One of our correspondents, who boarded a commercial vehicle from Ibadan shortly after 11am, did not arrive in Magboro, Ogun State, until about 5.30pm.

Another motorist lamented spending eight hours travelling from Mowe to Magboro, highlighting the severity of the traffic situation.

The gridlock persisted as late as 10pm, with both sections of the expressway reportedly almost completely blocked.

Efforts by some motorists to escape the congestion by driving against the flow of traffic further compounded the situation, as they obstructed vehicles moving in the appropriate lanes.

With vehicular movement severely restricted, commercial motorcyclists cashed in on the situation, making brisk business by conveying stranded commuters through alternative routes.

The renewed construction work on the pedestrian bridge at Aseese was identified as the immediate trigger of the traffic disruption.

title: FIFA picks Amokachi, four others to oversee NFF until May 2027
description:
World football governing body FIFA has appointed former Super Eagles striker Daniel Amokachi and four others to a five-member normalisation committee tasked with overseeing the affairs of the Nigeria Football Federation (NFF).



The committee will be chaired by former NFF electoral committee chairm
content:
World football governing body FIFA has appointed former Super Eagles striker Daniel Amokachi and four others to a five-member normalisation committee tasked with overseeing the affairs of the Nigeria Football Federation (NFF).

The committee will be chaired by former NFF electoral committee chairman Sampson Ebomhe and is expected to manage the federation’s transition and organise fresh elections for a new leadership.

Its mandate will run until May 31, 2027, at the latest.

FIFA communicated the appointments in a letter sent to the NFF secretariat on Wednesday, following consultations with the Confederation of African Football (CAF).

Other members of the committee are governance expert Dr Joe Abah, veteran sports journalist and administrator Godwin Enakhena, and Amina Yerima.

“We refer to the decision of the Bureau of the FIFA Council of 22 October 2026 to appoint a normalisation committee for the Nigeria Football Federation.

“In this respect, following consultation with CAF, we hereby communicate the composition of the normalisation committee as follows: Mr Sampson Ebomhe (chairman), Dr Joe Abah (member), Mr Godwin Enakhena (member), Ms Amina Yerima (member) and Mr Daniel Amokachi (member),” the letter read.

The world football governing body said the appointees would commence their duties immediately, subject to eligibility screening by its Review Committee in line with FIFA Governance Regulations.

Their final confirmation will depend on the outcome of the screening exercise.

FIFA also prohibited members of the committee from contesting any position in the forthcoming NFF elections, regardless of whether they resign or have their appointments revoked.

“None of the members of the normalisation committee will be eligible for the positions to be filled during the upcoming NFF elections under any circumstances, including in the event that their mandate as a member of the normalisation committee is revoked or that they resign from their position,” the letter added.

FIFA further stated that it could, in consultation with CAF, withdraw the appointment of any committee member or expand the committee by appointing additional members.

The intervention follows the resignation of NFF President Ibrahim Gusau, General Secretary Mohammed Sanusi and members of the federation’s executive committee on August 27, 2026, amid growing criticism of the country’s football administration.

The development disrupted arrangements for the NFF elective congress scheduled for September 27, prompting FIFA and CAF to step in and approve the establishment of a normalisation committee to supervise the transition.

Ebomhe, who will lead the committee, has previously held several positions in Nigerian sports administration.

In August 2025, he was appointed vice-chairman of the seven-member electoral committee established by the National Sports Commission to conduct elections into national sports federations.

He also chaired the NFF Electoral Committee responsible for conducting the federation’s executive committee elections in Warri, Delta State, in 2014.

Additionally, in February 2014, he was appointed member-secretary of the First Instance Body for the NFF Club Licensing System, where he worked alongside former NFF vice-president Shehu Dikko, who is now chairman of the National Sports Commission.

Lawyer and author Charles Omole has said that he does not expect President Bola Tinubu to make an alteration to the National Policing Bill transmitted to him by the National Assembly.

Omole, who stated this during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Wednesday.

He explained that altering the bill would return the process to the Senate, House of Representatives and state houses of assembly for their approval.

Omole noted further that the constitutional amendment is not the meat and bone of policing but simply allows state police to exist, while the National Policing Bill specifies the structure and functions of the state police.

He, however, said that the National Policing Bill could not be considered until the constitutional amendment had gone through.

He explained that while the 36 states would have their own police service, the police in the Federal Capital Territory would be under the control of the federal police service.

Omole, however, said that part of the recommendation under the bill is that states cannot buy their own arms and ammunition at will.

title: NFF Crisis: FIFA names Daniel Amokachi, Joe Abah, three others to oversee Nigerian football
description:
World football governing body FIFA has appointed a five-member normalisation committee to oversee the affairs of the Nigeria Football Federation (NFF), with former chairman of the federation’s electoral committee, Sampson Ebomhe, named as its chairman.
The committee is expected to manage the transit
content:
World football governing body FIFA has appointed a five-member normalisation committee to oversee the affairs of the Nigeria Football Federation (NFF), with former chairman of the federation’s electoral committee, Sampson Ebomhe, named as its chairman.

The committee is expected to manage the transition in Nigerian football administration and organise fresh elections to produce a new NFF leadership. Its mandate will run until May 31, 2027, at the latest.

In a letter sent to the NFF secretariat on Wednesday, FIFA announced the composition of the committee following consultations with the Confederation of African Football (CAF).

Other members are governance expert Dr Joe Abah, veteran sports journalist and administrator Godwin Enakhena, Amina Yerima and former Super Eagles forward Daniel Amokachi.

FIFA said the members would assume their responsibilities with immediate effect, subject to eligibility checks by its Review Committee in line with the organisation’s Governance Regulations.

Their appointments will be confirmed based on the outcome of the screening process.

The world football governing body also stated that none of the committee members would be eligible to contest any position in the forthcoming NFF elections.

It said the restriction would remain in force even if a member resigned or had their mandate revoked before the elections.

FIFA, in consultation with CAF, also reserved the right to withdraw the mandate of any committee member or appoint additional members where necessary.

The development follows the resignation of NFF President Ibrahim Gusau, General Secretary Mohammed Sanusi and members of the federation’s executive committee on August 27, 2026, amid growing criticism of the country’s football administration.

Their departures disrupted preparations for the NFF elective congress scheduled for September 27, prompting FIFA and CAF to intervene and approve the establishment of a normalisation committee to oversee the transition.

Ebomhe has previously held several positions in Nigerian football administration.

In August 2025, he was appointed vice-chairman of a seven-member electoral committee constituted by the National Sports Commission to oversee elections into national sports federations.

He also chaired the NFF Electoral Committee that conducted elections into the federation’s executive committee in Warri, Delta State, in 2014.

In February of the same year, he was appointed member-secretary of the First Instance Body for the NFF Club Licensing System, where he worked alongside former NFF vice-president Shehu Dikko, who is now chairman of the National Sports Commission.

title: Adegoke pledges to pursue federal projects, opportunities for Osun Central
description:
From Lateef Dada, Osogbo
The All Progressives Congress (APC) senatorial candidate for Osun Central, Barrister Kunle Rasheed Adegoke (SAN), has pledged to pursue federal projects, institutions and development opportunities for the district, saying it should no longer be overlooked in the allocation o
content:
From Lateef Dada, Osogbo

The All Progressives Congress (APC) senatorial candidate for Osun Central, Barrister Kunle Rasheed Adegoke (SAN), has pledged to pursue federal projects, institutions and development opportunities for the district, saying it should no longer be overlooked in the allocation of national resources.

Adegoke, popularly known as KRAD, made the pledge on Wednesday while unveiling his first-term development manifesto at his campaign office in Alekuwodo, Osogbo.

He said his bid to represent the district in the Senate was driven by a desire to attract greater federal investment, empower residents and ensure the area’s economic and human resources contribute to tangible development.

According to Adegoke, effective senatorial representation involves more than legislative debates and political engagement, and it also requires strategic advocacy, securing federal interventions and connecting constituents with available opportunities.

“I recognise that a senator cannot single-handedly build every road, employ every graduate or solve every challenge. But a senator can advocate effectively, legislate responsibly, connect people to opportunities, attract federal attention and insist on accountability,” Adegoke said.

He outlined five pillars for his proposed first-term programme: federal presence, human capital development, economic growth, legislative impact and accountability.

He pledged to advocate for the establishment and expansion of federal government offices, agencies, training centres and development programmes across the district’s 10 local government areas. He also said he would lobby for federal road rehabilitation, improved electricity infrastructure, water projects and other interventions.

On agriculture, Adegoke said he would work to shift the sector from predominantly subsistence farming towards a modern, commercially viable economy by improving access to finance, processing facilities, storage and markets.

“Agriculture remains central to Osun’s economy, and our farmers deserve more than seasonal promises. I will champion an agricultural programme focused on production, processing, financing, storage and market access,” he said.

He added that he would advocate for affordable agricultural loans through federal programmes and development finance institutions.

On human capital development, Adegoke proposed expanding scholarship opportunities, skills training, enterprise support and healthcare advocacy, with a particular focus on young people and women.

He also pledged to sponsor bills, scrutinise government policies and promote initiatives he said would benefit constituents. He said he would provide regular accountability reports and maintain engagement with communities across the district.

Osun Central comprises Boluwaduro, Boripe, Ifedayo, Ifelodun, Ila, Irepodun, Odo-Otin, Olorunda, Orolu and Osogbo local government areas. Describing the district as rich in agricultural, commercial, cultural and intellectual resources, Adegoke said federal support was needed to stimulate local growth.

“Osun Central must no longer be an afterthought in the distribution of federal projects, institutions, agencies and opportunities. We must be visible in Abuja and feel the impact of representation in our communities,” Adegoke added.

The post Adegoke pledges to pursue federal projects, opportunities for Osun Central appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: 2027: Atiku challenges Tinubu to live interview with Nigerian journalists
description:
Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar has criticised President Bola Tinubu over his recorded interview with American lobbyist and media personality, Diana London, challenging him to grant a live interview to Nigerian journalists.
Atiku, the African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate, al
content:
Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar has criticised President Bola Tinubu over his recorded interview with American lobbyist and media personality, Diana London, challenging him to grant a live interview to Nigerian journalists.

Atiku, the African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate, also questioned whether the interview was connected to a $4.5 million lobbying arrangement reportedly undertaken on behalf of the Nigerian government in the United States.

In a statement issued on Wednesday by his Director of Strategic Communications, Phrank Shaibu, Atiku described the engagement as a publicity exercise and called on the Presidency to release the full, unedited recording.

London had shared photographs of her meeting with Tinubu at the Presidential Villa in Abuja on Tuesday. Cameras and other recording equipment were visible in the background.

In a post on X, which was later deleted, she praised the security partnership between Nigeria and the United States, saying the relationship between Tinubu and US President Donald Trump was creating opportunities for economic and trade cooperation.

“The U.S-Nigeria security partnership is delivering results. Peace Through Strength,” London wrote.

She added: “None of this happens without the ongoing partnership between President Trump and President Tinubu, their steadfast commitment to eliminating terrorists, and Nigeria’s willingness to work closely with the U.S. government.

“Because of the success of their partnership and relationship, the economic and trade opportunities are endless. The best is yet to come. Nigeria is the United States greatest ally in Africa.”

The post attracted mixed reactions, with some Nigerians criticising the President for granting an interview to a foreign media personality while failing to engage local journalists.

Atiku said filings in the United States identified London as a consultant to DCI Group AZ on work carried out for the Republic of Nigeria through Aster Legal.

He claimed the filings showed that DCI Group received a $4.5 million retainer but did not establish whether the interview was among the services covered by the payment.

“After praising Tinubu’s government and Nigeria’s partnership with the United States on her social media accounts, Diana London deleted the posts. She has not explained why. Nigerians are entitled to ask what changed between the glowing praise and its disappearance,” Atiku said.

He argued that the deletion raised questions about the credibility and transparency of the interview.

“Someone who could delete her own public praise of this government without an explanation has given Nigerians reason to wonder what will survive the editing of her interview,” he said.

Atiku further questioned whether difficult questions and the President’s responses would remain in the final recording or whether Nigerians would be presented with what he described as a carefully edited account.

He said the Presidency could address the concerns by releasing the complete recording.

The former vice-president also questioned why the Presidency was promoting the interview through photographs and social media announcements before its release.

He argued that a credible presidential interview should allow journalists to ask spontaneous questions and follow up on the President’s responses.

Atiku also queried the presence of a large screen positioned in Tinubu’s line of sight during the recording, asking the Presidency to clarify whether the questions were spontaneous or prepared in advance.

He named Rufai Oseni, Ojy Okpe, Seun Okinbaloye and Reuben Abati as Nigerian journalists capable of asking the President questions on issues affecting citizens.

“Let him sit with them live. Let him explain why food costs so much, why wages no longer cover transport, and when families can expect relief. A flattering interview cannot wipe away poverty and hunger,” he said.

Atiku also demanded the publication of the lobbying agreement, disclosure of payments and invoices, identification of those who authorised the expenditure, and clarification on whether London’s interview formed part of the contracted services.

“Who authorised the $4.5 million payment, and from which public account did it come? At a time when Nigerians are told to endure the pain of fuel subsidy removal, they deserve to know whether the money saved is being spent on foreign publicity,” he said.

He urged the Presidency to publish the contract, provide details of the expenditure, release the unedited interview and grant Nigerian journalists a live session with the President.

The post 2027: Atiku challenges Tinubu to live interview with Nigerian journalists appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: EFCC arraigns Lagos socialite Halimat Tejuosho over alleged N1.1bn scam to secure victim NNPC GMD position
description:
The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) has arraigned socialite Halimat Adenike Tejuosho before the Federal Capital Territory High Court in Gwagwalada over an alleged N1. 1 billion job scam.
Tejuosho was arraigned on Wednesday before Justice A. S. Adepoju on a five-count charge bordering
content:
The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) has arraigned socialite Halimat Adenike Tejuosho before the Federal Capital Territory High Court in Gwagwalada over an alleged N1. 1 billion job scam.

Tejuosho was arraigned on Wednesday before Justice A. S. Adepoju on a five-count charge bordering on advance fee fraud, obtaining money by false pretence and other alleged criminal activities.

According to a statement published on the EFCC’s X account, the commission accused Tejuosho and another defendant, identified as Gidado Ibrahim, of obtaining N603.4 million from Oluseye Yomi-Sholoye between August and October 2024.

The prosecution alleged in the first count that the defendants collected the money under the pretence that they would facilitate Yomi-Sholoye’s appointment as Group Managing Director of the Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation (NNPC), knowing that the claim was false.

The charge was brought under Section 1(a) of the Advance Fee Fraud and Other Fraud Related Offences Act, 2006.

In another count, the EFCC accused Tejuosho of receiving N259.9 million, allegedly derived from criminal conduct, into her Access Bank account during the same period.

The fourth count alleged that she received an additional N50 million on September 30, 2024, into an Access Bank account belonging to Haleems Integrated Services Limited.

Tejuosho pleaded not guilty to all five counts.

Following her plea, defence counsel, Chuks Ugwuru, applied for bail on liberal terms, arguing that the offences were bailable and that his client’s health condition constituted special circumstances deserving the court’s consideration.

Ugwuru relied on a medical report which he said indicated that Tejuosho was critically ill. He urged Justice Adepoju to exercise discretion in her favour.

However, the EFCC opposed the application. Its lead prosecution counsel, Yahaya Tarfa, told the court that the commission had filed a 12-paragraph counter-affidavit, alongside an exhibit and written address.

Although Tarfa acknowledged that bail was at the court’s discretion, he urged the judge to impose conditions that would ensure the defendant remained available throughout the trial.

In his ruling, Justice Adepoju held that the offences were bailable and granted Tejuosho bail in the sum of N100 million, with one surety in like sum.

The judge directed that the surety must reside within the court’s jurisdiction and own land or property in the Federal Capital Territory.

He further ordered that the surety’s property documents be verified by the FCT Land Registry, with a copy deposited with the court registrar.

Tejuosho was also ordered to surrender her international passport to the registrar pending the hearing and determination of the case.

The judge, however, directed that she remain at the Kuje Correctional Centre until she fulfils the bail conditions.

The case was adjourned until February 1, 2027, for trial.

The EFCC had declared Tejuosho wanted in April 2026 over an alleged case of obtaining money by false pretence.

title: Plateau 2027: PDP’s Scores Gov Mutfwang 15-20% In Performance
description: The governorship candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), Kephas Ropshik, on Wednesday said that Governor Caleb Mutfwang performed poorly in governance in the state.Ropshik, who spoke during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today, said the governor had not scored more tha
content:
The governorship candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), Kephas Ropshik, on Wednesday said that Governor Caleb Mutfwang performed poorly in governance in the state.

Ropshik, who spoke during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today, said the governor had not scored more than 20 per cent in performance.

The PDP candidate said that leadership should be about performance and about the people.

“In fact, I can tell you on a scale of one to 100, you can give him like 15 to 20 per cent in performance,” he said. “He still remains someone that I respect, but of course that, completely, is different from politics.”

He alleged that the governor defected to the All Progressives Congress (APC) when he could not cope with the crisis in the PDP.

He, however, said that the governor did not leave with up to 15 per cent of the members of the PDP, insisting that Plateau is a PDP state.

“You know, a man’s strength and leadership qualities are being tested when there are crises, but the governor couldn’t stand the crisis. He left for APC, and so there was an opening in the PDP to contest for governorship because, of course, the truth is this. Plateau has been a PDP state.

“You can’t take that away from Plateau State, right? And so there was a vacancy, and so somebody needed to fill in the gap. And so even with the crisis, we believed in the PDP,” the candidate said.

“Mutfwang did not live with 15, 20 per cent of people, I mean, in PDP to APC. The people, in fact, not even 10 per cent, because the people that followed him to APC are his appointees, and that’s the truth.

“Ninety per cent of people on the Plateau still believe in the PDP.”

Ropshik said that Plateau is one of the frontrunners in the Rainbow Coalition.

He also said that he was working for the re-election of President Bola Tinubu.

Asked whether he was not confusing his followers by telling them to vote for the APC in the January 16 presidential election, and the PDP in the February 6, 2027 governorship election in the state, Ropshik said, “No, no, no, I am not reading because now if we want to be sincere to ourselves, the PDP presidential candidate, we all know that there’s no chance for him to win the election.

“And so why should we now waste the votes? We must find a platform to identify; what we’re after is good governance.”

title: Gombe PDP show solidarity, pays hospital visit to injured APC chieftains
description:
The Gombe State chapter of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) has demonstrated political tolerance and solidarity by visiting leaders of the All Progressives Congress (APC) who were injured in a road accident while returning from a campaign rally.
The PDP delegation, led by the Director-General of i
content:
The Gombe State chapter of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) has demonstrated political tolerance and solidarity by visiting leaders of the All Progressives Congress (APC) who were injured in a road accident while returning from a campaign rally.

The PDP delegation, led by the Director-General of its Campaign Council, Hon. Dan’azumi Adamu Pindiga, visited the injured APC members at the Federal Teaching Hospital (FTH), Gombe, on Wednesday, November 18, 2026.

The visit was aimed at expressing sympathy and wishing the victims a quick recovery following the accident, which occurred on Tuesday.

Those injured in the incident included the APC State Campaign Council Director-General, Hon. Sa’adu Hassan, and the Gombe State APC Chairman, Hon. Dantata Ndus, alongside other party members.

The visit highlights a show of political goodwill and solidarity between members of the two rival parties despite their differences.

Members of the PDP delegation included the party’s State Secretary, Hon. Adamu Abubakar; Hon. Abubakar Walama; Hon. Sani Hassan Dogarai; Hon. Hassan Santana; Hon. Abubakar Bello (Cikasoron Gombe); and Hon. Jalo Ahmed Ganga.

During the visit, Pindiga conveyed messages of solidarity and goodwill on behalf of the PDP leader in Gombe State, former Governor, Senator Ibrahim Hassan Dankwambo, OON, PhD, Talban Gombe; the party’s governorship candidate, Professor Isa Ali Pantami; and the entire PDP family in the state.

The delegation also offered prayers to Almighty Allah to grant the injured party chieftains and other victims of the accident complete healing, renewed strength and a speedy recovery.

Speaking during the visit, the PDP representatives stressed that political differences should not undermine the bonds of brotherhood, humanity and mutual respect among the people of Gombe State.

They maintained that, “beyond party affiliations and electoral interests, political actors remain members of one community with shared responsibilities and a common obligation to promote peaceful coexistence”.

According to the delegation, “an unfortunate incident involving members of another political party should attract the concern and sympathy of all, irrespective of political leanings”.

The visit, coming amid heightened political activities ahead of the 2027 general elections, underscores the need for political maturity, tolerance and civility among competing parties and their supporters.

It also sends a strong message that political competition should be anchored on issues, policies and the contest for public support, rather than hostility, animosity or division.

The PDP delegation reiterated its goodwill towards the injured APC leaders and prayed for their full recovery, stressing that humanity must always take precedence over partisan considerations.

According to them, “Politics Should Never Come Before Humanity; We Are All Brothers and sisters”.

title: ‘It’s too late to make amends’: Baba-Ahmed speaks on Tinubu’s 2027 chances
description:
Former presidential adviser Hakeem Baba-Ahmed has expressed doubts about President Bola Tinubu’s chances of recovering lost political support ahead of the 2027 general election, saying the administration may have waited too long to address Nigerians’ concerns.
Baba-Ahmed argued that the level of har
content:
Former presidential adviser Hakeem Baba-Ahmed has expressed doubts about President Bola Tinubu’s chances of recovering lost political support ahead of the 2027 general election, saying the administration may have waited too long to address Nigerians’ concerns.

Baba-Ahmed argued that the level of hardship, public dissatisfaction and anger across the country could make it difficult for Tinubu to secure another term if the 2027 election is free, fair and credible.

He made the remarks during an interview on Truth TV News, where he questioned the promises by some governors to deliver millions of votes for the president.

Reacting to reports of governors promising Tinubu between 1.5 million and 2.5 million votes, Baba-Ahmed said such assurances should not be accepted without scrutiny.

“On what basis would you deliver, would you promise 2 million votes? On what basis?” he asked.

Describing the promises as deceptive, he said governors should not be trusted simply because they occupy political offices, adding that some of them were also facing public resentment.

“I think President Tinubu, even at his current state, must know that you don’t trust governors. He was a governor, too, for some time,” Baba-Ahmed said.

He warned that relying on such promises could create complacency within the administration and prevent the president from recognising the level of dissatisfaction among Nigerians.

“If indeed they tell him that kind of thing and he believes them, then I think he deserves to lose even more,” he said.

Baba-Ahmed also criticised governors for what he described as their late response to the worsening security situation, particularly in northern Nigeria.

He questioned why governors and ministers from the region had not approached Tinubu earlier to demand urgent action against insecurity.

“Why couldn’t northern governors go to the president two years ago? All these ministers, their governors, they are defecting. And say, look, first discuss it,” he said.

He argued that political leaders should have collectively presented the security situation to the president as an emergency requiring immediate intervention.

“The North is being virtually invaded by crime. Killers, bandits, kidnappers, religious extremists. A whole army of all sorts of people. They’re taking on the lives of our people,” Baba-Ahmed said.

He added that criminal groups were taking over territories and keeping some villages and communities under their control for extended periods.

According to him, the government needed to act decisively before the situation further undermined its chances in the next election.

“We need to do something dramatic. We need to do something. Otherwise, if we leave it late, we’ll have no ground to cover to win the election,” he said.

The former presidential adviser also recalled an earlier meeting between religious leaders, including Catholic cardinals, and Tinubu, during which they reportedly raised concerns about the difficult living conditions in the country.

He said the president had previously dismissed suggestions that Nigerians were experiencing severe hardship, but members of the administration had since acknowledged the situation.

Baba-Ahmed referred to comments by the Chief of Staff to the President during the launch of the administration’s manifesto, saying the official had acknowledged that anyone denying the country’s difficulties was not being truthful.

He maintained that the government had a limited opportunity to address public grievances and restore confidence.

“There is a time to make amends. And there’s a time when it’s too late,” he said.

Asked whether it was already too late for Tinubu, Baba-Ahmed pointed to the level of public dissatisfaction, economic hardship and insecurity as major challenges facing the president ahead of 2027.

He said: “If this election in 2027, if it is free and fair and credible, there is no way with the level of disenchantment and suffering and anger that Nigerians bear towards this administration will not come back.”

title: Nigeria, Cameroon, Chad, Niger reach deal on military pursuit of terrorists
description:
By Kingsley Omonobi



Nigeria and three neighbouring countries — Cameroon, Chad and Niger — have reportedly agreed to allow military forces to pursue terrorists, armed bandits and other criminal groups up to five kilometres across their shared borders.



The arrangement is aimed at strengthening r
content:
By Kingsley Omonobi

Nigeria and three neighbouring countries — Cameroon, Chad and Niger — have reportedly agreed to allow military forces to pursue terrorists, armed bandits and other criminal groups up to five kilometres across their shared borders.

The arrangement is aimed at strengthening regional counterterrorism operations and preventing fleeing militants from escaping military pressure by crossing into neighbouring territories.

The Minister of Defence, General Christopher Gwabin Musa (retd.), disclosed the agreement in Abuja, explaining that it would enable security forces to sustain hot pursuit of fleeing terrorists across border areas.

The agreement is expected to strengthen military cooperation among the four countries, particularly in tackling transnational security threats posed by Boko Haram, the Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP) and other armed criminal groups operating around the Lake Chad Basin and adjoining border communities.

Musa also disclosed that Nigeria was receiving real-time intelligence, satellite imagery and training support from the United States to enhance its counterterrorism capabilities and improve the effectiveness of military operations.

The Defence Minister said Nigerian troops had recently neutralised several terrorist and bandit commanders during overnight operations across the North-East and North-West regions.

He said the cross-border pursuit arrangement is particularly significant for communities along Nigeria’s borders with Cameroon, Chad and Niger, where terrorist groups have exploited porous boundaries to evade security operations and sustain their activities.

In Cameroon’s Far North Region, Boko Haram and ISWAP activities have continued to pose security challenges, making closer military coordination between neighbouring countries critical to addressing the threat.

Details of the agreement, including its operational procedures, rules of engagement and safeguards for civilians in affected border communities, have not been provided in the information released.

The arrangement signals a renewed push for regional military cooperation, intelligence sharing and coordinated operations against terrorist networks whose activities extend beyond national boundaries.

title: FAAC distributes N2.44trn October revenue among FG, states, LGAs
description:
The Federal Government, state governments and local government councils have shared a total of N2.441 trillion as revenue generated into the Federation Account for October 2026.
The allocation was announced in a statement issued on Wednesday by Bawa Mokwa, Director of Press and Public Relations at t
content:
The Federal Government, state governments and local government councils have shared a total of N2.441 trillion as revenue generated into the Federation Account for October 2026.

The allocation was announced in a statement issued on Wednesday by Bawa Mokwa, Director of Press and Public Relations at the Office of the Accountant-General of the Federation (OAGF).

According to the statement, the revenue was distributed at the November 2026 meeting of the Federation Account Allocation Committee (FAAC), held in Abuja.

The N2.441 trillion distributable revenue comprised N1.688 trillion from statutory revenue and N752.488 billion generated from Value Added Tax (VAT).

The allocation represents the revenue available for distribution among the three tiers of government for the October 2026 period.

A communiqué issued by FAAC indicated that total gross revenue of N3.811 trillion was available in October 2026. The total deduction for the cost of collection stood at N128.797 billion, while transfers, refunds and savings amounted to N1.241 trillion.

According to the communiqué, gross statutory revenue of N2.999 trillion was recorded in October 2026. This was lower than the N3.096 trillion received in the preceding month by N97.323 billion.

Similarly, gross revenue of N812.446 billion was generated from VAT in October 2026, representing a decrease of N4.426 billion compared with the N816.872 billion recorded in September 2026.

The communiqué stated that, out of the N2.441 trillion total distributable revenue, the Federal Government received N856.065 billion, while state governments received N809.909 billion.

The local government councils received N568.701 billion, while N206.384 billion, representing 13 per cent of mineral revenue, was allocated to benefiting states as derivation revenue.

Regarding the N1.688 trillion distributable statutory revenue, the communiqué stated that the Federal Government received N780.816 billion, while state governments received N396.040 billion.

The local government councils received N305.331 billion, while N206.384 billion, representing 13 per cent of mineral revenue, was shared among the benefiting states as derivation revenue.

From the N752.488 billion distributable VAT revenue, the Federal Government received N75.249 billion, state governments received N413.868 billion, while the local government councils received N263.371 billion.

The communiqué further disclosed that Excise Duty and CET Levies recorded marginal increases in October 2026.

However, Petroleum Profit Tax, PPT, Hydrocarbon Tax, HT, Petroleum Royalties, Import Duty, Companies Income Tax, CIT, Capital Gains Tax, CGT, Stamp Duties, SDT, Value Added Tax, VAT, Mineral Royalties, Gas Flared Penalty, Rental Gas Flared Fee and Miscellaneous Oil Revenue recorded decreases.

The post FAAC distributes N2.44trn October revenue among FG, states, LGAs appeared first on Very Nigerian.

title: Gun can kill terrorists, only education can kill terrorism – Buratai
description:
The former Chief of Army Staff, retired Lt.-Gen. Tukur Buratai has called for inclusive education and wider access to learning opportunities, saying they are critical to addressing the conditions that sustain terrorism and violent extremism in Nigeria.



Buratai made the call at the 2026 Young Adul
content:
The former Chief of Army Staff, retired Lt.-Gen. Tukur Buratai has called for inclusive education and wider access to learning opportunities, saying they are critical to addressing the conditions that sustain terrorism and violent extremism in Nigeria.

Buratai made the call at the 2026 Young Adult Literature Prize Award and unveiling of the 2025 anthology of the T.Y. Buratai Literary Initiative (TYBLI), on Wednesday in Nasarawa State.

The former Nigerian Ambassador to Benin Republic said military force alone could not defeat terrorism without deliberate investment in education, intellectual development and the minds of young Nigerians.

“Gun can kill a terrorist, but only education can kill terrorism,” he declared.

Buratai said national development must go beyond infrastructure, military strength and economic resources to include the intellectual capacity, creative imagination and moral consciousness of citizens.

He stressed that young Nigerians, irrespective of their backgrounds, needed equal opportunities, platforms and encouragement to develop their talents and contribute meaningfully to society.

The former COAS said the initiative was established on the conviction that great nations were built not only by strong armies and economies but also by ideas, literature and educated citizens.

He urged universities to promote young adult literature through research, teaching and programmes that encouraged creativity, critical thinking and intellectual development.

“A school that produces excellent academic results but neglects imagination and critical thinking has not fully prepared its students for the future,” he said.

Buratai said the initiative had, since 2023, provided a platform for young Nigerians from diverse backgrounds to demonstrate their creativity and move from passive consumption to active production of literature.

He described the unveiling of the 2025 anthology as another milestone, providing a permanent record of the imagination, creativity and achievements of young authors.

He also announced plans to introduce full scholarships for deserving winners within the next three to five years, to enable them to complete their education.

In a goodwill message, the Vice-Chancellor of Nasarawa State University, Keffi, Prof. Sa’adatu Liman, described young adult literature as an important bridge between childhood and adulthood.

Liman said literature helped young people confront questions of identity, courage, faith, justice and leadership through stories that reflected their experiences.

She described the initiative as an investment in human development and nation-building, pledging the university’s readiness to strengthen its partnership with TYBLI.

Also, the Vice-Chancellor of the University of Ibadan, Prof. Peter Olamakinde Olapegba, commended the initiative for recognising the importance of academic leadership, scholarship and research mentorship.

Olapegba, who received an award for excellence in academic leadership and research mentorship, said the recognition affirmed the importance of building capacity and nurturing future generations.

He dedicated the award to his colleagues, mentors, students and mentees, particularly five PhD students who graduated from the university on the eve of the event.

“The true reward of mentorship is not simply what we accomplish as individuals, but the lives we influence, the capacity we build and the legacy we leave behind,” he said.

Olapegba said the award had renewed his commitment to scholarship, service and the development of future generations.

The event featured the presentation of awards to outstanding young writers and the unveiling of the 2025 anthology.

(NAN)

The post Gun can kill terrorists, only education can kill terrorism – Buratai appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: 2027: Yayi realised his looming defeat the day Adebutu returned to the ballot – PDP Nat’l Sec
description:
Claims 60% of Ogun APC members have joined PDP through Rainbow Coalition


The National Secretary of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), Samuel Anyanwu, has said the return of the party’s Ogun State governorship candidate, Oladipupo Adebutu, to the ballot signalled impending defeat for the All Progr
content:
• Claims 60% of Ogun APC members have joined PDP through Rainbow Coalition

The National Secretary of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), Samuel Anyanwu, has said the return of the party’s Ogun State governorship candidate, Oladipupo Adebutu, to the ballot signalled impending defeat for the All Progressives Congress (APC) candidate, Solomon Adeola, popularly known as Yayi.

Speaking on Wednesday at the PDP’s “Ogun Rescue Mission” mega rally in Abeokuta, Anyanwu also claimed that 60 per cent of APC members in the state had joined the opposition party through the Rainbow Coalition.

Anyanwu, who represented the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, presented the PDP flag to Adebutu and his running mate, Lateefat Sowunmi-Kolapo, expressing confidence that the party would win the governorship and legislative elections.

“This is the true Ogun for Ogun. The day Adebutu came back to the ballot was the day Solomon Yayi realised his looming defeat.

“I know him very well because I was in the Senate with him. This is Ogun and Ogun State must take their position,” Anyanwu said.

He urged supporters to translate their enthusiasm into votes for the party’s candidates, declaring that the PDP was positioned to secure victory across the state.

“On January 16, we are going to return our three senators and all other candidates. PDP has the best and most intelligent candidates and they are going to win. With my visit to Ogun State, I have observed that everybody wants Adebutu to win. He will take care of Ogun people,” he said.

Anyanwu described Wike as the party’s national leader and leader of the Rainbow Coalition, claiming that the coalition had substantially weakened the APC’s membership in Ogun.

“Sixty per cent of the APC have joined the PDP in Ogun State through the Rainbow Coalition,” he declared before presenting the flag to Adebutu and urging him to secure victory for the party.

In his address, Adebutu pledged to reserve one-third of positions in his administration for women, support youth enterprise and pursue wealth creation through his seven-point “ITURA DE” agenda.

He said his running mate would play a substantive role in government, stressing that women would receive responsibilities that reflected their competence and leadership abilities.

“My deputy is not a spare tyre and will never be. One-third of the government sector will be occupied by females. We will continue to promote the female gender.

“I can boldly tell you that it is my plan to run a government that gives women a prominent place in governance. Women will not be sidelined; they will be fully represented and entrusted with strategic positions in my government.

“I believe women have the capacity, competence and leadership qualities to contribute meaningfully to governance and the development of Ogun State.

“Their voices will be heard, their contributions valued, and their roles recognised,” he said.

Adebutu, who distributed pamphlets outlining his manifesto, urged residents to regard the document as a covenant between him and the people.

“The basis of ITURA DE is about humanity; we believe in ourselves and in humanity.

“We truly believe that for a nation to grow, we must support our young people. We believe in releasing the power of industry and enterprise and we will create wealth. With wealth creation, we shall have less tendencies for desperate behaviours,” he said.

Promoting his “Ogun for Ogun” campaign message, Adebutu said the PDP’s candidates had longstanding family and community ties that would enable them to understand the needs of residents.

He cited his running mate, the party’s Ogun Central senatorial candidate, Iyabo Obasanjo, and other candidates as members of a team with established grassroots relationships.

“We have candidates across all three senatorial districts who understand their communities, have established relationships with the people, and know what grassroots politics entails.

“We are not strangers to our people. We are part of the communities we seek to serve. That is the strength of our team,” he said.

Adebutu also acknowledged former governors Gbenga Daniel and Ibikunle Amosun, who were absent from the rally, recognising their contributions to the state’s political history.

“Their contributions to the political history of Ogun State and their respective roles in the state’s political journey remain part of our collective history. We recognise them and extend our warm regards,” he said.

He pledged to protect public funds and urged residents to collect their Permanent Voter Cards ahead of the elections.

“I won’t steal your money and we shall make Ogun State great again. It is for us to protect the heritage of our Ogun State. It is beyond political parties. Go and take your PVCs,” he said.

Earlier, Ogun PDP Chairman, Abayomi Tella, expressed confidence in Adebutu’s chances, saying the state’s electorate would scrutinise candidates and resist attempts to influence their choices with money.

“If you are coming to Ogun State to contest, you cannot cut corners. You can’t bamboozle them with money,” Tella said.

The rally featured a procession of party leaders, candidates and supporters from the NNPC underpass to the Ake Palace pavilion, with participants singing, dancing and chanting “ITURA DE,” meaning “relief has come.”
