title: Tinubu hails Alake’s 21-year reign, credits traditional institution with driving development
description:
From Juliana Taiwo-Obalonye, Abuja
President Bola Tinubu has commended the Alake of Egbaland, Oba Adedotun Aremu Gbadebo III, for complementing government efforts in promoting development, preserving cultural heritage and fostering peace in Ogun State.
Tinubu, in a congratulatory message to the mona
content:
From Juliana Taiwo-Obalonye, Abuja

President Bola Tinubu has commended the Alake of Egbaland, Oba Adedotun Aremu Gbadebo III, for complementing government efforts in promoting development, preserving cultural heritage and fostering peace in Ogun State.

Tinubu, in a congratulatory message to the monarch ahead of his 21st coronation anniversary on November 19, described his reign as a testament to selfless service, dedication to the welfare of his people and responsible leadership.

The President said the development recorded in Egbaland and across Ogun State over the past 21 years demonstrated the invaluable role of traditional institutions in complementing government efforts towards national development.

In the message issued by the State House on Wednesday, Tinubu also acknowledged the monarch’s distinguished military career, noting that discipline, courage, patriotism, loyalty and a deep sense of duty had shaped his approach to leadership.

He said: “For 21 remarkable years, your reign has witnessed tremendous development, not only within the Egba kingdom but also across the state. These strides in development stand as enduring reminders of the invaluable role of the traditional institution in complementing governments of the day for overall development.”

Tinubu further commended the monarch’s commitment to preserving and promoting Nigeria’s cultural heritage, describing his counsel on responsible leadership, humility, accountability, service to the people and respect for institutions as valuable guidance for elected leaders.

The President congratulated the people of Egbaland for having a monarch whose reign, he said, had been marked by wisdom, dedication to service, humility, peace and development.

“Your words of advice, with consistent emphasis on responsible leadership, humility, accountability, service to the people, and respect for institutions, continue to guide us as elected leaders of the people,” he said.

Tinubu, who conveyed the felicitations on behalf of his family and the Federal Republic of Nigeria, prayed for the monarch’s continued good health, renewed strength, divine wisdom and many more fruitful and peaceful years on the throne.

Oba Gbadebo III, also known as Okukenu IV, ascended the throne of his forefathers in 2005.

title: NIPR names auditorium after Uzodimma
description:
As governor attributes Imo success to inclusive, participatory governance

In an unprecedented endorsement of the sterling performance of a governor in the country, the Nigeria Institute of Public Relations (NIPR) on Wednesday named its auditorium after the governor of Imo State, Senator Hope Uzodim
content:
• As governor attributes Imo success to inclusive, participatory governance

In an unprecedented endorsement of the sterling performance of a governor in the country, the Nigeria Institute of Public Relations (NIPR) on Wednesday named its auditorium after the governor of Imo State, Senator Hope Uzodimma. 

This is the first time in its 63-year history that the institute has singled out an individual or institution for such an honour.

The historic announcement was made by the President of NIPR, Dr Ike Neliaku, shortly after Uzodimma addressed 3,000 delegates from 123 countries attending the 2026 World Public Relations Forum ( WPRF) in Abuja.

NIPR, which had earlier recommended Uzodimma to deliver a keynote address at the conference on the strength of his strategic and transformative leadership in Imo State, said the honour was well deserved.

Amidst a standing ovation by the delegates present, NIPR disclosed that it was proud of the verifiable achievements of Uzodimma since he took office as governor seven years ago, hence he was invited to share his experience at the conference.

An elated Uzodimma, while delivering his speech, attributed his success to his resolve to involve the people in governance by listening to them and ensuring that his actions were honest and transparent.

According to him, earlier in the day, he had evolved a strategic system of communication that enabled the people to be properly apprised of government activities with a robust feedback mechanism.

The governor who spoke on the topic, RESPONSIBLE GOVERNANCE AND COMMUNICATION: BUILDING TRUST THROUGH COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT, STAKEHOLDERS RELATIONS AND INCLUSIVE IMPACT, disclosed that he set up a stakeholders forum,Rsdip Town hall and Imo Elders Council as platforms for ventilation and exchange of ideas between him and the people.

“In Imo, we decided early that our people should be able to engage and question their government face to face. In less than six months in office, I set up the Stakeholders Forum, where I gave an account of what we have done and yielded the floor to the stakeholders.

“They took advantage of the opportunity to ask some difficult questions, and even some criticised some of our policies openly,” he said.

Uzodimma disclosed that his administration took advantage of the success of the forum to institute a town hall meeting on radio as well as set up the Elders Council as veritable platforms to interact with the people.

He noted that after he gained the trust of the people through a transparent, accountable, and inclusive governance, it became easier to execute policies and programmes acceptable to them.

He was happy that the communication and feedback platforms opened the way to reach the people under the shared prosperity agenda of his administration.

He listed the building of 150 solid roads, the training of more than 65 ,000 youths in digital skills and technology which thereafter created 80,000 jobs and the digitalisation of land reforms as some of the impacts made by his administration.

He also mentioned the Orashi Electricity Power Plant, the OKOBI INITIATIVE which has resulted to the establishment of 600 flourishing businesses, the health insurance scheme covering more than 2.5 million citizens and other infrastructural achievements in health, education, urban renewal, agriculture and improved security.

Uzodimma submitted that the communication system adopted by his government in recording the monumental success credited to it and which has been acknowledged by several groups and institutions aligned with the theme of the conference which is RESPONSIBLE COMMUNICATION: THE VOICE OF THE WORLD.

“For us in Imo, the voice that matters most is the voice of our people. We engage with them. We communicate. We listen to the feedback they share with us, and they see through our deliverables that we have been listening,” he declared.

He charged the delegates to ensure that they encouraged both those they work for and the people to listen to one another for effective communication, feedback, and results.

Wike also urged market traders in Abuja to support Tinubu’s re-election bi
content:
The Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, has defended President Bola Tinubu’s economic reforms, insisting that the policies will bring lasting prosperity to Nigeria if given sufficient time to mature.

Wike also urged market traders in Abuja to support Tinubu’s re-election bid in the 2027 general election, warning against politicians promising to reverse the removal of fuel subsidy.

The minister made the remarks on Wednesday during an interactive town hall meeting with representatives of various market associations across the FCT.

Acknowledging the economic difficulties Nigerians have experienced following the removal of fuel subsidy, Wike argued that previous administrations lacked the courage to address the challenges associated with the subsidy regime.

According to him, the country was heading towards economic collapse before Tinubu introduced the reforms, stressing that difficult decisions were necessary to establish a foundation for sustainable growth.

“This country is nearly gone. For you to say that you must try to change what is happening means that you must lay a foundation first, and when you lay a foundation, you give it time to grow,” he said.

Wike maintained that the removal of fuel subsidy had brought certain benefits, including increased revenue allocations to state and local governments, the clearance of pension arrears and an end to recurring strikes by the Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU).

He cautioned Nigerians against opposition politicians advocating a reversal of the subsidy removal, insisting that allowing the current policies to mature would produce better economic outcomes.

“If we allow these policies that the government has put in place to mature, what is going to happen in the next four years will be good. Forget about people coming to tell you stories,” he added.

The FCT minister also highlighted infrastructure and institutional reforms undertaken by the Tinubu administration in Abuja, pointing to road construction and rehabilitation projects across satellite towns and districts.

He said improved road networks would reduce transportation costs, facilitate commercial activities and create a more favourable environment for businesses.

Wike further disclosed that he would continue engaging market associations and promised to approve additional market development projects in the territory.

He also cited the establishment of the FCT Civil Service Commission, the creation of Mandate Secretariats for Women and Youth, and the appointment of an FCT indigene to the Federal Executive Council as some of the institutional changes under Tinubu.

The minister urged Nigerians to assess political leadership based on performance and tangible results rather than ethnic or regional considerations.

Meanwhile, representatives of various market associations at the meeting expressed support for the Tinubu administration and pledged to mobilise traders ahead of the 2027 general election.

The Chairman of the Wuse Market Traders Association, Okorie Ikechukwu-Raphael, commended the FCT administration for road improvements and market redevelopment projects.

He also appealed to Wike to approve the development of additional shops and shopping malls in emerging districts, including Katampe and Kaura, to expand business opportunities for traders.

The minister subsequently urged market associations to nominate representatives from their state chapters to participate in the campaign mobilisation structure ahead of the 2027 elections.

The post ‘His tough reforms will bring lasting prosperity’ — Wike begs Nigerians to give Tinubu another chance appeared first on Very Nigerian.

title: 2027: Federal polytechnic rectors pledge staff, students’ support for Tinubu’s re-election
description:
From Juliana Taiwo-Obalonye, Abuja
Federal polytechnic rectors across Nigeria have pledged to mobilise staff and students of their institutions to support President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid in 2027, citing reforms and interventions by his administration in the polytechnic sector.
The rectors, u
content:
From Juliana Taiwo-Obalonye, Abuja

Federal polytechnic rectors across Nigeria have pledged to mobilise staff and students of their institutions to support President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid in 2027, citing reforms and interventions by his administration in the polytechnic sector.

The rectors, under the umbrella of the Committee of Federal Polytechnic Rectors (COFER), made the pledge on Wednesday when they visited the Secretary to the Government of the Federation (SGF), George Akume, in Abuja.

The committee, led by its Chairman and Rector of Auchi Polytechnic, Dr Salisu Shehu Umar, said its decision to support Tinubu’s re-election was in recognition of what it described as unprecedented government interventions aimed at repositioning polytechnics and addressing longstanding challenges in the sector.

Umar said the rectors had resolved to deploy their collective influence and institutional networks to mobilise support for the President ahead of the 2027 general elections.

He urged the SGF to convey their appreciation and pledge of solidarity to Tinubu, assuring him that the committee would mobilise its members, staff and students towards the success of the administration.

Responding, Akume, who was represented by the Permanent Secretary, General Services Office, Dr Ibrahim Abubakar Kana, commended the rectors for their support, describing technical and vocational education as indispensable to national development.

He said no country could achieve meaningful development without prioritising skills-based education, adding that the Federal Government remained committed to repositioning polytechnics to address Nigeria’s skills gap and strengthen its productive capacity.

Akume said the interventions through the Federal Ministry of Education and the National Board for Technical Education (NBTE) represented significant steps towards restoring the relevance of technical and vocational education.

He noted that Nigeria’s previous emphasis on certificate acquisition at the expense of practical and technical skills had contributed to some of the challenges confronting the education sector.

The SGF said the Tinubu administration was determined to build an inclusive society in which every institution and individual had equal opportunities to contribute to national development.

On the longstanding discrimination between Higher National Diploma (HND) and university degree holders, Akume assured the rectors that the Federal Government was committed to equity and fairness.

He also disclosed that the bill seeking to address the disparity, which is before the President, would receive due attention to facilitate its eventual assent.

Earlier, Umar said polytechnics had for years been treated as inferior to universities, but expressed optimism that the current administration’s policies and interventions would address the imbalance.

He identified the removal of the HND/BSc dichotomy as a major priority for the sector, noting that successive administrations since 1999 had made efforts to resolve the issue without a permanent solution.

The rector expressed hope that the ongoing legislative process would finally end the discrimination and enable polytechnics to fulfil their mandate of producing skilled manpower for national development.

He said the committee remained committed to advancing the interests of polytechnic education while supporting government policies aimed at strengthening the sector.

title: FG, States, LGs Share ₦2.441trn October 2026 Revenue
description: A total sum of ₦2.441 trillion, being October 2026 Federation Account Revenue, has been shared among the Federal Government, states and the local government councils.The revenue was shared at the November 2026 Federation Account Allocation Committee (FAAC) meeting held in Abuja.The ₦2.441 trillion t
content:
A total sum of ₦2.441 trillion, being October 2026 Federation Account Revenue, has been shared among the Federal Government, states and the local government councils.

The revenue was shared at the November 2026 Federation Account Allocation Committee (FAAC) meeting held in Abuja.

The ₦2.441 trillion total distributable revenue comprised distributable statutory revenue of ₦1.688 trillion and distributable Value Added Tax (VAT) revenue of ₦752.488 billion.

A communiqué issued by the Federation Account Allocation Committee (FAAC) indicated that total gross revenue of ₦3.811 trillion was available in the month of October 2026.

Total deduction for cost of collection, according to the statement, was ₦128.797 billion, while total transfers, refunds and savings were ₦1.241 trillion.

According to the communiqué, gross statutory revenue of ₦2.999 trillion was received for the month of October 2026.

This was lower than the sum of ₦3.096 trillion received in the preceding month by ₦97.323 billion.

Gross revenue of ₦812.446 billion was available from the Value Added Tax (VAT) in October 2026.

This was lower than the ₦816.872 billion available in the month of September 2026 by ₦4.426 billion.

The communiqué stated that from the ₦2.441 trillion total distributable revenue, the Federal Government received a total sum of ₦856.065 billion and the state governments received a total sum of ₦809.909 billion.

The local government council, it revealed, received ₦568.701 billion, while the sum of ₦206.384 billion (13 per cent of mineral revenue) was shared to the benefiting State as derivation revenue.

On the ₦1.688 trillion distributable statutory revenue, the communiqué stated that the Federal Government received ₦780.816 billion and the state governments received ₦396.040 billion.

The local government councils received ₦305.331 billion, and the sum of ₦206.384 billion (13 per cent of mineral revenue) was shared to the benefiting States as derivation revenue.

From the ₦752.488 billion distributable Value Added Tax (VAT) revenue, the Federal Government received ₦75.249 billion, the state governments received ₦413.868 billion, and the local government councils received ₦263.371 billion.

In October 2026, excise duty and CET levies increased marginally, according to the communiqué, while Petroleum Profit Tax (PPT), Hydrocarbon Tax (HT), Petroleum Royalties, Import Duty, Companies Income Tax (CIT), CGT & SDT, Value Added Tax (VTA), Mineral Royalties, Gas Flared Penalty, Rental Gas Flared Fee and Misc. Oil Revenue all decreased.

The post FG, States, LGs Share ₦2.441trn October 2026 Revenue appeared first on Channels Television.

title: EFCC arraigns Lagos socialite Tejuosho for alleged N603.4m job scam
description:
The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) on Wednesday arraigned a socialite, Halimat Adenike Tejuosho, before the Federal Capital Territory High Court, Gwagwalada Division, for an alleged N603,400,000.00 job scam.



She was arraigned before Justice A. S. Adepoju on a five-count charge bo
content:
The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) on Wednesday arraigned a socialite, Halimat Adenike Tejuosho, before the Federal Capital Territory High Court, Gwagwalada Division, for an alleged N603,400,000.00 job scam.

She was arraigned before Justice A. S. Adepoju on a five-count charge bordering on advance fee fraud, obtaining by false pretence and criminal conduct, according to a statement posted on EFCC’s X page.

Count one reads: “That you Halimat Adenike Tejuosho and Gidado Ibrahim between August 2024 to October 2024 within the jurisdiction of this Honourable Court obtained the sum of N603,400,000.00 (Six hundred and three million four hundred thousand naira) from Oluseye Yomi-Sholoye under the false pretence that you will facilitate her appointment as the Group Managing Director, GMD of Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation (NNPC), which pretence you knew to be false and thereby committed an offence contrary to Section 1(a) of the Advance Fee Fraud and Other Fraud Related Offences Act, 2006 and punishable under Section 1(3) of the same Act.

Count two reads: “That you Halimat Adenike Tejuosho between August 2024 to October 2024 within the jurisdiction of this Honourable Court did corruptly receive a total of N259,900,000 (Two Hundred and Fifty-Nine Million, Nine Hundred Thousand Naira) proceeds of crime into your Access Bank account with number 0021083069, which sum you knew to be derived from criminal conduct and thereby committed an offence contrary to Section 17(a) of the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (Establishment) Act 2004 and punishable under Section 17(b) of the same Act.

Count four states: “That you Halimat Adenike Tejuosho on 30th September 2024 within the jurisdiction of this Honourable Court did corruptly receive a total of N50,000,000 (Fifty Million Naira) proceeds of crime into your Access Bank account with number 0021083069 and name HALEEMS INTEGRATED SERVICES LIMITED, which sum you knew to be derived from criminal conduct and thereby committed an offence contrary to Section 17(a) of the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (Establishment) Act 2004 and punishable under Section 17(b) of the same Act.”

Tejuosho pleaded not guilty to all the charges.

Following the plea, defence counsel, Chuks Ugwuru, urged the court to grant the defendant bail on liberal terms, noting that all five counts are bailable offences.

He said the application was anchored mainly on her ill health, citing a medical report which, he argued, showed that she was critically ill.

“The ill health of an accused person is a consideration worthy enough to be reckoned as a ground of special circumstances,” he said, urging Justice Adepoju to exercise his discretion in the defendant’s favour.

Responding, lead prosecution counsel, Yahaya Tarfa, said the EFCC opposed the application and had filed a 12-paragraph counter-affidavit with one exhibit, along with a written address.

Tarfa acknowledged that bail is at the court’s discretion but urged that any terms imposed should ensure the defendant is available to face trial. He then submitted the matter to the court’s discretion.

Delivering ruling on the application, Justice Adepoju held that the offences are bailable.

Relying on the medical reports before the court, the judge admitted Tejuosho to bail in the sum of N100 million, with one reasonable surety in like sum.

The court ordered that the surety must reside within the court’s jurisdiction and own land or property in the Federal Capital Territory. The title documents are to be verified at the FCT Land Registry, with a copy deposited with the Registrar of the court.

Tejuosho is also to deposit her international passport with the registrar pending the hearing and determination of the charge.

The judge ordered that Tejuosho be remanded at the Kuje Correctional Centre until she meets the bail conditions.

The matter was adjourned to February 1, 2027 for trial.

In April 2026, the EFCC declared Tejuosho wanted over an alleged case of obtaining money by false pretence.

The post EFCC arraigns Lagos socialite Tejuosho for alleged N603.4m job scam appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Ogun 2027: PDP presents governorship flag to Adebutu
description:
The National Secretary of the Peoples Democratic Party, Senator Samuel Anyanwu, has formally presented the party’s flag to Hon. Oladipupo Adebutu as its governorship candidate for the Ogun State governorship election, declaring that the opposition party is determined to reclaim the state.
Anyanwu pr
content:
The National Secretary of the Peoples Democratic Party, Senator Samuel Anyanwu, has formally presented the party’s flag to Hon. Oladipupo Adebutu as its governorship candidate for the Ogun State governorship election, declaring that the opposition party is determined to reclaim the state.

Anyanwu presented the party’s flag to Adebutu on Wednesday at the Ake Palace during the PDP governorship rally, describing the former House of Representatives member as the right candidate to lead Ogun State and insisting that the forthcoming election would provide an opportunity for the people to determine their political future.

The event had in attendance the party’s deputy governorship candidate, Alhaja Yemi Sowunmi-Kolapo; the campaign council chairman, John Obafemi; the party chairman, Dr Abayomi Tella; the Ogun Central senatorial candidate, Prof Iyabo Obasanjo; her counterparts for Ogun East and Ogun West, Femi Omotayo Omoowo and Babatunde Gbadamosi, among others.

Speaking before party leaders, supporters and other stakeholders, the PDP National Secretary said Adebutu’s return to the governorship race had strengthened the party’s chances, adding that his political experience and familiarity with the candidate placed him in a position to assess his capacity for leadership.

He described Adebutu as the incoming governor of the state and acknowledged his running mate, Yemi Sowunmi-Kolapo, while commending the Ogun PDP leadership, led by Dr Abayomi Tella, and members of the State Working Committee for their commitment to the party.

The presentation of the flag, which symbolises the party’s formal endorsement and mobilisation behind its candidate, was accompanied by a strong declaration of electoral confidence from the national leadership.

Anyanwu disclosed that “I said that the day that Adebutu return back to the ballot paper was the day Yayi went back home. I know him very well, because I was in the Senate with him. There’s no way you can compare Adebutu to Yayi. This is Ogun State, and the state must take its rightful position; it must be Ogun for Ogun.

“He was actually denied the opportunity in 2023, but this time around, nobody is going to rig it again. He’s going to win and win big because this one is only for Ogun State. A foreigner cannot come here and be a governor. It’s only an Ogun man who will be governor of Ogun State

“Adebutu is not coming to take money from government. He’s not coming to run a corrupt government. The government in Ogun now is very corrupt.

This is the man who will come and deliver. He has come to take care of the youths of Ogun State. Ogun people are very intelligent people. Ogun people, youths, they want to go to school. They need somebody who will help them, and Honourable Lado Adebutu has come. Today, that is why the slogan of the campaign is “Itura day”, which means that the much-needed relief is here in Ogun State.

“All the leaders, former governors, former deputy governors, are supporting Ladi Adebutu. As I was coming here, I got a call from former governors who told me that if I come here, I should tell the people that they believe in Rainbow Coalition, and for that Rainbow Coalition, they want Adebutu to be the governor of this state.

“Adebutu is not going to be just a governor. He must be a governor with 26 House of Assembly members. So as you’re voting on the 6th of February, as you’re voting for the governor, you’re voting for the 26 House of Assembly PDP candidates.

“And therefore, by the power conferred on me, on behalf of our national leader, PDP Nigeria, our own very right, His Excellency… the leader of PDP, and the national leader of Rainbow Coalition, on behalf of our national chairman, Honourable Mohammed, on behalf of the National Working Committee of PDP, we are handing over the flag of PDP today. What we are giving you is power, and so shall it be after the February 2027 governorship elections”.

Speaking on the party’s senatorial and legislative ambitions, Anyanwu predicted victory for PDP candidates across the three senatorial districts, naming Engineer Femi Omotayo Omoowo for Ogun East, Iyabo Obasanjo for Ogun Central and Hon. Babatunde Gbadamosi for Ogun West.

Anyanwu also expressed confidence in the party’s nine House of Representatives candidates, describing them as among the most competent and intelligent contestants in the state.

He challenged party members to intensify grassroots mobilisation across Ogun’s electoral constituencies, pointing to the state’s polling units and wards as critical to the PDP’s electoral calculations.

“We have 5,024 polling units in Ogun State. We have 236 wards in Ogun State. All these units and wards, PDP must win,” he said.

In his response, Adebutu expressed appreciation to the PDP national leadership, the Ogun State chapter and party supporters for their loyalty and commitment, assuring them that the party had continued to strengthen its structures across the state.

He specifically acknowledged the contributions of the national leadership and the state party structure under Hon. Abayomi Tella, while commending party members working across the state’s polling units.

Adebutu said the party had moved beyond merely building political structures at the state level, explaining that its mobilisation efforts had extended to grassroots engagement across thousands of polling units.

On the economic direction of his proposed administration, Adebutu identified wealth creation, entrepreneurship and enterprise as essential ingredients for sustainable development.

He argued that Ogun State, with its strong entrepreneurial culture, needed leadership capable of translating its economic potential into improved living conditions for residents.

“We believe in the power of industry, the power of enterprise in Ogun State. We are very enterprising people. We are great entrepreneurs, and the only way forward is to create wealth.

“With wealth creation, we shall have a better state. With wealth creation, we shall have less tendency for desperate behaviour. Security will improve, and there will be a better life for all,” he stated.

He described the party’s political mission as fundamentally centred on humanity, inclusion and the development of Ogun State.

Adebutu also used the occasion to reaffirm his commitment to gender inclusion, insisting that his running mate, Alhaja Yemi Sowunmi-Kolapo, was not a spare tyre but a substantive partner in the party’s governorship project.

He added that women would continue to occupy prominent positions in the party’s political and governance agenda, noting that the inclusion of women in leadership was essential to building a more representative political system.

He called on residents to defend their interests and take a more active role in determining the political future of the state, insisting that citizens must demand accountability from those seeking public office.

Adebutu promised to run transparent governance and responsible management of public resources, describing accountability as the first dividend of democracy.

“You people must get annoyed righteously, fight for your right, and take your right, and protect Ogun State. Your first dividend of democracy is that if I become your governor, I shall conduct the affairs of this state transparently.

“I shall be able to stand before you and say that I have not committed fraud or mismanaged the resources that are meant for the development of our dear state,” he declared.

The post Ogun 2027: PDP presents governorship flag to Adebutu appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Doctors risking heart disease through overwork, sleep deprivation – Experts
description:
By Chioma Obinna



Health experts on Wednesday expressed concerns that Nigerian medical doctors are exposing themselves to increased risks of cardiovascular diseases, including heart attacks and strokes, through excessive workloads, sleep deprivation, chronic stress and failure to undergo regular m
content:
By Chioma Obinna

Health experts on Wednesday expressed concerns that Nigerian medical doctors are exposing themselves to increased risks of cardiovascular diseases, including heart attacks and strokes, through excessive workloads, sleep deprivation, chronic stress and failure to undergo regular medical checks.

The experts, who spoke at the Annual General Meeting/Scientific Conference of the Medical and Dental Consultants’ Association of Nigeria (MDCAN), Federal Medical Centre (FMC), Ebute-Metta, Lagos, tagged: “ Your Body, Your Responsibility: A Personal Guide to Cancer Risk Reduction for Physicians, lamented that physicians, despite their knowledge of healthy living, often neglect their own health while attending to patients.

They called for a deliberate shift towards preventive healthcare among doctors, warning that professional dedication should not come at the expense of their lives.

Speaking at the conference, Chief Consultant Cardiologist at the Lagos State University Teaching Hospital, LASUTH, Dr Folashade Daniel, said doctors must consciously balance their professional responsibilities with adequate rest, exercise, healthy eating and routine medical examinations.

Daniel, who spoke on protecting the hearts of physicians, said: “I don’t think physicians can balance their work, healthy living, and their mobility. It has to be intentional.”

She noted that doctors sometimes work for extended hours, leaving little time for personal health, but stressed that they must make deliberate efforts to recover and maintain healthy lifestyles.

“First of all, know that your life is not just, your life doesn’t just entail your job. You are a person, you have a family, and you have responsibilities. Yes, to your patients, but also to your family, to yourself,” she said.

According to her, doctors should make adequate rest, relaxation, healthy eating and physical activity essential parts of their routines, rather than treating them as optional activities.

She advised physicians with a family history of cardiovascular disease to exercise extra caution and make annual health checks a priority.

“Take your birthday, for example, your one anniversary, to do a check-up. And then look up all the results with a colleague. Don’t just be your own doctors. Let somebody look at what you have, the results you have done, and give you advice as need arises,” Daniel said.

The cardiologist also urged government to strengthen policies that promote healthier food choices and safer working environments.

She identified excessive salt, preservatives and trans fats in food, particularly from repeatedly used frying oil, as concerns requiring stronger regulation.

Daniel further recommended accessible spaces for physical activity in workplaces, including walkways, trees and encouragement for workers to use stairs where appropriate.

She said access to affordable medicines and wider coverage of the National Health Insurance Scheme was equally important in preventing and managing cardiovascular diseases.

On the consequences of excessive working hours, she warned that sleep deprivation and prolonged shifts could expose doctors to additional health risks.

Earlier, Chairman of MDCAN, FMC Ebute-Metta, Dr Lucky Okpetu, said the theme was chosen because physicians frequently advise patients to adopt healthy lifestyles but fail to practise the same advice themselves.

“We found out that physicians hardly take care of themselves. They themselves don’t look after their hearts. They indulge in things they are not supposed to. They advise their patients to do the right thing. But they do not do what they tell the patients to do,” he said.

Okpetu, a consultant haematologist, urged doctors to have personal physicians and undergo regular medical examinations.

“The ideal thing to do is, as a physician, you must have your own physician. You have to see your physician regularly,” he said.

He listed kidney function, blood sugar and other necessary medical tests among the routine checks doctors should undertake, adding that lifestyle choices remained critical to cardiovascular health.

Speaking, the Medical Director and Chief Executive Officer of FMC Ebute-Metta, Dr Saheed Ogunme, also challenged physicians to make patients’ health and well-being their foremost consideration while strengthening collaboration between hospital management and consultants.

He stressed that healthcare delivery was a collective responsibility and that no single professional could claim credit for successful patient outcomes.

“If a patient comes to our hospital, has a successful surgery and goes home, it’s not the doctor or consultant that has done this alone. It’s the other people too, who participate in the care of that patient,” he said.

Ogunme also urged doctors to pay attention to their own health, noting that physicians often have no personal doctors to consult when they become ill.

The conference also examined the role of artificial intelligence in reducing workload and addressing manpower shortages in the health sector.

Also, Professor of Medicine and Chairman, Medical Advisory Committee, FMC Ebute-Metta, Prof. Adebowale Adekoya, said AI could help reduce burnout by automating routine documentation and administrative tasks.

He cited ambient scribe technology, which can listen to conversations between healthcare professionals and patients and convert them into clinical documentation.

“AI can listen to conversation between the doctor, the nurse, and their patients. And then transcribe that using voice-to-text, using language models,” he said.

However, Adekoya warned that doctors must verify AI-generated information before using it in patient care. “Although the responsibility of making sure that it’s accurate still lies with the caregiver of reading it before posting it,” he said.

He also cautioned against applying AI tools developed using foreign population data indiscriminately to Nigerian patients, insisting that local data must inform medical technologies used in the country.

“The responsibility is on us now to generate our own data,” he said.

Chairman of the occasion, Prof. Oluwatoyin Ashiru, urged medical professionals to protect their physical and emotional well-being, warning that exhausted and distressed doctors could struggle to provide the quality of care expected of them.

He challenged professional associations to protect the welfare of healthcare workers, strengthen institutional partnerships and ensure that professional disagreements did not undermine patient care.

His message was clear: doctors must protect themselves while protecting others.

The post Doctors risking heart disease through overwork, sleep deprivation – Experts appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Police deny declaring man wanted for impregnating eight women in Cross River
description:
The Cross River State Police Command has disowned a viral flyer circulating on social media, purportedly issued by the Nigeria Police, Okuku Division, declaring an individual wanted over allegations of impregnating eight women and subsequently abandoning them.
The command said the flyer did not orig
content:
The Cross River State Police Command has disowned a viral flyer circulating on social media, purportedly issued by the Nigeria Police, Okuku Division, declaring an individual wanted over allegations of impregnating eight women and subsequently abandoning them.

The command said the flyer did not originate from it and did not represent any official police communication.

In a statement signed by the Police Public Relations Officer, Sunday Eitokpah, and made available to journalists on Wednesday in Calabar, the police stated that they were not investigating any case involving the individual whose photograph appeared in the flyer, nor were they aware of any investigation relating to the allegations contained therein.

The statement read, “The Cross River State Police Command is aware of a viral flyer circulating on social media, purportedly issued by the Nigeria Police, Okuku Division, Cross River State, declaring an individual wanted over allegations of impregnating eight women and subsequently abandoning them.

“The Command wishes to categorically dissociate itself from the publication, as it did not originate from the Command and does not represent any official Police communication.”

The police clarified that there was no police division known as Okuku Division in Cross River State. What existed in the area was a police outpost, which was not an operational formation empowered to independently investigate a case of the magnitude portrayed in the circulating publication.

“The Command wishes to state unequivocally that it is not investigating any case involving the individual whose photograph appears in the flyer, nor is it aware of any investigation relating to the allegations contained therein. For the avoidance of doubt, there is no Police Division known as Okuku Division in Cross River State.

“What exists in the area is a Police Outpost, which is not an operational formation empowered to independently investigate a case of the magnitude portrayed in the circulating publication. The flyer is therefore fake and should be disregarded by members of the public,” the statement said.

Eitokpah strongly condemned the mischievous and malicious use of artificial intelligence and other communication platforms to fabricate information, impersonate security agencies, spread falsehood and mislead unsuspecting members of the public.

“Such acts are capable of damaging reputations, creating unnecessary panic, undermining public confidence in law enforcement institutions and threatening public peace”, he added.

The Commissioner of Police in the state, Ajo Ordue, directed a thorough investigation to establish the origin of the misleading publication and identify those responsible for its creation and circulation, warning that anyone found culpable would face the full weight of the law.

He urged members of the public to disregard the contents of the fake flyer, refrain from sharing or amplifying it, and always verify security-related information through the command’s recognised official communication channels and verified social media platforms @Cross River State Police Command.

“The Cross River State Police Command remains committed to protecting lives and property and will not tolerate the deliberate use of misinformation, impersonation or other deceptive communication practices to mislead the public or undermine public peace,” Ordue added.

title: How residents killed BEDC staff for disconnecting building over N300k electricity bill

content:
By Ozioruva Aliu

BENIN CITY – THE management of the BEDC Electricity Plc on Wednesday called on the security agencies and government to ensure that its 38 years old staff identified as Oscar Nduka Eze who was brutally killed while on duty on Monday gets justice.

Eze was reportedly stabbed to death around Idumobi Umunede in the Agbor Unit, Delta State after he disconnected a building said to be owing about N300,000 electricity bill.

Shortly after he disconnected the building, he was said to have been trailed to a nearby house by some people suspected to have been from previous place he had gone to work when they reportedly pounced on him and stabbed him severally till he died.

Addressing journalists at the company’s office, Acting Managing Director of the company, Jonathan Lawani said the killers wanted to conceal their act but unknown to them, the building which they took him to had security camera.

He said “Eze went to work on Monday 16th November 2026 for his official duty to earn a legitimate living. However, at about 12 noon of that same day while he was carrying out his official work along the Idumobi by Umunede within the Agbor Business Unit of our operations in Delta State, some hoodlums, some men who claim to be more powerful than God, who has the power to take life, traced him to a house within the same community and they stabbed him with knife until he died on the spot.

Caught on CCTV

“What they planned did not work. These people had planned to kill him without any evidence. And what they did was to push him into a compound, a very isolated place where he went to carry out another assignment. Unfortunately for them, that house has a CCTV camera and they were all captured directly.

“The simple reason for this is that this officer had disconnected their house for non-payment. The only instrument that have been approved by NERC, the Nigeria Electricity Regulatory Commission to ask for payment or to demand payment for those who refuse to pay us for our monthly electricity. I want to put it straight that what the late Oscar did was an approved and official assignment.

“The house in question owes us almost three hundred thousand naira and he disconnected them for non-payment and left the place quietly.”

Lawani said Eze just got married four months ago after his wife died.

He said five persons have been arrested in connection to the incident.

“We cannot bring him back but we must ensure that justice is served. We will do everything in line with the law to see that justice is served,” he added.

Vanguard News

title: PDP delegation visits injured APC leaders at Gombe hospital
description:
By Ben Ngwakwe



In a significant demonstration of political tolerance, sportsmanship and solidarity, the Gombe State chapter of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) has paid a solidarity visit to leaders of the All Progressives Congress (APC) who sustained injuries in a road accident while returning
content:
By Ben Ngwakwe

In a significant demonstration of political tolerance, sportsmanship and solidarity, the Gombe State chapter of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) has paid a solidarity visit to leaders of the All Progressives Congress (APC) who sustained injuries in a road accident while returning from a campaign rally on Tuesday.

The PDP delegation, led by the Director-General of its Campaign Council, Hon. Dan’azumi Adamu Pindiga, visited the injured APC leaders at the Federal Teaching Hospital (FTH), Gombe, on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, to express sympathy and wish them a speedy recovery.

Those involved in the accident included the APC State Campaign Council Director-General, Hon. Sa’adu Hassan, and the Gombe State APC Chairman, Hon. Dantata Ndus, alongside other party members.

Members of the PDP delegation included the party’s State Secretary, Hon. Adamu Abubakar; Hon. Abubakar Walama; Hon. Sani Hassan Dogarai; Hon. Hassan Santana; Hon. Abubakar Bello (Cikasoron Gombe); and Hon. Jalo Ahmed Ganga.

During the visit, Pindiga conveyed messages of solidarity and goodwill on behalf of the PDP leader in Gombe State, former Governor, Senator Ibrahim Hassan Dankwambo, OON, PhD, Talban Gombe; the party’s governorship candidate, Professor Isa Ali Pantami; and the entire PDP family in the state.

The delegation also offered prayers to Almighty Allah to grant the injured party chieftains and other victims of the accident complete healing, renewed strength and a speedy recovery.

Speaking during the visit, the PDP representatives stressed that political differences should not undermine the bonds of brotherhood, humanity and mutual respect among the people of Gombe State.

They maintained that, “beyond party affiliations and electoral interests, political actors remain members of one community with shared responsibilities and a common obligation to promote peaceful coexistence”.

According to the delegation, “an unfortunate incident involving members of another political party should attract the concern and sympathy of all, irrespective of political leanings”.

The visit, coming amid heightened political activities ahead of the 2027 general elections, underscores the need for political maturity, tolerance and civility among competing parties and their supporters.

It also sends a strong message that political competition should be anchored on issues, policies and the contest for public support, rather than hostility, animosity or division.

The PDP delegation reiterated its goodwill towards the injured APC leaders and prayed for their full recovery, stressing that humanity must always take precedence over partisan considerations.

According to them, “Politics Should Never Come Before Humanity; We Are All Brothers and sisters”.

The post PDP delegation visits injured APC leaders at Gombe hospital appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: ADC faults INEC over short notice for mock accreditation exercise
description: The African Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council has asked the Independent National Electoral Commission to postpone its proposed November 28, 2026, mock accreditation and results collation exercise, alleging that the short notice given to political parties would undermine their partici
content:
The African Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council has asked the Independent National Electoral Commission to postpone its proposed November 28, 2026, mock accreditation and results collation exercise, alleging that the short notice given to political parties would undermine their participation.

The council said INEC did not give political parties sufficient time to mobilise, train and submit their agents for the nationwide exercise, which is expected to cover all 774 local government areas and two polling units in each of the country’s 8,838 Registration Areas.

The ADC-PCC also accused the commission of bias, alleging that its invitation to participate in the exercise was deliberately delayed until November 18, the final day for the submission of names of participating agents.

In a statement issued in Abuja on Wednesday by its Director of Media and Publicity, Kola Ologbondiyan, the council said INEC’s letter, dated November 16, 2026, notifying stakeholders of the exercise barely two days before the submission deadline, was hasty and unfair.

It argued that political parties had been given less than two weeks to prepare for an exercise of national importance.

The statement read, “How does INEC expect political parties to adequately prepare, mobilise, train and submit their agents for an exercise of this magnitude within such a short time? This is not preparation; it is an ambush.

“A mock exercise designed to test the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) ahead of the 2027 General Elections cannot be credible if critical stakeholders are effectively excluded by an unreasonable timeline.

“INEC cannot test electoral credibility through an incredible process.

“We therefore demand that INEC immediately postpone the exercise to give political parties sufficient time to nominate their agents, prepare adequately and participate meaningfully in the process.”

The council said the exercise was too important to be conducted under a timeline that could prevent political parties from participating effectively.

It maintained that adequate preparation and the involvement of all critical stakeholders were necessary for the mock exercise to achieve its intended purpose of testing the BVAS ahead of the 2027 general elections.

ADC rejects INEC’s position on electronic transmission of collation results

Meanwhile, the ADC-PCC has rejected INEC’s reported position that results from Ward, Local Government and State collation levels would not be electronically transmitted and published on its Result Viewing Portal during the 2027 general elections.

The council was reacting to comments reportedly made on Tuesday by INEC’s Director of Information and Communication Technology, Lawrence Bayode, that the commission had neither developed nor tested the necessary system for uploading results from the three collation levels.

Describing the position as unacceptable, the ADC-PCC said it contradicted Nigerians’ expectations for greater transparency in the electoral process.

The statement said, “Nigerians fought for and demanded real-time electronic transmission of election results precisely to eliminate the manipulation that often occurs between the Polling Unit and subsequent collation levels.

“Any attempt to weaken, delay or abandon electronic transmission and public visibility of results at the various levels of collation is an invitation to electoral manipulation. INEC must not create loopholes that would undermine the credibility of the 2027 elections.”

The council recalled that former INEC Chairman, Professor Mahmood Yakubu, had assured Nigerians before leaving office that the commission would extend the uploading of results from Ward, Local Government and State levels to IReV.

It added that the current chairman, Professor Joash Amupitan, SAN, had also given assurances upon assuming office that the commission would pursue measures to strengthen transparency in the electoral process.

Questioning the reported position, the ADC-PCC said, “What has changed? Why the sudden retreat from commitments previously made to Nigerians? Why is INEC now seeking to retain an opaque collation system that limits public visibility of results to the Polling Unit level?

“The Commission’s position that Forms EC8B (Ward), EC8C (Local Government) and EC8D (State) will not be uploaded to IReV raises serious questions about its commitment to improving electoral transparency ahead of 2027.

“If Form EC8A, the Polling Unit result, can be captured and uploaded to IReV, there is no convincing reason why the corresponding results at subsequent collation levels cannot also be made publicly accessible. The same technology and process of capturing and uploading results should be extended to the other relevant forms.”

The council said INEC’s position had created an atmosphere of suspicion and heightened concerns about the commission’s preparedness to conduct transparent, credible and acceptable elections in 2027.

It urged the commission to demonstrate impartiality, competence and independence, adding that its credibility depended on treating political parties fairly and transparently.

The ADC-PCC further warned that Nigerians expected the commission to ensure that their votes counted in the forthcoming elections.

“The world is watching the INEC Chairman, Professor Joash Amupitan. He must be mindful of the weight of responsibility before him. His name, his legacy and the peace of this country are at stake. History will judge him not by assurances, but by the credibility of the elections he conducts.

“INEC must not give Nigerians any reason to doubt its independence, competence or readiness for the 2027 elections. The Commission must get this right, and getting it right begins with listening to Nigerians and respecting the legitimate concerns of political parties,” it read.

The council reaffirmed its commitment to peaceful democratic engagement, insisting that it would continue to advocate electoral transparency, accountability and the protection of Nigerians’ votes.

It said, “We will not be intimidated. We will not be silenced. We will continue to insist that every Nigerian’s vote must count.”

The post ADC faults INEC over short notice for mock accreditation exercise appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Tinubu  gives nod to establishment of Nigeria’s first University of Public Relations and Leadership
description:
President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has approved the establishment of Nigeria’s first University of Public Relations and Leadership, marking a new development in professional education and strategic communication in the country.
The approval was announced on Wednesday by Vice President Kashim Shettima, who
content:
President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has approved the establishment of Nigeria’s first University of Public Relations and Leadership, marking a new development in professional education and strategic communication in the country.

The approval was announced on Wednesday by Vice President Kashim Shettima, who represented the President at the ongoing World Public Relations Forum in Abuja.

Shettima described the proposed institution as a strategic investment in human capital development, professional training and the future of public relations and strategic communication in Nigeria.

The university is expected to provide specialised training and develop professionals with the skills and leadership capacity needed to advance the public relations industry in Nigeria.

The development was announced during the international gathering of public relations professionals and stakeholders, which brought together experts to discuss the growth and future of the profession.

He said the university would promote specialised education, research, professional development and leadership training, while preparing a new generation of communication experts for emerging global challenges.

According to him, the initiative is part of the Federal Government’s commitment to creating a lasting institutional legacy from Nigeria’s hosting of the international forum.

The Vice President commended the Nigerian Institute of Public Relations, NIPR, the Federal Ministry of Information and National Orientation, and the Nasarawa State Government for working together to actualise the project.

He also urged international delegates attending the forum to explore Nigeria’s investment opportunities, describing the country as a major economic force with enormous human and entrepreneurial potential.

Shettima challenged negative international perceptions about Nigeria, insisting that the country should not be defined by narratives surrounding internet fraud and other criminal activities.

He said, “Nigeria goes beyond 419. Nigeria is much much bigger than that.”

The Vice President highlighted the achievements of Nigerians in business, technology and other sectors, noting that the country has produced some of the wealthiest Black entrepreneurs in the world.

He also drew attention to Nigeria’s growing population and global influence, projecting that the country would become the world’s third most populous nation by 2050, with an estimated population of 440 million.

Shettima further described Nigerians in the United States as an exceptionally accomplished immigrant community, noting that about 60 per cent of Nigerian Americans have university degrees.

“The richest black man on earth is a bloody Nigerian. The second richest black man in the world is another bloody Nigerian. The third richest black man in the world is also a bloody Nigerian,” he said.

He urged foreign investors and international delegates to build partnerships with Nigerian institutions and businesses, stressing that the country offers significant opportunities beyond its portrayal on social media.

Shettima said the government expects participants to leave Nigeria with a better understanding of its economic prospects and renewed interest in investing and collaborating with local businesses.

He added that the administration recognises the growing importance of communication professionals in strengthening public trust, democratic governance, national development and international relations.

The Vice President also called on public relations practitioners to maintain high ethical standards, transparency, accountability and professionalism, particularly amid the growing challenges of misinformation, disinformation and artificial intelligence.

Very Nigerian reports that the university would be located in Nasarawa State, Nigeria.

The post Tinubu gives nod to establishment of Nigeria’s first University of Public Relations and Leadership appeared first on Very Nigerian.

title: After criticism, Tinubu expands campaign tour to 19 states, removes Bauchi, adds Katsina, Zamfara, Imo, Kwara, others
description:
President Bola Tinubu has expanded his personal campaign itinerary for the 2027 presidential election, increasing the number of states he plans to visit from 12 to 19, in addition to the Federal Capital Territory (FCT).
The revised schedule indicates that the President is now expected to attend 20 c
content:
President Bola Tinubu has expanded his personal campaign itinerary for the 2027 presidential election, increasing the number of states he plans to visit from 12 to 19, in addition to the Federal Capital Territory (FCT).

The revised schedule indicates that the President is now expected to attend 20 campaign rallies across the country between October 24, 2026, and January 13, 2027.

The updated itinerary adds Katsina, Taraba, Zamfara, Imo and Kwara to the original list, while Akwa Ibom, Jigawa and Kebbi have also been incorporated following Tinubu’s recent campaign appearances in the states.

The development marks a departure from the initial arrangement under which other APC leaders were expected to represent the President at some state rallies.

Tinubu has already attended campaign events in several locations outside his original itinerary, including Uyo, Akwa Ibom State, on November 6, where he also inaugurated projects executed by Governor Umo Eno’s administration.

He subsequently attended a rally in Port Harcourt, Rivers State, on November 7, followed by engagements in Dutse, Jigawa State, on November 10, and Birnin Kebbi, Kebbi State, on November 17.

Under the revised schedule, Tinubu is expected to visit Katsina on December 2, Kano on December 17, Jalingo, Taraba State, on December 19, and Abuja on December 21.

Other scheduled appearances include Gusau, Zamfara State, on December 28, and Owerri, Imo State, on December 30.

The President is expected to resume campaign activities in the New Year with rallies in Yola, Adamawa State, on January 4; Sokoto on January 5; and Ilorin, Kwara State, on January 8.

He will then visit Asaba, Delta State, on January 11, before rounding off the campaign with a major rally in Lagos on January 13.

The revised timetable also contains changes to the original schedule. The Sokoto rally has been moved from December 5 to January 5, while the Lagos finale has been shifted from January 9 to January 13.

The Bauchi rally, initially scheduled for November 29 with Tinubu expected to attend, has been moved to December 1. However, the revised programme does not indicate that the President will personally attend the event.

Although the APC has scheduled 37 rallies across the 36 states and the FCT, Tinubu is expected to personally participate in 20, leaving other party leaders to lead the remaining engagements.

A breakdown of the revised itinerary shows that the North-West has the highest number of states on the President’s campaign trail, with seven: Kaduna, Jigawa, Kebbi, Katsina, Kano, Zamfara and Sokoto.

The North-East and South-South have three states each, while the North-Central, South-West and South-East have two states each.

The distribution places the North-West at the centre of Tinubu’s planned campaign appearances, although the revised schedule includes engagements across the other geopolitical zones.

The President had earlier told members of the APC Presidential Campaign Council in Abuja that he would not be able to attend every rally because of the need to balance campaign activities with his responsibilities as head of government.

He, however, promised to make time to engage directly with Nigerians while other party leaders took the campaign to different states and local government areas.

According to Daily Trust, the expanded itinerary comes amid controversy over Tinubu’s initial decision to limit his personal campaign appearances to 12 states, leaving other APC leaders to represent him at rallies elsewhere.

At the inauguration of the APC Presidential Campaign Council on October 14, Tinubu had explained that he would not attend every campaign event, citing the demands of governance, the country’s financial obligations and the need to attract long-term investors.

“So, you will excuse me from going everywhere with you; we have bills to pay. The American creditors cannot wait,” he told members of the campaign council.

The decision triggered criticism from opposition figures and political groups, who questioned why a sitting President seeking re-election would not personally take his campaign to all parts of the country.

Among those who criticised the arrangement were the Social Democratic Party (SDP) presidential candidate, Adewole Adebayo, Peter Obi Media Reach and the Makinde/Daura Presidential Campaign Organisation.

They argued that party representatives could not replace the President in addressing Nigerians’ questions about his administration’s performance.

Adebayo alleged that Tinubu’s decision was an attempt to avoid confronting voters over economic hardship and what he described as unmet expectations.

The Makinde/Daura group also challenged the President to campaign across the country or withdraw from the presidential race.

Similarly, Peter Obi Media Reach argued that Nigerians were being asked to assess Tinubu’s policies, promises and performance, rather than those of party representatives campaigning on his behalf.

The APC, however, defended the President’s decision, maintaining that there was no legal requirement for a presidential candidate to visit all 36 states during an election campaign.

The post After criticism, Tinubu expands campaign tour to 19 states, removes Bauchi, adds Katsina, Zamfara, Imo, Kwara, others appeared first on Very Nigerian.

title: US strategist restricts X comments after Tinubu interview backlash
description:
An American political strategist and media personality, Diana London, has restricted access to the comment section of her X account following criticism from Nigerian users over her recent interview with President Bola Tinubu.







London interviewed Tinubu at the Presidential Villa, Abuja, on Tues
content:
An American political strategist and media personality, Diana London, has restricted access to the comment section of her X account following criticism from Nigerian users over her recent interview with President Bola Tinubu.

London interviewed Tinubu at the Presidential Villa, Abuja, on Tuesday and was subsequently photographed with the President and his Chief of Staff, Femi Gbajabiamila.

Following the interview, she published several posts on X expressing support for the Nigerian government’s security cooperation with the United States.

In one of the posts, London described the US-Nigeria security partnership as one that was “delivering results”, crediting Tinubu and US President Donald Trump for their commitment to tackling terrorism.

“The U.S.-Nigeria security partnership is delivering results. Peace through strength. None of this happens without the ongoing partnership between President Trump and President Tinubu, their steadfast commitment to eliminating terrorists, and Nigeria’s willingness to work closely with the U.S. government,” she wrote.

She also described Nigeria as the United States’ greatest ally in Africa, expressing optimism that the relationship could create additional economic and trade opportunities for both countries.

In another post, London expressed appreciation for the opportunity to work with individuals representing Nigeria, particularly on initiatives relating to the protection of religious groups and strengthening relations between the Trump administration and the Nigerian government.

However, the posts were subsequently deleted from her X account amid criticism from Nigerian social media users over her engagement with the Tinubu administration.

The controversy followed a report by Peoples Gazette alleging that London received $4.5 million for the interview assignment. The allegation generated reactions on social media, with some users questioning the reported payment and the nature of the engagement.

Checks on her X account on Wednesday showed that access to the comment section had been restricted, with a notice indicating that only selected accounts could respond to her posts.

Before the restriction, some users had questioned her decision to delete the posts praising the Nigerian government’s security partnership with the United States.

London had not publicly explained the deletion of the posts or the restriction of comments as of the time of filing this report.

The post US strategist restricts X comments after Tinubu interview backlash appeared first on Vanguard News.

Obi made this known in a statement on Wednesday, Nov
content:
Former Anambra State Governor and Labour Party presidential candidate, Peter Obi, has disclosed that he met with United States senators, including Senator James Lankford, during the second day of his engagements on Capitol Hill in Washington, D.C.

Obi made this known in a statement on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, saying the meeting took place on Tuesday, November 17, as part of his engagements aimed at strengthening Nigeria’s democracy and international relations.

He said Lankford invited him to his office, where they exchanged views on strengthening democratic institutions, promoting peace and advancing shared values.

Obi expressed appreciation to the American senator for his reception and the opportunity to discuss issues concerning Nigeria and its democratic development.

According to him, the discussions also focused on international cooperation, effective governance, credible democratic processes, as well as the security and well-being of Nigerians.

The former governor said the engagements provided an opportunity to deepen relationships and advance a shared vision of a peaceful, united and prosperous Nigeria.

“Our commitment to building a nation that serves every Nigerian remains steadfast,” Obi said.

He ended the statement with his campaign slogan, “A New Nigeria Is Possible.”

title: 2026 harvest reduces food prices, says Kyari
description:
…Niger leads rice, yam production — NAERLS report



By Gabriel Ewepu



ABUJA — The Minister of Agriculture and Food Security, Senator Abubakar Kyari, has said increased food production during the 2026 wet season has contributed to a reduction in food prices despite persistent challenges in the agr
content:
…Niger leads rice, yam production — NAERLS report

By Gabriel Ewepu

ABUJA — The Minister of Agriculture and Food Security, Senator Abubakar Kyari, has said increased food production during the 2026 wet season has contributed to a reduction in food prices despite persistent challenges in the agricultural sector.

Kyari spoke on Wednesday during the presentation of the 2026 Agricultural Performance Survey Report by the Executive Director of the National Agricultural Extension and Research Liaison Services (NAERLS), Professor Yusuf Sani, at the ministry’s headquarters in Abuja.

The minister said the report indicated an increase in agricultural output compared with 2025, attributing the development to government interventions aimed at boosting food production and improving affordability.

He cited reductions in the prices of commodities such as garri and millet, saying the trend reflected improvements in food supply.

“When you do comparison between 2025 and 2026, I am not even comparing 2023 and 2026, just within the one year, we have seen prices dropping — garri, millet, and so on and so forth, that has come down,” he said.

Kyari added that another harvest was expected within the next month, which he said could further improve food availability.

On agricultural mechanisation, he said deliveries under the second phase of the programme were expected within the next two to three months.

He also disclosed that the Federal Government planned to release food commodities stored under the Guaranteed Minimum Price (GMP) programme through the Bank of Agriculture to help stabilise market prices.

“That is also in the works, and very soon we will announce how the methodology of that release will be made,” he said.

On fertiliser supply, Kyari said the Presidential Fertiliser Initiative planned to release three million bags of fertiliser within one month to reduce input costs for farmers.

He said the programme, announced by Vice-President Kashim Shettima, was part of efforts to improve agricultural productivity and balance the interests of farmers, processors and consumers.

The minister also pointed to increased private-sector investment in agricultural processing, particularly in cocoa, sesame, soybean and shea nut.

He said investments by multinational companies in the country’s agricultural sector indicated growing confidence in Nigeria’s business environment.

Kyari further disclosed that $33 million had been invested in the Special Agro-Industrial Processing Zones (SAPZ) programme.

He said government interventions over the past three years had contributed to increased productivity across several crop categories, although some crops continued to record declines.

Presenting the survey findings, NAERLS Executive Director, Professor Yusuf Sani, said Niger State emerged as the country’s leading producer of rice and yam.

He said Ogun State ranked second in rice production, although its rice yield per hectare was lower than that of Niger State.

Sani attributed Niger State’s performance partly to the adoption of improved farming practices by farmers, noting the presence of the National Cereals Research Institute in Badeggi.

For yam production, he said Niger State also ranked first, with Akwa Ibom among the 10 leading producing states.

Kano State emerged as the leading onion producer, followed by Kebbi and Sokoto, while Taraba also featured among the top 10 states.

On national agricultural output, Sani said cereal production increased by 1.8 per cent compared with 2025, reaching approximately 29.4 million metric tonnes.

He disclosed that 13 of the 17 major crops assessed recorded higher production during the period, while ginger, cocoyam, millet and soybean recorded declines.

The survey also identified limited access to quality seeds as the leading constraint affecting farmers, accounting for 28.8 per cent of reported production challenges.

Other constraints included inadequate agricultural extension services and training, family and labour-related challenges, and insufficient access to grants and farm inputs.

Sani also identified ginger blight as one of the factors affecting farmers’ output.

On regional agricultural performance, he said the North-Central zone led production of cereals, legumes, roots and tubers, while the North-West accounted for the largest share of vegetable production at about 31 per cent.

The post 2026 harvest reduces food prices, says Kyari appeared first on Vanguard News.

content:
The naira depreciated to N1,470 per dollar at the parallel foreign exchange market on Wednesday, its weakest performance since January 28.

The latest rate represented a N25, or 1.73 per cent, decline from the N1,445 per dollar quoted on Tuesday.

Currency traders, popularly known as Bureau De Change operators, in Lagos quoted the buying rate at N1,450 per dollar and the selling rate at N1,470.

The local currency had traded at N1,430 per dollar on Monday, compared with N1,390 on November 13, representing a depreciation of N40, or 2.88 per cent.

At the Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM), the official window, the naira also weakened to N1,363.23 per dollar.

Data from the NFEM showed that the currency depreciated by N7.43, or 0.55 per cent, from the N1,355.80 per dollar recorded on Tuesday.

Meanwhile, Nigeria’s foreign exchange reserves stood at $43.64 billion as of November 14, compared with $45.56 billion recorded on January 2.

The figures, obtained from the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN), indicated a decline of $1.92 billion, or 4.21 per cent, in the country’s external reserves since the beginning of the year.

In a related development, the CBN and the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPC) on Wednesday signed a Memorandum of Understanding to strengthen foreign exchange inflows, energy financing and macroeconomic stability.

title: NNPC, CBN sign deal to boost oil production to 3m bpd
description:
By Udeme Akpan



The Nigerian National Petroleum Company (NNPC) Limited and the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to strengthen foreign exchange inflows, improve financial discipline and attract investment into the country’s energy sector.



The agreemen
content:
By Udeme Akpan

The Nigerian National Petroleum Company (NNPC) Limited and the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to strengthen foreign exchange inflows, improve financial discipline and attract investment into the country’s energy sector.

The agreement, signed at the CBN headquarters in Abuja on Wednesday, is also expected to support NNPC’s ambition to increase Nigeria’s crude oil production from the current 1.8 million barrels per day to three million barrels per day.

Speaking at the signing ceremony, the Group Chief Executive Officer of NNPC Limited, Mr. Bashir Bayo Ojulari, described the agreement as a defining moment in the relationship between the national oil company and the country’s monetary authority.

He said the MoU established a structured framework for collaboration between both institutions at the intersection of energy and finance.

“This MoU provides that structure by which the two institutions will collaborate at the meeting point between energy and finance,” Ojulari said.

He explained that the partnership would support NNPC’s initiatives, strengthen the flow of export proceeds into the Nigerian economy, address foreign exchange challenges affecting trade and improve financing arrangements for energy projects.

According to him, the agreement would also help the company raise capital based on its balance sheet and assets, with guidance from the CBN.

“We are here to build a working partnership that delivers results,” he said.

Providing further details, NNPC’s Group Chief Financial Officer, Mr. Adedapo Segun, said the agreement would replace previous practices of addressing financial issues through irregular arrangements with a more coordinated and structured approach.

He explained that improved coordination between the two institutions would help attract the investment required to raise crude oil production from 1.8 million barrels per day to three million barrels per day.

On implementation, Segun said NNPC would align domestic payments, contractor settlements and foreign exchange conversions with CBN regulations to support the stability of the naira and reduce dollarisation.

He added that both institutions had agreed to establish working groups, implementation timelines and accountability mechanisms to ensure effective execution of the MoU.

The Treasurer of NNPC Limited, Mr. John Etukudo, will oversee implementation on behalf of the company.

On his part, the CBN Governor, Mr. Olayemi Cardoso, described the agreement as a formalisation of an existing relationship between the two institutions.

He said their collaboration in account management, fund transfers and liquidity support would contribute to macroeconomic stability by ensuring the availability of revenue for government fiscal obligations and predictable foreign exchange inflows.

“Our continued collaboration in efficient account management, funds transfer and liquidity support directly contributes to macroeconomic stability by ensuring the availability of revenue to achieve fiscal mandates and predictable inflows into the foreign exchange markets,” Cardoso said.
