title: Mine murder: Court fixes December 21 for judgment
description:
By Egufe Yafugborhi



ASABA — A Delta State High Court sitting in Asaba has fixed December 21, 2026, for judgment in the trial of Assistant Superintendent of Police (ASP) Usman Nuhu, popularly known as Ogbegbe, and four others over the fatal shooting of Oghenemine Ogidi, alias Mine, in Effurun, Del
content:
By Egufe Yafugborhi

ASABA — A Delta State High Court sitting in Asaba has fixed December 21, 2026, for judgment in the trial of Assistant Superintendent of Police (ASP) Usman Nuhu, popularly known as Ogbegbe, and four others over the fatal shooting of Oghenemine Ogidi, alias Mine, in Effurun, Delta State.

The date was fixed on Tuesday after the prosecution and defence adopted their respective final written addresses, bringing proceedings in the case to a close ahead of judgment.

Justice Michael Obi, who presided over the trial, adjourned the matter after listening to the final submissions of counsel to both parties.

The five defendants are facing trial over the April 26 killing of Ogidi, an incident that attracted public attention and led to the dismissal of the police officers involved from the Nigeria Police Force.

The prosecution had earlier closed its case after presenting six witnesses, following which the defendants opened and concluded their defence.

Nuhu, the first defendant and principal suspect in the alleged shooting, remains in prison custody, while the court had earlier granted bail to the second to fifth defendants.

The other defendants are Onoloko Dauroupamo, Okoh Kelechi, Goodluck Kingsley and Omonigho Ahweyevu. They were members of the anti-crime squad allegedly led by Nuhu at the Effurun Area Command before their dismissal following the incident.

At an earlier sitting, counsel to Nuhu, Uche Chibuogwu, explained that the defence had deliberately refrained from filing a bail application for his client, citing concerns for his safety and the gravity of the murder charge.

He said: “We did not find it necessary filing bail application for the first defendant, one, for his own safety, and secondly, this is a capital offence — offence of murder.”

The Delta State Director of Public Prosecutions, Tejiri R. Anuwhin, had also explained that the four other defendants were granted bail because the offences they faced, bordering on negligence, carried a maximum six-month jail term.

According to Anuwhin, the defendants had been in custody since June 1, making their continued detention potentially disproportionate to the maximum punishment prescribed for the alleged offences.

With the adoption of final addresses by both parties, the court is expected to deliver its verdict on December 21, determining the culpability or otherwise of the defendants.

title: EFCC arraigns Lagos socialite over N603m NNPC job scam
description: The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission on Wednesday arraigned socialite Halimat Tejuosho before the Federal Capital Territory High Court in Gwagwalada, Abuja, over an alleged N603.4m scam involving a promise to secure a woman’s appointment as Group Managing Director of the Nigerian National Pe
content:
The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission on Wednesday arraigned socialite Halimat Tejuosho before the Federal Capital Territory High Court in Gwagwalada, Abuja, over an alleged N603.4m scam involving a promise to secure a woman’s appointment as Group Managing Director of the Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation.

Tejuosho was arraigned before Justice A.S. Adepoju on a five-count charge bordering on advance fee fraud, obtaining money by false pretence and criminal conduct.

EFCC announced the arraignment in a statement posted on its X handle on Wednesday.

The charge, marked FCT/CR/473/2026, accused her and one Gidado Ibrahim of obtaining N603.4m from Oluseye Yomi-Sholoye between August and October 2024 under the pretence that they would facilitate her appointment as NNPC GMD.

Count one of the charge read, “That you Halimat Adenike Tejuosho and Gidado Ibrahim between August 2024 to October 2024 within the jurisdiction of this Honourable Court obtained the sum of N603,400,000.00 (Six hundred and three million four hundred thousand naira) from Oluseye Yomi-Sholoye under the false pretence that you will facilitate her appointment as the Group Managing Director, GMD of Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation (NNPC), which pretence you knew to be false.”

The commission also accused Tejuosho of receiving N259.9m and N50m, among other sums, into bank accounts allegedly linked to her and Haleems Integrated Services Limited, knowing that the money was proceeds of crime.

She pleaded not guilty to all five counts when they were read to her.

Following her plea, defence counsel, Chuks Ugwuru, urged the court to grant her bail on liberal terms, arguing that all five counts were bailable offences.

He said the application was based mainly on her health condition, citing a medical report which, he argued, showed that she was critically ill.

“The ill health of an accused person is a consideration worthy enough to be reckoned as a ground of special circumstances,” he said, urging Justice Adepoju to exercise her discretion in the defendant’s favour.

However, lead prosecution counsel, Yahaya Tarfa, told the court that the EFCC opposed the bail application and had filed a 12-paragraph counter-affidavit, with one exhibit, alongside a written address.

Tarfa acknowledged that the decision to grant bail rested with the court but urged the judge to impose conditions that would ensure Tejuosho’s availability for trial.

In her ruling, Justice Adepoju held that the offences were bailable and granted Tejuosho bail in the sum of N100m, with one surety in like sum.

The judge ordered that the surety must reside within the court’s jurisdiction and own land or property in the Federal Capital Territory.

She directed that the property’s title documents be verified at the FCT Land Registry, with a copy deposited with the court’s registrar.

The defendant was also ordered to deposit her international passport with the registrar pending the hearing and determination of the case.

The EFCC had earlier declared Tejuosho wanted in April 2026 over an alleged case of obtaining money by false pretence.

The commission said she was 41 years old and gave her last known address as Aso Grove Estate, Maitama Extension, Abuja.

The post EFCC arraigns Lagos socialite over N603m NNPC job scam appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: EU Names 42 Jobs Facing Critical Worker Shortage - Full List And What It Means For Nigerian Applicants - Check Below For Full Details
description: The European Union has classified 42 occupations as facing critical workforce shortages across member states, from doctors and software developers to welders, truck drivers and cooks.
content:
The European Union has published a list of 42 occupations facing critical workforce shortages across its member states, classified under the international ISCO-08 standard. The list spans healthcare, engineering, IT, construction, transport, hospitality and domestic services - and it is being read closely by job seekers across Africa and Asia.

What the list actually is

It is an EU-wide shortage classification: a signal that these roles are hard to fill across the bloc, not in just one country. It does not, by itself, give anyone the right to work in Europe. Each member state still sets its own visa rules, salary thresholds and recognition requirements - but shortage lists like this one influence national work-permit policy, points systems and labour agreements.

The 42 occupations, by sector

Healthcare (5)

  • Generalist medical practitioners
  • Specialist medical practitioners
  • Nursing professionals
  • Nursing associate professionals
  • Health care assistants

Engineering and technical (10)

  • Civil engineers
  • Electrical engineers
  • Mechanical engineers
  • Chemical engineers
  • Industrial and production engineers
  • Environmental engineers
  • Environmental protection professionals
  • Electrical engineering technicians
  • Mechanical engineering technicians
  • Physical and engineering science technicians not elsewhere classified

IT and software (5)

  • Systems analysts
  • Software developers
  • Web and multimedia developers
  • Applications programmers
  • Software and applications developers and analysts not elsewhere classified

Construction and skilled trades (16)

  • Bricklayers and related workers
  • Concrete placers, concrete finishers and related workers
  • Carpenters and joiners
  • Roofers
  • Plasterers
  • Plumbers and pipe fitters
  • Air conditioning and refrigeration mechanics
  • Welders and flame cutters
  • Sheet metal workers
  • Structural metal preparers and erectors
  • Metal working machine tool setters and operators
  • Building and related electricians
  • Electrical mechanics and fitters
  • Motor vehicle mechanics and repairers
  • Agricultural and industrial machinery mechanics and repairers
  • Butchers, fishmongers and related food preparers

Transport, hospitality and services (6)

  • Bus and tram drivers
  • Heavy truck and lorry drivers
  • Cooks
  • Waiters
  • Cleaners and helpers in offices, hotels and other establishments
  • Accountants

What it means for Nigerians

Being on the list is not a visa. A Nigerian still needs a job offer from an EU employer, a recognised qualification where the role is regulated (doctors, nurses, engineers, electricians), and enough language ability to work safely - usually the local language for healthcare and trades.

The practical routes that reward these occupations:

  • EU Blue Card: for degree holders with a qualifying job offer; salary thresholds are set nationally.
  • National shortage-occupation permits: Germany's Opportunity Card and skilled worker visa, and similar schemes in the Netherlands, Sweden, Poland and Czechia, all use shortage and salary tests.
  • Qualification recognition: nurses, doctors and engineers must have their Nigerian credentials assessed before a permit is realistic - start that process early.
  • Language: B1/B2 in German, Dutch or a Nordic language transforms your chances in healthcare and trades.

Reality check

Shortage lists are updated regularly and differ by country, so a role that is in demand this year can drop off the list next year. Always confirm against the national immigration authority of the country you are targeting, not a Facebook post or an agent.

And no legitimate EU employer asks a candidate to pay for a work permit, a "quota slot" or a visa appointment. Fees go to the embassy or the migration agency, never to an individual.

Bottom line: Europe is short of nurses, engineers, welders, drivers and software developers, and the EU has now said so officially. If your skill is on that list, the door is widest for you - but you still walk through it with a genuine job offer, recognised papers and a national visa, not a shortcut.

title: Niger miners’ deaths: Senate demands sanctions, compensation
description:
By Henry Umoru



ABUJA — The Senate has urged the Federal Government to expedite the implementation of recommendations made by the independent investigative committee into the deaths of 37 artisanal miners in the custody of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) in Niger State.
content:
By Henry Umoru

ABUJA — The Senate has urged the Federal Government to expedite the implementation of recommendations made by the independent investigative committee into the deaths of 37 artisanal miners in the custody of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) in Niger State.

The lawmakers specifically called for accountability, appropriate sanctions against officers found culpable and institutional reforms within the NSCDC, warning that further delay in implementing the recommendations could undermine public confidence in the government’s commitment to justice.

The Senate also stressed the need for prompt payment of financial compensation recommended for the families of the deceased.

The resolutions followed a motion on Wednesday sponsored by the Chairman of the Senate Committee on Finance, Senator Sani Musa (APC, Niger East), and co-sponsored by 18 other senators from the North-Central geopolitical zone and Senator Nasir Sani Zango Daura (APC, Katsina North).

The Senate commended President Bola Tinubu and the Federal Government for establishing an independent investigative committee to probe the incident and acknowledged that the 10-member panel, chaired by Jonathan Kure, had submitted its report.

The committee reportedly identified serious lapses and recommended sanctions, institutional reforms and financial compensation for the victims’ families and other affected persons.

The lawmakers recalled that the 37 miners died on September 17, 2026, while in NSCDC custody in Minna, Niger State, after reportedly being arrested during operations against suspected illegal mining activities.

They expressed concern that the circumstances surrounding the deaths raised serious questions about the protection of fundamental human rights and the responsibility of security agencies to safeguard persons in their custody.

The Senate warned that any further delay in implementing the committee’s recommendations, particularly the payment of compensation, would prolong the suffering of the bereaved families.

It also called for comprehensive reforms in the management of detention facilities and the operational procedures of security agencies to prevent a recurrence.

Seconding the motion, Senator Ned Nwoko (APC, Delta North) described the incident as a national tragedy, insisting that the circumstances of the deaths should be examined objectively, irrespective of the alleged activities of the deceased.

He said: “It is a national tragedy when so many young lives are lost under circumstances such as the ones we are discussing.”

Nwoko, who drew parallels with incidents involving young people allegedly engaged in illegal activities in oil-producing communities in the South-South, said the country must apply consistent standards in addressing such cases.

He added: “The fact that some of these young men may have been involved in illegal activities should not mean that their lives are not valued.

“Life is life, regardless of the circumstances. We should be consistent in how we respond to such incidents.”

The Senate also resolved to constitute a delegation, to be led by the President of the Senate or his nominee, to pay a condolence visit to Niger State Governor, Mohammed Umaru Bago, and the bereaved families.

The delegation will comprise relevant senators, particularly those from Niger State and the North-Central zone, and will formally convey the Senate’s condolences and solidarity.

It further directed its relevant committees, particularly those on Interior, Solid Minerals, Human Rights, Police Affairs and Judiciary, to exercise oversight on the implementation of the investigative committee’s recommendations and report progress to the chamber.

In his presentation, Musa said the deaths had left families and communities devastated, underscoring the need for institutional accountability, respect for human dignity and strict adherence to established laws and procedures in the treatment of persons in custody.

He said the implementation of the investigative committee’s recommendations was essential to demonstrating the government’s commitment to protecting the lives and fundamental rights of Nigerians.

During deliberations, Senator Adams Oshiomhole (APC, Edo North) proposed an additional prayer condemning illegal mining and urging traditional rulers, state governments and local government authorities to sensitise their communities against the practice.

Oshiomhole argued that while the Senate was concerned about the deaths, it should also make clear its opposition to illegal mining, which he described as an attempt to divert the country’s mineral resources into private pockets.

The additional prayer was seconded by Senator Simon Lalong (APC, Plateau South).

However, Senator Abdul Ningi (PDP, Bauchi Central), raising a point of order under Order 56 of the Senate Standing Orders, challenged the relevance of the additional prayer to the substantive motion.

Ningi argued that the motion was specifically about the deaths of the 37 miners in NSCDC custody and the need to implement the investigative committee’s recommendations, not illegal mining.

He maintained that the issue was fundamentally about humanity and the circumstances surrounding the deaths.

Ruling on the point of order, Senate President Godswill Akpabio upheld Ningi’s objection, effectively dropping the additional prayer.

Akpabio said the Senate’s concern was to ensure justice for the deceased and their families, stressing that the miners were entitled to the presumption of innocence under the law.

He said: “The Nigerian law presumes every person innocent until proven guilty. That is the most important point here.

“The reason the Senate is sympathetic towards the deceased is that they had not been found guilty of any offence. If they had been prosecuted, they would have had the opportunity to defend themselves.”

The Senate President said the deceased had died under tragic and questionable circumstances without being given the opportunity to defend themselves before a competent court.

He added that the ongoing investigation should not be prejudged but stressed that the circumstances of the deaths warranted the Senate’s intervention.

Akpabio said the motion was necessary to bring the incident to national attention, adding that the Senate would continue to monitor efforts to ensure justice for the victims and their families.

The chamber thereafter observed a minute of silence in honour of the 37 deceased miners.

The post Niger miners’ deaths: Senate demands sanctions, compensation appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: FG plans release of stored grains to stabilise food prices
description:
The Federal Government has announced plans to release grains purchased and stored under the Bank of Agriculture’s Guaranteed Minimum Price programme into the market to increase food supply and prevent excessive increases in commodity prices.
The government also disclosed plans to distribute three mi
content:
The Federal Government has announced plans to release grains purchased and stored under the Bank of Agriculture’s Guaranteed Minimum Price programme into the market to increase food supply and prevent excessive increases in commodity prices.

The government also disclosed plans to distribute three million bags of fertiliser within the next month as part of measures to reduce farmers’ production costs and improve food availability across the country.

The Minister of Agriculture and Food Security, Abubakar Kyari, announced the measures on Wednesday during the presentation of the 2026 Wet Season Agricultural Performance Survey Report in Abuja.

According to a statement issued by the ministry, Kyari said the release of stored agricultural produce would form part of the government’s strategy to stabilise food prices while protecting farmers’ incomes.

“The same crops that we have that were stored under the guaranteed minimum price programme under the Bank of Agriculture will be released very soon to stabilise the market prices,” the minister said.

He disclosed that the government would announce the modalities for distributing the commodities, although he did not specify the quantity of grains available for release or the proposed distribution date.

Kyari explained that increased agricultural productivity, expanded cultivated land and improved access to farming inputs were expected to ease pressure on food prices.

He said a comparison of commodity prices between 2025 and 2026 indicated reductions in the prices of some agricultural products, particularly maize and dairy products.

“Just within the one year, we have seen a drop in dairy, maize and so forth that has come down,” he said.

The minister disclosed that the Presidential Fertiliser Initiative was preparing to release three million bags of fertiliser within the next month, following an intervention announced by Vice President Kashim Shettima.

He explained that the initiative would help reduce production costs and encourage farmers to expand cultivation.

Kyari also highlighted the National Agricultural Development Fund and the recapitalisation of the Bank of Agriculture as measures intended to improve farmers’ access to financing.

He said the Guaranteed Minimum Price programme provided farmers with a market for their produce, encouraging agricultural production while supporting price stability.

The minister attributed the expansion of cultivated farmland partly to improved security, explaining that military operations had enabled farmers to return to previously inaccessible agricultural areas.

On mechanisation, Kyari disclosed that the government had deployed 2,000 tractors, while deliveries under the second phase of the programme were expected within two to three months.

He also announced growing investment interest in agricultural processing, including cocoa, sesame, cassava and cashew nuts.

According to him, the government had signed a $33m investment agreement with a Turkish company for greenhouse projects under Nigeria’s Special Agro-Industrial Processing Zones.

Meanwhile, the Executive Director of the National Agricultural Extension and Research Liaison Services, Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria, Yusuf Sani, disclosed that production of 13 out of the 17 major crops assessed was projected to increase in 2026.

“Nineteen multidisciplinary teams conducted field assessments across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory between August 31 and September 6, 2026, in collaboration with state ministries of agriculture, agricultural research institutes, Agricultural Development Programmes and development partners,” Sani said.

He identified Niger as the leading rice-producing state, Kano as the largest producer of sorghum and Yobe as the leading millet-producing state.

Sani called for stronger storage facilities, improved post-harvest handling and better market access to prevent agricultural losses.

Kyari clarified that the assessment covered only wet-season production, adding that a separate dry-season survey had been commissioned to determine Nigeria’s overall agricultural output for 2026.

The announcement comes amid easing monthly food prices, although annual food inflation remains elevated.

According to the National Bureau of Statistics’ October 2026 Consumer Price Index report, released on Monday, food inflation stood at 19.13 per cent, compared with 19.59 per cent in September and 16.30 per cent in October 2025.

This means annual food inflation declined by 0.46 percentage points month-on-month but remained 2.83 percentage points above its level a year earlier.

On a month-on-month basis, average food prices fell by 0.75 per cent in October, following a larger 1.55 per cent decline in September. The figures indicate that food prices continued to fall, although the pace of the decline moderated.

The post FG plans release of stored grains to stabilise food prices appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: 2027: APM governorship candidate mourns Vanguard Online Editor, Femi Ajasa
description:
The Lagos State governorship candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), Laja Adeoye, has expressed sadness over the death of Mr Olufemi Finayon Ajasa, popularly known as Femi Ajasa, Online Editor of Vanguard Media Limited.







Ajasa died on Sunday at the Lagos University Teaching Hospital (L
content:
The Lagos State governorship candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), Laja Adeoye, has expressed sadness over the death of Mr Olufemi Finayon Ajasa, popularly known as Femi Ajasa, Online Editor of Vanguard Media Limited.

Ajasa died on Sunday at the Lagos University Teaching Hospital (LUTH) after a brief illness. He was aged 44.

Adeoye, who disclosed this in a condolence statement on Wednesday, described the late journalist as a professional who demonstrated passion, integrity and commitment to truth in the discharge of his duties.

He said Ajasa approached journalism with dedication and professionalism, adding that his contributions to Vanguard and the wider media industry would not be forgotten.

The APM governorship candidate, who described himself as an advocate of press freedom, said a free and responsible press remained indispensable to democracy.

He noted that journalists like Ajasa embodied the values that made press freedom meaningful, pledging his continued support for media practitioners and the protection of press freedom.

Adeoye said the deceased would be greatly missed by his colleagues at Vanguard, members of the Nigerian media community and all those who knew and worked with him.

He extended his condolences to Ajasa’s family, friends and the management and staff of Vanguard Media Limited, praying God to grant them the strength to bear the loss and for the repose of the deceased’s soul.

title: Chimamanda’s son: Coroner fixes January 19 for inquest hearing
description:
The Lagos State Coroner’s Court sitting at the Igbosere Magistrate Court has fixed January 19, 2027, for the commencement of the inquest into the death of Nkanu, son of Nigerian author Chimamanda Adichie.
Magistrate Atinuke Adetunji fixed the date on Wednesday after lawyers representing the parties
content:
The Lagos State Coroner’s Court sitting at the Igbosere Magistrate Court has fixed January 19, 2027, for the commencement of the inquest into the death of Nkanu, son of Nigerian author Chimamanda Adichie.

Magistrate Atinuke Adetunji fixed the date on Wednesday after lawyers representing the parties in the case agreed on the modalities for the proceedings, including the order in which witnesses would testify.

She directed counsel to file and exchange their clients’ statements on oath and ensure that their witnesses were available when the inquest resumes.

Nkanu died on January 7, 2026, during medical treatment at Euracare Multi-Specialist Hospital, Lagos.

His parents, Adichie and her husband, Dr Ivara Esege, had accused the hospital of “prima facie breaches of the duty of care” in the treatment of their son.

Euracare, however, denied allegations of medical negligence, describing the claims as inaccurate and unfounded.

The inquest was suspended indefinitely on June 3, 2026, following a restraining order issued by Justice Aishat Opesanwo of the Lagos State High Court, Ikoyi, on an ex parte application by Eurapharma Care Services Nigeria Limited.

The company had approached the court to halt the proceedings pending a judicial review of the legality of the inquest.

However, on October 12, 2026, Justice Opesanwo dismissed the application, holding that the cremation of the deceased’s body did not, in itself, deprive the coroner of the statutory jurisdiction to investigate the circumstances surrounding his death.

The judge also rejected the hospital’s argument that the coroner’s decision on the sequence for receiving statements and evidence from medical personnel and other relevant parties breached its right to a fair hearing.

Justice Opesanwo held that the hospital’s objections were based on a misunderstanding of the statutory framework and the nature of a coroner’s inquiry.

At Wednesday’s proceedings, counsel for the hospital, Taiwo Osipitan (SAN), informed the coroner that the matter before the High Court had been resolved and urged her to fix a date for the commencement of the inquest.

Counsel for the deceased’s family, Chukwudi Enebeli (SAN), and counsel for Atlantis, Abiodun Layonu (SAN), did not oppose the request but sought time to respond to the statement on oath filed by Euracare’s Medical Director, Tosin Majekodunmi, which they said they had received.

The lawyers also agreed that counsel for the deceased’s family would present their witnesses first, followed by Atlantis, while Eurapharma Care Services Nigeria Limited would call its witnesses last.

The post Chimamanda’s son: Coroner fixes January 19 for inquest hearing appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: 2027: FG urges political parties, others to tackle corruption
description:
The Federal Government has called on political parties, government institutions, the media and civil society organisations to strengthen democratic institutions, promote accountability and intensify the fight against corruption ahead of the 2027 general elections.
The Minister of State for Foreign A
content:
The Federal Government has called on political parties, government institutions, the media and civil society organisations to strengthen democratic institutions, promote accountability and intensify the fight against corruption ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, Ambassador Sola Enikanolaiye, stated this on Wednesday in Abuja through his representative, Mahmud Aliyu, at an international stakeholders’ engagement forum organised by the Diplomatic Correspondents’ Association of Nigeria.

Enikanolaiye stressed that anti-corruption and effective party-building were fundamental to democratic governance, warning that the country’s democratic development required more than periodic elections to guarantee transparency, public trust and responsive leadership.

The forum, which focused on anti-corruption, party-building and democratic governance, brought together political party leaders, diplomats, civil society organisations, government officials and other stakeholders to examine governance challenges and lessons from China’s experience.

Enikanolaiye said anti-corruption and party-building were critical pillars of democratic governance because of their roles in strengthening institutions, ensuring inclusive political participation, upholding the rule of law and promoting transparency.

He said, “Anti-corruption and party-building are fundamental pillars of democratic governance, essential for strengthening democratic institutions, ensuring inclusive political participation, upholding the rule of law, promoting transparency and accountability, and fostering public trust in governance.”

The minister noted that democratic governance went beyond conducting elections, stressing that it also involved protecting fundamental freedoms, maintaining institutional checks and balances and ensuring that public officeholders served the interests of citizens.

He said the principles were consistent with Nigeria’s 4-Ds foreign policy priorities of Demography, Development, Diaspora and Democracy.

According to him, democracy provides the institutional foundation for stability, accountability and good governance, while development translates diplomatic engagements into tangible economic and social benefits.

He explained that Nigeria’s demography positioned its population as a source of economic strength and international influence, while the diaspora connected the country to global opportunities, expertise, investment and innovation.

Enikanolaiye said achieving these objectives required the collective involvement of political parties, the media, civil society groups and government institutions.

Also speaking, the Executive Director of the Civil Society Legislative Advocacy Centre and Transparency International Nigeria, Auwal Rafsanjani, warned that Nigeria’s democratic challenges were rooted not merely in the absence of laws and institutions but in the failure to enforce rules and hold powerful individuals accountable.

He said political interests frequently took precedence over national interests, while political loyalty sometimes overshadowed competence and institutions established to protect public interest remained vulnerable to partisan interference.

Rafsanjani, whose presentation examined party organisation, discipline and anti-corruption reforms ahead of the 2027 elections, called for transparent political financing, credible party primaries and stronger anti-corruption institutions.

He said the increasing influence of money in political competition threatened democratic choice, particularly through financial inducements, expensive political gifts, opaque campaign contributions and the misuse of public resources.

“Those who spend excessively to acquire political power may subsequently face incentives to recover those investments through public contracts, political patronage and misuse of public resources,” he said.

He urged the Independent National Electoral Commission to strengthen its capacity to monitor campaign financing, investigate suspicious donations and enforce disclosure requirements by political parties.

The organisation also called on anti-corruption agencies to investigate allegations of illicit political financing and abuse of public office without discrimination or political interference.

“The credibility of the 2027 elections will depend not only on how votes are cast and counted, but also on how candidates emerge, how campaigns are financed and whether electoral offences attract consequences,” he said.

Rafsanjani further advocated stronger operational independence for the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission, Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission, Code of Conduct Bureau, INEC and other accountability institutions.

He maintained that anti-corruption agencies must not be perceived as strong against political opponents and weak against politically connected individuals.

On political party development, the National Chairman of the Inter-Party Advisory Council, Dr Yusuf Mohammad Dantalle, said weak political parties could not produce strong governments.

He called for internal democracy, respect for party constitutions, financial transparency, ideological clarity and capacity-building for party leaders and members.

“Without disciplined, ideologically-driven and internally democratic political parties, democratic governance will remain fragile,” Dantalle said.

He added that the fight against corruption must be collective, non-selective and institutional, urging political parties to embrace transparency in party funding and campaign financing.

Similarly, the Campaign Spokesperson of the National Democratic Congress, Dr Chiogo Constance Ikokwu, expressed concern over the state of internal democracy in political parties and the growing public distrust of the electoral process.

Ikokwu, a former journalist, said her experience in politics had exposed her to shortcomings that were not always apparent from the newsroom.

She said, “It is one thing to criticise the shortcomings of a political system from the newsroom. It is quite another to experience those shortcomings from inside the system.”

She argued that democracy should not be reduced to winning elections, insisting that political parties must respect their constitutions, internal rules and the democratic rights of members.

The National Orientation Agency, in its goodwill message, also called for collective responsibility in the fight against corruption, urging government officials to remain accountable and citizens to reject bribery, dishonesty and misuse of public resources.

The agency said political parties must promote fairness, discipline and democratic principles rather than concentrate solely on winning elections.

The forum also examined China’s experience in party organisation and anti-corruption under President Xi Jinping, with the Centre for China Studies presenting perspectives on how institutional discipline and governance principles could inform Nigeria’s development.

Participants called for stronger institutions, transparent political processes and sustained collaboration among government, political parties, civil society and international partners ahead of the 2027 elections.

The post 2027: FG urges political parties, others to tackle corruption appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Sweden Names 2 Jobs That Can No Longer Get A Work Permit - And A New Salary Rule Every Applicant Must Beat - Check Below For Full Details
description: Sweden's Migration Agency says forest berry pickers and personal assistants can no longer qualify for a work permit at all, while every other applicant must now earn at least 90% of the Swedish median salary.
content:
Sweden has confirmed that two occupations can no longer qualify for a work permit at all, no matter how good the job offer or the salary attached to it. The Swedish Migration Agency (Migrationsverket) says forest berry pickers and personal assistants have been removed from the list of jobs that can support a work permit.

The two excluded jobs

  • Forest berry pickers - occupational subgroup 9210 under Sweden's SSYK 2012 classification. The exclusion took effect on 1 June 2026.
  • Personal assistants - subgroup 5343, also excluded since 1 June 2026.

There is a narrow exception on berries: other forms of berry picking inside the same occupational subgroup may still be considered, and a berry picker hired by an employer established in Sweden can still apply for a seasonal work permit instead.

The bigger change most applicants miss

The two exclusions came in with a far wider reform: a new salary floor of 90 per cent of the Swedish median wage. For applications received since 16 June 2026 that works out at SEK 34,470 a month, based on a median of SEK 38,300.

Twenty-seven occupation groups are exempt from the full 90 per cent rule and instead sit at 75 per cent - SEK 28,725 a month. They include:

  • IT operations technicians, IT support and network technicians, systems administrators
  • Assistant nurses, care assistants, childcare and ambulance care assistants
  • Laboratory engineers, and chemistry/chemical engineering technicians
  • Welders, maintenance mechanics, electrical distribution technicians
  • Butchers, food-industry machine operators, forestry workers and farm animal caretakers

Extensions are next: from 2 December 2026, applications to extend an existing permit must also meet the 90 per cent rule.

What the rules require in practice

  • A signed employment contract, with pay and conditions at least equal to Swedish collective agreements or normal practice in the profession
  • Health, life, industrial-injury and occupational pension insurance taken out by the employer before you start
  • The job advertised in Sweden and across the EU/EEA and Switzerland for at least 10 days before hiring
  • A first permit applied for from outside Sweden (with limited exceptions), granted for up to two years
  • An application fee of SEK 2,200, paid by the applicant

What it means for Nigerians

Neither excluded job was a realistic route for most Nigerian applicants - berry picking is largely seasonal work drawing on Asian and Eastern European labour, and personal assistant roles are low-paid care work. The part that actually matters is the salary floor: a Swedish employer must now pay roughly SEK 34,470 a month (about 75 per cent of that for the exempt trades) before your application can succeed.

That pushes Nigerian applicants towards the exempt occupations - IT support, nursing and care work, welding, maintenance and laboratory roles - or towards well-paid specialist jobs that clear the full threshold. The strongest applications also come with recognised qualifications, verified experience and, increasingly, Swedish or strong English language ability.

Warning: Swedish work permits are applied for by the employer through the Migration Agency's e-service, and the agency charges a published fee only. Any agent promising a Swedish work permit for a "processing fee" - or offering a berry-picking contract as a fast route - should be treated as a red flag.

Bottom line: Sweden still wants foreign labour, but only where the job pays properly. Two occupations are now closed completely, and everyone else has to clear a salary line set by the national median wage. Check the exact figure on migrationsverket.se on the day you apply, because it is reset every June.

title: Varsity student stabbed to death in Osun
description:
Some assailants have reportedly stabbed to death a student of Westland University, Iwo, Osun State, identified as Monica Mary.
This has sparked panic among students and residents of the town.
Sources in the Agbowo area of Iwo who where Mary lived, told PUNCH Online during telephone interviews on Wed
content:
Some assailants have reportedly stabbed to death a student of Westland University, Iwo, Osun State, identified as Monica Mary.

This has sparked panic among students and residents of the town.

Sources in the Agbowo area of Iwo who where Mary lived, told PUNCH Online during telephone interviews on Wednesday that the incident occurred around 11:30pm on Tuesday.

It was gathered that Mary, a 300-level student, had previously lived on the university campus before moving into private accommodation in Agbowo, where she was killed.

A resident of the area, who spoke with our correspondent, said, “She was murdered around her hostel by 11:32pm at Agbowo, Iwo.

“Someone said she heard her noise when the incident happened but no one could come out. She had gone out to charge her mobile phone. She was a calm girl and does not get into trouble.

“It was pathetic such a thing happened to her. Her parents had been informed. The matter was reported to the police in Iwo Division but the entire student community in the town is in panic mood over the incident.”

When contacted, the spokesperson for the Osun State Police Command, Abiodun Ojelabi, confirmed the incident.

Ojelabi said police operatives had visited the scene and assured that those responsible would be apprehended.

He said, “We received the report of the murder of Monica Mary, a student of Westland University, Iwo, this morning. On arrival, we observed the area and the corpse, and a cut was discovered on her neck. It was suspected to be a knife cut.

“We got information that she went to charge her phone and was returning when the incident happened. She had been living on campus since she got admission into the university. She just moved out of campus this semester.

“We recovered a knife, a phone pouch and other items. The Commissioner of Police has directed that the case should be transferred to the Criminal Investigation Department. Investigation is ongoing and the parents are ready to support the police.”

The incident is not the first reported case of a university student being stabbed to death in Iwo.

In January 2025, a 200-level student of Bowen University, Iwo, identified as Paul Thinker, was reportedly stabbed to death by unknown assailants.

The Osun State Police Command had said detectives were deployed to the scene and an investigation commenced to identify those responsible.

The post Varsity student stabbed to death in Osun appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: NUPRC boss seeks 25% women representation in oil, gas leadership
description:
From Adanna Nnamani, Abuja
The Commission Chief Executive of the Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission (NUPRC), Mrs Oritsemeyiwa Eyesan, has advocated at least 25 per cent representation of women in leadership and decision-making positions in Nigeria’s oil and gas industry.
Eyesan said g
content:
From Adanna Nnamani, Abuja

The Commission Chief Executive of the Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission (NUPRC), Mrs Oritsemeyiwa Eyesan, has advocated at least 25 per cent representation of women in leadership and decision-making positions in Nigeria’s oil and gas industry.

Eyesan said greater inclusion of women was necessary not merely to achieve numerical balance but to ensure that their contributions and expertise were recognised in the sector.

She made the call on Wednesday while speaking on the topic “Breaking Barriers” at the 2026 Women in NNPC Limited (WIN) event held at the NNPC Towers, Abuja, under the theme “Powered by Her.”

According to a statement issued on Wednesday by NUPRC Spokesperson Eniola Akinkuotu, Eyesan also urged women to prioritise competence, resilience and continuous learning as critical tools for overcoming barriers in their careers.

The statement quoted the NUPRC boss as saying that women should not be discouraged by delayed promotions, noting that professional growth required patience, perseverance and commitment to excellence.

Sharing her career experience, Eyesan disclosed that she spent eight years in the same position without promotion but remained committed to her professional development.

She also stressed the importance of involving men in conversations about gender inclusion, noting that some of the major milestones in her career were made possible by men who recognised her competence and provided opportunities.

“I was appointed the first female Head of Strategy, not by a woman, but by a man who believed in my competence. I was also appointed as the first female EVP Upstream, NNPCL, by a man who believed in my competence, and today I stand as the first female CCE of NUPRC by Mr President, who is a man who believes that I will deliver,” she said.

On women’s representation in the industry, Eyesan acknowledged that opportunities were gradually increasing but insisted that more deliberate efforts were needed to achieve meaningful inclusion.

“Is it happening at the scale we want? Not quite, we need more. At least one in four. Not just because we want to make up the numbers but because we think we bring value to the table,” she said.

She commended the Group Chief Executive Officer of NNPC Limited, Bayo Ojulari, for establishing the WIN initiative, describing it as a valuable platform for preparing young women for greater opportunities and leadership roles in the oil and gas industry.

Eyesan also noted that the Nigerian oil and gas industry was recording significant progress through collaboration among the regulator, NNPC Limited and other industry operators.

The post NUPRC boss seeks 25% women representation in oil, gas leadership appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Tinubu approves world’s first PR university, says Nigeria bigger than 419
description:
By John Alechenu



ABUJA — President Bola Tinubu has approved the establishment of what he described as the world’s first University of Public Relations and Leadership, as part of efforts to develop a new generation of communication professionals through specialised education, research and professi
content:
By John Alechenu

ABUJA — President Bola Tinubu has approved the establishment of what he described as the world’s first University of Public Relations and Leadership, as part of efforts to develop a new generation of communication professionals through specialised education, research and professional training.

Tinubu announced the approval in a speech delivered by Vice President Kashim Shettima at the 13th World Public Relations Forum 2026 in Abuja.

The President said a major outcome of Nigeria’s hosting of the global forum was the determination to establish a lasting institutional legacy for the public relations profession.

He said: “In this regard, I am pleased to formally approve and support the establishment of the University of Public Relations and Leadership, a first-of-its-kind initiative designed to advance specialised education, research, professional development and leadership training in public relations, strategic communications and related disciplines.”

He described the proposed institution as a major investment in human capital and the future of communication, adding that it would provide opportunities to develop communication leaders capable of responding to the demands of a rapidly changing global environment.

Tinubu commended the Nigerian Institute of Public Relations, the Federal Ministry of Information and National Orientation, and the Nasarawa State Government for their collaboration and commitment to the initiative.

He urged stakeholders to work together to ensure that the institution developed into a centre of excellence.

The President also expressed Nigeria’s appreciation to the Global Alliance for Public Relations and Communication Management and the international public relations community for entrusting the country with the hosting of the global gathering.

He described the decision as recognition of Nigeria’s growing contribution to the global communication profession and its capacity to promote responsible communication.

Tinubu said hosting the forum provided an opportunity to showcase Nigeria’s people, cultural diversity, economic potential and commitment to constructive international engagement.

Addressing the changing communication landscape, the President said digital technologies and artificial intelligence were transforming how information was created, distributed and consumed.

He, however, warned that the developments had also created challenges, including misinformation, disinformation, hate speech and declining public trust.

“In this environment, public relations and communication professionals have responsibilities that go beyond managing images and reputations,” he said.

According to him, communication professionals must promote truth, accountability, transparency, mutual understanding and constructive engagement between governments, institutions and citizens.

Tinubu also urged international delegates to look beyond the conference and explore Nigeria’s economic and investment opportunities.

Highlighting the country’s technology ecosystem, he said six of Africa’s 10 unicorn companies were Nigerian, listing Flutterwave, OPay, Interswitch, Moove and Moniepoint among the companies.

The President also praised the resilience, confidence and hard work of Nigerians, describing himself as a “swashbuckling capitalist”.

He said Nigerians were generally confident and hardworking, adding that the country’s population and global influence would continue to grow.

According to him, one out of every four black men is Nigerian, a proportion he projected would rise to one in three by 2050.

He further projected that Nigeria would surpass the United States to become the world’s third most populous country, with an estimated population of 440 million by 2050.

Defending Nigeria’s international image, Tinubu said the country should not be defined by negative social media stereotypes and internet fraud, commonly referred to as 419.

He cited the educational achievements of Nigerians in the United States, claiming that 60 per cent of Nigerian Americans held college degrees.

“So Nigeria goes beyond 419. Nigeria is much more bigger than that,” he said.

The post Tinubu approves world’s first PR university, says Nigeria bigger than 419 appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Bauchi 2027: NDC candidate promises bill to tackle out-of-school children in Bauchi Federal Constituency
description:
From Paul Orude, Bauchi
The National Democratic Party (NDC) candidate for the House of Representatives, Bauchi Federal Constituency, Hon Sodangi Adam Chindo, has lamented the high number of out-of-school children in the area, saying it is unacceptable.
Chindo, who was a guest at the Bauchi State 202
content:
From Paul Orude, Bauchi

The National Democratic Party (NDC) candidate for the House of Representatives, Bauchi Federal Constituency, Hon Sodangi Adam Chindo, has lamented the high number of out-of-school children in the area, saying it is unacceptable.

Chindo, who was a guest at the Bauchi State 2027 Interview Series on Tuesday, described the high number of out-of-school children in the constituency as a major concern he would address if elected into the House of Representatives.

He noted that many schools outside Bauchi metropolis were operating without adequate teachers and essential learning facilities.

He proposed collaborating with community structures to identify unemployed graduates who could be engaged as temporary teachers to support schools in their communities, with the beneficiaries receiving stipends for their services.

He said he would sponsor bills that would prioritise reducing the number of out-of-school children while improving the quality of education available to those already enrolled.

Chindo unveiled a five-point development agenda focusing on healthcare, education, agricultural transformation, effective representation and sustainable empowerment of women and youths.

He assured that his proposed legislative agenda was designed to address critical development challenges confronting his constituency.

He lamented the poor state of education, pressure on healthcare facilities, agricultural constraints and unemployment in Bauchi Federal Constituency.

On healthcare, he proposed strengthening secondary healthcare facilities to reduce the increasing pressure on teaching hospitals, which he observed were overwhelmed by patients seeking medical attention.

According to him, improving the capacity of secondary healthcare institutions would enable teaching hospitals to concentrate on specialised treatment and referral services.

On agricultural transformation, the aspirant promised to work with relevant ministries and stakeholders to facilitate soft loans, timely fertiliser support and improved agricultural extension services for farmers.

He expressed concern that agricultural extension services were not reaching farmers adequately, attributing the situation partly to possible funding and implementation challenges.

He pledged to use legislative oversight to ensure that budgetary provisions for agricultural extension services were implemented and that farmers received the necessary support ahead of the rainy season.

On effective representation, the aspirant said his experience in civil society advocacy had equipped him with the knowledge and capacity to contribute meaningfully to national legislation and attract development opportunities to his constituency.

He cited his previous leadership of the Civil Society Legislative Advocacy Centre (CISLAC) and his involvement in legislative advocacy, including proposals seeking an extension of paid maternity leave from three to six months and legislation on mandatory vitamin A fortification of cooking oil.

The aspirant also outlined an ambitious youth empowerment programme under which he plans to train 1,250 young graduates annually in technology-related skills, including artificial intelligence, digital marketing, data analytics and cybersecurity.

He said the programme would provide six months of training to equip beneficiaries with practical skills that could enable them to become self-employed rather than depend entirely on government employment.

For youths without formal education or university qualifications, he promised vocational training in areas such as carpentry, mechanics and welding.

On women’s empowerment, he proposed supporting two women’s groups in each ward, targeting 40 groups, through sustainable economic empowerment initiatives.

He cited the experience of women’s groups previously supported under the Breakthrough ACTION project in Bauchi, which, according to him, had continued their economic activities and community interventions several years after the project’s closure.

He said the women had reportedly mobilised more than ₦100 million among themselves over five years, demonstrating the potential of collective economic empowerment.

The aspirant maintained that his proposed empowerment model would focus on building sustainable economic capacity among women rather than distributing temporary financial assistance that leaves beneficiaries dependent on politicians.

He said the five-point agenda had been documented into a roadmap that would guide its implementation if he secured the mandate of the electorate in 2027.

The post Bauchi 2027: NDC candidate promises bill to tackle out-of-school children in Bauchi Federal Constituency appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Chimamanda’s son’s death: Coroner resumes inquest
description:
The coroner’s inquest into the death of Nkanu Adichie-Esege, son of Nigerian author Chimamanda Adichie and her husband, Ivara Esege, resumed on Wednesday at the Igbosere Magistrate’s Court in Lagos following a Lagos High Court ruling affirming the coroner’s jurisdiction.







The coroner, Magistra
content:
The coroner’s inquest into the death of Nkanu Adichie-Esege, son of Nigerian author Chimamanda Adichie and her husband, Ivara Esege, resumed on Wednesday at the Igbosere Magistrate’s Court in Lagos following a Lagos High Court ruling affirming the coroner’s jurisdiction.

The coroner, Magistrate Atinuke Adetunji, resumed proceedings after the High Court dismissed an application by Euracare Hospital seeking to stop the inquest.

At Wednesday’s sitting, Taiwo Osipitan, counsel to Euracare Hospital, said it was the first time all parties were appearing before the coroner following the conclusion of proceedings at the High Court.

Osipitan said the High Court had ruled that the matter had not reached the stage at which judicial review was necessary and directed that the case be returned to the coroner’s court for continuation of the inquest.

He subsequently tendered a copy of the High Court judgment before Adetunji.

However, Chukwudi Enebeli, counsel to the deceased’s family, told the court that Euracare’s application was struck out because the coroner’s court had jurisdiction to proceed with the inquest.

Enebeli sought an adjournment, explaining that Euracare had only served the parties in open court with the witness statement on oath of Tosin Majekodunmi, a medical doctor.

He said the family needed time to examine the statement and determine whether a response would be necessary.

Abiodun Loyonu, counsel to Atlantis Paediatric Hospital, also asked the court for an opportunity to respond to Euracare’s witness statement.

In her response, the magistrate reminded the parties that the inquest was inquisitorial in nature, adding that guidelines for conducting the proceedings had been discussed at a preliminary meeting held at the commencement of the inquiry.

She urged all parties to bear the distinctive nature of the proceedings in mind as the inquest progressed.

The coroner also asked whether the parties had filed witness statements on oath in preparation for the hearing.

Osipitan, however, sought clarification on whether Lagos State Government officials would be required to file witness statements on oath or could appear in court to give oral evidence if subpoenaed.

Adetunji said filing witness statements on oath was not mandatory for such witnesses, adding that government officials summoned through subpoenas could appear before the court and give oral evidence.

The parties subsequently agreed that the deceased’s family would lead evidence, followed by Atlantis Paediatric Hospital and Euracare Hospital.

The coroner adjourned the inquest to January 19, 20 and 28, 2027.

Nkanu, one of Adichie’s twins, died on January 7, 2026, following complications during a series of preparatory medical procedures at Euracare Hospital after being referred from Atlantis Paediatric Hospital.

The coroner commenced the inquest in February to establish the circumstances surrounding the 21-month-old child’s death.

Proceedings earlier revealed that the child’s body had been cremated, raising questions about the availability of primary forensic evidence.

Euracare subsequently approached the Lagos High Court, seeking a judicial review of the coroner’s jurisdiction, particularly in view of the cremation.

In June, the High Court ordered a temporary suspension of the inquest pending a judicial review of how the proceedings were initiated and conducted.

The coroner subsequently adjourned the matter to October.

However, in October, the High Court, presided over by Justice Aishat Opesanwo, rejected Euracare’s application to stop the inquest.

The judge held that the coroner was legally constituted and that the cremation of the child’s body did not invalidate the decision to proceed with the inquiry.

content:
‎–Calls for vigilance against child sexual abuse
‎
‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru
‎
‎ABUJA — THE Nigeria’s First Lady, Senator Oluremi Tinubu, has called on parents, educators, the media, and law enforcement agencies to remain vigilant and committed to protecting children from sexual exploitation, abuse, and violence.
‎
In a message marking the World Day for the Prevention of and Healing from Child Sexual Exploitation, Abuse and Violence, Senator Tinubu urged Nigerians to reaffirm their collective duty to safeguard every child’s well-being.
‎
‎“I call upon parents, educators, the media, and law enforcement agencies to remain vigilant and committed. We must protect our children at all times,” she said.
‎
‎The First Lady stressed that no child should live in fear and that survivors must be treated with dignity.
‎
‎“Every child deserves a childhood free from fear, and every survivor deserves our respect, compassion and support,” she stated.
‎
‎Senator Oluremi Tinubu offered a prayer for the protection of children across the country: “May God protect all our children.”
‎
‎The observance, marked annually on November 18, was established by the United Nations General Assembly in 2022 to promote prevention, protection, and healing for children affected by sexual exploitation, abuse, and violence.

description:
By Luminous Jannamike







ABUJA – The African Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council, ADC-PCC, has accused the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, of giving political parties inadequate notice for its November 28 mock accreditation and results collation exercise, demanding
content:
By Luminous Jannamike

ABUJA – The African Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council, ADC-PCC, has accused the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, of giving political parties inadequate notice for its November 28 mock accreditation and results collation exercise, demanding its postponement.

The Council said the short notice would make it difficult for parties to mobilise, train and deploy agents for the nationwide exercise, warning that the process could undermine confidence in a test designed to assess electoral technology ahead of the 2027 general elections.

In a statement by its Director of Media and Publicity, Kola Ologbondiyan, the ADC-PCC also faulted INEC’s reported decision not to upload results from Ward, Local Government and State collation levels to its Result Viewing Portal, IReV, during the 2027 elections.

The Council said INEC’s November 16 notification, coming barely two days before the November 18 deadline for submitting agents’ names, was unfair, particularly as the exercise would cover all 774 Local Government Areas and two polling units in each of the country’s 8,838 Registration Areas.

“How does INEC expect political parties to adequately prepare, mobilise, train and submit their agents for an exercise of this magnitude within such a short time? This is not preparation; it is an ambush,” the Council queried.

“INEC cannot test electoral credibility through an incredible process.”

It demanded an immediate postponement to give political parties sufficient time to nominate agents and participate meaningfully.

On electronic transmission of results, the ADC-PCC rejected comments reportedly made by INEC’s Director of Information and Communication Technology, Lawrence Bayode, that the Commission had neither developed nor tested the system for uploading results from the various collation levels.

“Nigerians fought for and demanded real-time electronic transmission of election results precisely to eliminate the manipulation that often occurs between the Polling Unit and subsequent collation levels.

“Any attempt to weaken, delay or abandon electronic transmission and public visibility of results at the various levels of collation is an invitation to electoral manipulation,” the Council warned.

It recalled that former INEC Chairman, Professor Mahmood Yakubu, had promised to extend result uploads to Ward, Local Government and State levels, adding that his successor, Professor Joash Amupitan, SAN, had also pledged to strengthen electoral transparency.

Questioning the Commission’s apparent change of position, the ADC-PCC asked: “What has changed? Why the sudden retreat from commitments previously made to Nigerians?”

It further questioned why Forms EC8B (Ward), EC8C (Local Government) and EC8D (State) could not be uploaded to IReV when the Commission already had the technology to upload polling-unit results on Form EC8A.

Warning against actions that could confer undue advantage on the ruling All Progressives Congress, APC, the Council reminded INEC of its obligation to remain impartial.

“INEC is not an extension of the ruling party. It is an independent electoral umpire, and it must act like one,” it declared.

It warned Amupitan that his handling of the 2027 elections would shape his legacy and have consequences for the country’s peace.

“His name, his legacy and the peace of this country are at stake. History will judge him not by assurances, but by the credibility of the elections he conducts,” the Council said.

The ADC-PCC reaffirmed its commitment to defending electoral transparency and the sanctity of the ballot, declaring: “We will not be intimidated. We will not be silenced. We will continue to insist that every Nigerian’s vote must count.”

title: Lagos targets $1tr GDP by 2052, Sanwo-Olu declares
description:
By Olasunkanmi Akoni



Lagos State Governor, Babajide Sanwo-Olu, has unveiled an ambitious target of growing the state’s economy to a $1 trillion Gross Domestic Product (GDP) by 2052, declaring that his administration is laying the foundation for Lagos to become one of the world’s leading sub-natio
content:
By Olasunkanmi Akoni

Lagos State Governor, Babajide Sanwo-Olu, has unveiled an ambitious target of growing the state’s economy to a $1 trillion Gross Domestic Product (GDP) by 2052, declaring that his administration is laying the foundation for Lagos to become one of the world’s leading sub-national economies.

Sanwo-Olu, who disclosed this at the fourth Lagos State Employment Trust Fund (LSETF) Summit in Lagos on Wednesday, said the state’s budget had increased from less than ₦700 billion when he assumed office in 2019 to ₦4.2 trillion.

He said the increased financial capacity was being deployed to promote shared prosperity, economic empowerment, infrastructure development and job creation.

The summit, themed, “Lagos Works: Building Africa’s Most Productive City,” provided an opportunity for the governor to outline his administration’s economic development strategy and highlight the importance of institutional continuity in achieving sustainable growth.

Sanwo-Olu described a productive city as one where workers generate higher economic value, businesses expand their customer base and households enjoy improved disposable incomes.

According to him, achieving these objectives requires sustained investment in economic infrastructure, institutional capacity, private sector partnerships and employment-generating initiatives.

He said: “Guided by our T.H.E.M.E.S. Plus agenda, we have systematically scaled our financial capacity to accelerate this prosperity. From an operating budget below ₦700 billion when we assumed office, we are currently running a ₦4.2 trillion budget dedicated entirely to shared prosperity, strategic empowerment and aggressively reducing unemployment through enablers like the LSETF.”

The governor described the $1 trillion GDP target as ambitious but achievable, saying the state had commenced the foundational work required to attain the milestone.

“As the second-largest economy in Africa, Lagos is charting an ambitious yet achievable course towards a $1 trillion GDP by 2052. Achieving this milestone will position Lagos among the leading economic sub-nationals globally, and the foundational work required to reach that destination has already begun,” he said.

Sanwo-Olu also highlighted the importance of institutional continuity, citing the LSETF as an example of how successive administrations could strengthen existing programmes rather than abandon them.

He noted that the fund, established a decade ago before his administration, had been strengthened and expanded to improve access to finance for small businesses and stimulate employment.

According to him, the intervention has recorded a loan repayment rate of 95 per cent, disbursed funds to more than 20,000 small businesses and created over 320,000 jobs, while safeguarding another 173,000 jobs.

The Commissioner for Wealth Creation and Employment, Akinyemi Ajigbotafe, said the state had impacted more than 6,500 graduates and generated over 200,000 jobs through strategic wealth creation and employment initiatives since 2023.

He said the Sanwo-Olu administration remained committed to making employment opportunities accessible, sustainable and inclusive, particularly through programmes designed to equip young people with practical workplace experience.

Ajigbotafe identified the Graduate Internship Placement Programme (GIPP) as one of the flagship interventions aimed at bridging the gap between academic qualifications and labour market requirements.

He also described the Lagos State Job Fair as a major employment facilitation platform, noting that the 2025 and subsequent editions brought together more than 300 organisations and thousands of job seekers.

title: UNICEF holds media dialogue on humanitarian action for children in Benue
description:
From Scholastica Hir, Makurdi
The United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF), with support from the Government of Sweden through the Swedish International Development Cooperation Agency (Sida) and in collaboration with the Benue State Government, has commenced a two-day media dialogue on humanitarian a
content:
From Scholastica Hir, Makurdi

The United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF), with support from the Government of Sweden through the Swedish International Development Cooperation Agency (Sida) and in collaboration with the Benue State Government, has commenced a two-day media dialogue on humanitarian action for children in Makurdi, the Benue State capital.

The media dialogue is on “Amplifying Humanitarian Action: Strengthening Media Emergency and Advocacy for Integrated Humanitarian Funding in Benue State”, with the theme “Amplifying Humanitarian Action: Media, Evidence and Advocacy for Children.”

Speaking at the event on Tuesday, the Chief of the UNICEF Field Office, Enugu, Juliet Chiluwe, charged media practitioners to move beyond reporting challenges to amplifying solutions, strengthening accountability and inspiring collective action towards the humanitarian situation in Benue State.

Chiluwe, who was represented by UNICEF Social Policy Officer Dr Victor Chima, said the media dialogue was convened at a critical time when the humanitarian situation in Benue State called for sustained attention, stronger partnerships and collective action to protect and improve the lives of affected children and vulnerable communities.

She noted that the engagement is an important strategic communication and visibility component of that support, providing an opportunity to strengthen media understanding of Sida-supported interventions, amplify evidence of results and tell compelling stories of how the integrated, multisectoral response is making a difference.

She maintained that the media remains an indispensable partner in humanitarian action, pointing out that, beyond reporting events, their platforms have the power to shape public understanding, elevate the voices of affected communities, influence policy conversations and mobilise the commitment and resources required to address humanitarian needs.

While appreciating the Government of Sweden, through Sida, for its continued support for the humanitarian response, the UNICEF Chief of Office said the organisation is always willing to strengthen collaboration with government, development partners and other stakeholders to ensure that the needs, rights and voices of children remain central to humanitarian priorities and response efforts.

She encouraged participants to engage actively, deepen their understanding of UNICEF’s interventions and identify practical opportunities for more informed, ethical and sustained reporting on the humanitarian situation in Benue State.

Declaring the event open, the State Commissioner for Information and Orientation, Solomon Iorpev, represented by the Director of Information and Head of the Department of Enlargement and Orientation, Mrs Comfort Ajunwa, commended UNICEF for the initiative and for its continued commitment to promoting the rights, welfare and protection of children.

He acknowledged the media as a powerful partner in development, saying that, beyond informing the public, the media plays a vital role in shaping opinions, creating awareness, promoting positive values and holding stakeholders accountable.

Iorpev said effective collaboration between government, UNICEF and media practitioners is essential in amplifying issues affecting children, protecting their rights and ensuring that their voices are heard.

Speaking on the objective of the dialogue, UNICEF Communication Officer, Enugu Field Office, Dr Ijeoma Onuoha-Ogwe, explained that it seeks to strengthen media understanding and visibility by enhancing journalists’ understanding of the humanitarian situation in Benue State and the needs of crisis-affected children and vulnerable communities, while amplifying the results and impact of Sida-supported interventions through UNICEF’s integrated multisectoral humanitarian response.

She also said that it is meant to promote ethical, evidence-based and people-centred reporting by strengthening media capacity to produce compelling, child-sensitive and evidence-based stories across health, nutrition, WASH, education, child protection and social policy, while amplifying the voices, experiences and priorities of affected communities. It is also meant to strengthen strategic media partnerships and advocacy by consolidating UNICEF’s collaboration with media organisations to sustain public awareness, shape humanitarian discourse and strengthen advocacy for the rights and well-being of affected children and communities.

Ijeoma further said the dialogue helps to mobilise stakeholder commitment and accountability by fostering constructive engagement among government, humanitarian actors, development partners and the media to promote coordinated action, sustained investment, transparency and accountability in addressing humanitarian needs.

She emphasised that the expected outcome is a better informed, engaged and empowered media community that consistently amplifies Sida-supported interventions and UNICEF’s integrated humanitarian response in Benue State, while contributing to stronger public awareness, government accountability, stakeholder commitment and advocacy for the rights and well-being of crisis-affected children and vulnerable communities.

During the event, the UNICEF Humanitarian Coordinator/Emergency Specialist, Ihuoma Owuama, presented a profile of the Benue humanitarian situation.

The post UNICEF holds media dialogue on humanitarian action for children in Benue appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Navy seizes 11,700 litres of petrol, recovers boat engine in Lagos
description:
By Philip Nwosu
The Nigerian Navy said its operatives had seized 11,700 litres of suspected Premium Motor Spirit (PMS), valued at ₦15.795 million, during an intelligence-driven operation against petroleum smuggling off Ayito Beach, near the Seme Border in Badagry, Lagos State.
The operation, conduct
content:
By Philip Nwosu

The Nigerian Navy said its operatives had seized 11,700 litres of suspected Premium Motor Spirit (PMS), valued at ₦15.795 million, during an intelligence-driven operation against petroleum smuggling off Ayito Beach, near the Seme Border in Badagry, Lagos State.

The operation, conducted by personnel of the Forward Operating Base (FOB) Badagry Special Forces at about 7:30 p.m. on Friday, November 13, 2026, also led to the recovery of a 60-horsepower outboard engine.

The Navy said the operation followed credible intelligence about suspected illegal bunkering activities in the area, with the petroleum products allegedly being transported to the Republic of Benin by criminal networks operating across the border.

According to the Navy, its personnel intercepted a Cotonou boat conveying the suspected petroleum products. However, the occupants reportedly abandoned the boat and fled on sighting the approaching naval team.

A search of the abandoned boat led to the recovery of 390 jerrycans, each containing 30 litres of suspected PMS, bringing the total volume of the seized products to 11,700 litres.

The recovered petroleum products were valued at ₦15,795,000.

In a related development, FOB Badagry handed over 316 bags of 50-kilogramme foreign parboiled rice to the Nigeria Customs Service (NCS), Western Marine Command, Badagry, on Saturday, November 14.

The handover, which took place at the base jetty at about 10 a.m., comprised 231 bags of good rice and 85 damaged bags suspected to have been smuggled into the country.

The Navy said the rice was intercepted during intelligence-led operations within the base’s area of responsibility and was subsequently transferred to the Customs Service in accordance with existing regulations.

The handover was completed at about 11:30 a.m. without incident.

The two operations, according to the Navy, form part of its sustained efforts to curb petroleum products diversion, cross-border smuggling and other maritime-related criminal activities.

The Director of Naval Information, Navy Capt. Abiodun Folorunsho, said the Navy would continue to sustain intelligence-led operations, strengthen maritime surveillance and collaborate with relevant security and regulatory agencies to protect Nigeria’s maritime environment and economic interests.
