title: PFIPC Controversy: ICPC Opposes Adeyemi’s Bail, Says Alleged Fake DG Held In Custody For Safety
description: The Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC) has said that it kept the alleged fake Director-General (DG) of the Presidential Foreign Investment Promotion Council (PFIPC), Adeniyi Adeyemi, in custody for his own safety.According to the Commission, many of those alle
content:
The Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC) has said that it kept the alleged fake Director-General (DG) of the Presidential Foreign Investment Promotion Council (PFIPC), Adeniyi Adeyemi, in custody for his own safety.

According to the Commission, many of those allegedly defrauded by the defendant, some of whom have filed petitions against him, are capable of physically harming him on sight.

It therefore prayed the trial Judge, Justice Halilu Yusuf of the Federal Capital Territory High Court, to reject an application for Bail filed by Adeyemi, pending the determination of the criminal charge against him.

The ICPC urged the court to also deny bail to four civil servants who are facing trial alongside the alleged fake PFIPC DG.

The anti-corruption agency took the position after the defendants pleaded not guilty to a 36-count amended charge it entered against them.

All the defendants, through their respective lawyers, also asked the court to release them on bail pending the determination of the charge.

They anchored their bail applications on the provisions of sections 35(4) and 36(5) of the 1999 Constitution, as amended, as well as sections 158 and 162 of the Administration of Criminal Justice Act (ACJA) 2015.

The civil servants who were in the dock alongside Adeyemi are Aminu Abdullahi, Ogaba Harry, Florence Omameh and Patricia Akhigbe.

All the defendants, including Adeyemi, pleaded ill health, even as they pledged to make themselves available for trial.

Flight Risk

However, the prosecution counsel urged the court to refuse their bail requests and order an accelerated hearing of the case.

The ICPC specifically alleged that Adeyemi posed a flight risk, insisting he had enough funds at his disposal and the capacity to influence some of the proposed witnesses in the matter.

Meanwhile, in urging the court to grant him bail on very liberal terms, Adeyemi, through his counsel, Ibrahim Angulu, SAN, told the court that, contrary to the prosecution’s claim, all his bank accounts had been frozen.

Justice Halilu Yusuf subsequently adjourned the case to November 30 to rule on the defendant’s bail applications, as well as for the commencement of trial.

While the court ordered the remand of all the male defendants in the Kuje correctional facility, it directed that the two female defendants be taken to the Suleja correctional facility.

The ICPC alleged that Adeyemi, while passing himself off as a public servant, obtained over ₦27 billion to start the fake agency.

He was also alleged to have dubiously obtained another ₦3.8 billion for personnel costs.

The prosecution told the court that Adeyemi also obtained funds through a forged document addressed to the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy.

It alleged that the defendant forged documents purportedly signed by the Chief of Staff to the President, Femi Gbajabiamila, which he claimed appointed him Director-General of PFIPC, and used them to occupy government office facilities at the Federal Secretariat Complex Phase III, Abuja.

Besides, Adeyemi was accused of forging a document addressed to the Accountant-General of the Federation, captioned “RE: REQUEST FOR APPROVAL OF SELF-ACCOUNTING STATUS,” for the non-existent agency to operate within the government financial reporting structure.

He was said to have forwarded forged documents to the DG of the National Information Technology Development Agency (NITDA) to get a domain name for the agency.

The defendant was also accused of gifting ₦210,000, without official authorisation, to one of his co-defendants, Abdullahi, an Assistant Chief Technical Officer in the Office of the Secretary General of the Federation (OSGF), “to facilitate the allocation of office space.”

He allegedly gifted another ₦300,000 to another co-defendant, Harry, an officer in the Office of the Chief Economic Adviser to the President, to facilitate the release and handover of two official vehicles, a Prado SUV and a Land Cruiser SUV, to him.

Other counts in the charge included an allegation that on July 29, 2025, the defendant collected ₦20 million from one Oyekunle Gbenga, the Managing Director of Divine Dopacy Nigeria Limited, under the false pretence of a “project facilitation loan” for a purported ₦2.8 billion contract allegedly awarded by the fictitious agency for the procurement of furniture and renovation of the official residence of the DG of the said non-existent PFIPC.

The ICPC insisted that he committed the offences between 2024 and 2026.

He was said to have contravened Sections 364, 366 and 132 of the Penal Code Cap. 532, Laws of the Federation of Nigeria (Abuja) 1990; Section 1(1)(a) of the Advance Fee Fraud and Other Fraud Related Offences Act, 2006, punishable under Section 1(3); and Section 9(a) of the Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Act, 2000, punishable under Section 9(b).

Adeyemi, who has been in detention since July 14, was previously arraigned before the court on October 29.

His re-arraignment on Wednesday followed the amendment of the charge to include the names of the four civil servants identified as his accomplices.

The Federal High Court in Abuja had on October 12 struck out an initial eight-count charge that the Nigeria Police Force had filed against the first defendant, Adeyemi.

The matter was terminated after it was withdrawn by the Office of the Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice.

title: Tinubu unveils first varsity of public relations, leadership at WPRF 2026
description:
• Says Nigeria will become world’s third most populous nation by 2050, largest by century’s end
_______________________________________________________________________
From Juliana Taiwo-Obalonye, Abuja
President Bola Tinubu on Wednesday said he had approved the establishment of Nigeria’s first Univ
content:
• Says Nigeria will become world’s third most populous nation by 2050, largest by century’s end

_______________________________________________________________________

From Juliana Taiwo-Obalonye, Abuja

President Bola Tinubu on Wednesday said he had approved the establishment of Nigeria’s first University of Public Relations and Leadership, a major move to advance professional communication, research and leadership development in the country.

Tinubu made the disclosure while unveiling the university through Vice President Kashim Shettima, who represented him at the opening of the 38th World Public Relations Forum (WPRF) and 5th African Public Relations Association Conference in Abuja.

He said the specialised university would provide advanced education, research, professional development and leadership training in public relations, strategic communications and related disciplines.

“I am pleased to formally approve and support the establishment of the University of Public Relations and Media, a pioneering initiative designed to advance specialised education, research, professional development and leadership training in public relations, strategic communications and related disciplines,” he said.

The President described the institution as a lasting legacy of Nigeria’s hosting of the international forum, saying it represented a forward-looking investment in human capital and the future of the communication profession.

He said the university would help develop a new generation of communication leaders equipped to respond to the demands of a rapidly changing global environment.

Tinubu commended the Nigerian Institute of Public Relations (NIPR), the Federal Ministry of Information and National Orientation and the Nasarawa State Government for collaborating to actualise the initiative.

He particularly acknowledged Nasarawa State Governor Abdullahi Sule for his commitment to the project, urging relevant stakeholders to work together to develop the university into a centre of excellence with national, continental and international recognition.

The President’s approval comes against the backdrop of growing concerns over the impact of misinformation, disinformation, hate speech and declining public trust in an era increasingly shaped by digital technologies and artificial intelligence.

Speaking on the forum’s theme, “Responsible Communication: The Voice of the World,” Tinubu said public relations and communication professionals must move beyond managing images and reputations to promoting truth, accountability, transparency, mutual understanding and constructive engagement.

He said communication professionals have a responsibility to strengthen relations between governments and citizens and to contribute to national development, democratic governance, economic growth and strong institutions.

The President urged practitioners to uphold the highest standards of ethics, professionalism and responsibility in discharging their duties.

Shettima also used the occasion to project Nigeria’s economic and demographic potential, describing the country as a nation of enormous possibilities, with diverse cultures, a dynamic private sector, a youthful population and a strong entrepreneurial spirit.

He said six of Africa’s 10 unicorn companies were Nigerian, citing Flutterwave, OPay, Interswitch, Andela, Moniepoint and Moove as examples of the country’s growing technology and business ecosystem.

The President further projected that Nigeria would become the world’s third most populous country by 2050, with an estimated population of 440 million, before emerging as the most populous nation by the end of the century.

“One out of every four black men is a Nigerian. By 2050, one out of every three black men will be a Nigerian. We will surpass the United States. We will be the third most populous nation on earth with a population of 440 million people,” he said.

He urged international delegates to look beyond the conference and explore Nigeria’s investment opportunities, creative industries, tourism assets, cultural heritage and entrepreneurial ecosystem.

President Tinubu called on participants to establish professional relationships, explore partnerships and investments, and become ambassadors of Nigeria’s economic and development prospects.

“Nigeria welcomes you. Nigeria is open for partnership, and Nigeria is ready to engage with the world,” he said.

He expressed the Federal Government’s appreciation to the Global Alliance for Public Relations and Communication Management, the African Public Relations Association and NIPR for bringing the international gathering to Nigeria.

Speaking earlier, Kenyan President William Ruto, addressing the forum through a representative, urged African governments to make communication central to policymaking and governance. He warned that public trust cannot be manufactured through publicity but must be earned through honesty, transparency, consistency and accountability.

He said Kenya adopted a National Communication Policy in August 2026, requiring ministries, departments and agencies to provide citizens with timely, accurate and accessible information, while ensuring that communication strategies are integrated into major government projects from inception.

Information Minister Mohammed Idris, for his part, called on governments, media organisations and public relations practitioners to uphold truth, accuracy, transparency and professional ethics, warning that the misuse of information and digital platforms could fuel hatred, deepen divisions and threaten global security.

Speaking at the World Public Relations Forum in Abuja, Idris said responsible communication is essential for building public trust, promoting peaceful coexistence and strengthening democratic governance. “Our communication should build bridges, not walls,” he said, urging stakeholders to ensure that information empowers citizens rather than misleads them.

Idris also stressed the need to defend freedom of expression while promoting accountability and responsible advocacy, noting that journalism remains central to nation-building and democratic governance. He urged governments to communicate openly, media organisations to uphold professional standards and public relations practitioners to embrace honesty and transparency.

He further called for stronger international cooperation, investment in media literacy and collaboration with technology companies to address misinformation and disinformation, while urging Africa to promote fairer international narratives that reflect the continent beyond familiar accounts of conflict and challenges.

The President of the Nigerian Institute of Public Relations, Ike Neliaku, in his opening remarks, declared the 2026 World Public Relations Forum in Abuja the biggest in the event’s history, with 2,837 delegates from across the world attending as of the opening day.

He said Nigeria deliberately designed the forum to showcase its cultural diversity, professional capacity and leadership in public relations while hosting the event on behalf of Africa. He said the gathering brought together international public relations professionals, government officials, traditional rulers, young people, the private sector and civil society organisations.

He said the forum was conceived to go beyond conventional professional discussions, with programmes including a global youth public relations gathering, a women in public relations conference, a knowledge conference, a royal fathers’ session on community relations and peacebuilding, and engagements with governors and other sub-national leaders.

Neliaku said the participation of traditional rulers was particularly important because peacebuilding and community relations are central to effective public relations practice in Africa, adding that the forum would provide an opportunity for the continent to share lessons with the rest of the world.

He stressed that public relations should not be mistaken for propaganda, describing it as a profession built on trust, reputation management and responsibility.

“Public relations is not propaganda. Public relations is a business of trust,” he said, adding that practitioners must be prepared to take responsibility for the information they communicate and the impact of their work.

The NIPR president also disclosed that the organisers had incorporated a cultural festival and a corporate social responsibility initiative, including plans to feed 10,000 people, as part of efforts to make the forum impactful beyond the conference venue.

He said Nigeria had made a deliberate decision to host the event on a grand scale, insisting that the country and Africa have the history, capacity and cultural heritage to command a stronger place in global conversations.

Neliaku recalled the efforts that went into securing the hosting rights, including Nigeria’s presentation at the global level and the support of the Federal Government, particularly the Minister of Information and National Orientation, Mohammed Idris.

He thanked President Tinubu, represented at the event by the Vice President; the Nasarawa State Governor, Abdullahi Sule; and other partners for supporting the hosting of the international gathering.

The President of the Global Alliance for Public Relations and Communication Management, Justin Green, praised Nigeria’s determination and diplomatic efforts in securing the hosting rights for the 2026 World Public Relations Forum, describing the country’s successful bid as a victory for Africa.

Recounting how Nigerian officials, including the Minister of Information and National Orientation and Nigeria’s ambassador to Ireland, repeatedly contacted him during the final stages of the selection process, he said the country had demonstrated an exceptional commitment to bringing the global gathering to Abuja. He said Nigeria’s “fighting spirit to win” brought delegates from 126 countries to the Nigerian capital.

Green also hailed the establishment of the University of Public Relations and Leadership in Nasarawa State, describing it as the world’s first university dedicated to the profession and a major investment in education and professional excellence. He commended Governor Abdullahi Sule for making the project a reality, saying it represented a commitment to developing the next generation of communication professionals.

Illustrating the pride Nigerians have in their country, he recounted how a Nigerian taxi driver in Dublin offered to take him to the airport without charge after learning he was travelling to Nigeria, describing the gesture as “Nigerian pride at its greatest”.

Also speaking, Arik Karani, President of the African Public Relations Association (APRA), described Nigeria as a leading force in shaping public relations practice in Africa, noting that the country provided a model for other nations through its early adoption of legislation regulating the profession.

The APRA president said Nigeria was the only African country at the time to have enacted a public relations law, more than 20 years ago, providing a benchmark for other countries seeking to strengthen professional standards. “Nigeria is the table when we are discussing public relations,” the president said, stressing that Africa must move beyond being a passive participant in global conversations to taking a leading role in shaping them.

title: Tinubu transmits bill to Reps to decriminalise attempted suicide
description:
By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja



President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has transmitted the National Mental Health (Amendment) Bill, 2026, to the House of Representatives for consideration, seeking to decriminalise attempted suicide and provide support for persons who attempt to take their lives.



The Presiden
content:
By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja

President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has transmitted the National Mental Health (Amendment) Bill, 2026, to the House of Representatives for consideration, seeking to decriminalise attempted suicide and provide support for persons who attempt to take their lives.

The President’s request was contained in a letter dated November 10, 2026, addressed to the Speaker of the House, Tajudeen Abbas, and read on the floor of the House during plenary on Wednesday.

In the letter, Tinubu said the proposed legislation seeks to amend the National Mental Health Act, No. 46, 2021, to remove the criminalisation of attempted suicide and introduce support for affected persons.

The President said the transmission was made pursuant to Section 58(2) of the 1999 Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, as amended.
The letter, titled, “Transmission of the National Mental Health (Amendment) Bill, 2026 for Consideration,” reads in part: “I forward, herewith, the National Mental Health (Amendment) Bill, 2026 for the kind consideration of the House of Representatives.”

Explaining the objective of the proposed amendment, Tinubu stated that the bill “seeks to amend the National Mental Health Act, No. 46, 2021 (the ‘Principal Act’) to decriminalise attempted suicide and to provide support to any person who attempts to commit suicide in Nigeria.”

He expressed appreciation to the House of Representatives and urged lawmakers to give the proposed legislation expeditious consideration.
The proposed amendment, if passed by the National Assembly and assented to by the President, would change the existing legal framework governing attempted suicide in Nigeria, shifting the approach towards support for affected persons.

The bill is expected to be considered by the House in line with its legislative procedures.

title: Falana urges FG to pursue £420m British reparations, withdraw appeal
description:
Human rights lawyer, Femi Falana, SAN, has urged the Federal Government to mount diplomatic pressure on the British Government to pay £420 million in damages awarded by a Federal High Court to the families of 21 coal miners killed in the 1949 Iva Valley massacre in Enugu State.







Falana also ca
content:
Human rights lawyer, Femi Falana, SAN, has urged the Federal Government to mount diplomatic pressure on the British Government to pay £420 million in damages awarded by a Federal High Court to the families of 21 coal miners killed in the 1949 Iva Valley massacre in Enugu State.

Falana also called on the Federal Government to withdraw its appeal against the judgment, arguing that the British Government had not challenged the historic decision.

He made the call in a statement marking the 75th anniversary of the massacre, in which 21 Nigerian coal miners were shot dead by colonial authorities during a protest against harsh working conditions, racial discrimination in wages and unpaid back wages.

The judgment was delivered by Justice Anthony Onovo of the Federal High Court in the suit, Mazi Greg Onoh v. Secretary of State for Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Affairs & Ors (Suit No. E/909/2024).

Justice Onovo held the British colonial administration liable for the killings, describing the massacre as an unlawful and extrajudicial violation of the right to life.

The court ordered the British Government to pay £20 million to the families of each of the 21 deceased miners, amounting to £420 million in compensation.

The judge found that the miners were defenceless and were merely demanding improved working conditions when they were shot, stressing that they were not engaged in any violent action against the authorities.

The court also awarded post-judgment interest of 10 per cent per annum on the compensation until full payment, while claims for pre-judgment interest and exemplary damages were waived.

In addition, Justice Onovo ordered the British Government to issue unreserved written apologies to the victims’ families through their counsel.

The apologies are to be published in Nigeria’s Daily Sun, Daily Independent and The Punch, as well as three major national newspapers in the United Kingdom.

The court directed that evidence of the publications be filed within 60 days, while the monetary awards must be satisfied within 90 days of the judgment.

Justice Onovo further held that the Federal Government and the Attorney-General of the Federation had a constitutional responsibility under Sections 19(d) and 150(1) to pursue redress for the victims.

He faulted the prolonged failure of the Nigerian authorities to seek justice for the deceased miners, describing the inaction as a dereliction of their constitutional responsibility.

The judge consequently directed the Federal Government to initiate and pursue diplomatic engagement with the British authorities within 60 days to secure justice, effective remedies and reparations.

Falana urged the Federal Government to concentrate on enforcing the judgment rather than pursuing an appeal, insisting that the families of the slain miners deserved justice and compensation for the killings.

The Iva Valley massacre occurred in 1949 when coal miners protesting poor working conditions, racial disparities in wages and unpaid entitlements adopted a go-slow protest and occupied the mine to prevent management from locking them out.

The colonial authorities subsequently opened fire on the workers, killing 21 miners in an incident that became one of the defining episodes in Nigeria’s struggle against colonial rule.

title: Adeleke disowns stadium renaming, orders signpost removed
description:
The signpost announcing the renaming of Osogbo Township Stadium after Osun State Governor, Ademola Adeleke, has been removed, with the state government saying the move was made without the necessary approval.
The PUNCH had earlier reported on Wednesday that the Osun State Government had renamed the
content:
The signpost announcing the renaming of Osogbo Township Stadium after Osun State Governor, Ademola Adeleke, has been removed, with the state government saying the move was made without the necessary approval.

The PUNCH had earlier reported on Wednesday that the Osun State Government had renamed the facility, formerly known as Osogbo City Stadium, Ademola Adeleke Imole Stadium, Osogbo, Osun renames stadium after Adeleke

The development came about a week before Adeleke’s second-term inauguration, scheduled to hold at the stadium on November 27.

The facility, which is currently undergoing rehabilitation, previously served as the home ground for the state’s male and female football teams.

However, its deteriorating condition forced the teams to consider alternative venues for their league matches.

Our correspondent, who visited the stadium on Wednesday to monitor preparations for the inauguration, observed that a large signpost announcing the new name had been erected at a conspicuous spot near the entrance.

A staff member of the Osun State Sports Council, whose office is located within the stadium premises, who spoke on condition of anonymity because he was not authorised to comment on the development on behalf of the government said Adeleke was expected to visit the facility for an inspection in the coming days.

He added, “We all just observed that a big signpost announcing the new name was brought early this morning, Wednesday.

“It is true that the stadium has been named after the governor. We all witnessed it this morning, when those in charge brought the signpost and erected it at the entrance. However, there is no official announcement yet on the development.”

However, following The PUNCH report, the State Deputy Governor and Commissioner for Sports, Kola Adewusi, was said to have directed that the signpost be removed.

When our correspondent visited the facility again at about 6pm on Wednesday, the signpost had been taken down.

Explaining the development, the Osun State Commissioner for Information and Public Enlightenment, Kolapo Alimi, said those who erected the signpost had not obtained the governor’s approval.

“Those who went to put the signpost there didn’t get approval before doing so. What they did was inform someone to tell the governor that they intended to do it and the governor told them that he would consult and get back to them.

“But they didn’t wait for the final approval. The governor has asked for the signpost to be pulled down immediately. Even if the stadium will be renamed, the public will be properly notified,” Alimi said.

Also speaking, the General Manager of the Osun State Sports Council, Ademola Daini, said those who erected the signpost had acted out of overzealousness.

title: Germany Lists 31 Countries Whose Citizens Can Work Without A Visa - But Nigeria Is Not On The List - Check Below For Full Details
description: Germany has confirmed that citizens of 31 countries can live and work there without first applying for a visa or residence permit - but the list is made up of EU, EEA and Swiss nationals. Nigeria is not on it.
source: Make it in Germany / EU Commission / German Missions in Nigeria
content:
Germany has confirmed that citizens of 31 countries can move to the country and take up work without first obtaining a visa or a residence permit - a list that has sent Nigerian job seekers searching for their passports. But there is a catch: Nigeria is not one of the 31.

Who the 31 countries are

The 31 are made up of all 27 European Union member states, plus Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway and Switzerland.

  • EU (27): Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria, Croatia, Cyprus, Czech Republic, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malta, Netherlands, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden
  • EEA, outside the EU: Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway
  • Plus: Switzerland

What this actually means

This is not a new programme and not a visa lottery. It is the European Union's long-standing free movement of persons rule: citizens of those countries can live, work, study and retire in Germany using only a valid national ID card or passport.

German authorities have simply restated the rule in updated official guidance, which is why it is being reported as a fresh announcement.

What it means for Nigerians

Nigeria is a third country under EU rules. That means a Nigerian cannot travel to Germany and start working on arrival. You need a residence title, and in most cases you must obtain a visa before you enter Germany and take up employment.

That does not close the door. Nigerians with the right qualifications still have several legal routes:

  • Opportunity Card (Chancenkarte): a points-based job-search permit that lets qualified non-EU nationals enter Germany for up to a year to look for work, based on qualifications, experience, language skills and age.
  • EU Blue Card: for graduates with a recognised degree and a qualifying job offer in Germany.
  • Skilled worker visa: for people with a recognised vocational qualification or degree and a concrete job offer.
  • Job seeker visa: for degree holders who want to travel to Germany to search for a job within a limited period.
  • Study or training visa: study, then use the post-study route to stay and work.

Beware of agents

The German mission in Nigeria does not require payment to any agent for visa processing, and job offers that ask for money upfront are a red flag. Applications go through the German embassy or consulate, and official information is published on make-it-in-germany.com and the mission's own website.

Bottom line: the 31-country list is real, but it is a European free-movement list - not a new open door for Nigeria. If Germany is your target, the Opportunity Card, the Blue Card and the skilled worker visa remain the routes worth preparing for, and they reward qualifications, language skills and genuine job offers.

description:
By Dickson Omobola



Following a fatal road accident on Friday, November 13, 2026, the Airport Police Command, Ikeja, has called for assistance in identifying the family, relatives and friends of a male victim, Abraham Osakpolor, who died in the incident.







The accident occurred along the expr
content:
By Dickson Omobola

Following a fatal road accident on Friday, November 13, 2026, the Airport Police Command, Ikeja, has called for assistance in identifying the family, relatives and friends of a male victim, Abraham Osakpolor, who died in the incident.

The accident occurred along the expressway leading from the Murtala Muhammed International Airport towards the Oshodi axis of Lagos.

Osakpolor, who was born in Benin City, Edo State, on September 1, 1968, was hit by a moving vehicle and subsequently rushed to a hospital, where he was pronounced dead.

The command’s Police Public Relations Officer, ASP Mohammed Adeola, in a statement, said the deceased’s remains had been deposited in the hospital morgue

The statement reads: “The motorist involved in the accident was immediately apprehended by the Airport Police Command and will be charged to court.

“During an initial search of the deceased’s belongings, a Nigerian passport with passport number B51930694 and a mobile device without a SIM card were recovered. The mortuary attendants subsequently informed the Command that a Canadian passport with passport number AE763025 had also been discovered among his belongings during a further search. Despite concerted efforts by the Police to establish contact with his family or persons who may know him, these efforts have so far proved unsuccessful.

“The command is therefore urgently calling on members of the public, particularly those who may know the deceased or have information about his family, relatives or associates, to assist in notifying them of this unfortunate incident.

“The public is also encouraged to share and circulate this information widely to ensure it reaches anyone who may be able to identify the deceased and facilitate contact with his family. Anyone with useful information is urged to contact the Airport Police Command through the following channels: Airport Police Command, X: @airportcommand and Facebook: Airport Command.”

The post Police seek relatives of man killed in Lagos airport road crash appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: US applauds Nigerian troops for rescuing 125 kidnap victims
description:
By Favour Ulebor, Abuja



The United States has commended Nigerian troops for rescuing 125 kidnap victims during military operations across the country between November 6 and 12.







The US Bureau of African Affairs gave the commendation in a statement posted on its X handle on Wednesday, also p
content:
By Favour Ulebor, Abuja

The United States has commended Nigerian troops for rescuing 125 kidnap victims during military operations across the country between November 6 and 12.

The US Bureau of African Affairs gave the commendation in a statement posted on its X handle on Wednesday, also praising the troops for dismantling terrorist camps, recovering weapons and clearing explosive devices.

“The United States commends Nigerian military operations this month that have rescued 125 kidnapping victims, along with the dismantling of Islamic terrorist camps, the recovery of weapons, and clearance of explosive devices,” the statement read.

The bureau said Washington supported the Federal Government’s efforts to prevent kidnappings and ensure those responsible were brought to justice.

“We support all efforts by the Nigerian government to prevent kidnappings and hold the perpetrators of this violence fully accountable,” it added.

The Defence Headquarters had earlier disclosed that troops rescued the 125 victims during operations conducted between November 6 and 12.

It said the troops also killed eight terrorists and arrested 10 suspected collaborators and logistics suppliers during the operations.

The military said the largest rescue operation took place in Borno State, where troops freed 119 travellers abducted on November 6 along the Dutsen Kura-Bulazarma-Kamuya Road in Buratai, Biu Local Government Area.

According to the military, the attackers abandoned the captives while fleeing from pursuing troops.

Those rescued comprised 69 men, 35 women and 15 children.

Troops also rescued five kidnapped persons in separate operations in Zamfara State.

The military further disclosed that 12 terrorist fighters and members of their families surrendered during the operations.

title: Kwara raises students’ bursary to N50,000
description:
Kwara State Governor, AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq, has announced an increase in the annual bursary for students in the state from N20,000 to N50,000.
The governor made the announcement on Wednesday during a meeting with the leadership of the National Association of Nigerian Students, Joint Campus Committ
content:
Kwara State Governor, AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq, has announced an increase in the annual bursary for students in the state from N20,000 to N50,000.

The governor made the announcement on Wednesday during a meeting with the leadership of the National Association of Nigerian Students, Joint Campus Committee, at the Government House in Ilorin.

He noted that payment of the new amount would begin before the end of November.

In a 52-second video obtained by The PUNCH, AbdulRazaq said his administration had reconsidered the existing amount after further discussions on how to provide more financial support for students.

“The fund is just to support the students. We approved N20,000 in bursary for each student. We’ve had discussions among ourselves and resolved that we must give our students N50,000,” the governor said.

“Payment will start before the end of this month,” he added.

The latest increase brings the state bursary to ten times the N5,000 paid to students in 2019, representing a 150 per cent rise from the previous N20,000 allocation.

The increase also came on the same day that the National Association of Kwara State Students pledged the support of its more than 50,000 members for the governor, citing his administration’s interventions in education and student welfare.

The association’s National President, Muhammed Issa, had earlier disclosed this during a radio programme monitored by our correspondent, where he identified the increase in bursary payments and the provision of two new buses for the association as some of the administration’s notable interventions.

Issa, who appeared on the programme alongside the association’s Public Relations Officer, Muhammed Baba, and Senate President, Yahaya Oladimeji, said the students’ endorsement followed a recent gathering at the Kwara State House of Assembly.

According to him, students drawn from across the country unanimously passed a vote of confidence in AbdulRazaq at the gathering in recognition of his administration’s contributions to their welfare.

“The increase in bursary from N5,000 in 2019 to N20,000 and the provision of two new buses for our association are some of the interventions we appreciate this administration for,” Issa said.

He, however, urged the government to extend more assistance to Kwara indigenes studying outside the state, particularly those in the northern and southern parts of the country, who he said were struggling to meet their tuition obligations.

“We want the government to do more for our students studying outside Kwara State, especially those in the northern and southern parts of the country, who are finding it difficult to meet their tuition obligations,” he said.

The NAKSS president also called for sustained investment in education, describing AbdulRazaq as a youth-friendly governor.

He insisted that the association’s position was based on its assessment of student welfare rather than political affiliation.

title: UK warns visa applicants against four fraud red flags
description:
The United Kingdom Visas and Immigration (UKVI) agency has warned foreign nationals applying for British visas to watch out for four warning signs that could indicate fraud.







The agency issued the advisory in a post on its X handle on Wednesday, urging applicants to protect themselves against
content:
The United Kingdom Visas and Immigration (UKVI) agency has warned foreign nationals applying for British visas to watch out for four warning signs that could indicate fraud.

The agency issued the advisory in a post on its X handle on Wednesday, urging applicants to protect themselves against visa scams and fraudulent agents.

“4 RED FLAGS to watch out for when applying for a UK visa. Protect yourself from visa fraud by learning these crucial warning signs in our infographic,” UKVI said.

The warning signs include individuals who guarantee applicants UK visas or jobs, offer appointments or visa services that cannot be verified through official channels, make unsolicited contact to demand money or personal information, and pressure applicants to act immediately or keep transactions secret.

According to the agency, scammers operate through phone calls, websites, emails and social media platforms, while some also approach unsuspecting applicants outside visa application centres.

It said fraudsters often impersonate Home Office officials or representatives of visa application centres, offering to secure jobs, arrange appointments or process visa applications.

Some also claim that there is a problem with an applicant’s visa and demand urgent payment to prevent its cancellation or possible deportation.

UKVI warned that fraudsters could use official-sounding language and forged documents, including seemingly genuine job offer letters, to convince applicants to part with their money.

The agency also cautioned against agents who promise to fast-track visa applications in exchange for payments into personal bank accounts.

“Visa officers will never ask you for money in person, by email or phone,” the guidance stated.

It added that applicants seeking UK visas or permission to travel would never be asked to pay visa fees through email, at a visa application centre or into a personal bank account.

The agency advised applicants to book appointments through the official UK government website or its authorised commercial partner.

It further warned that submitting forged documents could result in visa refusal and a 10-year ban on future UK visa applications.

UKVI urged applicants who suspect fraud not to disclose personal information, surrender their passports or send money, gift cards or vouchers to suspected scammers.

It advised victims and individuals who suspect fraud in the UK to report the incidents to Report Fraud, while those outside the country should contact their local authorities.

Visa fraud remains a concern for international travellers, with applicants sometimes losing money to fraudulent agents and unauthorised service providers.

The post UK warns visa applicants against four fraud red flags appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: NELFUND urges federal workers to enrol children in loan scheme
description:
The Nigerian Education Loan Fund has launched a fresh drive to expand access to its interest-free student loan scheme, targeting children and wards of federal civil servants across the country.
The Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of NELFUND, Akintunde Sawyerr, made this known on Wednes
content:
The Nigerian Education Loan Fund has launched a fresh drive to expand access to its interest-free student loan scheme, targeting children and wards of federal civil servants across the country.

The Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of NELFUND, Akintunde Sawyerr, made this known on Wednesday during a sensitisation exercise at the Federal Ministry of Defence in Abuja, where he urged workers to encourage eligible children in public tertiary institutions to apply for the loans.

Sawyerr said the campaign was part of efforts to deepen awareness of the scheme across the 34 federal ministries before extending it to their departments and agencies.

He explained that the initiative was designed to remove financial barriers to higher education, reduce student dropouts and promote equal access to tertiary education.

According to him, NELFUND offers loans for institutional fees and monthly upkeep, with students allowed to choose whether to access both components or only the institutional fee support.

“While the institutional fee component is compulsory for applicants seeking support, the upkeep allowance is optional,” he said.

Also speaking, the Director of SERVICOM at NELFUND, Olusola Fowobaje, said the campaign would address misconceptions about the scheme and reassure Nigerians of its credibility.

He said the funds were drawn from public resources, including taxpayers’ contributions, and should be accessible to eligible Nigerians.

In a technical presentation, the Fund’s Director of Monitoring and Evaluation, Aliyu Mohammed, said applicants must be Nigerian citizens aged at least 18, have admission into a recognised public tertiary institution, and possess a National Identification Number and Bank Verification Number.

He disclosed that beneficiaries could receive N20,000 monthly as upkeep allowance, while approved institutional fees would be paid directly to their schools.

Mohammed added that repayment would begin two years after beneficiaries completed the National Youth Service Corps programme, provided they had secured employment.

Earlier, the Director of Education Services at the Ministry of Defence, Markus Kura, urged ministry staff to pay attention to the presentation, saying, “Our job today is to be enlightened because, they say, knowledge is power.”

The ministry’s Director of Reforms, Ogidi Paul, who gave the closing remarks, urged the workers to become ambassadors of the Fund by sharing information about the scheme with others.

The NELFUND scheme, established under the Student Loans (Access to Higher Education) Act, 2024, provides interest-free financial assistance to eligible students in public tertiary institutions to cover institutional fees and upkeep.

The programme has continued to expand since its application portal opened in May 2024. As of November 12, 2026, the Fund had disbursed N375.28bn to 1,675,474 students across 320 tertiary institutions, comprising N194.77bn for institutional fees and N180.51bn in upkeep allowances. It had also received about 2.45 million applications.

The latest campaign reflects the Fund’s efforts to enlist parents, guardians and government employees in promoting awareness of the scheme and expanding access to education financing.

title: US Democrats nominate Jeffries for House speaker
description:
US Democrats on Wednesday elected Hakeem Jeffries as their leader and nominee for Speaker of the House of Representatives, putting him on course to become the first Black politician to occupy the powerful position.







The 56-year-old New Yorker secured 251 votes in a closed-door, secret ballot,
content:
US Democrats on Wednesday elected Hakeem Jeffries as their leader and nominee for Speaker of the House of Representatives, putting him on course to become the first Black politician to occupy the powerful position.

The 56-year-old New Yorker secured 251 votes in a closed-door, secret ballot, with 11 votes cast against his nomination, according to US media reports.

Jeffries faced no declared challenger, although opposition from some newly elected progressive lawmakers exposed divisions within the Democratic Party over how to exercise its newfound power following a sweeping midterm election victory.

His nomination positions him to preside over a commanding Democratic majority during the final two years of President Donald Trump’s term, as the party prepares to reverse Republican policies and launch investigations into the administration.

However, Jeffries must still secure a formal vote of the full House when the new Congress convenes on January 3. With Democrats holding a large majority, his election is widely expected to be a formality.

Both returning Democrats and incoming lawmakers participated in Wednesday’s leadership election, including progressives who had sought concessions on issues ranging from US military support for Israel to the influence of money in politics.

Jeffries had requested a recorded vote rather than a nomination by acclamation, a process that would have allowed the party to endorse him without a formal ballot.

He argued that every Democrat should have the opportunity to assess his experience, record and vision, citing the precedent set when the party last took control of the House in 2018.

Although the overall voting figures were made public, individual ballots remained secret.

Ahead of the election, Jeffries met with progressive lawmakers to discuss issues including Israel and healthcare. Proposals to lower the Medicare eligibility age and expand healthcare coverage were among the issues considered.

The Democratic leader has also sought to shift attention to his party’s governing agenda following the Republican defeat, amid voter dissatisfaction over the Iran war and rising fuel costs.

“Folks are drowning in this Republican economy, and House Democrats are committed to turning that situation around, beginning on day one,” he told reporters on Tuesday.

“We’re going to relentlessly fight for an affordable America.”

Brooklyn roots

Raised in the working-class Crown Heights neighbourhood of Brooklyn, New York, Jeffries trained as a lawyer before entering the New York State Legislature in 2007. He was elected to Congress in 2012.

Known for his measured manner, sharp rhetoric and frequent references to hip-hop artists, he made history in 2022 when Democrats elected him to succeed Nancy Pelosi as their House leader, making him the first Black politician to lead a party in either chamber of Congress.

He also served as one of the House prosecutors during Trump’s first impeachment trial in 2020.

As Speaker, Jeffries would preside over one of Washington’s most powerful institutions and become second in the line of presidential succession, behind the vice-president.

However, he faces the challenge of managing a Democratic coalition comprising centrists and an increasingly assertive progressive wing.

The party has promised investigations into Trump and his administration, while lawmakers remain divided over issues including Israel, healthcare and how aggressively to pursue their legislative agenda against a president who retains veto powers.

Jeffries’ nomination comes amid a more competitive leadership contest among Senate Democrats, where veteran party leader Chuck Schumer is facing a challenge from progressive Maryland Senator Chris Van Hollen.

Van Hollen has attracted support from prominent left-wing figures, including Bernie Sanders, although he has acknowledged that he is the underdog.

Senate Democrats are expected to elect their leader in early December.

Meanwhile, Republicans chose their congressional leaders last week, elevating Trump ally Jim Jordan in the House and retaining John Thune as Senate leader.

AFP

The post US Democrats nominate Jeffries for House speaker appeared first on Vanguard News.

content:
The Federal Capital Territory (FCT) High Court sitting in Apo Abuja, on Wednesday November 18, 2026 ordered a lawyer, Victor Giwa who is put on trial alongside Ibitade Bukola Olugbenga for alleged forgery and impersonation to return his international passport on or before December 2, 2026, after questioning his failure to comply with an earlier directive to surrender the travel document which was part of the conditions of his bail granted 8 October 2026.

Justice Jude Onwuegbuzie issued the fresh order after the first defendant (Giwa) in the criminal case, told the court that his passport was being used to process his expired visa.

The matter, Charge No. CR/150/2025, was brought by the Inspector-General of Police brought against Victor Giwa and Ibitade Bukola, scheduled for the hearing of an application by a subpoenaed non-party witness, Chief Awa U. Kalu, SAN, seeking to set aside the subpoena issued against him.

At the commencement of proceedings on Wednesday, the prosecution counsel, Stanley Medugu, with E.T. Emmanuel, informed the court that the subpoenaed witness was absent.

He argued that a witness served with a subpoena was required to remain in court until formally discharged.

The prosecution also asked the court to establish whether Giwa had complied with its November 9, 2026 directive requiring him to return his international passport within 24 hours or show cause.

Rather than address the issue, the first defendant (Giwa), who appeared in person, sought the transfer of the case from Justice Onwuegbuzie’s court.

“I have no confidence in this court,” he declared, adding that he had filed an application seeking the judge’s recusal.

Counsel to the subpoenaed witness, Dr. Sunny Ajala, described the allegation as serious but urged the court to suspend proceedings pending the Chief Judge’s response to the petition.

Counsel to the second defendant, Ogbu Aboje, aligned himself with the position.

However, Justice Onwuegbuzie declined to suspend proceedings, stating that he had received no communication from the Chief Judge.

“The Honourable Chief Judge has not written me any letter. It is a criminal case. Have your motion,” the judge said.

Shortly afterwards, Giwa requested permission to use the toilet, complaining that there was no toilet facility within the court premises.

He subsequently left the courtroom and remained away for approximately one to two hours, during which the judge, prosecution and defence counsel, as well as other lawyers in the matter, waited for his return.

The delay interrupted the hearing of the application, which had previously suffered several adjournments.

Upon resumption, Ajala adopted the processes filed in support of his client’s application and urged the court to set aside the subpoena, describing it as excessively broad, oppressive, a fishing expedition and an abuse of court process.

The application, filed on October 30, 2026, was supported by an 11-ground argument and a 19-paragraph affidavit with two exhibits, alongside a further 10-paragraph affidavit filed on November 16, 2026.

Ajala argued that two subpoenas had been issued against his client, contending that the process interfered with his professional responsibilities as a legal practitioner under Rule 19 of the Rules of Professional Conduct for Legal Practitioners 2023.

He cited the Supreme Court decision in Josiah v. The State (1985) 1 NWLR (Pt. 1) 125.

In opposition, Medugu adopted the prosecution’s 41-paragraph counter-affidavit, deposed to by Salami Adewale, alongside five exhibits marked AKA to AKE and a written address dated November 10, 2026.

He urged the court to dismiss the application.

Giwa also attempted to oppose the application, relying on Section 398 of the ACJA, but the judge overruled his objection.

The court adjourned the application to December 2, 2026, for ruling.

It subsequently returned to the issue of Giwa’s international passport.

When Justice Onwuegbuzie asked where the document was, Giwa explained that it had been submitted as part of the documents required to process his expired visa.

He also argued that the earlier order concerning the passport was on appeal and that the record of appeal had been transmitted.

Giwa further contended that the prosecution was in possession of the document and that the court lacked jurisdiction to make further pronouncements on the matter.

The judge, however, questioned his failure to comply with the earlier directive.

“Are you aware that you are in contempt of this court for not returning the passport? I granted you the passport to enable you to go and see your family, with the expectation that you would return when you came back,” Justice Onwuegbuzie said.

Justice Onwuegbuzie consequently ordered Giwa to return the international passport to the court on or before December 2, 2026.

The post Alleged forgery: Court orders lawyer to surrender passport before December 2 appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Netherlands varsity opens scholarship opportunities for African students
description:
Wageningen University & Research (WUR) in the Netherlands has opened applications for its fully funded Africa Scholarship Programme, offering talented African students the opportunity to pursue two-year master’s degrees beginning in September 2027.
In a post obtained from the varsity’s website on We
content:
Wageningen University & Research (WUR) in the Netherlands has opened applications for its fully funded Africa Scholarship Programme, offering talented African students the opportunity to pursue two-year master’s degrees beginning in September 2027.

In a post obtained from the varsity’s website on Wednesday, the scholarship covers full tuition fees, monthly living allowances, return air tickets between Africa and the Netherlands, visa expenses and health insurance throughout the 24-month programme.

“The initiative is designed to support outstanding African graduates seeking postgraduate education in areas related to life sciences, agriculture, environmental studies and other disciplines offered by the university,” it stated.

According to the university’s scholarship guidelines, applicants must be citizens of an African country and hold a bachelor’s degree with First Class Honours or an equivalent qualification.

“Candidates are also required to have a minimum grade point average of 80 per cent and satisfy the university’s English language proficiency requirements.

“Applicants must have completed their undergraduate studies and secured unconditional admission to an eligible master’s programme at Wageningen University before the scholarship application deadline,” the varsity added.

The university also gives preference to candidates who have not previously obtained a master’s degree.

How to Apply

Interested candidates are required to apply directly for an eligible master’s programme through Wageningen University’s online application portal.

There is no separate scholarship application form. Instead, the university will identify eligible candidates from those who have submitted applications for admission and invite qualified applicants to participate in the scholarship selection process.

The deadline for submitting applications is December 1, 2026, for the September 2027 academic session.

Shortlisted candidates are expected to be contacted between March and April 2027, while final scholarship offers are scheduled to be announced on April 7, 2027.

The Africa Scholarship Programme provides an opportunity for outstanding African graduates to access international postgraduate education without bearing the major financial costs associated with studying abroad.

Wageningen University & Research is internationally recognised for its research and academic programmes in agriculture, food systems, environmental sciences and life sciences.

Through the scholarship initiative, the institution aims to attract talented African students and provide them with advanced academic training and research opportunities that could contribute to addressing development challenges across the continent.

title: Alkalanci, British High Commission train Benue religious leaders against disinformation, FIMI
description:
From Scholastica Hir, Makurdi
Alkalanci, a Hausa fact-checking platform, in partnership with the British High Commission, has commenced a two-day training for religious leaders in Benue State to strengthen their capacity to identify and counter misinformation, disinformation and foreign information
content:
From Scholastica Hir, Makurdi

Alkalanci, a Hausa fact-checking platform, in partnership with the British High Commission, has commenced a two-day training for religious leaders in Benue State to strengthen their capacity to identify and counter misinformation, disinformation and foreign information manipulation.

The workshop, which began on Wednesday, 18 November 2026, in Makurdi, brought together 20 Christian and Muslim religious leaders under the theme “Scaling Faith-Based Resilience Against Disinformation and FIMI”.

The programme, funded by the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO) through the Integrated Security Fund (ISF) West Africa, is aimed at equipping participants with fact-checking and information verification skills to prevent the spread of false narratives capable of triggering tension and conflicts in Benue communities.

Welcoming participants to the event, Alkalanci’s Programme Manager, Victoria Bamas, said the initiative adopted a train-the-trainer approach to enable participating religious leaders to transfer the knowledge acquired to their congregations and wider communities.

She explained that the training would help participants understand misinformation, disinformation and Foreign Information Manipulation and Interference (FIMI), as well as develop basic skills to verify information before sharing it.

Bama identified financial incentives from online content monetisation, advertising and audience engagement as some of the factors encouraging the spread of false information, noting that some individuals were increasingly motivated by the benefits of generating online traffic.

She said the initiative was designed to build community resilience by empowering people to recognise and reject false information rather than merely relying on those spreading it to change their behaviour.

She said: “The idea is to equip people and inoculate them so that when information gets to them they are able to identify it and not act on it. At the end of the day, we want to achieve a community inoculation and mitigation and we are working with FCDO and the British Government to achieve this.”

The Cyber and Hybrid Threats Project Lead at the British High Commission, Abuja, Oriola Odutoye, said the programme was part of the United Kingdom’s expanding security and defence cooperation with Nigeria, particularly in tackling emerging hybrid threats.

Odutoye said both countries were strengthening collaboration in cybersecurity and related areas, including foreign information manipulation and interference.

He disclosed that similar engagements had been conducted in Plateau, Kano and Adamawa states, while Benue was among the states covered by the initiative, with Gombe and Bauchi states also scheduled to benefit from the programme.

According to him, the broader objective was to give religious leaders across Northern Nigeria a common understanding of foreign information manipulation, its potential impact on communities and their role in addressing the threats.

Speaking to newsmen at the event, the Vice Chairman of the Christian Association of Nigeria (CAN), Benue State, Rev. Jonathan Ugbede, described misinformation and disinformation as big challenges bedevilling society, saying that most times they had created crises not only in Benue but across the nation.

While noting that misinformation and disinformation are capable of creating fear, tension and disharmony in society, Ugbede counselled that religious leaders should verify information before disseminating it, stressing that their sources must be credible, authentic and verifiable.

The CAN Vice Chairman said unverified claims, often attributed to unidentified sources, were frequently circulated and could create unnecessary panic, adding that religious leaders must exercise caution because of the influence they wield over their followers, who see their words as law.

Also, the Benue State representative of Jama’atu Nasril Islam (JNI), Malam Baba Ahmed, commended the initiative, describing it as timely and relevant to Benue State, which had experienced significant security and displacement challenges.

Ahmed called for greater tolerance and understanding among religious communities, stressing that peaceful coexistence and interfaith cooperation were essential to the unity and development of the state.

Ahmed, a participant, who was represented by the JNI State Chairman, Alhaji Garba Baba, reaffirmed the organisation’s commitment to promoting religious tolerance.

Also speaking, a traditional ruler from Apa Local Government Area (LGA), HRH Chief Solomon Audu, observed that community leaders sometimes received information and later discovered it was false after carrying out proper investigation.

He urged traditional and community leaders to collaborate in ensuring that information brought before them was verified before decisions were taken or actions initiated.

Earlier, the Editor of Alkalanci, Alhassan Bala, presented an overview of the organisation’s first project in Benue State and its activities.

The workshop also featured a presentation on the role of religious and community leaders in the digital age by Dr Peter Akunko of the Department of Philosophy, Moses Orshio Adasu University, Makurdi (MOAUM), alongside sessions on understanding misinformation, disinformation and Foreign Information Manipulation and Interference.

The post Alkalanci, British High Commission train Benue religious leaders against disinformation, FIMI appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Tinubu Approves Establishment Of University Of Public Relations, Leadership
description: President Bola Tinubu has approved the establishment of the University of Public Relations, Leadership, the first of its kind to advance specialised education, research, professional development and leadership training in public relations.Tinubu announced this at the 13th World Public Relations Foru
content:
President Bola Tinubu has approved the establishment of the University of Public Relations, Leadership, the first of its kind to advance specialised education, research, professional development and leadership training in public relations.

Tinubu announced this at the 13th World Public Relations Forum and the 51st Africa Public Relations Association Conference in Abuja on Wednesday.

He also described it as a forward-looking investment in human capital and the future of the communication profession.

The President also said it would provide an opportunity to develop a new generation of communication leaders equipped to respond to the demands of a rapidly changing global environment.

“An important outcome of hosting this forum is our determination to establish a lasting institutional legacy for the public relations profession,” Tinubu, who was represented by Vice President Kashim Shettima, said.

“In this regard, I am pleased to formally approve and support the establishment of the University of Public Relations and Leadership.”

He urged investors to explore Nigeria’s rich cultural heritage, tourism assets and the ingenuity of the Nigerian people.

“Naija no go carry last! Nigeria is a country of enormous possibilities. We are a nation of diverse cultures, talents and ideas, with a youthful population, a dynamic private sector and a strong determination to build a more prosperous future,” he added.

title: CBN, NNPC sign MoU to strengthen forex inflows, energy financing
description:
From Adanna Nnamani, Abuja
The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) and the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPC) have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to strengthen foreign exchange inflows, improve energy financing and deepen collaboration between the financial and energy sectors.
content:
From Adanna Nnamani, Abuja

The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) and the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPC) have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to strengthen foreign exchange inflows, improve energy financing and deepen collaboration between the financial and energy sectors.

Speaking at the signing ceremony in Abuja on Wednesday, the CBN Governor, Olayemi Cardoso, said the agreement would strengthen macroeconomic management and support economic growth, noting that NNPC’s operations were central to Nigeria’s foreign exchange inflows, reserves and fiscal revenue.

He said the CBN, as custodian of key operational foreign exchange accounts, played a critical role in ensuring the timely, secure and transparent settlement of oil and gas proceeds into the Federation Account and other designated government accounts.

Cardoso said efficient account management, transfers and liquidity support would improve fiscal revenue and provide more predictable foreign exchange inflows into the market.

He added that the apex bank would leverage its convening power to attract global financial institutions to support financing in the gas sector.

The CBN governor said the MoU would formalise and strengthen the longstanding relationship between both institutions, adding that regular engagements involving the NNPC, oil-related companies and regulators had produced positive outcomes.

He said the framework would cover consultations, information exchange, oil and gas asset monetisation, operational approvals, payment automation, digital innovation, cybersecurity, capacity development, regulatory alignment, ethics and risk management.

He said: “Today’s occasion marks a significant milestone in the development of stronger macroeconomic management. We believe this MoU will further the goals of providing enduring economic stability and sustainable prosperity for all Nigerians.

“The oil and gas sector is an important driver of Nigeria’s economic growth. The operations of NNPC Limited therefore remain central to Nigeria’s external reserves, fiscal revenue and foreign exchange inflows, and contribute significantly to economic activity.

“As custodian of NNPC Limited’s key operational foreign currency accounts, the Central Bank of Nigeria plays a critical role in ensuring the timely, secure and transparent settlement of oil and gas proceeds into the Federation Account and other designated government accounts.

“Our continued collaboration in efficient account management, funds transfer and liquidity support directly contributes to macroeconomic stability by ensuring the availability of revenue to achieve fiscal mandates and predictable inflows into the foreign exchange markets.

“As the financial system adapts to the global push for energy transition, the CBN is well positioned to collaborate with NNPC Limited by exercising its convening power to attract global institutions with financial structures that can help develop Nigeria’s vast natural gas resources.”

Also speaking, the Group Chief Executive Officer of NNPC Limited, Bayo Ojulari, said the agreement would provide a structured framework for collaboration between the national oil company and the monetary authority.

Ojulari said the energy and financial systems were interconnected, stressing that crude oil and gas remained major sources of foreign exchange for the country.

He noted that, following the Petroleum Industry Act (PIA), NNPC had become a commercial entity and needed stronger collaboration with the monetary authority to support its operations, based on transparency and accountability.

According to him, the MoU would deepen trade, improve foreign exchange inflows, support the repatriation of export proceeds and create financial structures to enable NNPC to raise capital using its balance sheet and assets.

He said the CBN’s convening role would also help the company engage financial institutions and develop financing opportunities.

Ojulari added that the agreement would cover digital payments, innovation, cybersecurity, data protection, regulatory compliance and risk management.

He said both institutions would establish a joint steering committee and working committee, co-chaired by their representatives, to monitor implementation and track agreed key performance indicators.

“Today’s signing is about one simple idea: Nigeria’s energy sector and its financial system are not separate stories. They are one story.

“Crude oil and gas remain among the most important sources of foreign exchange for our nation, with NNPC Limited designated as the national oil company.

“A commercial national energy company needs a clear, structured relationship with the country’s monetary authority, built on transparency rather than one-off requests. This MoU provides that structure, setting out the principles and framework through which our two institutions will collaborate at the meeting point between energy and finance.

“The anticipated collaboration will create opportunities for economic growth and financial stability, helping NNPC position its initiatives in line with national monetary and energy objectives. It will explore credible opportunities to deepen trade and address challenges affecting the enhancement of foreign exchange inflows, which will significantly support the flow of export proceeds into the Nigerian economy.

“Both organisations will collaborate in the areas of energy financing and the monetisation of hydrocarbons, working together on financial structures that will help NNPC raise capital on the strength of its own balance sheet and assets,” Ojulari stated.

The post CBN, NNPC sign MoU to strengthen forex inflows, energy financing appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Tinubu seeks Reps’ approval to decriminalise attempted suicide
description:
By Gift Chapi Odekina, Abuja



President Bola Tinubu has transmitted the National Mental Health (Amendment) Bill, 2026, to the House of Representatives for consideration, seeking to decriminalise attempted suicide and provide support for persons who attempt to take their lives.







The President
content:
By Gift Chapi Odekina, Abuja

President Bola Tinubu has transmitted the National Mental Health (Amendment) Bill, 2026, to the House of Representatives for consideration, seeking to decriminalise attempted suicide and provide support for persons who attempt to take their lives.

The President’s request was contained in a letter dated November 10, 2026, addressed to the Speaker of the House, Tajudeen Abbas, and read on the floor of the House during plenary on Wednesday.

In the letter, Tinubu said the proposed legislation sought to amend the National Mental Health Act, No. 46, 2021, to remove the criminalisation of attempted suicide and introduce support measures for affected persons.

The President said the transmission was made pursuant to Section 58(2) of the 1999 Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, as amended.

The letter, titled, “Transmission of the National Mental Health (Amendment) Bill, 2026 for Consideration,” reads in part: “I forward, herewith, the National Mental Health (Amendment) Bill, 2026 for the kind consideration of the House of Representatives.”

Explaining the objective of the proposed amendment, Tinubu stated that the bill “seeks to amend the National Mental Health Act, No. 46, 2021 (the ‘Principal Act’) to decriminalise attempted suicide and to provide support to any person who attempts to commit suicide in Nigeria.”

He expressed appreciation to the House of Representatives and urged lawmakers to give the proposed legislation expeditious consideration.

If passed by the National Assembly and assented to by the President, the bill would change Nigeria’s existing legal framework on attempted suicide, shifting the approach towards providing support for affected persons rather than criminal prosecution.

The proposed amendment is expected to be considered by the House in line with its legislative procedures.

The post Tinubu seeks Reps’ approval to decriminalise attempted suicide appeared first on Vanguard News.
