title: Tinubu unveils public relations varsity in Nasarawa
description:
President Bola Tinubu on Wednesday formally unveiled the University of Public Relations and Leadership in Nasarawa State, as Nigeria seeks to strengthen its influence in the global communication industry and train a new generation of public relations professionals.
Tinubu was represented by Vice-Pre
content:
President Bola Tinubu on Wednesday formally unveiled the University of Public Relations and Leadership in Nasarawa State, as Nigeria seeks to strengthen its influence in the global communication industry and train a new generation of public relations professionals.

Tinubu was represented by Vice-President Kashim Shettima at the ceremony organised by Global Alliance World Public Relations Forum in Abuja.

The event attracted public relations practitioners, communication experts, government officials and business leaders from different parts of the world.

Shettima, speaking on behalf of the President, said, “It’s my singular honour and privilege to, on behalf of my boss, Bola Ahmed Tinubu, President and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, unveil and launch the University of Public Relations and Leadership in Nasarawa State.”

In his address, Tinubu described the proposed institution as a lasting legacy of Nigeria’s successful bid to host the global forum, saying it would advance specialised education, research, professional development and leadership training in public relations and strategic communication.

“In this regard, I am pleased to formally approve and support the establishment of the University of Public Relations and Leadership, a first-of-its-kind initiative designed to advance specialised education, research, professional development and leadership training in public relations, strategic communications and related disciplines,” he said.

The President said the university would provide opportunities to develop a new generation of communication leaders equipped to respond to the demands of a rapidly changing global environment.

He commended the Nigerian Institute of Public Relations, the Federal Ministry of Information and National Orientation and the Nasarawa State Government for their collaboration towards making the project a reality.

Tinubu also urged stakeholders to ensure that the institution develops into a centre of excellence with national, continental and international recognition.

Beyond the university announcement, the President challenged public relations professionals to uphold truth, transparency and accountability in an era when digital technologies and artificial intelligence are transforming how information is created, distributed and consumed.

Tinubu also used the international gathering to project Nigeria’s economic potential, urging foreign delegates to look beyond the conference venue and explore investment opportunities in the country’s entrepreneurial ecosystem, creative industries, tourism and other sectors.

The President urged the delegates to establish relationships with Nigerian institutions and businesses, explore partnerships and become ambassadors of the country’s positive image.

“We want you to leave Nigeria, Prof Justin Green, not only with new professional knowledge and friendships, but also with a deeper appreciation of our country and a renewed interest in its prospects.

“We hope that your experience here will encourage you to return, invest, collaborate, and become ambassadors of Nigeria’s positive story,” he said.

Earlier, the President of the Global Alliance for Public Relations and Communication Management, Prof Justin Green, disclosed how Nigerian officials mounted an intense push to secure the hosting rights of the 2026 forum.

Green said the President of the Nigerian Institute of Public Relations, Dr Ike Neliaku, the Minister of Information and National Orientation and the Nigerian Ambassador to Ireland repeatedly called him during the final stage of the bidding process.

He said, “As President of Global Alliance, I must be impartial to all country member bids. I’m not allowed a vote. But during the final scoring process, the adjudicating panel had only a few meters to go. Africa and Nigeria were doing well. But so too were other continents.”

According to Green, he initially declined Neliaku’s calls to avoid any suggestion of influencing the adjudication process.

The situation became more delicate when the Minister of Information also called him, prompting him to cancel the calls three times.

He said, “I didn’t know what to do. So I cancelled his call, not once, not twice, but three times. I’m sorry, Minister.”

Green said the Nigerian Ambassador to Ireland subsequently called him as the country intensified its efforts to secure the hosting rights.

He added, “This is how determined Nigeria was to secure the hosting rights for the whole of Africa. It is this African and Nigerian fighting spirit to win that has the world in Abuja today.”

Welcoming the delegates, Green said Nigeria had defeated competing countries to secure the hosting rights, adding that the event had brought the world to Abuja.

In a light-hearted moment, Green declared himself Nigerian for the duration of the event and produced a Nigerian passport, saying he is now a citizen of both Ireland and Nigeria.

“Today, today we are no longer visitors from around the world. We are all Nigerians. So, Your Excellency, I surrender my Irish passport to the Minister of Foreign Affairs to collect my new Nigerian passport,” he said.

Also speaking, the President of the Nigerian Institute of Public Relations, Dr Ike Neliaku, urged Africans to be more assertive in projecting the continent’s contributions to global civilisation.

Neliaku said Africa must stop allowing others to define its history and identity, insisting that the continent had a responsibility to confidently tell its own story.

“As you are aware, though they don’t want to agree, civilisation started from Africa. And we must be bold in saying so,” he said.

He explained that the decision to host the forum on a grand scale reflected the organisers’ determination to demonstrate Africa’s capacity to stage major international events.

Neliaku also acknowledged the contributions of international delegates who travelled from countries including France, Australia, Turkey, Malaysia, Kenya, Peru, Bangladesh, the United States and South Africa.

He said the organisers had adopted ‘No Wahala’ as their rallying expression, adding that they wanted the gathering to be remembered as the biggest, brightest and boldest.

The post Tinubu unveils public relations varsity in Nasarawa appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: COAS tasks Armoured Corps personnel on innovative tactics to tame terrorists, others
description:
From Molly Kilete, Abuja
The Chief of Army Staff (COAS), Lieutenant General Waidi Shaibu, has charged officers and soldiers of the Nigerian Army Armoured Corps to embrace emerging military technologies to boost the combat readiness of the army to tackle evolving security threats.
He said that emergi
content:
From Molly Kilete, Abuja

The Chief of Army Staff (COAS), Lieutenant General Waidi Shaibu, has charged officers and soldiers of the Nigerian Army Armoured Corps to embrace emerging military technologies to boost the combat readiness of the army to tackle evolving security threats.

He said that emerging threats, including the increasing use of drones and sophisticated weapons by terrorists, demand innovative tactics and greater integration of armour with infantry, artillery, aviation and other combat support elements.

The COAS, who gave the charge at the maiden Nigerian Army Armoured Corps Biennial Conference, held alongside the Corps Reunion and Pulling-Out Ceremony in Bauchi State, said that the ongoing expansion of the Nigerian Army by the Federal Government must be complemented by modern equipment, skilled personnel and enhanced operational capabilities.

Lt Gen. Shaibu, while noting that the expansion of the Nigerian Army by President Bola Ahmed Tinubu had increased the responsibilities of the Armoured Corps, which now has four divisions, 10 brigades, 11 reconnaissance battalions and 26 tank battalions, said that the growing force structure required corresponding investments in modern combat platforms, specialised training, maintenance and logistics to ensure the operational effectiveness of newly established formations.

The army chief said that the ongoing rehabilitation of armoured fighting vehicles was expected to increase operationally available platforms by over 50 per cent, while newly procured driving and weapon-handling simulators would enhance training at the Nigerian Army Armour School.

Reaffirming his directive to “Train Better to Fight Better”, the COAS charged the Corps to prioritise realistic training, technological adaptation and equipment readiness to produce agile, professional and combat-ready troops capable of meeting the demands of army expansion and contemporary warfare.

Earlier, in his address, the Commander of the Nigerian Army Armoured Corps, Major General Umar Bichi Abubakar, described the conference as a strategic platform for professional development, knowledge sharing and improved operational effectiveness. He assured that the biennial conference would become a permanent feature of the Corps’ professional calendar.

Also speaking, the Governor of Bauchi State, Senator Bala Mohammed, represented by his Deputy, Rt Hon Mohammed Auwal Jatau, commended the Nigerian Army for its sacrifices and commitment to national security, pledging continued support of the state government for its operations.

title: Convoy attack: WoPU hails Tinubu over clemency to 78 suspects
description:
By Victor Ahiuma-Young



Working People United (WoPU) has commended President Bola Tinubu for granting clemency to the 78 individuals arrested in connection with the attack on his presidential convoy in Abuja, describing the decision as an act of statesmanship, magnanimity and compassionate leaders
content:
By Victor Ahiuma-Young

Working People United (WoPU) has commended President Bola Tinubu for granting clemency to the 78 individuals arrested in connection with the attack on his presidential convoy in Abuja, describing the decision as an act of statesmanship, magnanimity and compassionate leadership.

In a statement by its National Coordinator-General, Prince Williams Akporeha, the group said the President’s decision demonstrated his commitment to national unity, reconciliation and peace despite the gravity of the incident.

WoPU said the gesture reflected Tinubu’s willingness to prioritise forgiveness and national harmony over confrontation.

According to the statement, “President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has once again demonstrated the depth of his compassion, fatherly disposition, and unwavering commitment to the welfare of all Nigerians.

“By extending clemency to the 78 suspects arrested over the attack on his convoy, the President has shown that leadership is not merely about the exercise of authority but also about mercy, understanding, and the pursuit of national harmony.”

The group described the decision as a demonstration of the President’s belief in second chances and peaceful coexistence, adding that it would help prevent the incident from deepening divisions in the country.

WoPU said the gesture was consistent with the objectives of the Renewed Hope Agenda, which seeks to build an inclusive, prosperous and stable Nigeria.

It urged Nigerian youths to emulate the President’s example by embracing dialogue, patience and responsible civic engagement.

The movement also cautioned young people against allowing themselves to be used by individuals or groups seeking to promote violence and instability for political interests.

“It is imperative for Nigerian youths to remain vigilant and responsible. They must resist every attempt by unscrupulous elements to use them as instruments of violence, lawlessness, and political disruption.

“The future of our nation lies in peaceful participation, constructive engagement, and unwavering faith in democratic institutions,” the statement added.

The group also urged youths to appreciate the administration’s policies and reforms, which it said were designed to promote long-term economic growth, social stability and national development.

It reaffirmed its support for the Tinubu administration’s reforms and developmental initiatives, expressing confidence that the Renewed Hope Agenda would deliver positive outcomes for workers, entrepreneurs, artisans, professionals and other Nigerians.

WoPU, a civic and socio-political movement comprising workers, traders, artisans, professionals, entrepreneurs and grassroots stakeholders across the country, said it would continue to mobilise support for the President’s vision of a prosperous and united Nigeria beyond 2027.

title: Police arrest four suspected armed robbers in Cross River
description:
The Cross River State Police Command has arrested four suspected armed robbers in connection with two reported cases of motorcycle snatching in Akamkpa Local Government Area of the state.
The suspects were identified as Oyo Effiong Nakanda, 40; Udeme Bright Felix, 23; Saviour Victor Felicia, 18; and
content:
The Cross River State Police Command has arrested four suspected armed robbers in connection with two reported cases of motorcycle snatching in Akamkpa Local Government Area of the state.

The suspects were identified as Oyo Effiong Nakanda, 40; Udeme Bright Felix, 23; Saviour Victor Felicia, 18; and Moses Ernest Felicia, 17.

In a statement issued in Calabar on Wednesday by the state Police Public Relations Officer, ASP Sunday Eitokpah, the police said the arrest followed a credible tip-off from a member of the public.

He said the tip-off led to an intelligence-led operation at about 5:47 a.m. on Wednesday, 18 November 2026.

The statement read, “The Cross River State Police Command has arrested four suspected armed robbers identified as Oyo Effiong Nakanda, male, 40; Udeme Bright Felix, male, 23; Saviour Victor Felicia, male, 18; and Moses Ernest Felicia, male, 17, in connection with two reported cases of motorcycle snatching in Akamkpa Local Government Area.

“The arrests followed a credible tip-off from a member of the public, which led to an intelligence-led operation at about 5:47 a.m. on Wednesday, 18 November 2026. The information identified a suspected hideout along the Calabar–Ikom Highway, before Ekomita Junction.”

The police spokesman said operatives of the Violent Crime Response Unit, Sector 2, Akamkpa, mobilised to the location and arrested the suspects. A machete and suspected criminal charms were recovered during the operation.

“The suspects are currently being investigated in connection with two separate incidents of motorcycle snatching reported at Hitech Junction and Usang Road, Akamkpa LGA,” the statement read.

Eitokpah said investigation was ongoing to establish their possible involvement in the incidents, recover other weapons, identify and arrest other possible accomplices, and determine whether they were connected to other criminal activities.

The Commissioner of Police in the state, CP Ajo Ordue, commended the operatives for their prompt response and acknowledged the contribution of the informant.

He reaffirmed the Command’s commitment to intelligence-led policing and urged residents to sustain collaboration with the Police by providing credible and timely information.

He assured the public that the investigation would be pursued professionally and encouraged residents to report suspicious activities or emergencies through the Command’s Control Room numbers: 0704 177 7060 and 0705 335 5415.

“I commend the operatives for their prompt response. I hereby urge residents to sustain collaboration with the Police by providing credible and timely information to us. Ensure you report suspicious activities or emergencies through the Command’s Control Room numbers: 0704 177 7060 and 0705 335 5415,” he added.

The arrests come amid continued police action against motorcycle theft and robbery in the state. Earlier this month, the Command busted a cross-border syndicate that allegedly stole motorcycles and tricycles in Akwa Ibom and sold them in Cross River.

In April, police in Calabar arrested a 26-year-old man who allegedly attacked a motorcyclist with a machete and fled with his motorcycle and phone.

The Calabar–Ikom Highway, where the suspects were found, has also featured in earlier arrests over alleged robberies of travellers.

title: Reps demand NNPCL accountability, warn on PIA implementation
description:
By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja



The House of Representatives has called for stronger accountability in the petroleum sector, warning that poor implementation of the Petroleum Industry Act (PIA) could undermine the reforms intended to transform the industry.







The House said the success of the re
content:
By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja

The House of Representatives has called for stronger accountability in the petroleum sector, warning that poor implementation of the Petroleum Industry Act (PIA) could undermine the reforms intended to transform the industry.

The House said the success of the reforms would depend on transparency, institutional discipline and responsible corporate governance.

The position was reinforced at a conference on PIA implementation organised by the House in collaboration with the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPCL) and other partners in Abuja.

Speaking after the conference, Deputy Spokesman of the House, Philip Agbese, commended NNPCL Group Chief Executive Officer, Bayo Ojulari, for promoting transparency and constructive engagement with the National Assembly.

Agbese, a Labour Party member representing a constituency in Benue State, said engagement between the legislature and the national oil company was necessary to ensure that the objectives of the PIA translated into measurable improvements in the petroleum industry.

He urged other government agencies to adopt similar open-door approaches in their dealings with the legislature, stressing that transparency and institutional collaboration were essential to effective governance.

The conference, themed, “Petroleum Industry Act Implementation: The PIA, Corporate Governance and Legislative Oversight,” was organised in collaboration with the Office of the Speaker of the House, Rep. Abbas Tajudeen.

Declaring the conference open, Abbas, who was represented by the House Leader, Julius Ihonvbere, said the PIA was designed to establish a transparent, commercially viable, accountable and investment-friendly petroleum industry.

He, however, warned that the enactment of the law alone would not guarantee the desired reforms without effective implementation.

The Speaker said the transformation of the Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation into a commercially oriented company, the establishment of independent regulatory institutions and the introduction of a host community development framework were intended to address longstanding structural weaknesses in the industry.

He stressed that NNPCL’s commercial autonomy must be matched with corporate accountability, noting that the freedom to make business decisions must come with responsibility for their consequences.

Abbas also cautioned against turning legislative oversight into unnecessary interference in the company’s legitimate commercial operations, saying oversight should promote transparency, protect public resources and ensure compliance with statutory responsibilities.

He identified crude oil theft, pipeline vandalism, production constraints, infrastructure deficiencies, investment uncertainty and regulatory bottlenecks as major challenges confronting the industry.

The Speaker disclosed that the 10th House had continued to engage the petroleum sector through committee interventions, investigations and conferences, particularly on crude oil theft, pipeline surveillance arrangements and the protection of critical energy infrastructure.

He urged participants to identify gaps in the implementation of the PIA and recommend areas requiring legislative intervention, while distinguishing between challenges caused by inadequate laws and those resulting from failure to enforce existing provisions.

According to him, the ultimate test of the PIA would be increased oil production, greater investment, improved energy security, stronger domestic refining capacity, enhanced government revenue and tangible benefits for oil-producing communities.

Agbese described the conference as a practical demonstration of the Speaker’s commitment to an open parliament where lawmakers and critical institutions could engage on issues affecting national development.

He said legislative oversight should go beyond routine investigations to constructive engagement capable of producing practical solutions and strengthening public institutions.

The post Reps demand NNPCL accountability, warn on PIA implementation appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Viral Video: ‘We recovered 12 AK-47 rifles, kidnap victims’ – Military defends engagement with bandits
description:
By Kingsley Omonobi



The military has defended its engagement with armed bandits in Kwara State, dismissing allegations of fraternisation with terrorists. They added that the interaction led to the recovery of 12 AK-47 rifles and the release of 10 kidnapped persons.







The Joint Task Force, Op
content:
By Kingsley Omonobi

The military has defended its engagement with armed bandits in Kwara State, dismissing allegations of fraternisation with terrorists. They added that the interaction led to the recovery of 12 AK-47 rifles and the release of 10 kidnapped persons.

The Joint Task Force, Operation Savannah Shield, said the engagement, captured in a video circulating on social media, was part of a security initiative to recover illegal weapons and secure the freedom of abducted persons.

In a statement, the task force said the interaction involving military personnel, Department of State Services (DSS) operatives and the armed bandits should not be misconstrued as a compromise of the Armed Forces’ responsibilities.

The statement, signed by the Acting Deputy Director, Army Public Relations, 9 Division/Operation Savannah Shield, Lieutenant Colonel Ibrahim Shittu, said the armed elements had indicated their willingness to surrender their weapons and release their captives.

Shittu said the development followed sustained military operations that had put the bandits under intense pressure, leaving them with the options of surrendering or being neutralised.

He said the engagement resulted in the recovery of 12 AK-47 rifles and the release of 10 kidnapped persons.

The task force described the outcome as evidence of the effectiveness of its non-kinetic approach, which complements ongoing military offensives against terrorism and banditry.

It explained that its operational strategy combined military action, intelligence-driven engagements and other non-kinetic measures to address security challenges.

The task force added that individuals willing to surrender would undergo appropriate security screening and other applicable legal procedures.

Shittu also said surrendered combatants must not be harmed at the point of surrender, in line with the Law of Armed Conflict, international best practices and established rules of engagement.

He stressed that accepting the surrender of armed elements was a recognised and legitimate military outcome, not an indication of unprofessional conduct or compromise.

The task force reaffirmed the Armed Forces’ commitment to defending Nigeria’s territorial integrity and protecting lives and property.

It urged members of the public to disregard what it described as misleading interpretations of the video and avoid spreading unverified information capable of undermining ongoing security operations.

Operation Savannah Shield assured Nigerians that it would continue to provide updates on its activities through its official communication channels.

title: Nigeria’s security crisis complex, varies by region — Bishop Anagbe
description:
By Chidi Nkwopara



OWERRI — The Catholic Bishop of Makurdi Diocese, Most Rev. Wilfred Chikpa Anagbe, has described Nigeria’s security situation as troubling and complex, saying the nature of violence and insecurity varies across different parts of the country.



Anagbe spoke in Owerri while highl
content:
By Chidi Nkwopara

OWERRI — The Catholic Bishop of Makurdi Diocese, Most Rev. Wilfred Chikpa Anagbe, has described Nigeria’s security situation as troubling and complex, saying the nature of violence and insecurity varies across different parts of the country.

Anagbe spoke in Owerri while highlighting the challenges faced by displaced persons in parts of Nigeria.

He said religious identity was central to some attacks, while other incidents were linked to criminal banditry, land and resource disputes, communal tensions and failures of protection.

“The security situation in Nigeria is complex and varies from place to place. In some incidents, the religious identity of victims is central to the violence; in others, insecurity is also connected with criminal banditry, land and resource disputes, communal tensions and failures of protection.

“We must be courageous enough to name religiously targeted violence where the evidence supports that conclusion, and responsible enough to verify claims before repeating them.

“Accuracy does not weaken our advocacy. It gives it credibility, protects vulnerable people and makes it harder for those responsible for injustice to dismiss the truth,” he said.

The bishop urged public office holders and citizens to place the safety and dignity of Nigerians above party interests, ethnic loyalties and social standing.

He challenged people to reflect on whether political or ethnic affiliations had prevented them from speaking out when others needed protection.

“Standing with persecuted Christians does not require us to turn away from the suffering of others. It asks us to stand firmly with those who are targeted while treating every person with the respect the Gospel demands.

“Let us not allow a person’s political affiliation, ethnic background, wealth, or position in society to determine whose suffering deserves our concern.

“Our different backgrounds and responsibilities should become resources for a common mission: protecting people, pursuing justice, helping families rebuild, and defending the freedom of worship,” Anagbe said.

He noted that behind every report of an attack were families and communities dealing with fear, displacement, loss and uncertainty.

According to him, these include parents worried about their children’s safety, families forced to abandon their homes, communities struggling to rebuild and worshippers uncertain whether their plight is being heard.

Anagbe recalled that he had taken the concerns of affected communities from his Makurdi Diocese to national and international platforms, stressing that public awareness must translate into practical action.

He said efforts should focus on freeing communities from persecution, insecurity, banditry and violence.

“We must listen to the displaced family, the grieving widow, the child whose education has been interrupted, the parish community living under threat and the person who has lost the means to support a household.

“We must not allow repeated reports of violence to make suffering seem ordinary or routine, nor should we reduce the experience of affected communities to statistics or political arguments hinged on the ulterior benefits of security votes.

“Every human life has a dignity that demands our attention, and every credible account of suffering calls for a response marked by compassion, truth and responsible action,” he said.

title: Nigeria’s transition will fail if young businesses can’t get reliable power, Skills, trusted access to markets
description:
A Nigerian Founder, Sunny Idoko has said that Nigeria’s transition will fail if young businesses cannot get reliable power, skills and trusted access to markets while climate negotiators at COP31 debated emissions targets.
Sunny, founder and board member of SunnySide Eco Hub, is seeking $10 million
content:
A Nigerian Founder, Sunny Idoko has said that Nigeria’s transition will fail if young businesses cannot get reliable power, skills and trusted access to markets while climate negotiators at COP31 debated emissions targets.

Sunny, founder and board member of SunnySide Eco Hub, is seeking $10 million to build a youth-focused entrepreneurial hub in Lagos. He is pitching it not as a commercial workspace, but as development infrastructure for Nigeria’s youth economy.

In development terms, the problem he describes is familiar. Nigeria does not lack talent or enterprise. It lacks the systems that allow small firms to survive, grow and export.

“Africa has no shortage of young people with ideas,” Idoko said. “What is often missing is the environment that helps those ideas move from conversation to reality.”

For Idoko, sustainability starts with economics.

Unreliable electricity, he said, acts as a daily tax on productivity. Small firms spend money on fuel, generators and downtime instead of hiring, training or expanding. For freelancers and creative businesses operating on thin margins, that tax is often fatal.

“A lot of businesses run on traditional energy, fossil fuel, and rely on electricity distribution companies. But it is not reliable, and the cost of energy is going up,” he said. “How can businesses operate sustainably without these barriers?”

Inside the planned Lagos Island hub, power and connectivity will be built in. Members will not have to buy fuel, power generators, or pay separate electricity and internet bills.

The building is designed with LEED and EDGE principles for a net-zero future, with solar energy and storage, water recycling, energy-efficient systems, low-emission building materials, modular steel construction and passive design.

“Sustainability is at the core of Sunny Side,” the project states. “Use less. Waste less. Create more value.”

The model is to treat clean energy not as an add-on, but as basic business infrastructure that allows young firms to compete.

The second barrier, Idoko said, is trust.

Foreign businesses often view Nigeria as a risky venture because of a trust factor and an information gap, he said. Nigerian businesses, meanwhile, struggle to prove themselves to the world.

That gap keeps foreign capital away and keeps Nigerian talent undervalued. Foreign companies recruit Nigerian tech professionals, he said, but those professionals rarely get access to markets beyond Nigeria.

“We are selling within ourselves, consuming within ourselves, and we are locked in with the networks we know,” Idoko said.

SunnySide is therefore positioned as a market entry launchpad as well as a hub — offering market access and linkage, product demos and showrooms, pilot programmes and partnerships, business networking, community engagement and a gateway to West Africa.

It is designed as a two-way bridge: African businesses to the world, and foreign businesses to verified African partners.

“This is the time for Africa,” Idoko said. “There needs to be that synergy” between businesses coming into Africa and African businesses going out.

The Lagos hub will bring together tech entrepreneurs, photographers, designers, beauticians, makeup artists, hairdressers, freelancers and founders in one community-led ecosystem.

It will include workstations under the name The Hive, a creative hub, a beauty studio, a cafe called Wish Cafe, and learning, wellness and community spaces for mentoring, skills development and events.

The aim, according to the project, is to help young Nigerians discover opportunities, build businesses, learn new skills, meet mentors, find collaborators, access networks, experiment with ideas, showcase their work, and connect with investors and incubators.

title: Army commissions 20 transit flats, officers’ mess in Bauchi
description:
By Henry Obetta



The Nigerian Army has commissioned 20 transit flats and a modern officers’ mess at Obienu Barracks, Bauchi State, as part of efforts to improve personnel welfare, boost troops’ morale and enhance operational effectiveness.







The Chief of Army Staff (COAS), Lieutenant General
content:
By Henry Obetta

The Nigerian Army has commissioned 20 transit flats and a modern officers’ mess at Obienu Barracks, Bauchi State, as part of efforts to improve personnel welfare, boost troops’ morale and enhance operational effectiveness.

The Chief of Army Staff (COAS), Lieutenant General Waidi Shaibu, who commissioned the facilities on Wednesday, said the Army’s modernisation drive went beyond the acquisition of military equipment to include improved accommodation, infrastructure and welfare for personnel and their families.

According to a statement by the Acting Director, Army Public Relations, Colonel Appolonia Anele, Shaibu described decent accommodation and a conducive living environment as critical to troops’ morale, family stability and operational readiness.

He explained that the 20 transit flats were designed to address accommodation challenges faced by personnel posted to the barracks for assignments, military courses and other temporary engagements.

The COAS said the newly constructed officers’ mess, named the Lieutenant General Waidi Shaibu Officers’ Mess, featured modern accommodation, a Hall of Fame and recreational facilities to promote professional interaction, esprit de corps and institutional pride among officers.

He commended the Nigerian Army Armoured Corps and other stakeholders for the successful completion of the projects, describing them as evidence of the Army’s commitment to personnel welfare and prudent management of resources.

Shaibu urged personnel to ensure proper maintenance of the facilities to guarantee their sustainability and continued usefulness.

Reaffirming his commitment to the welfare of troops and their families, the Army chief said investments in accommodation, healthcare, education and other welfare programmes would continue alongside the force’s expansion and modernisation efforts.

He stressed that a well-motivated, professionally trained and adequately supported force was essential to sustaining operational successes against terrorism, insurgency, banditry and other security threats facing the country.

title: Tinubu’s economic gains bypass ordinary Nigerians, Makinde campaign tells Alake
description:
By Luminous Jannamike







ABUJA – The Makinde-Daura Presidential Campaign Organisation has faulted the Minister of Solid Minerals, Dele Alake, over his defence of President Bola Tinubu’s economic policies, saying the reforms have delivered gains for government institutions and corporate interests
content:
By Luminous Jannamike

ABUJA – The Makinde-Daura Presidential Campaign Organisation has faulted the Minister of Solid Minerals, Dele Alake, over his defence of President Bola Tinubu’s economic policies, saying the reforms have delivered gains for government institutions and corporate interests but little relief to ordinary Nigerians.

The organisation said increased federation revenue, foreign exchange reforms and the clearance of outstanding foreign exchange obligations had not translated into better living conditions, as millions of Nigerians continued to struggle with rising food prices, transportation costs, electricity tariffs and school fees.

In a statement by its Director of Strategic Communications, Richard Nnanna Ihediwa, the organisation was responding to Alake’s challenge to Nigerians to name any civilian administration that had achieved more across the socio-economic and political spectrum within three years or identify a viable alternative to Tinubu’s economic reforms introduced in May 2023.

Ihediwa accused the minister of measuring economic progress through macroeconomic and institutional adjustments while overlooking the daily struggles of ordinary Nigerians.

“For the average Nigerian, prosperity was not shared; austerity was distributed universally,” he said.

While acknowledging that previous administrations lacked the political will to remove petrol subsidy and unify the exchange rate, the campaign organisation faulted Tinubu for implementing the reforms simultaneously without adequate social protection measures.

It argued that combining subsidy removal with currency devaluation and electricity tariff increases imposed multiple economic shocks on households without sufficient measures to cushion their effects.

“Taking the bullet is admirable only if you protect the citizens standing behind you,” Ihediwa said.

On petrol subsidy removal, the organisation agreed that the previous arrangement was unsustainable and vulnerable to corruption but argued that the government should have provided mass transit alternatives, strengthened domestic refining capacity and introduced effective measures to contain transportation costs before or alongside the policy.

It also questioned Alake’s description of the clearance of $7 billion in foreign exchange backlogs and restoration of international card transactions as benefits of exchange rate unification.

According to Ihediwa, those gains primarily addressed the concerns of foreign investors, multinational companies and corporate institutions, rather than the immediate needs of Nigerians struggling with the cost of living.

He argued that celebrating improved corporate foreign exchange liquidity while local manufacturers battled high borrowing costs and exchange rate volatility reflected a disconnect between the government’s economic priorities and the realities of citizens.

The campaign organisation also rejected Alake’s argument that the reforms were necessary sacrifices to lay the foundation for future prosperity, insisting that their success should be judged by the improvements they delivered to citizens.

“Great economic reforms across history are remembered for the magnitude of prosperity they deliver and not for sufferings inflicted,” Ihediwa said.

The organisation called for what it described as a governance reset, anchored on expanded economic opportunities, fiscal discipline and macroeconomic stability that would translate into tangible improvements in citizens’ lives.

title: Explosion heard in Riyadh, Saudi capital; missiles intercepted
description:
A powerful explosion rattled homes in Riyadh on Wednesday, AFP journalists and residents said, as Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis pressed their campaign of attacks against the kingdom.



The Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis also said they intercepted two cruise missiles — the latest in weeks of
content:
A powerful explosion rattled homes in Riyadh on Wednesday, AFP journalists and residents said, as Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis pressed their campaign of attacks against the kingdom.

The Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis also said they intercepted two cruise missiles — the latest in weeks of strikes targeting military, civilian and oil infrastructure.

Later on Wednesday, the coalition said it had intercepted two drones launched by the Houthis in the Riyadh and southern regions, after Saudi authorities had issued and later lifted an alert for the southern Sharurah governorate.

Residents said Wednesday’s explosion came without warning, with no mobile-phone alert issued beforehand as is usually the case during aerial threats.

“The explosion was extremely loud,” said a resident in northern Riyadh. “Hearing a blast without receiving a warning is very frightening.”

An AFP journalist said doors throughout her home swung open and the lights briefly went out.

The location of the explosion was not immediately clear, but residents told AFP they saw smoke near Riyadh’s airport in the northeast of the city.

In October, a deadly attack targeting Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport killed 14 people and injured hundreds, forcing the suspension of flights for two weeks.

Within minutes, the Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis said its air defences had intercepted and destroyed a cruise missile launched by the group towards the Riyadh region.

Earlier, the coalition had reported intercepting another cruise missile also heading for the same region.

Saudi civil defence authorities also said they had activated early warning systems in the southern regions of Jazan, Najran and Khamis Mushait, near the Yemeni border.

The Saudi-led coalition, which backs neighbouring Yemen’s internationally recognised government in its war with the Houthis, has battled a surge in attacks since hostilities reignited in July.

The long-running civil war in Yemen, one of the world’s poorest countries, had been largely dormant after a ceasefire went into effect in 2022.

The Houthis are now nearing Aden, the government’s interim capital, having made sweeping territorial gains since the war resumed.

Since the summer, more than 1,600 people have been killed and over 300,000 displaced by the fighting, according to the United Nations.

title: Reps defer electricity tariff motion, await reform panel report
description:
The House of Representatives Ad-hoc Committee on Power Sector Reform is expected to present its findings to the Green Chamber next Wednesday, a development that could trigger fresh legislative interventions in the electricity sector.
The committee’s report came up during Wednesday’s plenary as lawma
content:
The House of Representatives Ad-hoc Committee on Power Sector Reform is expected to present its findings to the Green Chamber next Wednesday, a development that could trigger fresh legislative interventions in the electricity sector.

The committee’s report came up during Wednesday’s plenary as lawmakers considered a motion seeking a probe of the Nigerian Electricity Regulatory Commission’s Service-Based Tariff System and the classification of electricity consumers into Bands A to E.

Sponsored by Kwara lawmaker, Aluko Yinka, the motion raised concerns about alleged discriminatory electricity distribution practices and the failure of distribution companies (DisCos) to deliver the minimum supply hours promised to customers under the tariff arrangement.

Providing an update on the committee’s assignment, a member of the committee, David Agada, said the panel had completed consultations with regulatory agencies, electricity distribution and generation companies, as well as other stakeholders in the industry.

He disclosed that the committee had also “undertaken visits to Lagos and Rivers states to interact with stakeholders and assess the difficulties faced by electricity consumers.”

According to Agada, “the investigation covered outstanding electricity-related debts owed by government ministries, departments and agencies.”

The disclosure, however, prompted Speaker of the House, Tajudeen Abbas, to question why the committee was still functioning, given his earlier directive dissolving all ad-hoc committees and requesting the submission of their reports.

Members of the panel explained that they had concluded their assignment and were preparing to submit their findings the following week.

Abbas subsequently directed the House to defer consideration of Aluko’s motion until the committee presents its report on Wednesday. The motion was accordingly stepped down.

Earlier, Aluko told the House that NERC introduced the Service-Based Tariff System to ensure that electricity charges reflected the quality and duration of supply available to consumers.

He said the policy was designed to improve accountability in electricity distribution by making customers pay according to the level of service they received.

However, the lawmaker argued that its implementation had produced unequal access to electricity, “with affluent neighbourhoods, commercial districts and high-profile consumers enjoying relatively better supply than rural and low-income communities.”

He expressed concern that even customers classified under Band A, who were entitled to a minimum of 20 hours of electricity daily, were not consistently receiving the stipulated supply.

He added that consumers in Bands B to E continued to endure lengthy power outages despite paying electricity bills under the existing tariff structure.

Aluko also faulted the frequent increase in electricity tariffs, arguing that the higher charges had increased the financial burden on households and businesses without delivering corresponding improvements in power supply.

He accused some DisCos of resorting to practices such as “targeted load shedding against consumers in lower bands, estimated billing and arbitrary transfers of customers between tariff categories.”

The lawmaker further highlighted the metering gap in the electricity market, noting that millions of consumers remained without prepaid meters and were consequently vulnerable to inaccurate billing and possible exploitation.

He warned that the combination of high tariffs, unreliable supply and questionable billing practices was placing additional pressure on small businesses, undermining industrial activities and constraining economic growth.

According to him, access to affordable and reliable electricity was critical to economic development, employment generation and poverty reduction.

As part of the proposed intervention, Aluko urged the Federal Ministry of Power and NERC to review and suspend the existing band-based tariff arrangement pending wider consultations with stakeholders.

He also called for an investigation by the House Committee on Power into alleged discriminatory practices by electricity distribution companies, with a directive that the committee submit its findings within four weeks for further legislative action.

The motion was, however, stepped down following the Speaker’s directive that lawmakers await the findings of the Ad-hoc Committee on Power Sector Reform before proceeding with the matter.

The Service-Based Tariff System, introduced by NERC in 2020, was designed to link electricity tariffs to guaranteed minimum daily supply hours. Under the arrangement, customers in higher service bands pay higher tariffs in exchange for longer periods of electricity supply.

However, complaints over failure to meet promised supply levels, inadequate metering, estimated billing and tariff increases have continued to generate public concern and calls for regulatory intervention.

The House is expected to consider the committee’s recommendations when the report is presented on Wednesday.

title: Police tighten security for Tinubu rally, Obi visit
description:
The Anambra State Police Command has intensified security operations across the state ahead of President Bola Tinubu’s re-election campaign rally in Awka and a town hall meeting by the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, in Onitsha.



The two political engage
content:
The Anambra State Police Command has intensified security operations across the state ahead of President Bola Tinubu’s re-election campaign rally in Awka and a town hall meeting by the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, in Onitsha.

The two political engagements are scheduled for Thursday and Friday, respectively, as political activities gather momentum ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The Anambra State Presidential Campaign Council for Tinubu’s re-election is scheduled to hold a mega rally tagged “SoluTinubu 2027” on Thursday, November 19, at Dr Alex Ekwueme Square, Awka.

Obi, a former governor of the state, is expected to hold a town hall meeting with residents at 2pm on Friday, November 20, at the Archbishop C.J. Patterson Building, All Saints Cathedral, Onitsha.

In a statement on Wednesday, the Police Public Relations Officer, SP Tochukwu Ikenga, said the command had strengthened patrols, surveillance and personnel deployment in collaboration with other security agencies to ensure peaceful conduct of the events.

He said the measures were aimed at preventing criminal activities, maintaining public order and protecting residents, visitors and participants before, during and after the political engagements.

According to him, the command has strengthened operational coordination with sister security agencies, area commands, divisions and tactical units to provide adequate security coverage of strategic locations, public facilities, major roads and identified security flashpoints.

The statement said the security arrangements also included enhanced intelligence gathering and improved response capabilities to address emerging threats.

The Commissioner of Police, CP Nnanna Ama, was said to have directed operational commanders and personnel to remain vigilant, proactive and professional in the discharge of their duties.

Ama also emphasised that security operations must respect human rights and ensure that residents’ movements, businesses and other lawful activities were not unnecessarily disrupted.

The command cautioned members of the public, particularly social media users, against inflammatory publications, provocative statements and deliberate dissemination of false information capable of inciting violence or threatening public peace.

It, however, acknowledged citizens’ constitutional rights to freedom of expression, peaceful assembly and lawful public engagement, urging individuals and groups to exercise such rights responsibly.

“The police will take appropriate lawful measures against individuals whose actions constitute criminal offences, while ensuring that all enforcement activities are guided by due process, professionalism and respect for constitutionally guaranteed rights,” Ikenga said.

The command reassured residents, visitors and other members of the public of its commitment to providing a safe environment throughout the period of the scheduled activities.

It urged residents to remain calm, continue their lawful activities and cooperate with security personnel, while reporting suspicious movements, criminal activities and emerging threats to the nearest police station or through established emergency communication channels.

The police also called on traditional rulers, community leaders, youth organisations, civil society groups and media practitioners to support security efforts by promoting responsible communication, discouraging misinformation and encouraging peaceful coexistence.

The Tinubu campaign rally is being organised by the Anambra State Presidential Campaign Council, chaired by Governor Chukwuma Soludo, and is expected to attract supporters of the APC and the All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA).

The rally is anchored on the message of “progressives working together”.

Obi’s town hall meeting, on the other hand, is part of his nationwide political engagements ahead of the 2027 elections.

The former governor, who led Anambra State for eight years, remains a prominent political figure in the South-East.

The two events are expected to draw considerable political attention to the state as political parties intensify mobilisation ahead of the presidential election scheduled for January 16, 2027.

title: Alleged Medical Negligence: Coroner Inquest Into Death Of Adichie’s Son Begins January 2027
description: The Lagos State Coroner’s Court has fixed January 19, 2027, for the commencement of the inquest into the death of Nkanu, son of renowned Nigerian author, Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie, following the resolution of legal obstacles that had stalled the proceedings for months.The Coroner, Magistrate At
content:
The Lagos State Coroner’s Court has fixed January 19, 2027, for the commencement of the inquest into the death of Nkanu, son of renowned Nigerian author, Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie, following the resolution of legal obstacles that had stalled the proceedings for months.

The Coroner, Magistrate Atinuke Adetunji, sitting on Wednesday at the Magistrate Court, Igbosere, fixed the date after lawyers representing the parties agreed on the modalities for the inquest, including the sequence for calling witnesses.

The coroner directed all parties to file and exchange their clients’ statements on oath ahead of the next sitting and ensure the availability of their witnesses for the proceedings.

Nkanu Esege died on January 7, 2026, during medical procedures at Euracare Multi-Specialist Hospital in Lagos.

His parents, Adichie and her husband, Dr Ivara Esege, had accused the hospital of prima facie breaches of its duty of care in the treatment of their son.

Euracare, however, denied allegations of medical negligence, describing the claims as inaccurate and unfounded.

The inquest had been suspended indefinitely on June 3, 2026, following an interim restraining order issued by Justice Aishat Opesanwo of the Lagos State High Court, Ikoyi, on an ex parte application by Eurapharma Care Services Nigeria Limited.

The company had approached the High Court to challenge the legality of the coroner’s proceedings and sought to halt the inquest pending a judicial review.

But in a ruling delivered on October 12, 2026, Justice Opesanwo dismissed the application, holding that the cremation of the deceased’s body did not, in itself, deprive the coroner of the statutory jurisdiction to investigate the circumstances surrounding his death.

The judge also rejected the hospital’s objection to the sequence in which the coroner intended to receive statements and evidence from medical personnel and other relevant parties, finding no violation of its right to a fair hearing.

Justice Opesanwo held that the hospital’s objections were based on a misunderstanding of the statutory framework governing coroner’s inquiries and the nature of such proceedings.

At Wednesday’s sitting, counsel to the hospital, Senior Advocate of Nigeria, Taiwo Osipitan, informed the coroner that the proceedings before the High Court had been concluded and urged the court to fix a date for the commencement of the inquest.

Counsel to the deceased’s family and counsel to Atlantis, Chukwudi Enebeli and Abiodun Layonu, both Senior Advocates of Nigeria (SAN), did not oppose the request but sought time to respond to the statement on oath filed by Euracare’s Medical Director, Tosin Majekodunmi, which they said they had recently received.

The parties also agreed on the order in which witnesses would testify, with the family’s witnesses scheduled to appear first, followed by those of Atlantis, while Eurapharma Care Services Nigeria Limited will present its witnesses last.

The January 19 proceedings will mark the formal commencement of the inquest, which is expected to examine the circumstances surrounding the child’s death.

title: African ministers seek common front against fake news
description:
By John Alechenu



ABUJA — African Ministers of Information have called for a coordinated continental communication framework to combat misinformation, strengthen public trust in government and improve Africa’s representation in global narratives.







The ministers made the call at a high-level
content:
By John Alechenu

ABUJA — African Ministers of Information have called for a coordinated continental communication framework to combat misinformation, strengthen public trust in government and improve Africa’s representation in global narratives.

The ministers made the call at a high-level roundtable on responsible communication held in Abuja during the World Public Relations Forum (WPRF), where they advocated stronger collaboration among governments, professional capacity building and regular consultations to address the growing threat of misinformation.

Nigeria’s Minister of Information and National Orientation, Mohammed Idris, said the increasing influence of digital platforms and artificial intelligence had made credible, transparent and responsible communication essential to effective governance and public confidence.

Citing Nigeria’s experience with manipulated videos and misinformation, Idris warned that false narratives could distort public events, trigger unnecessary panic and erode citizens’ confidence in government.

“Technology has come to stay. AI is here to help us if we use it properly. The challenge is to ensure that what we communicate is credible and honest,” he said.

He proposed the revival of the Annual Conference of African Ministers of Information to provide a platform for regular dialogue, policy harmonisation and the development of a common continental position on issues affecting the continent.

“Collectively, we are stronger if we are united. There is a need to establish a robust system that enables us to look at Africa as one and speak with one voice once again,” Idris said.

The minister also urged African countries to support Nigeria’s UNESCO Category 2 International Media and Information Literacy Institute in Abuja, describing it as a continental resource for promoting responsible information consumption, particularly among young people.

“The Media and Information Literacy Institute is not just a Nigerian institution; it is a global opportunity. We should support it as part of a broader continental effort to promote media literacy, particularly among our young people,” he said.

Idris further called for stronger collaboration among African public broadcasters through content sharing and joint efforts to tell African stories from African perspectives.

Kenya’s Cabinet Secretary for Information, Communications and Digital Economy, William Kabogo Gitau, highlighted his country’s National Communication Policy, adopted in August 2026, as part of efforts to improve government communication and strengthen public engagement.

He said public trust was built through consistent government communication, accurate responses to citizens’ enquiries and effective delivery of public services.

“Trust between a state and its citizens is built through ordinary interactions: a question answered accurately, a service delivered as promised, and the same message from every part of the country. One government, one message, consistent,” he said.

Similarly, the Minister of Communication and Media and Government Spokesperson of the Republic of the Congo, Thierry Lezin Moungalla, called for a continental framework to institutionalise ministerial consultations, professional training, public-private media partnerships and joint content production.

He said government communication had evolved beyond its traditional public relations role and should become an integral part of government administration.

“Government communication is no longer simply a public relations function. It must be strategic and structural, embedded in the framework of government administration,” Moungalla said.

Zimbabwe’s Deputy Minister of Information, Publicity and Broadcasting Services, Dr Omphile Marupi, stressed the importance of grassroots communication structures in ensuring that government information reached citizens across communities.

“We must communicate not simply to be heard, but to be understood. We must not only disseminate information, but also listen, engage and respond to the concerns of our people,” he said.

The Chairman of the Information and Communications Committee of Ghana’s Parliament, Dr Abed-Nego Lamangin Bandim, called for increased investment in government communication, expanded rural connectivity and improved welfare for journalists.

Bandim disclosed that Ghana had earmarked 10 million Ghanaian cedis in its 2027 budget for journalists’ training, professional development and welfare.

Nigeria also indicated its readiness to host the next meeting of African Ministers of Information in Abuja.

title: PDP Launches 2027 Campaign In Katsina, Promises Free Healthcare, Others
description: The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) has officially launched its 2027 governorship campaign in Katsina State, with the party’s National Chairman,  Abdul-Rahman Mohammed, expressing confidence that the opposition will reclaim the state and build on what he described as the developmental legacy of
content:
The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) has officially launched its 2027 governorship campaign in Katsina State, with the party’s National Chairman, Abdul-Rahman Mohammed, expressing confidence that the opposition will reclaim the state and build on what he described as the developmental legacy of the late President Umaru Musa Yar’adua.

Speaking on Wednesday at the official flag-off ceremony in Katsina, Mohammed declared that the PDP was fully prepared for the 2027 general elections and urged party supporters to mobilise massively to ensure victory at the polls.

He also formally presented party flags to the PDP governorship candidate, Senator Yakubu Danmarke, the party’s three senatorial candidates and 15 House of Representatives candidates, while encouraging all PDP candidates to immediately commence campaigns across their constituencies.

The national chairman praised the unity and commitment of PDP members in Katsina, insisting that the state remained a stronghold of the opposition.

According to him, the PDP offers the best alternative for the people of Katsina and would work to consolidate the achievements associated with the administration of the late President Umaru Musa Yar’adua.

“I have seen for myself that Katsina is PDP-dominated. Come out en masse and vote for the PDP. Yakubu Lado Danmarke’s success is the success of Katsina State. We will do everything possible to ensure the PDP wins Katsina and consolidates the good work started by the late President Umaru Musa Yar’adua,” he said.

In his address, the PDP governorship candidate, Senator Yakubu Lado Danmarke, declared that the people of Katsina had become disillusioned with the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC), promising sweeping reforms if elected.

Lado pledged to restore the old pension scheme for civil servants, introduce free healthcare with essential drugs in public hospitals, provide free education, strengthen security, create jobs and expand economic opportunities for youths and women.

He also promised to equip hospitals with modern medical facilities to reduce the need for Nigerians to seek treatment abroad.

The PDP candidate criticised the APC-led administration in the state, alleging that key sectors had deteriorated despite significant federal allocations to Katsina.

He further expressed confidence that the PDP would emerge victorious in the 2027 elections, describing the party as the preferred choice of the electorate.

Earlier, the Katsina State PDP Chairman, Nura Amadi Kurfi, said the party remained united and well-positioned for victory, noting that the campaign flag-off featured the presentation of candidates for all elective positions, including three senatorial candidates, 15 House of Representatives candidates and 34 State House of Assembly candidates.

Kurfi thanked the party’s national leadership for its support and expressed optimism that the PDP would secure more than 1.5 million votes in the state.

Also speaking, the PDP senatorial candidate for Katsina South, Nura Khalil, described the campaign as “a battle between truth and falsehood,” urging supporters to remain committed to delivering victory for the party.

His counterparts for Katsina Central and Katsina North Senatorial Districts, Hon. Hamisu Gambo and Dauda Daura, also addressed supporters, expressing confidence that the PDP would reclaim Katsina State in the 2027 general elections.

title: Tinubu expands 2027 campaign appearances to 19 states, FCT
description:
President Bola Tinubu has expanded his planned appearances at the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rallies from 12 states to 19 states and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) ahead of the 2027 general elections.







The revised campaign timetable lists 20 locations where the
content:
President Bola Tinubu has expanded his planned appearances at the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rallies from 12 states to 19 states and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The revised campaign timetable lists 20 locations where the president is expected to attend rallies between October 24, 2026, and January 13, 2027, according to TheCable, which reported that the schedule was released by APC National Publicity Secretary, Felix Morka.

The revised itinerary adds Katsina, Taraba, Abuja, Gusau, Owerri and Ilorin to the president’s initial campaign trail, while also incorporating Akwa Ibom, Jigawa and Kebbi, where he has already attended rallies.

Tinubu was initially scheduled to attend rallies in only 12 states, with other party leaders expected to represent him at campaign events in the remaining states.

However, he has made appearances in several states outside the original schedule.

On November 6, the president visited Uyo, Akwa Ibom State, where he attended an APC rally and inaugurated projects executed by Governor Umo Eno’s administration.

He followed this with a campaign rally in Port Harcourt, Rivers State, on November 7.

Tinubu also attended the party’s rallies in Dutse, Jigawa State, on November 10, and Birnin Kebbi, Kebbi State, on November 17.

The revised timetable now formally includes the three states among the locations for his personal campaign appearances.

Under the updated schedule, Tinubu is expected to attend rallies in Katsina on December 2, Kano on December 17, Jalingo on December 19, Abuja on December 21, Gusau on December 28 and Owerri on December 30.

The president is also scheduled to visit Yola, Adamawa State, on January 4; Sokoto on January 5; Ilorin, Kwara State, on January 8; Asaba, Delta State, on January 11; and Lagos on January 13.

Other states listed for his personal appearances include Kaduna, Oyo, Borno and Enugu.

The revised timetable also changes the dates of some rallies in the original calendar.

The Bauchi rally, initially scheduled for November 29 with Tinubu expected to attend, has been moved to December 1, although the new timetable does not indicate a presidential appearance.

The Sokoto rally has been shifted from December 5 to January 5, 2027, while the Asaba rally moves from December 12 to January 11.

The Lagos rally, expected to serve as the campaign’s major closing event, has also been rescheduled from January 9 to January 13.

The updated calendar lists 37 rallies across the 36 states and the FCT, with Tinubu expected to personally attend 20 of them.

The North-West has the highest number of states on the president’s revised campaign itinerary, with seven: Kaduna, Jigawa, Kebbi, Katsina, Kano, Zamfara and Sokoto.

The North-East and South-South follow with three states each. The North-East states are Borno, Taraba and Adamawa, while the South-South states are Akwa Ibom, Rivers and Delta.

The North-Central, South-West and South-East have two states each: Plateau and Kwara; Oyo and Lagos; and Enugu and Imo, respectively.

Tinubu had indicated during the inauguration of the APC Presidential Campaign Council in Abuja that he would not attend every campaign rally, citing the need to balance political engagements with his responsibilities as president.

He, however, pledged to make time to engage Nigerians directly as party leaders take the campaign to states and local government areas.

title: INEC begins distribution of 173,241 PVCs in Rivers
description:
By Precious Akutamadu







The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) says it will commence the distribution of 173,241 Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) to registrants in Rivers on Friday.



Mr John Adie, the Head, Voter Education, Publicity, Gender and Inclusivity, INEC, Rivers Office, mad
content:
By Precious Akutamadu

The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) says it will commence the distribution of 173,241 Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) to registrants in Rivers on Friday.

Mr John Adie, the Head, Voter Education, Publicity, Gender and Inclusivity, INEC, Rivers Office, made the disclosure on Wednesday in Port Harcourt.

Adie stated that the distribution was to prepare Rivers residents ahead of the 2027 general elections.

He urged Rivers residents who participated in the continuous voter registration exercise to remain patient, explaining that the printing and distribution of the cards were being conducted in phases.

The INEC official said that the commission in Rivers had received 52,082 PVCs for voters who registered between August and December 2025.

“We are also distributing another 98,695 cards to those who registered between January and April,” he said.

According to him, 22,464 PVCs belonging to voters who transferred their registration between August and December 2025 have equally been received.

He said that the cards were being counted and sorted according to local government areas, wards and polling units in order to facilitate distribution.

Adie expressed optimism that the sorting exercise would be completed by the end of Thursday to enable eligible voters to collect their cards at INEC offices in the local government areas.

He said that the commission would conduct a nationwide mock accreditation exercise on Nov. 28 to test its technological devices ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Adie further said that the exercise would take place in two polling units in each of the 23 local government areas of the state.

According to him, the exercise is designed to assess the functionality of the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System, and test the electronic transmission of results at polling units.

Adie stated that although voters would present their PVCs for accreditation during the exercise, there would be no ballot papers or actual voting.

He said that the commission would use the exercise to ascertain the efficiency of the devices in accrediting voters, recording number of accredited voters, and uploading results to the designated platform.

The voter education official urged residents to cooperate with the commission and participate in its activities as part of efforts to strengthen the electoral process.(NAN)

title: ADC faults APC over claims of sponsored rally violence
description:
The African Democratic Congress (ADC) has rejected allegations by the All Progressives Congress (APC) that it is sponsoring hoodlums to disrupt campaign rallies, insisting that Nigerians do not need opposition parties to express dissatisfaction with the economic situation in the country.







The
content:
The African Democratic Congress (ADC) has rejected allegations by the All Progressives Congress (APC) that it is sponsoring hoodlums to disrupt campaign rallies, insisting that Nigerians do not need opposition parties to express dissatisfaction with the economic situation in the country.

The party said public anger over the policies of President Bola Tinubu’s administration should not be attributed to opposition-sponsored activities.

In a statement issued on Tuesday, Phrank Shaibu, Director of Strategic Communication of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, accused the APC of attempting to portray public discontent with the government as a political plot.

Shaibu said the policies of the Tinubu administration over the past three and a half years had increased the cost of food, fuel and other basic necessities, adding that Nigerians were entitled to assess the government’s performance based on their daily experiences.

The ADC was reacting to an earlier statement by Dele Alake, spokesperson of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, who accused the ADC and the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) of sponsoring hoodlums to disrupt campaign events and endanger young Nigerians.

Alake had also alleged that opposition parties were using artificial intelligence-generated images, deepfakes, fake news and sponsored protests to create tension ahead of the 2027 general elections.

He further accused the parties of mobilising young people with cudgels and directing them to chant “Bamaiyi” at APC campaign rallies.

However, the ADC questioned the allegations, particularly the circumstances surrounding the reported release of individuals arrested in connection with the incident.

The party asked the APC to provide evidence linking it to the alleged sponsorship of violence rather than making accusations against opposition groups.

“The Presidency earlier denied that the President’s motorcade had been pelted. Now the APC campaign council says people were detained for pelting the convoy with stones and that President Tinubu directed their release. Which account should Nigerians believe?” the statement asked.

It added: “If the APC has evidence that the ADC armed or sponsored those people, why were those detained released? Why have the alleged sponsors not been identified and prosecuted? A government with evidence of such a serious offence should hand it to investigators, not fling accusations at its opponents.”

The ADC denied sponsoring violence or recruiting young people to confront political opponents, saying it condemned attacks on campaigners, supporters, places of worship and public property, irrespective of political affiliation.

The party also urged the ruling APC to account for its own campaign activities, arguing that reports and images purportedly showing money being distributed at political events should also be scrutinised.

It maintained that public criticism of the government should not automatically be characterised as opposition-sponsored activity.

“Nigerians are entitled to judge this government by the cost of living and by their own daily experience. Calling their anger an opposition plot will not make it disappear,” the statement added.

title: Senate passes bills establishing research fund, granting medical college PhD powers
description:
By Henry Umoru



ABUJA — The Senate has passed two bills seeking to provide a framework for research funding and expand postgraduate medical education in Nigeria.







The bills are the National Research and Innovation Development Fund Establishment Bill, 2026, and the National Postgraduate Medic
content:
By Henry Umoru

ABUJA — The Senate has passed two bills seeking to provide a framework for research funding and expand postgraduate medical education in Nigeria.

The bills are the National Research and Innovation Development Fund Establishment Bill, 2026, and the National Postgraduate Medical College Act Amendment Bill, 2026.

Both bills were passed on Wednesday after consideration of their provisions, clause by clause, at the Committee of the Whole and subsequent third reading.

Their passage followed the presentation and consideration of reports by the Senate Committee on Tertiary Institutions and TETFund, chaired by Senator Mohammed Dandutse (APC, Katsina South).

Presenting the reports, Dandutse said the National Research and Innovation Development Fund Establishment Bill sought to establish a sustainable funding mechanism for research, development and innovation across the country.

He said the proposed legislation also provided for the establishment of the National Council on Research and Innovation, which would provide strategic direction, policy oversight and supervision for Nigeria’s research agenda.

According to him, the proposed fund would support research institutions and provide a dedicated funding framework for addressing the country’s development challenges.

He added that the fund and the council would work together to strengthen Nigeria’s research, scientific, technological and innovation capabilities.

On the National Postgraduate Medical College Act Amendment Bill, Dandutse said the proposed amendment sought to expand the academic and institutional functions of the college.

He explained that the amendment would empower the college to establish academic programmes and award Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) degrees in specialised medical disciplines.

The areas include clinical medicine, dentistry, basic medical sciences, pharmacology and other related fields.

Dandutse further explained that the amendment would empower the college’s Senate to develop, administer and supervise the proposed doctoral programmes.

He said the programmes would be subject to accreditation and regulation by the National Universities Commission (NUC) to ensure compliance with prescribed academic standards.

According to him, the proposed changes are intended to provide a framework for advanced medical education, clinical research and specialised medical training in the country.

title: 37 Niger Miners’ Deaths: Senate Demands Expedited Report Implementation, Sanctions On Errant NSCDC Officers
description: The Senate has asked the Federal Government to expedite implementation of all recommendations contained in the investigative committee report, to accelerate sanctions against officers found culpable in the deaths of 37 artisanal miners who died in the custody of the NSCDC in Niger State.The resoluti
content:
The Senate has asked the Federal Government to expedite implementation of all recommendations contained in the investigative committee report, to accelerate sanctions against officers found culpable in the deaths of 37 artisanal miners who died in the custody of the NSCDC in Niger State.

The resolutions followed a motion sponsored by Senator Mohammed Sani Musa titled, ‘The Unfortunate Death of 37 Young Artisanal Miners in the Custody of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps, Niger State Command and the Need for Expeditious Implementation of the Recommendations of the Federal Government’s Investigative Committee’.

The Senate, recalling that the 37 miners died on September 17, 2026, while in NSCDC custody in Minna, Niger State, expressed concern over the circumstances surrounding their deaths, noting that the incident raised serious questions about the protection of fundamental human rights and the responsibility of security agencies to safeguard persons in their custody.

The lawmakers acknowledged that the 10-member independent investigative committee, chaired by Jonathan Kure, had submitted its report, identifying serious lapses and recommending sanctions, institutional reforms and financial compensation for the victims’ families.

They warned that any further delay in implementing the recommendations, particularly the payment of compensation, would prolong the suffering of the bereaved families and undermine public confidence in the government’s commitment to justice.

The Senate also called for comprehensive reforms in the management of detention facilities and the operational procedures of security agencies to prevent a recurrence.

As part of its resolutions, the chamber directed its committees on interior, human rights, police affairs and judiciary to exercise oversight on the implementation of the investigative committee’s recommendations and report back on progress made.

The lawmakers also observed a minute of silence in honour of the deceased and resolved to constitute a delegation, to be led by the President of the Senate or his nominee, to pay a condolence visit to the Niger State governor.
