title: AMR: Africa bears world’s deadliest burden as WHO demands urgent action
description:
By Doris Obinna
The World Health Organisation (WHO) has warned that sub-Saharan Africa bears the highest rates of deaths associated with antimicrobial resistance (AMR), calling for urgent investment in surveillance, laboratory capacity and responsible use of medicines to contain the growing threat.
content:
By Doris Obinna

The World Health Organisation (WHO) has warned that sub-Saharan Africa bears the highest rates of deaths associated with antimicrobial resistance (AMR), calling for urgent investment in surveillance, laboratory capacity and responsible use of medicines to contain the growing threat.

WHO Regional Director for Africa, Dr Mohamed Janabi, said drug-resistant infections were undermining decades of medical progress, making previously treatable infections harder to cure and putting millions of lives at risk.

Janabi, in his message to mark the 2026 World Antimicrobial Resistance Awareness Week (WAAW), observed from 18 to 24 November, disclosed that bacterial AMR was associated with an estimated 4.7 million deaths globally in 2021, with Africa carrying the heaviest mortality burden.

He warned that the growing resistance of bacteria, viruses, fungi and parasites to medicines threatened the gains made through the discovery of antibiotics, which had transformed the treatment of infections and made procedures such as surgery, cancer treatment and organ transplantation safer.

Under the theme “One Health, One Action: Prevent AMR Now”, the WHO regional director stressed that tackling the crisis required coordinated action across human, animal, plant and environmental health.

He identified inappropriate use of antimicrobials in humans and animals, poor infection prevention, inadequate access to clean water and sanitation, and unsafe waste disposal as major factors accelerating the emergence and spread of resistant organisms.

Despite the challenges, Janabi said countries in the WHO African Region had recorded progress in developing systems to tackle AMR, although implementation remained uneven.

According to him, all 47 countries in the region now have national action plans on AMR and are enrolled in WHO’s Global Antimicrobial Resistance and Use Surveillance System, while 44 have the capacity to conduct susceptibility testing for priority bacterial pathogens.

He said 36 countries had also adopted WHO’s Access, Watch and Reserve classification of antibiotics, a framework designed to promote appropriate prescribing and reduce the misuse of medicines.

The global target, he noted, was to ensure that at least 70 per cent of antibiotics used in human health came from the Access group by 2030.

Janabi, however, warned that having policies and action plans was not enough without effective implementation, funding and measurable results.

He disclosed that the number of countries with functional One Health AMR governance mechanisms had increased from 15 in 2023 to 29 in 2026, reflecting improved coordination among sectors responsible for tackling the threat.

Calling for stronger government commitment, he urged countries to translate their national action plans into adequately funded interventions, with clear responsibilities and measurable targets.

He said domestic investment should prioritise laboratories, disease surveillance and responsible antimicrobial use, while ensuring that people could access quality-assured medicines and diagnostic services when needed.

The WHO official also called for stronger infection prevention measures, including vaccination, improved hygiene, clean water, sanitation and effective infection control in healthcare facilities and farms.

He stressed the need for safer management of waste and wastewater to prevent resistant organisms from spreading.

He urged healthcare professionals, veterinary workers and those in agriculture to use antimicrobials responsibly, while calling on researchers, pharmaceutical companies and development partners to support national priorities and expand equitable access to diagnostics and treatment.

Janabi also appealed to communities, young people, educators and the media to intensify public awareness, advising people to keep vaccinations up to date, practise regular hand hygiene, take antibiotics only when prescribed by qualified health professionals and avoid sharing leftover medicines.

He reaffirmed WHO’s commitment to working with governments and partners to strengthen the One Health response, warning that the effectiveness of lifesaving medicines must be protected for present and future generations.

The post AMR: Africa bears world’s deadliest burden as WHO demands urgent action appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: World Bank threatened to cut Nigeria’s financing over subsidy — Fashola
description:
Former Lagos State Governor, Babatunde Fashola, has said the World Bank warned Nigeria that it would stop financing the country unless the Federal Government removed petrol subsidy.







Fashola, who served as Minister of Power under the late President Muhammadu Buhari, made the disclosure on Tues
content:
Former Lagos State Governor, Babatunde Fashola, has said the World Bank warned Nigeria that it would stop financing the country unless the Federal Government removed petrol subsidy.

Fashola, who served as Minister of Power under the late President Muhammadu Buhari, made the disclosure on Tuesday during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today.

He said the decision to remove the subsidy was not merely a policy choice, but was also influenced by legal provisions and Nigeria’s financial position at the time.

Fashola urged Nigerians to revisit President Bola Tinubu’s inaugural address, arguing that public attention had focused largely on the declaration that “subsidy is gone” without sufficient consideration of other parts of the speech.

He also cited the Petroleum Industry Act (PIA), which he said provided for petroleum products to be sold at competitive market rates, arguing that the provision had implications for any move to reinstate subsidy.

“The World Bank simply said, ‘We won’t finance your country again unless you remove subsidy.’ It was that simple,” he said.

Fashola said the issue had been discussed during the previous administration, when he was a member of the Federal Executive Council, adding that Nigeria was spending close to 90 per cent of its revenue on debt servicing.

He argued that the country could not afford to sustain the subsidy regime and challenged those advocating its restoration to explain how they intended to fund it.

The former minister also asked political opponents of the Tinubu administration to explain how they would implement an alternative policy if elected, saying some politicians who had previously supported subsidy removal had changed their positions after it became unpopular.

He said the Tinubu administration deserved commendation for maintaining the policy despite the economic difficulties it had imposed on Nigerians.

“What this government deserves commendation for is not falling over on its word and saying, ‘Because the people like it, let’s bring it back.’ It was a road to perdition,” he said.

Fashola, however, acknowledged that subsidy removal had affected household livelihoods and increased the cost of living, but said the government was introducing other measures to cushion the impact.

He listed tax reforms, the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND), salary adjustments and compressed natural gas (CNG) initiatives among the measures being deployed to address the economic pressures.

He also cited a decline in inflation from above 30 per cent to about 14 per cent, arguing that reversing the subsidy policy midway could disrupt the progress recorded.

The former governor recalled the Subsidy Reinvestment and Empowerment Programme (SURE-P), introduced under former President Goodluck Jonathan, as an earlier attempt to manage the proceeds from subsidy removal.

He said the programme’s chairman resigned after developing concerns about the management of its funds.

In August, former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, the African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate, said he would restore petrol subsidy if elected president in the 2027 general election.

title: US Democrats back Jeffries for House speaker
description:
Hakeem Jeffries is on the cusp of becoming the first Black speaker of the US House of Representatives after Democrats elected him their leader on Wednesday following a sweeping midterm election triumph.
The 56-year-old New Yorker secured 251 votes in a closed-door, secret ballot, with 11 cast agains
content:
Hakeem Jeffries is on the cusp of becoming the first Black speaker of the US House of Representatives after Democrats elected him their leader on Wednesday following a sweeping midterm election triumph.

The 56-year-old New Yorker secured 251 votes in a closed-door, secret ballot, with 11 cast against his nomination, according to US media.

Jeffries faced no declared challenger, although opposition from some newly elected progressives had exposed divisions over how Democrats should wield their newfound power.

His nomination puts him on course to preside over a commanding Democratic majority during the final two years of President Donald Trump’s term, as his party prepares to reverse Republican policies and investigate the administration.

Jeffries must still win a formal vote of the full House when the new Congress convenes on January 3, when he would become the first Black politician to hold the powerful post. With a large Democratic majority, this is seen as something of a formality.

Both returning Democrats and incoming lawmakers participated in Wednesday’s election, including progressives who had sought concessions on issues ranging from US military support for Israel to the influence of money in politics.

Jeffries had requested a recorded vote rather than a nomination “by acclamation” — without a formal ballot — as some allies had hoped.

He argued that every Democrat should have an opportunity to weigh his experience, record and vision, citing the precedent set when the party last took control of the House in 2018.

The ballot remained secret, with the overall tally made public but individual votes kept anonymous.

Ahead of the election, Jeffries met progressive lawmakers to discuss issues including Israel and healthcare, with proposals to lower the Medicare eligibility age and expand coverage among the topics discussed.

The Democratic leader has also sought to shift attention to the party’s plans for governing after voters handed Republicans a crushing defeat amid anger over the Iran war and soaring fuel costs.

“Folks are drowning in this Republican economy, and House Democrats are committed to turning that situation around, beginning on day one,” he told reporters Tuesday.

“We’re going to relentlessly fight for an affordable America.”

Brooklyn roots

Raised in Brooklyn’s working-class Crown Heights neighborhood, Jeffries trained as a lawyer before entering the New York state legislature in 2007 and winning election to Congress in 2012.

Known for his measured manner, sharp rhetoric and penchant for quoting hip-hop artists, he became the first Black politician to lead a party in either chamber of Congress when Democrats chose him to succeed Nancy Pelosi in 2022.

He also served as a House prosecutor during Trump’s first impeachment trial in 2020.

As speaker, Jeffries would preside over one of Washington’s most powerful institutions and stand second in line to the presidency behind the vice president.

But he would face a formidable task in managing a Democratic coalition spanning centrists and an increasingly assertive left flank.

His party has promised investigations into Trump and his administration, while lawmakers remain divided over Israel, healthcare and how aggressively to pursue their agenda against a president who retains veto power.

Jeffries’s nomination contrasts with a more competitive leadership contest among Senate Democrats, where veteran party chief Chuck Schumer faces a challenge from progressive Maryland Senator Chris Van Hollen.

Van Hollen has attracted support from prominent left-wing figures, including Bernie Sanders, but acknowledges he is the underdog. Senate Democrats will elect their leader in early December.

Republicans chose their own congressional leaders last week, elevating Trump ally Jim Jordan in the House and retaining John Thune in the Senate.

AFP

The post US Democrats back Jeffries for House speaker appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: DSS challenges Atiku to prove it recruited protesters in Sokoto
description:
…Says preliminary investigation found no evidence against operatives



…Recalls rescuing ADC governorship candidate from attack



The Department of State Services (DSS) has challenged former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar to provide concrete evidence to support his allegation that the agency recrui
content:
…Says preliminary investigation found no evidence against operatives

…Recalls rescuing ADC governorship candidate from attack

The Department of State Services (DSS) has challenged former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar to provide concrete evidence to support his allegation that the agency recruited protesters to disrupt the African Democratic Congress (ADC) campaign rally in Sokoto State.

The secret police said its preliminary investigation into the allegation failed to establish any evidence linking its operatives to the organisation or sponsorship of protests against the ADC’s campaign activities in the state.

Atiku, the ADC presidential candidate, had earlier accused the Sokoto State Government of obstructing his party’s campaign activities ahead of its rally in the state.

Addressing journalists in Abuja, the former Vice-President also alleged that the DSS recruited protesters to cause unrest and create grounds for imposing a curfew that could prevent the opposition party from holding its rally as scheduled.

However, in a statement issued on Tuesday, the Deputy Director of Public Relations and Strategic Communications of the DSS, Favour Dozie, said the agency activated its internal investigation procedures following the public allegation.

Dozie said the investigation was conducted on the directive of the Director-General of the DSS, Adeola Ajayi, and involved interviews with ADC leaders in Sokoto, party members and other relevant stakeholders.

According to the spokesperson, Atiku had specifically alleged that the ADC knew where some of the protesters were assembled and how they were allegedly deployed to strategic locations.

Quoting the former Vice-President, Dozie said: “Where some of these protesters are assembled: an office behind Zenith Bank on Koko Road. Trucks are stationed there and dispatched to key points, including the roundabout.”

The DSS spokesperson, however, said the agency’s preliminary findings did not substantiate the allegation.

“Outcome of the preliminary investigation did not confirm the allegation, as there was no evidence to establish such,” the statement said.

In presenting its account of its activities in Sokoto, the agency recalled that on October 31, its operatives rescued Mannir Daniya, the ADC governorship candidate in the state, from an attack and evacuated him to safety.

It said two of its operatives were assaulted during the rescue operation and were receiving medical attention at the time of its earlier statement.

The agency further disclosed that Daniya subsequently contacted the State Director of the DSS to express appreciation for the intervention and request additional security reinforcement.

It also said it received letters of appreciation from the ADC state chairman and the governorship candidate, describing the correspondence as evidence of its efforts to protect political actors irrespective of their party affiliations.

Against this background, the DSS said it expected Atiku to publicly clarify his allegation or provide supporting evidence to enable further investigation.

“While the Service acknowledges the Letters of Appreciation from the ADC chairman and governorship candidate in Sokoto State, the DSS still requests that, in view of the fact that the allegation was made in public, His Excellency should set the records straight publicly or provide concrete evidence (if any) to enable further investigation,” Dozie said.

The agency added that it was open to an independent investigation into the matter.

“The Service welcomes any fair and independent enquiry into the issue,” the statement added.

The DSS said its appeal was made out of respect for the former Vice-President and in the interest of truth, fairness and the morale of its personnel, who it said risk their lives in the service of the country.

It reaffirmed its commitment to its constitutional responsibilities and the principles of professionalism and political neutrality.

title: Atiku questions Tinubu’s Villa interview over $4.5m US lobbying deal
description:
By Luminous Jannamike







ABUJA — Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has questioned whether President Bola Tinubu’s recently recorded interview at the Presidential Villa was connected to a $4.5 million lobbying contract involving the Nigerian government in the United States.



Atiku demanded t
content:
By Luminous Jannamike

ABUJA — Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has questioned whether President Bola Tinubu’s recently recorded interview at the Presidential Villa was connected to a $4.5 million lobbying contract involving the Nigerian government in the United States.

Atiku demanded that the Presidency disclose the terms of the contract, explain the purpose of the payment and release the full, unedited interview to establish whether the recording was an independent journalistic exercise or part of a government-funded publicity arrangement.

In a statement on Wednesday by his Director of Strategic Communication, Phrank Shaibu, Atiku said US filings identified Diana London as a consultant to DCI Group AZ, a firm reportedly engaged to work for the Nigerian government through Aster Legal.

He said the filings showed that DCI Group received a $4.5 million retainer but did not establish whether the presidential interview was covered by the contract.

Atiku also criticised the Presidency for presenting the recorded encounter as an interview while promoting it with photographs and a ‘coming soon’ announcement.

“When Tinubu is ready for an interview, he should let Nigerians know. He cannot invite a strategist registered to work for his government, record a publicity production and advertise Sitting on a Flat Mandate as ‘coming soon’, like a trailer from 51 Iweka Road, Onitsha.

“Hungry Nigerians are not here to market his failed movie. They have suffered through Part One of Tinubu’s government, and they will not sit through a sequel,” he said.

The former vice president also questioned London’s professional relationship with the lobbying firm and her decision to delete social media posts in which she had praised Tinubu’s administration and Nigeria’s partnership with the United States.

“After praising Tinubu’s government and Nigeria’s partnership with the United States on her social media accounts, Diana London deleted the posts. She has not explained why. Nigerians are entitled to ask what changed between the glowing praise and its disappearance,” Atiku said.

He argued that the deleted posts and questions surrounding London’s professional engagements reinforced the need for the Presidency to release the complete recording.

“Someone who could delete her own public praise of this government without an explanation has given Nigerians reason to wonder what will survive the editing of her interview. Will difficult questions and awkward answers remain in the final cut? Or will Nigerians be served a carefully redacted, defensive account that mutilates the facts? The Presidency can put those doubts to rest by releasing the full, unedited recording,” he said.

Atiku also questioned the presence of a large screen positioned within Tinubu’s line of sight during the recording, suggesting it might have been used to display prepared prompts.

“The Presidency staged a recorded publicity production, advertised it like a home video and called it an interview. It has offered no reason to believe the questions were spontaneous or that Tinubu answered without prepared prompts. If it was a genuine interview, let the Presidency release the full, unedited recording, including what appeared on that screen,” he said.

He maintained that Nigerian journalists were capable of subjecting the President to rigorous questioning, naming Rufai Oseni, Ojy Okpe, Seun Okinbaloye and Reuben Abati as potential interviewers.

“Let him sit with them live. Let him explain why food costs so much, why wages no longer cover transport, and when families can expect relief. A flattering interview cannot wipe away poverty and hunger,” Atiku said.

The former vice president further demanded to know who authorised the $4.5 million payment, where the money came from and whether public funds were used for the lobbying arrangement.

“Who authorised the $4.5 million payment, and from which public account did it come? At a time when Nigerians are told to endure the pain of fuel subsidy removal, they deserve to know whether the money saved is being spent on foreign publicity.

“My Affordable Life campaign is about making food, fuel and transport affordable again. Tinubu cannot ask families to suffer in silence while millions of dollars are committed to polishing his image. Publish the contract. Show the invoices. Release the unedited interview. Then face Nigerian journalists and answer the people,” Atiku said.

The post Atiku questions Tinubu’s Villa interview over $4.5m US lobbying deal appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Okpebholo promises end to excessive taxation in Edo
description:
Edo State Governor, Senator Monday Okpebholo, has promised traders at the New Benin Market in Benin City that their complaints about excessive taxation will be settled soon.
The governor made the pledge on Wednesday while addressing traders and market leaders during a rally the All Progressives Cong
content:
Edo State Governor, Senator Monday Okpebholo, has promised traders at the New Benin Market in Benin City that their complaints about excessive taxation will be settled soon.

The governor made the pledge on Wednesday while addressing traders and market leaders during a rally the All Progressives Congress (APC) held at the market.

The governor recalled that he visited the market during his campaign and promised to return if elected. He also said he had pledged to tar the access roads within and around the market.

“I remember when I was contesting, I came and sat down here that very day. I told you that when you vote for me, I will come back. I am back now,” he said.

He said traders had earlier complained of unstable electricity supply, and that he would direct the Edo State Electrification Agency (EDSEA) to find the cause of the problem.

“If it is a transformer, we will get you a new one. What we are after is to provide you with a good life. Your vote was for me to provide you with a good life,” he said.

On taxation, the Chairman of the Mother Union in the market, Mr Taiwo Aideyan appealed to the governor to reduce the levies imposed on traders. Okpebholo responded that he would meet the market leadership on Thursday in his office, together with the Chairman of the Edo State Board of Internal Revenue.

“We are going to resolve the issue of tax by Thursday in my office with your leaders and the state chairman of the Board of Internal Revenue, so that your leaders can tell us what you can pay.

“We are going to put it to rest. The tax issue will die completely, so that you can do your business very well,” he said.

The governor also assured members of the Igbo community in Edo State that they would be fairly represented in his administration. He appealed to them to vote for President Bola Tinubu and other APC candidates in the forthcoming general election.

Earlier, Aideyan commended the governor for ending illegal ticketing in the market and for improving security across the state.

Another market leader, Mr John Ogbu, praised Okpebholo’s developmental projects, saying his achievements in two years as governor were commendable.

“This is the only governor in the history of the state who has appointed an Igbo man to his cabinet in the person of Comrade Martins Oli Anayor,” Ogbu said.

title: Africa takes centre stage in global communication conversation as World PR Forum comes to Nigeria
description:
Africa is set to take a prominent place in the global public relations and communication conversation as Nigeria prepares to host the 2026 World Public Relations Forum (WPRF), bringing together communication professionals, policymakers, academics and industry leaders from across the world.
The event
content:
Africa is set to take a prominent place in the global public relations and communication conversation as Nigeria prepares to host the 2026 World Public Relations Forum (WPRF), bringing together communication professionals, policymakers, academics and industry leaders from across the world.

The event officially begins on Sunday, November 15, with a golf tournament at the IBB International Golf Club and Resorts, ahead of the main conference programme, which runs from November 16th to 22th.

The Forum marks the first time the global gathering will take place in West Africa and only the second time it will be hosted on the African continent. More than 3,000 delegates from over 126 countries are expected to attend, creating an opportunity for African perspectives and professional experiences to contribute to discussions shaping the future of the global communication industry.

Organised by the Global Alliance for Public Relations and Communication Management and hosted by the Nigerian Institute of Public Relations (NIPR), the Forum will be held under the theme, “Responsible Communication: The Voice of the World.”

Among the key figures expected at the gathering are President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, GCFR, President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria; H.E. Hakainde Hichilema, President of Zambia; Special guest of honour, H.E. Rt. Hon. Abbas Tajudeen, GCON, Ph.D, speaker of the 10th House of Representatives Federal Republic of Nigeria and Suleiman Haruna, Chairman of the National Planning Committee for WPRF 2026. Their participation reflects the collaboration between the global, national and continental institutions driving the event.

The theme speaks to the growing importance of trust, ethics, accountability and credible information at a time when technological disruption, misinformation and changing public expectations are reshaping how institutions and societies communicate.

For Africa, the gathering represents more than the opportunity to host an international professional event. It creates a platform for practitioners and institutions in the region to bring their experiences into wider conversations about the standards, responsibilities and direction of public relations. From navigating diverse cultural contexts and complex media environments to communicating across rapidly evolving digital platforms, African professionals have insights that can contribute meaningfully to the development of the profession globally.

The Forum will also take place alongside the 37th African Public Relations Association (APRA) Conference, strengthening its continental dimension. The convergence of both gatherings will bring global and African professional conversations into the same space, allowing delegates to examine shared challenges while considering the particular realities and opportunities within communication practice across the continent.

A major feature of the programme will be Africa Day, scheduled for November 19, under the theme, “Africa, The Voice of the World: Communication for Peace, Democracy and Development.” Hosted by APRA, the day will focus on responsible communication in Africa, with particular attention to professional self-regulation, information and media literacy. These discussions reflect the need for communication systems that support informed public participation, strengthen institutions and build trust across communities.

Nigeria’s hosting of the Forum also places the country’s communication industry within a wider international exchange. While the gathering will introduce international delegates to the country’s professional landscape and cultural diversity, it will equally provide practitioners with opportunities to engage directly with global peers, share local knowledge and build relationships that can extend beyond the event.

As communication becomes increasingly central to public trust, governance and international relations, the questions facing the profession are no longer confined by national boundaries. The ability to communicate responsibly, respond to misinformation and engage diverse audiences has become a shared global concern. WPRF 2026 therefore offers an opportunity to consider how different regions can contribute to solutions and how professional collaboration can strengthen the industry as a whole.

With Abuja set to welcome the international public relations community, the Forum places Africa at the centre of an important professional exchange, one in which the region is not only represented but has an opportunity to shape the ideas, standards and partnerships influencing the future of global communication.

The post Africa takes centre stage in global communication conversation as World PR Forum comes to Nigeria appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: NELFUND: I dare opposition to promise scrapping scheme — Fashola
description:
…Says students, beneficiaries would revolt against such proposal



Former Lagos State Governor, Babatunde Fashola, has challenged opposition politicians to campaign on a promise to scrap the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND), saying beneficiaries and their families would resist such a move.
content:
…Says students, beneficiaries would revolt against such proposal

Former Lagos State Governor, Babatunde Fashola, has challenged opposition politicians to campaign on a promise to scrap the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND), saying beneficiaries and their families would resist such a move.

Fashola, who spoke on Tuesday during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today, described the student loan scheme introduced by President Bola Tinubu’s administration as one of the reforms that had eased the financial burden on families across the country.

NELFUND was established in April 2024 after Tinubu signed the Student Loans (Access to Higher Education) Act into law to provide interest-free loans to eligible students in tertiary institutions.

As of October 3, 2026, the fund said it had disbursed more than ₦372 billion to 1,635,676 beneficiaries across 312 tertiary institutions nationwide.

Speaking at the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally in Jigawa on November 10, Tinubu had described NELFUND as a weapon deployed by his administration to tackle poverty, insisting that the scheme would not be discontinued.

Supporting the President’s position, Fashola said the initiative was introduced to help Nigerian families cope with financial obligations, particularly rent, transportation, healthcare and education.

“This led to the creation of NELFUND to help families pay school fees and provide student allowances,” he said.

He noted that more than one million Nigerians were already benefiting from the scheme, adding that the number was increasing.

Fashola challenged opposition candidates to make the discontinuation of the programme part of their campaign promises, saying such a position would attract resistance from beneficiaries and their families.

“I challenge the opponents to promise to scrap NELFUND and see how beneficiaries and their families react. They won’t dare,” he said.

The former Minister of Works and Housing also addressed the rising cost of living, describing it as a global challenge whose effects were being felt in Nigeria.

He called for a broader understanding of the factors contributing to the economic hardship, pointing to disruptions caused by the COVID-19 pandemic and subsequent global developments.

According to him, the pandemic disrupted economic activities worldwide, forcing governments to inject money into their economies to support businesses.

He said China, which he described as the world’s biggest production centre, took about two to three years to resume normal operations, contributing to supply shortages and rising prices.

Fashola also identified the Russia-Ukraine war as another factor that worsened the situation, citing disruptions to the supply of energy products, including diesel, and food commodities such as wheat.

He said increased shipping costs and war-related insurance premiums further contributed to rising prices, although the impact differed among countries depending on their locations and levels of development.

“Thirdly, there was the unexpected war in the Middle East, which further worsened the situation,” he said.

Fashola added that the conflict had brought renewed attention to the strategic importance of the Strait of Hormuz, with developments around the waterway influencing the cost of goods.

“Everybody now knows the Strait of Hormuz… even the tomato seller, and prices goods based on replacement costs,” he said.

title: 2027: ADC files 17-ground appeal against INEC over Atiku’s candidacy
description:
The African Democratic Congress (ADC) has filed a 17-ground appeal challenging the Federal High Court judgment that nullified its leadership structure and the process that produced former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar as its presidential candidate for the 2027 general election.
The opposition party
content:
The African Democratic Congress (ADC) has filed a 17-ground appeal challenging the Federal High Court judgment that nullified its leadership structure and the process that produced former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar as its presidential candidate for the 2027 general election.

The opposition party is also asking the Court of Appeal to restrain the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) from altering its leadership records and the nomination particulars of its presidential and governorship candidates pending the determination of the appeal.

The development was disclosed by the Director of Strategic Communication of the ADC Campaign Council, Phrank Shaibu, during an appearance on Channels Television’s The Morning Brief.

Shaibu said the party was challenging the November 5, 2026 judgment delivered by Justice Peter Lifu of the Federal High Court in Abuja, describing the decision as fundamentally flawed.

According to him, the 17 grounds of appeal raise questions about the jurisdiction of the trial court, the legal standing of the plaintiff, the evaluation of disputed evidence and the orders made against the party.

He explained that the ADC was also challenging an earlier ruling delivered on July 24, 2026, which granted former party official Nafiu Bala Gombe permission to amend his originating summons despite the party’s pending objection to the court’s jurisdiction.

The party argued that the amendment altered the description of the parties and the capacity in which a defendant was sued without the necessary leave of court.

Shaibu said the ADC was asking the appellate court to set aside the amendment order and determine its outstanding objection to the jurisdiction of the Federal High Court.

The party’s legal team, led by Chief J.S. Okutepa (SAN), also argued that Justice Lifu proceeded to deliver judgment on a court process whose validity was already being challenged before the Court of Appeal.

Expressing concern over the possibility of INEC implementing the judgment before the appeal is determined, Shaibu warned that such action could undermine the party’s legal challenge and create complications for its candidates ahead of the 2027 elections.

He said the party wanted the appellate court to preserve its existing leadership structure and candidate records until the legal dispute was resolved.

The legal battle followed a suit instituted by Bala Gombe, who challenged the emergence of the leadership led by former Senate President David Mark.

On November 5, Justice Lifu ruled against the Mark-led leadership structure, a decision that also affected the process through which Atiku emerged as the ADC’s presidential candidate.

The ADC, however, maintains that previous court decisions recognising its leadership transition remain valid and have not been set aside.

The party has vowed to pursue the matter through lawful judicial processes, insisting that INEC should not take administrative steps capable of prejudicing the outcome of the pending appeal.

title: FIFA President Infantino to commission Warri Stadium Saturday as Oborevwori, Keyamo campaign in Warri South
description:
From Joe Obukata Ogbodu, Warri
FIFA President Gianni Infantino will on Saturday, 21 November, commission the rehabilitated 15,000-capacity Warri City Stadium, in what is set to be one of the biggest sporting events in the state.
Delta State APC Chairman Chief Solomon Areyenka announced the commissio
content:
From Joe Obukata Ogbodu, Warri

FIFA President Gianni Infantino will on Saturday, 21 November, commission the rehabilitated 15,000-capacity Warri City Stadium, in what is set to be one of the biggest sporting events in the state.

Delta State APC Chairman Chief Solomon Areyenka announced the commissioning during the APC campaign held at Nana College, Warri, in Warri South Local Government Area.

Chief Areyenka, who presented the party’s flag to Hon. Austin Uroye and Hon. Benson Obire, the Warri South Constituency I and Warri South Constituency II candidates respectively, said the Warri Township Stadium would be commissioned on Saturday, 21 November, by FIFA President Gianni Infantino.

Noting the bright performances of the Flamingos, who won the World Cup and were adequately rewarded by the Nigerian government, Chief Areyenka enjoined APC supporters to give their children the opportunity to learn how to play football in the stadium when it is commissioned.

“When they play well, Governor Oborevwori will reward them,” he said.

Speaking at the event, where he received decampees of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), led by the NDC candidate for Warri South Constituency II, Willy Kuku, who was joined by others, Governor Oborevwori thanked Warri South for maintaining peace, saying, “Some people thought they will fight in Warri today. We will not fight and kill each other.”

He also predicted that, before the 2027 elections, five key politicians would defect to the APC.

Minister of Aviation, Festus Keyamo, SAN, warned Warri South voters that voting against President Bola Tinubu in 2027 would hurt Governor Oborevwori the most and could lead to the abandonment of ongoing projects in Delta State.

Keyamo spoke at the APC campaign at Nana College, Warri, where Governor Oborevwori also received decampees from the National Democratic Congress (NDC), including its Warri South Constituency II candidate, Willy Kuku.

“Your power is your PVC. Don’t say I will vote for this person, I will not vote for that person. The election is from top to bottom,” Keyamo said.

“All those projects will now be abandoned. Let no one deceive you. I beg you, vote all APC candidates.”

Keyamo noted that Governor Oborevwori was performing creditably in infrastructural development because President Bola Ahmed Tinubu had made funds available for him and all other governors in the country.

He warned that if the people voted against the president, it would hurt Governor Sheriff Oborevwori the most and he might not be able to complete the projects he had started.

“All those projects will now be abandoned. Let no one deceive you. I beg you, vote all APC candidates,” Keyamo said.

Meanwhile, the Commissioner for Works (Rural Roads) and Public Information, Charles Aniagwu, had on Tuesday, during an inspection tour of the stadium, disclosed that work on the rehabilitation and upgrade of the facility was near completion. He expressed satisfaction with the quality of work while stressing the governor’s determination to ensure that the facility met the required standards.

Aniagwu, who led the inspection of the main stadium bowl, swimming pool arena, VIP lounges, media centre, dressing rooms for home and visiting teams, and other supporting facilities, said the state government would not compromise on quality in its determination to restore the stadium to its former glory.

He explained that the inspection was part of the government’s commitment to ensuring that every component of the project was delivered according to specifications, adding that a few areas requiring attention had been identified and communicated to the contractor and consultant.

The commissioner added that the stadium had been designed to provide spectators with unobstructed views of activities on the pitch from virtually every section of the stands.

He said the ongoing rehabilitation extended beyond the main bowl to include the training pitch and facilities for indoor sporting activities, noting that considerable work had gone into restoring the entire complex.

Aniagwu described the project as another demonstration of Oborevwori’s commitment to fulfilling his campaign promises through the MORE Agenda, particularly its pillars of Meaningful Development and Opportunities for All.

He said the restored stadium would strengthen Delta’s position as Nigeria’s leading sporting state while providing young people with the facilities to develop their talents in football, athletics and other sporting activities.

According to him, the facility would also serve residents of Delta South and Delta Central Senatorial Districts, who would no longer have to travel to Asaba to enjoy sporting events in a standard stadium.

He said: “Just as the governor has provided a beautiful stadium in Asaba, he has also demonstrated his determination to bring the Warri City Stadium back to life. This shows his commitment to equitable development and the delivery of infrastructure across the state.”

The commissioner noted that the investment would further consolidate the state’s reputation for excellence in sports, pointing out that the development of sporting infrastructure was essential to sustaining Delta’s impressive performances at national competitions.

He also expressed satisfaction with the stadium’s floodlighting system, explaining that only one of the four floodlights was switched on during the inspection, yet it provided sufficient illumination to demonstrate its capacity.

He added that Oborevwori had personally visited the facility to monitor progress, just as other government officials had done, to ensure that the project was delivered as planned.

On the maintenance of the stadium after completion, Aniagwu said the immediate priority was to conclude the rehabilitation work before discussions on a maintenance arrangement could begin.

title: Atiku’s subsidy restoration plan is ‘abracadabra’ — Fashola
description:
…Demands figures, details on funding, crude oil supply



Former Lagos State Governor, Babatunde Fashola, has described former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar’s proposal to restore petrol subsidy as “abracadabra without proof”, challenging him to provide details of how he intends to implement the poli
content:
…Demands figures, details on funding, crude oil supply

Former Lagos State Governor, Babatunde Fashola, has described former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar’s proposal to restore petrol subsidy as “abracadabra without proof”, challenging him to provide details of how he intends to implement the policy if elected president in 2027.

Atiku, the African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate, had in August said he would restore petrol subsidy if elected in the 2027 general elections.

Fashola, who served as Minister of Power under former President Muhammadu Buhari, stated this on Tuesday during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today.

He recalled that major presidential candidates in the 2023 general elections had supported the removal of petrol subsidy, questioning what had changed to warrant a reversal of that position.

“For credibility’s sake, all major candidates, at least as at the last election, promised to remove this fuel subsidy. So what has changed?” he asked.

Fashola said politicians advocating a different approach should explain the reasons for changing their positions and provide concrete details of how they intended to sustain the proposed arrangement.

He questioned the source of funding for the subsidy, warning that its restoration could reduce allocations to state governments and undermine their ability to meet financial obligations.

“I was in a government that was paying subsidy. And the states were not getting money. So we are going to go back to partial, near-zero returns, states borrowing money to pay salaries. Is that where you want us to go?” he asked.

He urged voters to consider the financial implications of the proposal and use their votes to prevent a return to the revenue challenges experienced by state governments during the subsidy regime.

Asked whether Atiku’s proposal was unrealistic, the former minister said he wanted detailed explanations and supporting figures before reaching a conclusion.

“With the sketchy pronouncements that come with it, I want to see rigour, I want to see detail; I want to see numbers,” he said.

Fashola also questioned Atiku’s argument that increased local refining would promote competition and reduce petrol prices, asking where the crude oil required to supply domestic refineries would come from.

He explained that Nigeria’s crude oil production involved joint ventures and production-sharing contracts with international oil companies, meaning the country did not own all the crude produced.

According to him, the assumption that Nigeria could simply supply local refineries with cheap crude overlooked the fact that crude oil was traded internationally at benchmark prices.

Fashola further questioned Nigeria’s capacity to supply sufficient crude to domestic refineries, noting that the country had yet to fully optimise its production quota.

He attributed the production challenges to legacy issues, insecurity and vandalism.

“If we have refineries working, what is our current oil production quota? Are we optimising it yet? No, because there are legacy issues; there are challenges with security, vandalism, and so on and so forth, so where is this magic crude oil going to come from?” he asked.

He said Atiku needed to provide evidence and demonstrate how his proposal would address the country’s crude oil supply constraints to avoid disappointing Nigerians.

“Let people choose. But without proof, it’s like abracadabra,” Fashola said.

title: Bayern coach Kompany resumes work after health scare
description:
Bayern Munich manager Vincent Kompany has resumed work at the club’s training ground following his recovery from meningeal irritation, and is expected to return to media duties ahead of Friday’s Bundesliga clash with Cologne.
According to AFP, the 40-year-old Belgian is scheduled to address the medi
content:
Bayern Munich manager Vincent Kompany has resumed work at the club’s training ground following his recovery from meningeal irritation, and is expected to return to media duties ahead of Friday’s Bundesliga clash with Cologne.

According to AFP, the 40-year-old Belgian is scheduled to address the media on Thursday after returning to Bayern’s training centre earlier this week.

Kompany was taken to hospital on October 23 after collapsing while watching a training session. He was diagnosed with meningeal irritation and later discharged to continue his recovery at home.

During his absence, assistant coach Aaron Danks took charge of the team.

The Bayern manager had appeared unwell and was seen limping during the club’s 6-1 victory over RB Leipzig in mid-October. He was also a doubt for their Champions League encounter against Arsenal four days later but remained in charge as Bayern played out a 2-2 draw.

His return to the training ground marks a gradual resumption of his responsibilities, although Bayern have not confirmed whether he has fully returned to his duties.

His scheduled press conference on Thursday will be his first media engagement since the illness, ahead of Bayern’s meeting with Cologne on Friday.

title: EPL: Give me time – Pochettino vows to end Man City dominance
description:
Former Chelsea manager Mauricio Pochettino has vowed to challenge Manchester City’s dominance in Manchester following his appointment as the new manager of Manchester United.
The Argentine made the remarks after overseeing his final match as head coach of the United States national team, who defeate
content:
Former Chelsea manager Mauricio Pochettino has vowed to challenge Manchester City’s dominance in Manchester following his appointment as the new manager of Manchester United.

The Argentine made the remarks after overseeing his final match as head coach of the United States national team, who defeated Haiti 2-0 in Cincinnati on Tuesday.

The victory secured an 8-0 aggregate triumph for the US in their Concacaf Nations League quarter-final.

During a post-match interview on TNT Sports, former Manchester City player DaMarcus Beasley told Pochettino that Manchester would always remain blue, referring to City’s dominance over their local rivals.

However, the 54-year-old dismissed the suggestion, responding: “No way. You will see. Give me time. Give me time and that is going to change.”

Pochettino expressed excitement about his new assignment, describing the opportunity to manage United as a major challenge he was eager to embrace.

“We are excited because the new challenge is big, but at the same time, it’s the adrenaline that you want to feel,” he said.

He, however, acknowledged that United were not currently performing at the level expected of a club of their stature.
“We know that it is not a situation that deserves to be at a club like Manchester United, and the fanbase is amazing,” he added.

Pochettino is expected to begin work at Old Trafford on Wednesday, replacing Michael Carrick, who was relieved of his duties following the club’s poor run of results.

His first match in charge will be against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday, November 22.

The former Tottenham Hotspur, Chelsea and Paris Saint-Germain manager leaves the United States after guiding the team to the last 16 of the 2026 FIFA World Cup.

title: 2027 AFCON Qualifiers: With two games remaining, what Nigeria now need to qualify
description:
Nigeria’s Super Eagles face a difficult task in their bid to qualify for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations, with two matches remaining in their qualifying group.
After four matches, Nigeria sit second in the group with seven points, three behind leaders Guinea-Bissau, who have accumulated 10 points.
Ma
content:
Nigeria’s Super Eagles face a difficult task in their bid to qualify for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations, with two matches remaining in their qualifying group.

After four matches, Nigeria sit second in the group with seven points, three behind leaders Guinea-Bissau, who have accumulated 10 points.

Madagascar and Tanzania occupy third and fourth positions respectively, with two points each.

The Super Eagles must win their remaining two fixtures to finish with 13 points and strengthen their chances of securing qualification.

Nigeria are scheduled to travel to face Madagascar on March 24, 2027, before hosting Guinea-Bissau four days later in what could be a decisive encounter.

However, Nigeria may also need Guinea-Bissau to drop points against Tanzania in their March 24 fixture to improve their chances of finishing above the group leaders.

Head-to-head record could decide qualification

Even if Nigeria and Guinea-Bissau finish level on 13 points, the Super Eagles could still miss out because of their inferior head-to-head record.

Guinea-Bissau defeated Nigeria 3-0 in their first meeting, giving them an advantage under the head-to-head criteria used in CAF qualifying competitions.

The criteria consider points earned in matches between the tied teams, followed by head-to-head goal difference and goals scored before overall group goal difference is considered.

Consequently, Nigeria may need to secure a convincing victory when both sides meet in March to overturn the deficit and improve their position in the event of a tie on points.

Remaining fixtures

The final two rounds of matches are scheduled for March 24 and 28, 2027.

March 24:

– Guinea-Bissau vs Tanzania
– Madagascar vs Nigeria

March 28:

– Nigeria vs Guinea-Bissau
– Tanzania vs Madagascar

Tanzania have already secured qualification for the tournament as one of the host nations, although they remain listed among the teams in the qualifying group.

With two matches left, Nigeria’s qualification hopes will depend on their results, Guinea-Bissau’s performance and the applicable head-to-head criteria.

title: Lagos targets global economic prominence with $1tr GDP ambition
description:
By Lukman Olabiyi
Lagos State Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu has unveiled an ambitious economic growth target of $1 trillion Gross Domestic Product (GDP) by 2052, declaring that his administration is laying the foundation for the state’s emergence as one of the world’s leading subnational economies.
Sa
content:
By Lukman Olabiyi

Lagos State Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu has unveiled an ambitious economic growth target of $1 trillion Gross Domestic Product (GDP) by 2052, declaring that his administration is laying the foundation for the state’s emergence as one of the world’s leading subnational economies.

Sanwo-Olu, who disclosed this at the fourth Lagos State Employment Trust Fund (LSETF) Summit in Lagos, said the state had increased its budget from less than ₦700 billion when he assumed office in 2019 to ₦4.2 trillion, with a focus on shared prosperity, economic empowerment and job creation.

The summit, themed “Lagos Works: Building Africa’s Most Productive City”, provided an opportunity for the governor to outline his administration’s economic development strategy and highlight the role of institutional continuity in driving sustainable growth.

He described a productive city as one where workers generate higher economic value, businesses expand their customer base and households enjoy improved disposable incomes.

According to him, achieving these objectives requires sustained investment in economic infrastructure, institutional capacity, private sector partnerships and employment-generating initiatives.

“Guided by our T.H.E.M.E.S. Plus agenda, we have systematically scaled our financial capacity to accelerate this prosperity. From an operating budget below ₦700 billion when we assumed office, we are currently running a ₦4.2 trillion budget dedicated entirely to shared prosperity, strategic empowerment and aggressively reducing unemployment through enablers like the LSETF,” he said.

The governor described the $1 trillion GDP target as ambitious but achievable, adding that the state had commenced the foundational work required to attain the milestone.

“As the second-largest economy in Africa, Lagos is charting an ambitious yet achievable course towards a $1 trillion GDP by 2052. Achieving this milestone will position Lagos among the leading economic subnationals globally, and the foundational work required to reach that destination has already begun,” he said.

Sanwo-Olu also highlighted the importance of institutional continuity, citing the LSETF as an example of how successive administrations could build on existing programmes rather than abandon them.

He noted that the fund, established a decade ago before his administration, had been deliberately strengthened and expanded under his leadership to improve access to finance for small businesses and stimulate employment.

According to him, the intervention has recorded a loan repayment rate of 95 per cent, disbursed funds to more than 20,000 small businesses and created over 320,000 jobs, while safeguarding another 173,000 jobs.

The Commissioner for Wealth Creation and Employment, Akinyemi Ajigbotafe, said the state had impacted more than 6,500 graduates and generated over 200,000 jobs through strategic wealth creation and employment initiatives since 2023.

He said the Sanwo-Olu administration remained committed to making employment opportunities accessible, sustainable and inclusive, particularly through programmes designed to equip young people with practical workplace experience.

Ajigbotafe identified the Graduate Internship Placement Programme (GIPP) as one of the flagship interventions bridging the gap between academic qualifications and the demands of the labour market.

He also described the Lagos State Job Fair as a major employment facilitation platform, noting that the 2025 and subsequent editions brought together more than 300 organisations and thousands of job seekers.

The commissioner said the ministry had intensified efforts to promote entrepreneurship and strengthen the capacity of micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), artisans and tradesmen.

He disclosed that the government had equipped 800 artisans and 400 tradesmen across 60 trade associations with modern working tools.

The ministry had also facilitated the distribution of 1,425 Point of Sale (PoS) machines in partnership with Wembley Bank to expand digital financial inclusion and support participation in the growing digital economy.

In her remarks, the Executive Secretary of LSETF, Feyisayo Alayande, said the fund had disbursed more than ₦15 billion in loans to over 20,000 beneficiaries since its establishment 10 years ago.

She described the fund’s repayment performance of nearly 95 per cent as evidence that public sector financing could achieve commercial discipline while delivering measurable economic and social benefits.

“Every ₦100 entrusted to our entrepreneurs is repaid and redeployed to fuel the next business venture,” she said.

Alayande explained that the revolving financing model had enabled the fund to create more than 320,000 jobs directly and indirectly, while safeguarding approximately 173,000 others that might otherwise have been lost to economic pressures.

She added that the fund had also trained or connected more than 30,000 young people to employment opportunities and supported over 1,200 technology start-ups through its Lagos Innovates programme.

title: Galatasaray apologise over Samsunspor match relocation
description:
Turkish football giants Galatasaray have apologised to supporters following the relocation of their home match against Samsunspor to Başakşehir Fatih Terim Stadium due to ongoing pitch renovation work.
The club announced that the fixture would no longer take place at their home stadium, explaining t
content:
Turkish football giants Galatasaray have apologised to supporters following the relocation of their home match against Samsunspor to Başakşehir Fatih Terim Stadium due to ongoing pitch renovation work.

The club announced that the fixture would no longer take place at their home stadium, explaining that the renovation was necessary to provide the team with the best possible playing conditions.

In a statement to supporters on Wednesday on its X handle, Galatasaray acknowledged the inconvenience and disappointment caused by the decision, particularly among season ticket holders.

The club said, “We regret that we will not be able to welcome our team and supporters to our home ground for this match.

“We are aware of the inconvenience and disappointment this decision has caused all our supporters, particularly our season ticket holders.”

To compensate affected supporters, Galatasaray announced that all 2026/27 season ticket holders would receive priority rights to purchase tickets for the Samsunspor encounter.

The priority ticket sales window will run from 11am on Thursday, November 19, until 3pm on Friday, November 20.

The club also announced that an amount equivalent to the ticket price paid for their most recent home match would be deducted from the cost of renewing or purchasing season tickets for the following season.

Additionally, all season ticket holders will receive special gift vouchers redeemable at GSStore outlets.

Galatasaray said the measures were introduced in recognition of the loyalty and sacrifices of supporters who continue to back the club.

The Turkish champions also reaffirmed their determination to pursue a fifth consecutive league title under their #Hedef27 campaign, promising to continue their efforts with the support of their fans.

The statement added, “We know that what makes Galatasaray feel at home is not just its stadium, but its great supporters, who are always by its side.”

The club expressed appreciation for the understanding of supporters and reiterated that their backing remained crucial as the team continued its pursuit of domestic success.

description:
From Jude Chinedu, Enugu

content:
From Jude Chinedu, Enugu

The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) governorship candidate in Enugu State, Chief Uche Nnaji, has stepped up his grassroots mobilisation for the 2027 governorship election with the inauguration of campaign coordinators across the state’s wards and local government areas.

The coordinators are expected to take his campaign message of recovering, rebuilding and industrialising Enugu to communities across the state as the race for the Lion Building gathers momentum.

Speaking at the inauguration, Nnaji expressed confidence in the team’s ability to deliver, claiming that his campaign already enjoyed more than 80 per cent support among the electorate.

He, however, urged the coordinators not to rest on their oars but work to expand the support base.

“Precisely, that’s why we picked them. The people here, you can see that their job will be very easy. We enjoy more than 80 per cent of our people’s support,” he said.

The PDP candidate used the occasion to restate his economic agenda, promising to ease the tax burden on residents, reduce the cost of governance, rebuild destroyed markets and create an environment where businesses and industries could thrive.

He accused the present administration of subjecting residents to multiple taxation, particularly through overlapping charges on land and property, describing the practice as an unnecessary burden on households and businesses.

Nnaji maintained that government should focus on improving the living conditions of the people rather than imposing levies that make life more expensive.

“Governance is not about making money. Governance is about creating an enabling environment for your people to prosper. You make your people make money and live a good life,” he said.

On industrialisation, he identified inadequate electricity supply as a major obstacle to economic growth, promising to connect Enugu to the national grid and develop a stable power supply system to attract industries and generate employment.

“We will start by connecting to the grid and developing effective power supply to our people of Enugu. That way, industries will be stable, more industries will come in, and our people will be okay. Employment will soar,” he said.

He also urged residents to resist electoral manipulation and defend their votes in 2027, advising them not to allow financial inducements to determine their political choices.

“Take the money! It is not their money. They came empty-handed. It is now they are acquiring properties, buying cars and houses. It is not their money and it can never be their money,” he said.

Former Deputy Speaker of the Enugu State House of Assembly and Diaspora Community Coordinator, Jonathan Chukwuma, pledged the support of Enugu indigenes living abroad for Nnaji’s ambition.

Chukwuma, who resides in Georgia, United States, said members of the diaspora understood the importance of good governance and were prepared to contribute to the development of their home state.

The campaign’s Director-General, Charles Ndukwe, said the coordinators were carefully selected after interviews to establish their understanding of the campaign’s vision and readiness to work towards its success.

title: JUST IN: Presidential assent in view as Tinubu receives State Police Bill
description:
President Bola Tinubu has received the Constitution (Sixth Alteration) Bill, which seeks to pave the way for the establishment of state police in Nigeria.
The bill was formally presented to the President by his Special Advisers on Senate and House of Representatives Matters, Senator Basheer Lado and
content:
President Bola Tinubu has received the Constitution (Sixth Alteration) Bill, which seeks to pave the way for the establishment of state police in Nigeria.

The bill was formally presented to the President by his Special Advisers on Senate and House of Representatives Matters, Senator Basheer Lado and Dr Wasiu Olanrewaju-Smart.

The development was announced in a statement by the President’s Chief of Staff and Chairman of the Presidential Working Group on State Police, Rt. Hon. Femi Gbajabiamila.

The proposed amendment is aimed at providing the constitutional backing required for the creation of state police, a move expected to decentralise policing and give state governments a greater role in addressing security challenges.

‎According to the statement, “All 36 State Houses of Assembly have approved the Bill, exceeding the constitutional requirement of at least 24 States, representing two-thirds of the 36 States, as stipulated in Section 9(2) of the Constitution.”

‎It further stated that President Tinubu will review the Constitution Alteration Bill in consultation with the Attorney-General of the Federation.

‎”He will assent to the bill at a formal signing ceremony,” it added.

‎Meanwhile, Honourable Gbajabiamila, has said that the Presidential Working Group on State Police, which he chairs, with the support of the Policy Advisory Committee, has undertaken extensive stakeholder engagement and nationwide consultations towards developing a draft National Policing Bill.

‎”The draft bill has been submitted to the Federal Ministry of Justice for legislative drafting validation. Upon receipt of the validated version, the Working Group will review it and present it, alongside its report, to Mr President for consideration,” he said.

‎The former Speaker of the House of Representatives stated, “President Tinubu expresses his appreciation to the President of the Senate, the Speaker of the House of Representatives, members of the National Assembly, the Clerk to the National Assembly, the 36 State Governors, the State Houses of Assembly, and all Nigerians who have demonstrated a shared commitment to addressing the nation’s security challenges.”

title: No serious rift between Tinubu, Makinde – Oyo monarch
description:
The Olugbon of Orile-Igbon, Oba Francis Alao, on Wednesday disclosed that there was no rift between President Bola Tinubu and Oyo State Governor Seyi Makinde, saying “whatever disagreements between the duo would be resolved before the 2027 election.”
He made this known while receiving the APM govern
content:
The Olugbon of Orile-Igbon, Oba Francis Alao, on Wednesday disclosed that there was no rift between President Bola Tinubu and Oyo State Governor Seyi Makinde, saying “whatever disagreements between the duo would be resolved before the 2027 election.”

He made this known while receiving the APM governorship candidate in Oyo State, Bimbo Adekanmbi, his running mate, Mufutau Open-Salawu, and other party chieftains at his palace in Orile-Igbon, Surulere Local Government Area of the state.

Alao stressed that he was confident that the two leaders would resolve whatever differences they had, adding that he would attend the President’s scheduled visit to Ibadan on Saturday.

“There is no issue between Makinde and Tinubu. It is a family affair. It is a father and son issue. We will resolve all the issues before 2027,” he said.

He also expressed confidence that the South-West would retain the presidency until 2031, saying efforts would be made to secure the support of political stakeholders in the North.

“It is sacrosanct that the South-West should retain the presidency until 2031. We appeal to our people in the North to show understanding and allow us to maintain the North-South balance,” he said.

Recalling his meeting with Tinubu in 2023, the monarch said the President had told him that his administration inherited both assets and liabilities.

“When I visited President Tinubu in 2023, he told me that he had inherited both assets and liabilities. He has fantastic policies, but his policies are transformative. Before they become fully effective, they require time,” Olugbon said.

Alao recalled his support for Tinubu’s presidential ambition in 2023, saying he was among the few traditional rulers in the South-West who openly declared their support for the President at the time.

“Nobody can intimidate us. We have been in this game for a very long time. I was the National Secretary of the Tunji Braithwaite Foundation, but it is during critical situations that we come out.”

Describing both Tinubu and Makinde as close associates, the traditional ruler said his loyalty to the President did not diminish his relationship with the Oyo governor.

“Tinubu is a very close person to me, just like Makinde. Tinubu is a very good person, and Makinde is a very good person. The President knows how we played the game in 2023. But at the same time, Makinde is my man. I belong to the same political institution of the late Governor Abiola Ajimobi. Zacch is also from that political school.

“Zacch Adedeji is my son. Omo daadaa ni (He is a good child). But must we fight? We belong to the same family,” he said.

The monarch also praised Makinde’s administration for its management of state resources, particularly the payment of salaries, infrastructure development and care for retirees. He challenged Adekanmbi to surpass the governor’s achievements if elected in 2027.

“Before the allocation increased, Makinde was managing the resources of the state very well. Makinde pays salaries, promotes infrastructure development and takes care of retirees. You must do more than what Makinde has done. Please, serve Oyo State very well,” he said.

On Adekanmbi’s ambition, Oba Alao described him as a brilliant person and disclosed that the APM candidate had received endorsements from traditional rulers in other parts of the state.

“Before I arrived yesterday, Ogbomoso had already endorsed Bimbo. We must work collectively. I have known Bimbo for a while now, and he is a brilliant person.

“Onpetu, Oba Sunday Oyediran, and the Soun of Ogbomoso, Oba Ghandi Olaoye, have endorsed Bimbo. So, what am I going to do? I will pray for you.

“A week before the election, as I did in 2023, I will tell you who the next governor of Oyo State will be.

“All the governorship candidates are from Ibadan, but some Ibadan people are closer to Ogbomoso and Ibarapa. The Ibadan candidate who is close to us is the one we are endorsing.

“All the traditional rulers in Surulere asked me to tell you that they have endorsed you. We will ensure that we deliver the right candidate in 2027,” the monarch said.

Earlier, Adekanmbi said he visited the palace to pay homage to the monarch, whom he described as a father and mentor, rather than for political reasons.

“Baba is an accountant, and I am an accountant too. I have been drinking from his fountain of knowledge for a long time, and I will continue to do so.

“We must ensure that Oyo State moves forward and not backwards. It is about sustaining the good work Governor Makinde is doing. From the first day we assume office, it will be about continuity. We are here for Baba to pray for us. I am the APM governorship candidate and Olugbon’s son. We have heard everything you have told us, and I can assure you that we will implement them,” he stated.

Adekanmbi subsequently presented the party’s candidates for the various elective positions in Oyo North Senatorial District to the monarch ahead of the 2027 general elections.

title: Uzodimma, Sule: Governments must stop imposing projects on citizens at WPRF panel
description:
• Say communities must shape development priorities from conception to implementation
Governments must stop imposing development projects on communities and instead involve citizens in identifying their needs, setting priorities and determining how projects are implemented, Imo State Governor, Hope
content:
• Say communities must shape development priorities from conception to implementation

Governments must stop imposing development projects on communities and instead involve citizens in identifying their needs, setting priorities and determining how projects are implemented, Imo State Governor, Hope Uzodimma, and his Nasarawa State counterpart, Abdullahi Sule, have said.

The governors said public trust could only be sustained when citizens were actively involved in governance and could see their contributions reflected in policies, projects and service delivery.

They spoke during a panel session on “Responsible Governance and Communication: Building Trust through Community Engagement, Stakeholder Relations and Inclusive Impact” at the 2026 World Public Relations Forum in Abuja.

Uzodimma said his administration’s approach to governance was anchored on engaging stakeholders from the beginning of the decision-making process rather than presenting them with decisions already taken.

He explained that citizens and relevant groups were involved in planning, designing frameworks, developing ideas and implementing projects to ensure that government interventions reflected the actual needs of the people.

According to him, inclusive governance requires bringing different segments of society, including women, young people, persons with disabilities, students, traditional rulers, security agencies and political stakeholders,into the process.

He said his administration established an agency for persons with disabilities to ensure that their concerns were recognised and that they were not excluded from government programmes and decision-making.

Uzodimma stressed that participation must go beyond consultation, adding that citizens should be able to identify how their suggestions translate into concrete projects.

He said such an approach creates a sense of ownership among the people and strengthens confidence in government.

The governor also drew attention to the challenge posed by misinformation in the social media era, noting that information, whether true or false, could circulate rapidly and shape public perception.

He emphasised the need for strategic and transparent communication to ensure that citizens receive accurate information about government policies and activities.

On his part, Sule said development planning in Nasarawa State was based on identifying gaps and priorities with the involvement of the people, particularly in areas such as infrastructure, education and youth development.

He said citizens were not merely recipients of government projects but participants in the planning and design processes.

“They are part of the planning. They are part of the design,” Sule said, explaining that involving the people helped ensure that projects addressed their needs.

The governor said transparency and honesty were essential to building public confidence, adding that citizens should be able to assess government performance by comparing their circumstances and the level of development over time.

He noted that government policies and decisions must be guided by the law and informed by the realities and expectations of the people.

Sule said governments must work with citizens rather than assume that officials alone knew what communities needed.

In her remarks, the moderator, Ms Shreya Krishnan, Managing Director of AnitaB.org India and Chair of the Policy Advocacy Committee of UNESCO’s Women for Ethical AI in South Asia, said public trust was shaped not merely by government messaging but by citizens’ actual experiences.

She said people judged government by whether they were heard, whether decisions were explained, whether public services improved and whether authorities reached communities that needed attention.

“Public trust is shaped by more than what governments say. It is built by what citizens experience,” Krishnan said.

She challenged the governors to explain how they ensured that communication was backed by responsible decisions and tangible delivery, so that public confidence was earned through action rather than words.

In her concluding remarks, Krishnan said public trust could not be built through a single announcement or campaign, stressing that responsible communication must be reflected in how governments listen, make decisions, engage stakeholders and deliver outcomes citizens could see and experience.

She said effective public communication could not be separated from the quality of governance, adding that governments must demonstrate through their actions that citizens’ voices mattered.

The post Uzodimma, Sule: Governments must stop imposing projects on citizens at WPRF panel appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.
