title: Reps divided over proposal to write off farmers’ loans
description: A motion seeking the cancellation of outstanding loans obtained by Nigerian farmers under government-backed agricultural intervention programmes has divided members of the House of Representatives, with lawmakers disagreeing over whether debt forgiveness would offer relief to struggling farmers or r
content:
A motion seeking the cancellation of outstanding loans obtained by Nigerian farmers under government-backed agricultural intervention programmes has divided members of the House of Representatives, with lawmakers disagreeing over whether debt forgiveness would offer relief to struggling farmers or reward beneficiaries who diverted the funds.

The motion, moved on Wednesday by the member representing Yamaltu/Deba Federal Constituency, Gombe State, Inuwa Garba, sought a waiver of outstanding agricultural loans, citing insecurity, climate-related disasters and prevailing economic hardship that have undermined farmers’ ability to repay their debts.

Garba argued that many beneficiaries were unable to meet their repayment obligations because circumstances beyond their control had severely affected their farming activities, investments and incomes.

Over the years, the Federal Government, through the Central Bank of Nigeria and other financial institutions, introduced several agricultural financing initiatives, including the Anchor Borrowers’ Programme, the Commercial Agriculture Credit Scheme and NIRSAL-supported facilities, to boost food production, empower farmers and strengthen national food security.

Leading the debate on the motion, Garba said, “The House is concerned that widespread insecurity, banditry, insurgency, farmer-herder conflicts, flooding, drought, climate change and other natural and human-induced disasters like soil degradation, poor soil fertility, poor irrigation infrastructure and inadequate veterinary and disease control services have severely disrupted agricultural activities, resulting in substantial crop failures, food insufficiency, loss of investments and diminished farm incomes.

“The House is concerned that many beneficiaries of government-sponsored agricultural loans have been unable to meet their repayment obligations, not necessarily due to unwillingness to repay, but because circumstances beyond their control have substantially undermined their productive capacity and financial stability.

“We are worried that the continued accumulation and enforcement of outstanding agricultural debts, including principal, interest and penalties, could push already distressed farmers into deeper poverty, expose them to asset seizures and discourage their participation in future agricultural activities,” he said.

He further argued that compelling financially distressed farmers to repay the loans under prevailing economic conditions could undermine the objectives of the intervention programmes.

According to him, such pressure could worsen food insecurity, unemployment and poverty in rural communities rather than strengthen agricultural production.

However, opposing the proposed blanket waiver, the member representing Ede South/Ede North/Ejigbo/Egbedore Federal Constituency, Osun State, Bamidele Salam, said an audit report by the Auditor-General for the Federation before the House had exposed widespread abuse of the agricultural financing schemes.

Salam alleged that some beneficiaries who accessed more than N1tn under the Anchor Borrowers’ Programme diverted the funds into businesses and investments unrelated to agriculture, including real estate acquisitions.

He called for a comprehensive investigation into the intervention programmes to establish how the loans were utilised and identify beneficiaries who genuinely invested the funds in farming.

He said, “Over a trillion naira, given up as loans under the Anchor Borrowers Programme, a CBN intervention programme for Nigerian farmers, was largely abused by beneficiaries. People came, approached the CBN or their money deposit banks, and obtained loans for the purpose of farming, but diverted those monies into some other area of business endeavour, buying real estate in Abuja, in Lagos, and some in Dubai.

“The Bank of Agriculture, which unfortunately was set up as that special purpose vehicle for supporting farmers, has today become virtually immobile as a result of a sum of N795bn borrowed by persons, most of whom diverted that money into other purposes.”

Salam, who chairs the House Committee on Public Accounts, said granting a blanket waiver without first establishing the circumstances surrounding the loans would set a dangerous precedent.

“If we come as a parliament and recommend a holistic waiving of all loans given out to persons who are purportedly to be farmers, we will be setting a very, very dangerous precedent for people to come, access government facilities, some of them interest-free, some of them single-digit interest, only for them to go and use those monies for other things,” he said.

He consequently called for the constitution of an investigative committee or the outright rejection of the motion.

Also opposing an immediate blanket waiver, an Ogun State lawmaker, Isiaka Ibrahim, cited instances of beneficiaries who allegedly obtained government-backed loans but spent the money on personal engagements, including marrying additional wives.

He, however, said a thorough investigation would help identify farmers genuinely affected by economic hardship and unable to meet their repayment obligations.

Similarly, another All Progressives Congress lawmaker from Lagos State, Paul Kalejaiye, urged the House to exercise caution, stressing the need to investigate how beneficiaries utilised funds obtained under the various agricultural intervention programmes before considering any debt relief.

The disagreement prevented the House from reaching a resolution on the motion, prompting lawmakers to defer further consideration of the matter until Tuesday, November 24.

The proposed waiver has brought into focus the challenge of balancing relief for farmers whose livelihoods have been disrupted by insecurity and other economic pressures with accountability for public funds committed to agricultural development.

The outcome of the legislative consideration could have implications for the recovery of government-backed agricultural loans, the credibility of future intervention schemes and efforts to improve food production in the country.

The post Reps divided over proposal to write off farmers’ loans appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

content:
The presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Atiku Abubakar, has been included in the final list of candidates for the 2027 election released by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC).

The list, released on Wednesday, listed Atiku’s educational qualifications to include a First School Leaving Certificate, West African School Certificate and a Master’s Degree in International Relations.

It listed Atiku’s current age as 79.

Naija News reports that the list also included the name of Rotimi Amaechi as the ADC vice-presidential candidate for the 2027 elections.

Advertisement
Amaechi, 61, is listed as holding a Bachelor of Arts degree in English Studies.

The listing is despite the recent court order by Justice Peter Lifu of the Federal High Court, which sacked the David Mark- led national leadership of the ADC.

The ruling also effectively nullifies all actions taken by the Mark-led leadership, including Atiku’s emergence as the party’s presidential candidate.

The INEC list also featured President Bola Tinubu as the candidate of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Peter Obi as the candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), and Seyi Makinde as the candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), among others.

General elections will be held in Nigeria on 16 January 2027 to elect the president and vice president, members of the Senate and House of Representatives.

Advertisement
Elections for state governors and members of the House of Assembly will be held on 6 February 2027.

content:
PUBLIC NOTICE

MONI PULO LIMITED: CLARIFICATION ON MISLEADING PUBLICATIONS

We consider it necessary to issue this clarification following recent media publications concerning our Executive Chairman, Dr. Seinye Lulu-Briggs. The publications contain misleading assertions and representations which warrant clarification in the interest of truth, fairness and the confidence ofour stakeholders and the general public.

These very libelous publications, which originated from a purported petition by an organisation identified as the Public Interest and Diplomatic Centre (PIDC), sought to create the impression that our Executive Chairman was the subject of an outstanding criminal process, was evading lawenforcement authorities and was liable to arrest in connection with certain court proceedings. The representations are misleading, malicious and do not reflect the true position of the matter.

For the avoidance of doubt, there is no criminal charge pending against Dr. Seinye Lulu-Briggs in respect of any matter whatsoever and definitely not in respect of the matters being referenced in these publications. Theunderlying disputes relate to shareholding and interests in the Company.They are civil and corporate matters which have been fully litigated before the courts in Nigeria with the judgements and rulings delivered in favour of Moni Pulo Limited and our Executive Chairman.

It is therefore fundamentally misleading and terrible to portray these corporate and shareholding disputes as evidence of criminal wrongdoing or to suggest that our Executive Chairman is a fugitive from justice or isseeking to evade law enforcement authorities.

Furthermore, the purported Public Interest and Diplomatic Centre, onwhose representation the publications appear to have been predicated, does not exist. It is not registered with the Corporate Affairs Commission. This raises legitimate questions about these faceless unscrupulous persons and the authority under which they purport to act.

We wish to state unequivocally that our Executive Chairman remains a free citizen, continues to conduct her legitimate personal and business affairs without restraint and has no pending criminal charge arising from the referenced shareholding disputes.

Contrary to the wild, calculated, deliberate, misinformed, false, mischievous and callous publication in respect and concerning our Executive Chairman, we wish to point out the following unassailable points:

i. Our Executive Chairman is a private businesswoman who has invested heavily in the oil and gas sector in Nigeria and currently the Executive Chairman of one of the first indigenous exploration and production companies in Nigeria.
ii. For three decades, Moni Pulo Limited has maintained a significant presence in Nigeria’s oil and gas industry as an indigenous exploration and production company. And for 15 of those years, our Executive Chairmanhas remained the majority shareholder of the Company. The Company hasbuilt its reputation through sustained investment, operational experience,industry participation and contributions to the development of Nigeria’s petroleum resources.
iii. Our Executive Chairman’s huge investment in the oil and gas sector are products of her efforts in private business without any taint of any proceedof crime.
iv. She is a responsible, respectable, decent and accomplished businesswoman and philanthropist who has touched the lives of so many people both in Nigeria and beyond.
v. All through her private business endeavours, our Executive Chairmanhas maintained a very decent record and significant impact which has brought fame, pride and recognition to her person, family, her people inRivers State, Nigeria and the global business community.
vi. As an evangelist who is also committed to the propagation of the gospel of salvation and of Christ, she abhors every form of criminality, has maintained an unblemished record and shall therefore resist every effort to link her with any form of criminality as the publication would appear to have done.
vii. By recklessly assaulting her integrity and painting her as a common fugitive, the publication has assaulted the credibility and integrity of our Executive Chairman and subjected her to embarrassment, humiliation, character assassination and public ridicule.

In light of the above, we hereby refute these malicious and libelous publications and state categorically that the publications are complete falsehood as there is no order/warrant of any court

in Nigeria as at today, made or issued for the arrest of our chairman. If anything, all those cases brought against our Executive Chairman andMoni Pulo Limited in court have all been fully litigated and resolved in our favour.

Moni Pulo Limited remains an active and operating oil and gas company under the visionary leadership of Dr. Seinye Lulu-Briggs. Our business operations continue, and the Company remains focused on its corporate objectives, operational responsibilities, business relationships and long-term growth prospects.

We therefore urge the general public to kindly disregard any story, news and/or publication issued and/or disseminated by any media outlet or entity either physically or online suggesting that there

is any warrant of arrest issued against our Executive Chairman. Our Executive Chairman is a free woman and have been exercising full rights of ingress in and egress out of Nigeria without any impairment and/or harassments by any law enforcement and this is not likely to change in the foreseeable future.

We appreciate the continued confidence, support and understanding of our business partners, associates, regulators, host communities and other stakeholders. We reassure you all and the public that Moni Pulo Limited will continue to conduct its affairs with the professionalism, diligence and corporate responsibility that have characterised its operations over the past three decades.

FOR MONI PULO LIMITED:

MANAGEMENT

title: 2027: Wike urges traders to reject subsidy reversal, back Tinubu’s re-election
description:
• says tough reforms will deliver prosperity, cites increased allocations, pension payments, end to ASUU strikes
Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, hasurged Nigerians to reject opposition politicians promising to reverse the removal of fuel subsidy, insisting that Presiden
content:
• says tough reforms will deliver prosperity, cites increased allocations, pension payments, end to ASUU strikes

Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, hasurged Nigerians to reject opposition politicians promising to reverse the removal of fuel subsidy, insisting that President Bola Tinubu’s difficult economic reforms are necessary to secure the country’s long-term prosperity.

Wike made the appeal on Wednesday at an interactive town hall meeting with market traders in Abuja. He also urged them to mobilise support for Tinubu’s re-election in 2027, arguing that previous administrations failed to address the subsidy regime because they lacked the courage to take difficult decisions.

Acknowledging the economic hardship occasioned by the subsidy removal, the minister described the former arrangement as a scam that nearly crippled the country, insisting that the reforms’ gains would become more evident if the policies were allowed to mature.

“This country was nearly gone. To try to change what is happening means you must lay a foundation first, and when you lay a foundation, you give it time to grow,” he said.

Wike argued that successive administrations recognised the problems associated with fuel subsidy but failed to address them due to political considerations.

“There’s no government has not identified that this oil subsidy is a scam, why university teachers cannot work, no payment of salaries, no payment of pensioners. Everybody is afraid, they lacked courage. If you don’t have good leaders who have courage to take decisions, that country will not grow,” he said.

The minister listed increased revenue allocations to states and local governments, clearance of pension arrears and the absence of strikes by the Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU) for more than three and a half years among the benefits of the reforms.

He warned Nigerians against politicians campaigning on promises to reverse the policies, saying such assurances could derail the country’s recovery.

“If we allow these policies that the government has put in place to mature, what is going to happen in the next four years will be good. Forget about people coming to tell you stories,” he said.

Turning to his administration’s performance in the FCT, Wike said ongoing and completed road projects across satellite towns and districts, including Gwarinpa and Kubwa, were designed to improve commercial activities and reduce transportation costs for traders.

He also promised to facilitate further development of markets in the territory and institutionalise regular engagements with market associations at least twice a year.

The minister highlighted what he described as significant institutional changes in the FCT under Tinubu, including the appointment of an indigene of the territory to represent it in the Federal Executive Council for the first time since its creation in 1976.

He also cited the establishment of the FCT Civil Service Commission, which provides career progression opportunities for civil servants to attain the positions of Permanent Secretary and Head of Service, as well as the creation of Mandate Secretariats for Women and Youth.

Wike urged the traders to assess political leadership based on performance rather than ethnic or regional considerations.

“Governance has nothing to do with where I come from. It is not about Hausa, Yoruba, or Igbo; it is about ‘If I do my business here, am I happy?'” he said.

He also criticised opposition figures, questioning former Vice President Atiku Abubakar’s handling of past privatisation exercises and faulting former Rivers State Governor Rotimi Amaechi over projects he said were left uncompleted, including the Port Harcourt monorail and a proposed 1,000-bed specialist hospital.

The minister urged the traders to become actively involved in the 2027 campaign structure, asking market associations to nominate two representatives from each state chapter to serve on the campaign committee. He promised logistical support for grassroots mobilisation.

Responding, market leaders pledged to mobilise support for Tinubu and other candidates aligned with the administration in the 2027 elections, citing infrastructure development and market reforms in the FCT.

The Group Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Abuja Investments Company Limited (AICL), Ambassador Maureen Tamuno, described the meeting as a landmark engagement, saying it demonstrated Wike’s willingness to interact directly with traders and address issues affecting their businesses.

She commended the minister’s road construction and rehabilitation projects across the city centre and satellite towns, particularly the Saburi Road corridor, which she said had improved commercial movement.

Tamuno also disclosed that Wike had approved the procurement of a dedicated fire truck and establishment of a fire station within Wuse Market, describing the intervention as a major step towards improving safety.

She urged traders to reciprocate government interventions by complying with market rules and regulations.

Chairman of the Wuse Market Traders Association, Okorie Ikechukwu-Raphael, commended the minister for the rehabilitation of internal market roads, redevelopment of shops and opening up of communities across the FCT.

He appealed for approval for AICL to develop new shops and malls in emerging districts, including Katampe and Kaura, to provide traders with opportunities to expand their businesses.

He also declared the readiness of traders to commence grassroots political mobilisation through trade unions, cooperatives and community groups.

“Today, Your Excellency, we want to confirm to you that we are going into cluster mobilisation. Whoever follows you knows the road,” he said.

Similarly, Chairman of the Arewa Traders Association, Alhaji Adamu Ibrahim, pledged the support of northern traders for Tinubu, Vice President Kashim Shettima and other candidates aligned with the administration in the FCT.

He urged the minister to give market leaders a stronger voice in the formulation of policies affecting their businesses.

Also speaking, Chairperson of the National Assembly Quarters (Zone A) Market, Mrs Abiola Adekanbi, who said she had lived in Abuja for 26 years, described the pace of road construction under Wike as unprecedented.

She recalled the rehabilitation of previously deplorable roads around Sunnyvale and pledged the support of market women for Tinubu’s re-election.

Adekanbi said the traders would not only vote for the President but also remain at polling units to protect their votes.

“It is very simple: we are going to follow who knows the road. We are going to follow the ‘talk-and-do,'” she said.

The post 2027: Wike urges traders to reject subsidy reversal, back Tinubu’s re-election appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: iDICE targets 226 start-ups with $617m programme
description:
Lagos advises founders to focus on customer needs
______________________________________________________________________
By Chinenye Anuforo
The Federal Government’s Investment in Digital and Creative Enterprises (iDICE) programme is targeting at least 226 Nigerian start-ups for support through a $6
content:
Lagos advises founders to focus on customer needs

______________________________________________________________________

By Chinenye Anuforo

The Federal Government’s Investment in Digital and Creative Enterprises (iDICE) programme is targeting at least 226 Nigerian start-ups for support through a $617 million initiative, its National Coordinator, Ife Adebayo, has said.

Adebayo spoke on Wednesday at the southern preliminary of the iDICE Startup Summit in Lagos, where founders in the creative and digital technology sectors met investors, operators and policymakers.

He said the programme was designed to address gaps in skills, access to finance and policy support for businesses in the two sectors.

“We want to ensure that we have a conveyor belt of skills that continues to churn out people with the right level of skills for the sector,” Adebayo said.

He added that the programme would provide “patient capital and blended finance options for start-ups” and work with regulators and policymakers to promote policies that support the sectors.

The initiative is backed by the Federal Government, the African Development Bank, the French Development Agency, the Islamic Development Bank and the Bank of Industry.

Adebayo said Ventures Platform Limited, the programme’s technology fund manager, had launched its fund with an $84 million close, while Kuramo Capital was raising funds. He said iDICE was also concluding the process of appointing a creative fund manager.

The programme includes a $45 million Bank of Industry debt fund, with loans offered at a 10 per cent rate, he said. An Islamic finance option, funded by the Islamic Development Bank, is also available.

“About four start-ups have benefited from the tech fund,” Adebayo said, adding that applications for the debt funds were being processed through partner banks.

He said the application portal remained open, while banks assessed applications to determine which businesses qualified for funding.

On risk-sharing, Adebayo said the Federal Government had offered fund managers a 30 per cent first-loss position on equity investments. “If any of the start-ups fail, the Federal Government takes a 30 per cent first-loss position with the fund managers,” he said.

Lagos State Commissioner for Innovation, Science and Technology, Olatunbosun Alake, urged founders to identify a clear market niche and build products that meet customer needs.

“Start-ups need to identify a particular niche they want to deliver value in,” Alake said. “If you are delivering a service or a good better than what people are doing now, trust me, you will find consumers, customers and financiers.”

He said Lagos had supported nearly 100 start-ups through direct funding and programmes offering access to internet, electricity and office space.

Alake, however, warned that “it’s not just having an idea”; founders needed to research their markets, understand customer groups and build a structure capable of delivering their products or services.

Creative economy lawyer and managing partner at Zaeda Oracle Solicitors, Foza Oyinkansola Fawehinmi, advised founders to delegate as their businesses grow.

“Start-up mentality can work for one year, but after that year, you need to move away from that start-up mentality and begin to function as a CEO,” she said. “You can be a founder and not have CEO skills.”

Fawehinmi also urged entrepreneurs to seek professional advice and stay informed about government support schemes. “Hire professionals that understand the context and industry you work in and spend money looking for information,” she said.

The summit series continues in Ilorin on 23 November, with the national final scheduled for Abuja on 30 November.

title: African ministers move to establish annual conference to tackle fake news, misinformation
description:
• Nigeria to host the inaugural meeting as Idris calls for a united continental voice on global communication challenges

African ministers of information have agreed to establish an annual continental conference to develop a common position on misinformation, fake news and other communication chall
content:
• Nigeria to host the inaugural meeting as Idris calls for a united continental voice on global communication challenges

African ministers of information have agreed to establish an annual continental conference to develop a common position on misinformation, fake news and other communication challenges confronting the continent.

Nigeria’s Minister of Information and National Orientation, Mohammed Idris, disclosed this on Wednesday in Abuja, saying the initiative aimed to ensure African countries speak with one voice on issues affecting their collective interests.

Idris, who spoke on the sidelines of the 2026 World Public Relations Forum (WPRF) in Abuja, said the ministers had resolved that African countries could no longer afford to confront common communication challenges independently.

He said Nigeria would host the inaugural edition of the annual African Ministers Conference, which is expected to provide a platform for ministers across the continent to harmonise their positions and develop common strategies for engaging the international community.

According to him, although the conference existed in the past, it was abandoned but would now be revived for the benefit of African countries.

“The outcome is that ministers of information from the African continent have found it necessary to meet on the sidelines of the World Public Relations Forum happening in Abuja.

“One of the key resolutions is that, as Africans, we have found it necessary to confront our challenges collectively.

“The challenges of misinformation and fake news are what every country, not just on the African continent, is facing. So, we thought that as Africans, we should forge a common front, and as Africans, we have agreed to speak with one voice,” he said.

The minister said the absence of a coordinated African communication strategy had often weakened the continent’s ability to effectively project its interests on the global stage.

Using the COVID-19 pandemic as an example, Idris said African countries largely communicated their positions individually rather than adopting a coordinated continental response, a situation he described as undesirable.

He also cited the emergence of African rating agencies as an area requiring stronger continental collaboration, particularly in addressing concerns around access to capital and credit for businesses operating across the continent.

“If you look at the issue of the African rating agencies that the African continent came about, if we feel there is the necessity for us to communicate to our people so that access to capital, access to credit can be easier for our business people on the continent, this can only be achieved if we come together and form a common front for our people,” he said.

On concerns over the alleged use of doctored artificial intelligence-generated images by the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) at its campaign rallies, Idris rejected the suggestion that the ruling party was responsible for misinformation.

He instead alleged that opposition elements were involved in the misuse of artificial intelligence, though he provided no specific evidence to substantiate the claim.

“It is wrong for you to say that the ruling party has been accused of misinformation. We have seen the issue of misinformation, fake news and misuse of AI, but we feel this is not our forte. We actually feel the opposition is using them,” he said.

The minister, however, acknowledged the potential dangers of the irresponsible use of artificial intelligence and digital platforms, stressing that technology should promote understanding, unity and constructive communication.

He said technological innovation is irreversible and could offer significant benefits if properly harnessed.

“AI is very useful to us, but responsible use of AI is what is desirable to foster greater understanding and greater unity amongst us.

“The misuse of it can create chaos, division and disunity. And that is why all of us must use only responsible communication, responsible use of the digital platforms, including AI, to foster better understanding, communication and unity for our people,” Idris said.

He said the proposed annual conference would provide an opportunity for African countries to collectively address these challenges and strengthen the continent’s voice in international affairs.

The post African ministers move to establish annual conference to tackle fake news, misinformation appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Tinubu Receives State Police Bill, Prepares For Assent
description: President Bola Tinubu has received the Constitution (Sixth Alteration) Bill, which provides for the establishment of State Police in Nigeria.Chief of Staff to the President, Femi Gbajabiamila, confirmed this in a statement on Wednesday.Gbajabiamila said that the bill was formally transmitted to Tinu
content:
President Bola Tinubu has received the Constitution (Sixth Alteration) Bill, which provides for the establishment of State Police in Nigeria.

Chief of Staff to the President, Femi Gbajabiamila, confirmed this in a statement on Wednesday.

Gbajabiamila said that the bill was formally transmitted to Tinubu on Wednesday by his Special Advisers on Senate and House of Representatives Matters, Senator Basheer Lado and Wasiu Olanrewaju-Smart.

He said that the President would review the Constitution Alteration Bill in consultation with the Attorney-General of the Federation, Lateef Fagbemi, and assent to it at a formal signing ceremony.

Meanwhile, Gbajabiamila, who is the Chairman of the Presidential Working Group on State Police, said the working group, with the support of the Policy Advisory Committee, has undertaken extensive stakeholder engagement and nationwide consultations towards developing a draft National Policing Bill.

He noted that the draft bill had been submitted to the Federal Ministry of Justice for legislative drafting validation.

“Upon receipt of the validated version, the Working Group will review it and present it, alongside its report, to Mr President for consideration.

“President Tinubu expresses his appreciation to the President of the Senate, the Speaker of the House of Representatives, members of the National Assembly, the Clerk to the National Assembly, the 36 State Governors, the State Houses of Assembly, and all Nigerians who have demonstrated a shared commitment to addressing the nation’s security challenges,” he added.

The Senate had earlier directed the clerk to the National Assembly to transmit the Constitution alteration bill providing for the establishment of State Police to President Tinubu for assent.

The upper chamber had also asked the Executive to forward the National Policing Bill to the National Assembly for legislative scrutiny and expeditious passage to establish the operational framework for subnational policing.

The resolutions followed a motion sponsored by the Senate Leader, Opeyemi Bamidele, during plenary on Wednesday.

The Clerk to the National Assembly, Kamoru Ogunlana, announced on Monday that all 36 State Houses of Assembly had approved the proposed constitutional amendment to establish state police, clearing the way for the bill to be transmitted to the President.

The approval, he said, exceeded the constitutional requirement of at least 24 state assemblies under Section 9(2) of the 1999 Constitution, as amended.

Community Policing

Persistent security challenges in Nigeria have intensified calls for a policing system that brings law enforcement closer to communities, improves intelligence gathering and enables faster responses to local threats.

Supporters of state police argue that decentralising the current centralised structure would allow security agencies to better understand the peculiar challenges of different communities.

They also believe state-controlled forces could strengthen grassroots intelligence and complement existing security arrangements.

However, the proposal generated concerns about accountability, political interference and funding.

In September 2025, House of Representatives member Yusuf Gadgi argued that properly funded community policing would be more effective than state police, warning that placing police commands under governors could worsen insecurity.

But existing community-based security outfits, such as Amotekun in the South-West, have also faced operational limitations, including restricted access to superior weapons, despite their role in local security.

Human rights lawyer Femi Falana supported decentralised policing but warned that clear jurisdictions and legal safeguards are essential to prevent political intimidation and clashes between security agencies.

He also cautioned that state police alone cannot resolve insecurity without addressing poverty and unemployment.

The post Tinubu Receives State Police Bill, Prepares For Assent appeared first on Channels Television.

The facility, currently under rehabilitatio
content:
Osun State Government has renamed what was previously known as Osogbo City Stadium as Ademola Adeleke Imole Stadium, Osogbo.

The move came about one week to the second term inauguration of the governor, billed to hold at the renamed stadium on November 27.

The facility, currently under rehabilitation, had been the home ground for the state male and female football teams, until its condition deteriorated, forcing the teams to consider other alternatives for their league games.

Our correspondent, who visited the stadium on Wednesday to monitor preparation for the second term inauguration, reports that a large signpost announcing the new name of the facility had already been placed at a conspicuous point at the entrance to the stadium.

According to the programme line-up, the weeklong activities for the inauguration will commence with a Jummat at Osogbo Central Mosque, Oja Oba, Osogbo.

Inter-faith prayer session, the final of Ademola Adeleke Victory Soccer Tournament, inauguration lecture by Senator Shehu Sani on Federalism Dilemma: Navigating Institutional Friction, Local Government Allocations, and Executive Overreach, and thanksgiving service at All Souls’ Anglican Church Cathedral, Osogbo, are some other programmes scheduled to hold during the inauguration week.

A staff member of Osun Sports Council, whose office is located within the premises of the stadium, while speaking on condition of anonymity on the development since he was not officially permitted by government to speak on its behalf, said Adeleke is expected to pay an inspection visit to the facility in the coming days.

He added, “We all just observed that a big signpost announcing the new name was brought early this morning, Wednesday.

“It is true that the stadium has been named after the governor. We all witnessed it this morning, when those in charge brought the signpost and erected it at the entrance. However, there is no official announcement yet on the development.”

Efforts to reach the state Commissioner for Information and Public Enlightenment, Kolapo Alimi, and the spokesperson to the governor, Olawale Rasheed, for comment on the development failed.

The two officials could not be reached through their mobile lines as of 4:10pm on Wednesday when this report was filed.

They have also not responded to the messages that accompanied the pictures of the new name of the stadium sent to them.

title: Pochettino Arrives At Manchester United To Resume As Head Coach
description: Mauricio Pochettino arrived at Manchester United’s Carrington training ground on Wednesday to begin work as the club’s new manager, hours after leaving his role as USA coach.The Argentine ended his reign in the United States with a 2-0 win over Haiti in Cincinnati before flying to Britai
content:
Mauricio Pochettino arrived at Manchester United’s Carrington training ground on Wednesday to begin work as the club’s new manager, hours after leaving his role as USA coach.

The Argentine ended his reign in the United States with a 2-0 win over Haiti in Cincinnati before flying to Britain.

Pochettino was whisked to the club’s training base to meet United staff and start preparations for Sunday’s Premier League match against Liverpool.

His appointment was announced last Friday, 24 hours after United had confirmed the sacking of Michael Carrick following the Red Devils’ worst start to a top-flight campaign since the 1986/87 season.

The former Tottenham and Chelsea boss is understood to have signed a deal at Old Trafford until the end of the 2028/29 season.

On Tuesday, Pochettino said he needed time to make United the city’s dominant force again.

“The new challenge is a big challenge, but at the same time it’s adrenaline you want to feel,” he told TNT Sports US.

Sunday’s trip to Anfield will be a baptism of fire for the 54-year-old, whose new team are in the relegation zone after just one league win all season.

AFP

content:
President Bola Tinubu has received the constitutional amendment bill seeking to establish state police and will review it in consultation with the Attorney-General of the Federation before signing it into law.

The President’s Chief of Staff, Femi Gbajabiamila, disclosed this in a statement issued on Wednesday.

Gbajabiamila, who chairs the Presidential Working Group on State Police, said the bill was formally transmitted to Tinubu by his Special Advisers on Senate and House of Representatives Matters, Senator Basheer Lado and Dr Wasiu Olanrewaju-Smart.

He said all 36 State Houses of Assembly had approved the bill, exceeding the constitutional requirement of at least 24 states, representing two-thirds of the 36 states, under Section 9(2) of the 1999 Constitution.

“President Tinubu will review the Constitution Alteration Bill in consultation with the Attorney-General of the Federation. He will assent to the Bill at a formal signing ceremony,” Gbajabiamila said.

The Chief of Staff also disclosed that the Presidential Working Group on State Police, with support from the Policy Advisory Committee, had concluded extensive stakeholder engagements and nationwide consultations towards developing a draft National Policing Bill.

He said the draft legislation had been submitted to the Federal Ministry of Justice for legislative drafting validation.

“Upon receipt of the validated version, the Working Group will review it and present it, alongside its report, to Mr President for consideration,” he added.

Gbajabiamila said the President appreciated the leadership of the National Assembly, state governors, state lawmakers and other stakeholders for their contributions to the process.

The development followed the Senate’s resolution on Wednesday to transmit the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria (Sixth Alteration) Bill, 2026, to Tinubu for assent after all 36 state assemblies approved it.

The Senate’s resolution followed a motion sponsored by Senate Leader, Opeyemi Bamidele, who said the bill had fulfilled the constitutional requirements for an amendment.

The Senate and the House of Representatives had passed the bill on June 24 and July 23, 2026, respectively, before it was transmitted to the state assemblies for approval.

The proposed amendment seeks to establish State Police Services as part of Nigeria’s national policing structure, paving the way for a decentralised policing system alongside the existing federal police.

However, the constitutional amendment is separate from the National Policing Bill, which is expected to provide the legislative and operational framework for the proposed state police system.

title: 2027: INEC plans mock election in 638 Rivers polling units
description:
The Independent National Electoral Commission said it will conduct a mock accreditation and election results upload exercise in 638 polling units across Rivers State on November 28.
INEC said the move is part of preparatios for the general elections in 2027.
INEC Resident Electoral Commissioner in R
content:
The Independent National Electoral Commission said it will conduct a mock accreditation and election results upload exercise in 638 polling units across Rivers State on November 28.

INEC said the move is part of preparatios for the general elections in 2027.

INEC Resident Electoral Commissioner in Rivers State, Dr Johnson Sinikiem, disclosed this during the State-Level Stakeholders’ Meeting on the 2027 General Elections at the commission’s headquarters in Port Harcourt on Wednesday.

Sinikiem said two polling units would be selected in each of the state’s 319 registration areas, also known as wards, for the exercise.

He said the exercise will test the performance of the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System and network connectivity under real election conditions.

The INEC REC explained that the exercise was designed to identify possible technical challenges and assess the efficiency of the technology ahead of the general elections.

Sinikiem called on security agencies, political parties and the electorate to support the exercise to ensure its smooth conduct, saying adequate information would be provided to the public on the selected polling units and other arrangements for the exercise.

He said INEC was intensifying preparations for the 2027 elections, noting that Rivers State had approximately 3,736,434 registered voters spread across 23 local government areas, 319 registration areas and 6,866 polling units.

He disclosed that the commission currently had 6,399 fully functional and configured BVAS devices in its inventory.

He added that additional units would be deployed from the national headquarters to cover all polling units and provide operational backups.

The REC also announced that the commission had received 173,241 Permanent Voter Cards in different batches ahead of the elections.

Sinikiem further said 99,381 PVCs, comprising previously uncollected and newly printed cards, had been collected by voters as of Tuesday, November 17, urging those whose cards were ready to visit INEC offices in their respective local government areas.

He stated, “I strongly urge citizens who cards are available to visit our 23 LGA offices to claim them. Nationwide mock accreditation and results upload in Rivers State.

“INEC will be conducting a nationwide mock accreditation and result upload exercise on the 28th November 2026 to test the bimodal voter accreditation system, BVAS, ahead of the 2027 general elections.

“This exercise will span across all the 23 local government areas and 319 registration areas which is the wards across Rivers State.”

He noted that the commission had also taken delivery of essential non-sensitive election materials, including voting cubicles, mats, ballot boxes and other operational accessories, which had been audited and distributed to the 23 local government areas for safe storage.

He urged security agencies to strengthen surveillance around INEC offices to protect the materials against theft or damage.

On personnel mobilisation, Sinikiem said recruitment of ad hoc staff for the elections, which opened on September 18, would close at midnight on Wednesday, November 18.

He identified members of the National Youth Service Corps as critical partners in the electoral process, adding that the commission had sustained engagements with corps members to prepare them for their election duties.

The REC further disclosed that intensive training was ongoing for INEC personnel in electoral risk management, Election Monitoring and Support Centres, and the Collation Support and Result Verification System.

He said the training would improve risk assessment, field monitoring, rapid response and transparency in the collation of election results.

Sinikiem reiterated the commission’s commitment to conducting free, fair, credible, transparent and inclusive elections across Rivers State, stressing that the success of the electoral process required the cooperation of all stakeholders.

He said presidential and National Assembly elections were scheduled for January 16, 2027, while governorship and State House of Assembly elections would hold on February 6, 2027.

In his goodwill message, the Rivers State Commissioner of Police, Olugbenga Adepoju unveiled unveiled security measures to prevent electoral violence during the elections, including round-the-clock protection of INEC facilities, intelligence-led monitoring of flashpoints and deployment of more than 5,000 trained police officers.

CP Adepoju warned politicians, political parties and their supporters against thuggery, ballot snatching, vote buying and voter intimidation, declaring that anyone found sponsoring electoral violence would be arrested and prosecuted regardless of status.

He disclosed the measures during a stakeholders’ engagement on preparations for a peaceful and violence-free election in Rivers State.

Adepoju said it had concluded security planning in collaboration with other security agencies under the Inter-Agency Consultative Committee on Election Security, covering the state’s 23 local government areas, 319 wards and 6,866 polling units.

He said joint operational plans, patrol routes and deployment arrangements had been developed to secure the electoral process before, during and after the elections.

On the protection of electoral facilities and personnel, the police said arrangements had been concluded for 24-hour security at INEC offices, Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) vaults and Registration Area Centres.

He disclosed that more than 5,000 officers earmarked for election duties were undergoing refresher training on electoral laws, human rights and rules of engagement.

To improve public engagement and emergency response, he said the police had established an election situation room and control room, alongside dedicated telephone hotlines through which residents could report security incidents.

“Area commanders and Divisional Police Officers have also been directed to organise town hall meetings with stakeholders in their respective areas to identify community concerns and address potential threats before election day”, he said.

The police urged voters not to be intimidated by political interests, assuring them of adequate security to exercise their franchise.

He stressed that the responsibility for peaceful elections extended beyond security agencies, calling on INEC to ensure transparency in the electoral process and prompt transmission of results.

“Political parties and candidates are urged to sign and enforce peace accords, discipline their supporters and focus their campaigns on issues rather than personal attacks”, he said.

Adepoju also called on traditional rulers and religious leaders to use their influence to discourage do-or-die politics, mediate disputes and encourage communities to adopt peace commitments ahead of the elections.

He urged civil society organisations to intensify voter education, monitor the electoral process and report violations, particularly at the grassroots.

Also speaking, The National Orientation Agency in Rivers pledged to intensify grassroots mobilisation and voter education to discourage electoral violence, vote buying, hate speech and voter intimidation ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The agency said it would take its peace advocacy campaigns to communities, markets, schools, churches, mosques and youth groups to promote peaceful participation and responsible conduct before, during and after the elections.

The State Director of NOA, Dr Edward Banigo, described the 2027 general election as a collective responsibility rather than the exclusive business of INEC or political parties, stressing that its success would depend on cooperation among electoral authorities, security agencies, political actors and citizens.

He commended the level of preparedness demonstrated by INEC, security agencies, civil society organisations, the media, political parties and other stakeholders, particularly in early planning, voter education, deployment of materials and the adoption of technology to strengthen electoral transparency.

He said, “The 2027 general election is not just an INEC election. It is not a political party election. It is our election. And its success will depend on how prepared we are, how united we are, and how committed we are to peace.”

The NOA director warned political actors and their supporters against treating the elections as a do-or-die contest, urging them to reject violence, hate speech, vote buying, intimidation and misinformation.

He said credible elections could only be achieved through sustained collaboration among INEC, security agencies, political parties, candidates, observers, the judiciary, traditional and religious leaders, youth and women groups, and the media.

The meeting was attended by political party representatives, security agencies, youths, religious leaders, civil organisations and women groups among others.

The post 2027: INEC plans mock election in 638 Rivers polling units appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Nigeria needs competent workers to drive growth – Alausa
description:
The Minister of Education, Dr Tunji Alausa, has said Nigeria needs skilled workers capable of meeting industry demands rather than people who merely possess academic certificates, stressing the importance of practical competence in driving economic growth.
He said technical and vocational education
content:
The Minister of Education, Dr Tunji Alausa, has said Nigeria needs skilled workers capable of meeting industry demands rather than people who merely possess academic certificates, stressing the importance of practical competence in driving economic growth.

He said technical and vocational education must produce graduates who could secure employment, establish businesses and contribute to national development, rather than end with the award of certificates.

Alausa stated this on Wednesday in Abuja at the graduation and starter kit handover ceremony for the first cohort of beneficiaries of the Federal Government’s Technical and Vocational Education and Training Initiative.

He said Nigeria’s development depended on building a workforce equipped with practical skills to meet the needs of industry and society.

“Nigeria’s development depends on a workforce with the competence to meet the needs of industry and society.

“We need technicians who can maintain our machinery, electricians who can deliver safe installations, artisans who can build to high standards, and entrepreneurs who can turn their skills into sustainable businesses,” the minister said.

He stressed that vocational qualifications must reflect genuine occupational competence and command the confidence of employers.

“Qualifications under the National Skills Qualification Framework must represent genuine occupational competence and earn the confidence of employers,” he added.

The minister said the Federal Government would strengthen competency-based assessments, certification, employment tracking and entrepreneurship support to ensure that beneficiaries translated their training into sustainable livelihoods.

According to him, the success of the initiative would not be determined by the number of people trained but by the opportunities they secured after graduation.

“The lasting value of this initiative will be measured by what happens after training: graduates securing work, establishing businesses, improving their earnings and creating opportunities for others,” he said.

Alausa disclosed that 87,701 trainees had completed the first cohort across trades including welding, electrical installation, automobile mechanics, solar installation, fashion design, ICT, agriculture and hospitality.

He said 1.49 million applications were received for the second cohort, with 150,000 learners admitted into accredited training centres nationwide.

The minister explained that starter kits were being distributed in phases to help beneficiaries move from training to productive economic activities.

“A trained fashion designer needs equipment to take on orders. A welder requires tools to establish a workshop. A solar technician needs appropriate equipment to carry out installations safely and competently,” he said.

He urged beneficiaries to maintain the equipment and use it productively, adding that the government would continue to work with employers, training centres and private-sector partners to create employment and business opportunities for graduates.

The TVET initiative, launched in 2025, is part of the Federal Government’s efforts to address youth unemployment and bridge the gap between education and industry requirements. It provides tuition-free vocational training, stipends and start-up support, including starter kits, to help beneficiaries secure employment or establish businesses.

The government has also emphasised practical learning and stronger industry participation. Speaking at the 32nd Nigerian Economic Summit in October 2026, Alausa said the programme had been streamlined to 28 market-relevant trades, with about 80 per cent of training devoted to practical learning and 20 per cent to theory.

He said stronger collaboration between government, training institutions and employers was necessary to ensure that vocational qualifications translated into workplace competence and economic opportunities.

The post Nigeria needs competent workers to drive growth – Alausa appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Goodluck Jonathan’s second wife to unveil memoir, reveal why she stayed away from public spotlight during his presidency
description:
Ayima Lott-Jonathan, wife of former President Goodluck Jonathan, is set to unveil a memoir detailing her personal journey as she marks her 50th birthday, after largely keeping away from public attention during her husband’s presidency.
The book, titled Gold Dust: Treasures of Quiet Years, will be pr
content:
Ayima Lott-Jonathan, wife of former President Goodluck Jonathan, is set to unveil a memoir detailing her personal journey as she marks her 50th birthday, after largely keeping away from public attention during her husband’s presidency.

The book, titled Gold Dust: Treasures of Quiet Years, will be presented to the public in Abuja on November 19.

Former Vice-President Namadi Sambo is expected to chair the occasion, while Bauchi State Governor Bala Mohammed will serve as the chief book presenter.

Bayelsa State Governor Douye Diri will be the chief host and one of the book presenters, with Rivers State Governor Siminalayi Fubara serving as co-presenter.

The chairman of the Bayelsa State Council of Traditional Rulers, Bubaraye Agada IV, will attend as the royal father of the day, alongside other first-class traditional rulers.

Goodluck Jonathan is expected to attend as the chief special guest of honour.

The memoir will be reviewed by Professor G.G. Darah, a scholar of folklore and oral literature, Fellow of the Nigerian Academy of Letters and former chairman of the editorial board of The Guardian newspaper.

Lott-Jonathan studied law at the Rivers State University of Science and Technology and was called to the Nigerian Bar in 2003.

She later pursued studies in educational leadership and administration, obtaining qualifications from the National Teachers’ Institute, Nigeria, as well as master’s and doctorate degrees from Walden University in the United States.

In 2008, she founded Aduvie International School in Abuja.

The 12-chapter memoir chronicles her personal experiences, with particular focus on her years in the Niger Delta and the Federal Capital Territory.

According to the organisers, the book explores values such as patience, determination, courage, motherhood and purposeful service. It also reflects on faith, coping with bereavement and delayed fulfilment, with lessons intended particularly for younger generations.

title: 37 miners’ deaths: Senate demands sanctions against NSCDC officers
description:
The Senate on Wednesday called on the Federal Government to prosecute or appropriately punish officers found culpable in the deaths of 37 young artisans who died in the custody of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps in Minna, Niger State.
It also urged the government to pay compensation to
content:
The Senate on Wednesday called on the Federal Government to prosecute or appropriately punish officers found culpable in the deaths of 37 young artisans who died in the custody of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps in Minna, Niger State.

It also urged the government to pay compensation to the bereaved families and implement the recommendations of the independent investigative committee set up to probe the incident.

The resolutions followed a motion sponsored by Senator Mohammed Musa (Niger East), who raised concerns over the circumstances surrounding the deaths of the artisans on September 17, 2026, after their arrest during an operation against suspected illegal mining activities.

Presenting the motion, Musa described the incident as a serious human rights concern, saying it raised questions about the treatment of detainees and accountability within security agencies.

He said, “The incident should not be treated as an ordinary tragedy but as a serious matter requiring transparency, accountability and institutional reforms to prevent a recurrence.”

The senator told the chamber that the Federal Government had constituted a 10-member independent investigative committee to establish the circumstances surrounding the deaths.

He said the committee had completed its assignment and submitted a report which reportedly identified serious lapses and recommended sanctions, institutional reforms and compensation for the victims’ families.

Musa urged the Senate to intervene by demanding the immediate implementation of the recommendations, particularly those concerning officers found culpable and reforms within the NSCDC.

The deaths sparked public outrage, mourning and protests in Niger State, prompting calls for an independent investigation into the treatment of the young men while in detention.

The Senate, during Wednesday’s plenary, observed a minute of silence in honour of the deceased and commended President Bola Tinubu, the Federal Government and Niger State Governor, Mohammed Umaru Bago, for facilitating the establishment of the investigative committee.

It also resolved to constitute a delegation led by the Senate President to pay a condolence visit to the families of the deceased in Niger State.

The chamber directed its committees on Interior, Human Rights, Police Affairs and Judiciary to monitor the implementation of the investigative committee’s recommendations and report back.

The Acting Chief Whip, Senator Diket Plang (Plateau Central), moved an amendment to include the Senate Committee on Solid Minerals among the committees overseeing the implementation process.

The amendment was seconded by Senator Abdul Ningi (Bauchi Central) and adopted.

Contributing to the debate, former Edo State Governor, Senator Adams Oshiomhole (Edo North), called on the Senate to condemn illegal mining, arguing that it should be treated with the same seriousness as illegal oil bunkering.

He said, “Illegal mining should be treated with the same seriousness as illegal oil bunkering, given its implications for national revenue, economic stability and the exploitation of the country’s natural resources.”

Oshiomhole urged traditional rulers, state governments and local government authorities to intensify public enlightenment campaigns against illegal mining.

He described the activity as an economic crime, arguing that it deprived the government of legitimate revenue while allowing individuals and criminal networks to exploit the country’s mineral resources for personal gain.

He also called for stringent penalties for those involved in illegal mining but cautioned against interpreting the Senate’s position as an endorsement of the deaths of the 37 artisans.

He stressed that the need to tackle illegal mining should be separated from the circumstances surrounding the deaths, particularly as the victims’ involvement in the activity had not been conclusively established.

His additional prayer was seconded by Senator Simon Lalong (Plateau South).

Lalong also urged the Senate to commend state governors and the 36 State Houses of Assembly for supporting the constitutional amendment on state police.

He described the approval of the State Police Bill as a significant achievement, noting that the proposal had generated controversy over the years before securing unanimous support from the states.

The Senate President welcomed the additional prayers but cautioned lawmakers against assuming that the deceased were illegal miners.

He said the victims were in NSCDC custody when they died, adding, “The Senate must be careful not to make assumptions about their guilt or innocence.”

His clarification reinforced the need to establish the circumstances of the deaths and determine the responsibility of those involved in the detention of the artisans.

However, Ningi raised a point of order under Order 56, questioning the relevance of Oshiomhole’s additional prayer on illegal mining to the substantive motion.

He argued that the motion concerned the deaths of 37 Nigerians in the custody of a government security agency and that the Senate should focus on justice, human rights and compassion for the bereaved families.

Ningi maintained that although illegal mining was a serious national concern, it should not distract from the immediate issue of the deaths and the need to hold those responsible accountable.

The Senate subsequently adopted the prayers, including the demand for the implementation of the investigative committee’s recommendations, sanctions against culpable officers, compensation for the families and reforms within the NSCDC.

The PUNCH reported in September 2026 that 37 artisanal miners died in the custody of the NSCDC in Minna, Niger State, triggering public outrage, mourning and protests.

A presidential investigative panel subsequently concluded that the deaths resulted from severe overcrowding, extreme heat, dehydration and neglect, rather than a disease outbreak initially claimed by the NSCDC.

The incident raised concerns over the treatment of detainees and the accountability of security agencies, with families and rights advocates demanding justice for the victims.

The post 37 miners’ deaths: Senate demands sanctions against NSCDC officers appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Payaza CEO Seyi Ebenezer Joins Livestock Feeds Board After Sunbeth Treenuts And Sesame’s ₦19.5bn Acquisition
description: Payaza Africa founder and Chief Executive Officer Seyi Ebenezer has been appointed to the Board of Directors of Livestock Feeds Plc, one of Nigeria’s longest-established publicly listed agribusinesses.Effective November 17, 2026, his appointment follows Sunbeth Treenuts and Sesame Limited&rsqu
content:
Payaza Africa founder and Chief Executive Officer Seyi Ebenezer has been appointed to the Board of Directors of Livestock Feeds Plc, one of Nigeria’s longest-established publicly listed agribusinesses.

Effective November 17, 2026, his appointment follows Sunbeth Treenuts and Sesame Limited’s successful ₦19.5 billion acquisition of UAC of Nigeria Plc’s 73.29 per cent controlling stake in Livestock Feeds.

Payaza Africa, in a statement on Wednesday, disclosed that the landmark transaction, which received full regulatory approvals from the Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission (FCCPC), Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), and Nigerian Exchange Limited (NGX), ends UAC’s 13-year ownership of the company and ushers in a bold new era for the agribusiness.

Ebenezer is one of five newly appointed directors joining the company’s reconstituted eight-member board, bringing a wealth of experience in corporate finance, financial technology, business expansion, and strategic management.

His appointment marks a significant expansion of his corporate leadership portfolio from financial technology into Nigeria’s agricultural sector.

The payment solutions firm stated that Ebenezer’s appointment introduces a financial services and technology perspective to the governance of Livestock Feeds, a company with more than six decades of experience in Nigeria’s agricultural value chain.

According to the statement, the new board member is a chartered accountant with over 17 years of experience in financial services, having begun his professional career at KPMG before moving into corporate banking, where he held senior leadership positions at Access Bank and Keystone Bank.

“During his banking career, he structured and executed more than $1 billion in debt and capital transactions across industries, including energy, real estate, logistics, technology, and financial services, according to his professional profile published by Lagos Business School.

“During his banking career, he structured and executed more than $1 billion in debt and capital transactions across industries including energy, real estate, logistics, technology, and financial services, according to his professional profile published by Lagos Business School.

“He subsequently founded Payaza Africa in 2022, building a payments infrastructure company that supports businesses operating across African and international markets. The company has expanded its presence to 31 markets globally, providing payment processing and cross-border transaction solutions,” said Payaza Africa.

Ebenezer described his appointment as one that presents a profound opportunity to bring his experience into an industry fundamental to Nigeria’s economic prosperity.

“For much of my career, I have been driven by a singular focus: building financial systems that empower businesses to grow and thrive. Joining the board of Livestock Feeds presents a profound opportunity to bring that experience into an industry that is fundamental to Nigeria’s economic prosperity,” he was quoted as saying.

“Agriculture is not just about food production. It is about access to finance, efficient distribution, resilient supply chains, and the ability of businesses to operate sustainably at scale. What excites me most about this appointment is the opportunity to contribute my experience in financial services, technology, and business expansion to a company with more than six decades of history.

“I believe there is immense potential to strengthen operational efficiency, support long-term growth, and create sustainable value for shareholders, while actively contributing to Nigeria’s broader food security goals,” he added.

Alongside Ebenezer, the newly appointed board members are Sam Okuwlehi, Professor Franklin Nnaemeka Ngwu, Mary Mulili and Farrukh Siddiqui, who join continuing directors Joseph I.D. Dada, Adegboyega Adedeji and Abayomi Adeyemi, bringing together professionals with experience across financial services, corporate governance, aviation, investment management and business leadership.

The post Payaza CEO Seyi Ebenezer Joins Livestock Feeds Board After Sunbeth Treenuts And Sesame’s ₦19.5bn Acquisition appeared first on Channels Television.

title: Senate moves to send State Police Bill to Tinubu for assent
description:
The Nigerian Senate has directed the Clerk to the National Assembly, Kamoru Ogunlana, to transmit the constitutional amendment bill seeking the establishment of state police services to President Bola Tinubu for assent in accordance with the Acts Authentication Act, 2004.
The Senate also called on P
content:
The Nigerian Senate has directed the Clerk to the National Assembly, Kamoru Ogunlana, to transmit the constitutional amendment bill seeking the establishment of state police services to President Bola Tinubu for assent in accordance with the Acts Authentication Act, 2004.

The Senate also called on President Tinubu to forward the proposed National Policing Bill, which is expected to provide the framework for the operation of subnational police services, to the National Assembly for legislative consideration and speedy passage.

Speaking on the development, Senate President Godswill Akpabio said the executive arm of government was expected to submit the proposed modalities for implementing state police services to the National Assembly.

Akpabio explained that lawmakers were avoiding setting unnecessary deadlines but stressed that the process required urgent attention.

He noted that time was important in moving the state police initiative forward, as the National Assembly awaits the executive’s proposals on its implementation.

It is a bill for an Act to Alter the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria 1999, to Provide for the Establishment of State Police Services, and for Related Matters (Sixth Alteration) 2026.

The bill, titled “A Bill for an Act to Alter the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 to Provide for the Establishment of State Police Services and for Related Matters,” seeks to create the constitutional framework for the establishment of state police across the federation.

Resolutions of the Senate were sequel to a motion titled, “Passage of Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria (Sixth Alteration) Bill, 2026” and sponsored by the Senate Leader, Senator Opeyemi Bamidele, APC, Ekiti Central.

In his presentation, Senator Bamidele said, “The Senate: Recall that pursuant to Section 9(1) of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999, the National Assembly, processed an Executive Bill seeking to alter the provisions of the Constitution to establish State Police as part of the national policing structure;

“Also recall that the Senate and the House of Representatives on June 24th and July, 23rd 2026 respectively, overwhelmingly supported the Bill with over 2/3 majority votes, thereby meeting the Constitutional threshold for the passage of the Bill by the National Assembly;

“Aware that the National Assembly transmitted the Bill to the 36 State Houses of Assembly for the mandatory approval by resolution of not less than 2/3 majority of the State Houses of Assembly as provided by Section 9(2) of the Constitution before the Bill can be passed;

“Also, aware that the 36 State Houses of Assembly have transmitted their resolution the Bill to the National Assembly, namely: Abia, Adamawa, Anambra, Akwa-Ibom, Bauchi, Bayelsa, Benue, Borno, Cross-River, Delta, Ebonyi, Edo, Ekiti, Enugu, Gombe, Imo, Jigawa, Kaduna, Kano, Katsina, Kebbi, Kogi, Kwara, Lagos, Nasarawa, Niger, Ogun, Ondo, Osun, Oyo, Plateau, Rivers, Sokoto, Taraba, Yobe and Zamfara;

“Convinced that the Bill has fulfilled the conditions set out in Sections 9(1) and (2) of the Constitution for a Constitutional amendment of this nature to be passed.”

Details later.
