title: Fake drugs: Reps summon NAFDAC, seek tougher penalties
description: The House of Representatives has resolved to invite the heads of the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control, Department of State Services and Nigeria Police Force to brief its relevant committees on measures being taken to tackle the growing circulation of fake drugs and adulte
content:
The House of Representatives has resolved to invite the heads of the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control, Department of State Services and Nigeria Police Force to brief its relevant committees on measures being taken to tackle the growing circulation of fake drugs and adulterated drinks across the country.

The resolution followed the adoption of a motion of urgent public importance moved on Wednesday by the member representing Obi/Oju Federal Constituency of Benue State, Mr David Agada.

This followed reports that the consumption of a suspected poisonous herbal medicine had claimed four lives in the constituency.

The motion, titled, “Urgent need to investigate the alleged distribution and administration of suspected poisonous, unregistered/substandard herbal medicinal products in Obi/Oju Federal Constituency, Benue State to prevent further loss of lives,” called for urgent intervention to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident and prevent further casualties.

Moving the motion, Agada reminded lawmakers of their responsibility to protect the lives and welfare of their constituents.

He noted that the NAFDAC Act empowers the agency to regulate and control the manufacture, distribution, sale and use of drugs, herbal medicinal products and other regulated health-related products in Nigeria.

He also cited the Food and Drugs Act and the Counterfeit and Fake Drugs and Unwholesome Processed Foods (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act, which prohibit the manufacture, distribution and sale of unsafe, adulterated, counterfeit or unwholesome drugs and related products.

Speaking on the incident, Agada said, “The House is concerned that on October 31 2026, three individuals identified as Muhammad Sani Adamu, Musa Alhaji Kala who claim to come from Sokoto State and Alhaji Muhammad Sule from Bauchi States allegedly introduced and distributed a herbal medicinal product in Oju/Obi Federal Constituency, Benue State, claiming that the product could cure typhoid fever, waist pain and other ailments.

“We are concerned that several residents reportedly purchased and consumed the said product, after which a number of them developed severe symptoms within hours and were rushed to different hospitals for emergency medical attention.

“The House is disturbed that the incident has reportedly resulted in the deaths of four persons, namely-Awugo Joseph Oyije, who died on 2nd November, 2026; James Ogah Onma, who died on 4th November, 2026, following referral for further medical treatment; Ode Friday Ogah died on November 5, 2026; and Mr Agi Edugbeke who died on the 11th day of November, 2026.”

He added that 11 other persons were reportedly affected and were receiving medical attention, with two referred to hospitals in Makurdi, the Benue State capital.

The affected persons were identified as Otumala Ochele, Binta Sule, Onu Oboh, Adoga Onu, Upa James, Igbo Pius, Ochele Genesis, Otumala Amos, Uwa Baku, Ate Vivian Okpune and Roman Ehile.

Agada further warned that other residents might have consumed the suspected product without being identified or could be receiving treatment outside recognised health facilities, raising the risk of additional casualties.

He stated, “The House is worried that other residents within the affected communities may have consumed the suspected product without being identified or may be receiving treatment outside recognised health facilities, thereby increasing the possibility of further casualties.

“The House is further worried that the composition, source, manufacturing conditions, NAFDAC registration status, safety, dosage and possible adverse effects of the product remain unverified, raising serious concerns about the possible circulation of poisonous, adulterated, unregistered or substandard herbal medicinal products.”

He said the incident constituted a serious public health concern requiring immediate intervention by relevant federal and state authorities to establish the circumstances surrounding the deaths, prevent further exposure and ensure that those responsible, where culpability is established, were brought to justice.

Contributing to the debate, the House Leader, Prof. Julius Ihonvbere, said the proliferation of fake drugs and drinks had become a national challenge that required a broader response beyond NAFDAC’s current capacity.

He said the agency was struggling with inadequate personnel, noting that its workforce of about 2,000 was insufficient to effectively police the country’s drug distribution network.

“This issue has gone beyond NAFDAC which has only a staff strength of about 2,000 people. The agency requires at least 10,000 staff members to be able to execute its mandate. NAFDAC does not have a presence everywhere; it is not in my village in Edo State.

“I think we need to have a holistic conversation about this problem because it is getting out of hand. If we do not do something quickly, more Nigerians will continue to die of fake drugs and drinks.”

Ihonvbere urged the House to recommend stiffer penalties for manufacturers and distributors of fake and contaminated products.

“Mr Speaker, I think we can suggest life imprisonment or even the death penalty for those involved in this criminal enterprise and may bring the DG of NAFDAC to come and tell us where they are on this matter,” he added.

Similarly, Ali Shettima (APC, Yobe) urged lawmakers to look beyond the Benue incident and address the nationwide consequences of the circulation of fake drugs.

“Let us look beyond Benue and focus on what the issue of fake drugs is doing throughout the country. NAFDAC needs to intensify its work in regulaying the activities of herbal medicine producers. Selling fake products to innocent citizens in the name of drugs and drinks is very unfortunate. An enabling law should be enacted to ensure that those involved in this are penalised if they are found guilty,” he said.

Another Yobe lawmaker, Fatima Talba, however, urged caution, arguing that many Nigerians patronised unregulated herbal medicine sellers partly because of limited access to affordable and reliable healthcare alternatives.

She said, “Some of the people who patronise these do not have any other place to go to. It is not as if these people are forced to buy these products because even in the hospitals, there are fake drugs. We cannot tell these people not to patronise these fake herbal drug sellers because we have not given then alternatives.”

Peter Uzoekwe (NDC, Anambra) proposed holding market leadership accountable for the sale and distribution of counterfeit drugs, suggesting that the executives of markets where such products were manufactured or sold should be removed.

“Let us make it a duty that any market where fake drugs are manufactured or sold, we will depose the executives. If we do this, you will see that those executives would act as taskforce,” he said.

Also contributing, Ismaila Haruna, who represents Toro Federal Constituency of Bauchi State, called for an investigation into deaths allegedly linked to the use of sexual performance-enhancing drugs.

“There are existing laws in place guiding the regulation of herbal medicine. What is left is enforcement. Is NAFDAC doing its job? Again, we need to investigate why men are dying in their numbers because many times, we hear of men dying in hotel rooms and what have you,” he said.

At the end of the debate, the House resolved to invite NAFDAC, the Nigeria Police Force and the DSS to brief its relevant committees on measures being taken to curb the circulation of fake herbal medicines and adulterated drinks across the country.

The post Fake drugs: Reps summon NAFDAC, seek tougher penalties appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Police seek relatives of man killed in Lagos accident
description:
The Airport Police Command has appealed to members of the public to help locate the family and relatives of a man, Abraham Osakpolor, who died following a fatal road accident in Lagos.
The accident occurred on Friday, November 13, 2026, along the expressway leading from the Murtala Muhammed Internat
content:
The Airport Police Command has appealed to members of the public to help locate the family and relatives of a man, Abraham Osakpolor, who died following a fatal road accident in Lagos.

The accident occurred on Friday, November 13, 2026, along the expressway leading from the Murtala Muhammed International Airport towards the Oshodi axis.

According to a statement issued on Wednesday by the Police Public Relations Officer of the Airport Police Command, Assistant Superintendent of Police, Mohammed Adeola, the deceased was born in Benin City, Edo State, on September 1, 1968.

Adeola said Osakpolor was hit by a moving vehicle and rushed to a hospital, where he was later pronounced dead.

He added that the motorist involved in the accident was immediately arrested by the command and would be charged to court.

The police spokesman said the deceased’s remains had been deposited in a hospital mortuary, while efforts to identify and contact his family had so far proved unsuccessful.

During an initial search of his belongings, the police recovered a Nigerian passport and a mobile phone without a SIM card.

Adeola disclosed that mortuary attendants later informed the command that a Canadian passport had also been discovered among the deceased’s belongings during a further search.

He said, “Despite concerted efforts by the police to establish contact with his family or persons who may know him, these efforts have so far proved unsuccessful.”

The command, therefore, urged anyone who knew the deceased or could provide information about his relatives, friends or associates to assist in reaching his family.

It also appealed to Nigerians to share the information widely to ensure that it reached people who could identify him.

The statement said, “The Airport Police Command is urgently calling on members of the public, particularly those who may know the deceased or have information about his family, relatives or associates, to assist in notifying them of this unfortunate incident.”

Members of the public with useful information were advised to contact the Airport Police Command through its X account, @airportcommand, or Facebook page, Airport Command.

They can also reach the Police Public Relations Officer through X, @Moh_Adeola, Instagram, @moh_adeola, or telephone number 08058342093.

title: Trump meets Xi, Putin ahead of historic China summit
description:
The leaders of China, the United States and Russia exchanged greetings as they met in Shenzhen on Wednesday, a day before their history-making first formal trilateral summit in the Chinese city.
The agenda for Thursday’s meeting between presidents Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin — which
content:
The leaders of China, the United States and Russia exchanged greetings as they met in Shenzhen on Wednesday, a day before their history-making first formal trilateral summit in the Chinese city.

The agenda for Thursday’s meeting between presidents Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin — which has raised fears of a carve-up into new “spheres of influence” — was unclear, however.

When Trump touched down in Shenzhen, Xi became the first Chinese paramount leader in decades to welcome a foreign leader as he arrived, mirroring the US president’s gesture at Joint Base Andrews in September.

Trump descended the stairs from his plane to be met by Xi, as well as renditions of both countries’ national anthems and fighter jets that flew overhead and left colourful vapour trails.

The pair strolled down a red carpet lined with people waving pom-poms, brandishing Chinese and US national flags, and shouting: “A warm welcome to you!”

A motorcade of dark limousines later carried Trump into the city, where the streets had been cleared of traffic, an AFP reporter observed.

Xi, Trump, Putin and other leaders attending the broader Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit then gathered for a welcome dinner, and the three briefly exchanged greetings before a group photo.

“I look forward to an in-depth exchange of views with you on major issues concerning China-US relations, Asia-Pacific cooperation, and the global landscape, with the aim of advancing a constructive, strategically stable relationship between our two nations,” Xi told Trump, according to Chinese state news agency Xinhua.

– Sanctions ‘failed’: Putin –
Washington had signalled that the Ukraine war — something Xi vehemently sees as not China’s problem — was not expected to be addressed in the trilateral meeting, before Trump said that it would.

The summit is expected to include discussions of the Iran war and nuclear disarmament, according to Washington, after a US-Russia bilateral treaty on atomic weapons expired in February.

Beijing has long maintained that the US and Russia should reduce their giant nuclear arsenals before it agrees to talks on its smaller stockpile.

Earlier on Wednesday, Putin struck a defiant tone on his war in Ukraine, saying Western sanctions provoked by the 2022 invasion had “failed”.

Addressing the APEC gathering, the Russian leader said he expected the trilateral summit to be “highly useful”.

“At a time when military-political risks are on the rise, what is desperately needed is unity rather than division… and dialogue rather than ultimatums,” Putin said.

The Russian leader has been largely shunned by the West since his 2022 offensive in Ukraine began, but has found an audience with Trump.

However, “full-scale” talks solely between Putin and Trump are unlikely to take place during their visits to China, Moscow said, according to Russian state media.

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, also in Shenzhen, said sanctions would “continue to increase as long as this war goes on”.

Ukraine’s Foreign Minister Andriy Sybiga, speaking to reporters in Kyiv, said he hoped Xi and Trump would put “pressure on Russia to end the war”.

– Kim incoming? –
Putin and Xi met, their fifth tete-a-tete this year, including one by video link. The two men have long touted their strong personal friendship.

Xi urged yet closer ties with Moscow, saying the nations should “leverage the mechanisms for exchanges between the two countries’ governments, legislative bodies, militaries and political parties”.

Trump came to China from the Philippines, where a day earlier he met fellow leaders of the Quad — Australia, Japan and India — for the first time in his second term.

The grouping is broadly aimed at counterbalancing China’s regional influence.

Trump has also floated the possibility of meeting Kim Jong Un in China, saying the North Korean leader “would like” to meet, although there has been no confirmation from Pyongyang.

Trump was in the Philippines for a summit of the 11-member Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) where there were protests against a US supply chain initiative.

The spectre of Trump’s ongoing tariff blitz has loomed large over his recent travels.

Chinese Premier Li Qiang on Monday slammed what he called a “countercurrent of unilateralism and protectionism” while touting Beijing’s own expanding trade with ASEAN.

On Tuesday, a combative Trump doubled down, saying the United States would catch China in rare-earth production “within 10 months”.

AFP

title: Pochettino arrives at Man United ahead of Liverpool clash
description:
Mauricio Pochettino arrived at Manchester United’s Carrington training ground on Wednesday to begin work as the club’s new manager, hours after leaving his role as USA coach.
The Argentine ended his reign in the United States with a 2-0 win over Haiti in Cincinnati before flying to Britain.
Pochetti
content:
Mauricio Pochettino arrived at Manchester United’s Carrington training ground on Wednesday to begin work as the club’s new manager, hours after leaving his role as USA coach.

The Argentine ended his reign in the United States with a 2-0 win over Haiti in Cincinnati before flying to Britain.

Pochettino was whisked to the club’s training base to meet United staff and start preparations for Sunday’s Premier League match against Liverpool.

His appointment was announced last Friday, 24 hours after United had confirmed the sacking of Michael Carrick following the Red Devils’ worst start to a top-flight campaign since the 1986/87 season.

The former Tottenham and Chelsea boss is understood to have signed a deal at Old Trafford until the end of the 2028/29 season.

On Tuesday, Pochettino said he needed time to make United the city’s dominant force again.

“The new challenge is a big challenge, but at the same time it’s adrenaline you want to feel,” he told TNT Sports US.

Sunday’s trip to Anfield will be a baptism of fire for the 54-year-old, whose new team are in the relegation zone after just one league win all season.

AFP

title: Gaming Phenomenon ‘Grand Theft Auto’ Goes Live After 13-Year Wait
description:
After 13 years of waiting, including two delays and several leaks, the first gamers began playing Wednesday the latest instalment of “Grand Theft Auto”, the most expensive — and among the most profitable — video game ever developed.
“GTA VI” becomes available on P
content:
After 13 years of waiting, including two delays and several leaks, the first gamers began playing Wednesday the latest instalment of “Grand Theft Auto”, the most expensive — and among the most profitable — video game ever developed.

“GTA VI” becomes available on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series consoles at midnight Thursday in each region where it will be available.

That meant it launched first in New Zealand (at 1100 GMT on Wednesday), with many players around the world changing their console location settings to the far-eastern country to be among the first to enter the new Vice City.

“I’ve been playing GTA for such a long time that the anticipation for this is crazy,” Australian student Riley Fennel told AFP ahead of the launch.

Although Rockstar Games, the studio behind GTA, has not yet released advance unit sales figures, specialist firm Sensor Tower estimates they have already surpassed 15 million.

That would be more than $1.5 billion in revenue before the game even came out, for a budget estimated at $1 billion to $1.5 billion, which would be unprecedented.

According to the British analytics firm Omdia, sales of “GTA VI” could reach $3.2 billion by the end of the year.

‘Taylor Swift of games’

“No other concert or box office release has ever generated that much capital. And so that makes it one of the outliers in entertainment,” said Joost van Dreunen, a professor at New York University’s Stern School of Business.

“This is the Taylor Swift of video games,” the industry specialist said.

Rockstar’s parent company, US publisher Take-Two Interactive, has rolled out a massive marketing campaign to establish the title as a mass cultural product that transcends the boundaries of video games.

“The reach of the game is such that it will lead to a downstream effect on engagement on other entertainment services,” such as streaming platforms, said James McWhirter at Omdia.

“I’m going to take four days off,” said Dmytro Shkambara, a 27-year-old Ukrainian player living in Berlin, who said he had been planning this first game session “for a very long time”.

Like him, many fans have already booked time off to immerse themselves in the fictional state of Leonida, inspired by Florida.

The human resources platform Remote said it had seen a 32 percent increase in leave requests around the world for November 19.

Touted as bigger, better and more realistic than its predecessors, “GTA VI” follows the adventures of a Bonnie-and-Clyde-style couple trying to survive in the Miami-inspired, crime-ravaged Vice City.

Since its beginnings, the series has won players over with its increasingly realistic reconstructions of fictionalised cities and the great freedom of action offered in a highly detailed open world.

Gamers entering GTA’s worlds can drive cars, fly planes or go skydiving.

“GTA VI” promises to push its realism even further, with characters looking different depending on what they eat and players having to work at cultivating the relationship between the protagonists.

Ahead of its release, the game picked up eight nominations on Tuesday at the Game Awards, the American ceremony that will honour the best video games of the year on December 10.

Subversion And controversy

Rockstar, which by 2026 will have a dozen studios around the world and more than 4,700 employees, devoted more than eight years to building the latest GTA instalment.

Active production only began after the release of Rockstar’s previous game, “Red Dead Redemption II”, in 2018.

It was a rocky ride to release.

Shaken by a series of leaks in 2022 and the online release of stolen gameplay videos, the studio postponed the launch twice, then suffered a new round of leaks last summer.

The games have also regularly been accused of glorifying violence and illegal behaviour as GTA has carved out a place in pop culture as a symbol of subversion, unafraid to mock the flaws of American society.

Players can run over pedestrians, sell drugs and shoot at the police.

“It’s a series that is famous for being always over the top in terms of its representation of violence and different forms of abuse or harassment, for its representations of gender”, said Paolo Ruffino, a lecturer in digital cultures at King’s College London.

“I don’t expect to see necessarily major controversies unless there is something completely new,” he added.

But as a consequence of its scandalous legacy, several countries have banned the saga.

No official release is currently planned in Russia, China, Lebanon or Qatar.

AFP

description: The African Democratic Congress (ADC) has insisted that its presidential candidate in the upcoming 2027 general election, Atiku Abubakar, will be contesting the election and will win the election by a landslide despite the court judgement voiding its principal’s candidacy.The party’s Dir
content:
The African Democratic Congress (ADC) has insisted that its presidential candidate in the upcoming 2027 general election, Atiku Abubakar, will be contesting the election and will win the election by a landslide despite the court judgement voiding its principal’s candidacy.

The party’s Director of Strategic Communication, ADC Campaign Council, Phrank Shaibu, boasted when he appeared on Channels Television’s The Morning Brief on Tuesday.

Justice Lifu’s November 5 judgment in the suit instituted by Gombe had thrown the party’s leadership structure and its preparations for the 2027 general elections into fresh legal uncertainty.

However, while responding to the nullification of Atiku’s candidacy, Shaibu said the ADC presidential candidate would not only be on the ballot but would win the election against the candidate of the All Progressives Congress (APC) and sitting President, Bola Tinubu.

“My thought is simple, it’s clear and unambiguous. Our Affordable Life campaign is permeating in all the nooks and crannies of Nigeria. And Atiku Abubakar will be on the ballot, not just on the ballot; he will beat Bola Ahmed Tinubu silly on January 16, 2027”, Shaibu boasted.

The party’s spokesperson said it had filed a case in the Court of Appeal to restrain the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) from altering its leadership records and the nomination particulars of Atiku.

He also noted explained that the court has been asked to restrain INEC from tampering with records of its governorship candidates pending the determination of its appeal against the judgment of Justice Peter Lifu of the Federal High Court, Abuja.

The party said it had filed a 17-ground appeal challenging the November 5, 2026 judgment, which it described as fundamentally flawed, arguing that the trial court lacked jurisdiction to entertain the leadership dispute.

He noted that the party was also challenging an earlier ruling that granted Bala Gombe leave to amend his originating summons despite an unresolved objection to the court’s jurisdiction.

Shaibu said the 17 grounds of appeal questioned the jurisdiction of the Federal High Court, Gombe’s standing to institute the action, the assessment of disputed evidence and the orders made against the party.

The ADC maintained that allowing INEC to implement the November 5 judgment before the Court of Appeal determines the issues raised could undermine its appeal and expose its candidates to uncertainty.

It urged the appellate court to preserve the party’s existing leadership and candidate records until the legal dispute was resolved.

“The 17 grounds challenge the foundation, findings and orders of Justice Lifu’s judgment. The ADC has asked the Court of Appeal to examine whether the trial court had jurisdiction, whether the claimant had standing, whether disputed evidence was properly assessed, and whether the sweeping orders made against the party can stand in law,” he said.

The party is also challenging the July 24, 2026 ruling in a separate appeal, arguing that the trial court granted Gombe permission to amend his originating summons while deferring its decision on the ADC’s preliminary objection to jurisdiction.

Shaibu said that the party contended that the proposed amendment altered the description of parties and the capacity in which a defendant was sued without prior leave of court.

The appellant’s brief challenging that ruling was settled by Chief J.S. Okutepa (SAN), who leads the ADC’s legal team in the appeal.

The party is asking the Court of Appeal to set aside the amendment order and determine the outstanding objection to the trial court’s jurisdiction.

The ADC further argued that Justice Lifu proceeded to deliver judgment on a court process whose validity was already being challenged before the appellate court.

It expressed concern that INEC could act on the judgment before the appeal is determined, potentially creating a situation that would be difficult to reverse even if the appellate court eventually rules in its favour.

“INEC must not make changes that could preempt the court’s decision or put the party’s candidates in jeopardy while our applications are pending. We are asking the court to protect the subject of the appeal so that its eventual decision has practical effect,” Shaibu added.

The party said its decision to make the legal challenge public was intended to clarify the issues before the appellate court and assure its members and supporters that it would pursue the matter through lawful judicial processes.

The dispute centres on the leadership of the ADC and the legal validity of the processes through which its leadership records and related party affairs are being contested.

The ADC said it would defend the rights of its members, its leadership and the decisions taken by the party, urging that no administrative action be taken based on a contested judgment before the Court of Appeal has considered the issues raised.

The party’s applications and appeals are now before the appellate court for determination.

The latest appeal comes amid continuing litigation over the ADC’s leadership, with the party insisting that earlier court decisions recognising its leadership transition remain valid and have not been set aside.

The post Atiku Will Be On Ballot In 2027 And Will Beat Tinubu Silly — ADC appeared first on Channels Television.

title: JAMB introduces online process for change of course, institution, ends physical office visits
description:
The Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board (JAMB) has introduced a fully online system for candidates seeking to change their preferred institutions or courses, ending the need for physical visits to its offices to access the service.
Under the new arrangement, candidates can now independently pro
content:
The Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board (JAMB) has introduced a fully online system for candidates seeking to change their preferred institutions or courses, ending the need for physical visits to its offices to access the service.

Under the new arrangement, candidates can now independently process changes to their choice of institution or course through the Board’s e-Facility portal from any location with internet access.

The initiative is aimed at making the process easier and more accessible while reducing the challenges associated with visiting JAMB offices.

According to the new arrangement, candidates are expected to benefit from reduced queues, transportation expenses, waiting time and other inconveniences previously linked to accessing the service physically.

In a statement issued by its Acting Director, Public Affairs and Protocol, Dr Fabian Benjamin, the Board said the development was part of efforts to improve service delivery and align its operations with the Federal Government’s Ease of Doing Business policy.

Under the arrangement, candidates can complete the entire process, including payment, authentication and submission, online without visiting JAMB offices or accredited facilities.

To access the service, candidates are required to log into the JAMB e-Facility portal at https://efacility.jamb.gov.ng using their registered email addresses and passwords.

After logging in, they should select “Corrections and Uploads” from the sidebar menu, click on “Change of Programme/Institution”, select UTME and indicate the examination year for which the correction is required.

Candidates are then expected to generate a payment invoice by clicking on “Make New Payment” and complete the transaction through the CREDO payment platform using a debit card or bank transfer.

The Board advised candidates to return to the payment page on their profiles after making payment to confirm that the status has changed from “PENDING” to “PAID (Not Used)”.

After confirming payment, candidates should return to the Change of Institution/Course page, enter their preferred institution and/or programme details and validate the transaction using a One-Time Password (OTP) sent to their registered email addresses.

The process is completed by clicking the “SAVE” button, after which a confirmation message indicating that the change has been successfully made will be displayed.

Candidates are also required to print their Change of Programme/Institution slips and log into the Central Admissions Processing System (CAPS) to confirm that their new choices have been updated.

JAMB cautioned candidates to carefully review their selections before submitting requests to avoid errors.

It also stressed that candidates must ensure their payment status reads “PAID (Not Used)” before proceeding and have access to their registered email accounts to receive and validate the OTP.

The Board further advised candidates to carry out the process through their individual profiles rather than engage intermediaries or disclose their login details and OTPs to third parties.

It said there was no need to pay individuals to perform a service candidates could complete independently online.

According to the statement, the Registrar, Prof. Segun Aina, reaffirmed the Board’s commitment to using technology to remove bureaucratic bottlenecks, improve service delivery and make essential services accessible to candidates irrespective of their locations.

The Board said the objective was to enable candidates to spend less time dealing with administrative processes and more time pursuing their educational aspirations.

The initiative is the latest in a series of measures aimed at reducing physical visits to JAMB offices, easing pressure on its facilities and improving service delivery to candidates and other stakeholders.

The post JAMB introduces online process for change of course, institution, ends physical office visits appeared first on Very Nigerian.

title: State Police: Senate Directs NASS Clerk To Transmit Amendment Bill To Tinubu For Assent
description: The Senate has directed the clerk to the National Assembly to transmit the Constitution alteration bill providing for the establishment of State Police to President Bola Tinubu for assent.The upper chamber has also asked the Executive to forward the National Policing Bill to the National Assembly fo
content:
The Senate has directed the clerk to the National Assembly to transmit the Constitution alteration bill providing for the establishment of State Police to President Bola Tinubu for assent.

The upper chamber has also asked the Executive to forward the National Policing Bill to the National Assembly for legislative scrutiny and expeditious passage to establish the operational framework for subnational policing.

The resolutions followed a motion sponsored by the Senate Leader, Opeyemi Bamidele, during plenary today.

In its deliberations, Senator Bamidele recalled that the National Assembly had processed an executive bill seeking to amend the 1999 Constitution to establish state police as part of Nigeria’s national policing structure.

He noted that both chambers overwhelmingly approved the proposed amendment, with the Senate passing the bill on June 24, 2026, and the House of Representatives following suit on July 23, 2026, securing the constitutionally required two-thirds majority.

The bill was subsequently transmitted to the 36 State Houses of Assembly for approval in line with Section 9(2) of the Constitution.

The Senate Leader noted that the Senate confirmed that all 36 state legislatures had now endorsed the proposed amendment and transmitted their resolutions to the National Assembly.

Having satisfied the constitutional requirements under Sections 9(1) and 9(2), the Senate maintained that the amendment had fulfilled the conditions necessary for its passage.

The upper chamber therefore urged the Executive to submit the National Policing Bill to provide the legal and operational framework for the implementation of State Police.

The Clerk to the National Assembly, Kamoru Ogunlana, announced on Monday that all 36 State Houses of Assembly had approved the proposed constitutional amendment to establish state police, clearing the way for the bill to be transmitted to President Bola Tinubu for assent.

The clerk described it as 100 per cent approval by the state legislatures, as the approval exceeded the constitutional requirement of at least 24 state assemblies under Section 9(2) of the 1999 Constitution, as amended.

“The Clerk to the National Assembly wishes to announce that all the thirty-six (36) State Houses of Assembly have approved ‘A Bill for an Act to Alter the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 to Provide for the Establishment of State Police Services and for related Matters’.

“This represents one hundred percent (100%) endorsement by the State Houses of Assembly, which exceeds the threshold of twenty-four (24), provided under Section 9(2) of the Constitution (as amended),” Ogunlana had stated.

The development marked the completion of the state assemblies’ consideration of the proposed amendment, following weeks of legislative engagement over the establishment of state police.

The post State Police: Senate Directs NASS Clerk To Transmit Amendment Bill To Tinubu For Assent appeared first on Channels Television.

title: City Boy Movement dismisses Mas’ud Rahamaniyya as Sokoto director
description:
The national leadership of the City Boy Movement has removed Mas’ud Rahamaniyya from his position as the organisation’s Director in Sokoto State.
The decision, which took effect on Tuesday, was conveyed in an official letter issued on Wednesday and signed by the movement’s Director-General, Francis
content:
The national leadership of the City Boy Movement has removed Mas’ud Rahamaniyya from his position as the organisation’s Director in Sokoto State.

The decision, which took effect on Tuesday, was conveyed in an official letter issued on Wednesday and signed by the movement’s Director-General, Francis Shoga.

The letter, bearing reference number CBM/DG/SD.SOK/2026/700, was addressed to Rahamaniyya in Sokoto State, formally communicating the decision to relieve him of his appointment.

However, the movement did not disclose further details surrounding the decision in the information contained in the letter.

“I write on behalf of the national leadership of the City Boy Movement to inform you that you are relieved of your appointment as State Director of the Sokoto State Chapter with effect from 17 November 2026,” the letter stated.

The national leadership, however, clarified that the decision was purely administrative and should not be interpreted as a disciplinary action or an indication of any wrongdoing by the former state director.

It also expressed appreciation to Rahamaniyya for his contributions and commitment to the activities of the movement in Sokoto State during his tenure.

“On behalf of the movement, I wish to sincerely appreciate you for your service and the time and effort you devoted to the work of the Sokoto State Chapter during your tenure,” Shoga stated.

The letter further wished him success in his future endeavours.

The development comes as political activities gather momentum ahead of the 2027 general elections, with various support groups intensifying efforts to mobilise grassroots support for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid.

However, the movement had yet to announce a replacement for Rahamaniyya as of the time of filing this report.

title: NLC, TUC end rift over FG’s N70,000 transport allowance for workers
description:
The Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) and the Trade Union Congress of Nigeria (TUC) have settled their differences over the Federal Government’s N70,000 transport allowance introduced for workers for six months.
The two labour organisations announced their decision to resolve the disagreement during a j
content:
The Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) and the Trade Union Congress of Nigeria (TUC) have settled their differences over the Federal Government’s N70,000 transport allowance introduced for workers for six months.

The two labour organisations announced their decision to resolve the disagreement during a joint press conference held in Abuja on Wednesday, November 18, 2026.

They said they had agreed to put their differences aside and focus on protecting the interests and welfare of Nigerian workers.

In a joint statement signed by NLC President, Joe Ajaero, and TUC President-General, Festus Osifo, the unions admitted that their disagreement had become a public issue.

However, they maintained that their longstanding relationship and collective responsibility to workers were more important than their institutional differences.

The resolution is expected to strengthen cooperation between the two major labour centres in addressing issues affecting Nigerian workers.

They described the dispute as a family misunderstanding, which was resolved amicably through the intervention of former leaders of both labour centres.

The statement read, “The unity of the Nigerian working class is far greater than any disagreement between leaderships. Our common struggle, shared history, and collective responsibility to defend workers’ rights must never be sacrificed on the altar of misunderstanding or institutional differences.”

The disagreement centred on the N70,000 transport allowance approved by President Bola Tinubu for workers across different levels of government for six months.

The dispute became public after Ajaero and Osifo separately appeared on Channels Television’s The Morning Brief, where they disagreed over which labour centre had the authority to negotiate with the Federal Government on behalf of workers.

Ajaero argued that the NLC could negotiate independently, relying on the principle of representation under the International Labour Organisation.

“TUC can negotiate along with NLC, but NLC can negotiate alone based on the principle of most workers’ representatives of the ILO”, the NLC President noted.

Osifo, however, described the N70,000 agreement announced by Ajaero as an aberration, arguing that the TUC was not involved in the negotiations.

He challenged the NLC president to produce the ILO regulation that permitted one labour centre to negotiate on behalf of the other.

He stated, “He should show me in the ILO Regulations where it says one party is going to negotiate without the other one being there or consulted. He should show me! He should show Nigerians!

“ILO doctrine is that when you have more affiliates, and you are going for one of their events, it is not correct that the most represented will go and negotiate on behalf of the other one when the unions have their own umbrella.

“There is nowhere in ILO regulations that says a trade centre cannot negotiate for its members. It is not there! It is just that if you are going to the ILO, it is tripartite- the labour, government and the employers.”

Osifo also argued that the NLC could not negotiate on behalf of workers represented by the TUC simply because it had more affiliated unions.

He added, “But what we are saying is that you have about 60 affiliates while we have about 40. You cannot! You cannot negotiate for a body that is represented, for a body that has a trade union.

“You cannot negotiate on their behalf! It is not there anywhere!

“Yes, if we go to negotiations- I sit down, you sit down, and we agree”.

Ajaero, in his response, argued that the Trade Union Amendment Act 2005 made union membership voluntary and allowed workers to choose the organisations they wished to join.

“The 2005 Trade Union Amendment Act made membership of trade unions voluntary.

“It is the worker who determines the union he belongs to.

“Section 40 of the Nigerian 1999 Constitution, as amended, was clear that every Nigerian worker has the right to belong to any trade union, political or religious institution of his choice, which gives every worker the latitude to belong to any union of their choice,” Ajaero stated.

He also questioned Osifo’s claim of having a substantial number of workers in the federal civil service, arguing that only one TUC-affiliated union belonged to the Joint National Public Service Negotiating Council.

According to Ajaero, the council comprises eight union bodies, seven of which are affiliated with the NLC. He further argued that the TUC-affiliated union had subjected its negotiating authority to the joint body.

Osifo maintained that the two labour centres needed to participate in negotiations where their respective members were concerned.

He stated, “In that case, the two bodies must come together. We are not contesting the fact that NLC has more affiliates.

“But what we are saying is that you have about 60 affiliates while we have about 40. You cannot! You cannot negotiate for a body that is represented, for a body that has a trade union.

“You cannot negotiate on their behalf! It is not there anywhere!

“Yes, if we go to negotiations- I sit down, you sit down, and we agree.”

The TUC leader also questioned the legitimacy of the meeting at which the transport allowance was agreed, saying it was not a meeting of the Joint National Public Service Negotiating Council.

“But that meeting that took place was not the Council meeting. The Minister is not a member of the Council. Ajaero is not a member of the Council. The Council even has a quorum and the number of persons that must be seated to form a quorum. But at the end of the day, that meeting was not a JNC meeting. The members of JNC were not there!

“Again, if you see the release that was sent out by those three bodies, you will discover that after the last minimum wage, we got about a 33 per cent increment, and how does that work? Because from N30,000, we got N70,000.

“What you are supposed to do is that JNC will have to sit down and apply consequential adjustments,” he asked.

Ajaero, on his part, said the NLC had engaged the Federal Government after issuing an ultimatum over the workers’ demands.

“We gave the government an ultimatum; we were supposed to start an action. The government asked for four days to meet with us, and we met, and they resumed sitting after four days.

“After the meeting, the 70k allowance came up.”

He added that demands for a new minimum wage could not be negotiated without the establishment of a formal negotiation committee and wider consultations involving labour, government and employers.

The resolution of the disagreement comes amid renewed discussions over workers’ pay, following the Federal Government’s approval of a committee to examine concerns raised by the TUC over a new national minimum wage.

The TUC Secretary-General, Comrade General N.A. Toro, disclosed the development in a statement on Tuesday after a meeting between the union and the Federal Government.

The meeting followed a letter dated October 8, 2026, titled “Request for an Urgent Meeting to Address Critical National Economic, Security and Labour Challenges,” submitted by the TUC.

The Secretary to the Government of the Federation, Senator George Akume, chaired the meeting, while the TUC delegation was led by Osifo.

Other members of the delegation included Toro, Deputy President Shehu Mohammed, Trustee Akintola Benjamin and Auditor II Kamal Ibrahim.

The Head of the Civil Service of the Federation and the Permanent Secretary in the Office of the Secretary to the Government of the Federation, Ibrahim Kana, also attended.

The TUC said it had rejected the proposed six-month transport allowance, insisting that workers should receive a salary increase while discussions on a new national minimum wage were being concluded.

“In the course of the deliberations, the TUC made its position unequivocally clear on the proposed ₦70,000 transport intervention for a period of six months, which it rejected, preferring instead a salary increase pending the commencement and conclusion of discussions on a new National Minimum Wage.

“This position, alongside the other demands and concerns raised by Congress, will form part of the issues to be thoroughly interrogated by the High-Powered Committee,” the statement read in part.

The union said the committee would assess the issues raised, examine steps already taken by the government and make recommendations on outstanding matters.

“The Committee will therefore undertake a comprehensive review and reconciliation of the issues, establish the extent of actions already taken by the Government, identify outstanding matters and make appropriate findings and recommendations,” the statement said in part.

The committee comprises three TUC representatives, alongside officials from the Office of the Secretary to the Government of the Federation, the Office of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation, the National Salaries, Incomes and Wages Commission, and the Federal Ministry of Labour and Employment.

It is expected to begin work immediately and submit its report to the Secretary to the Government of the Federation within two weeks.

The post NLC, TUC end rift over FG’s N70,000 transport allowance for workers appeared first on Very Nigerian.

title: United Nigeria Airlines chairman honoured at global PR forum
description:
The Executive Chairman of United Nigeria Airlines, Prof. Obiora Okonkwo, has received the 2026 Global Alliance President’s Award in recognition of his contributions to the advancement of public relations and his support for the hosting of the 13th World Public Relations Forum (WPRF) Abuja 2026.
The
content:
The Executive Chairman of United Nigeria Airlines, Prof. Obiora Okonkwo, has received the 2026 Global Alliance President’s Award in recognition of his contributions to the advancement of public relations and his support for the hosting of the 13th World Public Relations Forum (WPRF) Abuja 2026.

The award was presented to Okonkwo by the Global Alliance President and Chief Executive Officer, Prof. Justin Green, at the organisation’s 25th Anniversary Gala Dinner and World Public Relations and Communication Awards held in Abuja on Tuesday, November 17, 2026.

The recognition came as Okonkwo called on businesses to embrace transparent, responsible and truthful communication to build customer confidence, protect corporate reputation and attract investor trust.

According to a statement made available to PUNCH Online on Wednesday, speaking at a high-level dialogue on Responsible Business Communication: Building Trust and Financing Investments for Sustainable Human Development at the 2026 WPRF, he said communication alone could not sustain public confidence unless organisations delivered on their promises.

“Communication alone cannot sustain public confidence unless organisations deliver on their promises,” he said.

He noted that the aviation industry faced particular challenges because passengers were more concerned about arriving at their destinations on time than receiving explanations for delays.

Illustrating the importance of meeting customer expectations, Okonkwo recalled an encounter with a passenger who vowed never to fly with the airline again because his flight had departed 10 minutes early.

He said he responded humorously by apologising for the airline “leaving on time.”

The airline chairman warned organisations against withholding information or presenting misleading accounts during crises, noting that concealing problems often caused greater reputational damage than openly acknowledging them.

He stressed that crisis communication should not be left exclusively to corporate affairs or public relations departments, but should be treated as a collective responsibility of organisational leadership.

Okonkwo urged airlines and other service providers to maximise available communication channels, including airport information displays, technology platforms and social media, to keep customers informed.

He also called for prompt disclosure of developments affecting flight operations, including industrial strikes and safety concerns.

On aviation safety, he maintained that commercial interests and customer satisfaction must never override safety considerations, stressing that decisions on aircraft airworthiness should remain the responsibility of the appropriate safety departments.

Okonkwo further identified trust as a critical factor in customer retention and long-term business sustainability.

He said, “Trust is central to customer retention and long-term business sustainability,” adding that customers who have confidence in a brand are more likely to defend it when challenges arise.

He maintained that responsible communication, backed by consistent service delivery, remained essential to building lasting relationships between businesses and their customers.

The post United Nigeria Airlines chairman honoured at global PR forum appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: US lists categories of foreigners exempt from green card application fees
description:
The United States Citizenship and Immigration Services has listed 11 categories of foreign applicants who are exempt from paying the filing fee when submitting Form I-485, the Application to Register Permanent Residence or Adjust Status, commonly known as a green card application.
For most applicant
content:
The United States Citizenship and Immigration Services has listed 11 categories of foreign applicants who are exempt from paying the filing fee when submitting Form I-485, the Application to Register Permanent Residence or Adjust Status, commonly known as a green card application.

For most applicants aged 14 and above, according to a Wednesday report by MSN, a Microsoft web portal, the standard fee is 1,390 (approximately KSh180,700) for online filing.

However, according to the USCIS fee schedule published in Form G-1055, specific groups are entirely exempt from the charge.

The following applicants pay no fee when filing Form I-485:

  1. Applicants who served honourably on active duty in the US armed forces and are filing under INA Section 101(a)(27)(K), also known as the Six and Six programme. This exemption does not cover non-military derivative spouses or children.
  2. Refugees or those who were paroled as refugees, filing under INA Section 207.
  3. Applicants in deportation, exclusion or removal proceedings before an immigration judge, where the court waives the application fee.
  4. Persons seeking or granted Special Immigrant Juvenile classification.
  5. U nonimmigrants seeking adjustment of status under INA Section 245(m) as victims of qualifying criminal activity.
  6. T nonimmigrants seeking adjustment of status under INA Section 245(l) as victims of human trafficking.
  7. Persons seeking or granted special immigrant visas or status as Afghan or Iraqi translators or interpreters; Iraqi nationals employed by or on behalf of the US government; Afghan nationals employed by or on behalf of the US government or the International Security Assistance Force (ISAF); or derivative beneficiaries of any of the above.
  8. Afghan diplomats or immediate family members who held valid A or G status on July 14, 2021, filing under Section 13 of Public Law 85-316.
  9. Persons seeking adjustment of status as abused spouses or children under the Cuban Adjustment Act (CAA).
  10. Persons seeking adjustment of status as abused spouses or children under the Haitian Refugee Immigration Fairness Act (HRIFA).
  11. Persons seeking immigrant classification as Violence Against Women Act (VAWA) self-petitioners, including derivatives.

Beyond the 11 categories that automatically qualify for an exemption, USCIS says certain other applicants may qualify for a fee waiver by submitting Form I-912.

This is separate from the automatic exemptions. Applicants must formally request the waiver, and USCIS considers whether they meet the eligibility requirements.

The existence of these exemptions does not mean that all foreign applicants qualify for free green card applications.

Most applicants must still pay the applicable Form I-485 filing fee unless they meet an exemption or receive an approved fee waiver.

(MSN/NAN)

The post US lists categories of foreigners exempt from green card application fees appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Unemployment, stigma may push ex-offenders back to crime – NCoS CG
description: The Nigerian Correctional Service has called on governments, private organisations, religious institutions and communities to support the reintegration of ex-offenders into society, warning that unemployment, economic hardship and stigmatisation could undermine their rehabilitation and push them bac
content:
The Nigerian Correctional Service has called on governments, private organisations, religious institutions and communities to support the reintegration of ex-offenders into society, warning that unemployment, economic hardship and stigmatisation could undermine their rehabilitation and push them back into crime.

The Controller-General of Corrections, Sylvester Nwakuche, made the appeal during the presentation of 2026 aftercare vocational starter packs to discharged inmates in Abuja.

He said sustained support was necessary to help them establish businesses and become productive members of society.

Nwakuche said the service had provided starter packs to nearly 33 ex-offenders to enable them to put the vocational skills acquired during incarceration into practice.

According to him, the aftercare programme is designed to bridge the gap between rehabilitation in correctional facilities and successful reintegration into society.

“For many inmates, the journey back into society is often confronted by stigma, unemployment, economic hardship, and rejection. Without adequate support, these challenges may undermine the gains of rehabilitation and increase the risk of reoffending,” he said.

The Controller-General explained that the starter packs covered seven vocational areas, including laundry, barbing, tailoring and fashion design, hairdressing, carpentry, masonry, and welding and metal fabrication.

He said the trades were selected to provide the beneficiaries with opportunities for self-employment, entrepreneurship and economic independence.

“These starter packs represent much more than tools of trade. They are instruments of empowerment, they are symbols of renewed confidence, and seeds of economic independence.

“They represent our belief that today’s offenders can become tomorrow’s entrepreneurs, employers of labour, and responsible contributors to national development,” he added.

The NCoS boss said empowering discharged inmates was also an investment in public safety, noting that successful reintegration would help reduce recidivism and build safer communities.

He urged the beneficiaries to make productive use of the materials and resist negative influences, stressing that the success of the programme would be measured by the businesses they established and the livelihoods they sustained.

“The true value of these starter packs will not be measured by what we hand over today, but by the businesses you establish, the families you support, the opportunities you create, and the positive lives you touch tomorrow,” he said.

He also called on employers and other stakeholders to look beyond the past mistakes of ex-offenders and give them opportunities to rebuild their lives.

“Governments, private organisations, religious institutions, community leaders, families, and individuals must all play their part in dismantling the walls of stigma and creating an environment where reformed persons can strive,” he said.

Earlier, the Director of Health and Welfare, Abdullahi Aldo, said the aftercare programme was designed to ensure that discharged inmates were not abandoned after regaining their freedom.

He said the initiative provided starter packs, skills support and mentorship to help beneficiaries reintegrate into their families and communities.

“The aftercare programme is designed to ensure that no ex-offender is abandoned at the gate of freedom,” Aldo said.

He urged the beneficiaries to use the materials as a foundation for a new life and become responsible members of their communities.

“Be good ambassadors of the service in your communities, and prove to the world that change is possible,” he said.

This is not the first time the service has empowered ex-offenders. In November 2025, it gave starter packs to 24 inmates to help them become financially independent after their release.

title: ICPC opposes bail for fake PFIPC DG
description:
The Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission has urged a High Court of the Federal Capital Territory to reject the bail application of a suspected fraudster, Adeniyi Adeyemi.
The commission argued that his continued detention is necessary for his personal safety.
The commi
content:
The Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission has urged a High Court of the Federal Capital Territory to reject the bail application of a suspected fraudster, Adeniyi Adeyemi.

The commission argued that his continued detention is necessary for his personal safety.

The commission said some individuals who allegedly lost money to Adeyemi were searching for him and could physically harm him if released.

Prosecution counsel, Sylvanus Tahir, SAN, made the submission on Wednesday while opposing the bail applications filed by Adeyemi and four civil servants charged alongside him over an alleged N27bn fraud involving a purported Presidential Foreign Investment Promotion Council.

“My lord, there are many petitions against him, and the people who lodged those petitions are after him,” Tahir told the court.

He cited the case of a petitioner from Ibadan who allegedly lost money to the defendant and had been searching for him.

“We believe that it will be in his own best interest to remain in custody for safekeeping,” the prosecution counsel said.

The ICPC also described Adeyemi as a flight risk, alleging that he had access to substantial funds and could interfere with some of the proposed witnesses.

However, Adeyemi, through his counsel, Ibrahim Angulu, dismissed the prosecution’s argument, insisting that he lacked the financial capacity to flee or influence witnesses because his bank accounts, including those belonging to his wives, had been frozen.

“My lord, the accounts of the defendant were frozen, including those of his wives. They have all been frozen. So he does not have the means to escape or to influence the witnesses,” Angulu said.

Adeyemi and the four other defendants, Aminu Abdullahi, Ogaba Harry, Florence Omameh and Patricia Akhigbe, had pleaded not guilty to a 36-count amended charge bordering on obtaining money by false pretence, forgery and corruption.

The defendants, through their respective lawyers, urged the court to admit them to bail, citing their constitutional rights to personal liberty and presumption of innocence, as well as provisions of the Administration of Criminal Justice Act.

They also pleaded ill health and promised to attend subsequent proceedings.

The prosecution, however, urged the court to reject the applications and order an accelerated hearing of the case.

Justice Halilu Yusuf adjourned proceedings until November 30 for a ruling on the bail applications and commencement of trial.

The judge ordered that the male defendants be remanded at the Kuje Correctional Centre, while the two female defendants were taken to the Suleja Correctional Centre.

The ICPC had alleged that Adeyemi fraudulently presented himself as the Director-General of the Presidential Foreign Investment Promotion Council, which it described as a non-existent government agency, and obtained more than N27bn under the guise of establishing the organisation.

He was also accused of obtaining another N3.8bn purportedly for the agency’s personnel costs.

According to the commission, Adeyemi allegedly forged documents bearing the purported signature of the Chief of Staff to the President, Femi Gbajabiamila, to portray himself as the agency’s director-general and secure government office facilities at the Federal Secretariat Complex, Phase III, Abuja.

The four civil servants were allegedly involved in facilitating his activities. Abdullahi, an Assistant Chief Technical Officer in the Office of the Secretary to the Government of the Federation, was accused of receiving N210,000 from Adeyemi to facilitate the allocation of office space.

Harry, an official in the Office of the Chief Economic Adviser to the President, was also accused of receiving N300,000 to facilitate the release of two official vehicles — a Prado SUV and a Land Cruiser SUV — to the defendant.

In another count, Adeyemi was accused of obtaining N20m on July 29, 2025, from Oyekunle Gbenga, Managing Director of Divine Dopacy Nigeria Limited, under the guise of a project facilitation loan for a purported N2.8bn contract awarded by the fictitious agency.

The contract was allegedly for the procurement of furniture and renovation of the official residence of the agency’s purported director-general.

The commission said the alleged offences were committed between 2024 and 2026.

Adeyemi has been in detention since July 14 and was first arraigned on October 29. His re-arraignment on Wednesday followed an amendment of the charge to include the four civil servants.

title: ‎CP Azare Charges Newly Promoted Officers On Discipline, Commitment To Duty
description: Akwa Ibom State Commissioner of Police, CP Baba Azare, has charged the newly promoted senior officers of the Command to live up to the demands of their new ranks and justify the confidence reposed in them.‎CP Azare gave the charge when he decorated the officers with their new ranks at the Comman
content:
Akwa Ibom State Commissioner of Police, CP Baba Azare, has charged the newly promoted senior officers of the Command to live up to the demands of their new ranks and justify the confidence reposed in them.

‎CP Azare gave the charge when he decorated the officers with their new ranks at the Command headquarters, Ikot Akpanabia, Uyo, on Monday.

‎The newly promoted senior officers were decorated with new ranks following their recent promotion by the Police Service Commission.

‎The Police Commissioner, who congratulated the officers on what he acknowledged as their well-deserved promotions, described their elevation as recognition of their dedication, professionalism, hard work and commitment in the discharge of their duties.

‎“Promotion comes with higher responsibilities and more expectations. You are therefore charged to justify the confidence reposed in you through greater commitment to duty, professionalism, respect for human rights and strict adherence to the rule of law.” CP Azare advised.

‎The promoted senior officers comprise three Chief Superintendents of Police (CSPs) namely: CSP Richard Oguntola, CSP Magret Alapa, CSP Bokima Bassey, three Superintendents of Police (SPs) namely: SP John Mamodu, SP Glory George, SP Victor Lane and two Deputy Superintendents of Police (DSPs) namely: DSP Emmanuel Ayoka and DSP Godwin Awana.

‎CP Azare commended the Police Service Commission for the timely promotion of deserving officers, noting that such a gesture would further boost morale and inspire more commitment among officers.

‎The Commissioner also expressed gratitude to the Inspector-General of Police, IGP Olatunji Rilwan Disu, for his visionary leadership, support and sustained commitment to the welfare of officers of the Nigeria Police Force.

‎CSP Richard Oguntola, responding on behalf of the newly promoted officers, expressed appreciation to the Almighty God for His mercy and grace to witness another memorable achievement.

‎He also expressed gratitude to the Police Service Commission and the Inspector-General of Police for finding them worthy for promotion.

‎CSP Oguntola particularly thanked CP Azare for his exemplary leadership, encouragement and support, which he stated had positively impacted their career progression.

‎He reiterated their commitment to the professional discharge of the constitutional duties of the Nigeria Police Force in their respective areas of responsibility in line with international best practices.

‎The decoration ceremony was attended by members of the management team, officers of the Command, families, friends and well-wishers who joined in celebrating the officers on their well-deserved promotions.

‎

title: 2027: Accept election results like Jonathan, group tells politicians
description:
Ahead of the 2027 general elections, politicians seeking elective offices have been urged to emulate former President Goodluck Jonathan by accepting the outcome of the polls in the interest of peace and democratic stability.
The Journalists Monitoring Performance for Democratic Governance, led by it
content:
Ahead of the 2027 general elections, politicians seeking elective offices have been urged to emulate former President Goodluck Jonathan by accepting the outcome of the polls in the interest of peace and democratic stability.

The Journalists Monitoring Performance for Democratic Governance, led by its President, Vincent Akpomefure, made the call at a press conference held in Maryland, Lagos, on Wednesday.

Jonathan, who contested the 2015 presidential election on the platform of the Peoples Democratic Party, conceded defeat to the candidate of the All Progressives Congress, Muhammadu Buhari, after the poll.

His decision to accept the outcome paved the way for Nigeria’s first transfer of power from an incumbent ruling party to an opposition party through the ballot box.

Akpomefure urged political actors across the country to learn from Jonathan’s decision to concede defeat in the 2015 presidential election and facilitate a peaceful transfer of power to the opposition.

The concerns come amid recent attacks on political gatherings and leaders ahead of the 2027 elections.

On November 12, suspected political thugs disrupted a town hall meeting organised by the Nigeria Democratic Congress for its presidential candidate, Peter Obi, in Oregun, Lagos, attacking supporters and damaging vehicles.

In a separate incident on November 13, President Bola Tinubu’s motorcade was attacked with stones and other dangerous objects shortly after he observed Friday prayers at a mosque in the Garki area of Abuja.

Also, the Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission, Prof. Joash Amupitan, was confronted by Nigerian protesters in London on November 12, 2026, who blocked his movement and demanded his resignation over allegations of irregularities in the preliminary voters’ register and fears about the neutrality of the commission ahead of the elections.

Akpomefure said the warning was prompted by growing political intolerance, attacks and threats of violence ahead of the elections, which could undermine the country’s stability.

He said the government and opposition must understand that they had a responsibility to protect democracy.

Akpomefure said, “A few months ahead of this all-important election, we have seen evidence of intolerance, violent attacks and threats of even greater violence.
“We are calling on politicians to learn from Dr Jonathan in the sense that they need to accept the outcome of the 2027 elections at the local, state and federal levels.”

He, however, pointed out that the appeal was not a call on President Bola Tinubu to hand over power to the opposition but a reminder that both winners and losers in the 2027 elections should respect the people’s choice.

He urged Nigerians to defend free and fair elections, stressing that the group was not advocating a situation in which the ruling party must lose power but one in which all political parties would respect a credible electoral outcome.

He said, “The important point is not that a ruling party must hand over to the opposition only to prove a free and fair election. No. What we seek is a free and fair election that Nigerians need to accept. If the ruling party wins, let the opposition respect the outcome of the election; if the opposition wins, let the ruling party respect the outcome.”

Akpomefure said the group was using the 2027 elections to draw attention to Jonathan’s decision to concede defeat in 2015, describing it as an example of humility and personal sacrifice for democratic stability.

He said the former President’s action demonstrated that the country’s interest should take precedence over the desire to retain political power, regardless of the ethnic background of the incumbent.

Akpomefure stressed, “We want an election that will leave us with confidence, peace, trust and stability, without which we can neither speak of democracy, liberty nor press freedom.

“As journalists, we need to insist on peaceful campaigns devoid of threats and violence, and devoid of religious and ethnic sentiments. We need to remember what the civil war cost us as a nation. We do not want to see a repeat of that ugly history.”

He said the 2027 elections would be significant because they would take place 60 years after the first military coup in Nigeria, which occurred on January 15, 1966, and warned against a repeat of the events that plunged the country into the civil war.

“The January election is significant in many ways. It will be taking place exactly 60 years after the first military coup,” he said.
He recalled that the 1964 general election contributed to the crisis that preceded the coup and the civil war, which lasted 30 months and claimed more than one million lives.

The media conference also marked the commencement of activities towards Jonathan’s 70th birthday celebration, during which the group announced plans to unveil a book titled “Goodluck Jonathan: The President Who Ruled With Golden Fingers.”

Akpomefure said the book would examine Jonathan’s political journey, presidency and contribution to Nigeria’s democratic development, with particular attention to the 2015 elections and the peaceful transfer of power that followed.

He said the publication would also explore the former President’s background, rise to power, electoral reforms, education policies and commitment to democratic values.
He added that the public presentation of the book would take place in 2027, after the general elections, as part of activities marking Jonathan’s 70th birthday.

The group also announced that the Ibenanawei of Bomo Kingdom in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State, King Joshua Igbugburu, would serve as the royal father of the occasion.

The monarch, who ascended the throne in 1958 at the age of 20, was described by the group as a longstanding traditional ruler with a place in the history of Bayelsa State and Nigeria.

The post 2027: Accept election results like Jonathan, group tells politicians appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Insecurity has declined under Tinubu — APC
description:
The All Progressives Congress has defended President Bola Tinubu’s handling of insecurity, claiming that the country has recorded a reduction in attacks and fatalities since he assumed office in 2023.
The party’s National Publicity Secretary, Felix Morka, made the assertion on Wednesday during an ap
content:
The All Progressives Congress has defended President Bola Tinubu’s handling of insecurity, claiming that the country has recorded a reduction in attacks and fatalities since he assumed office in 2023.

The party’s National Publicity Secretary, Felix Morka, made the assertion on Wednesday during an appearance on Channels Television’s The Morning Brief, where he highlighted what he described as improvements in the military’s capacity and the welfare of its personnel.

Morka attributed the progress to measures introduced by the administration, including improved remuneration for soldiers, an increase in military personnel and better working conditions.

He stated, “Over the last year, we have witnessed a consistent decline, both in terms of incidents of insecurity, in terms of you know, fatalities.”

He also pointed to the creation of additional army divisions and improved accommodation for military personnel as evidence of the government’s efforts to strengthen the armed forces.

“You know, I mean, is it the creation of, you know, more divisions of the army? Is it the better motivation of our soldiers who are fighting and putting their lives, you know, in a line of fire every day for our safety? Is it, you know, building, you know, safer accommodation for our soldiers?” he added.

Addressing concerns over the recent abduction of National Youth Service Corps members and persistent bandit attacks in the North, the APC spokesman argued that insecurity was not peculiar to Nigeria.

He said even countries with sophisticated security systems had been unable to eliminate threats completely, adding that the challenge could not be resolved overnight.

He noted, “You know, insecurity is not something that is extinguished overnight, Nigeria, not by the most sophisticated countries on earth, not by the United States, not by Israel.

“Some of the, you know, most effective, you know, states, national security-conscious states, have not managed to eliminate insecurity altogether. Now, I’m not saying that we’re not challenged.”

Morka further claimed that government security interventions had led to the surrender of more terrorists and bandits to the military.

He maintained that the administration had made considerable gains in tackling insecurity and urged media organisations to report the situation in a balanced manner, insisting that the government’s efforts and results should be recognised.

His comments followed criticism by the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, Peter Obi, who had raised concerns about the security situation in the country.

In a statement published in August, Obi warned against allowing Nigeria to become a ‘killing field’, citing attacks and abductions in parts of the North-Central region.

He expressed concern that communities were being attacked and residents displaced despite the country not being officially at war.

“Nigeria is not officially at war, yet citizens are being attacked in their villages, abducted after prayers, driven from their homes and stripped of their farms,” he said.

Nigeria continues to face multiple security threats, including insurgency by extremist groups, banditry, kidnappings and communal violence.

The Global Centre for the Responsibility to Protect, in a November 16 assessment, said attacks by armed bandit groups and Boko Haram and Islamic State West Africa Province militants continued to put civilians at risk.

In his August statement, Obi called on governments at all levels to strengthen intelligence gathering, improve rapid-response capabilities, protect vulnerable communities and intensify efforts to rescue abducted Nigerians.
