title: Obi denies seeking US lawmakers’ backing for 2027 race
description:
Nigeria Democratic Congress presidential candidate, Peter Obi, has said his recent engagements with American political figures in Washington, DC, were not intended to secure an endorsement for his 2027 presidential ambition.
Obi said his visit to the United States was primarily to discuss Nigeria’s
content:
Nigeria Democratic Congress presidential candidate, Peter Obi, has said his recent engagements with American political figures in Washington, DC, were not intended to secure an endorsement for his 2027 presidential ambition.

Obi said his visit to the United States was primarily to discuss Nigeria’s development, citizens’ welfare, and the country’s democratic future with American stakeholders.

The former Anambra State governor stated this in a post on his X handle on Wednesday, responding to media reports suggesting that his meetings with members of the United States Congress amounted to an endorsement of his presidential ambition.

Obi said he did not describe the engagements as endorsements by the US Congress or any of its members.

“As I expressly noted in my remarks, my visit to the United States was not intended to secure an endorsement, and I did not characterise my meetings as endorsements of my political aspirations by the US Congress or any of its members,” he said.

He explained that the discussions focused on Nigeria’s development, the welfare of its citizens and the consolidation of democracy.

“I am especially concerned with strengthening democratic institutions, advancing accountability, and ensuring that Nigeria’s electoral process produces elections that are free, fair, transparent and credible. These matters should concern every Nigerian who is committed to our country’s future,” he added.

The NDC candidate also encouraged other Nigerian political leaders, particularly those seeking public office, to engage international stakeholders on issues affecting the country.

“Our democracy can be strengthened through constructive dialogue, the exchange of experiences and a shared commitment to credible elections,” he said.

Obi warned against sensational headlines and inaccurate interpretations of his engagements.

“Nigeria’s democratic future is far too consequential to be distorted by sensational headlines or inaccurate interpretations. My mission centred on Nigeria, its people and the future of our democracy—not on endorsing any individual,” he stated.

Obi had, in an earlier post on Tuesday, disclosed that he arrived in Washington, DC, on Monday, November 16, for engagements with American political figures, including members of the US House of Representatives.

He listed Congressman Marlin Stutzman, Congresswoman Beth Van Duyne, former Congressman Todd Tiahrt, Suzanne Bock Grisham and retired US Army Colonel Albert V. Short among those he met.

He also disclosed that he granted an interview to American television commentator Glenn Beck, during which they discussed Nigeria’s development challenges, accountable leadership and resource management.

Obi said he also addressed a gathering on Capitol Hill, where he highlighted the need for international cooperation on Nigeria’s security, national unity, economic prosperity and democratic development.

However, Karl Von Batten, a representative of Washington-based lobbying firm Von Batten-Montague-York, which was hired by former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, disputed suggestions that the US Congress officially met with or endorsed Obi.

In a statement on Wednesday, Von Batten said the event attended by Obi was a private engagement and that none of the individuals featured in the circulated video belonged to the House Foreign Affairs Committee or its Subcommittee on Africa.

He acknowledged the presence of Stutzman and Van Duyne but said neither served on the House Foreign Affairs Committee.

“Congress did not meet with or endorse Mr Obi. The event he attended was private, and no one in the video is a member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee or its Subcommittee on Africa,” he said.

Von Batten added that no official from the US State Department’s Bureau of African Affairs was present at the event.

The post Obi denies seeking US lawmakers’ backing for 2027 race appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: UBEC plans annual grants for public primary schools
description:
The Universal Basic Education Commission has said public primary schools across the country will receive annual grants under the Federal Government’s $152m HOPE-EDU programme to address their immediate needs and improve learning environments.
The grants are expected to empower school management to a
content:
The Universal Basic Education Commission has said public primary schools across the country will receive annual grants under the Federal Government’s $152m HOPE-EDU programme to address their immediate needs and improve learning environments.

The grants are expected to empower school management to address pressing needs, including minor renovations and improvements to school facilities. State governments, meanwhile, must meet specified performance targets to access funds under the programme.

The Programme Manager of HOPE-EDU, Oluwomayowa Aleshin, disclosed this on Wednesday during a regional thematic workshop for officials from the South-South and South-East geopolitical zones in Asaba, Delta State.

Aleshin explained that the programme was designed to bring out-of-school children back to classrooms, improve school facilities and raise the quality of basic education across the country.

He said the programme, which became effective on February 27, 2026, had entered its implementation stage, with states expected to meet specific targets before accessing funds.

He said, “The total amount of funds in the project is around `$152m. The reward is to be given to the states based on their performance.

“States are expected to access their matching grants, decentralise the disbursement to the local government and the schools, and also ensure that their schools are given an annual school grant.”

He explained that the funding arrangement was based on a performance-for-results system, under which states would receive funds only after meeting agreed requirements and undergoing independent verification.

According to him, independent verification agents would be deployed to assess the results submitted by states before the release of funds.

“Once they have achieved the disbursement-linked results, they package the results to us at the national level. We then deploy independent verification agents to verify whatever has been done before rewards are given,” he said.

The programme manager said the initiative would also strengthen financial management by transferring greater responsibility for managing education funds to local government areas and schools.

Earlier, the Executive Secretary of UBEC, Dr Aisha Garba, represented by the Director of South-South UBEC, Akpanosson Udoh, said the programme would improve accountability and ensure that resources meant for basic education translated into better learning conditions.

She said the introduction of school grants would enable school management to make quicker decisions on pressing needs rather than wait for interventions from higher authorities.

Garba said, “The introduction of annual school grants for school development will empower our schools to locally manage their issues. It will enhance quick decision-making, especially on small renovations and school environment needs.

“The use of the school grant will not only empower the school management but also address the immediate needs of the schools that will make them friendly and safe.”

She, however, identified delayed release of funds, difficulties in accessing counterpart funding, unclear regulations and inadequate capacity among officers as possible challenges to the implementation of the programme.

The UBEC executive secretary urged state officials to develop practical solutions to these challenges, stressing that the success of the programme would depend on effective implementation at the state, local government and school levels.

The workshop focused on two Disbursement Linked Indicators under Result Area 3 of the HOPE-EDU programme. DLI 6 covers decentralised management of core Universal Basic Education funds, while DLI 7 focuses on annual school grants and the regulations guiding their use.

Aleshin said the Asaba workshop was organised to prepare states in the South-South and South-East zones for the implementation of the two indicators.

The DLI 6 session began on Wednesday, while the DLI 7 workshop was scheduled to hold from November 19 to 21, 2026.

The post UBEC plans annual grants for public primary schools appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Oyetola hails Oyebamiji at 61
description:
The Minister of Marine and Blue Economy, Dr. Adegboyega Oyetola, has congratulated the former Managing Director of the National Inland Waterways Authority (NIWA) and former All Progressives Congress (APC) governorship candidate in Osun State, Munirudeen Bola Oyebamiji, on his 61st birthday.
In a con
content:
The Minister of Marine and Blue Economy, Dr. Adegboyega Oyetola, has congratulated the former Managing Director of the National Inland Waterways Authority (NIWA) and former All Progressives Congress (APC) governorship candidate in Osun State, Munirudeen Bola Oyebamiji, on his 61st birthday.

In a congratulatory message issued on Wednesday by his Special Adviser, Dr. Bolaji Akinola, Oyetola described the celebrant as an accomplished banker, astute administrator, dependable political associate and committed public servant whose contributions to governance and institutional development remain commendable.

The minister acknowledged Oyebamiji’s record of service across various institutions and public offices, particularly his tenure as Managing Director of NIWA, his contributions to the Federal Ministry of Marine and Blue Economy and his service as Osun State Commissioner for Finance.

He noted that Oyebamiji had consistently demonstrated professionalism, administrative competence, political loyalty and commitment to the public good.

According to Oyetola, Oyebamiji’s journey through the banking sector, public service and politics reflects his dedication to excellence and societal development.

“At 61, Asiwaju Munirudeen Bola Oyebamiji represents the enduring values of diligence, integrity, loyalty and purposeful leadership. His remarkable journey in the banking sector, public service and politics reflects a deep commitment to excellence and the development of our society,” he said.

Oyetola further described the celebrant as a trusted associate and worthy ambassador of Osun State, noting that his leadership qualities and contributions continue to inspire confidence among his contemporaries and younger generations.

“On behalf of my family and the entire Ministry of Marine and Blue Economy, I heartily rejoice with a trusted associate and worthy ambassador of Osun State on this special occasion. AMBO, as he is fondly known, has demonstrated uncommon dedication to every responsibility entrusted to him. His professionalism, humility and steadfast commitment to service are qualities worthy of emulation,” the Minister stated.

He also commended Oyebamiji’s resilience and continued engagement in the political arena, describing it as a reflection of his passion for the progress of Osun State and Nigeria.

The minister expressed confidence that the experience and wisdom Oyebamiji had acquired over the years would continue to benefit the APC, Osun State and the country.

Oyetola wished him many more years of good health, peace and greater accomplishments.

title: NAFDAC intercepts suspected tramadol concealed in corn starch at Lagos port
description:
The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control has uncovered suspected tramadol hydrochloride powder concealed in a 40-foot container declared as corn starch at the Apapa Port in Lagos.
The agency disclosed this in a post on its official X handle on Wednesday, saying its Port Inspe
content:
The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control has uncovered suspected tramadol hydrochloride powder concealed in a 40-foot container declared as corn starch at the Apapa Port in Lagos.

The agency disclosed this in a post on its official X handle on Wednesday, saying its Port Inspection Directorate acted on intelligence.

“During examination, officers discovered bags labelled ‘Tramadol Hydrochloride’ concealed within outer bags marked ‘Corn Starch’, raising concerns about possible misdeclaration and concealment,” NAFDAC said.

It added, “The consignment also had no evidence of the requisite NAFDAC permits or payment receipt at the time of examination.”

According to the agency, samples of the suspected substance have been collected and sent for laboratory analysis. The container remains in the custody of the Nigeria Customs Service, Apapa Command, pending the laboratory findings and further regulatory action.

“The identity of the suspected substance remains subject to laboratory confirmation,” the agency stated.

The agency did not disclose the quantity or value of the consignment, the identity of the importer, its country of origin, or whether any arrests had been made.

The latest discovery comes amid a series of enforcement operations by the agency, mostly in Lagos.

PUNCH Online reports that a NAFDAC enforcement operation uncovered unlabelled and unregistered cosmetics and packaging materials at the Tools and Hardware Complex, Trade Fair Complex, Ojo. The raid followed an earlier operation in February, during which the agency said it seized banned and counterfeit cosmetics worth over ₦3bn in the same market.

The post NAFDAC intercepts suspected tramadol concealed in corn starch at Lagos port appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Alake seeks support for 10-year Egba development plan
description: The Alake and Paramount Ruler of Egbaland, Oba Michael Adedotun Gbadebo, has challenged Egbas at home and in the diaspora to take ownership of the proposed Egba Development Plan (2027–2037), declaring that the ancient kingdom has been shortchanged over the years and deserves a more equitable share o
content:
The Alake and Paramount Ruler of Egbaland, Oba Michael Adedotun Gbadebo, has challenged Egbas at home and in the diaspora to take ownership of the proposed Egba Development Plan (2027–2037), declaring that the ancient kingdom has been shortchanged over the years and deserves a more equitable share of government attention and development.

The monarch, who gave the charge at the conference on the Egba Development Plan held on Wednesday at the Abeokuta Club, Abeokuta, Ogun State, said the proposed 10-year blueprint presented an opportunity for Egbaland to redefine its development priorities, articulate its collective aspirations and demand the attention it deserves.

The monarch expressed concern over what he described as the inadequate attention successive administrations had paid to Abeokuta, the Ogun State capital, insisting that a capital city must enjoy infrastructure and development commensurate with its status.

He also called on Egbas, irrespective of their locations, political affiliations or positions in society, to become ambassadors of the development plan and ensure its promotion and implementation.

The monarch said the timing of the initiative was significant, coming as it did at a period when the Ogun State government was approaching a change of administration, making it imperative for Egbaland to have a clearly defined development agenda to engage successive governments.

He however praised n a former governor whom he described as his son for using his administration to aggressively develop the state capital adding that though the former governor was hated by some for towing this path but added that the former state helmsman had only done what was expected to be done with the state capital

He explained that, “I am very, very happy to be with you this morning to launch or to give the royal charge for the Egba 2027–2037 10 years Development Plan. We have been told several times that anyone that fails to plan has already planned to fail, so if you have no plan that you are following, then you are a failure.

“I want to charge all of you that we are ambassadors for Egbaland, wherever you are, whatever post you will occupy after the moment the development plan is promulgated, you hold one, and you be the one to represent Egbaland in promoting it.

“It’s a good thing that this is coming at the time when government of Ogun State is changing hands. It’s the right time for us to promote the plan for Egba development”.

The Alake lamented what he considered years of neglect of the state capital, arguing that Abeokuta had not received the level of infrastructural investment expected of a city occupying such an important administrative position.

According to him, Egbaland’s present developmental standing does not reflect its historical significance, contributions and potential.

“We have been shortchanged over the years because we are not supposed to be where we are now. The state has not taken care of the capital enough,” the monarch declared.

Earlier, the Olowu of Owu, Oba Saka Matemilola, in his keynote address titled, “Abeokuta Among the Great West African Cities: Proud Heritage, Present Strengths and a Bold Vision for the Future,” called for a deliberate transformation of Abeokuta from a city celebrated mainly for its historical accomplishments into a modern urban centre capable of competing with leading cities across West Africa.

Oba Matemilola argued that while Abeokuta possessed an enviable historical foundation, cultural identity, human capital and economic potential, these advantages must be converted into tangible economic opportunities, improved infrastructure and a better quality of life for residents.

He identified cities such as Lagos, Accra, Abidjan, Dakar, Kumasi, Ibadan and Cotonou as examples of urban centres with distinctive strengths, urging Abeokuta to develop its own competitive identity rather than imitate other cities.

“Abeokuta must move from being a city celebrated principally for what it was, to becoming a city admired for what it is building and what it will become,” Matemilola said.

In his welcome address, the President of Abeokuta Club, Dr Adewale Adeola, explained that the conference was organised as part of the club’s social responsibility to provide Egbaland with a comprehensive, evidence-based and forward-looking development framework for the next decade.

He recalled that Egbaland once operated an Egba United Government established in 1893 and recognised by the British government under the leadership of the Alake, before its sovereignty was abrogated in 1914 following the amalgamation of Nigeria.

According to him, the conference was designed to obtain stakeholders’ views, identify the most pressing challenges facing Egbaland and determine the projects, policies and interventions required to secure a prosperous future for the people.

The post Alake seeks support for 10-year Egba development plan appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Idris hails Tinubu, supporters after APC rally in Kebbi
description:
Kebbi State Governor, Nasir Idris, has expressed appreciation to President Bola Tinubu, Vice-President Kashim Shettima and leaders of the All Progressives Congress for their participation in the party’s presidential campaign rally held in Birnin Kebbi on Tuesday.
The governor also commended the peop
content:
Kebbi State Governor, Nasir Idris, has expressed appreciation to President Bola Tinubu, Vice-President Kashim Shettima and leaders of the All Progressives Congress for their participation in the party’s presidential campaign rally held in Birnin Kebbi on Tuesday.

The governor also commended the people of Kebbi State for their massive turnout and peaceful participation, describing the successful rally as a demonstration of the strong relationship between the state and the Federal Government.

The Commissioner for Information and Culture, Yakubu Ahmed-BK, conveyed the governor’s appreciation during a press conference in Birnin Kebbi on Wednesday.

In a statement issued by the Chief Press Secretary to the Governor, Ahmed Idris, the commissioner said the President’s visit underscored his commitment to Kebbi State’s development and strengthened the partnership between the two levels of government.

He said the state government particularly appreciated Tinubu for finding time, despite his demanding national responsibilities, to visit Kebbi and interact with its people.

“We equally appreciate the people of Kebbi State for their orderly participation, overwhelming turnout and remarkable enthusiasm throughout the visit,” the commissioner said.

He added that the President’s visit provided an opportunity to reaffirm the shared commitment of the Federal and state governments to infrastructure development, economic opportunities and improved public services.

The commissioner particularly highlighted the governor’s appreciation of Tinubu’s favourable consideration of his request for the establishment and full operationalisation of an inland dry port at Tsamiya in Bagudo Local Government Area.

According to him, the proposed facility would boost cross-border trade, facilitate the movement of goods, attract local and international investments and create employment opportunities.

He described the project as a strategic economic investment that would strengthen Kebbi’s position in regional commerce and complement the state’s development priorities.

“We also acknowledge the Federal Government’s interventions and ongoing infrastructure and empowerment initiatives in Kebbi State under the Renewed Hope Agenda,” he said.

On the political significance of the rally, Ahmed-BK said the massive turnout demonstrated the level of political engagement in the state and its longstanding relationship with the APC.

He described the reception accorded Tinubu as an expression of solidarity with his leadership, the Renewed Hope Agenda and the development partnership between the Federal Government and the Idris administration.

The commissioner, however, cautioned political actors against making sweeping claims about the political choices of Kebbi residents, insisting that the people retained the ultimate power to determine the state’s political direction through democratic elections.

“Let it be clearly understood that the political direction of Kebbi State is ultimately determined by its people through their democratic choices. No political party or group should assume that its declarations alone represent the collective position of the citizens,” he said.

He also acknowledged the constitutional rights of opposition parties, including the African Democratic Congress, to participate in the democratic process.

However, he urged opposition politicians to focus on presenting credible alternatives and engaging constructively on issues affecting the welfare of citizens.

Ahmed-BK further commended traditional and religious leaders, APC stakeholders, women and youth organisations, support groups, the business community and transport unions for their contributions to the successful hosting of the presidential rally.

He also praised security agencies, media organisations, volunteers, public servants and organising committees for ensuring a peaceful and well-coordinated event.

The commissioner reaffirmed the state government’s commitment to sustaining its partnership with the Federal Government to attract more development projects, expand infrastructure and promote economic growth.

He called on political leaders and supporters to uphold civility, respect the rule of law, and avoid actions capable of undermining peace and unity as the country approaches the 2027 general elections.

He said political differences should not be allowed to threaten the stability and collective progress of Kebbi State and Nigeria.

The post Idris hails Tinubu, supporters after APC rally in Kebbi appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: NLC, TUC end public disagreement over N70,000 workers’ allowance
description:
The Nigeria Labour Congress and the Trade Union Congress of Nigeria have resolved their disagreement over the Federal Government’s N70,000 six-month transport allowance for workers.
The unions announced the resolution on Wednesday during a joint press conference in Abuja, saying they had agreed to p
content:
The Nigeria Labour Congress and the Trade Union Congress of Nigeria have resolved their disagreement over the Federal Government’s N70,000 six-month transport allowance for workers.

The unions announced the resolution on Wednesday during a joint press conference in Abuja, saying they had agreed to put their differences behind them in the interest of Nigerian workers.

In a joint statement signed by NLC President, Joe Ajaero, and TUC President-General, Festus Osifo, the organisations acknowledged that their disagreement had played out publicly but stressed that their shared history and responsibility to workers were more important than institutional differences.

They described the dispute as a family misunderstanding, which was resolved amicably through the intervention of former leaders of both labour centres.

The statement read, “The unity of the Nigerian working class is far greater than any disagreement between leaderships. Our common struggle, shared history, and collective responsibility to defend workers’ rights must never be sacrificed on the altar of misunderstanding or institutional differences.”

The disagreement centred on the N70,000 transport allowance approved by President Bola Tinubu for workers across different levels of government for six months.

The dispute became public after Ajaero and Osifo separately appeared on Channels Television’s The Morning Brief, where they disagreed over which labour centre had the authority to negotiate with the Federal Government on behalf of workers.

Ajaero argued that the NLC could negotiate independently, relying on the principle of representation under the International Labour Organisation.

“TUC can negotiate along with NLC, but NLC can negotiate alone based on the principle of most workers’ representatives of the ILO”, the NLC President noted.

Osifo, however, described the N70,000 agreement announced by Ajaero as an aberration, arguing that the TUC was not involved in the negotiations.

He challenged the NLC president to produce the ILO regulation that permitted one labour centre to negotiate on behalf of the other.

He stated, “He should show me in the ILO Regulations where it says one party is going to negotiate without the other one being there or consulted. He should show me! He should show Nigerians!

“ILO doctrine is that when you have more affiliates, and you are going for one of their events, it is not correct that the most represented will go and negotiate on behalf of the other one when the unions have their own umbrella.

“There is nowhere in ILO regulations that says a trade centre cannot negotiate for its members. It is not there! It is just that if you are going to the ILO, it is tripartite- the labour, government and the employers.”

Osifo also argued that the NLC could not negotiate on behalf of workers represented by the TUC simply because it had more affiliated unions.

He added, “But what we are saying is that you have about 60 affiliates while we have about 40. You cannot! You cannot negotiate for a body that is represented, for a body that has a trade union.

“You cannot negotiate on their behalf! It is not there anywhere!

“Yes, if we go to negotiations- I sit down, you sit down, and we agree”.

Ajaero, in his response, argued that the Trade Union Amendment Act 2005 made union membership voluntary and allowed workers to choose the organisations they wished to join.

“The 2005 Trade Union Amendment Act made membership of trade unions voluntary.

“It is the worker who determines the union he belongs to.

“Section 40 of the Nigerian 1999 Constitution, as amended, was clear that every Nigerian worker has the right to belong to any trade union, political or religious institution of his choice, which gives every worker the latitude to belong to any union of their choice,” Ajaero stated.

He also questioned Osifo’s claim of having a substantial number of workers in the federal civil service, arguing that only one TUC-affiliated union belonged to the Joint National Public Service Negotiating Council.

According to Ajaero, the council comprises eight union bodies, seven of which are affiliated with the NLC. He further argued that the TUC-affiliated union had subjected its negotiating authority to the joint body.

Osifo maintained that the two labour centres needed to participate in negotiations where their respective members were concerned.

He stated, “In that case, the two bodies must come together. We are not contesting the fact that NLC has more affiliates.

“But what we are saying is that you have about 60 affiliates while we have about 40. You cannot! You cannot negotiate for a body that is represented, for a body that has a trade union.

“You cannot negotiate on their behalf! It is not there anywhere!

“Yes, if we go to negotiations- I sit down, you sit down, and we agree.”

The TUC leader also questioned the legitimacy of the meeting at which the transport allowance was agreed, saying it was not a meeting of the Joint National Public Service Negotiating Council.

“But that meeting that took place was not the Council meeting. The Minister is not a member of the Council. Ajaero is not a member of the Council. The Council even has a quorum and the number of persons that must be seated to form a quorum. But at the end of the day, that meeting was not a JNC meeting. The members of JNC were not there!

“Again, if you see the release that was sent out by those three bodies, you will discover that after the last minimum wage, we got about a 33 per cent increment, and how does that work? Because from N30,000, we got N70,000.

“What you are supposed to do is that JNC will have to sit down and apply consequential adjustments,” he asked.

Ajaero, on his part, said the NLC had engaged the Federal Government after issuing an ultimatum over the workers’ demands.

“We gave the government an ultimatum; we were supposed to start an action. The government asked for four days to meet with us, and we met, and they resumed sitting after four days.

“After the meeting, the 70k allowance came up.”

He added that demands for a new minimum wage could not be negotiated without the establishment of a formal negotiation committee and wider consultations involving labour, government and employers.

The resolution of the disagreement comes amid renewed discussions over workers’ pay, following the Federal Government’s approval of a committee to examine concerns raised by the TUC over a new national minimum wage.

The TUC Secretary-General, Comrade General N.A. Toro, disclosed the development in a statement on Tuesday after a meeting between the union and the Federal Government.

The meeting followed a letter dated October 8, 2026, titled “Request for an Urgent Meeting to Address Critical National Economic, Security and Labour Challenges,” submitted by the TUC.

The Secretary to the Government of the Federation, Senator George Akume, chaired the meeting, while the TUC delegation was led by Osifo.

Other members of the delegation included Toro, Deputy President Shehu Mohammed, Trustee Akintola Benjamin and Auditor II Kamal Ibrahim.

The Head of the Civil Service of the Federation and the Permanent Secretary in the Office of the Secretary to the Government of the Federation, Ibrahim Kana, also attended.

The TUC said it had rejected the proposed six-month transport allowance, insisting that workers should receive a salary increase while discussions on a new national minimum wage were being concluded.

“In the course of the deliberations, the TUC made its position unequivocally clear on the proposed ₦70,000 transport intervention for a period of six months, which it rejected, preferring instead a salary increase pending the commencement and conclusion of discussions on a new National Minimum Wage.

“This position, alongside the other demands and concerns raised by Congress, will form part of the issues to be thoroughly interrogated by the High-Powered Committee,” the statement read in part.

The union said the committee would assess the issues raised, examine steps already taken by the government and make recommendations on outstanding matters.

“The Committee will therefore undertake a comprehensive review and reconciliation of the issues, establish the extent of actions already taken by the Government, identify outstanding matters and make appropriate findings and recommendations,” the statement said in part.

The committee comprises three TUC representatives, alongside officials from the Office of the Secretary to the Government of the Federation, the Office of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation, the National Salaries, Incomes and Wages Commission, and the Federal Ministry of Labour and Employment.

It is expected to begin work immediately and submit its report to the Secretary to the Government of the Federation within two weeks.

The post NLC, TUC end public disagreement over N70,000 workers’ allowance appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

The PUNCH gathered that the incident occurred at Ile Hausa in the Ilorin East Local Government Area in the early ho
content:
Traders in the Opomolu area of Ilorin, Kwara State, have lost their shops and goods after a midnight fire swept through a shopping area, destroying eight shops and two container shops.

The PUNCH gathered that the incident occurred at Ile Hausa in the Ilorin East Local Government Area in the early hours of Wednesday.

The Kwara State Fire Service said its personnel arrived at the scene at 12:35 am after receiving a distress call and immediately began efforts to contain the blaze and prevent it from spreading to neighbouring properties.

In a statement signed by its Public Relations Officer, Hassan Adekunle, the agency said preliminary findings indicated that a power surge might have triggered the fire, although investigations were ongoing to establish the actual cause.

“Preliminary information gathered at the scene suggests that the fire may have been triggered by a power surge.

“However, investigations are still ongoing, as other possible factors are also being examined to establish the actual cause of the incident,” the statement read.

Reacting to the incident, the Chief Fire Officer, Alabi Muhammed, urged traders to adopt stricter fire safety measures, warning that negligence involving electrical appliances and cooking materials could expose business premises to fire outbreaks.

He particularly cautioned operators of local restaurants and food businesses using charcoal and firewood to ensure that their cooking materials and other sources of heat were completely extinguished before leaving their premises.

Muhammed also advised business owners to engage qualified professionals for electrical installations, switch off appliances and isolate power sources at closing time, and keep combustible materials away from sources of ignition.

He added that traders should equip their shops with functional fire extinguishers and immediately report unusual smoke, sparks or other signs of fire to the emergency service.

He described fire prevention as a collective responsibility, stressing that prompt reporting of emergencies could help minimise damage.

“Fire prevention is a collective responsibility, and early reporting remains essential in reducing the extent of damage during fire emergencies,” the Chief Fire Officer was quoted as saying.

The incident came three days after firefighters prevented a potential disaster involving a petrol tanker loaded with about 55,000 litres of Premium Motor Spirit during a fuel transfer operation at a filling station in Moro Local Government Area of the state.

title: UK warns foreigners of four red flags when applying for visas
description:
The UK Visas and Immigration agency has urged foreign nationals applying for its visas to watch for four warning signs that signal potential fraud.
UKVI gave the warning in an advisory posted on its X handle on Wednesday, urging applicants to protect themselves from visa scams.
“4 RED FLAGS to watch
content:
The UK Visas and Immigration agency has urged foreign nationals applying for its visas to watch for four warning signs that signal potential fraud.

UKVI gave the warning in an advisory posted on its X handle on Wednesday, urging applicants to protect themselves from visa scams.

“4 RED FLAGS to watch out for when applying for a UK visa. Protect yourself from visa fraud by learning these crucial warning signs in our infographic,” the agency said.

The warning signs include people who guarantee applicants a UK visa or job, offer appointments or visa services that cannot be verified through official channels, and make unexpected contact to request money or personal information.

The agency’s guidance also cautioned applicants against individuals who pressure them to act immediately or demand secrecy, describing such tactics as common signs of fraud.

According to UKVI, scammers may contact applicants through phone calls, websites, emails and social media, or approach them outside visa application centres.

It said fraudsters sometimes pose as Home Office officials or representatives of visa application centres, offering services such as securing jobs, arranging appointments or processing visa applications.

Some may claim there is a problem with an applicant’s visa and demand urgent payment to prevent cancellation or deportation.

Visa fraud remains a major concern, with unsuspecting applicants often falling victim to scammers.

In 2025 alone, rejected or fraudulent-adjacent Schengen visa application processes cost Nigerian applicants an estimated €11.5 million (approx. ₦19 billion) in non-refundable fees and related agent expenses.

UKVI warned that fraudsters could also use official-sounding language and forged documents, including seemingly genuine job offer letters, to convince victims.

The agency said applicants should be wary of agents who promise to speed up visa applications in exchange for payments into personal bank accounts.

“Visa officers will never ask you for money in person, by email or phone,” the guidance stated.

It added that anyone applying for a UK visa or permission to travel would never be asked to pay visa fees through email, at a visa application centre or into a personal bank account.

The agency advised applicants to make appointments through the official UK government website or its authorised commercial partner.

It also warned that using forged documents could lead to visa refusal and a 10-year ban on applying for a UK visa.

UKVI urged applicants who suspect fraud not to disclose personal information, hand over their passports or send money, gift cards or vouchers to suspected scammers.

It advised people in the UK to report suspected fraud to Report Fraud, while those outside the country should contact their local authorities.

The post UK warns foreigners of four red flags when applying for visas appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: PHOTOS: Army commandant decorates three senior officers in Lagos
description:
The Commandant of the Nigerian Army College of Logistics and Management, Major General Adewale Adetoba, has decorated three senior officers recently promoted from the rank of Lieutenant Colonel to Colonel in the Nigerian Army.
The officers were decorated during a ceremony held at the RC Duru Officer
content:
The Commandant of the Nigerian Army College of Logistics and Management, Major General Adewale Adetoba, has decorated three senior officers recently promoted from the rank of Lieutenant Colonel to Colonel in the Nigerian Army.

The officers were decorated during a ceremony held at the RC Duru Officers’ Mess, Nigerian Army College of Logistics and Management, Ojo Campus, Lagos.

According to a statement posted by the Public Relations Officer, Nigerian Army College of Logistics and Management, Major Innocent Audu, on X on Tuesday, the newly promoted officers are Colonel Stephen Aluko of the Nigerian Army Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, who is the Acting Chief Instructor, Junior Leadership and Staff Officers Course; Colonel Shadrach Akom of the Nigerian Army Signals, a member of the Directing Staff and Staff Officer Grade One Training at Moloney Campus; and Colonel Polycarp Offor of the Nigerian Army Education Corps, who serves as Acting Chief Instructor, Languages.

Speaking at the ceremony, Adetoba congratulated the officers and urged them to demonstrate greater professionalism, discipline and commitment in their new positions.

He noted that promotion came through God’s grace, hard work and discipline, urging the newly decorated colonels to continue improving their knowledge and leadership abilities.

The commandant also encouraged the officers to be more empathetic in carrying out their statutory responsibilities and to maintain high professional standards.

Adetoba further acknowledged the contributions of their spouses, appreciating their patience, loyalty and support in ensuring that the officers had a stable home front.

Speaking on behalf of the newly promoted officers, Colonel Stephen Aluko expressed gratitude to God for keeping them alive to witness their elevation.

He also appreciated the Chief of Army Staff, Lieutenant General Waidi Shaibu, for considering them worthy of promotion.

Aluko equally thanked the commandant for his mentorship and guidance, describing the support as valuable to their professional development.

He said, “We appreciate the Chief of Army Staff, Lieutenant General Waidi Shaibu NAM, for finding us worthy and deserving to be elevated to the ranks of Colonels in the Nigerian Army.”

The colonel assured the college of their commitment to greater service, pledging that the officers would redouble their efforts in carrying out their responsibilities.

He also reaffirmed their determination to discharge their duties to the best of their abilities.

The event was attended by the Deputy Commandant, Director of Studies, faculty and administrative staff, as well as friends and family members of the newly promoted officers.

title: Tinubu support group donates educational materials to FCT schools
description:
The Support Group for President Bola Tinubu, under the PBAT Door2Door Campaign, on Wednesday, distributed educational materials to pupils in four public primary schools in the Federal Capital Territory.
The intervention, held in Gwagwalada Area Council, saw hundreds of pupils receive school bags, no
content:
The Support Group for President Bola Tinubu, under the PBAT Door2Door Campaign, on Wednesday, distributed educational materials to pupils in four public primary schools in the Federal Capital Territory.

The intervention, held in Gwagwalada Area Council, saw hundreds of pupils receive school bags, notebooks, mathematical sets, pens, pencils, erasers and other writing materials to support teaching and learning.

Speaking at the event, the National Coordinator of the group, Sunday Asuku, said that each beneficiary received a school bag, five notebooks and a mathematical set, alongside other essential learning materials.

Asuku said the initiative was inspired by the philanthropic activities of the group’s benefactor, Chief Government Ekpemupolo, popularly known as Tompolo.

He said, “The aim is simple and short. Tompolo, in his usual magnanimity, has sent us here to distribute education relief materials. This initiative is not a new one. It is something he has been doing over time in the Niger Delta region. But he felt he should extend his tentacles to other parts of the country.

“We are here in Abuja today. This is the fourth school we are visiting today.”

Asuku said the intervention was not politically motivated but aimed at supporting pupils and improving their access to basic learning materials.

“This is far from politics. It is also to support the government of Asiwaju Bola Ahmed Tinubu by giving students what we call education relief materials. However, it is majorly to support the pupils to have what it takes to go to class,” he said.

He explained that although basic education was free, many pupils still needed essential materials to participate effectively in classroom activities.

“At this level, the pupils don’t pay school fees. Education here is actually free at this level, but they need other materials to enhance the learning process in the classroom,” he added.

The coordinator said the outreach would be extended to other states, noting that similar interventions had been ongoing in the Niger Delta.

“By the grace of God, it’s going to be taken one step at a time, state by state. Like I said earlier, in the Niger Delta they have been doing this for a very long time. He is only trying to extend his tentacles to other parts of the country,” Asuku said.

The Head Teacher of Gadonasko Science Primary School, Gwagwalada, Abah Friday, commended Tompolo for the intervention, describing it as a significant relief for the pupils.

Similarly, the Education Secretary of Gwagwalada Area Council, Mamman Musa, described the initiative as timely and impactful, praising Tompolo for supporting teaching and learning in public schools.

Musa also prayed for God’s continued guidance and strength for Tompolo and President Tinubu.

The pupils and teachers expressed excitement as the beneficiaries received the educational materials.

title: Super Eagles rise to 29th in latest FIFA world rankings, fifth in Africa
description:
Nigeria’s Super Eagles have moved up one position to 29th in the latest FIFA men’s world rankings, recording a slight improvement in their global standing.
The latest rankings, released on Wednesday, also placed Nigeria fifth among African countries, following Algeria’s drop from the continent’s top
content:
Nigeria’s Super Eagles have moved up one position to 29th in the latest FIFA men’s world rankings, recording a slight improvement in their global standing.

The latest rankings, released on Wednesday, also placed Nigeria fifth among African countries, following Algeria’s drop from the continent’s top five.

Morocco maintained its position as Africa’s highest-ranked team, while Senegal, Egypt and Côte d’Ivoire occupied the second, third and fourth positions, respectively.

The latest ranking represents a modest improvement for the Super Eagles as they continue to strengthen their position among Africa’s leading football nations.

The Super Eagles’ rise follows their two November 2026 fixtures in the qualifying campaign for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations.

Eric Chelle’s side began the international window with an impressive 3-1 win over Tanzania’s Taifa Stars in their Matchday Three encounter at the Godswill Akpabio International Stadium in Uyo last Friday.

However, Nigeria were held to a frustrating 0-0 draw by the same opponents in the return fixture on Tuesday at the Amaan Stadium in Zanzibar.

On the global stage, world champions Spain maintained their position at the summit of the FIFA rankings.

Argentina, France and England also retained their places in the top five, while Morocco made a significant two-place climb to join the world’s leading nations.

title: US strategist Diana London deletes posts on Tinubu interview amid reports of receiving $4.5m lobbying fee from Nuhu Ribadu
description: American political strategist and media personality Diana London has deleted her social media posts concerning her engagements with the Nigerian government and the security partnership between Nigeria and the United States, amid reports linking her to a multimillion-dollar lobbying contract involvin
content:
American political strategist and media personality Diana London has deleted her social media posts concerning her engagements with the Nigerian government and the security partnership between Nigeria and the United States, amid reports linking her to a multimillion-dollar lobbying contract involving the Nigerian government.

A report by Peoples Gazette published on Wednesday alleged that London was associated with a $4.5 million payment made under a lobbying arrangement involving Aster Legal, a firm reportedly acting on behalf of National Security Adviser Nuhu Ribadu.

According to the publication, documents filed with the United States Department of Justice under the Foreign Agents Registration Act (FARA) showed that London was affiliated with DCI Group, a Washington-based conservative lobbying firm engaged by Nigeria.

The report said the $4.5 million payment, described as a retainer, was completed on December 12, 2025.

However, the US Justice Department filings identify London as a consultant to DCI Group, with the Republic of Nigeria, through Aster Legal, listed as the foreign principal. The documents describe the payment as part of the lobbying arrangement and do not establish that the entire sum was paid personally to London.

The lobbying engagement was intended to assist the Nigerian government in communicating its efforts to protect Christian communities and maintaining US support for its campaign against jihadist groups and other destabilising elements in West Africa.

London had earlier shared photographs of herself at the Presidential Villa in Abuja, where she was pictured alongside President Bola Tinubu and his Chief of Staff, Femi Gbajabiamila.

In one of her now-deleted posts, she described the security partnership between Nigeria and the United States as one that was “delivering results”.

“The U.S.-Nigeria security partnership is delivering results. Peace through strength. None of this happens without the ongoing partnership between President Trump and President Tinubu, their steadfast commitment to eliminating terrorists, and Nigeria’s willingness to work closely with the U.S. government,” she wrote.

She also described Nigeria as the United States’ greatest ally in Africa and suggested that the relationship could create more economic and trade opportunities for both countries.

In another post, London expressed appreciation for the opportunity to work with individuals representing Nigeria, particularly on efforts to protect religious groups and strengthen relations between the Trump administration and the Nigerian government.

However, the posts were no longer visible on her X account as of Wednesday morning. She had not publicly explained why she removed them.

The circumstances surrounding the deletion remain unclear.

title: EU proposes new 45bn euro Ukraine loan
description:
The European Union on Wednesday proposed member states give Ukraine an extra 45-billion-euro ($49 billion) loan to plug Kyiv’s 2027 budget shortfalls as Russia’s war drags on.



The funding would go two-thirds of the way towards filling a 70-billion-euro black hole Kyiv is facing next year — with B
content:
The European Union on Wednesday proposed member states give Ukraine an extra 45-billion-euro ($49 billion) loan to plug Kyiv’s 2027 budget shortfalls as Russia’s war drags on.

The funding would go two-thirds of the way towards filling a 70-billion-euro black hole Kyiv is facing next year — with Brussels looking to incentivise other Ukraine backers to do the rest.

“Five years since the start of this war of aggression, Europe stands united. We are as committed as ever to support Ukraine in war and in peace,” European Commission chief Ursula von der Leyen said.

“We think this is the best way to give Ukraine a strong hand at the negotiation table, and Ukraine only needs to repay once Russia pays for the damage it has caused in Ukraine.”

EU leaders will discuss the loan at a summit in Brussels next week in the hope of reaching a deal.

The EU is currently paying out a 90-billion-loan to Kyiv that it hoped would see the country through to the end of next year.

But as Russia has intensified its attacks it has become clear that those funds would not be enough.

The new loan would follow the same format as the current one and be borrowed against headroom in the EU’s central budget.

It would also be linked to Kyiv pressing on with reforms.

While the aim is to forge agreement next week, the issue of the funding has now become wrapped up with broader fraught negotiations over the EU’s next central budget.

Budget brawl

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz has insisted that all of the EU must settle the financing and all 27 member states must be involved before a deal can be reached on the budget.

That has rankled several of the EU’s least pro-Ukraine countries who want to be left out of backing the loan, such as Bulgaria, the Czech Republic, Hungary, and Slovakia.

Last time round, Budapest, Bratislava and Prague managed to get themselves exempted from having to help cover the financing.

Von der Leyen insisted the aim this time remains to get all countries on board.

Beyond the bloc, Brussels is pushing other allies of Ukraine – such as Britain, Canada and Japan to fill in the rest of Kyiv’s needs next year.

Similar pleas have previously fallen short.

In a bid to incentivise them this time, Brussels says others could provide guarantees to help bolster the loan or use the interest on frozen Russian assets in the EU to cover their own financing.

The proposal for a new loan means that the EU for now won’t try to look into the thorny issue of directly tapping over 200 billion euros of frozen Russian central bank assets held in the bloc to fund Ukraine.

That plan was shot down in 2025 by Belgium — where the majority of the assets are held — and the position of its government has not shifted.

title: Ex-Spain midfielder Juan Mata retires at 38
description:
Former Spain international midfielder Juan Mata has announced his retirement from professional football at the age of 38, bringing an end to a career that included a World Cup triumph and major honours with Chelsea and Manchester United.
Mata, who earned 41 caps for Spain, was part of the country’s
content:
Former Spain international midfielder Juan Mata has announced his retirement from professional football at the age of 38, bringing an end to a career that included a World Cup triumph and major honours with Chelsea and Manchester United.

Mata, who earned 41 caps for Spain, was part of the country’s squad that won the 2010 FIFA World Cup in South Africa.

He also played a key role in Spain’s success at the 2012 European Championship, scoring in their 4-0 victory over Italy in the final.

The midfielder began his professional career after progressing through Real Madrid’s youth system before joining Valencia in 2007, where he established himself as one of Spain’s promising attacking players.

His performances earned him a move to Chelsea in August 2011, where he won the UEFA Champions League, Europa League and FA Cup during his spell at Stamford Bridge.

Mata joined Manchester United in January 2014 and went on to help the club secure the Europa League, FA Cup and League Cup before leaving Old Trafford in 2022.

Following his departure from England, the Spaniard continued his career abroad, featuring for Turkish side Galatasaray and Japanese club Vissel Kobe.

He later moved to Australia, where he represented Western Sydney Wanderers and Melbourne Victory.

As reported by BBC Sport on Wednesday, announcing his retirement, Mata said that although he was stepping away from playing professionally, his connection with football would remain.

“Football will never leave my life.

“There are so many ways to continue loving the game, so many ways to keep using it as a vehicle for development.

“I may stop playing professionally, but I will never stop being a footballer,” he said.

Mata’s retirement brings to a close a career spanning several countries and some of European football’s biggest clubs.

His achievements with Spain, Chelsea and Manchester United established him as one of the notable midfielders of his generation.

title: Blindness: Eritrea, 10 others, eliminate trachoma from Africa as Nigeria lags
description:
By Sola Ogundipe



Eritrea has become the 11th country in the World Health Organisation (WHO) African Region to eliminate trachoma as a public health problem, raising hopes of ending a neglected tropical disease (NTD) that continues to threaten the sight of millions of people across the continent.
content:
By Sola Ogundipe

Eritrea has become the 11th country in the World Health Organisation (WHO) African Region to eliminate trachoma as a public health problem, raising hopes of ending a neglected tropical disease (NTD) that continues to threaten the sight of millions of people across the continent.

The achievement, validated by WHO, places Eritrea among 11 African countries that have successfully tackled the disease through sustained public health interventions, improved access to treatment, hygiene promotion and community mobilisation.

Eritrea, Algeria, Benin, Burundi, Eritrea, The Gambia, Ghana, Malawi, Mali, Mauritania, Senegal and Togo are the African countries that have received WHO validation as the number of countries that have achieved elimination globally stands at 34. Eritrea is also the 66th country globally and the 23rd in the WHO African Region to eliminate at least one neglected tropical disease.

According to WHO, Eritrea achieved the milestone, following two decades of sustained interventions targeting the disease, particularly in remote rural communities where poor access to clean water, sanitation and healthcare had fuelled its spread.

Eritrea’s success followed nationwide surveys conducted between 2006 and 2020, which helped identify affected communities and guide the rollout of interventions across the country.

The government subsequently implemented WHO’s recommended SAFE strategy, a combination of surgery for advanced cases, antibiotics to clear infection, facial cleanliness to limit transmission and environmental improvements, particularly better access to water and sanitation.

A notable feature of the campaign was its community-led sanitation approach, which delivered significant public health gains despite limited external funding.

Health workers deployed digital tools for data collection and mapping to identify affected populations, track disease patterns and direct resources to hard-to-reach communities.

In a congratulatory message, WHO Director-General Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said, “I congratulate the government and people of Eritrea on this historic achievement. After two decades of determined effort, Eritrea has consigned trachoma as a public health problem to history. This is a victory for the communities most affected by this devastating disease and a powerful example of what sustained national commitment can achieve.”

On his part, WHO Regional Director for Africa, Dr Mohamed Janabi, said Eritrea’s achievement demonstrated the impact of political commitment, community participation and effective partnerships in tackling neglected tropical diseases.

“I congratulate Eritrea on this historic public health milestone. It shows what is possible through sustained political commitment, community leadership and strong partnerships. Eritrea’s achievement brings us closer to a world free from the suffering caused by neglected tropical diseases and sends a strong message of hope to other African countries working towards trachoma elimination,” he stated.

WHO Representative to Eritrea, Dr Mary Stephen, said, “This success belongs first and foremost to the people of Eritrea. The elimination of trachoma as a public health problem is the result of strong national leadership and ownership and collaboration between communities, the Ministry of Health, the Fred Hollows Foundation, development partners and health workers across the country,” she said.

While Eritrea has secured WHO validation, Nigeria is making significant progress towards eliminating trachoma, although the disease remains a public health challenge in some parts of the country.

The Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare disclosed that 11 local government areas (LGAs) remained to achieve elimination status out of 134 previously identified endemic LGAs.

The country has stopped mass drug administration (MDA) in 116 LGAs after they met the WHO elimination threshold, representing approximately 87 per cent progress towards eliminating the disease in affected areas.

Director and Programme Manager of the National Trachoma Programme, Nicholas Olobio, said Nigeria had also performed more than 100,000 surgeries for trachomatous trichiasis, the advanced stage of the disease that can cause irreversible blindness.

Nigeria’s progress has been hindered by the implementation of WHO’s SAFE strategy, supported by mass antibiotic distribution, eye surgeries, hygiene promotion and improved access to water and sanitation.

Trachoma is among the 21 diseases and disease groups covered by WHO’s Neglected Tropical Diseases Roadmap 2021–2030, which seeks to accelerate prevention, control, elimination and eradication efforts, particularly among populations living in poverty and underserved communities.

The disease is caused by the bacterium Chlamydia trachomatis and spreads through contact with eye and nasal discharge from infected people. Repeated infections can cause scarring of the inner eyelid, forcing the eyelashes to turn inward and scratch the eyeball. Without treatment, the condition can cause irreversible blindness.

It disproportionately affects poor and underserved communities, particularly those with inadequate access to clean water, sanitation, hygiene facilities and essential healthcare. Despite significant global progress, the disease remains a public health challenge in parts of the world.

Although Africa has recorded substantial progress, it remains the continent most affected by the disease. The global target for eliminating trachoma as a public health problem is part of WHO’s neglected tropical diseases roadmap for 2021 to 2030.

The post Blindness: Eritrea, 10 others, eliminate trachoma from Africa as Nigeria lags appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Germany To Cut Electricity Tax, Cap Fuel Prices
description: Germany said Wednesday that it would cut electricity taxes and introduce a temporary fuel price cap to help households and businesses struggling with the energy shock sparked by the US war against Iran.Chancellor Friedrich Merz’s conservatives and their centre-left coalition partners announced
content:
Germany said Wednesday that it would cut electricity taxes and introduce a temporary fuel price cap to help households and businesses struggling with the energy shock sparked by the US war against Iran.

Chancellor Friedrich Merz’s conservatives and their centre-left coalition partners announced an agreement on the measures after marathon talks that ran through the night.

“Intensive talks have paid off,” said Merz, adding that the government was fulfilling its promise to lower prices.

“Small businesses and families in particular will feel the relief,” he said.

The agreement comes after long-running tensions in the coalition, consisting of the CDU/CSU bloc and the centre-left SPD, over how to tackle a range of pressing issues including pension to healthcare reforms.

Like elsewhere, energy costs have surged in Germany since the outbreak of the US-Israeli war against Iran and its disruptions to oil and gas shipments through the Strait of Hormuz.

The electricity tax cut will initially be in place from January to December next year, the government said in a statement.

For private households, the reduction amounts to about two cents per kilowatt hour, taking it to just 0.1 cents.

The average German household consumed around 2,400 kilowatt hours of electricity last year, according to Germany’s BDEW association of energy and water utilities.

The average saving should thus amount to about 50 euros ($54) annually.

For businesses, a typical hairdressing salon would save hundreds of euros a year on its electricity bill while a supermarket would enjoy relief of thousands of euros annually, according to the government.

The government had already pledged to cut electricity taxes for households when it took power last year but had so far introduced only a reduction for some heavy industries, as the coalition struggled to agree on how to fund the measure.

The coalition also said that fuel prices would be capped from January, initially for three months, to provide relief for motorists.

The government had already introduced fuel subsidies to lower prices but they are set to expire at the end of this year.

“The fuel price cap is explicitly a crisis-related, and not a permanent, measure,” the government said.

AFP

title: ‘Congress did not meet with or endorse him’ — Atiku US lobbyist speaks on Peter Obi Washington visit
description: A Washington-based lobbying firm’s managing partner, Dr Karl Von Batten, has disputed claims that the United States Congress endorsed former Anambra State Governor Peter Obi, clarifying that the Nigerian politician attended a private event and was neither formally received nor endorsed by Congress.
content:
A Washington-based lobbying firm’s managing partner, Dr Karl Von Batten, has disputed claims that the United States Congress endorsed former Anambra State Governor Peter Obi, clarifying that the Nigerian politician attended a private event and was neither formally received nor endorsed by Congress.

Von Batten said his communications director had forwarded two media reports claiming that the US Congress endorsed Obi.

He explained that he decided to address the reports after a social media commentator, @Mimi_yakigar, mentioned his firm in connection with the claims.

“Congress did not meet with or endorse Mr Obi. The event he attended was private,” Von Batten said.

He identified US Representatives Marlin Stutzman and Beth Van Duyne in the footage but noted that neither serves on the House Foreign Affairs Committee.

According to him, the video also showed no members of the committee or its Subcommittee on Africa, nor officials from the State Department’s Bureau of African Affairs.

Von Batten said he considered it necessary to clarify the nature of the event because his firm had been mentioned in the reports, while acknowledging the significance of Obi’s visit to the United States.

Obi arrived in Washington, DC, on Monday, November 16, 2026, for a series of engagements with American political figures and other influential stakeholders ahead of Nigeria’s 2027 general elections.

The former governor, who is the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), said the visit was intended to draw international attention to Nigeria’s development challenges, security situation and democratic future.

In a statement posted on his X account, Obi said he had held discussions with members of the US House of Representatives and Senate, as well as other American personalities.

Those he identified included US Representatives Marlin Stutzman and Todd Tiahrt, Congresswoman Beth Van Duyne, Suzanne Bock Grisham and retired US Army Colonel Albert V. Short.

Obi also granted an interview to American television commentator Glenn Beck, during which he discussed Nigeria’s leadership challenges, accountability, management of national resources and development prospects.

He further disclosed that he addressed an audience on Capitol Hill, where he called for international cooperation to tackle insecurity, strengthen national unity and promote economic prosperity in Nigeria.

title: US Judge Orders Trump To Give Deposition In BBC Lawsuit By Jan 22
description: A US judge ordered President Donald Trump on Tuesday to testify under oath by January 22 in his multibillion-dollar defamation lawsuit against the BBC.Trump has accused the British broadcaster of deceptively editing a documentary to make it seem as if he was inciting violence when he told supporters
content:
A US judge ordered President Donald Trump on Tuesday to testify under oath by January 22 in his multibillion-dollar defamation lawsuit against the BBC.

Trump has accused the British broadcaster of deceptively editing a documentary to make it seem as if he was inciting violence when he told supporters to march on the US Capitol on January 6, 2021.

US District Judge Jeffrey T. Kuntz in Florida ordered an extension to a previous deadline of December 11 to give both Trump and the BBC more time to prepare for trial.

Both sides must be ready to go to trial by May 3, he said.

The BBC documentary at issue, “Trump: A Second Chance,” spliced together two separate sections of Trump’s speech on January 6, 2021, making it appear that he had explicitly urged supporters to attack the US Capitol.

Crowds proceeded to storm the building in an attempt to stop the formal certification of Democrat Joe Biden’s victory in the presidential election.

The BBC has apologized for the incident, which prompted the resignation of multiple senior executives, but has denied causing Trump any real injury.

Trump has sought at least $5 billion each for one claim of defamation and a separate claim under a Florida consumer protection law.

Kuntz has rejected the broadcaster’s bid to dismiss the defamation suit, but tossed the Florida protection law claim.

The BBC has accused Trump of dodging their efforts to get his sworn testimony.

Trump has made attacks on the media a signature of his two presidential terms, insulting reporters and seeking to ban outlets airing critical reports from the White House.

AFP

title: Xi Jinping welcomes Trump in China ahead of historic meeting with Putin
description:
Chinese President Xi Jinping personally welcomed US President Donald Trump at the airport on Wednesday as the American leader arrived in China for a historic trilateral meeting involving Russian President Vladimir Putin.
AFP footage showed Trump descending from Air Force One before standing alongsid
content:
Chinese President Xi Jinping personally welcomed US President Donald Trump at the airport on Wednesday as the American leader arrived in China for a historic trilateral meeting involving Russian President Vladimir Putin.

AFP footage showed Trump descending from Air Force One before standing alongside Xi on a red carpet lined with people waving colourful pom-poms and holding Chinese and American flags.

Trump saluted during the welcome ceremony before exchanging a handshake with the Chinese leader.

Meanwhile, Russian President Vladimir Putin described Western sanctions against Russia as a failure on Wednesday.

Putin also held a meeting with Xi Jinping in China ahead of the planned historic summit involving the three world leaders.

The gathering is expected to bring Trump, Xi and Putin together for discussions amid ongoing international tensions and strained relations between major global powers.

Thursday’s trilateral has triggered fears that the three powerful men could make decisions on the fate of Ukraine over the heads of Kyiv and Europe, and seek to carve up the world into 21st-century spheres of influence.

Washington had signalled that Ukraine – something Xi vehemently sees as not China’s problem – was not expected to be addressed, before Trump said that it would.

Putin, who met with Xi on Wednesday in China’s Shenzhen, was defiant on his war in Ukraine ahead of the three-man summit as he slammed Western sanctions provoked by the 2022 invasion.

“We see such examples in the failed attempts to isolate our country, Russia, which has faced an unprecedented sanctions pressure,” Putin said.

After meeting the Russian leader, Xi urged closer ties with Moscow, saying the nations should “leverage the mechanisms for exchanges between the two countries’ governments, legislative bodies, militaries and political parties”.

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, also in Shenzhen, said that sanctions on Russia “are going to continue to increase as long as this (Ukraine) war goes on.”

Also up for discussion in Thursday’s trilateral meeting are the Iran war and nuclear disarmament, according to Washington, after a US-Russia bilateral treaty on atomic weapons expired in February.

Beijing has long maintained that the US and Russia should reduce their giant nuclear arsenals before it agrees to talks on its smaller stockpile

title: 2027: Court upholds Suswam’s candidacy, declares him APC senatorial flagbearer in Benue
description:
The Federal High Court in Abuja has declared former Benue State Governor, Gabriel Suswam, the valid candidate of the All Progressives Congress (APC) for the 2027 Benue North East senatorial election.
Justice Inyang Ekwo delivered the judgment on Wednesday, ruling in favour of the former governor, wh
content:
The Federal High Court in Abuja has declared former Benue State Governor, Gabriel Suswam, the valid candidate of the All Progressives Congress (APC) for the 2027 Benue North East senatorial election.

Justice Inyang Ekwo delivered the judgment on Wednesday, ruling in favour of the former governor, who challenged his substitution by the party.

The judge agreed with Suswam’s argument that the APC unlawfully replaced him despite his victory in the party’s primary election, where he secured the majority of valid votes cast.

Justice Ekwo held that the party’s decision to substitute Suswam did not comply with the provisions of the Electoral Act, the 1999 Constitution (as amended), and the APC Constitution.

The ruling therefore recognises Suswam as the party’s valid candidate for the 2027 Benue North East senatorial contest.

The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that Suswam had, in the suit marked FHC/ABJ/CS/1470/2026, prayed the court to recognise him as the validly elected candidate of the APC for the senatorial district.

The former governor joined the APC, incumbent Sen. Emmanuel Udenbe and INEC as defendants in the suit.

At the last proceedings, counsel to INEC, Anthony Malik, SAN, told the court that documents relating to the conduct of the primary indicated that Suswam won the exercise.

Malik urged the court to determine the dispute in accordance with the result of the primary election, maintaining that the electoral body had placed before the court its report on the exercise, as well as the result.

He consequently asked the court to uphold the outcome showing Suswam as the winner of the primary.

Suswam’s counsel, Jibrin Okutepa, SAN, also urged the court to grant the reliefs sought by his client.

Okutepa asked the court to reject the preliminary objections raised against the suit by the APC and Udenbe, arguing that the objections lacked merit.

However, counsel to the APC, A. G. Yirvoms, asked the court to uphold the party’s preliminary objection and dismiss Suswam’s case.

Suswam is challenging the decision of the APC to hand its Benue North East senatorial ticket to Udenbe despite his claim that he won the party’s primary election. (NAN)

title: JAMB to refund UTME fees for candidates with disabilities
description:
The Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board has announced special examination support for candidates with disabilities, including refunds of application document fees, free audiobooks and transportation assistance for eligible candidates.
The board said candidates with disabilities who meet the req
content:
The Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board has announced special examination support for candidates with disabilities, including refunds of application document fees, free audiobooks and transportation assistance for eligible candidates.

The board said candidates with disabilities who meet the required O’Level qualifications would receive a refund of their application document fees at their respective examination centres.

JAMB disclosed this in an awareness message on its X handle on Wednesday, explaining the special provisions available to candidates with disabilities ahead of the Unified Tertiary Matriculation Examination (UTME).

According to the board, “candidates with visual impairments, particularly those who are blind, would also receive audiobooks of prescribed reading texts to support their examination preparation.”

The board said the initiative was designed to improve access to learning materials and ensure that candidates with visual disabilities could prepare adequately for the examination.

It added that JAMB would cover transportation and accommodation costs for blind candidates and their guides.

The examination body further explained that candidates with disabilities who meet the minimum acceptable UTME score would also be considered for admission into their preferred institutions.

The provisions form part of the board’s efforts to promote inclusive access to tertiary education and ensure that physical disabilities do not prevent eligible candidates from pursuing their academic ambitions.

JAMB emphasised that candidates must indicate their disability status during registration to enable the board to make the necessary arrangements for their examination.

“Remember, for the board to make necessary arrangements, you must indicate your disability status during registration,” the board stated.

It also clarified that the refund of application document fees would only be provided at the examination centre.

The board urged candidates with disabilities to ensure that they declare their status during registration so they can benefit from the available support services.

The initiative is expected to provide additional assistance to eligible candidates, particularly those who require special arrangements to participate in the UTME.

The post JAMB to refund UTME fees for candidates with disabilities appeared first on Punch Newspapers.
