title: UK church leader jailed for 12 years over rape
description:
A church leader in Coventry, United Kingdom, Brein Ayeni, has been sentenced to 11 years and nine months in prison for raping a woman and subjecting her to coercive and controlling behaviour.
Ayeni, 43, who headed the Christworld Nation Church in Coventry, was convicted of three counts of rape and o
content:
A church leader in Coventry, United Kingdom, Brein Ayeni, has been sentenced to 11 years and nine months in prison for raping a woman and subjecting her to coercive and controlling behaviour.

Ayeni, 43, who headed the Christworld Nation Church in Coventry, was convicted of three counts of rape and one count of coercive or controlling behaviour following a trial.

West Midlands Police disclosed this in a statement published on its website on Monday.

The offences reportedly began in June 2025, with the church leader recording some of the attacks on his mobile phone.

According to the police, Ayeni threatened to share the videos if the woman reported the abuse, claiming they showed that what happened was consensual.

He also made derogatory comments about her, comparing her previous lifestyle choices to poison, and displayed controlling behaviour after gaining her trust.

The woman reported the abuse to the police in March 2026, prompting an investigation by specialist officers from the force’s Rape and Serious Sexual Offences team.

Ayeni, who lived on Hurst Road, Coventry, was sentenced at Warwick Crown Court on November 10.

In a victim impact statement, the woman said the abuse had severely affected her ability to trust others and her mental and emotional well-being.

It read, “The title he held made me trust him, and that trust has been deeply damaged. The impact on my mental and emotional health is that I do not feel like the same person I was before all of this happened.

“I struggle to trust people and allow them to get close to me because I am frightened of being taken advantage of again. It has affected my family, who have had to watch someone they love go through something so painful.

“I understand how frightening it can be to speak up when you know that people may question you, judge you or turn against you. Reporting what happened took courage. It was not easy for me, and I have had to fight through fear, uncertainty and the emotional weight of revisiting these experiences.

“I am grateful for the people who have supported me. I do not want another woman to experience the fear, confusion, humiliation and emotional pain that I have had to live with.”

Detective Sergeant Evie Griffiths, of the force’s public protection unit, described the offences as horrific and said they had left a lasting impact on the victim.

Griffiths said, “These were horrific crimes which have understandably had a lasting impact. It is through her bravery in telling us what happened we were able to arrest Ayeni and stop him committing any further offences.

“We never underestimate the harm and distress caused by sex attackers which is why we have specially-trained officers who work tirelessly to catch offenders and support those who have been attacked.

“Ayeni abused the trust in him to carry out these terrible crimes, but he has quite rightly been put behind bars for a significant period of time.

“We hope she can use the strength from knowing her bravery has helped protect herself, and others, from Ayeni will assist in continuing her recovery from this truly awful ordeal.”

The post UK church leader jailed for 12 years over rape appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Huawei warns of AI-driven cyber risks
description:
Huawei has warned businesses and organisations about emerging cybersecurity threats associated with artificial intelligence, urging them to strengthen their data protection systems.
According to the company, autonomous AI agents are capable of actions that could expose critical business information
content:
Huawei has warned businesses and organisations about emerging cybersecurity threats associated with artificial intelligence, urging them to strengthen their data protection systems.

According to the company, autonomous AI agents are capable of actions that could expose critical business information to data loss and cyberattacks.

The warning was one of the key takeaways from Huawei IT Day Nigeria 2026, held in Lagos under the theme, ‘Powering AI in Nigeria Together: Compute. Collaborate. Create.’

Speaking on the growing risks of AI adoption, Huawei’s Director of Data Protection Solutions, Liu Ming, said organisations could no longer rely solely on traditional data backup and disaster recovery arrangements to protect their digital infrastructure.

He cited two incidents involving AI systems that demonstrated the potential risks of autonomous operations.

In July 2026, OpenAI disclosed that models undergoing internal cybersecurity evaluations had circumvented security controls, gaining unauthorised access to parts of the company’s research infrastructure and systems belonging to AI platform Hugging Face.

In a separate incident in April 2026, an AI coding agent used by PocketOS, a US-based software company, deleted the company’s production database and associated backups in approximately nine seconds while attempting to resolve a technical issue. The data was later recovered.

“These incidents illustrate how AI can introduce new vulnerabilities—both through sophisticated attacks and through unintended actions by autonomous agents. While no single technology can eliminate all risks, stronger data protection practices and purpose-built resilience solutions have become essential,” Liu said.

To address these threats, he recommended the 3-2-1-1-0 data protection rule, under which organisations maintain at least three copies of their data, store them on two different types of media, keep one copy offsite for disaster recovery, maintain another offline or immutable copy for protection against ransomware, and ensure zero errors during data restoration.

He also presented Huawei’s OceanProtect solution, designed to protect traditional and AI data centres against data loss, ransomware attacks and system disruptions.

According to Liu, the platform protects databases, virtual machines and files while extending its security capabilities across AI training, inference and autonomous AI operations.

He added that OceanProtect offers security assessment, real-time monitoring of AI agents’ activities and rollback capabilities to minimise the impact of erroneous operations.

Beyond security, Huawei’s Deputy Managing Director and Director of ICT Marketing and Solution Sales Department, Zhang Haijie, announced plans to expand the company’s AI computing infrastructure in Nigeria by the end of the year to strengthen local innovation and extend its business operations across West Africa.

Zhang said the company was transitioning from an ICT infrastructure provider to an AI computing and ecosystem enabler.

“For a few years, Huawei has served Nigeria as an ICT infrastructure provider. Today, we are stepping into a new era, transforming from an ICT supplier to an AI computing foundation and ecosystem level,” he said.

Zhang identified the provision of high-performance, cost-effective computing platforms, support for local partners and the development of a sustainable AI ecosystem as the company’s main priorities.

He said Huawei would take Nigeria’s infrastructure challenges, particularly power shortages, into account by prioritising energy efficiency to reduce the cost of AI adoption.

He also disclosed that the additional computing resources would be made available through Huawei’s local open laboratory, giving partners the opportunity to test and demonstrate their innovations.

Also speaking at the event, Huawei’s Director of Sub-Saharan Africa Enterprise Data Centre Marketing and Solution Sales Department, Chen Boyi, identified data, computing power and large models as the three fundamental requirements for successful AI development, describing data as the foundation, computing power as the engine and large models as the intelligence.

He stressed that technology providers could not drive AI adoption on their own without the involvement of local partners.

“Our Nigerian partners have good ideas, innovation, and knowledge across industries. Today, together, we can make AI better,” he said.

title: Iran, allies hit Gulf countries after US attack on island
description:
Gulf nations scrambled to intercept incoming fire on Wednesday, after Iran and its allies lashed out following a US strike on a strategic island, in attacks that threatened to derail efforts to end the war.



Kuwait activated its air defences to counter drone strikes – the first since early Septemb
content:
Gulf nations scrambled to intercept incoming fire on Wednesday, after Iran and its allies lashed out following a US strike on a strategic island, in attacks that threatened to derail efforts to end the war.

Kuwait activated its air defences to counter drone strikes – the first since early September – and Bahrain said it fended off an Iranian attack, after the United States struck Iran’s Qeshm Island in the flashpoint Strait of Hormuz.

Explosions were heard in Saudi Arabia, the world’s biggest crude oil exporter, which said it intercepted a cruise missile fired by the Iran-backed Houthis, who have been seizing fresh territory in neighbouring Yemen.

Bahrain has now suffered four Iranian attacks in six days, ending a weeks-long respite in the war that started with US-Israeli strikes on the Islamic republic on February 28.

Iran responded by striking America’s wealthy Gulf allies, which host US military bases, and blockading Hormuz, which before the war carried a quarter of global oil flows.

The Iranian army said “combat and kamikaze drones” targeted US air defence systems and launch platforms at Kuwait’s Ali Al-Salem air base on Wednesday.

A day earlier, American fighter jets hit a missile launch site on Qeshm Island with “precision munitions”, a US military official said, describing it as a riposte to Iranian aggression.

‘Dangerous escalation’

Iran’s army chief Amir Hatami warned of a “more devastating” reaction to America and its allies.

“Should the enemy make a mistake and repeat actions that have previously led them to despair, our response — directed at both the enemy and their backers — will undoubtedly be even more devastating and will know no geographical boundaries,” Hatami said, according to Iran’s Fars news agency.

Mediator Qatar, which held talks with Iranian officials on Tuesday, called the latest attacks a “dangerous escalation” and warned they undercut efforts to find a peaceful solution.

“The continuation of these attacks represents a dangerous escalation that could complicate efforts to contain tensions and undermine political and diplomatic efforts aimed at ensuring the security and stability of the region,” a foreign ministry statement said.

Kuwaiti residents described feelings of foreboding as attacks returned to the tiny, oil-rich country, which was hit hard by Iranian strikes earlier in the war.

“The explosions seemed to be coming from far away, but hearing them again after a period of calm was both surprising and worrying,” said Egyptian resident Hani Mohammed, 40.

“People had started to readjust to a normal life. The sounds of planes and explosions no longer set the pace of daily life as before. But what happened has revived feelings of anxiety.”

Windows rattled

Meanwhile, one seafarer was missing after a ship belonging to ADNOC, the United Arab Emirates’ oil giant, was struck late on Tuesday in Hormuz, the company said.

Ships transiting Hormuz have come under nearly daily fire from Iran, which insists they use routes it has authorised.

The US has responded by imposing a blockade on Iranian ports, and its navy escorts tankers through the narrow passage.

Saudi Arabia has endured weeks of attacks by the Houthis, who have completed their control of Yemen’s Red Sea coast and advanced close to the government’s interim capital, Aden.

A four-year truce in Yemen’s bloody civil war, where a Saudi-led coalition has fought for the government since 2015, dissolved in July.

On Wednesday, an “extremely loud” explosion was heard in the north of the Saudi capital Riyadh, a resident told AFP. Another said windows rattled throughout their house, while doors flew open and lights flickered.

Earlier, Saudi coalition spokesman Turki al-Malki posted on X that “a cruise missile, launched by the terrorist Houthi militia toward the Riyadh area, has been intercepted and destroyed”.

title: Benue North East: Court declares Suswam as APC valid senatorial candidate
description:
The Federal High Court in Abuja on Wednesday declared former Governor of Benue, Gabriel Suswam, as the valid candidate of the All Progressives Congress (APC) for the 2027 Benue North East senatorial election.



Justice Inyang Ekwo, in a judgment, agreed with the argument of the ex-governor that he
content:
The Federal High Court in Abuja on Wednesday declared former Governor of Benue, Gabriel Suswam, as the valid candidate of the All Progressives Congress (APC) for the 2027 Benue North East senatorial election.

Justice Inyang Ekwo, in a judgment, agreed with the argument of the ex-governor that he was unlawfully substituted by the party, having won the majority of the valid votes cast.

Justice Ekwo held that the substitution was not in synch with the provisions of the Electoral Act and the 1999 Constitution (as amended), including the APC’s Constitution.

The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that Suswam had, in the suit marked FHC/ABJ/CS/1470/2026, prayed the court to recognise him as the validly elected candidate of the APC for the senatorial district.

The former governor joined the APC, incumbent Sen. Emmanuel Udenbe and INEC as defendants in the suit.

At the last proceedings, counsel to INEC, Anthony Malik, SAN, told the court that documents relating to the conduct of the primary indicated that Suswam won the exercise.

Malik urged the court to determine the dispute in accordance with the result of the primary election, maintaining that the electoral body had placed before the court its report on the exercise, as well as the result.

He consequently asked the court to uphold the outcome showing Suswam as the winner of the primary.

Suswam’s counsel, Jibrin Okutepa, SAN, also urged the court to grant the reliefs sought by his client.

Okutepa asked the court to reject the preliminary objections raised against the suit by the APC and Udenbe, arguing that the objections lacked merit.

However, counsel to the APC, A. G. Yirvoms, asked the court to uphold the party’s preliminary objection and dismiss Suswam’s case.

Suswam is challenging the decision of the APC to hand its Benue North East senatorial ticket to Udenbe despite his claim that he won the party’s primary election. (NAN)

title: China’s Xi greets Trump on arrival at Shenzhen airport
description:
Chinese President Xi Jinping personally greeted Donald Trump at the airport as the US leader arrived Wednesday ahead of a trilateral meeting in Shenzhen that will also include Russia’s Vladimir Putin, AFP footage showed.



After descending from Air Force One, Trump saluted as he stood alongside Xi
content:
Chinese President Xi Jinping personally greeted Donald Trump at the airport as the US leader arrived Wednesday ahead of a trilateral meeting in Shenzhen that will also include Russia’s Vladimir Putin, AFP footage showed.

After descending from Air Force One, Trump saluted as he stood alongside Xi on a red carpet lined with people waving colourful pom-poms and brandishing Chinese and American national flags, before the two leaders shook hands.

Putin on war sanctions

Meanwhile, President Vladimir Putin called Western sanctions on Russia a failure on Wednesday and met with his counterpart Xi Jinping in China ahead of their historic summit with US leader Donald Trump.

Thursday’s trilateral has triggered fears that the three powerful men could make decisions on the fate of Ukraine over the heads of Kyiv and Europe, and seek to carve up the world into 21st-century spheres of influence.

Washington had signalled that Ukraine – something Xi vehemently sees as not China’s problem – was not expected to be addressed, before Trump said that it would.

Putin, who met with Xi on Wednesday in China’s Shenzhen, was defiant on his war in Ukraine ahead of the three-man summit as he slammed Western sanctions provoked by the 2022 invasion.

“We see such examples in the failed attempts to isolate our country, Russia, which has faced an unprecedented sanctions pressure,” Putin said.

After meeting the Russian leader, Xi urged closer ties with Moscow, saying the nations should “leverage the mechanisms for exchanges between the two countries’ governments, legislative bodies, militaries and political parties”.

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, also in Shenzhen, said that sanctions on Russia “are going to continue to increase as long as this (Ukraine) war goes on.”

Also up for discussion in Thursday’s trilateral meeting are the Iran war and nuclear disarmament, according to Washington, after a US-Russia bilateral treaty on atomic weapons expired in February.

Beijing has long maintained that the US and Russia should reduce their giant nuclear arsenals before it agrees to talks on its smaller stockpile

title: UK-based Nigerian pastor jailed nearly 12 years for rape
description:
A Nigerian church leader based in the United Kingdom, Brein Ayeni, has been sentenced to 11 years and nine months in prison for repeatedly raping a woman and subjecting her to coercive and controlling behaviour.



West Midlands Police disclosed this in a statement on Monday, saying Ayeni, 43, was c
content:
A Nigerian church leader based in the United Kingdom, Brein Ayeni, has been sentenced to 11 years and nine months in prison for repeatedly raping a woman and subjecting her to coercive and controlling behaviour.

West Midlands Police disclosed this in a statement on Monday, saying Ayeni, 43, was convicted of three counts of rape and one count of coercive or controlling behaviour following a trial.

The offences were committed from June 2025, while Ayeni was head of Christworld Nation Church in Coventry, where he was regarded as a trusted figure in the community.

The police said he recorded some of the attacks on his mobile phone and threatened to circulate the videos if the victim reported him, claiming they would show that the encounters were consensual.

According to the statement, Ayeni also made derogatory remarks about the woman’s previous lifestyle and exhibited controlling behaviour after gaining her trust.

The victim reported the abuse to the police in March 2026, prompting an investigation by specialist officers from the force’s Rape and Serious Sexual Offences team.

Ayeni, who lived on Hurst Road, Coventry, was sentenced at Warwick Crown Court on Tuesday, November 10.

In her victim impact statement, the woman said Ayeni’s position in the church had made her trust him, adding that the abuse had severely affected her mental and emotional well-being.

“The title he held made me trust him, and that trust has been deeply damaged. The impact on my mental and emotional health is that I do not feel like the same person I was before all of this happened,” she said.

She also described how the experience had affected her ability to trust others and maintain close relationships.

“I struggle to trust people and allow them to get close to me because I am frightened of being taken advantage of again,” she said.

The victim said reporting the abuse had required considerable courage because of the fear of being judged or disbelieved.

Detective Sergeant Evie Griffiths, of the police force’s public protection unit, described the offences as horrific, noting that they had left the victim with lasting trauma.

“These were horrific crimes which have understandably had a lasting impact. It is through her bravery in telling us what happened we were able to arrest Ayeni and stop him committing any further offences,” Griffiths said.

She added that Ayeni had abused the trust placed in him to commit the offences and had been appropriately sentenced.

The police also encouraged victims of rape and other sexual offences to seek support, whether or not they were ready to make a formal report.

title: Cambridge Dictionary picks ‘human’ as 2026 Word of the Year
description:
The Cambridge Dictionary has named “human” its 2026 Word of the Year, reflecting growing concerns about artificial intelligence and renewed interest in what distinguishes people from machines.
The dictionary announced the selection on Wednesday, saying it reflected a renewed appreciation for human c
content:
The Cambridge Dictionary has named “human” its 2026 Word of the Year, reflecting growing concerns about artificial intelligence and renewed interest in what distinguishes people from machines.

The dictionary announced the selection on Wednesday, saying it reflected a renewed appreciation for human creativity, connection and authenticity in an increasingly AI-driven world.

According to the dictionary, the choice captures the changing way people understand and discuss human identity as artificial intelligence becomes increasingly influential in everyday life.

Cambridge defines “human” as having the qualities, faults and feelings that people have, as opposed to gods, animals or machines.

The dictionary’s lexicographers also observed a rise in compound expressions such as “human-made”, reflecting the growing need to distinguish work and qualities produced by people from those generated by artificial intelligence.

Cambridge Dictionary lexicographer Colin McIntosh said, “AI is changing how we talk about being human.

“Fears about what humans may lose when we outsource our thinking have made us reconsider the extent to which we rely on AI: from top mathematicians to teachers of young children.”

He added that the renewed interest in what it means to be human had influenced the selection.

Other words considered for the 2026 title included “agent”, referring to an artificial intelligence system capable of operating in complex ways without human control, and “analogue”, which relates to activities or objects that do not involve digital technology.

“Wholesome”, describing something likely to improve a person’s life physically, morally or emotionally, was also among the contenders.

Meanwhile, Cambridge identified “FOBO”, meaning the fear of becoming obsolete, as one of the expressions to watch in 2027, amid concerns that artificial intelligence could make some jobs redundant.

Another expression highlighted was “weather whiplash”, describing a rapid change from one extreme weather condition to another.

The selection comes amid a growing debate about the implications of artificial intelligence for employment, education, creativity and human relationships.

In recent years, AI-related expressions have featured prominently in dictionary word-of-the-year selections. Cambridge chose “hallucinate” in 2023, referring to the tendency of artificial intelligence systems to produce false or misleading information, while Merriam-Webster selected “slop” in 2025 to describe low-quality digital content, often generated by AI.

The Cambridge Dictionary’s 2025 Word of the Year was “parasocial”, describing the feeling of having a connection with a famous person or fictional character whom one does not personally know.

content:

title: Police tighten security ahead of Tinubu rally, Obi’s Anambra visit
description:
The Anambra State Police Command has intensified security operations across the state ahead of a campaign rally for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election and a town hall meeting by the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, Peter Obi.
The command said it had increased patrols and s
content:
The Anambra State Police Command has intensified security operations across the state ahead of a campaign rally for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election and a town hall meeting by the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, Peter Obi.

The command said it had increased patrols and strengthened personnel deployment, in collaboration with other security agencies, ahead of the two political events scheduled for Thursday and Friday.

The Anambra State Presidential Campaign Council for Tinubu’s re-election is scheduled to hold a mega rally tagged “SoluTinubu 2027” on Thursday, November 19, at Dr Alex Ekwueme Square, Awka.

Obi is also expected to hold a town hall meeting in Onitsha, the state’s commercial centre, on Friday, November 20, as part of his nationwide engagements ahead of the 2027 general election.

In a statement on Wednesday, Anambra State Police Command spokesperson, SP Tochukwu Ikenga, said the enhanced security measures were designed to prevent criminal activities, maintain public order, and protect residents, visitors and participants before, during, and after the events.

Ikenga said the command had cautioned against inflammatory publications, provocative utterances and actions capable of threatening public peace.

The statement read, “As part of these arrangements, the command has strengthened operational coordination with sister security agencies, Area Commands, Divisions and tactical units to ensure adequate security coverage of strategic locations, public facilities, major roads and identified security flashpoints.

“The measures also include enhanced surveillance, intelligence gathering and improved response capabilities to address emerging security concerns. The Commissioner of Police, CP Nnanna Ama, has directed all operational commanders and personnel to remain vigilant, proactive and professional in the discharge of their duties.

“He emphasised that security operations must be conducted with respect for human rights, while ensuring that the movement, businesses and other lawful activities of residents are not unnecessarily disrupted.

“Meanwhile, the command cautions members of the public, particularly social media users, against inflammatory publications, provocative utterances, deliberate dissemination of false information and other actions capable of inciting violence, creating unnecessary tension or threatening public peace.”

According to him, the command recognises and respects the constitutional rights of citizens to freedom of expression, peaceful assembly and lawful public engagement.

He, however, urged individuals and groups to exercise these rights responsibly and refrain from conduct that constitutes criminal incitement, threats, intimidation or other offences under the law.

“The police will take appropriate lawful measures against individuals whose actions constitute criminal offences, while ensuring that all enforcement activities are guided by due process, professionalism and respect for constitutionally guaranteed rights.

“The command further reassures Ndi Anambra, visitors and other members of the public that the command, working closely with sister security agencies, remains fully committed to providing a safe and peaceful environment throughout the period of the scheduled activities.

“Residents are therefore encouraged to remain calm, go about their lawful activities without fear, cooperate with security personnel and promptly report suspicious movements, criminal activities or emerging threats to the nearest Police Station or through established emergency communication channels.

“The command equally calls on traditional rulers, community leaders, youth organisations, civil society groups, media practitioners and other stakeholders to support ongoing security efforts by promoting responsible communication, discouraging misinformation and encouraging peaceful coexistence.

“The Anambra State Police Command remains resolute in its commitment to intelligence-led, proactive and community-centred policing, while strengthening inter-agency cooperation to sustain peace, public confidence and security across the state,” the statement added.

The two engagements come as political parties and groups intensify mobilisation ahead of the 2027 general election.

The Tinubu campaign rally is being organised by the Anambra State Presidential Campaign Council, chaired by Governor Chukwuma Soludo, and is expected to draw supporters of the APC and the All Progressives Grand Alliance.

The rally is anchored on the message of “progressives working together”.

Obi, a former governor of Anambra State who is now the NDC’s presidential candidate, is expected to use his town hall meeting to engage residents as part of his nationwide political consultations.

The meeting is scheduled for 2pm at the Archbishop C.J. Patterson Building, All Saints Cathedral, Onitsha.

Anambra is expected to attract significant political attention ahead of the 2027 presidential election, partly because Obi governed the state for eight years and remains a prominent political figure from the South-East.

The presidential election is scheduled for January 16, 2027.

title: EPL: Give me time, Manchester will turn red – Pochettino
description:
New Manchester United head coach, Mauricio Pochettino, has vowed to restore the club’s dominance in the city, insisting that Manchester will turn red under his leadership.
The Argentine made the declaration after the United States defeated Haiti 2-0 in Cincinnati on Tuesday in his final match as hea
content:
New Manchester United head coach, Mauricio Pochettino, has vowed to restore the club’s dominance in the city, insisting that Manchester will turn red under his leadership.

The Argentine made the declaration after the United States defeated Haiti 2-0 in Cincinnati on Tuesday in his final match as head coach of the American national team.

During an interview with TNT Sports on Wednesday, analyst DaMarcus Beasley, who spent the 2006-07 season on loan at Manchester City, jokingly told Pochettino that “Manchester is blue, it will always be blue.”

However, the former Chelsea and Tottenham manager quickly dismissed the suggestion, replying: “No way, you will see. Give me time and that is going to change.”

Pochettino is expected to begin his new role at Old Trafford on Wednesday after agreeing to a two-and-a-half-year contract with Manchester United.

Speaking about his new challenge, the 54-year-old admitted that the task ahead was significant but expressed confidence in his experience and ability to turn things around.

“We’re excited because the new challenge is big, but it’s the adrenaline that you want to feel,” he said.

“We are going to have a different job but we have the experience to deal with that. We need to add our common sense in the way that we are going to approach all the things.

“We know that it is not a situation that deserves to be at a club like Manchester United and for the fanbase.”

Pochettino leaves the United States national team after recording 23 wins in 37 matches, giving him a 62.16 per cent win ratio.

During his time in charge, he guided the Americans to the 2025 Gold Cup final and the last 16 of the 2026 FIFA World Cup, which the United States co-hosted.

In a farewell message shared on Instagram, Pochettino expressed pride in his achievements with the national team and thanked everyone who supported his journey.

“When we arrived, I wanted us to believe that we could compete with anyone. I hope today that belief is stronger, not only with the players but with everyone who supports this team,” he wrote.

He added that leaving the team was difficult but explained that the opportunity to manage Manchester United was one he could not turn down.

“I have always believed in following my heart, even when it means leaving a place where I have been very happy,” he said.

Pochettino now faces the challenge of rebuilding Manchester United and restoring the club’s position among England’s leading sides.

content:
Nine countries have qualified for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations following the conclusion of Matchday Four of the qualifiers played on Tuesday.

Morocco, Burkina Faso, Benin, Cameroon and Mali are among the latest teams to secure their places.

The three co-hosts, Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda, automatically qualified for the tournament, while Senegal had also secured its place ahead of the latest round of matches.

Burkina Faso’s qualification also secured a ticket for Benin, while Cameroon’s place was confirmed after Comoros defeated Congo 1-0.

Morocco maintained their perfect record in Group A with a 1-0 victory over Niger at the Prince Moulay Abdellah Stadium in Rabat.

Abdellah Ouazzane scored the decisive goal in the 22nd minute to give Morocco their fourth consecutive victory and take their tally to 12 points.

The Atlas Lions have two matches remaining, while Gabon sit second with six points. Niger and Lesotho have three points each.

In Group F, Burkina Faso defeated Mauritania 3-1 at the Olympic Stadium in Nouakchott to secure qualification alongside Benin.

Aboubaccar Camara opened the scoring for Burkina Faso in the 12th minute before Lassina Traore doubled their advantage in the 27th minute.

Mauritania reduced the deficit through Mohamed Ali Diadie in the 75th minute, but Elohim Kabore restored Burkina Faso’s two-goal advantage a minute before full-time.

The victory took Burkina Faso to 10 points, level with Benin, with both countries securing qualification for the tournament.

Mauritania, with three points, and the Central African Republic, who have no points, are out of the qualification race.

Meanwhile, Uganda played out a 1-1 draw with Botswana at the National Stadium in Gaborone.

Godfrey Tauyatswala gave Botswana the lead in the 74th minute, but Tebogo Kopelang scored an own goal in the 86th minute to earn Uganda a share of the points.

The result left Uganda, who have already qualified as co-hosts, top of Group H with six points. Libya follow with five points, while Botswana have four and Tunisia three.

In Group G, Comoros boosted their qualification hopes with a 1-0 away victory over Congo at the Stade Alphonse Massamba-Debat in Brazzaville.

Ben Chayeel Hamada scored the only goal of the encounter in the 32nd minute to take Comoros to seven points.

However, the result also confirmed Cameroon’s qualification, with the Indomitable Lions maintaining their position at the top of the group with 10 points and two matches remaining.

Namibia have three points, while Congo have two.

Mali also secured their place at the 2027 tournament after defeating Rwanda 2-0 at the Amahoro Stadium in Kigali.

Modibo Sagnan opened the scoring for the visitors in the 27th minute before Gaoussou Diarra sealed the victory two minutes before full-time.

The result took Mali’s tally in Group K to 10 points, guaranteeing their qualification.

In the other Group K fixture, Liberia defeated Cape Verde 2-0 at the Samuel Kanyon Doe Stadium in Monrovia to revive their qualification hopes.

Kpah Sherman opened the scoring two minutes after the restart before Sylvanus Nimley added the second in the 86th minute.

The victory was Liberia’s first in the qualifying campaign, leaving them level on three points with Cape Verde. Rwanda occupy second place with six points, while Mali have already secured the group’s first qualification ticket.

In group L, Nigeria drew Tanzania, while Guinea-Bissau beat Madagascar on Tuesday to lead the group by three points over runner-up Super Eagles.

With Matchday Four concluded, 15 places remain to be decided when the qualifying campaign concludes in March, 2027.

Nine countries already qualified

  1. Kenya
  2. Tanzania
  3. Uganda
  4. Morocco
  5. Benin
  6. Burkina Faso
  7. Cameroon
  8. Senegal
  9. Mali.

The post 2027 AFCON: Nine countries secure qualification appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Ekiti deputy gov mobilises monarchs, PDP members for Tinubu’s re-election
description:
The Ekiti State Deputy Governor, Mrs Monisade Afuye, has intensified mobilisation for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election, seeking the support of traditional rulers and members of different political parties across the state.
Afuye, an All Progressives Congress chieftain, appealed to monarchs and ot
content:
The Ekiti State Deputy Governor, Mrs Monisade Afuye, has intensified mobilisation for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election, seeking the support of traditional rulers and members of different political parties across the state.

Afuye, an All Progressives Congress chieftain, appealed to monarchs and other traditional leaders to support Tinubu at the ballot box on January 16, 2027, in appreciation of what she described as his administration’s infrastructural commitment to Ekiti State.

According to a statement issued by the Director of Press in the Office of the Deputy Governor, Tope Ariyo, on Wednesday in Ado Ekiti, Afuye spoke during a visit to the palace of the Ogoga of Ikere, Oba Adejimi Adu-Alagbado, who is also the Chairman of the Ekiti State Council of Traditional Rulers.

The visit involved a coalition of Peoples Democratic Party and APC members mobilising support for Tinubu’s re-election.

Afuye said the President had contributed significantly to the development of Ekiti State, citing federal appointments given to indigenes of the state and what she described as unprecedented infrastructure projects under the Tinubu administration.

She listed the projects to include the Ado-Ekiti–Ikere–Akure Road, the modern Army Brigade barracks in Ikere, the Ado-Ekiti–Iyin–Aramoko–Itawure–Osun border Road, the Ado–Ijan–Ilumoba–Ikole Road, the Ado–Ilawe–Ilumoba–Ikole Road and the Ifaki–Kabba–Ado-Ekiti Road.

She said the projects were among several federal infrastructure interventions ongoing in the state.

Afuye said, “We have come to you today to seek your support for Mr President. As our traditional leaders, you hold a special place in the heart of this government. The Tinubu administration has given unprecedented support to Ekiti State, especially our Ikere community here. We can now boast of an Army Barrack that has positively changed the face of infrastructure in this axis.

“Several roads that were death traps for years are now being reconstructed across the state. We owe Mr President a massive vote from this axis of the country. We have come to seek your blessings and support because we know you are important in the scheme of things.”

The PDP candidate in the 2026 Ekiti governorship election, Dr Wole Oluyede, who recently joined the coalition for Tinubu’s re-election, said his decision was driven by the need to advance the state’s development beyond political and ideological differences.

Oluyede urged members and supporters of different political parties to prioritise collective prosperity over personal interests, saying the welfare of the people should take precedence over political benefits.

In his response, the Ogoga of Ikere, Oba Adu-Alagbado, expressed delight at the coming together of members of the APC and PDP, particularly the deputy governor and Oluyede.

The monarch said, “Your coming together is symbolic because Ikere Ekiti is one and indivisible. I am really elated that the coming together of the political class in Ikere is happening during my time. Let us sustain this development because there is much to gain when we work as one. Our strength is in our unity.”

Adu-Alagbado commended the Tinubu administration for what he described as improved infrastructure in the community, particularly the Army barracks, which he said had contributed to the expansion of the area and increased commercial activities.

He expressed hope that more development projects would come to the community and said the President deserved the support of residents of Ikere and Ekiti State because of his administration’s infrastructure interventions.

The mobilisation comes amid efforts by political groups in Ekiti State to build a broader alliance ahead of the 2027 presidential election.

In August 2026, Oluyede announced an alliance involving the PDP, Accord, Action Democratic Party, Young Progressive Party and Action Alliance, among other groups, under the Oluyede Progressive Alliance for Renewed Hope Agenda, to support Tinubu’s re-election bid.

Although Oluyede has declared support for Tinubu, he has maintained that the decision does not amount to leaving the PDP, saying he remains a member of the opposition party.

The Independent National Electoral Commission has fixed January 16, 2027, for the presidential and National Assembly elections, while the governorship and State Houses of Assembly elections are scheduled for February 6, 2027.

description:
Russian President Vladimir Putin said Wednesday that he expected his trilateral summit with US and Chinese leaders Donald Trump and Xi Jinping to be “very useful”.



“I expect the trilateral meeting between the Russian, Chinese, and American leaders, scheduled on the sidelines of the (APEC) summit,
content:
Russian President Vladimir Putin said Wednesday that he expected his trilateral summit with US and Chinese leaders Donald Trump and Xi Jinping to be “very useful”.

“I expect the trilateral meeting between the Russian, Chinese, and American leaders, scheduled on the sidelines of the (APEC) summit, will be highly useful,” Putin said in Shenzhen, China a day before the first ever meeting between the three leaders.

“In a contemporary world full of turbulence, amidst the fragmentation of the global economy, and at a time when military-political risks are on the rise, what is desperately needed is unity rather than division, equality rather than hegemony, partnership rather than isolation, and dialogue rather than ultimatums,” Putin said.

The Russian leader also said that Western sanctions imposed on Moscow since his 2022 invasion of Ukraine had “failed” and that Russia had come through “with dignity”.

title: 2027: ADC Files 17-Ground Appeal Against INEC Over Nullification Of Atiku’s Candidacy
description: The African Democratic Congress (ADC) has asked the Court of Appeal to restrain the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) from altering its leadership records and the nomination particulars of its presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar. It also asked the court to restrain INEC from tamper
content:
The African Democratic Congress (ADC) has asked the Court of Appeal to restrain the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) from altering its leadership records and the nomination particulars of its presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar.

It also asked the court to restrain INEC from tampering with records of its governorship candidates pending the determination of its appeal against the judgment of Justice Peter Lifu of the Federal High Court, Abuja.

The development was revealed on Tuesday by the Director of Strategic Communication, ADC Campaign Council, Phrank Shaibu, as he appeared on Channels Television’s The Morning Brief.

Justice Lifu’s November 5 judgment in the suit instituted by Gombe has thrown the party’s leadership structure and its preparations for the 2027 general elections into fresh legal uncertainty.

The party said it had filed a 17-ground appeal challenging the November 5, 2026 judgment, which it described as fundamentally flawed, arguing that the trial court lacked jurisdiction to entertain the leadership dispute.

The party said it was also challenging an earlier ruling that granted Bala Gombe leave to amend his originating summons despite an unresolved objection to the court’s jurisdiction.

Shaibu said the 17 grounds of appeal questioned the jurisdiction of the Federal High Court, Gombe’s standing to institute the action, the assessment of disputed evidence and the orders made against the party.

The ADC maintained that allowing INEC to implement the November 5 judgment before the Court of Appeal determines the issues raised could undermine its appeal and expose its candidates to uncertainty.

It urged the appellate court to preserve the party’s existing leadership and candidate records until the legal dispute was resolved.

“The 17 grounds challenge the foundation, findings and orders of Justice Lifu’s judgment. The ADC has asked the Court of Appeal to examine whether the trial court had jurisdiction, whether the claimant had standing, whether disputed evidence was properly assessed, and whether the sweeping orders made against the party can stand in law,” he said.

The party is also challenging the July 24, 2026 ruling in a separate appeal, arguing that the trial court granted Gombe permission to amend his originating summons while deferring its decision on the ADC’s preliminary objection to jurisdiction.

Shaibu said that the party contended that the proposed amendment altered the description of parties and the capacity in which a defendant was sued without prior leave of court.

The appellant’s brief challenging that ruling was settled by Chief J.S. Okutepa (SAN), who leads the ADC’s legal team in the appeal.

The party is asking the Court of Appeal to set aside the amendment order and determine the outstanding objection to the trial court’s jurisdiction.

The ADC further argued that Justice Lifu proceeded to deliver judgment on a court process whose validity was already being challenged before the appellate court.

It expressed concern that INEC could act on the judgment before the appeal is determined, potentially creating a situation that would be difficult to reverse even if the appellate court eventually rules in its favour.

“INEC must not make changes that could preempt the court’s decision or put the party’s candidates in jeopardy while our applications are pending. We are asking the court to protect the subject of the appeal so that its eventual decision has practical effect,” Shaibu added.

The party said its decision to make the legal challenge public was intended to clarify the issues before the appellate court and assure its members and supporters that it would pursue the matter through lawful judicial processes.

The dispute centres on the leadership of the ADC and the legal validity of the processes through which its leadership records and related party affairs are being contested.

The ADC said it would defend the rights of its members, its leadership and the decisions taken by the party, urging that no administrative action be taken based on a contested judgment before the Court of Appeal has considered the issues raised.

The party’s applications and appeals are now before the appellate court for determination.

The latest appeal comes amid continuing litigation over the ADC’s leadership, with the party insisting that earlier court decisions recognising its leadership transition remain valid and have not been set aside.

The post 2027: ADC Files 17-Ground Appeal Against INEC Over Nullification Of Atiku’s Candidacy appeared first on Channels Television.

title: Five things to know about ‘Grand Theft Auto’
description:
The video game that launched 1,000 controversies and made billions of dollars for its studio is back — “Grand Theft Auto VI” will hit a console near you on Thursday.



It is widely expected to become the biggest game of the decade, with its launch coming 13 years after the previous edition scaled n
content:
The video game that launched 1,000 controversies and made billions of dollars for its studio is back — “Grand Theft Auto VI” will hit a console near you on Thursday.

It is widely expected to become the biggest game of the decade, with its launch coming 13 years after the previous edition scaled new heights in terms of gameplay and profitability.

Here are five things to know about GTA:

– Trailblazer –

The first two games in the series, which debuted in 1997, offered a top-down view of the action as players took on the role of a criminal on missions around cities.

But “GTA III” set the standard in 2001 for what games could be, offering a combination of a three-dimensional open world, advanced graphics and gameplay that won widespread critical acclaim and legions of fans.

Each new GTA title since then has been hailed by both industry analysts and gamers for pushing the boundaries of the medium.

– Cash cow –

And they have all been bestsellers, bringing in billions of dollars for Take-Two Interactive, parent company of the Rockstar Games studio.

Despite not releasing a flagship GTA game for more than a decade, the series has remained a cash cow, especially thanks to its multiplayer online version, where users can buy in-game items.

The last game in the franchise, “GTA V”, was released in 2013 and reached $1 billion in retail sales “faster than any entertainment release in history”, Take-Two has said.

“GTA V” has sold around 230 million copies, according to the company’s most recent figures, making it the second best-selling game of all time behind Minecraft.

The entire GTA franchise has sold a mammoth 470 million units, according to Take-Two.

– Magnet for controversy –

With the wild success came a wave of controversies. Critics have accused the series of glorifying violence and encouraging players to engage in criminal behaviour — allegations Take-Two executives have denied.

GTA games have also faced strong criticism for depictions of torture and misogynistic portrayals of women, many of whom appear as sex workers or strippers.

It has also been accused of pushing ethnic caricatures — an AFP analysis found more than three-quarters of Italian and Russian characters were involved in criminal activity, compared with 27 percent of Americans.

Despite being praised for their often biting cultural satire, the level of violence in the games has led to occasional bans and restrictions in some countries, including a chain of stores in Australia in 2014.

– A cultural institution –

GTA has become a cultural institution, spawning countless memes and attracting huge stars to its cast.

Tommy Vercetti, the main character in 2002’s “GTA: Vice City”, was voiced by Hollywood star Ray Liotta.

Other cameos in the series include Samuel L. Jackson, Burt Reynolds, musician Phil Collins and comedian Ricky Gervais. In 2021, hip-hop superstar Dr. Dre featured.

The French electro duo Justice has put together the soundtrack for “GTA VI” and an album built around the game’s universe brings together musicians including rapper Travis Scott and Rolling Stones guitarist Keith Richards.

– The next chapter –

The studio formally revealed “GTA VI” with a trailer in December 2023.

The new game is set in Leonida, a fictionalised version of Florida that includes a return to the Miami-inspired Vice City. It follows a criminal couple, Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos.

Originally targeted for late 2025, “GTA VI” was pushed back twice before settling on its November 19 release date on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X and S.

The game reportedly cost between $1 billion and $1.5 billion to produce, which would make it the most expensive cultural product ever.

The post Five things to know about ‘Grand Theft Auto’ appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Explosion Heard In North Of Saudi Capital – Report
description: A powerful explosion was heard in Riyadh on Wednesday, AFP journalists and residents reported, following weeks of attacks on Saudi Arabia by Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis.Residents told AFP there were no warnings sent to phones before the blast, which one person in the north of the capital descr
content:
A powerful explosion was heard in Riyadh on Wednesday, AFP journalists and residents reported, following weeks of attacks on Saudi Arabia by Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis.

Residents told AFP there were no warnings sent to phones before the blast, which one person in the north of the capital described as “extremely loud”.

An AFP journalist said doors throughout her home swung open and the lights briefly went out.

“Hearing a blast without receiving a warning is very frightening,” one resident in northern Riyadh said.

The location of the explosion was not immediately clear, but residents told AFP they saw smoke near Riyadh’s airport in the northeast of the city.

In recent weeks the Houthis have launched strikes on a range of Saudi targets including airports, energy infrastructure, military sites and Riyadh’s financial district.

In October, a deadly attack targeting King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh killed 14 people and injured hundreds, forcing the suspension of flights for two weeks.

Earlier on Wednesday, the Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis said it had intercepted a cruise missile launched by the group towards the Riyadh area.

The coalition, which backs neighbouring Yemen’s internationally recognised government in its war with the Houthis, has battled a surge in attacks since hostilities reignited in July.

The long-running civil war in Yemen, one of the world’s poorest countries, had been dormant after a ceasefire was implemented in 2022, but the war sprang back to life in the summer.

The Houthis are now nearing Aden, the government’s interim capital, having made sweeping territorial gains in recent weeks.

Since the summer, more than 1,600 people have been killed and over 300,000 displaced by the fighting, according to the United Nations.

AFP

title: Avon Colour Run Takes Free Diabetes and Hypertension Checks to Over 1,000 Lagosians
description: On World Diabetes Day, more than 1,000 people at Eko Atlantic City, Lagos, did something many Nigerians put off for years: they checked their numbers. At the 2026 Avon Colour Run, organised by Avon Healthcare Limited (Avon HMO) and Avon Medical Practice, participants received free checks for noncomm
content:
On World Diabetes Day, more than 1,000 people at Eko Atlantic City, Lagos, did something many Nigerians put off for years: they checked their numbers. At the 2026 Avon Colour Run, organised by Avon Healthcare Limited (Avon HMO) and Avon Medical Practice, participants received free checks for noncommunicable diseases, including diabetes and hypertension, before and after a 5-kilometre run and walk.

Diabetes and hypertension are among the conditions that often develop quietly. Many people live with them for years without symptoms, only to learn of them when complications set in. Holding the Colour Run on 14 November, the day set aside worldwide to raise awareness of diabetes, was a deliberate choice to bring that conversation to where people already were: out in the open, in motion and in good company.

The Chief Executive Officer of Avon Medical Practice, Dr Akinbiyi Oke, said the aim was to make screening feel ordinary rather than frightening.

“Most people do not avoid a health check because they do not care. They avoid it because it feels like bad news waiting to happen. When a blood sugar check sits next to a fitness session and a family picnic atmosphere, it becomes something you simply do. Knowing your numbers is the first step. What you do with them is the next, and our doctors and nurses are here to help with both.”

Participants also took part in fitness sessions with Kemen and Mayorfit, a reminder that regular physical activity is one of the most accessible tools for lowering the risk of diabetes, hypertension and heart disease.

The Chief Executive Officer of Avon HMO, Osa Imasogie, said prevention is also better for families’ finances and for the health system.

“Treating advanced chronic disease is costly for families and for the whole system. Every condition caught early is a smaller bill, a shorter hospital stay and a longer, healthier life. A health plan gives you access to care but healthy habits give you fewer reasons to need it urgently. We want to help Nigerians build both.”

As a practical takeaway, the organisers encouraged all Nigerians, whether or not they attended, to have their blood pressure and blood sugar checked at least once a year, and more often if there is a family history of diabetes or hypertension.

The Colour Run was supported by Eko Atlantic City, UBA, Transcorp Plc, Heirs Technologies, Redtech, Heirs Energies, United Capital Group, Heirs Insurance Group and Aquafina.

title: ‘Heavily Involved’ In Casting Robert Pattinson As Bond, Says Bezos
description: Amazon boss Jeff Bezos said Tuesday he was “heavily involved” in choosing British actor Robert Pattinson as the new James Bond.Amazon MGM Studios announced on Monday that Pattinson, 40, would step into the coveted role of the world’s most famous fictional spy following months of sp
content:
Amazon boss Jeff Bezos said Tuesday he was “heavily involved” in choosing British actor Robert Pattinson as the new James Bond.

Amazon MGM Studios announced on Monday that Pattinson, 40, would step into the coveted role of the world’s most famous fictional spy following months of speculation.

“There was something special about Rob Pattinson and his performances,” Bezos said at the Semafor tech conference in California.

“Initially, I would say we were slightly biased a little against him just because he’s already so famous,” he added.

“But in the screening tests, it was so obvious, ‘he is James Bond'”.

Amazon bought the storied Hollywood studio MGM in 2022, but it was not until last year that the company struck a deal with Bond producers Barbara Broccoli and Michael Wilson to obtain full creative control over the franchise.

It had been fiercely guarded by the Broccoli family since 1962’s “Dr. No”, when screen legend Sean Connery first starred as Bond, as they insisted on preserving the integrity of the character and brand.

Pattinson got his early break in “Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire” (2005) as Cedric Diggory, a champion for Hogwarts, but rocketed to global fame as Edward Cullen in romantic vampire saga “Twilight”.

AFP

title: Paz At The Double As Argentina Thrash Costa Rica
description: Rising star Nico Paz scored a superb double as Argentina bounced back from defeat with a 7-0 thrashing of Costa Rica in a friendly on Tuesday.Italy-based Como attacking midfielder Paz — who has emerged as a reported transfer target for incoming Manchester United manager Mauricio Pochettino &md
content:
Rising star Nico Paz scored a superb double as Argentina bounced back from defeat with a 7-0 thrashing of Costa Rica in a friendly on Tuesday.

Italy-based Como attacking midfielder Paz — who has emerged as a reported transfer target for incoming Manchester United manager Mauricio Pochettino — underscored his talent with two spectacular first-half goals in Cordoba.

The 22-year-old, who scored twice in Como’s 4-1 Champions League drubbing of United last month, lashed in Argentina’s opener after just eight minutes at the Mario Alberto Kempes Stadium.

After Atletico Madrid striker Julian Alvarez doubled Argentina’s lead in the 35th minute, Paz then grabbed his second with the goal of the game.

Picking up the ball in midfield, the young forward held off the attention of several Costa Rican markers before twisting and turning into space inside the penalty area and crashing a shot into the top corner to make it 3-0.

Alvarez put Argentina into a 4-0 lead in the 43rd minute, beating Costa Rica goalkeeper Patrick Sequeira at the near post with a vicious shot that flew into the roof of the net.

Paz’s virtuoso first-half performance was the highlight of a one-sided encounter as Argentina bounced back from suffering a 2-1 defeat to Uruguay in Buenos Aires on Friday.

Paz was substituted at half-time by Argentina coach Lionel Scaloni for Franco Mastantuono, the 19-year-old Fiorentina forward.

Like Paz, Mastantuono is another member of Argentina’s next generation of young talent as the former world champions rebuild following the retirement from international football of Lionel Messi.

Mastantuono was quick to make his own mark on Tuesday’s friendly, scoring just three minutes after coming on at half-time to make it 5-0.

Liverpool’s Alexis Mac Allister swept in a sixth goal in the 78th minute before Mastantuono grabbed his second of the night two minutes from time with a thumping low strike.

AFP

title: Government neglect and poverty fueling deforestation, climate heat in Nigeria, Official warns
description:
By Oladosu Adebola Oluwaseun
​Speaking on behalf of the Directorate of Agriculture and Natural Resources, Kwali Area Council, Abuja, a representative, Bala Bako, has raised the alarm over the rapid rate of deforestation in Nigeria, attributing the crisis to government negligence, poor policy impleme
content:
By Oladosu Adebola Oluwaseun

​Speaking on behalf of the Directorate of Agriculture and Natural Resources, Kwali Area Council, Abuja, a representative, Bala Bako, has raised the alarm over the rapid rate of deforestation in Nigeria, attributing the crisis to government negligence, poor policy implementation, and widespread poverty among rural farmers.

​Although noting that his colleague from the Environment Department formerly part of the Agriculture and Natural Resources Department had already addressed key issues, Bako emphasized the severe consequences of indiscriminate tree felling.

​”Deforestation is the act of cutting down trees sporadically without following professional standards,” he explained.

“Professionally, when you cut down one tree, you are supposed to replace it with five, six, or ten others to prevent desertification.”

​He noted the vital biological cycle of trees, explaining that they absorb carbon dioxide and release oxygen while providing essential shade on sunny days.

However, he lamented that human destruction is dismantling this natural balance while the government fails to enforce its own environmental laws.

​”Today, the government of this country is not serious. We are very good at making laws, but we fail to implement them,” he said.

​Bako recalled past initiatives, such as the introduction of charcoal stoves, noting that while the program was mocked by many, providing affordable alternatives is the only way to keep rural populations out of the forests. “Even if you deploy soldiers to the forests, they cannot stop deforestation in this country without viable alternatives.”

​Citing his home village in Plateau State as a stark example, he described how a forest once so dense that visitors needed a flashlight during the day has now been completely cleared.

According to him, logging has become a primary source of income, with over 20 heavy-duty trucks (locally known as 911s) hauling timber out of the community daily toward areas like Gwagwalada and Gwari in the Federal Capital Territory.

​He also criticized the government for leaving forest guards unequipped, noting that many reserved areas around Abuja have been abandoned and degraded due to a lack of political will.

​Addressing the economic reality of rural dwellers, Bako pointed out that local farmers cannot afford cooking gas and rely on firewood to survive. He accused politicians of being insensitive to the plight of the common man, noting that leaders readily brave insecure areas—even those threatened by Boko Haram to campaign for votes, only to abandon citizens once elected.
​”How do you even expect a subsistence farmer who cannot feed his family to stop cutting down trees when you have provided no substitute?” he asked. “You cannot tell people to stop an activity without providing an alternative.”

​He further linked current extreme heat waves to both deforestation and poor agricultural practices, noting that the overuse of chemical fertilizers damages the ozone layer while the loss of tree cover exposes people to direct sunlight. He highlighted recent training on RIDA (Regenerative Agriculture), which promotes organic farming methods and the planting of cover crops to conserve soil and provide natural shade.

​To reverse the trend, Bako stressed the need for strict enforcement of policies that penalize and imprison individuals caught illegally felling trees or wasting water resources. He also called on authorities to promote water harvesting by constructing ponds to collect rainwater for dry-season farming and soil conditioning, alongside the adoption of smart drip irrigation systems to prevent water evaporation.

Furthermore, he emphasized that the government must ensure adequate funding by releasing budgeted funds to support agricultural officers and educate local farmers, rather than holding empty workshops without financial backing.

​Expressing frustration over unpaid entitlements and unimplemented budgets from January to December, Bako stated that he only agreed to the interview out of personal respect for the organizers.

​”Our entitlements are not being given; you have to shout and agitate just to get what is due,” he concluded. “We have the expertise, and we are ready to work, but the government must get serious, release the necessary resources, and stop deceiving the people.”

The post Government neglect and poverty fueling deforestation, climate heat in Nigeria, Official warns appeared first on Very Nigerian.

title: EPL: Pochettino set for Man Utd unveiling after US exit
description:
New Manchester United manager, Mauricio Pochettino is set to travel to the United Kingdom after taking charge of the United States men’s national team for the final time.
Pochettino ended his spell with the US team on Tuesday night after guiding them to a 2-0 victory over Haiti in the second leg of
content:
New Manchester United manager, Mauricio Pochettino is set to travel to the United Kingdom after taking charge of the United States men’s national team for the final time.

Pochettino ended his spell with the US team on Tuesday night after guiding them to a 2-0 victory over Haiti in the second leg of their CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final.

Christian Pulisic and Julian Gressel scored in the first half to secure the victory, giving the United States an 8-0 aggregate win and a place in the semi-finals.

The match marked Pochettino’s final assignment with the American national team before taking over as Manchester United’s new head coach.

Speaking after the game, the former Tottenham Hotspur and Chelsea manager admitted that leaving the American team was an emotional decision.

“Of course, it’s tough because it’s emotional. Because I really love these guys, and I love the players. I love the staff. I love the fans and everything,” he said.

Pochettino is expected to travel directly to Manchester, with the club reportedly arranging a private jet to ensure his early arrival.

Some members of his coaching staff have already arrived in England to prepare for his new assignment.

The 54-year-old faces the task of reviving Manchester United’s fortunes after the club managed just one victory in their opening 10 Premier League matches this season.

His first major test is expected to be Sunday’s Premier League encounter against Liverpool at Anfield.

title: Morocco, Senegal Qualify For 2027 AFCON As Cape Verde Lose
description: Morocco and Senegal — who both claim to have won the last Africa Cup of Nations — were among six countries to secure places at the 2027 tournament on Tuesday.Cameroon, Benin, Burkina Faso and Mali were the other sides to qualify for the two-yearly continental showpiece from June 19-July
content:
Morocco and Senegal — who both claim to have won the last Africa Cup of Nations — were among six countries to secure places at the 2027 tournament on Tuesday.

Cameroon, Benin, Burkina Faso and Mali were the other sides to qualify for the two-yearly continental showpiece from June 19-July 17.

Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda are automatic participants as co-hosts, but compete in the six rounds of qualifying to gain competitive match practice.

Cape Verde, who drew with eventual champions Spain in the group stage at the 2026 World Cup and took Argentina to extra time, have struggled since returning to Africa.

They suffered a third loss in Group K by falling 2-0 away to lowly Liberia. The defeat in Paynesville left the Blue Sharks bottom of the mini-league.

Togo were shock 3-0 winners over 2026 World Cup qualifiers Algeria in Group I. All the goals came in the first half with Thibault Klidje from Scottish club Hibernian scoring twice.

After trouncing Niger 5-1 last week, Morocco had to settle for a 1-0 win when the teams met again. The lone Group A goal came from 17-year-old Ajax Amsterdam midfielder Abdellah Ouazane.

Senegal, who overcame Sudan on Monday, were grateful to second-placed Mozambique, whose 1-0 win in Ethiopia ensured the Teranga Lions advanced from Group J.

Senegal beat hosts Morocco 1-0 through a Pape Gueye goal in extra time to win the latest AFCON final 1-0 in Rabat this year.

But CAF later declared Morocco champions because most of the Senegalese team temporarily left the field to protest a penalty, which Morocco missed when play resumed.

Mofokeng brace

Senegal have asked the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) in Switzerland to overturn the CAF ruling and a decision is expected this month.

After beating Namibia 3-0 on Monday, Cameroon had to wait 24 hours before confirming qualification from Group G after the Comoros won 1-0 in Congo Brazzaville.

Mali made it four wins from four Group K qualifiers thanks to a 2-0 victory in Rwanda. Modibo Sagnan netted midway through the first half and Gaoussou Diallo late in the second half.

By winning 3-1 in Mauritania, Burkina Faso ensured they and Benin, who edged the Central African Republic 1-0 on Monday, would advance from Group F.

Young Belgium-based midfielder Relebohile Mofokeng scored twice in the second half as South Africa regained top spot in Group D from Guinea by beating Kenya 2-1 in Nairobi.

His second goal on 86 minutes appeared to have wrapped up maximum points, but Mohammed Bajaber halved the deficit soon after to create a tense finish.

Nigeria fell three points behind surprise Group L pacesetters Guinea-Bissau after drawing 0-0 with Tanzania in Zanzibar City.

Guinea-Bissau, who missed the last AFCON tournament after four consecutive appearances, overcame Madagascar 2-0 through goals from Mama Balde and Mauro Rodrigues.

The final two matchdays are scheduled for March 22-30 with 15 qualifying places up for grabs before east Africa hosts the marquee African football event for the first time since 1976.

title: Ex-Ajax captain abandons football for Afrobeats career
description:
Former Ajax academy captain Elikia Mbinga has abandoned his football career to pursue music, emerging as one of the Netherlands’ rising Afrobeat artists with more than 30 million Spotify streams.
The 25-year-old once dreamed of becoming a professional footballer and playing before packed stadiums, h
content:
Former Ajax academy captain Elikia Mbinga has abandoned his football career to pursue music, emerging as one of the Netherlands’ rising Afrobeat artists with more than 30 million Spotify streams.

The 25-year-old once dreamed of becoming a professional footballer and playing before packed stadiums, having shared the pitch with several players who have since established themselves in the Premier League.

During his four-year spell at Ajax’s renowned De Toekomst academy, Mbinga played alongside Jurrien and Quinten Timber, Ryan Gravenberch and Brian Brobbey.

The midfielder, who captained his academy side, recalled his former teammates as exceptionally talented but said he could not have predicted how successful they would become.

“We had a feeling that we had joined this journey together. We stepped in together. Already then, you could see that Quinten and Jurrien were like machines. They were built like machines from a young age,” he told BBC Sport on Wednesday.

Mbinga also recalled Gravenberch’s technical ability and Brobbey’s physical strength, qualities that helped them progress to professional football.

However, while his former teammates continued their careers, Mbinga struggled to break into Ajax’s first team and returned to his boyhood club, PEC Zwolle, in 2021.

He made his professional debut against Ajax in September 2021 but managed only five further first-team appearances before Zwolle were relegated.

He subsequently dropped down the Dutch football pyramid, playing semi-professionally in the fourth tier while nurturing his growing interest in music.

Although football remained a major part of his life, his desire to create music and build something of his own gradually took precedence.

“I think it was also part of the personal growth. I really liked the music. I also liked looking up to the other artists at the time who were popping,” he said.

“For me, it was also a dream to do something in music, create my own songs. But at that time, I was really talented with football, but I couldn’t make music yet.”

His decision to pursue music has since paid off, with Mbinga building a growing following in the Dutch Afrobeat scene.

He now has nearly 500,000 monthly Spotify listeners, while his 2024 single, Mentality, has surpassed 16 million streams.

The former midfielder said the creativity he developed on the football pitch continues to shape his approach to music.

“As a footballer, I played in midfield and was a very creative player. That was my style on the pitch, and I try to bring that same creativity to my music,” he said.

“I want to experiment with songs, be as creative as possible and develop a sound of my own.”

Mbinga said musical success gives him the same excitement he once experienced playing football, likening the success of a song to scoring a goal or providing an assist.

He said a major hit feels like scoring the winning goal in an important final.

“And of course, if one of my songs really takes off, then it feels like I’m scoring the winning goal in a very important game – like a final!” he said.

Though his journey has taken a different path from that of his former Ajax teammates, Mbinga has found music another platform to showcase the creativity that once made him stand out on the football pitch.

title: Singapore Invites US To Inspect Use Of Advanced AI Chips
description: Singapore is ready to facilitate US government inspections of AI chip use in the city-state, Prime Minister Lawrence Wong said, responding to concerns over alleged abuse of advanced tech in overseas data centres.In the fallout from a spy scandal at industry giant Nvidia, Washington has introduced st
content:
Singapore is ready to facilitate US government inspections of AI chip use in the city-state, Prime Minister Lawrence Wong said, responding to concerns over alleged abuse of advanced tech in overseas data centres.

In the fallout from a spy scandal at industry giant Nvidia, Washington has introduced stricter rules on exports as questions emerged over whether Singapore-based Megaspeed aided Chinese firms in accessing advanced artificial intelligence chips.

“If the US has concerns about how these chips in Singapore are being used, as we have said before, we can facilitate checks by the US government,” Wong said late Tuesday.

“We are not here to implement or enforce the export controls of other countries,” Wong said following a regional summit in the Philippines also attended by US President Donald Trump.

“We want to make sure that businesses operating in Singapore comply with the rule of law and also comply with the export controls that other countries may have imposed,” he said.

Wong said Singapore was studying the new measures announced by Washington, aimed at stopping Chinese firms from renting AI computing power from data centres in Southeast Asia and elsewhere.

Data centres anywhere in the world will now need a US licence to provide large volumes of computing power from advanced chips to companies headquartered in China or other countries under US arms embargoes.

The rule also requires licences to ship advanced chips to Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil, which the US Commerce Department says present a “higher-than-normal risk of diversion”.

Wong acknowledged that chips were being transhipped through Singapore, but warned firms against violating laws.

“If there are businesses that want to make use of Singapore to circumvent these controls, or if there were businesses that were to infringe or to break Singapore laws, then obviously we will take clear and firm action,” the CNA news agency quoted him as saying.

AFP

title: Benue South 2027: Idoma diaspora organises debate for Abba Moro, Ottah, Agbese, others
description: The Idoma people in the diaspora, under the umbrella of the Idoma in Diaspora Leadership Association, with members and representatives across the United Kingdom, United States, Canada, Russia, Germany and other countries, have announced plans to organise a virtual debate involving candidates contest
content:
The Idoma people in the diaspora, under the umbrella of the Idoma in Diaspora Leadership Association, with members and representatives across the United Kingdom, United States, Canada, Russia, Germany and other countries, have announced plans to organise a virtual debate involving candidates contesting for the Senate and House of Representatives seats in Benue South ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The initiative is aimed at providing constituents, both in Nigeria and abroad, with an opportunity to hear directly from the candidates, assess their aspirations and make informed choices ahead of the elections.

According to a notice issued by the association, the engagement will be held on two separate days, with candidates contesting for the Senate scheduled to participate on Saturday, November 21, 2026, while House of Representatives candidates will have their session on Sunday, November 22, 2026.

Both sessions are scheduled to commence at 9:00 p.m. West Africa Time, WAT, via Zoom.
The association provided a common Zoom meeting ID, 249 497 5445, and passcode, 1000, for interested participants.

Explaining the importance of the initiative, the association said the virtual engagement would enable Idoma people to listen to the candidates, understand their aspirations and make informed decisions about who should represent them in the National Assembly.

The initiative is anchored on the themes of Idoma unity, informed choice and a stronger Idoma nation, with particular emphasis on effective representation in the Red and Green Chambers of the National Assembly.

The association urged eligible voters and other interested Idoma people to participate in the sessions, engage with the candidates and assess their visions for the development of Benue South.
Among those jostling for the Benue South senatorial seat are incumbent Senator Abba Moro of the Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, Francis Ottah Agbo of the All Progressives Congress, APC, David Olofu of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, Dan Onjeh of the Nigerian Democratic Congress, NDC, Samuel Onuh of the Labour Party, LP, among others.
For the House of Representatives seats, those in the race include Philip Agbese of the Labour Party, Aida of the Peoples Democratic Party, Onuh Blessing of the All Progressives Congress and Lilian Adoyi of the Peoples Democratic Party, Ojotu Ojema of the APC, and others.

The initiative is expected to provide a platform for greater political participation and accountability as political activities gather momentum ahead of the 2027 general elections.
