title: US Democrats Take Step Towards First Black House Speaker
description: Hakeem Jeffries is set to move closer Wednesday to becoming the first Black speaker of the US House of Representatives as Democrats prepare to choose their leader following a landslide midterm election victory.The 56-year-old New Yorker faces no declared challenger in a closed-door party election, b
content:
Hakeem Jeffries is set to move closer Wednesday to becoming the first Black speaker of the US House of Representatives as Democrats prepare to choose their leader following a landslide midterm election victory.

The 56-year-old New Yorker faces no declared challenger in a closed-door party election, but opposition from some newly elected progressives has exposed divisions over how Democrats should use their newfound power.

Jeffries is poised to preside over a commanding Democratic majority during the final two years of President Donald Trump’s term, with his party seeking to reverse the Republican president’s policies and hold his administration to account.

He said Tuesday he would request a recorded vote on his nomination, departing from the wishes of some allies who had hoped he would be chosen “by acclamation” — without a formal ballot.

Jeffries told reporters at the Capitol on the eve of the ballot that every Democrat should have the opportunity to weigh his experience, record and vision, citing the precedent set when the party last won control of the House in 2018.

Wednesday’s vote will select the party’s nominee for speaker, but Jeffries must still win a formal election of the full House when the new Congress convenes on January 3.

Both returning Democrats and incoming lawmakers can participate in Wednesday’s nomination, including progressives who have sought concessions from Jeffries on issues ranging from US military support for Israel to the influence of money in politics.

Some have threatened to withhold their votes, although the dissent has not produced a rival candidate.

Jeffries and his allies have been working to consolidate support, meeting with newly elected lawmakers and reassuring different factions that their voices will be heard.

The Democratic leader has also sought to shift attention to the party’s plans for governing after voters handed Republicans a crushing defeat amid anger over the Iran war and soaring fuel costs.

“Folks are drowning in this Republican economy, and House Democrats are committed to turning that situation around, beginning on day one,” he told reporters Tuesday.

“We’re going to relentlessly fight for an affordable America.”

Brooklyn Roots

Raised in Brooklyn’s Crown Heights neighborhood, Jeffries trained as a lawyer before entering the New York state legislature in 2007 and winning election to Congress in 2012.

Known for his measured manner, sharp rhetoric and penchant for quoting hip-hop artists, he became the first Black politician to lead a party in either chamber of Congress when Democrats chose him to succeed Nancy Pelosi in 2022.

He also served as a House prosecutor during Trump’s first impeachment trial in 2020.

His expected elevation would represent a landmark in American politics, putting him in charge of one of Washington’s most powerful institutions and second in line to the presidency behind the vice president.

But Jeffries would inherit a formidable task in managing a Democratic coalition spanning centrists and an increasingly assertive left flank.

His party has promised investigations into Trump and his administration, while lawmakers remain divided over Israel, healthcare and how aggressively to pursue their agenda against a president who retains veto power.

The relatively straightforward House leadership election contrasts with a more competitive contest among Senate Democrats, where veteran leader Chuck Schumer faces a challenge from progressive Maryland Senator Chris Van Hollen.

Van Hollen has attracted support from prominent left-wing figures, including Bernie Sanders, but acknowledges he is the underdog. Senate Democrats will elect their leader in early December.

Republicans chose their own congressional leaders last week, elevating Trump ally Jim Jordan in the House and retaining John Thune in the Senate.

AFP

title: Experts urge investors to fund pipeline infrastructure
description:
From Adanna Nnamani and Francis Onyedikachukwu, Abuja

The Pipelines Professionals Association of Nigeria (PLAN) has urged local and international investors to increase funding for the development and sustainability of Nigeria’s pipeline infrastructure, warning that the country’s energy security and
content:
From Adanna Nnamani and Francis Onyedikachukwu, Abuja

The Pipelines Professionals Association of Nigeria (PLAN) has urged local and international investors to increase funding for the development and sustainability of Nigeria’s pipeline infrastructure, warning that the country’s energy security and industrial growth depend largely on reliable pipeline networks.

The President of PLAN, Engr. Ngozi Adeleke, made the call at the Nigeria International Pipeline Technology and Security Conference (NIPITECS 2026), which opened in Abuja on Tuesday.

Adeleke said significant investment, innovative financing solutions, advanced technology, strong regulatory support and effective security frameworks were required to develop and sustain critical pipeline infrastructure.

She said pipelines remained the backbone of the energy value chain, connecting producing fields to processing facilities, power plants, industrial hubs, export terminals and consumers.

According to her, without reliable pipeline networks, Nigeria’s ambitions to achieve energy security, economic diversification and industrial development would be difficult to realise.

She noted that the conference, with the theme, “Financing the Future: Unlocking Capital for Resilient Pipeline Infrastructure in Nigeria,” was particularly relevant as the country seeks to increase hydrocarbon production, deepen domestic gas utilisation, expand energy access and strengthen industrial capacity.

The PLAN president said the two-day conference would provide an opportunity for industry stakeholders to examine ways of attracting investments into new and existing pipeline infrastructure, while exploring how technology could improve asset integrity and security.

She also called for stronger collaboration among operators, financiers, regulators, service providers, technology companies, academia and host communities to address challenges confronting the sector.

Adeleke stressed that NIPITECS should go beyond discussions to facilitate partnerships, stimulate innovation, encourage knowledge sharing and generate practical recommendations for strengthening Nigeria’s pipeline ecosystem.

“As an association, PLAN remains committed to promoting professionalism, operational excellence, safety, integrity and capacity development across the pipeline industry.

“We will continue to serve as a platform for engagement, learning and collaboration, while advocating policies and practices that support the growth and sustainability of the sector,” she said.

She further urged participants to use the conference to build meaningful relationships and develop partnerships capable of driving progress in the industry beyond the event.

According to her, Nigeria’s energy future would not be determined by its natural resources alone but by the collective ability of stakeholders to finance, build, protect and sustain the infrastructure needed to convert those resources into economic value.

She added that collaboration, shared innovation and collective responsibility were essential to unlocking investment and securing the country’s energy future.

The conference brings together industry leaders, government representatives, regulators, investors, technology companies and other stakeholders to discuss financing, technology and security challenges in Nigeria’s pipeline sector.

title: England eyes Nations League finals hosting rights
description:
England is considering a bid to host the UEFA Nations League finals in June as the Football Association (FA) explores the possibility of staging the competition’s final four matches.
The FA has registered its interest with UEFA, joining Spain and France, which have also expressed interest in hosting
content:
England is considering a bid to host the UEFA Nations League finals in June as the Football Association (FA) explores the possibility of staging the competition’s final four matches.

The FA has registered its interest with UEFA, joining Spain and France, which have also expressed interest in hosting the tournament.

The Nations League finals, scheduled to take place between June 9 and 13, will feature the semi-finals, final and third-place play-off, with all four matches hosted by one country.

According to BBC Sport on Tuesday, the FA is still discussing potential venues, with uncertainty over whether Wembley Stadium would be available for the competition.

The only publicly announced events at Wembley in June are two concerts by singer Sam Fender, although they are scheduled for after the Nations League finals.

Since the competition was introduced in 2019, England have never hosted the final stages. Previous hosts include Portugal, Italy, the Netherlands and Germany.

Generally, only countries that qualify for the Nations League semi-finals are considered eligible to host the final stages.

England’s interest comes after Thomas Tuchel’s side secured top spot in their group with an impressive 3-2 victory over Spain in Madrid.

The result means England will be seeded in Friday’s quarter-final draw, ahead of their next round of matches scheduled for March.

Tuchel’s team could face Belgium, the Netherlands, Denmark or Norway in the quarter-finals, with victory potentially taking them closer to a place in the June finals.

If the FA’s hosting bid is successful, it would provide England with an opportunity to stage a major international football tournament ahead of Euro 2028.

The European Championship will be jointly hosted by England, Scotland, Wales and the Republic of Ireland, giving the countries an opportunity to prepare for the tournament through international football events.

London had earlier shared photographs of herself at the Presidential Villa,
content:
American political strategist and media personality Diana London has deleted posts on her X account relating to her engagement with the Nigerian government and the security partnership between Nigeria and the United States.

London had earlier shared photographs of herself at the Presidential Villa, Abuja, where she was seen alongside President Bola Tinubu and his Chief of Staff, Femi Gbajabiamila.

Cameras were also visible in some of the photographs.

In another post, the American strategist described the security partnership between Nigeria and the United States as one that was “delivering results”.

“The U.S.-Nigeria security partnership is delivering results. Peace through strength. None of this happens without the ongoing partnership between President Trump and President Tinubu, their steadfast commitment to eliminating terrorists, and Nigeria’s willingness to work closely with the U.S. government,” she wrote.

She also suggested that the collaboration could unlock more economic and trade opportunities between the two countries.

“Because of the success of their partnership and relationship, the economic and trade opportunities are endless. The best is yet to come. Nigeria is the United States’ greatest ally in Africa,” London stated.

In a separate post, London expressed appreciation for the opportunity to work with individuals representing Nigeria, particularly on efforts to protect religious groups and strengthen relations between the Trump administration and the Nigerian government.

“It has been an honour to work on the team of people representing Nigeria and helping to protect religious groups and further the relationship between the Trump administration and the Nigerian government,” she wrote.

However, the posts had been deleted from her X account as of Wednesday morning, when our correspondent checked.

The circumstances surrounding their removal were not immediately clear, and London had yet to publicly explain why she deleted the posts.

title: Covenant University retains Africa’s top spot in interdisciplinary science ranking
description:
Nigeria has recorded its highest representation in the Times Higher Education Interdisciplinary Science Rankings, with 27 universities featuring in the 2027 edition, representing a 50 per cent increase from the 18 institutions ranked in the previous edition.
The Chairman of the Nigerian Tertiary Edu
content:
Nigeria has recorded its highest representation in the Times Higher Education Interdisciplinary Science Rankings, with 27 universities featuring in the 2027 edition, representing a 50 per cent increase from the 18 institutions ranked in the previous edition.

The Chairman of the Nigerian Tertiary Education Ranking Advisory Committee, Prof Emeritus Peter Okebukola, disclosed this in a statement issued on Wednesday, noting that Nigeria also improved its global position from 16th to 11th based on the number of universities ranked.

The 2027 ranking, released on November 18, assessed 1,058 universities across 102 countries and territories, with Nigeria retaining its second position in Africa behind Egypt, which recorded 37 ranked institutions.

Covenant University, Ota, Ogun State, retained its position as Africa’s leading university for interdisciplinary science, placing joint 49th globally, ahead of Egypt’s Cairo University, which came joint 52nd.

Covenant University was ranked 73rd globally in the 2025 edition before rising to joint 49th in 2026, maintaining its position in the global top 50 for the second consecutive year.

Landmark University, Omu-Aran, emerged as Nigeria’s second-best institution in the ranking, placing in the 251–300 band.

Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria, and the University of Ilorin followed in the 351–400 band, while the University of Calabar, the University of Lagos and the University of Nigeria, Nsukka, occupied the 401–500 band.

Ladoke Akintola University of Technology, Obafemi Awolowo University and the University of Benin completed Nigeria’s top 10, placing in the 501–600 band.

Okebukola said the latest performance reflected growing participation by Nigerian universities in international assessments but warned that increased representation had not translated into stronger overall performance across the ranking bands.

“We have good reason to be encouraged. More Nigerian universities are stepping forward to be measured against the best in the world, and one of our own has kept the first position in Africa,” he said.

He, however, noted that the number of Nigerian universities in the global top 300 declined from five in the previous edition to two, while those in the top 500 fell from eight to seven.

“The results also carry a lesson. As the field has grown from 749 universities in 2025 to 1,058 this year, competition has become keener and several of our established participants have slipped.

“Our task is to match wider participation with stronger performance,” he added.

The NiTERAC chairman identified inadequate funding for interdisciplinary research and weak institutional support structures as major factors affecting the performance of Nigerian universities.

He explained that many institutions recorded low scores in the inputs and process categories, which measure funding for interdisciplinary science, dedicated research facilities, administrative support and institutional policies that encourage collaboration across academic disciplines.

“These are matters within the reach of every university management. Full reporting of research grants and income from industry, and clear institutional policies on interdisciplinary research, can lift a university by one or two bands within a single edition, as this year’s results have shown,” he said.

Ahmadu Bello University and the University of Calabar recorded notable improvements, moving from the 601–800 band in 2026 to the 351–400 and 401–500 bands, respectively.

Eight universities made their debut in the ranking. They are the Federal University of Technology, Minna; Michael Okpara University of Agriculture, Umudike; Joseph Sarwuan Tarka University, Makurdi; the University of Jos; Rivers State University; Babcock University; Bells University of Technology; and Nile University of Nigeria.

Osun State University also returned to the ranking after a year’s absence.

Of the 27 Nigerian universities ranked, 14 are federally owned, seven are state-owned and six are privately owned. Seven other Nigerian institutions participated but were given Reporter status after submitting data.

The interdisciplinary science ranking, produced by Times Higher Education in association with Schmidt Science Fellows, measures universities’ capacity to support and deliver research that cuts across traditional academic disciplines.

It uses 11 performance indicators grouped into three broad areas: inputs, accounting for 19 per cent; processes, 16 per cent; and research outputs, 65 per cent.

The Massachusetts Institute of Technology, United States, retained the global first position for the third consecutive year.

Okebukola commended the Minister of Education, Dr Tunji Alausa, for prioritising the global competitiveness of Nigerian tertiary institutions and establishing NiTERAC to coordinate efforts towards improving their performance.

He disclosed that the committee had submitted a comprehensive report on the latest ranking, including recommendations, to the minister.

He added that NiTERAC, working with the League of Directors of Academic Planning and the Virtual Institute for Capacity Building in Higher Education, would support universities in preparing stronger submissions for the 2028 edition.

The committee also disclosed that the 2026 national ranking of universities, polytechnics and colleges of education was nearing completion, with the results scheduled for unveiling at a national conference on December 15, 2026.

Okebukola said the exercise was expected to strengthen data collection and healthy competition among institutions, adding that its impact could reflect in future international rankings.

The post Covenant University retains Africa’s top spot in interdisciplinary science ranking appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Meet Kunle Areogun, Taiwo Odukoya’s preferred successor
description:
Pastor Kunle Areogun, a senior pastor at The Fountain of Life Church and a maritime executive, has emerged at the centre of the church’s leadership crisis following the release of a video in which its late founder, Pastor Taiwo Odukoya, named him as his preferred successor.
The video, reportedly rec
content:
Pastor Kunle Areogun, a senior pastor at The Fountain of Life Church and a maritime executive, has emerged at the centre of the church’s leadership crisis following the release of a video in which its late founder, Pastor Taiwo Odukoya, named him as his preferred successor.

The video, reportedly recorded in December 2021 and released by the church’s trustees on Tuesday, has renewed attention on the succession controversy surrounding the church, particularly the disputed removal of Odukoya’s son, Pastor Jimmy Odukoya, as senior pastor.

In the recording, the late founder stated his preference for Areogun to take over the spiritual leadership of the church.

“Please, the next pastor of the church should be Kunle Areogun,” Odukoya said.

He, however, assigned Jimmy the positions of administrative assistant and head of the youth church in the proposed leadership arrangement.

The disclosure has added another dimension to the disagreement between factions within the church over who has the authority to determine its leadership and whether the succession arrangement outlined by its founder should supersede the decisions taken after his death.

The recording was reportedly made by Jimmy at his father’s request and witnessed by his elder brother, Pastor John Odukoya.

Explaining why he made the video, the late founder said the succession provision was among the aspects of the church’s constitution being reviewed at the time.

Things to know about Areogun

1. He is a longstanding pastor at The Fountain of Life Church

According to Church Gist, Areogun has been associated with The Fountain of Life Church for several years and was listed among its pastors in the memorial booklet published for the late Pastor Nomthi Odukoya in November 2021.

The church’s sermon archive also documents his preaching engagements dating back to at least July 2017.

Among his recorded sermons are God of the Unusual (2017), See the Invisible, Experience the Incredible (2018), Jesus, Our Image (2022), The Word of God and the Supernatural (2023) and The Unlimited God (2023).

His relationship with the late founder was also acknowledged by Odukoya’s daughter, Tolu Odukoya-Ijogun, during a Truth Table interview transcribed by Church Times Nigeria in October 2025.

“Uncle Areogun was quite close to my dad. His wisdom was top-notch,” she said.

2. He is a chemical engineer

Beyond his pastoral responsibilities, Areogun has a professional background in engineering.

Corporate publications identify him as a chemical engineer, while Excel Exploration and Production’s official website lists him as one of its directors.

3. He is an oil and gas executive

Areogun has built a career in Nigeria’s maritime and oil and gas industries.

He has served as managing director of Bourbon Interoil Nigeria Limited, an oil and gas and maritime services company.

A July 2009 report by maritime publication Riviera identified him as the company’s deputy managing director.

By December 2012, a Worldfolio report identified him as managing director and quoted him discussing the company’s operations and expansion into aluminium vessel construction.

Bourbon Interoil also identified him as its managing director in a corporate statement marking the International Day for Women in Maritime in May 2024.

4. He worked with Taiwo Odukoya outside the church

Areogun’s association with the late founder was not limited to religious activities.

An Afren regulatory announcement dated July 18, 2007, listed both Areogun and Taiwo Odukoya among the board and management team of Excel Exploration and Production.

The connection suggests that their relationship extended into the business sector before the current succession controversy.

5. He celebrated his 60th birthday in August 2024

A congratulatory advertisement published by Petromarine in THISDAY on August 15, 2024, celebrated his 60th birthday.

The advertisement identified him as Engineer Adekunle A. Areogun, managing director of Bourbon Interoil Nigeria Limited.

It described him as a leader in the marine, oil and gas industry and praised his professional achievements.

6. Odukoya named him as his preferred successor

Areogun’s name became a subject of national attention after the emergence of a video reportedly recorded in December 2021.

In the footage, Taiwo Odukoya explained that he was making the recording to clarify his wishes should he die or become unable to communicate.

“Please, the next pastor of the church should be Kunle Areogun,” the late founder said.

He also assigned his son, Pastor Jimmy Odukoya, the roles of administrative assistant to the incoming pastor and head of the youth church.

Odukoya explained that the arrangement was connected to an aspect of the church’s constitution that was undergoing review but had not been concluded.

7. His emergence has intensified the Fountain of Life leadership crisis

Following Taiwo Odukoya’s death in August 2023, Jimmy was appointed senior pastor of the church in September of the same year, while his sister, Tolu Odukoya-Ijogun, became associate senior pastor.

However, the emergence of the succession video prompted a fresh dispute over the circumstances surrounding Jimmy’s appointment.

The Board of Trustees subsequently withdrew recognition of Jimmy as senior pastor, citing the late founder’s recorded instructions and other concerns, including controversy surrounding his recent remarriage.

Jimmy rejected the decision, describing it as unconstitutional and insisting that he remained the duly appointed senior pastor and chairman of the Board of Trustees.

The trustees, meanwhile, appointed Pastor Rotimi Okpaise as interim spiritual and administrative leader pending further consultations.

8. He has not formally taken over as senior pastor

Although the recording identifies Areogun as Taiwo Odukoya’s preferred successor, he has not been formally installed or announced as the substantive senior pastor of The Fountain of Life Church.

The trustees have instead appointed Okpaise as interim leader while the dispute over the church’s leadership and constitutional arrangements continues.

His possible emergence as the church’s next substantive leader will therefore depend on how the competing positions over the founder’s wishes, the church’s constitution and the authority of its governing board are resolved.

The post Meet Kunle Areogun, Taiwo Odukoya’s preferred successor appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Orelope-Adefulire did not send Daniel Ojukwu to prison, the law did — Analyst
description: A public affairs commentator has pushed back against narratives framing the detention of journalist Daniel Ojukwu as an executive crackdown on the media, asserting that his remand was strictly the result of standard judicial procedure rather than the personal actions of Princess Adejoke Orelope-Adef
content:
A public affairs commentator has pushed back against narratives framing the detention of journalist Daniel Ojukwu as an executive crackdown on the media, asserting that his remand was strictly the result of standard judicial procedure rather than the personal actions of Princess Adejoke Orelope-Adefulire, the Senior Special Assistant to the President on Sustainable Development Goals (OSSAP-SDGs).

In an opinion piece published on Wednesday, analyst Odi Ehisuan argued that public commentary surrounding Ojukwu’s incarceration has largely misrepresented the facts of the case. According to Ehisuan, Orelope-Adefulire neither ordered the reporter’s arrest nor dictated his detention. Instead, the decision rested entirely with Justice Joyce Abdulmalik of the Federal High Court in Abuja, who ordered Ojukwu remanded pending the determination of his bail application.

The court is currently presiding over a 12-count charge against the journalist bordering on cyberstalking and criminal defamation. Ehisuan noted that the judge’s remand order followed standard courtroom rules, as Ojukwu’s legal team submitted their bail request behind schedule despite having been served the charges well in advance.

Defending the presidential aide’s conduct, the analyst emphasized that Orelope-Adefulire acted within her constitutional rights as a Nigerian citizen seeking to protect her reputation. Rather than resorting to intimidation or extrajudicial measures, she filed a formal complaint with the Nigeria Police Force, submitting her grievances to legal scrutiny.

“A person with something to hide runs from judicial scrutiny. She walked straight into it,” Ehisuan wrote, questioning whether critics would prefer a public official who bypasses the legal system over one who relies on it.

The legal dispute stems from a 2023 investigative series authored by Ojukwu and published by the Foundation for Investigative Journalism (FIJ), which alleged that OSSAP-SDGs disbursed ₦147.1 million to a restaurant for the construction of classrooms in Lagos.

Ehisuan pointed out that official documentation presented by the SDGs office contradicts the report’s central claim. Records from the Corporate Affairs Commission (CAC) indicate that the contracted firm is a properly incorporated business with valid tax clearance and proven expertise in construction and engineering, rather than a roadside eatery.

Furthermore, the office maintained that both the classrooms and a Skills Acquisition Centre in Lagos were fully constructed, commissioned, and put into active use, backed by photographic evidence and GPS coordinates. A relocation of the project from its initial site in Ajeromi was also documented as a routine adjustment caused by space limitations, which was resolved after a facilitating lawmaker provided an alternative site.

Highlighting core journalism ethics—specifically accuracy, fairness, and the right of reply—the commentator criticized the handling of the report prior to publication. According to accounts from the SDGs office, Ojukwu failed to properly verify procurement documents and declined an open invitation to inspect the completed Lagos project sites firsthand even after publishing the allegations.

While acknowledging the vital role of the media under Section 22 of the 1999 Constitution in holding government accountable, Ehisuan stressed that press freedom does not grant immunity from the law. He argued that treating every legal challenge against a reporter as an attack on democracy would strip ordinary citizens and diligent public servants of any legal recourse against defamation.

Concluding his remarks, the analyst urged Ojukwu, FIJ, and their supporters to present their evidence before the court rather than relying on public outrage to delegitimize an ongoing judicial proceeding.

The post Orelope-Adefulire did not send Daniel Ojukwu to prison, the law did — Analyst appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: US proposes 90-day recruitment rule for foreign worker sponsors
description:
The United States is proposing tougher requirements for employers seeking to sponsor foreign workers for permanent residency, including a mandatory 90-day recruitment period that gives qualified American workers hiring priority.
The proposal, introduced by the US Department of Labour, seeks to overh
content:
The United States is proposing tougher requirements for employers seeking to sponsor foreign workers for permanent residency, including a mandatory 90-day recruitment period that gives qualified American workers hiring priority.

The proposal, introduced by the US Department of Labour, seeks to overhaul the Permanent Labor Certification programme, commonly known as PERM, which is a key requirement for many employer-sponsored green card applications.

According to the proposed rule published in the Federal Register for public inspection and seen by PUNCH Online on Wednesday, employers would have to recruit qualified US workers for at least 90 calendar days before submitting permanent labour certification applications.

The proposed changes represent the first comprehensive update to the PERM programme in nearly two decades.

“Under the proposed requirements, employers seeking to sponsor foreign nationals for permanent employment would have to demonstrate that they made sufficient efforts to find qualified American workers before proceeding with foreign worker sponsorship.

“The Department of Labor plans to modernise recruitment requirements by allowing employers to use platforms that reflect current hiring practices. These include company websites, online job boards, social media platforms, job fairs and campus recruitment programmes.

“Employers would also be required to document their recruitment activities and demonstrate that they properly considered qualified American applicants,” the Federal Register stated.

The proposal further prohibits employers from tailoring job requirements to match the qualifications of a particular foreign candidate.

Additionally, businesses that routinely advertised the same or similar positions for more than 90 days during the preceding 12 months would be required to apply the longer recruitment period.

This means the proposed 90-day requirement would serve as a minimum rather than a fixed recruitment period for all employers.

The PERM programme is designed to establish whether qualified and available US workers can fill positions employers intend to offer to foreign nationals.

Labour certification is a key stage in many employment-based green card applications, particularly those under the EB-2 and EB-3 categories.

The proposed overhaul would also introduce tougher restrictions on employers that have recently laid off American workers.

Under the changes, certain employers that laid off US workers within the preceding two years would be barred from seeking permanent labour certification for the same or similar positions.

Employers would also be required to continue considering qualified American workers affected by layoffs throughout the labour certification and immigrant petition processes.

This would extend the obligation beyond the initial recruitment exercise and require employers to consider eligible workers who previously lost their jobs.

The Department of Labor also plans to remove recruitment exemptions currently available to certain occupations.

These include professional nurses, physical therapists and individuals with exceptional ability in the sciences or arts.

If adopted, employers sponsoring foreign workers in these occupations would have to comply with the standard recruitment requirements and demonstrate that qualified American workers are unavailable.

The proposed changes are intended to strengthen protections for domestic workers and ensure that employers give qualified US applicants appropriate consideration before recruiting foreign nationals for permanent positions.

The Department of Labor has proposed a 60-day public comment period beginning from the publication of the proposal in the Federal Register.

During this period, employers, immigration stakeholders and other interested parties would be able to submit comments on the proposed requirements.

The department would consider the submissions before deciding whether to proceed with the rulemaking process.

The proposed requirements are not yet final and would not take effect until the applicable regulatory process has been completed.

The latest proposal follows other US efforts to review employment-based immigration requirements and the obligations of employers hiring foreign nationals.

In March 2026, the Department of Labor was reviewing a separate proposal that could increase prevailing wage requirements for employers hiring foreign workers.

The proposed wage changes could affect H-1B workers and other foreign employees, including positions covered by the PERM programme.

Prevailing wage requirements determine the minimum compensation employers must offer for certain foreign worker positions.

Meanwhile, in December 2025, the United States announced plans to replace the traditional random H-1B visa lottery with a weighted selection system that favours higher-paid positions.

While the H-1B changes concern temporary employment visas, the latest PERM proposal focuses on recruitment requirements for employers seeking to sponsor foreign nationals for permanent employment and green cards.

The post US proposes 90-day recruitment rule for foreign worker sponsors appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Gulf Nations Attacked After US Strikes Iranian Island
description: Bahrain and Kuwait said Wednesday that they had repelled air attacks launched against them following US strikes on an Iranian island, as Gulf nations face retaliatory bombardment in the Middle East war.The conflict — which began with US-Israeli strikes on Iran in late February — has spil
content:
Bahrain and Kuwait said Wednesday that they had repelled air attacks launched against them following US strikes on an Iranian island, as Gulf nations face retaliatory bombardment in the Middle East war.

The conflict — which began with US-Israeli strikes on Iran in late February — has spilled over to Gulf states that host US military facilities.

The Iranian army said Wednesday its drones “targeted Patriot air defence systems and drone and missile launch platforms belonging to the terrorist US military at Ali Al-Salem Air Base in Kuwait,” in a statement carried by state television IRIB.

Kuwait’s military said Wednesday its air defences were “responding to hostile drone threats”, urging its public to follow security and safety advice.

While Bahrain said its air defences intercepted attacks from Iran early Wednesday, a day after Tehran’s Revolutionary Guards said they attacked a base used by Washington.

The United States and Iran are in a standoff over the vital Strait of Hormuz, with the US military working to escort ships transiting the waterway in defiance of Tehran’s attempts to close the waterway.

Iran’s official IRNA news agency cited a regional official as saying the United States had hit Qeshm Island in the Hormuz Strait without causing serious damage.

US fighter jets “used precision munitions to strike an Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) missile launch site on Qeshm Island”, an American official told AFP on condition of anonymity, adding that the strike was in response to Iranian “aggression targeting US personnel and assets”.

Meanwhile, the Saudi-led coalition fighting Yemen’s Houthis said on Wednesday it had intercepted a cruise missile launched by the Iran-backed group toward the Riyadh area.

Alleged Iran Plot

Explosions boomed across Bahrain’s capital on Tuesday as a mobile phone alert warned residents to seek safety.

Bahrain’s armed forces said they “confronted, intercepted and destroyed a number of treacherous Iranian aerial attacks today… before they could achieve their objectives”, while Iran’s Revolutionary Guards said they targeted a US-operated radar system.

“Combat drones belonging to the Revolutionary Guards carried out a precision operation this morning, targeting a radar system operated by US forces at the Sheikh Isa Air Base in Bahrain,” the Guards’ Sepah news website said.

The attack was in response to the “repeated violations of Iranian airspace by US military drones”, it added. The Guards also said they had intercepted and captured a US drone south of Qeshm.

Bahrain, which hosts the US Navy’s Fifth Fleet, was heavily targeted earlier in the war that started with US-Israeli strikes on Iran, but had not been hit for weeks until Iranian drone attacks on Friday and Sunday.

Despite Washington and Tehran holding back from a full resumption of hostilities, the sides have traded fire and accusations.

US President Donald Trump said on Tuesday he was taking “very seriously” reports that Iran was developing plans to use a so-called “dirty bomb” in Washington.

CNN cited seven anonymous US officials as saying Iran was plotting how to target senior administration figures with a bomb laced with chemical or radioactive material, though they stopped short of saying Iran planned to carry out such an attack.

“If there is (such a threat), they will pay a price the likes of which no other country has ever paid before,” Trump said, adding: “I hope it’s not, but we take it very seriously because they happen to be crazy.”

Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi dismissed the report and called it “Iraq War-style propaganda”.

‘Fear And Anxiety’

“I was on my way to work when the warning sirens went on,” Abdulrahman Abdullah, a Bahraini civil servant in his forties, told AFP on Tuesday.

“Fear and anxiety rise as attacks increase… We hope things will go back to how they were.”

The violence came as the United States moved the USS Theodore Roosevelt into the region, bringing the number of American carrier strike groups in the region to three.

The deployment adds to an already large US naval presence, which includes two other supercarriers — the George H W Bush and the George Washington — and more than a dozen destroyers.

Iranian drone attacks have resumed ahead of this week’s unprecedented trilateral summit between Trump and his Chinese and Russian counterparts.

Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin will discuss “world peace” at the talks in Shenzhen, according to China. Trump has said he plans to discuss the Iran war at the meeting.

AFP

The post Gulf Nations Attacked After US Strikes Iranian Island appeared first on Channels Television.

title: Last-Gasp Haaland Shoots Norway Into Nations League Quarters
description: Erling Haaland fired Norway into the Nations League quarter-finals on Tuesday with a last-gasp penalty which completed a stunning comeback from two goals down to win 3-2.Manchester City striker Haaland stroked home from the spot in the sixth minute of injury time in Copenhagen as Norway leapfrogged
content:
Erling Haaland fired Norway into the Nations League quarter-finals on Tuesday with a last-gasp penalty which completed a stunning comeback from two goals down to win 3-2.

Manchester City striker Haaland stroked home from the spot in the sixth minute of injury time in Copenhagen as Norway leapfrogged their hosts into second place in Group A, on head-to-head record as both teams finished on nine points.

Both teams ended the group stage six points behind winners Portugal, who got their first win of the post-Cristiano Ronaldo era with a 3-2 success against Wales.

The winner was one of two goals from Haaland, who also started the fightback in the 37th minute — and had a goal disallowed — after early strikes from Rasmus Hojlund and Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg gave Denmark a commanding lead in front of passionate support.

Haaland was given the chance to nick a spot in the last eight from the Danes, who only needed a draw to go through, after a handball from Joachim Andersen which was spotted by the VAR officials just as the hosts thought they had survived another in a series of scares.

Denmark had been on the back foot ever since Haaland halved the deficit when a howler from Denmark goalkeeper Mads Hermansen gifted possession to Martin Odegaard.

It was Odegaard who forced home Norway’s leveller with six minutes remaining and set up a grandstand finish which was completed with Haaland’s dramatic winner.

“This has been one of the craziest years in football I’ve ever experienced,” said a relieved Haaland to TV2 in Norway.

Norway will join Portugal in Friday’s draw in Nyon, where the four group winners will be seeded and each play against one of the four second-placed teams.

Portugal bounce back

Haaland’s winner made Portugal’s win over Wales irrelevant to their group placing, but Carlos Forbs’ classy strike in the 70th minute in Cardiff made sure of a positive finish for Jorge Jesus’ team.

Forbs’ first international goal decided a hugely entertaining encounter in which Wales, already guaranteed to finish bottom of the group, put in a performance which belied their position.

Wales will take part in the play-offs to decide the final promotion and relegation spots between Leagues A and B, and on Tuesday’s evidence they have a fighting chance of staying in the top tier.

David Brooks quickly replied to Bruno Fernandes’ superb opener for Portugal and Wales had their tails up when Sorba Thomas slid the hosts in front in the 40th minute.

But Pedro Neto, who was later sent off, almost immediately levelled the scores and Forbs decided an even contest and ensured Portugal would bounce back from a humiliating defeat at the hands of Denmark at the weekend.

“It’s a special feeling; I won’t forget today. The most important thing is that we managed to win,” said Forbs.

“We needed the goal to calm the game down, and it just so happened that I scored.”

Northern Ireland were promoted to League A for the first time after Justin Devenny’s thumping strike gave his team the draw they needed against Hungary in Budapest.

Devenny, who plays for Stoke City in England’s second tier, lashed home a beautiful strike in the 65th minute at the Ferenc Puskas Arena to level the match at 1-1 and secure a second successive promotion for Michael O’Neill’s team.

“I feel amazing. I’m due one, that was my second for Northern Ireland. To see the game out, we dug deep and we’ve deserved it. We’ve had a great campaign and we can’t wait for more,” said Devenny to the BBC.

Republic of Ireland will join Wales in the play-offs after closing out Group B3 with a 3-0 win over 10-man Kosovo and moving into second place.

The post Last-Gasp Haaland Shoots Norway Into Nations League Quarters appeared first on Channels Television.

title: Army intercepts ammunition supplier, recovers 300 bullets in Kogi
description:
Troops of the Nigerian Army have arrested a suspected ammunition supplier and recovered 300 rounds of 7.62 x 39mm ammunition concealed in a sack of beans in Kogi State.
The operation took place at about 9:30 pm on Tuesday, 17 November 2026.
Acting on credible intelligence, soldiers of the Atsawa Blo
content:
Troops of the Nigerian Army have arrested a suspected ammunition supplier and recovered 300 rounds of 7.62 x 39mm ammunition concealed in a sack of beans in Kogi State.

The operation took place at about 9:30 pm on Tuesday, 17 November 2026.

Acting on credible intelligence, soldiers of the Atsawa Blocking Force, working with local vigilantes, intercepted 47-year-old Umaru Muhammad, a resident of Ashe Village.

A thorough search revealed the ammunition carefully hidden inside the sack of beans.

Security operatives also recovered a Bajaj motorcycle, a mobile phone and the sum of ₦30,500 from the suspect.

Preliminary interrogation indicated that the ammunition was allegedly meant for two individuals identified as Gimba and Dare, said to
residents of Gori Village along the River Niger corridor in Lokoja Local Government Area.

The two were ldescribed as local vigilantes. The claims remain under investigation.

Umaru Muhammad is currently in military custody as investigators work to uncover the full extent of the suspected supply network and identify other persons who may be linked to the illicit transaction.

In a statement issued on Wednesday, the Acting Director of Army Public Relations, Colonel Appolonia Anele, said “the successful interception forms part of the Army’s sustained efforts to disrupt the logistics and ammunition supply chains that support banditry and other criminal activities.”

The army urged members of the public to remain vigilant and promptly report any suspicious movement of concealed arms, ammunition or other prohibited items to the nearest security agency.

title: Academic Activities Paralysed As MAPOLY Lecturers Embark On Indefinite  Strike
description: Academic activities at the Ogun State-owned Moshood Abiola Polytechnic (MAPOLY), Abeokuta, have been paralysed following an indefinite industrial action by members of the Academic Staff Union of Polytechnics and other unions.The lecturers say the action has become imperative over unsettled welfare p
content:
Academic activities at the Ogun State-owned Moshood Abiola Polytechnic (MAPOLY), Abeokuta, have been paralysed following an indefinite industrial action by members of the Academic Staff Union of Polytechnics and other unions.

The lecturers say the action has become imperative over unsettled welfare packages.

According to the Chairman of the Union, Adeleke Amos-Adebayo, the demands include payment of Earned Academic Allowances, review of the monthly subvention to tertiary institutions, and implementation of the Consolidated Academic Staff Allowance, among others.

The chairman of the Mishood Abiola Polytechnic Academic Staff Union say the indefinite industrial action has become imperative in view of notices given to the state government informing them about the need to FasTrack actions on the implementation of the issues raised, “the first letter was released in August, August 5th, 5th of August, which I took to the Governor personally, by myself.”

“September 21st, another reminder was sent to the State Governor for the implementation of this CONTISS and so on.”

“The last National Executive Council Meeting we had in Abuja, that was October 22nd. The NEC reached the conclusion that there should be an ultimatum to all the State Governors to implement with immediate effect,” he said

“So the following week, which happened to be October 26th, the letter came from our national body again, to all State Governors. So we took it down, and the ultimatum took effect from October 27th, which lasted till November 3rd. That is a 15-day ultimatum, that failure to implement or accede to the union’s demand, the chapters, meaning the State Polytechnics, are being given the mandate, or the directive, or permission to embark on industrial action, to push further their demands from the State Government”

” And November 11th, that happened to be the last day, that was last week Tuesday, so it was communicated, and the mandate, the directive was given. In Ogun State, all the chapters in Ogun State met, with the approval from the Zone and the National, and we commenced the strike Wednesday, 11th, November 2026. And up till now, we are still on strike.”

The indefinite industrial action followed the expiration of a 15-day ultimatum issued by members of the Academic Staff Union of Polytechnics.

“And I want to believe, maybe Mr. Governor has not been carried along, that he didn’t have to be… because we know him to be a listening… to have listening ears to people in the state, as the father. So I don’t mind using this medium, if permitted, to call his attention to what is happening in those tertiary institutions, so that he can come intervene, find a way to resolve this matter.

“We don’t, as union leaders, we don’t expect this industrial action to take long, because we have our children here, we have relatives here, and this is our own Jerusalem that we will not want anything to happen to it. So the Governor is the person we are now looking forward to to intervene, come in, attend to all these demands, by providing the necessary”

As monitored at the Moshood Abiola Polytechnic, Abeokuta, academic activities are grounded, classrooms deserted, as lecturers stay away from classes over welfare issues.

The situation has left many students of the institution in a state of uncertainty as to when the industrial action will come to an end.

Tope Adeleke, one of the students of the institution, laments the disadvantages of the ongoing strike on students’ academic pursuits.

“There will be a small delay in a lot of activities. We have a lot of activities, classes. There will be a lot of delays.

“And the second is, students are now being demotivated, since we actually resumed very early this time, that the school is now getting back on track, and you know, getting to this point where new students are now in, is going to be a very big struggle at the moment.”

” And my appeal is, what they know they can do for us, to actually help, this strike just being called off. We don’t understand the economic challenges of the country, and also every situation that the country is facing as at now, but what they can do to provide a solution, to get us, so that we students can actually be on track to continue our studies, and also continue to do what we know is best for us in the institution,”

On his experience in the last couple of days when the industrial action commenced

“The experience has not been good. The experience among students, I think, I will feel like it’s a big shock, because I think since last year that the school has been running, from the new Rector, there have been no strikes, you know, everything was running perfectly. So it was a shock, because we knew it was the Ogun State ASUP that actually made the order. So, I will say, it was a bit of a surprise, and students didn’t believe that it would actually take a bit longer to this stage. You know, it’s making us believe that, are we still going to have classes this year again? But we do hope that it gets resolved as soon as possible.”

Others, whose fate seems to be hanging in the balance, have appealed to the authorities and the lecturers to reach an amicable resolution to the impasse and call off the strike.

“We are making a passionate appeal to all concerned that they should consider the plight of the students and come to negotiation, resolve the impasse and let us have a smooth academic session”

And while this is ongoing, the lecturers say they are not averse to returning to classes as soon as their demands are met by the management of the institution and the State Government.

Efforts to get the reaction of the school management on the development proved abortive, as the Rector of the institution, Dr. Babatunde Jolaoso, was said to be unavailable for interview.

The post Academic Activities Paralysed As MAPOLY Lecturers Embark On Indefinite Strike appeared first on Channels Television.

title: Mining probe: NSCDC delegation stranded as lawmakers shun hearing
description:
A delegation of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps on Tuesday arrived at the National Assembly to honour a summons by the House of Representatives Committee on Solid Minerals but met a locked hearing room, with the lawmakers absent.
The development came days after the committee, chaired by
content:
A delegation of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps on Tuesday arrived at the National Assembly to honour a summons by the House of Representatives Committee on Solid Minerals but met a locked hearing room, with the lawmakers absent.

The development came days after the committee, chaired by Gaza Gbefwi, gave the NSCDC Commandant-General, Ahmed Audi, a 24-hour ultimatum to appear before it over allegations of misconduct, financial impropriety and human rights abuses involving the Mining Marshals.

The committee is investigating the activities, funding and operations of the Mining Marshals, including allegations of extortion, unlawful arrests, arbitrary detention and human rights violations.

It is also seeking explanations over an alleged transaction involving more than N2bn linked to the bank account of a former state commander and the reported killing of a serving NSCDC officer, Agada Agada, allegedly by fellow officers at a mining site.

The committee said its investigation was being conducted in exercise of its oversight powers under Sections 88 and 89 of the 1999 Constitution, as amended.

The Mining Marshals were inaugurated in March 2024, with more than 2,200 personnel deployed to tackle illegal mining, protect the country’s mineral resources and improve security at mining sites.

Several petitions were also presented to the committee by mining operators and other individuals.

One of the petitioners, Rachel Ogbonna, director of communications at Stone Rockers Nigeria Limited, alleged that NSCDC operatives subjected the company’s workers to arbitrary arrests, prolonged detention and harassment.

She also alleged that the company’s quarry site was sealed despite its possession of valid mining licences and other operational documents.

Another petitioner, Odey Polycarp, a security operative, accused the personnel of unlawfully arresting and detaining members of his workforce after picking them up in a residential area where no mining activities were taking place.

He further alleged that the workers were repeatedly assaulted in custody.

The committee also examined the circumstances surrounding Agada’s death, with Gbefwi reportedly expressing condolences to his family and calling for the protection of his widow, two children and other witnesses.

Other areas of concern included vehicle procurement, budgetary allocations, special intervention funds, publicity expenditure and other sources of funding for the Mining Marshals.

The NSCDC delegation, led by Assistant Commandant-General Emmanuel Fadeyi, who represented Audi, arrived at the designated hearing room at about 3pm but found it locked.

The officials subsequently proceeded to the office of Abdul Malik Danga, whom they were informed had been delegated by Gbefwi to receive the delegation.

However, the proposed meeting became contentious when Danga reportedly requested to meet Fadeyi alone, asking other members of the delegation, including the Mining Marshals commander, to wait outside.

Fadeyi initially questioned the arrangement, arguing that the delegation had been summoned for an official hearing and should be allowed to participate collectively.

The meeting eventually held between the two officials alone and lasted about 30 minutes.

Efforts by journalists to obtain details of the discussion and the reasons for the committee members’ absence were unsuccessful, as Danga reportedly declined to speak with the press.

Speaking after the meeting, Fadeyi said the delegation had honoured the summons despite the situation.

“We are here at the National Assembly to honour the summons of the House, but we met the venue locked. Given the urgency and threatening nature of the public summons, which did not carry the tone of an official engagement but appeared adversarial, we nevertheless came because we are an institution that respects the law and its provisions,” he said.

He said the Corps had nothing to conceal and remained committed to discharging its statutory responsibilities.

“We have nothing to hide other than ensuring that we uphold our mandate,” he added.

Meanwhile, the Commander of the Mining Marshals, Attah John Onoja, dismissed the allegations against the unit, describing them as false and claiming that they were being sponsored by defendants facing trial over illegal mining activities.

Onoja also accused some lawyers whose clients had failed to secure the reopening of mining sites sealed over alleged illegal operations of being behind the allegations.

He described the allegation involving the purported N2bn transaction as “weaponised blackmail”.

The commander said the unit had approached Zenith Bank and obtained the complete statement of account of Jibrin Labaran, who was allegedly linked to the transaction, before submitting it to the House committee.

He expressed surprise that the committee was still pursuing the allegation despite what he said was the submission of the bank statement.

Onoja also questioned the committee’s demand for the health histories and other personal information of Mining Marshals personnel, arguing that the disclosure of such sensitive details could compromise their security and expose them to danger.

He further faulted the committee for entertaining complaints relating to cases already before courts of competent jurisdiction.

The commander alleged that the investigation had been politicised to undermine the Federal Government’s efforts to sanitise the mining sector through the Ministry of Solid Minerals Development.

The post Mining probe: NSCDC delegation stranded as lawmakers shun hearing appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Ex-Ajax academy captain dumps football for music
description:
Former Ajax academy captain Elikia Mbinga has traded his football dreams for a career in music, emerging as one of the Netherlands’ rising Afrobeat artists with more than 30 million Spotify streams.
The 25-year-old once dreamed of becoming a professional footballer and playing in front of packed sta
content:
Former Ajax academy captain Elikia Mbinga has traded his football dreams for a career in music, emerging as one of the Netherlands’ rising Afrobeat artists with more than 30 million Spotify streams.

The 25-year-old once dreamed of becoming a professional footballer and playing in front of packed stadiums after sharing the pitch with several players who have gone on to establish themselves in the Premier League.

During his four-year spell at Ajax’s renowned De Toekomst academy, Mbinga played alongside the likes of Jurrien and Quinten Timber, Ryan Gravenberch and Brian Brobbey.

The midfielder, who captained his academy side, remembers his former teammates as exceptionally talented players but admits their subsequent success was not something he could have predicted.

“We had a feeling that we had joined this journey together. We stepped in together. Already then, you could see that Quinten and Jurrien were like machines. They were built like machines from a young age,” he told BBC Sport on Wednesday.

Mbinga also recalled Gravenberch’s technical ability and Brobbey’s physical strength, qualities that helped them progress to professional football.

However, while his former teammates continued their footballing journeys, Mbinga struggled to secure a breakthrough at Ajax and returned to his boyhood club, PEC Zwolle, in 2021.

He made his professional debut against Ajax in September 2021 but managed just five further first-team appearances before Zwolle’s relegation.

He subsequently dropped down the Dutch football pyramid, playing semi-professionally in the fourth tier while developing his interest in music.

Although football remained a significant part of his life, his desire to create music and establish something of his own gradually became stronger.

“I think it was also part of the personal growth. I really liked the music. I also liked looking up to the other artists at the time who were popping,” he said.

“For me, it was also a dream to do something in music, create my own songs. But at that time, I was really talented with football, but I couldn’t make music yet.”

The decision to pursue music has since paid off, with Mbinga building an impressive following in the Dutch Afrobeat scene.

He now boasts almost 500,000 monthly Spotify listeners, while his 2024 single, Mentality, has surpassed 16 million streams.

Interestingly, the former midfielder says the creativity he developed on the football pitch continues to influence his approach to music.

“As a footballer, I played in midfield and was a very creative player. That was my style on the pitch, and I try to bring that same creativity to my music,” he explained.

“I want to experiment with songs, be as creative as possible and develop a sound of my own.”

For Mbinga, musical success provides the same excitement he once experienced while playing football.

He compares the success of a song to scoring a goal or providing an assist, while a major hit feels like scoring the winning goal in an important final.

“And of course, if one of my songs really takes off, then it feels like I’m scoring the winning goal in a very important game – like a final!” he said.

Although his journey has taken a different direction from that of his former Ajax teammates, Mbinga has found another platform to showcase the creativity that once made him stand out on the football pitch.

The post Ex-Ajax academy captain dumps football for music appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Alleged Land Grabbing: Uni Abuja Protest Enters Day 3
description: The protest over alleged land grabbing against the FCT Minister, Nyesom Wike, by the University of Abuja entered its third day on Wednesday.Our correspondents who monitored the procession reported that students, staff and other workers of the University are completely shut out, as members of the joi
content:
The protest over alleged land grabbing against the FCT Minister, Nyesom Wike, by the University of Abuja entered its third day on Wednesday.

Our correspondents who monitored the procession reported that students, staff and other workers of the University are completely shut out, as members of the joint action committee of Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU), Senior Staff Association of Nigerian Universities (SSANU), National Association of Academic Technologists (NAAT), Non-Academic Staff Union of Educational and Associated Institutions (NASU), and National Association of Nigerian Students (NANS) continue the protest.

They called on President Bola Tinubu to prevail on the FCT Minister to hands off the land allocated to the school.

The protesting lecturers, staff and students had blocked the entrance into the university’s main campus since Monday, and vowed to continue their protest until the FCT minister is called to order.

The protest expanded today, with students and staff members seen loitering around the entrance of the school.

The protesting Uniabuja workers also blocked the Giri/Abuja expressway for a moment before filing out to their premises.

As of the time of filing this report, some students of the University have now blocked the two expressways leading in and out of Abuja, from the Ido axis of the airport road, a reaction to the protest at the main campus, which has shut students and some workers out of the school premises.

title: FG inaugurates 4 CNG stations to ease transportation in universities
description:
The Federal Government has commissioned Compressed Natural Gas stations in four universities to ease transportation burden of students, staff and other members of the host communities.
The instutions include University of Uyo, Akwa Ibom state, University of Calabar, Cross River state , University of
content:
The Federal Government has commissioned Compressed Natural Gas stations in four universities to ease transportation burden of students, staff and other members of the host communities.

The instutions include University of Uyo, Akwa Ibom state, University of Calabar, Cross River state , University of Nigeria, Enugu campus and Federal University of Petroleum Resources, Efurun in Delta state respectively.

‎Speaking during the commissioning ceremony at the University of Uyo , Minister of State, Petroleum Resources (Gas), Hon Ekperikpe Ekpo, said the initiative was a source of special pride to him as a project in his home state.
‎
‎Ekpo who commissioned other 3 CNG stations virtually , said the stations will give students, staff and surrounding communities access to cleaner and more economical mobility, while offering the institutions opportunity to build research, technical skills and local expertise in CNG technologies.
‎
‎“The benefits of adopting CNG for mobility are practical and immediate. CNG is generally cheaper than petrol and diesel, so vehicle owners, commercial drivers and transport operators spend less on fuel
‎
‎“For students, young people who earn a living from commercial transport, and vulnerable members of society who depend on public transport, these savings mean lower transport costs and more money kept in their pockets for education, enterprise, food and other household needs.”
‎
‎He commended president Bola Tinubu, whose Renewed Hope Agenda has placed natural gas at the heart of Nigeria’s economic renewal.
‎
‎“Under his watch, gas is no longer a resource we merely flare or export; it is a resource we are using to power our vehicles, create jobs and put money back in the pockets of our people,” he said.
‎
‎He said the President also approved the Special Palliative Relief on University Transportation Programme, in line with the 20 Universities CNG Ecosystem Initiative, to cushion the effect of petroleum subsidy reform on students and staff.
‎
‎He also commended the governors of Akwa Ibom, Cross River, Enugu and Delta states for deepening the penetration of natural gas in their states, and acknowledged the Minister of Education for supporting initiatives that connect educational institutions with national energy priorities.
‎
‎He appreciated the vice-chancellors and councils of the four universities, as well as host states and communities, for providing the enabling environment for the projects
‎
‎The Executive Director of Midstream and Downstream Gas Infrastructure Fund, Oluwole Adama, said the four newly commissioned Compressed Natural Gas stations in Uyo, Calabar, Enugu and Warri can fill about 540 vehicles every day.
‎
‎He said the figures are not just technical, but mean cheaper rides for students, lower costs for transport operators and a living classroom for young engineers.
‎
‎“For students, affordable and dependable transport means more than a cheaper ride. It can mean getting to lectures on time, spending less on daily travel and having more time and energy for learning,” he said.
‎
‎He added that more facilities will be executed, stressing that the facilities can also become living classrooms, offering young Nigerians practical exposure to gas operations, engineering, safety and maintenance.
‎
‎”About 50 more projects will be nearing commissioning by the end of this year. I urge transport operators and businesses to use the facilities judiciously. Our young Nigerians should embrace this opportunities in technical services, safety and maintenance”, he stated.
‎
‎On his part, the Chief Executive Officer of FEMADEC Energy Limited; Fola Akinnola, said the four newly commissioned Compressed Natural Gas daughter stations in universities will drastically cut daily fuel expenditure and bring clean, affordable fuel directly into the heart of tertiary institutions.
‎
‎Akinnola said establishing the daughter station within the University of Uyo alongside the three sister campuses going live across the South-South and South-East, was directly addressing the commuting challenges faced by students, lecturers, campus shuttle operators and surrounding host communities.
‎
‎He described the commissioning of four strategic university stations in a single day as a milestone made possible through deliberate, and high-impact collaboration.
‎
‎”On behalf of the board and management of FEMADEC Energy Limited, he thanked the Midstream and Downstream Gas Infrastructure Fund and the Presidential Initiative on Compressed Natural Gas and Electric Vehicles for their vision, catalytic funding and commitment to President Bola Tinubu’s Decade of Gas and clean mobility agenda”, Akinnola said.
‎
‎

title: ‘Don’t allow political ambition to tear Nigeria apart’ — Jonathan warns politicians ahead of 2027 poll
description:
Former President Goodluck Jonathan has cautioned political leaders against allowing their ambitions for power to undermine Nigeria’s unity, warning that political intolerance, ethnic rivalry and electoral violence could plunge the country into crisis ahead of the 2027 general elections.
Jonathan exp
content:
Former President Goodluck Jonathan has cautioned political leaders against allowing their ambitions for power to undermine Nigeria’s unity, warning that political intolerance, ethnic rivalry and electoral violence could plunge the country into crisis ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Jonathan expressed concern over the increasing use of political thugs and the recruitment of young people as instruments of violence, insisting that political competition must not threaten national cohesion and peaceful coexistence.

He spoke at the third edition of the Peace and Security Conference organised by the Goodluck Jonathan Foundation in Abuja. The conference was themed, “Safeguarding Peace and Strengthening Social Cohesion in a Competitive Political Environment.”

The former President urged political actors to place national unity above personal and political ambitions.

“We must never allow political ambition to undermine the bonds that hold us together as one nation and in our states,” he said.

Jonathan also expressed concern over controversies surrounding judicial pronouncements, particularly conflicting judgments delivered by courts of coordinate jurisdiction.

He warned that such developments could weaken public confidence in the judiciary and encourage citizens to resort to self-help.

“When citizens begin to lose faith in the courts and resort to self-help, the consequences can be disastrous. The descent from a loss of confidence in institutions to anarchy is a danger we must collectively prevent,” he said.

He called on political leaders to respect opposing views and acknowledge the right of others to seek political office.

Jonathan also urged Nigerians to prioritise competence, national interest and public service over prejudice and personal ambition when choosing their leaders.

In his remarks, the Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Professor Joash Amupitan, warned that political parties, candidates and their supporters would face legal consequences for engaging in violence, intimidation and inflammatory campaigns ahead of the elections.

Amupitan, who was represented by National Commissioner May Agbamuche-Mbu, acknowledged that political competition naturally involved vigorous debates, disagreements and passionate mobilisation but insisted that these must not degenerate into violence or lawlessness.

He specifically warned against harassment, intimidation and physical attacks on INEC officials and ad hoc election workers, saying offenders would be dealt with under the law.

“I must sound a stern warning against any form of harassment, intimidation, or physical attack directed at the leadership, staff, or ad hoc workers of INEC by supporters of any political party—whether within Nigeria or abroad.

“Election officials are public servants discharging a sacred constitutional duty; assaulting or threatening them is an assault on the Nigerian state and will be met with decisive legal consequences,” he said.

The INEC chairman also identified misinformation, disinformation, artificial intelligence-generated content, deepfake videos and cloned voices as emerging threats to peaceful elections.

He warned that fabricated information could trigger unrest within minutes and disclosed that the commission had established a dedicated Artificial Intelligence Division within its Information and Communication Technology department to monitor digital threats and verify online information.

Amupitan reaffirmed INEC’s commitment to institutional neutrality and the conduct of peaceful, credible and inclusive elections.

According to the commission’s timetable cited at the conference, the presidential and National Assembly elections are scheduled for January 16, 2027, while governorship and state assembly elections are expected to hold on February 6, 2027.

Also speaking, former President of the ECOWAS Commission, Dr Omar Alieu Touray, warned against the use of ethnic, religious and regional identities to divide Africans during political contests.

In his keynote address, Touray argued that democracy should be based on competing ideas and development programmes rather than divisions arising from people’s backgrounds.

“Competition is the lifeblood of democracy. It is the mechanism through which citizens express preferences, debate ideas and hold leaders accountable. We must never confuse political competition with political conflict,” he said.

He distinguished between opposing a candidate’s policies and denying the person the right to govern because of their ethnic, religious or regional identity.

“There is a profound difference between saying, ‘I disagree with your policies,’ and saying, ‘Because you belong to a different ethnic, religious or regional community, you do not have the right to govern me.’ The first is democracy. The second is exclusion masquerading as democracy,” Touray added.

In a goodwill message, the Minister of Defence, retired General Christopher Musa, urged political leaders to demonstrate restraint, maturity and statesmanship ahead of the elections.

Musa, who was represented by his Special Adviser on Strategic Communication, Mercy Ndi Bala, warned against hate speech, misinformation and inflammatory narratives capable of exploiting Nigeria’s ethnic, religious and political differences.

He stressed that national security extended beyond military deployment and equipment, noting that public trust, social cohesion and cooperation between communities and security agencies were equally important to maintaining stability.

The minister called for a whole-of-government and whole-of-society approach to security, involving government institutions, traditional and religious leaders, civil society organisations, the media and young people.

Earlier, the Executive Director of the Goodluck Jonathan Foundation, Ms Ann Iyonu, raised concerns over declining public confidence in Nigeria’s electoral process.

She cited a 2026 Afrobarometer survey released on November 11, which, according to her, showed that fewer than four in 10 Nigerians believed the 2027 general elections would be free and fair.

Iyonu warned that the credibility of the elections would have implications beyond Nigeria, given the country’s economic influence and strategic importance to regional security.

The post ‘Don’t allow political ambition to tear Nigeria apart’ — Jonathan warns politicians ahead of 2027 poll appeared first on Very Nigerian.
