title: Senate urges INEC to disqualify candidates linked to electoral violence
description: The Nigerian Senate has called on the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to disqualify candidates whose supporters are found to have instigated or participated in electoral violence, provided there is an established court conviction and the relevant provisions of the 2026 Electoral Act
content:
The Nigerian Senate has called on the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to disqualify candidates whose supporters are found to have instigated or participated in electoral violence, provided there is an established court conviction and the relevant provisions of the 2026 Electoral Act are satisfied.

The lawmakers also condemned the growing cases of political violence across the country, warning that attacks on political leaders, supporters and campaign gatherings could threaten national security, democratic participation and the peaceful conduct of the 2027 general elections.

The resolutions followed a motion sponsored by Senator Abdul Ningi, representing Bauchi Central, on the urgent need to address rising political violence, intolerance and attacks on political figures and their supporters.

During deliberations on the motion on Tuesday, the Senate urged governors to stop denying opposition parties access to public facilities, including stadiums, hotels and other venues under their control, for political activities.

It also called on security agencies to conduct impartial and transparent investigations into reported incidents of political violence in the Federal Capital Territory, Edo, Delta and Sokoto states, identify those responsible and prosecute them where evidence supports such action.

The lawmakers further urged the Federal Government to direct the Inspector-General of Police and other security agencies to strengthen security arrangements for political leaders, candidates, supporters and campaign gatherings nationwide.

They also called for effective early-warning and rapid-response mechanisms to prevent violence ahead of the 2027 elections.

Speaking during the debate, Senate President Godswill Akpabio said INEC should enforce the provisions of the 2026 Electoral Act against candidates and supporters linked to electoral violence.

“Any candidate or supporter caught instigating violence, then INEC has a right to disqualify,” Akpabio said.

He urged the electoral commission to ensure that the law was implemented without discrimination against any political party.

Akpabio also referred to Sections 121 to 128 of the Act, which he said outlined electoral offences and penalties, including intimidation and the snatching of Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) machines, ballot boxes and other electoral materials.

According to him, the legislation provides prison terms ranging from 12 months to five years, without an option of a fine for aggravated offences involving acts such as stoning, physical attacks and the use of dangerous weapons.

He also cited Section 92, which he said empowers INEC to suspend elections in areas affected by violence and reschedule them within 24 hours.

The Senate President further referred to the Electoral Offences Commission Bill 2025, which he said was passed alongside the Electoral Act to establish a dedicated mechanism for addressing offences such as vote-buying, electoral violence and attacks on election officials.

Akpabio said the responsibility for implementing the provisions now rested with the executive arm of government.

In his presentation, Ningi expressed concern over a series of reported attacks involving political figures and campaign supporters.

He cited the November 13 incident involving President Bola Tinubu’s convoy shortly after the President observed Jumu’ah prayers at the Shehu Shagari Central Mosque in Garki, Abuja. The convoy was reportedly attacked with stones and other objects, leaving vehicles damaged and security personnel injured.

The senator also recalled reported attacks on Peter Obi and other political stakeholders during a political gathering in Benue State, as well as the disruption of a procession involving Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) supporters and the Obidient Movement in Asaba, Delta State, on November 7.

The Asaba incident reportedly resulted in one death and five injuries.

Ningi also mentioned the reported attack on the convoy of former Vice-President and African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, in Sokoto State.

He warned that the incidents reflected a troubling pattern of political intolerance, intimidation and violence capable of undermining public confidence in the electoral process and discouraging citizens from exercising their democratic rights.

Senator Binos Yaroe, representing Adamawa South, proposed an additional resolution urging state governors to guarantee equal access to public facilities for all political parties and candidates.

He argued that restricting opposition parties from using public venues could undermine the principle of a level playing field and trigger unnecessary political conflicts.

Senator Sampson Ekong, representing Akwa Ibom South, also urged the Ministry of Information and the National Orientation Agency (NOA) to intensify public enlightenment campaigns against political violence.

Ekong said legal provisions alone would not adequately address the problem without sustained public education. He urged the agencies to discourage the recruitment and manipulation of young people for violent political activities.

Contributing to the debate, Senator Ali Ndume, representing Borno South, condemned the attack on Tinubu’s convoy, describing it as an embarrassment to the country.

He said political disagreements and public anger should be expressed through lawful means, rather than violence.

Ndume also commended the President for directing the release of those arrested over the incident, describing the decision as an act of statesmanship.

He proposed that security agencies should prohibit the carrying of dangerous objects, including knives and sticks, at campaign venues.

The lawmaker also recommended the establishment of mobile courts to handle cases involving people arrested for carrying weapons or engaging in violence during political campaigns.

According to him, such courts should operate across party lines, with offenders prosecuted and convicted where sufficient evidence exists.

Ndume further expressed concern over political slogans such as “Tinubu Must Go”, “Atiku Must Go” and “Obi Must Go”, describing them as potentially militant and calling for restraint in political campaigns.

Senator Sumaila Kawu, representing Kano South, supported Ndume’s recommendations, particularly the proposal for special courts to prosecute people found carrying dangerous weapons during campaign activities.

However, he challenged lawmakers to examine their own conduct and the behaviour of their supporters, questioning why some political candidates were surrounded by supporters carrying dangerous objects despite existing laws against electoral violence.

He said lawmakers must take responsibility for ensuring that political activities complied with the laws they had enacted.

The Senate also mandated its Committees on National Security and Intelligence, Police Affairs, and INEC to engage relevant institutions and report back within one week on measures to prevent political violence and protect the 2027 electoral process.

The post Senate urges INEC to disqualify candidates linked to electoral violence appeared first on Very Nigerian.

title: Two Clocks, One Election
description: The government wants economic improvement to reach voters. The opposition wants negotiations to produce cooperation. Both are running against time.
content:
The government wants economic improvement to reach voters. The opposition wants negotiations to produce cooperation. Both are running against time.

Two clocks are ticking towards Nigeria’s presidential election.

One measures how quickly economic improvement becomes visible in people’s lives. The other measures how quickly opposition leaders can turn discussions into an arrangement that strengthens their challenge.

This week has brought movement on both. Figures released on Monday put October’s annual headline inflation at 14.06 per cent, down from 14.63 per cent in September.

Meanwhile, opposition parties have announced a November 23 summit in Abuja to adopt cooperation documents.

These developments give the governing party and its challengers something concrete to discuss. Neither, by itself, settles the electoral argument.

For President Bola Tinubu, the task is to demonstrate that reform is improving living standards. For the opposition, it is to demonstrate that cooperation can survive competing ambitions.

Inflation Falls. The Household Test Remains. The latest inflation figures offer the government evidence for its argument that economic stabilisation is progressing.

Food inflation also moderated, to 19.13 per cent year on year from 19.59 per cent.

The political meaning requires care. A lower annual inflation rate means prices are rising more slowly than a year earlier.

It does not mean that the general price level has returned to where it stood before the cost of living shock.

Families judge affordability through income, food, transport, rent and other recurring expenses.

A household can recognise an improving economic indicator while remaining under considerable pressure. The government therefore has an opening, accompanied by a demanding question: how much improvement will citizens experience before they vote?

Its strongest argument would connect stabilisation with changes people can identify: more reliable services, stronger earnings, affordable essentials and business opportunities.

The opposition also needs to respond seriously to improving data. It can question the distribution and adequacy of recovery while explaining how its own policies would improve purchasing power.

The emerging debate should concern the route from economic stability to household security.

November 23: Cooperation Acquires a Date

The Coalition for Democracy says participating opposition parties will meet at the NAF Conference Centre in Abuja on Monday, November 23.

The proposed business includes a National Covenant for Democratic Renewal, a Framework for Opposition Unity and a National Reform Programme.

That is a clearer next step than another general declaration of willingness to work together.

But several forms of cooperation remain possible.

Parties can coordinate election monitoring, defend campaign freedoms and agree on institutional reforms while continuing to field competing presidential candidates.

The latest announcement does not identify a common candidate. Questions about the earlier proposed roadmap towards one ticket remain unresolved in the material examined.

The summit should therefore be judged by what participants actually authorise. Who signs? In what capacity? What obligations follow? Who implements the decisions?

What happens when national cooperation conflicts with a local candidate’s ambition?

Those details will determine whether the meeting strengthens the opposition’s ability to compete.

An endorsement can encourage supporters to back another candidate. Whether they follow depends on trust, local interests, and their assessment of the candidate receiving that support.

Political leaders cannot assume that their voters will move with them.

ADC Seeks Protection for Its Candidates

The ADC’s legal position remains a consequential uncertainty.

The party is reported to be asking the Court of Appeal to overturn the judgment against its David Mark-led leadership and restrain INEC from changing leadership records or candidate nomination details while the appeal is determined.

These are requests for relief; the report does not establish that the orders have been granted.

The distinction is essential.

Atiku’s campaign needs to sustain confidence while the courts address questions affecting participation. Its candidates elsewhere need clarity too.

For INEC, uncertainty complicates administration. For voters, it can make an already complex contest harder to follow.

The immediate indicator to watch is an authoritative court order or formal commission action. Statements of confidence from interested parties cannot provide the same certainty.

Kano Adds Urgency to Campaign Safety

Sunday’s violence in Bichi has produced competing accounts.

Kwankwaso’s camp reported an attack on his convoy.

The Kano information commissioner disputed that account. Police subsequently reported eight arrests following a political clash involving APC and NDC supporters.

Investigation must establish the sequence of events and individual responsibility.

The immediate duty is to protect lawful political activity and preserve evidence. Rival explanations should be examined against witness accounts, footage, medical records and other verifiable material.

Campaign intimidation can alter participation well beyond the scene of an incident.

People may avoid meetings, volunteers may withdraw, and organisers may find access to communities more difficult. Equal protection is therefore part of electoral fairness. It must apply regardless of party, candidate or location.

Obi Puts His Record Forward

Peter Obi has announced a ten-day presentation of his record as Anambra governor, following renewed criticism from Tinubu.

He argues that his approach to governance can be applied nationally. Those are claims now offered for public scrutiny.

This creates an opportunity for a more useful campaign exchange.

Records can be examined through budgets, completed projects, institutional changes, outcomes and the responsibilities held by each officeholder.

For Obi, the question extends beyond what happened in Anambra to how his proposed methods would work at federal scale.

The same scrutiny belongs across the field: Tinubu’s presidency, Atiku’s public service and Makinde’s governorship should all be examined with comparable rigour.

APC/Tinubu: The new inflation release strengthens the stabilisation argument. Its electoral value depends on whether voters connect it with improving circumstances.

ADC/Atiku: The reported appellate requests seek protection against consequential changes while the dispute continues. Legal certainty remains the most immediate issue.

NDC/Obi–Kwankwaso: Obi is advancing a defence of his governing record, while the Bichi incident places campaign safety and Kano’s political competition under closer scrutiny.

APM/Makinde and the wider opposition: The November 23 summit offers a defined opportunity to establish cooperation. Its announcement does not establish a completed common ticket.

The participating platforms listed by the coalition include the ADC, NDC, APM, PRP, SDP and the Kabiru Turaki-led PDP faction.

Describing the last participant precisely matters: factional involvement should not automatically be presented as a commitment by every part of the PDP.

State-level analysis should now focus on implementation: shared campaign activity, local agreements, functioning organisations and polling-agent preparation.

Recent local and off-cycle elections can inform that assessment when turnout, competitiveness and local circumstances are considered. They provide indicators rather than a ready-made presidential forecast.

Election Watch assessment: There is fresh economic evidence and a firmer date for opposition cooperation. Neither establishes a measurable national swing.

Affordability and the Decision to Participate

For younger Nigerians, the economic test often begins with the cost of reaching an opportunity. Can a graduate afford transport to work? Can a small business cover electricity and rent?

Does a training programme lead to paid employment?

Can someone without connections obtain enterprise support? Slower inflation can help create better conditions. Its practical value depends on earnings, access and the costs young people actually face.

The opposition summit offers another test. Young participants should have a voice in policy choices, organisational responsibilities and implementation, not merely a role in mobilising attendance.

Campaign safety matters here too. The possibility of intimidation raises the personal cost of volunteering, reporting and attending meetings.

Youth Metre assessment: Affordability, opportunity and confidence in participation remain the key measures. No fresh, credible age-specific polling reviewed for this edition establishes a shift in candidate preference.

  • Any appellate order or formal INEC action concerning the ADC.
  • Confirmation of participants and proposed commitments for November 23.
  • Investigative findings following the Bichi violence.
  • Responses to the inflation figures that explain practical policy choices.
  • Evidence supporting claims made in the candidates’ records of service.

The government’s opportunity is to make improving indicators meaningful at home. The opposition’s opportunity is to make cooperation useful at the polling unit.

Voters will ultimately judge both by what they can deliver and by whether they can be trusted to deliver.

EDITORIAL NOTE

Political Signals is an independent weekly political analysis produced for Channels Television. It examines political developments, personalities and electoral trends without endorsement of any political party or candidate. Its assessments are based on publicly available evidence and may change as events and evidence develop.

title: Barau, Atiku, others mourn late Vanguard Online Editor, Femi Ajasa
description:
By Henry Umoru & Olasunkanmi Akoni



ABUJA—THE presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, Alhaji Atiku Abubakar; Deputy President of the Senate, Senator Barau Jibrin (APC, Kano North) has mourned the passing of Mr. Olufemi Ajasa, the Online Editor of Vanguard Newspapers.



Als
content:
By Henry Umoru & Olasunkanmi Akoni

ABUJA—THE presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, Alhaji Atiku Abubakar; Deputy President of the Senate, Senator Barau Jibrin (APC, Kano North) has mourned the passing of Mr. Olufemi Ajasa, the Online Editor of Vanguard Newspapers.

Also, Chairman of Ikeja Local Government Area, Lagos, Akeem Dauda, mourned the death of Mr. Ajasa, describing his passing as a painful loss to the media industry and the journalism profession.

Ajasa passed away on Sunday at the Lagos University Teaching Hospital, LUTH, after a brief illness at the age of 44, according to the management of Vanguard Media Limited, publishers of the Vanguard Newspapers.

Ajasa’s death painful loss to journalism,  Vanguard — Atiku mourns

Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar has described the death of Vanguard Media Limited’s Online Editor, Olufemi Ajasa, as a painful loss to the journalism profession and the media organisation, extending his condolences to the management, staff and family of the deceased.

Atiku, in a condolence message on his X handle on Tuesday, expressed sadness over Ajasa’s death at the age of 44, saying his passing was a reminder of how suddenly a life devoted to work, family and service could be cut short.

He wrote: “Ajasa’s passing is a deep loss to @vanguardngrnews and to the journalism profession. Behind every story published and every deadline met is a commitment to keeping the public informed.

“His colleagues have lost a valued teammate, the media community a respected professional, and his family a beloved son, husband, father and brother.”

Atiku also extended his condolences to the management and staff of Vanguard Media Limited, the newspaper’s Editor, Eze Anaba, and everyone who knew and worked with the late journalist.

“I extend my heartfelt condolences to the management and staff of Vanguard Media Limited, Editor Eze Anaba, and all who loved and worked with him,” the statement added.

Memories

“May the memories they shared bring comfort in this difficult hour, and may God grant his family strength to bear this immeasurable loss”, he wrote. In a condolence message by his spokesperson, Ismail Mudashir, Senator Barau described the late Ajasa as a thoroughbred professional and one of the finest minds in Nigeria’s digital journalism space.

He said: “Femi Ajasa’s dedication and commitment to truth and accuracy set him apart and distinguished him among others. His death is a painful loss, not only to his immediate family, the Vanguard family, but to the entire Nigerian media industry.”

He noted that Mr. Ajasa’s journalism journey, which began as a photojournalist with the National Mirror in 2012, through TheNewsGuru and Pulse, to his return to Vanguard in June 2022 as Online Editor, was marked by excellence, integrity and selfless service to the country through his noble profession, journalism.

Senator Barau extended his heartfelt condolences to the Ajasa family of Ajido, Badagry, Lagos State, Management and Staff of Vanguard Media Limited, the Journalists union and all his friends and professional associates.

“We pray that God will grant his family, colleagues and loved ones the strength and fortitude to bear this irreparable loss, and grant his gentle soul eternal rest,” he said.

On his part, Dauda said the late journalist’s dedication, professionalism and contributions to the growth of digital journalism would remain part of his enduring legacy.

He noted that Ajasa was a committed media professional whose career journey, spanning several reputable media organisations, reflected his passion for journalism, commitment to excellence and determination to advance the evolving media landscape.

Dauda particularly commiserated with the management and staff of Vanguard Media Limited, the immediate family of the deceased, his friends and professional colleagues over the irreparable loss.

“Take solace in the impactful life and professional contributions of the late Ajasa, whose passing at the age of 44 is a painful reminder of the fragility of life,” he stated.

Dauda also prayed that Almighty God would comfort the bereaved family, grant them the strength to bear the irreparable loss and grant the departed journalist eternal rest.

Vanguard News

The post Barau, Atiku, others mourn late Vanguard Online Editor, Femi Ajasa appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Abia Govt sacks Enyimba Management, Technical Crew over poor performance
description:
The Abia State Government has dissolved the management structure and technical crew of Enyimba International Football Club, Aba, with immediate effect, following the club’s recent poor performances.
The government said the decision was part of a comprehensive restructuring exercise aimed at addressi
content:
The Abia State Government has dissolved the management structure and technical crew of Enyimba International Football Club, Aba, with immediate effect, following the club’s recent poor performances.

The government said the decision was part of a comprehensive restructuring exercise aimed at addressing administrative and structural challenges affecting the two-time CAF Champions League winners.

In a special announcement signed by the Commissioner for Information, Prince Okey Kanu, on Tuesday, the state government said it was committed to restoring Enyimba’s competitive identity and repositioning the club for sustainable success in Nigerian and continental football.

According to the statement, the decision followed a review of the club’s operations, which exposed the need for far-reaching measures to improve its performance, administration and overall management.

The government consequently directed the Ministry of Sports and Youth Development to take charge of the restructuring process and conduct a comprehensive assessment of the club’s management framework.

The ministry is also expected to introduce administrative, technical, operational and institutional reforms to restore stability, accountability and competitiveness.

“The dissolution takes immediate effect,” the statement said.

The government further directed all affected management and technical personnel, alongside individuals holding the club’s assets, properties, official documents and equipment, to ensure a formal handover to the Ministry of Sports and Youth Development.

It added that the ministry would provide further information on the handover arrangements and subsequent administrative procedures.

title: Magaji calls for stronger North Central representation in national leadership, youth development
description:
Hon. Suleiman Abubakar Magaji has called for stronger representation of the North Central region in national leadership, greater political inclusion and sustained investment in youth development.
He described the region as an important stakeholder in Nigeria’s development and democratic process, str
content:
Hon. Suleiman Abubakar Magaji has called for stronger representation of the North Central region in national leadership, greater political inclusion and sustained investment in youth development.

He described the region as an important stakeholder in Nigeria’s development and democratic process, stressing the need for its people, particularly young Nigerians, to play a greater role in national affairs.

Magaji made the remarks while reflecting on his recent engagements with political leaders and stakeholders across the region, including the Minister of Information and National Orientation, Mohammed Idris Malagi; Niger State Governor, Mohammed Umaru Bago; and former Nasarawa State Governor, Senator Umaru Tanko Al-Makura.

He described the meetings as valuable opportunities to exchange ideas, seek guidance and discuss grassroots participation, political organisation and the future of youth leadership in the North Central region.

He also expressed appreciation to the senior political leaders for their encouragement and commendation of his efforts in youth mobilisation and stakeholder engagement.

According to him, the recognition has further strengthened his commitment to public service, responsible leadership and building stronger relationships across the region.

Magaji said the North Central must strengthen its voice in national discussions through constructive engagement, strategic partnerships and active participation by its people, especially the younger generation.

He noted that the region’s diversity, human resources and strategic geographical location give it the potential to make even greater contributions to Nigeria’s development.

Reflecting on the recent presidential rally in Jos, Plateau State, he said the impressive turnout of youths and other stakeholders demonstrated the importance of organised grassroots mobilisation and cooperation among political and community groups.

He, however, stressed that political participation should go beyond attending rallies and public gatherings to include meaningful contributions to governance, community development, policy discussions and leadership.

Magaji also highlighted the need to prepare young people for leadership through mentorship, institutional support and opportunities to participate in decision-making.

He said developing the next generation of leaders should be a shared responsibility involving experienced politicians, government institutions and other stakeholders.

He further called for stronger cooperation among political stakeholders in Niger, Plateau, Benue, Kogi, Kwara and Nasarawa states, as well as the Federal Capital Territory (FCT).

According to him, sustained regional engagement and cooperation are necessary to address common challenges, promote shared interests and advance development across the North Central.

Magaji reaffirmed his commitment to youth inclusion, constructive political engagement and building stronger relationships among stakeholders in the region.

He maintained that the North Central’s future influence would depend not only on its political relevance but also on the quality of its leadership, the opportunities available to its young people and the collective determination of its stakeholders to pursue sustainable development.

title: U-23 AFCON Qualifiers: Olympic Eagles thrash DR Congo 4-0, advance 4-2 on aggregate
description:
Nigeria’s U-23 national team, the Olympic Eagles, have advanced to the final round of qualifiers for the 2027 Africa U-23 Cup of Nations after overturning a two-goal first-leg deficit to defeat the Democratic Republic of Congo 4-0 in the return fixture.
The Olympic Eagles secured the emphatic victor
content:
Nigeria’s U-23 national team, the Olympic Eagles, have advanced to the final round of qualifiers for the 2027 Africa U-23 Cup of Nations after overturning a two-goal first-leg deficit to defeat the Democratic Republic of Congo 4-0 in the return fixture.

The Olympic Eagles secured the emphatic victory on November 17, 2026, at the Remo Stars Stadium in Ikenne, completing a 4-2 aggregate win over their Congolese opponents.

Nigeria had entered the second leg under pressure after suffering a 2-0 defeat in the first leg at the Stade TP Mazembe in Lubumbashi.

However, the Nigerian side produced a commanding performance on home soil, scoring four unanswered goals to turn the tie around and secure qualification.

The victory means Nigeria will face Zambia in the final round of the qualifying series, with a place at the 2027 U-23 AFCON at stake.

title: Nvidia says no return for ousted CEO, reports revenue boom
description:
US chip giant Nvidia on Tuesday ruled out any comeback for ousted CEO Jensen Huang, who was forced out in a spy scandal, and reported that it had doubled revenue in the third quarter to more than $115 billion, beating expectations.



Huang sought to be reinstated despite resigning last week over an
content:
US chip giant Nvidia on Tuesday ruled out any comeback for ousted CEO Jensen Huang, who was forced out in a spy scandal, and reported that it had doubled revenue in the third quarter to more than $115 billion, beating expectations.

Huang sought to be reinstated despite resigning last week over an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, but his successor — interim CEO Colette Kress — said that it was now “business as usual” at the company as it charts a way ahead without him.

Harvey Jones, the chair of the company’s board, said in an earnings call that “the Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.”

Investors scoured the upbeat results for evidence that the artificial intelligence boom can withstand the Nvidia crisis, which highlighted a loophole allegedly exploited by Chinese companies.

“Our momentum is real. Nvidia is an exceptional technology leader, powered by the relentless innovation of our people,” Kress said in her first remarks since being appointed by the board last week.

She forecast stronger revenue growth of 75 percent in next fiscal year, up from 70 percent.

Huang’s bid on Tuesday to get his job back was the latest twist for the company at the center of an AI boom that has propelled markets to record highs and boosted global economic growth.

The recent upheaval has battered shares of Nvidia — which has lost $700 billion in market value since the scandal broke — and Huang is to be questioned by US lawmakers on December 1 over national security concerns.

A charismatic promoter of AI, his fall triggered immediate calls from Elon Musk and others for his return, and even President Donald Trump said he “would not mind” seeing Huang back at Nvidia, downplaying the espionage allegations.

– Battle over AI chips –

“Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from Nvidia’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO,” Huang said, hours before the earnings release.

“If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO.”

As the spy scandal deepened, Washington on Monday announced new restrictions on AI chip exports, drawing condemnation from Beijing.

The new US export curbs and the wider Nvidia scandal risk casting a shadow over talks between Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit, which starts this week in the Chinese city of Shenzhen.

Under Washington’s new rules, data centers anywhere in the world will need a US license to provide large volumes of computing power from advanced chips to companies headquartered in China, Macau or other countries under US arms embargoes.

The rules also require licenses to ship advanced chips to Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil — countries the US Commerce Department says present a “higher-than-normal risk of diversion” of the chips.

The changes are a response to a loophole that allowed Chinese firms to rent AI computing power from data centers in Southeast Asia and elsewhere that run on US hardware not available for export to China.

While the loophole has been known to authorities, the revelation of Huang’s affair has drawn intense scrutiny to the practice.

His lover Alice Huang, who is not related to the 63-year-old, is a former executive of Megaspeed — a Singapore-based cloud computing firm under US criminal investigation for allegedly helping Chinese companies procure advanced Nvidia AI chips in circumvention of export controls.

Investors are watching for signs of whether Kress will slow Huang’s aggressive investment strategy, which saw him commit tens of billions of dollars to AI companies.

Huang on Tuesday sounded a note of contrition in his statement, saying “I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at NVIDIA, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life.”

The post Nvidia says no return for ousted CEO, reports revenue boom appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Kwara APC Reps candidate unveils people-centred agenda

By Demola Akinyemi, Ilorin



ILORIN — The All Progressives Congress (APC) candidate for Ifelodun/Offa/Oyun Federal Constituency in the House of Representatives election, Dr Rafiu Ajakaye, has unveiled a legislative agenda focusing on secur
content:
…Says serving as AbdulRazaq’s CPS was greatest privilege

By Demola Akinyemi, Ilorin

ILORIN — The All Progressives Congress (APC) candidate for Ifelodun/Offa/Oyun Federal Constituency in the House of Representatives election, Dr Rafiu Ajakaye, has unveiled a legislative agenda focusing on security, education, youth employment, women’s economic empowerment and rural development.

Ajakaye, a former Chief Press Secretary to Kwara State Governor AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq, said his aspiration to represent the constituency was driven by a desire to provide accessible and effective leadership rather than pursue personal ambition.

He stated this on Tuesday while speaking on the News Keg programme organised by the Correspondents’ Chapel of the Nigeria Union of Journalists (NUJ) at its secretariat in Ilorin.

Presenting his manifesto titled, “Manifesto of Purpose: A Covenant with the People of Ifelodun/Offa/Oyun Federal Constituency”, Ajakaye described his service as the governor’s spokesperson as a major privilege in his professional career.

“Serving as the Chief Press Secretary to Governor AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq was one of the greatest privileges of my life,” he said.

He described public office as a responsibility that should be directed towards improving people’s lives.

Ajakaye cited his involvement in the 2021, 2024 and 2025 teachers’ recruitment exercises under the AbdulRazaq administration as an experience that reinforced his belief in merit-based employment opportunities.

According to him, the exercises demonstrated the importance of involving the right people in recruitment processes to ensure fairness and create opportunities for qualified applicants.

“Leadership is not about occupying an office. It is about inspiring hope, solving problems, expanding opportunities, and shaping a future in which every citizen can live with dignity,” he said.

The candidate, who hails from Alabe community in Ifelodun Local Government Area, said his background, academic training and professional experience had shaped his approach to governance and public service.

He said his experience as a journalist, public relations practitioner and public servant, particularly his years as the governor’s spokesperson, had exposed him to policymaking and the importance of transparency, competence and integrity in governance.

On security, Ajakaye identified banditry and kidnapping as major concerns affecting rural communities, saying the activities had disrupted livelihoods and economic activities.

He pledged to advocate stronger legislative oversight of security agencies, improved welfare and equipment for security personnel, intelligence-led operations and community-based security strategies.

He identified insecurity in parts of Ifelodun Local Government Area as a major priority, promising to make it the foremost issue on his legislative agenda if elected.

“Security is number one on my legislative agenda. I understand the pains of my people because that is where I come from, If elected, I will champion stronger legislative oversight of security agencies,” he said.

On education, the APC candidate said he would advocate reforms to align the country’s education system with technological developments and labour market demands.

He identified science, technical, vocational and digital education as areas requiring greater attention.

Addressing youth unemployment, Ajakaye promised to support legislation that would promote entrepreneurship, improve access to finance for small businesses, strengthen vocational training and encourage young people to embrace agriculture.

On women’s economic empowerment, he said he would pursue policies to support women-owned businesses through affordable financing, cooperative initiatives, improved market access and sustainable income-generating opportunities.

He also pledged to promote rural infrastructure, agricultural modernisation, small business development and improved public services, insisting that development should extend to every ward and community in the constituency.

title: ‘Human’ Is Cambridge Dictionary’s Word Of The Year
description: “Human”, meaning to have the “qualities, faults, and feelings that people have, as opposed to gods, animals, or machines” has been named Cambridge Dictionary’s Word of the Year.In an era of rapidly expanding Artificial Intelligence (AI) and dire warnings it could even w
content:
“Human”, meaning to have the “qualities, faults, and feelings that people have, as opposed to gods, animals, or machines” has been named Cambridge Dictionary’s Word of the Year.

In an era of rapidly expanding Artificial Intelligence (AI) and dire warnings it could even wipe out humanity, the word captured “the 2026 zeitgeist”, Cambridge University Press board member Francesca Woodward told AFP.

Over the past 12 months, she said, people had been “really considering what it is to be human” in particular due to concerns about AI taking over their jobs.

“I think people are trying to remind themselves of … what human means,” she said.

The word beat off competition from other words related to AI and the online world, reflecting intense global interest in how technology is changing our lives, she said.

The dictionary’s lexicographers had also observed an increased used of “human” in compound words such as human-made or human author, she added.

Tom McClelland, a philosopher of science at the University of Cambridge, described “human” as a “really interesting choice … because right now our understanding of humanity is changing”.

Global AI debate

“We’re trying to understand the difference between a human mind and an artificial mind, between living beings like us and artificial beings that we’re creating. What sets us apart, is it consciousness, creativity or compassion?” he said.

The focus on what it means to be human has seen global leaders and prominent figures such as Pope Leo XIV, Bill Gates, classicist Mary Beard and actor Cate Blanchett weigh in on the debate.

Other contenders for the word of the year crown included “agent, meaning an artificial intelligence system that can operate in a complicated way without human control.

Also in the running was “wholesome”, defined as “good for you, and likely to improve your life either physically, morally, or emotionally”.

“Dusking” was also in contention, the practice of watching daylight turn to darkness as a form of relaxation.

A Dutch tradition, it has been revived as a way of reconnecting with the natural world.

Other new words added to the dictionary in 2026 included “aura farming”, doing things to show a personality that people will admire, and “looksmaxing”, making yourself as physically attractive as possible.

The word of the year and new additions are selected using a range of criteria including the words searched for on the Cambridge Dictionary website.

Among words to watch for next year, according to Cambridge Dictionary, were FOBO, “fear of becoming obsolete” because your job can be performed by AI.

Another was “weather whiplash”, denoting a “quick change from one extreme of weather to another”.

Last year’s word of the year was “parasocial” to describe the sense of having a connection to a famous person you do not know personally or a fictional character.

The post ‘Human’ Is Cambridge Dictionary’s Word Of The Year appeared first on Channels Television.

SOKOTO — The Tinubu Again Movement (TAM), a political support group associated with the Minister of State for Defence, Bello Matawalle, has announced plans to facilitate the release of 2,000 inmates in Sokoto, Kebbi and Zamfara states through the payment of court-impose
content:
By Musa Ubandawaki, Sokoto

SOKOTO — The Tinubu Again Movement (TAM), a political support group associated with the Minister of State for Defence, Bello Matawalle, has announced plans to facilitate the release of 2,000 inmates in Sokoto, Kebbi and Zamfara states through the payment of court-imposed fines and other lawful interventions.

The proposed initiative is aimed at assisting indigent inmates whose continued detention is linked to their inability to pay fines and those eligible for release under applicable laws.

The group announced the plan on Tuesday during its participation in the presidential campaign rally of President Bola Tinubu in Birnin Kebbi, Kebbi State.

Hundreds of its members participated in the rally, wearing branded outfits and carrying banners bearing the images of Tinubu, Vice-President Kashim Shettima and Matawalle.

The supporters also marched through major streets of the state capital, expressing support for the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Speaking on the proposed intervention, TAM spokesman, Mallam Yusuf Dingyadi, said the initiative was designed to assist deserving inmates who could not secure their release because of financial constraints.

He said the movement would identify eligible beneficiaries and work towards settling outstanding fines in accordance with the law.

“Our intention is to facilitate the release of 2,000 inmates across Sokoto, Kebbi and Zamfara states by identifying deserving cases and assisting those whose continued detention is linked to their inability to pay relatively small fines.

“We believe that imprisonment should not become a permanent barrier to rebuilding one’s life, particularly for individuals who qualify for release under the law but remain in correctional facilities because of their financial circumstances,” Dingyadi said.

He added that the intervention was intended to support family reunification and the reintegration of eligible former inmates into society.

Dingyadi also disclosed that the movement was planning humanitarian interventions for internally displaced persons (IDPs) and other vulnerable communities across the three states.

According to him, the proposed programmes would include the distribution of food, clothing and other essential relief materials, as well as empowerment initiatives.

“We are equally concerned about the humanitarian challenges confronting internally displaced persons in Sokoto, Kebbi and Zamfara states. We intend to support them through the provision of foodstuffs, clothing and empowerment opportunities to cushion their hardships and restore their dignity,” he said.

On the proposed inmate-release programme, Dingyadi said the group would engage relevant correctional authorities, judicial institutions and other stakeholders to identify eligible beneficiaries and ensure compliance with existing laws.

He stressed that the initiative was not intended to interfere with judicial decisions but to support lawful processes for the release of inmates who had met the relevant conditions for discharge.

Beyond the humanitarian initiative, the TAM spokesman said the group’s participation in the Kebbi rally reflected its commitment to grassroots mobilisation for Tinubu’s re-election bid in 2027.

He said the movement planned to expand its political activities across the North-West through engagements with communities and political stakeholders.

If implemented, the proposed intervention could provide relief to affected inmates and their families, while drawing attention to the challenges faced by indigent persons unable to meet court-imposed financial obligations.

title: Immigration vows to fix gaps in Visa & Residency Reforms
description:
.As Army pledges stronger partnership on border security



By Omeiza Ajayi



ABUJA: The Nigeria Immigration Service NIS on Tuesday undertook a stakeholders’ assessment of its Visa and Residency Reforms, one year after the scheme was rolled out, promising to confront all the weak points.







Com
content:
.As Army pledges stronger partnership on border security

By Omeiza Ajayi

ABUJA: The Nigeria Immigration Service NIS on Tuesday undertook a stakeholders’ assessment of its Visa and Residency Reforms, one year after the scheme was rolled out, promising to confront all the weak points.

Comptroller General of the NIS, Kemi Nandap, made the pledge in Abuja, while declaring open a one-day stakeholders’ sensitization workshop on the Nigeria Visa and Residency Reforms.

At the event, the Nigerian Army also pledged a stronger partnership with the Service in securing the country’s borders, especially in areas where a large portion of the frontier remains porous.

The Chief of Civil-Military Affairs (Army), Major General Musa Etsu-Ndagi, who represented the Chief of Army Staff COAS, said: “Nigeria has a land border of 4,047km and there is a large portion of it that remains porous. The Nigerian Army will continue to support the NIS in manning the borders especially in those areas”.

On the reforms, the CGIS who was represented by the Deputy Comptroller General DCG in charge of Visa and Residency, Dr Franca Usiwoma Nwanneka, said; “As we assess the implementation of the reforms over the last one year, we have reasons to appreciate the progress made so far. However, we must also be ready to identify the areas where we have not done well and take the necessary steps to address them”.

The workshop was held under the theme: “Assessing the Implementation of the Nigeria Visa and Residency Reforms: Stakeholders’ Engagement and Strategies for Improved Service Delivery.”

Nandap said the purpose of the meeting was to look at the progress made since the introduction of the reforms, discuss the challenges encountered and identify areas where improvements are needed.”

She acknowledged that users may have run into difficulties since the introduction of these reforms. “These may include payment difficulties, technical issues and other concerns relating to the use of the portal. I want to assure you that the Service is willing to listen to your concerns and consider useful recommendations that will help us improve our operations,” she said.

According to her, the reforms were introduced “to address some of the challenges associated with the old manual processes, reduce delays, improve transparency, strengthen national security and make our immigration services more accessible to the public.”

Nandap listed the electronic visa (e-Visa) among the major gains, noting that it became operational on 1st May, 2025, and replaced the traditional Visa-on-Arrival arrangement.

“Applicants can now receive decisions on their visa applications within 48 hours, subject to meeting the necessary requirements and security checks,” she said.

She added that the e-Visa had “improved transparency, reduced unnecessary human interference and strengthened our ability to monitor visa applications and approvals.”

The Comptroller General also cited the creation of the F9A and F9B visa categories for adult and minor Nigerians returning with foreign passports respectively, which she said had “helped to address the needs of Nigerians in the diaspora who find themselves in this situation.”

On work permits, Nandap said the Electronic Temporary Work Permit (e-TWP) became operational on 1st August, 2025, replacing manual procedures that “sometimes resulted in delays.” According to her, biometric capturing machines had improved the identification and verification of applicants, while insurance requirements were introduced to improve the management of foreign nationals undertaking temporary work in Nigeria.

The e-TWP, she explained, is also linked to the Service’s border management system through the Landing and Exit Card facility, which “will assist in monitoring the movement of foreign nationals and ensuring that they comply with the conditions of their stay in Nigeria.”

The third pillar of the reforms, the electronic Comprehensive Expatriate Residence Permit and Automated Card (e-CERPAC), also took effect on 1st August, 2025. Nandap said the system had improved the handling of residence permit applications, renewals and status regularisation, and led to the introduction of the Investors Residence Permit in support of the Federal Government’s drive to attract investment.

She said the e-CERPAC’s integration with the border management system “will make it easier to verify the residence status of expatriates at our entry and exit points.”

The immigration boss stressed that the Service could not succeed alone, and called for the support of “relevant Ministries, Departments and Agencies, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Nigerian Missions abroad, security agencies, the private sector, international organisations and employers of expatriates.”

Urging participants to contribute actively, Nandap said: “Our goal is to have an immigration system that provides efficient services, protects the security of our country and supports the economic development of Nigeria.”

The post Immigration vows to fix gaps in Visa & Residency Reforms appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: FMCGs seek NAFDAC automation to cut registration delays, fake licences
description: By Cynthia AloFast-Moving Consumer Goods, FMCG, manufacturers and small businesses have urged the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control, NAFDAC, to automate most of its paper processes involving  product registration and licence renewal to reduce delays and curb circulation of
content:
By Cynthia Alo
Fast-Moving Consumer Goods, FMCG, manufacturers and small businesses have urged the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control, NAFDAC, to automate most of its paper processes involving  product registration and licence renewal to reduce delays and curb circulation of counterfeit products and fake registration numbers.

They said prolonged approvals were forcing some manufacturers to rely on intermediaries, exposing them to exploitation, including the use of fake NAFDAC registration numbers.

The call was made recently at the 2026 FMCG Festival in Lagos.

Speaking on behalf of manufacturers, Project Director of the FMCG Festival, Flora Mbeledeogu, said renewal of NAFDAC licences remained a major challenge, and that NAFDAC needed more hands and automation to make registration and renewal faster and more seamless.

Mbeledeogu said: “We need NAFDAC to employ more hands and automate our systems so that when a consumer brand wants to renew its NAFDAC certificate or licence, they can do so without having to raise an arm and a leg. It has to just be a seamless process, just like it is in other countries in Africa where you just need to upload the required documents on the portal; within 24 hours, receive notification for factory inspection; officials inspect and take samples; analysis is done;by 48 hours, the product registration number is issued. We need to get to that point.”

She warned that delays could expose smaller manufacturers to exploitation by intermediaries who claim to facilitate registration and renewal processes.
She urged the agency to address the bottlenecks before the next edition of the festival.
Responding to the concerns, Director, NAFDAC, North-West Zone, Dadi Mullah, said the agency’s processes were designed to ensure products met required health and safety standards.
He disclosed that food product registration could take up to 120 working days, covering facility inspection, laboratory testing, regulatory assessment and final approval.

Mullah said one challenge was that some small businesses wanted to produce from their domestic kitchens without meeting the facility requirements prescribed for commercial production.

He said NAFDAC could not allow such businesses to supply the wider market without complying with Good Manufacturing Practices, GMP.

He said: “The only thing I know that many of you will complain about is our facility requirement. We insist that unless the facility meets minimum good manufacturing practices requirements, we will not allow you to produce.Your kitchen cannot produce the kind of products for the international market.”
Speaking on delays in registration and renewal processing, he said NAFDAC’s laboratories handled a large volume of applications, making it difficult for applicants to expect immediate results.
He attributed part of the delays in Lagos to inadequate personnel at the agency’s food registration office.
He disclosed that NAFDAC had previously recorded more than 8,400 pending applications partly to having only one Local Office Director (LOD) handling applications at the office adding, “There was only one LOD in the food registration office, and until that person processes all those products, it sits in Lagos pipeline, moving slower.”
He said the agency had deployed additional LODs across its zonal offices to reduce the backlog.
He expressed optimism that the additional personnel would accelerate the process in the coming months, while urging manufacturers to continue providing feedback on delays and other challenges.
He added that to encourage registration of products , NAFDAC had discounted registration fees for micro, small and medium enterprises, MSMEs, since 2020.
According to him, no product registration fee exceeds N100,000, while some micro businesses pay between N40,000 and N60,000.
He said laboratory analysis could cost about N500,000, with the agency bearing part of the cost.
Mullah maintained that manufacturers did not need agents or intermediaries to obtain registration, advising businesses experiencing difficulties with the online process to approach the agency’s support desk for assistance at no cost.
He warned that anyone caught dealing in counterfeit products would face the law, saying offenders could be sentenced to seven years in prison.
” For now, anyone that is just dabbling into that, wherever, whenever we catch such a person, we will make sure that the law deals with you.”

He said consumers and traders could use NAFDAC’s online verification platform at registration.nafdac.gov.ng to confirm whether a product’s registration number was genuine.
He explained that the platform provides information such as the product name, packaging details, registration number and expiry date, enabling consumers to identify fake products.
He advised consumers to examine product labels, storage conditions and registration numbers before purchasing or consuming regulated products.
He also asked them to report suspected counterfeit products through the agency’s website, email and social media platforms, rather than merely complain about their circulation in the market.
The NAFDAC official further called for stronger collaboration with traders and distributors to identify and remove unregistered and counterfeit products from markets.
Supporting the call, President, Okearin Traders Association, Paulinus Ugwu , said traders had established a task force in the market to identify and remove counterfeit products.
Ugwu called for closer collaboration between traders and NAFDAC, noting that regulators could not know everything happening in markets without the cooperation of those operating there.
He said traders were also interested in promoting locally manufactured products, particularly those produced by small businesses, and called on manufacturers to bring their product samples for consideration by distributors.
In his keynote address, the Chief Operating Officer of Berger Paints Nigeria Plc, Kayode Momoh, urged manufacturers to strengthen supply chains, local sourcing, product quality and innovation to remain competitive.
Momoh said innovation must go beyond developing new ideas to ensuring that products could be produced, delivered and sustained consistently in the market.

He also called for a stable and predictable regulatory environment to give manufacturers confidence to invest for the long term.

title: ADC rejects claim it sponsored attack on Tinubu’s convoy
description:
The African Democratic Congress has denied involvement in the alleged stoning of President Bola Tinubu’s convoy in Abuja, accusing the All Progressives Congress of blaming the opposition for public anger over the economic situation.
The party’s National Publicity Secretary, Bolaji Abdullahi, on Wedn
content:
The African Democratic Congress has denied involvement in the alleged stoning of President Bola Tinubu’s convoy in Abuja, accusing the All Progressives Congress of blaming the opposition for public anger over the economic situation.

The party’s National Publicity Secretary, Bolaji Abdullahi, on Wednesday, stated this in a statement while responding to allegations against the ADC.

“We deny any involvement in the APC’s current predicament. We also cannot take responsibility for citizens who are expressing their genuine grievances against a failed regime that has pauperised them more than any other in recent history,” Abdullahi said.

He challenged the ruling party to provide evidence to support its claims, saying, “They have no evidence to support their claims.”

Abdullahi also accused the APC of being responsible for political violence in the country, stating, “Every Nigerian knows that.”

He added that the ADC had earlier warned the ruling party about the consequences of its actions.

“We warned them a long time ago that they would have their day of reckoning with the people. Now, judgment day has arrived, and they are looking for someone to blame,” he said.

The ADC spokesman also questioned the APC’s account of the alleged attack on the President’s convoy, asking, “By the way, didn’t they deny that the President’s convoy was stoned at the mosque? Liars.”

The response follows allegations by the APC Presidential Campaign Council that the ADC and the Nigeria Democratic Congress were sponsoring protests and violence at political campaign events ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The APC campaign council, in a statement by its spokesperson, Dele Alake, on Tuesday, alleged that opposition parties were mobilising youths to disrupt its activities through sponsored protests, fake news and propaganda.

It also accused the parties of mobilising hoodlums to pelt Tinubu’s motorcade with stones at an Abuja mosque on November 13, shortly after the President observed Jumu’ah prayers in Garki.

The council said security operatives attached to the President’s convoy exercised restraint during the incident and that Tinubu directed the police to release those arrested over the disruption.

However, the ADC Presidential Campaign Council had challenged the APC to provide evidence linking the opposition party to the alleged attack, questioning the circumstances surrounding the reported arrests and release of suspects.

title: Abia making steady progress under my watch — Otti
description:
Pledges support for emerging talents to attain global recognition



By Steve Oko



UMUAHIA — Abia State Governor, Alex Otti, has said the state is making steady progress, expressing optimism about its development prospects under his administration.







Otti spoke at the grand finale of the 13th
content:
Pledges support for emerging talents to attain global recognition

By Steve Oko

UMUAHIA — Abia State Governor, Alex Otti, has said the state is making steady progress, expressing optimism about its development prospects under his administration.

Otti spoke at the grand finale of the 13th edition of the Vision Africa Icons Talent Show 2026 in Umuahia, where he highlighted his administration’s efforts to reposition the state’s economy and promote development across various sectors.

The governor, who was represented by his Chief of Staff, Pastor Caleb Ajagba, also pledged government support for the discovery, development and international promotion of indigenous talents.

He said the administration was committed to creating opportunities for gifted young people to develop their abilities and gain recognition beyond Nigeria.

Reflecting on the state’s development journey, Otti said his administration had prioritised efforts to harness Abia’s economic and human resources.

“Before Otti came on board, Abia was lying fallow and prostrate. Nothing good was being said of Abia State. Today, Abia is being celebrated as a place of excellence,” he said.

The governor said purposeful leadership and collaboration were important in unlocking the state’s human and creative potential.

He assured participants in the talent show that the government would support successful contestants in pursuing opportunities for international recognition.

Otti also disclosed that the state government would partner with Vision Africa International to advance the initiative.

“Everybody that emerges here today is going global. His Excellency is going to make sure that global stardom is achieved,” he said.

He described the talent show as consistent with his administration’s commitment to identifying, nurturing and promoting the abilities of young people.

Earlier, the Chairman of the occasion, Noah Dallaji, represented by Theo Ubani, said Africa’s human talent remained one of the continent’s major competitive advantages.

“I tell people that Africa has talent to offer. We might not offer the best in technology, but what we can offer is talent,” he said.

In his welcome address, the founder and President of Vision Africa International, Archbishop Sunday Onuoha, called on political leaders to create conditions that would enable disadvantaged citizens to benefit from peace and development.

Onuoha, who is also Co-Chairman of the Interfaith Dialogue Forum for Peace, said Nigeria’s diversity should promote unity rather than division.

He urged Nigerians to work together across their differences to build a peaceful and prosperous country.

The 13th edition of the Vision Africa Icons Talent Show was held under the theme, “The Sound of Peace: Breaking Barriers, Building Bridges.”

The post Abia making steady progress under my watch — Otti appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Pattinson stood out among five finalists for iconic James Bond role — Bezos
description:
Jeff Bezos has revealed that he was “heavily involved” in selecting British actor Robert Pattinson as the next James Bond, admitting that he was initially opposed to the choice because of the actor’s fame.
The Amazon founder and chief executive said he was originally “biased against” Pattinson, who
content:
Jeff Bezos has revealed that he was “heavily involved” in selecting British actor Robert Pattinson as the next James Bond, admitting that he was initially opposed to the choice because of the actor’s fame.

The Amazon founder and chief executive said he was originally “biased against” Pattinson, who is known for his roles in Batman and the Twilight film series, because the franchise had traditionally favoured relatively less-established actors for the iconic 007 role.

However, Bezos said the actor’s performance during screen tests convinced him that he was the right choice.

Speaking at the Semafor Silicon Valley & The World event in California on Tuesday, Bezos said, “There was something special about Rob.”

BBC on Wednesday reported that he added that although Pattinson was already a household name, his performance during the casting process made the decision clear.

“In screen tests, it was so obvious he is James Bond,” Bezos said.

According to the Amazon boss, five actors made the final shortlist and participated in what he described as “real, old-fashioned screen tests”, performing three different scenes in full costume, with actual sets and other actors.

“We ran a really tight process and made the final decision on Friday,” he said.

Bezos added, “By the time we got to this list of five, they were all amazing. But there was something special about Rob and his performance. It was immediately un-debated. Denis [Villeneuve], the director … we all gravitated toward Rob.”

Pattinson was unveiled as the franchise’s seventh James Bond on Monday, replacing Daniel Craig, who played the British secret agent in five films. https://punchng.com/british-actor-pattinson-replaces-daniel-craig-as-new-james-bond/

The 40-year-old London-born actor will lead the 26th Bond film, which is scheduled for release in 2028.

Here are seven things to know about it. https://punchng.com/seven-things-to-know-about-the-next-james-bond-film/

In a statement following the announcement, Pattinson said, “James Bond is one of the most legendary characters in cinema, and to be entrusted with 007 is the honour of a lifetime.”

The forthcoming film will be directed by Denis Villeneuve, although its title and exact release date have yet to be announced.

The casting marks a significant change in the franchise’s history, as it will be the first Bond film without the Broccoli family’s creative control since the first instalment was released in 1962.

Amazon acquired MGM, which co-owns the James Bond franchise, in 2022.

Other actors reportedly considered for the role included Josh O’Connor, Callum Turner and Jack Lowden.

The casting decision comes amid challenges in Hollywood, including studio consolidation and efforts to attract audiences back to cinemas.

Hollywood journalist Matthew Belloni, who predicted Pattinson’s selection, described the actor as an obvious choice given the commercial stakes involved in the franchise.

Writing in his newsletter, Belloni said, “Maybe he’s boring. Maybe Hollywood would be passing up a chance to anoint a badly needed new star. But with so much at stake for everyone involved, that all makes him the obvious pick.”

The post Pattinson stood out among five finalists for iconic James Bond role — Bezos appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Itsekiri youths suspend campaign rally boycott after governor’s intervention
description:
Itsekiri apex youth bodies, Ugbarajo Itsekiri Youths, UIY, and Itsekiri National Youth Council, INYC, have reiterated their opposition to the inclusion of the Ijaw in the Warri South ward delineation.







They expressed surprise at the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC’s, decision t
content:
Itsekiri apex youth bodies, Ugbarajo Itsekiri Youths, UIY, and Itsekiri National Youth Council, INYC, have reiterated their opposition to the inclusion of the Ijaw in the Warri South ward delineation.

They expressed surprise at the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC’s, decision to upload wards with names that have no historical, geographical or traditional relationship with Warri South, saying the move could trigger serious crises.

They, however, decided to temporarily suspend mass action against all forms of political activities in Warri Kingdom following the intervention of Governor Sheriff Oborevwori.

The INYC President, Appearance Efejuku, and UIY President, Joseph Okotie, made this known in a statement.

The statement read: “Sequel to the memorandum of threat issued to the general public over the readiness of the Itsekiri apex youth bodies, UIY and INYC, to prevent the hosting of all forms of campaign rallies in any part of Warri Kingdom until all issues associated with the illegal creation of wards for the Ijaws are addressed satisfactorily, the Governor of Delta State, Right Honorable Elder Francis O. Oborevwori, invited us, leaders and other stakeholders, for a closed-door meeting, wherein he requested to know why the issuers of the threats took such a position. According to him, as of the last time he checked, the entire Itsekiri nation endorsed him and Mr. President. Thus, if this issue raised in the memo is not addressed, it could be misconstrued as a change in the position of the Itsekiri nation against the APC as a political party.

“In response, the leadership of the two youth bodies was very categorical in their vehement opposition to any inclusion of Ijaws by any consideration into Warri South ward delineation.

“As this would amount to disrespecting the directive of the President (His Excellency Bola Ahmed Tinubu), who asked the Itsekiris and the Urhobos of Warri South to go and meet, sort out the issues, and get back to him. They also said that the President further stated that if the parties involved in these delineation issues were not satisfied, he would have no other option than to take the Supreme Court judgment back to the Supreme Court for proper interpretation.

“They were therefore surprised to wake up one day and be told, in flagrant disregard of this directive of the President, that INEC had uploaded wards with names that have no historical, geographical or traditional relationship with Warri South.

“This, according to the bodies, is a recipe for serious crises if INEC is not made to retrace its steps.

“Thereafter, the Governor appealed to the leadership of the youth bodies to sheath their swords so he could take this issue back to the President for better clarification.

“Additionally, it was stated that the only ward structure that was operational before now was the 12-ward structure, and it is what will be used to conduct the 2027 general election.

“Consequent upon all that was mentioned, the leadership of UIY and INYC met and hereby resolved to temporarily suspend all forms of intended mass action and mobilisation towards stopping all Itsekiris from attending this rally. We therefore call on all members and critical stakeholders of our organisations to be on internal vigilance to monitor the activities of all political parties in the Kingdom to ensure that these ward delineations are not weaponised as a tool to undermine the Itsekiri people in their homeland of the Warri Federal Constituency.

“All these positions were corroborated by the Urhobos of Warri South who were in attendance at the meeting.”

The post Itsekiri youths suspend campaign rally boycott after governor’s intervention appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Anti-Tinubu protest: We’re not involved in your predicament – ADC spokesman fires back at APC
description:
National Publicity Secretary of African Democratic Congress (ADC), Bolaji Abdullahi has dissociated the party from alleged sponsorship of protests against President Bola Tinubu.
Abdullahi spoke in an X post on Wednesday in response to a Tuesday statement signed by spokesman of APC Presidential Campa
content:
National Publicity Secretary of African Democratic Congress (ADC), Bolaji Abdullahi has dissociated the party from alleged sponsorship of protests against President Bola Tinubu.

Abdullahi spoke in an X post on Wednesday in response to a Tuesday statement signed by spokesman of APC Presidential Campaign Council, Dele Alake.

Alake had alleged that opposition parties, specifically ADC and Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) were sponsoring young Nigerians to protest against the Tinubu administration to portray it as unpopular before Nigerians.

Alake cited last Friday’s incident involving the president’s convoy in Abuja as example of the machinations of the opposition against the ruling APC.

Abdullahi said, “We deny any involvement in the APC’s current predicament.

“We also cannot take responsibility for citizens who are expressing their genuine grievances against a failed regime that has pauperised them more than any other in recent history.”

The ADC spokesman accused the ruling party of clutching at straws.

“They have no evidence to support their claims. Every Nigerian knows that the only murderous party in Nigeria today is the APC. We warned them a long time ago that they would have their day of reckoning with the people. Now, judgment day has arrived, and they are looking for someone to blame.

“By the way, didn’t they deny that the President’s convoy was stoned at the mosque? Liars,” he said.

In Tuesday’s statement, APC Presidential Campaign Council accused the ADC and NDC of endangering innocent young Nigerians.

The APC said hours before the flag-off of its presidential campaign in Kaduna on October 24, 2026, it alerted Nigerians to a plot by opposition elements to create tension, sow disharmony, and introduce violence into the campaigns.

“We specifically informed Nigerians that the opposition, the African Democratic Congress and the Nigeria Democratic Congress, had perfected elaborate schemes to use deepfakes, artificial-intelligence-generated images, fake news, sponsored protests, and other forms of propaganda to manipulate public opinion and spread lies about our nation, President Bola Tinubu, the All Progressives Congress, and the processes leading to next year’s general elections,” its spokesman, Dele Alake, said.

He said the plots have started unfolding, with the major objective of deceiving Nigerians and the international community by driving a narrative of discontent against President Tinubu.

“To create the false narrative of citizens’ discontent against the President, the ADC and NDC now sponsor hoodlums, arm them with cudgels and banners, and commandeer them to chant ‘Bamaiyi’ at APC campaign rallies. The latest instance of this abhorrent and anti-democratic stunt was the desecration of an Abuja Mosque last Friday, where these thugs were mobilised to pelt the presidential motorcade with stones,” Alake said.

The APC commended security personnel attached to the presidential convoy for exercising restraint, and President Tinubu for directing the police command in Abuja to release those detained.

The party also raised concerns about violence targeting its members in the Southeast, where they are allegedly being threatened and labelled as saboteurs for not supporting Mr Peter Obi, the NDC presidential candidate.

It also complained about the destruction of its campaign billboards under cover of night by opposition-sponsored agents.

Alake said, “Our party and campaign council stand for peaceful, credible, free, and fair elections. We advocate that the democratic space should not be constricted for any party or candidate anywhere in the country.

“Again, we call on the ADC and NDC leaders to stop the dangerous conscription of ignorant young Nigerians for unwholesome political activities that put their lives at risk, while those leaders’ own children luxuriate in splendour abroad.”

The post Anti-Tinubu protest: We’re not involved in your predicament – ADC spokesman fires back at APC appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

content:

title: I can go home, sleep comfortably, Allah gives power to whom he pleases – Tinubu
description:
President Bola Tinubu has said he can return home and sleep comfortably because he believes that political power comes from Allah, as he urged residents of Kebbi State to support his re-election bid in 2027.
Tinubu made the remarks on Tuesday during his presidential campaign rally in Birnin Kebbi, t
content:
President Bola Tinubu has said he can return home and sleep comfortably because he believes that political power comes from Allah, as he urged residents of Kebbi State to support his re-election bid in 2027.

Tinubu made the remarks on Tuesday during his presidential campaign rally in Birnin Kebbi, the state capital, where he thanked residents for supporting him in the 2023 general election.

The President expressed confidence that the people of the state would turn out in large numbers to vote for him and other APC candidates in the next election.

“It’s Allah who gives power to whom He pleases. I ask for it. May Allah bless you. Thank you very much. I can go home comfortably and sleep; I know that you will come out to vote from top to bottom,” he said.

Tinubu also acknowledged the contributions of former and serving governors of the state, thanking Kebbi residents for their support during the previous election.

“I salute them, all the governors who served in this state. I come to thank you for the last election for voting for me; you voted for our senators; now I come back to say thank you,” he said.

The President assured the people of his administration’s commitment to Kebbi State and the North-West, as well as its agenda for national peace, stability and development.

He identified education, healthcare and other social infrastructure as key areas requiring continued attention, urging residents to maintain peace and unity.

“We are united with one voice; we want progress, we want development, we want education, medical health facilities that will speak for our people and will take care of all of us. I come once again to plead with you to maintain peace, friendship, and solidarity,” Tinubu added.

He also thanked residents for remaining at the rally under the sun, describing their presence as a demonstration of support for his party.
