title: Outrage in Kano as woman arranges abduction, murder of co-wife’s 14-year-old son
description:
Kano State Police Command has arrested four suspects, including a woman, over the alleged abduction and murder of a 14-year-old boy, Mahmoud Auwal.
The boy was abducted on April 20, 2026, and his corpse was later recovered by operatives of the Kwalli Division while on patrol.
A statement on Wednesda
content:
Kano State Police Command has arrested four suspects, including a woman, over the alleged abduction and murder of a 14-year-old boy, Mahmoud Auwal.

The boy was abducted on April 20, 2026, and his corpse was later recovered by operatives of the Kwalli Division while on patrol.

A statement on Wednesday by the Kano Police Public Relations Officer, Abdullahi Haruna Kiyawa said that upon discovery, the corpse was deposited at the Sir Muhammad Sunusi Specialist Hospital Mortuary.

His mother, a resident of Danbare Quarters, Kumbotso LGA, reported the abduction to the police on April 29, 2026, the statement held.

Following investigations by the Command, one 20 year old Muhammad Musa Isma’il, of Sharada Quarters, was arrested on November 3, 2026.

During interrogation, Isma’il allegedly confessed to luring the victim and named his accomplices as Abubakar Muhammad Isah, aged 27, of Semegu Quarters, and Auwal Muhammad, aged 26, of Dan-Agundi Quarters, all of whom have been arrested.

The suspects alleged that they acted on the instructions of the principal suspect, Hajiya Rukayya Auwal, aged 20, of Mararaba Quarters, New Karu LGA, Nasarawa State, who has also been arrested.

Police investigation revealed that Rukayya is a co-wife of the deceased’s mother. She allegedly planned to eliminate all four children of her husband so that her only son would solely inherit his father’s properties, even though the husband is still alive.

The police also said the principal suspect allegedly hired thugs who attacked Isma’il at Mararaba, Karu LGA, in an attempt to silence him and stop him from exposing the crime.

The Commissioner of Police, Ibrahim Adamu Bakori, condemned the act as heinous and assured the family and the public that justice will be served.

He said the case will be charged to court upon completion of investigation and appealed to the public to continue to provide timely and credible information to the police to aid crime prevention.

End.

title: New Enugu CP pledges people-centred policing, warns against extortion
description:
The newly appointed Commissioner of Police in Enugu State, CP Fidelis Ogarabe, has given officers a three-hour ultimatum to report political and election-related incidents across the state.
Ogarabe issued the directive while unveiling his policing priorities during his maiden address to officers at
content:
The newly appointed Commissioner of Police in Enugu State, CP Fidelis Ogarabe, has given officers a three-hour ultimatum to report political and election-related incidents across the state.

Ogarabe issued the directive while unveiling his policing priorities during his maiden address to officers at the State Command Headquarters, GRA, Enugu, on November 17, 2026.

The new CP also pledged to strengthen professional, intelligence-led and people-centred policing in the state.

He took over from CP Mamman Bitrus Giwa, who has been redeployed to the Force Criminal Investigation Department, Abuja, to head the Special Enquiry Bureau.

According to a statement issued by the Police Public Relations Officer, SP Daniel Ndukwe, Ogarabe pledged “to build a professional, disciplined, intelligence-led, technology-driven and people-oriented Command focused on crime prevention, protection of lives and property, and effective response to security threats.”

Outlining his priorities, the commissioner listed intelligence-led policing, decisive action against violent crimes, police visibility, professional investigation, community partnership, respect for human rights, personnel welfare and accountability as key focus areas.

He warned officers against “partisanship, corruption, extortion, abuse of power and other forms of unprofessional conduct,” insisting that personnel must “respect citizens’ rights, constituted authorities and traditional institutions, remain politically neutral and strictly comply with the law and court orders.”

Ogarabe charged officers to take responsibility for security within their respective areas of jurisdiction and adopt proactive policing. He also directed them to “promptly report political and election-related incidents to him within three hours of occurrence.”

He further directed the reinvigoration of the command’s X-Squad and other discipline-enforcing units to strengthen oversight and address misconduct, declaring zero tolerance for extortion and all forms of corruption.

A native of Ohaji/Egbema Local Government Area of Imo State, Ogarabe holds a Bachelor of Science degree in Political Science from the University of Nigeria, Nsukka, and a Master of Science degree in International Law and Diplomacy from Enugu State University of Science and Technology.

The new CP joined the Nigeria Police Force as a Cadet Assistant Superintendent of Police and was commissioned in 1994, beginning his career in Enugu State Command, where he served as Divisional Police Officer of the then Trade Fair Police Station.

He subsequently served as Officer in Charge of General Investigation, State CID, Abia State Command, before returning to Enugu, where he served as Chief Security Officer to two successive governors of the state.

He also served as Assistant Commissioner of Police and Deputy Commissioner of Police in charge of the command’s Criminal Investigation Department, as well as Deputy Commissioner of Police, Force CID Annex, Enugu, and Deputy Commissioner of Police in charge of Finance and Administration, Anambra State Command.

Following his promotion to the rank of Commissioner of Police, he served at the Office of the National Security Adviser, Abuja, and subsequently as Commissioner of Police, Independent National Electoral Commission, Abuja. Before his present posting, he was Commissioner of Police, INTERPOL Annex, Lagos.

Ogarabe is a professional member of the National Institute of Police Studies, where he attended the Institute Strategic Leadership and Command Course. He has also attended other professional courses, including the Chief Security Officers’ Course, Junior Command Course and Advanced Detective Course.

With over 30 years of policing experience spanning operations, criminal investigation and administration, the new CP assured residents of his commitment to “professional, disciplined, intelligence-led, preventive and people-centred policing, with emphasis on community partnership.”

He pledged to align the command’s policing strategies with the vision and mission of the Inspector-General of Police, IGP Olatunji Rilwan Disu, and “solicits the cooperation and support of residents and other stakeholders in maintaining peace, security and public order across the State.”

Ogarabe assured residents of “professional, impartial and people-oriented policing,” while calling on officers to embrace “discipline, integrity, courage and teamwork in the collective pursuit of a safer Enugu State and a Police Command worthy of public trust.”

He is married with children. His interests include football, physical exercise and philanthropy.

The post New Enugu CP pledges people-centred policing, warns against extortion appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: FG equips 15 tertiary institutions with 68.2MW off-grid power capacity
description:
…REA’s Energising Education Programme targets improved electricity supply to universities



By Udeme Akpan, Energy Editor



The Federal Government has equipped 15 tertiary institutions across the country with off-grid electricity systems having a combined installed capacity of 68.2 megawatts (MW),
content:
…REA’s Energising Education Programme targets improved electricity supply to universities

By Udeme Akpan, Energy Editor

The Federal Government has equipped 15 tertiary institutions across the country with off-grid electricity systems having a combined installed capacity of 68.2 megawatts (MW), under the Energising Education Programme (EEP) of the Rural Electrification Agency (REA).

The initiative is aimed at providing reliable electricity to universities and other tertiary institutions, reducing their dependence on the national grid and improving power supply for teaching, research and healthcare services.

According to a report titled Powering Tertiary Institutions through the Energising Education Programme, obtained from the REA, the University of Maiduguri and the University of Maiduguri Teaching Hospital have a combined installed capacity of 12MW.

The report showed that the University of Calabar and its Teaching Hospital have an installed capacity of 7MW, while Michael Okpara Federal University of Agriculture, Umudike, Abia State, has 3MW.

The Federal University of Agriculture, Abeokuta, Ogun State, and Yakubu Gowon University, formerly the University of Abuja, FCT, have installed capacities of 3MW each, while the Nigerian Defence Academy, Kaduna State, has 2.5MW.

It also indicated that the Federal University, Gashua, Yobe State, has an installed capacity of 1.5MW; the University of Port Harcourt, 10.7MW; and the Federal University of Technology, Owerri, Imo State, 8.2MW.

Other beneficiaries include Modibbo Adama University of Technology, Adamawa State, with an installed capacity of 5MW; the Federal University of Technology, Akure, Ondo State, 4.5MW; and the University of Uyo, Akwa Ibom State, 2.6MW.

The Federal University, Dutsin-Ma, Katsina State, has an installed capacity of 1.9MW; Federal University Lokoja, Kogi State, 1.7MW; and Federal University of Lafia, Nasarawa State, 1.6MW.

The report credited REA Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer, Abba Abubakar Aliyu, with repositioning the agency and strengthening its role in renewable energy deployment, investment mobilisation and local content development.

It stated: “Leading the charge at the REA is Abba Abubakar Aliyu, the Managing Director/CEO of the agency, whose 3+ years of leadership have repositioned the Agency as a global impact delivery institution and strategic platform for renewable energy scale-up, investment, and local content development.”

On the agency’s broader vision, the report said: “Aliyu’s approach reflects a broader vision: transforming Nigeria’s energy access challenge into one of the most compelling investment opportunities in the developing world and positioning Nigeria as the renewable energy hub of the African continent.”

It added that Aliyu was leveraging more than 20 years of experience in the public and private sectors to attract capital, coordinate national electrification programmes and ensure that renewable energy solutions were deployed where they could deliver the greatest socio-economic impact.

According to the report, “Aliyu’s leadership at the REA is advancing the deployment of utility-scale renewable energy infrastructure across the country.”

The post FG equips 15 tertiary institutions with 68.2MW off-grid power capacity appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Nasarawa gov seeks global support for PR varsity
description: Nasarawa State Governor, Abdullahi Sule, on Tuesday called on international public relations practitioners to support the proposed University of Public Relations and Leadership in the state, urging them to maintain their relationship with the institution through professional engagements and training
content:
Nasarawa State Governor, Abdullahi Sule, on Tuesday called on international public relations practitioners to support the proposed University of Public Relations and Leadership in the state, urging them to maintain their relationship with the institution through professional engagements and training.

Sule said the university, being established in partnership with the Nigerian Institute of Public Relations, would provide an opportunity for practitioners across the world to contribute to leadership development and strengthen the public relations profession.

The governor made the appeal at the 25th Global Alliance Gala Dinner and World Public Relations Awards in Abuja, where he welcomed delegates and practitioners from different countries.

He said the international gathering had brought global attention to Abuja, expressing optimism that the delegates would extend their engagements to Nasarawa State.

Sule described public relations as inseparable from effective leadership, saying the proposed institution reflected his state’s commitment to promoting the profession and developing future leaders.

“I have always loved public relations because, to me, public relations is leadership, and leadership is public relations,” he said.

He urged the practitioners to visit the state regularly, either for professional gatherings or training at the proposed university.

“That is why the only university of public relations and leadership is in Nigeria, in my state. We strongly believe that we should continue to see you here, again and again. If we do not see you at a forum, we hope to see you coming for training at that university. That is the whole idea,” he said.

The University of Public Relations and Leadership is expected to be located in Gudi, Akwanga Local Government Area of Nasarawa State.

The project followed a Memorandum of Understanding signed in July 2025 between the NIPR and the Nasarawa State Government.

The institution, expected to be unveiled in November 2026 during the World Public Relations Forum in Nigeria, is designed to make public relations and leadership core components of tertiary education.

At the signing of the agreement, NIPR President, Dr Ike Neliaku, described the university as a global project supported by 126 countries through the Global Alliance for Public Relations and Communication.

Neliaku said the initiative was conceived to address leadership and governance challenges in Africa, which he identified as major impediments to the continent’s development.

Under the agreement, Nasarawa State is expected to receive at least 20 annual scholarship slots for qualified indigenes, with representation from each of the state’s 13 local government areas.

The arrangement also provides 50 concessionary admission slots annually for qualified candidates sponsored by the state government.

Sule had pledged that his administration would provide the necessary support to ensure the commencement of academic activities, describing the university as an opportunity to make Nasarawa a hub for manpower development and leadership training.

The post Nasarawa gov seeks global support for PR varsity appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Nigeria, others lose $125bn yearly to illicit financial flows, $80bn to corruption — AU anti-graft body
description:
By Luminous Jannamike & Folarin Kehinde



ABUJA – Nigeria and other countries across Africa lose an estimated $125 billion annually to illicit financial flows and another $80 billion to corruption, with the losses potentially representing 50 per cent of the continent’s domestic revenue mobilisation
content:
By Luminous Jannamike & Folarin Kehinde

ABUJA – Nigeria and other countries across Africa lose an estimated $125 billion annually to illicit financial flows and another $80 billion to corruption, with the losses potentially representing 50 per cent of the continent’s domestic revenue mobilisation and 25 per cent of its Gross Domestic Product (GDP), African Union’s anti-graft body has said.

The staggering losses show how corruption and illicit financial transactions are draining resources that could otherwise finance development, strengthen public institutions and improve the lives of millions of Africans. The African Union is now seeking stronger asset recovery mechanisms and international cooperation to reverse the trend.

Chairman of the African Union Advisory Board Against Corruption (AUABC), Hon. Kwami Senanu, disclosed the figures at the First General Assembly of the African Asset Recovery Practitioners’ Forum (AARP-F) in Abuja, calling for urgent action to ensure that stolen wealth is recovered and put to productive use.

Senanu said estimates by the AU’s United Nations partners put annual losses to corruption at about $80 billion, while other stakeholders on the continent estimated that illicit financial flows cost Africa approximately $125 billion yearly.

“It is a fact that Africa continues to lose vast amounts of resources every year to corruption and illicit financial flows. Our UN partners put in about $80 billion annually.

“Some other stakeholders on the continent look at about $125 billion being lost annually just to illicit financial flows. Approximately, perhaps about 50% of our domestic revenue mobilization and 25% of GDP is being lost, this is a very important issue,” he said.

He urged African countries to move beyond declarations and commitments to concrete action, insisting that recovered assets must be returned, retained and managed in ways that directly benefit citizens.

“Beyond our convictions and commitments, let us leave Abuja with plans and sustained actions that ensure that under CAPAR, under this Forum and under this General Assembly, we will have assets recovered, we will have assets retained, and assets managed in ways that absolutely benefit our continent,” Senanu said.

Also speaking, Chairman of the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC), Dr Musa Adamu Aliyu, SAN, said the increasingly sophisticated and transnational nature of corruption had made asset recovery more difficult, with stolen wealth concealed, transferred or invested across multiple jurisdictions through complex financial arrangements designed to frustrate investigations.

Aliyu, who also chairs the Interim Steering Council of AARP-F, said no country or institution could effectively confront the challenge in isolation, stressing the need for mutual trust, sustained cooperation, timely information exchange, specialised expertise and collaboration across legal and institutional boundaries.

He said asset recovery should be treated not merely as an enforcement or financial investigation exercise but as an essential instrument of accountability, national development and protection of public resources.

The ICPC chairman warned that every resource lost through corruption represented an opportunity denied to Africans, particularly in education, healthcare, infrastructure, security, employment and other essential public services.

He stressed that the responsibility of African countries must not end with identifying and recovering stolen assets but must extend to ensuring that the proceeds are returned and managed in accordance with applicable laws and procedures in the public interest.

Aliyu identified six strategic priorities for strengthening the forum: institutional development and governance; capacity building and professional development; operational cooperation and information sharing; strategic partnerships; policy and legal development; and sustainability and resource mobilisation.

He said the priorities must translate into practical programmes backed by clear responsibilities, realistic timelines and measurable indicators of progress.

In his remarks, the African Union Commissioner for Political Affairs, Peace and Security, Ambassador Bankole Adeoye, represented by Commissioner Isiaka Garba, reaffirmed the African Union’s commitment to strengthening governance, promoting integrity in public institutions and improving cooperation in recovering and returning illicitly acquired assets.

Adeoye said the AU was moving beyond policy formulation and advocacy towards implementation, institutional strengthening and practical cooperation among member states through frameworks such as the African Union Convention on Preventing and Combating Corruption and the Common African Position on Asset Recovery (CAPAR).

He disclosed that the African Union Commission was developing a draft CAPAR Compliance Monitoring Tool to strengthen accountability and help member states assess their progress in implementing agreed continental commitments.

The Commission, he added, was also conducting a continental study on mutual legal assistance in Africa to identify practical ways of improving cross-border cooperation in criminal investigations, asset tracing and recovery. Both initiatives are expected to be considered at the General Assembly.

Adeoye identified four priorities requiring continental attention: stronger international cooperation, transparency and financial integrity, inclusive international tax cooperation, and investment in implementation and institutional resilience.

He said the true measure of asset recovery should go beyond the value of money retrieved to whether recovered resources improve public services, strengthen institutions, restore public confidence and deliver better development outcomes for African citizens.

The four-day General Assembly, holding from November 17 to 20, 2026, in Abuja, is themed, ‘From Commitment to Action: Enhancing Africa’s Asset Recovery Architecture through Effective Implementation of the Common African Position on Asset Recovery (CAPAR).’

The meeting is expected to validate the forum’s proposed work plan, elect its Steering Council and formally transfer leadership from the Interim Steering Council to the newly elected council.

The post Nigeria, others lose $125bn yearly to illicit financial flows, $80bn to corruption — AU anti-graft body appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: 2027: Coalition gives candidates 48 hours to curb political violence
description:
…Urges political leaders to promote peaceful campaigns ahead of elections



By Luminous Jannamike



ABUJA — The Coalition Against Electoral Violence in Nigeria (CAEVN) has given presidential candidates a 48-hour ultimatum to publicly caution their supporters against political violence ahead of the
content:
…Urges political leaders to promote peaceful campaigns ahead of elections

By Luminous Jannamike

ABUJA — The Coalition Against Electoral Violence in Nigeria (CAEVN) has given presidential candidates a 48-hour ultimatum to publicly caution their supporters against political violence ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The coalition warned that failure to address rising tensions at political gatherings could undermine public safety and threaten the peaceful conduct of the elections.

Addressing a press conference in Abuja, the coalition’s spokesperson, Dr Opialu Fabian Opialu, expressed concern over reports of confrontations at political events, the use of dangerous weapons and disruptions of campaign activities in parts of the country.

He said Nigeria must avoid a return to the violence associated with previous election seasons, urging political leaders to take responsibility for the conduct of their supporters.

“Nigeria is sliding back into the familiar pattern of election-season bloodshed, and the warning signs can no longer be ignored.

“If nothing is done, we may not be alive to witness another general elections,” Opialu warned.

The coalition referred to a town hall meeting organised by the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in Oregun, Lagos, as one of the recent political gatherings at which violence was reportedly recorded.

According to Opialu, the incident allegedly involved the use of cutlasses, cudgels and stones, with reports of injuries and damage to vehicles.

The coalition also expressed concern over reported tensions surrounding political activities in Asaba, Calabar, Enugu, Ebonyi, Warri and Benue.

It called on political parties and their candidates to ensure that their supporters conduct themselves peacefully and respect the rights of other political groups.

CAEVN stressed that its concerns extended across party lines, noting that reports of attacks, disruptions of political activities and destruction of campaign materials should be investigated by the appropriate authorities.

The group also expressed concern over reported disagreements between rival factions of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Gombe State over candidates and party structures.

It identified Delta, Cross River, Ekiti, Kebbi, Enugu, Ebonyi and Oyo as states where reported political confrontations, disruptions of meetings and other security concerns required attention.

The coalition called on the Inspector-General of Police and state commissioners of police to investigate reported incidents of political violence and ensure that anyone found culpable was dealt with in accordance with the law, irrespective of political affiliation.

It also urged the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) and security agencies to take appropriate measures to prevent violence and safeguard the electoral process.

Specifically, the coalition demanded that presidential candidates of the NDC, All Progressives Congress (APC), PDP, African Democratic Congress (ADC) and African Action Congress (AAC) publicly instruct their supporters to shun political violence within 48 hours.

“All presidential candidates, especially those of the NDC, APC, PDP, ADC and AAC, must publicly instruct their supporters to stop all forms of thuggery within 48 hours,” it said.

CAEVN further appealed to traditional rulers, religious leaders and community elders to use their influence to promote peaceful coexistence and discourage young people from being drawn into political confrontations.

“Traditional rulers, religious leaders and community elders must stop looking the other way. Your sons are the ones being used as foot soldiers. Speak up now,” the coalition said.

The group reiterated the need for political parties, candidates and their supporters to embrace peaceful engagement and respect democratic principles as preparations for the 2027 general elections gather momentum.

title: 2027: Nnaji inaugurates PDP campaign coordinators in Enugu
description:
Promises tax relief, stable electricity, industrialisation



By Chinedu Adonu



The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) governorship candidate in Enugu State, Chief Uche Nnaji, has inaugurated ward and local government campaign coordinators as part of efforts to strengthen the party’s grassroots mobili
content:
Promises tax relief, stable electricity, industrialisation

By Chinedu Adonu

The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) governorship candidate in Enugu State, Chief Uche Nnaji, has inaugurated ward and local government campaign coordinators as part of efforts to strengthen the party’s grassroots mobilisation ahead of the 2027 governorship election.

Nnaji, who spoke after the inauguration, expressed confidence in the coordinators’ ability to sell his manifesto to voters, claiming that his campaign already enjoyed more than 80 per cent support among residents of the state.

He charged the coordinators to take his message of recovery, rebuilding and industrialisation to every community, promising that his administration would prioritise economic growth, job creation and improved living conditions.

“Precisely, that’s why we picked them. The people here, you can see that their job will be very easy. We enjoy more than 80 per cent of our people’s support,” he said.

He, however, urged them to intensify efforts to expand the party’s support base, insisting that his campaign offered residents an alternative on the future direction of the state.

Outlining his economic blueprint, the PDP candidate promised to eliminate multiple taxation, reduce the cost of governance and create an enabling environment for businesses to thrive.

He argued that governance should focus on improving the economic well-being of the people rather than generating revenue at their expense.

“Governance is not about making money. Governance is about creating an enabling environment for your people to prosper. You make your people make money and live a good life,” Nnaji said.

He accused the incumbent administration of imposing multiple levies on residents, particularly property owners, arguing that the tax burden had worsened the economic difficulties facing households and businesses.

He promised to review the state’s tax regime and eliminate what he described as unnecessary and overlapping charges.

On industrialisation, Nnaji identified electricity as a critical requirement for economic development, promising to connect the state to the national grid and establish an effective power supply system to support industries.

“We are going to have industries, and industry is a good thing for our people. We will start by connecting to the grid and developing effective power supply to our people of Enugu. That way, industries will be stable, more industries will come in, and our people will be okay. Employment will soar,” he said.

He also pledged to rebuild markets destroyed in the state and stimulate economic activities through industrial development.

On the 2027 elections, the PDP candidate urged residents to protect their votes and resist attempts by politicians to influence their electoral choices through financial inducements.

He advised voters to collect money offered by politicians but reject them at the ballot box, alleging that public resources were being deployed to sway the electorate.

“Take the money! It is not their money. They came empty-handed. It is now they are acquiring properties, buying cars and houses. It is not their money and it can never be their money,” he said.

Nnaji cited Osun State as an example of voters standing firm to defend their electoral choices.

Also speaking, former Deputy Speaker of the Enugu State House of Assembly and Diaspora Community Coordinator, Rt. Hon. Barr. Jonathan Chukwuma, pledged the support of Enugu indigenes in the diaspora for Nnaji’s governorship ambition.

Chukwuma, who resides in Georgia, United States, said Nigerians living abroad understood the importance of good governance and were prepared to contribute to bringing the desired change to Enugu State.

The Director-General of the campaign, Charles Ndukwe, said the coordinators were carefully selected following interviews and interactions to assess their understanding of the campaign’s vision and commitment to its success.

He expressed confidence that they would work towards actualising the party’s ambition in the 2027 governorship election.

The Enugu State PDP Secretary, Chukwunonye Okereke, also expressed confidence in Nnaji’s governance blueprint, saying his experience in the business sector positioned him to contribute to the state’s economic development.

Okereke said Nnaji’s experience would enable him to make meaningful contributions across various sectors of the state’s economy.

title: Lagos moves to convert $50bn climate target into investments
description: The Lagos State Government says investors have begun expressing interest in partnerships across its climate investment projects, following engagements with financial institutions, energy companies and project developers at the ongoing 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference in Antalya, Türkiye
content:
The Lagos State Government says investors have begun expressing interest in partnerships across its climate investment projects, following engagements with financial institutions, energy companies and project developers at the ongoing 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference in Antalya, Türkiye.

The discussions have produced initial partnership opportunities in healthcare, solar energy, women’s empowerment and clean transportation, as the state seeks to turn its previously unveiled $25bn-$50bn investment pipeline into bankable projects.

The engagements followed the presentation of more than 300 potential climate projects by the state, with investors participating in project pitches, exchanging contacts and exploring financing arrangements with government representatives and local businesses.

In a statement issued on Tuesday following a reception at the Lagos Climate Investment Day, which capped a week-long engagement with investors, the Special Adviser to the Governor on Climate Change and Circular Economy, Titilayo Oshodi, said the interactions had strengthened the state’s confidence in its ability to attract private capital for climate investments.

She said, “We’ve brought in the public sector. We’ve brought in the private sector. We’ve brought in young enterprises who are already doing stuff in the green economy. We’ve brought in financial institutions who are ready to show that where we can take the risk, we can begin to fix green finance.

“We have experimented with these things and we have seen that there’s a possibility in them, and it gives us a lot of confidence right now. So, I just want to say thank you to our financial institutions, once again, Sterling Bank, for taking the pain, for taking a shot at us, taking a chance on government.”

Oshodi disclosed that project developers and investors had held discussions after a full day of presentations, with participants asking questions and exploring possible areas of cooperation.

“We had a full day of pitches just a few hours ago. The investors that we brought in asked questions, they were exchanging cards. They were having conversations to discover themselves, and they are beginning to look at what is possible going beyond now,” she said.

She added that the objective was to move beyond announcements and ensure that investment discussions translated into projects, employment and improved living conditions.

“Let’s carry this momentum. Let’s take it along with us. Let’s turn our pledges into projects. Let’s turn our projects into jobs. Let’s turn our jobs into real impact for Lagos State and, by extension, for Nigeria,” she said.

One of the private-sector partners, Tonye Cole, said the initiative provided an opportunity to connect international capital with sustainable development projects and businesses across Africa.

Cole, who said he had spent decades developing and financing sustainable projects, explained that he had worked with his partner, Funke Shobanjo, to establish a platform connecting available global funding with investment opportunities at the grassroots.

He said, “Together, we have developed this platform, and the platform works. What we are now working with Lagos State Government to bring to COP is the opportunity to partner with businesses like ours, with the state government, to develop and work on how sustainable projects and finance can meet the people that need it the most.

“This is an invitation to help you make a difference in a world that needs a difference. Let’s work together to make this happen.”

The Chief Operating Officer of FBNQuest Merchant Bank, Funke Shobanjo, also pledged support for the initiative, saying private investors were prepared to provide financing through a pan-African sustainable finance platform.

She said, “We are extremely excited about what Lagos State is doing, and we are passionate about driving the climate ambition forward for the projects under the umbrella.

“Our commitment is in private individuals coming together to provide capital and financing through a pan-African sustainable finance platform. I want to congratulate Lagos State on this goal and ambition and commit, on behalf of my co-founder and myself, our support to see the projects in the pipeline.”

The early engagements have also produced interest in social-sector projects. A member of the Lagos delegation disclosed that five investors had indicated willingness to partner with projects, including healthcare insurance initiatives aimed at reducing out-of-pocket medical expenses.

The delegate said Sterling Bank had also indicated support for providing between 50 and 100 tricycles for women’s empowerment programmes in Lagos, while Worldwide Energy had promised to solarise a primary healthcare centre.

Climate and carbon asset expert, Dr Adebola Odunsi, described the engagements as an opportunity to unlock economic value through partnerships across states and sectors.

He said the waste generated in one state could serve as raw material for businesses in another, creating opportunities for trade, investment and shared climate benefits.

“The waste that is being generated in one state can become the raw material in another state. So very soon, there are trade opportunities and climate outcome opportunities that we can share, all for the shared climate prosperity of our beautiful country, Nigeria,” Odunsi said.

He added that the investment platform had taken years of work to develop and had attracted considerable interest from international stakeholders.

The engagements come as Lagos seeks to bridge the financing gap between its climate ambitions and actual project delivery. Its previously announced pipeline covers more than 300 potential projects across clean energy, transportation, water management, climate resilience, circular economy, agriculture and green enterprise.

In a related development, the Lagos State Commissioner for Energy and Mineral Resources, Biodun Ogunleye, has identified private capital as a critical factor to addressing the state’s electricity supply deficit and financing its energy transition.

He said Lagos, with an estimated electricity demand of 12,000 megawatts, could not depend solely on government resources to finance the infrastructure required to bridge the gap.

“Our goal as government is to create an enabling environment and not to generate the power ourselves. But reforms alone must not build power plants. Indeed, capital does.

“Government balance sheet alone cannot fund the investment that we know is required,” Ogunleye said.

He disclosed that the state was targeting an additional 2,000 megawatts of electricity capacity and had established regulatory institutions to encourage private investment across generation, distribution and mini-grid development.

Ogunleye urged investors to take advantage of financing mechanisms, including the Global Fund for Infrastructure and Investment Finance, to support project preparation and reduce investment risks.

He said, “Government provides legitimacy, enabling policy and a pipeline, while the private sector provides structuring, capital, credit decisions and asset management.”

He added that the state was ready to share priority projects with financing partners and explore guarantees and other risk-sharing arrangements to make the investments attractive to lenders.

The post Lagos moves to convert $50bn climate target into investments appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Kano Govt pledges ₦100m, donates bus to Legal Aid Council
description:
The Kano State Government has pledged ₦100 million and a brand-new operational bus to the Legal Aid Council of Nigeria to strengthen the delivery of free legal services to indigent and vulnerable citizens.







Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf announced the support when he received the Chairman of the Go
content:
The Kano State Government has pledged ₦100 million and a brand-new operational bus to the Legal Aid Council of Nigeria to strengthen the delivery of free legal services to indigent and vulnerable citizens.

Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf announced the support when he received the Chairman of the Governing Board of the Legal Aid Council of Nigeria, Justice Sulaiman Durosinlorun Kawu, alongside the Director-General, management team and other officials of the Council during a courtesy visit to the Government House, Kano.

The governor said poverty should not deprive anyone of access to justice, stressing that no indigent or vulnerable citizen should remain in detention without legal representation simply because of a lack of financial resources.

He commended the Council for its contributions to the administration of justice, particularly its provision of free legal representation and assistance to Nigerians who cannot afford the services of private legal practitioners.

Yusuf reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to strengthening its partnership with the Council, promising necessary logistical, administrative and financial support within available resources.

As part of efforts to improve the Council’s operations in the state, the governor directed the commissioners for Justice and Works to assess its office facilities for possible renovation and upgrading.

He also ordered improvements in office furniture and electricity supply to provide a more conducive working environment.

In addition to the ₦100 million pledged to the Council’s national headquarters, Yusuf assured its Kano State office of continued financial assistance and promised a new bus to facilitate its operations and outreach activities across the state.

The governor urged government institutions, particularly agencies in the justice sector, to cooperate with the Council to enable it to discharge its responsibilities effectively.

He also called on Nigerians to sustain peaceful coexistence, support national development and pray for the country’s leaders, while urging collective commitment to ensuring free, fair and peaceful conduct of the 2027 general elections.

Earlier, Kawu commended the governor for his commitment to the welfare and development of Kano State.

He explained that the Council’s visit was part of its working tour of the North-West geopolitical zone, aimed at strengthening partnerships with state governments, assessing the delivery of legal aid services and promoting wider access to justice.

Kawu disclosed that the Council provided legal assistance to approximately 2,500 people in Kano State between 2021 and 2023.

He added that the Council had also facilitated the release of about 20 inmates by paying fines and court-ordered compensation on behalf of individuals who could not afford the payments.

The chairman noted that Kano occupied a strategic position in the administration of justice in the North-West, particularly because of its large custodial facilities and the significant number of awaiting-trial inmates requiring legal representation.

He appealed to the state government to further support the Council through the provision of operational vehicles, improved office facilities, information technology equipment and annual financial subventions.

According to him, such assistance would enhance the delivery of legal aid services across the state.

Kawu maintained that access to justice should not be determined by an individual’s financial circumstances, reaffirming the Council’s commitment to protecting the constitutional rights of indigent Nigerians.

The statement was signed by the Kano State Commissioner for Information and Internal Affairs, Sunusi Bature Dawakin Tofa, and dated November 17, 2026.

title: Jimmy Odukoya: Inside the Fountain of Life leadership crisis
description:
Two groups within The Fountain of Life Church are making competing claims over the leadership of the Lagos-based ministry, following an announcement that Pastor Jimmy Odukoya had been removed as senior pastor.
The leadership crisis at The Fountain of Life Church, Lagos, escalated on Tuesday, Novembe
content:
Two groups within The Fountain of Life Church are making competing claims over the leadership of the Lagos-based ministry, following an announcement that Pastor Jimmy Odukoya had been removed as senior pastor.

The leadership crisis at The Fountain of Life Church, Lagos, escalated on Tuesday, November 17, after a group of trustees announced that Pastor Jimmy Odukoya was no longer recognised as the church’s senior pastor, citing the late founder’s succession instructions.

The announcement was, however, rejected by the church, which described the purported removal as constitutionally invalid and maintained that Odukoya remained its duly appointed senior pastor and chairman of the Board of Trustees.

This disagreement later intensified after the trustees released a video in which the late founder, Pastor Taiwo Odukoya, reportedly named another person as his preferred successor and appointed his son to serve as an administrative assistant to that person.

The trustees also announced an interim leader, while citing concerns about Odukoya’s recent remarriage and other unresolved leadership and governance issues.

Here is what has happened so far.

Trustees announce Jimmy Odukoya’s removal

The controversy became public on Tuesday morning when some members of the church’s Board of Trustees announced that Odukoya’s tenure as senior pastor had ended with immediate effect.

In a statement reported by PUNCH on November 17, the trustees said the decision followed a review of the church’s constitution and recorded instructions left by its founder before his death in 2023.

They said the review was intended to ensure that the leadership transition reflected Taiwo Odukoya’s wishes and complied with the church’s governing provisions.

“Consequently, Pastor Jimmy Odukoya is no longer recognised as the Senior Pastor of The Fountain of Life Church effective immediately,” the statement said.

The trustees described the decision as an institutional action taken in the interest of the church.

However, their initial announcement did not disclose the identity of the person they said the late founder had designated as his successor.

Read more: here

Church rejects the announcement, says removal is invalid

Hours after the announcement, The Fountain of Life Church issued a counterstatement rejecting the purported removal.

In a report also published on Tuesday, PUNCH quoted the church as describing the announcement as constitutionally invalid.

The church said the statement reflected the position of certain individuals who had constituted themselves into a group called “Concerned Members of the Board”, rather than a valid decision of its authorised trustees.

It maintained that Odukoya remained its duly appointed senior pastor and chairman of the Board of Trustees.

“For the avoidance of doubt, Pastor Jimmy Odukoya remains the duly appointed Senior Pastor and Chairman of the Board of Trustees of The Incorporated Trustees of The Fountain of Life Church,” the statement said.

The church further maintained that his appointment was unanimously approved by the board in September 2023.

It also alleged that the trustees behind the removal announcement had been asked to resign on March 14, 2026, over alleged repeated violations of the church’s constitution and founding principles.

According to the church, one of the trustees subsequently resigned, while the remaining individuals continued to take decisions outside the church’s constitutional framework.

The church urged members and the public to distinguish between the pronouncements of the individuals behind the removal announcement and what it described as its constitutionally authorised position.

Read more: here

Trustees release video of Taiwo Odukoya’s succession instructions

The dispute took another turn later on Tuesday when the trustees released a video recording in which the late founder reportedly named Pastor Kunle Areogun as his preferred successor.

In the video, which PUNCH said was posted by Arise TV and sighted by its correspondent, Taiwo Odukoya stated that Areogun should take over the church if he died or became incapacitated.

He also outlined a role for his son, Jimmy, in the proposed leadership arrangement.

“In case of my demise, which I don’t expect to happen soon, or a situation where I cannot write or talk, please, the next pastor of the church should be Kunle Areogun,” Taiwo said.

He added, “To be his immediate assistant, that is in terms of administration, is Jimmy Odukoya, who will be the head of the youth church.”

The late founder also said, “Everything remains the same and that’s laid out in the constitution.”

Explaining the recording, he said an aspect of the church’s constitution was being reviewed but had not been concluded.

“We’re going to do that, but if for any reason I’m not able to see that through, this is what I do,” he said.

According to the trustees, the recording was made in December 2021 at Taiwo’s request by Jimmy and witnessed by his elder brother, Pastor John Odukoya.

They claimed they did not see the video until late December 2025, more than two years after the founder’s death.

The trustees further alleged that Jimmy told the board in 2023 that his father had handed the leadership mantle to him, and that the video was not presented when the succession arrangements were being considered.

They argued that the recording could have influenced the board’s decision on his appointment.

Read more: here

Trustees appoint Rotimi Okpaise as interim leader

Following their announcement that Odukoya was no longer recognised as senior pastor, the trustees named Pastor Rotimi Okpaise as the church’s interim spiritual and administrative leader.

PUNCH reported that the appointment was announced in a fresh statement on Tuesday, with the arrangement expected to remain in place pending consultations and the establishment of a substantive leadership structure.

The trustees said the interim arrangement was intended to provide continuity while the church addressed the leadership dispute.

They also reaffirmed their November 16 resolution withdrawing recognition of Odukoya as senior pastor.

The group further alleged that individuals acting on Odukoya’s behalf had taken control of the church’s official social media accounts without its authorisation.

It warned the public that posts on those platforms should not automatically be regarded as the board’s official position, insisting that only statements signed on its behalf represented its position.

The church, however, continued to reject the trustees’ authority to remove Odukoya.

Read more: here

Trustees cite Odukoya’s remarriage as part of their concerns

The succession disagreement is not the only issue raised by the trustees.

In their statement, they also expressed concerns about Odukoya’s recent remarriage and the public blessing of his marriage, describing the development as contrary to the church’s teachings, the founders’ values and the standards expected of its spiritual leadership.

The development followed Odukoya’s introduction of his new wife, Pastor Mo Odukoya, formerly identified as Mo Jasyme, to the congregation during a Sunday service on November 1, 2026.

PUNCH had reported that Odukoya announced the marriage during the service at the church’s headquarters in Ilupeju, Lagos, after posting a photograph of two hands wearing wedding rings with the caption, “To New Beginnings”.

Pastor Jimmy told the congregation that he had been alone since assuming leadership of the church before finding a suitable partner.

Pastor Tunde Bakare of The Citadel Global Community Church was also invited to bless the couple during the service.

PUNCH reported that Bakare said the couple had married in the United States.
Odukoya was previously married to Oluwakemi Banjoko, with whom he has two children.

Jimmy’s remarriage generated public debate, particularly over the circumstances surrounding the end of his previous marriage and differing Christian views on divorce and remarriage among ministers.

The trustees said the development had caused distress among some members and brought the church into public controversy.

The church’s counterstatement, however, did not accept the trustees’ purported removal decision.

Social media reactions reflect divisions over the dispute

The announcement also generated divergent reactions on social media, with users debating the church’s succession arrangements, Odukoya’s appointment and the timing of the trustees’ decision.

Some questioned why the alleged succession video was not considered before he was appointed in 2023, while others criticised the trustees for seeking to remove him after he had led the congregation for about three years.

One user, Dr Uzoma Alaneme, questioned the timing of the development, writing: “Dem no review the video since 2023 abi na the new marriage cause the wahala?”

Another user, @zed589662, also questioned the timing, writing: “He’s been their pastor for that long. What now changed? Lol.”

Some users also challenged the practice of transferring leadership positions in religious organisations to relatives of founders, while others expressed support for Odukoya.

The reactions reflected differing views about the church’s leadership succession, the trustees’ authority and the controversy surrounding the pastor’s remarriage.

Read more: here

How Jimmy Odukoya became senior pastora

The Fountain of Life Church was founded in 1992 by Pastors Taiwo and Bimbo Odukoya.

Bimbo died on December 11, 2005, from injuries sustained in the Sosoliso Airlines Flight 1145 crash in Port Harcourt.

Taiwo (Jimmy’s father) later married South African pastor Nomthi Zulu in 2010. She died in November 2021 after battling cancer for about two years.

Late Pastor Taiwo died on August 7, 2023, aged 67, in the United States.
Following his death, Jimmy was announced as the church’s senior pastor in September 2023 and formally installed on September 30, 2023.

His sister, Pastor Tolu Odukoya-Ijogun, was appointed associate senior pastor.

The trustees now argue that the appointment did not reflect the succession arrangement contained in the late founder’s video, while the church maintains that Jimmy’s appointment was unanimously approved by the board.

What happens next?

As of the reports published on November 17, the two sides had not reached a publicly announced resolution.

The trustees maintained that Odukoya’s removal took immediate effect and appointed Okpaise as interim leader.

Church, on the other hand, insisted that the announcement was constitutionally invalid and that Odukoya remained its senior pastor and board chairman.

The dispute therefore goes beyond the announcement of a new leader.

It raises questions about the authority of the church’s trustees, the interpretation of its constitution, the validity of the 2023 appointment and how the late founder’s recorded succession instructions should be implemented.

Until the competing claims are resolved through the church’s recognised governance processes or other appropriate means, the leadership of The Fountain of Life Church remains contested.

The post Jimmy Odukoya: Inside the Fountain of Life leadership crisis appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Nigeria is US’s greatest ally in Africa — American strategist says, as Tinubu grants interview to London
description:

London made the assertion in a post on her X handle on Wednesda
content:
An American political strategist, Diana London, has described Nigeria as the United States’ greatest ally in Africa, citing the growing security partnership between the two countries under Presidents Donald Trump and Bola Tinubu.

London made the assertion in a post on her X handle on Wednesday, praising the cooperation between the Trump and Tinubu administrations in tackling terrorism and strengthening bilateral relations.

She said the security partnership was producing results and could open up wider economic and trade opportunities for both countries.

“The U.S.-Nigeria security partnership is delivering results. Peace Through Strength

“None of this happens without the ongoing partnership between President Trump and President Tinubu, their steadfast commitment to eliminating terrorists, and Nigeria’s willingness to work closely with the U.S. government.

“Because of the success of their partnership and relationship, the economic and trade opportunities are endless. The best is yet to come. Nigeria is the United States’ greatest ally in Africa,” she wrote.

In another post, London expressed appreciation for the opportunity to work with individuals representing Nigeria and promoting relations between the Nigerian government and the Trump administration.

She said, “It has been an honour to work on the team of people representing Nigeria and helping to protect religious groups and further the relationship between the Trump administration and the Nigerian government.”

Meanwhile, President Tinubu has granted an exclusive interview to London, an American political strategist and media personality.

The development was disclosed by Imran Muhammad, Senior Special Assistant on New Media to the National Chairman of the All Progressives Congress, Prof. Nentawe Yilwatda, in a post on his X handle.

Muhammad said the interview was expected to be released soon.

“President Tinubu has held an exclusive interview with Dianna London, a prominent American media personality. The interview is anticipated to be released soon,” he wrote.

The interview is expected to provide further insight into the Tinubu administration’s engagement with the United States, particularly on security cooperation and bilateral relations.

title: Beyond the Asphalt: How Jetour’s High-Octane Lagos Convoy Brought Clean Water and Hope to Iwerekun Orile
description:
On Saturday, September 19, 2026, the roar of modern horsepower met the rhythm of drumming and celebration in Iwerekun Orile, Ibeju Lekki.
Jetour Nigeria proved that the ultimate destination of any journey isn’t just where the road ends, it’s the lives transformed along the way.
As part of the “2026
content:
On Saturday, September 19, 2026, the roar of modern horsepower met the rhythm of drumming and celebration in Iwerekun Orile, Ibeju Lekki.

Jetour Nigeria proved that the ultimate destination of any journey isn’t just where the road ends, it’s the lives transformed along the way.

As part of the “2026 Jetour Africa Expedition: A Road Trip Beyond Limits,” a striking fleet featuring the Jetour Dashing, X50, X70 Plus, X90 Plus, T2, T2 PHEV, X70 PHEV, and the flagship G700, embarked on an ambitious test of endurance.

Following a vital road safety briefing by the Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC) Deputy Corps Commander Zonal Training Officer, Lagos, Mrs Esther Uzoma, and with seamless escort from the Nigeria Police Force and LASTMA, the convoy rolled out of Falomo Square, Ikoyi, turning heads across Victoria Island before pushing past the city’s glossy borders.

Drivers and enthusiasts left the comfort of tarmac behind, putting the SUVs to the ultimate test across the unforgiving, swampy, and rock-strewn trails of the Coastal Highway. Yet, the real test of the day wasn’t mechanical resilience; it was human connection.

The convoy’s final stop was the Roman Catholic Mission Primary School in Iwerekun Orile, where dust and exhaustion gave way to unbridled joy. There, Jetour officially commissioned a brand new, solar-powered borehole, delivering clean, reliable running water to a community that has spent generations yearning for it.

The reception was deeply moving. School children broke into vibrant cultural dances,

welcoming the convoy alongside elders, farmers, and market women. Beyond water, the team distributed food supplies to households, while pupils beamed with arms full of new books and refreshments.

“This is where adventure meets purpose,” said Jetour Nigeria representative Kemi Adeola. “Our mission doesn’t stop at building capable vehicles; it lives in our pledge to drive tangible progress and touch the hearts of the communities we reach.”

For the community, the impact was profound. High Chief Michael Oluwa hailed the water project as an unprecedented miracle in Iwerekun Orile’s history, pledging that the community would cherish and protect it.

Equally overcome with emotion was the school’s head teacher, Mrs. Ariyike Bakre. “This is a special lifetime gift,” Bakre said, moved by the sight of water flowing on the school

grounds. “It’s my first time seeing a solar-powered borehole. I am grateful to God for making this possible in my time, and for allowing our elders to witness this day. We cannot thank Jetour Nigeria enough, this water changes everything for our children and our people.”

The day wound down at a tranquil beach lounge, where drivers and organizers gathered to celebrate the journey over good food, music, and shared memories.

It was a fitting close to an unforgettable expedition: one that conquered demanding terrain, ignited the spirit of adventure, and left behind a lasting lifeline of clean water.

title: Heritage steps up OML 30 drilling, targets 100,000bpd
description:
Heritage Energy Operational Services Limited (HEOSL), operator of Oil Mining Lease (OML) 30, has stepped up its drilling campaign to boost production, grow reserves and unlock the asset’s hydrocarbon potential, targeting output of 100,000 barrels per day (bpd) by 2030.



The campaign is being drive
content:
Heritage Energy Operational Services Limited (HEOSL), operator of Oil Mining Lease (OML) 30, has stepped up its drilling campaign to boost production, grow reserves and unlock the asset’s hydrocarbon potential, targeting output of 100,000 barrels per day (bpd) by 2030.

The campaign is being driven by sustained capital investment, improved reservoir management, technological advancement and operational efficiency.

Assistant General Manager, Technology Portfolio Development, Adejare Oni, who represented the Chief Executive Officer, Ado Oseragbaje, at the 44th Nigerian Association of Petroleum Explorationists (NAPE) Annual International Conference and Exhibition, said the initiative was central to the company’s asset development and production growth strategy.

Oni said unlocking the full potential of OML 30 required sustained investment, better understanding of subsurface resources and disciplined operational execution.

“Achieving this ambition requires an integrated approach to asset development, combining strategic investment, effective reservoir management, operational excellence and a deeper understanding of our subsurface potential,” he stated.

He added that the company was strengthening its technological capabilities through an accelerated digital transformation agenda and implementation of its flagship Operating Management System (OMS).

According to him, the initiatives are designed to standardise processes, improve operational efficiency, strengthen performance management and enhance business decision-making.

“The future competitiveness of Nigeria’s upstream industry will depend on our ability to translate resource potential into tangible value through technical innovation, strategic investment and operational discipline,” Oni said.

Heritage Energy operates OML 30 on behalf of its joint venture partners, NNPC Exploration and Production Limited (NEPL) and Shoreline Natural Resources Limited (SNRL).

title: 2027: Diaspora group plans debate for N’Assembly Benue South candidates
description:
The incumbent Senator representing Benue South, Abba Moro, and other aspirants seeking election into the National Assembly in 2027 are set to face public scrutiny as the Idoma in Diaspora Leadership Association announces plans to organise a virtual debate.
The association said the exercise would all
content:
The incumbent Senator representing Benue South, Abba Moro, and other aspirants seeking election into the National Assembly in 2027 are set to face public scrutiny as the Idoma in Diaspora Leadership Association announces plans to organise a virtual debate.

The association said the exercise would allow candidates to present their programmes, explain their positions on issues affecting the district and convince constituents why they deserve their votes.

Its President, Edwin Ochai, disclosed this in a statement made available to PUNCH Online on Wednesday, saying the initiative was aimed at promoting accountability, informed electoral choices and political participation.

“We believe that the people deserve an opportunity to hear directly from those seeking their mandate. Leadership should not be about political promises alone; candidates must be able to articulate their vision, explain their priorities and demonstrate how they intend to address the challenges confronting our people,” he said.

According to the association, the senatorial candidates’ debate will hold on Saturday, November 21, 2026, while aspirants for the House of Representatives will have their session on Sunday, November 22.

He disclosed that both sessions are scheduled to begin at 9pm West Africa Time via Zoom.

Ochai said the initiative was also intended to strengthen the relationship between Idoma people in the diaspora and their homeland.

“Being in the diaspora does not diminish our interest in the affairs of our homeland. We remain deeply connected to the aspirations, challenges and future of the Idoma nation. We believe that contributing to the quality of leadership and representation is a responsibility that transcends geographical boundaries,” he added.

He said the debate would encourage voters to assess candidates based on their competence, ideas and commitment to development rather than party affiliations.

“Our objective is to promote informed choices. We want the people to understand what each candidate stands for, what they intend to achieve and how they plan to contribute to the development of our communities. The quality of representation we get in the National Assembly matters to the future of our people,” Ochai said.

Among the senatorial aspirants are Moro of the Peoples Democratic Party, Francis Ottah Agbo of the All Progressives Congress, David Olofu of the African Democratic Congress, Dan Onjeh of the Nigerian Democratic Congress and Samuel Onuh of the Labour Party.

The association, which has members across the United Kingdom, United States, Canada, Russia and Germany, urged Idoma people at home and abroad to participate in the debate and demand accountability from those seeking public office.

title: Tinubu Announces ₦100m Housing Loans For Nigerians, Spreads Repayment Over 20 Years
description: President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has introduced a  ₦100m affordable housing scheme for eligible Nigerians, at a fixed interest rate of 9.75 per cent. The development was revealed in a message posted on his verified X handle, @officialABAT, on Tuesday.According to him, the initiative was designed to addre
content:
President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has introduced a ₦100m affordable housing scheme for eligible Nigerians, at a fixed interest rate of 9.75 per cent.

The development was revealed in a message posted on his verified X handle, @officialABAT, on Tuesday.

According to him, the initiative was designed to address decades of difficulties Nigerians have faced in securing affordable accommodation and accessing long-term financing, with a repayment period of up to 20 years under the Federal Government’s housing finance initiative.

The President explained that eligible citizens can benefit from the programme regardless of their location or social standing.

Tinubu said that more than 2,300 Nigerians across 27 states have already accessed ₦160 billion in mortgage financing through the ₦1 trillion Ministry of Finance Incorporated Real Estate Investment Fund (MREIF), established to expand home ownership opportunities.

He further said the programmes form part of his administration’s economic reforms, which commenced in 2023, to make homeownership achievable for hardworking citizens who have spent much of their lives paying rent.

“You should not need to know a minister, a governor or anybody in the Presidential Villa to apply and benefit from these opportunities.

“These programmes are for Nigerians who meet the requirements, wherever they live and whatever their beliefs”, the President declared.

President Tinubu said the ₦1 trillion MREIF provides eligible Nigerians with access to mortgages of up to ₦100 million at a fixed interest rate of 9.75 per cent, repayable over 20 years, with an initial deposit of just 10 per cent.

He gave an explanation with a prospective homeowner buying a property valued at ₦10 million, explaining that the beneficiary would need an initial payment of ₦1 million and monthly repayments of about ₦85,400 over 20 years.

On the burden of rent on Nigerians, the President noted the uncertainty workers face as they spend decades paying landlords without acquiring homes of their own.

“Imagine paying house rent for 25 years. Your children have grown up, you are approaching retirement, and you are still worried about the next rent increase.

“This is the reality for many hardworking Nigerians. When I embarked on my economic reforms in 2023, expanding access to affordable, long-term credit was a priority”, he said.

The post Tinubu Announces ₦100m Housing Loans For Nigerians, Spreads Repayment Over 20 Years appeared first on Channels Television.

title: 20-yr-old Kano woman allegedly plots stepson’s killing to enable own son inherit father’s properties
description:
The Kano State Police Command has arrested a 20-year-old woman, Hajiya Rukayya Auwal, and three others over the alleged conspiracy, abduction and culpable homicide of her 14-year-old stepson in an alleged plot to make her son the sole heir to her husband’s properties.
Police Public Relations Officer
content:
The Kano State Police Command has arrested a 20-year-old woman, Hajiya Rukayya Auwal, and three others over the alleged conspiracy, abduction and culpable homicide of her 14-year-old stepson in an alleged plot to make her son the sole heir to her husband’s properties.

Police Public Relations Officer (PPRO) of the command, CSP Abdullahi Haruna Kiyawa disclosed this in a Tuesday statement.

According to the command, at about 4:39pm on April 29, 2026, a female resident of Danbare Quarters, Kumbotso LGA, reported that her biological son, Mahmoud Auwal, aged 14, of Sheka Quarters, Kano State, had been abducted.

“Upon receipt of the complaint, and on the direction of the Commissioner of Police, operatives of the Command’s Anti-Kidnapping Squad immediately swung into action,” the statement reads in part.

Following sustained investigative efforts and intelligence-led operations, at about 10:30am on November 3, 2026, one Muhammad Musa Isma’il, aged 20, of Sharada Quarters, Kano State, was arrested.

“During interrogation, the suspect confessed to deceiving and luring the victim on 20th April, 2026, at about 12:30pm. He further named the following persons as his accomplices: Abubakar Muhammad Isah, ‘M’, aged 27 years, of Semegu Quarters, Kano; and Auwal Muhammad, ‘M’, aged 26 years, of Dan-Agundi Quarters, Kano.

“He alleged that they conspired to kill the victim and abandoned his corpse at the scene. The corpse was later recovered by Police operatives attached to Kwalli Division while on patrol, and conveyed to Sir Muhammad Sunusi Specialist Hospital Mortuary for preservation,” the statement further reads.

All the suspects have since been arrested.

During further investigation, the suspects disclosed that they acted on the directives of the alleged mastermind and principal suspect, one Hajiya Rukayya Auwal, aged 20, of Mararaba Quarters, New Karu LGA, Nasarawa State, who was subsequently arrested.

“Discreet investigation further revealed that the principal suspect allegedly hired another set of thugs who attacked Muhammad Musa Isma’il at Mararaba, Karu LGA, Nasarawa State, in an attempt to silence him and prevent him from exposing the alleged crime,” the command said.

Further investigation revealed that the principal suspect is a co-wife of the deceased’s mother.

“The alleged motive, as disclosed during investigation, was to eliminate all four children of her husband, so that her only son would in future solely inherit his father’s properties, even though the husband is still alive,” the police said.

The command said the case would be charged to court upon completion of investigation.

The Commissioner of Police, Kano State Command, CP Ibrahim Adamu Bakori, condemned the act in the strongest terms and assured the family of the deceased and the general public that the command would leave no stone unturned in ensuring that justice is served.

The command appealed to members of the public to continue to support the police with timely and credible information that will aid in crime prevention and detection.

The post 20-yr-old Kano woman allegedly plots stepson’s killing to enable own son inherit father’s properties appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Pandemonium as fire guts shops, destroys eight vehicles in Lagos mechanic village
description:
A midnight fire has destroyed about 10 shops and eight vehicles at a mechanic village on Arowo Iyabuna Street, Olodi-Apapa, Lagos State, with property worth an estimated N100 million lost in the incident.
The fire reportedly broke out around 8:30 p.m. on Monday behind St. Margaret Catholic Church in
content:
A midnight fire has destroyed about 10 shops and eight vehicles at a mechanic village on Arowo Iyabuna Street, Olodi-Apapa, Lagos State, with property worth an estimated N100 million lost in the incident.

The fire reportedly broke out around 8:30 p.m. on Monday behind St. Margaret Catholic Church in Olodi-Apapa. However, the cause of the inferno has yet to be established.

Eyewitnesses said the fire spread through several shops stocked with automobile spare parts, destroying valuable items such as car doors, bumpers, dashboards, sunshades, radiators and fibre components.

About eight vehicles were also reportedly consumed by the flames.

The affected vehicles include Toyota Highlander, Toyota Camry, Mercedes-Benz GLE, Mercedes-Benz G-Wagon, BMW and 2022 Toyota 4Runner models.

The incident reportedly resulted in losses estimated at about N100 million, although the full extent of the damage is yet to be officially confirmed.

One of the mechanics said: “We had to start pushing some of the vehicles so that it won’t affect many more vehicles. The fire was so big and spinning in the air.

Some of the shops that got burnt had money in them. I don’t know how we are going to begin rebuilding. This fire outbreaks always happens every year during this November and December period. It is a pity.”

Another trader said: “I had already gotten home and was about to sleep when I got called that fire was consuming my shop. I had to rush here 10p.m.”
Although the inferno caused extensive damage to property, no casualty was recorded.

The Lagos State Fire and Rescue Service reportedly arrived at the scene about 9:45 p.m., and battled the fire until about 1a.m., while police personnel were also on ground to maintain order and ease the situation.

The affected traders and mechanics are said to be counting their losses, with their immediate concern being the reconstruction of the burnt shops and the rebuilding of the mechanic village to enable them resume their businesses.
At press time, the cause of the fire had not been established.

The post Pandemonium as fire guts shops, destroys eight vehicles in Lagos mechanic village appeared first on Very Nigerian.

title: Fashola links Nigeria’s cost-of-living crisis to global conflicts
description:
Former Lagos State Governor, Babatunde Fashola, has attributed part of Nigeria’s cost-of-living challenges to global economic pressures, pointing to the effects of the COVID-19 pandemic, the Russia-Ukraine war and conflicts in the Middle East.
Fashola argued that rising living costs were not peculia
content:
Former Lagos State Governor, Babatunde Fashola, has attributed part of Nigeria’s cost-of-living challenges to global economic pressures, pointing to the effects of the COVID-19 pandemic, the Russia-Ukraine war and conflicts in the Middle East.

Fashola argued that rising living costs were not peculiar to Nigeria, noting that disruptions to international energy and food supply chains had affected economies across the world.

He made the remarks on Tuesday while appearing on Channels Television’s Politics Today, where he defended the economic policies of President Bola Tinubu’s administration.

“There is no need to deny that the cost of living is now a global challenge. Any right-thinking person will concede to that, and Nigeria is not immune to that challenge,” he said.

The former Minister of Works and Housing explained that the global economy was still dealing with the consequences of the COVID-19 pandemic, which disrupted production and supply chains.

He also identified the Russia-Ukraine war as a factor affecting the availability and prices of essential commodities, particularly energy and food products.

Fashola further pointed to tensions and conflicts in the Middle East, arguing that developments in the region had implications for international energy markets and the cost of transporting goods.

To illustrate how global events influence local prices, he referred to the Strait of Hormuz, a major international shipping route for petroleum products.

“Even the tomato seller knows the Strait of Hormuz and prices his or her goods according to replacement costs now,” he said.

His comment suggested that traders were adjusting prices based on the cost of replacing goods, which could be influenced by developments in international markets.

Fashola also defended some of the Tinubu administration’s measures to ease the pressure on households, including the minimum wage review, the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND), tax reforms and the introduction of compressed natural gas (CNG).

He said the interventions were intended to address expenses affecting families, including transportation, education and other basic needs.

However, the former governor acknowledged that the measures had not yet provided sufficient relief to Nigerians, stressing that there was a difference between announcing policies and delivering their intended benefits.

“I’m not saying it is enough. There are initiatives like the introduction of CNG, but there’s a distance between policy, between programme, between projects and resources,” he said.

Fashola added that the implementation of the programmes was progressing gradually and expressed confidence that their effects would become more visible over time.

The post Fashola links Nigeria’s cost-of-living crisis to global conflicts appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.
