title: 2027: Diri predicts Tinubu’s victory in Bayelsa
description:
Bayelsa State Governor, Douye Diri, has expressed confidence that President Bola Tinubu will win the state in the forthcoming presidential election, citing the President’s commitment to advancing true federalism.
Diri spoke in Yenagoa, the state capital, on Monday during the inauguration of the Baye
content:
Bayelsa State Governor, Douye Diri, has expressed confidence that President Bola Tinubu will win the state in the forthcoming presidential election, citing the President’s commitment to advancing true federalism.

Diri spoke in Yenagoa, the state capital, on Monday during the inauguration of the Bayelsa State chapter of the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement, where the movement’s Grand Patron, Government Ekpemupolo, popularly known as Tompolo, donated campaign vehicles and other mobilisation materials.

According to a statement issued on Tuesday by the media unit of the movement, the governor said the All Progressives Congress in the state was prepared to embark on grassroots mobilisation across the three senatorial districts to secure support for Tinubu’s re-election.

“We assure you that Bayelsa is APC. APC is Bayelsa. This is just testing the microphone. By the time we go around sensitising our people across the three senatorial districts, and the main day of the campaign, the presidential campaign in Bayelsa State, is on the 15th of December, 2026. By God’s grace, Bayelsa will showcase its support for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu,” he said.

Diri expressed delight that Tompolo, whom he described as a distinguished son of Ijawland, was spearheading a support movement for the President.

Describing Bayelsa as the Jerusalem of the Ijaw nation, the governor commended the former militant leader for his commitment to the political and developmental aspirations of the Ijaw people.

“As the Ijaw people, we are very proud of our son, Government Ekpemupolo. Let us keep up this spirit. The spirit of the Ijaw man that will never die. The spirit of the Ijaw man that must get to where we are going,” Diri said.

He also linked his support for Tinubu to the President’s position on restructuring and fiscal relations between the federal and state governments.

“Federalism is key, and we have been talking about true federalism. President Tinubu has started showing signs of leading us towards true federalism. That is what we want as a people,” he added.

Speaking through his representative and Managing Director of Tantita Security Services Nigeria Limited, Chief Kestin Pondi, Tompolo urged Bayelsans to support Tinubu’s re-election, describing their votes as an appreciation of the administration’s policies and the development projects executed by Diri’s government.

He urged the supporters at the event to take the re-election campaign to communities across Bayelsa State.

title: How Kano woman plotted to kill co-wife’s four children over inheritance
description:
A 20-year-old woman and three others have been arrested over the alleged abduction and killing of a 14-year-old boy in Kano, in a suspected plot to eliminate her husband’s four children and leave their father’s properties to her only son.
The Kano State Police Command said the suspects allegedly pla
content:
A 20-year-old woman and three others have been arrested over the alleged abduction and killing of a 14-year-old boy in Kano, in a suspected plot to eliminate her husband’s four children and leave their father’s properties to her only son.

The Kano State Police Command said the suspects allegedly planned to eliminate all four children of the woman’s co-wife so that her son would become the sole heir to his father’s properties, although the man is still alive.

The state Police Public Relations Officer, Abdullahi Kiyawa, disclosed this in a statement on Monday, identifying the alleged mastermind as Hajiya Rukayya Auwal, 20, of Mararaba Quarters, New Karu Local Government Area of Nasarawa State.

According to the statement, the victim’s mother reported his disappearance on April 29, 2026. The boy, identified as Mahmoud Auwal, 14, was allegedly lured by one of the suspects nine days earlier.

The police said their Anti-Kidnapping Squad launched an investigation following the complaint and arrested the first suspect, Muhammad Musa Isma’il, 20, on November 3.

“During interrogation, the suspect confessed to deceiving and luring the victim on 20th April, 2026, at about 12:30 pm,” the statement said.

Isma’il reportedly named two other men, Abubakar Muhammad Isah, 27, and Auwal Muhammad, 26, as accomplices.

The police said the suspects allegedly conspired to kill the boy and abandoned his body at the scene.

His corpse was later recovered by officers attached to the Kwalli Police Division and taken to the mortuary at Sir Muhammad Sunusi Specialist Hospital.

Further investigation reportedly led to the arrest of Rukayya, whom the other suspects allegedly identified as the person who directed them to carry out the crime.

The statement said, “Investigation revealed that the principal suspect is a co-wife of the deceased’s mother. The alleged motive, as disclosed during investigation, was to eliminate all four children of her husband, so that her only son would in future solely inherit his father’s properties, even though the husband is still alive.”

The police also alleged that Rukayya hired another group of thugs to attack Isma’il in Mararaba, Karu Local Government Area of Nasarawa State, in an attempt to silence him and prevent him from exposing the alleged crime.

The command said the suspects would be charged in court after the completion of investigations.

The Commissioner of Police, Kano State Command, CP Ibrahim Bakori, condemned the incident, describing it as a “heinous and dastardly act”.

He assured the victim’s family and the public that the command “will leave no stone unturned in ensuring that justice is served”.

The police urged members of the public to continue providing “timely and credible information” to assist in crime prevention and detection.

The post How Kano woman plotted to kill co-wife’s four children over inheritance appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: NPA boss seeks regional port cooperation to cut cargo costs
description:
By Godwin Oritse







President of the Port Management Association of West and Central Africa (PMAWCA), Dr Abubakar Dantsoho, has called for stronger regional cooperation among ports to reduce cargo clearance delays, lower logistics costs and boost intra-African trade.







Dantsoho, who is also
content:
By Godwin Oritse

President of the Port Management Association of West and Central Africa (PMAWCA), Dr Abubakar Dantsoho, has called for stronger regional cooperation among ports to reduce cargo clearance delays, lower logistics costs and boost intra-African trade.

Dantsoho, who is also Managing Director of the Nigerian Ports Authority (NPA), made the call at the association’s 46th Annual Council and Joint Gulf of Guinea Commission-PMAWCA Forum in Malabo, Equatorial Guinea.

He urged port authorities to prioritise strategic collaboration over unhealthy competition, identifying prolonged cargo dwell time, high port charges, expensive transport corridors and poor interoperability among customs systems as major obstacles to regional trade.

He noted that the challenges particularly affected landlocked countries, including Mali, Niger, Chad and Burkina Faso, which depend on coastal ports for international trade.

Dantsoho also identified geopolitical disruptions, climate change, cyber threats and emerging maritime decarbonisation regulations as challenges requiring urgent collective action by regional port authorities.

He called for increased investment in modern port infrastructure, digital security, green port initiatives and the blue economy, including ship repair, sustainable fishing and clean marine fuels.

Warning against the implications of failing to adapt to changing global shipping regulations, he said the energy transition could reshape international shipping routes and port calls.

“Moreover, the maritime decarbonisation regulations currently taking shape at the International Maritime Organization will soon redraw global shipping routes and ports of call: any port that fails to prepare for this energy transition risks being bypassed altogether.

“Finally, rapid digitalisation, while indispensable, exposes our operations to sophisticated cyber threats that we can no longer afford to underestimate,” he said.

The PMAWCA president urged member ports to develop clear implementation roadmaps and strengthen accountability, proposing that progress on agreed resolutions be presented at the association’s 47th Annual Council.

Also speaking, Executive Secretary of the Gulf of Guinea Commission, Mr Jose Mba Abeso, called for stronger maritime security cooperation to combat illegal fishing, drug and human trafficking, as well as protect critical offshore infrastructure, including subsea cables and gas pipelines.

Similarly, Equatorial Guinea’s Minister of Environment and Blue Economy, Mr Fidel Esono Mba Eyono, stressed the importance of sustainable exploitation of marine resources, warning against pollution, illegal fishing and other activities threatening marine ecosystems.

The post NPA boss seeks regional port cooperation to cut cargo costs appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: INEC debunks claims of remote BVAS log-out, result loss
description:
The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has dismissed claims that its Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) can be remotely logged out before voting concludes.



The commission described the claims as false and misleading in a clarification issued on Tuesday through its official X
content:
The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has dismissed claims that its Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) can be remotely logged out before voting concludes.

The commission described the claims as false and misleading in a clarification issued on Tuesday through its official X account.

INEC was responding to a viral Instagram video alleging that officials could remotely log out voters from BVAS before voting ended.

The commission described the video as fabricated and misleading, urging Nigerians to disregard its claims about the system’s operation.

“For the avoidance of doubt, the commission wishes to clarify the operational procedures of the BVAS and the process for uploading polling unit results to the INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV),” it stated.

According to INEC, each polling unit receives unique login credentials, which are issued to the presiding officer on the eve of an election.

The credentials enable the official to access BVAS for voter accreditation and subsequently upload the polling unit result sheet after voting.

“The claim that the BVAS can be remotely logged out before the conclusion of accreditation and voting is false,” the commission stated.

It explained that only the poll official operating the device could log in or log out during accreditation or result uploading.

“There is no provision for remote log-out by any external individual or authority,” INEC added.

The commission also dismissed claims that election results uploaded offline could be lost.

It said the IReV application was upgraded after the 2023 general election to incorporate an offline uploading capability.

INEC recalled that some election officials were held hostage at polling units during the 2023 elections because poor connectivity prevented result uploads.

It explained that the upgrade allows officials in areas with poor or no network coverage to upload results offline before stakeholders.

“The uploaded result sheet remains securely stored on the BVAS pending successful transmission,” the commission stated.

It added that results were automatically transmitted to IReV once the device regained internet connectivity.

This happens as officials proceed from their polling units to ward collation centres, without requiring further manual intervention.

INEC assured Nigerians that BVAS and IReV operate under established procedures designed to protect electoral integrity, transparency and credibility.

It urged the public to disregard the viral video and avoid creating or sharing unverified information.

The commission advised Nigerians to rely exclusively on its official communication channels for accurate information.

“INEC remains committed to transparency, accountability and the conduct of free, fair and credible elections,” it stated.

The post INEC debunks claims of remote BVAS log-out, result loss appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Otti woos US investors to Abia at trade conference
description:
Abia State Governor Alex Otti has invited the global investment community to explore the vast economic opportunities in the State, assuring prospective investors that all investment opportunities in Abia are promising and offer prospects for long-term value creation.
 Otti gave the assurance on Tues
content:
Abia State Governor Alex Otti has invited the global investment community to explore the vast economic opportunities in the State, assuring prospective investors that all investment opportunities in Abia are promising and offer prospects for long-term value creation.

 Otti gave the assurance on Tuesday, while declaring open the US-Africa Trade and Investment Conference and Expo, AfrICANDO 2026, at the International Conference Centre (ICC), Umuahia.

The governor, who titled his speech, “Access, Opportunities and Prosperity,” said Abia has witnessed significant developments across its 17 local government areas and various sectors of the economy, creating an enabling environment for investment and business partnerships.

He said, “There is so much going on in Abia, across the local government areas, and in all the sectors of our economic and social expressions.

“All the investment opportunities in the State are promising and have been consciously set up to create long-term value for interested investors seeking to partner with our community of resilient entrepreneurs.”

 Otti noted that local government areas, government ministries and departments, manufacturers, agricultural entrepreneurs and other business interests are participating in the exhibition to showcase investment opportunities to facilitate partnerships.

He therefore urged participants to take advantage of the conference to establish business relationships and conclude investment agreements, identifying manufacturing, real estate, hospitality, agricultural value chains and information communication technology (ICT) as priority investment areas.

“I invite all of us to take time to network and see what partnership deals can be initiated and completed right here, or shortly after.

“We are specifically targeting investments in manufacturing, real estate, hospitality, agricultural value chains, ICT and others. This is for reason of the fact that the atmosphere in Abia is very conducive and supportive of those ventures,” Otti stated.

The governor identified the African Growth and Opportunity Act (AGOA), enacted by the United States Congress in 2000, and the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), established through the African Union in 2018 and adopted by 54 member States, as important frameworks for promoting sustainable economic growth.

He informed the participants that his deliberate investments in public infrastructure, security and social services have repositioned Abia, particularly Aba, as an emerging investment destination.

Otti thanked the Foundation for Democracy in Africa (FDA) and the Abia Global Chamber of Commerce for bringing the first AfrICANDO event to be hosted on the African continent to Abia State.

He noted that the state recognised the importance of the conference to artisans, small business owners, industrialists, investors and multilateral development partners.

In their separate speeches, the President of the Foundation for Democracy in Africa, Dr. Fred Oladeinde; the Mayor of Miami-Dade County, United States of America, Hon. Daniella Levine Cava; the representative of the Democratic Republic of Congo, Dr. Milenge Mwenelwata; and the Head of Sub-Office, Lagos, of the International Organisation for Migration (IOM), Mr. Ali Ibrahim Ali, commended Governor Otti for his visionary leadership and commitment to economic development, while appreciating the State for hosting the international conference.

They highlighted the importance of international partnerships and intra-African trade, with Dr. Oladeinde announcing plans to collaborate with the Abia State Government and other partners to establish an Africa Trade Development Centre in the State.

Similarly, Hon. Levine Cava expressed the readiness of Miami-Dade County to strengthen its partnership with Abia State through the Miami-Dade Gateway to Africa initiative, particularly in expanding trade, attracting investment and promoting innovation.

Earlier, the Chairman of the Local Organising Committee (LOC) of AfrICANDO 2026 and Chief of Staff to the Governor, Pastor Caleb Ajagba,, described the 27th Annual US-Africa Trade and Investment Conference as a strategic platform for unlocking Africa’s economic potential, attracting investments and accelerating industrial development.

He noted that Abia’s hosting of the international event reflects Governor Otti’s commitment to creating an enabling business environment and positioning the State as an attractive investment destination.

Similarly, the Chairman of the Abia State Diaspora Commission, Dr Okey Agbara, and the Chairman, Abia Global Chamber of Commerce, Mr James Umekwe, said AfrICANDO 2026 is a practical economic opportunity for connecting local manufacturers, agricultural processors and service providers with international buyers, investors and technical partners.

They said the conference would promote export opportunities, boost local production, create jobs and strengthen Nigeria’s access to regional and global markets through AfCFTA and AGOA.

In their goodwill messages, Dr Oladeinde and Mr Umekwe commended Governor Otti for providing the platform to host, describing it as a significant milestone in strengthening economic relations between Africa and the United States.

Also, some elder statesmen, including former Chief of Army Staff, Lt. Gen. Azubuike Ihejirika (rtd) and former presidential candidate, Mazi Sam Ohuabunwa, applauded the Governor for attracting AfrICANDO and underscored its potential for investment and development in Abia.

The post Otti woos US investors to Abia at trade conference appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Pension fund assets hit N31.8trn, as 350,000 Nigerians join scheme
description:
By Rosemary Iwunze







Nigeria’s pension industry recorded an asset growth of more than N4 trillion in eight months to August 2026, as total assets under management stood at N31.8 trillion by August 2026.







The sharp increase was buoyed by strong equity market performance, investment returns
content:
By Rosemary Iwunze

Nigeria’s pension industry recorded an asset growth of more than N4 trillion in eight months to August 2026, as total assets under management stood at N31.8 trillion by August 2026.

The sharp increase was buoyed by strong equity market performance, investment returns as well as increase in the number of contributors, with approximately 350,000 new Retirement Savings Account (RSA) registrations recorded during the period.

The Executive Secretary/Chief Executive Officer, CEO, of the Pension Fund Operators Association of Nigeria, PenOp, Mrs. Anthonia Ifeanyi-Okoro, disclosed this yesterday during the 2026 Annual Media Retreat held virtually.

According to her, the continuous increase in subscriber base is attributable to increased awareness and enforcement of the scheme in both public and private sectors of the nation’s economy.

Ifeanyi-Okoro said: “Pension assets under management had climbed to N31.8 trillion as of August 2026, reflecting the industry’s strongest growth momentum in recent years and reinforcing its expanding role in Nigeria’s financial system.

“The industry also recorded growth in its membership base, with approximately 11.3 million RSA holders, as efforts to deepen pension participation and strengthen retirement savings continued.”

Ifeanyi-Okoro attributed the expansion to improved investment performance, increased contributor enrollment and the gradual diversification of pension fund portfolios.

She noted that the equities market recorded a bullish performance during the first two quarters of 2026, contributing positively to pension fund returns.

Also speaking, Head of Branding and Communications of PenOp’s Executive Committee, Adeola Oyegbade, identified the performance of the equities market and the entry of new contributors as important drivers of pension asset growth.

She disclosed that, approximately, 350,000 Nigerians registered under the pension scheme during the period, adding that, the increase in contributors complemented investment returns in driving the industry’s asset expansion.

Oyegbade also explained that the industry’s declining exposure to Federal Government securities was part of a deliberate investment diversification strategy and should not be interpreted as a loss of confidence in government instruments.

Ifeanyi-Okoro had earlier disclosed that pension fund allocation to Federal Government securities declined from about 65 per cent at the end of 2025 to 55.9 per cent as of August 2026, as operators increased exposure to other investment opportunities.

content:
The Nigerian Bar Association has celebrated a former President of the association and Senior Advocate of Nigeria, Chief Wole Olanipekun, on his 75th birthday, describing his contributions to the legal profession as remarkable.

The NBA, in a birthday message posted on its X handle on Wednesday, praised Olanipekun’s leadership, commitment to the rule of law and dedication to the development of the legal profession.

The association described the senior lawyer as a distinguished legal practitioner whose years at the Bar had been marked by excellence, integrity, courage and service.

It said, “Today, we celebrate a distinguished Senior Advocate of Nigeria, a respected former President of the Nigerian Bar Association, and a senior colleague whose contributions to the profession continue to command respect and admiration.

“Your years at the Bar reflect a sustained commitment to excellence, integrity, courage and service.

“Through your practice and leadership, you have demonstrated that distinction in our profession carries a responsibility to uphold its standards, defend the rule of law and guide those who follow.”

The NBA also acknowledged Olanipekun’s place in the history of the association, noting that his tenure as president and continued contributions had remained significant to the legal body.

“As a former President of the NBA, you hold a special place in the life of our Association. We honour your leadership and the experience and counsel you continue to offer the Bar.

“On behalf of the Association you proudly served, I wish you many happy returns of today. Happy Birthday sir!” it added.

Olanipekun is one of Nigeria’s prominent legal practitioners and a Senior Advocate of Nigeria.

title: ‘Why we must not abort this journey mid-term,’ Fashola defends Tinubu
description:
Former Lagos State Governor, Babatunde Fashola, has urged Nigerians to consider the policies introduced by President Bola Tinubu’s administration before deciding whether to support a change of government in the 2027 general election.
Fashola argued that the country should not abandon the ongoing ref
content:
Former Lagos State Governor, Babatunde Fashola, has urged Nigerians to consider the policies introduced by President Bola Tinubu’s administration before deciding whether to support a change of government in the 2027 general election.

Fashola argued that the country should not abandon the ongoing reform process without examining what opposition parties are offering as an alternative.

He made the remarks on Tuesday during an appearance on Channels Television’s Politics Today, where he defended Tinubu’s performance and called for continuity in the implementation of the administration’s policies.

The former Minister of Works and Housing pointed to the reviewed minimum wage, the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND), tax reforms, stamp duty waivers on lease agreements and the introduction of compressed natural gas (CNG) as some of the government’s interventions.

He acknowledged that the impact of some policies was not yet fully evident but maintained that their implementation was gradually progressing.

“We are seeing the roll-out slowly, and in the fullness of time, you will see the impacts,” he said.

Fashola questioned what opposition parties intended to offer that would justify abandoning the current reform programme.

“What are the other parties offering that is different, that is better, that is compelling as a reason to interrupt the process of reform, growth, and restructuring that is already underway?” he asked.

He maintained that Nigerians should assess the alternatives being presented by political parties rather than reject the government’s policies without considering their potential outcomes.

“These are the compelling reasons why we must not abort this journey mid-term and exchange it for uncertain promises without assurances,” Fashola added.

The former governor also acknowledged the economic difficulties facing Nigerians, but argued that the administration had introduced measures intended to ease pressure on households.

He cited NELFUND as an example of a programme designed to support families with the cost of educating their children.

According to him, the government’s interventions should be assessed alongside the resources and time required to translate policy decisions into tangible results.

The post ‘Why we must not abort this journey mid-term,’ Fashola defends Tinubu appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: YPP presidential hopeful unveils plan to cut governance cost
description:
By John Alechenu



ABUJA — The presidential candidate of the Young Progressives Party (YPP), Arc. Peter Agada, has unveiled a governance model, tagged LabourDirect, which he said would reduce the cost of governance through direct labour, lower infrastructure costs and the elimination of contract in
content:
By John Alechenu

ABUJA — The presidential candidate of the Young Progressives Party (YPP), Arc. Peter Agada, has unveiled a governance model, tagged LabourDirect, which he said would reduce the cost of governance through direct labour, lower infrastructure costs and the elimination of contract inflation and financial leakages.

Agada unveiled the initiative on Tuesday during the flag-off of his presidential campaign and the presentation of his manifesto in Abuja.

Describing LabourDirect as the centrepiece of his proposed administration, he said it was designed to replace inflated contracts with a more transparent and cost-effective system of delivering public infrastructure.

He said, “Today, we do not just launch a campaign. We launch a movement, we flag off a new Nigeria.

“I stand before you to unveil my manifesto. Not a manifesto of promises. A manifesto of numbers. A manifesto of infrastructure. A manifesto of accountability. My manifesto is called LabourDirect.”

The YPP candidate identified the high cost of governance as a major factor contributing to Nigeria’s economic challenges, arguing that excessive spending on roads, buildings, electricity and water infrastructure leaves insufficient resources for education, healthcare and job creation.

He said Nigeria’s population, currently estimated at approximately 245 million, was projected to rise to 305 million in 10 years and 365 million in 20 years.

Agada also put the country’s Gross Domestic Product at $386.67 billion, while claiming that 154 million Nigerians, representing 63 per cent of the population, were living in multidimensional poverty.

“We are growing, but we are getting poorer. This is a jobless boom,” he said.

On the country’s debt burden, Agada said public debt stood at ₦166.79 trillion as of June 30, 2026, while debt servicing consumed ₦15.52 trillion, representing 45.2 per cent of government revenue.

He argued that the amount spent servicing debt had significantly reduced the resources available for critical public services.

“We spend ₦15.52 trillion, 45.2 per cent of all our revenue, just to service debt. Almost half of everything we earn goes to pay old debts. That is why we have no money for schools, hospitals, and roads,” he said.

Explaining the LabourDirect model, Agada said it would eliminate unnecessary intermediaries, ghost workers and inflated contracts, thereby reducing the cost of executing government projects.

Using road construction as an example, he claimed that while the government spends about ₦2.5 billion to construct one kilometre of road, his model could deliver the same distance for between ₦375 million and ₦500 million.

“I stand here today on a road that I built. Not with government money. Not with a loan. With LabourDirect.

“The government standard rate for a road like this is ₦2.5 billion per kilometre. I built this road for a fraction of that,” he said.

He added that the model could save between ₦2 billion and ₦2.125 billion per kilometre, representing savings of between 80 and 85 per cent.

Agada further projected that constructing 7,500 kilometres of roads under the conventional system would cost about ₦6.85 trillion, but LabourDirect could deliver the same projects for between ₦1.02 trillion and ₦1.37 trillion.

According to him, the proposed approach would save between ₦5.48 trillion and ₦5.83 trillion, which could be redirected towards building schools, clinics and electricity infrastructure.

He said the model would also introduce greater transparency and accountability by allowing Nigerians to monitor government projects through their mobile phones using the proposed LIN App or LIN Network.

“You can see every bag of cement. Every metre of road. Every naira spent. From your phone. No more ‘we cannot see the project.’ You will see it,” he said.

The presidential hopeful also unveiled what he described as a $100 billion Success Budget for the next five years, aimed at growing Nigeria’s GDP from its current $386.67 billion to $1 trillion by 2031.

He said the government would contribute $25 billion, while the LabourDirect model would unlock an additional $75 billion.

“Let us build Nigeria not with promises, but with infrastructure. Let us govern Nigeria not with circulars, but with code. Let us develop Nigeria not with borrowing, but with accountability,” Agada said.

The post YPP presidential hopeful unveils plan to cut governance cost appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: FG targets $9.3bn care economy, woos private investors
description:
IFC push investment as Lagos develops care policy framework







By Peter Egwuatu







The Federal Government is targeting a $9.3 billion care economy as it moves to attract private sector investment into childcare, elderly care and disability support services.



The initiative follows the Fede
content:
IFC push investment as Lagos develops care policy framework

By Peter Egwuatu

The Federal Government is targeting a $9.3 billion care economy as it moves to attract private sector investment into childcare, elderly care and disability support services.

The initiative follows the Federal Executive Council’s approval of the National Care Policy and Implementation Plan 2026–2030, aimed at transforming the sector into an organised industry capable of creating millions of jobs and increasing women’s participation in the economy.

Minister of Women Affairs and Social Development, Hajiya Imaan Suleiman-Ibrahim, disclosed this yesterday in Lagos at the National Care Economy Forum hosted by the World Bank Group. She was represented by the Director, Child Development Department, Ali Andrew Maduga.

“Our task is to move beyond recognising care as a social responsibility to establishing it as an organised, productive and investable component of Nigeria’s economy,” she said.

She disclosed that the Council, on October 28, 2026, also directed the Ministers of Justice and Women Affairs to develop an executive bill to provide legislative backing for the policy.

Citing UN Women’s 2026 care economy modelling, she said closing unpaid care gaps and expanding universal childcare could contribute at least $9.3 billion to Nigeria’s Gross Domestic Product and generate between 9.4 million and 17 million jobs.

She added that caregiving responsibilities accounted for 20.16 per cent of women’s withdrawal from the labour force, compared with 0.6 per cent for men.

Earlier, Head of Office, Nigeria, International Finance Corporation (IFC), Christian Mulamula, described care as economic infrastructure rather than merely a family responsibility.

“Care may begin at home, but its impact does not end at the front door. It shapes whether people, particularly women, can take up opportunities and participate fully in the economy.

“Care is economic infrastructure,” he said.

He disclosed that 92 per cent of childcare facilities were small, independently owned businesses, while 76 per cent of childcare entrepreneurs lacked access to formal finance.

“Investing in childcare is about freeing talent and productivity into the economy while giving children a strong start in life,” he added.

Meanwhile, Lagos State Governor, Babajide Sanwo-Olu, represented by Commissioner for Finance, Abayomi Oluyomi, said the state was developing an investment-oriented care policy framework.

“We want a care economy in which families can access reliable and affordable services, care providers can operate viable businesses, and those who work in the sector can earn decent livelihoods under appropriate professional standards,” he said.

Sanwo-Olu urged financial institutions, employers and private investors to support the sector, noting that government funding alone could not provide the required facilities and services.

title: EXPLAINER: Things to know about Enugu’s proposed 2% rent cap
description:
The Enugu State House of Assembly has passed a bill seeking to restrict landlords from increasing rents by more than two per cent every four years, a proposal that could significantly change the relationship between property owners and tenants if it becomes law.
The proposed amendment to the state’s
content:
The Enugu State House of Assembly has passed a bill seeking to restrict landlords from increasing rents by more than two per cent every four years, a proposal that could significantly change the relationship between property owners and tenants if it becomes law.

The proposed amendment to the state’s Landlord and Tenant Law comes amid complaints about rising accommodation costs, arbitrary rent increases, excessive agency commissions and legal fees.

Although the bill has passed its third reading, it is yet to become law, as it requires the assent of Governor Peter Mbah.

If signed, the legislation could introduce new restrictions on rent reviews, provide additional safeguards for tenants and regulate certain charges associated with securing accommodation.

Here are five things the proposed law could mean for residents of Enugu State.

1. Landlords may not increase rent every year

One of the most significant provisions of the proposed amendment is the restriction on how frequently landlords can increase rent.

Under the proposal, landlords would have to wait at least four years before increasing the rent of a property. Any subsequent increase would be limited to two per cent of the existing rent.

This means tenants could potentially enjoy greater certainty about their accommodation costs instead of facing annual or frequent rent increases.

For instance, if a tenant currently pays ₦500,000 annually, a two per cent increase would amount to ₦10,000, bringing the annual rent to ₦510,000 after the permitted review period.

Similarly, a tenant paying ₦1m annually would face a maximum two per cent increment of ₦20,000, bringing the rent to ₦1.02m.

However, the actual effect would depend on the final wording of the legislation, particularly how the four-year period and rent calculation are defined.

2. Renovated properties could attract higher rent

The proposed amendment also makes provision for landlords who undertake reasonable renovations to their properties.

In such circumstances, landlords would be permitted to increase rent by not more than 10 per cent.

This means that a property owner who carries out qualifying renovations could potentially charge a higher rent than the ordinary two per cent limit allows.

For example, if a property attracts an annual rent of ₦500,000, a 10 per cent increase would amount to ₦50,000, bringing the new rent to ₦550,000.

The provision could allow landlords to recover part of the costs of improving their properties while preventing unlimited increases.

However, the definition of reasonable renovations, the evidence required and the conditions for applying the 10 per cent increase would be important in determining how the provision works.

3. Tenants could face lower accommodation-related charges

Beyond rent increases, the proposed amendment is also intended to address complaints about excessive agency commissions and legal fees when residents seek accommodation.

Such charges can significantly increase the amount prospective tenants must pay before moving into a property.

The House committee chairman, Okey Mbah, said the legislation was designed to protect residents from exploitation by landlords and estate agents.

“This bill will subsidise over 60 per cent of what residents used to pay while trying to secure accommodation,” he said.

A previous published version of the amendment bill contained provisions requiring estate agents to obtain permits from the Enugu State Housing Development Corporation.

It also proposed limiting agency fees to 10 per cent of the rent paid by prospective tenants and legal fees for preparing tenancy agreements to 10 per cent.

However, the final version passed by the Assembly should be examined to establish whether these provisions were retained and whether additional conditions apply.

4. Landlords may face greater restrictions over eviction

The proposed reform also raises questions about the procedures landlords must follow when seeking to recover their properties from tenants.

According to a report by THISDAY, the committee chairman said the amended legislation would require landlords to properly serve tenants before initiating court proceedings.

“A tenant must be properly served before being charged to court. Without proper service, no case should be established or treated in the first instance,” Mbah said.

If retained in the final legislation, the provision could strengthen procedural protections for tenants facing eviction disputes.

It would also emphasise that landlords must follow the legally prescribed process rather than resorting to arbitrary eviction.

However, it would not mean tenants could occupy properties indefinitely without paying rent or complying with their tenancy agreements.

5. Landlords could face financial and enforcement challenges

While the proposed restrictions could offer tenants greater predictability, property owners have questioned whether the two per cent limit is sustainable in an economy where the costs of maintaining buildings, purchasing construction materials, electricity and other services continue to change.

A landlord in Enugu, Onyekwere Johnson, according to a Punch report on Tuesday, described the proposed cap as unrealistic and difficult to enforce.

“That would have been a natural law if the prices of petroleum products and electricity tariffs increased by two per cent. Otherwise, it is an unnatural law. It is neither sustainable nor can it be obeyed,” he told PUNCH.

He added, “You cannot single out landlords and regulate their business while other sectors are struggling to meet the benchmark of inflation set by the managers of the Nigerian economy. It violates landlords’ rights against discrimination.”

The disagreement raises questions about how the government would enforce the proposed restrictions, verify qualifying renovations and address disputes between landlords and tenants.

It also raises the possibility that property owners could seek other ways to adjust their charges, making effective enforcement and clear regulations important.

When will the proposed law take effect?

The Enugu State House of Assembly passed the Landlord and Tenant Amendment Bill on Tuesday, November 17, 2026, after it scaled its third reading.

The bill, which passed its second reading on March 11 and underwent a public hearing on March 26, now awaits the assent of Governor Peter Mbah.

Until the governor signs it and it commences in accordance with its provisions, the proposed restrictions should not be treated as an existing law.

If assented to, the legislation could introduce significant changes to how rents are reviewed, accommodation charges are regulated and tenancy disputes are handled across Enugu State.

title: NYSC pays Oyo corps members’ delayed allowances, blames technical glitch
description:
The National Youth Service Corps says it has paid the delayed October 2026 allowance to corps members who served in Oyo State and completed their service year on October 29.
The scheme attributed the delay to a technical glitch in the Government Integrated Financial Management Information System, th
content:
The National Youth Service Corps says it has paid the delayed October 2026 allowance to corps members who served in Oyo State and completed their service year on October 29.

The scheme attributed the delay to a technical glitch in the Government Integrated Financial Management Information System, the Federal Government platform used to process corps members’ monthly allowances.

In a statement on Tuesday, the NYSC management said the affected corps members had been paid as of November 17, adding that anyone yet to receive the money by the close of business on Wednesday should contact the Oyo State Coordinator for verification.

The statement was signed by the Director of Information and Public Relations, Caroline Embu.

The management apologised for the delay, acknowledging that the affected corps members’ complaints were justified and that the situation might have caused them hardship.

It explained that while other corps members received their October allowances before completing their service, payments to those in Oyo State were delayed by the technical problem with the GIFMIS platform.

The NYSC, however, maintained that the allowance had been fully provided for in the budget and that no corps member’s entitlement had been withheld, diverted or reduced.

It added that the allowances were paid directly into individual bank accounts from the scheme’s Central Bank of Nigeria account through the GIFMIS platform.

According to the statement, the Oyo State Coordinator had earlier informed the affected corps members about the reason for the delay.

It also disclosed that the Director-General of the NYSC, Brigadier General Olakunle Nafiu, met some of the affected corps members during his visit to the Oyo State Orientation Camp in Iseyin on Saturday, November 14.

The management said Nafiu had assured them that the payment issue would be resolved.

The statement read, “As expected, the affected Corps Members were sensitised by the Oyo State Coordinator on the cause of the delay in their payment.

“Also, on Saturday, 14 November 2026, the Director-General, Brigadier General Olakunle Nafiu, met some of the affected Corps Members in person during his visit to the Oyo State Orientation Camp in Iseyin.

“In line with the Director-General’s assurance, as of today, 17 November 2026, the affected Corps Members have been paid, and any of them not credited by close of business tomorrow, 18 November 2026, should notify the Oyo State Coordinator for necessary verification.”

The development followed complaints by corps members who served in Oyo State that they had yet to receive their October allowance after completing their service year.

The complaints attracted public attention, with some affected members taking to social media to demand payment of their entitlements.

The NYSC management said it recognised the financial importance of the monthly allowance to corps members, particularly those posted to states where they had no family or established support networks.

It described prompt payment of their allowances as an obligation rather than a favour.

“Management appreciates the fact that Corps Members leave their homes to serve in States where many know no one, and that their allowance sustains them throughout the service year.

“For this reason, it regards prompt payment of allowance to these patriotic Nigerians as a duty, not a favour,” the statement added.

The management thanked the affected corps members for their patience and members of the public who drew attention to the delay.

It also urged Nigerians to rely on the scheme’s official communication channels for clarification and avoid spreading unsubstantiated claims.

The NYSC, established in 1973, is a mandatory one-year national service programme for eligible Nigerian graduates, with participants deployed to states outside their states of origin to promote national unity and development.

title: Canada charges eight Nigerians, four others over $4.5m vehicle theft
description:
Eight Nigerians have been charged alongside four other suspects in Canada over an alleged organised vehicle theft network linked to the recovery of 96 stolen vehicles valued at more than $4.5 million and reportedly meant for export to West Africa.
Peel Regional Police in Ontario disclosed this in a
content:
Eight Nigerians have been charged alongside four other suspects in Canada over an alleged organised vehicle theft network linked to the recovery of 96 stolen vehicles valued at more than $4.5 million and reportedly meant for export to West Africa.

Peel Regional Police in Ontario disclosed this in a statement published on its official website on Monday, stating that the 12 suspects were facing a combined 231 charges following an investigation into the theft and illegal exportation of luxury sport utility vehicles, pickup trucks and other expensive vehicles.

The investigation, code-named Project Cadetta, commenced in March 2026 in collaboration with the Canada Border Services Agency.

According to the police, the operation initially focused on a warehouse in Brampton, Ontario, which was allegedly being used to keep stolen vehicles before they were transported to West Africa through Canadian ports.

However, further investigations reportedly exposed a larger criminal network operating across the Greater Toronto Area and neighbouring jurisdictions.

According to the police, five key suspects allegedly coordinated the theft, movement and exportation of the vehicles, while others supported the operation through loading sites, container movements and transportation of vehicles with altered identification numbers.

The 96 recovered vehicles were discovered concealed in shipping containers, the police said.

Those listed as Nigerian include Stanley Udeh, 46, of Brampton; Odewale Abraham, 57; Oluyemi Sodade, 51; Tosin Damilola Oyebade, 45; Oluwaseyi Olawale Bameke, 39; and Olushola Oke, 42, all of Toronto.

Others are Gbolahan Qudus Babatunde, 29, of Vaughan, and Kenneth Okafor, 58, listed as having no fixed address.

The other accused are Karamveer Singh, 26, of Brampton; Henrik Gancz, 57; Jaspreet Singh, 25, both listed as having no fixed address; and Darryl Davance, 25, of Saint-Jerome, Quebec.

The accused face various charges, including possession of property obtained by crime, trafficking in stolen goods valued at more than $5,000, forgery and uttering forged documents. One of them also faces a charge of dangerous operation of a motor vehicle.

Peel Regional Police said nine of the accused were charged and released with future court dates, while three were held for bail hearings and subsequently released.

The police added that some of the accused could face immigration enforcement action, including possible removal from Canada, after the conclusion of their criminal proceedings.

Commenting on the investigation, the Deputy Chief of Peel Regional Police, Nick Milinovich, said organised vehicle theft was connected to wider criminal activities.

“Organised auto theft is a predatory business model run by transnational syndicates that terrorise families and fund broader criminal enterprises. Through Project Cadetta, our Commercial Auto Crime Bureau and partners dismantled this supply chain from street-level thieves to international export brokers,” he said.

Ontario’s Solicitor General, Michael Kerzner, said the operation demonstrated the government’s commitment to tackling organised criminal networks.

He said, “Organised auto theft is a serious crime that threatens the safety and security of our communities, and our government will never back down from taking on the criminal networks responsible.”

The Canada Border Services Agency’s Acting Regional Director General for the Greater Toronto Area, Trishann Pascal, said the agency helped prevent stolen vehicles from reaching international markets through targeted container examinations and intelligence-sharing with law enforcement partners.

Peel Regional Police said the investigation remained ongoing, adding that further charges were anticipated and arrest warrants had been issued for additional individuals.

The police also reported that auto thefts across Peel Region had declined by more than 50 per cent since reaching a peak in 2023, with a further 10 per cent reduction recorded year-to-date in 2026.

title: 2027: ‘Never allow political ambition to undermine Nigeria’s unity’ — Jonathan warns politicians
description:
Former President Goodluck Jonathan has warned politicians against allowing their ambitions for power to threaten Nigeria’s unity, urging them to embrace tolerance, peaceful competition and respect for democratic principles ahead of the 2027 general elections.
He cautioned that political intolerance,
content:
Former President Goodluck Jonathan has warned politicians against allowing their ambitions for power to threaten Nigeria’s unity, urging them to embrace tolerance, peaceful competition and respect for democratic principles ahead of the 2027 general elections.

He cautioned that political intolerance, ethnic rivalry and electoral violence could plunge the country into crisis, expressing concern over the growing use of youths as instruments of political thuggery.

Jonathan spoke at the third edition of the Peace and Security Conference organised by the Goodluck Jonathan Foundation in Abuja, with the theme, “Safeguarding Peace and Strengthening Social Cohesion in a Competitive Political Environment.”

“We must never allow political ambition to undermine the bonds that hold us together as one nation and in our states,” he said.

The former president also expressed concern over controversies surrounding judicial pronouncements, particularly conflicting decisions by courts of coordinate jurisdiction, warning that such developments could erode public confidence in the judiciary and encourage citizens to resort to self-help.

“When citizens begin to lose faith in the courts and resort to self-help, the consequences can be disastrous. The descent from a loss of confidence in institutions to anarchy is a danger we must collectively prevent,” he said.

He urged political actors to respect opposing views and recognise the right of others to seek political office, calling on Nigerians to prioritise competence, national interest and service over prejudice and personal ambition in choosing their leaders.

Meanwhile, the Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Prof. Joash Amupitan, threatened legal action against political parties, candidates and their supporters involved in violence, intimidation and inflammatory campaigns ahead of the elections.

Represented by INEC National Commissioner, May Agbamuche-Mbu, Amupitan said political competition naturally involved vigorous debates, sharp disagreements and passionate mobilisation, but warned against allowing these to degenerate into violence and lawlessness.

He also warned against harassment, intimidation and physical attacks on INEC officials and ad hoc election workers, insisting that offenders would face legal consequences.

“I must sound a stern warning against any form of harassment, intimidation, or physical attack directed at the leadership, staff, or ad hoc workers of INEC by supporters of any political party—whether within Nigeria or abroad.

“Election officials are public servants discharging a sacred constitutional duty; assaulting or threatening them is an assault on the Nigerian state and will be met with decisive legal consequences,” he said.

Amupitan identified misinformation, disinformation, artificial intelligence-generated content, deepfake videos and cloned voices as emerging threats to peaceful elections, warning that fabricated information could trigger unrest within minutes.

He disclosed that INEC had established a dedicated Artificial Intelligence Division within its ICT department to monitor digital threats and verify online information.

The INEC chairman reaffirmed the commission’s commitment to neutrality and peaceful, credible and inclusive elections. The presidential and National Assembly elections are scheduled for January 16, 2027, while the governorship and state assembly elections will hold on February 6, 2027.

In his keynote address, former President of the ECOWAS Commission, Dr Omar Alieu Touray, warned against allowing political competition in Africa to degenerate into ethnic, religious and regional divisions.

He argued that democracy should be driven by competing ideas and development programmes rather than identity politics.

“Competition is the lifeblood of democracy. It is the mechanism through which citizens express preferences, debate ideas and hold leaders accountable. We must never confuse political competition with political conflict,” Touray said.

He said there was a fundamental difference between disagreeing with an opponent’s policies and denying the person the right to govern on the basis of ethnic, religious or regional identity.

“There is a profound difference between saying, ‘I disagree with your policies,’ and saying, ‘Because you belong to a different ethnic, religious or regional community, you do not have the right to govern me.’ The first is democracy. The second is exclusion masquerading as democracy,” he said.

In a goodwill message, the Minister of Defence, Gen. Christopher Musa (retd.), urged political leaders to demonstrate restraint, maturity and statesmanship, warning against hate speech, misinformation and inflammatory narratives capable of exploiting the country’s ethnic, religious and political divisions.

Represented by his Special Adviser on Strategic Communication, Mercy Ndi Bala, the minister said national security went beyond military deployment and equipment, stressing that public trust, social cohesion and cooperation between communities and security agencies were equally critical to maintaining stability.

He called for a whole-of-government and whole-of-society approach to security involving government institutions, traditional and religious leaders, civil society organisations, the media and young people.

Earlier, the Executive Director of the Goodluck Jonathan Foundation, Ann Iyonu, raised concerns over declining public confidence in Nigeria’s electoral process.

She cited a 2026 Afrobarometer survey released on November 11, which indicated that fewer than four in 10 Nigerians believed the 2027 elections would be free and fair.

Iyonu warned that the credibility of the elections would have implications beyond Nigeria, given the country’s economic influence and strategic importance to regional security.

title: Paz, Alvarez shines as Argentina beat Costa Rica 7-0 in international friendly
description:
Argentina recorded a convincing 7-0 victory over Costa Rica in an international friendly on Tuesday, with Nico Paz, Julian Alvarez and Franco Mastantuono scoring twice each.
Paz opened the scoring in the eighth minute after receiving an assist from Enzo Fernandez, giving Argentina an early advantage
content:
Argentina recorded a convincing 7-0 victory over Costa Rica in an international friendly on Tuesday, with Nico Paz, Julian Alvarez and Franco Mastantuono scoring twice each.

Paz opened the scoring in the eighth minute after receiving an assist from Enzo Fernandez, giving Argentina an early advantage.

Julian Alvarez extended the lead in the 35th minute, converting a pass from Agustin Giay to make it 2-0.

Argentina continued to dominate as Paz grabbed his second goal of the match just three minutes later, finishing off Maximo Perrone’s assist to put his side firmly in control.

Alvarez added his second goal in the 43rd minute, finishing a move created by Gianluca Prestianni to give Argentina a commanding 4-0 lead at half-time.

Argentina continued their dominance after the break, with Mastantuono coming off the bench to score in the 48th minute following an assist from Perrone.

title: 10 records Arsenal’s Max Dowman has broken at 16
description:
From becoming the Premier League’s youngest goalscorer to rewriting England’s under-21 records, here are 10 milestones achieved by Arsenal youngster, Max Dowman.
At just 16, Dowman has already established himself as one of the most remarkable teenage talents in English football, setting records at c
content:
From becoming the Premier League’s youngest goalscorer to rewriting England’s under-21 records, here are 10 milestones achieved by Arsenal youngster, Max Dowman.

At just 16, Dowman has already established himself as one of the most remarkable teenage talents in English football, setting records at club, domestic and international levels.

The midfielder has made history in the Premier League, UEFA Champions League and several England youth teams, surpassing milestones previously held by established footballers, including Jude Bellingham, Cesc Fabregas and Phil Foden.

Dowman’s latest achievements came during England’s under-21 international fixtures in November 2026, when he became the youngest player to feature and score for the Young Lions.

According to an article published by Arsenal on November 17, 2026, by Jonathon Rogers, the following are 10 remarkable records Dowman has set in his budding career.

1. Premier League’s youngest goalscorer

Dowman became the youngest goalscorer in Premier League history when he scored for Arsenal against Everton on March 14, 2026.

Aged 16 years and 73 days, he broke a record that had stood for almost 21 years, previously held by James Vaughan, who scored for Everton against Crystal Palace in April 2005 at 16 years and 270 days.

Dowman surpassed Vaughan’s milestone by 197 days.

2. Premier League’s youngest-ever starter

The Arsenal youngster also became the youngest player to start a Premier League match.

He achieved the feat when he was named in Arsenal’s starting XI against Crystal Palace on May 24, 2026, aged 16 years and 144 days.

He surpassed the previous record held by Everton’s Jose Baxter, who started against Blackburn Rovers in August 2008 at 16 years and 198 days.

3. Youngest player to win the Premier League

Dowman became the youngest player to win a Premier League title after Arsenal clinched the 2025/2026 championship.

Having made six top-flight appearances during the campaign, he met the requirements for a winner’s medal.

At 16 years and 144 days, he surpassed Manchester City’s Phil Foden, who was 17 years and 350 days old when he won the title in the 2017/2018 season.

4. Arsenal’s youngest-ever starter

Dowman became Arsenal’s youngest-ever starting player when he was named in the starting XI for the club’s Carabao Cup fourth-round encounter against Brighton on October 29, 2025.

He was just 15 years and 302 days old.

The record had previously belonged to Jack Porter, who started against Bolton Wanderers in September 2024 at 16 years and 72 days.

Dowman became the first player to start a match for Arsenal aged 16 or younger.

5. Arsenal’s youngest goalscorer

His goal against Everton in March 2026 also made him Arsenal’s youngest-ever goalscorer.

At 16 years and 73 days, Dowman surpassed former Arsenal midfielder Cesc Fabregas, who held the record after scoring against Wolves in a League Cup encounter in December 2003, aged 16 years and 212 days.

Dowman broke the record by 139 days.

6. Champions League’s youngest-ever player

Dowman became the youngest player to feature in the UEFA Champions League when he appeared for Arsenal against Slavia Prague on November 4, 2025.

Introduced in the 72nd minute of Arsenal’s 3-0 victory, he was aged 15 years and 308 days.

He broke the previous record held by Borussia Dortmund’s Youssoufa Moukoko, who was 16 years and 18 days old when he featured against Zenit St Petersburg in December 2020.

Dowman also became the first 15-year-old to feature in the competition since it was rebranded in 1992.

7. England’s youngest under-21 player

Dowman made history for England’s under-21 team when he made his debut against Portugal on November 13, 2026.

Aged 16 years and 320 days, he became the youngest player to represent the Young Lions at that level.

He surpassed the previous record held by Jude Bellingham, who made his under-21 debut against Kosovo in September 2020 at 17 years and 67 days.

8. England’s youngest under-21 goalscorer

Three days after his debut, Dowman added another record when he scored the winning goal against France in a 3-2 victory at Bramall Lane.

He found the net in the 89th minute of the encounter on November 16, 2026, aged 16 years and 323 days.

The goal made him England’s youngest-ever under-21 goalscorer, breaking another record previously held by Bellingham, who scored against Kosovo aged 17 years and 67 days.

9. UEFA Youth League’s youngest goalscorer

Before making his senior-team breakthrough, Dowman had already made history in the UEFA Youth League.

He became the competition’s youngest-ever goalscorer when he scored on his debut for Arsenal’s under-19 side against Atalanta on September 19, 2024.

He was just 14 years and 263 days old.

He remains ahead of Arsenal teammate Luis Munoz, who scored at 14 years and 265 days, and Borussia Dortmund’s Hamzath Mohamadou, who found the net at 14 years and 274 days.

10. Premier League 2’s youngest-ever player

Dowman also holds the record as the youngest player to feature in Premier League 2, the competition for clubs’ under-21 sides.

He made his appearance for Arsenal’s under-21 team against Brighton on December 1, 2024, aged 14 years and 336 days.

He became the first 14-year-old to feature for Arsenal’s reserve side, surpassing Ethan Nwaneri, who made his debut in the competition aged 15 years and 166 days.

More records within reach

Beyond the records already secured, Dowman could make further history in the coming months.

Arsenal noted that he has until February 2027 to challenge Ansu Fati’s record as the youngest goalscorer in Champions League history.

Fati was 17 years and 40 days old when he scored for Barcelona against Inter Milan in 2019.

He could also challenge Wayne Rooney’s record as England’s youngest senior international goalscorer if he scores for the Three Lions before November 12, 2027.

Although Dowman will not be able to break Theo Walcott’s record as England’s youngest player, his achievements across club and international football have already placed him among the most record-breaking teenagers in the game.

The post 10 records Arsenal’s Max Dowman has broken at 16 appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: 2027: ADC files 17-ground appeal over Atiku’s candidacy
description: The African Democratic Congress (ADC) has filed a 17-ground appeal against the Federal High Court judgment on its leadership dispute, asking the Court of Appeal to restrain the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) from altering its leadership records and the nomination particulars of its
content:
The African Democratic Congress (ADC) has filed a 17-ground appeal against the Federal High Court judgment on its leadership dispute, asking the Court of Appeal to restrain the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) from altering its leadership records and the nomination particulars of its presidential and governorship candidates pending determination of the appeal.

The party is challenging the November 5, 2026 judgment of Justice Peter Lifu, describing it as fundamentally flawed and arguing that the trial court lacked jurisdiction to entertain the suit.

In a statement on Tuesday by the Director of Strategic Communication of the ADC Campaign Council, Phrank Shaibu, the party said it was also challenging an earlier ruling granting Bala Gombe leave to amend his originating summons while its objection to the court’s jurisdiction remained unresolved.

The ADC argued that allowing INEC to implement the judgment before the appeal is determined could undermine the legal challenge and create uncertainty for its candidates ahead of the 2027 general elections.

It urged the appellate court to preserve its existing leadership structure and candidate records pending the resolution of the dispute.

Shaibu said the 17 grounds of appeal challenged the jurisdiction of the Federal High Court, Gombe’s standing to institute the suit, the assessment of disputed evidence and the orders made against the party.

“The 17 grounds challenge the foundation, findings and orders of Justice Lifu’s judgment.

“The ADC has asked the Court of Appeal to examine whether the trial court had jurisdiction, whether the claimant had standing, whether disputed evidence was properly assessed, and whether the sweeping orders made against the party can stand in law,” he said.

The party is also appealing the July 24, 2026 ruling in a separate case, arguing that the trial court allowed Gombe to amend his originating summons while deferring its decision on the ADC’s preliminary objection challenging jurisdiction.

According to the statement, the party contends that the amendment altered the description of parties and the capacity in which a defendant was sued without prior leave of court.

The appellant’s brief challenging the ruling was prepared by Chief J.S. Okutepa (SAN), who leads the party’s legal team in the appeal.

The ADC is asking the Court of Appeal to set aside the amendment order and determine the outstanding objection to the trial court’s jurisdiction.

It further argued that Justice Lifu proceeded to deliver judgment on a court process whose validity was already being challenged before the appellate court.

The party expressed concern that INEC could implement the judgment before the appeal is decided, potentially creating a situation that could be difficult to reverse should the appellate court rule in its favour.

“INEC must not make changes that could preempt the court’s decision or put the party’s candidates in jeopardy while our applications are pending.

“We are asking the court to protect the subject of the appeal so that its eventual decision has practical effect,” Shaibu said.

The ADC said it made the legal challenge public to clarify the issues before the appellate court and reassure its members and supporters that it would pursue the dispute through lawful judicial processes.

The dispute centres on the party’s leadership and the validity of the processes through which its leadership records and related affairs are being contested.

Justice Lifu’s November 5 judgment in the suit filed by Gombe has thrown the party’s leadership structure and preparations for the 2027 general elections into fresh legal uncertainty.

The ADC maintained that earlier court decisions recognising its leadership transition remained valid and had not been set aside, insisting that no administrative changes should be made on the basis of a contested judgment while its appeals were pending.

The party’s appeals and applications are before the Court of Appeal for determination.

title: Sokoto protest staging: Withdraw or substantiate your claim – DSS tells Atiku
description:
The Department of State Services (DSS) has asked former Vice President Atiku Abubakar to publicly retract his allegation that the service planned to stage protests in Sokoto State to disrupt the African Democratic Congress (ADC) campaign, or provide concrete evidence to substantiate it.
The DSS made
content:
The Department of State Services (DSS) has asked former Vice President Atiku Abubakar to publicly retract his allegation that the service planned to stage protests in Sokoto State to disrupt the African Democratic Congress (ADC) campaign, or provide concrete evidence to substantiate it.

The DSS made the demand in a statement signed by its Deputy Director, Public Relations and Strategic Communications, Favour Dozie, on Tuesday, November 17, saying an internal investigation into the allegation found no evidence to back the claim.

The service said it was responding to a statement credited to Atiku on November 3.

In that statement, Atiku, the presidential candidate of African Democratic Congress (NDC), was reported to have said, “More disturbing still, the information available to us is that the leadership of the Department of State Services is recruiting people to stage protests in Sokoto. The objective is to create disorder, give the APC controlled state government a pretext to impose a curfew and prevent our campaign take off from holding as scheduled.

“We know where some of these protesters are assembled: an office behind Zenith Bank on Koko Road. Trucks are stationed there and dispatched to key points, including the roundabout.”

The DSS said its Director General had ordered an investigation into the allegation in deference to Atiku, despite the claim contradicting the service’s operations to protect all political parties.

“Pursuant to the directive of the Director General, the Service activated its internal investigation protocol, which was expanded to interview of ADC leadership in Sokoto State, members and relevant stakeholders,” the statement said.

“Outcome of the preliminary investigation did not confirm the allegation, as there was no evidence to establish such.”

The service recalled that its operatives deployed to the ADC governorship candidate in Sokoto, Mannir Daniya, evacuated him to safety unhurt on October 31, 2026, when he was attacked in Sokoto.

“Two (2) DSS operatives were assaulted during the incident and are still being treated in the hospital. The governorship candidate called personally to appreciate the State Director of Sokoto Command and even requested for reinforcement from the DSS,” the DSS said.

It added, “Though these operations to protect all Political Parties are at variance with the elder statesman’s allegation and tend to demoralize our gallant operatives who are risking their lives in the line of duty, the DGSS has still ordered an investigation into the allegation in deference to the elder statesman.”

While acknowledging letters of appreciation from the ADC chairman and governorship candidate in Sokoto State, the DSS said Atiku should set the records straight publicly since the allegation was made in public, or provide evidence to enable further investigation.

“The Service welcomes any fair and independent enquiry into the issue.

“This appeal is made with respect to His Excellency and in the interest of truth, fairness, and preservation of the morale of officers who risk their lives daily in the service of the nation,” the statement further reads.

The DSS said under its present Director General, it remains deeply committed to its constitutional mandate, set standards of professionalism and neutrality.

title: Fashola: Obi’s 2023 Lagos victory took us by surprise
description:
Former Lagos State Governor, Babatunde Fashola, has recalled how the outcome of the 2023 presidential election in Lagos surprised his political camp, admitting that they were caught off guard by President Bola Tinubu’s defeat in the state.
Fashola described the outcome as being “blindsided” during a
content:
Former Lagos State Governor, Babatunde Fashola, has recalled how the outcome of the 2023 presidential election in Lagos surprised his political camp, admitting that they were caught off guard by President Bola Tinubu’s defeat in the state.

Fashola described the outcome as being “blindsided” during an interview on Channels Television on Tuesday night.

He made the remarks while responding to a question on whether a similar electoral upset could occur in the 2027 general election.

The interviewer recalled that Tinubu, who had governed Lagos State for eight years, lost the state to the Labour Party’s Peter Obi in the 2023 presidential election, prompting speculation that a bigger surprise could happen in 2027.

Responding, Fashola said he had described the outcome at the time as being blindsided, but argued that political parties should understand that electoral victories cannot be guaranteed in every part of the country.

“Look, listen, I told you then, I think I recall the word I used was that we were blindsided in Lagos. I told you that. And, you know, our democracy is maturing,” he said.

The former governor, who served as Minister of Works and Housing under the late President Muhammadu Buhari, went on to compare electoral contests with football, arguing that teams sometimes keep visiting grounds where they have repeatedly failed to win.

He referenced former President Goodluck Jonathan’s football analogy, describing it as a useful way of understanding the unpredictability of elections.

“I heard President Jonathan in your intro speaking about how the analogy of a contest in an election and using football, and it’s a very brilliant analogy, if you ask me,” Fashola said.

He explained that some football clubs repeatedly visit opponents’ grounds despite having a history of losing there, because they still believe they can win.

According to him, political parties should similarly recognise that they cannot win every location and should concentrate on ensuring that their supporters participate in elections.

“In an election, sometimes you can’t win everywhere. And most times you can’t win everywhere. There are places where you have your ardent and fervent supporters. Your responsibility there is to ensure that you do enough to get them out to vote,” he said

In the 2023 presidential election, Obi defeated Tinubu in Lagos, polling 582,454 votes against the APC candidate’s 572,606.

Obi won nine of the state’s 20 local government areas, while Tinubu won the remaining 11.

The result was particularly significant because Tinubu had governed Lagos between 1999 and 2007 and remained a major political figure in the state.

title: APC congratulates Aiyedatiwa on Silverbird Governor of the Year award
description:
The All Progressives Congress has congratulated Ondo State Governor, Lucky Aiyedatiwa, on his emergence as the recipient of the 2026 Silverbird Governor of the Year Award, describing the honour as a recognition of his administration’s development initiatives and contributions to the state.
The party
content:
The All Progressives Congress has congratulated Ondo State Governor, Lucky Aiyedatiwa, on his emergence as the recipient of the 2026 Silverbird Governor of the Year Award, describing the honour as a recognition of his administration’s development initiatives and contributions to the state.

The party, in a congratulatory statement signed by its National Publicity Secretary, Felix Morka on Wednesday, said the award was a fitting recognition of the governor’s efforts in infrastructure development, education, healthcare, industrialisation and workers’ welfare.

The APC noted that since assuming office, Aiyedatiwa had pursued interventions across critical sectors, including road construction and rehabilitation projects across the state.

It also highlighted the restoration of the free shuttle scheme, which it said had helped ease transportation challenges faced by students.

“The honour is a fitting recognition of his administration’s development initiatives and contributions to infrastructure, education, healthcare, industrialisation and workers’ welfare in Ondo State,” the party stated.

On education, the APC commended the recruitment of over 2,000 teachers, rehabilitation of school facilities and payment of West African Examinations Council (WAEC) fees for public secondary school students.

It described the initiatives as evidence of the administration’s investment in human capital development and the future of young people in the state.

The party also acknowledged the administration’s efforts in the health sector, particularly the expansion of primary healthcare infrastructure, recruitment of medical personnel and implementation of the Orange Health Insurance Scheme.

According to the APC, these interventions demonstrate the government’s commitment to improving access to affordable and quality healthcare for residents.

The ruling party further praised Aiyedatiwa’s attention to workers’ welfare, citing interventions in the payment of outstanding gratuities and efforts to improve public service delivery.

The statement added that the governor’s development agenda reflected the broader Renewed Hope vision of President Bola Tinubu, which prioritises infrastructure development, economic growth, social investment and improved public service delivery.

“The APC notes that these initiatives reflect the broader Renewed Hope vision of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, which prioritises infrastructure development, economic growth, social investment and improved public service delivery,” Morka said.

The party congratulated the governor on the recognition and urged him to sustain his development agenda through accountable governance, economic expansion and policies capable of delivering tangible benefits to the people of the state.

It expressed confidence that continued attention to critical sectors would further support the state’s development and improve the welfare of its residents.
