title: Pochettino bows out with US victory ahead of Man United switch
description:
Mauricio Pochettino ended his tenure as head coach of the United States men’s national team with a 2–0 victory over Haiti in the second leg of their CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final on Tuesday.
Christian Pulisic and 18-year-old Julian Hall scored in the first half as the United States completed
content:
Mauricio Pochettino ended his tenure as head coach of the United States men’s national team with a 2–0 victory over Haiti in the second leg of their CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final on Tuesday.

Christian Pulisic and 18-year-old Julian Hall scored in the first half as the United States completed an 8–0 aggregate victory over Haiti at TQL Stadium in Cincinnati, securing qualification for the Nations League semi-finals.

The match was Pochettino’s final assignment with the American national team before he takes up his new role as Manchester United head coach on Wednesday, November 18.

According to The Washington Post, Pulisic opened the scoring in the 25th minute with a bicycle kick after receiving a cross from Weston McKennie.

Hall doubled the hosts’ advantage in the 43rd minute, controlling another pass from McKennie before directing the ball past Haiti goalkeeper Alexandre Pierre.

The victory followed the United States’ 6–0 win in the first leg played in Miami on November 14.

Pulisic scored three goals across the two matches, while Hall continued his scoring run with his fifth goal in six appearances for the national team.

The Washington Post reported that Pochettino received warm applause from 24,001 supporters at TQL Stadium after two years in charge of the Americans.

The 54-year-old Argentine finished his tenure with a 23-win, 12-loss and two-draw record, according to the newspaper.

NBC Sports reported that Pochettino spoke about his departure and the challenge awaiting him at Manchester United after Tuesday’s match.

On his new appointment, he said, “We are excited. I think the new challenge is a big challenge, but at the same time it’s adrenaline you want to feel.”

He also described his feelings about leaving the American team, saying, “My feelings are, difficult to find my feelings.”

He added, “I think it was our dream two years ago, to play in this [amazing] way. … I think the identity of the team, the way the play, they really believe that now we are playing how we want to play. That is my best present that I can receive from the players.”

He further said, “I’m going. So happy about that, but so sad because I leave a group of amazing players, amazing people, all the staff, the people here.”

Pochettino’s departure

The United States Soccer Federation announced Pochettino’s departure on November 13, confirming that he would leave his position after completing the team’s November international camp to become Manchester United’s head coach.

In its statement, the federation said, “Mauricio Pochettino will depart his role as Head Coach of the U.S. Men’s National Team following the conclusion of the current camp to become Head Coach of Manchester United.”

It added that Pochettino and his staff would remain in charge for the two scheduled matches against Haiti on November 14 and 17.

U.S. Soccer CEO and Secretary General JT Batson said, “Mauricio has left a lasting mark on U.S. Soccer through his leadership, professionalism and commitment to our players and culture.”

He added, “What we are most proud of goes beyond the wins. He and his staff raised standards, strengthened our culture and created clearer connections from the Youth National Teams to the senior team.”

Pochettino was appointed USMNT head coach in September 2024 and led the team to the 2025 CONCACAF Gold Cup final and the round of 16 at the 2026 FIFA World Cup.

Manchester United appointment

PUNCH had earlier reported Pochettino’s appointment as Manchester United’s new head coach on November 13, following the club’s decision to part ways with Michael Carrick.

In the report, PUNCH stated that the Argentine would take charge from November 18 after reaching an agreement with the United States Soccer Federation to complete his responsibilities with the national team.

His arrival in Manchester was scheduled after the Haiti fixture, allowing him to oversee both legs of the Nations League quarter-final before beginning work at Old Trafford.

NBC Sports reported that Pochettino was expected to travel to Manchester after Tuesday’s match to begin his new assignment on Wednesday.

He is expected to have a few days to work with his new squad before Manchester United’s Premier League trip to Liverpool on Sunday, November 22.

The post Pochettino bows out with US victory ahead of Man United switch appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Argentina thrash Costa Rica 7-0 in international friendly
description:
Argentina thrashed Costa Rica 7-0 in an international friendly on Tuesday, with Nico Paz, Julian Alvarez and Franco Mastantuono scoring twice each.
Paz opened the scoring in the eighth minute, converting Enzo Fernandez’s assist to put Argentina ahead at the start of the contest.
Julian Alvarez doubl
content:
Argentina thrashed Costa Rica 7-0 in an international friendly on Tuesday, with Nico Paz, Julian Alvarez and Franco Mastantuono scoring twice each.

Paz opened the scoring in the eighth minute, converting Enzo Fernandez’s assist to put Argentina ahead at the start of the contest.

Julian Alvarez doubled the lead in the 35th minute after being set up by Agustin Giay, before Paz scored his second three minutes later from Maximo Perrone’s pass.

Alvarez added his second goal in the 43rd minute, finishing a move created by Gianluca Prestianni to give Argentina a commanding 4-0 lead at half-time.

Argentina continued their dominance after the break, with Mastantuono coming off the bench to score in the 48th minute following an assist from Perrone.

Alexis Mac Allister made it 6-0 in the 78th minute before Mastantuono completed the rout in the 88th minute, connecting with Giuliano Simeone’s pass.

The result gave Argentina a seven-goal victory, with three players scoring twice as they overwhelmed Costa Rica.

The victory came after Argentina lost 2-1 to Uruguay in their first match following Lionel Messi’s farewell to international football in October.

Messi played his final game for Argentina in a 3-0 friendly victory over Benin on October 6, bringing an end to his international career with the national team.

title: No evidence of coordinated cyberattack behind US outages – Rubio
description:
United States Secretary of State Marco Rubio has dismissed fears that the country is under a coordinated cyberattack following a series of technology disruptions affecting government agencies, banks, airlines and major technology companies.
Rubio said there was no evidence linking the incidents or s
content:
United States Secretary of State Marco Rubio has dismissed fears that the country is under a coordinated cyberattack following a series of technology disruptions affecting government agencies, banks, airlines and major technology companies.

Rubio said there was no evidence linking the incidents or suggesting that they were orchestrated by hackers, criminals, foreign governments or other hostile actors.

“We are not under systemic attack,” Rubio told reporters in Manila, Philippines, on Tuesday, November 17, while travelling with President Donald Trump.

According to Reuters, Rubio acknowledged that the disruptions were unsettling but insisted that they were unrelated and had different technical causes.

“We have zero evidence or any reason to believe that any of these isolated or individual instances have anything to do with nefarious actors, with cyberhackers, with criminals, with another nation state, with a malign actor of any kind,” he said.

He added, “Each of them are distinct, and they’re different in their causation.”

The remarks followed a series of disruptions affecting Microsoft’s email services, United States air traffic control, major banks, United Airlines, Apple services and the National Security Agency’s internal communications network.

The Federal Aviation Administration had ordered a nationwide ground stop on Friday, November 13, which lasted approximately four and a half hours, disrupting air travel across the country.

The disruption followed a Microsoft outage affecting services including Outlook and Teams, while JPMorgan Chase experienced a software problem that affected some banking services on Monday.

United Airlines also reported a technology failure that delayed approximately 150 flights.

On Tuesday, the NSA disclosed that its network had experienced a temporary disruption during scheduled maintenance, although it maintained that its mission-critical capabilities remained operational.

The agency said its ability to defend national security had continued despite the technical problems.

Intelligence chief backs Rubio

Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton also dismissed suggestions that the disruptions were the result of a cyberattack or state-sponsored activity.

Speaking during an interview with CNBC on Tuesday, Clayton said, “This is not a cyberattack, and this is not a coordinated effort by a nation-state.”

He added, “We’ve looked very closely. Anytime we see something like this, those are the first questions that we ask on behalf of the American people.”

Clayton attributed some of the problems to technology upgrades and security patches introduced to address vulnerabilities in computer systems.

“As you patch and upgrade your systems, taking them down and bringing them back up, there are things like this that happen,” he said.

He also explained that artificial intelligence was enabling organisations to identify vulnerabilities more quickly, creating pressure to upgrade and secure their systems.

Concerns persist over repeated outages

Despite the administration’s assurances, the frequency of the disruptions has prompted questions from lawmakers and some supporters of Trump.

Republican Senator Josh Hawley expressed reservations about the incidents occurring within a short period.

“If this is all a coincidence, it’s like the greatest coincidence in the history of the world,” he told reporters.

Democratic Senator Mark Warner, vice-chairman of the Senate Select Committee on Intelligence, also said there was no indication that the incidents were the result of a coordinated attack.

However, he called attention to the pressure artificial intelligence was placing on technology companies and government agencies to identify and fix vulnerabilities.

In a statement, Warner said, “I understand why Americans are concerned about the widespread outages we’ve seen in recent days, affecting everything from banks and major technology companies to critical government systems.”

He added, “At this point, there is no indication that these incidents are the result of a cyberattack, foreign interference, or some coordinated effort.”

Meanwhile, Trump also played down concerns over the disruptions, saying that technical problems could occur even in large and well-funded organisations.

“It’s like when you’re big and powerful, and you have all the money. Things like that happen. It’s fine,” he told reporters in Manila.

The incidents have renewed scrutiny of the reliability of critical technology infrastructure in the United States, particularly as government agencies and private companies increasingly depend on interconnected digital systems.

The post No evidence of coordinated cyberattack behind US outages – Rubio appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Nvidia rules out Huang’s return as CEO, reports revenue surge
description:
US chip giant Nvidia on Tuesday ruled out any comeback for ousted CEO Jensen Huang, who was forced out in a spy scandal, and reported that it had doubled revenue in the third quarter to more than $115 billion, beating expectations.
Huang sought reinstatement despite resigning last week over an affai
content:
US chip giant Nvidia on Tuesday ruled out any comeback for ousted CEO Jensen Huang, who was forced out in a spy scandal, and reported that it had doubled revenue in the third quarter to more than $115 billion, beating expectations.

Huang sought reinstatement despite resigning last week over an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, but his successor—interim CEO Colette Kress—said it was now “business as usual” as the company charts a path forward without him.

Harvey Jones, the chair of the company’s board, said in an earnings call that “the Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.”

Investors scoured the upbeat results for evidence that the artificial intelligence boom can withstand the Nvidia crisis, which highlighted a loophole allegedly exploited by Chinese companies.

“Our momentum is real. Nvidia is an exceptional technology leader, powered by the relentless innovation of our people,” Kress said in her first remarks since being appointed by the board last week.

She forecast stronger revenue growth of 75 per cent in the next fiscal year, up from 70 per cent.

Huang’s bid on Tuesday to get his job back was the latest twist for the company at the centre of an AI boom that has propelled markets to record highs and boosted global economic growth.

The recent upheaval has battered Nvidia shares—which have lost $700 billion in market value since the scandal broke—and Huang is to be questioned by US lawmakers on December 1 over national security concerns.

A charismatic promoter of AI, his fall triggered immediate calls from Elon Musk and others for his return, and even President Donald Trump said he “would not mind” seeing Huang back at Nvidia, downplaying the espionage allegations.

• Battle over AI chips –

“Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from Nvidia’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO,” Huang said, hours before the earnings release.

“If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honoured to answer these calls and return as CEO.”

As the spy scandal deepened, Washington on Monday announced new restrictions on AI chip exports, drawing condemnation from Beijing.

The new US export curbs and the wider Nvidia scandal risk casting a shadow over talks between Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit, which starts this week in the Chinese city of Shenzhen.

Under Washington’s new rules, data centres anywhere in the world will need a US license to provide large volumes of computing power from advanced chips to companies headquartered in China, Macau or other countries under US arms embargoes.

The rules also require licenses to ship advanced chips to Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil — countries the US Commerce Department says present a “higher-than-normal risk of diversion” of the chips.

The changes are a response to a loophole that allowed Chinese firms to rent AI computing power from data centres in Southeast Asia and elsewhere that run on US hardware not available for export to China.

While the loophole has been known to authorities, the revelation of Huang’s affair has drawn intense scrutiny to the practice.

His lover Alice Huang, who is not related to the 63-year-old, is a former executive of Megaspeed — a Singapore-based cloud computing firm under US criminal investigation for allegedly helping Chinese companies procure advanced Nvidia AI chips in circumvention of export controls.

Investors are watching for signs of whether Kress will slow Huang’s aggressive investment strategy, which saw him commit tens of billions of dollars to AI companies.

Huang on Tuesday sounded a note of contrition in his statement, saying “I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at NVIDIA, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life.”

AFP

title: Democrats secure 56-seat Senate majority as Peltola wins Alaska
description:
Democrat Mary Peltola has defeated Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan to win Alaska’s United States Senate race, ending the last unresolved Senate contest in the 2026 midterm elections and expanding her party’s majority in the chamber to 56 seats.
Peltola’s victory, projected on Tuesday, November 17,
content:
Democrat Mary Peltola has defeated Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan to win Alaska’s United States Senate race, ending the last unresolved Senate contest in the 2026 midterm elections and expanding her party’s majority in the chamber to 56 seats.

Peltola’s victory, projected on Tuesday, November 17, gives Democrats a 56–44 majority in the Senate after the party flipped nine Republican-held seats in the midterm elections.

According to the Alaska Division of Elections’ preliminary results, Peltola secured 50.1 per cent of first-choice votes, crossing the threshold required to win outright under the state’s ranked-choice voting system without a further round of counting.

Sullivan received 45.8 per cent, while Daniel J. Sullivan, another candidate whose name became central to the controversy surrounding the election, received 1.7 per cent. Republican Gerald Heikes polled 2.1 per cent.

The Associated Press, in a report published by ABC News on Wednesday, November 18, said Peltola overcame allegations that members of her campaign helped recruit a candidate who shares the incumbent senator’s name.

The election was marked by allegations of political manipulation, competing investigations and legal battles over the possibility of voters confusing the two candidates named Sullivan.

Controversy over two Dan Sullivans

The controversy intensified following an October 28 investigation by The New York Times, which reported that operatives aligned with Peltola’s campaign, her lawyers and senior aides at the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee were involved in efforts to recruit Republican challengers to enter the race.

One of the candidates was Daniel J. Sullivan, a resident of Petersburg, Alaska, whose name closely resembles that of incumbent Senator Dan S. Sullivan.

The newspaper reported that the recruitment effort, internally referred to as a ballot-composition project, was intended to dilute support for the incumbent and improve Peltola’s chances of winning.

ABC News also reported that the Times based its investigation on interviews, text messages and documents.

However, Peltola’s campaign denied involvement in recruiting either Sullivan candidate.

The controversy prompted President Donald Trump to accuse Peltola of election fraud and call for her prosecution.

The Justice Department subsequently filed a lawsuit seeking to prevent certification of the election if the incumbent Sullivan lost by a margin smaller than the votes received by the similarly named candidate.

A federal judge dismissed the lawsuit, but the Justice Department appealed the decision.

Victory despite legal battles

Despite the controversy, Peltola secured a decisive enough lead to win without relying on additional ranked-choice calculations.

Alaska Public Media reported that her 50.1 per cent share of first-choice votes exceeded the combined votes received by the two Sullivans and Heikes.

The Justice Department’s investigation into the alleged recruitment effort remains ongoing, while the civil case continues through the appeals process.

Peltola’s victory makes her the first Democrat elected to the US Senate from Alaska since 2008 and the first Alaska Native person to serve in the chamber.

She previously represented Alaska in the House of Representatives, becoming the first Alaska Native woman elected to Congress in 2022.

Her campaign focused on affordability, healthcare costs, living expenses and the interests of Alaska residents.

The result also completes the Senate race count in the 2026 midterm elections, giving Democrats a substantial majority when the new Congress convenes in January.

title: 16 year-old talent JJ Gabriel exits Man United
description:
Manchester United youngster JJ Gabriel has announced his departure from the club with an emotional farewell message, thanking the Premier League side for supporting his development since he joined its academy in 2020.
The 16-year-old shared a farewell video on his Instagram account, #jjnr10, on Tues
content:
Manchester United youngster JJ Gabriel has announced his departure from the club with an emotional farewell message, thanking the Premier League side for supporting his development since he joined its academy in 2020.

The 16-year-old shared a farewell video on his Instagram account, #jjnr10, on Tuesday, November 17, 2026, reflecting on his six-year spell at the club and the memories he would cherish.

In the video, Gabriel described his arrival at Manchester United as a 10-year-old boy with big dreams and highlighted scoring at Old Trafford and winning the Jimmy Murphy Award among his memorable experiences.

“Dear Manchester United, I arrived in 2020 as a 10-year-old boy with big dreams. Here I grew as a player and a person. From scoring at Old Trafford to receiving the Jimmy Murphy Award.

“You gave me moments I will always treasure. To every coach and every member of staff, to my teammates and everyone who supported me, thank you for believing in me and helping me grow.

“As I begin my next chapter, Manchester United will always be a part of my story. Thank you for everything, JJ,” he wrote.

Sky Sports also reported on Tuesday, that Gabriel had announced his departure, adding that Real Madrid had reached an agreement with Manchester United earlier in November to sign the teenager.

The Spanish club is reportedly planning to bring him in during the January transfer window. Sky Sports

However, Gabriel did not mention Real Madrid or identify his next destination in his farewell message.

According to The Guardian, in a report published on November 17, Gabriel had been absent from Manchester United since requesting the cancellation of his registration in September, shortly before turning 16 on October 6.

The newspaper also reported that Manchester United had “initially hoped to persuade the teenager to remain at the club but appeared to be preparing to explore legal options against his next club over possible breaches of regulations.”

Gabriel joined Manchester United in 2020 and became the youngest recipient of the club’s Jimmy Murphy Award, presented to its young player of the year.

He also made an appearance for the senior side in a pre-season friendly against Atletico Madrid in August, although he did not feature in a competitive first-team match.

His final appearance for the club’s youth side appeared to be the UEFA Youth League fixture against Sabah on September 10, in which he scored a hat-trick in a 5-0 victory, according to The Guardian.

title: INEC receives 78,112 PVCs for distribution in Enugu
description:
The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) says it has received 78,112 newly produced Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) for distribution across the 17 Local Government Areas (LGAs) of Enugu State, ruling out collection by proxy.
INEC Resident Electoral Commissioner in the state, Dr Chukwuemeka
content:
The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) says it has received 78,112 newly produced Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) for distribution across the 17 Local Government Areas (LGAs) of Enugu State, ruling out collection by proxy.

INEC Resident Electoral Commissioner in the state, Dr Chukwuemeka Chukwu, disclosed this while briefing journalists on Tuesday in Enugu.

Chukwu said the PVCs would be made available to their rightful owners in line with the commission’s established procedures.

He said the PVC remained an essential requirement for eligible registered voters to exercise their civic responsibility during elections.

According to him, without the card, eligible voters cannot exercise their right to vote in any election organised by INEC.

“The commission is therefore committed to ensuring that all PVCs received are properly accounted for and made available to their rightful owners in line with the commission’s established procedures.

“I am pleased to announce that INEC Enugu State has so far received a total of 78,112 newly produced Permanent Voter Cards in three batches as follows:

“First Batch: 17,220 PVCs. (transfers and replacement across all categories). Second Batch: 20,137 PVCs. (first phase registration), Third Batch: 40,755 PVCs. (second phase registration); total PVCs received: 78,112,” he said.

The REC gave a breakdown of the PVCs allocated to each of the 17 LGAs and urged affected registrants to visit their respective INEC LGA offices to collect their cards promptly.

Chukwu appealed to political parties, community leaders, traditional rulers, religious leaders, civil society organisations and the media to assist INEC in sensitising citizens on the importance of PVC collection and active participation in the electoral process.

He also reiterated INEC’s commitment to conducting free, fair, credible, inclusive and transparent elections in the state and across the country.

Chukwu said the commission would continue to work closely with relevant stakeholders to ensure that all electoral activities were conducted in accordance with the law and established guidelines.

He assured residents that the commission would continue to discharge its responsibilities with diligence, transparency and professionalism. (NAN)

title: MTN gifts Flamingos N150m, one year free data
description:
Telecommunications giant MTN has presented Nigeria’s U-17 women’s national team, the Flamingos, with a N150m cash package and one year of free data subscriptions following their triumph at the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco.
At a reception held in their honour on Monday, MTN Chief Execu
content:
Telecommunications giant MTN has presented Nigeria’s U-17 women’s national team, the Flamingos, with a N150m cash package and one year of free data subscriptions following their triumph at the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco.

At a reception held in their honour on Monday, MTN Chief Executive Officer, Karl Toriola, announced the financial rewards in recognition of the team’s historic achievement at the tournament, where the Flamingos defeated Japan 2-1 in the final to become the first African nation to win the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup.

The package includes N5m for each of the 21 players, N7m for the head coach, N5m for the assistant coach, N5m for the programme liaison officer, N3m for the fitness coach and N20m for the technical team.

According to MTN, the players’ individual rewards will be disbursed through their respective parents into designated accounts provided by the telecommunications company, in line with the necessary legal requirements.

MTN’s gesture is the latest in a series of rewards and recognition extended to the Flamingos since their return to Nigeria. The Federal Government, the Senate and the Lagos State Government have also announced various incentives for the team following their World Cup success.

Speaking at the event, Toriola said the team had made history and deserved recognition for its resilience and determination throughout the tournament.

“You have made history as the first African women’s team to win a FIFA World Cup title at any level, and we are delighted to celebrate with you. You stumbled at the beginning, picked yourselves up and excelled at the end. The character of the team, the way you overcame setbacks and believed in yourselves, is impressive.

“As you move to the next chapter, remember you have shown the world what Nigerian talent can achieve, but never forget the hard work, ethics and discipline that took you there.”

Acting NFF General Secretary, Dr Emmanuel Ikpeme, commended MTN for its support of Nigerian football and expressed hope that the partnership would continue.

“It has been a wonderful partnership. In fact, I appreciate, and Nigerians appreciate, your support for all that you have done in the last five years, and we look forward to this partnership continuing.”

title: Adamawa deputy gov sits for teachers’ qualifying exam
description:
The Deputy Governor of Adamawa State, Prof. Kaletapwa Farauta, has sat for the Teachers Registration Council of Nigeria (TRCN) Professional Qualifying Examination (PQE).
Her participation comes ahead of the council’s plan to enforce compulsory professional certification for teachers nationwide.

The
content:
The Deputy Governor of Adamawa State, Prof. Kaletapwa Farauta, has sat for the Teachers Registration Council of Nigeria (TRCN) Professional Qualifying Examination (PQE).

Her participation comes ahead of the council’s plan to enforce compulsory professional certification for teachers nationwide.

The Registrar and Chief Executive Officer of TRCN, Dr Ronke Soyombo, disclosed this on Tuesday in Abuja during an interaction with newsmen.

She said the deputy governor sat for the examination on Friday.

Soyombo described her participation as a demonstration that everyone involved in education, irrespective of position or status, must meet professional teaching requirements.

“In Adamawa State, for the first time, we actually saw the Deputy Governor of Adamawa State coming to sit for our exam.

“She sat for the exam on Friday, and that is to tell you that everybody who owns schools or is making efforts in education is coming to sit for the exam,” she said.

The registrar said all practising teachers in Nigeria must obtain professional certification and licences by December 2027.

She stressed that no teacher would be exempted from the requirement.

Soyombo explained that professional certification would be obtained once in a teacher’s lifetime, while practising licences would be renewed every three years.

She said licence renewal would depend on evidence of participation in Mandatory Continuous Professional Development (MCPD) programmes.

The registrar expressed concern over examination malpractice, revealing that the council uncovered more than 47 suspected impersonators during its latest Professional Qualifying Examination in Taraba State.

She said TRCN had strengthened examination security through candidates’ photographs, surveillance cameras and other technological measures.

According to her, the council had also upgraded its examination platform to accommodate 5,000 candidates simultaneously, from its initial capacity of 120.

Soyombo disclosed that online registration had increased examination participation from about 13,000 candidates when she assumed office in May 2025 to approximately 26,000 by November 2025.

She added that the council currently had more than two million teachers on its online platform, although compliance with professional licensing requirements remained low.

This, she said, had prompted the introduction of an accelerated professionalisation pathway.

On fraudulent certification, Soyombo said TRCN discovered 250 fake certificates during a teacher recruitment exercise in Nasarawa State.

She added that a suspect identified as Godfrey was in custody over alleged certificate forgery.

The registrar said the council had introduced Quick Response (QR) codes on certificates to facilitate verification.

She said TRCN was also collaborating with the West African Examinations Council (WAEC) and the National Examinations Council (NECO) to strengthen enforcement.

Soyombo disclosed that the council was proposing a requirement for schools to have at least 75 per cent of their teachers professionally certified before registering candidates for NECO examinations. (NAN)

content:
The Commissioner of Police, Lagos State Command,  Tijani Fatai, has charged Area Commanders, Divisional Police Officers (DPOs), Tactical Commanders and heads of strategic departments to strengthen proactive security measures and ensure heightened operational vigilance ahead of the 2027 General Elections.

The CP gave the charge while conveying the directives of the Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Disu,  during a strategic briefing with the senior officers of the Command. He emphasised the need for effective supervision, strict compliance with operational directives and heightened vigilance across all formations of the Command.

Tijani directed the  officers to strengthen intelligence gathering, identify potential flashpoints and implement preventive security measures to forestall political violence, thuggery, cultism and other criminal activities capable of threatening public peace and disrupting the electoral process.

He  further stressed the importance of supervision and accountability, charging senior officers to closely monitor personnel under their supervision and ensure strict adherence to operational directives, discipline and professional standards. He warned that any supervisory failure, dereliction of duty or misconduct would attract appropriate sanctions.

In a statement,  the Police Public Relations Officer in the state,  SP Abimbola Adebisi, said the strategic briefing also featured the decoration of 71 newly promoted officers of the Command, comprising six Chief Superintendents of Police (CSPs), 15 Superintendents of Police (SPs) and 50 Deputy Superintendents of Police (DSPs). “Congratulating the newly promoted officers, the CP described their elevation as recognition of their dedication, commitment, and contributions to the Force. He urged them to regard their new ranks as a call to greater responsibility and higher standards of service, and to justify the confidence reposed in them through exemplary conduct, professionalism, and improved service delivery.”

title: Plateau: Gunmen kill 11, 9 buried in mass grave
description:
From Jude Dangwam and Jude Owuamanam, Jos
At least 11 people were killed in separate attacks in Mangu and Bokkos local governments, Plateau State, with nine victims buried in a mass grave, while the burning of houses in neighbouring Qua’an Pan LG forced the council chairman to impose a curfew.
Among
content:
From Jude Dangwam and Jude Owuamanam, Jos

At least 11 people were killed in separate attacks in Mangu and Bokkos local governments, Plateau State, with nine victims buried in a mass grave, while the burning of houses in neighbouring Qua’an Pan LG forced the council chairman to impose a curfew.

Among those killed was an Operation Rainbow commander who had recently completed a training programme in Jos. In a separate tragedy, a newly married couple died from burns sustained when fire engulfed their residence in Bukuru, Jos South Local Government Area.

The nine victims buried in a mass grave were killed during an attack on Zwagal village in Jipal District of Mangu LGA on Sunday night. Several houses were also razed at Bong community in Doemak District of Qua’an Pan LGA.

Local sources said the attackers, who reportedly arrived in their hundreds, stormed the hilltop communities, shooting residents, setting houses ablaze, looting property and stealing livestock.

Some of the animals were reportedly butchered by the attackers, who were said to have operated for several hours.

The village head of Zwagal, Jonathan Wadong, said the attack began at about 8 p.m. on Sunday, when sporadic gunshots shattered the peace of the community.

Wadong alleged that the attackers were Fulani militias, saying: “They were speaking Fulani language.”

He appealed to the government to deploy adequate security personnel to protect residents and prevent further attacks. He also commended the chairmen of Mangu and Qua’an Pan local LGAs  for promptly mobilising security personnel to the affected communities.

The burning of houses at Bong reportedly triggered panic in other parts of Qua’an Pan, with residents fleeing Doemak, the local government headquarters, amid fears of further attacks.

The Chairman of Qua’an Pan Local Government Council, Christopher Audu Manship, imposed a curfew late Monday evening to contain the situation and prevent a further breakdown of law and order.

Manship, who visited the affected communities, witnessed the mass burial at Zwagal alongside the Chairman of Mangu Local Government Council, Emmanuel Bala Mwolpun.

Describing the attacks as barbaric and inhuman, he reaffirmed the government’s commitment to tackling insecurity and urged residents, particularly youths, to remain vigilant and promptly report suspicious movements to security agencies.

During an assessment of the destruction at Bong, Manship assured residents that the government would not abandon them, pledging support for rebuilding their homes and strengthening security.

He also disclosed that efforts were being made to improve telecommunications coverage in the community to facilitate timely communication, security surveillance and monitoring.

In Bokkos LGA, gunmen killed two men in an ambush at about 3 p.m. on Monday as they returned from a condolence visit to Hurti village.

The victims were travelling to their community in Tadai, Manguna District, when they were attacked.

A community leader, Machief Paul, who confirmed the incident, said both victims were members of his community. He disclosed that one of them had recently completed a training programme for Operation Rainbow unit commanders.

“One of the victims was a newly graduated commander of Operation Rainbow who had recently completed a refresher training programme for unit commanders in Jos. He was agile and ready for the job, but unfortunately his career has been cut short,” Paul said.

Meanwhile, a newly married couple, Sikiru Habib and his wife, Ramlat Lawan, have died after suffering severe burns when fire engulfed their residence in Anguwan Miyango, Bukuru, Jos South LGA.

The fire reportedly broke out at about 2:30 a.m. on Saturday while the couple were asleep. Residents suspected a power surge, although the actual cause of the fire had yet to be established.

A neighbour, Lawal Suleiman, said residents woke up to discover the raging inferno and found that the door to the couple’s room would not open, trapping them inside as young men in the neighbourhood struggled to rescue them.

He said the rescuers eventually broke the window and brought the couple out before firefighters arrived to provide emergency assistance.

The victims were rushed to the Jos University Teaching Hospital, where Habib died on Sunday, while his wife succumbed to her injuries on Monday.

The post Plateau: Gunmen kill 11, 9 buried in mass grave appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Benue police arrest 26 suspects, kill 3 bandits
description:
From Scholastica Hir, Makurdi
The Benue State Police Command has arrested 26 suspects, neutralised three suspected bandits and rescued five kidnapped persons in separate security operations across the state.
Among those arrested are nine suspects allegedly involved in the killing of a 52-year-old ma
content:
From Scholastica Hir, Makurdi

The Benue State Police Command has arrested 26 suspects, neutralised three suspected bandits and rescued five kidnapped persons in separate security operations across the state.

Among those arrested are nine suspects allegedly involved in the killing of a 52-year-old man, Felix Ahemba, whose body was dumped in a cassava farm at Tyo Adu Village, Gboko Local Government Area (LGA) of the state.

The police also recovered four locally made firearms, 495 rounds of live ammunition, 290 ammunition chains, a stolen Toyota Camry, a Honda motorcycle, assorted charms and a locally made knife during the operations.

The Commissioner of Police, Cletus Nwadiogbu, disclosed this while briefing journalists  yesterday at the Command headquarters in Makurdi.

He said the successes were recorded through intelligence-led operations, proactive policing and collaboration with other security agencies.

Nwadiogbu disclosed that operatives of the Katsina-Ala Division, working in collaboration with the Police Mobile Force and Operation Whirl Stroke (OPWS), rescued five persons abducted at Utange Village, Tor-Donga District, Katsina-Ala LGA, on November 8.

He, however, regretted that three of the rescued victims, who sustained severe injuries during the incident, died while being conveyed to hospital, while the remaining two survived.

The police commissioner also disclosed that 10 suspects were arrested in connection with the abduction of a commercial driver, Mohammed Musa, a woman and her six-year-old son at Ojinebe-Adoka Village.

He said operatives of the Violent Crime Response Unit arrested the suspects on November 7, adding that the vehicle in which the victims were last seen was later discovered burnt along the route.

According to him, efforts are ongoing to locate the three missing persons and apprehend other suspects still at large.

On the fight against armed robbery, Nwadiogbu said two suspects, Saviour Shagbaor and Maakaven Matthew, were arrested in Gboko following an attack on a commercial motorcyclist and his passenger.

He said the assailants allegedly used a locally made firearm during the attack before escaping with the victim’s Bajaj motorcycle.

He further disclosed that two other suspects, Michael Tyonongu and Godwin Agaibge, were arrested along the Gbajimgba-Makurdi Road on November 16, with a locally fabricated pistol.

Another suspect, Tersoo Orjime, was arrested in Makurdi over an alleged attempted robbery, with a locally made revolver pistol and a knife recovered from him.

The CP added that a suspected cult member, Dan Azumi Audu, was arrested at Yagba Community, Makurdi, following a distress call. A locally fabricated revolver pistol and live ammunition were recovered from him.

Nwadiogbu also announced the arrest of a suspected car-snatching suspect, Anthony Nagu, by operatives of Operation Zenda at Otukpa, where a red Toyota Camry allegedly stolen from Badagry, Lagos State, was recovered.

On the burning of the Traditional Council Hall at Tyem-Imongu Community in Vandeikya LGA on November 4, the police commissioner said nine persons had been arrested in connection with the incident.

He disclosed that investigation had been concluded and the suspects charged to court.

On the arrest of suspected bandits and recovery of ammunition, Nwadiogbu said operatives of Operation Zenda intercepted a vehicle travelling from Jato-Aka towards Makurdi through Gboko on November 15.

He said a passenger identified as Shawon Order Timothy was arrested during the operation, while 490 rounds of ammunition of different calibres and 290 ammunition chains were recovered from him.

The suspect, according to the CP, was allegedly linked to the killing of security personnel at Agu Centre on September 19, 2025.

He said the suspect remained in custody as investigations continued.

Nwadiogbu urged residents to remain vigilant and provide credible and timely information to security agencies, stressing that lasting security could only be achieved through the cooperation of all stakeholders.

He reaffirmed the Command’s commitment to sustaining intelligence gathering, strengthening security operations and ensuring the safety of the people.

title: Visa issues almost cost me my career – Arokodare
description:
Super Eagles striker Tolu Arokodare has revealed how visa difficulties nearly ended his ambition of pursuing a professional football career in Europe.
The Nigerian forward disclosed that he missed several opportunities with European clubs despite attracting interest, including French side Toulouse a
content:
Super Eagles striker Tolu Arokodare has revealed how visa difficulties nearly ended his ambition of pursuing a professional football career in Europe.

The Nigerian forward disclosed that he missed several opportunities with European clubs despite attracting interest, including French side Toulouse and Belgian outfit Royal Charleroi.

Speaking on the Counter Attack Podcast, Arokodare recounted how repeated visa setbacks threatened his attempts to establish himself abroad.

“I almost lost the opportunity to play football because of my green card. Toulouse wanted me, but I was denied a visa. Victor Osimhen helped me get an offer from Charleroi, but I was denied again. Valmiera wanted me, but there was no Latvian embassy in Nigeria,” he said.

The striker also revealed that Osimhen, who was playing for Charleroi at the time, personally contacted the club’s president to help facilitate the move.

However, the proposed transfer fell through because of the visa complications.

Arokodare eventually secured an opportunity with Latvian club Valmiera in 2019, although the move also presented logistical challenges because Latvia did not have an embassy in Nigeria at the time.

He subsequently developed his career through spells in Germany, France and Belgium before earning a move to the Premier League with Wolverhampton Wanderers.

Despite the setbacks, the forward persevered and eventually established himself in European football, with Osimhen’s intervention representing one of the opportunities that could have accelerated his breakthrough.

title: Offa robbery:  Saraki, Ahmed’s  arraignment stalled till December 3
description:
From Taiwo Ogunniyi, Ilorin
The planned arraignment of former Senate President Bukola Saraki and former Kwara State Governor Abdulfatah Ahmed over the Offa robbery case suffered a setback yesterday as a Kwara State High Court, Ilorin ruled that proceedings could not commence until the defendants had
content:
From Taiwo Ogunniyi, Ilorin

The planned arraignment of former Senate President Bukola Saraki and former Kwara State Governor Abdulfatah Ahmed over the Offa robbery case suffered a setback yesterday as a Kwara State High Court, Ilorin ruled that proceedings could not commence until the defendants had been properly served with the charges against them.

The court, presided over by Justice Osuolale Ajayi, rejected the prosecution’s bid to proceed immediately with the arraignment, upholding the defence’s objection that serving the charges on the defendants’ lawyers did not satisfy the legal requirement for personal service and fair hearing.

Justice Ajayi consequently directed the prosecution to ensure that the charges were served on the defendants on or before November 20 and adjourned the matter until December 3, 2026, for arraignment.

The ruling followed arguments by the prosecution and defence teams at the previous sitting, during which the court reserved its decision on the procedural objections raised against the commencement of proceedings.

The prosecution had urged the court to arraign the four defendants without further delay, arguing that the trial should commence immediately.

However, the defence opposed the application, insisting that the defendants had not been personally served with the charges and that proceeding with their arraignment under the circumstances would violate due process and their constitutional right to a fair hearing.

At the previous sitting, counsel to Saraki, Adebayo Adelodun, SAN, had questioned the urgency surrounding the proceedings and challenged the manner in which the prosecution sought to bring the defendants before the court.

“My Lord, why the hurry?” Adelodun asked.

He also drew the court’s attention to a pending appeal challenging issues relating to jurisdiction and the competence of the trial court to entertain the case.

The defence urged the court to take cognisance of the appellate proceedings and the legal objections before taking further steps in the matter.

Justice Ajayi, however, declined to suspend proceedings on account of the pending appeal, explaining that there was no indication of when the Court of Appeal would deliver its ruling on the defence’s application seeking an order directing the parties to maintain the status quo ante bellum.

Meanwhile, the Court of Appeal, Ilorin has reserved its ruling on an application filed by Saraki and Ahmed seeking to compel the parties and the trial court to maintain the status quo ante bellum pending the determination of their appeal.

The application before the appellate court is separate from the issue of service of charges decided by the High Court.

With the latest ruling, the prosecution must comply with the November 20 deadline for service of the charges before the trial court can proceed with the planned arraignment on December 3.

title: Female soldiers critical to Army operations –COAS
description:
From Noah Ebije, Kaduna
The Chief of Army Staff (COAS), Lt.-Gen. Waidi Shaibu, has said that developing the professional capabilities of female personnel is essential to strengthening the Nigerian Army’s capacity to accomplish its operational missions.
Shaibu stated this at the Nigerian Army Women C
content:
From Noah Ebije, Kaduna

The Chief of Army Staff (COAS), Lt.-Gen. Waidi Shaibu, has said that developing the professional capabilities of female personnel is essential to strengthening the Nigerian Army’s capacity to accomplish its operational missions.

Shaibu stated this at the Nigerian Army Women Command’s Fourth Quarter 2026 Workshop held on Tuesday in Kaduna.

He was represented at the event by Maj.-Gen. Oladele Arogundade, Commander, Command Engineering Depot.

The workshop was themed: “Harnessing the Professional Capabilities of Nigerian Army Female Personnel in Support of Nigerian Army Operational Engagements in a Joint and Multi-Agency Environment.”

The COAS said the contemporary security environment continued to present complex and evolving challenges that required a highly professional, adaptive and resilient military force.

He noted that the professional capabilities of female officers and soldiers constituted an important component of the Nigerian Army’s human resources, stressing that their effective development and deployment were essential to strengthening the institution’s capacity to accomplish assigned missions.

According to him, operations against insurgency and terrorism, protection of vulnerable communities, internal security tasks and responses to humanitarian emergencies cannot be achieved through kinetic operations alone.

He said such operations required sound intelligence, cultural awareness, effective communication, discipline, civilian engagement and the ability to build confidence among affected populations.

Shaibu explained that during engagements with communities where cultural or religious sensitivities influenced who could freely interact with residents, the presence of trained female personnel could provide access that might otherwise be difficult to achieve.

He cited the contributions of female personnel during stabilisation operations in Jos North in April, where they served as force multipliers in efforts to restore peace and security following a breakdown of law and order in the Angwan Ruba area.

He said their professional conduct attracted commendation, noting that they demonstrated resilience and competence while performing operational duties alongside their male counterparts.

“The Nigerian Army remains committed to advancing professionalism, meritocracy and operational competencies across all its formations and units,” he said.

The COAS stressed that the development of female personnel must be anchored on established military standards, appropriate training and opportunities for professional growth.

He said the workshop would address critical areas, including identifying and developing professional capabilities, expanding opportunities in combat, specialist and leadership appointments, as well as adaptive leadership, mentorship and career progression.

Other areas, he said, included critical thinking, decision-making, peace support operations, humanitarian assistance and civil-military relations.

He urged participants to move beyond theoretical discussions and produce practical recommendations that would strengthen the professional development and effective deployment of female personnel.

“I wish to emphasise that expanding professional opportunities must be firmly anchored on competence, merit and established military standards,” he said.

Shaibu explained that the objective was not merely to increase the number of female personnel in particular appointments but to ensure that suitably qualified officers and soldiers were adequately prepared and effectively deployed.

He added that discipline, integrity and resourcefulness remained fundamental to military functionality and operational effectiveness.

Earlier, the Acting Commander, Nigerian Army Women Command, Col. Sule Ahmed, said the workshop’s theme reflected the importance of developing and effectively utilising the professional capabilities of female personnel to meet contemporary operational requirements.

Ahmed said the workshop was in line with the United Nations Women, Peace and Security Agenda, particularly United Nations Security Council Resolution 1325 of 2000, which underscores women’s participation in conflict prevention, conflict resolution, peacebuilding and security processes.

He disclosed that the workshop would also address drug and substance abuse, as well as mental health management, particularly their implications for personnel welfare and operational efficiency.

Ahmed thanked the Chief of Army Staff for approving and supporting the workshop.

In his lecture, retired Maj.-Gen. Adeniyi Oyebade said operational success depended on men and women working effectively together, rather than on women alone.

He stressed that the issue was not simply about women’s participation but about harnessing the complementary strengths of both sexes to improve operational outcomes.

“The women cannot do it alone, that is the truth, but when you have the men there, it enhances the operational capacity and they can deliver effectively on the outcomes,” he said.

Oyebade also stressed the need to expose female personnel to the same training opportunities as their male counterparts, particularly in emerging areas of warfare.

Citing the changing nature of modern battlefields, especially the ongoing war in Ukraine, he said drone technology had become central to military operations, with women playing significant roles as drone operators.

“Look at what is happening in Ukraine, the use of drone technologies. Many of the drone operators are women,” he said.

He observed that women had demonstrated proficiency in drone operations because the technology required precision, attention to detail and fine-tuning of operations.

According to him, modern warfare is no longer determined solely by physical strength.

“Once you start moving away from physical effectiveness and strength and start seeing what women can bring, you will achieve more,” he said.

Oyebade commended the Commander, Nigerian Army Women Command, and the Chief of Army Staff for organising the Fourth Quarter workshop.

He urged the Command to involve male officers in subsequent training programmes to enable both sexes to share perspectives, learn from one another and draw strength from their complementary capabilities.

In suit CV/101/2026,
content:
From Godwin Tsa, Abuja

A battle over the estate of the late former Governor of Kogi State, Alhaji Ibrahim Idris, has opened at an Upper Area Court in Abuja. Four of his children are asking the court to freeze his properties and appoint a receiver/manager to take charge of them.

In suit CV/101/2026, Asma’u, Fatima, Zainab and Jamila Ibrahim Idris are asking the court to restrain 13 other family members from selling, leasing, mortgaging, gifting, transferring or otherwise dealing with any part of the estate.

The respondents include Hajiya Aisha, Abubakar, Abdullahi, Sulaiman, Hussaini, Abdurahman, Idris (Atayi), Ibrahim, Hassan, Iman, Iram and Ilan Ibrahim Idris.

In a motion marked M/46/2026, filed by their lawyer, I. H. Nalaraba, and brought under sections 6(6)(b) and 272(1) of the 1999 Constitution and the court’s inherent jurisdiction, the applicants want an interlocutory injunction pending the determination of the substantive suit.

Properties in dispute

The properties listed include:

Grand Ibro Hotel and its Annex, both in Wuse Zone 5, Abuja; A house on Kwame Nkrumah Street, Asokoro, Abuja;

A house behind Government House, Lokoja; A house in Idah; Landed properties in Lokoja, Idah, Ayingba and Abejukolo.

Others are; a one-bedroom apartment in Dubai; Land behind SETRACO, Jabi, Abuja; Bank accounts in several Nigerian banks; The late governor’s personal effects, including cars, clothes, wristwatches, footwear and furniture.

The applicants want a receiver/manager to take over, preserve and manage the estate and collect its rents and income. They want the receiver to file a full inventory of the properties, within and outside Abuja, within 21 days of appointment. He would open a dedicated estate account in a reputable bank and file accounts of his stewardship every three months. He would also be barred from disposing of any property without the court’s leave, and paid a remuneration fixed by the court out of the estate’s income.

They also want the respondents, and any other heir who has collected rent or income or taken possession of any item since the governor’s death on September 20, 2026, to account for it and return it to the receiver within 14 days.

The applicants further want tenants, managers, staff and bankers of the estate properties, including the management of Grand Ibro Hotel, to deal only with the receiver.

They want the respondents ordered to preserve all title documents, bank statements, receipts and tenancy agreements, and an accelerated hearing of the main suit.

In a 16-paragraph affidavit, Sani Sambo, a lawyer in the applicants’ counsel’s firm, said the estate has not been shared among the heirs according to Islamic law, although the deceased was a practising Muslim.

He said some respondents and other family members have been collecting rents from the hotel and other properties. They have also allegedly taken the late governor’s cars, wristwatches and other belongings, to the exclusion of the other heirs.

Sambo also alleged that a mosque at the hotel was demolished after the governor’s death and new construction begun by some family members. He added that the hotel business continues to run without any accounting to the family.

The applicants have also applied for a plaint seeking a declaration of the deceased’s heirs and an order sharing the estate under Islamic law.

Judge Ado Muktar has directed all the family members to appear in court on November 23, the next adjourned date, when an inventory of the estate is also to be taken.

title: Okpe’s Baby: The Governor who is familiar with the Street
description:
By Patrick Akhere Ebojele
Two years ago,precisely 12th of November, 2024,Senator Monday Okpebholo took the oath as Governor of Edo State. Anyone who has followed him closely, since he took office, will know he rarely stays long in his office. He turns up at roadworks, hospital wards, school compound
content:
By Patrick Akhere Ebojele

Two years ago,precisely 12th of November, 2024,Senator Monday Okpebholo took the oath as Governor of Edo State. Anyone who has followed him closely, since he took office, will know he rarely stays long in his office. He turns up at roadworks, hospital wards, school compounds, and markets, sometimes before the people in charge expect him. Some critics find this untidy. Many Edo people find it reassuring.

That habit is the best way to understand why he accepted the name “Okpe’s baby,” a name that began as he inspected some projects. The name sounds playful, and it is. It also says something about how people see him: as someone close to them, not a distant figure behind tinted glass in an air-conditioned SUV. It belongs with other street names he has collected, including “Waka Waka Governor,” which some circles gave him alongside “Akpako-messiah, “Akpakorescue”,”Akpako bulldozer” among several others.

As governor, Senator Monday Okpebholo acceptance of these names is telling the public that he is not afraid of familiarity.

Across the state today, nobody can discuss the governor fairly without starting from security. Here is a governor who inherited a state close to a war zone, with more than 300 cult-related killings recorded in 2024 alone. His response was to replace the weak anti-cultism law with a stronger one, give security agencies new Hilux vans and motorcycles, in their hundreds, and recruit 2,500 officers into the Edo State Security Corps. He went further by recruiting 1000 forest guards to make the forests safe.

Is Edo now free of crime? No, and he has never claimed so, but crime has reduced drastically. The bloodbath that cultism foisted on the dead has been reduced to a dramatic extent. He once told worshippers in Auchi that insecurity remains on his mind and that criminal elements would be driven out. That honesty matters. A state does not heal in 24 months, but the direction of travel counts.

Some of the governor’s most telling work outside security has been his healthcare agenda. He met the Anegbette General Hospital closed for 19 years and reopened it. Obayantor General Hospital was also reopened after 22 years. The Central Hospital Annex in Benin City now runs 24-hour services with an accident and emergency unit. The administration recruited 1,376 health workers, supplied equipment to all 36 secondary health facilities, and enrolled more than 600,000 residents in the Edo State Health Insurance Scheme and has builtand renovatedwell over 70 Primary healthcare centres across the threesenatorial districts.

The personal gestures fit the same pattern. In March, the governor visited Irrua Specialist Teaching Hospital and settled the bills of a burned couple from Ekpoma, whose wife had delivered a baby by caesarean section, along with those of other patients on the wards. No policy paper produces that. It comes from a man standing at a hospital bed.

Edo people have, over time, judged governments by their roads, and the governor knows it. He has said plainly that bad roads were among the things he inherited. His administration has listed the Ramat Park flyover and a second flyover at Adesuwa junction in Benin City among its flagship projects. Motorists and residents in Benin City have commended the rehabilitation of inner-city roads. Local councils also received 54 units of heavy-duty equipment, including graders, excavators, and rollers, shared among all 18 councils to rehabilitate rural communities.

Not every road is finished, and flooding still threatens communities. Only this week, he inspected projects in Benin City and pledged to tackle flooding and erosion and to complete critical road and drainage works. The work is real, and so is the unfinished part. But the governor is committed.

In the classroom, Governor Monday Okpebholo has recruited 5,000 permanent teachers and upgraded 63 schools to modern standards. At the reopening of the renovated Oredo Girls School, the governor said better staffing and infrastructure were showing results. This is one of the many schools that have been turned around.

On the farm side, the state now has farms, warehouses, and tractors for mechanized agriculture. The state farms at Udomi is a beacon, a step meant to raise standards and give young farmers a firmer footing. Agriculture sits in the SHINE Agenda for a reason: a state that feeds itself is harder to push around.

Sport has been a quiet success. Team Edo won 302 medals at the 22nd National Sports Festival in Abeokuta and finished third at the maiden Niger Delta Sports Festival in Uyo. The Sports Writers Association of Nigeria named him Distinguished Governor of the Year. Young athletes are among the people who feel the change most directly.

Employment has come through recruitment as well as support for small businesses. Beyond the teachers and health workers, the government approved N1 billion in soft loans for market women and revitalised the Uromi and Igarra skills acquisition centers, which produced over 140 graduates in 2025. When 41 Edo citizens fled xenophobic attacks in South Africa, he gave N1 million to each returnee. The government has also paid salaries regularly and kept the N75,000 minimum wage.

The 2026 budget of N939.85 billion, he christened the Budget of Hope and Growth, rests on the SHINE Agenda: Security, Healthcare, Infrastructure, Natural Resources and Agriculture, and Education.

“Okpe’s baby,” the alias works well with the governor because his policies agree with it. A government that reopens a hospital shut for 19 years, pays a stranger’s medical bill, inspects a flooded street in person, and loans money to market women is not governing from a distance. It meets people where they are.

Recognition has followed.New TELEGRAPH gave him an award following his tremendous interventions in education, LEADERSHIP named him Governor of the Year 2026, SILVERBIRD also named him as Governor of the Year 2026,while still counting and the SHINE Agenda has drawn praise from several quarters. Honors are pleasant, but the governor himself would say the real test is a mother in Ekpoma, a trader in Benin, or a farmer in Etsako asking whether life is better than it was two years ago.

On that question, Edo people will decide, as they should. The roads must be finished, the floods tamed, and insecurity pushed back further. Two years is a beginning. Okpe’s baby has shown he can walk the streets.

The next two years will definitely, by the grace of God, be one that will ursher in more development and progress to Edo State.

• Ebojele, PhD is Chief Press Secretary to Governor Monday Okpebholo of Edo State.

title: Diplomatic row looms as South Africa summons Fani-Kayode
description:
• Protests Nigerian envoy’s social media remarks, invokes Vienna Convention
From Aidoghie Paulinus, Abuja
The diplomatic row involving Nigeria’s High Commissioner to South Africa, Femi Fani-Kayode, and the South African authorities has deepened, with Pretoria summoning the Nigerian envoy over his al
content:
• Protests Nigerian envoy’s social media remarks, invokes Vienna Convention

From Aidoghie Paulinus, Abuja

The diplomatic row involving Nigeria’s High Commissioner to South Africa, Femi Fani-Kayode, and the South African authorities has deepened, with Pretoria summoning the Nigerian envoy over his allegations that his presentation of letters of credence to President Cyril Ramaphosa was deliberately excluded from a live broadcast.

South Africa also expressed concern over Fani-Kayode’s subsequent remarks on social media, invoking the 1961 Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations and insisting that official communication with the host government must be conducted through established diplomatic channels.

Director-General of South Africa’s Department of International Relations and Cooperation (DIRCO), Zane Dangor, conveyed the government’s position during a meeting with Fani-Kayode yesterday, following the controversy that erupted after the Nigerian envoy presented his credentials alongside 14 other foreign diplomats last Friday.

In a statement made available to Daily Sun, DIRCO said Dangor expressed South Africa’s concern over developments following the ceremony and the Nigerian diplomat’s public comments, stressing the need to preserve the longstanding relationship between the two countries.

“The Director-General reaffirmed the importance of preserving the longstanding and historic bilateral relationship between South Africa and Nigeria, which is founded on mutual respect, friendship and cooperation,” the statement said.

The department disclosed that Dangor specifically drew Fani-Kayode’s attention to Article 41 of the Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations, which governs the conduct of diplomats in their host countries.

“Mr Dangor further recalled the provisions of Article 41 of the Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations (1961), which require diplomatic agents to conduct official business with the receiving State through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

“In this regard, it was emphasised that all official communication should be conducted through established diplomatic channels, including DIRCO,” the South African government stated.

The latest development followed a series of exchanges between Fani-Kayode, the South African Presidency and the South African Broadcasting Corporation (SABC) over the handling of the November 13 ceremony at the Sefako Makgatho Presidential Guest House in Pretoria.

Fani-Kayode, who presented his credentials alongside 14 other foreign envoys, alleged that his introduction and speech were deliberately excluded from the Presidency’s livestream, although the presentations of other diplomats were broadcast.

He claimed that the transmission was interrupted before his address and resumed after he had concluded his presentation to Ramaphosa.

The Nigerian envoy said he subsequently raised the matter with the South African President, who, according to him, intervened and directed officials to address the complaint.

However, Ramaphosa’s spokesperson, Vincent Magwenya, disputed aspects of Fani-Kayode’s account, explaining that the President had directed him to Sophie Mokoena, the SABC’s acting political and foreign editor, to resolve the broadcasting complaint.

Magwenya maintained that the President did not interfere with the broadcaster’s editorial operations.

The controversy took another turn when the Nigerian High Commission rejected Magwenya’s explanation and criticised his handling of the matter, widening what began as a disagreement over television coverage into a public exchange between the diplomatic mission and the South African Presidency.

The SABC subsequently defended its coverage, insisting that it operated as an independent public service broadcaster and that its editorial decisions were separate from the South African Presidency’s livestream arrangements.

In a statement issued on Sunday, the broadcaster said it covered the ceremony through its SABC News LIVE channel on SABC+ and also showed Fani-Kayode’s arrival on its television platform.

It disclosed that footage of the Nigerian envoy interacting with Ramaphosa had been published on its official social media account.

The broadcaster also expressed regret that Fani-Kayode declined an interview invitation following the ceremony, saying it remained willing to engage with him and the Nigerian High Commission.

However, the SABC’s explanation did not directly resolve the envoy’s complaint about the omission of his speech from the Presidency’s livestream.

The South African Presidency later released a recording containing Fani-Kayode’s address, although the development did not immediately end the disagreement.

Reports of the original broadcast indicated that the transmission appeared to develop a technical problem during the presentation by the French ambassador, Antoine Michon, who spoke immediately before Fani-Kayode. The available reports did not establish that the interruption was deliberate.

The diplomatic disagreement comes against the background of longstanding relations between Nigeria and South Africa, two major African economies whose ties have periodically been strained by attacks on foreign nationals, immigration-related tensions and disagreements over the treatment of Nigerian citizens.

Concerns over the safety of Nigerians in South Africa have remained a recurring issue in bilateral relations, with Nigerian authorities and lawmakers previously raising objections to attacks and harassment involving their citizens.

The latest dispute has therefore placed renewed attention on the conduct of diplomatic engagement between Abuja and Pretoria, particularly the procedures governing communication between foreign envoys and their host governments.

Despite the controversy, DIRCO maintained that South Africa remained committed to strengthening its strategic partnership with Nigeria and sustaining constructive diplomatic engagement in the spirit of African solidarity and mutual respect.
