title: FG orders recovery of excess payments to university workers
description:
The Federal Government has directed federal universities, polytechnics and colleges of education to recover all overpayments arising from the implementation of the 2025/2026 remuneration agreements with tertiary education unions within three months.
The government also capped the payment of excess w
content:
The Federal Government has directed federal universities, polytechnics and colleges of education to recover all overpayments arising from the implementation of the 2025/2026 remuneration agreements with tertiary education unions within three months.

The government also capped the payment of excess workload allowance for academic and non-academic staff in federal universities at a maximum of 52 hours per month.

The directives were contained in a November 11, 2026, circular issued by the National Salaries, Incomes and Wages Commission and signed by its Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, Maj. Gen. Junaid S. Bindawa.

The circular, with reference number SWC/S/04/S.149/T/187, was addressed to the Chief of Staff to the President, Secretary to the Government of the Federation, Head of the Civil Service of the Federation, ministers, federal permanent secretaries and heads of government agencies, among others.

The commission said the clarification became necessary following several requests from universities, colleges of education and polytechnics seeking guidance on the implementation of remuneration packages contained in the 2025/2026 agreements between the Federal Government and tertiary education-based unions.

It stated, “Following several requests from Universities, Colleges of Education and Polytechnics on the urgent need for clarification on the implementation of remuneration packages contained in the 2025/2026 Agreements between the Federal Government of Nigeria and the Tertiary Education Institutions Based-Unions, the Commission wishes to clarify as follows.”

On the Consolidated Academic Tools Allowance, the commission said the payment was restricted to academic staff on the Consolidated University Academic Salary Structure and the Consolidated Polytechnics and Colleges of Education Salary Structure.

It explained that vice-chancellors, rectors and provosts were not entitled to the allowance because they were not on the specified salary structures.

The circular stated that the allowance did not apply to the heads of the institutions because they were covered by the Certain Political, Public and Judicial Officer Salaries (Salaries, Allowance, etc.) (Amendment) Act 2008.

It further excluded staff on the Consolidated Medical Salary Structure and associated medical allowances, citing ongoing negotiations between the Federal Government and health-sector unions.

The commission said, “This does not apply to staff on Consolidated Medical Salary Structures and associated medical allowances, as collective bargaining is ongoing between the FGN and Health Sector-Based Associations and Unions on the review of CONMESS and associated medical allowances.”

Similarly, it restricted the Consolidated Non-Teaching Tools Allowance to non-academic staff on the Consolidated Tertiary Institutions Salary Structure and Consolidated Tertiary Education Institutions Salary Structure.

The commission also excluded workers on the Consolidated Health Salary Structure and associated medical allowances.

It said, “This does not apply to staff on the Consolidated Health Salary Structure and associated medical allowances, as collective bargaining is ongoing between the FGN and Health Sector-Based Associations and Unions on the review of CONHESS and associated medical allowances.”

On the Excess Workload Allowance, the commission specifically directed that payments to members of ASUU and NASU in federal universities must not exceed 52 hours monthly.

It stated, “A maximum of 52 hours per month applies to the payment of Excess Workload Allowance for the Academic Staff Union of Universities and the Non-Academic Union of Educational and Associated Institutions in Federal Universities.”

The circular also addressed the 10 per cent Earned Academic Allowance, explaining that the provision in the revised salary structure of university academic staff was designed for mainstreaming and budgeting, with five per cent allocated to employees funded by the Federal Government and the remaining five per cent to those funded by university councils through internally generated revenue.

According to the commission, the provision was captured on page 12 of the agreement between the Federal Government and ASUU.

It stated, “The provision of 10% academic earned allowance (EAA) in the table of revised total salary of universities’ academic staff as approved on page 12 of the agreement between FGN and ASUU was for mainstreaming and budgeting – 5% for those funded by FGN and 5% for those funded by Councils through Internally-Generated Revenue.”

However, the commission warned that the implementation must follow its earlier circular of December 30, 2025, which outlined the categories of beneficiaries funded by the Federal Government and university councils.

It said, “However, the implementation of EAA should be in line with the Commission’s Circular No. SWC/S/04/149/IV/924 dated 30th December 2025, which clearly identified those funded by FGN and Councils, respectively.”

The commission subsequently directed all federal universities, polytechnics and colleges of education to comply with the clarifications and recover excess payments within the stipulated period.

It stated, “All Federal Universities, Colleges of Education and Polytechnics are to comply with these clarifications, and all overpayments should be recovered within three months.”

It added, “All enquiries relating to this circular should be directed to the Commission.”

The directive comes amid the Federal Government’s efforts to implement renegotiated remuneration agreements with academic and non-academic unions in the tertiary education sector after years of disputes over workers’ welfare, salaries, funding and conditions of service.

The Federal Government and ASUU signed their renegotiated 2025 agreement on December 23, 2025, following prolonged negotiations over the 2009 agreement. The deal introduced a 40 per cent upward review of university academic staff emoluments, effective January 1, 2026, alongside improved allowances and pension benefits.

In February 2026, the Minister of Education, Dr Tunji Alausa, announced the commencement of implementation of the 40 per cent increase in the Consolidated Academic Allowance, directing federal universities to reflect the approved adjustments in their payroll systems.

The Federal Government subsequently unveiled the 2026 agreements with academic and non-academic staff unions in October, announcing the payment of approved allowances to eligible personnel across universities, polytechnics and colleges of education, effective January 1, 2026.

The agreements cover unions including ASUU, the Academic Staff Union of Polytechnics, the Colleges of Education Academic Staff Union, the Senior Staff Association of Nigerian Universities and NASU. The government said the agreements were designed to improve staff welfare, strengthen industrial harmony and reduce disruptions to academic calendars.

Meanwhile, healthcare professionals in federal universities have threatened legal action against the National Salaries, Incomes and Wages Commission over the contents of the circular.

The affected medical doctors, nurses, pharmacists, medical laboratory scientists and allied health professionals, under the Coalition of Healthcare Professionals in Tertiary Education Institutions of Nigeria, described the circular as discriminatory and contrary to earlier government directives on the allowance.

The National Chairman and Coordinator of CHPTEIN, Musa Shehu, said in his reaction that the disputed circular, with reference number SWC/S/04/S.149/T/187, restricted CONTTA payments to employees on the Consolidated Tertiary Institutions Salary Structure, excluding those on the Consolidated Medical Salary Structure and Consolidated Health Salary Structure.

He noted that the original circulars, “referenced SWC/S/04/S.149/V/1067 for SSANU and SWC/S/04/S.149/IV/1071 for NASU, did not expressly exclude healthcare professionals earning salaries under CONMESS and CONHESS.”

He also maintained that the affected workers were non-teaching employees of federal universities and legitimate members of the two unions, with their check-off dues regularly deducted from their salaries.

“The Budget Office of the Federation calculated the financial implications of CONTTA based on the entire workforce of the Non-teaching staff on the payroll.”

CHPTEIN added that the ministry warned vice-chancellors in paragraph five of the circular that any deviation from the approved scope of funds released by the Federal Government would attract appropriate sanctions.

Questioning the basis for excluding healthcare professionals, the coalition asked why workers classified as non-teaching staff should be denied the allowance when the funds were reportedly calculated based on the entire non-teaching workforce.

title: Electoral violence: No life worth wasting over politics, Kalu warns
description:
• Dismisses opposition coalition, says Tinubu has no formidable challenger  • Denies supplying arms to IPOB, disowns allegations against Abia deputy gov

From Adesuwa Tsan, Abuja
Former Abia State governor and Senator representing Abia North, Orji Uzor Kalu, has warned politicians and their supporte
content:
• Dismisses opposition coalition, says Tinubu has no formidable challenger  • Denies supplying arms to IPOB, disowns allegations against Abia deputy gov

From Adesuwa Tsan, Abuja

Former Abia State governor and Senator representing Abia North, Orji Uzor Kalu, has warned politicians and their supporters against turning the 2027 general elections into a battlefield, declaring that no political ambition or electoral victory is worth the loss of human lives.

Kalu, who condemned the growing wave of attacks on political leaders and their supporters, said political contests should be fought on the strength of candidates’ achievements, leadership records and capacity to deliver good governance rather than through intimidation, thuggery and violence.

He also dismissed the emerging opposition coalition as belated and divided, declaring that President Bola Tinubu had no formidable challenger in the forthcoming presidential election and describing the contest as a battle of “Tinubu versus Tinubu.”

Speaking with journalists shortly after receiving the Best Impactful Representation Award from the Senate Press Corps at the National Assembly, Abuja, on Tuesday, Kalu expressed concern that political violence, which had troubled Nigeria since independence, was again threatening to overshadow democratic competition.

“Nobody has asked anybody to go and fight or engage in violence. Campaigns should be fought based on what candidates have done for the country. No life is worth wasting because of politics.”

He urged political leaders to restrain their supporters and discourage inflammatory rhetoric, stressing that political disagreements should never be allowed to destroy relationships or threaten national unity.

According to him, leading politicians across party lines maintained cordial personal relationships despite their political differences, a lesson he said their supporters should learn rather than resort to violence in defence of individual political ambitions.

“Tinubu, Atiku, Obi, Makinde and others are all friends who eat at the same table. Nigeria needs unity. We don’t need fighting,” he said.

His warning came against the backdrop of mounting concerns over political attacks and intimidation ahead of the 2027 elections, with the Senate also debating incidents involving President Tinubu and opposition political leaders.

Turning to the emerging opposition coalition, Kalu argued that the parties seeking to challenge the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) had wasted valuable time and remained divided over leadership and the choice of a presidential candidate.

He said a genuinely united opposition could have presented a more difficult contest for the APC but maintained that the ongoing consultations had come too late to substantially alter the political calculations ahead of the election.

“If they had sincerely come together, it would have given APC a headache, but not a win. The game is already too late for them because they cannot even agree on who will be their presidential candidate.”

Kalu dismissed the possibility that consultations involving the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) and other opposition platforms would produce a coalition capable of defeating the ruling party.

“We are not afraid of any party. APC is the ruling party, and we have massive grassroots support,” he declared. The senator, however, cautioned against making unsubstantiated allegations of sponsorship of political violence, particularly against public office holders.

Reacting to claims by the Abia State Tinubu Support Group that the state’s deputy governor was sponsoring thugs to attack supporters of the President, Kalu said anyone found culpable of recruiting, financing or training political thugs should face the consequences of the law.

He stressed that such conduct should not be associated with persons entrusted with public responsibilities but maintained that he had no verified evidence linking the deputy governor to the allegation.

Kalu said he did not personally believe the claims, describing the deputy governor as a well-trained engineer with whom he had maintained a longstanding relationship.

He nevertheless appealed to Governor Alex Otti to engage his deputy and encourage actions that would promote political stability and peaceful coexistence in the state.

The senator said security agencies, including the Department of State Services (DSS), could investigate the allegations and invite anyone considered necessary for questioning, stressing that accusations of political violence should be established through credible investigations rather than public speculation.

On the controversy generated by his earlier remarks about international arms transactions, Kalu denied ever supplying weapons to the proscribed Indigenous People of Biafra (IPOB), insisting that he was neither a defence contractor nor involved in illegal arms dealings.

He explained that international arms transactions could constitute legitimate commercial activities when undertaken by licensed and authorised entities in accordance with applicable regulations, but stressed that his comments should not be interpreted as support for supplying weapons to terrorists, bandits or private individuals.

“I have never supplied arms to IPOB. I have never seen arms in my life,” he maintained.

Responding to speculation about his possible presidential ambition following a prophecy by Prophet Ebuka Obi of the Zion Prayer Movement that he would become Nigeria’s president before the age of 70, Kalu said the fulfilment of divine will could not be determined by human calculations.

He recalled contesting the presidential election in 2007 but said he had no immediate intention of seeking the office again, preferring to concentrate on his legislative responsibilities.

“The will of God is always the will of God, and nobody can stop it. I am capable, and I ran for president when I was much younger, but for now, I have no ambition. I want to sit quietly in the Senate,” he said.

Earlier, Kalu dedicated the Senate Press Corps’ Best Impactful Representation Award to the people of Abia North, describing the recognition as an acknowledgment of the development efforts undertaken across the senatorial district since his election to the National Assembly in 2019.

The award citation highlighted projects and interventions across the five local government areas of Bende, Ohafia, Isuikwuato, Umunneochi and Arochukwu, particularly in road construction, education, healthcare, agriculture and economic empowerment.

According to the organisers, Kalu had facilitated the construction and rehabilitation of more than 160 rural and agricultural access roads, alongside over 200 school structures and classroom blocks across the district.

Other interventions cited included scholarships, payment of Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board (JAMB) examination fees, provision of educational materials, rehabilitation of community health centres, installation of solar-powered streetlights and provision of boreholes in more than 150 communities.

The citation also recognised the distribution of agricultural inputs and more than 1,000 cassava processing machines, as well as the facilitation of cashew processing factories and tricycle assembly plants.

Under his constituency empowerment programmes, Kalu was credited with distributing motorcycles, sewing machines, generators, refrigerators, tricycles, laptops and financial grants to beneficiaries across Abia North.

In his acceptance speech, the senator disclosed that more than 49 additional roads were under construction across the district, with progress dependent on the release of relevant budgetary funds.

“If the budget has been released, there are more than 49 new roads currently being constructed in the district,” he said.

Kalu explained that his approach to representation prioritised infrastructure and human capital development over the routine distribution of material items, arguing that investments in roads, education and skills acquisition would deliver more enduring economic benefits.

“What is meant for the public is for the public. My duty is to serve the people.

“I don’t mostly do empowerment because empowerment is not the way to save the economy. We have to go back to providing roads, sending children to school and sending people to study so they can be useful to their communities.”

He reaffirmed his commitment to extending development projects across the five local government areas of Abia North, saying his legislative responsibilities remained focused on improving infrastructure, expanding educational opportunities and supporting economic activities in the district.

The post Electoral violence: No life worth wasting over politics, Kalu warns appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Senate orders probe of attacks on Tinubu, Obi, Atiku
description:
From Adesuwa Tsan, Abuja
Alarmed by the wave of attacks on political leaders and their supporters ahead of the 2027 general elections, the Senate, yesterday, ordered an investigation into reported assaults on President Bola Tinubu and opposition presidential candidates, Peter Obi and Atiku Abubakar,
content:
From Adesuwa Tsan, Abuja

Alarmed by the wave of attacks on political leaders and their supporters ahead of the 2027 general elections, the Senate, yesterday, ordered an investigation into reported assaults on President Bola Tinubu and opposition presidential candidates, Peter Obi and Atiku Abubakar, as lawmakers raised concerns that politicians themselves were sponsoring the violence threatening the electoral process.

The Senate also warned that candidates found culpable in electoral violence through the activities of their agents could face disqualification, with Senate President Godswill Akpabio drawing attention to provisions of the Electoral Act 2026 prescribing sanctions for political thuggery and intimidation.

The resolutions followed a motion of urgent public importance sponsored by Senator Abdul Ningi, which highlighted attacks on political leaders, campaign convoys and supporters across the country, including the reported stoning of Tinubu’s motorcade in Abuja on November 13, attacks involving Nigerian Democratic Congress (NDC) presidential candidate Peter Obi and African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate Atiku Abubakar, and violence at political gatherings.

In a particularly troubling contribution, Senator Samaila Kawu accused politicians of being behind much of the violence, alleging that some supplied weapons and drugs to young people to attack opponents and disrupt political activities.

“We are the sponsors of all what is going on,” he declared, urging security agencies to move beyond arresting perpetrators to identifying and prosecuting those financing and encouraging political thuggery.

The Senate consequently directed its Committees on National Security and Intelligence, Public Affairs and Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to engage relevant security and electoral institutions and report back within one week on measures to prevent further attacks and safeguard the elections.

It also urged the Federal Government to direct the Inspector-General of Police and other security agencies to strengthen protection for political leaders, candidates, supporters and campaign gatherings nationwide, while establishing effective early-warning and rapid-response mechanisms to contain electoral violence.

Moving the motion, Ningi expressed concern over what he described as an alarming escalation of political intolerance, intimidation and violence, warning that the trend could undermine public confidence in the electoral process and discourage citizens from exercising their democratic rights.

He specifically drew attention to the reported attack on Tinubu’s motorcade shortly after the President observed Jumat prayers at the Shehu Shagari Central Mosque, Garki, Abuja, on November 13.

According to the motion, the convoy was attacked with stones and other dangerous objects as it departed the mosque, resulting in damage to vehicles and injuries to security operatives.

The Senate also recalled the reported attack on Obi and other political stakeholders in Benue State, the disruption of a procession involving supporters of the NDC and Obidient Movement in Asaba, Delta State, on November 7, which reportedly left one person dead and five others injured, and the attack on Atiku’s convoy in Sokoto State.

Contributing to the debate, Senator Mohammed Ndume warned that the National Assembly must take a firm stand against political violence, irrespective of the party affiliation or political standing of those targeted. “What we need to do as a Senate is to stand up solely against any form of violence.”

Ndume described the reported attack on Tinubu as a national embarrassment, arguing that an assault on the President diminished the country’s democratic institutions.

“What happened last Friday to Mr President is not an embarrassment to Mr President, it is an embarrassment to Nigerians,” he declared.

Questioning the justification for attacking political leaders because of their positions, he asked: “What are the youths saying, that who God chose as president is wrong?”

He commended Tinubu’s response to the incident, contrasting it with what he suggested might have happened under military rule.

“The President is a democrat. If it were military, those 88 people that were arrested that day would have been dead,” he said.

Ndume urged the police to prohibit the carrying of knives, sticks and other objects capable of being used as weapons at political rallies, while advocating mobile courts for the speedy trial of suspects implicated in electoral violence.

He also warned against political slogans calling for the removal of leaders, arguing that inflammatory rhetoric could encourage intolerance and confrontation among supporters.

“Tinubu must go, Atiku must go, Obi must go. So if everybody goes, who will remain?” he asked.

Kawu, while condemning the attack on the President, said the problem of political violence could not be effectively addressed without confronting the politicians who allegedly recruited, armed and financed those responsible.

He alleged that some political actors supplied weapons and drugs to youths to unleash violence on opponents, citing an incident involving a National Assembly candidate who was allegedly seen carrying weapons without facing any known consequences.

Kawu, however, cautioned security agencies against excessive force, referring to an alleged incident during an All Progressives Congress (APC) rally in Sokoto State, where security operatives reportedly shot at supporters wearing party insignia as they entered the venue.

He stressed that the responsibility to prevent electoral violence must extend to both political actors and security personnel, whose conduct could either strengthen or undermine confidence in the electoral process.

Senate Minority Leader Abba Moro warned that persistent attacks on candidates and supporters could ultimately disenfranchise voters and weaken democratic participation.

He urged security agencies to rise to their responsibilities by ensuring that political campaigns and other electoral activities were conducted peacefully, without intimidation or harassment.

Senator Babangida Hussaini, in his contribution, recalled recommendations of the Justice Mohammed Uwais-led Electoral Reform Committee, particularly proposals for the establishment of an electoral offences commission and specialised courts to deal with electoral violence.

He lamented that the failure to implement far-reaching measures against electoral offences had allowed political thuggery and intimidation to persist.

“We have begun to see the results of what we have not done,” he said.

Hussaini also alleged that an ADC candidate in his state openly brandished a pistol without any known action being taken against him.

“We have paid lip service with this matter and we have to be serious about it,” he declared.

Senator Sampson Ekong called for a level playing field for candidates across political parties, stressing that the right to campaign freely and peacefully must be protected regardless of political affiliation.

He urged the Federal Ministry of Information and the National Orientation Agency to embark on intensive public enlightenment campaigns to discourage electoral violence and promote political tolerance.

In his closing remarks, Akpabio warned that the consequences of political violence could extend beyond the arrest and prosecution of thugs to the disqualification of candidates implicated in such activities.

He called for the full implementation of the Electoral Act 2026, particularly Sections 121 to 128, which he said contained provisions prescribing sanctions for electoral violence and misconduct.

According to him, candidates whose agents incited violence could face disqualification where INEC established a prima facie case against them.

He added that candidates who carried weapons or encouraged armed thugs to surround them could also face disqualification under the law.

Akpabio warned parents and guardians to caution their children against participating in attacks on political leaders, saying some actions could attract serious criminal charges.

“We must warn our children because there are certain things you can do and it will turn out to be treasonable felony,” he said.

Referring to the reported attack on Tinubu’s motorcade, the Senate President said those involved could have faced charges of treasonable felony, warning that a confrontation with security operatives could have resulted in fatalities.

“If the security agents had attacked, such a child may not get back home,” he said.

The Senate subsequently mandated its three committees to engage relevant security and electoral institutions and submit their findings and recommendations within one week, as concerns mount over the safety of political leaders, their supporters and the integrity of the electoral process ahead of the 2027 elections.

The post Senate orders probe of attacks on Tinubu, Obi, Atiku appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Flamingos coach gets CAF Awards nomination
description:
FIFA Women’s U-17 World Cup-winning coach Akeem Busari has been nominated for the CAF Women’s Coach of the Year Award, days after leading Nigeria’s Flamingos to a historic triumph in Morocco, PUNCH Sports Extra reports.
Busari’s nomination was announced on Tuesday alongside nine other coaches as the
content:
FIFA Women’s U-17 World Cup-winning coach Akeem Busari has been nominated for the CAF Women’s Coach of the Year Award, days after leading Nigeria’s Flamingos to a historic triumph in Morocco, PUNCH Sports Extra reports.

Busari’s nomination was announced on Tuesday alongside nine other coaches as the Confederation of African Football unveiled nominees for the final three women’s categories at the CAF Awards 2026, scheduled for Lagos on Wednesday, December 2.

The other categories are Women’s Club Player of the Year and Women’s Club of the Year.

The Nigerian will face competition from coaches across the continent, including Algeria’s Farid Benstiti, Cameroon’s Valentine Nguele, Ghana’s Kim Lars Bjorkegren, Morocco’s Jorge Vilda, South Africa’s Desiree Ellis and Tanzania’s Bakari Nyundo Shime.

Others nominated are Silveria Nedio of Cabo Verde, Lovemore Fazili of Malawi and Hicham Drissi of Moroccan club AS FAR.

Busari guided the Flamingos to Nigeria’s first FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup title in Morocco, making them the first African team to win the competition.

According to CAF, voting for the 2026 awards opened on November 5 and will close on November 20, with CAF Member Associations, clubs and eligible coaches and captains participating in the process.

The awards ceremony will hold at the Professor Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture and the Arts, formerly the National Theatre, in Lagos, with proceedings scheduled to begin at 7pm local time.

The CAF Awards 2026 will recognise outstanding achievements across 18 categories, honouring players, coaches, clubs and national teams for their performances in African football over the past year.

title: Eight Nigerians charged with over $4.5m car theft in Canada
description:
Eight Nigerians have been charged alongside four other people in Canada over an alleged organised vehicle theft network linked to the recovery of 96 stolen vehicles valued at more than $4.5m and reportedly destined for West Africa.
Peel Regional Police in Ontario disclosed this in a statement publis
content:
Eight Nigerians have been charged alongside four other people in Canada over an alleged organised vehicle theft network linked to the recovery of 96 stolen vehicles valued at more than $4.5m and reportedly destined for West Africa.

Peel Regional Police in Ontario disclosed this in a statement published on its website on Monday, saying the 12 suspects were facing a total of 231 charges following an investigation into the theft and exportation of luxury sport utility vehicles, pickup trucks and other high-value vehicles.

The investigation, code-named Project Cadetta, began in March 2026 in partnership with the Canada Border Services Agency and initially focused on a warehouse in Brampton, Ontario, allegedly used to store stolen vehicles before they were shipped to West Africa through Canadian ports.

Police said the investigation later uncovered a wider criminal network operating across the Greater Toronto Area and neighbouring jurisdictions.

According to the police, five key suspects allegedly coordinated the theft, movement and exportation of the vehicles, while others supported the operation through loading sites, container movements and transportation of vehicles with altered identification numbers.

The 96 recovered vehicles were discovered concealed in shipping containers, the police said.

Those listed as Nigerian include Stanley Udeh, 46, of Brampton; Odewale Abraham, 57; Oluyemi Sodade, 51; Tosin Damilola Oyebade, 45; Oluwaseyi Olawale Bameke, 39; and Olushola Oke, 42, all of Toronto.

Others are Gbolahan Qudus Babatunde, 29, of Vaughan, and Kenneth Okafor, 58, listed as having no fixed address.

The other accused are Karamveer Singh, 26, of Brampton; Henrik Gancz, 57; Jaspreet Singh, 25, both listed as having no fixed address; and Darryl Davance, 25, of Saint-Jerome, Quebec.

The accused face various charges, including possession of property obtained by crime, trafficking in stolen goods valued at more than $5,000, forgery and uttering forged documents. One of them also faces a charge of dangerous operation of a motor vehicle.

Peel Regional Police said nine of the accused were charged and released with future court dates, while three were held for bail hearings and subsequently released.

The police added that some of the accused could face immigration enforcement action, including possible removal from Canada, after the conclusion of their criminal proceedings.

Commenting on the investigation, the Deputy Chief of Peel Regional Police, Nick Milinovich, said organised vehicle theft was connected to wider criminal activities.

“Organised auto theft is a predatory business model run by transnational syndicates that terrorise families and fund broader criminal enterprises. Through Project Cadetta, our Commercial Auto Crime Bureau and partners dismantled this supply chain from street-level thieves to international export brokers,” he said.

Ontario’s Solicitor General, Michael Kerzner, said the operation demonstrated the government’s commitment to tackling organised criminal networks.

He said, “Organised auto theft is a serious crime that threatens the safety and security of our communities, and our government will never back down from taking on the criminal networks responsible.”

The Canada Border Services Agency’s Acting Regional Director General for the Greater Toronto Area, Trishann Pascal, said the agency helped prevent stolen vehicles from reaching international markets through targeted container examinations and intelligence-sharing with law enforcement partners.

Peel Regional Police said the investigation remained ongoing, adding that further charges were anticipated and arrest warrants had been issued for additional individuals.

The police also reported that auto thefts across Peel Region had declined by more than 50 per cent since reaching a peak in 2023, with a further 10 per cent reduction recorded year-to-date in 2026.

title: Abia PDP candidate pledges 552 boreholes in 100 days
description:
The governorship candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party in Abia State, Dr Kelechi Anosike, has promised to construct 552 solar-powered boreholes across the state’s 184 political wards within his first 100 days in office if elected in 2027.
Anosike said the proposed intervention was intended to en
content:
The governorship candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party in Abia State, Dr Kelechi Anosike, has promised to construct 552 solar-powered boreholes across the state’s 184 political wards within his first 100 days in office if elected in 2027.
Anosike said the proposed intervention was intended to end residents’ reliance on untreated stream water for drinking and reduce the incidence of water-borne diseases.
The PDP candidate made the pledge during a meeting with the Council of Ohafia Monarchs at Elu Ohafia, where he also sought the traditional rulers’ support for his governorship ambition; a statement detailing the interaction was made available to The PUNCH on Tuesday.
He said each political ward would receive three industrial solar-powered boreholes, insisting that access to safe drinking water should no longer be a challenge for communities in the state.

“If there is still a community that is drinking water from the stream, that will stop when we come in because that is the genesis of many water-borne diseases. At this age and time, nobody should take a bucket and go to the stream to fetch untreated water to drink,” he said.
Anosike added, “Within 100 days in office, every political ward in Abia will have three solar-powered industrial boreholes. You can go to the stream to fetch water for washing clothes and other uses, but not for drinking. We will make sure that the people have good quality and standard drinking water.”
The candidate said his proposed administration would prioritise residents’ welfare through investments in agriculture, industrial development, youth empowerment and healthcare.
He argued that infrastructure development must be accompanied by policies addressing the immediate economic needs of residents, particularly access to food.

Under his proposed ‘Let-your-money-work-for-you’ policy, Anosike said local governments would involve community stakeholders in deciding how development funds were spent.
He claimed that Ohafia had received about N19bn over three years, translating to between N550m and N600m monthly, but questioned the condition of community roads despite the reported allocations.
He promised that funds accruing to local governments would be deployed towards projects benefiting their respective communities, with residents participating in decisions on development priorities.
Anosike also blamed Abia’s high cost of living on the state’s dependence on other states for food supplies, claiming that about 90 per cent of the food consumed in Abia came from outside the state.
He alleged that the state lacked an effective agricultural programme and argued that greater investment in farming would help reduce food prices and create employment.

The PDP candidate also promised to review the allowances of traditional rulers, saying the existing payments did not adequately reflect their responsibilities as custodians of the state’s traditional institutions.
“I have what I call the Traditional Rulers Council regulation order. We will review it. Whatever they are paying you now, we will pay twice that because you are the custodians of our traditional heritage,” he said.
He described his proposed approach to governance as a welfare-driven model, summarising his development philosophy with the expression, “aruo uzo, aruo afo” — build roads, build stomachs.
At a subsequent rally in Ohafia, where he presented his manifesto, Anosike outlined additional proposals on education, youth employment, healthcare and economic development.

He proposed making skills acquisition compulsory in universities, with the state government providing students with two vocational skills alongside their academic qualifications.
He also promised start-up capital for aspiring entrepreneurs through a proposed Traders Microfinance Bank and pledged to export 30 talented young footballers annually.
The candidate said his administration would train young people for remote and virtual employment opportunities with companies in Europe, America and Asia.

On healthcare, he proposed a state health insurance arrangement under which the government would subsidise 60 per cent of patients’ medical bills, leaving them to pay the remaining 40 per cent.
He also promised to equip primary healthcare centres with functional diagnostic and laboratory facilities.

Responding to the candidate’s presentation, the Udumeze of Ohafia, Ezie Elder Awa Oji Udonsi, described his manifesto as people-centred but said the traditional rulers would hold him accountable for the promises.
The monarchs subsequently endorsed Anosike for the 2027 governorship election and prayed for the success of his ambition.

Other PDP candidates at the rally, including the party’s Abia North Senatorial candidate, Jude Udeachara, Emmanuel Agwu Ukpong and Gracelyn Oko Ejim, pledged to work with Anosike to improve governance in the state.
The Secretary-General of the Abia PDP Campaign Council, Ukpai Ukairo, and the party’s Ohafia Local Government Chairman, Ukaku Ojiegbe, also urged residents to support the PDP and its candidates in the forthcoming elections.

The post Abia PDP candidate pledges 552 boreholes in 100 days appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Unlicensed teachers face ban from classrooms by December 2027 —TRCN
description:
From Fred Ezeh, Abuja
The Teachers Registration Council of Nigeria (TRCN) has issued a December 2027 deadline for all teachers across the country to obtain professional certification and practising licences, warning that those who fail to meet the requirements will no longer be permitted to teach in
content:
From Fred Ezeh, Abuja

The Teachers Registration Council of Nigeria (TRCN) has issued a December 2027 deadline for all teachers across the country to obtain professional certification and practising licences, warning that those who fail to meet the requirements will no longer be permitted to teach in Nigerian schools.

The council also uncovered 250 forged professional certificates during a teacher recruitment exercise in Nasarawa State and more than 47 cases of impersonation during its recent qualifying examination in Taraba State, raising fresh concerns over the infiltration of the teaching profession by unqualified personnel and examination fraudsters.

Registrar and Chief Executive of TRCN, Ronke Soyombo, who disclosed this during an interaction with journalists in Abuja, said the council was intensifying its professionalisation programme to ensure that every teacher, whether in public or private schools, possessed the qualifications and credentials required to practise.

She said the certification requirement would apply to everyone seeking recognition as a professional teacher, irrespective of social or political status, revealing that the Deputy Governor of Adamawa State participated in the council’s recent Professional Qualifying Examination (PQE).

“In Adamawa State, for the first time, we actually saw the deputy governor of Adamawa State coming to sit for our exam. She sat for the exam last Friday.” Soyombo described the development as evidence of growing acceptance of professional certification and the need for everyone involved in teaching to meet the same standards.

“Every teacher must be certified, every teacher must be licensed before they can actually teach in our schools,” she declared.

Soyombo explained that while professional certification would be obtained once in a teacher’s lifetime, practising licences would be renewed every three years upon presentation of evidence of participation in Mandatory Continuous Professional Development (MCPD).

According to her, graduates of education programmes were now required to sit for the TRCN qualifying examination before completing their training, while teachers already in service must also undergo the examination to obtain professional recognition.

She acknowledged that compliance with licensing requirements remained low but said the council had introduced an accelerated professionalisation pathway to enable teachers without education degrees to acquire the necessary qualifications.

The registrar disclosed that participation in the qualifying examinations had increased considerably following the introduction of online registration and improvements in the council’s technological infrastructure.

She recalled that approximately 13,000 teachers participated in the examination when she assumed office in May 2025, but the figure rose to about 26,000 by November of the same year.

She added that more than two million teachers were currently registered on the council’s online platform, although many had yet to complete the professional certification and licensing processes.

As part of efforts to enforce compliance, Soyombo disclosed that TRCN was working towards making professional certification a major requirement for schools seeking to register candidates for National Examinations Council (NECO) examinations.

Under the proposed arrangement, schools would be expected to have at least 75 per cent of their teachers professionally certified before qualifying for examination registration.

She said the council had interfaced its website with those of the West African Examinations Council (WAEC) and NECO to facilitate verification of teachers’ credentials and strengthen enforcement.

On examination malpractice, Soyombo revealed that an invigilator in Taraba State detected more than 47 impersonators during the council’s recent Professional Qualifying Examination.

She said the discovery prompted additional measures to protect the integrity of the examination, including the use of candidates’ photographs, surveillance cameras and improved identity-verification technology.

According to her, the council had also upgraded its examination platform from a capacity of 120 candidates to 5,000 simultaneous users, although internet connectivity challenges affected the exercise in two states.

The registrar further disclosed that TRCN uncovered 250 fake professional certificates during a teacher recruitment exercise in Nasarawa State, describing the discovery as evidence of the activities of individuals producing and circulating forged teaching credentials.

She said a suspect identified as Godfrey was in custody over alleged involvement in the production of fake certificates, while the council was collaborating with the police to apprehend other suspects.

To curb certificate forgery and impersonation, Soyombo said TRCN had introduced Quick Response (QR) codes on professional certificates, enabling employers, school proprietors and other stakeholders to verify teachers’ credentials directly through the council’s website.

She explained that the measure would make it easier to identify forged documents and prevent unqualified individuals from gaining employment through fraudulent certification.

Soyombo also disclosed that a proposed amendment to the TRCN Act was before the National Assembly, with provisions intended to strengthen enforcement powers and review penalties considered inadequate for unlicensed teaching.

She, however, maintained that the ongoing legislative process would not derail the council’s professionalisation timetable.

“By 2027, end of the year, we expect everybody to be fully certified as teachers in Nigeria,” she declared.

The registrar said the reforms would also strengthen teacher induction, child protection and professional accountability, while ensuring that teachers continued to update their knowledge and skills throughout their careers.

She maintained that professional certification, periodic licence renewal and continuous training were essential to improving teaching standards, protecting pupils and restoring public confidence in the quality of education delivered in Nigerian schools.

The post Unlicensed teachers face ban from classrooms by December 2027 —TRCN appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Wike approves promotion of 7,714 FCT workers, clears backlog
description:
From Juliana Taiwo-Obalonye, Abuja
Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, has approved the promotion of 7,714 workers of the Federal Capital Territory Administration (FCTA), including 4,220 teachers and 3,494 other civil servants, in a fresh move to clear outstanding promotion
content:
From Juliana Taiwo-Obalonye, Abuja

Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, has approved the promotion of 7,714 workers of the Federal Capital Territory Administration (FCTA), including 4,220 teachers and 3,494 other civil servants, in a fresh move to clear outstanding promotion arrears and address years of stagnation in the civil service.

The approval followed the conclusion of the 2025 and 2026 promotion exercises, with the minister directing the FCT Civil Service Commission to ensure that all eligible workers were promoted and outstanding promotion arrears cleared.

Chairman of the commission, Emeka Ezeh, who announced the approval yesterday, said the exercise was part of the administration’s efforts to boost workers’ morale, reward dedication and resolve promotion backlogs inherited by the Wike-led administration.

Ezeh disclosed that the minister had also granted a pardon to education officers who disrupted the 2025 promotion exercise, allowing them to participate in the 2026 exercise rather than lose their promotion opportunities.

“You will also recall that the Minister approved that Education officers who disrupted the 2025 promotion exercise be pardoned and allowed to participate in the 2026 exercise.

“The Commission subsequently invited all 2025 and 2026 eligible education officers to participate in the just concluded exercise,” he said.

The commission chairman congratulated the successful candidates and urged them to justify their promotions through greater commitment, professionalism and diligence in the discharge of their responsibilities.

He said the administration expected the beneficiaries to reciprocate the gesture by improving service delivery and contributing more effectively to the development of the FCT.

Meanwhile, the commission has scheduled its second pre-retirement workshop for December 16, 2026, as part of preparations for workers expected to leave the service in the first quarter of 2027.

Ezeh said the workshop would cater for FCTA employees due to retire between January 1 and March 31, 2027, providing guidance to help them prepare for life outside the public service.

According to him, 116 workers are expected to retire during the period.

The latest approval follows an earlier promotion exercise in July, when Wike approved the elevation of 3,592 civil servants after the successful conclusion of the 2025 promotion exercise.

title: APC can’t blame opposition for Nigerians’ suffering -ADC
description:
From Ndubuisi Orji, Abuja
The African Democratic Congress (ADC) Presidential Campaign Council has said the All Progressives Congress (APC) cannot blame the opposition for public anger over hardship, challenging the ruling party to substantiate or withdraw allegations that it sponsors young Nigerians
content:
From Ndubuisi Orji, Abuja

The African Democratic Congress (ADC) Presidential Campaign Council has said the All Progressives Congress (APC) cannot blame the opposition for public anger over hardship, challenging the ruling party to substantiate or withdraw allegations that it sponsors young Nigerians to disrupt campaign activities.

In a statement by its Director of Strategic Communication, Phrank Shaibu, the council denied sponsoring violence or recruiting youths to confront political opponents, saying a party controlling the Federal Government should produce evidence of alleged offences and submit it to investigators.

The ADC campaign accused President Bola Tinubu’s administration of worsening living conditions over the past three and a half years, arguing that Nigerians needed no prompting from the opposition to express dissatisfaction.

“For three and a half years, President Bola Tinubu has plucked the feathers from the Nigerian people with policies that have made food, fuel and basic survival painfully expensive. Now he scatters a little campaign grain and expects the wounded to follow him singing his praises.

“Nigerians are wiser than the chicken in that tale. They know who caused their pain, and they need no sponsor to tell him so,” it stated.

The council also questioned what it described as contradictory accounts from the Presidency and the APC campaign council over an alleged attack on the President’s convoy.

“The Presidency earlier denied that the President’s motorcade had been pelted. Now the APC campaign council says people were detained for pelting the convoy with stones and that President Tinubu directed their release. Which account should Nigerians believe?

“If the APC has evidence that the ADC armed or sponsored those people, why were those detained released? Why have the alleged sponsors not been identified and prosecuted? A government with evidence of such a serious offence should hand it to investigators, not fling accusations at its opponents,” it stated.

Calling for an impartial investigation into any alleged attack, the ADC campaign condemned violence against political parties and their supporters.

“We condemn attacks on campaigners, supporters, places of worship and public property, regardless of the party involved. Any alleged attack should be investigated impartially, and responsibility established through evidence,” it said.

The council also called for scrutiny of alleged inducements at campaign events, saying the ruling party should answer questions about its own campaign practices.

“Reports and images of money being distributed at campaign events deserve scrutiny. The ruling party cannot escape that scrutiny by claiming every crowd that refuses to cheer the President has been paid by the ADC.

“Nigerians are entitled to judge this government by the cost of living and by their own daily experience. Calling their anger an opposition plot will not make it disappear,” it stated.

Insisting that the APC must substantiate its allegations or withdraw them, the council said: “Tinubu cannot preside over years of hardship, offer Nigerians a handful of campaign inducements, and demand gratitude. The people know who pulled out the feathers. They will decide for themselves whether to follow him.”

The post APC can’t blame opposition for Nigerians’ suffering -ADC appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Enugu Assembly caps rent increase at 2%, bans hikes for 4 years
description:
From Jude Chinedu, Enugu
The Enugu State House of Assembly has passed a bill seeking to regulate rent increases and check exploitative practices in the state’s housing sector.
The Houses restricted landlords to a maximum rent increment of two per cent in not less than four years, subject to specifie
content:
From Jude Chinedu, Enugu

The Enugu State House of Assembly has passed a bill seeking to regulate rent increases and check exploitative practices in the state’s housing sector.

The Houses restricted landlords to a maximum rent increment of two per cent in not less than four years, subject to specified exceptions.

The proposed legislation is expected to provide significant relief to tenants, particularly residents of Enugu metropolis, by addressing arbitrary rent increases, excessive agency charges and other financial demands imposed on prospective tenants when securing accommodation.

The bill, sponsored by Member representing Nkanu East Constituency, Hon. Okey Mbah, followed growing public outcry over rising rents and exploitative practices by some landlords and estate agents.

Governor Peter Mbah had, during a recent interactive television programme, Enugu Kwenu, hosted by Afia TV, promised to engage the State Assembly to expedite action on pending legislation aimed at addressing the rent crisis in the state.

The bill was subsequently given renewed attention, culminating in its passage yesterday following the adoption of a report presented by a special committee constituted by the House to review the proposed amendments to the state’s Landlord and Tenant Law. Its passage followed the successful completion of the third reading after lawmakers considered and adopted the committee’s recommendations.

The committee comprised members of the House Committees on Housing and Investment, Public Petition, Ethics and Privileges, and Judiciary.

The motion for consideration of the report was moved by the member representing Nkanu West Constituency, Hon. Iloabuchi Abugu, and seconded by the member representing Awgu North Constituency, Rt. Hon. Jane Eneh. Presenting the report, the committee chairman, Hon. Okey Mbah, said the recommendations were the outcome of extensive consultations with relevant stakeholders.

He described the proposed amendment as a people’s-oriented intervention designed to address exploitative practices in the housing sector, protect tenants’ interests and reduce the financial burden associated with securing accommodation. He said the legislation would substantially reduce the cost of renting properties, particularly by regulating ancillary charges that have become additional sources of financial pressure on prospective tenants.

“This bill will subsidise over 60 percent of what residents used to pay while trying to secure accommodation,” he said.

Under the proposed law, landlords would be permitted to review rents only after four years, with any increment capped at two per cent of the prevailing rent. However, an exception of not more than 10 per cent is provided where a landlord has undertaken reasonable renovation of their property.

In his remark after the passage, Speaker of the Assembly, Hon. Uche Ugwu, described the legislation as part of the good governance initiatives of the Peter Mbah administration. He said the proposed law would give tenants across Enugu State a new lease of life by providing legal safeguards against arbitrary rent increases and other exploitative practices.

Speaking with journalists after the passage, the sponsor, Okey Mbah, described the legislation as a people’s bill, saying its spirit and intent were directed at addressing the concerns and yearnings of residents. He expressed concern over the activities of some estate agents who, according to him, impose exorbitant charges on prospective tenants beyond the actual rent payable.

Mbah cited instances where accommodation advertised at N300,000 annually attracts a total payment of N950,000, while a N500,000 apartment could require as much as N1.4 million in overall charges. He said the legislation had addressed such additional financial demands by introducing specific limits on agency, legal and caution fees.

Under the proposed provisions, agency fees would be restricted to five per cent of the annual rent, while legal fees would be capped at 10 percent. Caution fees would also be limited to 10 percent of the annual rent and made refundable.

The lawmaker further explained that the bill provides for a bond account domiciled under the custody of the State Attorney-General to ensure that caution fees are safeguarded and refunded to tenants at the end of their tenancy, subject to an assessment of the property’s fittings and fixtures.

He said the arrangement would prevent the practice whereby tenants lose their caution deposits after vacating rented apartments, regardless of the condition in which they leave the properties.

The bill, titled A Bill for a Law to Amend the Landlord and Tenant Second Amendment Bill, Cap. 101, Revised Laws of Enugu State 2024, House Bill No. 3, 2025, passed its second reading on March 11, 2026, and subsequently underwent a public hearing on March 26, 2026.

With its passage by the House, the bill now awaits the assent of Governor Peter Mbah before it can become law and take effect in the state.

description:
From Okey Sampson, Umuahia 
The Abia State Government has disclosed that the Bank of Industry (BOI) has so far given approval of N1.041 billion for businesses operating in the state under the SME support initiative of Governor Alex Otti’s administration. 
The state has also recorded a 60 percent red
content:
From Okey Sampson, Umuahia

The Abia State Government has disclosed that the Bank of Industry (BOI) has so far given approval of N1.041 billion for businesses operating in the state under the SME support initiative of Governor Alex Otti’s administration.

The state has also recorded a 60 percent reduction in maternal mortality between 2024 and 2026, making Abia to emerge as the state with the second-lowest maternal mortality rate nationwide.

The Commissioner for Information, Prince Okey Kanu, made the disclosure at Government House Umuahia while briefing journalists on the outcome of this week’s state executive meeting.

The commissioner, represented by the Special Adviser to the Governor on Media and Publicity, Mr Ferdinand Ekeoma, said the fund was aimed at strengthening small businesses, creating jobs and expanding economic opportunities. He noted that the sum of ₦206.7 million represent applications that were approved but are currently undergoing documentations for drawing from the funds.

Kanu informed that in line with Goal 8 of the Sustainable Development Goals that speaks to the promotion of sustained, inclusive economic growth, full and productive employment, and decent work for all, the Ministry of Industries and SME’s has so far verified and documented over 110 workshops and 120 shops at the Ohiya- Umuogo- Nsukwe Industrial Cluster.

The information commissioner announced that the state government has approved a review of the remuneration of ad-hoc workers engaged by the Abia State Environmental Protection Agency (ASEPA), with the revised payment taking effect from November 2026. Prince Kanu also disclosed that the Abia State 2027 budget was almost ready for presentation to the state House of Assembly.

The Commissioner for Industries and SMEs, Mike Akpara, explained that out of the approved facilities, ₦382.9 million has already been disbursed to 29 micro entrepreneurs and two small and medium-scale enterprises across different sectors of the state’s economy, while about ₦206 million is awaiting the fulfilment of conditions precedent to drawdown.

Akpara explained that the outstanding facilities would be released once beneficiaries complete the necessary documentation, including the provision of guarantors and collateral, where applicable. He stressed that the intervention was designed to support genuine businesses in Abia, irrespective of their political affiliations.

Meanwhile, Abia State has recorded a 60 percent reduction in maternal mortality between 2024 and 2026.

Ekeoma, who spoke on behalf of the Commissioner for Information, disclosed that the development, which has made the state emerge as the state with the second-lowest maternal mortality rate nationwide, was as a result of the ongoing reforms in the health sector, stressing that it reflected the government’s commitment to strengthening healthcare delivery and expanding access to quality medical services.

He revealed that 190 out of the 200 Project Ekwueme Primary Healthcare Centres (PHCs) earmarked for renovation had been renovated, while 123 had been functionalised to provide essential healthcare services. He added that 27 of the centres had been solarised, with work ongoing on nine others, stating that all 77 World Bank Impact health projects had been completed.

The commissioner further announced that the National Nursing and Midwifery Council, in its accreditation report released on November 13, had increased the admission quota of the Aba Campus of the College of Nursing Sciences from 75 to 120 students.

He said the increase reflected growing recognition of the state’s investments and reforms in the health sector, particularly in strengthening healthcare manpower development.

title: 600 patients benefit from free eye surgeries in Ebonyi
description:
From Uchenna Inya, Abakaliki 
No fewer than 600 patients with cataract-related conditions in Ebonyi, have benefited from free surgeries at the Alex Ekwueme Federal University Teaching Hospital, Abakaliki (AE-FUTHA).
The surgeries were organised by the hospital, in collaboration with the Al-Basar Int
content:
From Uchenna Inya, Abakaliki

No fewer than 600 patients with cataract-related conditions in Ebonyi, have benefited from free surgeries at the Alex Ekwueme Federal University Teaching Hospital, Abakaliki (AE-FUTHA).

The surgeries were organised by the hospital, in collaboration with the Al-Basar International Foundation and the Ebonyi State government.

The figure, which exceeds the initial target of 400, highlights the growing demand for affordable eye care services and the burden of preventable blindness among underserved communities.

Regional Administrative Manager, Al-Basar International Foundation, Kano, Belo Abdullahi Yuguda, made the disclosure yesterday, during the flag-off of the medical intervention in Abakaliki. Yuguda said the programme was part of the foundation’s annual humanitarian intervention in eye healthcare, sponsored by the King Salman Humanitarian Aid and Relief Centre of Saudi Arabia.

He explained that while the Saudi-based humanitarian organisation provides funding, Al-Basar International Foundation serves as the technical partner responsible for deploying specialist medical personnel and coordinating the surgeries. He added that not all the patients screened would immediately qualify for surgery, as some have underlying medical conditions, including hypertension, retinal complications and corneal problems, which require further medical attention before surgery can be safely performed.

He said patients who could not undergo surgery during the Abakaliki exercise could access similar services at the foundation’s facilities in Ibadan, Bauchi, Kano, and other locations. Yuguda, however, appealed to the Ebonyi State Government to consider providing transportation assistance for patients requiring referral to other centres, to enable them to benefit from the intervention.

He further disclosed that over 400,000 free glasses were offered to those with minor cases, while some were given drugs for their eye care.

Chief Medical Director of AE-FUTHA, Professor Robinson Onoh, said more than 20 patients had undergone surgery since the commencement of the exercise, with the medical team targeting between 400 and 800 procedures, depending on the number of eligible patients.

Onoh said the initiative, which commenced with patient screening on Monday, November 16, was designed to make quality eye care accessible to people who could not afford the high cost of treatment.

He explained that the exercise featured phacoemulsification, an advanced cataract removal technique, which he described as more sophisticated than conventional cataract surgery and costs millions of naira in some medical facilities.

The CMD urged residents of Ebonyi and neighbouring states with cataract-related problems to take advantage of the programme, noting that screening and surgeries would continue until November 22. 

He commended Governor Francis Nwifuru for providing the necessary support and enabling environment for the visiting medical team. Onoh also acknowledged the contributions of Mary-Maudline Uzoamaka Nwifuru, the governor’s wife, through her Better Health for All initiative, as well as the Saudi sponsors and the Al-Basar Foundation.

He said about 20 members of the visiting foundation’s medical team were working alongside AE-FUTHA’s ophthalmology department to deliver the services. The intervention is expected to strengthen access to specialised eye care and reduce the financial burden of cataract treatment among low-income residents.

The post 600 patients benefit from free eye surgeries in Ebonyi appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: AWAF launches national health insurance scheme for Aku indigenes
description:
The Aku Welfare Association Federated (AWAF), an umbrella organisation comprising Aku indigenes living in the diaspora, has launched a National Health Insurance Scheme for the people of Aku in Igbo-Etiti Local Government Area of Enugu State.
The launch, which took place at the Aku Civic Centre, Onui
content:
The Aku Welfare Association Federated (AWAF), an umbrella organisation comprising Aku indigenes living in the diaspora, has launched a National Health Insurance Scheme for the people of Aku in Igbo-Etiti Local Government Area of Enugu State.

The launch, which took place at the Aku Civic Centre, Onuigba, Obarazu, Aku, Igbo-Etiti LGA of Enugu State, marks a significant milestone in the association’s efforts to improve the welfare and healthcare access of its people.

The initiative also forms part of activities marking AWAF’s 40th anniversary celebration, scheduled for December 27, 2026.

The epoch-making event attracted stakeholders from various AWAF branches, the Aku General Assembly (AGA), political leaders, Health Maintenance Organisations (HMOs), healthcare providers, community leaders and beneficiaries.

The scheme represents a strategic shift from ad hoc medical assistance to a structured, sustainable, and subsidised healthcare protection system. Key highlights included the unveiling of a comprehensive healthcare benefit package covering primary healthcare, maternal health, and emergency services, as well as the issuance of temporary hospital cards to pilot beneficiaries.

Those in attendance included members of AWAF branches in Port Harcourt, Lagos, Ebonyi, Enugu, and Nsukka; members of the National Executive Council of AWAF, led by its National President, Chief Uche L. Ocho, Esq.; the Aku General Assembly, led by its Chairman, Mathew Enyi; and the President-General of Obie Progressive Union (OPU), Dr. Nnanna Tony Alaku.

Others were political stakeholders; representatives of NEM Health Maintenance Organisation, led by Mrs. Susan Okeke; representatives of the healthcare provider, Attah Memorial Hospital, including Mr. Chinonso Attah and Mr. Amuche Charles Attah Jr.; community leaders and beneficiaries.

Speaking at the event, the National President of AWAF, Chief Uche L. Ocho, Esq., welcomed participants and described the launch as the beginning of the association’s 40th anniversary celebrations and a historic transition from occasional medical assistance to a structured and sustainable healthcare protection system.

He observed that many families in Aku spend a significant proportion of their income on out-of-pocket healthcare expenses, stressing that AWAF could no longer stand by while its people continued to face such challenges. He said the scheme is anchored on the guiding principle: “No Aku man or woman will be left behind”.

He disclosed that the AWAF National Executive, with the support of the Health Insurance Committee, had signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with an accredited Health Maintenance Organisation, NEM Health Insurance, to provide subsidised healthcare coverage for members of the community. He explained that the package covers primary healthcare, secondary referrals, maternal health, and emergency services at a highly subsidised community rate.

The National President, consequently, called on all hamlets in Aku to mobilise their residents for mass enrolment, emphasising that broad participation would guarantee the scheme’s success and sustainability.

Chief Ocho also highlighted some achievements of his administration, including the provision of a borehole for the Ugwuegede community, the successful hosting of the December 2025 Aku Cultural Festival, which attracted illustrious sons and daughters of the community, and the introduction of the health insurance scheme. He further used the occasion to formally draw attention to AWAF’s 40th anniversary celebration scheduled for December 2026.

In his remarks, the Chairman, AWAF National Health Insurance Committee, Dr. Chijioke Oke, commended the national leadership of the association for its commitment to the healthcare welfare of the Aku people. He gave a detailed account of the committee’s journey, from the needs assessment conducted in early 2026 to consultations with the National Health Insurance Authority (NHIA), the Enugu State Health Insurance Agency, and private health maintenance organisations.

Dr. Oke explained the scheme’s benefit package, enrolment model, and transparent fund management structure, noting that the committee had worked diligently to ensure that the deadline set by the AWAF national leadership for the programme’s seamless processing and commencement was met.

He expressed appreciation to the HMO and healthcare service provider for their commitment and partnership in establishing a well-structured healthcare programme that would adequately serve the needs of the people.

Also speaking, the Chairman, Aku General Assembly (AGA), Mathew Enyi, commended AWAF for the laudable initiative, describing healthcare as a fundamental pillar of community development. He pledged the AGA’s full support in sensitising residents across all the villages in Aku’s three major quarters to ensure widespread participation.

Enyi urged political leaders and other stakeholders in Aku to regard the initiative as entirely apolitical and support its objectives, particularly by encouraging more residents to enroll in the second phase of the programme.

He further called on all stakeholders to work collectively towards ensuring the sustainability of the scheme and supporting other initiatives capable of liberating the people from the burden of high healthcare costs and addressing other community development challenges.

In her presentation, the representative of NEM Health Maintenance Organisation, Mrs. Susan Okeke, outlined the operational procedures for accessing the scheme. She explained that the process would involve the following:

Registration: Biometric data capture, with the immediate issuance of a temporary hospital card, followed by a permanent card.

Access to Healthcare: Beneficiaries will present their cards at the accredited healthcare facility to access covered medical services.

Coverage: The package includes medical consultations, laboratory investigations, essential drugs, antenatal care, childbirth, childcare and minor surgical procedures.

Complaints and Enquiries: A toll-free telephone number will be printed on the permanent cards to enable beneficiaries to make enquiries and report complaints.

The representative of the lead healthcare provider, Attah Memorial Hospital, Aku, Mr. Amuche Charles Attah Jr., assured beneficiaries of quality healthcare delivery, non-discriminatory treatment and round-the-clock medical services.

He further assured enrollees that the hospital would work towards addressing concerns over the high cost of medical services, emphasising that beneficiaries under the AWAF scheme would receive healthcare services in accordance with the agreed benefit package.

Speaking on behalf of the beneficiaries, Hon. Dominic Didigwu of Amaogbo Amabokwu, Mrs. Augustina Agu of Awkuzu Orda, and Mrs. Nwani Angela Ngozi of Umuneri Ugwunani expressed profound appreciation to AWAF for introducing the initiative.

They described the scheme as a timely intervention that would significantly address the healthcare challenges confronting ordinary residents of Aku, particularly vulnerable families and individuals who struggle to meet rising medical expenses.

The post AWAF launches national health insurance scheme for Aku indigenes appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: NDIC warns Anambra corps members against Ponzi schemes, uninsured banks
description:
By Zika Bobby
The Nigeria Deposit Insurance Corporation (NDIC) has warned National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) members in Anambra State to steer clear of Ponzi schemes and uninsured financial institutions to avoid losing their hard-earned money.
The Zonal Comptroller of the corporation in Enugu, Chid
content:
By Zika Bobby

The Nigeria Deposit Insurance Corporation (NDIC) has warned National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) members in Anambra State to steer clear of Ponzi schemes and uninsured financial institutions to avoid losing their hard-earned money.

The Zonal Comptroller of the corporation in Enugu, Chidi Nwankwo, gave the warning, yesterday, during a sensitisation campaign at the Anambra State NYSC Orientation Camp in Umuawulu/Mbaukwu, Awka South Local Government Area.

Nwankwo, a lawyer, explained that the outreach was aimed at educating the public—and corps members in particular—on the corporation’s mandate and how to safeguard their finances from fraudsters.

“We are here to educate you on how to protect your deposits and what deposit insurance is all about,” he said.

Delivering a lecture titled: ‘Know Your Deposit Protection: A Practical Guide for NYSC Corps Members,’ the Zonal Comptroller walked the corps members through banking operations and the claims process in the event of a bank failure. “When a bank closes, what do you do? Can a bank fail? Yes. Those are some of the pertinent questions people ask. The essence of our coming here today is to create public awareness on how to protect bank deposits and understand the maximum insured limits.

“For instance, with Deposit Money Banks, the maximum insured limit is N5 million. If a bank fails and you have ₦6 million in your account, you will first be paid the insured sum of N5 million. The remaining N1 million—the uninsured portion—is paid later as a liquidation dividend after we realise and sell the assets of the failed bank,” he explained.

Also speaking at the event, a Senior Manager in the NDIC Communications Department, Chinenye Chimezie Amadi, lectured the corps members on personal financial management. She advised them to always conduct thorough background checks on any investment opportunity before committing their funds.
