title: Otti, Osinbajo urge lawyers to embrace technology
description:
Abia State Governor, Alex Otti, has urged legal practitioners in the country to embrace modern technology and continuously update their knowledge to remain relevant in the discharge of their professional responsibilities, stressing that technological advancement is changing the world.
Otti gave the
content:
Abia State Governor, Alex Otti, has urged legal practitioners in the country to embrace modern technology and continuously update their knowledge to remain relevant in the discharge of their professional responsibilities, stressing that technological advancement is changing the world.

Otti gave the charge at the International Conference Centre, Umuahia, while speaking at the Annual Conference of the Nigerian Bar Association Section on Public Interest and Development Law (NBA-SPIDEL).

The governor, who described technology as an emerging reality that legal practitioners must prepare for, said the state government was already investing in modern judicial infrastructure to support efficient justice delivery.

“Technology is real. Sometimes we pretend, but the point you (Prof. Yemi Osinbajo) raised is very, very critical. It does not call for us to be afraid but for us to start thinking ahead of time,” Gov. Otti stated.

Otti disclosed that his administration would, in a few days, commission 10 newly constructed courts across the state, explaining that the facilities were designed to meet the demands of modern-day judicial administration.

According to the governor, the court facilities have been equipped with renewable energy systems, digital infrastructure, broadband connectivity and other technological facilities to improve the efficiency of judicial operations.

“Renewable energy, digitalised systems and all the things that you require will be available in the court. We have also been able to digitalise court records. So, there will be no need to carry files.

“All the court halls have Wi-Fi. So, the challenge is for us to now catch up with the technology that we are installing. And they all have multiple broadband technologies, not one, just in case it fails. So, we are thinking of the future,”  Otti added.

The governor further announced plans to flag off the construction of new Courts with 1,000-capacity auditoriums in Aba and Umuahia, assuring that the facilities would have independent renewable energy sources.

Otti also urged lawyers to look beyond financial gains and embrace their responsibility to provide legal assistance to indigent citizens, vulnerable persons and members of society who cannot afford professional legal fees.

He said the impact of the NBA-SPIDEL conference should ultimately be measured by how its deliberations translate into improved access to justice and protection of the rights of ordinary citizens.

“Due to the fact that you are lawyers, we need to go the extra mile of asking ourselves, beyond all the things that have been said, how can we be of service to people who cannot pay? How can we be of service to the vulnerable? How can we help people who, on their own, cannot afford to help themselves?” he added.

The governor noted that while infrastructure such as roads, schools, hospitals, electric buses and environmental sanitation represented the visible aspects of his governance, the rule of law, justice and protection of citizens’ rights are equally important though less visible components.

Otti illustrated the importance of public-interest legal practice with instances of alleged unlawful and prolonged detention, revealing that shortly after assuming office, his administration discovered that some people were being held in correctional facilities despite having no sufficient reason to remain there, noting that he directed the state Attorney-General to work with the Chief Judge to ensure that nobody was kept in a correctional facility without lawful justification.

The governor emphasised that the NBA-SPIDEL conference should not merely be an avenue for professional discussions but should inspire lawyers to make meaningful contributions to society.

He commended the organisers of the NBA-SPIDEL Annual Conference for choosing Abia State as the host, expressing appreciation for the opportunity to welcome legal practitioners and other stakeholders to Umuahia.

Earlier, the keynote speaker and former Vice President of Nigeria, Prof. Yemi Osinbajo (SAN) called on legal practitioners to move beyond the traditional interpretation and application of the law to embrace their responsibility as social engineers and agents of positive change, committed to advancing justice, strengthening democracy and promoting national development.

Prof. Osinbajo emphasised the importance of people-centred public interest advocacy that prioritises citizens’ welfare, access to justice, job creation, healthcare, education and the protection of vulnerable groups.

He noted that the true measure of democracy lies not merely in the conduct of elections or formulation of government policies, but in its capacity to improve the living conditions of ordinary citizens, warning that poverty, corruption, unemployment and declining public confidence in democratic institutions remain significant threats to democratic growth.

He further noted that democracy must be judged on how people feel and access justice, insisting that “a just society protects everyone.”

Prof. Osinbajo challenged lawyers to embrace continuous learning and develop competencies in technology, negotiation, conflict resolution, institutional management and critical judgment, while ensuring the proper verification of AI-generated information.

In her opening address, the President of the Nigerian Bar Association (NBA), Oyinkansola Badejo-Okusanya, SAN, called on legal practitioners to uphold the principles of justice, accountability and public interest by ensuring that their professional responsibilities translate into meaningful improvements in the lives of citizens.

She identified persons held in detention without legal representation, traders unable to afford litigation and children treated as adults in detention facilities as examples of people whose circumstances should inform discussions on justice and development.

She explained that justice should guarantee effective remedies for those who suffer wrongs, pointing out that democracy should provide citizens with meaningful voices in decisions affecting their lives, while development should improve their opportunities and living conditions.

She condemned political violence across the country, calling for credible investigations and prosecution of those responsible for attacks on citizens participating in lawful political activities. The NBA President thanked  Otti for sponsoring the 2026 NBA-SPIDEL Conference.

The event featured a panel of discussants led by Justice Obisike Orji, with dignitaries like Prof. Pat Utomi, Dr. Sam Amadi, among others participating, while the Chair of the NBA-SPIDEL Conference, Prof. Uju Agomuo, Chief Okey Amaechi, among others, participated in the presentation of plaques to appreciate the contributions of some individuals to the success of the event.

The post Otti, Osinbajo urge lawyers to embrace technology appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: S’African court rejects Nigerian’s N430m claim over 117-day detention
description:
A South African court has rejected Nigerian Sunday Okoro’s bid to revive his R5.4m damages claim against the Minister of Police over his arrest and detention for 117 days following the discovery of a man’s body hanging in a room he had rented in Durban.
A South African news outlet, IOL, reported on
content:
A South African court has rejected Nigerian Sunday Okoro’s bid to revive his R5.4m damages claim against the Minister of Police over his arrest and detention for 117 days following the discovery of a man’s body hanging in a room he had rented in Durban.

A South African news outlet, IOL, reported on Tuesday that the Supreme Court of Appeal dismissed Okoro’s application for reconsideration after his attempts to secure leave to appeal against an earlier ruling failed.

Okoro was arrested without a warrant on July 3, 2002, after police discovered the body of a man hanging by a bedsheet in the shower of room 7 at Evaleigh Court, an apartment he was said to have rented days before the discovery.

The report said Okoro remained in custody until November 29, 2002, when the murder charges against him were withdrawn.

Following his release, Okoro sued the Minister of Police, seeking R5.41m in damages over what he described as unlawful arrest and detention, as well as the resulting loss and suffering.

According to Forbes Advisor, as of the time this report was filed, R5.41m was approximately N430m, at an exchange rate of R1 to N79.48.

However, the KwaZulu-Natal High Court in Durban dismissed his claim with costs, ruling that the police had reasonable grounds to suspect him of murder and that his arrest and detention were lawful.

After failing to obtain leave to appeal from both the High Court and the Supreme Court of Appeal, Okoro approached the president of the appeal court for reconsideration.

The matter was heard by a three-judge panel comprising Acting Judge of Appeal Mjali, Acting Judge of Appeal Molitsoane and Judge of Appeal Nicholls.

In its judgment, the majority, comprising Molitsoane and Nicholls, dismissed his application for reconsideration with costs.

According to IOL, the court heard that Warrant Officer Allen Mark Naidu and Warrant Officer Sunil Seosunker were conducting crime-prevention duties in Durban’s Point area when they encountered Okoro outside Evaleigh Court.

“Naidu testified that Okoro entered the building after seeing their police vehicle, prompting the officers to follow him.

“Naidu later saw Okoro emerging from room 7 in a distressed state, repeatedly shouting the name Francine.

“Okoro asked the officers to follow him into the room, where they discovered a man of Indian descent hanging by a bedsheet in the shower.

“The deceased’s body was cold and stiff, with no pulse. Naidu became suspicious that the hanging had been staged to conceal a murder.

“He testified that the deceased’s feet were not positioned close enough to the shower ledge to suggest that he had used it to hang himself.”

According to the report, the court found no evidence that the police had misled the prosecution or deliberately withheld or misrepresented information to ensure that Okoro remained behind bars.

It therefore concluded that there was no basis to hold the Minister of Police liable for his detention after his first court appearance.

The post S’African court rejects Nigerian’s N430m claim over 117-day detention appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Enugu Assembly caps rent hike at 2 per cent, landlords kick
description:
The Enugu State House of Assembly on Tuesday passed the Landlord and Tenant Amendment Bill, introducing strict statutory limits on rent increments and overhauling tenancy regulations across the state.
The legislation, formally titled “A Bill for a Law to Amend the Landlord and Tenant Second Amendmen
content:
The Enugu State House of Assembly on Tuesday passed the Landlord and Tenant Amendment Bill, introducing strict statutory limits on rent increments and overhauling tenancy regulations across the state.

The legislation, formally titled “A Bill for a Law to Amend the Landlord and Tenant Second Amendment Bill, Cap. 101, Revised Laws of Enugu State 2024 (House Bill No. 3, 2025),” scaled third reading following the adoption of a joint review report presented during plenary.

Under the newly passed provisions, landlords are barred from increasing rent until after a minimum period of four years, with any subsequent upward review strictly capped at two per cent of the prevailing rent.

However, where a property owner executes verifiable, substantial renovations, the bill permits an upward review of not more than 10 per cent.

The bill’s passage followed a motion moved by the member representing Nkanu West Constituency, Hon. Iloabuchi Abugu, and seconded by the Deputy Speaker and member representing Awgu North Constituency, Rt. Hon. Jane Eneh, after which the House dissolved into the Committee of the Whole for clause-by-clause consideration.

Presenting the joint report compiled by the House Committees on Housing and Investment, Public Petitions, Ethics and Privileges, and Judiciary, the Chairman of the review committee, Hon. Okey Mbah (Nkanu East), stated that the legislation was the product of extensive stakeholder consultations.

Mbah described the bill as a game-changer designed to curb arbitrary charges and protect residents from exploitation by property owners and middlemen.

“This bill will subsidise over 60 per cent of what residents used to pay while trying to secure accommodation,” the lawmaker stated.

In his remarks after the passage, the Speaker of the Assembly, Rt. Hon. Uche Ugwu, hailed the legislation as a milestone in the state’s good governance agenda, noting that it would grant tenants across Enugu State a new lease of life.

“This law is going to address all the cries of residents about the escalating rent in the state,” he said.

The bill, which passed its second reading on March 11, 2026, and underwent a public hearing on March 26, 2026, now awaits the assent of Governor Peter Mbah to become law.

The legislative intervention comes amid widespread public outcry across Enugu metropolis and surrounding urban centres over soaring house rents, arbitrary agent commissions, and exorbitant legal fees that have priced low- and middle-income earners out of decent housing.

While tenant groups have welcomed the move, the legislation has already triggered pushback from property owners, who argue that fixed rent caps ignore prevailing macroeconomic realities, high building material costs, and inflationary pressures.

Reacting to the development, a landlord in the state capital,  Johnson Onyekwere, dismissed the two per cent cap as unrealistic and unenforceable given the current economic climate.

Onyekwere said, “That would have been a natural law if the prices of petroleum products and electricity tariffs increased by two per cent. Otherwise, it is an unnatural law. It is neither sustainable nor can it be obeyed.

“You cannot single out landlords and regulate their business while other sectors are struggling to meet the benchmark of inflation set by the managers of the Nigerian economy. It violates landlords’ rights against discrimination,” he stated.

The post Enugu Assembly caps rent hike at 2 per cent, landlords kick appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Enugu solar greenhouses turn harvest into ownership for 225 farmers
description:
Fifteen solar-powered greenhouses in Ugwuomu-Nike, Enugu East Local Government Area, are turning harvest income into ownership for 225 smallholder farmers under a lease-to-own model that the Enugu State Government plans to extend to its 260 farm estates.

content:
Fifteen solar-powered greenhouses in Ugwuomu-Nike, Enugu East Local Government Area, are turning harvest income into ownership for 225 smallholder farmers under a lease-to-own model that the Enugu State Government plans to extend to its 260 farm estates.

Each greenhouse costs N10.5m, but farmers paid nothing upfront. The 225 members of the 15 cooperatives—including women, young people and persons with disabilities—will own their greenhouse once harvest income covers the cost.

The cluster was built and is run by Manamuz Electric, led by Chief Executive and Co-founder Uzochukwu Mbamalu, with partner firms.

It is backed by the Energising Women and Youth in Agri-Food Systems programme, a three-year partnership between the Global Energy Alliance for People and Planet and the Mastercard Foundation running in Nigeria and Ethiopia from 2024 to 2027, with RMI and All On as technical partners in Nigeria.

EWAS aims to create 17,000 jobs and support 136,000 livelihoods by 2027, with seven in 10 job openings intended for women. Manamuz has created more than 570 jobs so far.

Under the model, the state provides land, development partners fund construction, and Manamuz supplies technology and buyer links.

Each cooperative’s 15 members farm sell as a group, keep most of the income and use a smaller share to repay the greenhouse cost. Once paid off, the greenhouse belongs to the cooperative, and repayments fund the next group.

Mbamalu said, “Our agreement with the government is a state pilot of 150 greenhouses with two cold box stores. The government has already passed a policy to take this project to its 260 farm estates. Each estate covers 200 hectares, and 1 per cent of every estate will go to clean energy in agriculture. That means cold rooms linked to solar mini-grids and greenhouses. It will be youth-focused.”

The initiative comes as the Federal Government declared a state of emergency on food security and recapitalised the Bank of Agriculture with N1.5tn, with loans of up to N1m for young farmers.

The World Bank says Mission 300, a 2024 World Bank-African Development Bank initiative supported by the Rockefeller Foundation and Global Energy Alliance, will bring electricity to 17.5 million Nigerians by 2030.

On Monday, Chianda Njogu, who is Director for Powering Opportunity in Africa at the Global Energy Alliance, visited the site. He said, “The community is off-grid, but nothing is lacking here. There is power, there are sustainably run greenhouses, and there is water.

“The most important element is the people. You see it in how the greenhouses have been set up and in the participants’ attention to detail.”

Njogu said ending energy poverty means reaching unelectrified communities with new, better and affordable renewable energy. “The outcome that matters most to us is jobs and livelihoods, and the economic prosperity that follows for countries and communities,” he said, adding that scaling up will need private sector funding and investment, along with government funding.

Mrs Nkolika Ugokwe, President of the Donum De Caelo Cooperative, said the programme had made a difference to her group, whose first bell peppers should be ready by the end of November. Beekeeper Mrs Onyia Salome said, “As a beekeeper, I need a greenhouse where my bees can find nectar and give us honey. This is a big opportunity for me.”

The post Enugu solar greenhouses turn harvest into ownership for 225 farmers appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Labour needs unity, not needless bickering
description: IN an era when Nigeria’s economic crisis is squeezing workers to the bone, the last thing Organised Labour needs is a needless turf war. Consequently, negotiations for a new minimum wage appear to have hit a bad patch because of divisions between the Trade Union Congress and the Nigeria Labour Congr
content:
IN an era when Nigeria’s economic crisis is squeezing workers to the bone, the last thing Organised Labour needs is a needless turf war. Consequently, negotiations for a new minimum wage appear to have hit a bad patch because of divisions between the Trade Union Congress and the Nigeria Labour Congress, as reported by Daily Trust. This is both unfortunate and demoralising for workers whose welfare the two labour centres exist to protect.

The well-advertised feuding has raised concerns, particularly among civil servants, that the disunity could weaken labour’s bargaining power in negotiations with the Federal Government and the Organised Private Sector for an upward review of the current N70,000 monthly National Minimum Wage.

The immediate trigger was the TUC’s rejection of the Federal Government’s proposed N70,000 monthly transportation allowance for public servants for six months, beginning in November. The NLC promptly pushed back, insisting that the TUC had no authority to speak for the entire labour movement on an issue it was not party to negotiating.

On October 18, the Joint National Public Service Negotiating Council sided with the NLC, declaring that accepting the allowance was appropriate. Hours later, however, three unions – the Senior Staff Association of Statutory Corporations and Government-Owned Companies, the Senior Staff Association of Universities, Teaching Hospitals, Research Institutes and Associated Institutions, and the Nigerian Union of Allied Health Professionals – threw their weight behind the TUC.

This is a needless spectacle. What should be a coordinated campaign for better wages has degenerated into a contest over who controls the labour movement. Whatever the underlying institutional rivalries, workers should not be made to pay for the egos or ambitions of union leaders.

The Federal Government has maintained that the current minimum wage will be due for review in June 2027, relying on the amended National Minimum Wage Act, 2019, which provides for a three-year review cycle.

On October 12, the Minister of Labour and Employment, Muhammad Dingyadi, described calls for another review barely two years after the current wage took effect as “premature and potentially disruptive” to industrial relations.

The NLC strongly disagreed. It had earlier issued a two-week ultimatum demanding that the government reduce petrol prices to the levels prevailing when the current minimum wage was signed into law in 2024, commence negotiations for a new wage before the end of October and honour outstanding labour agreements. The ultimatum was subsequently extended to October 27.

The NLC argued that preparations for a new wage review should begin immediately and that the timetable in the original 2019 legislation remained relevant despite the 2024 amendment.

Following a conciliation meeting with the NLC on October 27, the Federal Government approved a N70,000 monthly transport allowance for public servants for six months, beginning in November. The concession was intended to cushion workers against soaring living costs and formed part of efforts to resolve renewed labour agitation over welfare and outstanding agreements.

The TUC rejected the arrangement, dismissing it as another set of “haphazard measures” to soften the impact of petrol subsidy removal. It instead demanded immediate salary increases, arguing that temporary allowances cannot substitute for a meaningful improvement in workers’ basic pay.

There is merit in the argument that a transport allowance, however welcome, is no substitute for a living wage. But rejecting an immediate concession without presenting a coordinated alternative risks leaving workers worse off. Labour must be pragmatic without surrendering its greater demands.

The disagreement has descended into personal exchanges. TUC President Festus Osifo accused his NLC counterpart, Joe Ajaero, of short-changing workers during negotiations with the Federal Government following the removal of the fuel subsidy.

He alleged that Ajaero rushed into negotiations and was prepared to accept a watered-down two-point proposal despite the TUC having submitted a 10-point demand to the government.

Osifo maintained that the TUC had explained the rationale behind its demands, only for the NLC to proceed without consulting it. Ajaero, in response, insisted that the NLC was negotiating independently, making the TUC’s opposition to the outcome unwarranted.

Both positions raise legitimate questions about consultation, representation and the respective mandates of the two labour centres. But none justifies the public acrimony.

If the NLC has a mandate to negotiate for its affiliates, it should exercise that mandate transparently. Equally, the TUC should be free to articulate its members’ grievances without turning every disagreement into a confrontation over legitimacy.

The TUC’s claim that it has more civil service workers than the NLC, and the NLC’s insistence that it can negotiate independently, are distractions from the real issue.

Nigerian workers are not interested in a statistical contest over union membership or a battle for institutional supremacy. They want wages that can sustain them in an economy where the cost of food, transport, housing and healthcare has become increasingly unbearable.

The rivalry between the two labour centres is not new. The TUC emerged in 2005 as a separate centre representing senior workers, and the institutional competition has persisted. But history is no excuse for allowing old animosities to undermine present-day negotiations.

The NLC secured the six-month transport allowance through its engagement with the government, while the TUC has pushed for a new minimum wage of N300,000.

Yet the TUC’s argument that the NLC cannot negotiate for its members does not resolve the wider question of how organised labour can present a united front on national wage policy. Nor does the NLC’s right to negotiate independently absolve it of the responsibility to build consensus where the interests of workers overlap.

The consequences of labour disunity are not theoretical. Previous disagreements have weakened industrial action and bargaining efforts, including the failed or fractured strikes of 2015, 2016 and 2023. The 2023 N35,000 wage award proved difficult to enforce in several states, exposing the limits of agreements that lack effective coordination and sustained pressure.

At a time when workers’ purchasing power has been devastated by inflation and the removal of fuel subsidy, labour cannot afford to negotiate with government from a position of division. A fragmented labour movement is an easy opponent for a government skilled at exploiting differences and delaying difficult concessions.

The OPS, too, will have little incentive to make meaningful compromises when workers cannot speak with a coherent voice.

The Petroleum and Natural Gas Senior Staff Association has rightly urged both labour centres to adopt a memorandum of understanding to regulate joint negotiations and prevent recurring disputes.

This proposal deserves serious consideration. Such an agreement should clearly define representation, consultation procedures, negotiation mandates and mechanisms for resolving disagreements before they spill into public confrontation.

Meanwhile, labour should accept the six-month transport allowance as an interim relief, without mistaking it for a victory or allowing it to derail the campaign for a substantially improved minimum wage.

The government should understand that a temporary allowance cannot compensate indefinitely for the erosion of workers’ real incomes. Preparations for a credible wage review should begin with transparent consultations and a realistic assessment of the cost of living.

Osifo and Ajaero should rise above personal rivalries and remember that their positions are positions of public trust. They are not competing for political office or fighting for personal prestige. Their responsibility is to defend workers whose salaries are being swallowed by the relentless rise in living costs.

Organised Labour was built on solidarity, collective action and the strength of numbers. Without these, its threats become hollow, its negotiations weak and its victories short-lived. Workers need better wages, not bigger egos. The NLC and TUC must stop fighting each other and start fighting for the people they claim to represent.

The post Labour needs unity, not needless bickering appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Reactions trail ‘No NIN, no flight’ policy
description:
Passengers have criticised the Federal Government’s plan to make the National Identification Number compulsory for domestic air travel from 1 January, 2027, questioning the rationale behind the policy and its implications for foreigners and Nigerians without NIN.
On Monday, while announcing the intr
content:
Passengers have criticised the Federal Government’s plan to make the National Identification Number compulsory for domestic air travel from 1 January, 2027, questioning the rationale behind the policy and its implications for foreigners and Nigerians without NIN.

On Monday, while announcing the introduction of the Verified Passenger Access System, a biometric facial recognition system designed for domestic air travel across Nigeria and which mandatorily requires a National Identification Numbers, the Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, insisted that all airlines must comply with the directive.

The proposed policy, Keyamo said, was part of plans to strengthen airport security and improve passenger identification, but the development has been met with concerns over data protection, freedom of movement and the possible exclusion of travellers who rely on other valid means of identification.

On Monday, many passengers at Lagos airport condemned the planned introduction of the requirement for local flights, describing it as unnecessary and questioning how it would address the country’s security challenges.

A mother of three, Mrs Juliet Adeoye, questioned how the policy would affect foreigners and Nigerians whose children hold citizenship of other countries.

She questioned the policy, saying two of her children held foreign citizenship and asking whether they would be barred from domestic flights from January for not having NIN, likening the requirement to demanding a UK National Insurance number to book a domestic flight.

“I have been wondering where this is coming from since I read the news yesterday, but I strongly hope they will have a rethink before the set date.”

Another passenger, Mr Kelvin Jones, commended the government’s intention to improve security but questioned the decision to make NIN a requirement for domestic flight bookings.

The concerns have also spilled onto social media, where Nigerians have questioned how the proposed verification system would accommodate foreign passengers and protect travellers’ personal information.

Speaking through their X handles, Adesina Adegbite, with the handle @fatiscoproduct, asked how foreign travellers using domestic airports would be verified under the proposed arrangement.

He said, “How will the foreigners travelling through the domestic airports passes through the NIN verification system ? What means of identification would be used to verify them?”

Similarly, another X user, Ademax, with the handle @Ademaxworld, described the NIN requirement as unnecessary, arguing that other measures could be adopted to address identity fraud and ticketing irregularities.

He said, “You don’t need our equivalent of social security numbers to fly domestically in Nigeria. Saying it’s to tackle fake identities and ticketing racketeering is ridiculous as ther should be other ways of doing that without further exposing passengers NIN to hackers!.”

Another user, Hon Jay, with the handle @Zellencekelly, acknowledged the importance of airport security but warned against making NIN the only acceptable means of identification for domestic air travellers.

He said, “Improving airport security is commendable, but making NIN the sole requirement for domestic flights unfairly excludes Nigerians with other valid means of identification. Security should not become a barrier to citizens’ freedom of movement.”

The controversy followed the Federal Government’s announcement of a new passenger verification system, known as VPASS, which will link travellers’ identities to their National Identification Numbers.

When contacted, spokesperson of the Airlines Association of Nigeria, Prof. Obiora Okonkwo, said the association has no reaction to the develolopment.

He said “We have no reaction.”

The post Reactions trail ‘No NIN, no flight’ policy appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: WAEC opens registration for 2027 WASSCE
description:
The West African Examinations Council has opened registration for the 2027 West African Senior School Certificate Examination for School Candidates.
The examination body announced the commencement of registration in a statement shared on its official account on Tuesday.
“WASSCE for School Candidates
content:
The West African Examinations Council has opened registration for the 2027 West African Senior School Certificate Examination for School Candidates.

The examination body announced the commencement of registration in a statement shared on its official account on Tuesday.

“WASSCE for School Candidates, 2027: Registration is now open! WAEC is making examination preparation smarter and more accessible,” the council said.

It urged schools to “complete their CASS uploads promptly and adhere strictly to all stipulated registration timelines.”

The examination body also announced that the 2027 examination would be conducted in a hybrid mode.

“Important: The 2027 examination will be conducted in hybrid mode,” it stated.

WAEC began transitioning to computer-based examinations in 2024 with private candidates through a hybrid model in which multiple-choice questions were answered on-screen, while essay and practical papers remained manual.

The examination body had earlier announced plans to fully implement computer-based examinations for school candidates in the May/June 2026 WASSCE, as part of efforts to modernise its assessment system, improve examination credibility and reduce malpractice.

In October 2025, WAEC’s Head of National Office, Dr Amos Dangut, said the transition would help eliminate logistical challenges and improve the timeliness and credibility of examinations.

He said, “Computer-based examinations will reduce fraud, examination malpractice. The records are there. For all five examinations we have conducted using CBT, there was a low rate of examination malpractice and higher performance of candidates. So, there is nothing to be afraid of.”

The PUNCH had reported that the council also planned to provide schools with access to a testing portal to familiarise candidates with the system ahead of the examinations. 

The post WAEC opens registration for 2027 WASSCE appeared first on Punch Newspapers.
author: Christabel Ndoeche

title: Police detain driver over Ogun VIO official’s death
description:
The Ogun State Police Command says it has detained the driver of an Iveco truck after it allegedly knocked down and killed a Vehicle Inspection Officer, Oluwaseun Adeshina, along the Agbara–Unilever Expressway.
The fatal incident occurred at about 11.10 am on Monday, November 16, opposite Tipper Gar
content:
The Ogun State Police Command says it has detained the driver of an Iveco truck after it allegedly knocked down and killed a Vehicle Inspection Officer, Oluwaseun Adeshina, along the Agbara–Unilever Expressway.

The fatal incident occurred at about 11.10 am on Monday, November 16, opposite Tipper Garage, Korogboji, in Ogun State.

The Police Public Relations Officer, Babaseyi Oluseyi, confirmed the incident in a statement on Tuesday, saying the truck and its driver had been taken to the station for investigation.

He noted that the truck reportedly knocked down Adeshina while he was performing his official duties, resulting in fatal injuries.

Oluseyi stated, “The Ogun State Police Command confirms a fatal road accident involving an Iveco truck and a VIO official, Oluwaseun Adeshina, at about 11:10 a.m. on Monday, 16 November 2026, opposite Tipper Garage, Korogboji, along the Agbara–Unilever Expressway.

“The truck reportedly knocked down the official while he was performing his lawful duty, resulting in fatal injuries. Police operatives promptly visited the scene, documented the incident and conveyed the remains to the hospital for necessary procedures.

“The truck and its driver have been taken to the station for further investigation and vehicle inspection.”

Babaseyi noted that the command commiserated with the deceased’s family and colleagues and urged motorists to exercise caution.

“The command commiserates with the family and colleagues of the deceased and urges motorists to exercise caution. The area remains calm,” he concluded.

This is not the first time a traffic official has been knocked down dead in the line of duty.

PUNCH Metro reported in December 2012 that a mob nabbed a truck driver and handed him over to the police after he reportedly crushed an official of the Federal Road Safety Corps to death and injured another on the Sagamu-Ijebu Ode Road, Ogun State.

The mob consisted of motorists and motorcycle riders who witnessed the accident.

The post Police detain driver over Ogun VIO official’s death appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Customs seized 844 rifles, withheld details to protect investigations – CG
description: The Comptroller-General of the Nigeria Customs Service, Bashir Adeniyi, on Tuesday said the NCS deliberately withheld immediate public disclosure of major arms seizures, including the interception of 844 rifles at Onne Port in June 2024, to avoid jeopardising investigations, releasing inaccurate inf
content:
The Comptroller-General of the Nigeria Customs Service, Bashir Adeniyi, on Tuesday said the NCS deliberately withheld immediate public disclosure of major arms seizures, including the interception of 844 rifles at Onne Port in June 2024, to avoid jeopardising investigations, releasing inaccurate information and exposing innocent persons to wrongful accusations.

He disclosed this at the Global Alliance World Public Relations Forum in Abuja.

Adeniyi explained that the pressure to speak immediately after security operations could undermine investigations if officials announced unverified figures, made premature accusations or disclosed the identities of persons who had not been properly investigated.

He cited the interception of 844 rifles concealed in a consignment at Onne Port in June 2024 and the subsequent discovery of another 399 rifles in a separate operation as examples of incidents that required careful handling of information.

According to him, the Service adopted a procedure of confirming facts, coordinating with relevant security agencies and ensuring that public statements were consistent before addressing the media.

He said, “In moments like this, the pressure to speak immediately is enormous, and social media will not wait for you. But a wrong figure, a careless accusation or a premature name can damage an investigation and hurt innocent people.

“So our rule is clear. We confirm the facts, we coordinate with security agencies, and then we speak with one voice.”

The Customs chief said the Service also ensured that its public briefing went beyond displaying the recovered weapons to explaining the potential national security implications of allowing them to fall into the wrong hands.

He said the approach was intended to turn enforcement successes into public reassurance while protecting the credibility of the Service.

“When we did the public briefing, we did not only display the weapons. We explained what could have gone wrong if they had fallen into the wrong hands. This is how an enforcement success becomes public reassurance.

“Speed matters, but accuracy is what keeps your credibility for the next crisis,” Adeniyi said.

The Customs boss made the remarks while sharing communication lessons from the Service’s operations and reform initiatives, stressing that effective communication should be treated as a deliberate strategy rather than an afterthought.

He identified the need to verify information before speaking as one of the major lessons the Service learnt from its anti-smuggling operations, particularly those involving sensitive security matters.

Adeniyi also cited the introduction of the B’Odogwu Unified Management System as an example of the importance of preparing stakeholders before implementing major reforms.

He said the Service learnt that the technological aspect of replacing its old cargo clearance platform was easier than managing the transition for importers, licensed agents, terminal operators, government agencies and Customs officers accustomed to the previous system.

He explained that the NCS organised training sessions for agents, established help desks and introduced the platform in phases to minimise disruptions.

“We knew that if we simply switched it on one Monday morning, we would have queues, complaints and headlines by Wednesday. So we went for training before the switch. We held sessions with agents. We opened up the help desk and rolled out in phases, one command at a time.

“We also spoke to our officers first. This is often forgotten. If the officer at the terminal cannot explain a new process with confidence, no press release will save you,” he said.

Adeniyi disclosed that the African Continental Free Trade Area Secretariat prescribed B’Odogwu as a model for other African countries in August.

He said the experience reinforced the need to ensure that reforms were understood and trusted by the people expected to use them.

The Customs chief also recalled the Service’s decision to publish findings from its Time Release Study, which showed that clearing goods at Nigerian ports took about five days, with more than 90 per cent of the period spent on idle time.

He said the Service could have kept the findings confidential to avoid criticism but chose transparency because identifying the problem was necessary to address it.

“Some would have advised us to keep the report in the drawer. We chose to publish it because you cannot fix a problem you are afraid to name,” he said.

Adeniyi explained that Customs was not solely responsible for delays and costs at the ports, noting that terminal operators, shipping lines and other regulatory agencies also contributed to the clearance process.

He said evidence-based communication allowed the Service to acknowledge its shortcomings while holding other stakeholders accountable for their respective responsibilities.

The Customs boss identified the introduction of the Authorised Economic Operator programme as another lesson in using communication to encourage compliance.

The post Customs seized 844 rifles, withheld details to protect investigations – CG appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Hamzat pushes stronger research commercialisation in universities
description:
The Lagos State Deputy Governor, Obafemi Hamzat, has called for stronger research commercialisation and university-industry partnerships to translate academic discoveries into practical solutions and economic opportunities.
Hamzat said Nigerian universities and research institutions needed to bridge
content:
The Lagos State Deputy Governor, Obafemi Hamzat, has called for stronger research commercialisation and university-industry partnerships to translate academic discoveries into practical solutions and economic opportunities.

Hamzat said Nigerian universities and research institutions needed to bridge the gap between research findings and commercially viable innovations to enable tertiary education to contribute more effectively to national development.

He spoke on Tuesday through the Commissioner for Tertiary Education, Tolani Sule, who represented him at the 38th convocation lecture of Yaba College of Technology, Lagos.

The lecture was titled, “From Silos to Synergy: Reimagining the Nigerian Tertiary Education System for National Transformation.”

Hamzat, who identified the disconnect between research and commercial application as one of the structural barriers limiting the potential of tertiary education, said research should not end with academic publications but should also produce solutions that improve lives.

He said, “A research paper that identifies a solution to an agricultural problem should have a pathway towards practical application.

“A laboratory discovery that can improve healthcare should have a route towards testing, development and deployment.

“An engineering innovation that can reduce production costs should have access to the partnerships and resources necessary to reach the market.”

The deputy governor said Nigeria had considerable intellectual talent in its universities and research institutions but needed to strengthen technology transfer, intellectual property management, research commercialisation and university-industry partnerships.

He urged tertiary institutions to establish stronger relationships with businesses and other stakeholders to facilitate the practical application of research findings.

Hamzat also called for increased research funding, more effective innovation hubs and university-based enterprises to support the development and commercialisation of locally generated knowledge.

He said the value of research should not be measured solely by the number of academic publications but also by the problems addressed, new knowledge contributed and practical solutions developed.

He, however, noted that fundamental research must be protected, stressing that not every worthwhile discovery would have immediate commercial value.

“A robust knowledge economy requires both curiosity-driven scholarship and targeted, problem-solving research. Our responsibility is to build a system that supports both,” he said.

The deputy governor also urged industries to see tertiary institutions as strategic partners in developing knowledge, technology and enterprise rather than merely suppliers of labour.

He asked private-sector organisations to invest in research, support innovation, offer internships, participate in curriculum reviews, provide mentorship and commission research addressing industry challenges.

Hamzat further advocated stronger collaboration among universities, polytechnics and colleges of education, saying their different mandates were complementary rather than competitive.

He said institutions should undertake joint research projects, share specialised facilities and develop multidisciplinary innovation centres to strengthen the country’s research and innovation ecosystem.

In his remarks, the Rector of YABATECH, Dr Ibraheem Abdul, said the institution was strengthening its research, innovation and industry partnerships to ensure its programmes addressed national development needs.

He said, “The future of tertiary education must be anchored on stronger connections between institutions and industries, between research and practical application, and between knowledge acquisition and economic opportunity.”

Abdul listed the National Skills Qualification Framework, proposed Solar-Powered Smart Campus Ecosystem, YABATECH Digital Technology Academy and YabaTech Skills Centre as initiatives designed to strengthen competency-based training, digital skills and graduate employability.

He added, “The measure of our success will not simply be the number of graduates we produce, but the difference they make in industry, enterprise, communities and the wider society.”

The rector also disclosed that the presidential approval for the conversion of YABATECH into the Federal University of Technology and Vocational Studies, Yaba, would provide an opportunity to strengthen applied research, technological innovation and industry partnerships.

The Chairman of the College’s Governing Council, Prof. Funso Afolabi, called for measurable outcomes in research, innovation and industry partnerships, saying institutional progress should be assessed through verifiable results rather than policy declarations.

He said, “We must establish measurable indicators for research output, graduate employment, staff development, industry partnerships, innovation and internally generated revenue. Institutional progress should be assessed against established baselines, annual targets and verifiable outcomes.”

Afolabi also said the institution’s conversion into a university should translate into improved research capacity, academic excellence, technological innovation and global competitiveness, stressing that “a change in nomenclature alone does not constitute transformation.”

The post Hamzat pushes stronger research commercialisation in universities appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Five-year-old Anambra boy abducted by father’s girlfriend rescued
description:
The Anambra State Police Command has rescued a five-year-old boy, Chiziterem Ifeadi, allegedly abducted by his father’s girlfriend, Precious Nnaji.
The 29-year-old suspect was also arrested at Nnodu, Okpuno, in the Awka South Local Government Area of the state, following a joint operation by the pol
content:
The Anambra State Police Command has rescued a five-year-old boy, Chiziterem Ifeadi, allegedly abducted by his father’s girlfriend, Precious Nnaji.

The 29-year-old suspect was also arrested at Nnodu, Okpuno, in the Awka South Local Government Area of the state, following a joint operation by the police and the Department of State Services.

The command’s spokesperson, SP Tochukwu Ikenga, disclosed this in a statement on Tuesday, saying operatives of the IGP’s Violent Crime Response Unit, in collaboration with DSS personnel, rescued the boy in the early hours of Monday.

Ikenga said the incident occurred on November 15, 2026, after the boy’s father left home for work, leaving his two sons in the care of their nanny.

According to him, the father returned to discover that his girlfriend had allegedly visited the residence without his consent and taken Chiziterem away to an unknown destination.

The police spokesperson said the father, after making several unsuccessful attempts to contact Nnaji, eventually reached her on the telephone.

He said the suspect allegedly demanded N2m, to be paid through a point-of-sale operator, as a condition for the release of the child.

Ikenga said the joint police-DSS operation subsequently led to the rescue of the boy and the arrest of the suspect at Nnodu, Okpuno.

He added that the suspect remained in police custody while investigations continued to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident and determine the appropriate legal action.

Meanwhile, the Commissioner of Police, Anambra State Command, CP Nnanna Ama, commended the operatives and their DSS counterparts for their swift response and effective collaboration.

Ama reassured residents of the state of the command’s commitment to intelligence-led policing, inter-agency cooperation and the protection of lives and property.

The post Five-year-old Anambra boy abducted by father’s girlfriend rescued appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Nvidia: ‘I’d Be Honoured To Return,’ Jensen Huang On Possible Reinstatement
description: Former Nvidia Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang has said he would be willing to return to the position if the company’s board of directors considers his reinstatement to be in its best interest.Huang made the announcement in a statement posted on his X account on Tuesday, his first public c
content:
Former Nvidia Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang has said he would be willing to return to the position if the company’s board of directors considers his reinstatement to be in its best interest.

Huang made the announcement in a statement posted on his X account on Tuesday, his first public comments since stepping down on November 12, following revelations about alleged extramarital affairs and concerns over his personal conduct.

The former chief executive said he had received an outpouring of support from Nvidia employees, investors, business partners and customers, with many urging him to return amid the company’s ongoing challenges.

“Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from NVIDIA’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO,” he wrote.

“If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honoured to answer these calls and return as CEO.”

Huang, however, acknowledged that his personal conduct had fallen short of the standards expected of the company’s leadership and expressed regret over the difficulties his actions had created for the board.

“I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at NVIDIA, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life. I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret,” he said.

“I own my mistakes completely, and I am committed to cooperating with the Board’s independent investigation.”

His resignation followed reports of alleged extramarital relationships, including one involving an executive of Singapore-based cloud computing firm Megaspeed International, which is under US criminal investigation over allegations that it helped Chinese companies obtain advanced Nvidia artificial intelligence chips in violation of American export controls.

The allegations have also drawn attention to Nvidia’s role in the global artificial intelligence industry and concerns over the possible diversion of advanced US technology to China.

The controversy has weighed on Nvidia’s shares, adding to uncertainty surrounding the company, which until recently was the world’s most valuable publicly traded company.

Huang’s possible return has attracted support from prominent figures in the technology industry, including billionaire entrepreneur Elon Musk and other artificial intelligence investors.

An online petition calling for his reinstatement has reportedly attracted more than 190,000 signatures.

US President Donald Trump also expressed support for Huang’s return on Monday. The Nvidia co-founder has been an adviser to the president on artificial intelligence policy and is one of the technology industry’s most prominent advocates for the development of the technology.

In his statement, Huang also reflected on his personal journey in the United States, saying he arrived in the country 53 years ago and regarded becoming an American citizen as one of the proudest moments of his life.

He described Nvidia as his life’s work and said building the company alongside his colleagues had been a privilege.

“NVIDIA has been my life’s work. Building it into the company it is today alongside my colleagues has been a privilege and an honour. Nowhere but in America could a company like NVIDIA be possible. I love our country, and I love NVIDIA,” he wrote.

He also expressed gratitude to those who had supported him and his family during the controversy.

“To my family: I love you, and I will spend the rest of my life being worthy of yours,” he added.

Meanwhile, Huang is expected to appear before three committees of the US House of Representatives on December 1 to answer questions over concerns that Chinese companies may have gained access to advanced Nvidia chips despite Washington’s export restrictions.

title: ‘Let Tinubu finish what he started, He deserves Second Term’ — Fashola tells Nigerians
description:
Former Minister of Works and Housing, Babatunde Fashola, has defended President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid, arguing that the President deserves a second term to complete the projects and reforms initiated by his administration.
Fashola made the remarks on Tuesday during an interview on Channels T
content:
Former Minister of Works and Housing, Babatunde Fashola, has defended President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid, arguing that the President deserves a second term to complete the projects and reforms initiated by his administration.

Fashola made the remarks on Tuesday during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today, where he was asked to assess Tinubu’s performance, economic reforms and prospects ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The former Lagos State governor said his close working relationship with Tinubu gave him firsthand knowledge of the President’s leadership style, resilience and capacity to govern.

According to him, he worked with Tinubu for several years, including four and a half years as his Chief of Staff, spending at least 14 hours daily working closely with him.

“I’ve worked with him. And I was his chief of staff for four and a half years. So, I worked with him on a minimum basis of over 14 hours a day. So, I saw him at close quarters,” Fashola said.

He described resilience, intelligence and determination as some of Tinubu’s major strengths, arguing that the President had demonstrated the ability to remain focused despite criticism and political challenges.

Fashola also defended the administration’s economic policies, particularly the removal of petrol subsidy and the unification of the foreign exchange rates, saying the decisions were necessary to address longstanding economic challenges.

He argued that although the reforms had generated difficulties for Nigerians, the country could have faced a worse economic situation without them.

The former minister maintained that the policies needed sufficient time to translate into the desired economic benefits, insisting that Tinubu should be allowed another four years to consolidate the ongoing reforms.

“Governance is not about sainthood, it’s about efficiency, it’s about performance, it’s about delivery,” he said.

To support his argument, Fashola referred to Tinubu’s eight-year administration as governor of Lagos State between 1999 and 2007.

He claimed that Tinubu increased the state’s Internally Generated Revenue from about N600 million monthly to more than N7 billion, while laying the foundation for reforms that influenced governance in other parts of the country.

Fashola also highlighted some of the major projects and initiatives introduced under Tinubu’s administration, including the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway, the Sokoto-Badagry Superhighway, the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND) and ongoing housing and infrastructure programmes across the states.

He urged Nigerians to assess the administration based on its policies and measurable achievements rather than what he described as propaganda.

“You underestimate his resilience and intelligence at your own peril,” Fashola added.

On the 2027 presidential election, the former governor argued that changing the country’s political arrangement midway through an eight-year tenure would be inappropriate.

He noted that Tinubu had overcome several challenges throughout his political career, suggesting that his emergence and continued political journey could serve a greater purpose.

Fashola further urged Nigerians to allow Tinubu to complete his constitutionally permitted second term, arguing that the South should be allowed to complete its eight-year presidential tenure, just as the North did under the late President Muhammadu Buhari.

“Let President Tinubu finish what he started. That is why he deserves a second term,” he said.

title: Presidential Election: We Were Blindsided In Lagos In 2023 – Fashola
description: Former Lagos State Governor and former Minister of Works, Babatunde Raji Fashola, has said the All Progressives Congress (APC) was caught off guard by its defeat in Lagos during the 2023 presidential election.That outcome is one he says the party is “working tooth and nail” to avoid in 2
content:
Former Lagos State Governor and former Minister of Works, Babatunde Raji Fashola, has said the All Progressives Congress (APC) was caught off guard by its defeat in Lagos during the 2023 presidential election.

That outcome is one he says the party is “working tooth and nail” to avoid in 2027.

Speaking in an interview on Politics Today, Fashola said the APC never anticipated losing Lagos, the political base of President Bola Tinubu, to the Labour Party candidate Peter Obi.

“We were blindsided in Lagos,” Fashola said on Tuesday during an interview on Politics Today.

The former governor, however, argued that the result reflected the growing maturity of Nigeria’s democracy rather than a collapse of the APC’s influence in Lagos.

According to him, electoral victories and defeats are part of democratic competition, and political loyalties can shift over time depending on prevailing circumstances.

Drawing a football analogy, Fashola said political parties, like football clubs, do not win every match and must constantly adapt to changing realities.

“In an election, sometimes you can’t win everywhere. Most times, you can’t win everywhere,” he said.

Fashola explained that in previous elections, the APC had strategically redirected its efforts to regions that were becoming more receptive to the party.

He suggested that a similar approach would be adopted as the ruling party prepares for the next general election.

“It remains to be seen whether, as happened in 2023, Lagos flipped, whether Lagos will flip back,” he said.

“And we’re working tooth and nail to ensure that we take back what we lost.”

Although he said the party was blindsided in the 2023 presidential election, Fashola dismissed suggestions that Tinubu had been politically “demystified” by the defeat, insisting that opponents underestimate the President at their own risk.

He maintained that the APC remains focused on convincing voters that the reforms being implemented by the Tinubu administration deserve continuity beyond 2027.

The former governor, who argued that President Tinubu deserves a second term, dismissed the ideas and plans being shared by opposition candidates.

“What are the other parties offering that is different, that is better, that is compelling as a reason to interrupt the process of reform, growth, and restructuring that is already underway?” he asked.

He also queried what he described as the opposition’s alternative message, asking, “What is the alternative message to what we are currently dealing with? What is the compelling message?

Obi contested the 2023 presidential election, finishing third nationally behind APC candidate Tinubu and Atiku Abubakar under the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP).

However, he defeated Tinubu in Lagos State, where he secured 582,454 votes against the APC candidate’s 572,606.

The APC has ruled the metropolitan state for 27 years. Tinubu, a former Lagos State governor, had enjoyed considerable political influence in the state, making Obi’s victory there one of the notable outcomes of the election.

The post Presidential Election: We Were Blindsided In Lagos In 2023 – Fashola appeared first on Channels Television.

title: ‘Even A Tomato Seller Knows Strait Of Hormuz’, Fashola Blames Global Conflicts For Economic Pressures
description: Former Lagos State Governor Babatunde Fashola has defended the economic policies of President Bola Tinubu’s administration, arguing that global developments, including the COVID-19 pandemic, the Russia-Ukraine war and conflicts in the Middle East, have contributed to the cost-of-living challen
content:
Former Lagos State Governor Babatunde Fashola has defended the economic policies of President Bola Tinubu’s administration, arguing that global developments, including the COVID-19 pandemic, the Russia-Ukraine war and conflicts in the Middle East, have contributed to the cost-of-living challenges Nigerians are grappling with.

Fashola, a Senior Advocate of Nigeria, said Nigeria was not insulated from global economic pressures, particularly disruptions to supply chains, energy supplies and food markets.

Speaking during an appearance on Politics Today, the former Minister of Works said the global economy was still recovering from the effects of the pandemic, which disrupted economic activity and production worldwide.

He explained that shortages of goods following the pandemic had pushed up prices, while the Russia-Ukraine war further affected the supply of major energy and food commodities, including diesel and wheat.

Fashola also identified the ongoing conflict in the Middle East as another factor affecting global markets, particularly energy supplies and shipping costs.

“It’s also important to contextualise the factors and the circumstances that have exacerbated the cost-of-living challenges,” he said.

“Even the tomato seller knows the Strait of Hormuz and prices his or her goods according to replacement costs now.”

‘Helping Families In Need’

Fashola, a former Minister of Works, also backed President Tinubu for a second term, defending the administration’s response to challenges.

Defending the Tinubu administration’s response to economic pressures, Fashola listed the minimum wage review, the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND), tax reforms, and the introduction of compressed natural gas (CNG) as part of measures intended to ease the burden on Nigerians.

He said the minimum wage review was one of the government’s early responses to the rising cost of living, aimed at putting more money in workers’ hands.

However, he argued that increasing wages alone could not address the problem, warning that continuously injecting cash into the economy could create what he described as “hyper-demand inflation”.

Fashola said the government had also sought to address some of the major expenses that reduce household disposable income, including rent, transportation, healthcare and children’s education.

He identified NELFUND as one of the interventions aimed at easing financial pressure on families by supporting students’ education.
“Your disposable income goes to rent, goes to transport, and goes to health care, and goes to your children’s education. And NELFUND was, okay, we will help families in need,” he said.

On the tax reforms, Fashola highlighted provisions he said were designed to reduce the tax burden on lower-income earners and ease household expenses.

He said people earning ₦800,000 or less annually were exempt from personal income tax, while about 10.7 million people had experienced reductions in their tax liabilities.

He also cited provisions he said would exempt certain rental agreements valued at ₦10 million or less from stamp duty, as well as the removal of value-added tax on petroleum products.

Fashola argued that the measures were intended to protect disposable income and reduce some of the financial pressures facing households.

‘I’m Not Saying It Is Enough’

The former governor acknowledged that the government’s interventions were insufficient to resolve the economic difficulties immediately, noting a gap between policy announcements and the resources needed to implement them.

“I’m not saying it is enough. There are initiatives like the introduction of CNG, but there’s a distance between policy, between programme, between projects and resources,” he said.

“But we are seeing the rollout slowly. And in the fullness of time, we will see the impact.”

With the 2027 elections less than three months away, Fashola dismissed the opposition, suggesting they can’t do any better.

He questioned whether their proposals offered a compelling reason for Nigerians to abandon the current reform programme.

“What are the other parties offering that is different, that is better, that is compelling as a reason to interrupt the process of reform, growth, and restructuring that is already underway?” he asked.

He also queried what he described as the opposition’s alternative message, asking, “What is the alternative message to what we are currently dealing with? What is the compelling message?

title: Atiku’s fuel subsidy reversal plan not realistic — Fashola
description:
Former Lagos State Governor, Babatunde Fashola, has challenged Atiku Abubakar to explain how he intends to fund his proposed return of fuel subsidy if elected president in 2027, describing the plan as unrealistic.



Fashola said the former vice-president had not addressed the practical difficulties
content:
Former Lagos State Governor, Babatunde Fashola, has challenged Atiku Abubakar to explain how he intends to fund his proposed return of fuel subsidy if elected president in 2027, describing the plan as unrealistic.

Fashola said the former vice-president had not addressed the practical difficulties that could undermine the proposal, particularly Nigeria’s inability to fully meet its crude oil production targets and persistent security problems in oil-producing areas.

He made the remarks on Tuesday during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today.

The former Minister of Works and Housing questioned the source of the crude oil needed to supply local refineries and support a subsidy arrangement, given the country’s production challenges.

“If we have refineries working, what is our current oil quota? Are we optimising it yet? No, because they are legacy issues, challenges with security people, vandalism. So where is this magic crude oil going to come from? People are entitled to ask,” he said.

Fashola insisted that Atiku must demonstrate that the proposal can work rather than rely on promises to win public support.

“If he can explain, good, let the people choose. But without proof, it is like abracadabra,” he said.

He maintained that his criticism was directed at the policy and not the former vice-president personally.

“The proposal is not realistic. I am looking at the proposal, not the personality,” he said.

Fashola also questioned the consistency of Atiku’s position, noting that the former vice-president had supported subsidy removal during the 2023 presidential campaign.

He said the change in position raised questions about the basis for the proposed reversal and what measures would make the policy sustainable.

Fashola further argued that bringing back subsidy would involve legislative processes, as lawmakers would have to amend the existing legal framework to accommodate the policy.

He wondered whether members of the National Assembly would be willing to support such a move, given its potential implications for public finances.

The former governor also drew on his experience in the Buhari administration, saying subsidy payments had previously constrained the funds available to state governments.

“I was in a government that was paying subsidy, and the states were not getting money. So are we going to go back to partial, near-zero returns, states borrowing money to pay salaries? Is that where you want us to go?” he asked.

Atiku announced in August 2026 that he would restore fuel subsidy if elected president in 2027. He proposed a temporary, audited arrangement focused on petroleum products refined locally, arguing that it would help bring down fuel and transportation costs and ease the burden on households.

Tinubu announced the removal of fuel subsidy during his inauguration on May 29, 2023, as part of his administration’s economic reforms.

The post Atiku’s fuel subsidy reversal plan not realistic — Fashola appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: ‘Nothing Suggests To Me Tinubu Is Not Fit,’ Fashola Dismisses Health Concerns
description: Former Lagos State Governor Babatunde Fashola has dismissed concerns about President Bola Tinubu’s physical and mental fitness for office, saying he has seen nothing to suggest that the president is incapable of performing his duties.Fashola, a former Minister of Works and Housing, made the re
content:
Former Lagos State Governor Babatunde Fashola has dismissed concerns about President Bola Tinubu’s physical and mental fitness for office, saying he has seen nothing to suggest that the president is incapable of performing his duties.

Fashola, a former Minister of Works and Housing, made the remarks on Tuesday during an appearance on Channels Television’s Politics Today, where he was asked whether he considered Tinubu physically fit to lead the country.

“Nothing suggests to me that he’s not fit for it. Yes, he’s older. That doesn’t mean his mental capacity is gone. He’s still giving directives. And when I see him, he’s working. He’s still reading, authorising, minuting on things,” he said.

Questions about Tinubu’s health and physical condition have featured in public discussions since the 2023 presidential election campaign.

During the campaign, concerns were raised by critics over his physical appearance, movements and stamina at public events. The debate continued after he assumed office in May 2023, with opposition figures and other critics occasionally questioning his capacity to discharge the responsibilities of the presidency.

The concerns resurfaced in 2026 amid renewed scrutiny of his public appearances, including videos circulated online showing him moving cautiously at some events.

The Presidency and the All Progressives Congress (APC) have repeatedly defended the president, maintaining that he is capable of carrying out his constitutional responsibilities.

Tinubu has also dismissed speculation about his health. In September 2026, following an extended stay in Europe, he told reporters that he was ready to “work, walk and kick.”

‘More Mature’

The former governor, who worked closely with Tinubu during his eight-year administration in Lagos from 2007 to 2015, said the president had become more experienced over the years.

Asked to compare the Tinubu he knew in the early 2000s with the president he knows today, Fashola said the president had become more mature.

“Well, a much more mature one, certainly, without doubt. I am not the chief of staff he employed in 2002. That’s 39 years. I was 39 then. I’m 63 now. So we must give him that credit for the experience he has gained,” he said.

Fashola acknowledged that Tinubu might no longer maintain the same work routine he had in the past, particularly when it came to keeping late nights, but maintained that the president remained capable of handling demanding responsibilities.

“Maybe not keeping late nights that he used to do. I’m not sure. He can still run the engine,” he added.

When asked about opposition figures who have described Tinubu as feeble and frail, Fashola said such views were their opinions, insisting that the president’s actions and the activities of his administration should also be considered.

He argued that the president’s leadership had produced results in government, adding that Tinubu often moved ahead of those who underestimated him.

“Every time he looks at you, you think there is nothing there. Before you know it, he has left you behind,” he said.

Fashola’s remarks add to public responses by political allies who have defended the president against questions about his health and capacity to govern.

title: 2027: ADC threatens street rally in Kaduna over stadium denial
description:
The African Democratic Congress (ADC) has threatened to move its planned campaign rally to the streets of Kaduna following the state government’s refusal to grant it access to the Ranchers Bees Stadium.
The opposition party accused the Kaduna State Government of deliberately frustrating its politica
content:
The African Democratic Congress (ADC) has threatened to move its planned campaign rally to the streets of Kaduna following the state government’s refusal to grant it access to the Ranchers Bees Stadium.

The opposition party accused the Kaduna State Government of deliberately frustrating its political activities by denying it the use of the stadium for its scheduled rally on November 17 and 18, 2026.

The ADC made the allegation in a press statement issued on Tuesday by its National Publicity Secretary, Mallam Bolaji Abdullahi.

The party expressed dissatisfaction with the decision, warning that it could take its planned political gathering to the streets if it was prevented from using the stadium.

According to the party, it had earlier applied to the state government for permission to use the stadium but was denied approval in a letter dated November 12 by the Ministry of Local Government.

The ministry reportedly attributed the refusal to ongoing renovation work at the facility.

However, the ADC questioned the explanation, noting that the ruling All Progressives Congress, APC, had used the same stadium to flag off its presidential campaign on October 24, barely three weeks earlier.

The party described the government’s explanation as ridiculous, alleging that the APC was afraid of the large crowds attracted by its rallies across the North.

“We find the excuse quite ridiculous. This was the same stadium where the APC flagged off its presidential campaign on October 24. But we know what they are afraid of,” the statement said.

The ADC further alleged that the government was attempting to prevent residents from comparing the attendance at its rallies with that of the ruling party.

Insisting that it would not abandon its planned rally, the opposition party threatened to hold a street demonstration if the government continued to deny it access to the stadium.

“If the Kaduna State Government will not allow us to campaign peacefully in the stadium, we will exercise our constitutional right to assemble peacefully in the streets.

“You may deny us a venue, but you cannot deny Nigerians their constitutional right to peaceful assembly,” the party said.

The ADC maintained that public facilities should not be used as instruments of political exclusion, arguing that they belong to the people regardless of the political party controlling the government.

It also warned that denying opposition parties access to public infrastructure amounted to violating citizens’ rights to peaceful assembly and democratic participation.

The party urged the Kaduna State Government to reconsider its position, citing the Bauchi and Yobe state governments as examples of administrations that had allowed opposition parties to carry out their political activities.

title: Tinubu moves to decriminalise attempted suicide, sends mental health bill to senate
description:
President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has transmitted the National Mental Health (Amendment) Bill, 2026, to the Senate, seeking to remove criminal penalties for attempted suicide and provide support for survivors.
Senate President Godswill Akpabio announced the development during plenary on Tuesday, explainin
content:
President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has transmitted the National Mental Health (Amendment) Bill, 2026, to the Senate, seeking to remove criminal penalties for attempted suicide and provide support for survivors.

Senate President Godswill Akpabio announced the development during plenary on Tuesday, explaining that the proposed amendment was intended to address concerns over the criminalisation of attempted suicide under existing laws.

Akpabio clarified that his earlier comments on the issue did not cover people experiencing mental health conditions, whose illnesses could affect their ability to understand or control their actions when attempting suicide.

The proposed amendment is expected to shift attention towards mental health support and assistance for survivors rather than criminal punishment.

“Perhaps, with this amendment, I should make a distinction in my earlier submission.

“I had said that if someone attempts suicide, such a person should ensure that the attempt succeeds. Otherwise, the person would be sent to prison.

“However, I did not include people who are mentally disturbed. I made that distinction because they do not have the mental balance to understand what they are doing.

“I want to thank the President for supporting the decriminalisation of attempted suicide because making it a criminal offence for people who are mentally disturbed would be insensitive,” he said.

Akpabio said the amendment was important, adding that the bill would decriminalise attempted suicide, particularly in cases involving people who were mentally disturbed.

“When I made my earlier submission, I clearly stated that I was referring to people who were mentally sound, not those who were mentally disturbed. Unfortunately, social media reports did not capture that distinction.

Read Also: 2027: Give me second term to complete ongoing reforms, Tinubu urges Kebbi voters
“Nevertheless, this is a welcome development. People who are mentally disturbed require our support,” he added.

The Senate President referred the bill to the Committee on Rules and Business for further legislative action, urging its consideration as soon as practicable.
