title: Military aircraft crashes, 19 dead
description:
A military transport plane crashed on Tuesday in the Siberian region of Kemerovo, killing all 19 onboard, Russian media reported, citing a statement from Moscow’s defence ministry.



“An An-12 military transport aircraft crashed in the Kemerovo Region while on a scheduled flight. The plane went dow
content:
A military transport plane crashed on Tuesday in the Siberian region of Kemerovo, killing all 19 onboard, Russian media reported, citing a statement from Moscow’s defence ministry.

“An An-12 military transport aircraft crashed in the Kemerovo Region while on a scheduled flight. The plane went down in an uninhabited area. There were 19 people on board, including the crew, they all perished,” the Russian defence ministry was quoted as saying by state news agency TASS.

The preliminary cause of the crash is a technical malfunction, TASS added.

“A commission from the Russian Aerospace Forces is working at the site to establish all the circumstances of the incident,” the ministry’s statement was quoted as saying by RIA Novosti.

Kemerovo region’s governor, Ilya Seredyuk, said earlier on Telegram that there had been an “aviation incident” near the village of Yagunovo.

He added that “an aircraft, which was in transit through our region, has presumably crashed”.

Seredyuk posted a video from the site in which multiple fire engines and ambulances could be seen, their lights blaring in the dark.

title: Benue Justice Commissioner resigns with immediate effect
description:
By Peter Duru, Makurdi



The Attorney-General and Commissioner for Justice of Benue State, Prof. Timothy Ornguga, has resigned his appointment with immediate effect, barely one year and two months in office.



The Attorney-General announced his decision in a resignation letter dated November 13, 2
content:
By Peter Duru, Makurdi

The Attorney-General and Commissioner for Justice of Benue State, Prof. Timothy Ornguga, has resigned his appointment with immediate effect, barely one year and two months in office.

The Attorney-General announced his decision in a resignation letter dated November 13, 2026, addressed to Governor Hyacinth Alia through the Secretary to the State Government, SSG.

The letter, titled, “Resignation from the Appointment as Honourable Attorney-General and Commissioner for Justice, Benue State,” formally communicated his decision to step down from the position with immediate effect.

He disclosed that he had served the state for one year, two months and two weeks, expressing appreciation to Governor Alia for the confidence reposed in him and the opportunity to serve.

The resignation letter, which bears an official receipt stamp dated November 16, 2026, stated: “I write with profound respect and deep sense of responsibility to formally tender my resignation from my appointment as the Attorney-General and Commissioner for Justice of Benue State. The resignation is with immediate effect. Having had the privilege of serving in this esteemed capacity for the past one year, two months, and two weeks.”

He further stated: “I consider it an honour to have been entrusted with the responsibility of serving our dear state and contributing in my own capacity to the administration of justice, the promotion of the rule of law and the advancement of good governance. I am sincerely grateful to Your Excellency for the confidence reposed in me and for the opportunity to serve.”

Contacted, the Media of the former Justice Commissioner, Jude Ekpendu confirmed the development.

Meanwhile, efforts to ascertain the circumstances surrounding his resignation were unsuccessful as the Commissioner for Information and Orientation, Chief Solomon Iorpev, said he was unaware of the development when contacted.

title: FGN bonds undersubscribed by 9% in November auction
description:
By Elizabeth Adegbesan



The Federal Government of Nigeria (FGN) bond auction in November 2026 was undersubscribed by 9.5 percent , attracting a total subscription of N1.81 trillion against N2 trillion offered by the Debt Management Office, DMO.



This reflects decline in investors’ demand for the
content:
By Elizabeth Adegbesan

The Federal Government of Nigeria (FGN) bond auction in November 2026 was undersubscribed by 9.5 percent , attracting a total subscription of N1.81 trillion against N2 trillion offered by the Debt Management Office, DMO.

This reflects decline in investors’ demand for the Federal Government of Nigeria (FGN) debt instrument.

According to the November FGN Bond Auction result released by DMO , investors bid N1.81 trillion for bonds worth N2 trillion with total allotments rising by 25 percent to N1.5 trillion in November, down from N1.2 trillion allotted in October 2026.
Four instruments were offered during the auction consisting 21 percent FGN March 2028 , 19.3 percent FGN April 2029, 17.94 percent FGN August 2030 and 19.89 percent FGN May 2033, with an offer of N700 billion, N250 billion, N750 billion and N300 billion respectively.
Investor interest was strongest for the May 2033 bond, which attracted N766.4 billion in bids from 233 successful applicants.
The bulk of allotments also went to this bond, totaling N676.6 billion.

The March 2028 bond received N162.99 billion and a non competitive allotment of N50 billion while the April 2029 bond received N241.03 billion and a non competitive allotment of N30 billion.
The August 2030 bond received an allotment of N336.12 billion.

Clearing yields for the bonds were as follows: March 2028: 16.89 percent, while that of other bonds were 16.99 percent.

The results reflect continuous declining appetite among investors for Nigerian government debt, even as allotments tightened compared with previous months.

title: ‘The Proposal Is Not Realistic,’ Fashola Faults Atiku’s Fuel Subsidy Reversal Plan
description: Former Minister of Works and Housing, Babatunde Fashola, has faulted the presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Atiku Abubakar’s proposal to restore fuel subsidy if elected president in 2027, describing it as unrealistic and questioning the availability of crude oil t
content:
Former Minister of Works and Housing, Babatunde Fashola, has faulted the presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Atiku Abubakar’s proposal to restore fuel subsidy if elected president in 2027, describing it as unrealistic and questioning the availability of crude oil to sustain the policy.

Fashola said the proposal lacked sufficient explanation on how the country would secure the crude oil required to support domestic refineries and maintain a subsidy regime.

The former Lagos State governor spoke on Tuesday during an appearance on Channels Television’s Politics Today, where he argued that Nigeria’s existing challenges with crude oil production, pipeline vandalism and insecurity raised questions about the feasibility of Atiku’s proposal.

“If we have refineries working, what is our current oil quota? Are we optimising it yet? No, because they are legacy issues, challenges with security people, vandalism. So where is this magic crude oil going to come from? People are entitled to ask,” he said.

Fashola added that Atiku needed to explain how he intended to implement the proposal, insisting that Nigerians should be allowed to assess its feasibility before deciding whether to support it.

“If he can explain, good, let the people choose. But without proof, it is like abracadabra. Because the reality that will come then is that he will say that, ‘I didn’t know that there was not enough crude oil.’ That was what happened,” he added.

When asked whether his position was that Atiku’s proposal was feasible, Fashola replied: “The proposal is not realistic. I am looking at the proposal, not the personality.

“In this environment, it is very easy to throw promises at people. When the rubber hits the road, reality sets in. First question is, in 2023, didn’t he see through this when he was making the promise to remove the subsidy? And that goes to a question of credibility. Those who believe at face value that promise, he will come back and tell you that, ‘Oh, I changed my mind. I didn’t think through it,’” he said.

Fashola argued that restoring the subsidy would require more than a presidential declaration, noting that legislative backing would also be necessary.

“Subsidy is not just about, ‘I said it.’ It will come down to the real economy, and legislators will have to repeal a law to say subsidy is now lawful. How many legislators are ready to stake their election on going back to subsidy? Those are the real issues,” he said.

According to him, all the major presidential candidates in the 2023 election had promised to remove the subsidy, and Atiku needed to explain what had changed to justify his current position.

“Is it because people are impacted? It’s true. But what are you going to do differently? Where are you going to find the money to sustain what you are offering? It’s not sustainable,” he said.

Fashola, who served in the administration of former President Muhammadu Buhari, recalled the financial difficulties states faced when the federal government was paying fuel subsidy, warning that a return to the arrangement could reduce allocations to state governments.

“I was in a government that was paying subsidy, and the states were not getting money. So are we going to go back to partial, near-zero returns, states borrowing money to pay salaries? Is that where you want us to go?” he asked.

In August 2026, Atiku pledged to restore fuel subsidy if elected in 2027. However, he proposed a time-bound, audited arrangement tied to locally refined petroleum products, rather than a return to the former import-dependent system. He said the policy would reduce petrol, transportation and food costs while easing the economic hardship faced by Nigerians.

President Bola Tinubu announced the removal of fuel subsidy during his inauguration on May 29, 2023, citing its rising cost to government finances. The decision, alongside the unification of the foreign exchange market, contributed to rising petrol prices and living costs.

Atiku has criticised the administration over the economic impact of the reforms, while Tinubu and the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) have rejected his proposal, warning that restoring the subsidy could reverse fiscal gains.

The post ‘The Proposal Is Not Realistic,’ Fashola Faults Atiku’s Fuel Subsidy Reversal Plan  appeared first on Channels Television.

title: 2027: Weigh alternatives before rejecting Tinubu’s reforms – Fashola tells Nigerians
description:
…Says cost-of-living crisis is global



…Subsidy return will hurt federation revenue



…Defends Lagos-Calabar highway







By Juliet Umeh







Former Lagos State Governor, Babatunde Fashola, has urged Nigerians to weigh opposition parties’ proposals before rejecting President Bola Tinubu’s ref
content:
…Says cost-of-living crisis is global

…Subsidy return will hurt federation revenue

…Defends Lagos-Calabar highway

By Juliet Umeh

Former Lagos State Governor, Babatunde Fashola, has urged Nigerians to weigh opposition parties’ proposals before rejecting President Bola Tinubu’s reforms, saying the country should not “abort this journey mid-term” without considering the alternatives.

Fashola, a former Minister of Works, spoke on Channels Television, where he said voters should be helped to make informed choices ahead of the 2027 general election.

“What are the other parties offering that is different, that is better, that is compelling as a reason to interrupt the process of reform and restructuring that is already underway?” he asked.

He acknowledged the hardship many Nigerians face but said the cost-of-living crisis was not unique to Nigeria.

“Anybody who is right-thinking will concede that the cost-of-living challenge is now a global challenge,” he said, citing the effects of the COVID-19 pandemic and conflicts that disrupted energy and food supplies.

Fashola said: The government had introduced measures including a higher minimum wage, support for students through the Nigerian Education Loan Fund, NELFUND, and tax reforms.”

He said the policies were aimed at easing pressure on households, while acknowledging that there was “a distance between policies, programmes, projects and results.”

On the removal of petrol subsidy, he said a return to the policy would have consequences for government revenue and the funds available to states and local governments.

“Subsidy is not just about ‘I said it, I did not say it’. It has to be paid for somewhere. One of the things that suffered because of that was the monthly receipts into the federation account.”

Fashola challenged politicians proposing a return to subsidy to explain how they would fund it and what they would do differently.

“I want to see rigour, I want to see detail, I want to see numbers,” he said, adding that Nigeria also needed to explain where the crude oil for subsidised supply would come from, given constraints on production.
Fashola said the government deserved credit for maintaining the subsidy removal, despite the hardship it had caused.
“What this government deserves commendation for is not falling over on the sword and saying because the people like it, let’s bring it back,” he said.
He cited the introduction of compressed natural gas, or CNG, as one of the measures aimed at reducing living costs.
Defending the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway, Fashola said it had reduced travel time to the Lekki Port.
“It took me 40 minutes from Ikoyi to get to that port. Traditionally, when I went to visit that site when I was governor, it used to take me all of one and a half hours. A 90-minute journey is now 40 minutes.
“Go and calculate the fuel savings in that corridor, and the relief to people’s disposable income,” he said.
Fashola also pointed to jobs created by construction activity along the route, saying: “I wish that somebody will commission a survey about how many people are earning a daily living from the construction activity that is going on there.”
Asked about the project’s cost, Fashola said the Bureau of Public Procurement was responsible for reviewing contract prices and issuing certificates of no objection.

On questions about Tinubu’s fitness to govern, he said: “Nothing suggests to me that he’s not fit.”
He described the president as “much more mature” than when they first worked together and said Tinubu was still reading, giving directives and managing government affairs.

title: ‘Stay prepared, don’t take it easy with them’ — Kwankwaso tells supporters after convoy attack
description:
The vice-presidential candidate of the opposition Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Rabiu Kwankwaso, has urged party supporters in Kano State to remain prepared for possible confrontations following an attack on his campaign convoy in Bichi Local Government Area.
Kwankwaso charged his supporters to
content:
The vice-presidential candidate of the opposition Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Rabiu Kwankwaso, has urged party supporters in Kano State to remain prepared for possible confrontations following an attack on his campaign convoy in Bichi Local Government Area.

Kwankwaso charged his supporters to stand their ground against those attacking them, urging them to adopt what he described as an “ambush” strategy to prepare for any eventuality.

His directive was captured in a viral video recorded during a campaign rally in Bichi, shortly after youths reportedly attacked his convoy with stones.

“Continue to stay prepared. These shameless people—don’t take it easy with them. We are telling you every day to stay prepared, but you should stay down and take the pattern of ambush to ensure that you are ready for any eventuality,” Kwankwaso said.

The former Kano State governor also launched a verbal attack on the member of the House of Representatives representing Bichi Federal Constituency, Abubakar Kabir, although he did not mention the lawmaker by name.

Kwankwaso alleged that the lawmaker had benefited from proceeds of corruption and used questionable funds to advance his political ambitions.

He also made references to the lawmaker’s late father, who served as a state legislator during the early years of the Fourth Republic before becoming a commissioner under former Kano State Governor Ibrahim Shekarau.

“There is a certain issue that dates back to when we were doing politics with their parents—when their parents were our boys. At this time, this is also a special moment. Now, they are dealing with little boys—these ragtag youths,” he said.

Kwankwaso further declared that the political movement he leads was beyond the influence of those he accused of benefiting from the country’s democratic system through questionable means.

“I want to tell the boys in Abuja, and tell the boys in Kano State: this moving train is beyond them; it is even beyond their grandfathers! And I want to tell them that they are the ones reaping the benefits of this democracy; they are the ones looting money; they are the ones benefiting from dirty money,” he stated.

He also warned those he accused of wrongdoing against provoking further political tensions, saying they should be careful about making accusations against others.

Addressing the youths at the rally, Kwankwaso commended their efforts during the campaign tour and urged them to remain committed to the party’s activities.

He said he had received reports that some supporters had already engaged in confrontations with their opponents before his campaign team arrived in Bichi.

“Even before you came—before we entered this town—I heard that you had already fought hard. Keep the spirit alive and prepare for them,” he added.

The remarks followed an earlier attack on the NDC campaign convoy led by Kwankwaso alongside the party’s Kano State governorship candidate, Aminu Abdussalam.

The campaign team had earlier visited Tofa, Rimin Gado, Kabo, Gwarzo, Shanono and Bagwai local government areas as part of a campaign tour before encountering youths who reportedly pelted the convoy with stones in Bichi.

The incident has added to concerns over political violence and rising tensions among supporters of rival political groups in Kano State.

content:
Tiger Woods will return to competitive golf for the first time in more than two years next month when he tees off at the Hero World Challenge event in the Bahamas, organisers said on Tuesday.

Woods, 50, was named in the line-up for the limited field PGA Tour event taking place in Albany from December 3-6.

It will mark the first time Woods has played an official PGA Tour event since July 2024.

The 15-time major champion has battled injuries and legal problems since his last appearance.

In March he was involved in a rollover car crash in Florida which led to him having his driver’s license suspended for five years.

Authorities determined the 15-time major champion had not been drinking alcohol but found he appeared to be impaired.

Woods, who has undergone multiple back operations and surgeries on severe leg injuries suffered in a separate 2021 California car crash, had two pills containing the opioid painkiller hydrocodone in his pocket.

He refused a urine analysis and was charged, jailed and released on bond.

Woods initially pleaded not guilty to charges of DUI (driving under the influence) with property damage and refusing to submit to a lawful test.

Days later, he said he was “stepping away” to seek treatment and focus on his health.

Since the crash, Woods has travelled outside the United States to seek treatment at an inpatient facility, reportedly in Switzerland.

He made his first public appearance since his arrest at the PGA Tour’s Travelers Championship in June, and later struck a plea agreement which led to his driver’s license being suspended.

Woods has not won a tournament since a victory at the ZoZo Championship in Japan in 2019.

The post Tiger Woods to return to competitive golf next month appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: 2027: INEC warns against attacks on staff, threatens sanctions
description:

INEC ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍‍‍‌‌‌⁠‍⁠‌​Chairman, Pro
content:
The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has warned against any form of harassment, intimidation or physical attack on its leadership, staff members or ad hoc workers by political supporters.

INEC ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍‍‍‌‌‌⁠‍⁠‌​Chairman, Prof. Joash Amupitan, gave the warning on Tuesday in Abuja at the 2026 Goodluck Jonathan Foundation (GJF) Peace and Security Conference.

Amupitan, represented by INEC National Commissioner, Mrs May Agbamuche-Mbu, described election officials as public servants discharging a sacred constitutional duty.

He warned that assaulting or threatening them constitutes a direct assault on the Nigerian state and would be met with decisive legal consequences.

Amupiatan also condemned the widespread incidents of political violence, intimidation and attacks on campaign convoys and party supporters recorded in some parts of the country in recent weeks.

According to him, democracy can not flourish in an atmosphere of fear and bloodshed.

“Let me issue a clear and unambiguous warning to all political actors, sponsors and their foot soldiers:

“The law will take its full course and security agencies working alongside the commission will go after the promoters and perpetrators of violent campaigns without fear or favour.

“Equally, I must sound a stern warning against any form of harassment, intimidation or physical attack directed at the leadership, staff or ad hoc workers of INEC by supporters of any political party—whether within Nigeria or abroad.

“Election officials are public servants discharging a sacred constitutional duty; assaulting or threatening them is an assault on the Nigerian state and will be met with decisive legal consequences,’’ he said.

Amupitan reminded political parties and candidates of the provisions of the Electoral Act 2026, noting that sections 96 and 97 prohibit abusive language, private thugs and use of force to intimidate voters.

He said that the Act raised financial penalties five-fold, imposing fines of up to five million Naira or 12 months imprisonment on individuals and up to 10 million Naira on political parties for initial breaches.

The INEC chairman added that under Section 148, INEC was statutorily empowered to prosecute electoral offenders directly upon receiving case files from the police.

On physical security and logistics, Amupitan said that the commission was leveraging the Inter-Agency Consultative Committee on Election Security (ICCES) to secure the electoral terrain against insurgency, banditry and communal tensions.

To tackle digital misinformation on elections, he said that INEC had established a dedicated Artificial Intelligence Division within its ICT Department.

He said that the department was established to monitor database anomalies, verify digital assets and counter deepfakes, synthetic broadcasts and Foreign Information Manipulation and Interference (FIMI).

Amupitan, while reiterating INEC’s absolute institutional neutrality ahead of the January and February 2027 general elections, pledged that the commission had no preferred party or candidate.

“My personal and constitutional loyalty belongs solely to the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, the Electoral Act 2026 and the sovereign will of the Nigerian voter,” he stated.

title: Woman arrested for allegedly hiring men to kill husband’s children over inheritance in Kano
description:
The Kano State Police Command has arrested a 20-year-old woman and three other suspects over an alleged plot to murder her husband’s four children from another wife to ensure that her only son inherits his father’s properties.
The arrests followed the abduction and killing of a 14-year-old boy, iden
content:
The Kano State Police Command has arrested a 20-year-old woman and three other suspects over an alleged plot to murder her husband’s four children from another wife to ensure that her only son inherits his father’s properties.

The arrests followed the abduction and killing of a 14-year-old boy, identified as Mahmoud Auwal, who police said was allegedly targeted as part of the plot.

The Police Public Relations Officer, CSP Abdullahi Haruna Kiyawa, disclosed this on Tuesday, saying the victim’s mother reported his disappearance on April 29, 2026, at Danbare Quarters in Kumbotso Local Government Area of Kano State.

Following the report, the Commissioner of Police, Ibrahim Adamu Bakori, directed operatives of the Anti-Kidnapping Squad to investigate the case.

According to the police, the first suspect, Muhammad Musa Isma’il, 20, of Sharada Quarters, Kano, was arrested on November 3, 2026.

During interrogation, he allegedly confessed to luring the victim on April 20, 2026, and identified two other suspects, Abubakar Muhammad Isah, 27, and Auwal Muhammad, 26, as his accomplices.

“During interrogation, he confessed to luring the victim on April 20, 2026, and identified Abubakar Muhammad Isah, 27, and Auwal Muhammad, 26, as his accomplices,” Kiyawa said.

The police alleged that the suspects conspired to kill the teenager before abandoning his body at the scene.

His remains were later recovered by officers attached to the Kwalli Division during a patrol and taken to the mortuary of Sir Muhammad Sunusi Specialist Hospital.

Further investigations reportedly led to the arrest of Hajiya Rukayya Auwal, 20, of Mararaba Quarters in New Karu Local Government Area of Nasarawa State, whom the police identified as the alleged mastermind.

The command said the other suspects claimed they carried out the crime on her instructions.

According to the police, investigations indicated that Rukayya was another wife of the deceased boy’s father and allegedly wanted to eliminate all four children of her co-wife so that her only son could inherit their father’s properties.

The police further alleged that the principal suspect hired another group of thugs to attack Isma’il in Mararaba, Karu Local Government Area of Nasarawa State, in an attempt to prevent him from disclosing details of the crime.

The command said the suspects would be charged in court after the conclusion of investigations.

The Commissioner of Police condemned the killing and assured the victim’s family and members of the public that the command would work to ensure justice.

He also urged residents to provide credible information to security agencies to help prevent and detect criminal activities.

The post Woman arrested for allegedly hiring men to kill husband’s children over inheritance in Kano appeared first on Very Nigerian.

content:
…Renovates 190 PHCs, functionalises 123, Polytechnic rector emerges Administrator of the Year

By Steve Oko

UMUAHIA — Abia State Government has announced a 60 per cent reduction in maternal mortality between 2024 and 2026, claiming that the state now has the second-lowest maternal mortality rate in the country.

The government attributed the improvement to ongoing reforms in the health sector, including the rehabilitation of primary healthcare facilities and increased investment in healthcare delivery.

Commissioner for Information, Prince Okey Kanu, disclosed this during a briefing on the outcome of this week’s State Executive Council meeting at Government House, Umuahia. He was represented by the Special Adviser to the Governor on Media and Publicity, Mr Ferdinand Ekeoma.

Kanu said the administration had made significant progress in its efforts to revitalise primary healthcare, disclosing that 190 of the 200 primary healthcare centres earmarked for renovation under Project Ekwueme had been completed.

Of the renovated facilities, 123 had been functionalised to provide essential medical services, while 27 had been equipped with solar power, with work progressing on nine additional centres.
He also announced the completion of all 77 World Bank-supported health projects in the state.

In another development, the Commissioner disclosed that the Aba Campus of the College of Nursing Sciences had secured an increase in its admission quota from 75 to 120 students following an accreditation exercise by the National Nursing and Midwifery Council.

The new quota, according to him, was communicated in an accreditation report released on November 13 and reflected growing confidence in the state’s investment in nursing education and healthcare manpower development.

Meanwhile, the Rector of Ogbonnaya Onu Polytechnic, Aba, Dr Christopher Okoro, has emerged Administrator of the Year in a nationwide poll organised by Leadership Excellence Award.

Kanu said Okoro secured 148,267 votes in the exercise, which recognised his contributions to institutional transformation, human capital development and technical and professional education.

He attributed the recognition to developments recorded at the institution under the Rector, including a student population increase of more than 6,000, improved infrastructure and better staff welfare.

The Commissioner also said the state government remained committed to education development, noting that the sector continued to receive 20 per cent of the state’s annual budget.

On public health surveillance, the government reported that Abia recorded no cases of Ebola, Lassa fever, COVID-19, diphtheria, cholera, mpox or yellow fever during the period under review.

The Commissioner for Health, Prof. Enoch Ogbonnaya Uche, who also addressed the briefing, provided an update on the Ebola situation in the country.

He disclosed that the index patient reported on October 20 had been transferred to Switzerland, where the patient subsequently recovered.

Uche further said all 62 contacts traced to the index case had completed the mandatory 21-day monitoring period and were cleared as of November 13, citing information from the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control.

He, however, urged residents not to lower their guard, stressing that personal hygiene and sustained public awareness remained critical to preventing infectious disease outbreaks.

Identifying hand hygiene as the focus of the state’s public health advisory for the week, the Commissioner advised residents to wash their hands regularly with running water, particularly at home, workplaces and after touching potentially contaminated surfaces.

He described regular handwashing as one of the simplest and most effective ways of preventing infections and curbing the spread of communicable diseases.

The post Abia records 60% drop in maternal mortality — Govt appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: ADC, NDC sponsoring thugs to disrupt our rallies with ‘Bamayi’ chants — APC PCC
description: The spokesperson for the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council, Dele Alake, has accused the opposition African Democratic Congress (ADC) and Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) of sponsoring thugs to disrupt the ruling party’s campaign rallies ahead of the 2027 general election
content:
The spokesperson for the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council, Dele Alake, has accused the opposition African Democratic Congress (ADC) and Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) of sponsoring thugs to disrupt the ruling party’s campaign rallies ahead of the 2027 general election.

Alake made the allegation in a statement on Tuesday, claiming that opposition parties were deploying protests, propaganda and other tactics to create public discontent against President Bola Tinubu and his administration.

The allegation comes amid reported protests and disruptions at some APC campaign events since the party commenced its re-election campaign on October 24, 2026.

At some rallies, protesters have reportedly chanted “Tinubu Must Go”, while others have used the Hausa expression “Ba mayi, ba ma so”, loosely translated as “We are not supporting you”, to express opposition to the ruling party.

Alake alleged that the ADC and NDC had also resorted to deepfakes, artificial intelligence-generated images, fake news and sponsored demonstrations to manipulate public opinion and discredit the President, the APC and the electoral process.

He said the campaign council had warned Nigerians about the alleged plans before the APC’s campaign flag-off in Kaduna.

“Hours before the flag-off of our presidential campaign rally in Kaduna on October 24, 2026, we alerted Nigerians to the plot by opposition elements to create undue tension, sow disharmony, and introduce violence into the campaigns across the country,” he said.

Alake further alleged that the opposition parties sponsored hoodlums to attend APC rallies with weapons and banners, claiming that their activities were intended to create the impression of widespread public dissatisfaction with the Tinubu administration.

He also linked the alleged sponsorship to the attack on President Tinubu’s convoy in Abuja on Friday, describing the incident as part of what he called an anti-democratic strategy by opposition elements.

“The latest instance of this abhorrent and anti-democratic stunt was the desecration of an Abuja Mosque last Friday, where these thugs were mobilised to pelt the presidential motorcade with stones,” he alleged.

The APC spokesman commended security operatives attached to the presidential convoy for exercising restraint during the incident. He also praised Tinubu for directing the police to release those detained over the attack.

Alake expressed further concern over what he described as attacks against APC members and supporters in the South-East, alleging that some had been threatened and labelled saboteurs for refusing to support the NDC presidential candidate, Peter Obi.

He also accused opposition-sponsored agents of destroying APC campaign billboards under the cover of darkness.

Reaffirming the party’s position, Alake said the APC Presidential Campaign Council supported peaceful, credible, free and fair elections and opposed any attempt to restrict political participation across the country.

He called on the ADC and NDC leadership to stop what he described as the recruitment of young Nigerians for dangerous political activities, accusing opposition leaders of exposing their supporters to risks while their own children lived comfortably abroad.

Neither the ADC nor the NDC’s response to the allegations was included in the statement.

The post ADC, NDC sponsoring thugs to disrupt our rallies with ‘Bamayi’ chants — APC PCC appeared first on Very Nigerian.

title: Ogun 2027: PDP, APC clash over Adebutu’s chances
description:
By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta



The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) and the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Ogun State have exchanged words over the 2027 governorship election, following the PDP’s prediction that its candidate, Ladi Adebutu, would win between 18 and 19 of the state’s 20 local gove
content:
By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta

The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) and the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Ogun State have exchanged words over the 2027 governorship election, following the PDP’s prediction that its candidate, Ladi Adebutu, would win between 18 and 19 of the state’s 20 local government areas.

While the PDP expressed confidence in Adebutu’s electoral prospects, the ruling APC dismissed the projection as political fantasy, insisting that the opposition party lacked the structures and grassroots support to secure victory.

The spokesperson for the 2027 PDP Governorship Campaign Council in Ogun State, Wale Adedayo, made the prediction during an interview on Arise Television, monitored on Sunday.

Adedayo, a journalist and former Chairman of Ijebu East Local Government, said Adebutu would defeat the APC candidate, Senator Solomon Adeola, popularly known as Yayi, despite the influence of federal power and the ruling party’s political structures.

He predicted that the PDP would win all six local government areas in Ogun Central, the entire Ogun East Senatorial District and at least two local government areas in Ogun West.

“PDP will clear between 18 to 19 local government areas in Ogun. I can assure you of that. Adebutu will win Ogun East, Adebutu will win the six LGAs of Ogun Central and a minimum of two in Ogun West,” he declared.

He argued that the political support demonstrated by some APC members and attendees at the ruling party’s events would not necessarily translate into votes, expressing confidence that many would eventually support the PDP candidate.

“It is not the noise that makes things happen. When it comes to the real show, those who are following them know the party they will vote for,” he said.

Adedayo attributed the PDP’s anticipated victory partly to what he described as widespread dissatisfaction with the country’s economic situation, claiming that voters would reject the hardship associated with the present administration.

On the possibility of the APC deploying federal influence to retain power in the state, he cited the 2023 governorship election in Ogun and the recent electoral experience in Osun State as examples of how such influence could be resisted.

“The federal might was there in 2023, it didn’t work. Federal might was there in Osun State and it didn’t work, and it won’t work again this time,” he said.

Adebutu’s candidature

Adedayo also commended the judiciary over its intervention in the dispute surrounding Adebutu’s candidature, following a court decision that restored his name to the list of candidates submitted to the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC).

He faulted INEC’s initial removal of Adebutu’s name, arguing that the commission ought to have sought clarification from the PDP, which submitted the party’s membership register.

According to him, the responsibility for determining party membership rests with the political party rather than the electoral commission.

“The PDP submitted the register and not INEC. It is the party that can prove who is a member and who is not a member. It is not INEC. The judgment of the court was very sound. INEC ought to have written to the party that submitted the list rather than removing his name from the list,” he said.

He further maintained that INEC had monitored the PDP governorship primary and recognised Adebutu as its winner, alleging that the controversy surrounding his candidature was politically motivated.

Adedayo claimed that the development was intended to weaken the opposition party and discourage its members ahead of the election.

He, however, said the controversy had not disrupted the party’s campaign activities, adding that Adebutu and his running mate, Hajia Lateefat Sowunmi-Kolapo, had continued visiting communities across the state to canvass support and present their manifesto.

“Those who orchestrated the thing wanted to demoralise members, but Ladi Adebutu continued with his campaign, and that is how he has been going round all villages and towns in Ogun State, meeting with the people.

“It didn’t stop our programme; we have been moving around. Seeing the leaders coming out to campaign boosted the morale of PDP members and supporters. There won’t be any battle in Ogun State,” he said.

On the PDP’s proposed development agenda, Adedayo identified grassroots development and local government autonomy as key priorities of an Adebutu-led administration.

He said the PDP candidate had promised to strengthen local government administration, revive moribund farm settlements, improve food production and provide functional healthcare facilities and potable water in rural communities.

“Ogun State is on a true path for real development because all our health centres must work. The farm settlement must be revived by all means, and their output in terms of food production must increase. There will be potable water in all villages,” he said.

He added that local government autonomy would enable elected council officials to deliver essential services and address challenges facing rural communities.

Adedayo also questioned Adeola’s ancestry, alleging that the APC candidate had not adequately clarified issues surrounding his identity and origin.

APC fires back

However, the APC dismissed the PDP’s projection, describing it as unrealistic and evidence of the opposition party’s alleged disconnect from grassroots political realities.

In a statement, the APC State Publicity Secretary, Comrade Femi Nuberu, challenged Adedayo to concentrate on rebuilding the PDP rather than making what he described as exaggerated electoral predictions.

Nuberu argued that the PDP had been weakened by internal crises, leadership disagreements, defections and the departure of prominent political figures, insisting that the party lacked the organisational capacity to deliver the projected victory.

He cited the defection of former Ogun PDP Chairman, Hon. Sikirullahi Ogundele; former State Publicity Secretary, Akinloye Bankole; and former State Youth Leader, Oyejide Sunkanmi, among other party chieftains, as evidence of the opposition party’s alleged declining fortunes.

He also recalled the defection of six PDP members of the Ogun State House of Assembly in March 2026 and the departure of former PDP Deputy Governorship Candidate, Hon. Adekunle Akinlade.

According to him, the loss of elected representatives, influential leaders and grassroots mobilisers had raised questions about the PDP’s ability to compete effectively across the state.

Nuberu described the PDP as an “empty political shell”, accusing Adedayo of creating false expectations about the opposition party’s electoral strength.

“How can a party that has lost touch with political reality suddenly boast of winning 18 out of 20 local government areas? Is Wale Adedayo merely making these claims to create false hope and mislead a desperate governorship aspirant?

“The PDP is an empty shell, and its spokesperson should stop mistaking political propaganda for genuine electoral strength,” he said.

The APC spokesman also questioned the PDP’s organisational capacity, asking where its structures, leaders and grassroots mobilisers were.

He further accused Adedayo of making the projections for personal political survival, arguing that the PDP’s previous record in government had eroded public confidence in the party.

Nuberu also raised issues surrounding the 2023 governorship election, alleging that the PDP candidate had faced court proceedings over allegations of vote-buying and electoral offences.

He cautioned the opposition party against presenting procedural court orders as final judicial pronouncements on outstanding political and electoral disputes, insisting that ongoing legal matters should be understood within their proper context.

Responding to Adedayo’s dismissal of federal influence, Nuberu maintained that Ogun remained firmly under APC control, declaring that the ruling party had no intention of surrendering its political structures and grassroots strongholds.

He attributed the APC’s confidence to its established political network, grassroots mobilisation and what he described as the achievements of the state government in infrastructure, education, healthcare, economic opportunities and security.

According to him, residents were more interested in sustaining the state’s development trajectory than in what he called the political theatrics of opposition politicians.

The APC spokesman went further to predict that the PDP would struggle to win even a single ward out of the state’s 236 wards.

“From our assessment of the political atmosphere across the state, the PDP will struggle to win even a single ward out of the 236 wards in Ogun State. The 2027 election will expose the true strength of every political party,” he said.

Nuberu urged APC members and supporters to remain united and intensify efforts to strengthen the party’s structures ahead of the 2027 general elections, reaffirming its determination to retain power in the state.

The post Ogun 2027: PDP, APC clash over Adebutu’s chances appeared first on Vanguard News.

The acquisition was carried out through Heirs Energies Limited, a company controlled by the Nigerian businessman. The tr
content:
Tony Elumelu, Chairman of Heirs Holdings, has increased his shareholding in Seplat Energy Plc to 22.05 per cent after purchasing additional shares worth approximately $70 million.

The acquisition was carried out through Heirs Energies Limited, a company controlled by the Nigerian businessman. The transaction involved the purchase of 5,888,341 ordinary shares, representing about one per cent of Seplat Energy.

The development was disclosed to the Nigerian Exchange Limited (NGX) on Tuesday in a notification signed by Edith Onwuchekwa, Seplat Energy’s Director, Legal and Company Secretary.

According to the disclosure, Heirs Energies Limited acquired the additional shares from the company.

Following the transaction, Heirs Energies’ direct shareholding in Seplat Energy increased to 33,832,208 shares, further strengthening Elumelu’s investment in the energy company.

The disclosure added that entities controlled by Elumelu — Heirs Energies Limited and Heirs Holdings Limited — now hold a combined 132,288,341 shares, representing a voting interest of 22.05 per cent of Seplat’s issued share capital of 599,944,561 shares.

The company said the notification was made in compliance with Rule 17.15(c) of the NGX Rulebook 2015 on disclosure of dealings in issuers’ shares and Article 19(3) of the United Kingdom Market Abuse Regulations.

The latest acquisition follows a similar transaction in September, when Elumelu, through Heirs Energies, purchased six million Seplat shares for £53.2 million.

That transaction raised the combined shareholding of Heirs Energies and Heirs Holdings in the company to 21.07 per cent.

Meanwhile, Seplat also disclosed a separate insider transaction involving its Chairman, Udoma Udo Udoma.

The company said Tierce Investments Limited, a firm wholly owned by Udoma, purchased Seplat Energy’s 9.125 per cent Senior Unsecured Notes due March 21, 2030.

The notes had a face value of $370,000, while the cash consideration for the purchase was $397,076.81.

title: ‘Nigerians are angry with APC; Dancing and display of money won’t win Tinubu votes’ — APC Senator admits
description:
The lawmaker representing Kano South Senatorial District, Senator Kawu Suleiman, has warned the All Progressives Congress (APC) that its campaign rallies are doing more harm than good to President Bola Tinubu’s re-election efforts.
Suleiman said the rallies were making Nigerians angry rather than wi
content:
The lawmaker representing Kano South Senatorial District, Senator Kawu Suleiman, has warned the All Progressives Congress (APC) that its campaign rallies are doing more harm than good to President Bola Tinubu’s re-election efforts.

Suleiman said the rallies were making Nigerians angry rather than winning their support, arguing that the dancing, celebrations and public display of money at political events were insensitive at a time when many citizens were struggling with hunger, insecurity and economic hardship.

The senator made the remarks in a statement issued on Monday to APC leaders and members, urging the party to engage in honest self-assessment and reconsider its campaign strategy ahead of the 2027 general election.

This is the second time Suleiman has raised concerns about the party’s campaign approach and its relationship with ordinary voters.

He argued that the APC had become increasingly disconnected from the people, particularly in northern Nigeria, where he said the gap between ordinary citizens and the political class had widened considerably.

According to him, organising rallies centred on celebrations and gatherings of influential politicians would not guarantee electoral support in 2027.

Suleiman urged the party leadership and the Presidential Campaign Council to change direction by taking the government’s policies and ongoing reforms directly to the grassroots.

Rather than concentrating on mobilising political elites, he said the APC should explain how the Tinubu administration’s policies affect farmers, traders, market women and other ordinary Nigerians.

He stressed that the party’s message must reach villages, markets, towns and local government areas, warning that relying on public office holders and influential politicians could prove ineffective because many no longer command the grassroots influence they once enjoyed.

Describing his intervention as a call for self-reflection, humility and grassroots reconnection, the senator said the party must acknowledge that its message had failed to reach many ordinary Nigerians.

He also expressed concern over what he described as a growing disconnect between northern communities and the political elite, insisting that direct engagement with voters was necessary to address the situation.

“Our presidential rally is making Nigerians angry. There is an urgent need to effectively communicate our government’s policies and the ongoing reforms of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu directly to the grassroots,” he said.

title: Two die, Gombe APC chairman, campaign DG injured in crash
description:
By Ben Ngwakwe, Gombe



The Gombe State Chairman of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Mohammed Dantata Ndus, and the Director-General of the party’s 2027 Governorship Campaign Council, Sa’du Hassan, have sustained injuries in a road accident that claimed two lives in Dasan Yunusa community.
content:
By Ben Ngwakwe, Gombe

The Gombe State Chairman of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Mohammed Dantata Ndus, and the Director-General of the party’s 2027 Governorship Campaign Council, Sa’du Hassan, have sustained injuries in a road accident that claimed two lives in Dasan Yunusa community.

The accident occurred on Tuesday along the Deba-Talasse Junction while the two party officials were travelling to join the campaign entourage of Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya in Balanga North Local Government Area of the state.

The APC State Campaign Council confirmed the incident in a statement, identifying the deceased as Haruna and Kabiru, both indigenes of Dasan Yunusa.

It said the two APC chieftains sustained injuries and were receiving medical attention at the Federal Teaching Hospital, Gombe.

Preliminary accounts indicated that the accident occurred when the driver conveying the party officials reportedly swerved to avoid a head-on collision with a motorcycle carrying three persons, which allegedly appeared suddenly at the junction.

The vehicle reportedly veered off the road in the process, resulting in the fatal incident.

Confirming the accident, the Gombe State Sector Commander of the Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC), Samson Kaura, said he had received information about the incident but was awaiting comprehensive details.

Kaura confirmed that the APC chairman and the campaign council’s Director-General were receiving treatment, adding that further information would be provided as investigations progressed.

The campaign council expressed sorrow over the incident and extended its condolences to the bereaved families, the people of Dasan Yunusa and others affected by the tragedy.

Meanwhile, Governor Yahaya, who was leading the APC campaign activities in the area, visited Dasan Yunusa following news of the accident to commiserate with the bereaved families and community leaders.

The governor described the incident as painful and unfortunate, noting that the loss of two lives had cast a shadow over what was intended to be a day of political engagement with the people.

He urged the bereaved families and residents to accept the tragedy as the will of Almighty Allah.

Yahaya prayed for the repose of the souls of the deceased in Aljannatul Firdaus and for strength for their families to bear the loss.

As part of efforts to support those affected, the governor donated N5 million to the families of the deceased and the community leadership.

He also prayed for the speedy recovery of those injured, particularly Ndus and Hassan, who were reported to be stable and responding to medical care.

The governor’s visit and donation followed the fatal accident that disrupted the party’s campaign activities in the area.

The post Two die, Gombe APC chairman, campaign DG injured in crash appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Benue police arrest 26 suspects, recover 495 rounds of ammunition
description:
By Peter Duru, Makurdi



The Benue State Police Command has arrested 26 suspects, recovered 495 rounds of live ammunition and four locally fabricated firearms, and neutralised three suspected bandits in security operations across the state.







The Commissioner of Police, CP Cletus Nwadiogbu, di
content:
By Peter Duru, Makurdi

The Benue State Police Command has arrested 26 suspects, recovered 495 rounds of live ammunition and four locally fabricated firearms, and neutralised three suspected bandits in security operations across the state.

The Commissioner of Police, CP Cletus Nwadiogbu, disclosed this on Tuesday during the command’s monthly press briefing in Makurdi.

He said the operations also led to the recovery of 290 ammunition chains, the rescue of five kidnapped victims, and the recovery of a stolen Toyota Camry and a Honda motorcycle.

Giving details of the operations, Nwadiogbu said operatives of Operation Zenda intercepted a vehicle travelling from Jato-Aka towards Makurdi through Gboko on November 15 and arrested a passenger, Timothy Shawon.

According to him, 290 rounds of 7.62×51mm ammunition and 200 rounds of 7.62×39mm ammunition were allegedly found concealed in the suspect’s bag.

He said further investigation led to the recovery of 290 ammunition chains, adding that the suspect was allegedly linked to the killing of security personnel at Agu Centre in September 2025.

The commissioner also disclosed the arrest of two suspects, Michael Tyonongu and Godwin Agaibge, during a stop-and-search operation along Gbajimgba-Makurdi Road, where a locally fabricated pistol was recovered.

In a separate operation, police arrested Dan Audu at Yagba community and recovered a locally fabricated revolver pistol and one live ammunition.

Nwadiogbu said the suspect confessed to belonging to the Black Scorpion confraternity.

On kidnapping, the police commissioner said five victims were rescued at Utange Village, Katsina-Ala, on November 8, but three died from injuries sustained during the incident, while two survived.

He added that 10 suspects were arrested over the alleged abduction of a commercial driver, Mohammed Musa, a woman and her six-year-old son at Ojinebe-Adoka Village.

According to him, the vehicle in which the victims were last seen was subsequently found burnt, while efforts to locate them were ongoing.

The command also arrested two suspected armed robbers, Saviour Shagbaor and Maakaven Matthew, over an alleged attack on a commercial motorcyclist along the Gboko-North axis.

Another suspect, Tersoo Orjime, was arrested in Makurdi, with a locally made revolver pistol and a knife recovered from him.

Nwadiogbu further disclosed that three suspected bandits were neutralised during separate encounters with security operatives in Ukum Local Government Area.

Items recovered during the operations included locally fabricated firearms, ammunition, cartridges, assorted charms and a stolen Honda motorcycle.

The commissioner also said nine suspects were arrested over the alleged killing of 52-year-old Felix Ahemba in Gboko, while another nine were arrested over the burning of the Traditional Council Hall at Tyem-Imongu community in Vandeikya Local Government Area.

He said the suspects arrested over the burning of the traditional council hall had been charged to court.

In another development, operatives of Operation Zenda arrested Isaac Viashima in Gboko over alleged involvement in a criminal syndicate linked to armed robbery, kidnapping, fraud and ransom-taking.

Nwadiogbu said two military uniforms, a dagger, desert boots and two rounds of ammunition were recovered from the suspect.

Assessing the operations, the commissioner attributed the successes to intelligence-led policing, prompt response to distress calls, sustained patrols and collaboration with other security agencies.

He urged residents to remain vigilant and provide credible information to security agencies, assuring that the command would sustain efforts to tackle criminal activities across the state.

“We remain determined to identify, arrest, and bring offenders to justice, through lawful means,” he said.

title: New Nasarawa police chief warns against extortion
description:
By Edwin Philip, Lafia



The new Commissioner of Police in Nasarawa State, Sheikh Mohammed Danko, has warned officers and personnel against intimidation, extortion, unlawful detention and abuse of police authority.







Danko, who has assumed duty as the 32nd commissioner of police in the state,
content:
By Edwin Philip, Lafia

The new Commissioner of Police in Nasarawa State, Sheikh Mohammed Danko, has warned officers and personnel against intimidation, extortion, unlawful detention and abuse of police authority.

Danko, who has assumed duty as the 32nd commissioner of police in the state, said the police uniform represented a responsibility to serve the public and not a licence to operate above the law.

He replaces Muhammed Shettima Jauro, who has been elevated to the rank of Assistant Inspector-General of Police.

Addressing journalists at the command headquarters in Lafia, Danko said his administration would not tolerate corruption, excessive use of force, harassment or any misuse of police authority.

He said: “Any officer found engaging in misconduct, political partisanship, corruption, or abuse of power will face immediate and appropriate disciplinary and legal actions.”

The commissioner said complaints against police personnel would be treated seriously and thoroughly reviewed through the appropriate channels.

He added that officers found culpable would be held accountable, irrespective of their positions, while personnel who discharged their duties honourably would receive the command’s support.

Danko also cautioned political actors against using their offices or influence to intimidate citizens, provoke violence, obstruct lawful police duties or shield individuals from accountability.

He directed officers to remain professional and non-partisan, warning against political pressure and private interests that could compromise their responsibilities.

On security, the commissioner warned criminal elements involved in kidnapping, armed robbery, drug trafficking, cult-related activities and other violent crimes that the command would respond through intelligence-led and lawful operations.

He also warned individuals providing shelter, weapons, information or other support to criminal networks that they could face the full weight of the law.

Danko called for greater cooperation between the police and residents, urging community leaders, traditional institutions, youth groups and business owners to report suspicious activities through appropriate channels.

He said public cooperation was essential to effective policing and reaffirmed the command’s commitment to protecting residents, enforcing the law impartially and strengthening public confidence across the state.

The commissioner also advised residents against taking the law into their own hands or confronting suspects, warning that such actions could endanger lives and jeopardise investigations.

title: Ebonyi demolishes shop over planning violations
description:
By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki



The Ebonyi State Government has demolished a shop on Ejiofor Street, Abakaliki, over alleged failure to obtain building plan approval and encroachment on designated land.







The demolition was carried out by the Ministry of Capital City and Urban Planning.







Spe
content:
By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki

The Ebonyi State Government has demolished a shop on Ejiofor Street, Abakaliki, over alleged failure to obtain building plan approval and encroachment on designated land.

The demolition was carried out by the Ministry of Capital City and Urban Planning.

Speaking during the exercise, the Commissioner for Capital City and Urban Planning, Richard Ugo Idike, said the property owner commenced construction without obtaining the required building plan approval from the ministry.

Idike explained that building plan approval was mandatory to enable the ministry assess proposed structures, conduct necessary inspections and provide professional guidance to ensure compliance with physical planning standards.

He said securing approval before commencing construction would also allow the ministry to identify potential structural, environmental and planning concerns and advise property owners accordingly.

The commissioner cautioned property owners and developers against unauthorised construction and encroachment on designated lands, warning that the state government would enforce relevant planning regulations against defaulters.

Idike was accompanied during the exercise by the Head of the Town Planning Department, TPL Esther Nwite, other town planners and members of the ministry’s task force.

He urged residents, developers and property owners in Abakaliki to obtain the necessary building plan approval from the ministry before embarking on construction projects.

The commissioner reaffirmed the state government’s commitment to enforcing physical planning regulations and promoting orderly development in the state capital.

title: 2027: Seven former Alia Commissioners dump camp, back PDP’s Aondoakaa
description:
…the only permanent thing in life is change – group leader



By Peter Duru, Makurdi



In a significant political development ahead of the 2027 Benue state governorship election, seven former commissioners who served under Governor Hyacinth Alia have declared their support for the Peoples Democrati
content:
…the only permanent thing in life is change – group leader

By Peter Duru, Makurdi

In a significant political development ahead of the 2027 Benue state governorship election, seven former commissioners who served under Governor Hyacinth Alia have declared their support for the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) governorship candidate, Chief Michael Aondoakaa, SAN, pledging to work towards his emergence as the next governor of the state.

According to a statement by the Director, Media and Communications for the Aondoakaa/Ogbenjuwa Campaign Organization, Dr. Terver Akase, the former commissioners announced their decision during a meeting with Aondoakaa, where they expressed confidence in his leadership experience, professional background and capacity to address the numerous challenges confronting Benue state.

They described the former Attorney-General of the Federation as a leader with the requisite exposure and administrative experience to provide purposeful leadership and reposition the state for sustainable development.

“The group pledged its commitment to mobilising support for Aondoakaa’s governorship ambition and expressed optimism about his ability to address critical issues affecting the state,” the statement said.

Those who declared support for the PDP candidate include Prof. Moses Ogbaji, former Commissioner for Agriculture and Natural Resources; Mr. Aondowase Kunde, former Commissioner for Humanitarian Affairs and Disaster Management; Mr. Martins Shaagee, former Commissioner for Lands, Survey and Solid Minerals; and Mrs. Anna Itodo, former Commissioner for Women Affairs and Social Welfare.

Others were Joyce Luga, former Commissioner for Cooperative, Urban and Rural Development; Mr Omale Omale, former Commissioner for Power, Transport and Renewable Energy; and Matthew Aboh, former Commissioner for Information, Culture and Tourism.

Responding, Aondoakaa expressed profound appreciation to the former commissioners for their decision to identify with his political aspiration, describing their support as “a demonstration of commitment to the collective interest of Benue State.”

He noted that their decision to support his ambition went beyond personal interests, stressing the importance of putting the welfare and future of the state above individual and partisan considerations.

The PDP governorship candidate assured the delegation that his administration, if elected, “will prioritise unity, security and inclusive development, with a clear commitment to bringing the people of Benue together.”

He further outlined his development priorities, which included “tackling insecurity, creating employment opportunities, expanding infrastructure and strengthening critical sectors of the state’s economy and social development.”

Aondoakaa maintained that “rebuilding Benue requires collective responsibility and the active participation of stakeholders across political, social and professional divides.”

He emphasised that “the state’s progress would depend largely on the willingness of its leaders and citizens to put the common good above personal interests and political differences.”

Contacted, leader of the group and former Commissioner for Lands, Survey and Solid Minerals, Martins Shaagee confirmed the development saying “the only permanent thing in life is change.”

The post 2027: Seven former Alia Commissioners dump camp, back PDP’s Aondoakaa appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Tinubu approves Kebbi inland dry port, promises completion of landmark projects, improved security
description: ‎‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru‎‎ABUJA — PRESIDENT Bola Tinubu on Tuesday approved the full operationalisation of the Tsamiya Inland Dry Port in Kebbi, describing the facility as strategic towards boosting the state’s economy.‎‎He also thanked the people of the state for their massive turnout and warm rece
content:
‎
‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru
‎
‎ABUJA — PRESIDENT Bola Tinubu on Tuesday approved the full operationalisation of the Tsamiya Inland Dry Port in Kebbi, describing the facility as strategic towards boosting the state’s economy.
‎
‎He also thanked the people of the state for their massive turnout and warm reception during the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally at the Haliru Abdu Multi Purpose Stadium in Birnin Kebbi. President Tinubu said he would not take their support and confidence for granted.
‎
‎This is as former governors from the state have declared that they would work for President Tinubu’s re-election because he supported the state in times of need.
‎
‎The former governors are Senator Adamu Aleiro, Sai’du Usman Nasamu Dankingari and Minister of Budget and Economic Planning Senator Atiku Bagudu.
‎
‎At the campaign rally, the President reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to complete ongoing landmark infrastructure projects, especially the Illela-Badagry Superhighway, which passes through Kebbi, as well as other federal road networks within Kebbi State.
‎
‎He commended Kebbi State Governor Comrade Dr Nasir Idris for complementing the federal government’s road-construction efforts and promised to expand the state’s agricultural programmes.
‎
‎The President said: “We will expand the existing agricultural programmes. We will support rice mills in Birnin Kebbi, Argungu, Bagudo and Yauri.
‎
‎” We will ensure that the Zuru–Rijau Road is actualised, while the Koko–Dabai road will soon be completed through the Kebbi State Government platform. We will rehabilitate the Goronyo–Argungu irrigation scheme and the Zauro Polder Project so that your farmers can farm year-round.”
‎
‎On Security, President Tinubu pledged to strengthen further the national security architecture and support sub-nationals’ capacity to fight crime by signing the state police bill into law.
‎
‎”We are mindful of the challenges in Zuru, Danko/Wasagu, Sakaba, Bagudo, Arewa, Shanga and some parts of Maiyama. We shall work together to end insecurity.
‎
‎” In the meantime, we have deployed more troops to the state. We have provided more equipment to the military and police. We have approved new operating bases in Zuru, Bagudo and Yauri.
‎
‎”By the grace of God, the days of bandits terrorising our innocent farmers are numbered, as we step up efforts to ensure that no farmer in Kebbi will be afraid to go to his farm again”, the President assured.
‎
‎He further stated his administration’s determination to ensure peaceful elections while thanking APC leadership, supporters, and residents of Birnin Kebbi for their solidarity and impressive turnout.
‎
‎In his remarks, Vice President Kashim Shettima reminded the audience of the support President Tinubu gave to late former President Muhammadu Buhari, enabling him to consolidate and win the 2015 presidential election.
‎He urged the northern voters to reciprocate the gesture.
‎
‎The Vice President told the gathering that President Tinubu sacrificed his resources and comfort to give the North what it wished in 2015. He also thanked the North for giving the President 60.2% of the votes that gave the APC victory in 2023.
‎
‎”The North repaid that kindness, and we are even more grateful that you are prepared to do the same in the coming election in January because you have rejected the lies, the distortions, the half-truths.
‎
‎Earlier, the host Governor, Nasir Idris, commended the President for graciously approving his request to fully operationalise the Kebbi Inland Dry Port and other critical road projects in the state.
‎
‎Gov. Idris assured the President of their support towards his re-election bid as a mark of appreciation for his support for the state’s socio-economic development.
‎
‎The APC National Chairman, Prof. Nentawe Yilwatda, commended some guests’ testimonies on President Tinubu’s commitment to infrastructure development in the country, especially in education, health, and security.
‎
‎He assured the President that the North has resolved to support his re-election in 2027.
‎
‎Senator AbdulAziz Yari, the Director-General of the APC Presidential Campaign Council (PCC), thanked Kebbi residents for the massive turnout and commended the President for his massive investment in the state’s economy.
‎
‎Yari urged Kebbi residents to come out en masse and vote for the President in the forthcoming 2027 Presidential general elections.
‎
‎He said the creation of the Federal Ministry of Livestock Development was deliberate, aimed at addressing farmer-herder clashes in the north and supporting the ongoing construction of the Sokoto-Badagry Superhighway, designed to ease traffic along the corridor in line with the vision of Nigeria’s founding fathers.
‎
‎Yari urged voters to disregard the deceitful voices of the opposition parties.
‎
‎The Kebbi APC Presidential campaign rally was attended by First Lady Senator Oluremi Tinubu, Governors Uba Sani of Kaduna, Dauda Lawal of Zamfara, Mai Mala Buni of Yobe, Babagana Zulum of Borno and Ahmad Aliyu of Sokoto.
‎
‎Others include Speaker of the House of Representatives Tajudeen Abbas; Senators Adams Oshiomhole and Ali Modu Sheriff; Minister of State for Budget and Economic Planning Doris Uzoka-Anite; Minister of Housing Muttaqha Darma; and former governors Ahmed Yerima of Zamfara, Ibrahim Shema of Katsina, and Abdullahi Ganduje.
‎
‎The APC Campaign train has continued to criss-cross the country, engaging party stakeholders and Nigerians across the six geopolitical zones.

title: Tinubu transmits mental health amendment bill to Senate
description:
President Bola Tinubu has transmitted the National Mental Health Amendment Bill, 2026 to the Senate, seeking decriminalisation of attempted suicide and support for survivors.



Senate ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍‍‍‌​‌‌‍​‌​President Godswill Akpabio, who announce
content:
President Bola Tinubu has transmitted the National Mental Health Amendment Bill, 2026 to the Senate, seeking decriminalisation of attempted suicide and support for survivors.

Senate ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍‍‍‌​‌‌‍​‌​President Godswill Akpabio, who announced the transmission during plenary on Tuesday, said that the proposed amendment would address concerns surrounding criminal penalties for attempted suicide.

Akpabio said his earlier comments had excluded persons experiencing mental illness, whose condition could affect their ability to understand their actions when attempting suicide.

“Perhaps, with this amendment, I should make a distinction in my earlier submission.

“I had said that if someone attempts suicide, such a person should ensure that the attempt succeeds. Otherwise, the person would be sent to prison.

“However, I did not include people who are mentally disturbed. I made that distinction because they do not have the mental balance to understand what they are doing.

“I want to thank the president for supporting the decriminalisation of attempted suicide because making it a criminal offence for people who are mentally disturbed would be insensitive,” he said.

Akpabio said the amendment was important, adding that the bill would decriminalise attempted suicide, particularly in cases involving people who were mentally disturbed.

“When I made my earlier submission, I clearly stated that I was referring to people who were mentally sound, not those who were mentally disturbed. Unfortunately, social media reports did not capture that distinction.

“Nevertheless, this is a welcome development. People who are mentally disturbed require our support,” he added.

The senate president, thereafter, referred the bill to the Committee on Rules and Business for further legislative action, urging its consideration as soon as practicable.

title: AFCON qualifier: Guinea-Bissau beat Madagascar 2-0, go three points clear of Eagles
description:
Guinea-Bissau opened a three-point gap over Nigeria at the top of Group L in the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying series after defeating Madagascar 2-0 on Tuesday.
The victory came hours after the Super Eagles were held to a goalless draw by Tanzania in Zanzibar, leaving Nigeria with more work
content:
Guinea-Bissau opened a three-point gap over Nigeria at the top of Group L in the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying series after defeating Madagascar 2-0 on Tuesday.

The victory came hours after the Super Eagles were held to a goalless draw by Tanzania in Zanzibar, leaving Nigeria with more work to do in their bid to qualify for the tournament.

Mama Baldé opened the scoring for Guinea-Bissau in the 32nd minute before Mauro Rodrigues doubled the lead in the 70th minute at the Estádio Nacional 24 de Setembro.

The result moved Guinea-Bissau to 10 points from four matches, while Nigeria remained second with seven points from the same number of games.

Madagascar and Tanzania occupy third and fourth positions, respectively, with two points each.

Nigeria had earlier dominated possession against Tanzania but failed to convert several scoring opportunities, with Tolu Arokodare coming closest when his effort struck the post in the 34th minute.

The Super Eagles also created chances after the break but could not find a breakthrough as the match ended goalless.

Nigeria had beaten Tanzania 3-1 in the first leg at the Godswill Akpabio International Stadium in Uyo, with Alhassan Yusuf opening the scoring before Arokodare netted twice in the second half.

Tanzania have already secured qualification for the 2027 AFCON as co-hosts alongside Kenya and Uganda, leaving Guinea-Bissau, Nigeria and Madagascar to contest the remaining qualification place in Group L.

The next round of fixtures, scheduled for March 24, 2027, will see Guinea-Bissau host Tanzania, while Madagascar face Nigeria.

Nigeria will then host Guinea-Bissau in the final round of matches on March 28, 2027, in what could prove decisive in the race for qualification.

title: NDC accuses Tinubu govt of fiscal mismanagement
description:
The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) Campaign Council has criticised the Federal Government over the cost of servicing the country’s debt, saying interest payments in the first half of 2026 exceeded the government’s total revenue for the period.







The council, in a statement issued on November
content:
The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) Campaign Council has criticised the Federal Government over the cost of servicing the country’s debt, saying interest payments in the first half of 2026 exceeded the government’s total revenue for the period.

The council, in a statement issued on November 16 and signed by its spokesperson, Dr Chiogo Constance Ikokwu, said Nigeria spent N7.7 trillion on debt interest payments between January and June 2026, against total federal revenue of N6.2 trillion.

Citing the World Bank’s 2026 Nigeria Development Update, the council said the figures meant that debt interest payments amounted to 124.19 per cent of the Federal Government’s revenue in the first half of the year.

It described the development as unsustainable, arguing that the rising cost of debt servicing was limiting funds available for infrastructure and other critical sectors.

According to the council, interest payments rose from N5.6 trillion in the first half of 2025 to N7.7 trillion in the corresponding period of 2026, representing 3.1 per cent of the country’s Gross Domestic Product.

It further claimed that capital expenditure fell to N700 billion, representing 0.3 per cent of GDP, from one per cent in the corresponding period of the previous year.

The council said the figures showed that the government was spending significantly more on servicing debt than on infrastructure and other capital projects.

It also faulted the administration of President Bola Tinubu over what it described as the failure of increased revenue collections to translate into improved living conditions for Nigerians.

The statement said federal revenue rose from N3.6 trillion to N6.2 trillion, but argued that the increase had not produced corresponding improvements in public services and infrastructure.

The council also referenced the question raised by the party’s presidential candidate, Peter Obi, over the use of public funds following the removal of the fuel subsidy and increased borrowing.

It said: “Despite the removal of the fuel subsidy and the massive borrowing, where is our money?”

The NDC Campaign Council called for an immediate halt to what it described as reckless domestic borrowing, warning that excessive government borrowing could limit access to credit for private businesses.

It also demanded a comprehensive audit and restructuring plan for the country’s debt, with the aim of reducing debt-servicing costs to sustainable levels.

Other recommendations included reprioritising government spending towards capital projects and human development, as well as redirecting what it described as wasteful overheads to infrastructure, healthcare, education and productive sectors.

Looking ahead to the 2027 general election, the council said the Obi-Kwankwaso ticket would pursue what it described as a programme of productivity, fiscal discipline and sustainable economic growth.

It said the proposed approach would focus on ensuring that public resources were directed towards national development.
