title: Elumelu raises Seplat stake to 22.05%
description:
By Ozumba Chika



Tony Elumelu, Chairman of Heirs Holdings, has increased his stake in Seplat Energy Plc to 22.05 per cent following the acquisition of additional shares valued at approximately $70 million.







The latest purchase, made through Heirs Energies Limited, involved 5,888,341 ordinary
content:
By Ozumba Chika

Tony Elumelu, Chairman of Heirs Holdings, has increased his stake in Seplat Energy Plc to 22.05 per cent following the acquisition of additional shares valued at approximately $70 million.

The latest purchase, made through Heirs Energies Limited, involved 5,888,341 ordinary shares, representing about one per cent of the company.

The transaction was disclosed to the Nigerian Exchange Limited (NGX) on Tuesday in a notification signed by Edith Onwuchekwa, Seplat Energy’s Director, Legal and Company Secretary.

According to the disclosure, Heirs Energies Limited, a company controlled by Elumelu, acquired the shares from the company.

Following the transaction, Heirs Energies’ direct shareholding in Seplat rose to 33,832,208 shares.

The disclosure added that entities controlled by Elumelu — Heirs Energies Limited and Heirs Holdings Limited — now hold a combined 132,288,341 shares, representing a voting interest of 22.05 per cent of Seplat’s issued share capital of 599,944,561 shares.

The company said the notification was made in compliance with Rule 17.15(c) of the NGX Rulebook 2015 on disclosure of dealings in issuers’ shares and Article 19(3) of the United Kingdom Market Abuse Regulations.

The latest acquisition follows a similar transaction in September, when Elumelu, through Heirs Energies, purchased six million Seplat shares for £53.2 million.

That transaction raised the combined shareholding of Heirs Energies and Heirs Holdings in the company to 21.07 per cent.

Meanwhile, Seplat also disclosed a separate insider transaction involving its Chairman, Udoma Udo Udoma.

The company said Tierce Investments Limited, a firm wholly owned by Udoma, purchased Seplat Energy’s 9.125 per cent Senior Unsecured Notes due March 21, 2030.

The notes had a face value of $370,000, while the cash consideration for the purchase was $397,076.81.

title: Senate okays N100.5bn reimbursement for Yobe’s Muhammadu Buhari cargo airport
description:
The Senate has approved a N100.5 billion Promissory Note Programme to reimburse the Yobe State Government for the construction of the Muhammadu Buhari International Cargo Airport in Damaturu.
The approval was granted on Tuesday following the consideration of a report submitted by the Senate Committe
content:
The Senate has approved a N100.5 billion Promissory Note Programme to reimburse the Yobe State Government for the construction of the Muhammadu Buhari International Cargo Airport in Damaturu.

The approval was granted on Tuesday following the consideration of a report submitted by the Senate Committee on Local and Foreign Debts.

The report was presented by the committee’s chairman, Senator Aliyu Wamakko, who represents Sokoto North Senatorial District under the All Progressives Congress (APC).

The committee was directed to verify the total cost of the airport project, estimated at N100,509,017,234.55, following a request from President Bola Tinubu.

The presidential request was referred to the committee on October 13 for review and verification before the Senate’s approval of the reimbursement programme.

Presenting the report, Wamakko said the Yobe State Government embarked on the airport project to address security challenges, improve air connectivity in the North-East and facilitate the evacuation of agricultural produce.

He added that the facility was also designed to support humanitarian operations and stimulate economic activities in Yobe and neighbouring states.

According to him, the airport features a 3.6-kilometre runway equipped with a Category II Instrument Landing System, taxiways and other essential aviation infrastructure.

He said the facility also has an apron capable of accommodating four Boeing 747 aircraft, a terminal building and a cargo shed.

Other facilities, he noted, include an air traffic control tower, fire station, perimeter fencing, navigational aids and aeronautical ground lighting.

Wamakko disclosed that the Yobe State Government formally requested the Federal Government’s takeover of the airport in a letter dated March 12, 2024, in line with aviation policies governing the ownership and operation of international airports across the country.

He said the Federal Executive Council approved the takeover on August 21, subject to verification of the project’s cost and reimbursement to the state government.

The senator explained that the reimbursement would be facilitated through a Promissory Note Programme after the relevant government agencies completed their verification and due-process assessments.

He said the committee confirmed that the N100.5 billion project cost had undergone a technical audit by the Federal Ministry of Aviation, while the Bureau of Public Procurement conducted a due-process review and issued a Certificate of No Objection on February 25.

According to him, the Nigerian Civil Aviation Authority also confirmed that the runway, safety facilities and navigational aids complied with international aviation standards.

The report further indicated that the airport had been completed and was operational, with test flights conducted by the NCAA ahead of its formal takeover by the Federal Government.

With the Senate’s approval, the Federal Government now has the necessary legislative backing to reimburse the Yobe State Government through the Promissory Note Programme.

title: Senate approves six NMDPRA executive directors for reappointment
description:
The Senate has confirmed the reappointment of six Executive Directors of the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority (NMDPRA).
The confirmation followed the consideration and adoption of a report submitted by the Senate Committees on Petroleum Resources (Downstream) and Petr
content:
The Senate has confirmed the reappointment of six Executive Directors of the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority (NMDPRA).

The confirmation followed the consideration and adoption of a report submitted by the Senate Committees on Petroleum Resources (Downstream) and Petroleum Resources (Gas) during plenary on Tuesday.

The report was presented by Senator Suleiman Kawu, representing Kano South Senatorial District.

Among those confirmed for reappointment are Abiodun Adeniji as Executive Director, Finance and Accounts; Ogbugo Ukoha as Executive Director, Distribution Systems, Storage and Retailing Infrastructure; and Dr Mustapha Lamorde as Executive Director, Health, Safety, Environment and Community.

The Senate’s confirmation covers six executive directors of the regulatory agency.

The three nominees approved for new appointments are Mobolaji Musa, Executive Director, Hydrocarbon Processing Plants, Installation and Partnership; Ogechukwu Modie, Executive Director, Economic Regulation and Strategic Planning; and Said Abutalib, Executive Director, Corporate Services and Administration.

The confirmation followed a request by President Bola Tinubu to the Senate to screen and confirm the appointments of the executive directors and the Secretary of the NMDPRA Board.

Tinubu’s request was conveyed in a letter addressed to Senate President Godswill Akpabio and read during plenary last week.

In the letter, the President said the appointments were made pursuant to Section 41, subsections (2) and (3) of the Petroleum Industry Act, 2021.

He urged the Senate to consider and confirm the nominees expeditiously.

Akpabio subsequently referred the request to the Senate Committees on Petroleum Resources (Downstream) and Petroleum Resources (Gas) for legislative consideration and directed them to report back to plenary within one week.

title: Passenger vows never to fly United Nigeria Airlines over early departure – Okonkwo
description:
By Dickson Omobola



Executive Chairman of United Nigeria Airlines, Professor Obiora Okonkwo, has said a passenger sent him a message last week threatening never to fly with the airline again because it departed earlier than its advertised time.



Okonkwo said the passenger complained that while U
content:
By Dickson Omobola

Executive Chairman of United Nigeria Airlines, Professor Obiora Okonkwo, has said a passenger sent him a message last week threatening never to fly with the airline again because it departed earlier than its advertised time.

Okonkwo said the passenger complained that while United Nigeria Airlines advertised an 11:30am departure, it took off at 11:20am.

He spoke during a dialogue on Responsible Business Communication: Building Trust and Financing Investments for Sustainable Human Development at the 2026 World Public Relations Forum, WPRF, in Abuja, where he urged organisations to always tell the truth, saying it was the best reputation management strategy.

He said: “A typical Nigerian traveller has his mind set on the timely departure of the airline, and if anything happens, you have to communicate the truth. You may have an AOG, technical issues, and sometimes that message doesn’t really sink.

“I had a passenger last week who sent me a message saying they will never fly United Nigeria Airlines anymore and I said, why? He said, because they left on time. He said United Nigeria Airlines advertised departure for 11:30am but departed at 11:20am, and as the chairman, I was actually worried about how to respond.

“I wanted to get angry, I wanted to shout back at him. But again, my experience being a member of this forum came into play, and I simply sent him a message saying, ‘I apologise for United Nigeria Airline leaving on time.’ That was my answer. He never got back.”

He also recounted an incident in which UNA diverted to Asaba instead of Abuja, saying the aircraft was scheduled to fly from Lagos to Abuja but landed in Asaba following an error by the dispatcher, who mistakenly entered Asaba as the destination in the flight documentation.

He said the pilots followed the destination indicated in the documents and landed accordingly, while the cabin crew, believing they had arrived in Abuja, welcomed passengers to the Federal Capital Territory.

According to him, the incident itself was not necessarily a major crisis until the airline’s communication team issued an inaccurate explanation.

Okonkwo said the airline’s communication team, in an attempt to protect the company’s reputation, attributed the incident to bad weather in Abuja, despite the fact that the aircraft had landed in Asaba because of an error in its flight documentation.

He, however, maintained that organisations must not confuse reputation protection with withholding or manipulating facts, warning that attempts to conceal the truth could eventually cause greater damage than the original crisis.

He added that telling verified truths demonstrates respect for stakeholders and helps build confidence in an organisation, irrespective of how uncomfortable the information might be.

He said: “The best word of public relations is to tell the truth and challenge responsibly. Whenever the truth is told, it builds trust, it builds confidence, and it also shows respect for stakeholders.

“Communication is not only the responsibility of the corporate affairs department. When there is a crisis and there is a need for proper communication, leadership quality is also called into question. It becomes a collective responsibility of leadership.”

He urged airlines and other service providers to deploy all available communication channels, including airport information displays, information technology platforms and social media, to keep customers informed about operational developments.

He also advocated prompt disclosure of issues affecting flight operations, including industrial actions and safety concerns.

“Do you have a strike? Announce that you have a strike. That’s why we are disrupting our services. Do you have a safety issue? Announce!” he said.

Also speaking, the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, said building public trust sometimes required organisations and government institutions to adhere strictly to communicated timelines, whether they were delivering earlier or later than expected.

He said the passenger’s complaint was a reminder that organisations must explain deviations from what they had communicated, even when such deviations appeared to be positive.

“Sometimes building trust requires that you be on time, not earlier and not later. And if you go earlier than you communicated previously, you must explain,” Oyedele said.

Drawing a parallel with government revenue performance, the minister said some departments under the Ministry of Finance occasionally exceeded their revenue targets without providing explanations.

He said where an agency projected revenue of 10 but generated 12, it was important to establish whether the original target was too conservative or whether the additional revenue was a one-off occurrence.

“I need to know whether your 10 was too conservative. Maybe it should have been 15. I also need to know whether this extra 2 is sustainable or whether it’s one-off,” he said.

The post Passenger vows never to fly United Nigeria Airlines over early departure – Okonkwo appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: 2027: Kalu promises Tinubu 75% votes in South-East
description:
By Ugochukwu Alaribe



UMUAHIA — Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Chief Benjamin Kalu, has assured President Bola Tinubu that the South-East will deliver 75 per cent of its votes to him in the January 16, 2027 presidential election, insisting that the President should not have to neg
content:
By Ugochukwu Alaribe

UMUAHIA — Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Chief Benjamin Kalu, has assured President Bola Tinubu that the South-East will deliver 75 per cent of its votes to him in the January 16, 2027 presidential election, insisting that the President should not have to negotiate for 25 per cent support in the zone.

Kalu gave the assurance during the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally in Abia State, where he said party members were mobilising voters across communities to secure Tinubu’s re-election.

He said the APC was going from house to house and village to village to canvass support for the President, adding that the party was determined to demonstrate its electoral strength in the state.

According to him, Tinubu has attracted several infrastructural interventions and political appointments to the South-East and would do more if re-elected.

Kalu said: “Mr President, the numbers you have in Abia will give you the votes you are looking for. Nobody should convert you to a beggar of 25 per cent.

“We have about 12.3 million voters in Abia State. We have millions of members of APC. We have told ourselves that each person will bring 10 people, 10 voters to vote for you. And that will give us 1,620,000 and more votes for you.

“That is about 75 per cent of the votes registered voters in Abia State. Mr President, let nobody deceive you that he is working to get 25 per cent for you in Abia.”

The Deputy Speaker also disclosed that supporters had assembled 100 branded vehicles for distribution across the state as part of the campaign mobilisation.

He said the January 16 election would provide an opportunity for the people of Abia to demonstrate their appreciation for Tinubu’s interventions.

Kalu dismissed suggestions that the APC lacked a significant presence in Abia, pointing to the turnout at the rally as evidence of the party’s support base.

“We are not sleeping. We are going from house to house. We are going from village to village. We are going from community to community. We are not playing our politics in Abuja,” he said.

The APC governorship candidate in Abia State, Chief Eric Opah, also expressed confidence in the party’s growing support base, assuring that its members were committed to Tinubu’s re-election.

Similarly, party stakeholders from the three senatorial districts — Chief Emeka Stanley of Abia South, Hon. Cosmas Ndukwe of Abia North and Chief Henry Ikoh of Abia Central — pledged their support for the President, citing his administration’s interventions in the South-East.

The Managing Director of the South-East Development Commission (SEDC), Chief Mark Okoye, said Tinubu had demonstrated commitment to the development of the region through the establishment of the commission.

Earlier, the Abia APC Chairman and state coordinator of the presidential campaign, Hon. Chijioke Chukwu, declared that the state was an APC stronghold and pledged that it would deliver 90 per cent of its votes to Tinubu.

Chukwu, however, appealed to the President to appoint a minister from Abia State to the Federal Executive Council following the resignation of former Minister of State for Labour and Employment, Hon. Nkeiruka Onyejeocha.

title: ADC asks court to stop INEC from altering party, candidates’ records
description: The African Democratic Congress has asked the Court of Appeal to restrain the Independent National Electoral Commission from altering its leadership records and the nomination particulars of its presidential and governorship candidates pending the determination of its appeal against the judgment of
content:
The African Democratic Congress has asked the Court of Appeal to restrain the Independent National Electoral Commission from altering its leadership records and the nomination particulars of its presidential and governorship candidates pending the determination of its appeal against the judgment of Justice Peter Lifu of the Federal High Court, Abuja.

The party said it had filed a 17-ground appeal challenging the November 5, 2026 judgment, which it described as fundamentally flawed, arguing that the trial court lacked jurisdiction to entertain the leadership dispute.

In a statement issued on Tuesday by its Director of Strategic Communication, Phrank Shaibu, the party said it was also challenging an earlier ruling that granted Nafiu Bala Gombe leave to amend his originating summons despite an unresolved objection to the court’s jurisdiction.

The ADC maintained that allowing INEC to implement the November 5 judgment before the Court of Appeal determines the issues raised could undermine its appeal and expose its candidates to uncertainty.

It therefore urged the appellate court to preserve the party’s existing leadership and candidate records until the legal dispute is resolved.

Shaibu said the 17 grounds of appeal questioned the jurisdiction of the Federal High Court, Gombe’s standing to institute the action, the assessment of disputed evidence and the orders made against the party.

“The 17 grounds challenge the foundation, findings and orders of Justice Lifu’s judgment. The ADC has asked the Court of Appeal to examine whether the trial court had jurisdiction, whether the claimant had standing, whether disputed evidence was properly assessed, and whether the sweeping orders made against the party can stand in law,” he said.

The party is also challenging the July 24, 2026 ruling in a separate appeal, arguing that the trial court granted Gombe permission to amend his originating summons while deferring its decision on the ADC’s preliminary objection to jurisdiction.

According to the statement, the party contends that the proposed amendment altered the description of the parties and the capacity in which a defendant was sued without prior leave of court.

The appellant’s brief challenging that ruling was settled by Chief J.S. Okutepa, SAN, who leads the ADC’s legal team in the appeal. The party is asking the Court of Appeal to set aside the amendment order and determine the outstanding objection to the trial court’s jurisdiction.

The ADC further argued that Justice Lifu proceeded to deliver judgment on a court process whose validity was already being challenged before the appellate court.

It expressed concern that INEC could act on the judgment before the appeal is determined, potentially creating a situation that would be difficult to reverse even if the appellate court eventually rules in its favour.

“INEC must not make changes that could pre-empt the court’s decision or put the party’s candidates in jeopardy while our applications are pending. We are asking the court to protect the subject of the appeal so that its eventual decision has practical effect,” Shaibu added.

The party said its decision to make the legal challenge public was intended to clarify the issues before the appellate court and assure its members and supporters that it would pursue the matter through lawful judicial processes.

The dispute centres on the leadership of the ADC and the legal validity of the processes through which its leadership records and related party affairs are being contested.

Justice Lifu’s November 5 judgment in the suit instituted by Gombe has thrown the party’s leadership structure and its preparations for the 2027 general elections into fresh legal uncertainty.

The latest appeal comes amid continuing litigation over the ADC’s leadership, with the party insisting that earlier court decisions recognising its leadership transition remain valid and have not been set aside.

The ADC said it would defend the rights of its members, its leadership and the decisions taken by the party, urging that no administrative action be taken on the basis of a contested judgment before the Court of Appeal has considered the issues raised.

The party’s applications and appeals are now before the appellate court for determination.

title: Reps move to protect Nigerians displaced by Gabon demolition
description:
By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja



The House of Representatives has called for urgent intervention to protect thousands of Nigerians, particularly Ilaje fishermen, reportedly displaced after authorities in Gabon demolished their homes and business premises.







The resolution followed the adoption of
content:
By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja

The House of Representatives has called for urgent intervention to protect thousands of Nigerians, particularly Ilaje fishermen, reportedly displaced after authorities in Gabon demolished their homes and business premises.

The resolution followed the adoption of a motion of urgent public importance moved by Rep. Donald Ojogo at plenary on Tuesday.

Presenting the motion, Ojogo expressed concern over the fate of thousands of Nigerians who were reportedly displaced last week following the demolition of their residences along Gabon’s fishing coast.

He said the affected Nigerians, predominantly of Ilaje extraction, had lived and conducted fishing and related businesses in Gabon for decades.

The lawmaker warned that the demolition had left many of them homeless and exposed to health risks and other humanitarian challenges.

He said the situation required urgent diplomatic intervention by the Nigerian Government to prevent further hardship and ensure that the rights and welfare of the affected citizens were protected.

Ojogo maintained that the government had a responsibility to safeguard Nigerians wherever they resided, including those living and working outside the country.

He cited Section 14(2)(b) of the 1999 Constitution, which identifies the security and welfare of the people as the primary purpose of government, as well as the provisions of Chapter II on the Fundamental Objectives and Directive Principles of State Policy.

The lawmaker also drew attention to regional protocols governing the Gulf of Guinea, particularly provisions relating to the protection of marine resources and fishing activities.

The House unanimously adopted the motion through a voice vote, urging the Federal Government to establish the circumstances surrounding the demolition and take necessary steps to protect the welfare and rights of the affected Nigerians.

It subsequently mandated its Committees on Foreign Affairs, Diaspora, Inland Waterways, and Cooperation and Integration in Africa to urgently intervene and investigate the circumstances surrounding the displacement.

The committees are also expected to ascertain the welfare and living conditions of the affected Nigerians, particularly the Ilaje fishermen, and submit their findings to the House within 14 legislative days.

title: Students’ Day: Foundation urges ethical AI use in schools
description:
The First Class Muslim Foundation has called on educational institutions, policymakers, and students across Nigeria and beyond to prioritise value-driven education and ethical technology adoption as the twin pillars of sustainable national development.
The FCMF’s Board of Trustees Chairman, Dr Sulai
content:
The First Class Muslim Foundation has called on educational institutions, policymakers, and students across Nigeria and beyond to prioritise value-driven education and ethical technology adoption as the twin pillars of sustainable national development.

The FCMF’s Board of Trustees Chairman, Dr Sulaiman Ogunmuyiwa, made the call in a statement on Tuesday to mark International Students’ Day.

International Students’ Day is observed annually on November 17.  The day honours student activism, academic freedom, and the multicultural diversity of students around the world.

Ogunmuyiwa said that while artificial intelligence and digital learning tools have expanded access to knowledge, technical proficiency alone is insufficient without a strong foundation of character, critical thinking, and integrity.

“Today, students have more technological power at their fingertips than any generation in history. However, tools like artificial intelligence can either become catalysts for genuine innovation or shortcuts that erode academic honesty.

“True progress requires education that shapes both the mind and the moral compass through equipping young people not just to use technology, but to use it responsibly,” Ogunmuyiwa said.

To advance this vision, he urged education stakeholders to embed practical lessons on digital ethics, data privacy, and intellectual honesty directly into curricula.

These, he said, would ensure students see emerging technologies as aids to original thought rather than substitutes for it.

Alongside ethical technology use, Ogunmuyiwa stressed the need to move away from purely exam-centric instruction toward experiential learning that cultivates problem-solving, civic responsibility, and principled leadership.

According to him, meaningful educational reform must include bridging infrastructure gaps so that students in underserved communities have reliable access to safe, modern learning tools and dedicated mentorship.

He also encouraged student leaders and academic administrators to intentionally foster campus cultures that reward originality, accountability, and service-oriented innovation throughout the academic year.

“Students are not merely passive recipients of the future; they are actively building it right now.

“By grounding their education in timeless values and technological integrity, we empower a generation capable of solving complex societal challenges without compromising their principles,” Ogunmuyiwa said.

The rally, tagged “SoluTinub
content:
By Vincent Ujumadu

AWKA — Anambra State is preparing to host a mega campaign rally in support of President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid, with members of the All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA) and the All Progressives Congress (APC) expected to participate.

The rally, tagged “SoluTinubu 2027”, is scheduled to hold on Thursday, November 19, 2026, at Dr Alex Ekwueme Square, Awka.

According to the state’s Presidential Campaign Council, the event is expected to attract party members from the 326 political wards across Anambra State and demonstrate the level of support for Tinubu’s re-election campaign.

The organisers said the rally was anchored on the mantra of “progressives working together”, a political message being promoted by Governor Chukwuma Soludo.

Preparations for the event are already underway, with Dr Alex Ekwueme Square and its surroundings undergoing decoration ahead of the rally.

The event is also expected to attract prominent political figures from across the South-East and other parts of the country, as supporters are expected to use the gathering to publicly declare their backing for Tinubu ahead of the January 16, 2027 presidential election.

title: 2027: Jonathan, Sambo warn against political violence
description: Former President Goodluck Jonathan and former Vice-President Namadi Sambo have expressed concerns over growing political intolerance ahead of the 2027 general elections, urging political actors to embrace tolerance, respect opposing views and prioritise national unity to avert a possible post-electi
content:
Former President Goodluck Jonathan and former Vice-President Namadi Sambo have expressed concerns over growing political intolerance ahead of the 2027 general elections, urging political actors to embrace tolerance, respect opposing views and prioritise national unity to avert a possible post-election crisis.

Jonathan, founder and chairman of the Goodluck Jonathan Foundation, gave the warning on Tuesday at the 2027 Peace and Security Conference in Abuja, themed “Safeguarding Peace and Strengthening Social Cohesion in a Competitive Political Environment.”

He cautioned that political intolerance, thuggery and ethnic rivalry could undermine national peace and stability.

The former president also raised concerns over conflicting judicial pronouncements, particularly decisions by courts of coordinate jurisdiction, warning that they could undermine public confidence in the judiciary and push citizens towards self-help.

He stated, “As we gradually approach the 2027 general elections, certain developments in our political environment are becoming increasingly worrisome.

“As a former president, I receive calls from Nigerians and friends of our country across the world who express concern about the direction Nigeria is heading. Rather than the confidence and optimism we should be inspiring, there is growing apprehension about the likelihood of crises that may follow the elections. We must not ignore these concerns.

“Among the issues demanding urgent attention is the growing culture of political intolerance. There appears to be an increasing unwillingness among political actors to accommodate opposing views or recognise the legitimate right of others to compete for political power.

“This is compounded by political thuggery, the exploitation of our young people as instruments of violence, and acts of political brigandage. Equally disturbing are controversies surrounding some judicial pronouncements, particularly those involving courts of coordinate jurisdiction.”

Jonathan warned that declining public confidence in the judiciary could lead to citizens taking the law into their own hands, with potentially disastrous consequences for the country’s stability.

Jonathan noted that while the judiciary’s responsibility is to interpret the law and adjudicate disputes, “conflicting decisions on similar matters can undermine public confidence in the institution and create unnecessary tension.”

“We must protect the integrity and independence of our judiciary,” he demanded.

He also cautioned against the use of ethnic sentiments in the 2027 elections, warning that political rivalry could deepen divisions and threaten national unity.

The former President added, “These are precisely the concerns that inform this Conference. We seek to hold a mirror before our political leaders and citizens, encourage reflection and promote a change in conduct that respects our laws, democratic values and shared responsibilities.

“As I observed a few days ago in Lagos, if Nigeria must make meaningful progress, we must review our political recruitment process. Our present system remains vulnerable to ethnic, religious and other primordial considerations, which often prevent competent and credible individuals from emerging as leaders.

“As we approach the 2027 elections, Nigerians will be choosing leaders at both national and subnational levels. We must therefore be deliberate about the quality of people we recruit into public office at both the state and federal levels. The future of our country depends on the choices we make. Leadership is very critical in the growth of any nation

“Let us choose competence over prejudice, service over personal ambition, and national interest over narrow considerations. Our democracy must produce leaders capable of uniting our people and advancing our collective development.”

Earlier in his remarks, Sambo, who is the Chairman of the occasion, urged political leaders to view political differences as opportunities for constructive engagement rather than sources of division.

Sambo called for inclusive governance, responsible leadership and respect for the rule of law, stressing the need to build bridges across ethnic, religious and political differences to strengthen national cohesion.

He stated, “As a nation, we must continually remind ourselves that political differences should be viewed as opportunities for constructive engagement rather than sources of division. Our collective responsibility is to promote tolerance, inclusive governance, responsible political leadership and respect for the rule of law.

“Having had the privilege of serving our country at the highest level of government, I strongly believe that national cohesion must transcend political affiliation and personal interest.

“We must deliberately build bridges across our ethnic, religious and political differences and create an environment where every Nigerian feels valued, protected and represented.”

Sambo expressed optimism that the discussions and recommendations at the conference would strengthen public trust, democratic institutions and national unity, stressing that “Our democracy must be competitive, but our nation must remain united.”

In her remarks, the Executive Director for the Goodluck Jonathan Foundation, Ann Iyonu, warned that insecurity, economic pressures and declining public trust could heighten political tensions ahead of the 2027 elections.

She cited an Afrobarometer survey showing that fewer than four in 10 Nigerians believe the 2027 polls will be free and fair, warning that electoral violence could threaten regional stability.

Political attacks on candidates and supporters of major parties have intensified as Nigeria prepares for the 2027 general elections.

The convoy of President Bola Tinubu, the All Progressives Congress presidential candidate, came under attack on November 13, 2026, shortly after he observed Jumu’ah prayers in Garki, Abuja, with some individuals reportedly throwing stones and other objects at it.

On November 15, 2026, suspected thugs attacked the campaign convoy of Nigeria Democratic Congress vice-presidential candidate, Senator Rabiu Kwankwaso, and its Kano governorship candidate, Aminu Gwarzo, in Bichi Local Government Area, leaving several vehicles damaged and supporters injured.

Earlier in November, the convoy of Nigeria Democratic Congress presidential candidate, Peter Obi, was attacked in Calabar, Cross River State, while some of his supporters were reportedly assaulted at a Lagos town hall meeting last week.

Also, Supporters of African Democratic Congress presidential hopeful, Atiku Abubakar, have also reportedly faced attacks in Edo, Kaduna and Cross River states.

Similarly, African Action Congress presidential candidate, Omoyele Sowore, and his entourage were attacked on October 30, 2026, at a restaurant in Ado-Ekiti, Ekiti State. The Allied Peoples Movement and other parties have also reported attacks on their supporters.

title: Senate Chief Whip escapes death as Boko Haram bombs APC campaign team in Borno
description:
Suspected Boko Haram fighters have reportedly attempted to attack a campaign team of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Kukawa Local Government Area of Borno State, forcing an emergency security response by troops of the Nigerian military.
The Senate Chief Whip, Senator Mohammed Tahir Monguno, w
content:
Suspected Boko Haram fighters have reportedly attempted to attack a campaign team of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Kukawa Local Government Area of Borno State, forcing an emergency security response by troops of the Nigerian military.

The Senate Chief Whip, Senator Mohammed Tahir Monguno, who represents Borno North Senatorial District, reportedly escaped the incident alongside former Borno State Governor, Senator Maina Maaji Lawan, and other APC leaders.

The politicians had travelled to Kukawa on Monday to canvass support for the ruling party ahead of the 2027 general elections.

According to Vanguard, sources in the area said the insurgents fired three mortar bombs towards the community while the APC campaign team was engaging residents.

The explosives were reportedly aimed at disrupting the political gathering and creating panic among residents and members of the entourage.

However, troops operating under the military’s Operation Hadin Kai reportedly moved into action after receiving intelligence about the movement of the insurgents in the area.

Their intervention was said to have prevented the attackers from carrying out their planned operation.

The politicians had travelled from Monguno town to Kukawa as part of their political engagements in Borno State.

The visit came amid heightened security concerns following alleged threats by Boko Haram insurgents to disrupt campaign activities in the area.

Monguno had earlier participated in the official launch of the APC campaign in Monguno town on Sunday alongside Borno State Governor, Babagana Zulum.

The governor reportedly departed Monguno for Maiduguri by helicopter on Monday, while some members of his entourage returned to the state capital by road.

Monguno, Lawan and other APC leaders, however, proceeded to Kukawa to continue their campaign activities and interact with residents ahead of the 2027 elections.

BENIN CITY — The General Overseer of the Redeemed Christian Church of God (RCCG), Pastor Enoch Adeboye, is expected to commission the Enoch and Folu Adeboye Dialysis Centre at the University of Benin Teaching Hospital (UBTH) on Tuesday, November 24, 2026.



The facility, an in
content:
By Olayinka Latona

BENIN CITY — The General Overseer of the Redeemed Christian Church of God (RCCG), Pastor Enoch Adeboye, is expected to commission the Enoch and Folu Adeboye Dialysis Centre at the University of Benin Teaching Hospital (UBTH) on Tuesday, November 24, 2026.

The facility, an intervention by His Love Foundation, the church’s Christian Social Responsibility arm, is aimed at expanding access to kidney care and strengthening dialysis services at the hospital.

According to a statement signed by Pastor Bode Olojede, Pastor-in-Charge of RCCG Region 38, Benin City, the commissioning ceremony will be performed by Edo State Governor, Senator Monday Okpebholo, at the hospital premises.

The centre is expected to provide dialysis services for patients living with kidney disease and requiring regular treatment, while increasing UBTH’s capacity to attend to patients from Edo State and neighbouring communities.

The statement said the project was part of the foundation’s humanitarian interventions, which cover healthcare, education, feeding programmes, social enterprise, environmental architecture, prison impact and rehabilitation.

It added that the foundation’s activities extend across the 36 states of the federation and the Federal Capital Territory, with interventions in 650 local government areas.

According to the statement, the dialysis centre reflects the foundation’s commitment to translating its Christian social responsibility objectives into practical interventions that address healthcare and other social needs.

His Love Foundation was established by the RCCG to support individuals, families and communities through interventions in healthcare, education, social welfare, environmental architecture and rehabilitation.

description:
By Shina Abubakar, Osogbo



An Osun State High Court sitting in Osogbo has ordered a stay of further action relating to the status of the Alagunbelewo of Agunbelewo, Oba Maruf Lawal, pending the determination of proceedings instituted by the monarch.







The court also granted Oba Lawal leave to
content:
By Shina Abubakar, Osogbo

An Osun State High Court sitting in Osogbo has ordered a stay of further action relating to the status of the Alagunbelewo of Agunbelewo, Oba Maruf Lawal, pending the determination of proceedings instituted by the monarch.

The court also granted Oba Lawal leave to commence judicial review proceedings challenging administrative decisions concerning the recognition and status of his traditional stool.

The matter followed a series of administrative correspondences concerning the monarch’s status, including a letter dated November 5, 2026, relating to the recognition of his stool under the Chiefs Law of Osun State.

Oba Lawal subsequently approached the court, seeking judicial review of the decisions and orders to preserve the existing position pending the determination of the case.

The respondents named in the suit include Governor Ademola Adeleke, the Osun State Commissioner for Local Government and Chieftaincy Affairs, the Attorney-General and Commissioner for Justice, and the Ataoja of Osogbo, Oba Jimoh Olanipekun.

In his application, filed through his counsel, Mr Yemi Abiola, the monarch asked the court to examine the administrative decisions contained in letters dated November 5 and 6, 2026, concerning the status of his stool and his position as Community/Traditional Head of Agunbelewo.

He sought orders restraining the respondents from taking further steps concerning the recognition of the stool, the instruments of office and other associated rights and privileges pending the determination of the substantive proceedings.

The applicant also requested that no steps be taken to recognise or install another person to the stool while the case remained before the court.

In his ruling, Justice Michael Awe held that the application succeeded and granted the applicant leave to commence judicial review proceedings.

The judge further ordered a stay of proceedings and actions relating to the subject matter of the suit pending further determination.

Justice Awe said: “Specifically, and in pursuance of Order 41 R. 3 (6) (a) of the Rules of this court, the grant of this application shall operate as a stay of every and all proceedings or action or steps being taken or to be taken by the Respondents as it relates to the subject matter of this suit.”

He directed that the order, alongside the applicant’s application on notice seeking the same reliefs, be served on the respondents.

The case was adjourned until November 26 for hearing.

The court’s ruling was on the application for leave and interim protection pending judicial review; it did not constitute a final determination of the substantive dispute over the monarch’s status.

title: Courts must stop installing candidates rejected at polls -Justice Adefope-Okojie
description:
By Innocent Anaba



Justice Oludotun Adefope-Okojie, has warned Nigerian courts against installing candidates voters rejected through judicial rulings.She noted that “a number of the people in the legislature, not only at federal but at state and local government levels are not the desire of the el
content:
By Innocent Anaba

Justice Oludotun Adefope-Okojie, has warned Nigerian courts against installing candidates voters rejected through judicial rulings.
She noted that “a number of the people in the legislature, not only at federal but at state and local government levels are not the desire of the electorate. They, in consequence, owe the electorate no duty to represent them. This is an aberration.”


Justice Adefope-Okojie, who retired from the bench of the Court of Appeal in 2023, also cautioned political parties to comply with the tenets of justice and to observe their various party constitutions in their selection of candidates, to avoid such cases ending up in court.


Speaking on “Electoral Process in Nigeria: Managing the Boundaries of Judicial Intervention,” at the 2026 GAVEL International Annual Lecture, in Lagos, Justice Adefope-Okojie said: “The credibility of an electoral system depends not only on the conduct of elections but also on the existence of effective mechanisms for resolving disputes arising before, during, and after elections.


“The ideal situation should be that the vote of the people should be decided at the polling unit, rather than the court of law. The contrary is, however, the prevalent situation in this country. The political parties have done immeasurable harm to the polity.
“They seem incapable of abiding by their own party’s Constitution in their selection of the rightful candidates to be fielded in the election, which, contrarily, in a number of instances has boomeranged against them, with the rightfully elected but rejected candidate working for the opposing side in the actual election, out of spite.
“The parties have also taken advantage of the courts’ position of not intervening in the domestic affairs of the party, to commit all manner of atrocities.


“It is the flawed congresses and wrongful substitution of successful candidates by imposition of handpicked ones, and an electoral system challenged by honesty, that led to most of the litigations in the past elections.


“At the actual election were accusations of ballot snatching, vote rigging, vote buying, manipulations and outright falsification of results. The resultant effect is the recourse to the courts for determination of the rightful candidate, a duty which should have been resolved at the polling booth and the rightful declaration by INEC.


“The unfortunate result is that a number of the people in the legislature, not only at federal but at state and local government levels are not the desire of the electorate. They, in consequence, owe the electorate no duty to represent them. This is an aberration.”
Accoring to her, “The simplistic answer to the avoidance or reduction of judicial intervention in electoral matters is for the parties to comply with the tenets of justice and to observe their various party constitutions in their selection of candidates. It is also for the electoral body to abide by its mandate in its impartial conduct of the elections.


“It is also incumbent on the courts to change their posture in their refusal to intervene in intra-party affairs but to come down heavily in deserving cases, in order to stop the manipulations going on in the parties, with their unlawful and unjust substitution of deserving candidates by the imposition of undeserving and unelected ones.


“This, the Supreme Court did in the recent unreported case between PDP v Alhaji Sule Lamido in Appeal No. SC/CV/164/2026 delivered on April 30, 2026, on the issue of justiciability of internal or domestic affairs of a party. The court, in their majority judgment of 3-2, delivered by Stephen Adah JSC, (Tsammani and Abubakar Sadiq Umar JJSC dissenting), while reiterating their position that internal affairs of a party are not justiciable, held that where a political party violates its own constitution and “rubbishes” the Electoral Act and the Constitution, the court must intervene (Emphasis Mine).


“I agree with the majority decision of their Lordships. The courts must no longer refuse to intervene where political parties violate their own constitution and “rubbish” the Electoral Act, as stated in the case above, they must intervene to sanitise the system.
“The duty of the vourts is to ensure that justice is done and not to shut its eyes against its bastardisation by the political parties.
Judicial intervention in electoral disputes is, therefore, indispensable to the preservation of constitutional government, the enforcement of electoral laws, and the protection of citizens’ political rights,” she added.

The post Courts must stop installing candidates rejected at polls -Justice Adefope-Okojie appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Balotelli: From ‘Why always me?’ to talent that never fully delivered — Report
description:
From crashing his Audi R8 to providing the assist for Manchester City’s historic Premier League title-winning goal in 2012, Italian footballer Mario Balotelli has had a career marked by extraordinary talent and repeated off-field controversies.
In a report published on Tuesday, BBC Sport examined th
content:
From crashing his Audi R8 to providing the assist for Manchester City’s historic Premier League title-winning goal in 2012, Italian footballer Mario Balotelli has had a career marked by extraordinary talent and repeated off-field controversies.

In a report published on Tuesday, BBC Sport examined the 36-year-old’s eventful career, which has taken him to 13 clubs across six countries and included an assist for arguably the most famous goal in Premier League history.

The report traced Balotelli’s journey from Italian third-tier side Lumezzane to Inter Milan, Manchester City and several other clubs, highlighting how his disciplinary problems and unpredictable behaviour often overshadowed his footballing achievements.

The Italian footballer first came across Roberto Mancini, the Italian manager, who was hired to manage Inter Milan, during which the club signed Balotelli.

Regarded as his “great mentor,” Balotelli’s relationship with Mancini was likened to that of a father and son.  Under the Italian coach’s tutelage, Balotelli flourished.

The report said, at the age of 17, Balotelli had won the 2007-08 Serie A title with the club and reached the Coppa Italia final. Before then, he scored a brace against Juventus to send Inter into the semi-finals.

Life changed for Balotelli with the arrival of Jose Mourinho in the weeks after that campaign ended.

Following the arrival of the Portuguese manager, there were concerns about likely disagreements and disciplinary action over Balotelli’s attitude.

According to a report by The Guardian in 2009, following Inter’s 1-1 draw against Roma, Mourinho said, “Balotelli? In my opinion, he came close to a zero rating. I didn’t like how he played. He is 19 but could have done much better.”

According to World Soccer in a 2012 publication, the platform quoted Mourinho as saying on CNN, “The most problematic players were funny. Mario was good fun. I could write a book of 200 pages of my two years at Inter with Mario, but the book would not be a drama; it would be a comedy.

“I remember one time we went to play Kazan in the Champions League. In that match, I had all my strikers injured. No Milito, no Eto’o, I was really in trouble, and Mario was the only one.

“Mario got a yellow card in the 42nd minute, so when I went to the dressing room at half-time, I spent about 14 minutes of the 15 available speaking only to Mario.

“I said to him, ‘Mario, I cannot change you; I have no strikers on the bench, so don’t touch anybody and play only with the ball. If we lose the ball, no reaction. If someone provokes you, no reaction; if the referee makes a mistake, no reaction.’ The 46th minute, red card.”

BBC Sport noted that Balotelli still won three Serie A titles and one Champions League with Inter, but his “reputation as a supposed loose cannon was already beginning to overshadow his feats as a player.”

In August 2010, Balotelli joined his former boss at Manchester City.

The report noted that Mancini set out to show that the “unpredictable ways of Balotelli could be harnessed for the team’s good,” aiming to get more out of him than Mourinho could.

“A hardline stance on discipline often appeared to soften when Mancini dealt with Balotelli, who by spring 2011 had garnered a reputation in England as a fantastic footballer who could not stay away from controversy.”

At City, the Italian player was known for many controversies, including a car crash with his Audi R8, throwing a dart at a youth-team player and attempting a backheel trick shot when through on goal during a pre-season friendly against LA Galaxy.

Balotelli was also instrumental in helping City win the FA Cup in 2011, ending their 35-year major trophy drought.

According to the report, after the trick shot against Galaxy, Mancini questioned Balotelli’s mentality, saying: “If you are serious, you can play 90 minutes. If not, you can come and sit by me on the bench.”

Sometimes the audacity paid off – like the famous shoulder goal and subsequent nonchalant celebration against Norwich; on other occasions, not so much, said the report.

In October 2011, the report said firefighters visited Balotelli’s home in Cheshire county, Northwest England, in an emergency service to put out a fire at his home after a firework was reportedly set off in his bathroom.

Days later, Balotelli was back in the spotlight, this time for his performance on the pitch.

This time, Balotelli scored City’s first goal in a 6-1 win over Manchester United.

He raised his jersey over his head, with an inscription on the inner wear that read ‘Why always me?’.

In April 2012, Balotelli was sent off against North London side Arsenal in the league campaign. This, the report stated, “seemed like a season-defining moment” that could end City’s title bid.

However, he later made history, providing the assist for Sergio Aguero’s 93rd-minute winner in City’s 3-2 victory over QPR.

“It was his only Premier League assist that season,” the report noted.

Mario Balotelli scored 30 goals in 80 games for Manchester City

In January 2013, Balotelli’s relationship with Mancini hit rock bottom. They had an argument at the training ground, and  Balotelli consequently left for AC Milan later that month.

“He is not a bad guy, and a fantastic player, but I’m very sorry for him as he continues to lose his talent and his quality. I don’t have any words for his behaviour.

“I hope for him he can understand he is in a bad way for his future,” Mancini said of his former player.

However, “affection remained on both sides, but the relationship had become too fraught.”

One of Balotelli’s teammates at City, Micah Richards, stated that Balotelli was “crazy” and “brilliant.”

“He was crazy in a good way. He was brilliant to have around the squad – a cult hero not just for the nonsense he did off the field but on it as well.

“The best thing about him is he’s a lovely guy – he’s not arrogant, or how the papers try to perceive him; he’s just a bit mad,” Richards, an English right back at City, said.

Another teammate, Nedum Onuoha, noted that while Balotelli’s career might have fallen short of expectations despite his talent, it was still better compared to some others.

“Once upon a time, Mario did genuinely believe he was one of the best players in the world.

“There are lots of stories about him from his time at City, but the one I remember is at our old training ground in Carrington when someone was talking about Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo, and Mario said he was as good as them – and he was deadly serious.

“It obviously hasn’t worked out that way, but he still has done so much more with his career than most players could even dream of,” Onuoha said.

Balotelli was briefly recalled for Italy by his old boss in 2018.

The post Balotelli: From ‘Why always me?’ to talent that never fully delivered — Report appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Making better money decisions in 2027 (2)
description:
By Babajide Komolafe, Economy Editor



In the first part of this article, I said the first financial goal you should set for 2027 is to have a note to record all your income and expenses, if you are not already doing so. Let me explain how to create the note.







The note will contain three colu
content:
By Babajide Komolafe, Economy Editor

In the first part of this article, I said the first financial goal you should set for 2027 is to have a note to record all your income and expenses, if you are not already doing so. Let me explain how to create the note.

The note will contain three columns. The first column is for numbering, the second column will contain the list of expenses, including income, with abbreviations for each of them. The third column will contain what you spent on each item for the day.

Some items on the list will have zero expenses for most of the month (for example, capital projects), because these are not things you spend money on regularly. However, items you spend money on regularly, such as food and transportation, will have figures for each day. At the end of each day, or whenever you spend money, open the note and record what you spent on each item. (See the figure for a sample of the note.)

Thus, at the end of the day, month or year, this note will help you know how much you earned, how much you spent and what you spent it on.

I consider the habit of keeping a daily record of how you spend money the beginning, and perhaps the most important key, to making better money decisions.


First, it makes you more conscious of how you spend money and automatically compels you to be careful and more considerate about what you spend money on. This habit also helps you identify unnecessary spending and, hence, reduce it.


Most importantly, the record helps you know if you are spending more than your income and compels you to find ways to cut down your expenses and/or increase your income.


The second financial goal you need to set to make better money decisions in 2027 is to ensure that you do not spend all your income and that you always save a specific portion of it.


This is very empowering, beyond your imagination. The habit of not spending all your income compels you to focus your money on your most important needs. It gives you the discipline to avoid non-essential spending. When you begin to do this, you will soon realise that a significant amount of your money has been going into things you can really do without.
In this regard, you can decide to always save 5% of your income. When you master this habit, you can increase it to 10%.
(To be continued)

title: 2027: INEC cautions against unofficial election results
description:
The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) says independent election results tabulation must complement, not replace, its statutory collation process ahead of the 2027 general elections.



INEC Chairman, Prof. Joash Amupitan, stated this on Tuesday in Abuja at a stakeholder roundtable org
content:
The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) says independent election results tabulation must complement, not replace, its statutory collation process ahead of the 2027 general elections.

INEC Chairman, Prof. Joash Amupitan, stated this on Tuesday in Abuja at a stakeholder roundtable organised by Yiaga Africa to develop a Code of Conduct for Independent Election Results Tabulation.

Amupitan, represented by the commission’s Director of Information and Communication Technology, Dr Bayo Boyode, said independent tabulation should promote transparency without creating competing centres of authority.

He said the credibility of elections depended not only on voting but also on the accuracy and transparency of vote counting, collation and declaration of results.

“The proposed Code of Conduct represents an opportunity to strengthen electoral transparency, promote responsible information management and reinforce public confidence in the integrity of election outcomes.

“Independent tabulation must not be presented as a substitute for the statutory collation process, nor should unofficial projections or privately aggregated figures be communicated as officially declared election results.

“The Commission’s position is clear: Independent verification should complement electoral accountability, not create competing centres of statutory authority,” he said.

Amupitan said INEC was strengthening the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS), the INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV) and validation checks to improve the traceability of election results.

He, however, noted that technology alone could not guarantee credible elections without sound procedures and responsible conduct by political actors.

He urged participants to develop practical standards around six guiding principles, including methodological integrity, data security and safeguards against artificial intelligence-driven disinformation.

Also speaking, Chairman of Yiaga Africa’s Board, Dr Abdul Hussaini, said the roundtable was organised in response to growing interest in independent citizen-led election results tabulation.

He said differences in methodology and the potential misuse of artificial intelligence could undermine electoral integrity and national security if not properly regulated.

Hussaini said the proposed code would establish common standards for organisations involved in independent tabulation while recognising INEC as the sole statutory authority responsible for declaring election results.

In his keynote address, Chairman of the Editorial Board of ThisDay Newspapers, Mr Oluṣẹgun Adeniyi, called for a voluntary code addressing methodology, sampling, artificial intelligence and election-related violence.

In an address titled “Navigating the Promise, Perils and Politics of Independent Result Tabulation in 2027 Election”, Adeniyi said safeguards were necessary to protect ballot integrity and public confidence.

He urged organisations involved in independent tabulation to disclose their methodologies before election day, clearly label their findings, release results only after INEC’s announcement and verify information before sharing it.

Also, Director-General of the Inter-Party Advisory Council and National Chairman of the National Rescue Movement, Mr Chinedu Obi, said independent tabulation could help rebuild public confidence following concerns over the 2023 elections.

He, however, acknowledged INEC’s statutory authority to announce election results.

Obi expressed concern over election-related violence, citing a report of 126 deaths recorded across the country within 60 days of the general election.

He urged political stakeholders and Nigerians to reject violence and support peaceful elections.

The News Agency of Nigeria reports that representatives of civil society organisations, development partners, the National Broadcasting Commission and political parties attended the roundtable.

The post 2027: INEC cautions against unofficial election results appeared first on Vanguard News.

description:

Adeleke, in a statement sig
content:
Osun State Governor, Ademola Adeleke, the Ooni of Ife, Oba Adeyeye Ogunwusi and the All Progressives Congress in Osun, on Tuesday, congratulated the party’s candidate in the recently held governorship election in the state, Bola Oyebamiji, on the occasion of his birthday.

Adeleke, in a statement signed by his spokesperson, Olawale Rasheed, obtained in Osogbo, the state capital, recognised Oyebamiji’s sincere contributions to the governance of Osun.

The governor noted in particular Oyebamiji’s tenure as Commissioner of Finance, “where his expertise guided the state through turbulent moments,” applauding him as a fine professional who never misses an opportunity to make an impact for the people through service.

He commended the Ikire-born politician for striking a balance between personal aspiration and duty to the state, saying that through political maturity and a profound demonstration of patriotism, the celebrant accepted the verdict of the Osun people and saved the state the needless distraction that comes from litigation.

Similarly, Oba Ogunwusi described Oyebamiji as a distinguished public servant, accomplished administrator and committed stakeholder in the development of Osun State, whose years of service in public office have contributed to the growth of the state and the country at large.

The monarch, in a statement by his media aide, Moses Olafare, acknowledged Oyebamiji’s “wealth of experience in governance, financial management and public administration,” noting that his contributions to public service reflect his commitment to the development of society.

He also expressed hope that “Oyebamiji would continue to deploy his experience, leadership capacity and knowledge towards promoting peace, unity and sustainable development in Osun State and Nigeria.”

The Osun APC, in a statement signed by its spokesperson, Kola Olabisi, described Oyebamiji as a peaceful politician who is “excessively and verifiably loyal to the cause of the progressive party.”

The statement further read, “Asiwaju Munirudeen Bola Oyebamiji, AMBO, has proven to be a blessing to the APC, his family, his hometown in Ikire, the state and the entire nation, as it is on record that he served meritoriously as the Chief Executive Officer/Managing Director of the National Inland Waterways Authority (NIWA) without blemish.

“For someone to have successfully served two governors as a finance commissioner in a complex state like Osun State, the way Oyebamiji diligently served without any record of sharp practices, is an indication that the ‘Birthday Boy’ is a virtuous human being.

“Asiwaju Oyebamiji has proven through conduct to be a tolerant Muslim who has been investing his God-given resources for the advancement of his religion and other faiths, as it is on record that he has built churches for the Christians in his hometown despite the fact that he is a Muslim.”

title: 2027: ‘Prove ADC armed youths against Tinubu’s convoy or withdraw allegation’ – Atiku camp
description:
By Luminous Jannamike



ABUJA – The ADC Presidential Campaign Council has challenged the All Progressives Congress (APC) to produce evidence that the opposition party sponsored youths to attack President Bola Tinubu’s convoy in Abuja or withdraw the allegation.







The Council said the ruling pa
content:
By Luminous Jannamike

ABUJA – The ADC Presidential Campaign Council has challenged the All Progressives Congress (APC) to produce evidence that the opposition party sponsored youths to attack President Bola Tinubu’s convoy in Abuja or withdraw the allegation.

The Council said the ruling party could not accuse its opponents of arming youths and organising violence without identifying the alleged sponsors and providing evidence, questioning why those arrested over the incident were released if the APC had credible information against them.

In a statement by its Director of Strategic Communication, Phrank Shaibu, the Council was reacting to allegations by the APC Presidential Campaign Council, through its spokesperson, Dele Alake, that the ADC and Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) sponsored youths to disrupt campaign rallies and pelt Tinubu’s convoy with stones.

Shaibu challenged the APC to explain what happened to those arrested over the alleged attack, raising questions about conflicting accounts from the Presidency and the ruling party.

“The Presidency earlier denied that the President’s motorcade had been pelted. Now the APC campaign council says people were detained for pelting the convoy with stones and that President Tinubu directed their release. Which account should Nigerians believe?

“If the APC has evidence that the ADC armed or sponsored those people, why were those detained released? Why have the alleged sponsors not been identified and prosecuted? A government with evidence of such a serious offence should hand it to investigators, not fling accusations at its opponents.”

The Council denied sponsoring violence or recruiting young Nigerians to confront political opponents, condemning attacks on campaigners, supporters, places of worship and public property, regardless of political affiliation.

It also challenged the APC to account for reports and images of money allegedly distributed at its campaign events, arguing that the ruling party could not dismiss every expression of public anger as an opposition-sponsored protest.

“Nigerians are entitled to judge this government by the cost of living and by their own daily experience. Calling their anger an opposition plot will not make it disappear,” Shaibu said.

The Council blamed the administration’s policies for worsening the cost of food, fuel and other basic necessities, arguing that campaign inducements would not erase the hardship confronting Nigerians.

It urged the APC to substantiate its allegations or withdraw them, insisting that Nigerians would ultimately judge the Tinubu administration by its performance, not accusations against political opponents.

title: Senate confirms six NMDPRA executive directors
description:
By Henry Umoru



ABUJA — The Senate has confirmed the appointments of six Executive Directors of the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority (NMDPRA).







The confirmation followed the consideration and adoption of a report by the Senate Committees on Petroleum Resources
content:
By Henry Umoru

ABUJA — The Senate has confirmed the appointments of six Executive Directors of the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority (NMDPRA).

The confirmation followed the consideration and adoption of a report by the Senate Committees on Petroleum Resources (Downstream) and Petroleum Resources (Gas), presented by Senator Suleiman Kawu (Kano South), on Tuesday.

Those confirmed for reappointment are Abiodun Adeniji, Executive Director, Finance and Accounts; Ogbugo Ukoha, Executive Director, Distribution Systems, Storage and Retailing Infrastructure; and Dr Mustapha Lamorde, Executive Director, Health, Safety, Environment and Community.

The three nominees approved for new appointments are Mobolaji Musa, Executive Director, Hydrocarbon Processing Plants, Installation and Partnership; Ogechukwu Modie, Executive Director, Economic Regulation and Strategic Planning; and Said Abutalib, Executive Director, Corporate Services and Administration.

The confirmation followed a request by President Bola Tinubu to the Senate to screen and confirm the appointments of the executive directors and the Secretary of the NMDPRA Board.

Tinubu’s request was conveyed in a letter addressed to Senate President Godswill Akpabio and read during plenary last week.

In the letter, the President said the appointments were made pursuant to Section 41, subsections (2) and (3) of the Petroleum Industry Act, 2021.

He urged the Senate to consider and confirm the nominees expeditiously.

Akpabio subsequently referred the request to the Senate Committees on Petroleum Resources (Downstream) and Petroleum Resources (Gas) for legislative consideration and directed them to report back to plenary within one week.

title: Nigeria records 100% pipeline availability for first time in 20 years – NNPC
description:
Stakeholders call for increased investment, deployment of advanced technologies, others
__________________________________________________________________________
From Adanna Nnamani and Francis Onyedikachukwu, Abuja
Nigeria has recorded 100 per cent availability of its major pipelines for the first
content:
Stakeholders call for increased investment, deployment of advanced technologies, others

__________________________________________________________________________

From Adanna Nnamani and Francis Onyedikachukwu, Abuja

Nigeria has recorded 100 per cent availability of its major pipelines for the first time in two decades, the Nigerian National Petroleum Company (NNPC) Limited has said.

The development, according to the company, followed the implementation of an integrated pipeline security framework involving security agencies, pipeline operators and host communities.

The Group Chief Executive Officer of NNPC Limited, Bayo Ojulari, disclosed this at the 2026 Nigeria International Pipelines Technology and Security Conference (NIPITECS 2026) in Abuja.

The two-day event was organised by the Pipelines Professionals Association of Nigeria (PLAN) under the theme: “Financing the Future: Unlocking Capital for Resilient Pipeline Infrastructure in Nigeri.”

Ojulari, who was represented by the Head of NNPC Gas, Audu Ibrahim, said pipeline availability had remained between 95 and 100 per cent over the preceding 18 months, attributing the improvement to the security framework coordinated by the Office of the National Security Adviser, alongside enhanced surveillance and community engagement.

He said the improved security situation had contributed to increased crude oil production, which rose to 1.71 million barrels per day, the highest level recorded in five years.

The NNPC boss also disclosed that recovery across Nigeria’s five crude oil terminals averaged 98 per cent between April 2025 and May 2026, reflecting improved operational efficiency across the country’s oil infrastructure.

According to him, the progress recorded in pipeline security and availability underscores the importance of sustained collaboration among government agencies, industry operators and host communities in protecting critical national energy assets.

On gas infrastructure development, Ojulari said Nigeria’s gas production had reached 7.5 billion standard cubic feet per day, with the government targeting 10 billion standard cubic feet daily by 2027 and 12 billion by 2030.

He said the targets were backed by Nigeria’s estimated 215 trillion cubic feet of gas reserves, the Petroleum Industry Act, the Decade of Gas Framework and the Gas Master Plan.

Ojulari further disclosed that NNPC had signed gas sales and purchase agreements covering 1.29 billion standard cubic feet per day for long-term supply and 750 million standard cubic feet per day for domestic industrial use.

He said the agreements represented more than $20 billion in associated investments, adding that reliable pipeline infrastructure remained critical to translating the country’s gas resources into electricity, industrial development and economic growth.

On major gas transportation projects, he said the 640-kilometre Ajaokuta-Kaduna-Kano (AKK) gas pipeline had reached about 95 per cent completion, with gas delivery to Abuja expected before the end of 2026, followed by Kaduna and Kano.

The 40-inch pipeline, valued at approximately $2.8 billion, is designed to transport up to 2.2 billion standard cubic feet of gas daily to support power generation, fertiliser production and manufacturing.

He also highlighted progress on the 130-kilometre Obiafu-Obrikom-Oben (OB3) gas pipeline, designed to transport up to two billion standard cubic feet of gas daily.

According to him, NNPC completed the technically challenging Niger River crossing on April 3, 2026, using horizontal directional drilling technology, while pre-commissioning was completed in August.

Ojulari said the project would strengthen connectivity across Nigeria’s eastern and western gas networks and improve the country’s overall gas transportation capacity.

He stressed that sustained investment in pipeline infrastructure, technology and security would be essential to achieving Nigeria’s energy ambitions.

Meanwhile, the President of PLAN, Engineer Ngozi Adeleke, called for increased investment, stronger collaboration and the deployment of advanced technology to strengthen the country’s pipeline infrastructure.

Adeleke said pipelines remained the backbone of the energy value chain, connecting producing fields to processing facilities, power plants, industrial centres, export terminals and consumers.

She said the association would continue to promote professionalism, operational excellence, safety, integrity and capacity development across the pipeline industry.

According to her, PLAN would also sustain its advocacy for policies and practices that encourage local and international investment in critical pipeline infrastructure.

She urged operators, financiers, regulators, technology companies, service providers, academia and host communities to work together to develop practical solutions to the sector’s financing, security and operational challenges.

Adeleke said the association would use the conference as a platform to foster partnerships, stimulate innovation and encourage knowledge sharing capable of advancing Nigeria’s pipeline ecosystem.
