title: Tinubu sends bill to Senate to decriminalise attempted suicide
description:
President Bola Tinubu has forwarded the National Mental Health Amendment Bill 2026 to the Senate, seeking to remove criminal penalties for attempted suicide and provide care and support for survivors.
The letter conveying the proposed legislation was read by the President of the Senate, Godswill Akp
content:
President Bola Tinubu has forwarded the National Mental Health Amendment Bill 2026 to the Senate, seeking to remove criminal penalties for attempted suicide and provide care and support for survivors.

The letter conveying the proposed legislation was read by the President of the Senate, Godswill Akpabio, during plenary on Tuesday.

In the letter, Tinubu said the bill sought to amend the National Mental Health Act 2021 by decriminalising attempted suicide and ensuring that people who survive such attempts receive appropriate support.

“Pursuant to Section 58, subsection 2 of the 1999 Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, as amended, I forward herewith the National Mental Health Amendment Bill 2026 for the kind consideration of the Nigerian Senate,” the President said.

He expressed hope that the lawmakers would give the bill expeditious consideration.

The President’s move comes amid a legislative debate over the criminalisation of attempted suicide, following the Senate’s passage of a separate bill on the matter for second reading.

The bill, sponsored by Senator Asuquo Ekpenyong, who represents Cross River South, seeks to replace criminal punishment with medical treatment, rehabilitation and other support measures.

Leading the debate, Ekpenyong argued that Nigeria’s legal framework was inconsistent, noting that while the National Mental Health Act recognises attempted suicide as a psychiatric emergency requiring immediate intervention, the Criminal Code and Penal Code still treat it as an offence.

He warned that criminalising attempted suicide could discourage people experiencing suicidal thoughts from seeking help and make families conceal such incidents for fear of prosecution and social stigma.

Ekpenyong said the proposal raised a fundamental question about whether the state should respond to people who survive suicide attempts with prosecution or protection.

During the earlier debate, Akpabio had opposed the proposed decriminalisation, insisting that people who attempted suicide should face imprisonment if they survived.

“As far as we are concerned, we are saying that suicide is a crime for now. Therefore, if you attempt it, you better succeed. If you don’t succeed, we will send you to prison,” the Senate President had said.

However, reacting to Tinubu’s letter on Tuesday, Akpabio welcomed the proposed amendment, clarifying that his earlier position did not include people experiencing mental health challenges.

“I did not include people who are mentally disturbed because they don’t have a mental balance to know what they are doing,” he said.

He added that punishing people whose actions were influenced by mental health challenges would be insensitive, maintaining that his earlier comments had distinguished between those who were mentally sound and those who were mentally disturbed.

Akpabio subsequently referred the amendment bill to the Senate Committee on Rules and Business for further legislative action.

The post Tinubu sends bill to Senate to decriminalise attempted suicide appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Retired Justice Ogunade celebrates 90th birthday, unveils autobiography
description:
The Anglican Diocese of Lagos West has celebrated the 90th birthday of its Lord Chancellor, Justice Babasola Ogunade (retd.), with a special thanksgiving service and the launch of his autobiography titled God’s Hand in My Life.
The celebration, which attracted eminent bishops of the Anglican Communi
content:
The Anglican Diocese of Lagos West has celebrated the 90th birthday of its Lord Chancellor, Justice Babasola Ogunade (retd.), with a special thanksgiving service and the launch of his autobiography titled God’s Hand in My Life.

The celebration, which attracted eminent bishops of the Anglican Communion, clergy, church officials, family members and well-wishers, was held on Monday, November 16, 2026, at Christ Anglican Church in the Agege area of the state.

The thanksgiving service was presided over by the Bishop of the Diocese of Lagos West, the Rt Rev Dr James Odedeji, who described the nonagenarian as a man of exceptional integrity, diligence and honesty, according to a statement made available to PUNCH Online on Tuesday.

Delivering the sermon, the Bishop of Ibadan North Diocese and Archbishop of the Ibadan Province, Church of Nigeria, the Most Reverend Dr Williams Aladekugbe, who represented the Primate of the Church of Nigeria, said the celebrant’s contributions to the Anglican Communion extended far beyond the Diocese of Lagos West.

He recalled the celebrant’s decade-long service as head of the House of Laity of the Church of Nigeria between 2010 and 2020, describing him as a shining light within the church and a worthy role model for younger generations, the report said in part.

A major highlight of the celebration was the unveiling of Ogunade’s autobiography.

Speaking at the launch, renowned chemical engineering scholar, Prof. Ogunye, described Ogunade as a “community leader and tireless advocate for truth and justice”.

He particularly commended Justice Ogunade’s efforts in providing free legal advice and support to vulnerable members of society over the years.

Reviewing the book, Senior Advocate of Nigeria, Barrister Adebambo Adesanya, who serves as Registrar of the Diocese of Lagos West, praised the former judge’s determination and resilience in pursuing his ambitions despite numerous challenges.

He recounted one of the inspiring stories captured in the autobiography, detailing how Justice Ogunade secured admission for studies abroad but lacked the financial resources to proceed. According to Adesanya, the young Ogunade sought help from an aunt who had just received proceeds from a thrift contribution.
Moved by his determination, she gave him the entire sum and assisted in raising additional funds to support his education.

The experience, he noted, became a defining moment in Justice Ogunade’s life, shaping his values of selflessness, sacrifice and commitment to empowering younger people, the statement read.

Dignitaries at the event included the Chief Judge of Ogun State, Justice Mosunmola Dipeolu; the President of Ogun State Customary Court of Appeal, Justice Adebisi Femi-Segun; and the Pro-Chancellor of Ajayi Crowther University, Oyo, Dr Olutoyin Okeowo, among others.

Born on November 16, 1936, in Ijebu-Igbo, Ogun State, Ogunade obtained his law degree in 1970 and built a distinguished career at both the Bar and the Bench. He later served as a High Court Judge in Ogun State until his retirement.

In 1999, he was appointed the pioneer Chancellor of the Anglican Diocese of Lagos West, a position he continues to hold more than two decades later.

The post Retired Justice Ogunade celebrates 90th birthday, unveils autobiography appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: AfDB approves $102m financing for Nigerian SMEs, farmers
description:
The African Development Bank Group has approved a $102m financing package for Sterling Bank Nigeria Limited to expand access to credit for small and medium-sized enterprises, women and youth-led businesses, and vulnerable farming communities across Nigeria.
The facility is expected to support at lea
content:
The African Development Bank Group has approved a $102m financing package for Sterling Bank Nigeria Limited to expand access to credit for small and medium-sized enterprises, women and youth-led businesses, and vulnerable farming communities across Nigeria.

The facility is expected to support at least 200 businesses, create up to 6,000 jobs and provide financial assistance to more than 5,000 smallholder farmers affected by insecurity, displacement and climate-related challenges.

According to a statement issued by the AfDB on Tuesday, the financing package combines long-term credit, sustainable financing, concessional agricultural loans and trade guarantees to address funding constraints facing Nigerian businesses.

The statement read, “The Board of Directors of the African Development Bank Group has approved a $102m financing package for Sterling Bank Nigeria Limited to expand access to finance for small and medium-sized enterprises, women and youth-led businesses, businesses pursuing sustainable green and social investments, and vulnerable farming communities across Nigeria.”

The bank disclosed that the $102m package comprises a $50m line of credit, a $20m sustainable loan, a $2m concessional loan under its Agri-Food SME Catalytic Financing Mechanism and a $30m Trade Finance Transaction Guarantee.

The $50m credit facility will provide competitively priced long-term financing to businesses operating in priority sectors, including healthcare, education, agriculture, renewable energy and transportation.

At least 30 per cent of the line of credit, equivalent to $15m, will be allocated to eligible women-owned, women-led and youth-owned enterprises.

The $2m concessional component will support vulnerable agricultural communities through the Sterling Affordable Microlending Programme, implemented in collaboration with the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees.

The programme is expected to assist more than 5,000 smallholder farmers and agricultural SMEs in rebuilding their livelihoods and strengthening resilience against economic and environmental shocks.

The $20m sustainable loan will support qualifying green and social projects under Sterling Bank’s Sustainable Financing Framework.

Similarly, the $30m trade finance guarantee is expected to facilitate up to $150m in trade transactions, enabling Nigerian businesses to access new markets and participate in regional and international supply chains.

Commenting on the approval, the AfDB’s Acting Vice President for Regional Development, Integration and Business Delivery and Director General for Nigeria, Abdul Kamara, said, “A vibrant private sector is critical to Nigeria’s economic transformation, but different businesses face different financing challenges. This package reflects the African Development Bank’s understanding that there is no one-size-fits-all solution.

“By combining financing for SMEs, women- and youth-led enterprises, vulnerable farming communities, sustainable investments, and trade, we are helping more Nigerian businesses access the capital they need to grow, create jobs and contribute to economic development. The operation also supports two of the Bank’s Four Cardinal Points: harnessing demographic transformation for economic development and mobilising capital for inclusive and sustainable growth.”

The Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Sterling Bank, Abubakar Suleiman, welcomed the financing arrangement, describing it as an opportunity to strengthen productive businesses.

“Nigeria’s long-term economic growth will depend significantly on our ability to strengthen the productive capacity of local businesses and ensure that financing reaches sectors with the greatest potential to create jobs and improve livelihoods,” Suleiman said.

He explained that the partnership would help address financing gaps affecting SMEs, women entrepreneurs, young business owners and underserved communities.

The latest approval follows two other AfDB financing packages for Nigerian financial institutions earlier in 2026.

These included a $61m package for the Development Bank of Nigeria to support women-led enterprises and a $200m facility for the Bank of Industry to strengthen industrial development and business expansion.

Together, the three financing packages amount to $363m in approved support for Nigerian financial institutions this year.

The post AfDB approves $102m financing for Nigerian SMEs, farmers appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Kebbi APC rally: Tinubu approves dry inland port for Kebbi, seeks support for APC in 2027
description:
Abbas, Yari, Bagudu rally Kebbi electorate, hail APC unity
_______________________________________________________________________
From Romanus Ugwu, Ola Muhammad, Birnin Kebbi
President Bola Tinubu has approved the establishment of a Dry Inland Port in Kebbi State, appealing to the state’s electora
content:
Abbas, Yari, Bagudu rally Kebbi electorate, hail APC unity

_______________________________________________________________________

From Romanus Ugwu, Ola Muhammad, Birnin Kebbi

President Bola Tinubu has approved the establishment of a Dry Inland Port in Kebbi State, appealing to the state’s electorate to vote, from top to bottom, for all the candidates of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in the 2027 general elections.

Tinubu gave the approval on Tuesday during the APC presidential campaign rally held at Haliru Abdu Stadium, Birnin Kebbi, attributing the approval to requests by the Kebbi State government.

He added that his administration remained committed to the peace, stability and development of the state and the North West.

His words: “I understand your request for a dried inland port, and it is approved for Kebbi State. I have listened carefully to the Kebbi Governor, and we are working together. What I want to ask the youths of great Kebbi is: Are you ready to go? Do you have your Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs)?”

The President expressed confidence that the people would support the APC in next year’s elections, urging them to vote for the party’s candidates at all levels.

“I know you are ready to vote for all APC candidates, from top to bottom. May Almighty Allah bless you all,” he said.

While appreciating the people for the massive turnout and warm reception, President Tinubu said that their show of love, prayers and support had deeply touched him.

He acknowledged the economic challenges facing Nigerians, particularly the rising cost of living, but assured them that his administration was working to deliver tangible benefits through its ongoing reforms.

“To our farmers, traders, mothers and hardworking families, I hear you. I know the cost of living remains a burden, and I am determined to see our reforms bring real relief to your homes.

“More affordable food, better incomes for our farmers, jobs for our young people and opportunities for every child. That is my commitment to you,” he said.

Tinubu described the 2027 general election as a defining moment for the country’s future, urging Nigerians to sustain the reforms initiated by his administration.

He said the election would determine whether the country built on the foundations already laid or returned to what he described as policies that had brought Nigeria close to the brink.

“We have confronted difficult problems, dismantled harmful policies and laid the foundations for a more secure and prosperous Nigeria. We have come too far to turn back. There is more work to do, and I am determined to see it through,” he said.

The President also thanked Allah for granting him the opportunity to serve the country in his first term, saying he was seeking the people’s renewed mandate to continue his administration’s programmes.

Speaking earlier, the APC Presidential Campaign Council (PCC) Director-General, Senator Abdulaziz Yari, thanked the people for their impressive turnout, describing it as a strong demonstration of support for Tinubu’s re-election bid.

Yari said: “No previous administration had contributed as much to infrastructure development in northern Nigeria as the Tinubu administration. The establishment of the Ministry of Livestock Development and the proposed Sokoto-Badagry Superhighway are major initiatives expected to promote economic growth in the region.

“I urge Kebbi residents not to be misled by opposition parties. Tinubu is committed to addressing the country’s security challenges,” he said.

Also speaking, former state governor and the senator representing Kebbi Central Senatorial District, Muhammad Adamu Aliero, assured the President that the state would deliver votes for all the APC candidates in the 2027 elections.

Aliero commended Tinubu for visiting the state and pledged the support of Kebbi residents for the party at both national and state levels.

The Director-General of the Kebbi APC Campaign Council, Saidu Dakingari, argued that successive administrations had contributed to the state’s development, while commending Idris for his achievements.

“I urge the electorate to sustain the current administration because abandoning an administration that had initiated development projects could undermine ongoing progress. You cannot leave someone who has started bringing development and go for someone who does not know where to start,” he said.

In his remarks, Senator Abubakar Atiku Bagudu, Minister of Budget and Economic Planning, argued that Kebbi is more united in its support for Tinubu’s re-election than it was during the 2023 general elections.

Bagudu recalled that stakeholders in the state had endorsed Tinubu two years earlier, describing the rally as a reaffirmation of their commitment to his leadership.

He said the President had facilitated infrastructure projects, particularly roads, worth more than N2 trillion in Kebbi within three and a half years.

“We are facing the 2027 election more united than we did in 2023, and this is as a result of your magnanimity and hard work. You have helped us deliver a more prosperous Kebbi,” he said.

Bagudu added that the President’s inclusive leadership and support for the state had strengthened unity among political stakeholders and deepened their commitment to the APC.

Earlier, the Kebbi State Governor, Nasir Idris, assured President Tinubu of Kebbi’s total support and 100 per cent of the votes for the APC in the 2027 general elections.

Idris, who described the massive turnout at the rally as evidence of the people’s confidence in the President’s leadership, said the state had consistently supported the APC and would not disappoint the party in the forthcoming elections.

He said the people of Kebbi were satisfied with the Tinubu administration’s Renewed Hope Agenda and deserved another four years to consolidate its achievements.

The governor commended the Federal Government for supporting farmers, increasing the minimum wage, creating opportunities for youths and investing in roads, schools, hospitals and other critical sectors.

He also acknowledged the contributions of security agencies, including the military, police and other paramilitary organisations, towards protecting lives and property, while pledging continued collaboration with the Federal Government to strengthen security across the state.

Idris said ongoing road construction and other infrastructure projects across Kebbi were evidence of the commitment of APC-led governments to delivering democratic dividends.

He dismissed attempts by some individuals on social media to portray a contrary picture of the rally, saying the massive crowd at the stadium demonstrated the people’s genuine support for Tinubu and the APC.

The Speaker of the House of Representatives, Tajudeen Abbas, also canvassed support for Tinubu and Idris, describing the President as humble and hardworking.

Abbas, who disclosed that he holds a traditional title in Kebbi, said his experience at the National Assembly had exposed him to successive administrations, but maintained that he had not seen a President as responsive to the needs of ordinary Nigerians as Tinubu.

He urged the people to support Idris for another term, arguing that the governor’s leadership was necessary to sustain development in the state.

The post Kebbi APC rally: Tinubu approves dry inland port for Kebbi, seeks support for APC in 2027 appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Troops arrest seven suspects, recover 38 phones in Jos
description:
By Golok Nanmwa



JOS – Troops of Sector One, Operation Enduring Peace (OPEP), have arrested seven suspected criminals and recovered 38 mobile phones and other suspected stolen items during separate operations in Jos North Local Government Area of Plateau State.







The operations, involving tro
content:
By Golok Nanmwa

JOS – Troops of Sector One, Operation Enduring Peace (OPEP), have arrested seven suspected criminals and recovered 38 mobile phones and other suspected stolen items during separate operations in Jos North Local Government Area of Plateau State.

The operations, involving troops deployed in Jos and Naraguta, also led to the recovery of a suspected stolen motorcycle, a toy pistol and a Mercedes-Benz E350 car.

Parading the suspects before journalists, the Media and Information Officer of OPEP, Captain Polycarp Oteh, said the first operation followed a report of phone-snatching at gunpoint on November 6, 2026.

He said the report led troops to Prime House Hotel along Ring Road, Jos, where five suspects were arrested.

Oteh identified them as Tahir Suleiman, 25; Muhammed Ahmed, 25; Muhammed Labaran Haruna, 27; Yahya Yunusa, 20; and Aisha Mohammad, 22.

Items recovered during the operation included 38 mobile phones, 27 phone pouches, three MP3 devices, two earpods, an HP laptop, four smartwatches, a dagger, four power banks and a Mercedes-Benz E350 with registration number Plateau BBK-01NB.

He said the operation was in line with the mandate of the Commander, Operation Enduring Peace, Maj. Gen. W.M. Dangana, to sustain peace and security across Plateau State, particularly during the yuletide season.

The OPEP spokesman further disclosed that troops deployed at Naraguta, working with members of the Vigilante Group of Nigeria (VGN), arrested two additional suspects during a routine patrol.

He identified them as Mudasiru Ishaq, 27, and Hasiya Sani, 22, adding that they were allegedly found in possession of a suspected stolen Boxer motorcycle and a toy pistol.

Oteh said all seven suspects, alongside the recovered items, would be handed over to the Plateau State Police Command for further investigation and possible prosecution.

“These operational successes underscore the commitment of the Commander of Operation Enduring Peace, Maj. Gen. W.M. Dangana, to combating criminal activities while ensuring the safety of lives and property within its Joint Operations Area,” he said.

He reiterated the commander’s directive for sustained intelligence-driven operations and effective collaboration with other security agencies and local vigilante groups to deny criminal elements freedom of action.

Oteh urged members of the public to remain vigilant and provide credible and timely information to security agencies to support ongoing efforts to restore and sustain peace in Plateau State.

title: Kano disburses N5bn to settle pension arrears
description:
Kano State Governor, Abba Kabir Yusuf, has released another N5bn to settle outstanding gratuities and death benefits owed to retired civil servants and families of deceased public servants.
The payment, which is the seventh tranche under the state government’s pension settlement programme, brings th
content:
Kano State Governor, Abba Kabir Yusuf, has released another N5bn to settle outstanding gratuities and death benefits owed to retired civil servants and families of deceased public servants.

The payment, which is the seventh tranche under the state government’s pension settlement programme, brings the total amount committed by the administration towards clearing the liabilities to N37bn.

This was disclosed in a statement signed by the Commissioner for Information and Internal Affairs, Sunusi Bature Dawakin Tofa, on Monday.

Yusuf made the disclosure on Monday during the distribution of the seventh tranche at the Government House, Kano, where he reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to clearing the for inherited pension backlog.

“We inherited substantial unpaid gratuities, retirement benefits and death entitlements that had accumulated over several years. Failing to pay retirees their legitimate entitlements after decades of public service is an injustice that this administration is determined to correct,” the governor said.

He stated that the payments had provided financial relief to thousands of households, eased economic hardship and restored the dignity of retired public servants and families of deceased workers.

“Although some beneficiaries are still awaiting their entitlements, I assure them that the state government will settle all outstanding pension liabilities by April 2027,” Yusuf said.

The governor also commended retired civil servants for their patience, sacrifices and contributions to the development of the state.

“Every eligible beneficiary will receive their outstanding entitlements. We will not abandon those who dedicated their lives to serving Kano State,” he added.

Yusuf praised the Kano State Pension Fund Trustees, the Office of the Head of Civil Service, the Ministry of Finance and the Nigeria Union of Pensioners, led by its President, Comrade Godwin Abumisi, for their contributions to the settlement programme.

He also acknowledged an award presented to him by the Association of Senior Civil Servants of Nigeria in recognition of his administration’s efforts to address pension liabilities. He appreciated the Correspondents’ Association of Nigeria for recognising him as its Friendly Governor of the Year 2026.

The governor further commended the Emir of Kano, Dr Muhammadu Sanusi II, for his continued support for the welfare of senior citizens and the people of the state.

title: US loses measles-free status as cases, deaths mount
description:
The United States has lost its long-held status of having eradicated measles, as declining vaccination rates have seen cases of the deadly and highly contagious virus soar across the country, the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) announced Tuesday.
Mexico and Bolivia have also lost their statu
content:
The United States has lost its long-held status of having eradicated measles, as declining vaccination rates have seen cases of the deadly and highly contagious virus soar across the country, the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) announced Tuesday.

Mexico and Bolivia have also lost their statuses this year, said Jarbas Barbosa, the Washington-based institution’s director, after Canada was similarly downgraded last year due to its persistent outbreak.

The United States has been facing its largest outbreak in over three decades, with over 5,400 cases recorded this year and numerous deaths associated with the disease across the country, including in Pennsylvania, New York and Wisconsin.

The country was first declared measles-free in 2000. The designation of having eliminated measles does not mean there are no cases at all. Rather, it means a country’s sporadic outbreaks end within a year.

Health experts have blamed US President Donald Trump and his health secretary, noted vaccine skeptic Robert F. Kennedy Jr, for fanning distrust in vaccinations.

Of the cases reported this year, almost all of them were in people who had not been vaccinated. At least 12 deaths have been reported since 2025 — when the disease came roaring back — mainly in young children.

“It’s going to be back next year and the year after that. And until we get immunization rates up, it’s going to continue to be back,” Paul Offit, an American pediatrician specializing in infectious diseases, told AFP ahead of the PAHO’s official announcement.

The virus has also spread to Mexico and Guatemala, where it has caused 23 and 53 deaths, respectively, since early 2026, according to PAHO data.

Measles causes fever, respiratory symptoms and a rash, and in some cases more serious complications such as pneumonia and brain inflammation, which can lead to severe long-term health problems or even death.

The virus is transmitted through the air and is extremely contagious, remaining airborne for up to two hours after an infected person has left the area.

To curb its spread, experts say that the vaccination rate must hit at least 95 percent of the population. However, in the United States, the vaccination rate among young children was below 93 percent in 2025, with much lower rates in some local areas, especially among some conservative religious communities.

Several of the deaths in Pennsylvania, and one death in New York, have reportedly occurred among the Amish community.

Before the vaccine was developed in the early 1960s, measles killed hundreds of children each year across the US. It continues to claim tens of thousands of lives worldwide.

AFP

title: Ododo inaugurates Kogi APC presidential campaign council
description:
Kogi State Governor, Usman Ododo, has inaugurated the Kogi State All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council, appointing himself chairman and former Senator Smart Adeyemi as Director-General ahead of the 2027 general elections.
The inauguration was held on Tuesday at the Government House
content:
Kogi State Governor, Usman Ododo, has inaugurated the Kogi State All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council, appointing himself chairman and former Senator Smart Adeyemi as Director-General ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The inauguration was held on Tuesday at the Government House, Lokoja, according to a statement by the state Commissioner for Information, Kingsley Femi Fanwo.

The statement said former Governor Yahaya Bello, former Governor Captain Idris Wada, former Deputy Governor Yomi Awoniyi and Chief Edward Onoja were named as campaign patrons.

“Governor Ododo charged members of the council to place party unity above personal interests, describing collective responsibility, grassroots mobilisation and effective coordination as critical to the task ahead.

“He said the APC must engage Nigerians with its record of achievements and vision for the future rather than political rhetoric, urging members to take the campaign message across the three senatorial districts, 21 local government areas, 239 wards and 3,508 polling units in Kogi State,” the statement said.

The governor also highlighted President Bola Tinubu’s support for Kogi’s development, citing the approval of the Kogi International Airport, improved federal revenue allocations and other infrastructure initiatives as significant opportunities for the state.

He listed ongoing projects and interventions in education, healthcare, roads, agriculture, security and youth empowerment as areas where his administration was translating available resources into tangible benefits for residents.

“Ododo maintained that the relationship between the Federal Government and Kogi State had opened new development opportunities, stressing that another four years of collaboration could further expand infrastructure, investment, healthcare, education and economic opportunities,” the statement said.

In his remarks, the Director-General, Adeyemi, commended the governor’s leadership and highlighted the Tinubu administration’s appointments of Kogi indigenes to important national positions, including ministerial and strategic institutional offices.

Adeyemi also referenced the ongoing Kogi International Airport project, recalling how critics had previously questioned his appointment as Chairman of the Senate Committee on Aviation because the state had no airport.

Other key appointments include Deputy Governor Joel Oyibo Salifu and Aliyu Ezzu Momoh as vice-chairmen; Ali Bello as council coordinator, with Hilary Ojomah Egwudah as deputy; and Kingsley Femi Fanwo as coordinating director, strategic communication.

Majeed Dahiru was named state presidential campaign spokesman, while Abdulaziz Idris King, Suberu Adagu, Aliyu Umar Yusuf, Yakubu Yusuf Okala and Commander Jerry Omodara (retd.) were assigned responsibilities for election planning, administration, stakeholder mobilisation, logistics and security, respectively.

“Governor Ododo congratulated the appointees and charged them to demonstrate commitment, discipline and integrity, stressing that the council’s success would be measured by effective grassroots engagement and a united party structure across the state,” the statement said.

title: Nigeria establishes direct flights to Ireland
description:
From Isaac Anumihe, Abuja
As part of efforts to strengthen bilateral relations, trade, tourism and people-to-people connectivity between Nigeria and Ireland, the Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, has established direct flight operations between both countries.
The minist
content:
From Isaac Anumihe, Abuja

As part of efforts to strengthen bilateral relations, trade, tourism and people-to-people connectivity between Nigeria and Ireland, the Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, has established direct flight operations between both countries.

The minister made this known when he received the Irish Ambassador to Nigeria, Ms Lesley Ní Bhriain, who paid him a courtesy visit to discuss areas of mutual interest and opportunities for enhanced co-operation in the aviation sector.

During the meeting, Ambassador Ní Bhriain identified improved visa services as a critical requirement for expanding bilateral engagements, particularly in aviation, trade and tourism. She disclosed that since assuming office in September, she had recognised the need to improve Ireland’s visa processing capacity and had engaged her Ministry of Justice on the deployment of additional personnel to visa offices.

The ambassador explained that improving visa services would be essential to facilitating discussions around direct flights, business partnerships and other areas of co-operation between Nigeria and Ireland.

Responding, the minister welcomed the ambassador and commended her decision to make aviation one of the priority areas of her diplomatic engagement with Nigeria.

He described the relationship between both countries as longstanding and mutually beneficial, noting that Dublin occupies a strategic position in the global aviation industry, particularly as a major centre for aircraft leasing and aviation finance.

In a statement, the minister recalled Nigeria’s longstanding participation in the annual Airline Economics Conference in Dublin, where global aircraft lessors and key aviation stakeholders converge to explore business opportunities and negotiate industry partnerships.

He also acknowledged the support and co-operation extended to Nigeria by the ambassador’s predecessor, particularly in facilitating Nigeria’s participation in the Ireland-Africa Summit in April 2025.

Keyamo noted that Nigeria’s signing and implementation of the Cape Town Convention had significantly improved the country’s standing in the global aircraft leasing market, creating fresh opportunities for engagement with international lessors.

He specifically highlighted the growing relationship with AerCap, one of the world’s leading aircraft leasing companies, which has supported Nigeria’s efforts in establishing an aircraft leasing company and facilitating access to dry-lease arrangements for domestic airlines.

On the possibility of direct flights between Nigeria and Ireland, the minister expressed strong interest, observing that the growing Nigerian community in Ireland, coupled with increasing movements for education, tourism, business and family engagements, makes direct air connectivity increasingly necessary.

He proposed that both countries establish a technical team to examine the existing Bilateral Air Services Agreement (BASA), determine whether it requires updating and identify opportunities for Nigerian and Irish airlines to commence direct flight operations, even if initially on a limited weekly schedule.

To ensure that the discussions translate into concrete action, the minister immediately set up a team to follow up engagements with the relevant directors and technical officials of the ministry and to work with the Irish Embassy on the proposed BASA review and connectivity arrangements.

Explaining the importance of the approach, Keyamo said that diplomatic engagements must be backed by structured follow-up mechanisms to ensure that agreements and discussions produce measurable results.

The minister further welcomed the ambassador’s disclosure that Ireland was preparing for another Africa Trade Horizons Conference in the last week of June 2027, assuring her of Nigeria’s interest in sustaining participation in initiatives that promote trade and investment between both countries.

In her remarks, Ambassador Ní Bhriain disclosed that the Irish Government had recently hosted a Doing Business in Sub-Saharan Africa Summit, which attracted about 200 Irish companies interested in exploring business opportunities across the continent.

She emphasised that improved air connectivity would be fundamental to unlocking these opportunities, noting that while digital technology had transformed business engagements, physical interaction and direct access to markets remained indispensable.

Both parties expressed optimism that the engagement would open a new chapter in Nigeria-Ireland aviation relations, with improved visa services, a possible review of the BASA and the establishment of direct air links identified as immediate areas for collaboration.

title: ADC to INEC: Don’t tamper with our leadership, candidates
description:
…files 17 grounds of appeal against Lifu’s judgment



By Luminous Jannamike



ABUJA – The African Democratic Congress (ADC) has asked the Court of Appeal to restrain the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) from altering its leadership records and the nomination particulars of its pres
content:
…files 17 grounds of appeal against Lifu’s judgment

By Luminous Jannamike

ABUJA – The African Democratic Congress (ADC) has asked the Court of Appeal to restrain the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) from altering its leadership records and the nomination particulars of its presidential and governorship candidates pending the determination of its challenge to a judgment by Justice Peter Lifu of the Federal High Court, Abuja.

The party is seeking to stop INEC from implementing a judgment it considers legally defective, arguing that any changes to its leadership records or candidates’ particulars before the appeal is decided could undermine the outcome of the proceedings and jeopardise its preparations for the 2027 elections.

In a statement by the Director of Strategic Communication of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, Phrank Shaibu, the party said its 17-ground Notice of Appeal challenged the trial court’s jurisdiction to entertain what it described as an internal party leadership dispute.

It also questioned the treatment of an earlier Federal High Court judgment delivered on July 2, 2026, concerning its leadership transition, which it maintained remained valid and had not been set aside.

“The 17 grounds challenge the foundation, findings and orders of Justice Lifu’s judgment. The ADC has asked the Court of Appeal to examine whether the trial court had jurisdiction, whether the claimant had standing, whether disputed evidence was properly assessed, and whether the sweeping orders made against the party can stand in law,” Shaibu said.

Beyond the substantive appeal, the ADC is separately challenging a July 24, 2026, ruling which granted Hon. Nafiu Bala Gombe leave to amend his originating summons despite the party’s pending preliminary objection to the trial court’s jurisdiction.

In its appellant’s brief, the party argued that the court ought to have determined the jurisdictional objection before considering Gombe’s application to amend the suit.

It further contended that the proposed amendment altered the description of parties and the capacity in which a defendant was sued without prior leave of court.

The brief, settled by Chief J.S. Okutepa, SAN, the ADC’s lead counsel in the appeal against the amendment ruling, seeks to set aside the order and have the outstanding jurisdictional objection considered.

The ADC also argued that Justice Lifu proceeded to judgment on the basis of an amended court process that was already the subject of an appeal, before the appellate court had determined whether the amendment was properly granted.

The party warned that allowing INEC to act on the November 5 judgment before the appeal is resolved could create changes that would be difficult to reverse, even if the ADC eventually succeeds.

“These are serious questions before the Court of Appeal. INEC must not make changes that could preempt the court’s decision or put the party’s candidates in jeopardy while our applications are pending. We are asking the court to protect the subject of the appeal so that its eventual decision has practical effect,” Shaibu said.

The ADC said it was making the legal challenge public to clarify the issues before the appellate court, insisting that it would defend its leadership and the decisions of its members through lawful means.

The post ADC to INEC: Don’t tamper with our leadership, candidates appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Ukraine Missile Strike Severs Russia’s Crimean Bridge
description: A section of the bridge connecting Russia to the annexed Crimean peninsula appeared to be lying in rubble in the water on Tuesday after Ukraine hit the road-and-rail link with missiles in a brazen overnight attack.Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky hailed the strike as “unprecedented&rdquo
content:
A section of the bridge connecting Russia to the annexed Crimean peninsula appeared to be lying in rubble in the water on Tuesday after Ukraine hit the road-and-rail link with missiles in a brazen overnight attack.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky hailed the strike as “unprecedented” and a justified retaliation for Russia’s barrages of its infrastructure in the almost five years since Moscow invaded.

Road traffic was completely halted, with Russian-installed officials on the peninsula urging locals not to panic and saying the delivery of food and essentials would not be affected.

Moscow also launched attacks on key Ukrainian bridges, firing ballistic missiles at two major river crossings in Kyiv.

AFP reporters saw crater-like holes on Kyiv’s Northern Bridge and people crossing on foot during the morning rush hour.

“It’s cold, raining, just a total mess. It feels like I’m in some kind of movie… This is hardcore for Ukrainians,” Veronika Roshchenko, a 20-year-old jewellery workshop employee said.

The wave of attacks comes ahead of a historic meeting of the Chinese, US and Russian leaders, and could disrupt Russian President Vladimir Putin’s attempts to cast the meeting as a new Yalta: an image of unassailable world leaders dividing up spheres of influence.

Zelensky had warned of a major Russian attack in the days leading up to Thursday’s meeting in China’s Shenzhen, when Putin meets Presidents Xi Jinping and Donald Trump.

“We have repeatedly offered Russia steps toward de-escalation — and every proposal has been met with loud rejection,” Zelensky said on social media, posting footage of a Ukrainian missile approaching the bridge in the dark of night.

“We are also reminding Russia that war will always return to where it began,” he said.

Russia annexed Crimea in 2014, one of the opening moves in what became a deadly war between Kyiv and Russian-backed separatists in the east of the country.

Ukraine’s SBU security service said one of the bridge’s metal arches “and the road span beneath it have been completely destroyed”.

“The central arch and spans have collapsed, and the rail section has suffered critical damage,” Kyiv’s defence ministry added.

Images published by the SBU showed piles of concrete rubble lying on the base — the bridge broken in two parts with a clean gap, several dozen metres wide, in the middle.

The Kremlin said the bridge — a symbol of Putin’s rule and Russia’s annexation of Crimea — would be “restored and will be even better than before”.

The Russian transport ministry said that railway traffic across the bridge has been resumed “on one track” and that repair work was underway “on the second section”.

Russia’s defence ministry said it downed 1,441 Ukrainian drones in a major overnight barrage — the second-highest one-day figure this year.

Two people were killed in Crimea in the attack, the Russian-installed governor said.

Strikes On Ukraine

The strike on the bridge comes as Russia’s attacks on Ukrainian infrastructure intensified with the onset of winter.

AFP reporters in Kyiv heard waves of attacks as Russia fired missiles and drones at the city overnight.

Both the Northern and Southern bridges in the capital — key bridges across the Dnipro river that form part of the city’s ring road — were hit.

Traffic was suspended, causing gridlock on Tuesday morning.

Russia’s army confirmed it had hit both bridges.

Kyiv’s Mayor Vitali Klitschko posted a video from the Northern Bridge showing debris strewn across the road. He later said traffic was partially resumed through the Southern Bridge.

The strikes on Kyiv also disrupted heating and water in parts of the capital, he said.

New Yalta

The wave of strikes comes as the United States renews its push for an end to the war.

But diplomatic efforts have so far failed to reach a breakthrough, with fighting grinding into another winter.

Moscow wants a sweeping deal to rewrite “Europe’s security architecture” as part of any agreement to halt the fighting.

Russia has previously demanded curbs on NATO’s presence in central and eastern Europe and restrictions on the deployment of foreign troops and hardware to Ukraine.

Kyiv and Europe are resisting any attempts to overhaul the continent’s post-Cold War defence, calling for a ceasefire in the Ukraine war before any discussion of terms.

Zelensky has raised alarm that the Shenzhen meeting could be a Yalta-like “redistribution of spheres of influence” for the 21st century.

The 1945 Yalta summit — held in Crimea, then part of the Soviet Union — saw US president Franklin D. Roosevelt, Britain’s Winston Churchill and Soviet leader Joseph Stalin carve up new post-WWII territorial boundaries.

title: APC accuses ADC, NDC of sponsoring violence at rallies
description: The All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council has accused opposition parties, the African Democratic Congress (ADC) and Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), of allegedly sponsoring violence and orchestrating protests at its campaign rallies ahead of the 2027 general elections.
content:
The All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council has accused opposition parties, the African Democratic Congress (ADC) and Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), of allegedly sponsoring violence and orchestrating protests at its campaign rallies ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The council also alleged that the opposition parties were using artificial intelligence-generated images, deepfakes, fake news and other propaganda techniques to manipulate public opinion against President Bola Tinubu and the APC.

The allegations were contained in a statement issued on Tuesday by the council’s spokesperson, Dele Alake.

The council recalled that ahead of the flag-off of its presidential campaign rally in Kaduna on October 24, it had warned Nigerians about what it described as plans by opposition elements to create tension, promote disharmony and introduce violence into political campaigns.

It alleged that the ADC and NDC had devised strategies involving sponsored protests and misinformation to portray widespread public discontent against the Tinubu administration.

The APC campaign council further alleged that opposition elements were mobilising young Nigerians to disrupt its rallies by chanting ‘Bamaiyi’ and carrying banners.

It cited an incident at a mosque in Abuja last Friday, alleging that some protesters threw stones at the presidential motorcade.

The council commended security personnel attached to the presidential convoy for exercising restraint during the incident.

It also praised Tinubu for directing the Abuja Police Command to release those detained in connection with the incident.

The statement further expressed concern over alleged attacks and threats against some APC members and supporters in the South-East, claiming that they were being labelled saboteurs for not supporting the NDC presidential candidate, Peter Obi.

It also alleged that APC campaign billboards were being destroyed by individuals sponsored by opposition elements.

The council described the alleged incidents as unacceptable, insisting that the country’s democratic space should remain open to all political parties and candidates.

Reaffirming its position on peaceful political campaigns, the APC campaign council said it supported credible, free and fair elections across the country.

It urged leaders of the ADC and NDC to desist from allegedly mobilising young Nigerians for activities that could expose them to danger.

The council also called on political parties to conduct their campaigns peacefully and allow Nigerians to freely support candidates of their choice.

title: Zamfara: Suspected bandits kill guard, abduct family members in fresh attack
description:
By Philip Nwosu
Gunmen suspected to be bandits have killed a security guard and abducted several members of a family and their visitor during an attack on the residence of a businessman, Alhaji Babangida Sama’ila, in Sabuwar Kaura, Kaura Namoda Local Government Area of Zamfara State.
The attack, whi
content:
By Philip Nwosu

Gunmen suspected to be bandits have killed a security guard and abducted several members of a family and their visitor during an attack on the residence of a businessman, Alhaji Babangida Sama’ila, in Sabuwar Kaura, Kaura Namoda Local Government Area of Zamfara State.

The attack, which reportedly lasted about an hour on Monday, came barely 24 hours after gunmen killed seven worshippers, including a senior aide to Governor Dauda Lawal, during an attack on a mosque in the same community.

The latest incident has heightened tension in Kaura Namoda, where residents have expressed growing concern over the worsening security situation and the apparent freedom with which armed groups operate.

A resident of Sabuwar Kaura, who spoke on the incident, said the attackers initially abducted three girls, their mother, two boys and a visitor to the family.

The mother was subsequently released, while the other abductees remained in captivity as of Monday.

The resident said three of the girls were minors, aged between 14 and 16, while the abducted visitor was also between 15 and 16 years old.

“They are my neighbours. The children are between 14 and 16 years old. One of those abducted was a visitor to the family and is also between 15 and 16,” he said.

According to the resident, the gunmen killed the security guard when he attempted to prevent them from gaining access to the residence.

He said the attackers subsequently used a makeshift structure to climb over the fence, while Sama’ila and one of his sons escaped by jumping over it.

The resident expressed concern that the attackers operated for about an hour without immediate intervention from security personnel, despite the residence being close to the General Hospital, Kaura Namoda.

He alleged that warning shots fired by soldiers stationed at the residence of the Rector of the Federal Polytechnic, Kaura Namoda, alongside local vigilantes, might have disrupted the attackers’ operation.

He also identified nearby settlements, including Gidan Sambo, Unguwar Sarkin Musulmi and Madira, as possible routes through which the bandits could have accessed the town.

The resident further alleged that some communities around Kaura Namoda had entered into reconciliation arrangements with bandits, warning that such agreements could create additional security risks.

He claimed that Unguwar Sarkin Musulmi was less than a kilometre from the camp of a notorious bandit leader identified as Dan Sadiya.

Another resident expressed suspicion that some bandits might be secretly living within the town, making it difficult for security agencies to identify and monitor their movements.

Death toll from mosque attack rises to seven

Meanwhile, the death toll from Sunday’s attack on worshippers at a mosque in the Sabuwar Kaura Low-Cost area of Kaura Namoda has risen to seven, while 15 others were reportedly abducted.

The attack occurred shortly after worshippers concluded their early morning congregational prayers.

Among those killed was Hon. Nasiru Sani Abubakar, an aide to Governor Lawal.

Other victims were identified as Lauwali Abubakar, Malam Abdulrazak, Malam Abubakar, Malam Musa, Malam Usman and Malam Lawal Abubakar.

A resident, Mallam Yusuf Bello Kaura, told Daily Trust that the gunmen opened fire on worshippers as they were leaving the mosque after prayers.

He said the incident had thrown the community into mourning, adding that although the area had experienced previous attacks, residents had never witnessed such a deadly incident.

Another resident, Auwalu Ibrahim, suspected that the attackers had laid an ambush around the mosque before the commencement of prayers.

He expressed concern that the attack occurred less than 10 miles from a military base, questioning how the gunmen managed to operate without resistance.

Muhammad Aliyu, another resident, said the remains of the seven victims were buried on Monday at about 11am.

He added that the bandits had yet to contact the families of those abducted as of Monday.

The killing of Governor Lawal’s aide and other worshippers had sparked public anger, with some residents reportedly booing the governor during the funeral prayers on Sunday.

Police deploy personnel

Meanwhile, the Zamfara State Commissioner of Police, Ahmad Bello, confirmed the mosque attack but gave a lower casualty figure.

Bello said one person was killed and four worshippers were abducted during the incident.

In a statement, the police commissioner said about 30 armed bandits, allegedly loyal to notorious kingpin Bello Wakkala, popularly known as Dan Sadiya, attacked the mosque in the Low-Cost area.

He said the motive behind the attack and the actual number of abducted persons were still being investigated.

Bello added that police personnel had been deployed to the community to prevent further attacks, while additional officers would be sent to the local government area to protect lives and property.

The two attacks within 24 hours have renewed concerns over the security situation in Zamfara, where banditry, kidnappings and attacks on rural communities continue to threaten residents.

title: Fountain Of Life Church Board Insists Jimmy Odukoya Remains Removed As Senior Pastor, Appoints Interim Leader - Check Below For Full Details
description: The board of trustees says its November 16 resolution removing Jimmy Odukoya, son of the late founder Taiwo Odukoya, remains in force, and has handed interim leadership to Pastor Rotimi Okpaise.
content:
The board of trustees of Fountain of Life Church has insisted that Jimmy Odukoya, son of the late church founder Taiwo Odukoya, remains removed as senior pastor, despite his public rejection of the decision, and has appointed an interim leader to run the church.

In a statement issued on Tuesday, November 17, 2026, the board said it had resolved to entrust the church's interim spiritual and administrative leadership to Pastor Rotimi Okpaise, a pastor in the church. The interim arrangement will remain in place pending the conclusion of consultations and processes for appointing a substantive leadership structure, in line with the church's governing instruments and established procedures.

The timeline of the crisis:

  • November 16: the board announced it was withdrawing its recognition of Jimmy Odukoya as senior pastor with immediate effect, asking him to step down "forthwith from the office and all functions of Senior Pastor". It cited a review of the church's leadership and succession arrangements, longstanding governance concerns, and what it described as present doctrinal and moral controversies.
  • Same day: Jimmy Odukoya publicly rejected the removal, declaring that he remains senior pastor, while supporters described the board's action as invalid.
  • November 17: the board doubled down, stating that "its resolution of 16 November 2026 remains in force" and that it "stands by its earlier statement in its entirety".

The social media battle: the board also revealed that since the removal announcement, persons linked to the pastor had taken over the church's social media channels without its authorisation, using them to publish an account of events it considers "inaccurate and misleading". The board warned that statements currently appearing on those channels do not represent its position, and that only statements issued and signed on its behalf should be regarded as official. It said it is taking steps to restore the official communication channels to authorised control.

Why the board acted: it maintained that the decision was not intended as an act of "vindictiveness, humiliation or personal condemnation", but a necessary response to circumstances that could inflict lasting damage on the church and its legacy - and that the move was needed to create an atmosphere conducive to restoring peace, rebuilding trust and resolving the church's leadership and governance challenges.

Background: Fountain of Life Church, based in Lagos, was founded by the late Pastor Taiwo Odukoya, who died in November 2023. His son Jimmy Odukoya - also a Nollywood actor - took over as senior pastor after his death. The current standoff between the founder's son and the board of trustees has dominated Nigerian social media conversation for days, with mixed reactions from members of the public.

As it stands, the church now has an interim leadership structure under Pastor Rotimi Okpaise, while consultations continue towards a substantive leadership appointment.

title: NRS seeks media partnership to tackle illicit financial flows
description:
By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief



The Nigeria Revenue Service (NRS) has called for stronger collaboration with the Nigerian media to combat illicit financial flows (IFFs), which it said continue to deprive the country of substantial revenue needed for economic growth and national development.
content:
By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief

The Nigeria Revenue Service (NRS) has called for stronger collaboration with the Nigerian media to combat illicit financial flows (IFFs), which it said continue to deprive the country of substantial revenue needed for economic growth and national development.

The Service made the call on Tuesday at a media workshop in Abuja, where it urged journalists to deepen their understanding of illicit financial flows and strengthen investigative reporting to expose financial leakages and revenue losses.

An NRS official, Idris Abdullahi, said illicit financial flows were denying the government resources that could otherwise be channelled into critical infrastructure, healthcare, education and other socio-economic development programmes.

He emphasised the importance of media engagement in raising public awareness, exposing vulnerabilities and promoting accountability in the management of the nation’s financial resources.

Speaking at the workshop, an expert in illicit financial flows investigations, Adebayo Kayode, said Nigerian journalists required specialised training to enable them to play a more effective role in identifying and exposing suspicious financial activities.

Kayode said there was a fundamental difference between reporting that money had disappeared and investigating how, why, through whose arrangements and under what institutional circumstances it disappeared.

He said journalists needed the capacity to examine customs declarations, corporate ownership structures, extractive-sector export records, government budgets, procurement processes and tax policies to identify inconsistencies and potential revenue losses.

According to him, journalists must also understand the implications of financial statistics and regulatory decisions to ensure accurate reporting without exaggerating or downplaying their significance.

He described the fight against illicit financial flows as a national development imperative rather than a political contest, stressing that the scale of the challenge required collective action by government agencies, regulators, development partners, civil society organisations, the private sector and the media.

However, Kayode cautioned that collaboration must not compromise press independence, insisting that journalists should remain free to question government policies, investigate wrongdoing and hold public institutions accountable.

He said responsible governments should welcome an informed media that demands evidence, insists on transparency and helps citizens understand how public resources are managed.

On the way forward, Kayode identified the National Action Plan for 2027–2030 as an important framework for strengthening Nigeria’s response to illicit financial flows.

He said the plan’s success would depend not only on the institutions responsible for its implementation but also on effective public scrutiny and media engagement.

He urged journalists to pay closer attention to emerging areas of financial vulnerability, including virtual assets and cryptocurrency transactions, blockchain monitoring, extractive-sector activities, beneficial ownership, customs and trade integrity, public procurement and public asset transparency.

Other areas he identified included the licensing and taxation of virtual asset service providers, suspicious financial transactions, trade misinvoicing, corporate ownership disclosures, procurement-related financial risks and evidence-based investigations into unexplained wealth.

He also stressed the need to monitor production, valuation, exports and proceeds in the extractive sector to ensure that Nigeria receives the full value of its natural resources.

Kayode maintained that journalists had an important role in moving the country from fragmented financial information to integrated intelligence, from detection to prevention, and from policy declarations to measurable results.

Although journalists might not conduct forensic audits, issue regulatory licences or prosecute financial crimes, he said their investigations could expose institutional weaknesses, uncover financial irregularities and stimulate public demand for accountability.

He urged participants to ensure that the training translated into more rigorous investigative reporting, better-informed citizens and stronger institutions.

“The fight against illicit financial flows is ultimately a fight for the future of Nigeria. It is about protecting the integrity of our economy, safeguarding public revenue, strengthening our institutions and ensuring that the nation’s resources serve the people,” he said.

He called on journalists and relevant institutions to work together to trace financial movements, interrogate evidence, expose vulnerabilities and promote accountability, warning that funds whose movements were not properly traced could remain beyond public scrutiny.

title: Makinde Campaign faults Tinubu over federal recruitment embargo
description:
The Makinde-Daura Presidential Campaign Organisation (MDPCO) has criticised President Bola Tinubu over the Federal Government’s decision to impose an embargo on federal employment, describing the policy as insensitive to the plight of Nigerians, particularly youths seeking jobs.







The organisat
content:
The Makinde-Daura Presidential Campaign Organisation (MDPCO) has criticised President Bola Tinubu over the Federal Government’s decision to impose an embargo on federal employment, describing the policy as insensitive to the plight of Nigerians, particularly youths seeking jobs.

The organisation said the decision contradicted the All Progressives Congress (APC)’s promises on job creation and raised concerns about the government’s commitment to addressing unemployment.

In a press statement dated November 17, 2026, and signed by its Director of Strategic Communications, Richard Nnanna Ihediwa, the campaign organisation described the recruitment freeze as an indication of what it called the shortcomings of the Tinubu administration’s economic policies.

It also expressed concern that the embargo could precede possible mass retrenchment in the public service under the guise of fiscal discipline, particularly if Tinubu secured re-election in 2027.

The organisation cited World Bank estimates that approximately 3.5 million Nigerians enter the labour market annually, arguing that restricting federal recruitment would further limit employment opportunities for young people.

The MDPCO also rejected the Presidency’s explanation that the embargo was intended to consolidate public service reforms and enable the government to properly determine personnel requirements for the 2027 budget.

It argued that the government should instead focus on expanding the economy, harnessing the country’s human and natural resources, and creating employment opportunities.

The campaign organisation further faulted comments attributed to the Director-General of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Abdulaziz Yari, describing Nigerians complaining about hunger and hardship as lazy.

According to the statement, the 2027 general election would provide Nigerians an opportunity to assess the economic direction of the country and decide on the leadership they want.

It contrasted the Federal Government’s recruitment policy with what it described as employment-generating initiatives under Oyo State Governor, Seyi Makinde.

The organisation said Makinde’s administration had expanded economic opportunities in Oyo State through public and private sector initiatives, particularly in agriculture, infrastructure, education, transportation and other critical sectors.

It specifically highlighted the establishment of the Oyo State Agribusiness Development Agency (OYSADA), which it said had transformed traditional farm settlements into modern agro-industrial hubs.

Other initiatives cited included investments in power generation, aviation, road infrastructure, water resources, revenue reforms and improvements in the public workforce.

The campaign organisation said Makinde’s proposed RESET Nigeria Agenda was anchored on expanding economic opportunities, reducing waste without weakening public institutions, maintaining fiscal discipline without restricting employment, and pursuing economic stability without undermining citizens’ livelihoods.

It said the agenda offered an alternative economic direction ahead of the 2027 presidential election.

The organisation urged Nigerians to consider Makinde, who is the presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), for the 2027 election, arguing that his administration’s development approach in Oyo State could be replicated at the national level.

The post Makinde Campaign faults Tinubu over federal recruitment embargo appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: INEC urges stakeholders to collaborate for peaceful, credible elections
description:
The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) in Kwara has called on stakeholders to collaborate with the commission to ensure credible, peaceful and successful elections in 2027.



The state Resident Electoral Commissioner (REC), Mr Ahmed Yushau, made the call during a stakeholders’ meeting
content:
The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) in Kwara has called on stakeholders to collaborate with the commission to ensure credible, peaceful and successful elections in 2027.

The state Resident Electoral Commissioner (REC), Mr Ahmed Yushau, made the call during a stakeholders’ meeting held on Tuesday at the INEC office, Ilorin.

Yushau urged Nigerians to recognise that the responsibility for ensuring credible elections rests on all citizens, not on INEC alone.

According to him, every stakeholder has a role to play in the electoral process.

He stressed the need for stakeholders to respect the rights of others while fulfilling their obligations to the state.

He also urged citizens to support security agencies in maintaining a safe and peaceful environment.

The REC noted that the police and other security agencies need public cooperation to discharge their responsibilities effectively.

He emphasised the importance of public knowledge of electoral laws and guidelines, urging stakeholders to study INEC regulations, manuals and procedures rather than relying solely on the commission for information.

According to him, adequate knowledge of the legal framework will prevent misinformation, misunderstanding and possible manipulation during elections.

He urged stakeholders, particularly media practitioners and political actors, to keep and study copies of relevant electoral documents to understand their rights and responsibilities.

The REC, recalling his time as a pension officer in the Office of the Head of Service, said the knowledge of regulations and circulars was essential to avoid misleading the public.

He stressed that stakeholders with informed understanding of the electoral laws would be better positioned to engage constructively with INEC and hold the process accountable.

He reiterated that credible elections required collective responsibility, mutual respect and compliance with the law, urging all stakeholders to work together towards peaceful elections in the state.

A stakeholder, Mr Olatunji Gabriel, representing the African Democratic Congress (ADC) in Kwara, commended INEC for organising the forum.

Gabriel described the meeting as successful, saying it enabled political parties, NGOs and other stakeholders to exchange views with INEC on its level of preparedness for the elections.

The Kwara chairman of the National Democratic Party (NDP), Mr David Ifabiyi, urged political parties to adhere to electoral rules and promote peaceful conduct ahead of the forthcoming general elections.

Ifabiyi called on state chairmen of political parties to caution their members against acts that could disrupt public peace and advised them to remain law-abiding throughout the electoral process.

The NDP chairman urged security agencies and other social actors to support efforts towards ensuring a peaceful election.

He said Kwara was known for its peaceful disposition, urging stakeholders to sustain the reputation by promoting unity, tolerance and peaceful coexistence.

The post INEC urges stakeholders to collaborate for peaceful, credible elections appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: I don’t intend to limit myself to content creation – Finegurldivvy
description:
Nigerian content creator Innocent Divine Mmesommachukwu, popularly known as Finegurldivvy, has said she intends to venture into acting, mainstream entertainment and entrepreneurship beyond her social media career.
The TikTok creator disclosed this while speaking about her ambitions for the next five
content:
Nigerian content creator Innocent Divine Mmesommachukwu, popularly known as Finegurldivvy, has said she intends to venture into acting, mainstream entertainment and entrepreneurship beyond her social media career.

The TikTok creator disclosed this while speaking about her ambitions for the next five years, noting that she has plans beyond creating online videos.

“I have so many dreams and aspirations, and I don’t intend to limit myself to just content creation. I’m open to exploring mainstream entertainment, acting, entrepreneurship, and other exciting opportunities that allow me to express my creativity and expand my reach,” she said.

Finegurldivvy, who creates skits featuring different characters and everyday situations, said her journey into content creation began with a passion for entertaining people.

She, however, noted that her growing experience on TikTok had made her aware of the business opportunities available to content creators.

“TikTok is both a platform for entertainment and self-expression, as well as a business opportunity. For me, it started with a genuine passion for creating content and entertaining people, but as I’ve grown, I’ve also come to understand the opportunities that come with having a strong social media presence,” she said.

She also identified brand partnerships, collaborations and other business ventures as areas she intends to explore.

The content creator added that she hoped to build a career that would extend beyond social media and allow her to explore opportunities across different industries.

title: 63 Million Americans Now Care For Sick Loved Ones At Home - And It Is Quietly Breaking Their Mental Health - Check Below For Full Details
description: A new AARP report shows 1 in 4 US adults now provides unpaid family care, averaging 26 hours a week for years. The mental health toll is growing - and in Nigeria and Africa, where all care is family care, the lesson hits home.
content:
A new report has revealed that 63 million Americans - nearly one in every four adults - now provide unpaid care for sick, disabled or ageing loved ones at home, and the emotional and mental health cost of that silent work is becoming a crisis of its own.

The numbers (AARP/National Alliance for Caregiving 2025 report):

  • 63 million Americans are family caregivers - about 20 million more than in 2015
  • Those caring for adults aged 50 and above spend an average of 26 hours every week on care - and have been doing it for about five years
  • Nearly 1 in 4 caregivers say their own health has suffered because of their caregiving duties
  • 6 in 10 caregivers also hold down jobs, and half of them report their work being disrupted - late arrivals, reduced hours, or quitting entirely
  • Caregivers spend an average of $7,200 (about N11 million) of their own money every year on care
  • The care family members provide was valued at $1.01 trillion in 2024 - money they never receive

The mental health toll: a 2024 CDC analysis found caregivers report more frequent mental distress than non-caregivers, and are more likely to skip their own doctor visits because of cost. Worry, exhaustion, isolation and anticipatory grief build up quietly while the caregiver keeps smiling for the family.

Why this story matters in Nigeria and across Africa: in our culture, this burden is even heavier - because all care is family care. There are no state-funded respite programmes, no paid family leave, and only a handful of professional care homes. Children care for ageing parents, mothers carry children with disabilities alone for decades, and families nurse the chronically sick at home with little more than love and prayer - while the caregiver's own health quietly collapses.

The japa angle is real too: millions of Nigerian households now have their strongest adults abroad. Money arrives monthly, but it cannot hold a patient's hand at 2am. The parent, spouse or sibling left behind carries the full 26-hour weekly load alone - and rarely has anyone ask how THEY are doing.

What experts say helps: sharing the load among siblings instead of one person carrying it all; respite breaks so the caregiver can rest, see a doctor or simply breathe; keeping medications, appointments and provider contacts in one clear plan; and honestly watching for burnout signs - constant exhaustion, irritability, isolation, or neglecting your own health.

Bottom line: caring for a loved one is one of the most beautiful things a human can do - but the person holding everybody up also needs to be held. If you are the family caregiver, your health matters too. Ask for help. It is not weakness - it is how you keep being able to care.

title: 2027: Anambra set for Tinubu’s re-election state mega rally
description:
From Aloysius Attah, Onitsha
The Anambra State Presidential Campaign Council for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election is set to hold a campaign rally tagged “SoluTinubu 2027” on Thursday, November 19, at Dr Alex Ekwueme Square, Awka.
SoluTinubu, which translates literally as “follow Tinubu”, is more
content:
From Aloysius Attah, Onitsha

The Anambra State Presidential Campaign Council for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election is set to hold a campaign rally tagged “SoluTinubu 2027” on Thursday, November 19, at Dr Alex Ekwueme Square, Awka.

SoluTinubu, which translates literally as “follow Tinubu”, is more than a campaign slogan.

It is also a statement of assurance to the rest of Nigerians that Ndi Igbo also support President Tinubu’s re-election.

The SoluTinubu campaign is anchored on the mantra that progressives are working together, which was propagated by Governor Chukwuma Soludo, who is also the Chairman of the Anambra State Presidential Campaign Council for President Tinubu’s re-election.

A statement from the campaign council said the rally is expected to attract several heavyweights and political icons of Igbo extraction, who will make a bold statement affirming the support of Ndi Igbo for President Tinubu come January 16.

Ahead of the 2027 presidential election, Anambra State is one of the keenly contested states because of the two competing political forces.

However, with sustained mobilisation, nationalist and reasoned argument, progressives are gaining ground, such that during a recent outing of Governor Soludo in Awka, youths in the town publicly declared their support for President Tinubu’s re-election.

The rally on Thursday is taking shape as another major milestone for progressives in the state.
