title: Kebbi APC rally: Shettima urges North to disregard opposition lies, distortions, repay Tinubu’s kindness
description:
From Romanus Ugwu, Ola Muhammad, Birnin Kebbi
Vice President Kashim Shettima has urged the North to disregard the lies, distortions, half-truths, taunts, insinuations, threats and noise of the opposition and to repay President Bola Tinubu for his kindness to the region.
He spoke at a presidential ra
content:
From Romanus Ugwu, Ola Muhammad, Birnin Kebbi

Vice President Kashim Shettima has urged the North to disregard the lies, distortions, half-truths, taunts, insinuations, threats and noise of the opposition and to repay President Bola Tinubu for his kindness to the region.

He spoke at a presidential rally organised by the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Birnin Kebbi, the Kebbi State capital, on Tuesday. He disclosed that the northern region would be the biggest beneficiary of the N200 billion worth of fertiliser that was about to be procured for distribution to farmers in the dry season.

His words: “President Tinubu sacrificed his resources and comfort to give the North what it wished for. We are grateful that the North, too, kept its promise in 2023 by giving the president 60.2 per cent of the votes that cost us a victory.”

“The North repaid their kindness. We are even more grateful that you are prepared to do the same in January next year. You have rejected the lies, the distortions, the half-truths, the taunts, the insinuations, the threats and the noise of the opposition,” he said.

Defending why the North must vote for the re-election of President Tinubu, Shettima said: “He also understands the needs of our farmers. Thousands of them participate in dry-season farming. And just on Monday, he gave me the honour of chairing a committee that will procure fertiliser worth N200 billion for distribution to our farmers in the dry season.”

“And you and I know where those farmers are. They are in Kebbi, they are in Jigawa, they are in Kano, they are in Yobe, they are largely in Kaduna, they are in Niger, they are in Sokoto, they are in Kebbi, they are in Zamfara.

“So, my brothers in the North, this is why we have to continue to support the President. On the highway the government is building from Sokoto to Badagry to ease movement across the country, 258 kilometres run through Kebbi. This is the longest stretch in any state.

“We have also undertaken refuels on the Jega, Koko, Yauri and Birnin Kebbi, Argungu Federal Roads to ease your journeys. But roads alone are not enough without electricity. We have increased the capacity of the Birnin Kebbi transmission substation while constructing a 3.5-megawatt solar project in Ambursa to serve homes and businesses.

“Your Governor, Comrade Nasir Idris, began his career in the classroom. In February, Mr President commissioned the College of Nursing and Midwifery in Ambursa to train nurses and midwives. This complements our commitment to the education of your children.

“This is why we introduced NELFUND to support their studies. In Aliero alone, the State University received 693 million naira in student loan funding. In healthcare, we have upgraded the Federal Medical Centre in Birnin Kebbi to a teaching hospital.

“While primary healthcare centres across the state receive federal support through the Basic Health Care Provision Fund. We have also invested in the skills of your young people. Mr President’s economic reforms have increased the revenue available to states to fund their initiatives and projects,” he enumerated.

Shettima strongly believes that his boss has done excellently well, stressing: “Kebbi State, like other states, struggles to fund its projects. We will not rest until every kobo and every naira from these reforms is invested in your welfare. This is why we have come again to continue what we started about three years ago.”

“On January 16th, I trust you to come out en masse and vote for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu. On February 6th, I trust you to return Governor Nasir Idris for a second term. We have so much to do to fix this great country and we must all do our part,” he said.

title: NRS seeks improved data collection to combat illicit financial flows
description:
From Adanna Nnamani, Abuja
The Nigeria Revenue Service (NRS) has identified inadequate data availability and poor record-keeping among relevant government agencies as major challenges undermining efforts to combat illicit financial flows (IFFs) in Nigeria.
The Head of Anti-Graft and Law Enforcement
content:
From Adanna Nnamani, Abuja

The Nigeria Revenue Service (NRS) has identified inadequate data availability and poor record-keeping among relevant government agencies as major challenges undermining efforts to combat illicit financial flows (IFFs) in Nigeria.

The Head of Anti-Graft and Law Enforcement Liaison at the NRS, Idris Abdullahi, said the fight against IFFs was largely data-driven, making the availability, proper organisation and presentation of relevant information critical to estimating the scale of the problem and developing effective policies.

Abdullah spoke at a one-day Stakeholders Engagement on Illicit Financial Flows (IFFs) with the Nigerian Media, held on Tuesday in Abuja.

He said that although relevant agencies had data that could support the exercise, ensuring that such information was properly organised and presented in an analysable format remained a major challenge.

Abdullah, who also heads the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Unit at the NRS and serves as Secretary of the Technical Working Group on IFFs, said the group had engaged relevant agencies to improve their understanding of the type of information required for effective IFF estimations.

According to him, the Technical Working Group comprises the NRS, which serves as its secretariat, the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC), the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC), the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS), the Nigerian Financial Intelligence Unit (NFIU) and the Bureau of Public Procurement (BPP).

He explained that strengthening the capacity of these institutions to generate and analyse data was central to understanding the magnitude of illicit financial flows and developing appropriate interventions.

Abdullah said findings from IFF estimations would also help identify companies and other entities involved in illicit financial activities, as well as sectors more vulnerable to such practices.

He noted that identifying high-risk sectors would enable the government to deploy resources more effectively and develop targeted strategies to address the problem.

On measures to address the challenge, he said the Technical Working Group had prioritised capacity building for agencies responsible for conducting IFF estimations, alongside public awareness and stakeholder engagement.

He stressed the need to work with the media, government and the general public to deepen understanding of illicit financial flows, noting that many Nigerians were still unfamiliar with the concept, its implications and the activities that could constitute IFFs.

Abdullah said the group’s secretariat had been engaging journalists to improve public understanding and encourage accurate reporting of issues relating to illicit financial flows.

He added that the group had also commenced engagements with the private sector, including sensitisation programmes organised in collaboration with the Manufacturers Association of Nigeria (MAN) last year and this year.

He said: “The fight against illicit financial flows is data-driven. Therefore, the availability of data from the relevant agencies responsible for generating it has been one of the major challenges.

“Another issue has been ensuring that such data is properly organised and presented in a format that can be analysed and translated into meaningful information.

“We have engaged most of these agencies, and they now understand the kind of data they need to maintain for the purpose of conducting IFF estimations.

“The first and foremost priority is to build the capacity of the agencies responsible for carrying out IFF estimations. These estimations are important because they help policymakers understand the scale of the problem and develop appropriate policy directions.

“By identifying sectors that are more vulnerable to illicit financial flows, the government can determine where to deploy more resources and develop targeted strategies to combat the problem.”

Also speaking at the engagement, financial crime investigator, chartered accountant and forensic expert Adedayo Adeyinka Kayode said commercial and tax-related activities account for more than 60 per cent of global illicit financial flows, indicating that the problem goes beyond corruption.

Kayode identified trade misinvoicing, profit shifting by multinational companies and aggressive tax avoidance through tax havens as major channels through which illicit financial flows occur.

He also identified crude oil theft, illegal bunkering, manipulation of production and export data, contract inflation, diversion of public funds and cyber fraud as some of the practices driving illicit financial flows in Nigeria.

According to him, Nigeria’s vulnerability is heightened by its heavy dependence on oil revenue, large informal economy, weak data integration among government agencies and gaps in enforcement and prosecution.

He warned that illicit financial flows undermine government revenue, increase borrowing, weaken public trust and limit funding for critical sectors such as education, healthcare and infrastructure.

On compliance measures, Kayode urged businesses to strengthen internal controls, conduct proper due diligence, verify beneficial ownership and improve transaction monitoring to prevent illicit financial activities.

He also called for stronger inter-agency cooperation, effective whistleblowing mechanisms, responsive justice systems and political leadership to strengthen the fight against illicit financial flows.

He urged journalists to go beyond reporting allegations by following financial transactions, examining ownership structures and tracking the prosecution of offenders and the recovery of stolen assets.

Kayode said: “Commercial and tax-related activities account for over 60 per cent of global illicit financial flows. Tackling the menace requires strong laws, data sharing, international cooperation and effective enforcement.”

The post NRS seeks improved data collection to combat illicit financial flows appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Reps to probe 22 States over unpaid pensions
description:
By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja



The House of Representatives has resolved to investigate the failure of 22 states to pay retirement benefits regularly, following concerns that thousands of elderly pensioners are being abandoned to hunger, poverty and preventable deaths.



The resolution was sequel t
content:
By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja

The House of Representatives has resolved to investigate the failure of 22 states to pay retirement benefits regularly, following concerns that thousands of elderly pensioners are being abandoned to hunger, poverty and preventable deaths.

The resolution was sequel to a motion of urgent public importance sponsored by Rep. Adesola Adebayo, representing Apapa Federal Constituency of Lagos State, on Tuesday at plenary.

Moving the motion, Rep. Adebayo cited a report indicating that only 14 of Nigeria’s 36 states pay pensions regularly, while the remaining 22 owe retirees several months or, in some cases, several years of entitlements.

He described pensions as an earned right rather than a privilege or charity, stressing that retirees who had devoted between 30 and 35 years to public service deserved to enjoy their benefits without unnecessary hardship.

The lawmaker expressed concern that many pensioners aged between 70 and 90 were dying in poverty because they could not afford food, medication, rent and other basic necessities.

He also raised concerns over the practice of subjecting elderly retirees to prolonged verification exercises, forcing some to queue for days under harsh weather conditions, with reports of pensioners collapsing and dying in the process.

Adebayo argued that the non-payment of pensions amounted to a violation of constitutional provisions and human dignity, while creating fear among serving public workers who could begin to see retirement as a death sentence.

The motion, however, generated disagreements among lawmakers over the constitutional powers of the National Assembly to intervene in pension matters involving state governments.

Rep. Mark Essiet opposed the motion, arguing that state pension obligations fell within the jurisdiction of state governments and their respective Houses of Assembly.

He cautioned against any suggestion that the Federal Government should deduct money from states’ allocations to settle outstanding pension liabilities, describing such an approach as unconstitutional.

Umoh urged the House to concentrate on the pension challenges facing military personnel, who, he said, had repeatedly protested over their entitlements.

Similarly, Rep. Dominic Okafor cautioned against generalising the allegations against all states, noting that some governors had fulfilled their pension obligations.
He cited Anambra State as an example, arguing that the motion should distinguish between states that had failed to pay and those that were meeting their responsibilities.

But Rep. Billy Owasaro urged the House not to abandon the motion, proposing amendments to remove provisions outside its constitutional jurisdiction.

He argued that the suffering of elderly pensioners was too serious for lawmakers to ignore.

Owasaro said: “We know what our fathers are going through. We know what it means for a man to work for 35 years only to be called to stand in the sun, under the sun, to review, to keep reviewing until he can’t stand it no more.

“So, Mr Speaker, instead of killing this beautiful motion, I would like to go in for amendments. I would like to take out areas our mandates don’t cover and go with those areas that our mandates cover.”

The Deputy Speaker, who presided over the sitting, subsequently directed lawmakers to examine the House Standing Orders to establish the jurisdiction of the Committee on Pensions.

Reading the committee’s mandate, the presiding officer noted that it was empowered to examine pension-related issues across the public service, recommend measures to ensure timely payment of retirement benefits and investigate employers’ failure to meet their pension obligations.

Its responsibilities also include oversight of the National Pension Commission (PenCom), the Military Pension Board and other relevant institutions.

Rep. Tersee Udo subsequently urged the House to allow the motion to proceed, arguing that the suffering of pensioners across the country warranted urgent legislative attention.

Another lawmaker, Rep. Zainab Gimba, also supported the motion, citing Section 210 of the 1999 Constitution, as amended, which protects the pension rights of persons in the public service of a state.

She particularly drew attention to Section 210(2), which provides that pension benefits due to a person under the law shall not be withheld or altered to the person’s disadvantage, except as permitted by law.

Gimba argued that although state pension liabilities must be distinguished from federal obligations, the National Assembly had the constitutional authority to debate the issue, make recommendations and encourage state legislators to exercise the necessary oversight.

She warned that continued failure to pay pensions could trigger humanitarian challenges, undermine the dignity of retirees and negatively affect their families and society.

The House Leader, Rep. Julius Ihonvbere, also defended the motion, insisting that lawmakers should not shy away from addressing the plight of Nigerians simply because some of the affected matters fell within the jurisdiction of state governments.

Ihonvbere argued that members of the National Assembly represented Nigerians across the country and had a responsibility to speak out when citizens were subjected to hardship.

He maintained that the House could intervene through motions, investigations and recommendations without necessarily usurping the constitutional powers of state governments.

Recalling previous interventions by the Ninth Assembly in matters involving state governments, he said the National Assembly had a responsibility to engage relevant authorities where circumstances demanded it.

“We need to be very careful not to diminish our powers and responsibilities by hiding over some of the local sections, under the Standing Order of the Constitution, not to perform our duties.

“Technically, there is nothing in which this House or the National Assembly cannot engage in, whether they are in the local government, the state, or anywhere, because we represent the entire country”, he said.

The House Leader further called on governors who had yet to clear outstanding pension liabilities to fulfil their obligations, insisting that the availability of public funds should not be an excuse for abandoning retired workers.

He also commended governors who had maintained regular pension payments, urging others to follow their example.

Following deliberations, the House unanimously adopted the motion and resolved to call on the Federal Government, through the Secretary to the Government of the Federation, to urge state governments to prioritise the payment of pensions.

It also mandated its Committee on Pensions to interface with PenCom and engage state governments to ascertain the challenges responsible for irregular pension payments, identify possible solutions and report its findings to the House.

title: Tinubu approves inland dry port for Kebbi
description:
President Bola Tinubu has approved the full operationalisation of the Tsamiya Inland Dry Port in Kebbi to boost trade, investment and economic activities in the state.



Tinubu gave the approval on Tuesday at the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally at Haliru Abdu Township St
content:
President Bola Tinubu has approved the full operationalisation of the Tsamiya Inland Dry Port in Kebbi to boost trade, investment and economic activities in the state.

Tinubu gave the approval on Tuesday at the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally at Haliru Abdu Township Stadium, Birnin Kebbi.

The approval followed a request by Gov. Nasir Idris, who described the facility as a strategic economic project capable of transforming Kebbi into a major commercial hub.

Tinubu assured residents of the state that his administration would address their requests, particularly those relating to critical infrastructure.

He specifically promised to deliver road projects, including the road linking Kalgo to Bunza and extending towards border communities.

“I thank you from the bottom of my heart, the people of Kebbi State, for enduring the blazing sun to welcome me.

“I urge you all to get your PVCs to vote for me, the governor and other APC candidates in Kebbi State.

“I have received all your requests on road construction and the Kebbi dry port. I want to assure you that it is approved; we will deliver the dry port,” he said.

The President urged residents to obtain their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) and vote for him, Idris and other APC candidates in the 2027 general elections.

He said he returned to the state to appreciate residents for their support during the previous election and seek their renewed mandate.

Earlier, Idris said the dry port would strengthen trade, stimulate economic activities and create employment opportunities for residents.

He commended the Federal Government’s interventions in agriculture, security, education and healthcare, but appealed to Tinubu to prioritise the dry port and other critical infrastructure projects in the state.

“Mr President, what you are witnessing now tells you that Kebbi is for you, for APC, for all our candidates and me,” the governor said.

Idris also pledged to deliver 100 per cent votes for the APC in Kebbi in the 2027 general elections, saying residents were ready to reciprocate Tinubu’s support for the state.

In his remarks, the Director-General of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, Sen. Abdulaziz Yari, described Tinubu as a committed supporter of development in the North, citing federal infrastructure projects and interventions across the region.

Yari challenged opposition politicians to tell northerners what they had done for the region when they occupied positions of authority.

He also urged voters in the North-West not to be swayed by opposition claims that the APC had lost its political support in the region.

The News Agency of Nigeria reports that thousands of APC supporters, including women and youth groups, gathered at the rally venue, displaying party flags and posters of Tinubu and Idris.

The rally was attended by Vice-President Kashim Shettima, Speaker of the House of Representatives, Tajudeen Abbas, Deputy Senate President Barau Jibrin, governors from the North-West and other parts of the country.

Some of the governors in attendance include: Uba Sani of Kaduna, Dauda Lawal of Zamfara, Mai Mala Buni of Yobe, Babagana Zulum of Borno and Ahmad Aliyu of Sokoto.

Others were Minister of Budget and Economic Planning Atiku Bagudu, Minister of State for Budget and Economic Planning Doris Uzoka-Anite, Minister of Housing Muttaqha Darma and APC National Chairman, Prof. Nentawe Yilwatda.

Also present were Senators Adams Oshiomhole and Ali Modu Sheriff, and former governors Ahmed Yerima, Ibrahim Shema and Abdullahi Ganduje.

The post Tinubu approves inland dry port for Kebbi appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Osun court restrains Adeleke, Ataoja over demotion of Alagunbelewo
description:
From Lateef Dada, Osogbo
The Osun State High Court sitting in Osogbo has granted an interim order restraining Governor Ademola Adeleke and other respondents from removing, demoting or altering the status of the Alagunbelewo of Agunbelewo, Oba Maruf Lawal.
Oba Lawal was originally elevated to a Part
content:
From Lateef Dada, Osogbo

The Osun State High Court sitting in Osogbo has granted an interim order restraining Governor Ademola Adeleke and other respondents from removing, demoting or altering the status of the Alagunbelewo of Agunbelewo, Oba Maruf Lawal.

Oba Lawal was originally elevated to a Part II Oba on 15 August 2024. However, controversy ensued when a letter dated 5 November 2026 announced the de-recognition of the stool.

Shortly afterwards, on November 13, the state government formally installed Prince Muritala Abiola Adejumobi as the new Alagunbelewo.

Despite the action, Governor Adeleke publicly distanced himself from the purported demotion on 16 November.

Seeking legal redress, Oba Lawal dragged Governor Adeleke, the Osun State Commissioner for Local Government and Chieftaincy Affairs, the Attorney General and Commissioner for Justice, and the Ataoja of Osogbo, Oba Jimoh Olanipekun, before the court to quash his removal.

In a motion ex parte filed through his counsel, Mr Yemi Abiola, the monarch sought an order to review and nullify the 5 November letter, which reverted his recognised stool to a minor chieftaincy under Part III of the Chiefs Law.

He also challenged a 6 November directive from the fourth respondent suspending him as the Community/Traditional Head of Agunbelewo and demanding his instruments of office within seven days.

Oba Lawal contended that the decisions were null and void due to a breach of fair hearing, procedural impropriety, bad faith and lack of statutory power by the respondents.

Furthermore, he sought injunctions to prevent the implementation, gazetting or enforcement of the de-recognition, as well as to protect his rights, allowances and the installation of any successor while the substantive suit is pending.

Ruling on the application, Justice Michael Awe held that the applicant’s case succeeded, granting him leave to commence an action for judicial review.

“Specifically, and in pursuance of Order 41 R. 3 (6) (a) of the Rules of this court, the grant of this application shall operate as a stay of every and all proceedings or action or steps being taken or to be taken by the Respondents as it relates to the subject matter of this suit,” Justice Awe ruled.

The judge directed that the order be served alongside the applicant’s motion on notice to all respondents and adjourned the matter to November 26 for hearing.

title: Enugu Assembly Passes Landlord-Tenant Amendment Bill, Caps Rent Increase At 2%
description: The Enugu State House of Assembly has passed the Landlord and Tenant Amendment Bill, which seeks to regulate rent increases and protect tenants from arbitrary hikes in rental charges.The bill was passed after its third reading, following the consideration of a report submitted by a joint committee c
content:
The Enugu State House of Assembly has passed the Landlord and Tenant Amendment Bill, which seeks to regulate rent increases and protect tenants from arbitrary hikes in rental charges.

The bill was passed after its third reading, following the consideration of a report submitted by a joint committee comprising the House Committees on Housing and Investment, Public Petition, Ethics and Privileges, and Judiciary.

Titled A Bill for a Law to Amend the Landlord and Tenant Second Amendment Bill, Cap 101, Revised Laws of Enugu State 2024, House Bill No. 3 of 2025, the legislation passed its second reading on March 11, 2026, and subsequently underwent a public hearing on March 26, 2026.

Under the proposed amendment, landlords will only be permitted to increase rent after four years, with any increment capped at two per cent of the existing rent.

However, where a landlord undertakes reasonable renovations to a property, the bill allows for a rent increase of not more than 10 per cent.

Following the presentation of the committee’s report, the House dissolved into the Committee of the Whole to consider the report and the bill before its eventual passage.

Speaking after the exercise, the Speaker of the House, Rt. Hon. Uche Ugwu, described the legislation as part of the good governance initiatives of the current administration.

He said the passage of the bill would give tenants in Enugu State a new lease of life.

The bill now awaits the assent of Governor Peter Mbah to become law.

title: Nigeria must produce 70% of medicines locally – WHO
description:
The World Health Organisation and the Nigerian Academy of Pharmacy have called for stronger local pharmaceutical manufacturing, improved regulation and increased investment in research and innovation to strengthen Nigeria’s health security.
They made the call on Tuesday at the Academy’s 2026 Annual
content:
The World Health Organisation and the Nigerian Academy of Pharmacy have called for stronger local pharmaceutical manufacturing, improved regulation and increased investment in research and innovation to strengthen Nigeria’s health security.

They made the call on Tuesday at the Academy’s 2026 Annual General Meeting and Investiture of New Fellows, held under the theme, “Pharmacy for National Health Security: Advancing Innovation, Medicine Sovereignty and Sustainable Healthcare.”

In a keynote address delivered on behalf of the WHO Country Representative in Nigeria, Dr Pavel Ursu, by Dr Akinola Fatiregun, the organisation stressed the need for Nigeria to reduce its dependence on imported medicines and build a resilient pharmaceutical sector.

He said, “Nigeria needs to strengthen local pharmaceutical manufacturing, reduce dependence on imported medicines and build a resilient pharmaceutical sector capable of safeguarding national health security. The Presidential Initiative for Unlocking the Healthcare Value Chain targets 70 per cent local production of pharmaceuticals by 2030.”

Ursu said medicine sovereignty was essential to national health security, noting that disruptions to global supply chains could expose countries heavily dependent on imported medicines to serious risks.

He identified six areas of potential collaboration between the WHO and the Academy: policy development, implementation research, regulatory science, workforce development, pharmacists’ involvement in health emergencies, and antimicrobial resistance and pharmacovigilance.

He also emphasised the importance of strengthening quality standards, supporting active pharmaceutical ingredient manufacturing and exploring opportunities under the African Continental Free Trade Area to expand access to locally produced medicines.

The WHO representative reiterated that pharmacists had a critical role to play in achieving universal health coverage, adding that “there is no universal health coverage without pharmacy.”

The President of the Academy, Prof. Lere Baale, urged the newly inducted fellows to use their expertise to transform the pharmaceutical sector and contribute to national development.

“Let your fellowship become a platform for collaboration, for mentorship, innovation and service. Do not merely wear this honour of fellowship. Let that honour define your actions,” he said.

Baale said Nigeria had the human resources and scientific capacity to become a major pharmaceutical manufacturing hub but needed stronger collaboration among professionals, government and industry.

“The time for isolated excellence is over,” he said, calling for collective efforts to strengthen the industry and position Nigeria to serve the wider African market.

He added, “Nigeria must work towards producing 70 per cent of its medicine requirements locally to strengthen medicine security, reduce dependence on imports and build a sustainable pharmaceutical manufacturing industry.”

The recipient of the Lifetime Achievement Award, Pharm. Stella Okoli, expressed appreciation to the Academy, describing the recognition as an encouragement to continue contributing to the profession.

“Quote me anywhere: Nigeria is the best country in the world. Nobody should feel sorry that they are Nigerian. The only thing we have to do is push hard,” she said.

Okoli urged pharmacists to remain committed to developing the country’s pharmaceutical industry and encouraged young professionals to gain practical exposure to manufacturing.

She also recalled periods when government policies supported local pharmaceutical production, saying sustained government engagement was necessary to help manufacturers grow.

A former President of the Pharmaceutical Society of Nigeria and Vice-President of the Academy, Pharm. Ahmed Yakasia, said professional recognition must be matched with integrity, competence and commitment to public health.

“It is not just enough to have knowledge; you have to have character,” he said.

Yakasai urged pharmacists to intensify efforts against fake and substandard medicines through improved pharmacovigilance, stronger professional standards and collaboration across the pharmaceutical supply chain.

He also stressed the need for pharmacists to take responsibility for protecting the public and strengthening confidence in medicines produced and distributed in Nigeria.

The Academy inducted 11 new fellows at the ceremony. They are Dr Shakirat Adeshiyan Adeosun, Dr Solomon Aigbavboa, Pharm. Ignatius Kenechukwu Anukwu, Dr Josephine Ihanene Ehimen, Pharm. Bankole Aminu Ezebuilo, Rasheed Oladele Faworaja, Dr Ukamaka Gladys Okafor, Pharm. Prof. Henry Akpobor Okeri, Professor Ogbonna Okorie, Prof. Ibrahim Adekunle Oreagba and Pharm. Dr Titilayo Abidemi Onedo.

The Academy also conferred honorary fellowships on Dr Obiora Anthony Chukwuka and Alhaji Auwalu Abdullahi Rano, while a Distinguished Award was presented as part of the ceremony.

title: No federal job in 2027 – Nigerian govt bars all agencies from hiring
description:
The Federal Government has directed all federal Ministries, Departments and Agencies (MDAs) to suspend fresh recruitment in 2027, except where special approval is obtained.
Under the new directive, government institutions are expected to maintain their existing workforce levels and refrain from crea
content:
The Federal Government has directed all federal Ministries, Departments and Agencies (MDAs) to suspend fresh recruitment in 2027, except where special approval is obtained.

Under the new directive, government institutions are expected to maintain their existing workforce levels and refrain from creating new positions or recruiting additional personnel without authorisation.

The government said any agency seeking to increase its staff strength must provide clear reasons for the request and demonstrate that adequate funds have been provided in its budget to cover the salaries, allowances and other financial obligations of the proposed employees.

It also warned that MDAs that fail to submit their staff records or justify their personnel budget proposals risk being excluded from the approved 2027 staff list, a move that could affect the allocation of funds for their personnel costs in the next national budget.

The directive is contained in a circular dated November 9, 2026, titled 2027 Workforce Budget Call Circular.

The circular, issued by the Office of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation, was signed by Ishiyaku Musa Mohammed, Permanent Secretary in charge of the Service Policies and Strategies Office.

It was circulated to the Chief of Staff to the President, Deputy Chief of Staff to the Vice President, Secretary to the Government of the Federation, ministers, permanent secretaries, service chiefs and heads of federal institutions.

The document directed the institutions to prepare and submit their workforce budget proposals for 2027 for review and approval.

According to the government, the exercise is part of ongoing efforts to reform the public service, strengthen human capacity and ensure proper planning and management of personnel expenditure ahead of the next budget year.

It further instructed all federal institutions to operate within their approved staff ceilings and avoid conducting recruitment exercises without the required authorisation.

“MDAs are advised to strictly maintain their current staff position for the 2027 fiscal year,” the circular stated.

The government, however, acknowledged that some agencies might have genuine reasons to employ additional personnel, but insisted that such requests must be properly justified and supported by evidence of available funding.

It stressed that applications for an increase in workforce strength must explain the need for additional employees and show how the resulting salary and allowance obligations would be financed.

“However, where it is necessary to seek an increase, such requests should be supported with justifications attaching relevant information, including financial provision in the budget to meet additional emolument commitment; otherwise the existing workforce ceiling should not be exceeded,” the circular added.

title: Africa loses up to $125bn annually to corruption, illicit financial flows – AU
description:
From Adanna Nnamani and Francis Onyedikachukwu, Abuja
Africa loses between $80 billion and $125 billion annually to corruption and illicit financial flows, the African Union (AU) has disclosed, calling for stronger continental cooperation and practical measures to stem the tide.
The Chairperson of t
content:
From Adanna Nnamani and Francis Onyedikachukwu, Abuja

Africa loses between $80 billion and $125 billion annually to corruption and illicit financial flows, the African Union (AU) has disclosed, calling for stronger continental cooperation and practical measures to stem the tide.

The Chairperson of the African Union Advisory Board Against Corruption (AUABC), Kwami Senanu, made the disclosure at the inaugural General Assembly of the African Asset Recovery Practitioners Forum (AARPF) in Abuja.

Senanu said the scale of financial losses underscored the urgent need for African countries to move beyond policy declarations and strengthen efforts to trace, confiscate and recover stolen assets.

“Neither convictions, nor commitments, nor talk, nor position papers can themselves stem the tide of illicit financial flows in the continent or help us recover a single asset,” he said.

Senanu traced the origins of the forum to a proposal made in Dakar, Senegal, in September 2022, followed by consultations in Dar es Salaam in January 2024 and Addis Ababa in May 2024, where its charter was adopted.

He said the forum was formally launched in Nairobi in April 2025 with the signing of the Nairobi Declaration.

The AU official commended Nigeria for championing the Common African Position on Asset Recovery (CAPAR), which was endorsed by AU heads of state in February 2020.

Also speaking at the event, the Chairman of the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC) and Interim Chairperson of the Forum, Dr Musa Aliyu, said the growing sophistication of cross-border financial crimes made it imperative for African countries to strengthen cooperation in tracing, freezing, confiscating and recovering stolen assets.

He said stolen assets were often moved across several jurisdictions through complex financial arrangements, making it difficult for individual countries to investigate and recover them without international collaboration.

According to him, the establishment of the forum was driven by the recognition that no country could effectively tackle corruption and illicit financial flows in isolation.

Aliyu said asset recovery should not be viewed merely as a law enforcement activity but as an important instrument for national development, accountability and the protection of public resources.

“Every resource lost through corruption represents more than a financial loss. It is an opportunity denied to our people,” he said.

He explained that funds recovered from corruption could help finance critical sectors such as education, healthcare, infrastructure, security and employment, while strengthening public confidence in government institutions.

The ICPC chairman identified institutional capacity, professional development, operational cooperation, strategic partnerships, legal reforms and sustainable resource mobilisation as six strategic priorities for establishing an effective continental asset recovery framework.

On his part, the representative of the African Union Commissioner, Bankole Adeoye, said asset recovery remained central to Africa’s development ambitions, accountability framework and efforts to strengthen public institutions.

Adeoye disclosed that the African Union Commission was developing a draft CAPAR Compliance Monitoring Tool to help member states assess progress in implementing agreed commitments.

He said the commission was also undertaking a continental study on mutual legal assistance to identify challenges and opportunities for improving cooperation in criminal investigations, asset tracing and recovery.

According to him, stronger international cooperation, beneficial ownership transparency, financial integrity, inclusive international tax cooperation and institutional capacity were essential to addressing illicit financial flows.

He stressed that the success of asset recovery should not be measured solely by the value of recovered funds but also by how effectively such resources improve public services, strengthen institutions and promote development.

Meanwhile, Germany reaffirmed its commitment to supporting African institutions in strengthening asset recovery systems and combating illicit financial flows.

Speaking on behalf of the German government and the German development agency, GIZ, Dr Karin Jansen described the establishment of the forum as an important milestone in Africa’s collective response to corruption and financial crimes.

She identified improved operational capacity, stronger cooperation, effective management and return of recovered assets, as well as accountability and knowledge sharing, as priorities for strengthening the continent’s asset recovery efforts.

Jansen stressed that asset recovery must not end with confiscation, noting that recovered assets must be properly preserved, managed and transparently returned to ensure they deliver meaningful benefits to citizens.

The four-day assembly, hosted by the ICPC, brought together anti-corruption agencies, prosecutors and development partners from across Africa to strengthen cooperation in recovering assets stolen through corruption.

The post Africa loses up to $125bn annually to corruption, illicit financial flows – AU appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: A vote for Tinubu will translate into preservation of the North – Shettima
description:
Vice President Kashim Shettima has called on the people of the North to vote massively for the re-election of President Bola Tinubu on January 16, 2027.



Shettima made the call on Tuesday in Birnin Kebbi during the All Progressives Congress (APC) Campaign Rally, held at Haliru Abdu Stadium in Kebb
content:
Vice President Kashim Shettima has called on the people of the North to vote massively for the re-election of President Bola Tinubu on January 16, 2027.

Shettima made the call on Tuesday in Birnin Kebbi during the All Progressives Congress (APC) Campaign Rally, held at Haliru Abdu Stadium in Kebbi.

The vice president stated that a vote for President Tinubu and VP Shettima would be a vote for the preservation of the North.

“We are grateful that the North kept its promise in 2023. The North repaid Tinubu’s kindness and support for late former President Muhammadu Buhari.

“We are even more grateful that you are prepared to do the same in January 2027. You have rejected the lies, the distortions.

“And the half-truths, the taunts, the insinuations, the threats and the noise of the opposition. We are here because you can see through them.

“A vote for His Excellency, President Bola Tinubu, and for me as your Vice President is a vote for the preservation of the North,” he said.

On security, Shettima said President Tinubu increased the salaries of the armed forces by up to 80 per cent and prioritised the welfare of all security agencies.

“He also understands the needs of our farmers. Thousands of you participated in our dry-season programme to grow rice, maize and cassava.

“That is why we have continued to supply you with the equipment you need.

“Of the superhighway we are building from Sokoto to Badagry to ease movement across the country, 258 kilometres run through Kebbi. That is the longest stretch in any state,” the VP added.

Shettima said Tinubu’s administration also undertook repairs on the Jega-Koko-Yauri and Birnin Kebbi-Argungu federal roads to ease journeys.

“But roads alone are not enough without electricity.

“We have increased the capacity of the Birnin Kebbi transmission substation while constructing a 3.5-megawatt solar project in Ambursa to serve homes and businesses,” he said.

On healthcare, he said the Renewed Hope administration of Tinubu upgraded the Federal Medical Centre in Birnin Kebbi to a teaching hospital.

“While primary healthcare centres across the state receive federal support through the Basic Health Care Provision Fund.

“We have also invested in the skills of your young people.

“Mr. President’s economic reforms have increased the revenue available to states to fund their initiatives and projects,” Shettima revealed.

The Vice President said that Kebbi, like other states, struggled to fund its projects.

He assured that the administration would not rest until every kobo earned and saved through “these reforms is invested in your welfare.

“This is why we have come again: to continue what we started about three years ago.

“On 16 January 2027, I trust you to come out en masse and vote for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu.

“On 6 February 2027, I trust you to return Gov. Nasir Idris for a second term. We have so much to do to fix this country, and we must all do our part,” he said.

The post A vote for Tinubu will translate into preservation of the North – Shettima appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: INEC cautions parties, observers against announcing unofficial election results
description:
The Independent National Electoral Commission has warned political parties, election observers and other stakeholders against presenting collated election results independently as officially declared outcomes ahead of the 2027 general elections.
The commission said independent verification of electi
content:
The Independent National Electoral Commission has warned political parties, election observers and other stakeholders against presenting collated election results independently as officially declared outcomes ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The commission said independent verification of election results should complement, rather than undermine, its statutory responsibility for the collation and declaration of election results.

INEC Chairman, Prof Joash Amupitan, stated this on Tuesday at a stakeholder roundtable on Independent Results Tabulation in Abuja, where he was represented by the commission’s Director of Information and Communication Technology, Dr Lawrence Bayode.

Amupitan said the proposed voluntary code of conduct for independent election results tabulation presented an opportunity to strengthen electoral transparency, protect individual rights and reinforce public confidence in election outcomes.

He, however, warned that incomplete, inaccurate or misleading independently collated results could create confusion, heighten political tension and undermine confidence in the electoral process, particularly in an era of instant digital communication.

He said, “Indeed, transparency should not be regarded as a threat to electoral administration; rather, credible independent scrutiny will serve as an additional layer of accountability. However, transparency must be accompanied by responsibility.”

The INEC chairman stressed the need to distinguish between independent verification of election results and the official collation and declaration of results, which he said remained the statutory responsibility of the commission.

He said election observers, political parties, media organisations and other stakeholders were free to collect, analyse and independently verify election information in accordance with the law.

However, he cautioned that independent tabulation must not be presented as a substitute for the commission’s statutory responsibilities, while unofficial projections and privately generated figures must not be communicated as officially declared results.

“The Commission’s position is clear. Independent verification should complement electoral accountability, not create competing centres for statutory authority,” he said.

Amupitan said INEC was strengthening safeguards within its election results management architecture ahead of the 2027 elections.

He listed improvements in the use of the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System, the commission’s results-viewing platform and additional consistency and validation checks to improve the accuracy of polling unit results.

According to him, the measures are designed to ensure that results originate from the appropriate polling units, are accurately documented and remain verifiable throughout the legally prescribed collation process.

He, however, acknowledged that technology alone could not guarantee electoral integrity, stressing the need for sound procedures, trained personnel, effective oversight and informed public participation.

The INEC chairman outlined six principles that should guide the proposed code of conduct, including methodological integrity, verification of election-related information, safeguards against electoral misinformation and adequate cybersecurity measures.

Others are mechanisms for identifying discrepancies and correcting inaccurate publications, as well as broad consultations to ensure that the framework does not compromise the independence of election observers, editorial freedom of media organisations or the lawful participation of political parties.

In his keynote address, the Chairman of the Editorial Board of THISDAY Newspapers, Olusegun Adeniyi, said the period between the conclusion of voting and the official declaration of results was particularly vulnerable to rumours, competing claims and misinformation.

He argued that independent results verification already existed and that the important question was whether it would help narrow the information gap during that period or worsen it.

Adeniyi identified premature declarations, inadequate verification methodologies, artificial intelligence-generated misinformation and the inability of citizens to distinguish between verified results and unofficial projections as major challenges facing independent results tabulation.

He warned that premature victory declarations could be deliberately deployed to mobilise supporters and portray competing claims as evidence of electoral manipulation.

Adeniyi welcomed the voluntary nature of the proposed code, arguing that credible self-regulation by election observers, political parties and media organisations would protect against excessive government regulation.

The post INEC cautions parties, observers against announcing unofficial election results appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: NDLEA busts cocaine syndicate, arrests eight swallowers in Lagos, Kano
description:
From Godwin Tsa, Abuja
The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) says it has dismantled a transnational cartel that moves cocaine from Lagos through Kano and across the desert via Niger Republic and Libya to Europe. Eight suspected members of the syndicate, all drug mules, were arrested in in
content:
From Godwin Tsa, Abuja

The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) says it has dismantled a transnational cartel that moves cocaine from Lagos through Kano and across the desert via Niger Republic and Libya to Europe. Eight suspected members of the syndicate, all drug mules, were arrested in intelligence-led operations in Lagos and Kano.

The suspects were picked up between Friday, 30 October, and Saturday, 31 October 2026. Having swallowed cocaine pellets, they excreted 634 wraps weighing 13.795 kilogrammes over several days in custody.

The operation began on 30 October, when operatives of the agency’s Special Operations Unit arrested the first suspect, 57-year-old Okwudiba Ifeanyichukwu Damian, at Nice Touch Hotel, Ago Palace, Okota, Lagos. He excreted 74 wraps weighing 1.650kg.

The next day, four more suspects were intercepted at the MM2 Terminal of the Murtala Muhammed Airport, Lagos, as they prepared to board a flight to Kano:

Jackson Ahamefule, 43: 90 wraps, 1.950kg; Nwafor Osita Emmanuel, 47: 85 wraps, 1.750kg; Marcel Nnabuike, 38: 75 wraps, 1.655kg; and Onyenwuba Ignatius, 44: 75 wraps, 1.650kg. In all, the five mules arrested in Lagos excreted 399 wraps weighing 8.655kg.

Intelligence from the Lagos operation showed that other members of the cartel had already travelled to Kano. Officers of the agency’s Mallam Aminu Kano International Airport (MAKIA) Command were mobilised and intercepted three suspects at the arrival hall of the airport’s domestic terminal:

Chinweike Ephraim Ifechukwu, 48: 85 pellets, 1.853kg; Edezuno John Nwaorji, 45: 80 pellets, 1.752kg; and Chukwudi Chinaka, 31: 70 pellets, 1.535kg.

Body scans showed that all three had swallowed drugs, and they were placed under excretion observation. The Kano suspects said they planned to travel by road from Kano through Niger Republic to Libya, with Europe as the final destination.

The NDLEA Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, Brig. Gen. Mohamed Marwa (Rtd), commended the officers of the Special Operations Unit and the MAKIA Command for their “intelligence-driven synergy, speed and professionalism,” which he said ensured that none of the eight mules “slipped through our net.”

“This cartel thought it had found a back door to Europe through our northern borders and the Sahara,” he said. “Their arrests are a message to drug barons and their couriers that there is no safe route out of Nigeria. Whether they go by air, by road or through the desert, we will trace them, find them and bring them to justice.”

He appealed to young people not to sell their lives to drug barons. “Swallowing wraps of cocaine is a death wish,” he warned. “One burst pellet can kill a mule before the journey ends. No amount of money is worth that risk.”

title: Iran reports US strikes on Qeshm Island
description:
The United States on Tuesday carried out several attacks on Iran’s southern Island of Qeshm, located in the Strait of Hormuz, a local Iranian official said.
“The American attack on locations on Qeshm island caused no damage to residential, commercial, or infrastructural areas,” said Ahmad Nafisi, de
content:
The United States on Tuesday carried out several attacks on Iran’s southern Island of Qeshm, located in the Strait of Hormuz, a local Iranian official said.

“The American attack on locations on Qeshm island caused no damage to residential, commercial, or infrastructural areas,” said Ahmad Nafisi, deputy provincial governor of the southern province of Hormozgan, quoted by the official IRNA news agency.

“The situation on Qeshm island is under control, and all relief, service, and executive agencies are on full alert,” he added.

“The sounds of five to six explosions were heard on Qeshm on Tuesday evening,” IRNA said.

Earlier in the day Iran’s Revolutionary Guards said they had launched a drone attack targeting a radar system in Bahrain operated by the United States.

“Combat drones belonging to the Revolutionary Guards carried out a precision operation this morning, targeting a radar system operated by US forces at the Sheikh Isa Air Base in Bahrain,” the Guards’ Sepah news website said.

It added that the attack was in response to the “repeated violations of Iranian airspace by US military drones”.

Since the outbreak of the Middle East war in late February, Tehran has attempted to restrict traffic through the strategic waterway, insisting vessels use only routes authorised by the Islamic republic.

It has regularly targeted ships that transit without its authorisation.

The United States has in response imposed a naval blockade on Iranian ports and helped tankers travel the strait, which normally carries about one-fifth of global oil supplies.

In recent weeks, Tehran has made multiple announcements saying ships have caught fire in the strait, often claiming they struck mines.

On Tuesday, the Iranian armed forces said three oil tankers struck naval mines while attempting to transit Hormuz.

The US military recently said it had cleared all mines from the main routes through the waterway.

US Central Command, which oversees US military operations in the region, said last month that it had helped Gulf countries export 1.5 billion barrels of oil via Hormuz since the summer.

AFP

title: Fountain of Life crisis: Trustees release Odukoya’s succession video, name interim leader
description:
The Board of Trustees of The Fountain of Life Church, Lagos, has released a video in which its late founder, Pastor Taiwo Odukoya, named Pastor Kunle Areogun as his successor
In the video, posted by Arise TV and sighted by our correspondent on Tuesday, Odukoya said Areogun should take over if he die
content:
The Board of Trustees of The Fountain of Life Church, Lagos, has released a video in which its late founder, Pastor Taiwo Odukoya, named Pastor Kunle Areogun as his successor

In the video, posted by Arise TV and sighted by our correspondent on Tuesday, Odukoya said Areogun should take over if he dies or becomes incapacitated, while his son, Jimmy, would serve as the successor’s administrative assistant and head of the youth church.

“In case of my demise, which I don’t expect to happen soon, or a situation where I cannot write or talk, please, the next pastor of the church should be Kunle Areogun,” Odukoya said.

He added, “To be his immediate assistant, that is in terms of administration, is Jimmy Odukoya, who will be the head of the youth church.”

The late founder said, “Everything remains the same and that’s laid out in the constitution.”

Odukoya explained that he was making the pronouncement because of an aspect of the constitution they were trying to rework which had not been concluded at the time.

“We’re going to do that, but if for any reason I’m not able to see that through, this is what I do,” he said.

The trustees said the video was recorded in December 2021 at the founder’s request by Jimmy and witnessed by his elder brother, Pastor John Odukoya.

They said they did not see it until late December 2025, more than two years after the founder’s death.

In a statement on Tuesday, the board said it had appointed Pastor Rotimi Okpaise as interim leader pending consultations.

It also reaffirmed its resolution of November 16 that Jimmy was no longer recognised as Senior Pastor of The Fountain of Life Church.

The trustees alleged that Jimmy told the board in 2023 that his father had handed the mantle of leadership to him.

They said the video was not presented when the succession was considered.

PUNCH ONLINE had earlier reported that the church rejected the removal.

In a statement earlier on Tuesday, it described the decision as constitutionally invalid and said Jimmy remains the duly appointed Senior Pastor and Chairman of the Board of Trustees.

The church’s counterstatement also alleged that the trustees behind the decision had been asked to resign in March 2026 over alleged violations of the church’s constitution.

It said Jimmy’s appointment in September 2023 was unanimously approved.

The trustees alleged that the church’s official social media channels had been taken over without the board’s authorisation. They warned the public against treating posts on those platforms as the board’s position.

Jimmy, a Nollywood actor, was announced as senior pastor on September 17, 2023, weeks after his father’s death.

The announcement was made by Okpaise at a church service, and the board said it had unanimously elected him.

He was installed on September 30, 2023, with his sister, Pastor Tolu Odukoya-Ijogun, as associate senior pastor.

The church was founded in 1992 by Pastors Taiwo and Bimbo Odukoya and is headquartered in Ilupeju, Lagos.

title: NDC alleges N11.2trn Pipeline Security  bill exceeds Military budget
description:
Says President Tinubu Presides oover Opaque N11,2 trillion Pipeline Security bill that



Doubles the Entire military budget while Starving of Armed Forces, Security continues to escalate







By Henry Umoru







ABUJA- The Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC has the alarm that  President Bola Tinu
content:
Says President Tinubu Presides oover Opaque N11,2 trillion Pipeline Security bill that

Doubles the Entire military budget while Starving of Armed Forces, Security continues to escalate

By Henry Umoru

ABUJA- The Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC has the alarm that President Bola Tinubu’s administration is presiding over what it termed, an opaque N11.2 trillion pipeline security expenditure, alleging that the amount exceeds Nigeria’s entire defence and security budget.

According to the party, the figure was contained in the audited financial disclosures of the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPCL), which reportedly showed N11.2 trillion in “other receivables from the Federation” linked to energy security costs and what it described as unverified off-budget deductions.

In a statement signed yesterday by the Spokesperson, NDC National Campaign Council, Dr. Chiogo Constance Ikokwu, NDC explained that the amount is more than twice the N4.91 trillion allocated to all defence and security agencies in the 2025 budget and over three times the ₦3.10 trillion appropriated to the Ministry of Defence for the Army, Navy and Air Force.

The NDC further expressed concern over inadequate funding for military equipment, claiming that 75.9 per cent of the 2026 core defence budget of N3.15 trillion was allocated to personnel, while only 14.7 per cent, representing N464 billion, was earmarked for capital weapons as it further alleged that only seven per cent of the 2025 Defence Capital Budget was released, questioning the government’s commitment to adequately equipping the armed forces.

The NDC while calling for what it described as an immediate forensic audit of the ₦11.2 trillion NNPCL energy security balance to establish the amounts paid to private contractors and those arising from legacy deductions, also asked for full disclosure of funds released for military capital equipment and troop welfare in 2025 and 2026.

Ikokwu who questioned the reason for the expenditure at a time when insecurity, including kidnapping, killings and ransom payments, continues to threaten communities across the country, alleged that the huge pipeline security bill raised questions about transparency and accountability in the management of public resources, describing the expenditure as a possible political patronage fund disguised as energy security.

Ikokwu urged Nigerians to vote for the Peter Obi/ Rabiu Kwankwaso ticket to dismantle the criminal system in Nigeria, adding that the ticket believes that Nigeria must work for all, and not a few.

The statement read, “The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) National Campaign Council is deeply concerned about the audited financial disclosures from the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPCL), which reveals an opaque balance sheet of ₦11.2 trillion in “other receivables from the Federation,” tied to energy security costs and unverified off-budget deductions.

“We note that this ₦11.2 trillion claim is more than double the entire ₦4.91 trillion budgeted for all defence and security agencies in 2025, and over triple the ₦3.10 trillion allocated directly to the Ministry of Defence for the Army, Navy, and Air Force combined.

“While insecurity continues to escalate across Nigeria, with citizens abducted, slaughtered on farmlands, and forced to pay crippling ransoms, this administration presides over books showing trillions tied to protecting oil conduits, even as our Armed Forces remain starved of modern weaponry.

“Strip away the accounting jargon, and this ₦11.2 trillion expenditure looks like nothing more than a massive political patronage slush fund disguised as “energy security.” Are patronage pay outs to political allies now worth more than Nigerian lives?

“Securing our pipelines is vital, yet modern energy producers protect assets at a fraction of this cost using fiber-optic sensors, surveillance drones, satellite radar, and transparent Host Community Trusts, while equipping their national military to respond rapidly. Instead of 21st-century technology and empowering our Armed Forces, where 75.9 percent of the 2026 core ₦3.15 trillion budget goes to personnel and only 14.7 percent (₦464 billion) to capital weapons, after just 7 percent of the 2025 Defence Capital Budget was released, this government chose opaque patronage.

“The Nigeria Democratic Congress demands the following: an immediate forensic audit of the ₦11.2 trillion NNPCL energy security balance, exposing every kobo paid to private contractors versus legacy deductions. Second: full disclosure of military releases for capital equipment and troop welfare across 2025 and 2026. Third: an end to off-budget deductions, ensuring all oil revenues enter the Federation Account for National Assembly appropriation.

“A government that prioritizes opaque political patronage over human life while insecurity continues to escalate has lost its moral legitimacy. The NDC urges Nigerians to vote for the Obi/Kwankwaso ticket to dismantle the criminal system in Nigeria. The Obi/Kwankwaso ticket believes that Nigeria must work for all, and not a few.”

Speaking during APC rally
content:

He lauded president Bola Tinubu for providing all the money for projects in the area and solicited votes to reciprocate such gestures

Eno disclosed that the decayed Technical Secondary School in the area would be reconstrucred while Ukam market would be reconstructed and upgraded to modern market ststus in the area .

” This can only be possible if you give your 80,000 votes in 2027 election

Earlier, the Director General of the campaign Ambassador Assam Assam had promised N30m for the people if they could vote for APC in 2027 election.

” If you vote APC next year , I promise you N30m .Just vote , we would do our own part of the bargain”

title: Kwara suspends hospital CMD for locking out patients
description:
The Kwara State Government has suspended the Chief Medical Director of the Children’s Specialist Hospital, Centre Igboro, Ilorin, Mosunmola Folorunsho, following complaints that patients and their caregivers were locked out of the facility over a shortage of medical personnel.
The suspension followe
content:
The Kwara State Government has suspended the Chief Medical Director of the Children’s Specialist Hospital, Centre Igboro, Ilorin, Mosunmola Folorunsho, following complaints that patients and their caregivers were locked out of the facility over a shortage of medical personnel.

The suspension followed an emergency visit to the hospital by the Executive Secretary of the Kwara State Hospitals Management Board, Dr Abdulraheem Malik, and members of the management team to investigate the circumstances surrounding the incident.

In a statement issued on Tuesday by the board’s Press Secretary, Adamu Sabi, the management said the CMD had also been issued a query to explain her role in the incident within 48 hours.

The board further directed the suspended medical director to hand over the administration of the hospital to the most senior doctor pending further directives.

Explaining the circumstances that led to the disruption, the management said its findings showed that the hospital experienced a temporary shortage of doctors after one of the medical personnel scheduled for morning duty was absent to attend a malaria-related training programme.

The absence, according to the statement, contributed to a backlog of patients awaiting medical attention at the facility.

“The Executive Secretary directed the immediate deployment of a doctor from the Board’s pool of medical personnel to fill the gap pending the return of the doctor from training,” the statement read.

Malik also warned the hospital management against preventing patients and their caregivers from accessing the facility, regardless of operational challenges.

“Under no circumstances should the hospital gate be locked in a manner that prevents patients and their caregivers from entering the facility,” the statement quoted the Executive Secretary as directing.

The board attributed the staffing challenge partly to the increasing number of patients seeking medical attention at the hospital, adding that steps were being taken to address the manpower shortage.

According to the statement, the state government had recently approved the recruitment of additional healthcare workers, including doctors and other medical professionals, to strengthen service delivery across public health facilities.

The management, while expressing regret over the inconvenience suffered by affected patients and their caregivers, assured residents that the hospital remained operational and that immediate steps had been taken to prevent a recurrence.

It added that the welfare and safety of patients, particularly children, remained a priority, promising to strengthen staff deployment, monitoring and supervision across its facilities.

The board also reaffirmed its commitment to accountability, professionalism and strict adherence to administrative procedures, urging residents to continue accessing medical services at the Children’s Specialist Hospital without fear of interruption.

The post Kwara suspends hospital CMD for locking out patients appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Why Customs delayed announcing arms seizures – CG
description: Comptroller-General of the Nigeria Customs Service, Dr Bashir Adeniyi, on Tuesday said the NCS deliberately withheld immediate public disclosure of major arms seizures, including the interception of 844 rifles at Onne Port in June 2024, to avoid jeopardising investigations, releasing inaccurate info
content:
Comptroller-General of the Nigeria Customs Service, Dr Bashir Adeniyi, on Tuesday said the NCS deliberately withheld immediate public disclosure of major arms seizures, including the interception of 844 rifles at Onne Port in June 2024, to avoid jeopardising investigations, releasing inaccurate information and exposing innocent persons to wrongful accusations.

He disclosed this at the Global Alliance World Public Relations Forum in Abuja.

Adeniyi explained that the pressure to speak immediately after security operations could undermine investigations if officials announced unverified figures, made premature accusations or disclosed the identities of persons who had not been properly investigated.

He cited the interception of 844 rifles concealed in a consignment at Onne Port in June 2024 and the subsequent discovery of another 399 rifles in a separate operation as examples of incidents that required careful handling of information.

According to him, the Service adopted a procedure of confirming facts, coordinating with relevant security agencies and ensuring that public statements were consistent before addressing the media.

He said, “In moments like this, the pressure to speak immediately is enormous, and social media will not wait for you. But a wrong figure, a careless accusation or a premature name can damage an investigation and hurt innocent people.

“So our rule is clear. We confirm the facts, we coordinate with security agencies, and then we speak with one voice.”

The Customs chief said the Service also ensured that its public briefing went beyond displaying the recovered weapons to explaining the potential national security implications of allowing them to fall into the wrong hands.

He said the approach was intended to turn enforcement successes into public reassurance while protecting the credibility of the Service.

“When we did the public briefing, we did not only display the weapons. We explained what could have gone wrong if this had fallen into wrong hands. This is how an enforcement success becomes public reassurance.

“Speed matters, but accuracy is what keeps your credibility for the next crisis,” Adeniyi said.

The Customs boss made the remarks while sharing communication lessons from the Service’s operations and reform initiatives, stressing that effective communication should be treated as a deliberate strategy rather than an afterthought.

He identified the need to verify information before speaking as one of the major lessons the Service learnt from its anti-smuggling operations, particularly those involving sensitive security matters.

Adeniyi also cited the introduction of the B’Odogwu Unified Management System as an example of the importance of preparing stakeholders before implementing major reforms.

He said the Service learnt that the technological aspect of replacing its old cargo clearance platform was easier than managing the transition for importers, licensed agents, terminal operators, government agencies and Customs officers accustomed to the previous system.

He explained that the NCS organised training sessions for agents, established help desks and introduced the platform in phases to minimise disruptions.

“We knew that if we simply switched it on one Monday morning, we would have queues, complaints and headlines by Wednesday. So we went for training before the switch. We held sessions with agents. We opened up the help desk and rolled out in phases, one command at a time.

“We also spoke to our officers first. This is often forgotten. If the officer at the terminal cannot explain a new process with confidence, no press release will save you,” he said.

Adeniyi disclosed that the African Continental Free Trade Area Secretariat prescribed B’Odogwu as a model for other African countries in August.

He said the experience reinforced the need to ensure that reforms were understood and trusted by the people expected to use them.

The Customs chief also recalled the Service’s decision to publish findings from its Time Release Study, which showed that clearing goods at Nigerian ports took about five days, with more than 90 per cent of the period spent on idle time.

He said the Service could have kept the findings confidential to avoid criticism but chose transparency because identifying the problem was necessary to address it.

“Some would have advised us to keep the report in the drawer. We chose to publish it because you cannot fix a problem you are afraid to name,” he said.

Adeniyi explained that Customs was not solely responsible for delays and costs at the ports, noting that terminal operators, shipping lines and other regulatory agencies also contributed to the clearance process.

He said evidence-based communication allowed the Service to acknowledge its shortcomings while holding other stakeholders accountable for their respective responsibilities.

The Customs boss identified the introduction of the Authorised Economic Operator programme as another lesson in using communication to encourage compliance.

The post Why Customs delayed announcing arms seizures – CG appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Army Arrests Seven Suspects, Recovers 38 Phones, Mercedes-Benz In Plateau
description: Troops of Sector 1, Joint Task Force, Operation Enduring Peace, have arrested seven suspected criminals and recovered 38 mobile phones, a Mercedes-Benz E350, a motorcycle and other items in separate operations in Jos North Local Government Area of Plateau State.The spokesperson for the Joint Task Fo
content:
Troops of Sector 1, Joint Task Force, Operation Enduring Peace, have arrested seven suspected criminals and recovered 38 mobile phones, a Mercedes-Benz E350, a motorcycle and other items in separate operations in Jos North Local Government Area of Plateau State.

The spokesperson for the Joint Task Force, Captain Chinonso Oteh, disclosed this while presenting the suspects at the task force headquarters in Jos, where he gave details of the operations.

According to the task force, the arrests followed intelligence-led operations conducted on November 6 and 10, 2026, as part of efforts to curb armed robbery, phone snatching and other criminal activities in the state.

In the first operation, troops acted on a report of a phone-snatching incident involving a gunman. The report led to the identification of the location of the stolen phone at Prime House Hotel, along Ring Road, Jos North.

A raid on the hotel resulted in the arrest of five suspects.

Items recovered during the operation included 26 mobile phones, 27 phone pouches, three MP3 devices, two earpods, an HP laptop, a dagger, four power banks and a Mercedes-Benz E350 with registration number Plateau BBK-01NB.

The task force said a further search of the suspects’ vehicle, after it was towed to the Sector 1 headquarters, led to the recovery of 12 additional mobile phones, bringing the total number of phones recovered in the operation to 38.

In a separate operation on November 10, troops deployed at Naraguta, working with members of the Vigilante Group of Nigeria, arrested two more suspects during a routine patrol.

The suspects were reportedly found with a suspected stolen Boxer motorcycle and a toy pistol.

The task force said the seven suspects and the recovered items would be handed over to the Plateau State Police Command for further investigation and possible prosecution.

The Commander of Operation Enduring Peace, Major General Maxwell Dangana, reaffirmed the task force’s commitment to combating crime and sustaining peace across its joint operations area.

He said the task force would continue to rely on intelligence-driven operations and collaboration with other security agencies and local vigilante groups to tackle criminal activities.

Dangana also urged residents to remain vigilant and provide credible and timely information to security agencies to support efforts to restore and sustain lasting peace in Plateau State.

The post Army Arrests Seven Suspects, Recovers 38 Phones, Mercedes-Benz In Plateau appeared first on Channels Television.

title: AFCON 2027: Super Eagles held to goalless draw by Tanzania
description:
Nigeria’s Super Eagles were held to a 0-0 draw by Tanzania in their 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying match in Zanzibar on Tuesday, missing the chance to consolidate their position in Group L.
The Eagles dominated much of the first half and created several scoring opportunities but were let down
content:
Nigeria’s Super Eagles were held to a 0-0 draw by Tanzania in their 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying match in Zanzibar on Tuesday, missing the chance to consolidate their position in Group L.

The Eagles dominated much of the first half and created several scoring opportunities but were let down by poor finishing.

Tolu Arokodare came closest to breaking the deadlock in the 34th minute when his low effort beat the Tanzanian goalkeeper but struck the post.

Moses Usor also tested the hosts’ goalkeeper four minutes later, forcing him to go down and parry his effort, while Fisayo Dele-Bashiru fired wide from outside the penalty area.

Arokodare also failed to find the target with another attempt as Nigeria went into the break without a goal.

The hosts grew more adventurous after the restart, with Kibu Denis sending two efforts wide from the right side of the penalty area in the opening 10 minutes of the second half.

Seeking a breakthrough, Super Eagles coach Eric Chelle introduced Alex Iwobi and Akor Adams for Taiwo Awoniyi and Dele-Bashiru in the 61st minute.

Tochukwu and Alhassan Yusuf later replaced Wilfred Ndidi and Usor in the 73rd minute as Nigeria continued to press for a winner.

Adams and Bassey had opportunities in the closing stages, but neither could convert, while Arokodare also missed the target in the 85th minute.

The draw followed Nigeria’s 3-1 victory over Tanzania in Friday’s first leg at the Godswill Akpabio International Stadium in Uyo. Alhassan Yusuf opened the scoring before Arokodare struck twice in the second half.

Before Tuesday’s encounter, Nigeria had six points from three matches, one behind Group L leaders Guinea-Bissau, who had drawn 1-1 with Madagascar.

Tanzania have already qualified for the 2027 tournament as co-hosts, leaving Nigeria, Guinea-Bissau and Madagascar to contest the group’s remaining qualifying place.

The 2027 AFCON will be jointly hosted by Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda from June 19 to July 17.

The post AFCON 2027: Super Eagles held to goalless draw by Tanzania appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.
