title: United Nigeria Airlines’ false weather excuse worsened Asaba diversion crisis, Okonkwo admits
description:
• Says communication team failed to verify facts before issuing statement; insists truth, not reputation management, is best PR strategy
Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of United Nigeria Airlines, Obiora Okonkwo, has admitted that the airline’s attempt to manage public perception following an i
content:
• Says communication team failed to verify facts before issuing statement; insists truth, not reputation management, is best PR strategy

Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of United Nigeria Airlines, Obiora Okonkwo, has admitted that the airline’s attempt to manage public perception following an incident in which one of its aircraft landed in Asaba instead of Abuja was worsened by a false explanation issued by its communication team.

Okonkwo said the airline’s communication team, in an attempt to protect the company’s reputation, attributed the incident to bad weather in Abuja, despite the fact that the aircraft had landed in Asaba because of an error in its flight documentation.

He said the explanation, which was not properly verified before being released, triggered widespread criticism and ridicule on social media and in international media, turning what could have been a manageable operational error into a major reputational crisis.

The airline chairman spoke during a high-level dialogue on Responsible Business Communication: Building Trust and Financing Investments for Sustainable Human Development at the 2026 World Public Relations Forum (WPRF) in Abuja.

Recounting the incident, Okonkwo explained that the aircraft was scheduled to fly from Lagos to Abuja but landed in Asaba following an error by the dispatcher, who mistakenly entered Asaba as the destination in the flight documentation.

He said the pilots followed the destination indicated in the documents and landed accordingly, while the cabin crew, believing they had arrived in Abuja, welcomed passengers to the Federal Capital Territory.

According to him, the incident itself was not necessarily a major crisis until the airline’s communication team issued an inaccurate explanation.

“Our own communication team, in a little bit to protect us or probably not verify, just quickly came out with a statement that the aircraft went to Asaba because there was bad weather in Abuja,” he said.

“That’s just a lie because of it that naturally, took over all the whole airways because the weather was as good as just anything you can imagine.”

Okonkwo said the false explanation gave critics more ammunition, with the incident attracting widespread attention, including comic satire and reports in different languages.

He argued that proper verification and a truthful explanation would have spared the airline the additional reputational damage.

“I really think that if a little bit of verification was done and if the truth was told, it probably would have put us in a better position and saved us some trouble,” he said.

The airline chief maintained that organisations must not confuse reputation protection with withholding or manipulating facts, warning that attempts to conceal the truth could eventually cause greater damage than the original crisis.

“The best way of public relations is to tell the truth, but tell it responsibly,” he said.

He added that telling verified truths demonstrated respect for stakeholders and helped build confidence in an organisation, irrespective of how uncomfortable the information might be.

Okonkwo also cited another experience involving a passenger who threatened never to fly United Nigeria Airlines again, not because of a delayed flight but because the airline departed earlier than its advertised time.

He said the passenger complained that the airline had advertised an 11.30 a.m. departure but took off at 11.20 a.m.

Recounting his response, he said: “I wanted to get angry, I wanted to shout back at him, but again my experience being a member of this forum came into play and I simply sent him a message. I apologise for United Nigeria leaving on time.”

He said the experience illustrated the importance of understanding customer expectations and communicating appropriately, even when complaints appeared unusual.

Reacting to the incident, Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, said building public trust sometimes required organisations and government institutions to adhere strictly to communicated timelines, whether they were delivering earlier or later than expected.

He said the passenger’s complaint was a reminder that organisations must explain deviations from what they had communicated, even when such deviations appeared to be positive.

“Sometimes building trust requires that you be on time, not earlier and not later. And if you go earlier than you communicated previously, you must explain,” Oyedele said.

Drawing a parallel with government revenue performance, the minister said some departments under the Ministry of Finance occasionally exceeded their revenue targets without providing explanations.

He said where an agency projected revenue of 10 but generated 12, it was important to establish whether the original target was too conservative or whether the additional revenue was a one-off occurrence.

“I need to know whether your 10 was too conservative. Maybe it should have been 15. I also need to know whether this extra 2 is sustainable or whether it’s one-off,” he said.

The minister’s intervention reinforced the importance of transparency and accountability in institutional communication, stressing that stakeholders deserved explanations for outcomes that differed from prior commitments.

Okonkwo, who welcomed the inclusion of private-sector representatives in discussions on responsible communication, stressed that communication must go hand in hand with service delivery.

He said organisations could not rely on strategic communication to compensate for failures in delivering on their promises.

His remarks formed part of discussions involving the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele; Director of External Affairs at the World Bank Group, Edith Jibunoh; and Founder of Honor Public Relations, United Kingdom, Sharon Ezzeldin.

The session was moderated by Kyembe Kyalusanza, Head of Corporate Communications at Zambia National Commercial Bank (Zanaco).

The post United Nigeria Airlines’ false weather excuse worsened Asaba diversion crisis, Okonkwo admits appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: ‘I will vote for Tinubu in 2027’ — Ex-NFF President Amaju Pinnick
description:
Former Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) president Amaju Pinnick has declared his intention to vote for President Bola Tinubu in the 2027 general election, citing what he described as improvements in sports administration and his desire to see Nigeria remain united.
Pinnick, who is the Deputy Chairp
content:
Former Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) president Amaju Pinnick has declared his intention to vote for President Bola Tinubu in the 2027 general election, citing what he described as improvements in sports administration and his desire to see Nigeria remain united.

Pinnick, who is the Deputy Chairperson of the FIFA Men’s National Teams Competition Committee, made the declaration during an interview on Arise News on Tuesday.

He praised the Tinubu administration for what he described as the appointment of capable individuals to key positions in the sports sector, specifically mentioning the leadership of Shehu Dikko and Bukola Olopade.

According to him, the appointments and preparations for major international competitions, including the Commonwealth Games and Olympic Games, show that the government is taking the right steps in sports administration.

“This is the first time in a long time that we are getting sports administration right through appointments into leadership roles, Shehu Dikko and Bukola Olopade. The Tinubu administration is doing the right thing, and you can see it from the Commonwealth Games to the Olympic Games; they are getting it right,” Pinnick said.

The former NFF president also linked his support for Tinubu to the First Lady, Oluremi Tinubu’s Itsekiri heritage, saying it was one of the factors influencing his position.

Pinnick expressed confidence that the Itsekiri community would deliver at least 500,000 votes for the President in the 2027 election.

“I am 100% convinced that the Itsekiris will deliver at least 500,000 votes to Tinubu’s re-election. Some may be subjective, and some may be objective; the subjective ones are because Remi Tinubu is Itsekiri.

“The truth is that we are a very fragile nation, and I love Nigeria. I want Nigeria to be one,” he said.

Pinnick’s remarks come as political activities gradually gather momentum ahead of the 2027 general election, with public figures declaring their positions on the next presidential contest.

title: COP31: Tinubu seeks cheaper climate financing for developing nations
description: President Bola Tinubu has called for increased concessional climate financing and lower borrowing costs for developing countries, warning that the global climate finance ambition of mobilising at least $1.3tn annually by 2035 must translate into affordable and accessible funding for vulnerable econo
content:
President Bola Tinubu has called for increased concessional climate financing and lower borrowing costs for developing countries, warning that the global climate finance ambition of mobilising at least $1.3tn annually by 2035 must translate into affordable and accessible funding for vulnerable economies.

Tinubu said the high cost of capital confronting developing countries was undermining their ability to implement climate programmes, strengthen resilience and accelerate the transition to cleaner energy.

The President made the call in Nigeria’s national statement delivered by the Minister of Environment, Balarabe Lawal, at the resumed high-level segment of the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference in Antalya, Türkiye, on Tuesday.

High-level meetings at the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) resumed on Tuesday, November 17, in Antalya, Türkiye, following the two-day Antalya Leaders’ Summit held on November 11 and 12.

In his speech delivered before the COP 31 President, Murat Kurum and other heads of states, he urged the international community to ensure that the Fund for Responding to Loss and Damage provided timely and meaningful assistance to countries suffering the consequences of climate change.

The demand comes amid growing concerns among developing countries over the gap between international climate finance commitments and the availability of affordable funding to implement national climate action plans.

Tinubu said climate action must be aligned with the development priorities of individual countries, particularly in areas of energy access, food security, industrialisation, employment and improved livelihoods.

He maintained that Nigeria’s energy transition must reflect its economic realities, insisting that the country would continue to expand renewable energy while using natural gas as a transition fuel to support energy security and electricity access.

“For Nigeria, the energy transition must be just, inclusive and responsive to national circumstances. Nigeria remains committed to expanding renewable energy deployment while safeguarding energy security and improving access to affordable and reliable electricity. Natural gas will continue to serve as an important transition fuel within our energy mix,” he said.

The President highlighted Nigeria’s adaptation efforts, including the submission of its National Adaptation Plan in September 2026, which outlines interventions in climate-resilient agriculture, early-warning systems and disaster preparedness for vulnerable communities.

He said the plan incorporated climate risk analysis, economic appraisal, sector strategies and financing approaches to strengthen the country’s capacity to respond to climate-related challenges.

On efforts to attract private investment into clean energy, Tinubu disclosed that Nigeria commercially launched a `$300m Distributed Renewable Energy Fund in September to mobilise capital for expanding access to reliable electricity.

He added that the Federal Government was strengthening its national carbon market framework and exploring opportunities under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement to mobilise additional resources for domestic climate action.

Article 6 provides a framework for countries to cooperate through carbon markets and other mechanisms to achieve their emissions-reduction targets under the global climate agreement.

However, Tinubu argued that domestic initiatives alone would not provide the scale of financing required to address the climate crisis, calling for stronger international cooperation and more accessible funding mechanisms.

“National initiatives alone cannot deliver the scale of transformation required. The global ambition to mobilise at least US$1.3 trillion annually in climate finance by 2035 must translate into accessible and affordable resources, particularly for developing countries.

“We call for increased concessional financing and reduced costs of capital confronting developing economies. We must ensure that the Fund for responding to Loss and Damage delivers timely and meaningful assistance to affected countries,” he said.

The President urged world leaders to make COP31 a turning point in the implementation of climate commitments, arguing that climate ambition must be matched with financing and measurable outcomes.

“COP31 must mark a decisive turning point in the global climate response. We must strengthen the alignment between climate ambition, financing and implementation, ensure that investments translate into tangible benefits for communities and foster partnerships that deliver lasting and meaningful outcomes,” he stated.

He reaffirmed Nigeria’s commitment to multilateral climate cooperation, urging participating countries to move beyond pledges towards practical interventions that would improve resilience and support sustainable development.

“Let Antalya be remembered as the moment the world moved decisively from commitment to implementation, and from investment to resilience, prosperity and shared development,” Tinubu said.

COP31, hosted by Türkiye in Antalya, has brought together governments, development institutions, climate negotiators, businesses and civil society organisations to deliberate on global climate action, including financing, adaptation, energy transition and the implementation of the Paris Agreement.

The resumed high-level segment on November 17 and 18 provides an opportunity for ministers and senior government representatives to present their countries’ positions and push for political agreement on outstanding climate priorities.

The resumption comes as negotiations enter a critical phase ahead of the conference’s November 20 closing date. Delegates are working to bridge disagreements over climate finance, adaptation funding, the transition away from fossil fuels, renewable energy and the proposed target of increasing electricity’s share of global energy use to 35 per cent by 2035.

The post COP31: Tinubu seeks cheaper climate financing for developing nations appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Tinubu Approves Establishment Of Kebbi Inland Dry Port
description: President Bola Tinubu has approved the establishment of an inland dry port in Kebbi State as part of efforts to boost economic activities and improve trade in the state.The President announced the approval on Tuesday during the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally in Birnin Ke
content:
President Bola Tinubu has approved the establishment of an inland dry port in Kebbi State as part of efforts to boost economic activities and improve trade in the state.

The President announced the approval on Tuesday during the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally in Birnin Kebbi, the state capital.

He also pledged to approve additional road infrastructure projects for the state following requests by Governor Nasir Idris.

The rally, held at the Birnin Kebbi Stadium, attracted thousands of APC supporters who gathered to express their support for Tinubu’s re-election bid ahead of the 2027 presidential election.

Vice President Kashim Shettima and other party leaders were also present at the event, which featured speeches and goodwill messages from party chieftains.

Speaking at the rally, Governor Idris expressed satisfaction with the turnout and pledged that Kebbi State would deliver 100 per cent of its votes to Tinubu in the 2027 election.

Also addressing the crowd, the Director-General of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Abdulazeez Yari, said the President had done much for the North-West, including Kebbi State.

Yari attributed the large turnout to Tinubu’s acceptance in the region, citing the Sokoto-Badagry Superhighway project, which he said would pass through more than 200 kilometres of Kebbi State.

In his remarks, Shettima urged residents of the North to support Tinubu’s re-election, recalling the President’s support for the late President Muhammadu Buhari, who governed Nigeria for eight years.

He said Tinubu had stood by Buhari during his political journey and throughout his administration.

Taking the podium, Tinubu thanked the people of Kebbi for their support and commended Governor Idris for his leadership.

He subsequently announced the approval of some federal projects requested by the governor, including the establishment of the Kebbi Inland Dry Port.

The rally also featured goodwill messages from the Speaker of the House of Representatives, the Deputy President of the Senate and other APC leaders and supporters.

title: ‎FG launches CNG stations in four varsities
description:
By Chidi Ndaa







‎TO ease the transport challenges of varsity students, staff and host communities, the Federal Government on Tuesday inaugurated Compressed Natural Gas Stations in four universities.



The CNG stations are located at the University of Uyo (Akwa Ibom State), University of Nsukka
content:
By Chidi Ndaa

‎TO ease the transport challenges of varsity students, staff and host communities, the Federal Government on Tuesday inaugurated Compressed Natural Gas Stations in four universities.

The CNG stations are located at the University of Uyo (Akwa Ibom State), University of Nsukka (Enugu State), Federal University of Petroleum Resources, Effurun (Delta State), and the University of Calabar (Cross River State).

‎The Minister of State, Petroleum Resources (Gas), Ekperikpe Ekpo, said the scheme was aimed at ensuring that students, staff and members of the host communities enjoyed cheap transportation to their various destinations.

Ekpo, who launched the scheme at UNIUYO, added that CNG was generally cheaper than petrol and diesel, offering motorists within the communities the opportunity to spend less on cleaner fuel.

The minister hailed President Bola Tinubu for his (Tinubu) Renewed Hope Agenda, which has placed natural gas at the heart of the country’s economic renewal programme.

Ekpo disclosed that the President had also approved the Special Palliative Relief on University Transportation Programme.

According to him, the programme is in line with the 20 Universities CNG Ecosystem Initiative to mitigate the effect of petroleum subsidy reform on students and staff.

He said, “For students, young people who earn a living from commercial transport, and vulnerable members of society who depend on public transport, these savings mean lower transport costs and more money kept in their pockets for education, enterprise, food and other household needs.”

“The benefits of adopting CNG for mobility are practical and immediate. CNG is generally cheaper than petrol and diesel, so vehicle owners, commercial drivers and transport operators spend less on fuel.

‎“Under the watch of Mr President, gas is no longer a resource we merely flare or export; it is a resource we are using to power our vehicles, create jobs and put money back in the pockets of our people.”.

Thanking the governors of Akwa Ibom, Cross River, Enugu and Delta states for deepening the penetration of natural gas in their states, Ekpo hailed the Minister of Education, Dr. Tunji Alausa, for backing the scheme.

He pointed out that the scheme was connecting educational institutions with national energy priorities.

‎The Executive Director of the Midstream and Downstream Gas Infrastructure Fund, Oluwole Adama, said the newly inaugurated CNG stations in Uyo, Calabar, Enugu and Warri could fill about 540 vehicles every day.

Adama said, “For students, affordable and dependable transport means more than a cheaper ride. It can mean getting to lectures on time, spending less on daily travel and having more time and energy for learning,” he said.

‎He stated that the facilities could become living classrooms that would offer young Nigerians practical exposure to gas operations, engineering, safety and maintenance.

‎He added, “About 50 more projects will be nearing commissioning by the end of this year. I urge transport operators and businesses to use the facilities judiciously. Our young Nigerians should embrace these opportunities in technical services, safety and maintenance”, he stated.

title: MSMEs face $4tn financing gap in developing countries – World Bank
description:
Micro, small and medium-sized enterprises in developing economies face a $4tn financing gap, limiting their ability to expand operations and create jobs, the World Bank Group said in a news release on Tuesday.
The funding shortfall, estimated over the 2019 to 2023 period, highlights the difficulty s
content:
Micro, small and medium-sized enterprises in developing economies face a $4tn financing gap, limiting their ability to expand operations and create jobs, the World Bank Group said in a news release on Tuesday.

The funding shortfall, estimated over the 2019 to 2023 period, highlights the difficulty smaller businesses face in securing credit despite their importance to employment and economic activity in emerging markets and developing economies.

According to the lender, MSMEs account for about 90 per cent of businesses and 75 per cent of workers in these economies, making access to finance a key factor in efforts to support private-sector growth and absorb millions of young people entering the labour market.

The bank said about 1.2 billion young people would reach working age in the next 10 to 15 years, increasing pressure on developing economies to create employment opportunities. Improving access to finance for smaller businesses could help them expand and take on more workers.

The financier’s findings show that formal loans can have a significant effect on business performance. Firms that obtain such credit record an average 12 per cent increase in employment, while sales and profits rise by about 18 per cent.

“MSMEs face four major constraints to growth: they are invisible to financial systems because they lack a digital footprint of their transactions, disconnected from markets and services, burdened by regulatory complexity, and chronically underfinanced,” the World Bank Group’s Vice President for Prosperity, Pablo Saavedra said.

He said the institution’s new MSME strategy would use its financing alongside private lenders and investors to increase credit access for businesses with the greatest potential to grow.

The strategy, launched in October 2026, seeks to address barriers that prevent smaller firms from accessing capital and connecting with markets. It includes the use of data and digital tools to improve businesses’ visibility to lenders, as well as support for banks, fintech companies and governments.

The World Bank plans to deploy risk-sharing arrangements and equity investments to encourage lending and investment in smaller businesses. It also intends to work with governments to reduce regulatory obstacles, with particular attention to fragile and conflict-affected countries where access to finance is often more constrained.

The financing challenge is part of a wider set of concerns about the resilience of financial systems in developing economies, according to the World Bank’s Finance and Prosperity 2026 report.

The report examines how financial sectors are performing amid the effects of conflict in the Middle East on commodity prices, financial conditions and market volatility. It points to uneven resilience across markets and highlights risks associated with sovereign debt exposure among banks.

The bank said stronger prudential supervision and effective safety nets were important to maintaining financial stability as economies navigate external shocks and changing market conditions.

The report also draws attention to the limited availability of insurance protection in developing regions. In parts of Africa, Asia and Latin America, more than 80 per cent of financial losses recorded over the past decade were uninsured, leaving households, businesses and governments exposed to the cost of disasters.

It recommends measures to reduce risks and expand access to affordable disaster insurance, arguing that stronger protection could help limit the economic damage caused by climate-related and other shocks.

The World Bank’s focus on MSME financing reflects the wider challenge facing developing economies: turning the large share of economic activity accounted for by smaller businesses into sustainable employment and growth. Without better access to capital, many firms may struggle to invest, expand, and take advantage of opportunities in their markets.

The post MSMEs face $4tn financing gap in developing countries – World Bank appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: ICPC seeks stronger African cooperation on stolen asset recovery
description:
The Chairman of the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission, Dr Musa Aliyu, SAN, has called on African countries to strengthen collaboration and institutional cooperation to tackle illicit financial flows and recover assets stolen through corruption.
Aliyu made the call o
content:
The Chairman of the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission, Dr Musa Aliyu, SAN, has called on African countries to strengthen collaboration and institutional cooperation to tackle illicit financial flows and recover assets stolen through corruption.

Aliyu made the call on Tuesday at the First General Assembly of the African Asset Recovery Practitioners Forum, held in Abuja, where he described asset recovery as a critical tool in the fight against corruption and the promotion of sustainable development.

The assembly was held under the theme, “From Commitment to Action.”

The ICPC chairman, who also chairs the Forum’s Interim Steering Council, said Africa could not afford to lose resources needed to improve the living conditions of its people.

He said, “Every asset lost to corruption represents a development opportunity denied to Africa and its people.”

Aliyu called for a coordinated and sustained approach to tackling illicit financial flows through effective asset recovery mechanisms, stronger institutional collaboration and enhanced cooperation among African countries.

Declaring the assembly open, the Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, Lateef Fagbemi, SAN, described illicit financial flows as a major obstacle to Africa’s development.

Fagbemi said the continent continued to lose resources that could have been invested in improving the welfare of its citizens.

He stressed that Africa’s progress should not be measured by commitments and policy declarations alone but by tangible results and their impact on people’s lives.

The Attorney-General called for effective mechanisms to freeze, confiscate and manage recovered assets, while emphasising the need for information sharing, international cooperation and capacity building.

Similarly, the Head of Development Cooperation at the German Embassy, Dr Karen Jansen, expressed concern over the enormous resources Africa continued to lose through illicit financial flows.

She said recovering the stolen resources was essential to financing development, improving citizens’ welfare and restoring public confidence in governance.

Jansen also called for stronger international partnerships and sustained cooperation to improve Africa’s capacity to trace, freeze and recover assets acquired through illicit means.

The Chairperson of the African Union Advisory Board Against Corruption, Kwami Edem Senanu, said the successful commencement of the first general assembly demonstrated the benefits of unity, shared responsibility and cooperation among African countries.

Senanu commended Nigeria for supporting and championing the Common African Position on Asset Recovery (CAPAR), urging stakeholders to translate existing commitments into practical actions and stronger institutional engagement.

The Head of the Political Affairs, Peace and Security Department of the African Union Commission, Ambassador Bankole Adeoye, represented by Isiaka Garba, said the initiative was designed to move Africa’s asset recovery commitments beyond policy declarations to measurable results.

In his keynote address, titled “From Commitment to Action: Enhancing Africa’s Asset Recovery Architecture through Effective Implementation of the Common African Position on Asset Recovery (CAPAR),” Abdullahi Shehu Yibaikwal said asset freezing and confiscation must be firmly rooted in law.

He emphasised the need to respect due process and the right to a fair hearing, noting that transparency, legitimacy and public trust were essential to successful asset recovery efforts.

Yibaikwal also proposed a four-pillar framework to strengthen the implementation of CAPAR and translate the continent’s commitments into concrete outcomes.

The assembly comes amid growing concerns over the scale of financial resources Africa continues to lose through illicit financial flows.

Estimates indicate that the continent lost as much as 150bn.

In response to the challenge, the African Union Assembly adopted CAPAR in February 2020 as a continental framework for strengthening the identification, tracing, freezing, confiscation and return of assets acquired through illicit means.

A major highlight of the assembly was a high-level panel discussion moderated by a former ICPC chairman, Ekpo Nta, on the theme, “From Commitment to Action: What Will It Take to Make CAPAR Work?”

Participants examined challenges confronting asset recovery efforts, including institutional weaknesses, limited cooperation among agencies and difficulties in securing international assistance.

They called for stronger institutional capacity, improved inter-agency collaboration and effective mechanisms to ensure that recovered assets were transparently managed and channelled towards development.

The stakeholders maintained that Africa must move beyond declarations and political commitments to effective implementation, stressing that recovered assets should ultimately benefit citizens and advance sustainable development across the continent.

title: Nigeria records highest pipeline availability in 20 years – NNPC
description: Nigeria has recorded 100 per cent availability of its major oil and gas pipelines over the past 18 months for the first time in two decades, the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited has said, attributing the improvement to enhanced security coordination, collaboration with host communities an
content:
Nigeria has recorded 100 per cent availability of its major oil and gas pipelines over the past 18 months for the first time in two decades, the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited has said, attributing the improvement to enhanced security coordination, collaboration with host communities and increased stakeholder engagement.

The development comes as the national oil company seeks greater private-sector investment in pipeline infrastructure, warning that Nigeria’s ambitions to expand gas utilisation, improve electricity generation and accelerate industrialisation depend on reliable transportation networks.

NNPCL also disclosed that the 640-kilometre Ajaokuta-Kaduna-Kano gas pipeline project was about 95 per cent complete, with gas delivery to Abuja expected before the end of 2026, followed by Kaduna and Kano states.

The Head of NNPC Gas, Audu Ibrahim, who represented the Group Chief Executive Officer, Bashir Ojulari, disclosed this at the opening of the Nigeria International Pipeline Technology and Security Conference 2026 in Abuja on Tuesday.

The conference, organised by the Pipelines Professionals Association of Nigeria, was themed ‘Financing the Future: Unlocking Capital for Resilient Pipeline Infrastructure in Nigeria.’

Speaking on the importance of pipeline infrastructure, Ojulari said the availability of transportation networks determined the performance of the entire oil and gas value chain, from production to processing, power generation and distribution.

“Pipelines are central to the energy business. Without reliable transportation, resources cannot reach the people and industries that need them. Without availability, there would be no value chain.

“We often speak of upstream, midstream, and downstream as separate worlds. In reality, they form one connected system. A gas field that cannot reach the power plants is stranded potential. A refinery without pipelines cannot operate. A petrochemical plant without reliable gas cannot support our economy. A country that cannot move energy cannot industrialise,” he said.

He said the company’s experience had shown that no single organisation could unlock Nigeria’s energy potential without partnerships among resource owners, operators, investors, technology providers, regulators and host communities.

According to him, NNPCL is working to connect capital, technology, policy, talent and markets to develop an integrated energy value chain.

On pipeline security, Ibrahim said the country had achieved availability levels of between 95 and 100 per cent on major pipelines over the past 18 months through a coordinated security framework involving the Office of the National Security Adviser, the NNPCL’s command centre, security agencies and host communities.

“Confidence and strong partnership with both community and security agencies have helped Nigeria achieve the milestone of 100 per cent pipeline availability for the first time in two decades,” he said.

He said the improved performance was the result of combining conventional security measures with community participation, stressing that host communities must be treated as partners in protecting critical energy infrastructure.

Ojulari called for the effective implementation of Host Community Development Trusts established under the Petroleum Industry Act, saying community relationships were as important as technical measures in maintaining pipeline integrity.

He said that the NNPCL’s wider operational improvements had also translated into increased crude oil production, with output rising to 1.71 million barrels per day, the highest level in five years, according to the company’s one-year performance scorecard presented earlier in the year.

Ojulari further disclosed that the recovery across five crude oil terminals averaged 98 per cent between April 2025 and May 2026, compared with operational lows of about one per cent at the Bonny Oil and Gas Terminal in June 2022.

On gas infrastructure, he said the OB3 project, which connects the eastern and western parts of the country’s gas network, had overcome a major engineering obstacle after the completion of its River Niger crossing.

The 130-kilometre, 48-inch pipeline is designed to transport up to two billion standard cubic feet of gas per day, linking gas resources in the eastern region with industries and consumers in other parts of the country.

Ojulari said the crossing involved drilling approximately two kilometres beneath the River Niger using horizontal directional drilling technology, adding that the project is evidence that difficult infrastructure challenges could be overcome through engineering expertise, adequate financing, patience and collaboration among contractors and project owners.

On the AKK project, he said the 40-inch pipeline was designed to transport up to 2.2 billion standard cubic feet of gas daily and would support electricity generation, fertiliser production, manufacturing and other gas-based industries.

The NNPC official also highlighted the commercial significance of the $1.5bn financing secured for the AKK project based on projected pipeline revenues.

He said the financing arrangement demonstrated that pipeline infrastructure could attract investment independently of upstream oil production or downstream projects, provided the projects had credible revenue structures and effective governance, among others.

Earlier, PLAN President, Ngozi Adeleke, said the conference was designed to address the funding and operational challenges confronting Nigeria’s pipeline infrastructure as the country pursued increased hydrocarbon production, expanded gas utilisation and industrial growth.

She said the development and sustainability of pipeline infrastructure required significant investment, innovative financing, regulatory support, advanced technology and effective security arrangements.

“Importantly, NIPITECS is not merely a platform for dialogue. Our objective is to foster partnerships, stimulate innovation, encourage knowledge sharing and contribute practical recommendations that can strengthen Nigeria’s pipeline ecosystem,” Adeleke said.

title: Single Window: Nigeria’s $6.1bn non-oil exports drive fresh trade reforms
description:
By Obas Esiedesa, Abuja







The Federal Government on Tuesday disclosed that it is set to streamline export documentation and regulatory approvals from December 14, 2026, as part of efforts to sustain growth in Nigeria’s non-oil exports, which hit a record $6.1bn in 2025.







The reform, under
content:
By Obas Esiedesa, Abuja

The Federal Government on Tuesday disclosed that it is set to streamline export documentation and regulatory approvals from December 14, 2026, as part of efforts to sustain growth in Nigeria’s non-oil exports, which hit a record $6.1bn in 2025.

The reform, under the second phase of the National Single Window project, is expected to eliminate multiple documentation processes, reduce bureaucratic bottlenecks and lower the cost of exporting Nigerian products.

The Director of the National Single Window Project, Tola Fakolade, disclosed this at a stakeholders’ engagement in Abuja, saying the export-focused phase would provide businesses with a single digital platform for processing regulatory licences, permits and certificates.

He explained that the platform would enable exporters to submit required documents through one entry point rather than visiting different government agencies to obtain multiple approvals.

Fakolade said the first phase of the project, which focused on import licences and certificates, had processed more than 169,000 licences, certificates and permits since its launch.

He added that feedback from users had helped improve the platform, while lessons from the import phase would guide the implementation of the export component.

The initiative comes as Nigeria’s non-oil export earnings increased by 11.5 per cent to a record $6.1bn in 2025, while export volume rose by 10 per cent to 8.02 million metric tonnes.

The Executive Director and Chief Executive Officer of the Nigerian Export Promotion Council, NEPC, Nonye Ayeni, who disclosed the figures, said the country exported 281 products to 120 countries, including 36 African nations.

Ayeni, however, warned that sustaining the growth would require addressing trade procedures and regulatory delays, which she identified as major challenges confronting exporters.

She said exporters often had to visit several government offices, submit identical documents repeatedly and secure multiple approvals before their goods could leave the country.

According to her, such delays sometimes result in contract cancellations, increased business costs and deterioration of perishable products, leading to rejection by international buyers.

She said the National Single Window would address the challenges by connecting relevant government agencies to a centralised digital platform for submitting, processing and approving trade documents.

Ayeni disclosed that NEPC was working with the National Single Window Secretariat to integrate its export certification registration process, currently operated through the council’s e-registration portal, into the platform.

She added that the council was also working to connect its Export Expansion Grant platform through an application programming interface to facilitate seamless processing and eliminate the movement of physical documents between institutions.

Also speaking, the Chairman of the Nigeria Revenue Service, Zach Adedeji, represented by the Group Director, Transformation and Strategy, Alfred Okoh, described the National Single Window as a major reform of Nigeria’s trade processes rather than merely an information technology project.

Adedeji said the initiative represented a shift from fragmented regulatory compliance towards integrated, data-driven trade facilitation.

He reaffirmed the NRS’s commitment to providing the technical and institutional support required to ensure the project’s success, stressing that interoperability, transparency and improved exporter experience would be critical to achieving its objectives.

He expressed confidence that the targets set for 2027 were achievable if stakeholders sustained their collaboration.

The post Single Window: Nigeria’s $6.1bn non-oil exports drive fresh trade reforms appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Police rescue five-year-old boy abducted by father’s girlfriend in Anambra
description:
The Anambra State Police Command has rescued a five-year-old boy, Chiziterem Ifeadi, who was allegedly abducted by his father’s girlfriend.
The police also arrested the suspected perpetrator, identified as 29-year-old Precious Nnaji, at Nnodu, Okpuno, Awka South Local Government Area of the state, i
content:
The Anambra State Police Command has rescued a five-year-old boy, Chiziterem Ifeadi, who was allegedly abducted by his father’s girlfriend.

The police also arrested the suspected perpetrator, identified as 29-year-old Precious Nnaji, at Nnodu, Okpuno, Awka South Local Government Area of the state, in connection with the incident.

In a press statement released on Tuesday, the spokesperson for the Anambra State Police Command, SP Tochukwu Ikenga, said operatives of the IGP’s Violent Crime Response Unit, in collaboration with personnel of the Department of State Services, arrested the suspect on Monday.

Ikenga added that the boy was abducted on November 15, after his father had left home for work, leaving his two sons in the care of their nanny.

He said that, upon his return, the boy’s father discovered that his girlfriend had allegedly visited the residence without his consent and taken away his five-year-old son to an unknown destination.

The statement read, “The Anambra State Police Command, through operatives of the IGP’s Violent Crime Response Unit, in collaboration with personnel of the Department of State Services, in the early hours of November 16, 2026, successfully rescued a five-year-old boy allegedly abducted by his father’s girlfriend.

“The suspected perpetrator, identified as 29-year-old Precious Nnaji, at Nnodu, Okpuno, has also been arrested in connection with the incident.

“Preliminary information reveals that on November 15, 2026, the father of the child had left his residence for work, leaving his two sons in the care of their nanny.

“Upon his return, he discovered that his girlfriend, identified as Precious Nnaji, had allegedly visited the residence without his consent and taken away his five-year-old son, Chiziterem Ifeadi, to an unknown destination.

“The father further reported that, after several unsuccessful attempts to reach the suspect by telephone, she eventually responded and allegedly demanded the sum of ₦2,000,000, to be paid through a Point-of-Sale operator, as a condition for the release of the child.

“The suspect is currently in police custody, while investigations are ongoing to establish the full circumstances surrounding the incident and ensure that appropriate legal action is taken.”

Meanwhile, the Commissioner of Police, Anambra State Command, CP Nnanna Ama, has commended the operatives and their DSS counterparts for their swift response and effective collaboration, which led to the safe rescue of the child.

Ama reassured people of the state of the command’s unwavering commitment to intelligence-led policing, inter-agency cooperation and the protection of lives and property across the state.

The post Police rescue five-year-old boy abducted by father’s girlfriend in Anambra appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: I contemplated suicide at height of Man United career,  Rooney reveals
description:
By Adegboyega Adeleye



Wayne Rooney has revealed he contemplated suicide during the height of his Manchester United career, despite success on the pitch and major milestones in his personal life.



Speaking on the Life At The Midpoint with Gabby Logan podcast, the former England captain said he s
content:
By Adegboyega Adeleye

Wayne Rooney has revealed he contemplated suicide during the height of his Manchester United career, despite success on the pitch and major milestones in his personal life.

Speaking on the Life At The Midpoint with Gabby Logan podcast, the former England captain said he struggled with his mental health, spent two days at a time drinking at home and withdrew from people around him.

“I can look back and say I was selfish, but I knew I was going through something which I was really struggling to deal with,” Rooney said.

“Then I didn’t want Kai seeing me like that, so that’s why I’d hide away as well.

“I got to a place where you’re contemplating suicide. You just didn’t want to be around anyone. I didn’t want to see people in the streets. I didn’t want to go into shops.

“I was always comfortable on a football pitch, but everything else (I) really struggled with it.”

Rooney, Manchester United’s all-time record goalscorer with 253 goals, said he found it difficult to admit he was struggling because he feared it would be seen as a sign of weakness.

“You don’t want to show any weakness, so you try to mask it,” he said.

“Even though I knew the position I was in, it was difficult to actually admit that I was in that position because I felt like you feel less of a man if you like for doing that.

“I was speaking to a therapist to try and figure out what was up with me because, when I look back, I was probably at the height of my career, I’ve just had a young son, I’ve just been married. It should be the happiest point in my life, and it wasn’t.

“It was probably the lowest point because of the selfish acts I was taking.”

Rooney, who married Coleen in 2008 and became a father to their first child, Kai, the following year, credited his wife with helping him through the period.

“Coleen helped me massively. She could have walked away, it was that bad, but she stuck by me and helped me get through it,” he said.

Rooney left Manchester United in 2017 and later had spells with Everton, DC United and Derby County. His last managerial role was at Plymouth Argyle, which he left in December 2024.

title: AFCON 2027 Qualifier: Super Eagles held to goalless draw by Tanzania
description:
Nigeria’s Super Eagles suffered a setback in their quest to secure qualification for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) after playing a goalless draw against Tanzania on Tuesday in their Group L qualifying match in Zanzibar.
Despite dominating possession and creating several clear scoring chance
content:
Nigeria’s Super Eagles suffered a setback in their quest to secure qualification for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) after playing a goalless draw against Tanzania on Tuesday in their Group L qualifying match in Zanzibar.

Despite dominating possession and creating several clear scoring chances, the Nigerian side failed to convert their opportunities into goals.

The Super Eagles came close to taking the lead in the 34th minute when Tolu Arokodare’s low shot beat the Tanzanian goalkeeper but struck the woodwork.

Moses Usor also threatened the hosts four minutes later with a well-directed effort, but the Tanzania goalkeeper reacted quickly to push the ball away and prevent Nigeria from scoring.

The draw means Nigeria missed the opportunity to claim maximum points from the encounter as their campaign for a place at the 2027 AFCON continues.

Fisayo Dele-Bashiru had earlier tried his luck from outside the box, but his effort went wide, while Arokodare also sent an attempt off target.

Nigeria continued to search for the breakthrough after the restart, but Tanzania’s back proved resilient.

The hosts threatened through Kibu Denis, who had two attempts from the right side of the penalty area in the opening 10 minutes of the second half, but both went wide.

Head coach Eric Chelle introduced Alex Iwobi and Akor Adams for Taiwo Awoniyi and Dele-Bashiru in the 61st minute as Nigeria sought to increase their attacking threat.

Tochukwu and Alhassan Yusuf were later brought on for Wilfred Ndidi and Usor in the 73rd minute.

Adams and Bassey also had chances in the final minutes, but their attempts were not enough.

Arokodare also failed to hit the target in the 85th minute, while an earlier through ball from Yusuf found the forward in an offside position.

Nigeria had beaten Tanzania 3-1 in Friday’s first leg at the Godswill Akpabio International Stadium in Uyo, with Alhassan Yusuf opening the scoring before Arokodare netted twice in the second half.

The Super Eagles began Tuesday’s fixture with six points from three matches, one behind Group L leaders Guinea-Bissau, who had drawn 1-1 with Madagascar in their previous outing.

Tanzania had already secured qualification for the tournament as co-hosts, leaving Nigeria, Guinea-Bissau and Madagascar to contest the group’s remaining qualifying place.

The 2027 AFCON will be jointly hosted by Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda from June 19 to July 17.

The post AFCON 2027 Qualifier: Super Eagles held to goalless draw by Tanzania appeared first on Very Nigerian.

title: 2027: We’ll never disappoint you — Kebbi governor assures Tinubu
description:
Kebbi State Governor, Nasir Idris, has assured President Bola Tinubu that the state will remain loyal to the All Progressives Congress (APC) and deliver overwhelming support for his re-election in the 2027 presidential election.



Idris gave the assurance on Tuesday while welcoming Tinubu to the st
content:
Kebbi State Governor, Nasir Idris, has assured President Bola Tinubu that the state will remain loyal to the All Progressives Congress (APC) and deliver overwhelming support for his re-election in the 2027 presidential election.

Idris gave the assurance on Tuesday while welcoming Tinubu to the state during the APC campaign rally, saying Kebbi had consistently supported the President and would do even more in the forthcoming election.

“Mr President, Kebbi State has never disappointed you, and we will never disappoint you. In 2023, we gave you total support. In this election, we will give you even more,” the governor said.

He added, “I assure you that Kebbi State will deliver APC 100 per cent by God’s grace.”

The governor described the large turnout at the rally as evidence of the state’s support for Tinubu and his running mate, Vice-President Kashim Shettima.

“This massive crowd you see here is a clear testimony that Kebbi State is APC and Kebbi State is for Bola Ahmed Tinubu and Kashim Shettima,” he said.

Idris also commended the President for what he described as his administration’s interventions in the state, particularly in agriculture, infrastructure, education, healthcare and security.

He thanked Tinubu for the Renewed Hope Agenda and support for farmers, which he said had contributed to a rice revolution in Kebbi.

“We thank you for the roads, for the schools, for the hospitals, and for security support you give us,” he said.

The governor said his administration had also invested in strengthening the state’s security architecture, improving health facilities, providing free agricultural inputs to farmers and constructing rural and township roads across the state.

According to him, the investments have helped farmers work with confidence, created employment opportunities for young people and supported the empowerment of women.

Idris, however, used the occasion to appeal to Tinubu to facilitate the full operationalisation of the Samia Inland Dry Port in Bagoro Local Government Area of the state.

He said the facility, when fully operational, would boost revenue generation, create jobs and promote economic growth in Kebbi.

title: Super Eagles held to dissapointing goalless draw by Tanzania in AFCON qualifier
description:
By Adegboyega Adeleye



The Super Eagles of Nigeria were held to a 0-0 draw by Tanzania on Tuesday, missing the chance to strengthen their Africa Cup of Nations qualifying campaign.



Eric Chelle’s side had more possession and created several chances but could not find a way past the hosts’ defenc
content:
By Adegboyega Adeleye

The Super Eagles of Nigeria were held to a 0-0 draw by Tanzania on Tuesday, missing the chance to strengthen their Africa Cup of Nations qualifying campaign.

Eric Chelle’s side had more possession and created several chances but could not find a way past the hosts’ defence in 90 minutes.

The Super Eagles started brightly, with Moses Usor seeing an effort blocked inside the opening 15 minutes. Fisayo Dele-Bashiru also tested Tanzania with a shot from outside the penalty area, while Tolu Arokodare fired wide in the 35th minute.

Tanzania remained a threat after the break, with Kibu Denis and Iddi Selemani both missing opportunities to put their side ahead.

Nigeria continued to press, but Akor Adams sent an effort wide from the centre of the penalty area in the 70th minute. Arokodare later came close with a left-footed attempt from inside the box, but his shot also failed to hit the target.

Tanzania nearly snatched a late winner when a speculative effort from the edge of the area struck the post.

Alhassan Yusuf then tried to release a forward with a through ball, but the move was stopped for offside. Nigeria could not find a breakthrough in the closing minutes as Tanzania held on for a point.

Nigeria will now hope Madagascar defeat Guinea-Bissau in Group L to keep their qualification hopes alive.

Eric Chelle’s side had claimed a 3-1 victory over Tanzania in Friday’s first leg at the Godswill Akpabio International Stadium in Uyo. Alhassan Yusuf scored the opener before Tolu Arokodare struck twice after the break.

The Super Eagles went into Tuesday’s match with six points from three games, one point behind Group L leaders Guinea-Bissau, who had played out a 1-1 draw with Madagascar in their previous fixture.

Tanzania had already qualified for the tournament as one of the co-hosts, leaving Nigeria, Guinea-Bissau and Madagascar to battle for the group’s other qualification spot.

Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda will jointly host the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations from June 19 to July 17.

title: Delta gov backs CAN Prayer Retreat Centre project
description:
The Governor of Delta State, Sheriff Oborevwori, has pledged his administration’s support for the proposed Christian Association of Nigeria Prayer Retreat Centre, assuring the Christian community that the government will work with the Church to identify suitable land for the project.
The governor ga
content:
The Governor of Delta State, Sheriff Oborevwori, has pledged his administration’s support for the proposed Christian Association of Nigeria Prayer Retreat Centre, assuring the Christian community that the government will work with the Church to identify suitable land for the project.

The governor gave the assurance on Tuesday at the 2026 CAN Day celebration in Delta State, held under the theme, “One God; One People” (Ephesians 4:4-6). He also appealed to Christians to sustain their prayers for peace, security and development in the state and the country.

Oborevwori said the proposed retreat centre would provide an appropriate environment for prayer, spiritual reflection and renewal, while acknowledging the contributions of religious leaders to peacebuilding and social development.

According to him, “the Church has an important responsibility to promote love, tolerance, forgiveness and peaceful coexistence”.

Quoting Ephesians 4:5-6, the governor reminded Christians that there was “one Lord, one faith, one baptism, one God and Father of all,” urging them to uphold the values of love, mutual respect and understanding.

He said, “Our differences should never become reasons for division. Delta State belongs to all of us, irrespective of our religious beliefs, ethnic backgrounds or political affiliations. Our responsibility is to build a state where everyone can live, worship and work in peace.”

The governor appealed to Christian leaders to continue praying for those in positions of authority, security agencies and the nation, stressing that his administration was committed to maintaining peace and stability across the state.

He said nobody desired violence or bloodshed in Delta, adding that the government needed the cooperation and prayers of religious leaders to sustain an atmosphere where residents could pursue their legitimate aspirations without fear.

According to him, governance requires wisdom, consultation and prayer, noting that leaders must constantly seek God’s direction when making decisions that affect the people.

Earlier, the guest speaker, Archbishop Goddowell Avwomakpa, called on Christians across denominations to embrace unity, love and cooperation, insisting that differences in church affiliations, ethnicity and social backgrounds should not weaken their common identity in Christ.

He commended Oborevwori for his support for the Christian community and the declaration of CAN Day, describing the gesture as evidence of his administration’s recognition of the Church and its contributions to society.

The Delta State CAN Chairman, Rev. Lucky Osagbakhoe, in an address, described the celebration as an important platform for fellowship, reflection and the strengthening of relationships among Christians across denominations.

He thanked the governor for supporting the Church and contributing to Delta State’s development, while acknowledging the presence of religious leaders, government officials and other distinguished guests.

title: Why I will vote for Tinubu in 2027 – Pinnick
description:
By Adegboyega Adeleye



Former Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) president and Deputy Chairperson, FIFA Men’s National Teams Competition Committee Amaju Pinnick says he will vote for President Bola Tinubu in the 2027 election, citing what he described as improved sports administration and his desir
content:
By Adegboyega Adeleye

Former Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) president and Deputy Chairperson, FIFA Men’s National Teams Competition Committee Amaju Pinnick says he will vote for President Bola Tinubu in the 2027 election, citing what he described as improved sports administration and his desire to see Nigeria remain united.

In an interview on Arise News on Tuesday, Pinnick said the Tinubu administration had made the right appointments in sports and pointed to Shehu Dikko and Bukola Olopade’s leadership, as well as preparations for the Commonwealth Games and Olympic Games.

“This is the first time in a long time that we are getting sports administration right through appointments into leadership roles, Shehu Dikko and Bukola Olapade. The Tinubu administration is doing the right thing, and you can see it from the Commonwealth Games to the Olympic Games; they are getting it right.

Pinnick, who is the deputy chairperson of the FIFA Men’s National Teams Competition Committee, said his support for Tinubu was based partly on the administration’s sports appointments and partly on the First Lady’s Itsekiri connection.

He predicted that the Itsekiri community would deliver at least 500,000 votes for the president’s re-election.

“I am 100% convinced that the Itsekiris will deliver at least 500,000 votes to Tinubu’s reelection. Some may be subjective, and some may be objective; the subjective ones are because Remi Tinubu is Itsekiri.

“The truth is that we are a very fragile nation, and I love Nigeria. I want Nigeria to be one.”

title: Nigeria can’t afford to ignore technology in education — Minister
description:
The Minister of Education, Dr Tunji Alausa, has said Nigeria cannot afford to ignore the opportunities offered by technology in addressing challenges in the education sector and improving learning outcomes.
Alausa spoke in Abuja on Tuesday at the unveiling of Nigeria’s first National Education Techn
content:
The Minister of Education, Dr Tunji Alausa, has said Nigeria cannot afford to ignore the opportunities offered by technology in addressing challenges in the education sector and improving learning outcomes.

Alausa spoke in Abuja on Tuesday at the unveiling of Nigeria’s first National Education Technology Strategy, developed by the Federal Government in collaboration with the Federal Ministry of Communications, Innovation and Digital Economy.

He said the strategy would provide a common national framework for coordinating investments in digital infrastructure, learning platforms and teacher preparation across basic, secondary, tertiary and non-formal education.

The minister said the government had invested substantially in digital infrastructure and educational technology initiatives over the past three years, making it necessary to harmonise the interventions to achieve measurable results.

“Today, it’s not just about unveiling. It’s a national framework, a common framework to improve teaching, expand learning opportunities, and strengthen educational management across all tiers of our education system: basic education, secondary school education, tertiary education, and non-formal education,” he said.

Alausa said Nigeria had moved from the conceptualisation stage to implementation and was preparing to enter the expansion phase.

“We need to use technology to improve education, deliver education, and not just deliver education, but to ensure that the quality of education is significantly improved,” he said.

He also stressed the need to extend internet connectivity to underserved communities, particularly schools in riverine areas of the Niger Delta.

The minister recalled discussions with the Minister of Communications, Innovation and Digital Economy, Dr Bosun Tijani, on efforts to expand internet access to schools in the region.

He said improved connectivity would help bridge geographical barriers and ensure pupils in remote communities had access to digital learning resources.

Speaking at the event, the World Bank Country Director, Matthew Verghis, said artificial intelligence and other emerging technologies were changing how people worked, learned and accessed information.

He said Nigeria must prepare learners for the changing global economy by strengthening digital literacy, critical thinking, creativity and continuous learning, while maintaining literacy and numeracy as the foundations of education.

Verghis said technology should complement teachers rather than replace them.

“Their promise is not to replace teaching, but to strengthen teaching and human relationships at the heart of education,” he said.

He added that the success of educational technology should be measured by its impact on learning outcomes rather than the number of digital tools deployed.

Verghis also warned against widening existing educational inequalities through digital innovation, stressing the need for safeguards to protect learners and promote inclusion.

The strategy was developed with support from the World Bank and the Mastercard Foundation, against the backdrop of persistent challenges in Nigeria’s education sector, including inadequate school connectivity, teacher shortages and millions of out-of-school children.

It builds on other Federal Government digital education interventions, including the Digital National Education Management Information System, launched in July 2026 to improve education data collection, planning and accountability.

title: How I Considered Suicide At My ‘Lowest Point’ With Man Utd – Rooney
description: Wayne Rooney has revealed that he contemplated suicide even as he flourished on the pitch for Manchester United when the Premier League club was at the height of its powers.The former England forward, 41, said his mental health was suffering even though he was newly married and a father to his eldes
content:
Wayne Rooney has revealed that he contemplated suicide even as he flourished on the pitch for Manchester United when the Premier League club was at the height of its powers.

The former England forward, 41, said his mental health was suffering even though he was newly married and a father to his eldest child, Kai.

He married Coleen in 2008, and his first child was born the following year.

Rooney was part of a powerful squad assembled by Alex Ferguson that won multiple Premier League titles and the Champions League.

The striker, who would spend two days at a time drinking at home, told the “Life At The Midpoint with Gabby Logan” podcast that he considered taking his own life when he was at his lowest ebb.

“I can look back and say I was selfish, but I knew I was going through something which I was really struggling to deal with,” he said.

“Then I didn’t want Kai seeing me like that, so that’s why I’d hide away as well.

“I got to a place where you’re contemplating suicide. You just didn’t want to be around anyone. I didn’t want to see people in the streets. I didn’t want to go into shops.

“I was always comfortable on a football pitch, but everything else (I) really struggled with it.”

Rooney, United’s all-time record goalscorer with 253 goals, said the issues he faced occurred at the height of his Red Devils career.

“You don’t want to show any weakness, so you try to mask it,” he added.

“Even though I knew the position I was in, it was difficult to actually admit that I was in that position because I felt like you feel less of a man if you like for doing that.

“I was speaking to a therapist to try and figure out what was up with me because, when I look back, I was probably at the height of my career; I’ve just had a young son; I’ve just been married. It should be the happiest point in my life, and it wasn’t.

“It was probably the lowest point because of the selfish acts I was taking.”

Rooney, who was England’s record goalscorer before Harry Kane overtook him, credits Coleen with helping him turn the tide.

“Coleen helped me massively. She could have walked away; it was that bad, but she stuck by me and helped me get through it,” he said.

After Rooney left United in 2017, he had spells with Everton, DC United and Derby before embarking on a managerial career.

His last job was at Plymouth, which he left in December 2024.

title: Obi Meets US Lawmakers, Calls For Stronger Democratic Institutions In Nigeria
description: The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, met with United States lawmakers in Washington, DC, where he called for accountable leadership, stronger democratic institutions and credible elections in Nigeria.Obi said the meetings, which took place on Monday, focuse
content:
The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, met with United States lawmakers in Washington, DC, where he called for accountable leadership, stronger democratic institutions and credible elections in Nigeria.

Obi said the meetings, which took place on Monday, focused on Nigeria’s security challenges, economic development, national unity and the future of its democracy.

In a post on X on Tuesday, the former Anambra State governor said he engaged congressional leaders from both chambers of the US Congress, alongside other American political and public figures.

He also disclosed that he granted an interview to television commentator Glenn Beck, during which they discussed Nigeria’s challenges, the management of its human and natural resources, and the need for responsible leadership.

Among those he met were US Congressmen Marlin Stutzman and Todd Tiahrt, Congresswoman Beth Van Duyne, Suzanne Bock Grisham and retired US Army Colonel Albert Short.

Obi said one of the major highlights of his visit was an address on Capitol Hill, where he emphasised the need for international cooperation and support for Nigeria, particularly in addressing insecurity, promoting economic prosperity and improving citizens’ welfare.

He added that discussions also centred on protecting Nigeria’s democracy and strengthening institutions to guarantee free, fair, transparent and credible elections.

“Our conversations also addressed the protection of Nigeria’s emerging democracy and the strengthening of democratic institutions to ensure elections are free, fair, transparent, and credible, accurately reflecting the will of the Nigerian people,” he said.

The NDC presidential candidate maintained that Nigeria had the potential to become a leading nation but needed accountable leadership, responsible management of resources and resilient institutions to achieve that ambition.

He also stressed that Nigerians must determine the country’s future through a democratic process in which every vote counts and citizens’ rights are protected.

The Washington engagements come as Nigeria prepares for the 2027 general elections, with security, economic hardship and electoral credibility expected to feature prominently in political campaigns.

Obi formally declared his intention to contest the 2027 presidential election under the NDC after leaving the Labour Party. He has continued to criticise the Federal Government’s economic policies and advocate greater transparency and accountability in governance.

The 2027 presidential election is expected to feature several prominent political figures, including President Bola Tinubu of the All Progressives Congress (APC), former Vice President Atiku Abubakar of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Obi of the NDC and Omoyele Sowore of the African Action Congress (AAC).

In the 2023 presidential election, Tinubu won with 8,794,726 votes, while Abubakar secured 6,984,520 votes. Obi finished third with 6,101,533 votes.
