title: Electoral violence: Senate urges INEC to disqualify candidates over supporters’ actions
description:
Condemns Actions, Asks State governors to stop denying opposition parties access to public facilities, including hotels and stadia under their control for political activities



It is a shame to see candidates contesting for the Senate, House of Representatives or governorship surrounded by support
content:
• Condemns Actions, Asks State governors to stop denying opposition parties access to public facilities, including hotels and stadia under their control for political activities
  • It is a shame to see candidates contesting for the Senate, House of Representatives or governorship surrounded by supporters carrying dangerous weapons, Senator Kawu

By Henry Umoru

ABUJA- DISTURBED by recurring cases of political thuggery and violence across the country, the Senate has
asked the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to disqualify any political candidate whose supporters are found to have instigated or participated in acts of electoral violence, irrespective of party affiliation, in accordance with the provisions of the 2026 Electoral Act and an established conviction by the court.

The Senate has condemned in very strong terms escalation in the frequency and spread of political violence across the country, characterised by what it described as attacks on political leaders, supporters and political gatherings, with grave implications for National Security, democratic participation and the peaceful conduct of the 2027 General Elections.

The Senate further asked state governors to stop denying opposition parties access to public facilities, including hotels and stadiums under their control, for political activities.

The Senate has urged all the rrelevant security agencies to conduct impartial and transparent investigations into reported incidents of political violence in Abuja, Edo, Delta and Sokoto states, as well as other affected areas.

Resolutions of the Senate on Tuesday were sequel to a motion on the urgent need to check the rising incidence of violence, intolerance and attacks on political leaders and supporters in the country sponsored by Senator Abdul Ningi, Bauchi Central.

Ningi’s motion came as a recent of reports of attacks on political figures, including the incident involving President Bola Tinubu at a mosque on Friday.

In a robust debate, the lawmakers asked security agencies to investigate reported incidents in four states (Abuja, Edo, Delta and Sokoto states), identify the perpetrators and their sponsors and ensure prosecution.

The Senate further urged the agencies to identify the perpetrators and sponsors of such incidents and ensure their prosecution in accordance with the Electoral Act 2026.

It urged the Federal Government to direct the Inspector-General of Police and other relevant Security Agencies to strengthen security arrangements for political leaders, candidates, supporters and political gatherings nationwide, and establish effective early-warning and rapid-response mechanisms to prevent political violence ahead of the 2027 General Elections.

The Senate has also mandated its Committees on National Security and Intelligence; Police Affairs; and Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to engage relevant institutions and report to the Senate within one week on measures to prevent political violence and safeguard the 2027 General Elections.

Following an additional prayer by Senator Sampson Ekong, APC, Akwa Ibom South, the Senate resolved that the. Federal Ministry of Information and the National Orientation Agency (NOA) should intensify public enlightenment campaigns against political violence.

Ekong who argued that legal provisions alone would not sufficiently address the problem without sustained public awareness and education, said the proposed campaign should discourage the growing culture of political violence and help prevent young people from being recruited or influenced to engage in violent activities.

Asserting the need to guarantee a level playing field for all political parties, the Upper Chamber has warned that restrictions on opposition activities could heighten political intolerance and trigger avoidable conflicts.

Speaking during discussions on the motion, the President of the Senate, Senator Godswill Akpabio said, ‘Any candidate or supporter caught instigating violence, then INEC has a right to disqualify. We should call the attention of INEC to the 2026 Electoral Act; no matter the political party, such a candidate should immediately be disqualified. They are embedded in the 2026 Electoral Act and require strong implementation.

He urged the electoral commission to enforce the provisions of the 2026 Electoral Act, which they reminded provides for sanctions against electoral violence, underscoring the need for strict implementation ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Akpabio said, “Let us refer to the Electoral Act 2026.
If you examine Sections 121 to 128, you will see that electoral offences and violence are clearly spelt out.These include intimidation, snatching of BVAS machines, ballot boxes and other electoral materials.

“We recommended penalties ranging from 12 months to five years’ imprisonment, with no option of a fine for aggravated offences such as stoning, beating with sticks or using other dangerous objects. That was what we recommended.

“Furthermore, under Section 92, we provided that INEC could suspend elections in areas where violence is reported and reschedule such elections within 24 hours.

“We also provided for the Electoral Offences Commission Bill 2025, which was passed alongside the Electoral Act, to establish a dedicated mechanism for addressing electoral offences, including vote-buying, electoral violence and attacks on INEC officials.

“We made provisions to protect INEC personnel and other individuals involved in the electoral process.The fact that we have enacted the law means the responsibility now rests with the executive to implement it. The provisions are very clear.”

Lawmakers expressed concern over the growing tension in the political space and called on the Federal Government to direct the Inspector-General of Police and other security agencies to strengthen security arrangements for political leaders, candidates, supporters and political gatherings across the country.

They also called for effective early-warning and rapid-response mechanisms to identify and prevent potential attacks ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Earlier in his presentation, Senator Ningi said that “The Senate: Disturbed by the alarming escalation in the frequency and spread of political violence across the country, characterised by attacks on political leaders, supporters and political gatherings, with grave implications for National Security, democratic participation and the peaceful conduct of the 2027 General Elections;

“Notes with grave concern the reported attack on the motorcade of His Excellency, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, GCFR, on Friday, 13th November, 2026, shortly after he observed Jumu’ah prayers at the Shehu Shagari Central Mosque, Garki, Abuja, when the departing convoy was reportedly attacked with stones and other dangerous objects, resulting in damage to vehicles and injuries to security operatives;

“Recalls the reported attack on Mr. Peter Obi and other political stakeholders during a political gathering in Benue, Edo State; the violent disruption of a political procession involving supporters of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) and the Obidient Movement in Asaba, Delta State, on 7th November, 2026, which reportedly resulted in one death and five injuries; and the reported attack on the convoy of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate, former Vice President, Atiku Abubakar in Sokoto State;

“Observes that these incidents reflect a disturbing pattern of political intolerance, intimidation and violence capable of undermining public confidence in the electoral process and discouraging citizens from exercising their democratic rights.”

Senator Ningi further said that the Senate is “Worried that failure to promptly investigate and prosecute perpetrators and sponsors of political violence could embolden further attacks, deepen political divisions and threaten the peaceful conduct of the 2027 General Elections;

“Aware that Sections 39 and 40 of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 (as amended), guarantee freedom of expression, peaceful assembly and association, including political association;

“Convinced that democracy can only thrive where political differences are resolved through peaceful engagement and the contest of ideas rather than intimidation, violence and the suppression of opposing views.”

In his contribution, Senator Binos Yaro, ADC, Adamawa South moved an additional prayer urging state governors to ensure that rival political parties and candidates are not denied access to public facilities, including public arenas and hotels controlled by state governments.

According to him, such restrictions could undermine the principle of a level playing field for political parties and create unnecessary conflicts.

On his part, Senator Ali Ndume, APC, Borno South said, “I had tried to reach out to Senator Ningi after observing these incidents over the last two weeks. Fortunately, the motion has now been presented, and I commend you, Mr President, for recognising its urgency and allowing the Senate to consider it immediately.
The mover of the motion has already enumerated the necessary steps the Senate needs to take. We must stand firmly against every form of violence, as you rightly stated last week.What happened to Mr President was not an embarrassment to him alone; it was an embarrassment to Nigerians.

“In my religion, the Quran clearly states that God gives power to whoever He chooses. Therefore, what are the youths saying? Are they suggesting that God’s choice of our President is wrong?
Secondly, this is our President. There are several legitimate ways to express anger or stage protests, but what happened to Mr President on a Friday at a mosque was unacceptable. We must also acknowledge that the President is a true democrat. If he had a military mentality, the 88 people arrested that day might not have been treated with the magnanimity they received.
Within 24 hours of their arrest, the President directed that they be released unconditionally. That demonstrated fatherliness and statesmanship.
However, what is happening is like a fire that, if not completely extinguished, could spread and become uncontrollable.
God forbid that situations similar to what we have witnessed in France, Germany, Finland, the Netherlands and Kenya should happen in Nigeria.

“As members of the National Assembly, we must recognise that we, too, could become victims of political violence. If Mr President, despite the security protection provided for him, could experience such an incident, then nobody is completely safe.
“In addition to the prayers already proposed, I suggest that during the campaign period, the police and armed forces should prohibit the carrying of anything that could be considered a weapon. What candidates and their supporters should carry to campaign grounds are posters and other legitimate campaign materials, not sticks, knives or other dangerous objects.
“Anybody caught carrying knives, sticks or other harmful objects during campaigns should be arrested immediately.
Furthermore, we should establish mobile courts to accompany campaign activities. Wherever campaigns are taking place, a magistrate should be available to ensure that anybody arrested for carrying dangerous weapons or engaging in violence is promptly prosecuted.
Where sufficient evidence exists, offenders should be convicted in accordance with the law. This arrangement should apply to all political parties, including the APC.
I believe this would go a long way towards preventing political violence during the campaigns.
Politics should have nothing to do with violence.

“Finally, there is a slogan being introduced into our political campaigns which I consider militant and should be discouraged.
I have seen the President’s picture displayed alongside the slogan, “Tinubu Must Go.” The APC has also introduced its own version, while other political parties have slogans such as “Atiku Must Go” and “Obi Must Go.”
If everybody must go, who will govern the country?:

In his contribution, Senator Sumaila Kawu, APC, Kano South said, ” I also commend our leader, Senator Ali Ndume, for his courage and nationalistic approach to this important issue. I listened attentively to his contributions and support his recommendations, particularly the proposal to establish special courts to prosecute people found carrying dangerous weapons during political campaigns. However, let us ask ourselves some important questions. Are we not the same people who enacted the Electoral Act? Are we not responsible for the laws governing our electoral process?

” It is a shame to see candidates contesting for the Senate, House of Representatives or governorship surrounded by supporters carrying dangerous weapons. Where are we going as lawmakers when we appear to encourage conduct that violates the laws we enacted?
“We must be honest with ourselves. How many of our supporters and young people follow us to political activities carrying weapons?”

The post Electoral violence: Senate urges INEC to disqualify candidates over supporters’ actions appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: AFCON qualifier: Wasteful Eagles held 0-0 by Tanzania
description:
Nigeria’s Super Eagles dropped points in their bid to qualify for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations after playing out a goalless draw with Tanzania in Tuesday’s Group L qualifier in Zanzibar.
The result came despite Nigeria creating several scoring opportunities, particularly in the first half, when th
content:
Nigeria’s Super Eagles dropped points in their bid to qualify for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations after playing out a goalless draw with Tanzania in Tuesday’s Group L qualifier in Zanzibar.

The result came despite Nigeria creating several scoring opportunities, particularly in the first half, when they dominated possession but failed to find the back of the net.

Tolu Arokodare came closest to breaking the deadlock in the 34th minute when his low effort beat the Tanzania goalkeeper but struck the post.

Moses Usor also tested the hosts’ goalkeeper four minutes later, forcing him to get down and parry his effort away.

Fisayo Dele-Bashiru had earlier tried his luck from outside the box, but his effort went wide, while Arokodare also sent an attempt off target.

Nigeria continued to search for the breakthrough after the restart, but Tanzania’s back proved resilient.

The hosts threatened through Kibu Denis, who had two attempts from the right side of the penalty area in the opening 10 minutes of the second half, but both went wide.

Head coach Eric Chelle introduced Alex Iwobi and Akor Adams for Taiwo Awoniyi and Dele-Bashiru in the 61st minute as Nigeria sought to increase their attacking threat.

Tochukwu and Alhassan Yusuf were later brought on for Wilfred Ndidi and Usor in the 73rd minute.

Adams and Bassey also had chances in the final minutes, but their attempts were not enough.

Arokodare also failed to hit the target in the 85th minute, while an earlier through ball from Yusuf found the forward in an offside position.

Nigeria had beaten Tanzania 3-1 in Friday’s first leg at the Godswill Akpabio International Stadium in Uyo, with Alhassan Yusuf opening the scoring before Arokodare netted twice in the second half.

The Super Eagles began Tuesday’s fixture with six points from three matches, one behind Group L leaders Guinea-Bissau, who had drawn 1-1 with Madagascar in their previous outing.

Tanzania had already secured qualification for the tournament as co-hosts, leaving Nigeria, Guinea-Bissau and Madagascar to contest the group’s remaining qualifying place.

The 2027 AFCON will be jointly hosted by Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda from June 19 to July 17.

title: Senate Chief Whip Monguno, APC chieftains escape Boko Haram attack in Borno
description:
The Senate Chief Whip and Senator representing Borno North, Mohammed Tahir Monguno, has reportedly escaped an attempted Boko Haram attack in Kukawa Local Government Area of Borno State alongside some All Progressives Congress (APC) chieftains.
Monguno and former Governor of Borno State and Senator,
content:
The Senate Chief Whip and Senator representing Borno North, Mohammed Tahir Monguno, has reportedly escaped an attempted Boko Haram attack in Kukawa Local Government Area of Borno State alongside some All Progressives Congress (APC) chieftains.

Monguno and former Governor of Borno State and Senator, Maina Maaji Lawan, were among the politicians who travelled to Kukawa as part of their ongoing campaign tour ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The politicians reportedly visited the area after participating in the official launch of the campaign in Monguno town last Sunday, alongside Governor Babagana Zulum.

The governor, however, left Monguno for Maiduguri by helicopter on Monday, while some members of his entourage returned to the state capital by road later that day.

Sources said some APC politicians, including Monguno, subsequently proceeded from Monguno to Kukawa to canvass for votes ahead of the 2027 elections.

However, their visit reportedly coincided with an attempted attack by Boko Haram insurgents, who made efforts to dislodge the community. Monguno and other members of the delegation were said to have escaped the attack.

It was also gathered that, based on intelligence, troops of Operation Hadin Kai swung into action and foiled the attempted attacks by terrorists on the campaign entourage.

According to reports by Yerwa News Express, a local online media outlet said, “The terrorists fired three mortar bombs toward Kukawa on Monday while Mr Monguno, former Borno State Governor Maina Maaji Lawan, and other political figures were in the town for campaign activities.

“Local sources had earlier reported threats by the terrorists to disrupt the campaign, prompting heightened security measures.

“Troops of Operation Hadin Kai detected the movement of the terrorists around Kukawa and swiftly responded, preventing them from carrying out the attack.

“The campaign team subsequently returned safely to Monguno without any casualties.

“The terrorists reportedly made further attempts to attack the town throughout the night but were prevented from gaining access.”

In a related development, troops foiled another attempted attack on Kekeno village in the early hours of Tuesday, November 17, 2026.

“At about 1:20 a.m., alert troops spotted suspicious movements by suspected terrorists travelling on foot from the general area of Barwati toward Kekeno village.

“The troops immediately advanced toward the suspected terrorists and engaged them with heavy gunfire.

“Unable to withstand the troops’ firepower, the terrorists reportedly fled into the surrounding bush.

“The military said follow-up operations are ongoing in the area to track down the fleeing terrorists.

“It added that the situation remained calm, with troops maintaining heightened surveillance.” Sources and Yerwa Express News reported.

Due to a lack of telecommunication networks in the zone, the Senate Chief Whip’s phone number was not available at the time our correspondent dialled to confirm the incident.

title: Super Eagles Held To Frustrating Goalless Draw By Tanzania In AFCON Qualifier
description: Nigeria’s Super Eagles missed an opportunity to strengthen their Africa Cup of Nations qualification campaign after being held to a frustrating 0-0 draw by Tanzania on Tuesday.Despite enjoying greater possession and producing more attempts on goal, Eric Chelle’s side lacked the cutting e
content:
Nigeria’s Super Eagles missed an opportunity to strengthen their Africa Cup of Nations qualification campaign after being held to a frustrating 0-0 draw by Tanzania on Tuesday.

Despite enjoying greater possession and producing more attempts on goal, Eric Chelle’s side lacked the cutting edge to break down the hosts, settling for a point in a contest that offered plenty of effort but little attacking reward.

Nigeria made an encouraging start, with Moses Usor having an effort blocked inside the opening 15 minutes before Fisayo Dele-Bashiru tested Tanzania’s defence with a shot from outside the penalty area.

The Super Eagles continued to push forward, with Tolu Arokodare firing wide in the 35th minute as Tanzania struggled to contain Nigeria’s attacking advances.

However, the hosts remained competitive, relying on their physical approach and occasional attempts to threaten the Nigerian defence. Kibu Denis and Iddi Selemani both had opportunities after the restart but failed to find the target.

Super Eagles resumed the second half with the same urgency, but the breakthrough remained elusive. Akor Adams missed an opportunity in the 70th minute, sending his effort from the centre of the penalty area wide.

With time running out, the Super Eagles intensified their search for a winner. Arokodare came close again with a left-footed effort from inside the box, but his attempt also missed the target.

That moment appeared to wake Tanzania up, as they also hit the post immediately following a speculative shot from the edge of the area.

Alhassan Yusuf subsequently attempted to release the striker with a through ball, only for the move to be halted by an offside decision.

The final minutes produced no reprieve for Nigeria, as Tanzania held firm to secure a share of the points.

However, that numerical advantage counted for little as the Super Eagles failed to turn their territorial dominance and attacking opportunities into goals.

The Super Eagles would be hoping Madagascar could cause an upset against Guinea-Bissau in Group L to keep them in the running

title: Reps seek NYSC posting reforms over rising kidnapping risks
description:
By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja



The House of Representatives has called for an urgent review of the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) mobilisation and deployment policy to reduce the exposure of corps members to kidnapping, accidents and other security threats while travelling to their places of pr
content:
By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja

The House of Representatives has called for an urgent review of the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) mobilisation and deployment policy to reduce the exposure of corps members to kidnapping, accidents and other security threats while travelling to their places of primary assignment.

The call followed a motion of urgent public importance sponsored by Rep. Yallema Makki, who raised concerns over the growing security risks faced by young graduates travelling across the country for their mandatory national service.

The lawmaker noted that corps members were often required to travel long distances from their states of residence to their states of deployment, sometimes passing through areas affected by insecurity.

He expressed concern over reported cases of corps members being kidnapped, particularly while travelling to their states of deployment or places of primary assignment.

Makki warned that the dangers associated with long-distance journeys, coupled with poor road conditions and insecurity along some routes, could undermine the confidence of corps members and their families in the safety of the scheme.

He emphasised that the safety and welfare of young Nigerians undertaking national service should remain a priority throughout their mobilisation, orientation, deployment and service periods.

The lawmaker recalled that the NYSC was established in 1973 to promote national unity, integration, patriotism and mutual understanding among Nigerian youths through the deployment of graduates to different parts of the country.

However, the he argued that the objectives of national integration could still be achieved without exposing corps members to unnecessary security risks.

Makki maintained that a more flexible deployment arrangement, which takes into account geographical proximity, prevailing security conditions and identified high-risk routes, would help reduce the dangers associated with inter-state journeys.

The motion further observed that posting corps members to states closer to their places of residence, where practicable, could minimise their exposure to kidnapping and road accidents without undermining the objectives of the national service programme.

Consequently, the House adopted the motion and mandate its relevant committees to engage the NYSC management and other stakeholders to immediately review the existing mobilisation and deployment policy, with greater emphasis on the safety and security of corps members.

It also called on the NYSC to develop a more flexible deployment framework that would allow corps members to be posted to states geographically closer to their states of residence, particularly where long-distance journeys could expose them to significant security threats.

The relevant committees are also expected to monitor compliance with the proposed measures and report their findings and recommendations to the House.

The proposed review is expected to ensure that security intelligence, high-risk routes and prevailing security conditions become key considerations in decisions concerning the deployment and movement of corps members across the country.

title: Tinubu approves Kebbi dry port take-off
description:
President Bola Tinubu has approved a request by Kebbi State Governor, Nasir Idris, for the full operationalisation of the Tsamiya Inland Dry Port to boost trade, investment and economic activities in the state.
Tinubu gave the approval on Tuesday during the All Progressives Congress presidential cam
content:
President Bola Tinubu has approved a request by Kebbi State Governor, Nasir Idris, for the full operationalisation of the Tsamiya Inland Dry Port to boost trade, investment and economic activities in the state.

Tinubu gave the approval on Tuesday during the All Progressives Congress presidential campaign rally at Haliru Abdu Township Stadium, Birnin Kebbi, the state capital.

Idris had appealed to the President to facilitate the full take-off of the dry port, describing it as a strategic economic project capable of transforming the state into a major commercial hub.

The governor said the facility would strengthen economic activities, improve trade and create employment opportunities for residents.

While commending the Federal Government’s interventions in agriculture, security, education and healthcare, Idris urged Tinubu to give special attention to the dry port and other critical infrastructure projects in the state.

“Mr President, what you are witnessing now tells you that Kebbi is for you, for APC, for all our candidates and me,” the governor said.

He also pledged to deliver 100 per cent votes for the APC in Kebbi during the 2027 general elections, saying the people were prepared to reciprocate Tinubu’s support for the state.

Responding, Tinubu assured the people of Kebbi that his administration would address their demands, including the development of critical infrastructure.

He specifically promised to deliver on road projects, including the road linking Kalgo to Bunza and extending towards border communities.

The President also urged residents to obtain their Permanent Voter Cards and vote for him, the governor and other APC candidates in the 2027 elections.

“I thank you from the bottom of my heart, the people of Kebbi State, for enduring the blazing sun to welcome me.

“I urge you all to get your PVCs to vote for me, the governor and other APC candidates in Kebbi State.

“I have received all your requests on road construction and the Kebbi dry port. I want to assure you that it is approved; we will deliver the dry port,” he added.

Tinubu said he returned to the state to appreciate residents for their support during the previous election and seek their renewed mandate.

Earlier, the Director-General of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Abdulaziz Yari, described Tinubu as a committed supporter of developments in the North, citing federal infrastructure projects and interventions across the region.

Yari challenged opposition politicians to tell northerners what they had done for the region when they occupied positions of authority.

He also urged voters in the North-West not to be deceived by the opposition’s claims that the APC had lost its political support in the region.

The rally was attended by Vice-President Kashim Shettima, Minister of Budget and Economic Planning Atiku Bagudu, APC National Chairman Nentawe Yilwatda, Senate President Godswill Akpabio, among others.

title: Tinubu campaigns in Kebbi and pleads with voters to support second-term bid
description:
By Haruna Aliyu, Birnin Kebbi



President Bola Ahmed Tinubu on Tuesday in Kebbi State appealed to Kebbi voters who gathered at Haliru Abdu Stadium to witness his campaign to obtain permanent voters’ cards to enable them to vote for him in the 2027 general elections.



Tinubu, alongside the preside
content:
By Haruna Aliyu, Birnin Kebbi

President Bola Ahmed Tinubu on Tuesday in Kebbi State appealed to Kebbi voters who gathered at Haliru Abdu Stadium to witness his campaign to obtain permanent voters’ cards to enable them to vote for him in the 2027 general elections.

Tinubu, alongside the presidential campaign council, told Kebbi voters to support the candidature of Tinubu and his vice president, Kashi Shettima, to enable them to continue enjoying massive infrastructure already being executed in Kebbi state, which he said is evidence of federal presence.

“I thank you from the bottom of my heart, the people of Kebbi State, for enduring the blazing sun to welcome me in Kebbi State. I urge you all to get your PVCs to vote for me, the governor, and other APC candidates in Kebbi State.”

The president added that he was in Kebbi during the last elections; he is here again to thank Kebbi voters for their massive support in the last polls and appealed to them to do so in 2027.

He pledged to continue his job in education security, healthcare and agriculture, describing it as a catalyst for food security in the country.

Earlier, the presidential campaign director general of the ruling All Progressives Congress, Senator Abdul Aziz Yarima, challenged the opposition candidate to tell the people of the north what he did to them when he was at helm of affairs.

Yari pointed out that Tinubu is the real lover of the north because of the massive infrastructure presence in the region.

He urged the opposition in the country to reconsider their claims that Tinubu has no support in the north, saying no president in Nigeria has developed the north like president Tinubu.

Yari appealed to Northwest voters not to be carried away by the lies of the opposition, who think the APC doesn’t have support in the north.

In his welcome address, the governor of Kebbi state, Dr Nasir Idris, thanked the president for the presidential campaign rally in Kebbi state.

He assured the president that Kebbi is for Tinubu and APC, for him as governor and all the candidates of the ruling party.

“Mr President, what you are witnessing now tells you that Kebbi is for you, for APC, for me and all our candidates.”

Idris pledged to deliver APC for Tinubu in the one hundred percent of the 2027 elections, saying the people of Kebbi state are eager to repay the good works of the president for the state.

While commending his efforts in agriculture, security, education and healthcare, he appealed to him to grant full operation of Tsamiya inland dry port to boost economic activities in the state; the request was granted by the mister president.

Kebbi rally was attended by three former Kebbi governors, serving budget minister Atiku Bagudu, APC National Chairman Netenwe, Senator Adams Oshimole, Senate President Godwill Apkabio, Speaker of the National Assembly, Abass Tajjudeen, former APC National Chairman, Vice President Kashi Shettima, Senator Remi Tinubu and top APC brass.

title: NDC urges opposition parties, Nigerians to scrutinise INEC voter register
description: The Nigeria Democratic Congress has urged opposition political parties and Nigerians to scrutinise the Independent National Electoral Commission’s preliminary voter register in every polling unit ahead of the 2027 general elections, warning that unexplained increases in registered voters could creat
content:
The Nigeria Democratic Congress has urged opposition political parties and Nigerians to scrutinise the Independent National Electoral Commission’s preliminary voter register in every polling unit ahead of the 2027 general elections, warning that unexplained increases in registered voters could create opportunities for electoral manipulation.

The party made the call in a statement on Tuesday by the Director-General of its Presidential Campaign Council, Ibrahim Abdulkarim.

Abdulkarim urged opposition parties to deploy agents to examine the register, identify unusual changes in voter numbers and submit claims and objections to INEC before the final register is certified.

He said, “Political parties, civil society organisations, and citizens should actively examine the displayed register in their polling units and file claims and objections before the window closes.”

He also urged opposition parties to deploy trained agents to polling units with unusual voter growth patterns on election day to protect the integrity of the electoral process.

The NDC said preliminary findings from an analysis of voter registration figures in Ebonyi State had revealed significant and unexplained increases across several polling units, raising concerns about possible irregularities in the voter database.

Abdulkarim warned that similar discrepancies could exist in other states and the Federal Capital Territory, calling for a nationwide examination of the register by political parties, civil society organisations and citizens.

According to him, the increases were significantly above historical growth rates recorded between previous election cycles and required urgent investigation.

He said, “One clear illustration of these concerns is the situation observed in Ebonyi State, where a joint analysis by the Data and Intelligence Directorate of Governance Index for the Coalition for Protection of Democracy and the Diaspora Affairs Directorate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress National Campaign Council flagged significant and unexplained increases in voter numbers across multiple polling units.”

Abdulkarim said the scale of the changes in Ebonyi was above the historical rate of growth recorded between previous elections, raising concerns about the possibility of similar anomalies elsewhere.

He said, “Such anomalies, wherever they occur, undermine public confidence. Between the 2019 and 2023 elections, national voter registration growth was relatively modest.

“Sudden, concentrated jumps that cannot be readily explained by new registrations or legitimate transfers therefore require urgent attention from the Independent National Electoral Commission. An inflated register creates opportunities for manipulation if not addressed before election day.”

The call comes as INEC intensifies preparations for the 2027 general elections. The presidential and National Assembly elections are scheduled for January 16, while the governorship and State Houses of Assembly elections will hold on February 6.

The commission conducted the physical display of the preliminary register nationwide from October 9 to 15, 2026, allowing registered voters to inspect their details and submit claims and objections.

Following concerns about accessibility, INEC also uploaded the preliminary register to its online platform on October 26 to enable wider public scrutiny.

The commission said it was processing claims and objections ahead of the publication of the final register on December 15, 2026.

The post NDC urges opposition parties, Nigerians to scrutinise INEC voter register appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Gombe APC chairman, campaign DG injured in road accident
description:
The Gombe State Chairman of the All Progressives Congress, Mohammed Dantata Ndus, and the Director-General of the party’s 2027 Campaign Council, Sa’adu Hassan, sustained injuries in a road accident on Tuesday while travelling to Balanga Local Government Area of the state.
The accident occurred short
content:
The Gombe State Chairman of the All Progressives Congress, Mohammed Dantata Ndus, and the Director-General of the party’s 2027 Campaign Council, Sa’adu Hassan, sustained injuries in a road accident on Tuesday while travelling to Balanga Local Government Area of the state.

The accident occurred shortly after the two party chieftains left Gombe to join the entourage of Governor Muhammadu Yahaya for the APC 2027 governorship campaign rally in Balanga North.

Preliminary reports indicated that Ndus sustained serious injuries, while Hassan suffered minor injuries.

Both officials were reportedly receiving medical attention at the Federal Teaching Hospital, Gombe, following the incident.

Confirming the accident in a telephone interview with our correspondent, the Sector Commander of the Federal Road Safety Corps in Gombe State, Samson Kaura, said, “I have received information about the accident. Although the Information is still sketchy, the APC chairman and DG are receiving treatment.”

Kaura, however, said he was still gathering further details about the incident and the condition of those involved.

Sources said the accident occurred after a motorcyclist allegedly appeared suddenly on the road, forcing the driver conveying the APC chairman to swerve to avoid a collision.

“The driver reportedly swerved to avoid hitting the motorcyclist, but the vehicle veered off the road in the process. One of the occupants of the motorcycle, which was carrying three, has died,” a source said.

The two injured officials were among APC leaders and stakeholders scheduled to accompany Governor Yahaya to the party’s 2027 governorship campaign rally in Balanga North.

Further details about the accident and the condition of the injured officials were still being awaited at the time of filing this report.

title: Strong economy vital to Nigeria’s foreign policy – FG
description:
The Federal  Government has said Nigeria’s foreign policy can only achieve meaningful results when anchored on a strong domestic foundation, stating the need to align the country’s diplomatic engagements with its national security and economic development priorities.
The Minister of State for Foreig
content:
The Federal  Government has said Nigeria’s foreign policy can only achieve meaningful results when anchored on a strong domestic foundation, stating the need to align the country’s diplomatic engagements with its national security and economic development priorities.

The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, Sola Enikanolaiye, stated this on Tuesday while declaring open the sixth edition of the Foreign Policy School at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Tafawa Balewa House, Abuja.

The three-day programme, organised by the Nigerian Institute of International Affairs and the Peace-Building Development Consult, is themed “Foreign Policy as a Tool for National Security and Economic Growth” and runs from November 16 to 18, 2026.

Enikanolaiye said the President Bola Tinubu-led administration was repositioning Nigeria’s foreign policy through reforms within the ministry, with improved diplomatic operations and a performance-driven approach to the country’s foreign missions.

He described the administration’s foreign policy as bold, pragmatic and citizen-centred, anchored on the reformulated 4Ds of Demography, Development, Diaspora and Democracy, with Nigeria and its citizens at the centre.

The minister, however, clarified that the renewed emphasis on domestic priorities did not diminish Africa’s position in Nigeria’s foreign policy, arguing that the country must first build a strong and resilient economy to sustain its leadership role on the continent.

He said the ongoing economic reforms under Tinubu were intended to provide the domestic foundation required for effective diplomatic engagement.

Recalling that the ministry adopted the motto, “Nigeria First”, in 2007, Enikanolaiye said the present administration was working to translate the principle into practical outcomes.

He explained that efforts were underway to reform the Ministry’s internal operations and reposition Nigerian missions abroad as economic hubs and centres for trade and technology facilitation, while improving consular services for Nigerians.

“We are moving beyond the mantra of diplomacy for diplomacy’s sake to a purposeful engagement calibrated to serve our people.”

To strengthen accountability and improve service delivery, the minister unveiled three instruments for assessing the performance of Nigeria’s foreign missions.

They include the Stations Charter, which assigns specific priorities to each mission; the Strategic Career Performance Evaluation and Review, an annual performance assessment for heads of mission; and the Global Best Practices Project, designed to enable Nigerian missions to identify international practices that could inform national policy.

He said the initiatives represented a shift from measuring diplomatic success by activities to assessing tangible results.

“Together, they mark a decisive shift from diplomacy as activity to diplomacy as measurable delivery,” he said.

On Nigeria’s international relations, Enikanolaiye said the country remained a confident, assertive and responsible global actor, committed to strategic autonomy, economic diplomacy and citizen diplomacy.

He added that Nigeria would continue to strengthen partnerships across the Atlantic, the Global South, the United Nations, the African Union and the Commonwealth, guided by reciprocity, mutual respect and respect for national sovereignty.

Addressing security challenges in West Africa, the minister identified insecurity in the Sahel, unconstitutional changes of government, the proliferation of small arms and humanitarian crises as major threats confronting the Economic Community of West African States.

He said Nigeria had no territorial ambitions in the region and remained committed to good neighbourliness, dialogue and mediation, including engagements with member states of the Alliance of Sahel States, to restore constitutional order and rebuild confidence.

“For Nigeria, it is zero tolerance for unconstitutional change of government; this being key to the defence and protection of our democracy.”

Enikanolaiye called for stronger preventive diplomacy, effective early-warning mechanisms and frank but respectful dialogue among African countries, noting that preventing conflicts was less costly than managing their consequences.

He described the Foreign Policy School as a strategic investment in the intellectual capacity of Nigeria’s diplomatic service, urging participants to see themselves as custodians of the country’s national interest.

The post Strong economy vital to Nigeria’s foreign policy – FG appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: NUC declares University of America campuses in Nigeria illegal
description:
The National Universities Commission has warned Nigerians against enrolling at the University of America, Curaçao, and its affiliated centres in the country, describing their operations as illegal.
The commission said the institution had been admitting students, conducting academic programmes and cl
content:
The National Universities Commission has warned Nigerians against enrolling at the University of America, Curaçao, and its affiliated centres in the country, describing their operations as illegal.

The commission said the institution had been admitting students, conducting academic programmes and claiming to award degrees through unauthorised campuses and learning centres in Nigeria.

In a public notice issued on Tuesday and signed by its Director of Public Affairs, Rita N. Okonjo, the NUC identified the affected centres as Cosmopolitan International Business School, Garki, Abuja, its purported Federal Capital Territory Learning Centre, and the University of America College of Science and Technology, also known as UAPOLY, in Ekpoma, Edo State.

It said neither the foreign university nor the centres had been approved by the commission to operate or award degrees in Nigeria.

The NUC also said investigations showed that the University of America was not accredited by any recognised agency.

The statement read, “Investigations have established that the University is not accredited by any agency recognised by the United States Department of Education or the Council for Higher Education Accreditation (CHEA).

“Its purported listing in the Integrated Postsecondary Education Data System (IPEDS), as well as its claimed registrations in California and Florida, does not confer accreditation or authority to award recognised university degrees.

“Similarly, its claims of approval by the Federal Ministry of Education, JAMB, NBTE and the Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria do not authorise it to operate a university or award degrees in Nigeria.

“The commission is particularly concerned about the institution’s advertisements offering programmes in Law, Nursing Science, Engineering, Pharmaceutical Science, Aerospace and Rocket Engineering, and postgraduate studies, including Ph.D. degrees, alongside misleading promises of NYSC mobilisation, professional recognition and Green Cards to live and work in the United States or Europe.

“The NUC emphasises that qualifications obtained from unapproved institutions are not recognised for NYSC mobilisation, professional registration with relevant Nigerian regulatory bodies or admission into the Nigerian Law School. Furthermore, the use of reputable public institutions as venues for ceremonies does not constitute endorsement or confer legitimacy on an unapproved university.”

Consequently, the NUC urged prospective students, parents, guardians and the general public to avoid the institution and its affiliated centres.

“Members of the public are advised against seeking admission, paying fees or participating in its academic programmes,” the notice stated.

The commission warned that individuals and organisations involved in the operations risked appropriate regulatory and legal action, advising the public to consult its website for the list of approved universities in Nigeria before making admission or financial commitments.

The warning comes as the NUC intensifies efforts to tackle the proliferation of illegal universities and degree-awarding institutions in the country.

Findings by PUNCH Online reveal that the authentic University of America, Curaçao, is located in Willemstad, the capital of Curaçao, a constituent country of the Kingdom of the Netherlands.

According to information on its official website, the institution operates a hybrid learning model of online distance education and on-campus sessions for programmes requiring practical or laboratory work.

However, the institution’s identity should be distinguished from the Nigerian campus named by the National Universities Commission.

A review of the website bearing the address uoa.edu.ng, which describes itself as the University of America Curaçao Gad Campus in Anambra State, shows several apparent shortcomings.

Its homepage contains no substantive account of the campus’s history, academic activities, recognition or accreditation, despite providing headings for those sections.

It also wrongly spells Anambra as “ANANBRA”.

The website also lists colleges and faculties without providing detailed information about their programmes or operations.

The University of America, Curaçao, is also distinct from the American University of Nigeria, located in Yola, Adamawa State.

The latter was founded by former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar and began admitting students in 2005. It was accredited by the NUC in 2008.

The post NUC declares University of America campuses in Nigeria illegal appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: FG warns against unrecognised degrees, titles from UK college
description:
The Federal Government has warned members of the public against obtaining unrecognised academic degrees and titles from the London College of Management and Leadership Education, United Kingdom.
The National Universities Commission said the college was offering Executive Master’s Degrees, honorary d
content:
The Federal Government has warned members of the public against obtaining unrecognised academic degrees and titles from the London College of Management and Leadership Education, United Kingdom.

The National Universities Commission said the college was offering Executive Master’s Degrees, honorary doctorates, professorships and associate professorships for specified fees, with plans to confer the awards at a ceremony scheduled for December 11, 2026, at the NAF Conference Centre, Abuja.

The commission, in a statement on Tuesday signed by its Director of Public Affairs, Rita Nkonjo, said the college was not a recognised higher education institution in the United Kingdom and was not authorised to award recognised university degrees in Nigeria.

“The Commission wishes to state categorically that the College is not a recognised higher education institution in the United Kingdom, nor is it authorised to award recognised university degrees in Nigeria,” the statement read.

It explained that the college’s registration as a private company with the UK Companies House did not confer academic recognition or degree-awarding authority on it.

The NUC expressed concern over what it described as the commercialisation of academic qualifications and titles, noting that the college had advertised prices for professorships, associate professorships, honorary doctorates and other awards.

“The Commission is particularly concerned that the College is commercialising academic qualifications and titles, with advertised prices for Professorship, Associate Professorship, Honorary Doctorates and other awards,” it stated.

It stressed that professorship and associate professorship were academic ranks conferred by recognised universities on qualified academic staff and were not qualifications or titles to be purchased.

“The public is hereby informed that Professorship and Associate Professorship are academic ranks conferred by recognised universities on qualified academic staff and are not qualifications or titles to be purchased,” the commission added.

The NUC also said that, under its guidelines, honorary doctoral degrees could only be conferred by approved Nigerian universities that had graduated doctoral students, without payment of fees and through appropriate nomination procedures.

“Furthermore, under the NUC’s guidelines, honorary doctoral degrees may only be conferred by approved Nigerian universities that have graduated doctoral students, without payment of fees and through appropriate nomination procedures,” it stated.

The commission further faulted the college’s proposed arrangement to present the awards at the NAF Conference Centre and Suites, Abuja, through an unnamed Nigerian learning partner.

It said the use of a reputable public facility as a venue did not amount to endorsement, accreditation or recognition of the college or its awards.

“The use of a reputable public facility as a venue does not constitute endorsement, accreditation or recognition of the College or its awards,” the statement read.

The NUC warned that using unrecognised degrees and academic titles to seek employment, promotion or professional recognition in Nigerian universities and the public service was unacceptable and could attract appropriate consequences.

“The Commission warns that the use of such unrecognised degrees and academic titles to seek employment, promotion or professional recognition in Nigerian universities and the public service is unacceptable and may attract appropriate consequences,” it added.

The commission consequently advised members of the public, particularly academics, public office holders and other professionals, to disregard the awards being offered by the college.

“Consequently, the NUC strongly advises members of the public, particularly academics, public office holders and other professionals, to disregard the awards being offered by the London College of Management and Leadership Education,” it stated.

It also warned the public against applying for, paying for or participating in any of the college’s award programmes.

“Members of the public are warned against applying for, paying for or participating in any of its award programmes,” the statement added.

The NUC urged members of the public to consult its website, www.nuc.edu.ng, for guidance on recognised universities and the conferment of honorary degrees in Nigeria.

The statement ended with a warning: “Beware of degree mills and fraudulent academic titles! Do not apply, do not pay, do not be deceived.”

The post FG warns against unrecognised degrees, titles from UK college appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Africa loses $125bn annually to illicit financial flows – AU
description:
Africa loses between $80bn and $125bn annually to illicit financial flows, with the losses accounting for about 25 per cent of the continent’s Gross Domestic Product, the African Union Advisory Board Against Corruption has said.
The Chairperson of the board, Kwami Edem Senanu, disclosed this at the
content:
Africa loses between $80bn and $125bn annually to illicit financial flows, with the losses accounting for about 25 per cent of the continent’s Gross Domestic Product, the African Union Advisory Board Against Corruption has said.

The Chairperson of the board, Kwami Edem Senanu, disclosed this at the first General Assembly of the African Asset Recovery Practitioners’ Forum in Abuja on Tuesday.

Senanu said the continent was losing approximately 50 per cent of its domestic revenue mobilisation to illicit financial flows, warning that the development was undermining efforts to address its socioeconomic challenges.

He said while some United Nations partners estimated the annual losses at about $80bn, other stakeholders put the figure at approximately $125bn.

“It is a fact that Africa continues to lose vast amounts of resources every year to corruption and illicit financial flows. Our UN partners quoted about $80bn annually.

“Some other stakeholders on the continent look at about $125bn being lost annually just to illicit financial flows. Approximately, perhaps about 50 per cent of our domestic revenue mobilisation and 25 per cent of GDP is being lost,” he said.

The AUABC chairperson said recovering stolen assets would provide African countries with resources to address critical infrastructure and social development deficits.

“Asset recovery provides for us the door to address substantive socioeconomic deficits on our African landscape. It also provides for us an opportunity to build and provide hospitals, schools, and roads and to address other key challenges of our people,” he stated.

Senanu said African countries needed to move beyond commitments and policy declarations to sustained action capable of tracing, recovering and returning illicitly acquired assets.

He explained that the African Asset Recovery Practitioners’ Forum was established to provide a platform for experts, prosecutors and anti-corruption institutions across the continent to work together to tackle illicit financial flows and recover stolen assets.

Speaking at the event, the Minister of Justice and Attorney General of the Federation, Lateef Fagbemi (SAN), called for a harmonised continental standard operating procedure for tracing, freezing, seizing, confiscating, repatriating and managing stolen assets across Africa.

He said the framework should respect the domestic laws and sovereignty of member states while setting common minimum standards, clear channels for timely mutual legal assistance, secure information-sharing protocols and safeguards for due process and third-party rights.

“Our objective must be simple, to make cooperation faster, recovery more effective, and the management of recovered wealth more transparent and accountable to the people of Africa,” he said.

The minister also urged stronger beneficial ownership transparency, improved digital asset-tracing capabilities, professional training and independent reporting on how recovered assets were used.

He stressed that asset recovery should not be judged only by the value of assets retrieved.

“The success of our asset recovery efforts must not be measured solely by the monetary value of assets recovered, but by the transparency of the process, effective asset management, accountability, and the ultimate developmental benefit to our citizens,” Fagbemi said.

Fagbemi said no country could tackle the concealment of criminal proceeds across borders alone.

“No country can effectively address these challenges in isolation,” he said, calling for stronger cooperation and information exchange among national and international institutions.

He welcomed the Forum’s decision to widen its reach beyond traditional law enforcement and anti-corruption bodies to include ministries of finance, tax authorities and revenue agencies.

In his welcome address, the Chairman of the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission and Chair of the Interim Steering Council of the AARP-F, Dr Musa Aliyu (SAN), said the assembly offered an opportunity to reflect on progress since the Forum’s establishment, exchange professional experiences and agree on a common direction for its future.

He said delegates would focus on three institutional milestones over the four days: validating the Forum’s Work Plan and Strategic Priorities, electing a Steering Council, and formally handing over from the Interim Steering Council to the new one.

title: PHOTOS: APC supporters throng Kebbi stadium for Tinubu’s rally
description:
President Bola Tinubu’s presidential rally in Kebbi State on Tuesday attracted a massive crowd of All Progressives Congress supporters, party loyalists and political stakeholders from across the state.
The rally, held at the Haliru Abdu Township Stadium in Birnin Kebbi, witnessed a large turnout of
content:
President Bola Tinubu’s presidential rally in Kebbi State on Tuesday attracted a massive crowd of All Progressives Congress supporters, party loyalists and political stakeholders from across the state.

The rally, held at the Haliru Abdu Township Stadium in Birnin Kebbi, witnessed a large turnout of party members, women, youths, farmers and grassroots mobilisers ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Governor Nasir Idris, who hosted the President and other top APC leaders, described the massive attendance as a demonstration of the people’s support for the party and its leadership.

The stadium was filled with supporters carrying party flags, banners and campaign materials as they gathered to welcome Tinubu and reaffirm their loyalty to the ruling party.

The turnout followed weeks of mobilisation by the state government, APC leadership and various support groups across the 21 Local Government Areas of the state.

Speaking ahead of the presidential visit, Idris had assured the President that the state was fully prepared to give him a rousing reception.

He said the government, party structures and supporters had put necessary arrangements in place to ensure a successful rally.

The rally also provided an opportunity for APC leaders to mobilise support for Tinubu’s re-election bid and strengthen the party’s political structures ahead of the 2027 elections.

The presence of party stakeholders and supporters from different parts of the state underscored the APC’s efforts to consolidate its political influence in Kebbi.

The presidential visit further highlighted the growing political activities in the state as parties intensify preparations for the next general elections.

title: Radda Warns Against ‘419 Politicians’ As Supporters Rally For APC In Katsina
description: Katsina State Governor, Malam Dikko Umaru Radda, has urged voters to reject what he described as “419 politicians” in the 2027 general elections, declaring that only leaders with proven records of service deserve the people’s mandate.The governor appealed on Tuesday during the Tinu
content:
Katsina State Governor, Malam Dikko Umaru Radda, has urged voters to reject what he described as “419 politicians” in the 2027 general elections, declaring that only leaders with proven records of service deserve the people’s mandate.

The governor appealed on Tuesday during the Tinubu/Dikko 2027 Campaign Council rally at the Mai’adua International Border Market in Mai’adua Local Government Area, where thousands of APC supporters gathered as the campaign tour continued across the Daura Senatorial Zone.

Addressing the enthusiastic crowd, Governor Radda said the massive turnout reflected public confidence in his administration’s performance, particularly in healthcare delivery, education, teacher recruitment, youth empowerment and other development programmes.

He expressed appreciation to the people of Mai’adua for their overwhelming support and pledged to consolidate on the achievements of his administration if re-elected.

“We have nothing to say but to thank God for the people of Mai’adua. We are grateful for the support we have received from women, youths and the elderly. This massive turnout shows that the people are satisfied with our achievements and leadership, especially in healthcare, education, teacher recruitment and empowerment.»

“Please don’t make the mistake of electing 419 politicians. I know you are not in support of such politicians, and by the grace of God, we will reciprocate this confidence if re-elected. You have also demonstrated that you are genuine supporters and true admirers of the late President Muhammadu Buhari.”

The governor also welcomed thousands of defectors from the African Democratic Congress (ADC) into the All Progressives Congress (APC), describing the development as further evidence of the ruling party’s growing popularity across the state.

The rally’s highlight was the presentation of an Award of Excellence to Governor Radda by health workers in Mai’adua Local Government Area in recognition of what they described as his transformative leadership and commitment to strengthening the state’s healthcare sector.

Earlier, Governor Radda commissioned the newly constructed Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) Dumurkul Division in Mai’adua Local Government Area.

The security facility was built by the Chairman of Mai’adua Local Government, Hon. Mamman Salisu Na-Allahu, as part of efforts to strengthen grassroots security and enhance the fight against insecurity in the border communities.

Commissioning the project, Governor Radda commended the council chairman for his foresight and commitment to safeguarding lives and property, stressing that security remains the cornerstone of his administration’s development agenda.

He charged officers of the NSCDC to uphold professionalism, diligence, and discipline in the discharge of their duties while fostering stronger collaboration with other security agencies and host communities.

The governor reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to supporting local governments and security agencies with the necessary resources to sustain peace and ensure the safety of residents across Katsina State.

title: Obama Would Beat Trump By 11 Points In 2028 Rematch, Poll Shows - But Constitution Bars Both Men - Check Below For Full Details
description: A Daily Mail/J.L. Partners poll of 1,013 US voters put Barack Obama ahead of Donald Trump 52% to 41% in a hypothetical 2028 rematch - but the 22nd Amendment bars both men from running again.
content:
A viral claim making the rounds on social media this week says former US President Barack Obama would defeat President Donald Trump by double digits if the two faced each other in a dream 2028 rematch. The claim is based on a real poll - here are the verified facts behind it.

The poll: a survey conducted by pollster J.L. Partners together with the Daily Mail asked 1,013 registered US voters who they would support if Obama and Trump ran against each other in 2028. The result: Obama 52%, Trump 41%, with 7% undecided - an 11-point lead for the former president.

Where Obama was strongest: the poll found Obama drawing heavy support from Hispanic, Black and Independent voters. Interestingly, the same survey showed Trump would narrowly defeat other potential Democratic challengers such as Hillary Clinton and Joe Biden in hypothetical matchups.

But here is the catch - neither man can legally run in 2028: the 22nd Amendment of the US Constitution, ratified in 1951 after Franklin D. Roosevelt was elected four times, prohibits anyone from being elected president more than twice. Obama served two full terms (2009-2017), and Trump is currently serving his second term - so both men are constitutionally barred from a 2028 run, no matter what any poll says.

Timing matters too: the poll is not actually new - it was conducted in July 2025 and has simply been resurfacing on social media recently, often shared as if it were fresh research. Trump has repeatedly joked about the idea of a third term despite the constitutional ban, keeping the speculation alive.

Why Nigerians are watching: US politics directly affects visa policy, and the Trump administration has already tightened several visa categories that Nigerians rely on. Whoever wins in 2028 - and it will legally be neither Obama nor Trump - will set the tone for Africa policy, migration and trade for the next four years.

Bottom line: the poll is real, the 52-41 result is accurate - but the "Obama vs Trump 2028" rematch itself is constitutionally impossible. Treat viral posts claiming otherwise with caution.

title: Senate chief whip, Monguno, others escape suspected Boko Haram attack in Borno
description:
By Ndahi Marama, Maiduguri



The Senate Chief Whip and Senator representing Borno North, Mohammed Tahir Monguno, alongside some All Progressives Congress (APC) stalwarts, have escaped Boko Haram’s attempted attack in the Kukawa Local Government Area of the state.



Sources said Monguno and a forme
content:
By Ndahi Marama, Maiduguri

The Senate Chief Whip and Senator representing Borno North, Mohammed Tahir Monguno, alongside some All Progressives Congress (APC) stalwarts, have escaped Boko Haram’s attempted attack in the Kukawa Local Government Area of the state.

Sources said Monguno and a former Governor Senator Maina Maaji Lawan, among others, stormed Kukawa in continuation of their 2027 campaign tour.

Earlier, Monguno had joined Governor Babagana Zulum at the official launch of the campaign in Monguno town last Sunday, before the governor disengaged on Monday from Monguno back to Maiduguri via a helicopter, while some of his entourage arrived in Maiduguri the same day by road.

Sources said some politicians, including the Senate Chief Whip, proceeded from Monguno to Kukawa to canvass for votes, in which the terrorists attempted to dislodge the community.

It was also gathered that, based on intelligence, troops of Operation Hadin Kai swung into action and foiled the attempted attacks by terrorists on the campaign entourage.

According to reports by Yerwa News Express, a local online media outlet said, “The terrorists fired three mortar bombs toward Kukawa on Monday while Mr Monguno, former Borno State Governor Maina Maaji Lawan, and other political figures were in the town for campaign activities.

“Local sources had earlier reported threats by the terrorists to disrupt the campaign, prompting heightened security measures.

“Troops of Operation Hadin Kai detected the movement of the terrorists around Kukawa and swiftly responded, preventing them from carrying out the attack.

“The campaign team subsequently returned safely to Monguno without any casualties.

“The terrorists reportedly made further attempts to attack the town throughout the night but were prevented from gaining access.”

In a related development, troops foiled another attempted attack on Kekeno village in the early hours of Tuesday, November 17, 2026.

“At about 1:20 a.m., alert troops spotted suspicious movements by suspected terrorists travelling on foot from the general area of Barwati toward Kekeno village.

“The troops immediately advanced toward the suspected terrorists and engaged them with heavy gunfire.

“Unable to withstand the troops’ firepower, the terrorists reportedly fled into the surrounding bush.

“The military said follow-up operations are ongoing in the area to track down the fleeing terrorists.

“It added that the situation remained calm, with troops maintaining heightened surveillance.” Sources and Yerwa Express News reported.

Due to a lack of telecommunication networks in the zone, the Senate Chief Whip’s phone number was not available at the time our correspondent dialled to confirm the incident.

title: Reps demand FG intervention as Gabon demolitions displace Nigerians
description:
The House of Representatives has called on the Federal Government to urgently intervene in the demolition of homes and business premises belonging to thousands of Nigerians, particularly Ilaje fishermen, by the Gabonese authorities.
The lawmakers warned that the affected Nigerians, many of whom have
content:
The House of Representatives has called on the Federal Government to urgently intervene in the demolition of homes and business premises belonging to thousands of Nigerians, particularly Ilaje fishermen, by the Gabonese authorities.

The lawmakers warned that the affected Nigerians, many of whom have lived and earned their livelihoods in the Central African country for decades, risk further hardship unless the Federal Government takes immediate steps to protect their welfare and secure their rights.

The resolution followed the adoption of a motion of urgent public importance sponsored by the member representing Ilaje/Ese Odo Federal Constituency of Ondo State, Donald Ojogo, during Tuesday’s plenary.

Moving the motion, Ojogo raised concerns over the fate of thousands of Nigerian fishermen who were reportedly displaced last week after Gabonese authorities demolished their residences along the country’s fishing coast for reasons yet to be made public.

He said, “The affected Nigerians, largely of Ilaje ethnic stock from Ondo State, had lived legally in Gabon for decades, engaging in fishing and related businesses as their primary means of livelihood.”

The lawmaker warned that the demolition had “left many of them homeless, disrupted their sources of income and exposed them to health risks, food insecurity and other humanitarian challenges.”

He expressed concern that failure by the Nigerian government to intervene could worsen the plight of the displaced citizens and raise further human rights and diplomatic concerns.

Ojogo maintained that the protection of Nigerians “should not end at the country’s borders,” insisting that the Federal Government had a responsibility to safeguard citizens living and working abroad.

He cited Section 14(2)(b) of the 1999 Constitution, which identifies the security and welfare of the people as the primary purpose of government, alongside the provisions of Chapter II on the Fundamental Objectives and Directive Principles of State Policy.

The lawmaker also drew attention to regional cooperation frameworks governing the Gulf of Guinea, particularly those relating to the protection of marine resources and fishing activities.

He noted that countries with interests in the Gulf of Guinea had demonstrated the capacity to protect shared marine resources and provide opportunities for legitimate fishing businesses, including those operated by foreign nationals.

Ojogo argued that the circumstances surrounding the demolition required urgent diplomatic engagement to establish the reasons for the action and prevent further hardship for the affected Nigerians.

Following the adoption of the motion, the House urged the Federal Government to urgently establish the circumstances surrounding the demolition and take necessary steps to ensure that the welfare and rights of the affected Nigerians were protected.

The House subsequently mandated its Committees on Foreign Affairs, Diaspora, Inland Waterways, and Cooperation and Integration in Africa to intervene in the matter and investigate the circumstances surrounding the displacement.

The committees are also expected to ascertain the welfare and living conditions of the affected Nigerians, particularly the Ilaje fishermen, and report their findings to the House within 14 legislative days.

The intervention comes against the backdrop of the longstanding presence of Nigerian fishing communities in parts of the Gulf of Guinea, where cross-border fishing and maritime trade provide livelihoods for many coastal populations.

The Ilaje, an indigenous coastal community in Ondo State, have a long history of fishing and maritime-related economic activities. Some members of the community have established livelihoods beyond Nigeria’s shores, making the protection of their interests abroad an important concern for Nigerian diplomatic and consular authorities.

The House’s resolution is expected to bring the matter before the relevant government agencies, particularly the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Nigeria’s diplomatic mission in Gabon, for engagement with the Gabonese authorities.

title: NDIC sensitises A’Ibom corps members on safe banking, deposit protection
description:
‎The Nigeria Deposit Insurance Corporation has sensitised corps members in Akwa Ibom State on deposit protection and the need to guard against digital fraud.
‎
‎The sensitisation was held on Tuesday at the National Youth Service Corps orientation camp in Ikot Itie Udung community, Nsit Atai Local Go
content:
‎The Nigeria Deposit Insurance Corporation has sensitised corps members in Akwa Ibom State on deposit protection and the need to guard against digital fraud.
‎
‎The sensitisation was held on Tuesday at the National Youth Service Corps orientation camp in Ikot Itie Udung community, Nsit Atai Local Government Area of the state, as part of efforts to ensure that every household in the country knows that their deposits are protected.
‎
‎Speaking during the exercise, the NDIC Port Harcourt Zonal Controller, Adefemi Shaba, said depositors remain key stakeholders of the corporation, hence the need to engage corps members and educate them on their rights.
‎
‎He said, “NDIC decided to meet the corps members in camp to let them know that the corporation exists. We are here to protect your deposits and sensitise you on how the deposit insurance scheme works.
‎
‎“The management of the corporation felt that we should gather the corpers together, talk to them, let them know about their deposit protection, and let them know that there is the NDIC that protects their deposits. We want a situation where every household will know that their deposit is protected by NDIC. So, we take this sensitisation beyond corps members.”
‎
‎Shaba explained that the NDIC visits markets in conjunction with market associations, participates in trade fairs where it educates the public, and also organises programmes for journalists under the Finance Correspondents Association of Nigeria, as well as for judges.
‎
‎He added that the NDIC has also begun teaching corps members how to save smartly and invest wisely, noting that the programme would be expanded in stages.
‎
‎On the rise in digital fraud, Shaba advised members of the public never to compromise their banking details, noting that as security measures improve, criminals also devise new tricks, urging depositors to remain vigilant and to promptly report suspicious transactions to their banks and relevant authorities.
‎
‎In her remarks, the state NYSC Coordinator, Ngozi Akuagbaogu, described the initiative as a welcome development, noting that the camp was privileged to be among the states selected to benefit from the sensitisation exercise.
‎
‎She expressed joy over the programme, stressing that such an opportunity to educate participants on the importance of financial awareness had not been available at the camp before.
‎
‎”The sensitisation has helped participants gain a better understanding of the role of the NDIC, particularly in protecting bank depositors and promoting confidence in the banking system”, Akuagbaogu said.
‎
‎Speaking on behalf of the participants, ThankGod Chigozie described the sensitisation lecture organised by the corporation as timely and life-changing.
‎
‎He thanked the corporation for the lecture, saying it had exposed corps members to mistakes they make in managing their finances and how to correct them.

The post NDIC sensitises A’Ibom corps members on safe banking, deposit protection appeared first on Punch Newspapers.
