title: Fani-Kayode faces diplomatic reprimand as South Africa invokes Vienna Convention, summons him over livestream controversy
description: South Africa’s Department of International Relations and Cooperation (DIRCO) has summoned Nigeria’s newly accredited High Commissioner, Ambassador Femi Fani-Kayode, over his public comments following the controversy surrounding the livestream of his presentation of credentials to President Cyril Ram
content:
South Africa’s Department of International Relations and Cooperation (DIRCO) has summoned Nigeria’s newly accredited High Commissioner, Ambassador Femi Fani-Kayode, over his public comments following the controversy surrounding the livestream of his presentation of credentials to President Cyril Ramaphosa.

The meeting took place on Tuesday, November 17, 2026, when DIRCO Director-General, Zane Dangor, met with the Nigerian envoy to convey Pretoria’s concerns about events that followed the presentation of his Letters of Credence, as well as his subsequent remarks on social media.

In a statement, the South African foreign ministry said Dangor reminded Fani-Kayode of the provisions of Article 41 of the 1961 Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations, which requires diplomats to conduct official business with their host governments through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs or other established diplomatic channels.

The reminder underscored Pretoria’s position that official communications and diplomatic disagreements should be handled through recognised government-to-government procedures.

The development followed Fani-Kayode’s public allegation that Nigeria was deliberately excluded from the livestream of the November 13 ceremony in Pretoria, where ambassadors from 15 countries presented their credentials to Ramaphosa.

The Nigerian envoy had complained that the introductions and speeches of 14 other ambassadors were broadcast, while Nigeria’s segment was omitted from the initial livestream.

He subsequently criticised the South African Presidency’s media team and said he raised the matter directly with Ramaphosa after the ceremony.

However, the South African President’s spokesperson, Vincent Magwenya, disputed Fani-Kayode’s account of the President’s intervention, insisting that Ramaphosa had no authority to interfere with the operational and editorial decisions of the South African Broadcasting Corporation.

The South African Presidency later released the full recording of the ceremony, including Fani-Kayode’s speech.

DIRCO’s statement did not indicate that the Nigerian envoy had been recalled or declared persona non grata. Rather, it emphasised the need to observe diplomatic protocols and maintain official communication through recognised channels.

During the meeting, Dangor also reaffirmed South Africa’s commitment to preserving its longstanding relationship with Nigeria, describing the bilateral ties as being founded on mutual respect, friendship and cooperation.

He said Pretoria remained committed to strengthening its strategic partnership with Abuja and maintaining constructive diplomatic engagement in the spirit of African solidarity.

A diplomatic demarche is a formal communication through which a government conveys its concerns or position to another government or its representative. It does not automatically mean a breakdown in diplomatic relations.

The meeting comes barely four days after Fani-Kayode formally presented his Letters of Credence to Ramaphosa, marking the commencement of his assignment as Nigeria’s High Commissioner to South Africa.

The Nigerian envoy had pledged to work towards rebuilding relations between both countries and addressing areas of mutual concern through dialogue.

The latest development has, however, placed diplomatic protocol and the handling of official disagreements at the centre of his early assignment in Pretoria.

title: Too Late For Opposition To Agree On Consensus Candidate, Kalu On 2027 Election
description: Senator Orji Uzor Kalu, representing Abia North, has declared that it is too late for opposition political parties to agree on a consensus presidential candidate ahead of the 2027 general elections.Speaking to Senate correspondents Tuesday in response to questions about plans by opposition parties t
content:
Senator Orji Uzor Kalu, representing Abia North, has declared that it is too late for opposition political parties to agree on a consensus presidential candidate ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Speaking to Senate correspondents Tuesday in response to questions about plans by opposition parties to meet on the 23rd of this month to discuss a possible consensus candidate, Sen. Kalu argued that the opposition had already delayed efforts to build a formidable political coalition.

He stated that a united opposition could have posed a challenge to the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) but maintained that the time left was insufficient for the parties to agree on a common candidate.

The former Abia State governor, who expressed confidence in President Bola Tinubu’s re-election prospects, attributed this to what he described as the APC’s extensive grassroots support and political network across the country.

He consequently described the 2027 presidential election as a contest of ‘Tinubu versus Tinubu’, arguing that none of the opposition contenders had the political strength to defeat the President.

On the recurring incidents of political violence, Sen. Kalu condemned the use of thugs, intimidation and physical attacks during election campaigns.

He further described political violence as an unfortunate feature of Nigeria’s political history since independence and urged politicians and their supporters to embrace peaceful campaigns and democratic engagement.

According to him, electoral victory should be determined by candidates’ records, achievements and capacity to deliver good governance, rather than violence and intimidation.

The lawmaker equally noted that no political contest was worth the loss of human lives, insisting that nobody should encourage supporters to engage in violence, calling for political tolerance, noting that prominent politicians across party lines maintained cordial personal relationships despite their differences.

title: 2027: Kalu dismisses opposition’s planned alliance against Tinubu
description: Former Abia State Governor and Senator representing Abia North, Orji Uzor Kalu, has dismissed the planned November 23 meeting of opposition parties to agree on a consensus presidential candidate for the 2027 election, describing the move as belated and unlikely to pose a serious challenge to Preside
content:
Former Abia State Governor and Senator representing Abia North, Orji Uzor Kalu, has dismissed the planned November 23 meeting of opposition parties to agree on a consensus presidential candidate for the 2027 election, describing the move as belated and unlikely to pose a serious challenge to President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid.

Kalu said the opposition parties, including the African Democratic Congress and the Peoples Democratic Party, had lost the opportunity to build a united front capable of mounting a formidable challenge to the ruling All Progressives Congress.

He argued that the divisions and disagreements among opposition figures had made it difficult for them to agree on a common candidate, adding that an earlier and sincere alliance could have caused concern within the APC.

The former governor spoke on Tuesday in Abuja after receiving the Best Impactful Representation Award from the Senate Press Corps.

“The meeting has no meaning to people like me. If people cannot sit and agree to work together. Is it in the middle of the Atlantic Ocean which everybody is fighting to escape that they will agree on who should be the presidential candidate? The game is too late for them,” he said.

Kalu, who was the presidential candidate of the Progressive Peoples Alliance in the 2007 election, said a united opposition would have at least made the ruling party more concerned about the political contest.

“I thought they could have sincerely come together and presented one presidential candidate. That would have made us start having headaches. Not that they would win,” Kalu said.

He, however, insisted that the political situation currently favoured Tinubu, describing the 2027 presidential election as a contest without a credible opposition challenge.

“I have told them many times. The election is Tinubu versus Tinubu. That is the truth. I ran for president in 2007. So I am more experienced than all of them. The election is Tinubu versus Tinubu. That is what it is on the ground today, if you understand this politics,” he said.

Kalu added, “I know people might laugh, people might start making jokes. I really have no opposition. Let me leave it there. Let them finish the meeting. Let us see the outcome of the meeting.”

The senator also dismissed reports that the APC was becoming apprehensive over the activities of opposition parties, insisting that the ruling party was not intimidated by their planned alliance.

“One of the newspapers reported that APC people are jittery. We are not jittery. Rather, we are playing the game according to the rules. We cannot go out and start fighting. It is people fighting us. We have never fought anybody,” he said.

He challenged opposition parties to move beyond political confrontations and present Nigerians with alternative policies and programmes capable of addressing the country’s challenges.

According to him, opposition politicians should focus on explaining what they would do differently if elected rather than relying on attacks against the ruling party.

“Fighting is not in the name of the game. They should go and tell the people what they will do for them. If they can do anything better, let them say it. If I am in opposition and running for president, I will set an alternative agenda for Nigeria to see what I will do.

“None of these presidential candidates have been able to do that. We want to see an alternative agenda. You don’t pay people to go and say the APC is jittery. Jittery for whom? How can a lion fear a lamb?” Kalu asked.

The senator maintained that Tinubu and the APC were interested in a fair political contest and national unity, warning against actions capable of escalating political tensions.

“What the APC is looking for and what the president has been preaching is fair play. Let us not look for anybody’s trouble. But we cannot be in our room, and you come and pour us hot water. We must defend ourselves. So, let us not cause trouble. I need the unity of this country. It is very important.

“People want this country to disintegrate. But that is not what we are talking about now. They should allow the lion to lie with the lamb. Can a lion lie with a lamb? Yes. A lion and a lamb can lie together if they are civilised enough,” he said.

The planned opposition meeting comes amid ongoing discussions among opposition leaders over possible cooperation and the emergence of a common presidential candidate to challenge the APC in 2027.

title: Ajasa’s death painful loss to journalism, Vanguard — Atiku mourns
description:
Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar has described the death of Vanguard Media Limited’s Online Editor, Olufemi Ajasa, as a painful loss to the journalism profession and the media organisation, extending his condolences to the management, staff and family of the deceased.



Atiku, in a condolence m
content:
Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar has described the death of Vanguard Media Limited’s Online Editor, Olufemi Ajasa, as a painful loss to the journalism profession and the media organisation, extending his condolences to the management, staff and family of the deceased.

Atiku, in a condolence message on his X handle on Tuesday, expressed sadness over Ajasa’s death at the age of 44, saying his passing was a reminder of how suddenly a life devoted to work, family and service could be cut short.

He wrote, “Ajasa’s passing is a deep loss to @vanguardngrnews and to the journalism profession. Behind every story published and every deadline met is a commitment to keeping the public informed.

“His colleagues have lost a valued teammate, the media community a respected professional, and his family a beloved son, husband, father and brother.”

Atiku also extended his condolences to the management and staff of Vanguard Media Limited, the newspaper’s Editor, Eze Anaba, and everyone who knew and worked with the late journalist.

“I extend my heartfelt condolences to the management and staff of Vanguard Media Limited, Editor Eze Anaba, and all who loved and worked with him,” the statement added.

“May the memories they shared bring comfort in this difficult hour, and may God grant his family strength to bear this immeasurable loss. “May his soul rest in peace.”

Ajasa died on Sunday at the Lagos University Teaching Hospital, LUTH, after a brief illness. He was aged 44, according to a statement by the management of Vanguard Media Limited.

His death has continued to attract tributes from political figures, media practitioners and other Nigerians, who have mourned his passing and remembered his contributions to journalism.

The
content:
Taraba State Governor Agbu Kefas on Tuesday approved full payment of the Consolidated Academic Tools Allowance, Consolidated Non-Teaching Tools Allowance, and Earned Academic Allowances to staff of the state-owned tertiary institutions, including outstanding arrears dating back to January 2026.

The governor also appealed to the striking unions to suspend their industrial action and allow academic activities to resume in the affected institutions.

The approval followed the recommendations of a committee set up by the state government to examine wage-related concerns and other issues surrounding the allowances.

The governor announced the approval while receiving the committee’s report at the TY Danjuma House, in Jalingo, the state capital.

He equally directed the Commissioner for Tertiary Education and his counterpart in the Finance Ministry to see to the modalities of the payments.

“I have received the report of the committee, and I want to announce that I have approved the committee’s recommendations, including 100 per cent payment of CATA, CONTTA and EAA allowances of all outstanding arrears from January 2026.

“I want to appeal to the unions to reciprocate the government’s intervention by suspending the strike to enable students to return to their classrooms, especially for those of Taraba State University who were writing their final year examinations.

“The Commissioner for Tertiary Education and the Commissioner for Finance are hereby directed to work out modalities for the payment. All allowances due to the striking unions would be paid in full,” he directed.

The industrial action, which has disrupted teaching, learning and other academic activities in the state-owned tertiary institutions in the past month, has raised concerns among students, parents and other stakeholders over the implications for academic calendars and students’ progression.

The governor urged the unions to always embrace dialogue and cooperation in resolving the dispute, stressing the need to restore normal academic activities in the institutions.

title: Flamingos’ World Cup-winning coach Akeem Busari makes CAF award shortlist (Full list)
description:
Nigeria’s U-17 women’s national team coach, Akeem Busari, has earned a nomination for the 2026 Confederation of African Football (CAF) Women’s Coach of the Year award.
The nomination comes after Busari guided the Flamingos to a historic triumph at the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup, where Nigeria claim
content:
Nigeria’s U-17 women’s national team coach, Akeem Busari, has earned a nomination for the 2026 Confederation of African Football (CAF) Women’s Coach of the Year award.

The nomination comes after Busari guided the Flamingos to a historic triumph at the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup, where Nigeria claimed the title for the first time.

The Nigerian team secured the historic victory with a 2-1 win over Japan in the final, played in Rabat, Morocco, on November 7.

Following the achievement, Busari was included among 10 coaches shortlisted by CAF in its final list of nominees for the women’s categories ahead of the 2026 CAF Awards.

Other nominees include Farid Benstiti of Algeria, Silveria Nedio of Cabo Verde, Valentine Nguele of Cameroon, Kim Lars Bjorkegren of Ghana, Lovemore Fazili of Malawi, Hicham Drissi of AS FAR, Jorge Vilda of Morocco, Desiree Ellis of South Africa and Bakari Nyundo Shime of Tanzania.

CAF said the final three women’s categories were announced after the conclusion of the CAF Women’s Champions League in Egypt on Sunday, November 15.

“The three categories were held back to ensure that performances at Africa’s premier women’s club competition could be considered before the nominees were finalised,” the continental football governing body said.

The other two categories are Women’s Interclub Player of the Year and Women’s Club of the Year.

The ceremony will hold at the Professor Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture and the Arts, popularly known as the National Theatre, in Lagos on Wednesday, December 2, beginning at 7pm local time.

Voting for the awards is taking place from November 5 to 20, with CAF member associations, clubs and eligible coaches and captains participating in the process.

title: Pattinson ‘Perfect’ As Bond, Says ‘Twilight’ Co-Star After Viral Post
description: Actor Justin Chon who starred alongside Robert Pattinson in the “Twilight” series told AFP Tuesday that his former co-star was “perfect” for the coveted role of James Bond.Chon was speaking after wryly posting on Instagram that he may even have predicted Pattinson’s ris
content:
Actor Justin Chon who starred alongside Robert Pattinson in the “Twilight” series told AFP Tuesday that his former co-star was “perfect” for the coveted role of James Bond.

Chon was speaking after wryly posting on Instagram that he may even have predicted Pattinson’s rise to be the world’s top secret agent all those years ago.

“Not saying I predicted this but …” Chon posted online late Monday, before showing a clip from the franchise’s first film in which his character Eric Yorkie is handing out posters for the school prom.

“Gambling, tuxedos, and Bond. James Bond,” Yorkie says, before the camera tracks to a shot of Pattinson as vampire Edward Cullen emerging from a white car.

Chon laughed about his Instagram post which had received more than 2.5 million views by Tuesday afternoon.

“It’s like 20 years ago and we’re all young you know, I don’t think those kind of thoughts even enter your mind frame at all,” Chon told AFP.

“But I think if someone had told me, hey, this guy, 20 years from now, is going to play James Bond, I don’t think I would doubt it,” the American-Korean actor added.

“Even back then I think everybody knew he was incredibly talented, and he is British so it’s not like a departure.”

Pattinson was named on Monday as the new incarnation of agent 007, taking over from Daniel Craig for the Bond reboot, although no release date has been published by new studio owner Amazon MGM.

Chon, who has gone on to direct films including “Gook” which won an award at the Sundance festival in 2017, described the 40-year-old Pattinson as “a chameleon” who was “going to do an absolutely incredible job”.

“I think he absolutely brings a new audience to the franchise,” Chon told AFP in an interview via video call from California, acknowledging Amazon MGM had a lot riding on the success of the Bond franchise.

“I think he’s really turned out to be one of our generation’s greatest actors. The guy… can do any accent, can do any role,” Chon added.

“It’s been such a pleasure watching him grow and becoming such a sort of behemoth in the industry. I’m definitely going to cheer him on.”

The post Pattinson ‘Perfect’ As Bond, Says ‘Twilight’ Co-Star After Viral Post appeared first on Channels Television.

title: ₦70,000 Transport Controversy: FG Constitutes Committee To Review New Minimum Wages For Workers
description: The Federal Government has approved the constitution of a new committee to comprehensively examine and address the issues raised by the Trade Union Congress (TUC) regarding a new minimum wage for Nigerian workers.The development was revealed by the TUC’s Secretary-General, Comrade General N.A.
content:
The Federal Government has approved the constitution of a new committee to comprehensively examine and address the issues raised by the Trade Union Congress (TUC) regarding a new minimum wage for Nigerian workers.

The development was revealed by the TUC’s Secretary-General, Comrade General N.A. Toro, in a statement on Tuesday, following a meeting with the Federal Government in response to a letter dated 8th October, 2026, titled “Request for an Urgent Meeting to Address Critical National Economic, Security and Labour Challenges,” submitted by the Union.

While the meeting was chaired by the Secretary to the Government of the Federation (SGF), Senator George Akume, the TUC delegation was led by the President, Comrade Engr. Festus Osifo, and comprised Comrade General N.A. Toro, Secretary-General; Comrade Shehu Mohammed, Deputy President; Comrade Akintola Benjamin, Trustee; and Comrade Kamal Ibrahim, Auditor II.

Also in attendance were the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation and the Permanent Secretary in the Office of the Secretary to the Government of the Federation, Ibrahim Kana.

While providing further explanation, TUC noted that it had insisted on a salary increment rather than a mere one-off N70,000 six-month transportation package.

“In the course of the deliberations, the TUC made its position unequivocally clear on the proposed ₦70,000 transport intervention for a period of six months, which it rejected, preferring instead a salary increase pending the commencement and conclusion of discussions on a new National Minimum Wage.

“This position, alongside the other demands and concerns raised by Congress, will form part of the issues to be thoroughly interrogated by the High-Powered Committee”, the statement read in part.

According to the statement, the government has already attended to some of the demands raised by the TUC.

“The Committee will therefore undertake a comprehensive review and reconciliation of the issues, establish the extent of actions already taken by the Government, identify outstanding matters and make appropriate findings and recommendations”, the statement said in part.

The composition of the High-Powered Committee includes three representatives from the TUC, led by the Secretary-General, Office of the Secretary to the Government of the Federation (OSGF), Permanent Secretary, Office of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation (OHCSF), National Salaries, Incomes and Wages Commission, and the Federal Ministry of Labour and Employment.

The High-Powered Committee is expected to commence work immediately and submit its report to the Secretary to the Government of the Federation within two weeks.

The post ₦70,000 Transport Controversy: FG Constitutes Committee To Review New Minimum Wages For Workers appeared first on Channels Television.

title: ‘Nigeria is finished’ narrative costing economy investments, jobs — FG
description:
By John Alechenu, Abuja



The Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, has said Nigeria is paying a heavy economic price for negative narratives, misinformation and damaging perceptions about the country.



Negative stories, he said, are not merely public relati
content:
By John Alechenu, Abuja

The Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, has said Nigeria is paying a heavy economic price for negative narratives, misinformation and damaging perceptions about the country.

Negative stories, he said, are not merely public relations problems. They discourage investors, constrain businesses, and drive away skilled talent.

Oyedele spoke at the ongoing 2026 World Public Relations Forum (WPRF) in Abuja on Tuesday.

He identified public trust as a critical factor in attracting investment, sustaining businesses and securing citizens’ support for government policies.

According to him, trust is the currency that underpins economic activities and determines whether citizens cooperate with government, investors commit capital and businesses expand.

Oyedele said, “Trust is the one currency that sits beneath all the other currencies. When trust is strong, citizens cooperate, capital flows, businesses invest, and reforms get a fair hearing. When trust is weak, even sound policies meet suspicion, and every explanation sounds like an excuse.”

The minister said the economic consequences of negative narratives are often overlooked. The country could lose investments and valuable human capital when its public image was dominated by stories of failure and hopelessness.

He cited damaging perceptions expressed in phrases such as “Nigeria is finished”, “Nigeria is a scam”, and “Nigeria happened to me”, warning that such narratives could influence investment decisions and undermine confidence in the country’s economic prospects.

Oyedele further explained that the cost went beyond reputational damage. Investors demand higher returns to compensate for perceived risks, businesses postpone expansion plans, and talented Nigerians seek opportunities elsewhere.

He, however, acknowledged that citizens have the right to expose government failures, demand accountability and draw attention to the difficulties they faced. Responsible communication, he insisted, must not be confused with suppressing criticism.

The country’s story must reflect both its challenges and progress, he added. Government and businesses could not rely on publicity to conceal poor performance or substitute communication for service delivery.

“We cannot communicate our way out of conflicts,” he said.

Oyedele stressed that public communication must be backed by measurable results. Citizens judged government not by announcements or budgetary provisions but by what they experienced.

The minister noted that the disconnect between government claims and citizens’ everyday experiences had contributed to distrust, making it difficult for even well-intentioned policies to gain public acceptance.

He used the public’s response to declining inflation figures to illustrate the challenge. Although the October 2026 inflation rate was reported at 14.06 per cent, the lowest in six years, many Nigerians remain unconvinced because prices of essential commodities such as bread and milk were still high.

Oyedele equally explained that a decline in inflation did not mean prices were falling but that the rate at which prices increased was slowing down. Failure to explain that distinction, he said, could deepen frustration and create expectations that further influence market behaviour.

In the controversy surrounding the government’s tax reforms, Oyedele said misinformation had distorted the intention and benefits of the measures, including provisions designed to protect small businesses and exempt low-income earners.

Some of the people the reforms were intended to benefit had opposed them because of misleading information, he said, underscoring the need for clear and sustained public engagement.

“Facts do not defend themselves,” he said, adding that “in a contest between a careful explanation and a frightening headline, the headline wins.”

The minister also expressed concern about social media platforms, where sensational and divisive content often attracts more attention than factual corrections.

“Outrage pays, correction does not,” he said.

He warned that the growing use of artificial intelligence had made the spread of misinformation more dangerous, as convincing images, voices and documents could now be fabricated and circulated rapidly.

Oyedele urged public relations and communication professionals to become involved in policy formulation from the beginning rather than being brought in only when government or businesses faced communication crises.

He challenged media organisations, influencers and other information gatekeepers to take greater responsibility for the content they circulate.

“Verify before you amplify. Correct as loudly as you reported when you make mistakes. Hold good news and bad news to the same standard of proof,” he urged.

He also called on government institutions and businesses to make policy and economic information accessible, respond to public complaints and measure the effectiveness of their communication by whether people understood the message and could see the results.

Oyedele maintained that the credibility of any national or corporate narrative ultimately depended on the lived experiences of the people, not the volume of publicity deployed to promote it. “Experiencing is knowing,” he said.

The post ‘Nigeria is finished’ narrative costing economy investments, jobs — FG appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Fan gets 11-month jail term for racist abuse of Mbappe
description:
A Spanish court has sentenced a football fan to 11 months in prison for racially abusing Real Madrid forward Kylian Mbappe during a La Liga match against Real Oviedo in August 2025.
Real Madrid disclosed this in a statement on Tuesday, saying the Second Section of the Provincial Court of Asturias fo
content:
A Spanish court has sentenced a football fan to 11 months in prison for racially abusing Real Madrid forward Kylian Mbappe during a La Liga match against Real Oviedo in August 2025.

Real Madrid disclosed this in a statement on Tuesday, saying the Second Section of the Provincial Court of Asturias found the individual guilty of a hate crime over racist insults directed at Mbappe during the fixture at the Carlos Tartiere Stadium on August 24, 2025.

The club said the sentence also included disqualification penalties and a financial fine.

“The suspension of the prison sentence is conditional upon the individual not attending football stadiums hosting official sports competitions for a period of two years,” the statement said.

Real Madrid said the latest ruling added to previous criminal convictions over racist abuse directed at its players at the Mestalla, Son Moix, Vallecas and José Zorrilla stadiums.

The club, which acted as a private prosecutor in the case, reaffirmed its commitment to tackling racism in football.

“Real Madrid, which has acted as a private prosecutor in this case and continues to do so in others involving similar incidents, reaffirms its commitment to combating racism and eradicating any racist behaviour in football and sports,” it added.

PUNCH Online reports that the incident occurred in the 37th minute of the match, shortly after Mbappe scored Real Madrid’s opening goal in their 3-0 victory.

The supporter reportedly made monkey gestures and noises directed at the French forward as he celebrated with his teammates. The incident was captured on video and subsequently circulated on television and social media, drawing widespread condemnation.

La Liga reported the incident to the relevant football authorities and later expanded its complaint to include racist noises directed at Brazilian forward Vinicius Junior when he came on as a substitute in the 63rd minute.

Spanish police arrested a Real Oviedo supporter on September 10, 2025, after identifying him through an analysis of video footage from the match. He was investigated for alleged offences against moral integrity and hate crime.

Real Oviedo subsequently apologised to Mbappe and Real Madrid over the incident, saying it would take appropriate action against the supporter.

title: Why goods remain expensive despite falling inflation — Oyedele
description:
The Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, on Tuesday, warned Nigerians against interpreting falling inflation as a reduction in the prices of goods and services, explaining that it only means prices are rising at a slower rate.
Oyedele said the continued high c
content:
The Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, on Tuesday, warned Nigerians against interpreting falling inflation as a reduction in the prices of goods and services, explaining that it only means prices are rising at a slower rate.

Oyedele said the continued high cost of essential commodities, including bread and milk, had fuelled public doubts about declining inflation figures, highlighting the need for better communication of the government’s economic reforms.

He explained that falling inflation did not mean prices of goods and services were falling, but that they were rising more slowly.

The minister spoke at the Global Alliance World Public Relations Forum in Abuja.

Using the latest inflation figures as an example, the minister said Nigeria’s inflation rate for October 2026 stood at 14.06 per cent, its lowest level in six years, describing the development as a direct reflection of the reforms introduced by the administration of President Bola Tinubu.

He said, “The confusion is understandable, and we must own our part of it. Falling inflation does not mean falling prices. It means prices are rising more slowly than before.”

Continuing, Oyedele explained that households could find it difficult to accept declining inflation figures when their daily market expenses remained high, adding that the disconnect could undermine confidence in official economic data.

According to him, when consumers lose confidence in inflation figures, their expectations could influence market behaviour, as traders and producers increase prices in anticipation of further increases in the cost of goods.

He said, “When people stop believing in numbers, they expect prices to rise, and expectations behave like instructions. So traders mark up in advance. Producers protect themselves. The baker and the dairy supplier price in that increase because they fear prices will go up. And the increase arrives in higher prices of bread and milk. It’s a self-fulfilling cycle.”

The minister argued that government communication must acknowledge the economic realities confronting households while explaining improvements in macroeconomic indicators.

“An improving indicator does not mean a struggling family’s experience is untrue. Just as a struggling family’s experience does not make an improving indicator false. Responsible communication must make room for both, which is how we explain progress without appearing indifferent to hardship,” he said.

He also blamed misinformation and distorted public narratives for undermining the government’s tax reforms, saying some commentators and analysts misrepresented provisions designed to protect small businesses and exempt low-income earners.

Beyond economic policies, the minister identified what he described as the ‘narrative cost’ of negative perceptions about Nigeria, warning that repeated claims portraying the country as a failed or unsafe investment destination could have serious economic consequences.

“We must desist from narratives such as ‘Nigeria is finished’, ‘Nigeria is a scam’ and ‘Nigeria happened to me.’ Such lines may begin in genuine frustration, and citizens, of course, have every right to expose government failure and demand accountability.

“But when repeated carelessly, they become a lens through which every development is judged, and they reach global investors pricing risk and young people deciding whether to build their future at home or abroad,” he warned.

Earlier in her speech, the Minister of Foreign Affairs, Bianca Odumegwu-Ojukwu, called for stronger diplomatic relations between Nigeria, members of the Economic Community of West African States and neighbouring Sahel countries to protect cross-border trade and tackle shared security challenges.

She warned that strained relations between neighbouring countries could undermine longstanding economic, social and cultural ties, stressing the need for sustained dialogue and cooperation regardless of political differences between governments.

The minister stated this while outlining Nigeria’s foreign policy priorities under President Bola Tinubu, which she said were anchored on democracy, development, demography and diaspora, adding that Nigeria’s relations with its West African neighbours should be guided by practical considerations, including the need to keep trade routes open and protect communities facing common security threats.

She said, “Here in West Africa, we know much is at stake when relations between neighbours become strained. Our borders run through places where people have traded, worked, and raised families for generations. Whatever differences governments may have, those ties endure.

“Nigeria values dialogue with our fellow members of ECOWAS and our neighbours in the Sahel because there are practical matters we must continue to address together, from keeping trade routes open to protecting communities that face common security threats.”

On Africa’s position in global affairs, she said the continent must move beyond being a subject of international discussions to actively influencing decisions affecting its people and institutions.

Explaining the Tinubu administration’s foreign policy direction, the minister said its four pillars must translate into measurable benefits for Nigerians, particularly young people and communities.

The foreign affairs minister also warned against the potential consequences of misinformation and disinformation on diplomatic relations, particularly in an era when fabricated audio and other digital content could spread rapidly through mobile devices.

The post Why goods remain expensive despite falling inflation — Oyedele appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

Ifie-kporo Community in Warri South Local Government Area has faulted the delineation report uploaded on the portal of the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC.

The community demanded the inclusion of Ijala Ward, arguing that some areas allocated wards were not as large as theirs.

Vice Chairman of Ifiekporo Community, Mr Jolomi Enonuya, in a statement, warned that the threat to cripple the country’s economy remained strong if the report was not revised.

According to him, since the creation of Warri South Local Government Area in 1991, governments at all levels had refused to acknowledge the numerical growth and economic viability of Ifiekporo, Ajaetan, Ikeren and Utunwa.

Enonuya reminded the Federal Government that oil facilities, including oil fields operated by Conoil and Seplat, petroleum depots belonging to Matrix Energy Ltd, AYM Shafa, Pinnacle Oil and Gas, Parker Oil, A & E Petrol, and Keonamex Oil and Gas, as well as the Warri Refining and Petrochemical Company (WRPC), were located in their communities.

He said: “What is the rationale behind INEC uploading three wards for the riverbank of Warri GRA, a marketplace where people come to do business and return to their respective homes in Ogbe-Ijoh and neighbouring LGAs, but not doing the same for Ijala (comprising Ifie, Ajaetan, Ikeren and Utunwa)?

“It is with a great sense of anger and utter displeasure that I call on President Bola Tinubu and INEC to immediately address the lopsided units and wards uploaded on INEC’s portal as they relate to Warri South Local Government Area.

“Since the creation of this LGA in 1991, the government and leaders of Warri South have refused to acknowledge our numerical growth and economic viability, which are what have conferred oil-producing status on this LGA.

“This Ijala axis of the Warri Islands has four communities and hosts oil companies, including the Warri Refinery. It also has arable lands, which are the mainstay of Warri South today.

“The demand for the creation of Ijala Ward from the existing Obodo/Omadino Ward is legitimate because we have the numerical and economic strength to become a stand-alone ward.

“For clarity, Obodo and Omadino are two autonomous communities in Warri South. The other communities are Ifie, Ajaetan, Ikeren, Utunwa, Ubeji, Egbokodo, Orere-Uluba, Ubiro, Aja-Osolo, Uwakeno, Ugboritseduwa, Ubarira, Ugbikoko and Jaluwa-Efueye.

“When the Supreme Court-ordered ward delineation commenced in 2023, INEC officials visited our communities to carry out their fieldwork.

“But to our greatest disappointment, in all the proposals INEC shared with ethnic stakeholders, not a single ward was proposed for us. Frustratingly, we are still pegged back in Obodo/Omadino Ward.

“Is INEC telling us that we have not increased numerically since 1991? Is INEC telling us that only those with dollars and violent tendencies are fit to be allotted wards?

“Allotting Ijala Ward to us based on what INEC uploaded on its portal is non-negotiable, and it is now or never. Otherwise, we will speak the only language the Federal Government understands – crippling the economy.”

The post Warri community threatens economic shutdown over INEC ward delineation appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Court adjourns Kano governor’s divorce case to December 15

content:
The Upper Area Court sitting in Gudu District, Abuja, has adjourned till December 15 the divorce case involving Kano State Governor, Abba Yusuf, and his second wife, Zainab Musa Kwankwaso.

The matter, marked CV/97/26, came up for mention on Tuesday before Justice Ado Mukhtar, following a civil summons directing the governor to appear in court on November 17, 2026.

At the proceedings, the Kano State Commissioner for Information, Sanusi Bature, who received the court processes on behalf of the governor, told the court that he had yet to brief his principal on the development.

Bature, who appeared as the governor’s representative, consequently requested an adjournment to enable him to brief Yusuf and his lawyers on the court processes.

Counsel for the petitioner, Aliyu Musa Baba, did not oppose the request.

The presiding judge subsequently adjourned the matter till December 15 for hearing.

Speaking with journalists after the proceedings, Bature said he became aware of the case after hearing reports that a matter involving the governor had been filed before the court.

He said he subsequently collected the court processes on behalf of the governor but had yet to brief him on the development.

“Since the court fixed today for mention, I came to inform the court that I had not been able to brief him on the service I collected. He will have to decide on the next course of action,” he said.

Bature said he would exercise restraint in commenting on the matter because it was personal and already before the court.

“This is a personal matter, so I want to exercise some level of restraint because it concerns him personally and is also before the court. We do not want to overflog an issue that is already before the court,” he said.

He also urged journalists to remain neutral in their reporting, stressing that the dispute involved a family.

“We have to remain very neutral in issues like this because they involve families. There are many other stories that are newsworthy, rather than focusing on sensational issues like this,” he added.

The development comes a day after Yusuf publicly acknowledged the marital crisis involving him and Zainab, a niece of his former political mentor, Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso.

The governor disclosed this on Monday while addressing pensioners at the Government House in Kano.

Speaking in Hausa, Yusuf likened his marital situation to a demotion in military rank, saying he had moved from being a “corporal” to a “constable” because he now had only one wife.

“Some days ago, I was being forced to become a constable. I want to thank the good people of Kano who advised me to keep two wives, but for now I have accepted one,” he said.

The governor, however, suggested that he might marry again in the future, adding that he had accepted the development.

He also indicated that steps had been taken towards the dissolution of the marriage, saying, “The governor has agreed to divorce her. The paper for the dissolution has been issued.”

title: British Airways plane bound for Lagos veers off runway
description:
By Dickson Omobola



British Airways Flight BA75 from Heathrow, London, to Lagos, Nigeria, veered off the runway shortly before take-off today.



The aircraft, which had up to 215 passengers on board, was subsequently grounded, resulting in the cancellation of the flight.



Pictures shared with T
content:
By Dickson Omobola

British Airways Flight BA75 from Heathrow, London, to Lagos, Nigeria, veered off the runway shortly before take-off today.

The aircraft, which had up to 215 passengers on board, was subsequently grounded, resulting in the cancellation of the flight.

Pictures shared with The Sun showed the Boeing 787 Dreamliner stranded, with its nose wheel stuck in a grass verge.

According to The Sun, emergency services raced to the scene of the stranded aircraft, which had sparked disruption at the airport.

Airport sources suggested to The Sun that pilot error could have been responsible for the incident, which occurred at about 10.40am.

A source told The Sun, “The packed plane was all set to go and had pushed back from its stand, taxiing to the runway for take-off to Lagos.

“Bafflingly, the plane appears to have simply been driven off the tarmac onto a grass verge. It is hard to understand what could be to blame for this, other than a most basic pilot error.

“There are red faces all around the airline, and a hefty task clearing up the mess and looking after hundreds of disgruntled passengers who were strapped in their seats for lift-off.”

British Airways told The Sun, “We are very sorry to our customers for the disruption to their flight. Our teams are working to get them on their way as quickly as possible and are in touch with them to put things right.”

The post British Airways plane bound for Lagos veers off runway appeared first on Vanguard News.

In recognition of her creative achievement, Alade received a £10,000 cash prize, while an additional £10,000 was donated to her c
content:
Super Group, the parent company of leading sportsbook brand Betway, has announced Nigerian artist Omomurewa Alade as the winner of its global Art of the Game competition. In recognition of her creative achievement, Alade received a £10,000 cash prize, while an additional £10,000 was donated to her chosen charity, the Feed the Widows Project in Lagos.

Launched by Super Group earlier this year,Art of the Game invited artists from around the world to create a custom basketball design inspired by their culture, identity and personal creative vision. The competition was designed to celebrate the connection between sport, art and community, while creating a lasting impact beyond the competition itself.

Alade’s winning design stood out among entries submitted from across the globe, impressing judges with its creativity, originality and representation of cultural identity.

As part of her prize, Alade received £10,000, while a further £10,000 donation was awarded to Feed the Widows Project, a Lagos-based organisation dedicated to supporting widows and vulnerable members of the community.

The donation forms part of Super Group Cares, the company’s global social impact programme focused on empowering communities and creating meaningful opportunities around the world.

: “Art of the Game was created to celebrate the powerful connection between sport, creativity and community. Omomurewa Alade’s design captured that spirit brilliantly, and we’re delighted that her success will also make a meaningful difference through Feed the Widows Project. Through Super Group Cares, we remain committed to supporting initiatives that create lasting impact in the communities where we operate.”

Representatives from Feed the Widows Project welcomed the donation, highlighting the positive impact it will have on the organisation’s ongoing programmes and outreach efforts.

Since launching earlier this year, Art of the Game has showcased the creativity and diversity of artists from around the world, demonstrating how sport can inspire artistic expression while helping to deliver meaningful community impact.

The competition culminates with Alade being recognised as the inaugural Art of the Game winner, with her success serving as a reminder that creativity has the power not only to connect people across cultures and continents, but also to create positive change where it is needed most.

title: Vinicius hits 12-minute hat-trick as Brazil thrash Singapore 7-0
description:
Vinicius Junior hit a 12-minute hat-trick in the first half as Brazil turned on the style in a 7-0 trouncing of Singapore on Tuesday.



Endrick, Estevao, Rayan and substitute Allan also scored as the South Americans brushed aside the hosts with a dominant performance at the National Stadium.



Bra
content:
Vinicius Junior hit a 12-minute hat-trick in the first half as Brazil turned on the style in a 7-0 trouncing of Singapore on Tuesday.

Endrick, Estevao, Rayan and substitute Allan also scored as the South Americans brushed aside the hosts with a dominant performance at the National Stadium.

Brazil were much changed from their 3-2 loss to Japan on Saturday in which manager Carlo Ancelotti and captain Raphinha were shown red cards, with Vinicius one of only four players retaining their places in the starting line-up.

Bruno Guimaraes took over as skipper and set up the opener after nine minutes, playing a quick pass to Vinicius who wrong-footed Singapore captain Hariss Harun with his first touch before despatching a left-footed shot past goalkeeper Izwan Mahbud.

The Real Madrid forward notched his second in the 15th minute after a quick counter-attack as Endrick laid the ball off for his unmarked team-mate to slot home.

Vinicius was denied by Izwan shortly afterwards but he completed his hat-trick in the 21st minute when he was found unmarked in the six-yard box by Estevao’s low centre.

Rayan had an effort disallowed for offside but Endrick added to Brazil’s lead in the 31st minute with a low effort from range which found the bottom right corner.

Estevao also had a goal disallowed for a foul by Vinicius but the Chelsea winger added to Brazil’s tally just after the interval with a deflected shot from the edge of the box.

Rayan rocked the crossbar soon after but the endeavour of the Bournemouth forward was rewarded in the 65th minute when he rounded substitute goalkeeper Syazwan Buhari to make it 6-0.

Brazil rang the changes in the closing stages and Allan came off the bench to grab the seventh goal in the 74th minute.

Speaking in the absence of the suspended Ancelotti, Brazil assistant Francesco Mauri lauded the commitment shown by Vinicius.

“His attitude was fantastic. As we discussed before the match, you shouldn’t focus solely on the quality of the opponents, you just have to give your absolute best,” said the Italian.

“He was a constant threat, providing great depth to our attack. He forced the opposition to double-mark him, which in turn allowed us to defend a bit more effectively.”

Despite lengthy travel for the friendlies in Singapore, Mauri felt the effort had been worthwhile for the squad’s development.

“Before the game, we told the players that it was really important to finish in the best way in these November FIFA dates because after this we have to wait until March for our next games, so it’s good to go home with a good feeling,” he said.

The post Vinicius hits 12-minute hat-trick as Brazil thrash Singapore 7-0 appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Draft Short Promo Clips from Text Prompts via AI Marketing Studio
description: Brands can share product value in a concise manner using short visuals, movement, and memorable messaging in short promotional clips. These videos include key features with a focus on social media and digital advertising. But to create interesting promotional material, you need clear creative direct
content:
Brands can share product value in a concise manner using short visuals, movement, and memorable messaging in short promotional clips. These videos include key features with a focus on social media and digital advertising. But to create interesting promotional material, you need clear creative direction and appropriate visuals. Dreamina offers an AI-driven platform to convert written ideas into promotional videos. It has tools that include text prompts, product references, and video production. Describe the desired air, product presentation, visual sequence, and storyline direction. This method can be used to make marketing concepts applicable to short-form video content without the need for traditional production setups.

Understand How Text Prompts Shape Short Promotional Videos

Text prompts convey the desired look, motion, and flow of the story in promotional videos. They give information regarding products, backgrounds, lighting, camera moves, and environments. For instance, a skincare bottle on a marble surface sets the scene. Incorporating directions for camera movement makes for a more dynamic presentation. Certain adjectives also have a specific effect on the visual atmosphere, such as warmth, brightness, contrast, and color relations. Use clear language, such as good advertising, as vague words don’t offer much in the way of visual guidance. Rather, describe what you see, how the products interact, and what is going on in the environment. Dreamina’s Marketing Studio delivers written instructions and AI video generation. This enables ideas to be expanded into visual advertising material via descriptive prompts.

Identify the Essential Elements of an Effective Promo Clip

There are a number of creative elements that are combined to create an effective promotional video that sends one message that is easily understood by all. All elements align with the video’s structure, visual consistency, and promotional intent. Keep these elements in mind when developing your creative direction:

  • Opening Visual: Start with a good composition to introduce the product. It has a unique opening frame that sets the context and draws in attention.
  • Product Focus: Make sure that the main product is easily recognizable throughout the main sequence. Positioning is important, as it tells viewers what exactly the ad is about.
  • Visual Movement: Add intentional movement by moving the camera or interacting with products. The controlled movement is visually interesting but not distracting.
  • Brand Atmosphere: Create appropriate colors, lighting, and environmental elements. Visual treatments that are always applied contribute to the desired brand.
  • Promotional Message: Deliver a short message that talks about a single product benefit. Don’t clutter the composition with conflicting promotional material.
  • Closing Moment: End with a product-related visual/promotional statement to remember. A clear ending provides a familiar conclusion to the ad.

Write Detailed Prompts That Translate Ideas into Visual Sequences

Write instructions for a specific product and state the promotional goal. Determine if the clip should be an introduction to a product, a feature demonstration, or an offer announcement. Then, write the initial shot, product interaction, and intended final shot. Add elements of the environment: indoor settings, store displays, or outdoor scenes. Lighting directions can set a mood with soft lighting, shadow play, or daylight. Camera moves should be described, such as a gradual zoom, tracking, or a rotation in camera direction. Reference pictures can convey product appearance, colours, and composition more accurately. Storytelling structure, movement, and overall creative style can be inspired by reference videos. Include instructions in terms of actions seen, not random descriptive words. By providing clear and concise instructions, AI can better understand the desired sequence and generate more cohesive promotional visuals.

Draft Short Promo Clips from Text Prompts via AI Marketing Studio

Step 1: Open the studio and write your text prompt

  1. Sign up or log in to Dreamina first, so you can start drafting your clips.
  2. Next, click “Marketing Studio” on the left bar to open your promo drafting workspace.
  3. Here, pick “AI video” for clips, “AI image” for stills, or “AI agent” for both.
  4. Inside “AI video”, tap “Change style” to choose the look your promo clip should follow.
  5. Then click “Product” to upload your photo, and click “Avatar” to add a presenter too. You can also choose existing products and avatars from the built-in library whenever you prefer.
  6. Write a text prompt describing the look and feel of your clip, and add custom direction freely.

Step 2: Pick your model and generate the draft

  1. Click the “Reference” tab to add a video that guides the AI’s look and feel.
  2. Choose a model for your draft, such as HappyHorse 1.1 or Dreamina Seedance 2.5. Other choices include Dreamina Seedance 2.0, Dreamina Seedance 2.0 Fast, Dreamina Seedance 2.0 Mini, Wan 3.0, etc.
  3. Select a custom size and quality from the “Aspect ratio” and “Resolution” tabs for your clip.
  4. Click the “Duration” tab to select a custom length that keeps your promo short.
  5. Use the “@” option to mention or highlight the specific product within your video.
  6. Finally, click “Generate” to begin creating your first draft.

Step 3: Review the draft and save your clip

  1. Watch the finished draft on full screen and check the product framing, the avatar’s delivery, and the pacing.
  2. If the draft misses your idea, use “Edit prompt” or “Regenerate” to refine the result.
  3. You can also open “Edit in canvas” to replace the background, add effects, crop the video, and more.
  4. Once the clip looks right, click “Download” to save it and share it across your marketing channels.

Create Different Promotional Concepts from One Product Description

There are several different written instructions that can be used with a single product reference to support multiple advertising concepts. A beverage description can generate product introductions and demonstrations that focus on product features, for instance. Seasonal prompts can add festive backgrounds, appropriate decorations, and even lighting. Packaging, product information, and announcement graphics can be highlighted in limited-time promotional concepts. There are lifestyle shots, studio demos, and product reveals as well. Using product references will keep similar looks if there are variations of the creatives. At the same time, there is visual diversity as camera directions, environments, and storytelling approaches are changed. This is a way to develop a campaign without having to swap out the product repeatedly.

Refine Short Clips Through Visual Editing and Creative Adjustments

Promotional videos that are generated should be carefully reviewed before publishing. Analyze whether the movement is effective in conveying the message and maintains the visibility of the product information. Background replacement can add appropriate retail environments, studio settings, or lifestyle compositions. You can use Edit in Canvas to crop video clips and add visual effects. Be sure to check framing, as too much cropping may result in the loss of important product features. When clips have several visual transitions, scene continuity is important as well. If the original result does not go in the desired direction, tweak the prompt of the original result. You can re-generate the video with better instructions to get a better composition.

Prepare Prompt-Based Promotional Clips for Different Marketing Channels

Video dimensions vary depending on the marketing channel where they will be displayed. Vertical formats tend to be used in mobile-first placements such as short-form social media videos. Square compositions are also a choice for flexible social media advertising. Landscape is used for larger formats, websites, and some digital advertising spaces. Choose the aspect ratio based on where the video will be published. The length of the video also affects the story, the speed of the video, and the amount of information conveyed. When changing dimensions, keep product names, packaging, and important information visible. Dreamina supports various output configurations to develop multiple versions of the same creative concepts. Check each version individually for proper framing and clarity.

Conclusion

Text prompts give a versatile starting point for creating short promotional videos. Product presentation, atmosphere, movement, and storytelling direction are defined by clear descriptions. Visual generation is also informed by product mentions and available AI models. The editing tools can be used to make the background, framing, and other creative elements perfect. Dreamina combines all these features into one content creation platform. Promotional concepts are turned into reusable video assets with purposeful instructions and thoughtful refinement. A consistent visual direction allows for a recognizable product presentation in each of the marketing channels.

title: RMAFC moves to reduce Nigeria’s reliance on oil revenue
description:
The Revenue Mobilisation, Allocation and Fiscal Commission has begun preparing a national policy framework to expand government revenue sources, reduce dependence on oil earnings, and strengthen fiscal sustainability across the three tiers of government.
The commission disclosed that the proposed fr
content:
The Revenue Mobilisation, Allocation and Fiscal Commission has begun preparing a national policy framework to expand government revenue sources, reduce dependence on oil earnings, and strengthen fiscal sustainability across the three tiers of government.

The commission disclosed that the proposed framework would emerge from a National Revenue Summit expected to bring together federal, state and local governments, revenue-generating agencies, private sector operators, academics and development partners.

According to a statement issued on Tuesday by the commission’s Head of Information and Public Relations, Maryam Umar-Yusuf, the initiative formed part of efforts to improve revenue mobilisation, strengthen compliance and identify alternative sources of funding for national development.

Speaking during a two-day strategic planning retreat at Zuma Rock Resort, Niger State, the Chairman of the Mobilisation and Diversification Committee, Victor Eboigbe, said the commission intended to develop a policy document to guide revenue expansion nationwide.

“We are hoping that this Summit will be able to come up with a policy framework that the nation can rely on,” Eboigbe said.

He explained that the initiative would enable the commission to fulfil its constitutional responsibility of advising the three tiers of government on revenue generation and diversification.

“One of our very important functions is to advise the three tiers of government on how to increase their revenue,” he added.

Eboigbe argued that Nigeria needed to reduce its dependence on oil revenue and identify sustainable funding sources to support infrastructure development and broader economic growth.

He noted that achieving President Bola Tinubu’s development objectives would require adequate and predictable government revenue.

Earlier, the Chairman of RMAFC, Mohammed Shehu, called for a coordinated roadmap that would identify specific responsibilities, implementation timelines and measurable outcomes for the proposed summit.

Shehu explained that the retreat, held from November 16 to 17, was designed to determine the summit’s objectives, scope, major discussion areas and expected outcomes.

He emphasised that the gathering should produce recommendations capable of improving Nigeria’s revenue system rather than merely serving as another policy discussion.

“It should be a platform capable of generating meaningful dialogue and practical recommendations on the nation’s revenue system,” Shehu said.

According to him, the proposed summit aligns with the Federal Government’s efforts to increase non-oil revenue and improve fiscal sustainability.

Also speaking, the Vice Chairman of the Mobilisation and Diversification Committee and Federal Commissioner representing Abia State, Nkechi Oti, advocated greater attention to revenue opportunities outside the petroleum sector.

She explained that the commission’s responsibilities included advising governments on revenue generation and reducing economic wastage.

Oti disclosed that the proposed diversification initiative would extend to all six geopolitical zones to encourage grassroots participation.

She added that government institutions, private businesses, young people and other stakeholders would be involved in identifying opportunities for economic diversification.

The Director of the Mobilisation and Diversification Department, Khadija Kumo, said the retreat marked the beginning of detailed preparations for the national summit.

“We are looking at how to improve the revenue base of the Federation, the essence of the retreat is to kick-start the preparation so that we will have a successful National Revenue Summit,” Kumo said.

She explained that improving government revenue was necessary to provide adequate resources for development projects across the country.

The commission said the retreat would also examine opportunities to strengthen revenue administration, improve compliance and develop actionable recommendations for consideration at the summit.

Other federal commissioners from Kwara, Katsina, Ekiti, Osun, Bayelsa, Akwa Ibom, Gombe and Nasarawa states attended the retreat.

title: Obasanjo begged Tinubu to make daughter Ogun governor, Fayose alleges
description:
By Adegboyega Adeleye



Former Ekiti State Governor, Ayodele Fayose, has alleged that former President Olusegun Obasanjo sought President Bola Tinubu’s support for his daughter, Iyabo Obasanjo, to become governor of Ogun State but turned against the president after the request was unsuccessful.
content:
By Adegboyega Adeleye

Former Ekiti State Governor, Ayodele Fayose, has alleged that former President Olusegun Obasanjo sought President Bola Tinubu’s support for his daughter, Iyabo Obasanjo, to become governor of Ogun State but turned against the president after the request was unsuccessful.

Fayose made the allegation on Monday during an interview on TVC while reacting to Obasanjo’s criticism of Tinubu’s administration and its economic reforms.

The former governor claimed that Obasanjo approached former Ogun State Governor Olusegun Osoba to help persuade Tinubu to support his daughter’s governorship ambition. According to Fayose, Obasanjo’s decision to welcome Tinubu during the president’s visit to Ogun State in April 2026 was connected to the ambition.

He said, “You know Iyabo Obasanjo, Obasanjo’s daughter. Obasanjo went to Chief Aremo Olusegun Osoba to help him beg Tinubu so that Iyabo Obasanjo would become governor of Ogun State.

“That was the reason Obasanjo came to welcome President Tinubu.

“The moment that did not work, Obasanjo simply remembered what Osoba wrote about him in his book and went to reply to him because what he wanted did not fly.

“He will go and be begging behind the scene; when he does not get it, he will attack you.”

Fayose also dismissed Obasanjo’s criticisms of the Tinubu administration, saying the former president had a history of finding fault with successive administrations and seeking attention.

“We are overrating Obasanjo. That is the truth. It is a style. Nobody gets it done better than Obasanjo in life. If anybody wants to talk, it is either Obasanjo or nobody,” he said.

“Obasanjo still wants attention, and he sees no good in anyone. That is the truth. If you look at Obasanjo, he criticised Yar’Adua and Jonathan.

“In fact, he made himself an enemy of Jonathan. The moment he does not follow a day-to-day taking of permission from him, Obasanjo becomes uncomfortable.”

Fayose further recalled that Obasanjo welcomed Tinubu to Ogun State in April 2026 for the inauguration of the Gateway International Cargo Airport, where he reportedly wore a matching outfit with the President and spoke favourably about him.

Iyabo Obasanjo, a former senator and daughter of the ex-president, declared interest in the Ogun governorship race in February 2026 on the platform of the All Progressives Congress (APC).

She later suspended her ambition after the party adopted Senator Solomon Adeola as its consensus candidate and defected to the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP).

Fayose and Obasanjo have had a long-running political disagreement, with both men exchanging criticisms and allegations publicly over the years.

The post Obasanjo begged Tinubu to make daughter Ogun governor, Fayose alleges appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Baboon Siblings Get Jealous Just Like Human Kids – Scientists
description: Sibling rivalry isn’t just a problem for humans — young baboons also compete for their mother’s attention, scientists said on Wednesday.The scenario is familiar for many parents: just when they finally get to share a special moment with one of their children, a little brother or si
content:
Sibling rivalry isn’t just a problem for humans — young baboons also compete for their mother’s attention, scientists said on Wednesday.

The scenario is familiar for many parents: just when they finally get to share a special moment with one of their children, a little brother or sister pops up trying to get noticed.

Axelle Delaunay, an evolutionary biologist at Finland’s University of Turku and lead author of a new study, told AFP that jealousy is a “very striking” emotion in humans.

However, it has been little studied among our fellow primates because jealousy is “very complicated to measure”, she said.

Female primates usually only have one baby at a time, so “it was generally thought there was no real competition between siblings, because brothers and sisters are different ages and do not necessarily need their mother and her resources at the same time”, Delaunay explained.

For the study, a team of researchers observed two troops of wild chacma baboons in Tsaobis Nature Park in central Namibia between August and December 2021.

There were 16 families living in the troops, with a total of 49 young siblings.

Baboons live in societies ruled by women, with the position of power handed down from mother to daughter. Males, meanwhile, leave after puberty.

Like humans, baboon infants have a long developmental period during which they maintain strong bonds with their mother.

The mothers often groom their children — and have been known to play favourites.

So the scientists spent lots of time watching baboon mothers either resting or grooming their children.

They meticulously noted when another infant interfered with a mother’s grooming by biting, slapping, crying out or more gently asking for affection.

What they observed “strikingly mirrors patterns of sibling jealousy reported in humans”, according to the study published in Proceedings of the Royal Society B: Biological Sciences.

The young baboons were more likely to interrupt their mother when she was grooming one of their siblings than when she was just resting.

The scientists also developed an index to show how the mothers played favourites, choosing to groom some kids more than others.

Delaunay pointed out that the displays of sibling jealousy did not appear to offer “many immediate benefits”.

Baboon mothers only stopped grooming one of their children because of an outburst from another roughly one-fifth of the time, the scientists found.

And she only then started grooming the jealous child nine percent of the time.

The post Baboon Siblings Get Jealous Just Like Human Kids – Scientists appeared first on Channels Television.

title: Disqualify Candidates Over Political Violence, Senate Urges INEC
description: The Senate has asked the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to disqualify any political candidate whose supporters are found to have instigated or participated in acts of electoral violence, irrespective of party affiliation, in accordance with the provisions of the 2026 Electoral Act
content:
The Senate has asked the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to disqualify any political candidate whose supporters are found to have instigated or participated in acts of electoral violence, irrespective of party affiliation, in accordance with the provisions of the 2026 Electoral Act and an established conviction by the court.

According to the Senate President, ‘Any candidate or supporter caught instigating violence, then INEC has a right to disqualify. We should call the attention of INEC to the 2026 Electoral Act; no matter the political party, such a candidate should immediately be disqualified. They are embedded in the 2026 Electoral Act and require strong implementation.

He urged the electoral commission to enforce the provisions of the 2026 Electoral Act, which they reminded provides for sanctions against electoral violence, underscoring the need for strict implementation ahead of the 2027 general elections.

This followed a motion sponsored by Senator Abdul Ningi on the urgent need to check the rising incidence of violence, intolerance and attacks on political leaders and supporters in the country.

The motion was prompted by recent reports of attacks on political figures, including the incident involving President Bola Tinubu at a mosque on Friday.

In a robust debate, the lawmakers asked security agencies to investigate reported incidents in four states (Abuja, Edo, Delta and Sokoto states), identify the perpetrators and their sponsors and ensure prosecution.

Lawmakers expressed concern over the growing tension in the political space and called on the Federal Government to direct the Inspector-General of Police and other security agencies to strengthen security arrangements for political leaders, candidates, supporters and political gatherings across the country.

They also called for effective early-warning and rapid-response mechanisms to identify and prevent potential attacks ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The Senate further asked state governors to stop denying opposition parties access to public facilities, including hotels and stadiums under their control, for political activities.

Asserting the need to guarantee a level playing field for all political parties, the lawmakers warned that restrictions on opposition activities could heighten political intolerance and trigger avoidable conflicts.

The post Disqualify Candidates Over Political Violence, Senate Urges INEC appeared first on Channels Television.

title: FULL LIST: UNILAG, Covenant, four other Nigerian universities in 2027 QS Sustainability Rankings
description:

According to data published on the TopUniversities website on Tuesday, six Nigerian universities featured in the 2027 QS Sustainabilit
content:
Six Nigerian universities have been ranked in the 2027 QS Sustainability Rankings, with the University of Lagos emerging as the country’s highest-ranked institution.

According to data published on the TopUniversities website on Tuesday, six Nigerian universities featured in the 2027 QS Sustainability Rankings, with the University of Lagos emerging as the country’s highest-ranked institution

The university was also described as the biggest riser in Africa, having moved up more than 700 places.

Other Nigerian universities featured in the ranking were Covenant University, University of Ibadan, Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria, University of Nigeria, Nsukka, and Obafemi Awolowo University.

Covenant University placed between 1,151st and 1,200th, while the University of Ibadan ranked between 1,201st and 1,250th.

Ahmadu Bello University, University of Nigeria, Nsukka, and Obafemi Awolowo University were all placed in the 1,501-and-above category.

Below is the list of the Nigerian universities and their respective global rankings:

University of Lagos (UNILAG) – Joint 697th

UNILAG was ranked 14th in Africa, with an overall score of 65.5. It recorded 61.8 in Environmental Impact, 69.1 in Social Impact, and 65.9 in Governance.

Covenant University – 1,151–1,200

The Ota-based institution, which was Nigeria’s highest-ranked university in the 2026 edition, recorded 46.6 in Environmental Impact, 58.3 in Social Impact and 51.2 in Governance.

University of Ibadan – 1,201–1,250

The university recorded 40.5 in Environmental Impact, 64.9 in Social Impact and 35.4 in Governance.

Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria – 1,501+

ABU recorded 40.7 in Environmental Impact, 52.3 in Social Impact and 23.2 in Governance.

Obafemi Awolowo University – 1,501+

OAU recorded 29.7 in Environmental Impact, 51.4 in Social Impact and 26.2 in Governance.

University of Nigeria, Nsukka – 1,501+

UNN recorded 31.8 in Environmental Impact, 58.5 in Social Impact and 30.7 in Governance.

Across Africa, 13 universities from other countries ranked ahead of UNILAG. They included the University of Cape Town, which placed 88th globally, the University of Pretoria (243rd), Alexandria University in Egypt (412th), Cairo University (525th), the American University in Cairo (627th), Mansoura University (633rd) and Ain Shams University in Egypt (665th).

Stellenbosch University of South Africa ranked joint 688th, just ahead of UNILAG, which placed joint 697th.

The QS Sustainability Rankings assess universities based on their environmental and social impact, as well as governance.

The post FULL LIST: UNILAG, Covenant, four other Nigerian universities in 2027 QS Sustainability Rankings appeared first on Punch Newspapers.
