title: I considered suicide at ‘lowest point’ with Man Utd — Rooney
description:
Wayne Rooney has revealed that he contemplated suicide even as he flourished on the pitch for Manchester United when the Premier League club was at the height of its powers.
The former England forward, 41, said his mental health was suffering even though he was newly married and a father to his elde
content:
Wayne Rooney has revealed that he contemplated suicide even as he flourished on the pitch for Manchester United when the Premier League club was at the height of its powers.

The former England forward, 41, said his mental health was suffering even though he was newly married and a father to his eldest child, Kai.

He married Coleen in 2008, and his first child was born the following year.
Rooney was part of a powerful squad assembled by Alex Ferguson that won multiple Premier League titles and the Champions League.

The striker, who would spend two days at a time drinking at home, told the “Life At The Midpoint with Gabby Logan” podcast that he considered taking his own life when he was at his lowest ebb.

“I can look back and say I was selfish, but I knew I was going through something which I was really struggling to deal with,” he said.

“Then I didn’t want Kai seeing me like that, so that’s why I’d hide away as well.

“I got to a place where you’re contemplating suicide. You just didn’t want to be around anyone. I didn’t want to see people in the streets. I didn’t want to go into shops.

“I was always comfortable on a football pitch, but everything else (I) really struggled with it.”

Rooney, United’s all-time record goalscorer with 253 goals, said the issues he faced occurred at the height of his Red Devils career.

“You don’t want to show any weakness, so you try to mask it,” he added.

“Even though I knew the position I was in, it was difficult to actually admit that I was in that position because I felt like you feel less of a man if you like for doing that.

“I was speaking to a therapist to try and figure out what was up with me because, when I look back, I was probably at the height of my career, I’ve just had a young son, I’ve just been married. It should be the happiest point in my life, and it wasn’t.

“It was probably the lowest point because of the selfish acts I was taking.”

Rooney, who was England’s record goalscorer before Harry Kane overtook him, credits Coleen with helping him turn the tide.

“Coleen helped me massively. She could have walked away, it was that bad, but she stuck by me and helped me get through it,” he said.

After Rooney left United in 2017, he had spells with Everton, DC United and Derby before embarking on a managerial career.
His last job was at Plymouth, which he left in December 2024.

AFP

content:
A truck has killed an official of the Vehicle Inspection Office, Oluwaseun Adeshina, in Ogun State.

The Ogun State Police Command confirmed the incident in a Tuesday statement made available to PUNCH Online by its Police Public Relations Officer, Oluseyi Babaseyi.

“The Ogun State Police Command confirms a fatal road accident involving an Iveco truck and a VIO official, Oluwaseun Adeshina, at about 11:10 am on Monday, 16 November 2026, opposite Tipper Garage, Korogboji, along the Agbara–Unilever Expressway,” the statement read.

The command said the truck knocked down Adeshina while he was performing his lawful duty, resulting in fatal injuries.

“Police operatives promptly visited the scene, documented the incident and conveyed the remains to the hospital for necessary procedures,” it added.

The statement further disclosed that the truck and its driver had been taken to the station for further investigation and vehicle inspection.

“The Command commiserates with the family and colleagues of the deceased and urges motorists to exercise caution. The area remains calm,” it stated.

title: CJN Kekere-Ekun Swears In 12 New Appeal Court Justices
description: The Chief Justice of Nigeria CJN, Justice Kudirat Kekere-Ekun, on Tuesday, swore in 12 new Appeal Court Justices, charging them to do everything humanly possible to decide cases according to relevant laws and their individual conscience to sustain and enhance the integrity of the judiciary.The CJN
content:
The Chief Justice of Nigeria CJN, Justice Kudirat Kekere-Ekun, on Tuesday, swore in 12 new Appeal Court Justices, charging them to do everything humanly possible to decide cases according to relevant laws and their individual conscience to sustain and enhance the integrity of the judiciary.

The CJN urged them to dispense justice without being unduly influenced by seniority, reputation, personal affinity or the desire for unanimity.

According to her, judicial office is increasingly exercised in an environment in which decisions are subjected to immediate public commentary.adding that they must remain conscious of the reality without allowing it to influence your adjudicatory responsibilities.

“Public approval must not be the basis for you to depart from the law, just as criticism must not deter you from reaching a decision that your conscience and the law require.

“Your judicial independence must be guarded against political, financial, social and personal pressures, including those that may arise through professional familiarity or established relationships.

“Conduct yourselves in a manner that leaves no reasonable basis for doubt about your impartiality. The diversity of your professional backgrounds should also enrich the work of the Court.

“Your experience in different jurisdictions will provide valuable insights into the legal and social realities of our country. Bring that experience to your deliberations, but always subject it to the common discipline of constitutional adjudication. The law must be applied consistently, fairly and without prejudice.

“I encourage you to remain committed to continuing judicial education. The legal landscape is constantly evolving, with developments in digital commerce, data protection, intellectual property, financial regulation, labour relations and other emerging fields. Artificial intelligence is also changing the way legal information is generated and accessed.

“Today marks an important transition in your judicial careers. By the oaths you have just taken, you assume the responsibilities of Justices of the Court of Appeal, an institution whose work is central to the administration of justice and the development of our jurisprudence. I congratulate each of you on this elevation and welcome you to this new phase of judicial service.

“Your Lordship’s appointments bring together judicial experience from different parts of the country and from courts with distinct jurisdictions and responsibilities.

“Some of you come from the High Courts of Gombe, Bayelsa, Cross River, Benue, Kebbi, Taraba and Ondo States. Others have served at the Federal High Court, the National Industrial Court of Nigeria and the Customary Courts of Appeal of Ekiti and Plateau States.

“This breadth of experience is valuable. It brings to the Court of Appeal different professional perspectives, shaped by varied jurisdictions, legal traditions and the practical realities of adjudication across our Federation.

“Each of Your Lordships has spent years discharging judicial responsibilities and developing the experience and temperament required for this office.

“Your elevation recognises that service, while placing before you a new set of 3 demands. The experience you bring will serve you well, but the transition to an appellate court requires an appreciation of a different mode of adjudication.

” In the courts from which most of you have been elevated, you have ordinarily exercised jurisdiction as the sole presiding Judge. You heard the parties, controlled proceedings, evaluated the evidence, resolved the issues and delivered decisions in the exercise of your individual judicial authority.

“At the Court of Appeal, you will sit with other Justices in panels, deliberate collectively and arrive at decisions through a process of judicial engagement.

“This calls for teamwork, a willingness to engage with the views of colleagues, test your initial conclusions and consider issues from perspectives that may differ from your own. The effectiveness of a collegiate court depends on the quality of this engagement.

“I encourage you to approach panel conferences through preparation with intellectual openness and mutual respect. Listen attentively, contribute meaningfully and be prepared to reconsider a position where the arguments persuade you to do so.

“The ability to listen and reflect is a mark of judicial maturity. Seek guidance from your more experienced colleagues on the appellate Bench.

“You are called upon to promote consistency in the application of the law, clarify legal principles, correct errors where necessary and contribute to the coherent development of our jurisprudence.

“This requires a disciplined and principled approach to appellate adjudication. An appeal is not an invitation to rehear a case simply because another judicial officer might have reached a different conclusion.

“You must identify the complaints properly raised, examine the record of proceedings, consider the findings and reasoning of the court below, and determine whether the law justifies appellate intervention.

“Particular care is required when reviewing findings of fact and the evaluation of evidence, especially where the appellate court has not had the opportunity to observe the witnesses.

“The task is to correct errors where they are established, while respecting findings that are properly supported by the evidence and the applicable law.

“I urge you to give equal attention to the quality and clarity of your judgments”, she charged them.

The post CJN Kekere-Ekun Swears In 12 New Appeal Court Justices appeared first on Channels Television.

title: Femi Ajasa: Onigbinde, Adeyanju, Do2dtun, others mourn late Vanguard Online Editor
description: Co-founder of BudgIT, Oluseun Onigbinde, Lawyer and human rights activist Deji Adeyanju, on-air personality Oladotun Kayode, popularly known as Do2dtun, and former presidential aide Bashir Ahmad are among public figures who have mourned the death of Vanguard Media Limited’s online editor, Olufemi Aj
content:
Co-founder of BudgIT, Oluseun Onigbinde, Lawyer and human rights activist Deji Adeyanju, on-air personality Oladotun Kayode, popularly known as Do2dtun, and former presidential aide Bashir Ahmad are among public figures who have mourned the death of Vanguard Media Limited’s online editor, Olufemi Ajasa, who died on Sunday at the age of 44.

The deceased’s death was announced by Vanguard Media Limited, which said he passed away at the Lagos University Teaching Hospital after a brief illness.

In a statement, the newspaper’s editor, Eze Anaba, described Ajasa’s death as a major loss to the organisation and the journalism profession, noting his contributions to the growth of its digital operations and online journalism.

Reacting to his death on Tuesday, Onigbinde said, “What a loss. This is a shocking exit. He always stayed in touch for data. May memories remain blessed.”

Adeyanju, in a tribute shared on Facebook, described Ajasa as a longtime friend and brother, saying they shared a close relationship for nearly two decades.

He wrote, “We shared a close friendship for nearly two decades, and losing such a trusted ally to the cold hands of death is truly heartbreaking. My heartfelt condolences go out to his family and the entire Vanguard Newspaper team for this irreparable loss. I will always hold onto the wonderful memories of our travels together and the countless ideas we exchanged.

“The kindhearted never truly die—they live on in our hearts forever. May God comfort his loved ones, and may his gentle soul rest in perfect peace.”

Do2dtun, who worked with Cool FM, also expressed grief over Ajasa’s death in a post on X, describing him as an exceptional journalist who maintained professionalism in his work.

He said Ajasa refused to accept money to publish a blackmail-related story against him, adding that the journalist declined attempts to persuade him to run the report.

“Femi Ajasa, your loss broke me. You are an amazing journalist, never biased and you were a professional to the core. You never used your pen for evil,” he wrote.

Similarly, Bashir Ahmad, a former media aide to ex-President Muhammadu Buhari, said he had known Ajasa since 2016 and valued his professionalism, dedication to journalism and warmth towards people.

In a post on X, Ahmad said the journalist’s death was a painful loss to his family, friends and the Nigerian media industry.

“I have had the privilege of knowing and sharing a friendship with Mr. Ajasa since 2016. Over the years, I came to appreciate his professionalism, dedication to journalism and the warmth with which he related with people. His passing is a painful loss, not only to his family and loved ones but also to the Nigerian media industry, where he made meaningful contributions,” he wrote.

Director of New Media and Strategic Communication of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Theo Aguda, also described Ajasa as a friend and brother.

“In Femi, I have lost a dear friend and brother. His absence leaves a void that words cannot fill. Good night Femi, Until we meet at the feet of the Master,” he wrote.

Other tributes came from broadcaster Rufai Oseni, who described the news as sad. Ayodele Lawal Adio, the African Democratic Congress candidate for Eti-Osa Constituency II, described Ajasa as a gentleman and gifted journalist.

Demola Olarewaju, a senior political aide to former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, also described the late editor as a good man and a professional who was always willing to share work-related information.

Ajasa began his journalism career as a photojournalist with National Mirror in 2012 before joining Vanguard in December 2013 as an online reporter and content developer.

He later worked with TheNewsGuru.com as online editor and head of digital operations and subsequently joined Pulse as an editorial quality assurance manager in December 2021.

He returned to Vanguard in June 2022 as Online Editor, a position he held until his death.

A service of songs and wake-keep in his honour will hold on Thursday, November 19, at 5pm, at 14 Sylvia Crescent, Anthony Village, Lagos.

The post Femi Ajasa: Onigbinde, Adeyanju, Do2dtun, others mourn late Vanguard Online Editor appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Female soldiers vital to tackling insecurity – Army chief
description:
The Chief of Army Staff, Lt.-Gen. Waidi Shaibu, has said that female soldiers are critical to strengthening the Nigerian Army’s operational capacity and tackling the country’s security challenges.
Shaibu said the professional skills of female personnel, particularly in intelligence gathering, commun
content:
The Chief of Army Staff, Lt.-Gen. Waidi Shaibu, has said that female soldiers are critical to strengthening the Nigerian Army’s operational capacity and tackling the country’s security challenges.

Shaibu said the professional skills of female personnel, particularly in intelligence gathering, community engagement and specialised military operations, remained vital to the success of the Army’s engagements.

He stated this on Tuesday in Kaduna at the Nigerian Army Women Command’s Fourth Quarter 2026 Workshop, with the theme, “Harnessing the Professional Capabilities of Nigerian Army Female Personnel in Support of Nigerian Army Operational Engagements in a Joint and Multi-Agency Environment.”

The COAS, who was represented by the Commander, Command Engineering Depot, Maj.-Gen. Oladele Arogundade, said the increasingly complex security environment required a professional, adaptable and resilient military capable of responding effectively to emerging threats.

He described female officers and soldiers as important components of the Army’s human resources, stressing that their professional development and effective deployment would enhance the military’s ability to accomplish assigned missions.

“Their effective development and employment are therefore essential to strengthening our institutional capacity to accomplish all assigned missions,” he said.

Shaibu noted that counter-insurgency operations, efforts to protect vulnerable communities, internal security assignments and humanitarian interventions required more than the use of military force.

According to him, such operations also depended on intelligence, cultural awareness, effective communication, discipline and constructive engagement with civilians.

He explained that female personnel could provide access to communities where cultural and religious sensitivities might make it difficult for male soldiers to interact freely with women.

The Army chief cited the contributions of female personnel during stabilisation operations in Jos North, Plateau State, in April, following a breakdown of law and order in the Angwan Ruba area.

He said the female soldiers helped facilitate the restoration of peace and security, adding that their resilience, professional conduct and competence were highly commended.

Shaibu stressed that female personnel were eligible for all operational duties, like their male counterparts, adding that their deployment and career advancement must be guided by competence, merit and established military standards.

“The Nigerian Army remains committed to advancing professionalism, meritocracy and operational competencies across all its formations and units,” he said.

He said the workshop would examine ways of identifying and developing the professional capabilities of female personnel, expanding their opportunities in combat, specialist and leadership appointments, and strengthening mentorship and career progression.

Other areas of focus, he said, included critical thinking, decision-making, peace support operations, humanitarian assistance and civil-military relations.

He urged participants to develop practical recommendations that would improve the professional development and effective deployment of female personnel.

Earlier, the Acting Commander, Nigerian Army Women Command, Col. Sule Ahmed, said the workshop was designed to strengthen the contribution of female personnel to contemporary military operations.

Ahmed said the programme aligned with the United Nations Women, Peace and Security Agenda, particularly United Nations Security Council Resolution 1325 of 2000, which promotes women’s participation in conflict prevention, resolution, peacebuilding and security processes.

He added that the workshop would address drug and substance abuse, as well as mental health management, noting their implications for personnel welfare and operational efficiency.

A retired major-general, Adeniyi Oyebade, who delivered a lecture at the workshop, said the success of military operations depended on effective collaboration between male and female personnel.

Oyebade argued that the growing sophistication of modern warfare made it necessary for the Army to expose female soldiers to the same training and operational opportunities as their male counterparts.

“The women cannot do it alone, that is the truth, but when you have the men there, it enhances the operational capacity and they can deliver effectively on the outcomes,” he said.

Citing the ongoing war in Ukraine, the retired general said the increasing use of drone technology had demonstrated that modern warfare was no longer determined by physical strength alone.

“Look at what is happening in Ukraine, the use of drone technologies. Many of the drone operators are women,” he said.

He added that female personnel could contribute significantly to specialised military operations requiring technical expertise, precision and attention to detail.

“Once you start moving away from physical effectiveness and strength and start seeing what women can bring, you will achieve more,” he said.

Oyebade commended the Army leadership for organising the workshop and urged the Women Command to involve male officers in subsequent programmes to promote collaboration and the exchange of professional experiences between both sexes.

The post Female soldiers vital to tackling insecurity – Army chief appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

description:

The governor made the announcement on Monday while addressing pensioners at the Kano Government House.



Yusuf said he had accepted the decision to remain with one wife for now but was open
content:
By Hadiza Yusuf

Kano State Governor, Abba Yusuf, has invited women interested in marrying him to apply.

The governor made the announcement on Monday while addressing pensioners at the Kano Government House.

Yusuf said he had accepted the decision to remain with one wife for now but was open to marrying again.

“Some days ago, I was being forced to become a being with one wife. I want to thank the good people of Kano who advised me to keep two wives, but for now, I have accepted one wife,” he said.

He also confirmed that the divorce process had been initiated.

“The governor has agreed to divorce her. Is it not the paper (notice of marriage dissolution)? The governor has issued that,” he said.

He disclosed that he had directed the Commissioner for Information to place advertisements on radio stations and social media platforms to invite women interested in becoming his wives.

The development comes after Zainab Musa Kwankwaso, daughter of former Kano State Governor and Yusuf’s former political godfather, Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, filed for divorce at the Upper Area Court in Gudu, Abuja, on Saturday.

title: Immigration seeks Customs, Police, Navy support for visa reforms
description:
The Nigeria Immigration Service has called for stronger inter-agency collaboration, improved intelligence sharing and sustained institutional commitment as the foundation for the successful implementation of the country’s ongoing visa and residency reforms.
The Comptroller-General of Immigration, Mr
content:
The Nigeria Immigration Service has called for stronger inter-agency collaboration, improved intelligence sharing and sustained institutional commitment as the foundation for the successful implementation of the country’s ongoing visa and residency reforms.

The Comptroller-General of Immigration, Mrs Kemi Nandap, made the call on Tuesday at a one-day stakeholders’ sensitisation workshop on the Nigeria Visa and Residency Reforms, held at the service’s headquarters in Abuja.

The workshop, themed “Assessing the Implementation of the Nigeria Visa and Residency Reforms: Stakeholders’ Engagement and Strategies for Improved Service Delivery,” drew senior representatives of key security and regulatory agencies, including the Nigerian Customs Service, the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps, the Nigeria Police Force, the Nigerian Navy, the Federal Fire Service and members of the diplomatic corps.

Nandap said the reforms, introduced to address the challenges of old manual processes, were designed to reduce delays, enhance transparency and make immigration services more accessible while preserving critical security checks.

“Our goal is to have an immigration system that provides efficient services, protects the security of our country, and supports the economic development of Nigeria,” he said.

The CG listed three technology platforms introduced under the reforms, including the e-Visa, which went live on May 1, 2025, enabling eligible foreign nationals to apply for Nigerian visas online and receive decisions within 48 hours.

The reforms also introduced new visa categories, including the F9A and F9B categories for adult and minor Nigerians returning with foreign passports.

The Electronic Temporary Work Permit, launched on August 1, 2025, digitised the previously manual process for companies seeking foreign technical experts, while introducing biometric capture and insurance requirements.

The electronic Comprehensive Expatriate Residence Permit and Automated Card, also effective from August 1, 2025, overhauled residence permit applications and renewals and introduced a new Investors Residence Permit to support government efforts to attract foreign direct investment.

However, Nandap noted that challenges remained, including payment difficulties and technical portal issues, adding that the workshop provided an opportunity to hear directly from users and partners.

She urged stakeholders to take full advantage of the workshop, saying, “The success of these reforms is not the responsibility of the Nigeria Immigration Service alone. We need the support and cooperation of all stakeholders.”

Meanwhile, Comptroller-General of Customs Bashir Adeniyi, represented by the Assistant Comptroller-General for Tariff and Trade, FT Nmadu, described the reforms as a national border-management challenge requiring coordinated institutional efforts.

“No single agency can effectively address the complexity of modern border management on its own.

“Our success depends largely on our ability to work together, share expertise, and develop practical solutions to common challenges,” Adeniyi said.

He noted that while Customs regulated the movement of goods across the borders, Immigration was responsible for regulating the movement of persons, adding that the two mandates were “closely connected and demand effective cooperation, intelligence sharing, and coordinated operations.”

“The Nigerian Customs Service recognises that successful implementation of these reforms requires strong institutional collaboration, technological innovation, effective information sharing, and sustained commitment to improve service delivery,” he said.

Adeniyi also reaffirmed the Service’s commitment to continued collaboration with the Immigration Service and other stakeholders “towards achieving safer borders, improved service delivery, and a more prosperous Nigeria.”

The Commandant-General of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps, Prof. Ahmed Audi, represented by the Deputy Commandant-General (Crisis Management Directorate), Pedro Ideba, also described the immigration reforms as directly connected to the NSCDC’s internal security mandate.

Audi said, “A well-managed visa and residency system strengthens national security, curbs irregular migration and identity-related crimes, and promotes an environment where lawful residents can live, work, and contribute to national development.”

He pledged the Corps’ continued partnership with the Immigration Service and all stakeholders “as we collectively assess progress made, identify gaps, and chart the course for more efficient, transparent, and secure service delivery.”

For his part, the Controller-General of the Federal Fire Service, Dr Ombode Adeyemi, represented by the Head of Corporate Services, Umar Abubakar, pledged the service’s cooperation with the reform process.

The post Immigration seeks Customs, Police, Navy support for visa reforms appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

The singer made this known while speaking about his career and personal achievements, declaring that he c
content:
Nigerian singer, Joseph Akinwale Akinfenwa-Donus, popularly known as Joeboy, has said he no longer makes music for financial gains or fame, stressing that his focus is now on passion and legacy.

The singer made this known while speaking about his career and personal achievements, declaring that he considers himself successful in life.

According to him, his decision to continue making music is now driven by his love for the craft rather than the desire to accumulate more wealth or attract public attention.

“The truth of the matter is, I’ve won in life. Any other thing I do is for legacy. I make music right now because I love making music, and not for extra money or attention,” he said.

Joeboy also disclosed that he has never been comfortable with public attention, revealing that he was the quietest student in his secondary school class.

“I don’t even like attention. I was the quietest guy in my class in secondary school. The reason why you know me is because I’m good at what I do,” he added.

title: NDLEA busts transnational cocaine syndicate, arrests 8 members in Lagos, Kano
description:
…Couriers on Nigeria-Niger-Libya-Europe Trip Excrete 634 Pellets in Custody



By Kingsley Omonobi



The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) said on Tuesday that its operatives have dismantled a transnational drug trafficking cartel that moves cocaine from Lagos through Kano and across the
content:
…Couriers on Nigeria-Niger-Libya-Europe Trip Excrete 634 Pellets in Custody

By Kingsley Omonobi

The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) said on Tuesday that its operatives have dismantled a transnational drug trafficking cartel that moves cocaine from Lagos through Kano and across the desert via the Republic of Niger and Libya to Europe.

The spokesman of the agency, Femi Babafemi, in a statement said, “As a result, eight members of the syndicate were arrested in well-coordinated intelligence-guided operations in Lagos and Kano.

“All eight suspects who were nabbed between Friday 30th and Saturday 31st October 2026 were drug mules who had swallowed cocaine pellets, excreting a total of 634 wraps weighing 13.795 kilograms over several days in custody.

Babafemi said, “The operation began on Friday, 30th October, when operatives of a Special Operations Unit of the Agency arrested the first suspect, 57-year-old Okwudiba Ifeanyichukwu Damian, at Nice Touch Hotel, Ago Palace, Okota, Lagos.

“He later excreted 74 wraps of cocaine weighing 1.650 kg.

“The next day, Saturday, 31st October, four more members of the cartel were stopped at the MM2 Terminal of the Murtala Muhammed Airport, Lagos, as they prepared to board a flight to Kano.

“They are Jackson Ahamefule, 43, who excreted 90 wraps weighing 1.950 kg;

Nwafor Osita Emmanuel, 47, who excreted 85 wraps weighing 1.750kg; Marcel Nnabuike, 38, who excreted 75 wraps weighing 1.655kg; and Onyenwuba Ignatius, 44, who excreted 75 wraps weighing 1.650kg.

“The five mules arrested in Lagos excreted 399 wraps of cocaine weighing 8.655 kg in all.

Intelligence from the Lagos operation showed that other members of the cartel had already travelled to Kano, where NDLEA officers at the Mallam Aminu Kano International Airport (MAKIA) were swiftly mobilised to intercept them at the arrival hall of the domestic terminal of the Kano airport.

As a result, three other members of the syndicate, namely Chinweike Ephraim Ifechukwu, 48; Edezuno John Nwaorji, 45; and Chukwudi Chinaka, 31, were identified and arrested.

A body scan showed that all three had swallowed drugs, after which they were placed under excretion observation.

Over the following days, Ifechukwu excreted 85 pellets of cocaine weighing 1.853 kg; Nwaorji expelled 80 pellets weighing 1.752 kg, while Chinaka excreted 70 pellets with a total weight of 1.535 kg.

The suspects said they had planned to travel by road from Kano through the Republic of Niger to Libya, with Europe as the final destination for the drugs.

Commenting on the arrests, the Chairman/Chief Executive Officer of NDLEA, Brig. Gen. Mohamed Buba Marwa (Rtd), commended the officers of the SOU and the MAKIA Command of the Agency.

He praised them for their “intelligence-driven synergy, speed and professionalism, which ensured that not one of the eight mules slipped through our net between Lagos and Kano.”

“This cartel thought it had found a back door to Europe through our northern borders and the Sahara.

“Their arrests are a message to drug barons and their couriers that there is no safe route out of Nigeria.

“Whether they go by air, by road or through the desert, we will trace them, find them and bring them to justice,” Marwa said.

He appealed to young people not to sell their lives to drug barons.

“Swallowing wraps of cocaine is a death wish. One burst pellet can kill a mule before the journey ends. No amount of money is worth that risk,” he warned.

The post NDLEA busts transnational cocaine syndicate, arrests 8 members in Lagos, Kano appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: EDOHERMA permanently shuts down clinic in Edo over defiance of closure order
description:
The Edo State Healthcare Regulation and Monitoring Agency (EDOHERMA) has permanently shut down Mama Funmi Clinic in Ekiadolor over alleged illegal medical operations and repeated violation of regulatory closure orders.
The enforcement exercise, carried out, followed undercover investigations which r
content:
The Edo State Healthcare Regulation and Monitoring Agency (EDOHERMA) has permanently shut down Mama Funmi Clinic in Ekiadolor over alleged illegal medical operations and repeated violation of regulatory closure orders.

The enforcement exercise, carried out, followed undercover investigations which revealed that the clinic had resumed operations weeks after it was initially sealed by the agency.

According to EDOHERMA, the facility had operated for over 15 years without registration with the Edo State Government.

Its operator, popularly known as Mama Funmi, was reportedly an auxiliary nurse allegedly providing medical and maternity services beyond her professional qualifications.

During the enforcement operation, the team discovered four patients receiving treatment at the facility, including an elderly man with a diabetic foot condition, a woman who had delivered a baby the previous day, a seriously ill man and a young boy receiving intravenous treatment.

The agency’s Chief Executive Officer, Dr. Adesuwa Urhoghide-Edigin, immediately directed that arrangements be made to transfer the patients to government-owned health facilities, with EDOHERMA offering to cover their treatment bills.

However, the patients and their families reportedly declined the offer.

The enforcement team subsequently served a fresh closure notice on the operator through her husband, who pledged that the clinic would not reopen.

During the exercise, the operator’s young daughter reportedly broke down in tears, pleading with the CEO not to arrest her mother and promising that she would never resume the illegal operation.

There was also an attempt by the operator’s husband to seek intervention from an individual identified as Patrick, whom he claimed worked in the Commissioner for Health’s office.

However, the CEO declined to entertain the call, insisting that regulatory enforcement could not be compromised through informal interventions.

Addressing residents at the scene, Urhoghide-Edigin stressed that operating a healthcare facility for 15 years did not confer medical qualifications on an auxiliary nurse or make an unregistered clinic legitimate.

She warned that EDOHERMA would not tolerate quackery, illegal healthcare operations or the deliberate violation of closure orders, adding that no personal connection or claimed influence would be allowed to obstruct lawful enforcement.

The CEO urged residents and community leaders to stop patronising unregistered healthcare facilities and report any attempt to reopen the clinic.

She also announced that the agency would monitor the premises every other day to ensure compliance.

EDOHERMA warned other healthcare facility operators that reopening sealed facilities without written authorisation would attract appropriate sanctions, including prosecution.

The agency reaffirmed its commitment to protecting residents from unsafe medical practices and ensuring that all healthcare facilities in Edo State operate within approved regulatory standards.

The post EDOHERMA permanently shuts down clinic in Edo over defiance of closure order appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Brymo questions Davido, Burna Boy, Wizkid’s Afrobeats Big Three status
description:
Singer Brymo has challenged the position of Davido, Burna Boy and Wizkid as Afrobeats’ leading trio, arguing that their popularity does not make them owners of the genre.
He expressed his views during an interview in which he discussed Rema’s place in the Nigerian music scene and the influence of es
content:
Singer Brymo has challenged the position of Davido, Burna Boy and Wizkid as Afrobeats’ leading trio, arguing that their popularity does not make them owners of the genre.

He expressed his views during an interview in which he discussed Rema’s place in the Nigerian music scene and the influence of established artistes on the industry.

According to Brymo, the recognition given to the three musicians should not be interpreted as exclusive control over Afrobeats or its direction.

He said he had concerns about what he considered their attitude towards the mainstream, adding that the genre should not be reduced to the influence of a few successful performers.

“My real problem with those so-called Big Three before is that they’ve forgotten that it’s called the mainstream,” he said.

The singer also questioned how the trio earned the Big Three label, asking whether their ranking was based on their songwriting abilities, vocal delivery, stage performances or willingness to express independent opinions.

“If you want to nail yourself down somewhere and say, ‘I’m the king, I’m the…’ Then go and create something. First of all, Afrobeats is not yours. Yours is a derivative of the real thing. So what’s Big Three? Big Three as what? As songwriting? As vocal performances? As live performances? As speaking up for yourself?” he queried.

Brymo further criticised what he described as a lack of personal independence among some prominent musicians.

Without mentioning the individual by name, he referred to a pregnancy-related controversy in which an artiste’s father reportedly came forward to defend him.

He also questioned the maturity of another unnamed musician, making reference to his mother’s reported involvement in his overseas travels.

“You claim to be the number one artist in Nigeria, your mom carries you around the whole world, you’re saying you’re the biggest artist in Nigeria. You’re not a man! Put on a man!” he declared.

On Wizkid, Brymo specifically discussed the singer’s decision to reside outside Nigeria.

He suggested that the country’s prevailing circumstances could be a factor behind the decision, arguing that Wizkid might have spent more time at home if conditions were different.

“I know Wizkid for sure, and I know why he’s here out here. If things were really working out in Nigeria, he probably would be back home full-time, just like me,” he added.

content:
Abia State Government has in a decisive anno⁠unced the immediate dissolution of the management structure and te⁠chnical cre⁠w‌ off En‌yimba International Football Club,‌ Aba over poor performance.

In a statement signed by the Commissioner for Information, Prince Okey Kanu, Government said it took the move to⁠ a⁠ddress⁠ the club’s recent disappointing performances and identified administrative and structural challenges.

‌T⁠he statement said the decisi⁠on underscore⁠ government’s resolve t⁠o undertake a comprehensive restructuring of the t‌wo-time CAF Cha⁠mp⁠ions League winners, re‌sto⁠re the club’s competitive i⁠denti‍ty and reposition it for sustainable success in Nigerian and continental football.

“Foll‌owing a re‍view of the club’s curr‌ent state of affa‍irs, th‌e g‌overnment⁠ has concluded that‍ far‍-r‌eaching interventions are nece‌ssary to add‍ress the underlying issues affecting its performance, admi‍nistrati‍on and overall operations.⁠

“Co‌nsequently, the Ministr‌y of Sports and Youth De⁠velopmen‍t has b⁠een ma‍nda⁠ted to lead the restruc‌turing process, undertake a comprehensive asses‍sment of the⁠ cl‌ub’s management framework and implement appropriate administra‌tive, technical, o‍perational an‌d insti⁠tutional‍ reforms aimed at restoring st‍a‌bi‌l‍ity, acco‌untability‍ and competitiveness”.

Government said the dissol⁠ution‍ takes immediate effect and directed all affected management an⁠d technical p⁠erso‍nnel, as well as other persons cur‌rentl⁠y in possession of Enyimba International FC’s assets, properties, official d⁠o‌cuments, equipment and other institutional materials, to ensure an order⁠ly and formal handover of all such items to the Mi⁠nis⁠try of Spo⁠rts and Youth Development.

title: Temu Risks Second Large EU Fine Over Sale of Illegal Items
description: Temu could face a second hefty EU fine after Brussels accused the Chinese-owned online retailer on Tuesday of failing to protect consumers from the sale of unsafe items.The EU already ordered a 200-million-euro ($220-million) fine on Temu in May for allowing the sale of illegal products, including d
content:
Temu could face a second hefty EU fine after Brussels accused the Chinese-owned online retailer on Tuesday of failing to protect consumers from the sale of unsafe items.

The EU already ordered a 200-million-euro ($220-million) fine on Temu in May for allowing the sale of illegal products, including dangerous baby toys and defective chargers.

Now the European Commission said Temu was breaking more rules under the Digital Services Act (DSA) by failing “to put in place reasonable, proportionate and effective measures to mitigate the risk of illegal products being offered”.

Temu said it “respectfully” disagreed with the commission’s preliminary view.

The retailer is popular in the European Union, with more than 120 million users after entering the bloc’s market in 2023.

Under the DSA, fines can go as high as six percent of a company’s total worldwide annual turnover.

Tuesday’s findings are about the measures Temu is taking to protect EU users, a senior European official said, whereas the fine in May focused on the failure to conduct a proper risk assessment to understand what dangers the platform poses.

‘Making The Online World Safer’

The EU said Temu did not have effective controls in place to check whether products complied with the bloc’s safety requirements.

High-risk categories include toys, electronics and cosmetics.

Brussels also said Temu’s sanction system was not a strong enough deterrent, with traders able to commit several serious infringements — such as selling products that fail safety checks — before Temu suspended any of their stores.

EU regulators found Temu’s moderation system did not prevent unsafe and illegal products being offered to consumers, and appeared to focus more on complying with the company’s rules than a product’s safety.

“Shopping online should not mean risking the purchase of illegal and unsafe products,” EU tech chief Henna Virkkunen said in a statement.

“The preliminary findings against Temu mark another step towards making the online world safer,” she added.

Small Package Levies

The DSA law is part of the EU’s wide-ranging legal toolbox for oversight of the world’s biggest online retailers, social media platforms and search engines.

Temu now has the right to examine the EU’s documents and reply in writing.

The company said it “invests significantly in compliance infrastructure and human expertise and implements a suite of control measures that effectively mitigate illegal product risks”.

“We will review and respond to the preliminary findings carefully and will continue to engage constructively with the commission,” it said.

The Temu investigation that began in 2024 is one of many under the DSA, including probes into China’s AliExpress and the Chinese-founded Shein.

The EU in July imposed a fine of 550 million euros on AliExpress over the sale of illegal goods on its platform.

Consumers are buying more items from outside the EU, often because of the cheaper prices, but Brussels is cracking down on small parcel imports.

Last year, nearly six billion small packages entered the bloc, mostly from China, up from around 4.6 billion in 2024.

The EU this month set a two-euro handling fee on packages from outside the bloc, coming just months after imposing a three-euro levy on low-cost parcels.

AFP

The post Temu Risks Second Large EU Fine Over Sale of Illegal Items appeared first on Channels Television.

title: Nigeria must reclaim its place in African football — Pinnick
description:
…Says FIFA to announce Nigeria football normalisation committee soon







…Notes grassroots investment key to reviving Nigerian football



By Juliet Umeh







Former Nigeria Football Federation, NFF, President, Amaju Pinnick, has called for renewed investment in football administration and gras
content:
…Says FIFA to announce Nigeria football normalisation committee soon

…Notes grassroots investment key to reviving Nigerian football

By Juliet Umeh

Former Nigeria Football Federation, NFF, President, Amaju Pinnick, has called for renewed investment in football administration and grassroots development, saying Nigeria must regain its place among Africa’s leading football nations.

Pinnick, Deputy Chairperson of the FIFA Men’s National Teams Competition Committee, spoke on Arise Television, where he discussed the state of Nigerian football and plans for a new football administration.

He said FIFA would announce a normalisation committee for Nigeria in the coming days, adding that it would help usher in the next football administration.

He said: “Within the next few days, FIFA will be announcing a normalisation committee. That will usher in the next Nigerian football administration.

“The committee should include people with experience in football and sports administration, as well as business leaders who understand the commercial side of the game.

“Nigeria is the biggest country on the continent. Based on that, we should have our pride of place,” he said.

He added: “Nobody is resting. They know the importance of football in Nigeria, it’s a major unifying factor.”

Pinnick said reviving Nigerian football would require a broad reset that includes the domestic league, clubs and junior teams.

“There’s a complete reset when it comes to Nigerian football. It’s not going to be restricted to just the federation; it’s also going to be the league.

“The league is a major component. The league is the future. The league is everything. The league will also trickle down to the junior teams.”

He said taking clubs out of government control was among the issues being considered, but did not give further details.

Pinnick also stressed the importance of supporting young players through school and community football facilities. He cited a pitch and academy project at Hussey College in Warri, his former school, funded by his foundation.

He said the facility was designed to give young people access to quality football infrastructure and could host league matches.

“If we don’t invest in the future of our kids, there will be no tomorrow,” he said.

Pinnick also defended FIFA President Gianni Infantino against critics who argue that private investment is changing the character of the game.

“Gianni is an excellent man. Gianni protects and projects the developing countries,” he said, adding that football should remain the ultimate beneficiary of leadership decisions.

“Football will always be the winner,” Pinnick said.

title: Obasanjo should take a back seat, allow Tinubu to govern — Fayose
description:
Former Ekiti State Governor, Ayodele Fayose, has urged former President Olusegun Obasanjo to take a “back seat” and allow President Bola Tinubu to run his administration.
Fayose also urged Nigerians to focus on critical issues affecting the nation’s economy rather than trivial matters on social medi
content:
Former Ekiti State Governor, Ayodele Fayose, has urged former President Olusegun Obasanjo to take a “back seat” and allow President Bola Tinubu to run his administration.

Fayose also urged Nigerians to focus on critical issues affecting the nation’s economy rather than trivial matters on social media.

The former governor stated this during an interview on TV Continental on Monday.

Asked whether criticism from figures such as Obasanjo could influence Nigerians to vote against Tinubu, Fayose said that while everyone was entitled to support any candidate of their choice, successive administrations could adopt different approaches to governance.

Fayose said, “The moment you go away from contesting, you are no more on the ballot year after year. Another set of superstars will come up. Yes, they will remember you, but don’t tell me you have the followership of a man who is contesting.

“Obasanjo should count himself lucky. Because Obasanjo still has the privilege of living; that’s why you still hear about him. One day, people will ask, ‘Who is Obasanjo? I used to hear (about him).’ That is life.

“So let him speak as much as he can. He will be in the annals of history on the net. Obasanjo should not teach Tinubu. He has spent his time. Let Obasanjo allow Tinubu to do his own time.

“You can support anybody you want to support. It’s not a crime. You don’t have to support anybody the way you imagine they will be supported. Even if you hand over power to your own son, he will govern differently. He has paid his dues; he’s tried his best. Let him take a back seat.”

Fayose further clarified that he did not share the former president’s political views, adding that people should criticise governments in power responsibly.

“We don’t agree, and that’s not out of place. We don’t have to agree.

That’s why we have different political parties. That is why I am Ayo Fayose, and he is Olusegun Obasanjo.”

The former Ekiti governor also referred to the military invasion of Odi, a predominantly Ijaw community in Kolokuma/Opokuma Local Government Area of Bayelsa State.

According to an interview with an indigene of Odi, Mr Tari Bolou, a two-time commissioner in the state and council chairman during the 1999 massacre, the attack occurred amid conflicts in the oil-rich Niger Delta region over widespread agitation for control of oil resources and environmental protection.

There were reports that armed bandits had murdered 12 police officers near Odi. Unconfirmed reports also indicated that military personnel deployed to the community were ambushed near the town, further heightening tensions in the area. The soldiers broke through the ambush and exchanged gunfire with the armed bandits in the town, further escalating the tension.

In retaliation, the military, allegedly acting on Obasanjo’s orders, invaded the town and razed the community. During the invasion, many people were killed, while most of the houses in the community were set ablaze.

Fayose, in the interview, condemned the military’s actions, allegedly carried out on Obasanjo’s orders.

“Obasanjo, under him, went to level Odi. Odi is a community. The military levelled Odi at Obasanjo’s instruction.

“Do you want people to be behaving like that? A life is sacred. You can’t, because of a crime by a group of people, level the whole community.

“Tinubu is careful; the military is careful. Because the moment you get so mad and use power arbitrarily, the innocent will suffer. That is why when our Air Force team misses the target, the gravity is heavy,” Fayose lamented.

Fayose also said the Tinubu-led administration was better than that of his predecessor, the late Muhammadu Buhari.

He said his conviction was based on his experience serving as governor under the Buhari-led administration, describing those who disagreed with his assessment as people driven by hatred for Tinubu’s government.

The post Obasanjo should take a back seat, allow Tinubu to govern — Fayose appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Fayose reveals what allegedly changed Obasanjo’s relationship with Tinubu
description:
Former Ekiti State Governor Ayodele Fayose has claimed that former President Olusegun Obasanjo’s relationship with President Bola Tinubu was affected by an unsuccessful attempt to secure political support for his daughter, Iyabo Obasanjo.
Fayose alleged that Obasanjo wanted Tinubu to support Iyabo’s
content:
Former Ekiti State Governor Ayodele Fayose has claimed that former President Olusegun Obasanjo’s relationship with President Bola Tinubu was affected by an unsuccessful attempt to secure political support for his daughter, Iyabo Obasanjo.

Fayose alleged that Obasanjo wanted Tinubu to support Iyabo’s ambition to become Ogun State governor and reportedly approached former Ogun governor Olusegun Osoba to facilitate the request.

He suggested that Obasanjo became critical of Tinubu after the alleged arrangement failed to materialise.

Fayose made the allegation on Monday during an interview on TVC while discussing Obasanjo’s recent comments on the economic policies of the Tinubu administration.

The former Ekiti governor accused Obasanjo of frequently positioning himself at the centre of national political discussions and finding fault with successive governments.

“We are overrating Obasanjo. That is the truth. It is a style. Nobody gets it done better than Obasanjo in life. If anybody wants to talk, it is either Obasanjo or nobody,” Fayose said.

He cited Obasanjo’s disagreements with former Presidents Umaru Musa Yar’Adua and Goodluck Jonathan, arguing that the former president had difficulty accepting leadership decisions that did not align with his expectations.

Fayose also questioned the change in Obasanjo’s public disposition towards Tinubu, recalling their appearance together in Ogun State in April 2026 during the inauguration of the Gateway International Cargo Airport.

He noted that Obasanjo welcomed Tinubu at the event, wore a matching outfit with him and made positive remarks about the president.

However, Fayose linked the former president’s conduct at the ceremony to the alleged effort to obtain support for Iyabo’s governorship ambition.

“You know Iyabo Obasanjo, Obasanjo’s daughter. Obasanjo went to Chief Aremo Olusegun Osoba to help him beg Tinubu so that Iyabo Obasanjo will become governor of Ogun State,” he said.

“That was the reason Obasanjo came to welcome President Tinubu.”

Fayose maintained that Obasanjo’s subsequent criticism of Tinubu followed the failure of the alleged political request.

“The moment that did not work. Obasanjo simply remembered what Osoba wrote about him in his book and went to reply to him because what he wanted did not fly.

“He will go and be begging behind the scene, when he does not get it, he will attack you,” Fayose added.

Obasanjo had faulted Tinubu’s economic reforms, arguing that they had increased the hardship faced by Nigerians. Fayose dismissed the criticism, accusing the former president of routinely opposing the policies of successive administrations.

Iyabo Obasanjo had announced her intention to contest the Ogun governorship election in February 2026 under the All Progressives Congress (APC).

She subsequently put her ambition on hold after the party settled on Senator Solomon Adeola as its consensus candidate.

The post Fayose reveals what allegedly changed Obasanjo’s relationship with Tinubu appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Rivers CP warns officers against conduct capable of compromising credibility of 2027 polls
description:
By Davies Iheamnachor







PORT HARCOURT: The Rivers State Commissioner of Police, Olugbenga Adepoju, has warned officers of the command against actions that are capable of compromising the credibility of the forthcoming general elections.







Adepuju gave the warning while decorating some offi
content:
By Davies Iheamnachor

PORT HARCOURT: The Rivers State Commissioner of Police, Olugbenga Adepoju, has warned officers of the command against actions that are capable of compromising the credibility of the forthcoming general elections.

Adepuju gave the warning while decorating some officers of the command who were recently promoted to new ranks.

According to statement in Port Harcourt by the Public Relations Officer of the Command, Blessing Agabe, an Assistant Superintendent of Police, the commissioner charged police personnel to uphold the highest standards of professionalism, discipline, integrity and accountability in the discharge of their duties.

The CP congratulated the beneficiaries on their well-deserved elevation in rank, urging them to see their promotion as a call to greater responsibility, dedication and improved service delivery.

He emphasised the need for officers to remain professional, disciplined and respectful in their dealings with members of the public, noting that promotion comes with increased expectations and a greater responsibility to the Force and the nation.

However, speaking on the forthcoming election, Adepoju charged officers to remain proactive, intelligence-driven and vigilant in identifying and responding promptly to potential security threats.

He stressed the importance of maintaining political neutrality, impartiality and strict adherence to the rule of law, warning against any conduct capable of compromising the credibility of the electoral process.

Adepoju further enjoined personnel to ensure adequate security, prevent electoral violence, maintain public order and protect lives and property before, during and after the election.

He also urged officers to discharge their responsibilities without fear or favour, while respecting the fundamental rights of all citizens, even as he encouraged the newly promoted officers to justify their elevation through exemplary conduct, commitment to duty and unwavering loyalty to the ideals of the Nigeria Police Force.

Adepoju reaffirmed the command’s commitment to providing a safe and secure environment for all residents of Rivers State and ensuring a peaceful electoral process.

title: UNIMED VC congratulates Education Minister, Alausa, on 2026 Sun Minister of the Year Award
description: The Vice-Chancellor of the University of Medical Sciences (UNIMED), Ondo, Prof. Ebunoluwa Adejuyigbe has congratulated the Minister of Education, Dr. Maruf Tunji Alausa on his recognition as the 2026 Sun Minister of the year, describing the award as well deserved and a recognition of his purposeful
content:
The Vice-Chancellor of the University of Medical Sciences (UNIMED), Ondo, Prof. Ebunoluwa Adejuyigbe has congratulated the Minister of Education, Dr. Maruf Tunji Alausa on his recognition as the 2026 Sun Minister of the year, describing the award as well deserved and a recognition of his purposeful leadership and commitment to transforming Nigeria’s education sector.

Prof Adejuyigbe said the prestigious honour was a fitting acknowledgement of the Minister’s dedication, visionary leadership and sustained efforts towards repositioning the nation’s education system in line with the Renewed Hope Agenda of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu.

She noted that the Minister’s commitment to driving far-reaching reforms in the sector, particularly through the Nigeria Education Sector Renewal Initiative (NESRI) has continued to provide fresh impetus for expanding access to quality education, improving learning outcomes and equipping Nigerian youths with relevant skills for the demands of a rapidly evolving global economy.

According to the Vice-Chancellor, the award is not only a personal recognition of Dr. Alausa’s contributions but also an endorsement of the renewed focus on making education more responsive to national development priorities.

Prof Adejuyigbe particularly commended the Minister’s vision, encapsulated in the philosophy, “Learn to Work, not just Teach to Learn,” describing it as a progressive approach that places employability, productivity, innovation and practical skills at the centre of educational delivery.

She said, “The recognition of Dr. Maruf Tunji Alausa as the 2026 Sun Minister of the Year is indeed well deserved. His commitment to repositioning Nigeria’s education sector through purposeful policies, strategic reforms and innovative interventions is commendable.

“His vision of making education a pathway to employability, productivity and national development reflects the changing realities of the world and the urgent need to produce graduates who are not only academically sound but also equipped with the practical competencies to contribute meaningfully to society.

“Through initiatives such as NESRI, the Federal Ministry of Education is demonstrating a clear commitment to strengthening the education system, improving the quality of learning and creating opportunities for Nigerian youths to compete favourably on the global stage.”

The UNIMED Vice-Chancellor further stressed the importance of sustained collaboration among the Federal Ministry of Education, universities and other stakeholders at ensuring that the ongoing reforms translate into measurable improvements in the quality and relevance of education across the country.

She reaffirmed UNIMED’s commitment to supporting national education priorities through quality teaching, impactful research, innovation and the production of highly skilled medical and health professionals capable of addressing Nigeria’s healthcare needs.

Prof Adejuyigbe expressed confidence that the Minister’s recognition would further inspire him and other stakeholders in the education sector to remain steadfast in their pursuit of excellence and sustainable development.

She wished Dr. Alausa greater accomplishments in his service to the nation, noting that his award was a source of encouragement to all those working towards building a stronger, more inclusive and globally competitive Nigerian education system.

“On behalf of the University of Medical Sciences, Ondo, I warmly congratulate the Honourable Minister on this remarkable achievement. We celebrate this well-deserved honour and wish him continued wisdom, strength and success in advancing the cause of education in Nigeria,” she added.

The post UNIMED VC congratulates Education Minister, Alausa, on 2026 Sun Minister of the Year Award appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Simon Ekpa released from Finnish prison – Lawyer
description:
Nigerian-born separatist leader, Simon Ekpa, has been released from custody in Finland, a former lead counsel to the convicted leader of the Indigenous People of Biafra, Nnamdi Kanu, Aloy Ejimakor, has confirmed.
Ejimakor announced Ekpa’s release in a Facebook post on Tuesday, saying he received con
content:
Nigerian-born separatist leader, Simon Ekpa, has been released from custody in Finland, a former lead counsel to the convicted leader of the Indigenous People of Biafra, Nnamdi Kanu, Aloy Ejimakor, has confirmed.

Ejimakor announced Ekpa’s release in a Facebook post on Tuesday, saying he received confirmation from the separatist leader’s close friend and ally, David Matsanga.

“Mazi SIMON EKPA has just been freed. His close friend and ally, Dr David Matsanga, confirmed it to me just minutes ago during our telephone conversation,” Ejimakor wrote.

The Deputy Prime Minister of the Biafra Government in Exile, Ngozi Orabueze, also announced Ekpa’s release in a post on her official X handle on Tuesday.

Orabueze shared a video showing herself with Ekpa as he emerged from prison, while some Nigerians gathered to celebrate his return.

In the video, Ekpa made a brief statement, saying, “You can’t hide the truth forever; it will always come out.”

Ekpa, who was arrested by Finnish authorities in November 2024 over terrorism-related offences linked to activities of IPOB in Nigeria, had been in custody since then.

He was convicted in September 2025 by the Päijät-Häme District Court for participating in the activities of a terrorist organisation and inciting crimes for terrorist purposes.

His release came on the date earlier announced by his legal support team, which had said he was scheduled to regain his freedom on November 17, 2026.

In October 2026, PUNCH Online reported that a Finnish Court of Appeal has reduced the prison sentence of pro-Biafran agitator Simon Ekpa from six years to four years while upholding his conviction on terrorism-related charges.

While the ruling is not final and can still be appealed to a higher court, PUNCH Online cannot confirm whether he is released on parole.

The case relates to Ekpa’s activities between August 2021 and November 2024, when the district court found that he had used his significant social media following to fuel tensions in the Biafra region as part of efforts to establish an independent state in south-eastern Nigeria.

Ekpa, who moved to Finland from Nigeria in 2007, is a long-term resident of Lahti and previously served on the Finnish city’s council, representing the National Coalition Party.

PUNCH Online reported that the court found him guilty of participating in a terrorist organisation, inciting crimes for terrorist purposes, aggravated tax fraud and violating provisions of the Lawyers Act.

The court also found that he had supplied armed groups with weapons, explosives and ammunition through his network of contacts and encouraged followers on X, formerly Twitter, to commit crimes in Nigeria.

Ekpa denied the charges during the trial.

His arrest in Finland in November 2024 followed investigations into alleged separatist activities linked to efforts to establish an independent Biafran state.

Biafra, in south-eastern Nigeria, declared independence in 1967, triggering a civil war that lasted until 1970, when the secessionist bid ended.

title: Miss World Nigeria urges communicators to use words to uplift, not stigmatise
description:
• Says words can build confidence, restore dignity and inspire people to go beyond limitations
Miss World Nigeria 2026, Tamunosoye Karibi-George, urged public relations professionals and other communicators to use their words to inspire, encourage and uplift people rather than reinforce negative lab
content:
• Says words can build confidence, restore dignity and inspire people to go beyond limitations

Miss World Nigeria 2026, Tamunosoye Karibi-George, urged public relations professionals and other communicators to use their words to inspire, encourage and uplift people rather than reinforce negative labels and stereotypes.

She said communication has the power to shape people’s perception of themselves, stressing that individuals made to feel unworthy or incapable by society need positive messages that restore their confidence and sense of worth.

Karibi-George made the appeal while addressing participants at the Global Alliance World Public Relations Forum (WPRF) 2026 in Abuja, where she expressed pride in being associated with the professional body and its commitment to communication and advocacy.

The beauty queen, who traced her journey from being the Face of Port Harcourt to Miss Africa and subsequently Miss World Nigeria, said her experience on the international stage in Vietnam gave her an opportunity to represent not only Nigeria and Africa but also the wider communication community.

Reflecting on the power of communication, she said: “In this very room, it has been established that communication is power and communication is responsibility.”

Speaking about her advocacy, she said she was committed to encouraging people labelled by society as unworthy, incapable and other derogatory names to look beyond such descriptions.

“What matters the most is what you say about yourself,” she said.

She challenged communicators to be more deliberate and responsible in their choice of words, urging them to tell people how worthy and capable they are of achieving great things.

“As communicators, we should use our words kindly. We should use words of worth. We should use them to uplift others, encourage them and tell them they are always beyond limits,” she said.

Karibi-George also expressed appreciation for the opportunity to address the gathering and acknowledged the support of her father, who served as the master of ceremonies at the event.

The 26-year-old beauty queen was crowned Miss World Nigeria 2026 after representing Bayelsa State at the national competition. She is also known for her advocacy through the Beyond Labels initiative, which promotes inclusion and empowerment for children with special needs.

content:
By John Alechenu


Global public relations experts have warned governments and corporate organisations to stop using PR, propaganda or strategic messaging to hide leadership failures.

Trust, they said, cannot be bought with publicity. It must be earned through integrity, accountability and actions that match promises.

The warning came at a session on Ethical Leadership and Trust in a Divided World at the ongoing 2026 World Public Relations Forum (WPRF) in Abuja, organised by the Global Alliance for Public Relations and Communication Management and the Nigeria Institute of Public Relations.

The panel featured the Alliance’s regional council chairs for Europe, Asia-Pacific, Africa, Middle East and South Asia, and North America. It was moderated by Chimdi Neliaku, Chair of the NIPR Young Professionals Hub.

For Europe, Global Alliance Vice President and Chair of its European Regional Council, Silvia Arto, said ethical leadership is shown in personal conduct, not public declarations.

“To me, ethical leadership is lead by example. It’s walk the talk. It’s integrity,” she said, adding that integrity meant doing what was right even when nobody was watching.

Trust, she warned, takes years to build but can be destroyed within seconds, particularly through social media.

“Trust and ethical leadership, personal leadership, is built through actions, not declarations,” Arto said.

She urged professionals to promote transparency, media literacy and dialogue while combating misinformation, propaganda and misuse of artificial intelligence.

Citing the European Union’s AI Act, she called for human accountability and ethical guidelines for emerging technologies. Arto also invoked Yoruba wisdom, declaring: “Character is beauty.”

From Asia-Pacific, Chair Jaffri Osman said effective leadership requires more than intellectual intelligence. Emotional and social intelligence matter just as much in building relationships across diverse communities.

“Trust is built by leaders who understand beyond IQ. They have to understand EQ and SQ,” he said.

Using Malaysia’s Sarawak region as an example of multicultural coexistence, Osman said professionals must understand local cultures, traditions and relationships to influence communities responsibly.

“When we talk about influence, when we talk about communication, and when we talk about going ahead effectively in ethical communication, we must go respect,” he said.

For Africa, Chair Ms Irene Lungu Chipili identified political messaging, democratic competition and misinformation as major threats to public confidence. She questioned whether citizens could trust messages from political parties and governments, arguing that the credibility of the messenger was as important as the information.

Citing Zambia’s Public Relations and Communication Act No. 11 of 2022, she said the country had moved to professionalise communication practice and encourage employment of professional communicators in the public sector.

But speed, she warned, now pressures practitioners to disseminate information before competitors.

“Every minute, because if you don’t communicate it, somebody else will,” she said.

Speed must not override accuracy, she cautioned, asking: “But even as we are quick to disseminate information, where is our role as responsible communicators? How do we communicate responsibly?”

From the Middle East and South Asia, Chair Serra Gorpe said accountability, transparency and stakeholder engagement were essential to institutional legitimacy.

“Legitimacy is accountability, transparency, stakeholder communication, engagement,” she said.

Gorpe called for stronger ethics education in universities, urging institutions to use regional case studies rather than relying predominantly on Western textbooks.

“When I started my profession in my home country, what inspired us were Western textbooks. We learned from those textbooks. And then later we realised that we need to integrate our own perspective in those textbooks,” she said.

She also urged professionals to respect cultural identities, religious traditions and political sensitivities.

From the private sector, North American Chair Ms Bonnie Caver warned that organisations risk reputational damage when public commitments do not reflect actual performance. Companies often promise community engagement and ambitious initiatives without delivering, creating a damaging disconnect between statements and reality.

She urged executives to move beyond surveys and engage directly with employees, customers and communities.

She also stressed the importance of professionalising public relations, distinguishing trained practitioners from ordinary users of communication platforms.

“Everybody in the world is a communicator. My son, who’s an engineer, is a communicator. My son, who’s a scientist, is a communicator. In today’s world, everyone is a communicator. We are not communicators. We’re communication professionals,” she said.

In closing, moderator Neliaku said leadership must precede communication, while credibility must be built through relationships, emotional intelligence and strong institutions. She challenged young professionals to show the same accountability they demand from leaders.

“We must also start to build a record of conduct that our own generation will be trusted on and judged on,” she said.

The post PR cannot cover bad leadership, global experts warn appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Enugu Assembly caps rent increase at 2%, bans hikes for four years
description:
The Enugu State House of Assembly has passed a bill restricting landlords from increasing rents by more than two per cent of the current rent within a four-year period.
The bill, which seeks to check arbitrary rent increases and protect tenants from exploitation, was passed on Tuesday after the Hous
content:
The Enugu State House of Assembly has passed a bill restricting landlords from increasing rents by more than two per cent of the current rent within a four-year period.

The bill, which seeks to check arbitrary rent increases and protect tenants from exploitation, was passed on Tuesday after the House adopted the report of its committee on the proposed amendment.

Under the new provisions, landlords must wait for four years before reviewing rents, while any increase within the period must not exceed two per cent of the existing rent. However, landlords who undertake reasonable renovations to their properties are permitted to increase rents by not more than 10 per cent.

The Chairman of the House Committee on the amendment, Okey Mbah, who represents Nkanu East Constituency, said the proposed law followed extensive consultations with relevant stakeholders.

Presenting the committee’s report during plenary, Mbah described the amendment as a major intervention in the landlord-tenant relationship, saying it would end the exploitation of tenants and make accommodation more affordable for residents.

He said the provisions would substantially reduce the financial burden on residents seeking accommodation in the state.

“This bill will subside over 60 per cent of what residents used to pay while trying to secure accommodation,” the lawmaker said.

The report was considered following a motion moved by Hon. Iloabuchi Abugu, representing Nkanu West Constituency, and seconded by the Deputy Speaker, Jane Eneh, representing Awgu North Constituency.

The committee was constituted from the House Committees on Housing and Investment, Public Petition, Ethics and Privileges, and Judiciary.

Following the presentation and adoption of the report, the House dissolved into the Committee of the Whole to consider the bill clause by clause before its eventual passage.

Speaking after the exercise, Speaker of the House, Rt. Hon. Uche Ugwu, described the legislation as part of the good governance initiatives of the Peter Mbah administration.

He said the law would give tenants in Enugu State a new lease of life by providing safeguards against arbitrary rent increases.

The bill, titled A Bill for a Law to Amend the Landlord and Tenant Second Amendment Bill, Cap 101, Revised Laws of Enugu State 2024, House Bill No. 3, 2025, passed second reading on March 11, 2026, and subsequently underwent a public hearing on March 26, 2026.

With its passage by the Assembly, the bill now awaits the assent of Governor Peter Mbah to become law.
