title: AFCON 2027: Chelle, Ndidi Target Victory As Super Eagles Prepare For Tanzania Return Leg
description: Super Eagles head coach Eric Chelle says Nigeria are motivated to secure victory against Tanzania as both sides prepare for their return-leg encounter in the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) qualifiers at the Amaan Stadium in Zanzibar on Tuesday.The Super Eagles emerged 3-1 victors when the two te
content:
Super Eagles head coach Eric Chelle says Nigeria are motivated to secure victory against Tanzania as both sides prepare for their return-leg encounter in the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) qualifiers at the Amaan Stadium in Zanzibar on Tuesday.

The Super Eagles emerged 3-1 victors when the two teams met on Friday at the Godswill Akpabio International Stadium, with goals courtesy of Alhassan Yusuf and a brace from Tolu Arokodare.

Chelle, in a pre-match press conference, acknowledged that Tanzania would be eager to win on home soil but insisted that his players were ready for the challenge despite a difficult journey ahead of the match.

The Nigerian coach said he was surprised by Tanzania’s tactical approach in their previous meeting, particularly their decision to deploy a five-man defence instead of the formations they had traditionally used.

Another victory would take the Super Eagles to nine points and increase the pressure on Group L leaders Guinea-Bissau, who also face Madagascar on Tuesday.

Meanwhile, Tanzania have already qualified automatically as a tournament co-host.

“I was a little disappointed because they went to Uyo and played five at the back. Normally, they used to play in 4-2-3-1 or 4-1-4-1. So I was a little disappointed,” Chelle said.

“But now I think they are at home and they want to win this game. Like us, we are ready to make a good game. The travel was not easy yesterday, but we are here, excited and motivated to play this game.”

The Super Eagles coach also defended his tactical decisions, insisting that his choice of formation would depend on the players available, the opposition and the team’s overall philosophy.

Chelle said preparations for the encounter had been ongoing for months, stressing that selecting the best-performing players remained central to his approach.

“We prepared for the game against Tanzania during two or three months before the game. We saw a lot of things, and after that, you have to put the best players,” he said.

He added that players who regularly feature in the starting lineup must continue working hard to maintain their places, explaining that every member of the squad must be at their best.

Chelle also praised the commitment of his players, insisting that they continued to give their all for the national team even when results did not go their way.

“I can tell you that these guys, they give everything for this jersey,” he said.

Meanwhile, Super Eagles captain Wilfred Ndidi has expressed confidence in the team’s blend of experienced players and emerging talents, describing the integration of younger players into the squad as encouraging.

Ndidi said the younger members of the team had settled in well and urged them to communicate freely with their more experienced teammates, both on and off the pitch.

“It’s very inspiring seeing the young lads coming into the team and actually gelling with the team. For us as a team, old players and young players, we are all the same,” the midfielder said.

He maintained that communication and unity would be crucial as Nigeria seek to maintain their momentum, adding that the players must remain committed to the coach’s philosophy and game plan regardless of the pressure they face.

Reflecting on the team’s previous performance, Ndidi noted that Nigeria improved in the second half, attributing the response to the players’ ability to stay together as a unit.

Ndidi said the team remained focused on securing victory in their next outing, insisting that their immediate priority was the encounter against Tanzania before turning attention to subsequent matches.

“We as a group, we have a plan, we have a philosophy, we have a game plan and we try as much as possible to win every game. Every game that comes our way now, that sits at the top of the table. So the most important game now is the game tomorrow. We get this one done, and then we look forward to the next one,” Ndidi said.

Match Details

  • Match: Tanzania vs Nigeria
  • Date: Tuesday, November 17, 2026
  • Time: 2:00 PM WAT

title: NDLEA arrests eight cocaine couriers, recovers 634 wraps
description:
Operatives of the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency have arrested eight members of a transnational drug trafficking cartel accused of moving cocaine from Lagos through Kano, Niger Republic and Libya to Europe.
The suspects, who allegedly swallowed cocaine pellets to evade security checks, excrete
content:
Operatives of the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency have arrested eight members of a transnational drug trafficking cartel accused of moving cocaine from Lagos through Kano, Niger Republic and Libya to Europe.

The suspects, who allegedly swallowed cocaine pellets to evade security checks, excreted a total of 634 wraps weighing 13.795 kilogrammes while in NDLEA custody.

The agency said the suspects were arrested during intelligence-led operations in Lagos and Kano between October 30 and 31, 2026.

In a statement on Tuesday, the NDLEA Director of Media and Advocacy, Femi Babafemi, said the operation began with the arrest of a 57-year-old suspect, Okwudiba Ifeanyichukwu Damian, at Nice Touch Hotel, Ago Palace, Okota, Lagos, on October 30.

The statement partly read, “Operatives of the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency have dismantled a transnational drug trafficking cartel that moves cocaine from Lagos through Kano and across the desert via Niger Republic and Libya to Europe. As a result, eight members of the syndicate were arrested in well-coordinated intelligence-guided operations in Lagos and Kano.

“All eight suspects who were nabbed between Friday 30 and Saturday 31 October 2026 were drug mules who had swallowed cocaine pellets, excreting a total of 634 wraps weighing 13.795 kilograms over several days in custody.

“The operation began on Friday 30th October when operatives of a Special Operations Unit of the Agency arrested the first suspect, 57-year-old Okwudiba Ifeanyichukwu Damian, at Nice Touch Hotel, Ago Palace, Okota, Lagos. He later excreted 74 wraps of cocaine weighing 1.650kg.

“The next day, Saturday October 31, four more members of the cartel were stopped at the MM2 Terminal of the Murtala Muhammed Airport, Lagos, as they prepared to board a flight to Kano. They are: Jackson Ahamefule, 43, who excreted 90 wraps weighing 1.950kg; Nwafor Osita Emmanuel, 47, who excreted 85 wraps weighing 1.750kg; Marcel Nnabuike, 38, who excreted 75 wraps weighing 1.655kg; and Onyenwuba Ignatius, 44, who excreted 75 wraps weighing 1.650kg.”

Babafemi said the five suspects arrested in Lagos excreted a combined 399 wraps of cocaine weighing 8.655kg.

He said intelligence gathered during the Lagos operation indicated that other members of the cartel had travelled to Kano, prompting NDLEA operatives at the Mallam Aminu Kano International Airport to intercept them at the domestic terminal.

The three suspects arrested in Kano were identified as Chinweike Ephraim Ifechukwu, 48; Edezuno John Nwaorji, 45; and Chukwudi Chinaka, 31.

He said body scans confirmed that the suspects had swallowed drugs, adding that they were placed under observation until they excreted the cocaine pellets.

The statement said Ifechukwu excreted 85 pellets weighing 1.853kg, Nwaorji expelled 80 pellets weighing 1.752kg, while Chinaka excreted 70 pellets weighing 1.535kg.

It added that the suspects disclosed that they planned to travel by road from Kano through Niger Republic and Libya, with Europe as their final destination.

Reacting to the arrests, the NDLEA Chairman, Brig. Gen. Mohamed Buba Marwa (retd.), commended operatives of the agency’s Special Operations Unit and Kano command for the operation.

Marwa said, “Their intelligence-driven synergy, speed and professionalism ensured that not one of the eight mules slipped through our net between Lagos and Kano.”

He added, “This cartel thought it had found a back door to Europe through our northern borders and the Sahara. Their arrests are a message to drug barons and their couriers that there is no safe route out of Nigeria.

“Whether they go by air, by road or through the desert, we will trace them, find them and bring them to justice.”

The NDLEA boss also warned young people against allowing drug traffickers to use them as couriers.

“Swallowing wraps of cocaine is a death wish. One burst pellet can kill a mule before the journey ends. No amount of money is worth that risk,” he warned.

The post NDLEA arrests eight cocaine couriers, recovers 634 wraps appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Jonathan Warns Against Ethnic Rivalry, Political Intolerance Ahead Of General Elections
description: Former President Goodluck Jonathan has warned that the rising tide of political intolerance, thuggery, and deliberate stoking of ethnic rivalries pose a severe threat to Nigeria’s national existence and stability ahead of the 2027 general elections.‎Speaking at a high-level peace and secur
content:
Former President Goodluck Jonathan has warned that the rising tide of political intolerance, thuggery, and deliberate stoking of ethnic rivalries pose a severe threat to Nigeria’s national existence and stability ahead of the 2027 general elections.

‎Speaking at a high-level peace and security conference hosted by the Goodluck Jonathan Foundation in Abuja, Jonathan stressed that upcoming electoral cycles must not become catalysts for destructive division.

He urged political leaders and citizens alike to prioritise national unity, democratic values, and responsible leadership over narrow partisan ambitions.

The former president also urged Nigerians to treat the upcoming 2027 general elections as a critical opportunity to choose credible leadership at both state and federal levels, prioritising competence over ambition.

He warned that undermining national cohesion for political ambition poses a severe danger to the country’s existence.

“Nothing could be more dangerous to our national existence than the deliberate encouragement of ethnic rivalry. We must never allow political ambition to undermine the bonds that hold us together as one nation and one country, both at the national level and at the state level”, he said.

title: Tinubu has performed better than Buhari, says Fayose
description:
Former Ekiti State Governor, Ayodele Fayose, has compared President Bola Tinubu’s administration with that of his predecessor, the late Muhammadu Buhari, saying the former has performed better.
He said his conviction was based on his experience serving as governor under the Buhari-led administration
content:
Former Ekiti State Governor, Ayodele Fayose, has compared President Bola Tinubu’s administration with that of his predecessor, the late Muhammadu Buhari, saying the former has performed better.

He said his conviction was based on his experience serving as governor under the Buhari-led administration, describing those who disagreed with his assessment as people driven by hatred for Tinubu’s government.

Fayose stated this during an interview on TVC on Monday.

Speaking about the achievements of Tinubu’s administration and why Nigerians should support his re-election bid in 2027, the former governor cautioned that no president could meet the expectations of all Nigerians.

“There’s no perfect president. There’s no president in Nigeria who will meet the yearnings of everybody. It’s not possible. You can’t meet the yearnings of your family.

“I laugh when people say that his government is worse than Buhari’s government. I was a critic of Buhari, and I know what I’m saying. I was a governor in Buhari’s time. I know what I’m talking about. But if anybody living today says Tinubu has not done better than Buhari, that is… I consider that either hate or political lineage that taught you. You can’t praise your enemy. I can say that,” Fayose said partly.

In his inaugural address on May 29, 2023, shortly after assuming office, Tinubu announced the removal of the petrol subsidy.

The government subsequently harmonised and floated the foreign exchange market, triggering significant adjustments in petrol prices and exchange rates, with consequential effects on the cost of living and doing business.

Fayose, however, acknowledged that although the achievements of the present administration might not have reached the “perfect” level expected by Nigerians, the economy was recovering, adding that the process of recovery “is not easy”.

“Tinubu has stabilised the economy. He might not be to the extent everybody will say, he’s perfect, or he’s getting there. When things go bad, recovery is not easy.

“When the economy fails, recovery is not easy. I’m not saying Tinubu is perfect. I have not hidden my support for him, because I’ve seen him through. He has done so well, so far, so good. But there must be contest against him. Somebody must contest against him. Somebody must say ill of him to win an election,’ he added.

Fayose cited some of the present administration’s efforts to improve the living conditions of Nigerians and strengthen the economy, including the Nigerian Education Loan Fund and the removal of the petrol subsidy.

Since the launch of its student loan portal on May 24, 2024, NELFUND has disbursed a total of N375.28bn as of Monday, November 9, 2026, comprising N194.77bn in institutional fees and N180.50bn in upkeep allowances.

“Are you telling me Tinubu has done well on loans? Who remembers students in loans? Have we not gone as far as N1,670 to the dollar? Has it not gone down? Today, the dollar is under N1,400. Yes, it’s not perfect, but it’s better.

“The removal of the subsidy. Is it not better that the subsidy, whatever gains they make out, is now fairly in the space to make sure that salaries are paid, than the money to go to the hands of a few minorities?.

“If you even see those people criticising Tinubu, when you ask them, would you reverse it (the fuel subsidy)? They get confused. They don’t know what to say. ‘Today, I will reverse. Tomorrow, I will not reverse.’ You understand? So, you see, this is politics. Nigeria is not just a country you govern at will,” Fayose said, among other things.

Speaking about the opposition ahead of the 2027 elections, Fayose lamented that politicians made numerous promises during campaigns to secure electoral victory.

He said Nigerians would have to decide whom to vote for between the incumbent, Tinubu; Peter Obi of the Nigeria Democratic Congress; and former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar of the African Democratic Congress.

He said, “Nigeria today is like a young lady. Everybody comes in election season to say, ‘I would like you. I would do everything for you. Just leave your boyfriend and come to me. I will do everything for you. Don’t worry.’

“It is the decision of the young girl whether to leave a Tinubu for an Atiku, or from an Atiku to an Obi. It’s a decision they have to make. So everybody is just saying what they love to say, in their own interest.

“Atiku has had his time. I will not criticise him for contesting and contesting. If you have the means, if you have the resources, if you feel you can still make it through, fine. But if you don’t make it through, take it in good strides. We should stop hitting the system.

“No Nigerian president will be in the seat. It’s not common. Yes, it happened in the days of Jonathan, but it’s not common to be removed cheaply. Not because you want to rig, but because you put in everything humanly possible to retain your seat.”

The post Tinubu has performed better than Buhari, says Fayose appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

The House described the unanimous endorsement as a significant milestone in the constitutional amendmen
content:
The House of Representatives has welcomed the approval by all 36 State Houses of Assembly of the proposed constitutional amendment to provide for the establishment of State Police Services.

The House described the unanimous endorsement as a significant milestone in the constitutional amendment process, saying it represents 100 per cent approval by the state legislatures and exceeds the constitutional requirement of at least 24 State Houses of Assembly under Section 9(2) of the 1999 Constitution.

The House Spokesman, Rep. Akin Rotimi Jr., disclosed this in a statement issued in Abuja on Tuesday, November 17, 2026.

According to the statement, the approval was confirmed by the Clerk to the National Assembly, Kamoru Ogunlana, who said the bill had satisfied the constitutional and administrative requirements for transmission.

Ogunlana, in a statement issued on Monday, November 16, explained that the bill had earlier met the requirements for transmission but that the leadership of the National Assembly directed a brief delay to allow for broader national consensus and engagement with all states.

He said: “The Bill had long satisfied all the constitutional and administrative requirements for transmission as prescribed by the Constitution and the Acts Authentication Act Cap. A2, Laws of the Federation of Nigeria, 2004, but the Leadership of the National Assembly directed a brief delay of transmission to allow for broader national consensus and engagement of all the States of the Federation.”

The Clerk further confirmed that following the completion of the verification process by his office, the bill was ready for transmission to President Bola Tinubu for assent.

He described the unanimous endorsement as an unprecedented demonstration of cooperation between the National Assembly and the State Houses of Assembly, as well as between the executive arms of government at federal and state levels.

The House of Representatives acknowledged the collective efforts of both chambers of the National Assembly and all 36 State Houses of Assembly in advancing the proposed constitutional reform.

It particularly recognised the work of the House Committee on Constitution Review, chaired by the Deputy Speaker, Benjamin Kalu.

The House also commended the 36 state governors, speakers and members of the State Houses of Assembly, as well as other stakeholders, for their cooperation and commitment to the proposed reform of policing in Nigeria.

It said the unanimous approval marked an important step towards strengthening the country’s security architecture, improving responses to local security challenges and advancing the establishment of State Police Services.

The House added that the development would provide a foundation for the National Assembly to complete and transmit the remaining Sixth Constitution Alteration Bills to the State Houses of Assembly for consideration.

It reaffirmed its commitment to working with relevant institutions and stakeholders to advance constitutional reforms and other legislative measures aimed at strengthening national security and safeguarding the lives and property of Nigerians.

title: 30-year-old man killed, parents injured as gunmen attack Jigawa community
description:
Gunmen have killed a 30-year-old man and injured his parents during a midnight attack on their home in Nabai Fulani Settlement, Kargo Ward, Garki Local Government Area of Jigawa State.
The attack reportedly occurred around 3:50 am on Monday, November 16, 2026, when about seven unidentified armed men
content:
Gunmen have killed a 30-year-old man and injured his parents during a midnight attack on their home in Nabai Fulani Settlement, Kargo Ward, Garki Local Government Area of Jigawa State.

The attack reportedly occurred around 3:50 am on Monday, November 16, 2026, when about seven unidentified armed men invaded the residence of 70-year-old Yahaya Jibrin.

The Public Relations Officer of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), Jigawa State Command, ASC Badaruddeen Tijjani, confirmed the incident in a statement made available to journalists in Dutse, the state capital, on Tuesday.

Tijjani said the attackers were suspected armed robbers who stormed Jibrin’s residence and assaulted him and his 45-year-old wife, Zainab Yahaya.

The attack also left their 30-year-old son dead, while his parents sustained injuries.

According to Tijjani, their son, Lawan Yahaya, aged about 30, was allegedly shot dead when he attempted to rescue his parents.

“Preliminary information revealed that the suspects were armed with AK-47 rifles,” he said.

The NSCDC spokesperson added that the attackers fled with a red Boxer motorcycle without a registration number and an undisclosed sum of money.

He said the two injured victims were immediately taken to Garki General Hospital for medical attention.

Tijjani further disclosed that the Garki Police Division evacuated the deceased’s body to the hospital, where a doctor confirmed him dead.

“The deceased was confirmed dead by a medical doctor,” he said.

The corpse was subsequently released to the family for burial in accordance with Islamic rites.

The NSCDC spokesperson said the Jigawa State Commandant, CC Kabiru Ingawa, condemned the attack and expressed his condolences to the bereaved family.

“The Commandant assured members of the public that the Corps would continue to collaborate with other security agencies to strengthen security, protect lives and property, and ensure that criminal elements are brought to justice,” Tijjani stated.

He added that the commandant urged residents to remain vigilant and promptly report suspicious movements or activities to the nearest security formation.

Tijjani also urged residents to provide credible information that could assist in identifying and apprehending the fleeing suspects.

He reassured residents of the command’s commitment to safeguarding lives and property across the state.

title: CJN swears in new A’Court Justices, urges judicial independence
description:
The Chief Justice of Nigeria, Justice Kudirat Kekere-Ekun, has warned 12 newly appointed Justices of the Court of Appeal against political, financial, social and personal pressures, urging them to protect their judicial independence and uphold the integrity of the Bench.
She also cautioned the justi
content:
The Chief Justice of Nigeria, Justice Kudirat Kekere-Ekun, has warned 12 newly appointed Justices of the Court of Appeal against political, financial, social and personal pressures, urging them to protect their judicial independence and uphold the integrity of the Bench.

She also cautioned the justices against allowing public opinion, professional relationships or the desire for unanimous decisions to influence their judgments.

Kekere-Ekun gave the warning on Tuesday during the swearing-in ceremony of the 12 justices at the Supreme Court complex in Abuja.

Addressing the newly appointed appellate court justices, the CJN stressed that their elevation came with greater responsibilities, particularly the need to balance collective judicial deliberations with individual independence.

She said, “Your judicial independence must be guarded against political, financial, social and personal pressures, including those that may arise through professional familiarity or established relationships.”

The CJN also warned that public approval must not determine judicial decisions, just as criticism should not discourage judges from reaching decisions required by the law.

“My Lords, judicial office is increasingly exercised in an environment in which decisions are subjected to immediate public commentary. You must remain conscious of this reality without allowing it to influence your adjudicatory responsibilities.

“Public approval must not be the basis for you to depart from the law, just as criticism must not deter you from reaching a decision that your conscience and the law require,” she said.

She further urged the justices to demonstrate courage in expressing dissenting opinions where necessary, stressing that judicial independence must not be sacrificed for collegiality.

According to her, “You must decide according to the law and your conscience, without being unduly influenced by seniority, reputation, personal affinity or the desire for unanimity.

“Where, after careful consideration, your view differs from that of the majority, you must have the
courage to maintain and express it with clarity, restraint and respect.

“A well-reasoned dissent is a legitimate feature of appellate adjudication and may, in time, contribute to the development or reconsideration of the law.”

Kekere-Ekun explained that unlike their previous positions, where most exercised judicial authority as sole presiding judges, their new responsibilities would require them to sit in panels, deliberate collectively and arrive at decisions through consultations with other justices.

She urged them to approach such deliberations with intellectual openness, mutual respect and a willingness to reconsider their positions when presented with convincing arguments.

The CJN, however, warned that differences in judicial opinions must not degenerate into personal disagreements, adding that the strength of an appellate court depended on the quality of its reasoning rather than an artificial appearance of unanimity.

She reminded the justices that the Court of Appeal played a critical role in Nigeria’s judicial system, exercising appellate jurisdiction over civil, criminal, constitutional, electoral, commercial and labour disputes, among other matters.

Kekere-Ekun also cautioned them against treating appeals as opportunities to rehear cases merely because they might have reached different conclusions from the lower courts.

“An appeal is not an invitation to rehear a case simply because another judicial officer might have reached a different conclusion,” she said.

She urged them to carefully examine records of proceedings, identify properly raised complaints and determine whether the law justified interfering with decisions of lower courts.

The CJN further charged the new justices to embrace continuing judicial education, particularly in emerging areas such as digital commerce, data protection, intellectual property, financial regulation and artificial intelligence.

She noted that although technology could assist judicial research and the organisation of court processes, legal authorities must be verified and judicial decisions must remain products of independent judicial reasoning.

The 12 new justices are Yakubu Abdulhammeed Mohammed, Monisola Oluwatoyin Abodunde, Raphael Ajuwa, Elias Ojie Abua, Mbalamen Jennifer Ijohor, Sabiu Bala Shuaibu, James Kolawole Omotosho, Emeka Nwite, Dauda Njane Buba, Sanusi Kado, Enikuomehin Ademola and Julcit Veronica Dadom.

The justices were drawn from various courts, including the High Courts of Gombe, Bayelsa, Cross River, Benue, Kebbi, Taraba and Ondo states, the Federal High Court, the National Industrial Court of Nigeria and the Customary Courts of Appeal of Ekiti and Plateau states.

The PUNCH recalls that the National Judicial Council had recommended their appointment following its 111th meeting held on May 13, 2026, under the chairmanship of the CJN.

The council said the appointments were intended to fill vacancies arising from the elevation and retirement of judicial officers and strengthen the capacity of the courts for effective justice delivery.

The post CJN swears in new A’Court Justices, urges judicial independence appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

content:
The Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPC Ltd) has confirmed that a fire outbreak at an affiliated filling station along Ekoro-Ajasa Road, in Alimosho Local Government Area of Lagos State, has been contained.

The company said preliminary information indicated that no fatalities or injuries were recorded in the incident, which occurred on Monday, November 16, 2026.

NNPC disclosed this in a statement issued by its Chief Corporate Communications Officer, Andy Odeh, in Abuja.

The company acknowledged the fear and distress caused by the incident among residents, customers and businesses in the area, expressing sympathy with those whose properties or livelihoods might have been affected.

NNPC commended the Lagos State Emergency Management Agency, LASEMA, the Lagos State Fire and Rescue Service and other emergency responders for containing the fire and preventing further damage.

It said its Retail, Health, Safety and Environment teams, alongside the management of the affected filling station, were reviewing the cause of the incident.

The company assured residents that the safety of customers, employees and neighbouring communities remained a priority.

It added that it would support relevant authorities and the management of the affiliated filling station in addressing the incident, promising to provide further updates as verified information became available.

title: Abia records 60% drop in maternal mortality – Commissioner
description:
Abia State has recorded a 60 per cent reduction in maternal mortality between 2024 and 2026, emerging as the state with the second-lowest maternal mortality rate nationwide.
The Commissioner for Information, Okey Kanu, disclosed this on Monday at Government House, Umuahia, while briefing journalists
content:
Abia State has recorded a 60 per cent reduction in maternal mortality between 2024 and 2026, emerging as the state with the second-lowest maternal mortality rate nationwide.

The Commissioner for Information, Okey Kanu, disclosed this on Monday at Government House, Umuahia, while briefing journalists on the outcome of this week’s State Executive Council meeting presided over by Governor Alex Otti.

Kanu, who was represented by the Special Adviser to the Governor on Media and Publicity, Ferdinand Ekeoma, attributed the improvement to ongoing reforms in the health sector.

“Abia State has recorded a 60 per cent reduction in maternal mortality between 2024 and 2026. This reflects our commitment to strengthening healthcare delivery and expanding access to quality medical services for our mothers and children,” he said.

He disclosed that 190 of the 200 Project Ekwueme Primary Healthcare Centres earmarked for renovation had been renovated, while 123 had been functionalised to provide essential healthcare services.

“190 out of the 200 Project Ekwueme Primary Healthcare Centres have been renovated, and 123 have been functionalised to provide essential healthcare services to our people,” he stated.

He added that 27 of the centres had been solarised, with work ongoing on nine others, while all 77 World Bank Impact health projects had been completed.

Kanu further announced that the National Nursing and Midwifery Council, in its accreditation report released on November 13, had increased the admission quota of the Aba Campus of the College of Nursing Sciences from 75 to 120 students.

“The increase in admission capacity reflects growing recognition of the state’s investments and reforms in the health sector, particularly in strengthening healthcare manpower development,” he said.

In another development, Kanu announced that the Rector of Ogbonnaya Onu Polytechnic, Aba, Dr Christopher Okoro, had emerged Administrator of the Year in a nationwide poll conducted by the Leadership Excellence Award.

He said Okoro polled 148,267 votes in the exercise, which recognised his contributions to institutional transformation, human capital development, and technical and professional education.

“Dr Okoro polled 148,267 votes. They cited his contributions to institutional transformation, human capital development, and technical and professional education in Abia State,” he said.

Kanu said the recognition reflected ongoing changes at the institution, citing increased student enrolment of over 6,000, infrastructure improvements and enhanced workers’ welfare as some of the achievements recorded under the rector’s leadership.

He reaffirmed that the Otti administration remained committed to sustaining its development agenda, adding that the education sector continued to receive 20 per cent of the state’s budgetary allocation, with the impact being felt across the education ecosystem.

On public health surveillance, Kanu disclosed that no cases of diseases of public health importance, including Ebola, Lassa fever, COVID-19, diphtheria, cholera, mpox and yellow fever, were reported in Abia during the period under review.

Contributing, the Commissioner for Health, Professor Enoch Ogbonnay-Uche, spoke on the Ebola situation in the country and disclosed that the index case reported on October 20 had been transferred to Switzerland, where the patient subsequently recovered.

“All 62 contacts traced to the index case had completed the mandatory 21-day monitoring period and were cleared as of November 13, according to information from the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control (NCDC),” Professor Uche said.

He urged residents to remain vigilant and maintain good personal hygiene, stressing that sustained public awareness and preventive measures were essential to safeguarding public health.

Professor Uche emphasised the importance of hand hygiene, which he identified as the focus of the state’s public health advisory for the week.

“This week, the health advisory focuses on hand hygiene. Hand hygiene is very important in preventing infection. We want to ensure that in this season, people wash their hands regularly with running water,” he stated.

He explained that hand hygiene remained one of the simplest and most effective ways of preventing infections and reducing the spread of communicable diseases.

The post Abia records 60% drop in maternal mortality – Commissioner appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Nvidia To Reveal First Earnings Since Spy Scandal
description: AI chip giant Nvidia reports its first earnings on Tuesday since a spy scandal forced co-founder Jensen Huang to quit and the United States to tighten export curbs on chips.Investors will closely scrutinize the results for indications that the artificial intelligence boom can withstand the crisis, w
content:
AI chip giant Nvidia reports its first earnings on Tuesday since a spy scandal forced co-founder Jensen Huang to quit and the United States to tighten export curbs on chips.

Investors will closely scrutinize the results for indications that the artificial intelligence boom can withstand the crisis, which highlighted a loophole allegedly exploited by Chinese companies.

Huang, perhaps the tech industry’s most recognized booster of artificial intelligence, stepped down on Thursday following revelations of extramarital affairs, including with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy.

The scandal has battered shares of Nvidia — until recently the world’s most valuable publicly traded company — which is at the centre of an AI buildout that has helped propel markets to record highs and boosted economic growth around the globe.

Nvidia said Tuesday it had created an oversight committee for the company’s national security policies and export control compliance.

That news followed Washington’s announcement Monday of new restrictions on AI chip exports, drawing condemnation from Beijing just before the high-profile APEC summit where US President Donald Trump and his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping are set for talks.

Beijing’s foreign ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun said: “China will take necessary measures to resolutely safeguard its legitimate rights and interests”.

The new US export curbs and the wider Nvidia scandal risk casting a shadow over Trump and Xi’s talks at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) meeting, which starts this week in the Chinese city of Shenzhen.

Under Washington’s new rules, data centers anywhere in the world will need a US license to provide large volumes of computing power from advanced chips to companies headquartered in China, Macau or other countries under US arms embargoes.

The rules also require licenses to ship advanced chips to Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil — countries the US Commerce Department says present a “higher-than-normal risk of diversion” of the chips.

The changes are a response to a loophole that allowed Chinese firms to rent AI computing power from data centers in Southeast Asia and elsewhere that run on US hardware not available for export to China.

While the loophole has been known to authorities, the revelation of Huang’s affair has drawn intense scrutiny to the practice.

His lover Alice Huang, who is not related to the 63-year-old, is a former executive of Megaspeed — a Singapore-based cloud computing firm under US criminal investigation for allegedly helping Chinese companies procure advanced Nvidia AI chips in circumvention of export controls.

The scandal has exposed a rift within the Trump administration, with Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent accusing the Commerce Department of ignoring reports that Megaspeed was shifting Nvidia technology to China.

The US government confirmed on Monday it was investigating Megaspeed, with the Commerce Department launching a probe in 2024 for potential export control violations.

‘Business-as-usual’ unlikely

Tuesday’s third-quarter results, which are scheduled for 5:00 pm ET (2200 GMT), will be the first presented under Nvidia’s chief financial officer, Colette Kress, who is serving as interim CEO.

“If they try to keep a business-as-usual tone in the call, I think that it probably wouldn’t be well received,” said Jacob Bourne of Emarketer.

Investors will be watching for signs of whether Kress will slow Huang’s aggressive investment strategy, which saw him commit tens of billions of dollars to AI companies.

Analysts said they would also be eyeing Nvidia’s guidance on future sales, along with its chip sales in Asia, particularly Singapore.

That could ripple across the AI investments propping up the US economy — with Nvidia backing major labs including Anthropic, the maker of the Claude chatbot, which is expected to begin trading on Wall Street on Thursday.

Tech firms dragged Asian stock markets down again Tuesday as the fallout from the Nvidia crisis rattles trading floors, with the new US moves on chip controls adding to uncertainty.

On Tuesday, Singapore said it was engaging with affected companies and talking to US authorities to ascertain the scope and implementation of the new measures.

The city-state is also “exploring how to facilitate trusted access (to AI chips) for Singapore companies”, a government statement said.

Indonesia said it was reviewing the measure “and seeking industry input on its potential impact on operations and investment, including in the data centre sector”.

AFP

The post Nvidia To Reveal First Earnings Since Spy Scandal appeared first on Channels Television.

title: 2027: US providing real-time intelligence to Nigerian military against terrorists — Musa
description:
By Adegboyega Adeleye



Nigeria’s Minister of Defence, General Christopher Musa, has said the United States is providing real-time intelligence, satellite imagery and training to the Nigerian military to track and target terrorist leaders ahead of the 2027 general elections.



According to Reuters
content:
By Adegboyega Adeleye

Nigeria’s Minister of Defence, General Christopher Musa, has said the United States is providing real-time intelligence, satellite imagery and training to the Nigerian military to track and target terrorist leaders ahead of the 2027 general elections.

According to Reuters, Musa disclosed this on Monday during a briefing with journalists, saying the improved intelligence support had strengthened the military’s ability to identify and strike militant targets.

The minister said Nigerian troops had killed several terrorist and bandit leaders in overnight operations in the Northwest and Northeast, adding that the military was conducting almost daily operations with improved intelligence.

“We took out a lot of the bandit leaders and the terrorists themselves,” Musa said.

He said Nigeria and the United States had continued to expand their security cooperation as the country battles Islamist insurgencies in the North-East, armed banditry in the North-West and kidnapping gangs across the country.

Musa also disclosed that Nigeria was expecting additional military helicopters from the United States and Italy to strengthen its operational capacity.

On preparations for the 2027 general elections, the defence minister said security agencies were intensifying intelligence-led operations to prevent violence before, during and after the polls.

He said authorities were also monitoring the use of Starlink satellite internet services, cryptocurrencies and commercial drones by militant groups, while working with US authorities to disrupt their financing networks.

Musa further disclosed that Nigeria had reached a five-kilometre cross-border right-of-pursuit arrangement with Cameroon, Niger and Chad, allowing troops to pursue terrorists and bandits across border areas.

The arrangement is aimed at restricting the movement of armed groups that exploit porous borders to escape security operations.

The minister also warned that Islamic State Sahel was seeking to recruit criminal gangs in North-West Nigeria, raising concerns that largely profit-driven bandit groups could develop into ideologically driven insurgent organisations similar to the Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP).

According to him, militants and bandits have continued to exploit dense forests and porous borders with Niger and Benin to evade security forces after carrying out attacks.

However, he said improved surveillance had strengthened the military’s ability to track armed groups through difficult terrain and restricted their freedom of movement.

“We don’t want them to develop that capacity,” Musa said.

“We’re blocking the logistics and taking them out from within Nigeria.”

The post 2027: US providing real-time intelligence to Nigerian military against terrorists — Musa appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Obi highlights institutional reforms during Anambra tenure
description:
Former Anambra State Governor and the presidential candidate of Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, Peter Obi, has highlighted the institutional reforms undertaken by his administration, saying rebuilding the machinery of government was essential to achieving sustainable development.







Obi disclo
content:
Former Anambra State Governor and the presidential candidate of Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, Peter Obi, has highlighted the institutional reforms undertaken by his administration, saying rebuilding the machinery of government was essential to achieving sustainable development.

Obi disclosed this on Tuesday in the second instalment of his series, titled Nigerians, Go and Verify, published on his X handle.

In the article, titled Building the Institutions of the State, the former governor explained that his administration prioritised strengthening government institutions under the Anambra Integrated Development Strategy, ANIDS, before embarking on broader development projects.

He said his administration was guided by the principles of character, competence, capacity and compassion, adding that a development vision could not succeed without strong institutions to implement it.

According to him, the physical and administrative structures of governance were in deplorable condition when he assumed office, making it necessary to rebuild institutions across the executive, legislature, judiciary, civil service and local government system.

Restoring the seat of government

Obi said his administration rebuilt, re-equipped and furnished the Government House in Awka after it was vandalised and burnt in 2004.

He added that the Governor’s Lodge in Amawbia was rehabilitated, while a new Governor’s Lodge was constructed in Onitsha to strengthen executive presence and facilitate governance across the state’s major administrative and commercial centres.

Strengthening the legislature and judiciary

The former governor said his administration also rehabilitated the Anambra State House of Assembly Complex in Awka and provided vehicles to lawmakers to facilitate the discharge of their legislative responsibilities.

He said the judiciary was equally strengthened through the provision of brand-new vehicles to High Court judges, which he described as the first of its kind in the state’s history.

Obi also said vehicles were provided to magistrates for the first time since the creation of Anambra State.

He explained that the interventions were aimed at improving mobility, strengthening the administration of justice and enabling judicial officers to perform their duties more effectively.

Rebuilding the civil service

On the civil service, Obi said many Ministries, Departments and Agencies, MDAs, operated from scattered rented apartments before his administration, while civil servants lacked a centralised and decent working environment.

He said the arrangement undermined administrative coordination, efficiency and the dignity of public service.

To address the situation, he said his administration constructed the two-phase Chief Jerome Udoji State Secretariat Complex, comprising Blocks 1 and 2, to bring the MDAs together and provide civil servants with a more conducive working environment.

Obi said the complex was named after Chief Jerome Udoji, the first indigenous Chief Secretary of the Eastern Region during the First Republic, in recognition of his contributions to public administration and the civil service tradition.

He maintained that rebuilding the institutions and structures of government was a necessary foundation for effective service delivery and sustainable development.

title: Tinubu unveils N100m mortgage scheme for Nigerians at 9.75% interest rate
description:
President Bola Tinubu has announced that eligible Nigerians can obtain mortgages of up to ₦100 million at a fixed interest rate of 9.75 per cent, with repayment spread over a period of up to 20 years.
The mortgage facility is being provided through the Federal Government’s ₦1 trillion MOFI Real Esta
content:
President Bola Tinubu has announced that eligible Nigerians can obtain mortgages of up to ₦100 million at a fixed interest rate of 9.75 per cent, with repayment spread over a period of up to 20 years.

The mortgage facility is being provided through the Federal Government’s ₦1 trillion MOFI Real Estate Investment Fund (MREIF), as part of efforts to improve access to affordable housing and enable more Nigerians to own homes instead of relying on rented accommodation.

Tinubu disclosed this in a statement shared on his verified X handle on Tuesday.

According to the President, interested and qualified Nigerians can access the facility by making an initial deposit of 10 per cent of the property’s value.

He explained that the initiative was designed to ease the financial burden of homeownership and make mortgage financing more accessible to Nigerians.

Using a ₦10m house as an example, he said a prospective homeowner would need an initial deposit of ₦1m and could repay approximately ₦85,400 monthly over 20 years.

According to the President, more than 2,300 Nigerians across 27 states have accessed ₦160bn in mortgages through MREIF.

“Imagine paying house rent for 25 years. Your children have grown up, you are approaching retirement, and you are still worried about the next rent increase. This is the reality for many hardworking Nigerians,” he said.

Tinubu said expanding access to affordable, long-term credit was a priority when he introduced his economic reforms in 2023, leading to the establishment of the ₦1tn MREIF.

He also announced that the Federal Mortgage Bank of Nigeria had been strengthened to provide eligible Nigerians with housing loans of up to ₦50m at an interest rate of six per cent, repayable over a maximum period of 30 years.

The President said contributors to the Contributory Pension Scheme could also qualify to use up to 25 per cent of their retirement savings towards their initial mortgage deposit.

He added that married applicants could submit joint applications with their spouses to increase their chances of accessing higher mortgage amounts.

“For Nigerians who cannot afford a mortgage, Family Homes Fund supports the delivery of affordable housing, with more than 53 social homes delivered for vulnerable and underserved households,” he said.

Tinubu also said the Renewed Hope Social Housing Programme was targeting 77,400 affordable homes across the country.

He disclosed that the government had delivered 100 free homes to widows in Kaduna and another 50 to the wives of fallen heroes in Ibadan.

The President further said more than 15,000 homes were under construction nationwide through the Renewed Hope Cities and Estates Programme.

He assured Nigerians that access to the housing initiatives would not depend on political connections or personal relationships with government officials.

“You should not need to know a minister, a governor or anybody in the Presidential Villa to apply and benefit from these opportunities.

“These programmes are for Nigerians who meet the requirements, wherever they live and whatever their beliefs,” he said.

Tinubu said he took particular satisfaction in seeing hardworking Nigerians become homeowners and families enjoy the security of owning their properties.

“That, too, is what my economic reforms are about. From Reforms to Opportunities,” he added.

The MREIF is a Federal Government-backed housing finance initiative designed to provide long-term funding for mortgages through participating financial institutions.

Its mortgage facility offers fixed-rate financing at 9.75 per cent, with a minimum equity contribution of 10 per cent and repayment periods of up to 20 years.

The Federal Mortgage Bank’s National Housing Fund mortgage facility, on the other hand, provides eligible contributors with loans for purchasing, building, improving or renovating residential properties.

Applications are processed through accredited mortgage institutions.

The post Tinubu unveils N100m mortgage scheme for Nigerians at 9.75% interest rate appeared first on Very Nigerian.

title: FG introduces NIN-linked verification system for domestic air passengers
description:
The Federal Government has introduced a biometric passenger verification system linked to the National Identification Number (NIN) for domestic air travel, in a move aimed at strengthening airport security and curbing identity fraud.







The Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus
content:
The Federal Government has introduced a biometric passenger verification system linked to the National Identification Number (NIN) for domestic air travel, in a move aimed at strengthening airport security and curbing identity fraud.

The Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, disclosed this on Tuesday after unveiling the Airport Passenger Verification System, known as V-PASS, at the domestic terminal of the Murtala Muhammed Airport, Lagos.

Keyamo said the system would make it mandatory for passengers on domestic flights to verify their identities using their NIN before boarding.

He explained that the technology was designed to eliminate cases of passengers travelling with fake identities, as well as address touting and ticket racketeering at airports.

According to him, the biometric identity verification system would enhance passenger processing, strengthen airport security and provide a faster and more seamless travel experience.

The minister said the project was executed through a Public-Private Partnership (PPP) arrangement.

He was accompanied at the unveiling by the Managing Director of the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria (FAAN), Mrs Olubunmi Kuku; Director-General of the Infrastructure Concession Regulatory Commission (ICRC), Dr Jobson Oseodion Ewalefoh; and other senior FAAN officials.

Keyamo said he had directed the Nigeria Civil Aviation Authority (NCAA) to give all airlines operating in the country until December 31 to integrate with the system.

He clarified that the verification system was designed exclusively for domestic flights.

title: Drug insecurity threatens national security, PSN warns
description:
By Doris Obinna
The Pharmaceutical Society of Nigeria (PSN) has warned that pharmaceutical insecurity poses a grave threat to national security, urging the Federal Government to retain control of critical aspects of the country’s drug distribution system and strengthen the fight against illicit drug
content:
By Doris Obinna

The Pharmaceutical Society of Nigeria (PSN) has warned that pharmaceutical insecurity poses a grave threat to national security, urging the Federal Government to retain control of critical aspects of the country’s drug distribution system and strengthen the fight against illicit drug activities.

The society proposed a special fund to tackle illicit financial flows in healthcare, recommending that one per cent of assets seized from drug trafficking be dedicated to strengthening the enforcement activities of the Pharmacy Council of Nigeria (PCN) and the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC).

The resolutions were contained in a communiqué signed by the PSN President, Tanko Ayuba, and National Secretary, Gafar Madeh, issued at the end of the Society’s 99th Annual National Conference, tagged IJELE 2026, held from November 2 to 7 at the International Convention Centre, Awka, Anambra State.

The conference, themed, “One Health, One Pharmacy: Bridging Knowledge, Practice and Policy for National Impact,” also called for the integration of over 10,000 community pharmacies into Nigeria’s national security architecture and the proposed NHIA Pharmacy First initiative to strengthen early detection and reporting of suspicious drug activities.

The pharmacists warned that transferring control of public sector drug distribution to private interests could weaken regulatory oversight and undermine collaboration among the PCN, NAFDAC and the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA).

While supporting private sector involvement in financing and technology, the conference insisted that government must retain control of medicine procurement, quality assurance, storage, dispensing and the handling of controlled drugs.

It also urged the Federal Government to support the proposed Drug Revolving Fund and Federal Drug Management Agency Bill, which has passed first reading at the House of Representatives, to establish a central platform for medicine procurement and supply.

The society further called for a review of the Federal Ministry of Health’s Memorandum of Understanding with Medipool, recommending that private operators serve only as competitively selected, non-exclusive price negotiators or framework suppliers in line with the Public Procurement Act.

To drive reforms, the conference proposed an independent presidential committee on the pharmaceutical sector, led by a registered pharmacist recommended by the PSN, with representatives of relevant regulatory and research institutions.

On workers’ welfare, the conference urged organised labour to conclude negotiations on the adjustment of the Consolidated Health Salary Structure (CONHESS), which it said had remained unresolved for about 13 years. It also called for fairness to health workers in ongoing collective bargaining negotiations.

The pharmacists further advocated a specialised humanitarian pharmacy workforce to ensure access to essential medicines and continuity of treatment for displaced populations during emergencies.

The conference also endorsed stronger collaboration between the PSN and the West African Society for Parenteral and Enteral Nutrition (WASPEN), including a standardised framework for integrating advanced pharmacists into multidisciplinary clinical teams.

It approved the speedy construction of the PSN Pharmacy House at Victoria Island and directed its leadership to regularise the society’s property documents and address outstanding debenture subscribers’ entitlements.

The conference also endorsed a one-off support contribution towards the PSN’s centenary celebration in March 2027.

Anambra State Governor, Prof. Chukwuma Charles Soludo, declared the conference open, while the Minister of Humanitarian Affairs and Poverty Reduction, Bernard Doro, delivered the keynote address.

At the conference, Tanko Ayuba emerged as PSN president for the 2026/2027 administrative year.

The post Drug insecurity threatens national security, PSN warns appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Tinubu: Nigerians can access ₦100m mortgages at 9.75%
description:
President Bola Tinubu has said eligible Nigerians can access mortgage loans of up to ₦100 million at a fixed interest rate of 9.75 per cent under the Federal Government’s ₦1 trillion MOFI Real Estate Investment Fund (MREIF).







Tinubu, who disclosed this in a post on his X platform on Tuesday, s
content:
President Bola Tinubu has said eligible Nigerians can access mortgage loans of up to ₦100 million at a fixed interest rate of 9.75 per cent under the Federal Government’s ₦1 trillion MOFI Real Estate Investment Fund (MREIF).

Tinubu, who disclosed this in a post on his X platform on Tuesday, said the initiative was designed to expand access to affordable, long-term housing finance and help more Nigerians become homeowners.

He explained that beneficiaries could repay the loans over a period of up to 20 years, with an initial deposit of 10 per cent.

Illustrating the arrangement, the President said a Nigerian seeking to purchase a house worth ₦10 million would need an initial deposit of ₦1 million and could repay approximately ₦85,400 monthly over 20 years.

According to him, more than 2,300 Nigerians across 27 states have so far accessed ₦160 billion in mortgages through MREIF.

Tinubu said the Federal Government had also strengthened the Federal Mortgage Bank of Nigeria (FMBN), through which eligible Nigerians could access housing loans of up to ₦50 million at six per cent interest, with repayment periods of up to 30 years.

He added that contributors to pension schemes could qualify to use up to 25 per cent of their retirement savings towards the initial deposit, while married applicants could submit joint applications with their spouses to improve their chances of accessing higher loan amounts.

The President also highlighted the role of the Family Homes Fund in providing affordable housing for Nigerians who cannot afford mortgage arrangements.

He said the fund had delivered more than 53 social homes for vulnerable and underserved households.

Tinubu further disclosed that the Renewed Hope Social Housing Programme was targeting 77,400 affordable homes across the country.

According to him, 100 free homes had been delivered to widows in Kaduna, while another 50 were provided to wives of fallen military personnel in Ibadan.

He added that more than 15,000 housing units were under construction nationwide through the Renewed Hope Cities and Estates Programme.

The President stressed that access to the housing initiatives should be based on eligibility rather than political connections or religious affiliation.

“You should not need to know a minister, a governor or anybody in the Presidential Villa to apply and benefit from these opportunities,” he said.

Tinubu maintained that the programmes were open to Nigerians who met the stipulated requirements, irrespective of their location or beliefs.

He said providing opportunities for hardworking Nigerians to own homes and secure their families’ future remained an important objective of his administration’s economic reforms.

Over the years, the December festivities have attracted Niger
content:
Detty December in Lagos, the unofficial festive-season celebration that has become a major entertainment attraction in Nigeria, is gathering momentum as international music stars prepare to headline concerts and festivals across the city.

Over the years, the December festivities have attracted Nigerians in the diaspora, foreign visitors and international celebrities, turning Lagos into a destination for music, nightlife, tourism and entertainment.

While international celebrities were among the visitors who added glamour to last year’s festivities, several foreign artistes are billed to perform at major events in Lagos this year.

Among the international stars announced for the 2026 edition are American singers Brandy, Kehlani and Summer Walker, as well as rappers Lil Baby, Latto, Sexyy Red, A Boogie Wit da Hoodie and Young Thug.

The line-up also includes legendary singer Lauryn Hill, alongside her sons YG Marley and Zion Marley, and Jamaican rapper Wyclef Jean.

Here is a list of some of the international artistes expected to perform in Lagos during Detty December 2026.

Flytime Promotions will host a series of events at the Eko Convention Centre, Victoria Island, from December 20 to 25.

The announced international artistes and their performance dates include:

  • December 20 – Flytime’s House of R&B: Brandy.
  • December 21 – Coca-Cola Rhythm Unplugged: Lil Baby, Kehlani and Yung Miami.
  • December 22 – Flytime Fest: Latto, Sexyy Red and A Boogie Wit da Hoodie.
  • December 23 and 24 – Flytime Fest: More international artistes are expected to be announced.
  • December 25 – Flytime Circle: Further artiste announcements are expected.

Detty December Fest, scheduled to run from December 18 to 30 at Detty December Village, Ilubirin, Lagos, has also announced several international performers.

They include:

  • December 21: Lauryn Hill, YG Marley, Zion Marley and Wyclef Jean.
  • December 27: Summer Walker and Fridayy.
  • December 28: Young Thug

More performers are expected to be announced as organisers unveil additional details of the festival.

With international stars taking up headline slots at major concerts, the 2026 edition further highlights Lagos’ growing appeal as a destination for music and entertainment during the festive season.

title: FG orders airlines to adopt NIN-linked passenger verification system
description:
The Federal Government has directed all airlines operating domestic flights in Nigeria to implement a new biometric passenger verification system known as V-PASS to strengthen airport security and prevent identity fraud.
The Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, announced th
content:
The Federal Government has directed all airlines operating domestic flights in Nigeria to implement a new biometric passenger verification system known as V-PASS to strengthen airport security and prevent identity fraud.

The Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, announced the directive on Monday through a post on his X handle following the unveiling of the technology at the domestic terminal of the Murtala Muhammed Airport in Lagos.

Keyamo explained that the system, officially known as the Airport Passenger Verification System, is linked to the National Identification Number (NIN) of Nigerian passengers.

He added that the technology would be used exclusively for domestic air travel as part of efforts to improve passenger identification, eliminate identity-related fraud and enhance security across the country’s airports.

He said, “The system is a smart system that is linked to the National Identification Number (NIN) of all Nigerians, and it will be mandatory for all passengers to check in with their NIN. It is designed only for domestic flights.”

The minister said the technology would help prevent passengers from boarding flights with fake identities and tackle touting and ticket racketeering.

He added that he had directed the Nigerian Civil Aviation Authority to give all airlines in the country until December 31 to integrate the system into their operations.

Keyamo said, “I have directed the NCAA to give all airlines in the country up till December 31st to key into the system.”

He explained that the biometric verification system was designed to improve passenger processing, strengthen airport security and make air travel faster and safer.

According to him, the project was executed through a Public-Private Partnership arrangement.

The unveiling was attended by the Managing Director of the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria, Olubunmi Kuku; the Director-General of the Infrastructure Concession Regulatory Commission, Jobson Oseodion Ewalefoh; and other senior FAAN officials.

The development follows the Federal Government’s approval of the deployment of the V-PASS system across domestic airports, announced in April 2026.

At the time, Keyamo said the initiative was intended to address inconsistencies in passenger data and prevent unauthorised boarding by ensuring that travellers were properly identified.

He also said the system would extend identity verification measures already in place for international travel to domestic flight operations.

title: 2027 Oyo Governorship poll: Candidates to sign Peace Accord November 19
description:
The Central Council of Ibadan Indigenes (CCII) has fixed November 19 for governorship candidates in Oyo State to sign a peace, non-violence and democratic conduct accord ahead of the 2027 governorship election.
The President-General of the council, Chief Ajeniyi Ajewole, announced this in a statemen
content:
The Central Council of Ibadan Indigenes (CCII) has fixed November 19 for governorship candidates in Oyo State to sign a peace, non-violence and democratic conduct accord ahead of the 2027 governorship election.

The President-General of the council, Chief Ajeniyi Ajewole, announced this in a statement released by the CCII Publicity Secretary, Kola Olomide, in Ibadan on Tuesday.

Ajewole said the signing ceremony would take place at Ibadan House, Oke Aremo, Ibadan, by 10 am on Thursday, November 19.

The initiative is aimed at securing the commitment of governorship candidates to peaceful conduct, non-violence and democratic principles ahead of the forthcoming election.

He said, “Among the candidates expected to participate in the exercise are Senator Sharafadeen Alli of the All Progressives Congress, Bimbo Adekanmbi of the Allied Peoples Movement, Oriyomi Hamzat of the Accord Party, Taofeek Adegoke of the African Democratic Congress, Hazeem Gbolarumi of the Peoples Democratic Party and Saheed Oladele of the African Action Congress.

“The accord is aimed at securing the commitment of governorship candidates to peaceful political engagement, issue-based campaigns and responsible democratic conduct before, during and after the election.”

Ajewole said the council considered the initiative necessary given Ibadanland’s strategic position in the political, economic and demographic landscape of Oyo State.

He noted that Ibadanland accounts for about 50 per cent of the state’s electoral strength, making it a significant constituency in the forthcoming governorship election.

“We believe that political competition should be based on ideas, policies and the capacity to deliver good governance rather than violence and intimidation.

“The initiative is part of the council’s commitment to promoting peaceful coexistence, responsible leadership and the protection of the democratic rights and welfare of residents of Ibadanland and Oyo State,” the President-General stated.

The initiative comes against the backdrop of recurring political violence in Nigeria, including recent clashes among supporters of major political parties in Oyo State.

Ajewole said the incidents underscored the importance of early engagement among political stakeholders to prevent violence, promote tolerance and ensure that political disagreements did not degenerate into confrontations capable of threatening lives and property.

He said the proposed accord would require participating candidates to reject political violence, respect their opponents, discourage hostility among their supporters, and protect lives and property.

The President-General urged all governorship candidates to honour the invitation and demonstrate their commitment to a peaceful electoral process, stressing that political differences should not threaten the unity, security and development of the state.

The statement added that the governorship candidates were also expected to return to Ibadan House on January 6, 2027, for a town hall meeting organised by the council. At the meeting, representatives of more than 250 affiliated organisations would engage the candidates on their demands, desires and expectations.

It said the town hall would provide an opportunity for the candidates to present their programmes and plans for various sectors of the state, while representatives of the affiliated clubs would raise issues affecting their organisations and the people of Ibadanland.

The CCII is the umbrella body for associations, clubs and socio-cultural organisations in Ibadanland, with more than 250 affiliated organisations.

Very Nigerian reports that the Independent National Electoral Commission has listed 16 candidates for the Oyo governorship election scheduled for February 2027.

title: BREAKING: Omotosho, Nwite join Court of Appeal as CJN swears In 12 new Justices
description:
The Chief Justice of Nigeria (CJN), Justice Kudirat Kekere-Ekun, has sworn in 12 new Justices of the Court of Appeal, including two Federal High Court judges who handled several high-profile criminal cases.
The newly elevated judges include Justices James Omotosho and Emeka Nwite, whose appointments
content:
The Chief Justice of Nigeria (CJN), Justice Kudirat Kekere-Ekun, has sworn in 12 new Justices of the Court of Appeal, including two Federal High Court judges who handled several high-profile criminal cases.

The newly elevated judges include Justices James Omotosho and Emeka Nwite, whose appointments were recommended by the National Judicial Council (NJC) at its meeting on May 13.

Justice Omotosho convicted and sentenced the detained leader of the proscribed Indigenous People of Biafra (IPOB), Nnamdi Kanu, to life imprisonment on November 20, 2025, after finding him guilty on a seven-count terrorism-related charge filed by the Federal Government.

Similarly, Justice Nwite handled the N80.2bn fraud case involving former Kogi State Governor, Yahaya Bello.

He also presided over the trial of four members of the Al-Shabaab terrorist group, whom he sentenced to death by hanging on June 3 for their roles in the June 5, 2022 attack on St. Francis Catholic Church in Owo, Ondo State.

The other judges sworn in by the CJN on Tuesday are Justices Yakubu Abdulhammeed Mohammed, Abodunde Monisola Oluwatoyin, Ajuwa Raphael, Abua Elias Ojie, Ijohor Mbalamen Jennifer, Shuaibu Sabiu Bala, Buba Dauda Njane, Kado Sanusi, Ademola Enikuomehin and Dadom Julcit Veronica.

Following their elevation, criminal cases previously handled by the judges, including the trial of former Governor Bello, are expected to be reassigned to other judges and heard afresh, a process known as de novo.

Speaking at the swearing-in ceremony, Kekere-Ekun said the appointments brought together judicial experience from different parts of the country and courts with distinct jurisdictions and responsibilities.

She disclosed that some of the new appellate court justices were selected from Gombe, Bayelsa, Cross River, Benue, Kebbi, Taraba and Ondo, following their service at various High Courts, the National Industrial Court and the Customary Courts of Appeal in Ekiti and Plateau states.

The CJN urged the new justices to understand that their responsibilities at the Court of Appeal would differ from their previous roles, as they would now sit in panels, deliberate collectively and reach decisions through judicial engagement.

She said their duties extended beyond affirming or setting aside decisions of lower courts, stressing that they were expected to promote consistency in the application of the law, clarify legal principles, correct judicial errors and contribute to the development of Nigeria’s jurisprudence.

Kekere-Ekun cautioned them against treating appeals as opportunities to rehear cases simply because they might have reached different conclusions from the judges of lower courts.

She advised them to carefully examine the grounds of appeal, records of proceedings, findings and reasoning of the lower courts before deciding whether there were sufficient legal grounds to intervene.

The CJN also stressed the need for caution when reviewing findings of fact and the evaluation of evidence, particularly in cases where appellate judges did not have the opportunity to observe witnesses.

She urged the new justices to ensure that their judgments were clear, well-reasoned and guided strictly by the law, regardless of public opinion or criticism.

Kekere-Ekun further warned against political, financial, social and personal pressures, including those arising from professional relationships and familiarity.

She charged them to protect their judicial independence and conduct themselves in ways that would leave no reasonable doubt about their impartiality.

“The law must be applied consistently, fairly and without prejudice,” the CJN told the new appellate court justices.

title: Gunmen kill 30-year-old man, injure parents in Jigawa
description:
Gunmen have killed a 30-year-old man and injured his parents during a midnight attack on their residence in Nabai Fulani Settlement, Kargo Ward, Garki Local Government Area of Jigawa State.
The attack occurred at about 3:50 am on Monday, November 16, 2026, when about seven unidentified armed men sto
content:
Gunmen have killed a 30-year-old man and injured his parents during a midnight attack on their residence in Nabai Fulani Settlement, Kargo Ward, Garki Local Government Area of Jigawa State.

The attack occurred at about 3:50 am on Monday, November 16, 2026, when about seven unidentified armed men stormed the home of a 70-year-old man, Yahaya Jibrin.

Confirming the incident in a statement made available to journalists in Dutse, the state capital, on Tuesday, the Public Relations Officer of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps, Jigawa State Command, ASC Badaruddeen Tijjani, said the attackers were suspected to be armed robbers.

He said the assailants invaded Jibrin’s residence and assaulted him and his wife, Zainab Yahaya, aged 45.

According to Tijjani, their son, Lawan Yahaya, aged about 30, was allegedly shot dead when he attempted to rescue his parents.

“Preliminary information revealed that the suspects were armed with AK-47 rifles,” he said.

The NSCDC spokesperson added that the attackers fled with a red Boxer motorcycle without a registration number and an undisclosed sum of money.

He said the two injured victims were immediately taken to Garki General Hospital for medical attention.

Tijjani further disclosed that the Garki Police Division evacuated the deceased’s body to the hospital, where a doctor confirmed him dead.

“The deceased was confirmed dead by a medical doctor,” he said.

The corpse was subsequently released to the family for burial in accordance with Islamic rites.

The NSCDC spokesperson said the Jigawa State Commandant, CC Kabiru Ingawa, condemned the attack and expressed his condolences to the bereaved family.

“The Commandant assured members of the public that the Corps would continue to collaborate with other security agencies to strengthen security, protect lives and property, and ensure that criminal elements are brought to justice,” Tijjani stated.

He added that the commandant urged residents to remain vigilant and promptly report suspicious movements or activities to the nearest security formation.

Tijjani also urged residents to provide credible information that could assist in identifying and apprehending the fleeing suspects.

He reassured residents of the command’s commitment to safeguarding lives and property across the state.

title: FULL LIST: World Cup-winning Flamingos coach Busari nominated for CAF award
description:
Nigeria’s U-17 women’s national team coach, Akeem Busari, has been nominated for the 2026 Confederation of African Football Women’s Coach of the Year award.
Busari’s nomination follows his achievement with the Flamingos, who won the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup for the first time after beating Japan
content:
Nigeria’s U-17 women’s national team coach, Akeem Busari, has been nominated for the 2026 Confederation of African Football Women’s Coach of the Year award.

Busari’s nomination follows his achievement with the Flamingos, who won the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup for the first time after beating Japan 2-1 in the final in Rabat, Morocco, on November 7.

The Nigeria coach is among 10 nominees announced by CAF on Tuesday in its final list of nominees for the women’s categories ahead of the 2026 CAF Awards.

Other nominees include Farid Benstiti of Algeria, Silveria Nedio of Cabo Verde, Valentine Nguele of Cameroon, Kim Lars Bjorkegren of Ghana, Lovemore Fazili of Malawi, Hicham Drissi of AS FAR, Jorge Vilda of Morocco, Desiree Ellis of South Africa and Bakari Nyundo Shime of Tanzania.

CAF said the final three women’s categories were announced after the conclusion of the CAF Women’s Champions League in Egypt on Sunday, November 15.

“The three categories were held back to ensure that performances at Africa’s premier women’s club competition could be considered before the nominees were finalised,” the continental football governing body said.

The other two categories are Women’s Interclub Player of the Year and Women’s Club of the Year.

The ceremony will hold at the Professor Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture and the Arts, popularly known as the National Theatre, in Lagos on Wednesday, December 2, beginning at 7pm local time.

Voting for the awards is taking place from November 5 to 20, with CAF member associations, clubs and eligible coaches and captains participating in the process.
