title: $4.5m car theft: Canadian police arrest eight Nigerians, four others
description:
By Matthew Johnson



Peel Regional Police, Canada, has arrested eight Nigerians among 12 suspects following the dismantling of a transnational auto theft syndicate allegedly shipping stolen luxury vehicles to West Africa.



The suspects, who are facing a combined 231 criminal charges, were nabbed
content:
By Matthew Johnson

Peel Regional Police, Canada, has arrested eight Nigerians among 12 suspects following the dismantling of a transnational auto theft syndicate allegedly shipping stolen luxury vehicles to West Africa.

The suspects, who are facing a combined 231 criminal charges, were nabbed after detectives with the Commercial Auto Crime Bureau recovered 96 stolen high-value vehicles, predominantly luxury sport utility vehicles, SUVs, and pickup trucks valued at approximately $4.5 million.

In a video posted on its official X (formerly Twitter) handle on Tuesday, November 17, 2026, the Peel Regional Police disclosed that the investigation, code-named Project Cadetta, was launched in March 2026 in collaboration with the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA).

According to the police, the operation initially focused on a warehouse in Brampton, Ontario, which served as a primary staging facility where stolen vehicles with altered Vehicle Identification Numbers (re-VINed) were concealed inside shipping containers destined for West African markets through Canadian ports.

Further investigations uncovered a broader criminal network operating across the Greater Toronto Area (GTA) and surrounding jurisdictions.

Police alleged that the syndicate was spearheaded by five principal suspects—all bearing Nigerian names who coordinated the theft, movement, and overseas export of the vehicles. They were identified as Odewale Abraham (57), Tosin Oyebade (45), Oluyemi Sodade (51), and Oluwaseyi Bameke (39), all of Toronto, alongside Stanley Udeh (46) of Brampton.

Seven other suspects accused of facilitating the racket through transportation, container movements, and managing loading sites were identified as Gbolahan Babatunde (29) of Vaughan; Olushola Oke (42) of Toronto; Kenneth Okafor (58) of no fixed address; Karamveer Singh (26) of Brampton; Darryl Davance (25) of Saint Jerome, Quebec; Henrik Gancz (57) of no fixed address; and Jaspreet Singh (25) of no fixed address.

Following a series of coordinated search warrants and arrests, nine of the accused were charged and released with future court dates, while three were held for bail hearings and subsequently granted release.

Canadian authorities disclosed that some of the charged suspects may be referred to the CBSA for immigration enforcement action, including possible deportation from Canada, upon the conclusion of their criminal trials.

Meanwhile, arrest warrants have been issued for two additional suspects still at large: 32-year-old Steven Gyamfi and a 16-year-old minor from Hamilton whose identity is protected under Canada’s Youth Criminal Justice Act.

Commenting on the breakthrough, Deputy Chief of Peel Regional Police, Nick Milinovich, vowed that the force would sustain its clampdown on organised crime syndicates.

“Organised auto theft is a predatory business model run by transnational syndicates that terrorise families and fund broader criminal enterprises. Through Project Cadetta, our Commercial Auto Crime Bureau and partners dismantled this supply chain from street-level thieves to international export brokers. We have already driven auto thefts in Peel down by more than 50 per cent since our 2023 peak, and we are not taking our foot off the gas—there is no safe harbour in Peel for organised crime,” Milinovich stated.

Also reacting, the Solicitor General of Ontario, Michael Kerzner, commended the law enforcement agencies for the operation, noting that government investments were yielding results.

“Organised auto theft is a serious crime that threatens the safety and security of our communities, and our government will never back down from taking on the criminal networks responsible. Project Cadetta is another example of the outstanding work being done by Peel Regional Police and their law enforcement partners to dismantle these sophisticated operations and hold offenders accountable. Through investments like our Preventing Auto Theft Grant, we are ensuring police have the tools and resources they need to disrupt organised crime, recover stolen vehicles and protect Ontario families,” he said.

On her part, the Acting Regional Director General for the Greater Toronto Area Region at the CBSA, Trishann Pascal, highlighted the importance of intelligence sharing in curbing cross-border vehicle smuggling.

“CBSA officers play a critical role in stopping stolen vehicles from reaching international markets through targeted container examinations and referrals. The CBSA is helping to disrupt organised crime networks by combining intelligence, expertise and coordinated action with law enforcement partners. This investigation demonstrates the impact of that partnership,” Pascal added.

As of when the post was made, police said that investigations remain ongoing, with further charges anticipated against the accused.

title: Singapore In Damage Control After Nvidia Scandal Exposes China Loophole
description: Singapore is working to maintain its reputation as a trusted business hub, tainted by allegations that Chinese companies had exploited it to gain access to top-end AI chips despite US export restrictions.A widening scandal sparked by an affair between Jensen Huang, until recently head of US chip tit
content:
Singapore is working to maintain its reputation as a trusted business hub, tainted by allegations that Chinese companies had exploited it to gain access to top-end AI chips despite US export restrictions.

A widening scandal sparked by an affair between Jensen Huang, until recently head of US chip titan Nvidia, and a suspected Chinese spy has spotlighted the city-state’s position as a global crossroads for the advanced semiconductors that power artificial intelligence.

The United States on Monday moved to close a loophole in its controls — which it says protect national security — on the export of powerful AI chips to China.

The new US rules crack down on illicit chip smuggling, but also the large grey market of Chinese companies renting computing power from data centres full of advanced Nvidia chips in third countries, often in Southeast Asia.

It follows explosive reports of Huang’s affair with Alice Huang, a former executive at the Singapore-based cloud computing company Megaspeed International, which Washington is investigating for the alleged transfer of Nvidia chips to China in circumvention of US rules.

The scandal “is obviously not a good look for Singapore”, Chong Ja Ian, a political scientist with the National University of Singapore, told AFP.

Singapore is also probing what Megaspeed was up to, but Chong said the city-state must strengthen regulatory oversight to avoid the perception of “systemic issues”.

The Nvidia case may make it harder “to maintain the reputation of being a clean business hub by simply dealing with individual cases, rather than putting more stringent regulations and laws in place”, he said.

Some US officials also reportedly believe that Alice Huang, no relation to the leather jacket-clad Jensen, was spying for Beijing.

Caught in crossfire?

Singapore said it was carefully studying the new US measures, which require data centres worldwide to hold a US licence to provide a large volume of computing power from advanced chips to companies headquartered in China, or other places under US arms embargoes.

A US licence will also be needed to ship advanced chips to Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil — countries the US Commerce Department says present a “higher-than-normal risk of diversion” of the sensitive components.

“We take our international reputation seriously,” the Singaporean government said.

The city-state does not “condone companies using their association with Singapore to circumvent or violate the laws of other countries in their international business activities, including export controls”, it said.

Some analysts said Singapore was grappling with factors largely beyond its control, caught in the crossfire of US-China tech rivalry.

Nvidia controls an estimated 90 percent of the market for chips used to train and run AI models, and Washington began restricting their sales to China four years ago.

“The responsibility for such export controls should primarily rest with the government issuing” them, “rather than outsourcing enforcement of laws to other jurisdictions”, said Rajiv Biswas, chief of the risk consultancy Asia-Pacific Economics in Singapore.

“Singapore has already been taking strong enforcement measures in a number of previous cases where companies have used Singapore as a transhipment point for restricted high-tech AI chips.”

‘Open-door policy’

Megaspeed — which before 2023 operated under a different name as an arm of a Chinese video game developer — reportedly traded in upwards of $4 billion worth of Nvidia chips over just two years.

A financial trail weaving through Singapore, Malaysia and the Cayman Islands suggests Megaspeed’s business may have been boosted by a connection to Chinese tech giant Alibaba.

Singapore has positioned itself as a “critical node” in the global semiconductor supply chain — attracting more than $23 billion in investments between 2022-25.

The city accounted for “one in 10 chips and one in five semiconductor equipment units worldwide”, its economic development board says.

Singapore is seeking to attract further investment from tech giants, but its vulnerabilities to global business flashpoints have been underscored as a small, open economy.

Lian Jye Su, chief analyst at tech research firm Omdia, described the Megaspeed scandal as an “isolated controversy” borne of various factors, including a recent change of guard in the United States following midterm elections.

Singapore “will continue to be exposed to controversies like this due to its open-door policy when it comes to trade and commerce”, he told AFP.

“I believe the government will do whatever it can to exert more regulatory oversight.”

AFP

title: Tinubu offers Nigerians ₦100m housing loans at 9.75% interest
description:
President Bola Tinubu has announced that eligible Nigerians can access mortgages of up to ₦100m at a fixed interest rate of 9.75 per cent, with a repayment period of up to 20 years, under the Federal Government’s housing finance initiative.
The President said the facility, provided through the ₦1tn
content:
President Bola Tinubu has announced that eligible Nigerians can access mortgages of up to ₦100m at a fixed interest rate of 9.75 per cent, with a repayment period of up to 20 years, under the Federal Government’s housing finance initiative.

The President said the facility, provided through the ₦1tn MOFI Real Estate Investment Fund (MREIF), was part of his administration’s efforts to expand access to affordable housing and help Nigerians move from renting to homeownership.

Tinubu disclosed this in a statement on his verified X handle on Tuesday, explaining that beneficiaries could secure mortgages with an initial deposit of 10 per cent of the property’s value.

Using a ₦10m house as an example, he said a prospective homeowner would need an initial deposit of ₦1m and could repay approximately ₦85,400 monthly over 20 years.

According to the President, more than 2,300 Nigerians across 27 states have accessed ₦160bn in mortgages through MREIF.

“Imagine paying house rent for 25 years. Your children have grown up, you are approaching retirement, and you are still worried about the next rent increase. This is the reality for many hardworking Nigerians,” he said.

Tinubu said expanding access to affordable, long-term credit was a priority when he introduced his economic reforms in 2023, leading to the establishment of the ₦1tn MREIF.

He also announced that the Federal Mortgage Bank of Nigeria had been strengthened to provide eligible Nigerians with housing loans of up to ₦50m at an interest rate of six per cent, repayable over a maximum period of 30 years.

The President said contributors to the Contributory Pension Scheme could also qualify to use up to 25 per cent of their retirement savings towards their initial mortgage deposit.

He added that married applicants could submit joint applications with their spouses to increase their chances of accessing higher mortgage amounts.

“For Nigerians who cannot afford a mortgage, Family Homes Fund supports the delivery of affordable housing, with more than 53 social homes delivered for vulnerable and underserved households,” he said.

Tinubu also said the Renewed Hope Social Housing Programme was targeting 77,400 affordable homes across the country.

He disclosed that the government had delivered 100 free homes to widows in Kaduna and another 50 to the wives of fallen heroes in Ibadan.

The President further said more than 15,000 homes were under construction nationwide through the Renewed Hope Cities and Estates Programme.

He assured Nigerians that access to the housing initiatives would not depend on political connections or personal relationships with government officials.

“You should not need to know a minister, a governor or anybody in the Presidential Villa to apply and benefit from these opportunities.

“These programmes are for Nigerians who meet the requirements, wherever they live and whatever their beliefs,” he said.

Tinubu said he took particular satisfaction in seeing hardworking Nigerians become homeowners and families enjoy the security of owning their properties.

“That, too, is what my economic reforms are about. From Reforms to Opportunities,” he added.

The MREIF is a Federal Government-backed housing finance initiative designed to provide long-term funding for mortgages through participating financial institutions.

Its mortgage facility offers fixed-rate financing at 9.75 per cent, with a minimum equity contribution of 10 per cent and repayment periods of up to 20 years.

The Federal Mortgage Bank’s National Housing Fund mortgage facility, on the other hand, provides eligible contributors with loans for purchasing, building, improving or renovating residential properties.

Applications are processed through accredited mortgage institutions.

The post Tinubu offers Nigerians ₦100m housing loans at 9.75% interest appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Abia Govt Dissolves Enyimba FC Management, Technical Crew Over Poor Management
description: The Abia State Government has announced the immediate dissolution of the management structure and technical crew of Enyimba International Football Club. The development was revealed in a statement signed by the Commissioner for Information, Prince Okey Kanu, and made available to Channels Television
content:
The Abia State Government has announced the immediate dissolution of the management structure and technical crew of Enyimba International Football Club.

The development was revealed in a statement signed by the Commissioner for Information, Prince Okey Kanu, and made available to Channels Television by the Ministry of Sports and Youth Development on Tuesday.

According to the government, the move is to address the club’s recent disappointing performances and identify administrative and structural challenges.

The Sports Ministry has been mandated to oversee the restructuring process, including a review of the club’s management framework and the implementation of administrative, technical, and operational reforms.

“The decision underscores the government’s resolve to undertake a comprehensive restructuring of the two-time CAF Champions League winners, restore the club’s competitive identity and reposition it for sustainable success in Nigerian and continental football.

“Following a review of the club’s current state of affairs, the government says far-reaching interventions have become necessary to address the underlying issues affecting its performance, administration and overall operations.

“Consequently, the Ministry of Sports and Youth Development has been mandated to lead the restructuring process, assess the club’s management framework and implement appropriate administrative, technical and operational reforms.

“All affected management and technical personnel, as well as individuals in possession of the club’s assets, official documents and equipment, have been directed to ensure a formal handover to the Ministry.

“The government says the intervention is aimed at safeguarding Enyimba’s historic legacy, strengthening its institutional capacity and restoring the pride and competitive standards associated with the club.”

Enyimba, a two-time CAF Champions League winner, is currently chaired by former Super Eagles Captain Nwankwo Kanu.

The government said the club’s restructuring begins immediately.

title: 2027: Oyo gov candidates to sign peace pact Thursday
description:
The Central Council of Ibadan Indigenes has scheduled the signing of a peace, non-violence and democratic conduct accord by governorship candidates in Oyo State ahead of the 2027 governorship election.
The CCII President-General, Chief Ajeniyi Ajewole, disclosed this in a statement issued by the cou
content:
The Central Council of Ibadan Indigenes has scheduled the signing of a peace, non-violence and democratic conduct accord by governorship candidates in Oyo State ahead of the 2027 governorship election.

The CCII President-General, Chief Ajeniyi Ajewole, disclosed this in a statement issued by the council’s Publicity Secretary, Kola Olomide, in Ibadan on Tuesday.

According to Ajewole, the event will be held at Ibadan House, Oke Aremo, Ibadan, on Thursday, November 19, at 10 am.

He said, “Among the candidates expected to participate in the exercise are Senator Sharafadeen Alli of the All Progressives Congress, Bimbo Adekanmbi of the Allied Peoples Movement, Oriyomi Hamzat of the Accord Party, Taofeek Adegoke of the African Democratic Congress, Hazeem Gbolarumi of the Peoples Democratic Party and Saheed Oladele of the African Action Congress.

“The accord is aimed at securing the commitment of governorship candidates to peaceful political engagement, issue-based campaigns and responsible democratic conduct before, during and after the election.”

Ajewole said the council considered the initiative necessary given Ibadanland’s strategic position in the political, economic and demographic landscape of Oyo State.

He noted that Ibadanland accounts for about 50 per cent of the state’s electoral strength, making it a significant constituency in the forthcoming governorship election.

“We believe that political competition should be based on ideas, policies and the capacity to deliver good governance rather than violence and intimidation.

“The initiative is part of the council’s commitment to promoting peaceful coexistence, responsible leadership and the protection of the democratic rights and welfare of residents of Ibadanland and Oyo State,” the President-General stated.

The initiative comes against the backdrop of recurring political violence in Nigeria, including recent clashes among supporters of major political parties in Oyo State.

Ajewole said the incidents underscored the importance of early engagement among political stakeholders to prevent violence, promote tolerance and ensure that political disagreements did not degenerate into confrontations capable of threatening lives and property.

He said the proposed accord would require participating candidates to reject political violence, respect their opponents, discourage hostility among their supporters, and protect lives and property.

The President-General urged all governorship candidates to honour the invitation and demonstrate their commitment to a peaceful electoral process, stressing that political differences should not threaten the unity, security and development of the state.

The statement added that the governorship candidates were also expected to return to Ibadan House on January 6, 2027, for a town hall meeting organised by the council. At the meeting, representatives of more than 250 affiliated organisations would engage the candidates on their demands, desires and expectations.

It said the town hall would provide an opportunity for the candidates to present their programmes and plans for various sectors of the state, while representatives of the affiliated clubs would raise issues affecting their organisations and the people of Ibadanland.

The CCII is the umbrella body for associations, clubs and socio-cultural organisations in Ibadanland, with more than 250 affiliated organisations.

The PUNCH reports that the Independent National Electoral Commission has listed 16 candidates for the Oyo governorship election scheduled for February 2027.

The post 2027: Oyo gov candidates to sign peace pact Thursday appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: FG orders compulsory NIN verification for domestic flights
description:
The Federal Government has directed airlines operating domestic flights to adopt V-PASS, a passenger biometric verification system linked to the National Identification Number, and aimed at eliminating identity fraud and improving security across Nigeria’s airports.
The Minister of Aviation and Aero
content:
The Federal Government has directed airlines operating domestic flights to adopt V-PASS, a passenger biometric verification system linked to the National Identification Number, and aimed at eliminating identity fraud and improving security across Nigeria’s airports.

The Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, disclosed this on Monday in a post on his X handle, following the unveiling of the system at the domestic terminal of the Murtala Muhammed Airport, Lagos.

Keyamo said the system, known as the Airport Passenger Verification System, was linked to the National Identification Number of Nigerians and would be used exclusively for domestic flights.

He said, “The system is a smart system that is linked to the National Identification Number (NIN) of all Nigerians, and it will be mandatory for all passengers to check in with their NIN. It is designed only for domestic flights.”

The minister said the technology would help prevent passengers from boarding flights with fake identities and tackle touting and ticket racketeering.

He added that he had directed the Nigerian Civil Aviation Authority to give all airlines in the country until December 31 to integrate the system into their operations.

Keyamo said, “I have directed the NCAA to give all airlines in the country up till December 31st to key into the system.”

He explained that the biometric verification system was designed to improve passenger processing, strengthen airport security and make air travel faster and safer.

According to him, the project was executed through a Public-Private Partnership arrangement.

The unveiling was attended by the Managing Director of the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria, Olubunmi Kuku; the Director-General of the Infrastructure Concession Regulatory Commission, Jobson Oseodion Ewalefoh; and other senior FAAN officials.

The development follows the Federal Government’s approval of the deployment of the V-PASS system across domestic airports, announced in April 2026.

At the time, Keyamo said the initiative was intended to address inconsistencies in passenger data and prevent unauthorised boarding by ensuring that travellers were properly identified.

He also said the system would extend identity verification measures already in place for international travel to domestic flight operations.

title: He is a true leader, He succeeded where others failed – US Congressmen praise Peter Obi in Washington
description:
Some United States congressmen have praised the leadership style of Peter Obi, describing the former Anambra State governor as a leader who prioritises public interest over personal considerations.
The lawmakers made the remarks during Obi’s visit to Washington, D.C., where he held engagements with
content:
Some United States congressmen have praised the leadership style of Peter Obi, describing the former Anambra State governor as a leader who prioritises public interest over personal considerations.

The lawmakers made the remarks during Obi’s visit to Washington, D.C., where he held engagements with American political figures and congressional leaders.

Speaking about his record in office as governor of Anambra State, the US lawmakers reportedly commended his approach to governance, particularly his direct communication with the people and what they described as his commitment to public service.

“Peter Obi is a true leader. He succeeded where others have failed. When he was governor, he spoke directly to the people. He is a man who puts public interest first before even considering his personal interests,” the lawmakers were quoted as saying.

The comments have drawn attention to Obi’s record as Anambra governor and his ongoing engagements in the United States.

Obi, the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) for the 2027 election, has continued to advocate free, fair and credible elections in Nigeria, making electoral integrity a central message of his Washington visit.

The reported commendation comes as he engages international stakeholders on Nigeria’s democratic process and the need to strengthen public confidence in the country’s electoral system.

title: Reno Omokri mourns Vanguard Online Editor, Femi Ajasa
description:
Former presidential aide and Nigeria’s Ambassador to Mexico, Guatemala, Honduras and Nicaragua, Bemigho Reno Omokri, has mourned the passing of Vanguard Newspapers’ Online Editor, Mr Femi Ajasa, describing his death as a loss to Nigerian journalism.







Omokri, in a condolence message posted on h
content:
Former presidential aide and Nigeria’s Ambassador to Mexico, Guatemala, Honduras and Nicaragua, Bemigho Reno Omokri, has mourned the passing of Vanguard Newspapers’ Online Editor, Mr Femi Ajasa, describing his death as a loss to Nigerian journalism.

Omokri, in a condolence message posted on his Facebook page on Tuesday, said Ajasa embodied the Omoluabi principle and demonstrated professionalism, ethical conduct and commitment to excellence in journalism.

He said he had known the late journalist personally, recalling that Ajasa extended a hand of fellowship to him during his lifetime.

“On behalf of my family and I, please accept my condolences on the death of your staff member, Online Editor Femi Ajasa.

“I knew Mr Ajasa, and he truly embodied the Omoluabi principle. He extended his right hand of fellowship to me in his lifetime, and it is a sad day for Nigerian journalism that he is no more,” he said.

The ambassador described Ajasa as a model of high-level reporting, drawing a comparison between his journalistic standards and those of Vanguard’s founder, Mr Sam Amuka.

He also credited Ajasa’s dedication to journalism and pursuit of excellence with contributing to Vanguard’s prominence in online publishing.

According to him, the late editor’s professional ethics and insight had created a vacuum that would be difficult to fill.

“The vacuum that Mr Ajasa’s passing has created will be difficult to fill because of the ethics and insight he brought to his job,” Omokri said.

He prayed for the repose of Ajasa’s soul and asked that his memory remain blessed. “May his soul rest in peace and his memory be forever blessed,” he added.

title: 2027: APC zones Bayelsa West Senate seat to Ekeremor
description:
…Reserves Reps seat for Sagbama, insists on rotation



By Samuel Oyadongha, Yenagoa



YENAGOA — Critical stakeholders of the All Progressives Congress, APC, in Bayelsa West Senatorial District have reaffirmed their commitment to the existing power-sharing arrangement between Sagbama and Ekeremor L
content:
…Reserves Reps seat for Sagbama, insists on rotation

By Samuel Oyadongha, Yenagoa

YENAGOA — Critical stakeholders of the All Progressives Congress, APC, in Bayelsa West Senatorial District have reaffirmed their commitment to the existing power-sharing arrangement between Sagbama and Ekeremor Local Government Areas, insisting that Ekeremor should produce the next senator while Sagbama takes the House of Representatives seat.

The stakeholders also resolved to mobilise support for all APC candidates, from President Bola Tinubu to the State House of Assembly, ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The resolutions were reached at the APC Bayelsa West stakeholders’ meeting in Yenagoa, where party leaders reiterated their commitment to the rotation arrangement, which they said was designed to promote fairness, unity and political balance between the two local government areas.

Speaking at the meeting, the Deputy Governor, Dr Peter Akpe, urged party members to unite, reconcile their differences and intensify grassroots mobilisation ahead of the elections.

Akpe, who is from the senatorial district, restated Governor Douye Diri’s charge to APC members to work towards an overwhelming victory in 2027, stressing that the party should aim to secure more than 75 per cent of the votes in every polling unit.

He also urged the party’s candidates to extend a hand of fellowship to members who did not support them during the primaries, saying the election presented an opportunity to rebuild relationships within the party.

“I think we have passed the stage of saying this man or woman should not have been the candidate. We have moved past that time.

“They might not have been the best among us, but know that in the business of selection, there is always the God factor. At this point, we all have to sink our differences and work for the success of our party,” he said.

Akpe urged members to regard the election as a collective responsibility, noting that voters would identify the party by its name and symbol on the ballot.

He particularly appealed to the candidates to reach out to aggrieved members rather than wait for them to initiate reconciliation.

“To the candidates, you really have to extend your arm of fellowship. Don’t say this person supported me and that person did not. Reach out to everybody and don’t wait for the other person to do it. You are the one to do it,” he admonished.

The Deputy Governor also cautioned members against undermining party leaders, stressing that electoral success required cooperation and collective effort.

Also speaking, the Minister of State for Petroleum Resources (Oil), Senator Heineken Lokpobiri, challenged APC leaders in the district to work towards delivering all the votes for Tinubu and other party candidates in 2027.

Lokpobiri attributed the district’s past political successes to unity, describing Sagbama and Ekeremor as closely connected communities capable of achieving more through cooperation.

He warned against members secretly supporting opposition parties while publicly professing allegiance to the APC, urging party leaders to translate their political influence into votes.

“If all of us here are committed to delivering APC 100 per cent, from President Tinubu to the House of Representatives candidates and the senatorial candidate, it is something that we can easily do,” he said.

The minister recalled that in 2015, he had stepped aside from seeking a third term in the Senate following an agreement aimed at ensuring equal representation between the two local government areas.

He said the arrangement was maintained in 2023 when some APC members supported Senator Seriake Dickson’s re-election in the interest of political understanding.

Lokpobiri, however, alleged that the existing agreement was now being threatened.

In his remarks, Hon. Fyneman Wilson urged politicians from the district to honour the subsisting political arrangement in the interest of fairness and unity, insisting that Ekeremor should be allowed to produce the senator.

Speaking on behalf of the candidates, the APC senatorial candidate, Chief Fidelis Agbiki, expressed appreciation to Governor Diri, Akpe, Lokpobiri and other stakeholders for their support in securing their respective candidacies.

Stakeholders at the meeting included former Deputy Governor and Deputy Director-General of the State Presidential Campaign Council, Chief Peremobowei Ebebi; Deputy Speaker of the Bayelsa State House of Assembly, Rt. Hon. Michael Ogbere; Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of the Niger Delta River Basin Development Authority, Prince Ebitimi Amgbare; and the Governor’s Special Adviser on Political Matters, High Chief Collins Cocodia.

Others included former Secretary to the State Government, Ambassador Felix Oboro; APC State Secretary, Mr Japan Udoji; APC Senatorial Vice Chairman, Akwakwa B. Akwakwa; Bayelsa representative in the Niger Delta Development Commission, Denyabofa Dimaro; former Speaker of the State House of Assembly, Rt. Hon. Boyelayefa Debekeme; Comrade Felix Odubo; Chief Fedude Zimughan, SAN; and Chief Kemi Prefa.

Also present were the Acting Chairman of Sagbama Local Government Area, Mrs Diepriye Yankee-Robbinson; APC State Women Leader, Mrs Rose Itoko-Amadi; Managing Director of the Bayelsa Transport Company, Hon. Emomotimi Fanama; and Dr Ayakeme Whisky, among other political figures.

The post 2027: APC zones Bayelsa West Senate seat to Ekeremor appeared first on Vanguard News.

By Olasunkanmi Akoni

LAGOS — Operatives of the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency, NDLEA, have dismantled a suspected transnational cocaine trafficking syndicate allegedly operating a smuggling route from Lagos through northern Nigeria and across the Sahara Desert into Europe, arresting eight suspected drug couriers in coordinated operations in Lagos and Kano.

The suspects were arrested between October 30 and 31, 2026, following intelligence-led operations, while a combined total of 634 wraps of cocaine weighing 13.795 kilogrammes were recovered after they excreted the drugs in custody.

NDLEA Chairman, Brig. Gen. Mohamed Buba Marwa (retd.), on Tuesday commended operatives of the agency’s commands for their collaboration and professionalism, saying their coordination prevented the suspects from escaping between Lagos and Kano.

“This cartel thought it had found a back door to Europe through our northern borders and the Sahara. Their arrests are a message to drug barons and their couriers that there is no safe route out of Nigeria. Whether they go by air, by road, or through the desert, we will trace them, find them, and bring them to justice,” Marwa said.

He cautioned young Nigerians against serving as drug couriers, warning that ingesting narcotics could have fatal consequences.

“Swallowing wraps of cocaine is a death wish. One burst pellet can kill a mule before the journey ends. No amount of money is worth that risk,” he added.

The agency’s Director of Media and Advocacy, Femi Babafemi, said the operation began on October 30 when operatives of the Special Operations Unit arrested a 57-year-old suspect, Okwudiba Ifeanyichukwu Damian, at a hotel in the Ago Palace area of Okota, Lagos.

Babafemi said Damian subsequently excreted 74 wraps of cocaine weighing 1.650 kilogrammes under observation.

He disclosed that on October 31, operatives intercepted four other suspects at the domestic terminal of the Murtala Muhammed Airport, MM2, Lagos, as they prepared to board a flight to Kano.

The suspects were identified as Jackson Ahamefule, 43, who excreted 90 wraps weighing 1.950kg; Nwafor Osita Emmanuel, 47, with 85 wraps weighing 1.750kg; Marcel Nnabuike, 38, with 75 wraps weighing 1.655kg; and Onyenwuba Ignatius, 44, with 75 wraps weighing 1.650kg.

According to Babafemi, the five suspects arrested in Lagos excreted a combined 399 wraps of cocaine weighing 8.655 kilogrammes.

He said intelligence gathered from the arrests indicated that an advance team of the syndicate had already travelled to Kano.

NDLEA operatives stationed at the Mallam Aminu Kano International Airport, MAKIA, subsequently intercepted three other suspects at the arrival hall of the domestic terminal.

The suspects, identified as Chinweike Ephraim Ifechukwu, 48; Edezuno John Nwaorji, 45; and Chukwudi Chinaka, 31, reportedly tested positive for ingested substances during body scans and were placed under observation.

Babafemi said Ifechukwu excreted 85 pellets weighing 1.853kg; Nwaorji excreted 80 pellets weighing 1.752kg; while Chinaka expelled 70 pellets weighing 1.535kg.

During interrogation, the suspects allegedly confessed that they planned to travel by road from Kano across the border into Niger Republic, transit through Libya and eventually smuggle the cocaine into Europe.

title: I was glad Portugal lost to Denmark — Ronaldo’s mother
description:
Cristiano Ronaldo’s mother, has revealed that she was glad Portugal suffered a heavy defeat against Denmark following her son’s international retirement.
Portugal were beaten 4-1 by Denmark in their first match since Ronaldo announced his retirement from international football on November 5.
Ronaldo
content:
Cristiano Ronaldo’s mother, has revealed that she was glad Portugal suffered a heavy defeat against Denmark following her son’s international retirement.

Portugal were beaten 4-1 by Denmark in their first match since Ronaldo announced his retirement from international football on November 5.

Ronaldo, 41, brought an end to his international career after representing Portugal for several years, making 234 appearances and scoring 146 goals.

His retirement came less than a month after he was handed a 30-day suspension and fined £215 for walking out of the Portugal camp in September after learning that he would not start their Nations League encounter against Denmark.

As reported by BBC Sport, speaking at a Sporting event on Monday, Aveiro was asked about her son’s decision to retire from international football.

She admitted that Ronaldo was unhappy with the situation and claimed that he had been deceived.

“Of course he was sad. They deceived him. And I’m sad, too,” she said.

Reacting to Portugal’s 4-1 defeat against Denmark, she added: “The defeat was well-deserved. I was actually glad.”

Meanwhile, Portugal coach Jorge Jesus was asked about Aveiro’s comments ahead of Portugal’s Nations League clash against Wales in Cardiff on Tuesday.

The Portuguese manager appeared surprised that he was expected to respond to comments made by Ronaldo’s mother.

“Now I have to respond to Cristiano Ronaldo’s mother?” Jesus said.

“She is a lady I greatly respect. She suffered a lot to raise her children.”

Asked whether the debate surrounding Ronaldo’s international retirement would eventually come to an end, Jesus admitted that he was unsure.

“I don’t know when it’s going to stop. If you guys ask the questions, I have to answer. If you ask about Ronaldo next year, I will answer,” he added.

Portugal will now turn their attention to their encounter against Wales as discussions surrounding Ronaldo’s departure from the national team continue.

title: Breaking: Omotosho, Nwite, 10 others sworn in as Appeal Court Justices
description:
By Ikechukwu Nnochiri



ABUJA – The Chief Justice of Nigeria (CJN), Justice Kudirat Kekere-Ekun, on Tuesday swore in 12 new Justices of the Court of Appeal.







Among the new appellate court justices whose elevation the National Judicial Council (NJC) recommended at its meeting on May 13 are two
content:
By Ikechukwu Nnochiri

ABUJA – The Chief Justice of Nigeria (CJN), Justice Kudirat Kekere-Ekun, on Tuesday swore in 12 new Justices of the Court of Appeal.

Among the new appellate court justices whose elevation the National Judicial Council (NJC) recommended at its meeting on May 13 are two Federal High Court judges, Justices James Omotosho and Emeka Nwite, who hitherto handled high-profile cases.

Justice Omotosho had on November 20, 2025, convicted and sentenced the detained leader of the proscribed Indigenous People of Biafra (IPOB), Nnamdi Kanu, to life imprisonment after finding him guilty on a seven-count terrorism-related charge that the federal government filed against him.

Likewise, Justice Nwite, who is handling the N80.2 billion fraud case against the immediate past Governor of Kogi State, Alhaji Yahaya Bello, had on June 3 convicted and sentenced four members of the Al-Shabaab terrorist group to death by hanging for their roles in the June 5, 2022 attack on St. Francis Catholic Church in Owo, Ondo States.

Meanwhile, the other justices also sworn in to the appellate court bench by the CJN on Tuesday are Justices Yakubu Abdulhammeed Mohammed, Abodunde Monisola Oluwatoyin, Ajuwa Raphael, Abua Elias Ojie, Ijohor Mbalamen Jennifer, Shuaibu Sabiu Bala, Buba Dauda Njane, Kado Sanusi, Ademola Enikuomehin and Dadom Julcit Veronica.

All criminal cases previously before the judges, including the trial of former Governor Bello, will be reassigned to another judge of the court and heard de-novo (afresh).

In her address at the occasion, the CJN said the appointments of the new justices brought together “judicial experience from different parts of the country and from courts with distinct jurisdictions and responsibilities.”

She disclosed that some of the justices were selected from Gombe, Bayelsa, Cross River, Benue, Kebbi, Taraba and Ondo, following their service at the High Court, the National Industrial Court and the Customary Courts of Appeal in Ekiti and Plateau states.

She urged the justices to be mindful that, unlike before when they presided over cases alone, their new assignment would require them to sit with other justices in panels, deliberate collectively and arrive at decisions through a process of judicial engagement.

“Your responsibility, therefore, extends beyond determining whether a decision should be affirmed or set aside. You are called upon to promote consistency in the application of the law, clarify legal principles, correct errors where necessary and contribute to the coherent development of our jurisprudence.

“This requires a disciplined and principled approach to appellate adjudication.

“An appeal is not an invitation to rehear a case simply because another judicial officer might have reached a different conclusion. You must identify the complaints properly raised, examine the record of proceedings, consider the findings and reasoning of the court below, and determine whether the law justifies appellate intervention.

“Particular care is required when reviewing findings of fact and the evaluation of evidence, especially where the appellate court has not had the opportunity to observe the witnesses.

“The task is to correct errors where they are established, while respecting findings that are properly supported by the evidence and the applicable law.

“I urge you to give equal attention to the quality and clarity of your judgments. My Lords, judicial office is increasingly exercised in an environment in which decisions are subjected to immediate public commentary. You must remain conscious of this reality without allowing it to influence your adjudicatory responsibilities.

“Public approval must not be the basis for you to depart from the law, just as criticism must not deter you from reaching a decision that your conscience and the law require.

“Your judicial independence must be guarded against political, financial, social and personal pressures, including those that may arise through professional familiarity or established relationships.

“Conduct yourselves in a manner that leaves no reasonable basis for doubt about your impartiality. The diversity of your professional backgrounds should also enrich the work of the Court.

“Your experience in different jurisdictions will provide valuable insights into the legal and social realities of our country. Bring that experience to your deliberations, but always subject it to the common discipline of constitutional adjudication.

“The law must be applied consistently, fairly and without prejudice,” the CJN told the new appellate court justices.

The post Breaking: Omotosho, Nwite, 10 others sworn in as Appeal Court Justices appeared first on Vanguard News.

description:
…Orders immediate handover of club’s assets



By Steve Oko



UMUAHIA — Abia State Government has dissolved the management structure and technical crew of two-time African champions, Enyimba International Football Club of Aba, with immediate effect, following what it described as the club’s disappo
content:
…Orders immediate handover of club’s assets

By Steve Oko

UMUAHIA — Abia State Government has dissolved the management structure and technical crew of two-time African champions, Enyimba International Football Club of Aba, with immediate effect, following what it described as the club’s disappointing performances.

The government also directed affected officials and other individuals in possession of the club’s assets, properties, official documents, equipment and other institutional materials to hand them over to the Ministry of Sports and Youth Development immediately.

The decision, announced in a special government statement on Tuesday, is part of efforts to restructure the administration and operations of the club.

The Commissioner for Information, Prince Okey Kanu, who signed the statement, said the decision followed a review of the club’s affairs, which revealed administrative and structural challenges requiring far-reaching interventions.

According to the government, the Ministry of Sports and Youth Development has been mandated to take charge of the restructuring process, review the club’s management framework and implement necessary administrative, technical and operational reforms.

The ministry is also expected to establish a new institutional framework to restore stability, accountability and competitiveness to the club.

The government said further details on the handover arrangements and subsequent administrative procedures would be communicated by the ministry.

It described the intervention as necessary to restore Enyimba’s competitive identity and reposition the club for sustainable success in Nigerian and continental football.

Reaffirming its commitment to the club’s future, the government said Enyimba remained an important sporting heritage of Abia State, given its historic achievements and status as one of Nigeria’s most successful football institutions.

It assured supporters, players and other stakeholders that the intervention was aimed at protecting the club’s long-term interests, strengthening its institutional capacity and restoring the pride and competitive standards associated with the Enyimba name.

“The rebuilding of Enyimba begins now,” the government declared.

Enyimba, which has won the CAF Champions League twice, remains one of Nigeria’s most decorated football clubs.

description:

…Nursing college gets increased admission quota



By Steve Oko



UMUAHIA — The Abia State Government has announced a 60 per cent reduction in maternal mortality between 2024 and 2026, saying the state now has the second-lowest maternal mortality rate in t
content:
…Renovates 190 PHCs, functionalises 123

…Nursing college gets increased admission quota

By Steve Oko

UMUAHIA — The Abia State Government has announced a 60 per cent reduction in maternal mortality between 2024 and 2026, saying the state now has the second-lowest maternal mortality rate in the country.

The government attributed the reported improvement to ongoing reforms in the health sector, including the rehabilitation of primary healthcare centres and increased investment in healthcare delivery.

Commissioner for Information, Prince Okey Kanu, disclosed this during a briefing on the outcome of this week’s State Executive Council meeting at Government House, Umuahia. He was represented by the Special Adviser to the Governor on Media and Publicity, Mr Ferdinand Ekeoma.

Kanu said the administration had made progress in its efforts to revitalise primary healthcare, disclosing that 190 of the 200 primary healthcare centres earmarked for renovation under Project Ekwueme had been completed.

He said 123 of the renovated facilities had been made functional to provide essential medical services, while 27 had been equipped with solar power, with work ongoing at nine additional centres.

The Commissioner also announced the completion of all 77 World Bank-supported health projects in the state.

In another development, Kanu disclosed that the Aba Campus of the College of Nursing Sciences had secured an increase in its admission quota from 75 to 120 students following an accreditation exercise by the National Nursing and Midwifery Council.

According to him, the revised admission quota was communicated in an accreditation report released on November 13, reflecting the outcome of the institution’s accreditation exercise.

Meanwhile, the Rector of Ogbonnaya Onu Polytechnic, Aba, Dr Christopher Okoro, has emerged Administrator of the Year in a nationwide poll organised by Leadership Excellence Award.

Kanu said Okoro secured 148,267 votes in the exercise, which recognised his contributions to institutional development, human capital development and technical and professional education.

He attributed the recognition to developments recorded at the institution under the Rector, including an increase in student enrolment by more than 6,000, improved infrastructure and better staff welfare.

The Commissioner also said the state government remained committed to education development, noting that the sector continued to receive 20 per cent of the state’s annual budget.

On public health surveillance, the government reported that Abia recorded no cases of Ebola, Lassa fever, COVID-19, diphtheria, cholera, mpox or yellow fever during the period under review.

The Commissioner for Health, Prof. Enoch Ogbonnaya Uche, who also addressed the briefing, provided an update on the Ebola situation in the country.

He disclosed that the index patient reported on October 20 had been transferred to Switzerland, where the patient subsequently recovered.

Uche further said all 62 contacts traced to the index case had completed the mandatory 21-day monitoring period and were cleared as of November 13, citing information from the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control.

He, however, urged residents to remain vigilant, stressing that personal hygiene and sustained public awareness were essential to preventing infectious disease outbreaks.

Identifying hand hygiene as the focus of the state’s public health advisory for the week, the Commissioner advised residents to wash their hands regularly with running water, particularly at home, workplaces and after touching potentially contaminated surfaces.

He described regular handwashing as one of the simplest and most effective ways of preventing infections and curbing the spread of communicable diseases.

title: Pope calls for ‘less division’ after US midterm elections
description:
Pope Leo XIV on Tuesday voiced hope for “less war” and “less division” following the midterm elections in his native United States, as he returned from a tour of South America.



The first American pope has clashed repeatedly with US President Donald Trump over the war with Iran and made history th
content:
Pope Leo XIV on Tuesday voiced hope for “less war” and “less division” following the midterm elections in his native United States, as he returned from a tour of South America.

The first American pope has clashed repeatedly with US President Donald Trump over the war with Iran and made history this month by announcing that he had cast a ballot in the midterms — the first time a pope has been known to have voted.

“I would like to see a greater capacity for dialogue, for building bridges, for reconciliation. Less polemics, less war, less division,” the US-born pontiff told reporters including AFP on the papal plane.

“I know this is also a dream, but I know it is possible so we shall see,” he said.

Trump’s Republican party was handed a resounding defeat in the midterms in large part due to anger over soaring energy prices and the president’s costly war with Iran.

– ‘Seeds of hope’ –

Leo’s comments echoed his repeated calls for an end to polarisation during his 12-day tour of Uruguay, Argentina and Peru.

The visit, which came less than a month after the 71-year-old underwent lung cancer surgery, also highlighted the social justice priorities shaping his papacy.

From the high Andes to the sweltering Amazon, Leo crisscrossed a continent where he spent nearly two decades as a missionary, picking up Peruvian citizenship along the way.

Visiting care homes and prisons, the leader of the world’s 1.4 billion Catholics reminded political leaders like Argentina’s Javier Milei that economic growth must benefit all, speaking in defence of the poor, the elderly and disabled people.

In a lighter moment, the pope joked with reporters about being hit in the face with a rosary bracelet thrown from the crowd as he arrived for a mass in Lima.

“The affection of Peruvians — including that person who, with great faith, simply wanted to offer me a rosary — these are things one carries in one’s heart, perhaps in one’s eye,” he said.

Asked about his apparent criticism of Milei, he said his comments about Argentina’s austerity policies were “not political” but he encouraged the Argentine leader “to take greater account above all of those most in need”.

“I hope that once again we’ve sown seeds of hope, a message of the possibility of unity despite difficulties and differences,” he said.

Leo also applied his message of unity to the Catholic Church, which saw periods of factionalism under his predecessor Pope Francis.

“What I believe is important in my ministry to the Church is to bring healing, to bring people together.

“First let us come together, let us consider what we think the priorities must be, and then we will see how we move forward from there,” he said.

– No resignation letter –

The visit went ahead exactly as planned despite doubts among many observers after the pope’s surgery on October 13 in which part of his right lung was removed.

The cancer diagnosis fewer than 18 months into his papacy shook the Catholic Church but the surgery was successful and doctors have said he does not require more therapy.

The pope was asked on the papal plane whether he had signed a resignation letter before his operation — a precaution taken by Francis as Canon Law does not clearly stipulate what happens to the governance of the Church if a pope is physically or mentally incapacitated.

“For now I don’t see any need, thanks be to God,” Leo told reporters.

“As I said before I was elected Pope, I trust that if it ever becomes necessary, I will do it, I think”.

title: Drones Behind Nearly 75% Of Civilian Deaths This Year In Sudan War — UN
description: Drones caused nearly three quarters of all the verified civilian fatalities this year in the war in Sudan, the UN said Tuesday.The war between the Sudanese Armed Forces and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) erupted in April 2023 and is estimated to have killed more than 200,000 people in t
content:
Drones caused nearly three quarters of all the verified civilian fatalities this year in the war in Sudan, the UN said Tuesday.

The war between the Sudanese Armed Forces and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) erupted in April 2023 and is estimated to have killed more than 200,000 people in total.

The conflict has forced more than 13 million to flee their homes, creating the world’s largest hunger and displacement crisis, according to aid groups.

Out of 2,230 civilian deaths confirmed by the UN human rights office OHCHR to have occurred this year between January and the end of October, more than 1,630 were a result of drone attacks, it said on Tuesday.

Drone attacks have “eclipsed the use of other tactics and weaponry”, it said, adding that the full civilian casualty figures are likely to be higher.

Both warring parties have increasingly relied on drones capable of striking targets hundreds of kilometres away.

In a report on the human rights situation in Sudan, OHCHR said the first six months of the year were marked by an “unmistakable increase in drone strikes against civilians and civilian objects”.

The use of drones has now become “one of the defining features of the conflict”, it said.

With the war well into its fourth year, “a robust war economy and steady supply of weapons and other external support enabled the parties to sustain fighting as the conflict continued to spread and evolve,” the report said.

The conflict is exacting an “unbearable toll” on civilians, while the prospects for a ceasefire and a peaceful resolution to the conflict remain elusive, it said.

‘World Is Watching’

From January 1 to June 30, OHCHR said it continued to document indiscriminate attacks, reprisals against civilians accused of collaborating with opposing forces, and the widespread use of sexual violence as a weapon of war.

Civilians in the Kordofan region accounted for more than two-thirds of documented casualties, followed by Darfur, where most of the remaining casualties occurred.

“The findings in our report provide more evidence, if any were needed, of the ceaselessly unbearable civilian suffering of the war in Sudan and the warring parties’ continued and brazen disregard for the laws of war,” UN rights chief Volker Turk said in a statement.

“Amid pervasive impunity, the report documents, once again, serious violations of international humanitarian law. Such violations may amount to war crimes.”

The intensification of drone strikes targeting power stations and fuel supplies had become a “worrying trend”, the report said.

Between October 20 and November 4, some 29 drone strikes, attributed to the RSF, hit electricity facilities and fuel stations, “triggering widespread power blackouts and further fuel shortages affecting millions far from the conflict frontlines”, it said.

“These drone strikes had a devastating impact on civilians and essential services, ” it said.

“The parties to the conflict must protect civilians and uphold their international law obligations — the world is watching,” Turk said.

AFP

The post Drones Behind Nearly 75% Of Civilian Deaths This Year In Sudan War — UN appeared first on Channels Television.

title: Deputy Senate President mourns late Vanguard Online Editor, Femi Ajasa
description:
Deputy President of the Senate, Senator Barau I. Jibrin, has mourned the passing of Mr Olufemi Finayon Ajasa, the Online Editor of Vanguard Newspapers.







Mr Ajasa passed away on Sunday at the Lagos University Teaching Hospital (LUTH) after a brief illness at the age of 44, according to the mana
content:
Deputy President of the Senate, Senator Barau I. Jibrin, has mourned the passing of Mr Olufemi Finayon Ajasa, the Online Editor of Vanguard Newspapers.

Mr Ajasa passed away on Sunday at the Lagos University Teaching Hospital (LUTH) after a brief illness at the age of 44, according to the management of Vanguard Media Limited, publishers of the Vanguard Newspapers.

In a condolence message issued by his spokesperson, Ismail Mudashir, Senator Barau described the late Ajasa as a thoroughbred professional and one of the finest minds in Nigeria’s digital journalism space.

“Femi Ajasa’s dedication and commitment to truth and accuracy set him apart and distinguished him among others. His death is a painful loss, not only to his immediate family, the Vanguard family, but to the entire Nigerian media industry,” he said.

The Deputy President of the Senate noted that Mr Ajasa’s journalism journey, which began as a photojournalist with the National Mirror in 2012, through TheNewsGuru and Pulse, to his return to Vanguard in June 2022 as Online Editor, was marked by excellence, integrity and selfless service to the country through his noble profession, journalism.

Senator Barau extended his heartfelt condolences to the Ajasa family of Ajido, Badagry, Lagos State, Management and Staff of Vanguard Media Limited, the Nigeria Union of Journalists (NUJ) and all his friends and professional associates.

“We pray that God will grant his family, colleagues and loved ones the strength and fortitude to bear this irreparable loss, and grant his gentle soul eternal rest,” he said.

title: Bangladesh Garment Workers, Police Clash In Fresh Wage Protest
description: Bangladeshi police fired tear gas and stun grenades on Tuesday in clashes with thousands of garment workers who were protesting after a key wage board meeting was postponed.Protesters hurled bricks, torched vehicles, and blocked the main highway between the capital, Dhaka, and the key financial dist
content:
Bangladeshi police fired tear gas and stun grenades on Tuesday in clashes with thousands of garment workers who were protesting after a key wage board meeting was postponed.

Protesters hurled bricks, torched vehicles, and blocked the main highway between the capital, Dhaka, and the key financial district of Mymensingh as demonstrations over wage conditions turned violent.

The South Asian nation of 170 million people is the world’s second-biggest garment exporter behind China, producing clothes for major international brands including Fruit of the Loom and Levi Strauss.

But growing worker unrest over wages that began in October has threatened to disrupt the industry that generates $38 billion in revenues annually and employs more than four million people.

Workers are demanding a minimum monthly wage of 30,000 taka ($240) — a 140-percent increase on the current 12,500 taka, as they struggle to cope with rising food, housing, transport and healthcare costs.

Some 500 factories out of 4,500 are currently shut, sources told AFP, something that is further stoking unrest among workers.

“The owners seem unwilling to meet our salary demands. They are already dragging their feet,” said Khanom, 24, who gave only one name.

In a joint statement, the Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA) and the Bangladesh Knitwear Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BKMEA) called for a resumption of wage negotiations as soon as possible.

The disruption comes during the run-up to Christmas, the busiest export period for Bangladesh’s garment industry.

title: BREAKING: Pro-Biafra agitator Simon Ekpa released from Finnish prison
description:
Controversial pro-Biafra agitator Simon Ekpa has reportedly regained his freedom from a Finnish prison, following the completion of his detention period.
The development was disclosed by Barrister Aloy Ejimakor, Special Counsel to the detained leader of the Indigenous People of Biafra (IPOB), Nnamdi
content:
Controversial pro-Biafra agitator Simon Ekpa has reportedly regained his freedom from a Finnish prison, following the completion of his detention period.

The development was disclosed by Barrister Aloy Ejimakor, Special Counsel to the detained leader of the Indigenous People of Biafra (IPOB), Nnamdi Kanu, who said Ekpa’s close associate, Dr David Matsanga, confirmed the release during a telephone conversation on Tuesday, November 17, 2026.

According to Ejimakor, Matsanga informed him that the separatist figure had been released from Finnish custody.

The reported development comes after Ekpa’s conviction in Finland over terrorism-related activities linked to separatist agitation in Nigeria’s South-East.

Ekpa was arrested on November 21, 2024, following an investigation by the Finnish National Bureau of Investigation into his alleged involvement in terrorism-related activities.

At the time, Finnish authorities suspected him of publicly inciting violence with terrorist intent and financing terrorism. Four other individuals were also arrested during the investigation on suspicion of financing terrorism-related offences.

The allegations concerned Ekpa’s activities between August 2021 and November 2024, particularly his use of social media to promote the Biafran independence campaign and allegedly encourage violent actions in South-East Nigeria.

Ekpa, who had lived in Finland for years and previously served as a municipal politician in Lahti, denied committing the offences.

On May 16, 2025, Finnish prosecutors formally charged him with participating in a terrorist organisation and publicly inciting crimes for terrorist purposes.

His trial was subsequently held at the Päijät-Häme District Court, which found him guilty on September 1, 2025, and sentenced him to six years in prison.

The court also convicted him of aggravated tax fraud and an offence relating to Finland’s Lawyers Act.

According to the court’s findings, Ekpa operated from Finland and used his influence and network of contacts to support armed separatist groups in Nigeria’s South-East. The court said his activities included facilitating the supply of weapons, explosives and ammunition to the groups, as well as using his social media following to encourage criminal activities.

Ekpa challenged his conviction and sentence before the East Finland Court of Appeal.

On October 15, 2026, the appellate court upheld his convictions for participating in a terrorist group and publicly inciting crimes for terrorist purposes but reduced his prison sentence from six years to four.

The court considered arguments about the security situation in South-East Nigeria and whether the violence in the region amounted to an armed conflict under international humanitarian law.

Although it acknowledged evidence of organised armed groups and the use of heavy weapons, the court ruled that the intensity of the fighting did not meet the legal threshold for classification as a civil war.

The appellate court nevertheless considered the circumstances surrounding the offences in reducing his sentence.

Ahead of the reported release, Ekpa’s legal representatives had indicated that November 17, 2026, was his scheduled release date. His legal team had also cautioned supporters against celebrating unverified reports of his freedom.

The reported development therefore follows the release date previously communicated by his legal representatives.

However, the confirmation attributed to Matsanga has not been accompanied by an independent announcement from Finnish prison authorities or the judiciary. The reported release should therefore be distinguished from an official confirmation by the Finnish authorities.

The post BREAKING: Pro-Biafra agitator Simon Ekpa released from Finnish prison appeared first on Very Nigerian.

title: 2027: Enugu NDC guber candidate unveils manifesto, vows tax relief, pension reform
description:
Jude Chinedu, Enugu
The Enugu State governorship candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in the 2027 election, Sir Chinyeaka Ohaa, has promised to end multiple taxation, introduce a 12-month tax relief programme for eligible small businesses and clear inherited gratuity arrears within the
content:
Jude Chinedu, Enugu

The Enugu State governorship candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in the 2027 election, Sir Chinyeaka Ohaa, has promised to end multiple taxation, introduce a 12-month tax relief programme for eligible small businesses and clear inherited gratuity arrears within the first 24 months of his administration.

The promises are contained in his manifesto, titled Rescue Mission 2027: Make Enugu great for all, in which he outlined plans to revive businesses, improve workers’ welfare, reform land administration and extend development to rural communities across the state.

Unveiling the policy document, Ohaa said Enugu needed a change in its approach to governance, particularly in taxation, economic management and the distribution of public infrastructure.

He said his administration would move away from what he described as excessive taxation and urban-centred development to “enterprise-driven economic growth” and equitable development of rural and urban communities.

On taxation, Ohaa promised to end unjustified daily tolls, multiple taxation, arbitrary assessments and unauthorised collections, which he identified as major burdens on traders and small businesses.

He proposed a Single Unified Business Assessment System, electronic payments, verifiable receipts and an accessible complaints and appeals mechanism to check illegal collections and make the tax system more transparent.

The candidate also promised a 12-month state-level tax relief programme for eligible registered micro and small businesses, within the lawful authority of state and local governments.

On pension and retirement benefits, he pledged to establish an Enugu State Retirees Gratuity Redemption Fund, conduct an independent audit of outstanding liabilities and publish a verified register of retirees alongside payment schedules.

“We commit to clearing inherited gratuity arrears within the first 24 months of the administration,” he declared.

He also promised consequential pension adjustments to reflect prevailing economic realities and restoration of the welfare practice of allowing retired permanent secretaries to retain their official vehicles.

The manifesto further addresses the plight of traders affected by market demolitions, with a promise to establish an independent Market Traders Recovery Committee within seven days of assuming office.

The committee would investigate and document affected traders at Ogige Nsukka, Garriki, Holy Ghost and Abakpa markets, as well as the Nnamdi Azikiwe Stadium. It is expected to submit a preliminary report within 30 days, while compensation assessments would begin within 60 days.

Beyond taxation and pension reforms, the candidate promised to direct 60 per cent of new road infrastructure projects to rural areas, establish 17 agro-processing hubs and provide solar-powered water schemes in all 260 wards by the end of his administration’s third year.

He also pledged to upgrade at least one primary healthcare centre in every ward to 24-hour service, establish community security networks and forest guards across the state and undertake an independent review of the Smart Green Schools programme.

On transparency, Ohaa promised to publish government revenues, expenditure, debt obligations and audited financial reports, insisting that public resources must be managed in the interest of the people.

title: Obasa celebrates son’s LG chairman of the year award
description:
The Speaker of the Lagos State House of Assembly, Mudashiru Obasa, has congratulated his son, Abdul-Ganiyu Obasa, on receiving the Local Government Chairman of the Year Award at the Silverbird Man of the Year Awards 2026.
Obasa, in a Facebook post on Tuesday, expressed pride in his son’s recognition
content:
The Speaker of the Lagos State House of Assembly, Mudashiru Obasa, has congratulated his son, Abdul-Ganiyu Obasa, on receiving the Local Government Chairman of the Year Award at the Silverbird Man of the Year Awards 2026.

Obasa, in a Facebook post on Tuesday, expressed pride in his son’s recognition, describing the moment he presented the award as fulfilling.

“Standing proudly beside you on stage last night as you received the Local Government Chairman of the Year Award at the Silverbird Man of the Year Awards 2026 was a deeply fulfilling moment for me as a father, seeing the seeds of purposeful leadership, hard work and dedication begin to bear fruit,” he wrote.

The Speaker congratulated his son on the recognition, saying he was proud to see him making his mark in grassroots governance and bringing pride to Agege.

“Watching you make your mark in grassroots governance and bring pride to Agege is truly fulfilling. You are making your generation and the hood proud while putting Agege on the global stage for all the right reasons,” Obasa said.

He urged Abdul-Ganiyu to regard the award as a call to greater service rather than a destination, encouraging him to continue making a difference in the lives of residents.

“I encourage you to see this honour not as a destination but as a call to greater service. Keep raising the bar, touching lives and making a lasting difference,” he added.

Abdul-Ganiyu is the Chairman of Agege Local Government in Lagos State.

He was confirmed as substantive chairman following the resignation of his predecessor, Tunde Azeez, who cited persistent health challenges that made it difficult for him to perform his duties.

Azeez had proceeded on medical leave shortly after the new administration was sworn in on July 27, 2025, leaving Abdul-Ganiyu, who was then acting chairman, to oversee the council’s activities.

Following the reading of Azeez’s resignation letter, councillors unanimously voted to confirm Abdul-Ganiyu as chairman.

The lawmakers said his confirmation was based on his contributions to the council while serving in an acting capacity and the need to prevent a leadership vacuum.

title: Why Nigeria’s Credit Market Must Finance Both the Buyer and the Seller
description: Credit plays an important role in keeping economic activity moving. For many households, access to credit makes it possible to spread the cost of major purchases over time rather than pay the full amount upfront. This improves purchasing power, supports household consumption and creates demand for b
content:
Credit plays an important role in keeping economic activity moving. For many households, access to credit makes it possible to spread the cost of major purchases over time rather than pay the full amount upfront. This improves purchasing power, supports household consumption and creates demand for businesses across different sectors. When individuals can afford to make purchases, businesses have more opportunities to sell their products and services.

However, financing buyers alone is not enough to drive economic growth. The businesses that supply these goods and services also need access to credit to purchase inventory, pay suppliers, manage operating costs and fulfil orders.

Supporting both consumers and merchants requires lenders to recognise that the two groups have different financing needs and cannot be assessed in the same way. Lenders must understand these differences when determining how much to lend, the appropriate repayment terms and the risks involved. Chukwuma Nwanze, Managing Director of Credit Direct, highlighted this distinction during a panel discussion at Moonshot. He explained that while lenders assess an individual’s earnings, disposable income, existing financial obligations, and borrowing behaviour, evaluating merchants requires a closer look at their cash flow, turnover, and business growth.

A credit market that serves only one side of this relationship risks leaving important parts of the economy underserved. For many businesses, the ability to meet demand depends on having enough working capital. Merchants need funds to purchase inventory, pay suppliers, manage operating expenses and fulfil customer orders. These costs often arise before revenue from sales is received, creating a gap between the money a business needs to operate and the money coming into it. This challenge can become more evident when demand increases. A business may have an opportunity to serve more customers but lack the funds to purchase additional stock or expand its capacity. Delayed access to financing can therefore limit its ability to respond to market opportunities, even when there is a clear demand for its products.

Working capital financing can help businesses manage these gaps and maintain the flow of goods and services. It can also give merchants greater flexibility to plan inventory purchases, meet supplier obligations and sustain operations through periods of uneven cash flow. The importance of merchant financing becomes clearer when considered alongside consumer credit. Financing customers’ purchases creates demand for a product, and financing merchants gives businesses the resources to meet that demand. This, therefore, builds a credit market that contributes meaningfully to economic growth.

Merchant assessment requires a closer examination of business performance. This includes cash flow, the speed at which money moves through the business, turnover, operating costs and growth patterns over time. These indicators help lenders understand how consistently a business generates revenue and whether its operations can support the proposed financing.

The distinction matters because the amount of money passing through an account does not necessarily represent the amount available for repayment. For an individual, income must be considered alongside personal expenses, existing debt, and other financial commitments. For a business, turnover must be assessed alongside the cost of maintaining operations, paying suppliers, replacing inventory, and the wider financial demands of running the business. A lending approach that overlooks these differences can produce decisions that do not reflect the borrower’s actual financial position. Consumer credit and merchant financing therefore require assessment methods, repayment structures and products suited to the needs of each group.

Developing a credit market that serves both consumers and merchants requires lenders to understand where financing is needed within the commercial process and make appropriate products accessible at those points. Credit Direct‘s personal and business loans offering reflects this approach, catering to individuals seeking financing for personal needs and businesses looking for capital to support their operations.

A stronger credit market recognises that buyers and sellers are part of the same economic relationship. For Nigeria’s credit market to contribute meaningfully to economic growth, access to financing must prioritise both consumers and businesses. Financing consumers helps create purchasing power, while financing merchants strengthens their ability to supply goods and services. Both are necessary for commerce to function effectively. Supporting one without adequately financing the other leaves that relationship incomplete.

About Credit Direct

Credit Direct is building Africa’s leading embedded credit company by integrating credit into the supply chains and payment flows of partners, unlocking financial success for individuals and businesses. The company also provides retail investment solutions, expanding its role from access to credit to broader financial growth and wealth-building. Credit Direct has served millions of customers nationwide, including those historically underserved by traditional banking. Credit Direct is a wholly owned subsidiary of First City Monument Bank (FCMB) Group Plc.

The post Why Nigeria’s Credit Market Must Finance Both the Buyer and the Seller  appeared first on Vanguard News.
