title: Ukraine, Russia Hit Key Bridges Ahead Of Putin-Xi-Trump Summit
description: Ukraine struck Russia’s Crimean bridge for the second night in a row on Tuesday, shutting it down, while Russia hit two major bridges in Kyiv — the latest wave of attacks that come ahead of a historic meeting of the Chinese, US and Russian leaders.Russia’s defence ministry said it
content:
Ukraine struck Russia’s Crimean bridge for the second night in a row on Tuesday, shutting it down, while Russia hit two major bridges in Kyiv — the latest wave of attacks that come ahead of a historic meeting of the Chinese, US and Russian leaders.

Russia’s defence ministry said it downed 1,441 Ukrainian drones in a major overnight barrage — the second-highest one-day figure this year.

Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin reported that more than 800 of them were headed to the capital itself, while officials reported attacks across 19 regions of the country.

Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelensky had warned of a major Russian attack in the days leading up to a meeting in China’s Shenzhen on Thursday between presidents Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin.

Trump said the fighting in Ukraine would be among the topics canvassed in the talks, which come at a time of renewed diplomatic efforts to end almost five years of war.

Traffic was halted across the Crimean bridge — a highly symbolic target for Ukraine — for hours after it was hit shortly after midnight on Tuesday.

There was no official comment on the damage, but unverified social media images appeared to show a section of the road bridge completely collapsed and in the water. The bridge carries both automobile and rail traffic.

“Experts are assessing the damage caused,” Russia’s transport ministry said.

“Motorists are advised not to travel in the direction of the Crimean bridge,” it added.

An emergency government commission was to convene on Tuesday to assess the damage and the repair work.

Traffic had been halted on the bridge for almost 17 hours from 23:54 (2054 GMT) on Monday following a previous attack, according to the road traffic authority.

In Kyiv, Russian ballistic missiles hit the Northern and Southern bridges — two major transport arteries that cross the Dnipro river.

Traffic was also suspended, causing gridlock early on Tuesday morning.

Russia’s army confirmed it had hit both bridges in a “massive attack” on Ukraine’s infrastructure.

Mayor Vitali Klitschko posted a video from the Northern Bridge showing debris strewn across the road.

The strikes on Kyiv also disrupted heating and water in parts of the capital, he said.

New Yalta

The wave of strikes comes as the United States renews its push for an end to the war.

But diplomatic efforts have so far failed to reach a breakthrough, with fighting grinding into another winter.

Moscow wants a sweeping deal to rewrite “Europe’s security architecture” as part of any agreement to halt the fighting.

Russia has previously demanded curbs on NATO’s presence in central and eastern Europe and restrictions on the deployment of foreign troops and hardware to Ukraine.

Kyiv and Europe are resisting any attempts to overhaul the continent’s post-Cold War defence, calling for a ceasefire in the Ukraine war before any discussion of terms.

Zelensky has raised alarm that the talks between the leaders of Russia, China and the United States on the sidelines of a regional summit could be a Yalta-like “redistribution of spheres of influence” for the 21st century.

The 1945 Yalta summit — held in Crimea, then part of the Soviet Union — saw US president Franklin D. Roosevelt, Britain’s Winston Churchill and Soviet leader Joseph Stalin carve up new post-WWII territorial boundaries.

Ukraine’s Foreign Minister Andriy Sybiga said the presidents’ meeting would “only encourage Putin to continue this war”.

China has not provided specific details on the topics to be discussed beyond “safeguarding world peace” and “promoting strategic stability in major power relations”.

The White House had earlier signalled the Ukraine war was not expected to be addressed — before Trump said on Monday that it would be.

“We’ll talk about my favourite subject, Ukraine,” Trump told reporters.

As the trio gathers in China, Ukraine and its allies will this week hold meetings on defence support and aligning positions ahead of any future talks.

AFP

title: Anambra South 2027: NDC faithful, over 1,000 APGA stakeholders declare support for Nwachukwu
description:
…Say 18 Months Not Enough
Party faithful and political stakeholders across the seven LGAs reaffirm support for Senator Emmanuel Nwachukwu in the January 2027 general elections, insisting he deserves a full four-year term to consolidate on his representation.

A growing number of political stakeholde
content:
…Say 18 Months Not Enough

Party faithful and political stakeholders across the seven LGAs reaffirm support for Senator Emmanuel Nwachukwu in the January 2027 general elections, insisting he deserves a full four-year term to consolidate on his representation.

A growing number of political stakeholders and party faithfuls across Anambra South Senatorial District have declared support for the re-election of Senator Emmanuel C. Nwachukwu (Ọnọdugo), insisting that his one year and six months in office is insufficient to fully deliver on the mandate entrusted to him.

The supporters, comprising members of the National Democratic Congress (NDC), the All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA) and other political stakeholders, expressed confidence in the senator’s representation, arguing that he deserves the opportunity to consolidate on the foundation already established and serve a full four-year term.

The endorsements followed a series of political engagements involving the senator and party stakeholders, including a meeting with more than 1,000 APGA faithfuls drawn from the State, Local Government and Ward Executive Working Committees across the seven local government areas of Anambra South.

The meeting, which took place at Senator Nwachukwu’s residence in Ukpor, Nnewi South Local Government Area, brought together party leaders, executives and grassroots representatives from across the senatorial district.

Those in attendance included members of the State Working Committee (SWC) from Anambra South, the seven Local Government Party Chairmen and members of their respective executive committees, as well as ward executives and other stakeholders representing the district’s 118 wards.

The engagement provided an opportunity for interaction, exchange of ideas, assessment of party preparedness and discussions on strengthening coordination and cooperation across the various levels of the party.

In his remarks, Senator Nwachukwu emphasised that effective representation extends beyond legislative responsibilities, noting that accessibility, consistent engagement and maintaining meaningful relationships with constituents and political structures remain important aspects of public service.

He expressed appreciation to the party leaders and faithfuls for their commitment to strengthening APGA across the district, describing their participation as an indication of the importance of unity, inclusiveness and grassroots involvement in the political process.

The senator also called on members to expand the party’s membership base by encouraging more people to join APGA, assuring them that the party remained open to accommodating new members.

“We don’t do use and dump. Our party, APGA, is big enough to accommodate all of you. I urge you to bring more people into our fold. If you go on social media, what they show you is not necessarily what is obtainable in real life,” Nwachukwu said.

He further commended the party’s leadership and acknowledged the contributions of stakeholders towards sustaining a united and coordinated political structure across Anambra South.

The senator said he was particularly encouraged by the spirit of solidarity demonstrated at the meeting, noting that the stakeholders’ declaration of support for his return to the Senate ahead of the January 16, 2027 election came with an even greater responsibility to remain accessible and committed to the people.

He assured them of his continued engagement, adding that their confidence would encourage him to sustain his commitment to purposeful representation.

NDC Faithful in Aguata Declare Support

In a related development, NDC faithful and prominent political stakeholders from Aguata Local Government Area have also reaffirmed their support for Senator Nwachukwu’s re-election following a separate strategic engagement with the senator.

The meeting provided an opportunity for the stakeholders to interact with Nwachukwu, strengthen existing relationships and discuss their collective commitment to the political process ahead of the forthcoming senatorial election.

Speaking on behalf of the NDC stakeholders in Aguata, Richard Nwankwo declared the group’s support for the senator, assuring him of their solidarity.

“You are welcome to our midst. We, the NDC in Aguata, are solidly behind you,” Nwankwo stated.

Richard described the senator’s physical appearance and direct engagement with the group as significant, observing that he was the first senator to visit them physically to address their concerns, while others had previously communicated through telephone conversations.

He expressed optimism that Nwachukwu would be given the opportunity to complete a four-year term, maintaining that the senator’s relatively short period in office should not be considered sufficient time to assess the full extent of his mandate.
The stakeholders maintained that continuity in representation would provide an opportunity for the senator to consolidate on the work already commenced and pursue further initiatives for the benefit of the district.

Across the engagements, the argument advanced by supporters was that one year and six months is not enough time for a senator to fully execute his legislative agenda, establish sustainable development initiatives and consolidate relationships with constituents.

They argued that effective representation requires consistency, experience, continuity and sufficient time to translate legislative intentions and development plans into measurable outcomes.

For the NDC faithful in Aguata and APGA stakeholders across Anambra South, the January 16, 2027 senatorial election presents an opportunity to determine whether Senator Nwachukwu should receive another mandate to complete a full four-year term.

The APGA gathering, which brought together more than 1,000 party faithful from the seven local government areas and 118 wards, also underscored the importance of grassroots participation and sustained engagement with party structures.

In his appreciation message following the gathering, Nwachukwu thanked the party leaders, executives and stakeholders for their presence and contributions, reiterating his commitment to accessibility, inclusiveness and purposeful representation.

As political activities ahead of the 2027 elections continue to develop, the separate endorsements from APGA faithfuls and NDC stakeholders in Anambra South have brought renewed attention to the senator’s re-election bid and the arguments surrounding continuity in legislative representation.

The post Anambra South 2027: NDC faithful, over 1,000 APGA stakeholders declare support for Nwachukwu appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: 2027: Makinde’s record merits consideration; only Obi can match him — Mark
description:
…Sees possible alignment between APM candidate, former Anambra governor



By Juliet Umeh



Former Peoples Democratic Party chieftain, Jacob Mark, has described Oyo State Governor Seyi Makinde as a “fresh hand” for Nigeria’s leadership, saying Peter Obi is the only presidential hopeful he believes
content:
…Sees possible alignment between APM candidate, former Anambra governor

By Juliet Umeh

Former Peoples Democratic Party chieftain, Jacob Mark, has described Oyo State Governor Seyi Makinde as a “fresh hand” for Nigeria’s leadership, saying Peter Obi is the only presidential hopeful he believes can compete with him.

Mark, who recently joined the Allied Peoples Movement, APM, made the remarks during an interview on Channels Television. He said Makinde’s record in Oyo State deserved consideration ahead of the 2027 general election.

Mark said, “His record within eight years, which is seven years now, is something to look at and refer to. The only person that can compete with him is Peter Obi.

“I am happy that there is a possible alignment between them before the elections,” he said, adding that “in politics, five days is enough.”

Mark, however, said he was not aware of any ongoing discussion for Makinde to step aside for Obi or former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar.

“I am not sure I have heard that anywhere. I am not sure, because there is no discussion on that that I have heard,” he said.

The comments come ahead of a November 23 opposition summit in Abuja. Mark said any alliance should not be made compulsory, arguing that voters should have a choice among candidates.

He said, “People have a right to aspire, but Nigerians have the final say. The ballot is in the hands of Nigerians. Nigerians should be allowed to have as many choices as possible.”

He said he was backing the APM at the presidential level but would support PDP candidates in Kaduna State’s governorship and other contests.

“I participated in the primaries for the nomination of the gubernatorial candidate for the PDP. So I am going to support him,” Mark said.

title: 2027: ‘Reject rice politics, don’t sell your votes for food’ — Ex-Anambra gov, Obiano warns Nigerians
description:
Former Anambra State Governor, Willie Obiano, has urged Nigerians to reject what he described as “rice politics”, warning against allowing politicians to exploit poverty and hunger to secure electoral support.
Obiano said voters must look beyond the distribution of food items and carefully assess th
content:
Former Anambra State Governor, Willie Obiano, has urged Nigerians to reject what he described as “rice politics”, warning against allowing politicians to exploit poverty and hunger to secure electoral support.

Obiano said voters must look beyond the distribution of food items and carefully assess the character, competence and track records of candidates before electing them into public office in the 2027 general elections.

He also called on Nigerians to demand accountability from political leaders rather than celebrate the provision of basic necessities as exceptional achievements.

The former governor made the remarks while delivering the keynote address at the 11th Chinua Achebe Literary Festival and Memorial Lecture in Awka, Anambra State.

Speaking on the theme, “The Writer as a Nation-Builder: Achebe’s Literary Philosophy and the Quest for a Better Society,” Obiano urged Nigerians to embrace the legacy of the late literary icon, particularly his commitment to confronting injustice, questioning political authority and advocating responsible leadership.

He argued that Achebe did not write merely to entertain readers but used literature to expose injustice, challenge political failures, defend African identity and stimulate conversations about the future of society.

Obiano challenged Nigerian writers and intellectuals to speak out against corruption, insecurity, poor governance, historical distortion and other challenges confronting the country.

He also warned against allowing outsiders or individuals with ulterior motives to control the narration of Nigeria’s history and experiences.

Describing Achebe as an exceptional intellectual institution, the former governor said the literary icon gave Africans the confidence to tell their stories from their own perspectives while challenging misconceptions about the continent.

“Achebe remains a representative of a typical Igbo Man with great wisdom,” he said.

Obiano maintained that Achebe’s greatness went beyond his literary achievements, noting that his courage to question leadership failures and defend the dignity of African people distinguished him.

He cited Achebe’s globally acclaimed novel, Things Fall Apart, published in 1958, as one of the works that transformed international perceptions of African literature.

The former governor also recalled Achebe’s rejection of Nigeria’s national honour of Commander of the Order of the Federal Republic (CFR) on two occasions, in 2004 and 2011, describing the decisions as evidence of his commitment to principles over personal recognition.

According to Obiano, Achebe rejected the first honour under former President Olusegun Obasanjo because of concerns about political instability, lawlessness and the crisis in Anambra State.

He said the literary icon also declined the second offer under former President Goodluck Jonathan because he believed concerns about corruption, accountability and governance had not been adequately addressed.

Obiano further recalled the political crisis that engulfed Anambra between 2003 and 2004, including the abduction of then Governor Chris Ngige and the destruction of government facilities in Awka and other parts of the state.

He said Achebe’s actions demonstrated that patriotism required more than public declarations of love for one’s country, stressing that it also demanded the courage to question those entrusted with political authority.

The former governor also referenced Achebe’s 1983 book, The Trouble with Nigeria, particularly its identification of leadership failure as the country’s central problem.

He noted that issues highlighted by the late writer more than four decades ago, including corruption, tribalism, nepotism, religious intolerance, indiscipline and the celebration of mediocrity, continued to undermine Nigeria.

Obiano said the continued relevance of Achebe’s observations should concern Nigerians, particularly writers and intellectuals, who have a responsibility to examine the country’s challenges and contribute ideas capable of changing its direction.

He also advocated the restoration of history to Nigeria’s educational system and public discourse, warning that societies that neglect their past risk losing the knowledge needed to understand the present and prepare for the future.

He insisted that young Nigerians deserved accurate accounts of the country’s history, including difficult and contested periods such as the Nigerian Civil War, rather than distorted narratives, half-truths or deliberate silence.

Referencing Achebe’s famous observation that until the lions have their own historians, the history of the hunt will continue to glorify the hunter, Obiano urged Nigerians to take responsibility for documenting their experiences.

Returning to the 2027 elections, the former governor said politicians should be assessed based on their ability to provide security, quality education, employment opportunities, functional institutions and other basic necessities, rather than their distribution of food items.

He also questioned the tendency to celebrate the discharge of basic government responsibilities as extraordinary achievements, urging Nigerians to demand sustainable solutions to insecurity, poor infrastructure, unemployment, electricity challenges and rising living costs.

The post 2027: ‘Reject rice politics, don’t sell your votes for food’ — Ex-Anambra gov, Obiano warns Nigerians appeared first on Very Nigerian.

title: Eight Nigerians charged over $4.5m car theft in Canada
description:
Eight Nigerians are among 12 people charged in Canada over an alleged organised vehicle theft network linked to the recovery of 96 stolen vehicles valued at $4.5m and reportedly destined for West Africa.
Peel Regional Police in Ontario disclosed this in a statement published on its website on Monday
content:
Eight Nigerians are among 12 people charged in Canada over an alleged organised vehicle theft network linked to the recovery of 96 stolen vehicles valued at $4.5m and reportedly destined for West Africa.

Peel Regional Police in Ontario disclosed this in a statement published on its website on Monday, saying the suspects were facing a total of 231 charges following an investigation into the theft and exportation of high-value vehicles.

The investigation, known as Project Cadetta, began in March 2026 in collaboration with the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA).

It initially focused on a warehouse in Brampton, Ontario, which investigators suspected was being used to store stolen vehicles before they were shipped to West Africa through Canadian ports.

Police said the investigation later uncovered a wider criminal network operating across the Greater Toronto Area and neighbouring jurisdictions.

According to the police, five key suspects allegedly coordinated the theft, movement and exportation of the vehicles, while others assisted with loading operations, container movements and transporting vehicles with altered identification numbers.

The 96 recovered vehicles, including luxury sport utility vehicles and pickup trucks, were discovered concealed in shipping containers.

Those listed among the accused with Nigerian names include Stanley Udeh, 46, of Brampton; Odewale Abraham, 57; Oluyemi Sodade, 51; Tosin Damilola Oyebade, 45; Oluwaseyi Olawale Bameke, 39; and Olushola Oke, 42, all of Toronto.

Others are Gbolahan Qudus Babatunde, 29, of Vaughan, and Kenneth Okafor, 58, who was listed as having no fixed address.

The other accused are Karamveer Singh, 26, of Brampton; Henrik Gancz, 57; Jaspreet Singh, 25, both listed as having no fixed address; and Darryl Davance, 25, of Saint-Jerome, Quebec.

The suspects face charges including possession of property obtained by crime, trafficking in stolen goods valued at more than $5,000, forgery and uttering forged documents. One of them also faces a charge of dangerous operation of a motor vehicle.

Police said nine of the accused were charged and released with future court dates, while the remaining three were held for bail hearings and subsequently released.

The force added that some of the accused could face immigration enforcement action, including possible removal from Canada, after their criminal cases have been concluded.

Commenting on the operation, Deputy Chief of Peel Regional Police, Nick Milinovich, described organised vehicle theft as a criminal business that supports wider illegal activities.

“Organized auto theft is a predatory business model run by transnational syndicates that terrorize families and fund broader criminal enterprises. Through Project Cadetta, our Commercial Auto Crime Bureau and partners dismantled this supply chain from street-level thieves to international export brokers. We have already driven auto thefts in Peel down by more than 50 per cent since our 2023 peak, and we are not taking our foot off the gas—there is no safe harbour in Peel for organized crime.”

Ontario’s Solicitor General, Michael Kerzner, also commended the police and their partners for disrupting the alleged criminal network.

He said the operation reflected the government’s commitment to tackling organised vehicle theft and protecting communities.

The CBSA’s Acting Regional Director General for the Greater Toronto Area, Trishann Pascal, said the agency worked with the police to prevent stolen vehicles from reaching international markets through container inspections and intelligence sharing.

Peel Regional Police said investigations were ongoing, with more charges expected. It also disclosed that arrest warrants had been issued for additional suspects.

The police further reported that vehicle thefts across Peel Region had dropped by more than 50 per cent since reaching a peak in 2023, with a further 10 per cent decline recorded year-to-date in 2026.

title: South Korea Tightens Exam Security After AI Cheating Scandal
description: South Korea will deploy thousands of extra personnel to prevent cheating on its college entrance exam sites this week and may introduce tougher penalties, Prime Minister Han Seong-sook said Tuesday.The announcement comes after an individual confessed on Sunday to cheating on the national tax account
content:
South Korea will deploy thousands of extra personnel to prevent cheating on its college entrance exam sites this week and may introduce tougher penalties, Prime Minister Han Seong-sook said Tuesday.

The announcement comes after an individual confessed on Sunday to cheating on the national tax accountant exam using artificial intelligence tools, an admission that brought panic ahead of the college test.

Known as the Suneung, the intense once-a-year exam — widely seen as a ticket to well-paid jobs and even better marriage prospects — will bring much of South Korea to a standstill on Thursday to minimise distractions.

As a measure to detect phones that have not been handed over, an emergency alert will be sent before the exam begins, Han said at a press conference.

Students will also be ordered to place their glasses on their desks so supervisors can verify they are not smart devices.

“We also strongly urge students to avoid wearing clothing with buttons wherever possible,” Han said.

Students “will be asked to roll up both sleeves, and collars, buttons and other areas will also be checked to determine whether electronic devices, including miniature cameras, are concealed”, she added.

Those caught cheating could be banned from taking the Suneung for 10 years, up from the current one-year restriction, Han said.

The government will also file criminal complaints over serious cases of cheating, including those involving smart devices.

In addition to the 75,000 supervisors deployed to 1,312 test centres nationwide, an additional 8,400 personnel will be deployed this year.

“You may feel nervous and intimidated by the unfamiliar atmosphere inside and outside examination centres and the stricter inspection procedures,” said Han, addressing the 550,000 students who will take the Suneung.

The extra staff “are minimum safeguards designed to protect the value of the hard work you have put in over the years and to guarantee a fair competition in which everyone can hold their head high”, she added.

At a meeting held Sunday, officials decided to investigate all suspected cases of cheating involving AI across national qualification examinations.

The individual who confessed to cheating said he had photographed the exam questions with a miniature camera before using AI and checking the answers on his smartphone.

Han said the government “will define such cheating as a ‘social evil'”.

AFP

title: Fire From Gas Explosion Razes Seven Classrooms, Vehicles In Lagos
description: A fire outbreak caused by a gas explosion at an NNPC filling station along Command-Ekoro Road, Alimosho, Lagos State, has burnt down a total of seven classrooms, a DAF truck, and a Toyota Camry, with registration number EKY 430 JS.The Lagos State Emergency Management Agency disclosed this in a state
content:
A fire outbreak caused by a gas explosion at an NNPC filling station along Command-Ekoro Road, Alimosho, Lagos State, has burnt down a total of seven classrooms, a DAF truck, and a Toyota Camry, with registration number EKY 430 JS.

The Lagos State Emergency Management Agency disclosed this in a statement signed by its Permanent Secretary, Dr Olufemi Oke-Osanyintolu, on Monday.

According to the statement, the fire also destroyed three fuel dispensing pumps and electrical appliances in the affected classrooms.

The inferno reportedly started while a tanker was discharging diesel at the filling station before spreading to the adjoining St. Lawrence Greater Height School.

According to Oke-Osanyintolu, LASEMA’s Igando-based Beta Team was deployed to the scene after receiving a distress call.

He said preliminary investigations indicated that the fire started from a tanker while discharging diesel before spreading to the filling station’s dispensing pumps and the adjoining school building.

“On arrival, responders discovered that fire had engulfed the NNPC filling station and had also spread to the adjoining St. Lawrence Greater Height School.

“To the glory of God and the dedication of the responders, no casualty was recorded in the incident. The Government, however, acknowledges with deep sympathy the material losses recorded,” he stated.

Oke-Osanyintolu said the combined efforts of LASEMA, the Lagos State Fire and Rescue Service, the National Emergency Management Agency, the Lagos State Ambulance Service, the Lagos State Traffic Management Authority, the Lagos Neighbourhood Safety Corps and police officers from the Ile-Iwe Division led to the successful extinguishing of the fire.

Meanwhile, he disclosed that the agency also responded to two other emergencies in different parts of the state on the same day.

In a separate incident, a Mack tipper broke down at Ladipo Bus Stop, inward Ikeja, following a mechanical fault involving its shaft, obstructing vehicular movement.

Oke-Osanyintolu said the response team worked with LASTMA to divert traffic and deployed heavy-duty equipment to remove the vehicle from the road.

“The Response Team, alongside the Lagos State Traffic Management Authority, diverted oncoming vehicles to prevent secondary accidents, while the Agency’s heavy-duty equipment, Super Metro, was deployed for recovery. The broken-down tipper was successfully recovered off the road and parked at a layby, thereby ensuring free vehicular movement, and the operation was concluded with the Response Team and equipment returning to base in good condition,” he stated.

In another incident at Alaro City, along the Epe Expressway, a tanker conveying 45,000 litres of Premium Motor Spirit (PMS) overturned after its driver reportedly lost control while attempting to avoid a Dangote truck overtaking it at close range.

The tanker had registration number AKD-387YK.

According to Oke-Osanyintolu, no casualty was recorded, while firefighters applied foam to the tanker to prevent a possible fire outbreak. He added that the petroleum product was subsequently transferred to another tanker before the overturned vehicle was recovered.

The Lagos State Government urged filling station operators, tanker drivers and motorists to observe safety regulations, ensure regular vehicle maintenance and avoid speeding and dangerous overtaking.

The government also appealed to school owners and managers to maintain clear emergency access routes and cooperate with emergency responders.

He added, “The Lagos State Government uses this moment to appeal passionately to filling station operators, tanker drivers and motorists to adhere strictly to safety protocols, particularly during the discharge of petroleum products, ensure regular maintenance of vehicles, avoid speeding and dangerous overtaking, and remain vigilant at all times”.

title: ₦100m Extortion, ₦2bn Transaction: Reps probe mining marshals, summon NSCDC boss
description: The House of Representatives Committee on Solid Minerals has given the Commandant-General of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), Prof. Ahmed Abubakar Audi, 24 hours to appear before it over allegations of financial irregularities, extortion, unlawful arrests and abuse of power invo
content:
The House of Representatives Committee on Solid Minerals has given the Commandant-General of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), Prof. Ahmed Abubakar Audi, 24 hours to appear before it over allegations of financial irregularities, extortion, unlawful arrests and abuse of power involving personnel of the Mining Marshals.

The committee is also investigating the circumstances surrounding the death of a serving NSCDC officer, Deputy Superintendent Agada Levi Agada, whose family alleged that he was shot dead by fellow officers at a mining site.

The ultimatum was issued on Monday during an investigative hearing following a motion moved by Ali Amburura, representing Sokoto State, and seconded by a lawmaker from Katsina State.

Chairman of the committee, Gaza Gbefwi, said the lawmakers would examine complaints of harassment and unlawful detention of licensed mining operators, an alleged ₦2 billion transaction linked to the bank account of a former state commander, and suspected misconduct among Mining Marshals operating across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory.

The investigation will also cover the procurement of operational vehicles and the sources of funding for the special security unit.

Gbefwi recalled that more than 2,200 Mining Marshals were inaugurated in March 2024 to tackle illegal mining and protect the country’s mineral resources.

He, however, warned that the initiative must not become an avenue for violating citizens’ fundamental rights or conducting operations outside the provisions of the law.

One of the major issues raised at the hearing was the death of Agada, whose family accused fellow NSCDC personnel of shooting him.

Presenting a petition on behalf of the family, their lawyer, Obasi-Obi Nwabueze, alleged that the deceased sustained a gunshot wound to the right side of his chest after being shot by fellow officers.

He told the lawmakers that medical affidavits from doctors who attended to Agada contradicted the NSCDC’s account that the officer died following an attack by bandits.

According to the lawyer, Agada was taken to three medical facilities before he eventually died at the Federal Medical Centre, Keffi.

Nwabueze further alleged that two NSCDC officers were indicted and three others arrested during a police investigation into the incident. He, however, claimed that the investigation was subsequently frustrated.

He urged the committee to ensure that the investigation was concluded and that anyone found culpable was prosecuted.

The lawyer also appealed for protection for the deceased officer’s widow, two children and other witnesses, alleging that some had received threats and faced intimidation.

In response, Gbefwi expressed condolences to the family and requested an executive summary of the petition to enable the committee to consider further action.

The lawmakers also heard allegations from Stone Rockers Nigeria Limited, whose Director of Communications, Rachel Ogbonna, accused the Mining Marshals of unlawfully arresting 12 workers at the company’s quarry site despite its possession of valid operating licences.

Ogbonna alleged that the company’s chairman and director were also detained after visiting an NSCDC facility along Airport Road in an attempt to secure the release of the workers.

In a separate submission, security operative Odey Cosmas Polycarp accused the Mining Marshals, allegedly led by one Onoja Attah, of arresting members of his workforce and demanding ₦100 million for their release.

Polycarp claimed that the workers were arrested in a residential area where no mining activities were taking place. He also alleged that the detainees were beaten while in custody.

The allegations have raised concerns about the operations, accountability and enforcement powers of the Mining Marshals, particularly their treatment of licensed mining operators and the conduct of personnel deployed to tackle illegal mining.

The committee is expected to hear from the NSCDC leadership and other relevant stakeholders as it investigates the alleged ₦2 billion transaction, the reported ₦100 million extortion demand, the death of Agada and questions surrounding the unit’s funding and procurement activities.

The NSCDC leadership’s response to the allegations was not contained in the submissions presented at the hearing.

The post ₦100m Extortion, ₦2bn Transaction: Reps probe mining marshals, summon NSCDC boss appeared first on Very Nigerian.

title: France, Malaysia Boost Cooperation On Rare Earths, Defense
description: France and Malaysia agreed on Tuesday to deepen ties in the lucrative field of rare earth minerals and in defence, with visiting President Emmanuel Macron hailing a “new milestone” in relations.Macron, who is on a two-day whistle-stop tour of the Southeast Asian nation, told a news confe
content:
France and Malaysia agreed on Tuesday to deepen ties in the lucrative field of rare earth minerals and in defence, with visiting President Emmanuel Macron hailing a “new milestone” in relations.

Macron, who is on a two-day whistle-stop tour of the Southeast Asian nation, told a news conference that a joint rare earths project will include “the option for refining in France” — a “unique” agreement, according to Malaysia’s Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim.

Malaysia plays a major role in rare earth processing, courted by many countries as an important option outside China, which holds a monopoly on critical minerals used in products ranging from smartphones to fighter jets, electric cars and wind turbines.

The country already hosts the largest rare earths processing plant outside of China, and the planned project between French firm Carester and Malaysia’s Malaco Mining would add another 13,000 tonnes of processed minerals, including those needed for high-performance magnets.

Macron said the joint project was set for an operational launch early next year.

It will “not only encompass extraction, but also local processing of reserved volumes and capacities, including the option for refining in France, which was a key element for our entire value chain,” Macron said.

Anwar said that “we have done something which is unique”, adding: “We do not export raw materials. But with France, we’ll do so because you are committed to that — processing and working with Malaysians as a team”.

Carester in July announced plans with Malaco to build a rare earths separation plant in Malaysia’s northern Perak state under a 10-year joint venture.

Macron’s visit also saw the two governments sign agreements on defence, energy supply and digital cooperation.

This included the establishment of a regional centre for “countering hybrid threats” and the provision of Airbus-built search-and-rescue helicopters to the Malaysian armed forces.

“As we approach the 70th anniversary of our diplomatic relations, our two countries are reaching a new milestone with this visit,” Macron said.

Bilateral trade between France and Malaysia reached more than 4.9 billion euros ($5.4 billion) last year.

AFP

title: Wabara rejects A’Court ruling on PDP leadership crisis, warns against making Tinubu sole presidential candidate
description:
Ex- Senate President and Chairman of the Board of Trustees (BoT) of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), Senator Adolphus Wabara has rejected the Appeal Court’s ruling in the PDP leadership crisis, describing it as travesty of justice.
This is even as Wabara has warned against using the courts to mak
content:
Ex- Senate President and Chairman of the Board of Trustees (BoT) of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), Senator Adolphus Wabara has rejected the Appeal Court’s ruling in the PDP leadership crisis, describing it as travesty of justice.

This is even as Wabara has warned against using the courts to make Tinubu a sole presidential candidate in 2027, saying that will not in its own save the APC.

Wabara accused the All Progressives Congress (APC) of systematic weakening of opposition parties using public institutions and warned the ruling party to accept responsibility should Nigeria’s democracy suffer any setback.

The Court of Appeal, in a unanimous decision by a three-member panel, had declined to upturn the July 17, judgment of the Federal High Court in Abuja, which dismissed the suit filed by the Wabara-led BoT faction.

The appellate court held that the trial judge, Justice Salim Ibrahim, was right to have dismissed the suit seeking to validate actions taken on behalf of the PDP by the Tanimu Turaki, SAN-led faction.

Those actions included a national convention organised by the faction, which subsequently announced former President Goodluck Jonathan as its consensus presidential candidate for the 2027 election.

In the lead judgment delivered virtually by Justice R. O. Ayoola, the appellate court held that the Wabara-led group lacked the locus standi to institute the action on behalf of the PDP.

It consequently struck out the party’s name as the eighth appellant and held that the appeal had become academic and amounted to an abuse of judicial process.

However, expressing strong reservations over the judgment, Wabara accused the APC of benefiting from the protracted crises in opposition parties and warned that attempts to weaken political alternatives ahead of the 2027 general elections could undermine Nigeria’s democratic foundations.

He described the appellate court’s refusal to compel the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to recognise his faction’s position as a travesty of justice, insisting that the circumstances surrounding the emergence of the Alhaji Abdulrahman Muhammad-led faction raised serious questions about democracy in Nigeria.

He warned that accepting the Muhammad-led faction’s position without adequately addressing the issues surrounding its emergence amounted to “standing truth in the head”.

Wabara expressed surprise at what he described as the Appeal Court’s questionable legal reasoning, wondering how it arrived at what he called an inverted interpretation of the issues before it.

He cautioned the judiciary against becoming entangled in political disputes in ways that could further erode public confidence in the institution.

“The growing legal battles within opposition parties, particularly the PDP, the African Democratic Congress (ADC), and the Nigeria Democratic Congress, (NDC), have raised troubling questions about the ability of opposition parties to participate effectively in the 2027 elections”.

Wabara alleged that the APC was benefiting from the weakening of opposition parties and urged the judiciary to protect its independence and credibility by ensuring that its decisions do not create the impression of favouring any political interest.

“The opposition should be allowed to breathe. Nigeria cannot afford a situation where formidable opposition parties are weakened to the point that nobody can effectively challenge the ruling party in 2027.

“Tinubu should not be made a sole presidential candidate in 2027. That would be anti-democratic and a dangerous precedent capable of bringing avoidable embarrassment to our country.

“Using the courts to make Tinubu the sole presidential candidate in 2027 will not save the APC,” he declared.

Wabara recalled that the APC itself benefited from a competitive political environment before taking power in 2015, and challenged the ruling party to demonstrate its confidence in its performance by allowing opposition parties to operate freely.

title: Mother Bear On The Loose Prompts Japan City To Shut Schools
description: Authorities in Japan’s Maebashi city ordered school closures as officials were looking for a bear on the loose on Tuesday, after media reports said at least one person had been attacked.Officials in the city north of Tokyo have captured a cub, one of two animals seen roaming in residential are
content:
Authorities in Japan’s Maebashi city ordered school closures as officials were looking for a bear on the loose on Tuesday, after media reports said at least one person had been attacked.

Officials in the city north of Tokyo have captured a cub, one of two animals seen roaming in residential areas. The search for the bear believed to be its mother continues.

Bear sightings nationwide have sharply decreased from the last fiscal year, when a record 13 people were killed.

Still, experts say growing bear populations, declining human populations in rural areas, and fluctuations in the availability of food in mountains have driven the animals into residential neighborhoods in search of food.

In a post on X, Maebashi Mayor Akira Ogawa urged residents to stay indoors, warning of “an extremely dangerous situation”.

“All residents, especially those living in the areas where the animals have been and the surrounding neighborhoods, are urged to refrain from non-essential outings such as walks and to act with safety as your top priority,” she said.

The mayor said one person was injured, without elaborating.

Local media said a man in his 50s suffered a non-life-threatening injury.

With the search ongoing, officials said the city’s schools will be closed on Wednesday as a precaution.

In September alone, 1,759 bear sightings were reported nationwide, sharply lower than the 4,766 cases recorded a year earlier.

AFP

title: Abia sacks Enyimba management, technical crew over poor performance
description:
The Abia State Government has announced the immediate dissolution of the management structure and technical crew of Enyimba International Football Club, Aba.
In a statement issued on Tuesday, the state Commissioner for Information, Okey Kanu, said the decision was “in a decisive move to address the
content:
The Abia State Government has announced the immediate dissolution of the management structure and technical crew of Enyimba International Football Club, Aba.

In a statement issued on Tuesday, the state Commissioner for Information, Okey Kanu, said the decision was “in a decisive move to address the club’s recent disappointing performances and identified administrative and structural challenges”.

The statement said the decision “underscores the government’s resolve to undertake a comprehensive restructuring of the two-time CAF Champions League winners, restore the club’s competitive identity and reposition it for sustainable success in Nigerian and continental football”.

It further stated, “Following a review of the club’s current state of affairs, the government has concluded that far-reaching interventions are necessary to address the underlying issues affecting its performance, administration and overall operations.

“Consequently, the Ministry of Sports and Youth Development has been mandated to lead the restructuring process, undertake a comprehensive assessment of the club’s management framework and implement appropriate administrative, technical, operational and institutional reforms aimed at restoring stability, accountability and competitiveness.

“The dissolution takes immediate effect”.

The government directed all affected management and technical personnel, as well as anyone in possession of Enyimba International FC’s assets, properties, official documents, equipment and other institutional materials, “to ensure an orderly and formal handover of all such items to the Ministry of Sports and Youth Development”.

According to the statement, the ministry will communicate further details regarding the handover arrangements and subsequent administrative procedures.

The Abia State Government acknowledged Enyimba’s historic place in Nigerian and African football as one of the country’s most successful and decorated football institutions, noting that “the club’s legacy remains an important sporting heritage of Abia State, and the government is determined to safeguard that legacy while laying the foundation for a more professionally managed and competitive future”.

The government also reassured Enyimba supporters, players, stakeholders and the general public that the intervention was aimed at securing the club’s long-term interests, strengthening its institutional capacity and restoring the pride, identity and competitive standards associated with the Enyimba name.

The post Abia sacks Enyimba management, technical crew over poor performance appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Vanguard Online Editor Olufemi Ajasa dies at 44
description:
Vanguard Media Limited has announced the death of its Online Editor, Olufemi Finayon Ajasa, who passed away on Sunday at the Lagos University Teaching Hospital (LUTH) after a brief illness. He was 44.
The company announced his death in a statement issued by its Editor, Eze Anaba, describing the loss
content:
Vanguard Media Limited has announced the death of its Online Editor, Olufemi Finayon Ajasa, who passed away on Sunday at the Lagos University Teaching Hospital (LUTH) after a brief illness. He was 44.

The company announced his death in a statement issued by its Editor, Eze Anaba, describing the loss as a major blow to the Vanguard family and the journalism profession.

Ajasa was a valued member of the organisation, where he made significant contributions to the growth of its digital operations and online journalism.

Born into the Ajasa family of Ajido in Badagry Local Government Area of Lagos State, he obtained a Bachelor of Science degree in Mass Communication, specialising in Journalism, from Lagos State University between 2004 and 2009.

He further strengthened his professional skills in 2015 after obtaining a certificate in Advanced Writing and Reporting Skills from the School of Media and Communication, Pan-Atlantic University.

Ajasa began his journalism career as a photojournalist with National Mirror Newspaper in February 2012, where he worked until November 2013.

He joined Vanguard Media Limited in December 2013 as an online reporter and content developer, remaining with the organisation until September 2016.

He later moved to TheNewsGuru.com, where he worked between 2016 and 2021, serving first as Online Editor before becoming Team Lead and Head of Digital Operations.

In December 2021, he joined Pulse as Editorial Quality Assurance Manager before returning to Vanguard in June 2022 as Online Editor, a position he held until his death.

His return to Vanguard marked the continuation of a professional relationship with the organisation that began early in his journalism career.

In the statement, the management of Vanguard Media Limited expressed deep sorrow over his death and extended condolences to his immediate family, friends, professional associates and colleagues.

The company also prayed for strength and comfort for the bereaved family, while wishing the deceased eternal rest.

The Service of Songs and Wake-Keep in his honour is scheduled to hold on Thursday, November 19, at 5 p.m. at 14 Sylvia Crescent, Anthony Village, Lagos.

The family is expected to announce other funeral arrangements.

title: Vanguard online editor dies
description:
The Online Editor of Vanguard Media Limited, Olufemi Finayon Ajasa, is dead.
Ajasa died on Sunday at the Lagos University Teaching Hospital after a brief illness, the management of Vanguard Media Limited has announced.
In a Monday statement signed by the Editor of Vanguard, Eze Anaba, the management
content:
The Online Editor of Vanguard Media Limited, Olufemi Finayon Ajasa, is dead.

Ajasa died on Sunday at the Lagos University Teaching Hospital after a brief illness, the management of Vanguard Media Limited has announced.

In a Monday statement signed by the Editor of Vanguard, Eze Anaba, the management described his death as a massive loss to the organisation and the journalism profession.

“His death is a massive loss to the Vanguard family and the journalism profession,” the statement said.

The management said the 44-year-old Ajasa was a valued member of the organisation who made significant contributions to the growth of its digital operations and online journalism.

Born into the Ajasa family of Ajido, in Badagry Local Government Area of Lagos State, he obtained a Bachelor of Science degree in Mass Communication, specialising in Journalism, from Lagos State University between 2004 and 2009.

He also obtained a certification in Advanced Writing and Reporting Skills from the School of Media and Communication, Pan-Atlantic University, in 2015.

Ajasa began his journalism career as a photojournalist with National Mirror Newspaper in February 2012, where he worked until November 2013.

He joined Vanguard Media Limited in December 2013 as an online reporter and content developer, serving until September 2016.

He subsequently moved to TheNewsGuru.com, where he worked from 2016 to 2021, first as Online Editor and later as Team Lead and Head of Digital Operations.

In December 2021, he joined Pulse as Editorial Quality Assurance Manager before returning to Vanguard in June 2022 as Online Editor, a position he held until his death.

The management said Ajasa’s return to the organisation marked the continuation of a relationship that began early in his professional career.

It expressed condolences to his immediate family, friends, professional associates and members of the Vanguard family.

“The management of Vanguard Media Limited deeply regrets this irreparable loss and extends its heartfelt condolences to his immediate family, friends, professional associates and all members of the Vanguard family,” the statement said.

The statement added that the organisation’s thoughts and prayers were with his family, expressing hope that God would grant them the strength and fortitude to bear the loss.

The Service of Songs/Wake-Keep in his honour will hold at 14 Sylvia Crescent, Anthony Village, Lagos, on Thursday, November 19, at 5 pm.

Other funeral arrangements will be announced by the family.

The post Vanguard online editor dies appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: ADC crisis: Gombe asks INEC to recognise him as chairman
description:
A factional leader of the African Democratic Congress, Nafiu Gombe, has formally written to the Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission regarding his resumption as the National Chairman of the African Democratic Congress.
The letter, dated November 16, 2026, which was issued by Gom
content:
A factional leader of the African Democratic Congress, Nafiu Gombe, has formally written to the Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission regarding his resumption as the National Chairman of the African Democratic Congress.

The letter, dated November 16, 2026, which was issued by Gombe and sighted by PUNCH Online on Tuesday, was titled, ‘Notification of resumption of duty as National Chairman pursuant to the declaration delivered by Hon. Justice Peter Lifu on 5th November, 2026,’ with reference number ADC/NHQ/CH/2026/001.

Gombe requested that the commission update its portal to this effect and also recognise him for official purposes.

On November 5, 2026, the Federal High Court in Abuja nullified the ADC leadership led by former Senate President David Mark and invalidated all decisions taken by the party under its leadership, including the emergence of former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar as its presidential candidate for the 2027 general elections.

Justice Peter Lifu, in his judgment, declared the Mark-led Caretaker Committee illegal, nullifying the process through which it conducted the party’s presidential primary that produced Atiku as its flag bearer.

The court also nullified the emergence of former Minister of Interior, Rauf Aregbesola, as National Secretary, as well as the appointments of other national officers and the nominations of candidates presented by the party for the 2027 elections.

Based on this, Gombe noted that owing to the “valid and subsisting judgment of the Honourable Court,” his resumption has commenced with immediate effect.

The letter read, “I write in my capacity as the National Chairman of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) to formally notify the Commission of my resumption of duty.

“This notification follows the declaration delivered on the 5th day of November, 2026, by Hon. Justice Peter Lifu of the Federal High Court, Abuja Division, in Suit No. FHC/ABJ/CS/1819/2025, Hon. Nafiu Bala Gombe V. African Democratic Congress & 4 Others, wherein the Honourable Court declared and affirmed my position as the National Chairman of the Party.

“In obedience to the said valid and subsisting judgment of the Honourable Court, I have resumed duty as the National Chairman of the African Democratic Congress with immediate effect.

“Accordingly, I respectfully request the Commission to take formal notice of this resumption; recognise me as the National Chairman of the African Democratic Congress for all official purposes, correspondence, and filings; and update the Commission’s portal accordingly.”

Gombe equally noted that he had attached a “Certified True Copy of the judgement/declaration of the Honourable Court” for INEC’s record and necessary action.

He assured the commission of his commitment to “constitutional order, due process and a harmonious working relationship” in the interest of democracy.

On Sunday, November 15, The PUNCH reported that Gombe extended an olive branch to former Vice-President Abubakar, Mark and other party chieftains, calling for reconciliation and a united front ahead of the 2027 general elections.

In an interview with the BBC Hausa Service, Gombe said he was ready to work with the party’s opposing faction to rebuild the party and strengthen the opposition, despite a recent Federal High Court judgment, which he described as a vindication of his faction’s position in the protracted leadership dispute.

The post ADC crisis: Gombe asks INEC to recognise him as chairman appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Canada charges eight Nigerians, four others over $4.5m car theft
description:
Twelve people, including Nigerians, have been charged in Canada over an alleged organised vehicle theft network that police say recovered 96 stolen vehicles worth $4.5m and destined for West Africa.
Peel Regional Police in Ontario announced the arrests in a statement posted on its website on Monday.
content:
Twelve people, including Nigerians, have been charged in Canada over an alleged organised vehicle theft network that police say recovered 96 stolen vehicles worth $4.5m and destined for West Africa.

Peel Regional Police in Ontario announced the arrests in a statement posted on its website on Monday.

It said the suspects faced 231 charges following an investigation into the theft and exportation of luxury sport utility vehicles, pickup trucks and other high-value vehicles concealed in shipping containers.

The investigation, code-named Project Cadetta, was launched in March 2026 in partnership with the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA).

It initially focused on a warehouse in Brampton, Ontario, allegedly used as a staging area for stolen vehicles being prepared for shipment to West Africa through Canadian ports.

Police said the investigation later uncovered a wider criminal network operating across the Greater Toronto Area and neighbouring jurisdictions.

According to the police, five key suspects allegedly coordinated the theft, movement and export of the vehicles, while other accused persons supported the operation through loading sites, container movements and the transportation of vehicles whose identification numbers had been altered.

The 96 recovered vehicles were found concealed in shipping containers, police said.

The charge sheet released by the police listed eight individuals with Nigerian names and four other nationals.

They include “Stanley Udeh, 46, of Brampton; Odewale Abraham, 57; Oluyemi Sodade, 51; Tosin Damilola Oyebade, 45; Oluwaseyi Olawale Bameke, 39; and Olushola Oke, 42, all of Toronto.”

Others are “Gbolahan Qudus Babatunde, 29, of Vaughan; Karamveer Singh, 26, of Brampton; Henrik Gancz, 57; Kenneth Okafor, 58; Jaspreet Singh, 25, all listed as having no fixed address; and Darryl Davance, 25, of Saint-Jerome, Quebec.”

The accused face various charges, including possession of property obtained by crime, trafficking in stolen goods valued at more than `$5,000, forgery and uttering forged documents. One of them also faces a charge of dangerous operation of a motor vehicle.

Peel Regional Police said nine of the accused were charged and released with future court dates, while three were held for bail hearings and subsequently released.

The police added that some of the accused could face immigration enforcement action, including possible removal from Canada, after the conclusion of their criminal proceedings.

Commenting on the investigation, Deputy Chief of Peel Regional Police, Nick Milinovich, said organised vehicle theft was linked to wider criminal activities.

“Organized auto theft is a predatory business model run by transnational syndicates that terrorize families and fund broader criminal enterprises. Through Project Cadetta, our Commercial Auto Crime Bureau and partners dismantled this supply chain from street-level thieves to international export brokers. We have already driven auto thefts in Peel down by more than 50 per cent since our 2023 peak, and we are not taking our foot off the gas—there is no safe harbour in Peel for organized crime.”

Ontario’s Solicitor General, Michael Kerzner, said the operation demonstrated the government’s commitment to tackling organised criminal networks.

“Organized auto theft is a serious crime that threatens the safety and security of our communities, and our government will never back down from taking on the criminal networks responsible. Project Cadetta is another example of the outstanding work being done by Peel Regional Police and their law enforcement partners to dismantle these sophisticated operations and hold offenders accountable. Through investments like our Preventing Auto Theft Grant, we are ensuring police have the tools and resources they need to disrupt organized crime, recover stolen vehicles and protect Ontario families.”

The Canada Border Services Agency’s Acting Regional Director General for the Greater Toronto Area, Trishann Pascal, said the agency helped prevent stolen vehicles from reaching international markets.

“CBSA officers play a critical role in stopping stolen vehicles from reaching international markets through targeted container examinations and referrals. The CBSA is helping to disrupt organized crime networks by combining intelligence, expertise and coordinated action with law enforcement partners. This investigation demonstrates the impact of that partnership.”

Peel Regional Police said the investigation remained ongoing and further charges were anticipated. It also disclosed that arrest warrants had been issued for additional individuals.

The police said auto thefts across Peel Region had declined by more than 50 per cent since reaching a peak in 2023, with a further 10 per cent reduction recorded year-to-date in 2026.

The post Canada charges eight Nigerians, four others over $4.5m car theft appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Epstein’s death was murder, not suicide — Forensic expert
description:
A forensic expert has questioned the official conclusion that convicted American sex offender Jeffrey Epstein died by suicide in prison in 2019, saying his examination of autopsy photographs and medical records suggests he was strangled.
Professor Michael Freeman, who reviewed the New York City medi
content:
A forensic expert has questioned the official conclusion that convicted American sex offender Jeffrey Epstein died by suicide in prison in 2019, saying his examination of autopsy photographs and medical records suggests he was strangled.

Professor Michael Freeman, who reviewed the New York City medical examiner’s files, told the BBC’s Newsnight on Monday that he believed Epstein was killed, most likely by strangulation from behind.

Epstein was found dead in his cell at the Metropolitan Correctional Centre in New York on August 10, 2019, while awaiting trial on federal sex trafficking charges.

The medical examiner who conducted the autopsy ruled that his injuries were consistent with suicide by hanging and said there was no evidence of the defensive wounds typically expected in a homicide.

However, Freeman said his review identified injuries that he believed pointed to an assault, including a deep haemorrhage to Epstein’s left shoulder and marks that appeared consistent with blows to the face.

He said the evidence suggested that a ligature was used to strangle Epstein before the same material was used to suspend his body from the bunk bed.

Freeman also pointed to what he described as fingernail marks above the ligature mark on Epstein’s neck.

He said the marks “would be consistent with strangulation, particularly from behind. And the attempt by the victim to try to remove the ligature from the neck”.

He added, “The injuries and the way the body was found don’t match up. There’s only one remaining explanation then, and that is that the death was as a result of a homicide.”

He said he would have expected investigators examining a death by hanging in custody to have taken a photograph of the body before it was removed.

Freeman, who has served as a cause-of-death expert for US attorneys-general in cases involving deaths in police custody, including that of George Floyd, published his research and the medical examiner’s files after presenting his findings in London on Monday.

BBC reports that he did not examine Epstein’s body. His assessment was based on photographs and documents from the autopsy report supplied by Epstein’s brother, Mark Epstein, who has consistently maintained that his brother was murdered.

Freeman said his research was independent and that he had not been paid by Mark Epstein. However, his findings have not been peer-reviewed.

Asked who might have killed Epstein if his interpretation was correct, Freeman said he had “no idea”.

“That is not something I have an opinion about. That isn’t any part of any investigation that I’ve done,” he said.

Responding to suggestions that his conclusions could fuel conspiracy theories, Freeman said, “I have the luxury of being able to say, don’t take my word for it, let everybody look at it.

“If you think I’m still a conspiracy theorist because I’m looking at something that looks like a strangulation and say, I think it is a strangulation and I don’t think it could be a hanging, show me where I got it wrong.

“I’m wide open to that. I’m an academic. I’m quite happy to hear people’s theories on things that are informed.”

The medical examiner who performed Epstein’s autopsy, Dr Barbara Sampson, previously defended the suicide ruling, telling the BBC, “I stand firmly behind our determination of the cause and manner of death for Mr Epstein.”

Sampson had told the US Department of Justice’s Office of the Inspector General that Epstein’s injuries were more consistent with suicide by hanging than homicide by strangulation, adding that there was no evidence of defensive wounds associated with strangulation victims.

The BBC said it had approached Sampson for further comment.

A US Department of Justice investigation into Epstein’s time in prison said a guard who discovered his body called another colleague for assistance, after which they lowered him to the floor and attempted to resuscitate him.

The report also said Epstein had been briefly placed on suicide watch a month before his death.

Epstein was convicted in 2008 of soliciting prostitution from a minor and was registered as a sex offender. He avoided a lengthy prison sentence through a plea deal.

In 2019, he was charged with operating a sex trafficking network involving underage girls and was awaiting trial when he died.

The case has continued to attract international attention because of Epstein’s connections to influential figures in politics, business and royalty.

His longtime associate, Ghislaine Maxwell, was convicted in 2021 of helping him sexually abuse underage girls and sentenced to 20 years in prison.

Documents released in connection with the investigations have also featured prominent names, including former US President Bill Clinton, President Donald Trump and Britain’s former Prince Andrew, although being named in the records does not establish criminal wrongdoing.

The post Epstein’s death was murder, not suicide — Forensic expert appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Customs officers must outsmart smugglers, go intelligence-led — Adeniyi
description:
Says technology should drive operations







By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief







The Comptroller-General of the Nigeria Customs Service (NCS), Mr. Adewale Adeniyi, has challenged officers of the Service to stay ahead of smugglers by adopting intelligence-led operations, deploying technology an
content:
Says technology should drive operations

By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief

The Comptroller-General of the Nigeria Customs Service (NCS), Mr. Adewale Adeniyi, has challenged officers of the Service to stay ahead of smugglers by adopting intelligence-led operations, deploying technology and strengthening professionalism in the discharge of their duties.

Adeniyi, who gave the charge at the inaugural Customs Police Summit in Abuja, yesterday, said criminal networks were becoming increasingly sophisticated, requiring Customs officers to devise smarter strategies to combat smuggling and other transnational crimes.

He said the era of relying largely on conventional enforcement methods was giving way to intelligence-driven operations capable of identifying and disrupting criminal networks.

His words: “Criminal networks have grown more sophisticated. They use the same routes as legitimate traders to move firearm components, narcotics, fake medicines, protected wildlife and illicit funds, often through digital channels. Our answers must be smarter; they must not be harder.”

The Customs boss called for a more professional, accountable and technology-driven Customs Police Unit (CPU) to tackle emerging security threats, combat illicit trade, strengthen institutional integrity and protect the nation’s borders.

He charged CPU personnel to demonstrate the highest standards of integrity, stressing that the Service must lead by example before demanding accountability from traders and members of the public.

“Before we demand integrity from traders and the public, we must show it ourselves,” he said.

Adeniyi also cautioned officers against abusing their enforcement powers, noting that the Nigeria Customs Service Act 2023 had conferred extensive police powers on the Service, which must be exercised within the limits of the law.

“Authority requires restraint. The NCS Act 2023 gives us sweeping police powers, but every search, arrest and detention must rest on lawful grounds and withstand public and judicial scrutiny,” he said.

He explained that enforcement and trade facilitation should complement each other, citing initiatives such as the One-Stop Shop and World Customs Organisation (WCO) instruments, including the Safe Framework of Standards, Authorised Economic Operator programmes, Advance Rulings, Time Release Studies and the Revised Kyoto Convention.

According to him, these instruments help reduce opportunities for abuse, corruption and arbitrary exercise of discretion.

The Customs boss said the Service had undergone meaningful structural renewal and remained committed to building a disciplined, responsive and professional police unit.

The post Customs officers must outsmart smugglers, go intelligence-led — Adeniyi appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Benue varsity, students bicker over staff audit, mass demotion
description:
The management of the Federal University of Health Sciences, Otukpo, Benue State, has dismissed claims of mass demotions at the institution, saying its staff audit exercise resulted in no dismissals and was aimed at correcting discrepancies in appointments and placements.
The university’s response f
content:
The management of the Federal University of Health Sciences, Otukpo, Benue State, has dismissed claims of mass demotions at the institution, saying its staff audit exercise resulted in no dismissals and was aimed at correcting discrepancies in appointments and placements.

The university’s response followed a petition by the Benue Students Network to President Bola Tinubu on Monday, seeking an independent investigation into the audit exercise and its implications for employees.

In an open letter to the President on Monday, the group called for a review of the administration of the Vice-Chancellor, Prof. Francis Aba Uba, following concerns over the audit exercise.

The petition, signed by the network’s Coordinator, Yusuf Adakole, and Secretary, Tersoo Igbor, was copied to the Minister of Education, Dr Tunji Alausa; the Executive Secretary of the National Universities Commission, Professor Abdullahi Ribadu; and the National Security Adviser, Nuhu Ribadu.

The students said some employees who were recruited, confirmed and promoted through the university’s established procedures had, years later, been informed that their original appointments did not meet the requirements for their respective grades.

The group said, “Some senior professionals received letters in October 2026 stating that they lacked the requisite cognate experience for the grades at which they were initially employed, despite years of service and subsequent promotions.

“Some academic staff were also demoted or redeployed to non-teaching positions despite possessing advanced qualifications in related fields.

“A staff audit should strengthen an institution, not destroy the confidence of its workforce. It should correct established irregularities, not create new grievances.”

The students urged Tinubu to direct the NUC to investigate the audit, review affected appointments, promotions and reclassifications, ensure fair hearings for affected employees and examine the university’s administrative procedures.

“FUHSO belongs to the Nigerian people. Its future must not be jeopardised by administrative decisions that are perceived to be arbitrary, discriminatory or inconsistent with established procedures,” the group added.

The network also called for the protection of staff members who might cooperate with the proposed investigation against intimidation or victimisation.

However, in a statement issued on Monday by its Head of Information, Public Relations and Protocol Unit, Sunday Adakole Igah, the university said the exercise was initiated following complaints from members of its community about appointments and staff placements.

It said the Governing Council ordered a comprehensive audit to address concerns about inappropriate placement, unequal treatment and inconsistencies in career progression.

According to the management, the committee that conducted the exercise comprised experts from the NUC, the Office of the Head of Service, public stakeholders, legal practitioners and representatives of staff unions.

The statement said the committee examined employees’ records, including qualifications, credentials, cognate experience and existing placements, before submitting its findings and recommendations to the Governing Council.

It added that the Council subsequently referred the report to a subcommittee for further consideration, with emphasis on fairness, staff welfare and a humane approach to implementation.

The university stated, “No member of staff was dismissed as a result of the exercise. Employees found to have been placed above the levels justified by their qualifications and experience were retained at their existing grades without further progression pending regularisation, while those placed below their appropriate levels were upgraded.”

It said the measures were intended to correct disparities while protecting employment and ensuring fairness in staff placement and career progression.

“Management therefore rejects the characterisation of the exercise as a mass demotion of staff. It was a Council-directed process undertaken in response to concerns raised within the University community, with safeguards to ensure careful scrutiny, institutional oversight and opportunities for redress,” the statement added.

The university also said affected employees could submit additional documents, explanations and objections through its Staff Appeals and Regularisation Committee.

It said some employees had already submitted complaints for review and assured staff that each case would be considered on its merits.

“Where an error or inconsistency is established, the necessary correction will be made. The review process remains open to legitimate representations and is intended to ensure that no employee suffers an injustice,” it stated.

The management further said records relating to the audit were available for scrutiny through appropriate university channels, subject to confidentiality requirements and the protection of personal staff information.

It maintained that the exercise was guided by Federal Government regulations, approved Schemes of Service, NUC guidelines and the university’s Conditions of Service.

The post Benue varsity, students bicker over staff audit, mass demotion appeared first on Punch Newspapers.
