title: FULL LIST: Nigerian artistes with the most Grammy nominations of all time
description:
Grammy-winning singer Burna Boy has extended his record as Nigeria’s most-nominated artiste at the Grammy Awards, with 14 career nominations, following the announcement of the 2027 nominees.
The 2027 Grammy nominations, announced on Monday, November 16, added to the career totals of several Nigerian
content:
Grammy-winning singer Burna Boy has extended his record as Nigeria’s most-nominated artiste at the Grammy Awards, with 14 career nominations, following the announcement of the 2027 nominees.

The 2027 Grammy nominations, announced on Monday, November 16, added to the career totals of several Nigerian music stars, with Tems emerging as the country’s most nominated artiste in the latest edition after receiving four nods.

Here is a look at the Nigerian artistes who have accumulated the most Grammy nominations over the years, based on their career totals:

1. Burna Boy — 14 nominations

Burna Boy earned his latest nomination for “Dìá Dìá”, his collaboration with Colombian singer Shakira, in the Best Global Music Performance category at the 2027 Grammys. The recognition takes his career tally to 14, including his 2021 win for Best Global Music Album with Twice as Tall.

His first nomination came in 2020, when African Giant was nominated for Best World Music Album. He received another nomination in 2021 for Twice as Tall, which won the Best Global Music Album award.

His subsequent nominations include “Do Yourself”, his collaboration with Angélique Kidjo, for Best Global Music Performance, and Justin Bieber’s Justice for Album of the Year in 2022 (on which he featured on the track ‘Loved by You’).

In 2023, “Last Last” was nominated for Best Global Music Performance, while Love, Damini received a nomination for Best Global Music Album.

Burna Boy earned four nominations in 2024: “Sittin’ On Top Of The World” featuring 21 Savage for Best Melodic Rap Performance; “Alone” for Best Global Music Performance; “City Boys” for Best African Music Performance; and I Told Them… for Best Global Music Album.

He received another nomination in 2025 for “Higher” in the Best African Music Performance category. In 2026, “Love” was nominated for Best African Music Performance, while No Sign of Weakness earned a nod for Best Global Music Album.

2. Tems — 12 nominations

Tems received four nominations at the 2027 Grammys, taking her career total to 12. Her song “Big Daddy” was nominated for Best African Music Performance, while her album Love Is a Kingdom earned a nod for Best Global Music Album.

She also received two nominations for “What You Need” in the Best R&B Solo Performance and Best R&B Song categories.

Her first Grammy nomination came in 2022 for her contribution to Wizkid’s “Essence”, which was nominated for Best Global Music Performance.

In 2023, she earned three nominations through her contribution to Future’s “Wait For U”, featuring Drake. The song was nominated for Best Melodic Rap Performance, which it won, and Best Rap Song. She also shared an Album of the Year nomination for Beyoncé’s Renaissance.

In 2024, Tems received a nomination for Best Song Written for Visual Media for “Lift Me Up”, from the Black Panther: Wakanda Forever soundtrack.

She earned three nominations in 2025: Best R&B Song for “Burning”, Best African Music Performance for “Love Me JeJe”, which won the category, and Best Global Music Album for Born in the Wild.

3. Wizkid — 7 nominations

Wizkid has received seven Grammy nominations and won once. His latest recognition came through “Jogodo”, his collaboration with Asake, which was nominated for Best African Music Performance at the 2027 awards.

His first nomination came in 2017 through Drake’s album Views, which was nominated for Album of the Year.

In 2021, he won Best Music Video for “Brown Skin Girl”, his collaboration with Beyoncé, Blue Ivy Carter and Saint Jhn.

He received two nominations in 2022: Best Global Music Album for Made in Lagos: Deluxe Edition and Best Global Music Performance for “Essence”, his collaboration with Tems.

Wizkid was nominated again in 2025 for “MMS”, his collaboration with Asake, in the Best African Music Performance category. In 2026, he earned another nomination in the same category for “Gimme Dat”, his collaboration with Ayra Starr.

4. Davido — 6 nominations

Davido’s six Grammy nominations have come across four consecutive editions of the awards. He received three nominations in 2024 for “Feel” in the Best Global Music Performance category, “Unavailable” featuring Musa Keys in the Best African Music Performance category, and his album Timeless for Best Global Music Album.

In 2025, he was nominated for Best African Music Performance for “Sensational”, his collaboration with American singer Chris Brown and Nigerian singer Lojay.

He earned another nomination in 2026 for “With You”, his collaboration with Omah Lay, in the Best African Music Performance category.

His latest nomination is for his album Oriadé, which will compete for Best Global Music Album at the 2027 Grammys.

4. Femi Kuti — 6 nominations

Afrobeat musician Femi Kuti is also on six Grammy nominations. His first came in 2003, when his album Fight to Win was nominated for Best World Music Album.

He received another nomination in 2010 for Day by Day in the Best Contemporary World Music Album category. This was followed by nominations for Africa for Africa in 2012 and No Place for My Dream in 2014, both in the Best World Music Album category.

In 2022, Femi received two nominations: Best Global Music Performance for “Pà Pá Pà” and Best Global Music Album for Legacy +, his joint project with his son, Made Kuti.

6. Asake — 4 nominations

Asake has received four Grammy nominations, all in the Best African Music Performance category. His first came in 2024 for “Amapiano”, his collaboration with Olamide.

He received another nomination in 2025 for “MMS”, his collaboration with Wizkid.

At the 2027 Grammys, Asake earned two nominations in the same category: one for his song “Gratitude” and another for “Jogodo”, his collaboration with Wizkid.

6. Ayra Starr — 4 nominations

Ayra Starr also has four Grammy nominations. Her first came in 2024 for her song “Rush”, which was nominated for Best African Music Performance.

In 2026, she received another nomination in the category for “Gimme Dat”, her collaboration with Wizkid.

For the 2027 edition, she earned two nominations: Best African Music Performance for “Aye Kan (Are You Coming Back?)”, her collaboration with Beninese singer Angélique Kidjo, and Best Global Music Album for Starrgirl.

The 69th Grammy Awards will hold on February 7, 2027, at the Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles, United States.

title: Economic Reforms: Tinubu more courageous than past leaders – Alawuje, APC-PCC member
description:
A member of the President Bola Ahmed Tinubu Campaign Council, Hon. Comrade Abdulhakeem Adegoke Alawuje, has defended President Tinubu’s economic reforms, describing him as a courageous democrat and fearless reformer willing to confront Nigeria’s longstanding economic challenges.
Alawuje, in a press
content:
A member of the President Bola Ahmed Tinubu Campaign Council, Hon. Comrade Abdulhakeem Adegoke Alawuje, has defended President Tinubu’s economic reforms, describing him as a courageous democrat and fearless reformer willing to confront Nigeria’s longstanding economic challenges.

Alawuje, in a press statement titled “Tinubu: A Courageous Democrat, A Fearless Reformer and a Determined Seeker of National Progress,” said the President had demonstrated the political courage required to address structural economic problems that successive administrations had struggled to resolve.

According to him, Nigeria has reached a defining moment in its history when difficult decisions and necessary sacrifices must be embraced to secure a better future.

“For Nigeria, that moment is now,” he declared.

He argued that genuine national transformation could not be achieved through political convenience, unrealistic promises or the continuous postponement of difficult decisions.

“President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has demonstrated the courage of a leader who understands that genuine national transformation cannot be achieved through political convenience, unrealistic promises or the continuous postponement of difficult decisions,” Alawuje stated.

The campaign council member acknowledged that the government’s reform policies had imposed significant economic difficulties on Nigerians but urged citizens not to allow their sacrifices to become meaningless.

He said Nigerians had demonstrated remarkable resilience despite rising economic pressures, uncertainty and other social challenges.

“Our people have endured enormous economic difficulties, uncertainty and hardship. They have carried a burden that demands national recognition and sincere appreciation,” he said.

Alawuje, however, maintained that the ultimate justification for the reforms would depend on their ability to improve the living conditions of ordinary Nigerians.

He urged the President to ensure that the foundations being laid through the reforms translated into tangible economic relief, employment opportunities, improved living standards, social justice and sustainable prosperity.

“The pains are real, the frustrations are understandable, and the sacrifices must never be dismissed or taken for granted,” he acknowledged.

“However, we must also recognise that the ultimate justification for every reform lies in its ability to deliver measurable improvements in the lives of the people.”

The Tinubu campaign council member also criticised calls by an opposition-associated presidential aspirant for the restoration of fuel subsidy, questioning the sustainability of such a proposal.

He argued that Nigerians deserved more than politically attractive promises, insisting that anyone advocating a return to subsidy must explain how the policy would be funded and how the country would avoid the economic difficulties associated with the previous arrangement.

“Is returning to fuel subsidy genuinely a sustainable economic solution, or is it another politically attractive promise designed to win public sympathy?” he queried.

Alawuje recalled that successive administrations had struggled with the fuel subsidy question because of the enormous financial burden it placed on the national economy and the political consequences associated with its removal.

He said Tinubu eventually took the decision to remove the subsidy, confronting a challenge that previous administrations had repeatedly struggled to resolve.

“My question is simple: If returning to fuel subsidy is the solution, how will it be funded, how will the country avoid the mistakes of the past, and what sustainable economic strategy accompanies that promise?” he asked.

He further cautioned politicians against making promises without explaining their economic implications.

“It is easy to promise immediate relief when one is not responsible for managing the consequences. But genuine leadership requires the courage to make difficult decisions, accept responsibility and provide sustainable solutions,” he stated.

He urged Nigerians to scrutinise the competence, consistency, courage and economic understanding of individuals seeking political power, rather than being swayed by attractive campaign promises.

While expressing support for Tinubu’s reform agenda, Alawuje stressed that the government must not take the patience and resilience of Nigerians for granted.

He called for a renewed commitment to national unity, accountability, fairness and people-centred governance, insisting that the sacrifices being made by citizens must produce meaningful results.

“Let us give the necessary reforms the opportunity to produce the desired results, while continuing to demand compassion, accountability, fairness and people-centred governance,” he appealed.

He also maintained that national progress should not be presented as the personal achievement of the President or any political organisation, but as a collective victory belonging to all Nigerians.

According to him, the success of the reform process must be dedicated to citizens who have endured the difficulties and continued to believe in the country’s future.

“This victory, when it comes, must belong to all Nigerians. It must not be celebrated as the personal achievement of President Tinubu or any political group,” he said.

Alawuje further urged Nigerians to move beyond political divisions and support efforts aimed at addressing the institutional failures and social injustices that have hindered national development for decades.

He also referenced remarks attributed to the Emir of Kano, noting that rebuilding a country whose economic foundations had suffered years of deterioration could not be expected to be an easy undertaking.

The Tinubu campaign council member expressed optimism about Nigeria’s future and called on citizens to remain resilient while demanding improved governance and better economic outcomes.

“Our pains must not be in vain. Our sacrifices must produce results. Our future must be better than our past,” he declared.

He prayed for divine guidance, wisdom and strength for President Tinubu to lead Nigeria towards economic recovery, national unity and lasting prosperity.

The post Economic Reforms: Tinubu more courageous than past leaders – Alawuje, APC-PCC member appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: UBA intensifies fight against phishing, scam
description:
…as 2026 fraud awareness week begins







The United Bank for Africa (UBA) Plc, has stepped up its fight against fraud, urging customers and the public to stay alert to phishing scams where criminals increasingly use fake bank messages, cloned websites and impersonation accounts to steal account d
content:
…as 2026 fraud awareness week begins

The United Bank for Africa (UBA) Plc, has stepped up its fight against fraud, urging customers and the public to stay alert to phishing scams where criminals increasingly use fake bank messages, cloned websites and impersonation accounts to steal account details and money.

To this end, the Bank is set to hold the 2026 edition of its Fraud Awareness Week, from Monday, November 16 to Friday, November 20, 2026, with the theme “Fraud Dynamics: Staying One Step Ahead.”

UBA’s Group Chief Internal Auditor, Eugene Inotu, who spoke ahead of the campaign, said the bank wants every customer to recognise a phishing or fraud attempt before it causes harm.

“Fraudsters are counting on panic. They want you to click before you think, so the strongest defence is to pause,” Inotu said. He added, “UBA will never ask for your PIN, password, OTP or BVN through a link, a text message, an email or a phone call. If a message asks for any of these, it is not from us, no matter how genuine it looks.”

Offering practical guidance, UBA’s Group Head, Brands, Marketing and Corporate Communications, Alero Ladipo, urged customers to treat every unsolicited link with suspicion and to confirm requests only through the Bank’s official channels.

She said, “Avoid clicking links in messages you did not ask for. Type the UBA website address directly into your browser or use the official UBA Mobile App, and download banking apps only from official app stores’’.

title: Nigeria losing revenue by criminalising cannabis, Sowore insists
description: The human rights activist and presidential candidate of the African Action Congress for the 2027 general election, Omoyele Sowore, has renewed his call for Nigeria to legalise cannabis, arguing that the country could generate substantial government revenue from a regulated industry instead of contin
content:
The human rights activist and presidential candidate of the African Action Congress for the 2027 general election, Omoyele Sowore, has renewed his call for Nigeria to legalise cannabis, arguing that the country could generate substantial government revenue from a regulated industry instead of continuing to criminalise its cultivation and use.

Sowore made the call on Tuesday in a post on X, where he cited revenue generated from cannabis sales and taxation in Canada and the United States as examples of the economic benefits of legalisation.

He said Nigeria was losing potential revenue while authorities continued to arrest people, destroy cannabis farms and prosecute those involved in the trade.

“Since 2018, I have advocated cannabis legalisation, arguing that Nigeria should stop criminalising an economically valuable plant and develop a properly regulated cannabis industry.

“While Nigerian authorities continue to arrest citizens, destroy cannabis farms, and criminalise the plant, countries that have legalised and regulated cannabis are collecting substantial government revenue,” he said.

Citing figures for the 2023-2024 fiscal year, Sowore said Canada generated approximately CA$2.2bn in government revenue from recreational cannabis. He also cited about $1.067bn in cannabis tax revenue generated by California in 2024 and $255.4m in marijuana taxes and fees collected by Colorado in the same year.

Statistics Canada reported that federal and provincial governments earned CA$2.2bn from recreational cannabis in the fiscal year ending March 31 2024. The figure included income from cannabis authorities, excise duties, retail sales taxes, other specific taxes and licensing fees.

California’s tax authority reported approximately $1.067bn in cannabis tax revenue for 2024, while Colorado’s Department of Revenue recorded $255.36m in marijuana tax and fee collections that year.

Sowore said Nigeria could generate between $550m and $2.2bn annually under different revenue scenarios, depending on the size of a legal market and the effectiveness of its taxation and regulatory systems.

Using an illustrative exchange rate of N1,300 to the dollar, he put the possible annual revenue at between N715bn and N2.86tn.

He stressed that the figures were hypothetical and that Nigeria’s actual earnings would depend on factors including market size, taxation, licensing, exports and regulatory effectiveness.

The activist also argued that legalisation could create employment opportunities in agriculture, pharmaceutical manufacturing and industrial hemp production, while supporting scientific research and export earnings.

He called for a legal framework that would regulate production, protect public health, support farmers and generate government revenue.

Cannabis remains illegal in Nigeria under the country’s Indian Hemp Act, which prohibits its cultivation, unlawful importation, sale, exportation, smoking and possession. The law defines Indian hemp to include plants and parts of plants belonging to the cannabis genus.

The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control has also previously stated that cannabis cultivation, consumption, handling and possession remain illegal under Nigerian law.

Sowore has advocated cannabis legalisation since 2018, arguing that the country should consider its economic potential through a regulated industry.

The post Nigeria losing revenue by criminalising cannabis, Sowore insists appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Nollywood star, Chioma Chukwuka makes Nigeria proud in Texas
description:
From Noah Ebije, Kaduna
Veteran Nollywood actress, Chioma Chukwuka, has received the prestigious Lifetime Achievement Award at the 2026 Global African Diaspora Awards (GADA) in recognition of her outstanding contributions to the Nigerian film industry and her enduring influence on African entertainm
content:
From Noah Ebije, Kaduna

Veteran Nollywood actress, Chioma Chukwuka, has received the prestigious Lifetime Achievement Award at the 2026 Global African Diaspora Awards (GADA) in recognition of her outstanding contributions to the Nigerian film industry and her enduring influence on African entertainment.

This was contained in a statement made available to newsmen in Nigeria by GADA Founder and Executive Producer, Obi-West Utchaychukwu, popularly known as the Obi of Houston.

According to the statement, the award was presented at the third edition of the GADA Awards, held on Saturday, November 7, 2026, at the Golden Tree Banquet in Houston, Texas, United States.

The glamorous ceremony attracted approximately 500 guests from different parts of the world, bringing together prominent personalities and members of the African diaspora to celebrate excellence and outstanding achievements by Africans across various fields.

Chukwuka, who is regarded as one of Nollywood’s most accomplished actresses, began her acting journey in 1998 and ventured into professional acting in 2000.

Her first movie appearance was in The Apple (2000), directed by renowned filmmaker, Lancelot Oduwa Imasuen.

Over the years, she has distinguished herself through her exceptional acting skills, versatility, dedication and consistency, earning admiration from audiences and colleagues within and outside Nigeria.

Her memorable performances and sustained contributions have also helped promote the growth and international visibility of Nigerian cinema.

The Lifetime Achievement Award, according to the organisers, recognises not only her professional accomplishments but also her enduring influence on the entertainment industry and her role in inspiring emerging generations of actors.

Speaking on the significance of the recognition, the founder and executive producer of GADA, Obi-West Utchaychukwu, popularly known as the Obi of Houston, said the award was a celebration of Chukwuka’s remarkable journey and lasting contributions to African entertainment.

He noted that the actress represents the talent, resilience and creative excellence that African entertainers continue to project on the international stage.

The organisers said the recognition was also in line with the vision of the Global African Diaspora Awards to celebrate Africans whose achievements have continued to make meaningful contributions to society across national and continental boundaries.

The third edition of the awards was held under the theme, “Bridging Continents, Celebrating Diaspora Excellence,” which underscores the importance of recognising outstanding Africans and members of the diaspora whose accomplishments have strengthened the continent’s global presence.

By honouring Chukwuka with the Lifetime Achievement Award, GADA has further acknowledged her place among the leading figures whose dedication and creative accomplishments have helped shape the Nigerian movie industry over the years.

The recognition is also seen as a celebration of the growing influence of Nollywood and the contributions of African creative talents to global entertainment.

The post Nollywood star, Chioma Chukwuka makes Nigeria proud in Texas appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Pique says Owono’s 12-match ban after De Miguel death is unfair
description:
FC Andorra’s majority shareholder Gerard Pique criticised Jesus Owono’s 12-match ban following a fatal collision with Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel, saying it unfairly blamed the goalkeeper for “consequences that were not his fault”.



Equatorial Guinea international Owono was sent off in a Span
content:
FC Andorra’s majority shareholder Gerard Pique criticised Jesus Owono’s 12-match ban following a fatal collision with Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel, saying it unfairly blamed the goalkeeper for “consequences that were not his fault”.

Equatorial Guinea international Owono was sent off in a Spanish second division clash on November 2 after racing into midfield and colliding heavily with De Miguel while trying to clear.

De Miguel, 30, was placed in intensive care in hospital and died the next day, plunging football into shock and mourning.

In a video posted to TikTok late on Monday, former Spain and Barcelona great Pique said the Spanish football federation’s punishment put Owono “in a situation that isn’t fair”.

“What it does is blame Jesus for consequences which were not his fault,” Pique said in his first public comments on the decision.

“I think the punishment should be for the action, not for the consequences,” added Pique, who compared the tragedy in Tenerife to a similar incident which led to a shorter ban.

Owono, 25, has said he is enduring the “hardest days of my life” after De Miguel’s death, which Pique described as an “accident” that was “totally inexplicable”.

FC Andorra coach Carles Manso said the goalkeeper will decide if and when he returns to football after the tragedy

“Jesus will need more than 12 games in order to be available and compete,” said Pique.

“No suspension will bring Demi back to us,” added Pique, referring to De Miguel by a popular nickname.

Spanish police sources have told AFP an investigation into what happened had been opened under judicial supervision, a standard procedure for unnatural deaths.

title: Polysmart commissions 60,000mt food-grade rPET plant
description:
…as FCMB provides N40bn financing







Polysmart Packaging Limited has commissioned a plant with an annual production capacity of 60,000 tonnes of food-grade recycled polyethylene terephthalate (rPET) in Ileke town, Ogun State, with N40 billion in machinery and working-capital financing from First
content:
…as FCMB provides N40bn financing

Polysmart Packaging Limited has commissioned a plant with an annual production capacity of 60,000 tonnes of food-grade recycled polyethylene terephthalate (rPET) in Ileke town, Ogun State, with N40 billion in machinery and working-capital financing from First City Monument Bank (FCMB).

The facility, which Polysmart describes as Africa’s largest plastic recycling plant, will convert recovered post-consumer plastic waste into food-grade recycled PET materials for manufacturers.

It is expected to strengthen local packaging production, support plastic-waste recovery and reduce dependence on imported raw materials.

At the commissioning ceremony on October 29, Minister of Environment Balarabe Lawal, said the facility would enhance Nigeria’s capacity to recover and recycle plastic waste while supporting the country’s environmental sustainability objectives.

Ogun State Governor Dapo Abiodun described the investment as a demonstration of Nigerian enterprise, innovation and the opportunities created by a supportive investment environment.

Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of FCMB, Yemisi Edun, said the Bank’s support reflects its commitment to financing businesses that combine industrial development with environmental responsibility and economic opportunity.

“At FCMB, we believe that financing sustainable businesses is essential to building a resilient economy and securing long-term shared prosperity.

By converting recovered plastic into new products, this plant shows how manufacturing and environmental responsibility can work together,” Edun said.

She added, “Polysmart embodies our commitment to sustainable manufacturing practices, environmental sustainability and wealth creation, reflected in our ₦40 billion in funding for machinery and working capital.”

Polysmart Group Managing Director, Wasiu Balogun, said the investment demonstrates the capacity of Nigerian businesses to develop recycling infrastructure that serves local industry and creates opportunities across the waste-recovery chain.

“This is climate action made in Nigeria. The investment demonstrates the capacity of Nigerian businesses to develop world-class recycling infrastructure,” Balogun said.

He added, “At full capacity, the facility will process up to 100,000 tonnes of mixed plastics annually, equivalent to about 6.5 billion bottles.”

title: Gov Mbah commissions Premium Trust Bank Branch in Enugu
description:
….Highlights investments in security, infrastructure, others to attract investors
…As Premium Bank targets SMEs, Businesses
Governor Peter Mbah of Enugu State, on Monday, unveiled the first branch of Premium Trust Bank in the state, describing the development as a demonstration of growing private-se
content:
….Highlights investments in security, infrastructure, others to attract investors

…As Premium Bank targets SMEs, Businesses

Governor Peter Mbah of Enugu State, on Monday, unveiled the first branch of Premium Trust Bank in the state, describing the development as a demonstration of growing private-sector confidence in the state’s economy and investment prospects. 

Mbah reiterated his administration’s determination to restore Enugu’s historic position as a major economic hub through deliberate investments, private-sector partnerships and policies designed to accelerate economic growth.

This was even as the bank’s Group Managing and Chief Executive Officer, Mr Emmanuel Efe Emefienim (CON, FCIB), commended Mbah for improved business environment and reaffirmed the bank’s commitment expanding its national footprint and supporting businesses, small and medium-scale enterprises (SMEs) and financial inclusion.

The Governor recalled that Enugu’s economic significance predated Nigeria’s amalgamation, noting that the discovery of coal in 1909 established the city as an important commercial and administrative centre.

He said his administration was growing the state’s economy in line with its development blueprint anchored on growing the state’s economy from $4.4 billion to $30 billion within eight years, eliminating poverty and making Enugu a preferred destination for living, working, business and tourism.

He emphasised that the administration’s strategy was to create an enabling environment for private capital to drive economic expansion, stressing that government alone could not deliver the desired level of growth.

The governor identified security as one of the major considerations for investors,recalling that the administration inherited security challenges, including the disruption of economic activities associated with the Monday sit-at-home order.

According to him, the interventions have helped restore confidence and reduce the risks associated with doing business in Enugu.

The governor further disclosed plans to establish a 660-megawatt coal-fired powerplant, expressing optimism that reliable and affordable electricity would stimulate industrialisation and create opportunities across the state’s economic value chain.

He also cited the expansion of Enugu’s air connectivity, including international routes, as part of efforts to improve access to global markets and attract investment. C

Congratulating the bank’s management, disclosed that Premium Trust Bank was already a partner of the state government and the headline sponsor of the National Sports Festival scheduled to hold in Enugu. He noted that the bank’s expansion into Enugu was consistent with the administration’s development philosophy of government-enabled, private-sector-driven growth.

The governor expressed optimism that the bank would establish additional branches in the state, potentially expanding its presence to 10 branches as economic activities and investment opportunities increase.

Earlier, Emefienim said the bank’s decision to establish a presence in Enugu was informed by confidence in the state, its people and its economic future.

He disclosed that the Enugu branch was the bank’s fourth branch opening in November, bringing its nationwide network to 38, with plans to establish four additional branches before the end of the year.

According to him, the expansion reflects the bank’s commitment to bringing financial services closer to individuals, entrepreneurs, SMEs and corporate organisations across the country.

“Our decision to establish a presence here is a strong belief in this state, its people and its future.

“More importantly, it is a demonstration of our readiness to partner with the state government, individuals, entrepreneurs, SMEs, corporates and the good people of Enugu in building a stronger and more prosperous economy,” he said.

The bank’s managing director commended the Mbah administration for its investment infrastructure, security, technology, ease of doing business and investment promotion, noting that the initiatives were helping to create an environment conducive to enterprise and investment.

He said that while the government had the responsibility of providing an enabling environment, financial institutions and private businesses also had critical roles to play the provision of capital, innovation and financial solutions.

Describing the new branch as more than an additional banking facility, Emefienim said it would serve as a platform for expanding financial inclusion and supporting individuals and businesses in achieving their financial goals.

He identified entrepreneurs seeking to expand their businesses, traders requiring efficient payment solutions, professionals planning their financial future,students pursuing education and families working towards financial security as some of the categories the bank intended to serve.

On support for SMEs, he described the sector as a major driver of economic growth and job creation, stressing that businesses required financial partners capable of understanding their needs and providing solutions to support their expansion.

He highlighted the bank’s Silver Premium Business Account, designed to help businesses manage operating costs, improve efficiency and access collections,digital payment solutions and other banking services.

Emefienim also introduced Blaze, the bank’s lifestyle and digital financial platform,which he said was designed to simplify transactions, improve banking convenience and expand access to financial services.

Reaffirming the bank’s commitment to the state, he said Premium Trust Bank was prepared to build a long-term relationship with Enugu and contribute to the growth of businesses and the wider economy.

“We are here for the long term. We are here to support enterprises. We are here to create opportunities. We are here to help businesses grow and help individuals achieve their financial goals,” he said.

He attributed the bank’s growing national presence to its emphasis on sound corporate governance, innovation, service excellence and prudent management.

title: Inflation rate moves in divergent positions
description:
Drops year-on-year, rises month-on-month







By Elizabeth Adegbesan







The National Bureau of Statistics, NBS, has disclosed that Nigeria’s headline inflation rate dropped to 14.06 percent in October 2026 from 14.63 percent in the previous month.



NBS stated this in its latest Consumer Pric
content:
Drops year-on-year, rises month-on-month

By Elizabeth Adegbesan

The National Bureau of Statistics, NBS, has disclosed that Nigeria’s headline inflation rate dropped to 14.06 percent in October 2026 from 14.63 percent in the previous month.

NBS stated this in its latest Consumer Price Index, CPI, Report noting that food inflation also declined to 19.13 percent from 19.59 percent in September.

However, Month-on-Month, MoM, inflation rate rose by 0.43% in October, up by 0.38 percentage point from 0.06 percent recorded in September 2026.

This increase also reflected in the MoM trend in food inflation for October.

NBS stated: “In October 2026, the Headline inflation rate stood at 14.06 percent, down from 14.63 percent in September 2026 and stood at 18.97 percent in the same month of the preceding year (October 2025).

“Looking at the movement, the October 2026 Headline inflation rate showed a decrease of 4.9 percent compared to the October 2025 (18.97 percent) Headline inflation rate.

“On a month-on-month basis, the Headline inflation rate in October 2026 was 0.43 percent, which was 0.38 percent higher than the rate recorded in September 2026 (0.06 percent).

“This means that in October 2026, the rate of increase in the average price level was higher than the rate of increase in the average price level in September 2026.”

On food inflation, NBS, said: “The Food inflation rate in October 2026 was 19.13 per cent on a year-on-year basis and stood at 16.3 per ent in the same month of the preceding year (October 2025). “However, on a MoM basis, the Food inflation rate in October 2026 was -0.75 percent , up by 0.80 percent points from September 2026 (-1.55 per cent).

“This can be attributed to the rate of change in the average prices of the following products: vegetable oil (75cl), Titus sardines (125g), green peas (Prepacked), mackerel frozen, croakers (apo), rice local, catfish fresh, beef tripes, palm oil (75cl), millet flour (sold loose), etc”

In October 2026, food inflation on a year-on-year basis was highest in Ondo (31.74 percent), Lagos (31.43 percent), and Imo (29.75 percent), while Nasarawa (3.7 percent), Bayelsa (7.11 percent) and Kano (7.13 percent) recorded the slowest rise in food inflation on a Year-on-Year basis.

“On a MoM basis, however, October 2026 food inflation was highest in Yobe (18.41 percent), Kebbi (16.45 percent), and Borno (13.96 percent), while Lagos (-5.93 percent), Plateau (-5.83 percent), and Benue (-5.49 percent) recorded the slowest rise in Food inflation on a Month-on-Month basis.”

description: Germany, Austria, Greece, Denmark and the Netherlands will open a migrant "return hub" in Rwanda in 2027. Here is what the deal means for Nigerians and Africans living in Europe - and who it applies to.
content:
Five European countries - Germany, Austria, Greece, Denmark and the Netherlands - have announced that they will open a migrant deportation centre, called a "return hub", in Rwanda, ready to accept transfers from 2027. The announcement was made at a joint press conference in Vienna on Monday, November 17, 2026.

Who the deal applies to: the scheme covers migrants who are staying illegally in these countries and have exhausted every legal avenue to remain - people whose asylum claims and appeals have all failed and who are already facing deportation. It does not apply to asylum seekers whose cases are still being processed.

How it will start: the hub will begin as a pilot hosting about 100 people, with each of the five countries possibly sending about 20 migrants. The Dutch government said the first phase will cover only single men, and that its focus will be on people from the same region as Rwanda.

What happens in Rwanda: deportees will have two options - either integrate into Rwandan society, which gives them the right of residence plus access to education, healthcare, the labour market and the legal system, or return to their home country. Rwanda's Interior Minister Vincent Biruta called the arrangement a "safe, legal and dignified solution for migrants".

What this means for Nigerians and Africans abroad: if you are living in Germany, Austria, Greece, Denmark or the Netherlands without valid papers, and your asylum or appeal case has failed, you could now be deported to Rwanda instead of your home country. The deal is also a signal of how seriously Europe is now enforcing immigration rules - the UK has already said it is watching the scheme "with interest" and has not ruled out joining.

The message is clear: the safest path is a legal route - a proper work visa, student visa or skilled-worker programme, like the routes we have covered for Romania's 372 shortage occupations and the UK Skilled Worker visa. Falling into an illegal status in Europe is becoming more dangerous than ever, because even deportation no longer means simply going home.

The backlash: the deal has drawn sharp criticism. Human Rights Watch said the choice of Rwanda was concerning, and Spain's Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez said the plan has no "future or humanity". The EU Agency for Fundamental Rights said any country hosting a return hub must respect fundamental rights, and unaccompanied children will not be sent to the hub - which the Dutch government has confirmed.

Context: the deal follows a recent EU reform that allowed the creation of hubs outside the bloc. According to the European Border and Coast Guard Agency, there were almost 110,000 irregular border crossings into the EU in the first 10 months of 2026 - a 29% decrease compared to the previous year.

content:
A leading media entrepreneur in Bayelsa State and Chief Executive Officer of Closer TV, Mr. Ogbomade Johnson Itutumeni, has commended the Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of the Niger Delta Development Commission (NDDC), HRH King Samuel Ogbuku, PhD, for his remarkable support towards the growth and development of entrepreneurs in the Niger Delta.

In an appreciation message, Mr Itutumeni said the NDDC boss showed a strong commitment to empowering individuals and businesses through initiatives and interventions that promote entrepreneurship, innovation, and economic development across the Niger Delta region.

He noted that such support remains a major boost to emerging entrepreneurs, particularly those in the media and creative industries, as it would encourage business expansion, stimulate innovation, create employment opportunities and strengthen the local economy.

Mr. Itutumeni further applauded Ogbuku for recognising the importance of indigenous entrepreneurs, adding that his sustained support, strategic partnerships and deliberate empowerment programmes have gone a long way in addressing the challenges confronting small and emerging businesses.

Speaking as a beneficiary of Ogbuku’s philanthropic gesture, Itutumeni expressed profound gratitude, describing the support as a significant contribution to his personal and professional development.

Itutumeni also appreciated President Bola Ahmed Tinubu for appointing Dr Samuel Ogbuku as the Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of the Niger Delta Development Commission (NDDC), noting that Dr Ogbuku has performed remarkably well in office by bringing development closer to the people through impactful projects and initiatives of the Commission.

title: Dead Melbourne Cup Racehorse Found Dumped In Bin
description: A dead Australian racehorse has been found in an industrial rubbish bin on the outskirts of Sydney two weeks after running in the prestigious Melbourne Cup.Trainer Bjorn Baker said Tuesday he was “deeply distressed” after a member of the public stumbled across the carcass of thoroughbred
content:
A dead Australian racehorse has been found in an industrial rubbish bin on the outskirts of Sydney two weeks after running in the prestigious Melbourne Cup.

Trainer Bjorn Baker said Tuesday he was “deeply distressed” after a member of the public stumbled across the carcass of thoroughbred So You Are, which finished eighth in this year’s race.

The five-year-old horse was euthanised earlier this week after a bout of severe colic, local media reported.

“Like everyone who has seen the footage I am deeply distressed by the handling of So You Are’s remains,” Baker said in a statement on social media.

“He was a much-loved horse and he deserves to be treated with respect and dignity after his death.

“I understand the specialist hospital facility REC Equine Specialists are investigating the circumstances and I expect a full explanation of what occurred.”

Horse vets REC Equine Specialists apologised and said the animal should have been buried respectfully, national broadcaster ABC reported.

“After his death So You Are was collected by our contracted service provider and taken to a licensed landfill. He should have been promptly and respectfully buried,” the company said.

“What happened was unacceptable and disrespectful to So You Are and to everyone else who cared for him.

AFP

The post Dead Melbourne Cup Racehorse Found Dumped In Bin appeared first on Channels Television.

title: A/Ibom technical college emerges winner at innovative science competition
description: Government Technical College, Ewet Ofot in Uyo local government area in Akwa Ibom state has emerged winner of 2026 science , technology and  innovation competition organized by Vcare for development supported by Sterling Oil Exploration and Energy Production company and supervised by the state minis
content:
Government Technical College, Ewet Ofot in Uyo local government area in Akwa Ibom state has emerged winner of 2026 science , technology and  innovation competition organized by Vcare for development supported by Sterling Oil Exploration and Energy Production company and supervised by the state ministry of education . 

A statement signed by the Media and Communication Manager of Sterling Oil Exploration and Energy  Production company Aniekeme Finbarr and made available to Journalists in Uyo stated that the competition was part of Corporate Social Responsibility to host communities to haunt for talents in science and technology that provide practical solutions to daily community  challenges .

Finbarr said the competition targetted 4,186 students across 141 secondary schools in the state as students worked in groups to proffer solutions to technical problems facing their communities with teachers supervising them.

Finbarr listed projects by the students to include water distribution, renewable energy, flood monitoring and alternative heating systems at the grand finale of the competition where Government Technical Secondary School , Ewet Ofot emerged winner.

“The grand finale showcased innovative student projects addressing critical societal challenges, including water distribution, renewable energy, flood monitoring and alternative heating systems

” The projects demonstrated how scientific knowledge, creativity, critical thinking and teamwork can be translated into practical solutions to real-life problems”

He said since introduction of the programme in 2024, it has provided secondary school students with opportunities to advance beyond classroom theories through applications of science, technology, engineering and mathematics knowledge to tackle challenges within their communities.

“The 2026 edition commenced with orientation sessions designed to equip teachers with the knowledge and skills to guide students through hands-on learning, critical thinking, teamwork and problem-solving activities.

“The programme targeted  4,186 students across 141 secondary and technical schools in Akwa Ibom State

” Following STEM workshops and teacher orientation sessions, students worked in teams under the guidance of their coordinating science teachers to identify challenges in their communities, examine their possible causes and develop practical, technology-driven solutions

“The journey culminated in a grand finale where 14 selected schools, out of 75 funded projects, presented their innovations before judges and stakeholders”

Finbarr explained  that the competition attracted representatives of the state government,  education stakeholders, teachers and students, who gathered to celebrate the creativity, ingenuity and problem-solving abilities of the young innovators.

He said  the Permanent Secretary in  Ministry of Education, Akparawa Okon Effiong Tom, expressed delight at the programme’s growth and expansion reach across schools in the state and commended Sterling Oil and VCDF for encouraging students to develop interest in science and particularly apply their knowledge to tackle society challenges

“I want to sincerely thank Sterling Oil and Vcare for Development Foundation because you have encouraged our students to be interested in science subjects, not just to be interested but to take a step further by being practical”

Finbarr said the  students’ ingenuity was evident in the prototypes presented at the grand finale, with each project reflecting a deliberate attempt to address practical challenges through the application of science and technology.

” Government Technical College, Ewet, Uyo, emerged overall winner with Sharepump, an automatic water pump and power-switching prototype designed to regulate water supply and improve water distribution in homes and multi-storey buildings.

” While Secondary Grammar School, Ibeno, secured second place with its Footstep Energy Harvester, a prototype that converts the mechanical energy generated by footsteps into electrical energy, demonstrating the possibilities of alternative and renewable energy sources.

“Afaha Inang Secondary School, Onna, came third with Community FloodGuard, a flood-monitoring and protection prototype designed to help communities detect potential flooding, strengthen early-warning systems and respond more effectively to flood risks”.

He said one the the teachers  Ubong Sunday Ukpong in the winning team while reflecting on his experience while coordinating the students   said the journey involved challenges that required teamwork, collaboration and determination to overcome.

“We faced challenges, but we worked together to develop ideas, identify solutions and bring them to life

” We sincerely appreciate Sterling Oil and VCDF for providing this platform and giving our students the opportunity to develop practical solutions to societal problems,” he said.

The post A/Ibom technical college emerges winner at innovative science competition appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: S’Africa now super racist against Whites, Asians – Elon Musk replies Ramaphosa over appeal to remember origin
description:
World’s richest man, Elon Musk has hit back at South African President, Cyril Ramaphosa after the president appealed to him to remember his origin and give back to his home country.
Ramaphosa spoke about Musk during an interview in Silicon Valley after leading a South African delegation focused on a
content:
World’s richest man, Elon Musk has hit back at South African President, Cyril Ramaphosa after the president appealed to him to remember his origin and give back to his home country.

Ramaphosa spoke about Musk during an interview in Silicon Valley after leading a South African delegation focused on artificial intelligence to California on November 14.

“I have met Elon Musk in the past, and I’ve been awed by his brilliance. But I’d also like to chat to him about remembering his country and being loyal to his home country,” Ramaphosa said.

The president also faulted South Africa-born Musk’s description of the country’s empowerment policies as “Apartheid 2.0.”

“He doesn’t understand the harm of apartheid policies and how the apartheid policies chose white people only for advancement, and the education he received was much better than what I received.

“Where the apartheid government spent R12 on his education, it spent R1 on my education. So if one does not understand that, one will never be able to understand precisely what needs to be done to remedy the harm that was done,” the president said.

Ramaphosa argued that Musk’s success was shaped by the knowledge and education made available to him in South Africa, and urged him contribute to the nation’s development.

He said, “I would say to Elon, what you’ve become today is by dint of your own origin. You started dabbling with the game machines. It is because of the knowledge and the education that was made available to you.

“And it is this endowment that you now have that was formed in South Africa. And he should be one of those who would say, I would like to contribute to the development of South Africa and give back to this country that made me who I am today.”

Musk was quick to respond on Tuesday after a clip of the interview circulated on X.

“South Africa is now super racist against Whites and Asians,” the Space X and Tesla CEO said.

Musk, who was born in Pretoria, has repeatedly criticised South Africa’s Broad-Based Black Economic Empowerment (B-BBEE) framework, which mandates telecommunications companies to have at least 30% equity owned by historically disadvantaged groups.

He has also previously claimed that Starlink was denied a licence in South Africa simply because he is not Black, a claim the South African government has rejected, insisting the rules apply to all operators.

The post S’Africa now super racist against Whites, Asians – Elon Musk replies Ramaphosa over appeal to remember origin appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Tinubu’s visit: Kebbi commuters hail President over Malando-Ngaski road reconstruction
description:
From Ola Muhammad, Birnin Kebbi

Commuters and residents along the Malando-Garin Baka-Ngaski-Wara-Auna corridor in Ngaski Local Government Area of Kebbi state have commended President Bola Tinubu for the ongoing reconstruction of the road, saying it has cut travel time, boosted trade and improved se
content:
From Ola Muhammad, Birnin Kebbi

Commuters and residents along the Malando-Garin Baka-Ngaski-Wara-Auna corridor in Ngaski Local Government Area of Kebbi state have commended President Bola Tinubu for the ongoing reconstruction of the road, saying it has cut travel time, boosted trade and improved security.

They spoke to the newsmen ahead of Tinubu’s visit to Kebbi State on Tuesday for the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally.

Residents described the project as a dividend of democracy that has reconnected communities long cut off by bad roads.

Malam Mamman Garba, a commercial driver on the Ngaski-Auna route, said the road had slashed travel time by almost 50 per cent.

” Previously, we spent several hours navigating bad portions, especially during the rainy season.Vehicles frequently broke down, while transport fares increased.

” Now, movement is faster and safer. Our daily income has improved because we can make more trips,” he said.

Hajiya Mohammed Aliyu, a trader from Wara, said the road had made it easier and cheaper to move farm produce to markets.

” Before now, transporting farm produce to markets was difficult and expensive, leading to losses for traders and farmers. The road has reduced these challenges and created more business opportunities for our people,” she said.

A former Commissioner for Lands and Housing in Kebbi, Alhaji Mahmuda Mohammed-Wara, called the project a major federal intervention that had brought relief to the communities.

He recalled that Minister of Budget and Economic Planning, Sen. Abubakar Atiku Bagudu, had assured residents on an earlier visit that funding would not stall the project, adding that the minister had kept his word.

A former Chairman of Ngaski Local Government Area, Alhaji Abdullahi Buhari-Wara, commended Tinubu, Gov. Nasir Idris and Bagudu for the collaboration that brought the project to the area.

He said many residents had initially doubted that the road would be completed, given the history of failed and abandoned contracts along the corridor.

” However, during his visit to the state last year, the Minister of Works, Sen. Dave Umahi, assured stakeholders of strict supervision and zero tolerance for substandard work.

” We have since witnessed significant progress, which has renewed the confidence of the people,” he said.

The Federal Government awarded the contract in late 2024, after years of failed attempts and abandoned contracts largely blamed on the difficult terrain.

Our correspondent who visited the site observed considerable progress by the contractor, Epsilon Sky Global Engineering Ltd.

The firm’s Managing Director, Mr Marcel Hattab, said the work had advanced despite bad weather and occasional disruptions in material supply caused by insecurity.

He said the wearing course on the Auna-Wara section had been completed, while the binder course and final earthworks were progressing towards Ngaski town.

Hattab said the project covers the rehabilitation of about 35 kilometres of severely deteriorated road.

According to him, the road will ease the movement of goods and services between Niger, Kebbi, Sokoto and Zamfara states and other parts of the country.

He added that the project had created hundreds of jobs, supported mining activities around Wara and helped reduce travel time, vehicle damage and insecurity along the corridor.

Hattab also commended Tinubu, Idris and Bagudu for their roles in facilitating the project.

The post Tinubu’s visit: Kebbi commuters hail President over Malando-Ngaski road reconstruction appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Lagos ADC deputy gov candidate warns against rigging, dares riggers
description:
Babatunde Gbadamosi, the Lagos State deputy governorship candidate of the African Democratic Congress, has warned against electoral manipulation in the state, citing President Bola Tinubu’s past warning against election rigging.
Gbadamosi issued the warning in a post on X on Tuesday while reacting t
content:
Babatunde Gbadamosi, the Lagos State deputy governorship candidate of the African Democratic Congress, has warned against electoral manipulation in the state, citing President Bola Tinubu’s past warning against election rigging.

Gbadamosi issued the warning in a post on X on Tuesday while reacting to a video of Nollywood actor and social media personality, Lege Miamii, in which he cautioned Nigerians calling for a revolution to stage it in their respective states rather than Lagos.

Responding to the video, Gbadamosi recalled Tinubu’s 2014 remark against election rigging, as well as similar statements previously made by former President Muhammadu Buhari.

He wrote, “Bola Ahmed Tinubu @officialABAT said the words ‘Rig and Roast’ in April 2014, during a speech at Ladoke Akintola University of Technology (LAUTECH) in Ogbomoso, Oyo State.

“He made the remark while speaking about the upcoming governorship elections in Ekiti and Osun states at the time. He warned that if the elections were rigged, the consequences would be severe, stating: ‘It is going to be rig and roast’.”

Gbadamosi also cited Buhari’s past remarks on electoral offences, writing, “Buhari: In 2011, he used the word ‘Halaka’ at a rally. In 2012, he said ‘Kare jini, biri kini’.

“In 2019, during an APC caucus meeting, Buhari warned that anyone planning to snatch ballot boxes or disrupt elections would be doing so ‘at the expense of their lives.’ He stated he had instructed security agencies to be ruthless with electoral offenders.”

He further referenced Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, in his comparison of the reactions to the statements.

“@fkeyamo went on TV to explain that it was legal to say so,” he wrote.

Gbadamosi added, “What is good for the goose, is good for the gander.”

He challenged anyone who considered his warning an empty threat to attempt to rig an election in Lagos.

“If you think it’s a joke, please, by all means, try rig the election in Lagos,” he said.

He ended the post with the hashtags #RigAndDie2027 and #TakeYourFitnessSeriously.

The post followed comments by Lege Miamii, who, in a video circulated on social media on Monday, cautioned those advocating a revolution against the Federal Government to stage it in their respective states rather than Lagos.

The actor, a known supporter of Tinubu and the All Progressives Congress, was responding to criticism of the government and calls for political action, with some social media users linking his remarks to blogger Tunde Ednut.

Lege has previously spoken against protests and unrest in Lagos, including during the 2024 #EndBadGovernance demonstrations, when he urged Nigerians to give the Federal Government more time.

title: FG orders hiring freeze across federal agencies
description: The Federal Government has directed Ministries, Departments and Agencies to maintain their existing workforce strength in 2027, warning that institutions that fail to submit their staff records and defend their personnel budget proposals may be denied authorised establishments and budgetary provisio
content:
The Federal Government has directed Ministries, Departments and Agencies to maintain their existing workforce strength in 2027, warning that institutions that fail to submit their staff records and defend their personnel budget proposals may be denied authorised establishments and budgetary provisions for the fiscal year.

The government also prohibited federal institutions from creating additional positions or expanding their organisational structures without approval from the Office of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation.

The directives were contained in a November 9, 2026, circular titled ‘2027 Workforce Budget Call Circular,’ issued by the Office of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation and signed by the Permanent Secretary, Service Policies and Strategies Office, Ishiyaku Musa Mohammed.

The circular, addressed to the Chief of Staff to the President, Deputy Chief of Staff to the Vice President, Secretary to the Government of the Federation, ministers, permanent secretaries, service chiefs, heads of federal institutions and chief executives of government agencies, directed all Ministries, Departments and Agencies to submit their workforce budget proposals for the 2027 fiscal year for consideration and approval.

It said the directive was aimed at consolidating the gains of the Federal Government’s public service reform programmes, particularly in human capacity development, while ensuring that personnel requirements were properly captured in the next budget.

The Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission assessed 344 MDAs in its 2025 Ethics and Integrity Compliance Scorecard, according to reports, indicating that Nigeria has over 300 federal MDAs.

The circular stated, “MDAs are advised to strictly maintain their current staff position for the 2027 fiscal year.”

It, however, acknowledged that some institutions might have genuine manpower needs but insisted that requests for additional personnel must be properly justified and supported by evidence of funding.

“However, where it is absolutely necessary to seek an increase, such requests should be supported with justifications attaching relevant information, including financial provision in the budget to meet additional emolument commitment; otherwise the existing workforce ceiling should not be exceeded,” it stated.

Additional departments banned

The government further warned against creating additional departments, units and other organisational structures without clearance from the Office of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation.

It directed that every workforce budget proposal must be accompanied by a copy of the institution’s approved organisational structure, stressing that vacancies must not be created for positions in structures that had not received official approval.

The circular specifically cautioned MDAs against creating unauthorised vacancies, particularly for positions at Salary Grade Levels 15 to 17 or their equivalents, which cover senior and top-level officers in the federal public service.

The directive effectively places restrictions on workforce expansion across federal institutions, requiring agencies seeking additional personnel to demonstrate that their requests are necessary, approved, and financially sustainable.

The circular further mandated MDAs to submit detailed nominal rolls of their employees as of October 31, 2026, alongside their workforce budget proposals, in what appears to be an effort to establish the actual number of workers across federal institutions and verify their personnel records.

It prescribed three categories of nominal rolls: an omnibus nominal roll arranged according to grade levels, a department-by-department record, and a cadre-by-cadre record.

Under the omnibus arrangement, institutions are required to list officers from the highest to the lowest grade levels, irrespective of their cadres.

For departmental records, employees must be listed according to their departments, beginning with the director or most senior officer, while the cadre-by-cadre nominal roll must capture personnel in each cadre according to seniority.

Requirements for promotion

The government also directed MDAs to submit the names of all officers due for promotion during the 2027 budget year, indicating their cadres and salary grade levels.

Other documents required include a summary of promotion cases according to cadres and salary grade levels, a breakdown of vacancies available for recruitment, and a summary of the number of officers in each cadre.

The circular stated that the information must be submitted using the prescribed formats, including personnel cost summaries, workforce budget summaries and details of existing staff positions.

It also directed institutions operating different salary structures to harmonise them into either the Salary Grade Level 03–17 or 02–15 structure, as appropriate.

The government fixed November 20, 2026, as the deadline for submitting the workforce budget proposals, which must be endorsed by the Permanent Secretary or Chief Executive/Accounting Officer of each institution.

The submissions are to be forwarded electronically in Excel spreadsheet format to the Office of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation through designated email addresses.

Budget consequences

The government warned that failure to comply with the November 20 deadline could have serious consequences for the affected institutions’ personnel budget provisions.

According to the circular, bilateral discussions with ministries, departments and agencies to examine their workforce budget proposals would commence on November 23, 2026.

It directed institutions to adhere strictly to the meeting schedule, warning that requests to reschedule the discussions would not be entertained.

More significantly, the government threatened to exclude defaulting institutions from the 2027 authorised establishment process, potentially leaving them without personnel provisions in the next Appropriation.

It stated, “Any MDA that fails to submit its workforce budget by Friday, 20th November, 2026 or fails to attend the meetings to defend its proposal may not have Authorised Establishments for the year 2027.

“This would imply that provisions may not be made in the Appropriation for the year under consideration.”

The implication is that institutions that fail to submit their proposals or defend their manpower requirements could be left without approved staffing establishments for the 2027 fiscal year, potentially affecting their ability to secure budgetary provisions for personnel requirements.

The government also directed every MDA to attend the bilateral discussions with copies of its approved organisational structure or organogram and the current year’s staff-in-post records, showing established positions and vacancies.

It further instructed ministries to submit lists of all agencies under their supervision and ensure that the agencies participate in the 2027 manpower budget exercise. The circular warned that inaccuracies or shortcomings in the records submitted would attract sanctions under the Public Service Rules.

“Inaccuracies and shortcomings in records submitted shall be treated in accordance with the Public Service Rule 100402,” it stated.

The meetings are scheduled to be held at the Conference Room of the Permanent Secretary, Service Policies and Strategies Office, on the third floor of Block A, Office of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation, Federal Secretariat Complex, Abuja.

The circular concluded by directing all concerned institutions to ensure strict compliance with its provisions.

The latest directive comes amid a series of measures by the Federal Government to strengthen personnel management, curb irregularities in the public service payroll and ensure that government institutions operate within approved staffing and expenditure limits.

It also represents another layer of scrutiny in the preparation of the 2027 budget, following earlier measures introduced by the Budget Office of the Federation to tighten controls over personnel expenditure and the eligibility of government agencies to receive public funding.

In September 2026, the Budget Office issued a separate 2027 Personnel Costs Budget Call Circular, directing MDAs to submit their personnel cost proposals alongside their establishment Acts to establish their legal status.

The circular, signed by the Director-General of the Budget Office, Tanimu Yakubu, warned that failure to submit the required establishment Acts could lead to the rejection of an agency’s budget proposal.

The Budget Office also directed that no personnel cost provision should be made in the 2027 budget for serving federal employees who were not captured on the Integrated Personnel and Payroll Information System or enrolled on the Government Integrated Financial Management Information System, except where specific exemptions had been granted.

The measures followed concerns over the existence of fictitious government agencies and questionable personnel expenditure, with the government seeking to prevent unauthorised institutions and workers from accessing public funds.

The new directive by the Office of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation, however, places additional emphasis on the actual workforce strength, approved organisational structures, vacancies, promotions and manpower requirements of individual institutions.

It comes against the backdrop of the Federal Government’s ongoing Personnel Audit and Skills Gap Analysis, initiated in August 2025 to determine the actual size, structure and skills composition of the federal civil service.

The exercise, coordinated by the Office of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation, was designed to identify the competencies required across government institutions and establish a more efficient and fit-for-purpose public service.

The government said the audit would help identify existing workforce gaps and determine the skills required to improve service delivery.

title: Pique faults 12-match ban for goalkeeper after footballer’s death
description:
Former Barcelona defender and FC Andorra owner Gerard Pique has criticised the 12-match suspension handed to his club’s goalkeeper Jesus Owono following a collision that led to the death of Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel.
Owono and De Miguel collided during a Spanish second-tier match on November
content:
Former Barcelona defender and FC Andorra owner Gerard Pique has criticised the 12-match suspension handed to his club’s goalkeeper Jesus Owono following a collision that led to the death of Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel.

Owono and De Miguel collided during a Spanish second-tier match on November 2. De Miguel was taken to intensive care but died the following day.

The disciplinary committee of the Spanish football federation (RFEF) last week suspended Owono for 12 matches for violent conduct resulting in serious injury.

However, in a video posted on TikTok on Monday, Pique said the goalkeeper did not deserve the punishment, insisting that the incident was an accident.

“Players, former players, coaches, goalkeepers, everyone has called it an accident.

“I truly believe that imposing the maximum sanction on Jesus for this action puts him in a situation he does not deserve, because he is not to blame for all of this having happened,” he said.

Pique compared Owono’s punishment with the three-match suspension given to Albacete’s Jose Corpas for accidentally kicking Sabadell player Quadri Liameed in the head during another Spanish match.

“Fortunately Quadri is fine, the consequences in this case were not fatal, and the committee decided to sanction Corpas with three matches,” he added.

Questioning the basis for the difference in the punishments, Pique said, “With all this, my reflection is: what is being sanctioned, the action or the consequences?”

Owono, 25, has withdrawn from Equatorial Guinea’s squad for this month’s Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers against Zimbabwe.

Pique also expressed doubt that the goalkeeper would be ready to return to competitive football immediately after serving his suspension.

“Jesus is going to need far more than 12 matches before he is available and able to compete.

“No sanction is going to bring Demi (De Miguel) back to us,” he added.

In its disciplinary ruling, the RFEF said the referee’s report described Owono as striking De Miguel in the chest with his raised leg and using excessive force while the ball was in play.

The federation classified the incident as a serious offence under Article 102 of its disciplinary code and said the circumstances justified the maximum punishment of 12 matches.

PUNCH Online reports that the Tenerife coach, Álvaro Cervera, had earlier said Owono’s 12-match suspension appeared light considering De Miguel’s death, although he acknowledged that the Spanish football federation had imposed the maximum punishment allowed under its existing regulations.

“It might seem a bit light when compared to other cases, but in reality, I don’t think the rules allow for anything else,” Cervera said.

The post Pique faults 12-match ban for goalkeeper after footballer’s death appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Kano targets $700m sesame, hibiscus exports by 2027
description:
Kano State exported sesame seeds and hibiscus flowers worth more than $350m in 2025, an official of the Nigerian Export Promotion Council has said.
The State Coordinator of the NEPC, Yusuf Ahmed, disclosed this on Monday during the National Single Window Phase Two Sensitisation and Joint Stakeholder
content:
Kano State exported sesame seeds and hibiscus flowers worth more than $350m in 2025, an official of the Nigerian Export Promotion Council has said.

The State Coordinator of the NEPC, Yusuf Ahmed, disclosed this on Monday during the National Single Window Phase Two Sensitisation and Joint Stakeholders Forum in Kano.

Ahmed expressed optimism that the value of the state’s exports of the two commodities could double to $700m by 2027 with the commencement of the National Single Window project, expected to begin operations in December.

“Kano exported over $350 million worth of Sesame and Hibiscus alone in 2025. But we can double this to $700 million by 2027 if documentation becomes easier.

“National Single Window phase two is the tool to double it,” he said.

Ahmed described Kano as Nigeria’s leading exporter of sesame seeds, hibiscus flowers and leather.

He commended Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf for supporting non-oil exports in the state, while acknowledging the contributions of other export regulatory agencies to the sector.

The NEPC coordinator urged exporters to participate actively in the engagement by asking questions and sharing their experiences to help achieve the project’s objectives.

Earlier, the NEPC North-West Regional Coordinator, Amina Abdulmalik, described the forum as timely, noting that Kano was a major commercial centre in northern Nigeria and accounted for more than 40 per cent of the region’s non-oil exports.

She listed sesame, hibiscus flowers, ginger, groundnuts, onions, cowpeas, chilli peppers and leather among the region’s major non-oil export products.

Abdulmalik, however, said exporters continued to face delays, multiple charges and repeated physical examinations at different government agency offices.

“This forum is timely and strategic. Kano State is the commercial nerve center of commerce in Northern Nigeria, contributing over 40% of non-oil exports from the North: Sesame, Hibiscus Flower (Zobo), Ginger, Groundnut, Onions, Cowpea, Chilli Pepper, and Leather.

“Yet our exporters face delays, multiple charges, and physical examination at every agency desk. National Single Window is the Federal Government’s answer to that problem,” she said.

The engagement is part of the Federal Government’s efforts to sensitise stakeholders, deepen understanding and encourage participation in the implementation of the National Single Window project.

The initiative is designed to establish a centralised electronic trade platform that will streamline import and export processes by integrating and harmonising documentation and procedures across government agencies and other stakeholders.

The National Single Window is a Federal Government initiative aimed at reducing the administrative burden associated with international trade by allowing traders to submit required information and documents through a single electronic platform rather than dealing separately with multiple agencies.

The system is expected to improve coordination among government agencies, reduce delays and make trade documentation more transparent and efficient.

For exporters in Kano and other parts of northern Nigeria, improved processing could help reduce the time and costs involved in moving agricultural commodities and other products to international markets.
