According to a regulatory filing submitted to the Nigerian Exchange Limited on Monday, Osuachala, who serves as the Group Head, SME Banking, disposed
content:
A senior executive of Access Holdings Plc, Arinze Osuachala, has sold five million ordinary shares of the financial services group valued at N129.5m.

According to a regulatory filing submitted to the Nigerian Exchange Limited on Monday, Osuachala, who serves as the Group Head, SME Banking, disposed of the shares in a single transaction conducted in Lagos on 6 November 2026.

The disclosure, signed by the Company Secretary of Access Holdings Plc, Sunday Ekwochi, indicated that the ordinary shares were sold at a unit price of N25.90 per share.

In the notification titled Notification of Share Dealing by Insiders, the financial institution stated, “Details of the transaction(s): Description of the financial instrument, type of instrument, Identification Code: Ordinary Shares, ISIN: NGACCESS0005.

Nature of the transaction: Sale. Aggregated volume: 5,000,000. Price: N25.90k. Date of Transaction: November 6, 2026. Place of Transaction: Lagos.”

The filing noted that the submission represents an initial notification made in compliance with post-listing disclosure requirements governing share dealings by directors and insiders on the Nigerian Exchange Limited.

Insider dealing disclosures are mandated under the listing rules of the Nigerian Exchange Limited and the Investments and Securities Act to promote transparency, accountability and investor confidence in the capital market. Under these rules, directors, persons discharging managerial responsibilities and closely associated persons are required to notify the issuer and the exchange of any transactions conducted on their own account in the shares or debt instruments of the company.

Meanwhile, trading data from the Nigerian Exchange Limited showed that Access Holdings Plc closed Monday’s trading session at N27.00 per share, representing a 0.74 per cent decline from its previous closing price, with a total market capitalisation of N1.47tn. The tier-one financial group also emerged as the most actively traded equity by volume on the exchange on Monday, recording a turnover of 203.62 million shares across 1,488 deals.

Access Holdings Plc operates from its head office at Oniru Estate, Victoria Island, Lagos, with Aigboje Aig-Imoukhuede as Chairman and Innocent Ike as Group Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer.

title: 1,200 business leaders for Lagos summit
description:
Lagos is set to host approximately 1,200 business leaders, policymakers, diplomats, investors and academics at the 14th edition of the GAH Awards & Business Summit, scheduled for Wednesday, December 16, 2026, at Eko Hotels & Suites, Victoria Island.
The summit, themed “The New Africa Economy: Vision
content:
Lagos is set to host approximately 1,200 business leaders, policymakers, diplomats, investors and academics at the 14th edition of the GAH Awards & Business Summit, scheduled for Wednesday, December 16, 2026, at Eko Hotels & Suites, Victoria Island.

The summit, themed “The New Africa Economy: Vision, Capital & Influence,” will bring together influential voices from across Africa and beyond to discuss investment, business growth, economic development and the continent’s position in the global economy.

Former United Nations Under-Secretary-General and Executive Secretary of the UN Economic Commission for Africa, Dr. Vera Songwe, will deliver a keynote address. The Consul General of the United Arab Emirates in Lagos, His Excellency Salem Aljaberi, will attend as the Special Guest.

Other confirmed keynote speakers include investment banker and Group Chief Executive Officer of Emerging Africa Group, Dr. Oluwatoyin F. Sanni; Professor Lere Baale, Director at Business School Netherlands Nigeria; Adebola Williams, Co-Founder and CEO of RED; Professor Chris Ogbechie of Lagos Business School; and Professor Ahmadou Aly Mbaye of Cheikh Anta Diop University, Dakar.

Founder and Executive Chair of the GAH Awards & Business Summit, Dr. Princess Oghene, said the gathering would provide an important platform for investors, governments and entrepreneurs to examine practical solutions to Africa’s economic challenges.

“A business owner deciding whether to open a second factory needs to know whether she can finance it, whether she can reach customers across borders and whether the rules will hold long enough for her to invest,” Oghene said.

“Those are decisions that investors, governments and entrepreneurs often discuss in separate rooms. We are bringing them together in Lagos to examine what each can do to make the next investment possible.”

According to the organisers, discussions will focus on financing African businesses, developing infrastructure, expanding regional trade and strengthening the continent’s influence in international investment decisions.

The programme will also examine opportunities arising from the African Continental Free Trade Area and the African Union’s Agenda 2063, particularly in mobilising long-term capital for industrialisation, enterprise development and job creation.

The featured speakers and panellists will include retired Commissioner of Police Fatai Owoseni, Pharm. Chidinma Odu-Obi, Professor Olu Ogunsakin, Dr. Chinyere Almona, Director-General of the Lagos Chamber of Commerce and Industry, and Hon. Joshua Audu Gana. Dr. Joseph Ogebe will serve as moderator.

The 14th edition builds on the summit’s record of bringing together prominent figures from government, diplomacy, business and traditional institutions.

The 13th edition, held in December 2025 under the theme “Africa Reimagined: Innovation, Inclusion & Sustainable Growth,” attracted more than 1,000 guests to Eko Hotels & Suites.

His Imperial Majesty, Oba Adeyeye Enitan Ogunwusi, CFR, Ajájá II, the Ooni of Ife, served as Grand Patron and Father of the Day, while Dr. Babatope Agbeyo, Group Managing Director of Cornfield Group, served as Chairman.

Other notable participants included Zamfara State Governor, Dr. Dauda Lawal; Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, SAN, CON; Chairman and CEO of Air Peace, Dr. Allen Ifechukwu Onyema; and Chairman and CEO of United Nigeria Airlines, Professor Obiora Gregory Okonkwo.

Founded in 2012, the GAH Awards & Business Summit reports that its first 12 editions recognised more than 350 distinguished honourees and attracted over 20,000 cumulative guests and delegates, with more than N700 million in media visibility and partnership value.

title: Fountain varsity don urges action on inequalities in schools
description:
A Professor of Language Education at Fountain University, Osogbo, Serifat Labo-Popoola, has called on governments and educational institutions to address inequalities in school facilities, teacher availability, learning resources and digital access to improve learning outcomes in Nigeria.
She made t
content:
A Professor of Language Education at Fountain University, Osogbo, Serifat Labo-Popoola, has called on governments and educational institutions to address inequalities in school facilities, teacher availability, learning resources and digital access to improve learning outcomes in Nigeria.

She made the call while delivering her inaugural lecture, titled “Inside the English Learning Ecosystem: The Combined Power of Schools, Teachers, Learner Behaviours and Digital Tools,” at the university’s ninth inaugural lecture on Friday.

Labo-Popoola said effective English Language Education required more than classroom teaching, noting that school conditions, teacher quality, learners’ behaviour, access to technology and educational policies were interconnected factors influencing students’ academic performance.

She urged governments and educational institutions to prioritise equitable access to educational opportunities, particularly for learners in disadvantaged schools and communities.

“Government and educational institutions should give priority to reducing disparities in school conditions, staffing, learning resources, digital access and opportunities for participation,” she said.

The professor also called for stronger connections between academic research, educational policies and classroom practices to ensure that research findings translated into practical improvements in teaching and learning.

She said, “Research-policy-practice linkages in English Language Education should be more deliberately connected to policy formulation, institutional decision-making and classroom practice.”

According to her, educational policies must recognise the relationship between school conditions, teacher quality and learner behaviour, stressing that interventions should address the factors collectively rather than treating them as separate challenges.

Labo-Popoola explained that students’ academic performance was influenced by several interconnected factors, including school population, student-to-classroom ratio, student-teacher ratio, motivation, study habits and access to learning resources.

She noted that the availability of digital technology did not automatically translate into improved learning outcomes, observing that although many teachers had internet-enabled mobile phones, only a few used them for instructional purposes.

The don attributed the limited adoption of technology in some classrooms partly to inadequate school facilities, adding that teachers needed appropriate resources, skills and institutional support to integrate digital tools effectively into teaching.

She also highlighted the importance of learners’ motivation and study habits, citing research findings which showed that motivated students performed substantially better in English Language.

On educational equity, Labo-Popoola drew attention to the challenges facing disadvantaged learners, particularly girls whose educational opportunities were affected by poverty, child labour, early marriage and teenage pregnancy.

She argued that providing access to schools was insufficient without addressing the social and economic conditions that enabled children to remain in school and benefit from education.

The professor further examined the relationship between language, technology and sustainable development, emphasising the need to strengthen indigenous languages while improving English Language Education.

She concluded that English Language Education was a complex and interconnected enterprise, explaining that students’ learning and academic achievements were shaped by the interaction of human resources, school environments, technology and educational policies.

The inaugural lecture was chaired by the Vice-Chancellor of Fountain University, Prof Olayinka Kareem.

Highlighting Labo-Popoola’s contributions to academic development, Kareem said, “Professor Serifat Olubunmi Labo-Popoola has supervised four PhD projects, five master’s dissertations and 20 undergraduate projects.”

title: Lasaco Assurance granted one-year free-float extension
description:
NGX Regulation Limited has extended Lasaco Assurance Plc deadline by one year, to 2 November 2027, to address its free-float shortfall and meet the post-listing requirements of the Nigerian Exchange Limited.
In a corporate disclosure signed by the Company Secretary and Investor Relations Officer, Ge
content:
NGX Regulation Limited has extended Lasaco Assurance Plc deadline by one year, to 2 November 2027, to address its free-float shortfall and meet the post-listing requirements of the Nigerian Exchange Limited.

In a corporate disclosure signed by the Company Secretary and Investor Relations Officer, Gertrude Olutekunbi, and filed with the exchange on Monday, 16 November 2026, the insurer notified its shareholders and the investing public that its free float currently falls below the minimum 20 per cent issued share capital threshold required for companies listed on the NGX Main Board.

The company stated that the extension would enable it to meet the exchange’s Main Board free-float benchmark of 20 per cent issued and fully paid share capital or N20bn free-float market capitalisation.

The notice explained the regulatory basis for the grace period: “This is in line with Rule 3.1.4 of The Exchange’s Rules Governing Free Float Requirements, which states that ‘The Exchange may suspend trading in the Company’s securities if the Company does not achieve the required free float within the stipulated time frame.’”

Reassuring investors of its commitment to resolving the shortfall before the new deadline, the insurer added, “The Board and Management of Lasaco remain committed to taking all necessary steps to achieve the required free float within the approved period and will keep shareholders and NGX RegCo informed of progress.”

Free-float requirements are designed by the Nigerian Exchange Limited to ensure sufficient liquidity, fair price discovery and broad public participation in listed equities, preventing excessive share concentration among majority shareholders.

Meanwhile, trading data from the Nigerian Exchange Limited showed that Lasaco Assurance Plc closed Monday’s trading session at N1.87 per share, representing a 1.58 per cent decline from its previous closing price of N1.90, with a total market capitalisation of N38.00bn after investors exchanged 1.84 million shares across 111 deals.

Lasaco Assurance Plc operates from its head office at Ogba, Ikeja, Lagos, and is regulated by the National Insurance Commission, with Babatunde Dabiri serving as Chairman and Ademoye Shobo as Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer.

title: Lagos urged to unlock $2.5bn waste economy potential
description:
Stakeholders in the Lagos waste management sector have said that the industry has the potential to generate about $2.5bn and create thousands of jobs if the state adopts a circular economy model.
They called on the Lagos State Government to move beyond conventional waste collection and disposal to a
content:
Stakeholders in the Lagos waste management sector have said that the industry has the potential to generate about $2.5bn and create thousands of jobs if the state adopts a circular economy model.

They called on the Lagos State Government to move beyond conventional waste collection and disposal to a system that treats recyclable and reusable materials as valuable economic resources.

The stakeholders made the call during a virtual policy dialogue organised by the Lagos Waste Forum in collaboration with SWEEP Foundation NG recently.

The dialogue, themed ‘The Governor’s Brief: Setting a Waste Policy Agenda for the Next Lagos’, focused on developing policies to unlock the economic potential of the state’s waste sector.

According to a statement issued on Sunday by SWEEP Foundation, participants cited an estimate attributed to the Lagos State Waste Management Authority that the state’s waste economy had a potential value of about $2.5bn.

They said achieving the projection would require increased investment in recycling infrastructure, composting and biogas facilities, as well as the development of structured markets for recovered materials.

The participants identified organic waste and plastics as major resources that could be recovered and processed to support local industries, create employment and reduce the volume of waste transported to dumpsites.

They also called for stronger private sector participation and policies capable of attracting investment in waste recovery and recycling.

The stakeholders further urged the government to integrate informal waste operators, including waste pickers, into the state’s waste management value chain to improve efficiency and provide better working conditions for those involved in recycling activities.

They stressed the need for reliable and disaggregated waste data to help the government and investors identify opportunities and make informed decisions in the sector.

Convener of the Lagos Waste Forum, Amb. Obuesi Phillips, said the dialogue was organised to generate practical recommendations that would guide the incoming Lagos State administration.

Phillips said the recommendations from the engagement would be compiled into a policy document for presentation to the incoming governor and other relevant stakeholders.

The Publisher of Prime Business Africa, Dr Marcel Mbamalu; Metro Editor of PUNCH Newspapers, Joel Nwokeoma; BBC senior journalist, Esther Omaporiola; and City Scope Africa’s John Fatanmi were among those who participated in the dialogue.

The seventh edition of the Lagos Waste Forum, themed ‘The Circular Megacity’, is scheduled to hold on December 10, 2026, at the Adeyemi Bero Auditorium, Lagos State Secretariat, Alausa, Ikeja.

title: Okebukola-led committee validates data for national varsity ranking
description:
The National Tertiary Education Research and Accreditation Centre, chaired by Prof. Peter Okebukola, has completed the collation, validation, and peer review of data for the December ranking of Nigerian universities.
Okebukola disclosed this in an interview with The PUNCH in Abuja, saying the centre
content:
The National Tertiary Education Research and Accreditation Centre, chaired by Prof. Peter Okebukola, has completed the collation, validation, and peer review of data for the December ranking of Nigerian universities.

Okebukola disclosed this in an interview with The PUNCH in Abuja, saying the centre had also commenced a dry run of the ranking exercise ahead of its planned release.

He expressed confidence that the exercise would be completed ahead of schedule, ruling out any challenges that could affect the December timeline.

He said, “No challenges at all, at all. We will achieve the target date even earlier by God’s grace. All ranking data are in, fully validated and peer-reviewed. We have started the dry run of the ranking.”

The NiTERAC chairman said the centre expected to finalise the ranking in the first week of December before forwarding the report to the Minister of Education, Dr Tunji Alausa, for approval.

“We should finalise the ranking by the first week of December and send it to the HME for approval, following which NiTERAC will release it during a national virtual conference on December 15,” he said.

The ranking exercise is part of efforts to strengthen the assessment of Nigerian tertiary institutions through data-driven evaluation and provide comparative information on their performance.

The university ranking will use 22 indicators, with weightings agreed with the League of Directors of Academic Planning, while the three subsector rankings are scheduled for completion before December 15, 2026.

The national ranking is expected to provide institutions with a domestic benchmark against which they can measure their performance, identify gaps and plan improvements.

title: Polaris Bank deepens commitment to girl-child education
description:
Polaris Bank, in partnership with Evolve Charity Trust, has provided essential learning materials to 640 students across 10 public secondary schools in Nigeria, reinforcing its commitment to improving access to education and supporting the girl child.
Now in its sixth year, the intervention forms pa
content:
Polaris Bank, in partnership with Evolve Charity Trust, has provided essential learning materials to 640 students across 10 public secondary schools in Nigeria, reinforcing its commitment to improving access to education and supporting the girl child.

Now in its sixth year, the intervention forms part of the bank’s Corporate Social Responsibility commitment to reducing the financial barriers that limit access to education, particularly for indigent students. By providing essential school supplies, the initiative seeks to ease the burden on families, curb the out-of-school menace, improve students’ readiness to learn, and encourage school attendance, especially among girls.

The distribution, according to the bank’s statement on Monday, covered public schools across Kano, Kogi, Imo, and Lagos states, as well as the Federal Capital Territory, Abuja. Beneficiaries included 100 students at Government Girls Secondary School, Kundila, Kano, and 60 students each at Government Junior Secondary School, Garki, and Model Junior Secondary School, Maitama, Abuja.

In Lagos, Opebi Junior Grammar School, Gbaja Girls Junior Secondary School, and Gbaja Girls Senior Secondary School each received materials for 60 students. Fortune Secondary School, Lokoja; National High School, Arondizuogu; Iheme Memorial Secondary School, Arondizuogu; and Akokwa High School, Akokwa, also benefited, with 60 students from each of the schools receiving the learning materials.

Beyond the provision of school supplies, the programme incorporates developmental interventions focused on brain training, emotional intelligence, and life skills to help students build confidence, strengthen their decision-making abilities, and prepare for opportunities beyond the classroom. Teachers in the affected schools also benefited from extended capacity building during the long holidays.

Speaking on the initiative, the Managing Director/Chief Executive Officer of Polaris Bank, Mr Kayode Lawal, said the programme reflected the bank’s commitment to creating meaningful social impact through education.

“The initiative is designed to support 50,000 students by 2028, building on its current reach of 24,000 students across 49 locations. Our goal, working with our CSR partners, is to help more children, particularly girls, access education and develop the required academic and functional skills and confidence to realise their potential,” he said.

Lawal said the initiative formed part of wider efforts to tackle Nigeria’s out-of-school problem and expand access to quality education. He stressed that the learning materials went beyond providing immediate academic assistance, reassuring students that their dreams were valid and that they could grow into accomplished scholars, innovators, and future leaders.

Speaking during the intervention at Gbaja Girls Junior and Senior Secondary Schools in Lagos, the Group Head, Customer Experience and Value Management, Polaris Bank, Mrs Bukola Oluyadi, said making basic learning resources available remained essential to helping students participate fully in their education.

“Every child deserves the opportunity to learn, grow and pursue their ambitions, regardless of their family’s financial circumstances. By providing this intervention, we are hopeful that the outcome will be to help ease some of the challenges students face and encourage them to remain focused on their education and future,” she said.

On his part, the Head, Brand Management and Corporate Communications, Polaris Bank, Rasheed Bolarinwa, said the initiative demonstrated the value of sustained partnerships in addressing community needs.

“Effective CSR goes beyond making commitments; it requires interventions that respond to real needs and deliver practical benefits. Through this partnership, we are helping students access essential learning resources while reinforcing the importance of education in building stronger communities,” he said.

Polaris Bank’s representatives across the participating states also encouraged beneficiaries to make the most of the intervention. In Kano, the Branch Head, Madiebo Godwin, reaffirmed the bank’s commitment to expanding access to educational opportunities, while in Lokoja, the Business Development Manager, Lokoja Branch, Shola Ogundele, urged students to use the materials responsibly and remain committed to their academic goals.

School leaders also welcomed the intervention, noting the importance of providing students with the resources required to participate effectively in classroom activities.

The Principal of Government Girls Secondary School, Kundila, Kano, Hajiya Aisha Yakasai, highlighted the importance of educational support for students whose families struggle to meet the cost of basic school supplies, while the Principal of Government Junior Secondary School, Garki, Abuja, Mr Rayyanu Ogande, welcomed the intervention and its contribution to supporting students’ educational needs.

The Principal of Fortune Secondary School, Lokoja, Mrs Abu Esther, noted that access to essential learning materials could improve students’ morale, encourage classroom participation, and help them concentrate on their studies.

At Model Junior Secondary School, Maitama, Abuja, the Director/Principal, Dr Mary Ebong, acknowledged the financial pressures many families face in providing for their children’s educational needs, describing interventions that address these gaps as valuable support for students and their parents.

Similarly, the Principal of Gbaja Girls Junior Secondary School, Surulere, Lagos, Mrs Dabiri Adetoun Iyabo, and the Principal of Opebi Junior Grammar School, M. O. Owolabi, highlighted the importance of sustained educational support in enabling students to make the most of available learning opportunities.

In Imo State, the principals of the beneficiary schools, Mrs Oraneto F. C. of National High School, Arondizuogu; Mrs Nwosu Adanna of Iheme Memorial Secondary School, Arondizuogu; and Mrs Nwokeji C. A. of Akokwa High School, Akokwa, welcomed the intervention and commended its contribution to supporting students’ educational needs.

The initiative builds on Polaris Bank’s partnership with Evolve Charity Trust, which commenced in 2021, and contributes to the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals, particularly SDG 4 (Quality Education) and SDG 5 (Gender Equality).A

content:

title: Criminal cases suffer over court rejection of confessional statements – Nasarawa gov
description:
Nasarawa State Governor, Abdullahi Sule, has raised concerns over the loss of criminal cases due to procedural lapses in obtaining and presenting confessional statements, urging prosecutors and law enforcement officers to keep abreast of evolving legal requirements.
Sule said inadequate knowledge of
content:
Nasarawa State Governor, Abdullahi Sule, has raised concerns over the loss of criminal cases due to procedural lapses in obtaining and presenting confessional statements, urging prosecutors and law enforcement officers to keep abreast of evolving legal requirements.

Sule said inadequate knowledge of emerging legal principles and failure to comply with established procedures could weaken prosecution and allow criminal cases to fail in court.

The governor spoke on Monday in Lafia through the Secretary to the State Government, Labaran Magaji (SAN), at a one-day workshop on the practice and procedure for obtaining, tendering and admissibility of confessional statements in criminal trials.

The workshop was organised by the Nasarawa State chapter of the Law Officers Association of Nigeria, with the theme, “Navigating Charles v. State of Lagos and Compliance with ACJA 2015 and ACJL of Nasarawa State, 2018 for Effective Prosecution.”

Sule described the workshop as an opportunity for prosecutors and other justice-sector stakeholders to examine emerging legal challenges and strengthen their capacity to handle criminal cases.

He lamented that some law officers concentrated more on reviewing case files and appearing in court than studying developments in the law, a situation he said could contribute to unsuccessful prosecutions.

“You are always excited going to court and reviewing your case files, but you have never had time to understudy the trending issues and emerging legal questions.

“And therefore, when you go to court, rather than winning more cases, you are always losing cases. So, opportunities like this will give us the time to look at the past, consider the present and determine what we are going to do tomorrow in our jobs,” he said.

The governor urged participants to take advantage of the workshop, engage the resource persons and ensure that the knowledge acquired translated into improved performance in their respective institutions.

He reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to the rule of law, judicial independence and strengthening institutions responsible for maintaining law and order.

Also speaking, the Attorney General and Commissioner for Justice, Isaac Danladi, said the government was committed to strengthening criminal prosecution in response to emerging security challenges.

Danladi explained that effective prosecution required coordinated efforts among investigators, prosecutors and other justice-sector stakeholders, beginning from the investigation and evidence-gathering stages to trial and post-trial proceedings.

He said the introduction of the Administration of Criminal Justice Act 2015 and its domestication in Nasarawa State through the 2018 law had fundamentally changed the procedures for obtaining and tendering confessional statements.

According to him, the police and other law enforcement agencies are now under binding legal obligations to comply with prescribed procedures before confessional statements can be admitted as evidence in court.

“Unlike the previous regime, where the process of obtaining and tendering confessional statements by the police and prosecutors was treated as merely administrative, the laws have created binding obligations on the police and other law enforcement agencies before such statements can be extracted, tendered and admitted in court,” he said.

The Attorney General stressed that compliance with the relevant provisions was essential because confessional statements could be relied upon by courts in determining criminal cases.

In her remarks, the Chief Judge of Nasarawa State, Justice Aisha Uthman, represented by Justice Abdullahi Shammah, said procedural errors in obtaining confessional statements remained a major challenge to successful criminal prosecution.

She observed that cases involving seemingly sufficient evidence could suffer setbacks where investigators failed to follow the legally prescribed procedures for obtaining confessional statements.

According to her, such lapses could render statements inadmissible and undermine the prosecution’s case, potentially resulting in the discharge of defendants.

The Chief Judge urged investigators to familiarise themselves with the Evidence Act and the state’s Administration of Criminal Justice Law, particularly provisions relating to the presence of legal representatives or video recording during the taking of confessional statements.

Earlier, the Chairman of the Law Officers Association of Nigeria, Nasarawa State chapter, Raymond Umoru, said the workshop was organised to address emerging legal developments and improve compliance with procedures governing criminal investigations.

Umoru said confessional statements constituted a significant part of evidence relied upon by prosecutors but regretted that some were rejected by courts because investigators failed to observe statutory requirements.

He explained that suspects were entitled to safeguards during the recording of their statements, including the presence of their lawyers, family members, civil society representatives or other persons of their choice.

Where such persons were unavailable, he said,  the law provided for video recording of the statement to promote transparency and protect suspects against torture, coercion and other unlawful practices.

The workshop featured judicial officers, legal practitioners and human rights advocates as facilitators. They included Justice Solomon Ayenajeh of the Nasarawa State Judiciary; Nuhu Egya, Second Vice-President of the Nigerian Bar Association; and Emmanuel Kuza, a human rights legal practitioner.

Participants included representatives of the Nigeria Police Force, Department of State Services, Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps, National Drug Law Enforcement Agency, National Agency for the Prohibition of Trafficking in Persons, the judiciary, Magistrates Association of Nigeria and Nigerian Bar Association, among other justice-sector stakeholders

title: Sokoto gov’s aide advocates home-grown technology to fight insecurity
description:
The Special Adviser on Security Matters to the Sokoto State Governor, Col. Ahmed Abdul Usman (retd.), has called on the Federal Government to harness the expertise of indigenous engineers and technologists to develop home-grown solutions to Nigeria’s security challenges.
Usman said the country could
content:
The Special Adviser on Security Matters to the Sokoto State Governor, Col. Ahmed Abdul Usman (retd.), has called on the Federal Government to harness the expertise of indigenous engineers and technologists to develop home-grown solutions to Nigeria’s security challenges.

Usman said the country could no longer rely solely on conventional security methods, stressing that emerging threats required innovative responses driven by technology and local expertise.

He spoke on Friday after receiving a Platinum Award from the Nigerian Association of Technologists in Engineering at its 42nd Conference of Technologists in Engineering and Annual General Meeting in Port Harcourt, Rivers State.

The conference, held from November 11 to 13, 2026, at the Obi Wali International Conference Centre, recognised his contributions to national development, particularly in security administration and the application of technology.

In his remarks, made available to ArewaPunch, the retired military officer said the recognition should encourage stronger partnerships between security agencies and professionals in the engineering and technology sectors.

He said such collaborations would help develop practical solutions tailored to Nigeria’s peculiar security challenges.

“Technology has become an indispensable tool in modern security operations. We must continually explore innovative ways of deploying technology to strengthen our security architecture and respond effectively to emerging threats,” he said.

Usman said Nigerian engineers and technologists possessed the expertise required to contribute meaningfully to national security, industrial growth and development.

“Nigeria must increasingly harness the expertise and ingenuity of its indigenous engineers and technologists to develop home-grown solutions capable of addressing our security, industrial and developmental challenges,” he added.

Describing the award as a call to greater responsibility, the governor’s aide said he considered the honour both an appreciation of his contributions and an encouragement to continue serving the country.

“I see this honour not only as an appreciation of my modest contributions to national development but also as a renewed call to greater service,” he said.

The conference was held under the theme, “Safety, Regulation and Enforcement in Engineering: A Panacea for Industrial and Technological Growth in Nigeria.”

Usman also emphasised the need for professionalism, accountability, effective regulation and compliance with safety standards in the deployment of technology.

The Rivers State Governor, Siminalayi Fubara, was represented at the event by his Chief of Staff, Mr Sunny Ewule.

title: NGX gives Lasaco until 2027 to meet free float requirement
description:
Lasaco Assurance Plc has secured a one-year extension from the Nigerian Exchange Limited’s regulatory arm to comply with the exchange’s minimum free float requirement for companies listed on its Main Board.
The extension, granted by NGX Regulation Limited, gives the insurer until 2 November, 2027, t
content:
Lasaco Assurance Plc has secured a one-year extension from the Nigerian Exchange Limited’s regulatory arm to comply with the exchange’s minimum free float requirement for companies listed on its Main Board.

The extension, granted by NGX Regulation Limited, gives the insurer until 2 November, 2027, to raise its free float to the required level.

Lasaco disclosed this in a notice to the investing public dated 16 November, 2026, stating that its free float currently falls below the minimum requirement of 20 per cent of its issued share capital.

Under the NGX rules, Main Board companies are required to maintain a free float of at least 20 per cent of their issued and fully paid-up share capital or a free float market capitalisation of N20bn.

The company said its board and management remained committed to taking necessary steps to meet the requirement within the approved extension period.

It also pledged to keep shareholders and NGX Regulation informed of progress towards compliance.

The extension is significant because failure to meet the requirement within the stipulated period could expose the insurer to trading suspension.

Rule 3.1.4 of the NGX Rules Governing Free Float Requirements empowers the exchange to suspend trading in a company’s securities if it fails to achieve the required free float within the stipulated timeframe.

Lasaco said it would continue working towards restoring compliance with its post-listing obligations.

The post NGX gives Lasaco until 2027 to meet free float requirement appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: UNDEF empowers 200 Plateau women to tackle climate change, prevent conflicts
description:
No fewer than 200 women in four communities in Plateau State are being equipped with skills to tackle climate change and prevent conflicts under a 24-month initiative funded by the United Nations Democracy Fund.
The project, implemented by the Grassroots Researchers Association, covers Angwan Rogo,
content:
No fewer than 200 women in four communities in Plateau State are being equipped with skills to tackle climate change and prevent conflicts under a 24-month initiative funded by the United Nations Democracy Fund.

The project, implemented by the Grassroots Researchers Association, covers Angwan Rogo, Farin Gada, Bukuru and Anglo Jos communities in Jos North and Jos South Local Government Areas of the state.

It seeks to establish women-led advocacy platforms to enable participants to influence community decisions, engage stakeholders on environmental challenges and promote peaceful coexistence.

Speaking with journalists on Friday during a workshop in Bukuru, Jos South LGA, the Executive Director of GRA, Friday Bitrus, said women were among the most affected by climate change because of their dependence on natural resources and their responsibilities in sustaining household livelihoods.

“Women are always at the receiving end when climate crises occur. They bear the consequences of flooding, changing weather patterns and other environmental challenges, yet they often lack the resources and capacity to respond effectively,” he said.

Bitrus said the initiative was designed to bridge the gap by equipping women with practical knowledge and skills to adapt to climate change and participate actively in community decision-making.

“We want women to move beyond being victims of climate change to becoming active participants in finding solutions. They must have the knowledge, confidence and platforms to engage those responsible for decisions affecting their communities,” he added.

He said the project, which would run from July 2026 to June 2028, would also bring community leaders together to develop action protocols for responding to environmental challenges and preventing conflicts.

According to him, participants would be encouraged to identify problems affecting their communities and collectively demand appropriate interventions from relevant government authorities.

The GRA Mobilisation Officer, Bashir Ibrahim, said the project was also aimed at addressing the exclusion of women and young people from community governance and peacebuilding processes.

“Women and young people are important stakeholders in community development, but they are often left out when decisions are being made. We want to change that by ensuring their voices are heard and their contributions recognised,” Ibrahim said.

He disclosed that 25 traditional rulers, religious and youth leaders had undergone training and signed a pledge to promote inclusive governance by involving women and youths in peace committees and decision-making processes.

Ibrahim said the women would also serve as knowledge multipliers by taking the lessons acquired during the workshops back to their communities.

“Our expectation is that the knowledge will not end with the participants. They will return to their communities, educate other women and encourage collective action on climate resilience and conflict prevention,” he said.

A community leader, Habu Suleman, said the training had exposed participants to practical ways of addressing environmental challenges and managing disagreements before they escalated into conflicts.

“The training has opened our eyes to the connection between environmental challenges and community conflicts. We have learnt that people can prevent many disagreements through dialogue, cooperation and proper management of available resources,” he said.

A participant, Hannatu Gobim, said she was prepared to share the knowledge acquired with other women to strengthen community awareness.

“I have learnt that women should not remain silent when issues affecting their environment and livelihoods arise. We can contribute to finding solutions, and I will take this knowledge back to other women in my community,” she said.

Another participant, Zainab Danladi, said flooding and changing weather patterns had continued to affect farming, livestock and household livelihoods.

“Flooding and unpredictable weather affect our farms, animals and sources of livelihood. This training has helped us understand some practical ways of responding to these challenges. I will also share what I have learnt with other women,” she said.

The women-led multi-stakeholder workshops, tagged “Empowering Women for Climate Resilience and Conflict Prevention in Plateau State,” also exposed participants to practical climate adaptation strategies, including environmental hazard mapping, soil conservation, rainwater harvesting and seasonal resource-sharing schedules.

Other areas covered included alternative dispute resolution, gender governance, constitutional rights, local government budget tracking, engagement with ward development committees and legislative advocacy.

The post UNDEF empowers 200 Plateau women to tackle climate change, prevent conflicts appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Govt deploys technology to expand access to education
description:
The Federal Government has unveiled a National Education Technology Strategy aimed at addressing the challenges of out-of-school children and teacher shortages through digital learning platforms, improved learner identification and expanded access to educational resources.
The National Coordinator,
content:
The Federal Government has unveiled a National Education Technology Strategy aimed at addressing the challenges of out-of-school children and teacher shortages through digital learning platforms, improved learner identification and expanded access to educational resources.

The National Coordinator, Special Programmes Operation and Implementation Unit at the Federal Ministry of Education, Adebayo Onigbanjo, disclosed this on Monday while outlining the strategy, which seeks to integrate 26 government initiatives into a unified digital education system.

Onigbanjo said the initiatives were designed to operate as interconnected interventions rather than separate projects, with the aim of strengthening teaching, learning, education management, skills development and financing.

He explained that the National Education Verification and Identification initiative would “enable the government to map children and assign them unique Learner Identification Numbers, making it easier to identify those outside the education system and direct interventions towards them.”

According to him, the data would support targeted programmes for out-of-school children, girls and learners enrolled in home education programmes.

He said the Inspire Live initiative would connect pupils in schools without qualified subject teachers to certified teachers through digital platforms, while zero-rated data would eliminate internet subscription costs as a barrier to accessing online lessons.

“The main message today is that these are not 26 separate projects; they form one connected system. The digital infrastructure is what connects them,” he said.

Onigbanjo said the strategy would also link education with employment and entrepreneurship through programmes such as the Digital Training Academy, Technical and Vocational Education and Training and entrepreneurship initiatives.

He identified the NELFund loans, Student Venture Capital Grant and Tertiary Institution Staff Support as interventions designed to ease financial constraints facing students and educators.

The coordinator said public portals and dashboards would also strengthen transparency by allowing citizens to monitor government commitments and assess the implementation of education programmes.

He explained that the strategy would be driven by five pillars, including data and interoperability, digital infrastructure, technology and procurement, teacher transformation and other measures aimed at strengthening education delivery.

On data management, he said the government would build on the Nigeria Education Data Infrastructure by adopting common data standards to enable existing education databases to exchange information automatically while preserving institutional autonomy.

He said priority would be given to data on schools, teachers, enrolment and education financing, with personal records protected under the Nigerian Data Protection Act.

On infrastructure, he said the government would prioritise reliable electricity, broadband connectivity and digital devices for schools, particularly in rural and underserved communities, while making provisions for the maintenance of such facilities.

He added that the strategy would build on existing national connectivity initiatives, including Project BRIDGE and the Universal Service Provision Fund.

Onigbanjo said the government would also adopt vendor-neutral standards and transparent, performance-based procurement systems to encourage Nigerian developers to produce technology solutions aligned with the national curriculum.

He said the National Teachers’ Digital Competency Framework would establish standards for teachers’ digital skills, certification and career progression, supported by a national teacher professional development portal.

The strategy, he said, aligned with President Bola Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda and the Federal Ministry of Education’s vision of using education to drive national development, innovation and global competitiveness.

He acknowledged the contributions of the Federal Ministry of Communications, Innovation and Digital Economy, state governments, development partners, the private sector, academia and civil society to the strategy’s development, particularly the Mastercard Foundation and the World Bank Group.

The strategy comes amid persistent challenges in Nigeria’s education sector, particularly the large population of children excluded from formal education and shortages of qualified teachers in public schools.

A 2024 UNICEF report estimated that 18.3 million Nigerian children were out of school, comprising 10.2 million primary school-age children and 8.1 million junior secondary school-age children. The Federal Ministry of Education, however, has cited an estimated 15 million out-of-school children in its recent interventions.

Teacher shortages also remain a major concern. Data reported from the Federal Ministry of Education’s digital education database showed that 31.8 million learners in public schools were served by 592,077 teachers, representing a learner-teacher ratio of approximately 54 to one.

The Universal Basic Education Commission has estimated that an additional 194,876 qualified teachers are needed in basic education.

The strategy also builds on the Federal Government’s rollout of the Digital National Education Management Information System (DNEMIS), launched in July 2026 to improve education data collection, planning and accountability.

As of its initial nationwide rollout, the platform had captured data from 124,548 schools, covering more than 40 million learners and 1.19 million teachers.

The government said the new EdTech strategy would provide a coordinated framework for using technology to address these challenges and ensure that investments in digital education translate into improved learning outcomes.

The post Govt deploys technology to expand access to education appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Banks increase lending as loan demand rises – CBN survey
description:
Nigerian banks raised credit supply to households and businesses in the third quarter of 2026, as demand for secured, unsecured and corporate loans strengthened, according to the Central Bank of Nigeria.
The improvement was accompanied by higher loan approval rates and lower default rates across maj
content:
Nigerian banks raised credit supply to households and businesses in the third quarter of 2026, as demand for secured, unsecured and corporate loans strengthened, according to the Central Bank of Nigeria.

The improvement was accompanied by higher loan approval rates and lower default rates across major lending categories, although borrowing costs remained elevated in some segments.

The findings are contained in the CBN’s Q3 2026 Credit Conditions Survey, which examined changes in banks’ lending behaviour, loan demand, approval rates and repayment performance.

For secured lending, the demand index stood at 25.6, driven largely by consumer loans to households, which recorded 42.9, and credit for house purchases at 28.0. Mortgage and remortgage lending recorded 12.0, while lending to small businesses by households declined to -19.7.

In the unsecured lending segment, the demand index stood at 7.2. Overdrafts and personal loans to households recorded an index of 24.7, while credit card lending contracted to -20.0.

Corporate lending recorded a demand index of 18.9, reflecting increased demand from small businesses, medium-sized private non-financial corporations and large companies, which recorded indices of 22.6, 18.3 and 20.7, respectively.

However, demand from other financial corporations weakened, with the index falling to -16.2.

Banks attributed increased demand for corporate loans mainly to inventory financing, balance sheet restructuring and capital investments, which recorded indices of 18.6, 2.5 and 0.7, respectively.

The survey also identified changing economic outlook, liquidity positions and market share objectives as factors influencing banks’ decisions to expand secured lending. For unsecured credit, market share objectives, economic outlook and the cost and availability of funds were among the major drivers.

The proportion of loan applications approved increased across secured, unsecured and corporate lending categories compared with the previous quarter.

However, the spread between lending rates and the Monetary Policy Rate widened in several categories, suggesting that improved credit availability has not necessarily translated into lower borrowing costs.

The spread for secured lending widened to -14.5 index points.

For corporate loans, the spreads widened to -13.6 index points for medium-sized private non-financial corporations, -12.2 for other financial corporations, -11.0 for small businesses and -10.3 for large private non-financial corporations.

The spread for unsecured lending remained unchanged during the quarter.

Banks also reported declining default rates across secured, unsecured and corporate lending, including loans to small businesses and medium-sized and large companies.

The improvement in banks’ lending conditions comes against the backdrop of declining outstanding credit to Nigeria’s private sector.

Credit to the private sector fell by N537.6bn to N83.93tn in September 2026 from N84.47tn in August, despite annual growth.

The decline followed the CBN’s September decision to cut the MPR by 350 basis points to 23 per cent, its largest reduction since 2006.

The Monetary Policy Committee also adjusted the interest rate corridor to +50 and -300 basis points around the benchmark rate, while retaining the Cash Reserve Requirement for commercial banks at 45 per cent.

Cost of funds remains a major challenge facing businesses. Nigerian manufacturers faced a 53 per cent increase in the average cost of bank credit between 2020 and 2025, underscoring the growing financial pressure on businesses seeking funds for production and expansion.

Data from the Manufacturers Association of Nigeria showed that manufacturers paid an average interest rate of 32.2 per cent on borrowed funds in 2025, compared with 21 per cent in 2020.

The difference represents an 11.2 percentage-point increase in five years, despite a moderation in borrowing costs last year.

Manufacturers’ average lending rate stood at 32.5 per cent in the first half of 2025 before declining to 31.8 per cent in the second half, bringing the full-year average to 32.2 per cent.

MAN said that commercial bank credit allocation to manufacturing contracted by N1.92tn, from N8.53tn in December 2024 to N6.61tn in December 2025.

This represents a significant year-on-year contraction of -22.5 per cent, which is particularly disturbing, given that manufacturing recorded one of the largest credit contractions among the top sectors, surpassed only by the General Services sector at -25 per cent.

Director-General of MAN, Segun Ajayi-Kadir, said this steep decline leaves manufacturing lagging far behind the extractive oil & gas industry’s N10.59tn and a booming finance sector’s N9.24tn, demonstrating a systemic preference for speculative and rent-seeking activities over tangible productivity.

The post Banks increase lending as loan demand rises – CBN survey appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Gombe philanthropist pledges 11-LGA mobilisation for Tinubu, Yahaya
description: A Gombe State philanthropist and chieftain of the All Progressives Congress, Alhaji Ahmad-Bulama Hassan, popularly known as Dujuman Pindiga, has pledged to mobilise massive grassroots support for President Bola Tinubu, Governor Muhammadu Yahaya and other APC candidates ahead of the 2027 general elec
content:
A Gombe State philanthropist and chieftain of the All Progressives Congress, Alhaji Ahmad-Bulama Hassan, popularly known as Dujuman Pindiga, has pledged to mobilise massive grassroots support for President Bola Tinubu, Governor Muhammadu Yahaya and other APC candidates ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Hassan made the pledge on Monday after leading a delegation of political supporters on a solidarity visit to Yahaya at the Government House, Gombe.

He told Arewa PUNCH that his political structure had commenced mobilisation across the state’s 11 local government areas to secure victory for Tinubu and other APC candidates in the forthcoming elections.

The philanthropist, who reaffirmed his loyalty to the APC, said the visit was to pay homage to the governor, whom he described as his political leader, father figure and source of inspiration.

He commended Yahaya’s administration for what he described as significant achievements in infrastructure, healthcare, education, water supply, industrialisation and security.

“Your Excellency, you are a visionary leader. Your giant strides in just a few years have repositioned Gombe State as a pride of the North-East.

“We, the young generation, are proud of you and will continue to mobilise massive grassroots support to consolidate the good works of your administration,” Hassan said.

He also declared support for Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda, expressing confidence in the President’s economic reform programme.

Hassan disclosed that his political structure, operating under the guidance and inspiration of Seyi Tinubu, was working across the state to mobilise support for the President, Yahaya and other APC candidates.

Responding, the governor commended Hassan for his philanthropic interventions, particularly in youth empowerment, support for vulnerable persons and community development.

Yahaya described him as a committed party loyalist and grassroots mobiliser whose contributions to the APC and Gombe State had been recognised.

“Alhaji Ahmad-Bulama Hassan is a young man with a large heart. His philanthropic gestures and consistent support for our great party, the APC, have not gone unnoticed.

“He is a true party man who believes in unity, loyalty and service,” the governor said.

The governor, who is also Chairman of the Northern States Governors’ Forum, urged Hassan and other APC supporters to sustain their commitment to peace, unity and political tolerance as the 2027 elections approach.

He also called on party members to remain united and support Tinubu’s administration, expressing confidence that Gombe would remain an APC stronghold.

The post Gombe philanthropist pledges 11-LGA mobilisation for Tinubu, Yahaya appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Nigeria’s FX turnover rebounds 89% to $3.42bn
description:
Trading activity in Nigeria’s foreign exchange market rebounded sharply in the week ended 13 November, 2026, as dollar transactions rose by 89.17 per cent to $3.42bn from $1.81bn recorded in the previous week.
The increase represents an additional $1.61bn in transactions, reversing much of the 51.29
content:
Trading activity in Nigeria’s foreign exchange market rebounded sharply in the week ended 13 November, 2026, as dollar transactions rose by 89.17 per cent to $3.42bn from $1.81bn recorded in the previous week.

The increase represents an additional $1.61bn in transactions, reversing much of the 51.29 per cent decline recorded in the preceding week, according to the latest data from FMDQ.

The report, which tracks transactions between authorised dealers and their clients, showed that average daily FX turnover increased to $684.18m from $361.67m.

Despite the recovery, weekly turnover remained below the $3.71bn recorded in the week ended 30 October, indicating continued fluctuations in activity at the official FX market.

Spot transactions accounted for most of the increase, rising by 81.73 per cent to $3.25bn during the review week from $1.79bn in the preceding week.

The segment contributed about $1.46bn, representing approximately 90.5 per cent of the total increase in weekly turnover.

Spot transactions accounted for 94.89 per cent of total FX trading, compared with 98.77 per cent in the previous week, while average daily turnover rose to $649.19m from $357.23m.

However, spot trading remained about 11 per cent below the $3.64bn recorded in the week ended 30 October.

FX forward transactions recorded a much faster percentage increase, although from a significantly smaller base.

Turnover in the derivatives segment jumped by 687.97 per cent to $174.93m from $22.20m, representing an increase of $152.73m.

Forward transactions accounted for 5.11 per cent of total turnover, up from 1.23 per cent in the preceding week.

Average daily derivatives turnover also climbed to $34.99m from $4.44m.

The latest figure was more than twice the $73.83m recorded in the week ended 30 October.

The reported figure represents forward contracts executed during the week, rather than the value of outstanding forward positions.

The recovery in FX turnover coincided with pressure on the naira at both the official and parallel markets.

At the official window, the naira weakened to N1,364 per dollar on 11 November from N1,349 recorded at the close of the previous week, before recovering slightly to N1,358.50 on 12 November, according to Central Bank of Nigeria data.

This represented a depreciation of about 0.7 per cent from the previous Friday’s closing rate.

In the parallel market, the local currency weakened to N1,445 per dollar on 12 November from N1,430 the previous day, widening the gap with the official rate to N86.50.

Meanwhile, interbank transactions at the Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market stood at about $644.85m on 12 November, while total NFEM turnover was approximately $397.54m on 11 November.

The latest figures highlight the volatility in Nigeria’s FX trading activity, with weekly turnover moving from $3.71bn to $1.81bn before recovering to $3.42bn over three weeks.

The post Nigeria’s FX turnover rebounds 89% to $3.42bn appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Adamawa APC denies crisis in the party over Ribadu’s absence at campaign inauguration
description:
The Adamawa state chapter of the Ruling All Progressive Congress (APC) has denied the allegations that the party has enveloped into crisis over the candidature of Alhaji Tijani Galadima.
Speaking to Arewa Punch exclusively on Monday the state publicity secretary of the party Mr. Victor Dogo, said th
content:
The Adamawa state chapter of the Ruling All Progressive Congress (APC) has denied the allegations that the party has enveloped into crisis over the candidature of Alhaji Tijani Galadima.

Speaking to Arewa Punch exclusively on Monday the state publicity secretary of the party Mr. Victor Dogo, said that the allegations were baseless and  a deliberate disinformation to create confusion in the party.

“You don’t expect  Nuhu Ribadu National Security Adviser NSA to the president to come to Yola when the president was going on campaign the following day”, he said.

“ The security of the president is more important to Nigerians than NSA attending campaign flag-off in his state, when the governor and other chieftains are there doing the good jobs for APC to win the general elections without losing one position, “he stated.

Ribadu was conspicuously missing onThursday, during the party’s campaign flag-off in Yola.

However, the master of ceremony claimed that Ribadu was represented, but his representative was not giving chance to present Ribadu’s message to the APC supporters in Adamawa state.

Punch investigations revealed that Ribadu was not happy with the composition of the campaign team, which according to sources close to the the NSA, Governor Ahmadu Fintiri’s close political associates dominated the campaign team.

Speaking at the flag-off of the APC campaign Fintiri, commended President Bola Tinubu’s economic reforms, pointing out that the second coming of the president will reshape the country for better economic reforms.

Fintiri claimed that the president’s reforms had created opportunities for state governments to access more resources and execute developmental projects and tackle security challenges, particularly in the North-east region of the country.

The governor who confirmed that the reforms has  brought economic hardship to Nigerians, noted that the reforms were necessary policy decisions whose benefits would become evident over time.

According to the governor Adamawa State had benefited from the opportunities created by President Tinubu’s reforms, pointing out that the president deserved re-election for more people-oriented projects in the country.

“President Bola Tinubu has taken the bullet. He has introduced a policy that is making this country to work. He has introduced reforms. Yes, we agree they are hardship, but then they will not last forever because they are very good policies that are working.”

“If you have agreed that we have really worked in Adamawa, Bola Ahmed Tinubu should have a share in the work that the state government has done in Adamawa State because he has taken the bullet for all of us”.

The governor disclosed that Tinubu-led Federal Government, security agencies and state governments were working together to restore peace and create an enabling environment for development to thrive.

The governor assured Adamawa state people that his administration would continue to prioritise their welfare, reduce insecurity and deploy available resources to cushion the effects of economic hardship.

In his welcome address, the APC state chairman Alhaji Hamza Madagali, threatened to sack any party executive that failed to deliver his ward to his party.

“If you fails to deliver your place to APC, just consider yourself out of the party”, he warned.

The former governor Jibrrila Bindow, urged the people of Adamawa state to vote massively for Tinubu for economic prosperity according to him.

“ Late president Muhammadu Buhari and other leaders did 8 years so, Tinubu too should not be denied the same opportunity to serve 8 years two terms, “he said.

The post Adamawa APC denies crisis in the party over Ribadu’s absence at campaign inauguration appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Photographer deploys 5D technology to showcase Nigeria’s tourism
description: Nigerian documentary photographer, Dayo Adedayo, is deploying immersive 5D technology at the DAP Experience Centre in Lagos to showcase the country’s tourism assets and cultural heritage, as he seeks to use digital innovation to change how Nigerians and international visitors experience the country.
content:
Nigerian documentary photographer, Dayo Adedayo, is deploying immersive 5D technology at the DAP Experience Centre in Lagos to showcase the country’s tourism assets and cultural heritage, as he seeks to use digital innovation to change how Nigerians and international visitors experience the country.

The technology will enable visitors to take a virtual journey through different parts of Nigeria, including the Atlantic Ocean, the Niger Delta creeks, Onitsha and Lokoja, before returning to Lagos. The experience is designed to simulate environmental conditions such as rainfall, turbulence, sunrise and sunset without requiring visitors to wear virtual reality goggles.

Adedayo disclosed this during a media breakfast at the DAP Experience Centre in Lekki, Lagos, recently, where he explained that the facility would combine digital experiences with traditional photography to tell stories about Nigeria’s history, landscapes and cultural identity.

“Virtually, 5D. Not wearing goggles. That’s an old technology of 3D. This will be looking at everything live,” he said, describing the centre’s virtual experience.

The facility will also feature a large exhibition room where visitors can view different parts of Nigeria, as well as a documentary room for films relating to the exhibitions. Adedayo said the digital content would be regularly updated, allowing visitors to encounter different experiences on subsequent visits.

Beyond the digital installations, the centre will preserve the history of photography through an analogue section featuring a darkroom where visitors can observe how photographs are developed and printed.

Visitors will be photographed with both analogue and digital cameras. While digital images will be available immediately, the analogue photographs will be processed in their presence, giving them an opportunity to understand the traditional photographic process.

Adedayo said the facility was also intended to support education, with plans to attract school visits from across the country and expose younger generations to the evolution of photography.

The project reflects his broader ambition to use photography as a tool for documenting Nigeria’s heritage and promoting its tourism potential. He argued that the country’s visual stories could improve its international image and draw more visitors.

“If we tell our story, a very interesting visual story with our pictures, with our images, it will increase not just our GDP but also our image globally,” he said.

He also linked tourism to employment and spending across several sectors, including transportation, hospitality, food services and logistics, arguing that visitors generate economic activity beyond the destinations they visit.

“Tourism is the largest employer of labour,” Adedayo said, pointing to the range of businesses that benefit from the movement of visitors from airports to tourist destinations.

The centre is also expected to provide a commercial platform for photographers to exhibit and sell their work. Adedayo said he hoped to begin selling photographs before the end of 2026, with the centre earning a percentage from transactions.

He said the platform would give photographers an opportunity to generate income from their work and support further documentation of the country.

Adedayo has built an archive of more than four million photographs documenting Nigeria, which he said informed his decision to establish the centre as a place where his collection and other photographic works could be preserved and displayed.

The DAP Experience Centre combines the digital exhibition spaces with traditional photographic displays, positioning the project as both a tourism attraction and a platform for preserving the country’s visual history.

The post Photographer deploys 5D technology to showcase Nigeria’s tourism appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: NYSC seeks Army’s support to protect corps members in North-East
description:
The National Youth Service Corps has called for stronger collaboration with the Nigerian Army to enhance the security of corps members serving in the North-East, particularly in areas affected by insecurity.
The Area Director, NYSC North-East Area Office 2, Mr Odoba Oche, made the call on Friday dur
content:
The National Youth Service Corps has called for stronger collaboration with the Nigerian Army to enhance the security of corps members serving in the North-East, particularly in areas affected by insecurity.

The Area Director, NYSC North-East Area Office 2, Mr Odoba Oche, made the call on Friday during a courtesy visit to the General Officer Commanding, 10 Division, Nigerian Army, Major General CR Nnebeife, at the division’s headquarters in Jalingo, Taraba State.

Oche, who oversees NYSC activities in Adamawa, Gombe and Taraba states, acknowledged the Army’s contributions to securing orientation camps and protecting corps members, particularly during their movement to places of primary assignment.

He said closer cooperation between the two institutions was necessary to sustain the safety of corps members and strengthen their contributions to national development.

The NYSC director recalled that the scheme was established in 1973 to promote national unity, integration and peaceful coexistence, describing it as one of the enduring legacies of military leadership in Nigeria.

He said the scheme had continued to promote discipline, patriotism and national consciousness among young Nigerians, adding that the military remained an important partner in achieving its objectives.

Responding, Nnebeife described the NYSC as a strategic partner of the Nigerian Army, noting that both institutions shared a common commitment to national unity, patriotism and peaceful coexistence.

The GOC disclosed that the 10 Division was established in July 2026 as part of the Nigerian Army’s expansion from eight to 12 divisions to strengthen its operational capacity and improve security across the country.

He assured the NYSC delegation of the division’s commitment to protecting lives and property, particularly corps members participating in orientation exercises and travelling to their places of primary assignment.

Nnebeife added that the division’s permanent headquarters was located close to the NYSC orientation camp, a development he said would further facilitate security cooperation between the two institutions.

He congratulated Oche on his appointment and reaffirmed the Army’s readiness to deepen its partnership with the NYSC in advancing national unity, peace and security.

title: Foundation empowers Taraba women, unveils development centre
description: The Africa Nature Investors Foundation has commissioned a Women Development Centre and three schools in Gashaka Local Government Area of Taraba State as part of efforts to promote women’s economic empowerment, improve access to education and strengthen community participation in environmental conser
content:
The Africa Nature Investors Foundation has commissioned a Women Development Centre and three schools in Gashaka Local Government Area of Taraba State as part of efforts to promote women’s economic empowerment, improve access to education and strengthen community participation in environmental conservation.

The projects, supported by the European Union and implemented in partnership with the National Park Service, are expected to benefit residents of communities surrounding the Gashaka-Gumti National Park, Nigeria’s largest national park.

Located in Tonga (Bodel), the Women Development Centre will serve women from Serti, Bodel, Goje and Mayo Selbe communities, providing opportunities for vocational training, agricultural processing, skills acquisition and entrepreneurship.

Speaking at the commissioning ceremony on Friday, the Executive Director of ANI Foundation, Tunde Morakinyo, said the organisation had continued to attract development support, including funding from the European Union, to improve the livelihoods of communities around the national park.

He said the centre was established to provide women with a common platform to acquire skills, engage in productive activities and improve their economic circumstances.

Morakinyo disclosed that the foundation had also supported farmers through beekeeping initiatives and facilitated the vaccination of thousands of cattle to improve livestock health and strengthen rural livelihoods.

He added that the foundation planned to construct three blocks of classrooms in each of the communities across Gashaka Local Government Area to improve educational infrastructure and access to learning.

Also speaking, the Conservator of Gashaka-Gumti National Park, George Karngong, described the centre as another milestone in the partnership between the National Park Service and ANI Foundation.

He said the facility would serve as a hub for women’s savings groups established by the foundation, enabling beneficiaries to mobilise savings, exchange ideas, access training and establish small-scale businesses.

According to him, the initiative would strengthen women’s economic independence, improve household incomes and encourage greater community participation in conservation activities.

Karngong listed other interventions by the foundation to include alternative livelihood programmes, scholarships, classroom and teachers’ quarters construction, provision of portable water, cattle vaccination, volunteer ranger initiatives and environmental restoration projects.

He stressed that sustainable conservation required the cooperation of communities living around the park rather than reliance on enforcement alone.

“Conservation cannot succeed through enforcement alone; it requires the active participation and support of surrounding communities,” he said.

He explained that providing alternative livelihood opportunities, particularly for women, would reduce excessive dependence on the park’s natural resources and encourage residents to take greater responsibility for protecting the environment.

The conservator appealed to the Taraba State Government to provide the park with operational facilities, including patrol vehicles, motorcycles and communication equipment, to strengthen its capacity to protect the country’s important ecological asset.

He described the Gashaka-Gumti National Park as a strategic national resource with significant contributions to climate change mitigation, watershed protection, tourism, research, education and employment generation.

The Leader of the European Union Delegation, Iusan Liviu, expressed satisfaction with the intervention, describing it as a positive step towards community development and institutional strengthening.

Liviu called for sustained cooperation among the government, development partners, conservation authorities and host communities to ensure that the initiative delivered lasting benefits.

He assured that the European Union would continue to support ANI Foundation’s interventions aimed at improving community welfare and strengthening the management of the park.

Similarly, the Taraba State Commissioner for Heritage and Ecotourism, Titus Nagombe, commended the foundation for its contributions to communities around the park and urged women to take full advantage of the opportunities provided by the centre.

The Commissioner for Women and Child Development, Mary Sinjen, who was the special guest of honour, urged beneficiaries to cultivate a strong maintenance culture to ensure that the facility remained useful to present and future generations.

She also expressed her ministry’s readiness to collaborate with ANI Foundation in advancing women’s development and economic empowerment.

The Chairman of Gashaka Local Government Council, Umar Alluran Gari, described the foundation as a dependable development partner and urged residents to continue supporting its programmes and the National Park Service.

He, however, called on the foundation to intensify efforts to address the increasing influx of people into the park.

The Lamdo of Gashaka, Alhaji Zubairu Hammangabdo, who spoke on behalf of traditional rulers from Bodel and Mayo Selbe, acknowledged the foundation’s interventions and appealed to residents to sustain their support for the conservation partnership.
