title: 89% of Niger children miss full vaccination – Agency
description:
The Niger State Primary Healthcare Development Agency has disclosed that only 11 per cent of children in the state are fully immunised, leaving about 89 per cent without complete vaccination.
The Executive Director of the agency, Dr Junaidu Inuwa, raised the concern during an interview with AREWA PU
content:
The Niger State Primary Healthcare Development Agency has disclosed that only 11 per cent of children in the state are fully immunised, leaving about 89 per cent without complete vaccination.

The Executive Director of the agency, Dr Junaidu Inuwa, raised the concern during an interview with AREWA PUNCH on Monday, saying the situation had compelled the agency to adopt new strategies to improve immunisation coverage across the state.

Inuwa said the agency had entered into partnerships to provide incentives to parents and caregivers who brought their children for immunisation, particularly to encourage uptake among families facing transportation and other challenges.

He also disclosed that additional measures had been introduced to reach children in hard-to-reach communities and areas affected by insecurity.

According to him, the agency remains concerned about inadequate awareness of the importance of routine immunisation, despite efforts by the state government and development partners to improve access to healthcare.

“The Primary Healthcare Development Agency, one of our key strategies is immunisation. The last time I checked my data, when you look at the figures, you find out that 11 per cent of children in Niger State are fully immunised.

“That tells you that out of 100 children, only 11 are fully immunised in Niger State, meaning I am still battling with about 89. To us, that calls for a lot of concern,” he said.

Inuwa explained that the agency had introduced several interventions to address the challenge, including partnerships aimed at encouraging parents to utilise routine immunisation services.

He said although he was initially not convinced about the idea of offering incentives to parents, the agency eventually recognised it as an opportunity to engage caregivers and educate them on the importance of vaccination.

“There are lots of strategies we have put in place. One of the things we have done is that we found out there is still a lack of awareness about immunisation, so we partnered with a particular group. We call them New Incentives.

“They were piloting some of these services, even though, for me, I did not come from that school of thought that incentives should be given to people to bring their children.

“But what we looked at was the opportunity to interact with the caregivers. So, every time a parent knows that he will get something to support his transportation, he now brings his child to the facilities,” he said.

The agency’s executive director added that the intervention provided an opportunity for health workers to educate parents about their responsibility to ensure that their children received routine vaccinations.

“When they do that, we use the opportunity to let them know that it is their right, privilege and duty that their children get immunised. We also try to tell them some of the things we have done and let them know that across all our facilities, routine immunisation is free,” Inuwa stated.

He commended the Niger State Government and development partners, including the World Health Organisation and the United Nations Children’s Fund, for supporting efforts to improve immunisation coverage and strengthen primary healthcare delivery.

Meanwhile, the Executive Director of Global Promoters for Community Initiatives, Mr Olasukanmi Kalejaiye, said the Media Chat was a quarterly engagement organised by the Niger State Primary Healthcare Development Agency.

He said the engagement, themed, “Strengthening Primary Health Care Delivery and Improving Access to Quality Healthcare 1.0,” provided a platform for the agency’s executive director to interact with journalists on its achievements, challenges and strategies for improving healthcare delivery.

Kalejaiye, who spoke to ArewaPunch on a sideline of the Media Chat,  explained that the initiative, powered by Global Promoters for Community Initiatives, was designed to strengthen media engagement, address public concerns and promote awareness of primary healthcare services across the state.

title: Katsina villagers share pond with cattle, pay N450 for water

content:
The young man bends over the edge of a muddy pond, carefully lowering his container into the water. He scoops it up, empties its contents into a jerrycan and prepares for another round. A few metres away, cattle gather around the same water source, dipping their mouths into it as they struggle to quench their thirst.

For the young man, it is another day at work. For the animals, it is a routine search for water. But for residents of Rimi-Muduru community in Mani Local Government Area of Katsina State, the scene represents a painful reality they have lived with for about five decades.

The water collected from the pond is not simply for watering livestock or irrigating farmland. It is also what families depend on to cook their meals, wash their clothes, bathe their children and, in some cases, satisfy their thirst.

There is little distinction between the water humans and animals consume. Both depend on the same earth pond, which residents say has served as their main water source for about 50 years.

For those who cannot afford to fetch the water themselves, there is a price to pay. Young men who have turned the community’s water shortage into a means of livelihood now sell a 25-litre jerrycan for N450.

In a country where access to clean water remains a major development challenge in many rural settlements, the experience of Rimi-Muduru raises troubling questions about communities that have waited for generations for basic infrastructure.

During our correspondent’s visit to the community on Wednesday, the scale of the problem became evident. Several young men were seen scooping water from the pond, filling jerrycans and transporting them to customers.

Women and children also gathered around the same water point, collecting what they needed for domestic use. Livestock moved around the pond, sharing the source with residents without any visible arrangement to separate human and animal consumption.

For the people of Rimi-Muduru, this is not an emergency that began yesterday. It is a way of life inherited from their parents and, in some cases, grandparents.

A resident, who identified himself simply as Aliyu, said the pond was dug by earlier generations when the community struggled to find water.

“Our community has depended on this pond for several decades because there are no alternative water facilities. I am over 40 years old, and this pond was dug by our parents because of the scarcity of water. It is the only one we have been using till today,” he said.

Another resident, Bala, describes the pond as indispensable, explaining that residents had little choice but to continue using it for their daily needs.

For Bala and other residents, the concern is not that they do not understand the importance of safe water but that they have no dependable alternative.

A commodity bought at a heavy price

The water shortage has also created an informal business around the community’s most basic necessity.

Young men who fetch water from the pond have become vendors, supplying households willing to pay for the service. What may have started as an opportunity to earn a living has gradually become part of the daily survival system of the community.

Paying N450 for a 25-litre jerrycan could be overwhelming for many households in the community.

A family that buys four jerrycans of water daily spends N1,800 in a day. They would have to cough up N54,000 to use water for 30 days.

For families requiring more water, the financial burden is considerably higher. Households with several children and other dependants must buy more for cooking, cleaning, bathing and other domestic activities.

The situation presents a difficult choice for low-income families who have to spend a substantial part of their income buying water or spend hours fetching it themselves.

Even those who get free water are not spared the burden. They must contend with the time spent walking to the pond, waiting for their turns and carrying heavy containers back home.

For women and children, who often shoulder much of the responsibility for household water collection in rural communities, the daily routine can interfere with other activities, including education, childcare and income-generating work.

The irony is that residents buy water whose quality is highly questionable, as no quality checks are carried out before they consume it.

In effect, the community is paying for a resource that should be available through reliable public infrastructure, without any guarantee that what it buys is safe to drink.

A health threat beneath the surface

Beyond the financial implications, the health risks associated with sharing an open water source with livestock are a major concern.

An infectious disease specialist, Dr Muhammad Abubakar, warned that the practice could expose residents to several infectious diseases.

Abubakar, a consultant in infectious diseases and tropical medicine at the Department of Internal Medicine, Federal Teaching Hospital, Katsina, told ArewaPUNCH that stagnant water could harbour disease-causing organisms, including bacteria, viruses and parasites.

He described the situation in Rimi-Muduru as worrisome, noting that water, although essential to human and animal survival, could become a vehicle for disease transmission when contaminated.

“Water is an integral part of life. There is virtually no aspect of life that is without water. Even our human body is mainly composed of water, likewise animals and plants,” he said.

According to him, the presence of livestock at the same water source increases the possibility of contamination through animal waste and physical contact.

“Animals are not only putting their mouths into the water; they may defecate there, pass their faeces and urinate inside. Even their hooves carry a lot of diseases from the farm and the bush, and they put their legs and hooves into the water,” Abubakar added.

His warning highlights the dangers associated with an unprotected water source where animals and humans have unrestricted access.

The specialist identified zoonotic infections, which are diseases that can spread between animals and humans, as another concern.

Among the diseases he mentioned were brucellosis and bovine tuberculosis, alongside other bacterial, viral and parasitic infections.

He explained that disease-causing organisms introduced into the water by animals could then infect humans who drink it without adequate treatment.

For residents, the warning raises an uncomfortable question: how safe is the water that has sustained their households for generations?

While the community’s dependence on the pond has continued for decades, the absence of a documented health assessment means the actual burden of water-related infections remains unclear.

Familiarity is not immunity

Some may argue that the community residents have used the water for years without experiencing a major health crisis.

However, Abubakar cautioned against interpreting decades of exposure as proof of safety or immunity.

He said residents’ continued use of the pond did not mean they were protected from diseases that could arise from contaminated water.

Responding to concerns about reported cases of diarrhoea among children in the community, the specialist said a possible connection with unsafe water could not be dismissed. However, he stressed that establishing the actual disease burden would require proper epidemiological investigations.

“We may not objectively know their health status because we don’t have the epidemiological demography, meaning the number of people in the community over so many years, how many people are alive, how many have fallen sick and how many are currently alive,” he noted.

He explained that appropriate medical investigations, including stool, blood and sputum examinations where clinically indicated, alongside a comprehensive community health survey, could help establish infection prevalence.

Abubakar also acknowledged that repeated exposure to certain organisms could trigger immune responses, a concept sometimes discussed under the hygiene hypothesis.

However, he warned that such a possibility should not be mistaken for universal protection against infectious diseases.

“The only lucky part is what we call the hygiene hypothesis, whereby people in the same community, through subsequent or continuous exposure to an antigen, may develop immunity. But this is more of a hypothesis, more of an assumption. There are some diseases; they do not respect immunity,” he said.

His explanation reminds us that survival under difficult environmental conditions does not necessarily mean those conditions are harmless.

For Rimi-Muduru, the priority should therefore be to establish the water’s quality, determine the health risks and provide residents with a safer alternative rather than rely on the assumption that generations of use have made the pond safe.

When human, animal and environmental health meet

Abubakar also advocated the adoption of the One Health approach, which recognises the interconnectedness of human, animal and environmental health.

He explained that the approach was particularly relevant in rural communities where people and livestock share the same environment and potentially contaminated water sources.

According to him, the response should not be left to health authorities alone. Relevant agricultural, environmental and water agencies must work together to address the problem.

“The One Health approach is very important. You need to understand the interface between humans and animals,” he said.

He called for public awareness campaigns, health education and practical interventions to ensure that residents understood the dangers of sharing unprotected water sources with livestock.

He also urged the community to engage primary healthcare authorities and other relevant institutions to seek intervention.

For Rimi-Muduru, such collaboration would need to go beyond sensitisation. Residents require an alternative water supply that is accessible, reliable and safe.

Five decades of waiting

The continued dependence on a single earth pond for approximately 50 years raises broader questions about rural infrastructure, public service delivery and the challenges confronting communities outside major urban centres.

Access to safe drinking water is essential to public health, sanitation, education and economic development. Yet residents of the Mani community still negotiate daily survival around a pond dug by an earlier generation.

The Katsina State Government, through the Ministry of Water Resources, the State Rural Water Supply and Sanitation Agency and relevant local government authorities, has an important role to play in addressing the situation.

The first step should be an immediate water-quality assessment to determine the extent of possible contamination and the required treatment.

This should be followed by providing emergency treated water, constructing functional boreholes and establishing separate drinking points for humans and livestock.

Any intervention must also be sustainable. A borehole that breaks down after a few months without maintenance would only provide temporary relief.

Community participation in planning and maintaining water facilities is also needed to ensure any new infrastructure serves residents over the long term.

When contacted by phone for comment, the Katsina State Commissioner for Water Resources, Manir Ayuba, did not pick up our correspondent’s calls as of the time of filing this report.

The question of dignity

For the young men who fetch and sell water, the pond represents an opportunity to earn an income. For the women who collect water for their families, it is part of an exhausting daily routine. For the children growing up in the community, it is the only water source they have known.

But behind these different experiences is one common reality: a community that has spent nearly half a century without a dependable alternative to an open pond shared with livestock.

The N450 charged for a jerrycan is more than a commercial transaction. It reflects how the absence of basic infrastructure can turn an essential human need into a recurring financial burden.

For Aliyu, who has spent more than 40 years watching his community depend on the same muddy pond, the situation is a painful reminder that the hardship inherited from one generation has become the burden of another.

His greatest concern is that children growing up in Rimi-Muduru may grow old under the same conditions, fetching water from a pond shared with cattle, while their parents continue to spend money on a resource that should be a basic public service.

After nearly five decades of waiting, residents say they want more than promises or temporary interventions. They want functional boreholes, reliable access to clean drinking water and an end to the daily struggle that has defined life in their community for generations.

For a community that has waited 50 years, access to safe water should no longer be treated as a favour from the government. It is a basic necessity and a right that should not depend on a family’s ability to pay N450 for a jerrycan.

The people of Rimi-Muduru have inherited their parents’ thirst. They should not be forced to pass it on to their children

The post Katsina villagers share pond with cattle, pay N450 for water appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

By Ben Ngwakwe, Gombe



GOMBE — The Gombe State Executive Council (SEC), presided over by Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, has approved seven roa
content:
…SEC endorses 2027–2029 expenditure framework, updates social protection policy

..Government targets December resumption of Kolmani oil exploration

By Ben Ngwakwe, Gombe

GOMBE — The Gombe State Executive Council (SEC), presided over by Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, has approved seven road projects valued at billions of naira, covering approximately 97 kilometres across four local government areas of the state.

The council also approved the procurement of 40 emergency response and public utility vehicles, comprising 20 firefighting trucks and 20 water tankers, at a combined cost of about N3.8 billion.

Other major decisions taken at the council meeting on Monday included the approval of the 2027–2029 Medium-Term Expenditure Framework (MTEF), an updated Social Protection Policy for 2027–2030 and measures to position the state to benefit from the anticipated resumption of oil exploration in the Kolmani area in December.

Briefing journalists after the meeting, the Commissioner for Information and Culture, Moses Kyari Bolda, said the decisions reflected the administration’s commitment to infrastructure development, improved public services and long-term economic growth.

On the road projects, the Commissioner for Works and Infrastructure, Shehu Yarima Abdullahi, said the council approved seven memoranda presented by his ministry for projects covering Yamaltu-Deba, Balanga, Shongom and Kaltungo Local Government Areas.

Among the approved projects is the 18.9-kilometre Talasse-Bangu-Boka Bundi-Walalunguda Road, including a spur to Dalawaja, awarded to Datum Construction Company Limited at N23.98 billion, with a completion period of 24 months.

Similarly, the 38-kilometre Lapan-Labariya-Lasanjan-Latatar-Lakunturum Road, with a spur to Burak, was awarded to EEC International Limited at N49.3 billion, also with a 24-month completion period.

The council also approved the first phase of the Bangunji-Dadiya-Yelwa-Gombe/Yola Road project, covering approximately 15 kilometres, to be executed by EEC International Limited at N26.3 billion.

Other projects include the initial four-kilometre section of the Degri-Sikam-Nyuwar Kindiyo Road, covering Degri to Sikam, awarded to Datum Construction Company Limited at approximately N4 billion.

The 10.5-kilometre Dogon Ruwa-Kaltin Road was also awarded to the company at about N10.1 billion, while the nine-kilometre Kurjale-Pata Road was awarded to EEC International Limited.

The seventh project, covering 1.5 kilometres of the Kunuwal Road Network, was awarded to Swas Grade Limited.

Abdullahi explained that the Degri-Sikam-Nyuwar Kindiyo Road would be implemented in phases, with the initial four-kilometre stretch from Degri to Sikam approved as the first phase.

He described the approvals as an expansion of the state’s infrastructure development programme, particularly the administration’s Network 1,100 Kilometres Road Initiative, designed to open up rural communities, improve access to markets and facilitate the movement of people, goods and services.

He added that the projects would strengthen inter-community connectivity, promote agricultural and commercial activities and improve access to essential public services.

Governor Yahaya, he said, was expected to perform the foundation-laying ceremony for the Talasse-Bangu-Boka Bundi-Walalunguda Road, including the Dalawaja spur, to formally signal the commencement of construction.

N3.8bn for emergency vehicles

In another development, the council approved the procurement of 20 firefighting trucks and 20 water tankers at a combined cost of approximately N3.8 billion.

The Commissioner for Finance, Muhammad Gambo Magaji, said the acquisition of the firefighting trucks would strengthen the operational capacity of the State Fire Service, particularly as the government expands fire service stations beyond the state capital.

He explained that the additional water tankers would provide temporary relief to residents while the ongoing revitalisation of the Gombe Regional Water Supply Scheme was being completed, including plans to transition its operations to solar-powered energy.

Magaji disclosed that all 40 vehicles would be converted from diesel-powered engines to Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) to reduce fuel expenditure, improve operational efficiency and promote cleaner energy.

Kolmani oil exploration

Meanwhile, the state government said it had intensified preparations to position Gombe for the anticipated resumption of oil exploration activities in the Kolmani area, with drilling expected to resume in the first week of December 2026.

The Commissioner for Energy and Mineral Resources, Sanusi Ahmad Pindiga, said the government was working with Rift Oil Nigeria Limited, a consultant engaged to facilitate the state’s institutional engagement, recognition and registration as an oil and gas-producing state.

He disclosed that the consultant had completed 12 of its 14 planned deliverables, representing significant progress in developing the institutional framework and human capital required for the state’s participation in the oil and gas industry.

One of the major achievements, according to him, was the training of 100 graduates in artisan skills, including plumbing, carpentry, information and communication technology and welding.

The beneficiaries were also provided with starter kits and financial support to enable them establish businesses, become self-reliant and position themselves for employment and entrepreneurial opportunities arising from the anticipated expansion of oil and gas activities.

Pindiga said the consultant’s engagements had also facilitated the preparation of relevant documentation and institutional support mechanisms considered necessary for the state’s participation in the emerging petroleum industry.

He described the expected resumption of drilling in Kolmani as a significant economic opportunity, stressing the need to prepare the state’s institutions, workforce and communities to benefit from the development.

SEC approves 2027–2029 fiscal framework

In another major decision, the council approved the Gombe State Medium-Term Expenditure Framework for 2027–2029, which will provide the fiscal and economic projections guiding revenue generation and expenditure priorities over the next three years.

The Commissioner for Budget, Micah Sunday Hamman, said the framework would serve as the foundation for preparing the 2027 budget while strengthening fiscal discipline, resource allocation and effective implementation of government programmes.

He explained that the MTEF would provide a realistic basis for projecting revenue and expenditure, ensuring that government policies, projects and programmes were aligned with available resources and clearly defined development priorities.

The council also approved an updated Gombe State Social Protection Policy for 2027–2030 to strengthen the state’s social welfare system and provide coordinated and sustainable support for vulnerable and disadvantaged citizens.

According to Hamman, the policy would consolidate existing government interventions and establish a comprehensive framework for protecting vulnerable groups, particularly children and other citizens requiring social assistance.

He identified the five pillars of the policy as social assistance, social insurance, labour market interventions, systems strengthening, and protection against discrimination, violence, exploitation and social exclusion.

The commissioner said the framework would emphasise transparency, inclusion and evidence-based implementation to ensure that social protection interventions reached their intended beneficiaries and improved their living conditions.

The latest decisions, he added, underscored the state government’s determination to combine infrastructure expansion with sound fiscal management, improved emergency services, social welfare and strategic economic planning as Gombe prepares for its next phase of development.

The post Gombe approves N97bn road projects, N3.8bn emergency vehicles appeared first on Vanguard News.

content:
…Urges Ondo governor to deepen dividends of democracy

By Dayo Johnson, Akure

Former Governor of Ondo State, Dr Olusegun Mimiko, has congratulated Governor Lucky Orimisan Aiyedatiwa on emerging as the 2026 Silverbird Governor of the Year.

Mimiko described the award as recognition of the achievements recorded so far by the Aiyedatiwa administration and its efforts towards developing the state.

The award was presented at the 20th edition of the Silverbird Man of the Year Awards held at Eko Hotels, Lagos.

In a congratulatory message, the former governor urged Aiyedatiwa to see the recognition as a call to do more for the people of Ondo State and deepen the dividends of democracy.

He said the honour by the Silverbird Group showed that the governor’s efforts were receiving recognition beyond the state.

“This honour from the Silverbird Group is an acknowledgement that your efforts are being noticed and should, therefore, spur you to do more for the benefit of the greater majority of our compatriots in our dear state,” Mimiko said.

He described Ondo State’s selection for the award among the 36 states as encouraging, noting that it reflected efforts being made across different sectors and communities.

“It is encouraging to see Ondo State singled out among the 36 states for this award. It speaks to some work being done across sectors and locations in the state,” he added.

Mimiko prayed for greater strength and wisdom for Aiyedatiwa as he continues to steer the affairs of the state.

By Chimaobi Nwaiwu

content:
By Chimaobi Nwaiwu

NNEWI — A political pressure group in Anambra State, Anambra Patriots, APS, has endorsed the alliance between the All Progressives Grand Alliance, APGA, and the All Progressives Congress, APC, adopting President Bola Tinubu as its preferred candidate for the 2027 presidential election.

The group also declared its support for the re-election of Anambra State Governor, Professor Chukwuma Soludo, and urged Ndigbo to support his political direction, including his backing for Tinubu.

The convener of APS and Anambra State Commissioner for Works, Architect Okey Ezeobi, disclosed the group’s position on Sunday during the Anambra Patriots Women Summit held in Awka, the state capital.

Ezeobi expressed dissatisfaction with those criticising Soludo for aligning politically with Tinubu rather than supporting former Anambra State governor and Labour Party presidential candidate in the 2023 election, Peter Obi.

He argued that politics should be driven by interests rather than sentiments, insisting that Soludo’s decision to support Tinubu was in the interest of Ndigbo.

“My problem with Ndigbo is that they don’t know how to play politics. We do politics of emotion instead of interest. In politics, you get what you contributed, not what you deserve. Politics is about interest,” he said.

According to him, Soludo’s support for Tinubu was not motivated by personal gains but by what he described as the need for greater political inclusion of the South-East in national affairs.

He said: “Prof. Soludo’s support for Tinubu is not for personal gain, but for the interest of Ndigbo. It is time for Ndigbo to come back to Nigeria. And Soludo is a professor; he has analysed Nigerian politics.”

Ezeobi also argued that Soludo should not be criticised for his political choice, saying other ethnic groups had members supporting Obi without attracting similar criticism.

He urged Anambra residents to recognise Soludo’s position as governor and support his political decisions, adding that backing Obi was not compulsory for every Igbo politician.

“Why is everybody seeing Soludo as an enemy because he is supporting Tinubu? If we accept Soludo as our leader and governor in Anambra State, we must follow him anywhere he is pitching his political tent. It is not compulsory that we must support Peter Obi. Politics is not about sentiments,” he said.

The commissioner also made several claims about the political relationship between Obi and Soludo, alleging that Obi had opposed Soludo’s governorship ambition on previous occasions.

He cited the 2013, 2021 and 2025 governorship election cycles in Anambra, claiming that Obi had supported different political moves against Soludo, which ultimately failed.

Ezeobi, however, maintained that Soludo had not insulted Obi but had only responded to comments he considered critical of Anambra State and APGA.

He further criticised the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, describing it as the political platform of a Bayelsa politician, while questioning Obi’s influence within the party.

The commissioner said the APS had resolved to support Tinubu in the presidential election while backing APGA candidates in other electoral contests.

“Today, we are adopting President Tinubu as the candidate to support in the 2027 presidential election, and we have approved Governor Soludo-led APGA and Tinubu’s APC. We will vote APC in the presidential election and vote APGA in other elections,” he declared.

Also speaking, the Secretary to the Anambra State Government, Lady Chiamaka Nnake, a founding member of APS, urged residents to join Soludo in supporting Tinubu.

The acting APGA state woman leader and APS woman leader, Mrs Joy Orah, said she was mobilising women across the state’s 21 local government areas to support Tinubu and APGA in the elections.

Similarly, the Chairman of APS, Ozoh Ejiamatu Damian Enekwechi, urged the people of the state to follow Soludo’s political direction.

“We are only following our leader. That is what we are doing. We must follow our leader in the 2027 presidential election and other elections,” he said.

Meanwhile, Vanguard observed that strategic locations across Awka had been adorned with giant campaign billboards bearing the inscription: “Solu Tinubu — The Progressives Train is on Track: Join Now and in Our Own Interest.”

content:
… Backs YASA Foundation’s drive for inclusive society
By Ogochukwu Agha

lagos—The Ooni of Ife, Oba Adeyeye Ogunwusi, has urged Nigerians, corporate organisations and philanthropists to support initiatives that empower vulnerable people, saying true fulfilment lies in making positive impact on others.


The monarch spoke at the unveiling of the Yeye Afolashade Shona-Aluko (YASA) Foundation in Lagos, where he donated N5 million.


Describing the foundation’s humanitarian mission as worthy of support, Oba Ogunwusi said: “What gives the greatest happiness in this world is a life of impact and fulfilment. Everybody is chasing money. But when you attain a certain level of wealth, you discover that money does not necessarily bring happiness.


“The essence of life is what you can give to others.”


Senator Sylvia Mthethwa of Eswatini urged governments and institutions to promote inclusive development, asking: “Are we developing societies in which everybody has an opportunity to participate or contribute and prosper?”


She called for improved access to education, healthcare and employment for persons with disabilities.


The Ooni’s wife, Olori Temitope Enitan-Ogunwusi, commended the foundation’s founder, urging her to remain committed to humanitarian service despite challenges.


Earlier, Shona-Aluko said her youngest son’s disability inspired her intervention. She recalled employing eight specialised teachers to support him and other children at Ikeja High School for about nine years.


She said the experience exposed the difficulties faced by families unable to afford specialised education.


“YASA Foundation was born from a burden… a burden to give voice to the voiceless, strength to the weak, and to say boldly: ‘You are not forgotten,’” she said.


The foundation focuses on inclusive education, healthcare, rehabilitation, assistive devices, vocational training and livelihood support.


The event featured beneficiaries’ testimonies and recognition of Shona-Aluko by two international institutions.

The post True fulfilment lies in impacting lives, says Ooni appeared first on Vanguard News.

description:
By Sola Ogundipe







Nigeria needs a unified emergency response system that connects patients to ambulances, appropriately equipped hospitals, medical specialists and health insurance providers through a single call, an emergency care expert and healthcare entrepreneur has stated.







Giving t
content:
By Sola Ogundipe

Nigeria needs a unified emergency response system that connects patients to ambulances, appropriately equipped hospitals, medical specialists and health insurance providers through a single call, an emergency care expert and healthcare entrepreneur has stated.

Giving the warning in Lagos,during the inaugural ResQ Summit 2026, Dr. Aisha Onisarotu Atanda, who is the Chief Executive Officer of The Ambulance Company, ResQCore and TAC Care, said that the absence of such coordination continues to expose patients to avoidable delays and risks.

Atanda, who convened the Summit themed “Building a Coordinated Emergency System”, said an integrated emergency care network would eliminate the burden on patients and their relatives to independently arrange transportation, identify suitable hospitals, secure specialist intervention and negotiate access to treatment during life-threatening situations.

Speaking at the Rescue Summit 2026, themed “Building a Coordinated Emergency Care System”, Atanda said Nigeria already had organisations and resources providing different aspects of emergency care, but poor coordination prevented them from functioning as one effective system.

She said the current arrangement often left families struggling to determine which emergency number to call, secure an ambulance and identify a hospital capable of managing the patient’s condition, resulting in delays that could compromise survival.

“The problem we have at the moment is that many organisations operate in silos. Hospitals operate independently. Ambulance companies and health maintenance organisations are also doing their own thing, all with the right intention of improving emergency care.

“However, when these organisations operate in silos, patients and their relatives are left to navigate the system themselves. They have to figure out which number to call, contact an ambulance and then decide where the patient should be taken,” Atanda said.

She noted that the proposed model would ensure that once an emergency call was received, the patient’s location and condition would be established, an appropriate ambulance dispatched and a receiving hospital with the capacity to provide the required treatment identified.

Atanda said the initiative is particularly important in emergencies involving burns, complicated pregnancies and other conditions requiring specialised intervention, where taking a patient to the wrong facility could result in dangerous delays.

“The patient’s relatives may not have the expertise to know, for instance, that a burn victim needs to be taken to a specialist burns centre. As a result, valuable time is wasted accessing the wrong care when the patient could have been connected to the right facility through a coordinated system,” she added.

Atanda, who co-founded an ambulance service provider and subsequently developed technology for coordinating emergency services, said her organisation had also extended its activities to intensive care and surgical services through TAC Care at the Lagos State University Teaching Hospital, LASUTH.

She said the objective was to demonstrate how an integrated emergency response model could work and encourage governments to adopt and strengthen similar arrangements.

On complaints about unanswered emergency calls and delayed ambulance response, Atanda said a properly coordinated system must guarantee round-the-clock communication and effective dispatch of emergency services.

“We operate a 24-hour communication centre where someone is available to receive calls, establish the caller’s location and coordinate assistance. The goal is to ensure that patients receive the support they need throughout their emergency care journey,” she said.

She added that private sector initiatives could demonstrate workable models that government agencies could subsequently integrate into the national emergency response framework.

On the cost of emergency treatment, Atanda acknowledged that quality healthcare remained expensive but argued that health insurance offered one of the most sustainable ways of reducing the financial burden on patients and their families.

“We cannot continue to rely on out-of-pocket payments for every healthcare emergency. It is simply not sustainable,” she said.

Beyond insurance, Atanda called for stronger government-private sector partnerships, noting that the government had the authority to formulate policies and wider community reach, while private organisations could contribute operational expertise and service delivery capacity.

“There should be policies that make health insurance compulsory, while the government can also pool resources and allocate funds specifically for emergency care,

“The faster a patient accesses appropriate care, the better the chances of survival and recovery. If it takes days before someone receives treatment, the likelihood of a positive outcome becomes significantly lower,” she said.

The emergency care advocate also called for stronger public preparedness, saying Nigerians needed to understand how to recognise emergencies, seek assistance and provide basic first aid before professional responders arrived.

She said public education and first aid training were essential because emergency responders might not reach victims immediately after an incident.

“When you call for help, it may take at least five minutes for emergency responders to reach you. What do you do during those minutes before help arrives?” she asked.

She urged Nigerians to acquire basic skills to recognise conditions such as seizures and strokes, understand the appropriate response and provide accurate information when contacting emergency services.

Atanda said her ambulance company provided first aid training for individuals, corporate organisations and healthcare professionals, but stressed the need to expand such programmes and make emergency preparedness part of everyday life.

“We need to make emergency response information part of our everyday lives so that people understand how to seek help when emergencies occur,” she said.

She maintained that building a functional emergency care system would require sustained collaboration, public education, accessible health insurance and a reliable network capable of connecting patients to appropriate care without unnecessary delays

title: 67th NCH: Nasarawa seeks actionable resolutions to improve healthcare delivery
description:
By Chidinma Chukwu, Abuja



The Nasarawa State Government has called on health sector leaders across the country to translate commitments and policy decisions into measurable outcomes that will improve healthcare delivery, particularly at the grassroots.







The Governor of the State, Abdullahi
content:
By Chidinma Chukwu, Abuja

The Nasarawa State Government has called on health sector leaders across the country to translate commitments and policy decisions into measurable outcomes that will improve healthcare delivery, particularly at the grassroots.

The Governor of the State, Abdullahi Sule, made the call on Monday while declaring open the Technical Session of the 67th National Council on Health (NCH) in Lafia, the state capital.

This was contained in a statement signed by the Assistant Director of Information and Public Relations, Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, Ado Bako.

Represented by the Deputy Governor, Dr. Emmanuel Akabe, Sule said the Council provided an important platform for stakeholders to develop practical solutions to the challenges confronting Nigeria’s health sector.

He expressed confidence that deliberations under the theme, “From Commitments to Results: Delivering Quality and Equitable Healthcare for All Nigerians,” would produce actionable recommendations to strengthen the country’s healthcare system.

The Governor described Nasarawa’s selection as host of the national meeting as a privilege and an opportunity to showcase the state’s peaceful environment, hospitality and economic potential.

He also reaffirmed the state government’s commitment to supporting national health sector reforms and ensuring a successful meeting. He urged delegates to take advantage of the state’s hospitality during their stay.

Earlier, the Nasarawa state Commissioner for Health, Dr. Gwamna Gaza, described the meeting as a historic opportunity for the state to host health sector leaders from across the country for the first time.

He stressed that decisions reached at the Council would have far-reaching implications for the country’s health sector, urging participants to remain conscious of the fact that they were also beneficiaries of the policies and reforms being formulated for Nigerians.

He also called for active participation and constructive contributions, assuring delegates that the state government and relevant institutions were available to address any challenges they might encounter during the meeting.

Presenting the procedures for the Technical Session, the Permanent Secretary of the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare and Chairman of the Technical Committee, Daju Kachollom, said the two-day meeting, scheduled for November 16 and 17, would provide the technical foundation for the main Council meeting on November 19 and 20.

She explained that the main Council meeting would be chaired by the Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Prof. Muhammad Ali Pate.

According to her, the Technical Committee would review proceedings and the implementation status of resolutions reached at the 66th Regular National Council on Health, consider memoranda submitted by the Federal Government, state governments and other ministries, and develop recommendations for consideration by the Council.

Kachollom, said the memoranda submitted for consideration were organised around the four pillars of the Health Sector Strategic Blueprint.
The pillars, she listed, were effective governance; efficient, equitable and quality health systems; unlocking value chains; and health security.

She said the submissions would address critical areas, including the implementation of the National Health Act, multisectoral health interventions, clinical research and development, as well as strengthening Nigeria’s capacity to detect, prevent and respond to public health threats. These threats, she noted, included cholera, Lassa fever, cerebrospinal meningitis and measles.

To ensure focused deliberations, the Permanent Secretary said summaries of the memoranda had been prepared as working documents, while authors would be given five minutes each to present their submissions, highlight key issues and outline recommendations.

“The Secretariat will subsequently consolidate the Technical Committee’s recommendations for consideration by the Council,” she said.

She also disclosed that the Ministry had adopted an electronic documentation system for the Council, with relevant meeting documents preloaded onto tablets provided to participants.

The post 67th NCH: Nasarawa seeks actionable resolutions to improve healthcare delivery appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Diabetes: 3 in 4 Africans unaware as Afonchies screens Lagos residents
description:
By Chioma Obinna







Millions of people living with diabetes in Nigeria and Africa at large risk developing serious health complications because they are unaware of their condition, the International Diabetes Federation (IDF) has warned, underscoring the need for wider access to screening and ear
content:
By Chioma Obinna

Millions of people living with diabetes in Nigeria and Africa at large risk developing serious health complications because they are unaware of their condition, the International Diabetes Federation (IDF) has warned, underscoring the need for wider access to screening and early diagnosis.

The IDF disclosed that approximately 24.6 million adults aged 20–79 were living with diabetes in Africa in 2024, with nearly three out of every four unaware of their condition.

The figure highlights the growing public health challenge posed by undiagnosed diabetes and the need for community-based interventions to encourage regular health checks, particularly among people who may not have access to routine medical services.

Against this backdrop, Afonchies Pharmacy Limited last Saturday provided free blood glucose and blood pressure screening for residents of Addo, Badore, Langbasa and neighbouring communities in the Ajah area of Lagos State as part of activities marking the 2026 World Diabetes Day.

The exercise, held on Saturday, November 14, at the company’s Addo branch, targeted 200 adults and aligned with this year’s theme, “Early Action on Diabetes,” which emphasises early diagnosis and timely intervention to prevent complications.

Participants also received health counselling and professional medication advice as part of efforts to improve awareness of diabetes, hypertension and the importance of monitoring key health indicators.

Speaking, the Managing Director of Afonchies, Pharm. Adebayo Afon, said the initiative reflected the company’s commitment to making healthcare more accessible and encouraging people to take greater responsibility for their health through regular screening and early intervention.

He explained that the company’s community pharmacy model went beyond dispensing medicines to providing health education, identifying potential health risks and connecting people to appropriate care.

Afon also emphasised the importance of community-based interventions in addressing the burden of undiagnosed diabetes and hypertension.

Speaking on the activities at the screening centre, the Chief Pharmacist representing the Addo branch, Pharm. Michael Akpala, said the exercise was designed to address the fear and cost that often discourage people from checking their blood sugar and blood pressure.

He disclosed that beneficiaries with concerning results would receive counselling and be linked to nearby primary healthcare facilities, including those in Addo and Badore, for further evaluation and care.

He added that the company hoped to build on the initiative by encouraging regular health checks.

Also speaking, the Chief Operating Officer, Pharm. Oluwatosin Majoyeogbe, disclosed that Afonchies currently had 13 active branches, with another nearing completion.

He said the company intended to make the screening programme an annual event, rotating it across different communities where it operates.

Majoyeogbe also highlighted the company’s online ordering platform, which allows customers to submit prescriptions, select their preferred branch, arrange medicine delivery or collect their orders, subject to regulatory requirements.

Community pharmacies, he said, serve as the first point of healthcare contact for many residents, making them important in promoting medication safety and appropriate treatment.

One of the beneficiaries, 78-year-old elder statesman, Mr Samuel Akinrinifin, commended Afonchies for the initiative, describing it as a valuable opportunity, particularly for elderly residents, to monitor their health.

Akinrinifin, who said regular health checks had been part of his personal healthcare routine, expressed satisfaction with the exercise, adding that he had never been hospitalised because of his commitment to regular monitoring.

He urged Afonchies and other healthcare providers to sustain such initiatives and extend them to more elderly people.

World Diabetes Day is observed annually on November 14 to raise awareness about diabetes and promote prevention, early diagnosis and effective management.

The high proportion of people living with diabetes without knowing their status highlights the importance of accessible screening, public education and timely referral to health facilities to reduce the risk of complications.

The post Diabetes: 3 in 4 Africans unaware as Afonchies screens Lagos residents appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Nollywood stars, iconic comedians rally support for Hajiya Hadiza Foundation
description:
By Chioma Obinna



Leading Nigerian Nollywood actors and celebrated comedians have pledged their support for the Hajiya Hadiza Foundation (HHF), commending its President and Founder, Ambassador Hadiza Umar, for her humanitarian interventions among vulnerable Nigerians.



The entertainers made thei
content:
By Chioma Obinna

Leading Nigerian Nollywood actors and celebrated comedians have pledged their support for the Hajiya Hadiza Foundation (HHF), commending its President and Founder, Ambassador Hadiza Umar, for her humanitarian interventions among vulnerable Nigerians.

The entertainers made their commitment at a press conference held in Abuja over the weekend, where they applauded the Foundation’s efforts in supporting widows of fallen heroes, victims of terrorism, internally displaced persons (IDPs), indigent students and other less privileged members of society.

Over the years, the Foundation has implemented various humanitarian and empowerment programmes, including economic support for widows, educational scholarships for disadvantaged students and interventions in communities affected by insecurity and poverty.
Speaking at the event, veteran Nollywood actor, Chief Jide Kosoko, described Ambassador Umar’s humanitarian activities as a reflection of her personal experiences and understanding of the challenges faced by disadvantaged people.

Kosoko noted that Umar’s difficult childhood, during which she lost both parents and 12 siblings at the age of 13, had shaped her determination to support people experiencing poverty, deprivation and hardship.

He urged well-to-do Nigerians to emulate her philanthropic disposition and contribute to efforts aimed at improving the living conditions of vulnerable citizens.

“We must all rally round to support the humanitarian works of this young lady. There are many Nigerians who are far richer than her but have refused to help the less privileged. I urge wealthy individuals to emulate the kind gesture of the Hajiya Hadiza Foundation. We promise to support you through our various platforms,” he said.

Also speaking, popular comedian Julius Agwu commended the Foundation for its interventions among vulnerable women, widows, orphans, poor students and other disadvantaged groups.

Agwu disclosed that his foundation would explore collaboration with HHF, particularly in economic empowerment initiatives targeting women and young people in rural communities.

In his remarks, veteran Nollywood actor and octogenarian, Chief Chika Okpala, popularly known as Zebrudaya, appealed to the Foundation to extend its humanitarian interventions to struggling veterans in the entertainment industry.

He called attention to the plight of some veteran Nollywood actors, musicians and comedians facing financial difficulties, poverty and health challenges, urging the Foundation to consider providing them with assistance.

Okpala also praised Ambassador Umar’s commitment to economic empowerment programmes in underserved communities and internally displaced persons’ camps.

Responding, an emotional Ambassador Umar disclosed that the Foundation had implemented humanitarian and economic empowerment programmes worth approximately N850 million nationwide over the past three years, with particular attention to IDP camps and underserved communities.

She explained that the interventions included skills acquisition training, livelihood support, scholarship awards and the distribution of thousands of grinding machines, sewing machines, hairdressing and barbing kits, generators and cash assistance to beneficiaries.

According to her, the programmes are designed to promote self-reliance, restore dignity and provide sustainable livelihood opportunities for vulnerable individuals and families.

Ambassador Umar described the Foundation as a lasting legacy she hopes to bequeath to her child, expressing appreciation to the entertainment industry veterans for identifying with its humanitarian mission.

She said their support would further strengthen the Foundation’s capacity to sustain and expand its interventions across the country.

The event underscored the growing involvement of members of Nigeria’s creative industry in humanitarian advocacy and efforts to mobilise support for vulnerable populations.

The post Nollywood stars, iconic comedians rally support for Hajiya Hadiza Foundation appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Drug insecurity threatens national security, pharmacists warn FG
description:

… Demands government control of medicine supply chain



By Chioma Obinna



The Pharmaceutical Society of Nigeria (PSN) on Monday warned that pharmaceutical insecurity poses a serious threat to Nigeria’s national security, urging t
content:
… Seeks 1% of seized drug trafficking assets to fund enforcement

… Demands government control of medicine supply chain

By Chioma Obinna

The Pharmaceutical Society of Nigeria (PSN) on Monday warned that pharmaceutical insecurity poses a serious threat to Nigeria’s national security, urging the Federal Government to strengthen regulatory control of medicines and prevent the transfer of critical drug management responsibilities from public authorities to private interests.

The society also called for the establishment of a special fund to tackle illicit financial flows in the healthcare sector, proposing that one per cent of assets seized from drug trafficking be dedicated to strengthening the enforcement activities of the Pharmacy Council of Nigeria (PCN) and the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC).

The resolutions were contained in a communiqué issued at the end of the 99th Annual National Conference of the PSN, tagged IJELE 2026, held from November 2 to 7 at the International Convention Centre, Awka, Anambra State.

The conference, which brought together pharmacists and other stakeholders in the pharmaceutical and healthcare sectors, was held under the theme, “One Health, One Pharmacy: Bridging Knowledge, Practice and Policy for National Impact.”

In the communiqué signed by the President, Pharm. Ibrahim Tanko Ayuba, and National Secretary, Pharm. Gafar Madehin, the pharmacists maintained that medicines were not merely commercial commodities but matters of permanent regulatory control and national security.

Citing Part I, Item 21 of the Second Schedule of the 1999 Constitution, the conference argued that the government’s responsibility for drug regulation and control could not be compromised by private-sector participation in the pharmaceutical supply chain.

It cautioned against what it described as a private takeover of drug distribution responsibilities at the public-sector level, warning that such an arrangement could weaken inter-agency collaboration among the PCN, NAFDAC and the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA).

The communiqué stated: “Conference reminded Government that drugs are a matter of permanent regulatory control and National Security, which is why it is listed as Part I item 21, in the 2nd Schedule of the 1999 Constitution.”

It added that while government could engage private-sector expertise in financing and technology deployment, it should not surrender its regulatory standing or the cooperation currently extended by relevant agencies to Federal Central Medical Stores and Federal Health Institutions.

The PSN further called for the integration of community pharmacies into Nigeria’s national security architecture and the Nigeria Health Insurance Authority’s proposed Pharmacy First initiative.

According to the conference, more than 10,000 community pharmacies across the country could serve as frontline health and security stakeholders by identifying and reporting suspicious drug-related activities.

The pharmacists also urged the Federal Government to support the Drug Revolving Fund and Federal Drug Management Agency Bill, which has passed its first reading at the House of Representatives.

They proposed that the agency should serve as a single purchasing and supply platform for medicines, while government pharmacists should retain responsibility for procurement decisions, quality assurance, storage, dispensing and the handling of controlled medicines in the civil service.

On the existing Memorandum of Understanding between the Federal Ministry of Health and Medipool, the conference called for a review to limit private-sector participation to pooled price negotiations or competitively selected framework suppliers on a non-exclusive basis, in line with the Procurement Act.

To drive the proposed reforms, the PSN recommended a Federal Government-initiated Independent Presidential Committee on the Pharmaceutical Sector, to be chaired by a registered pharmacist recommended by the society, with representation from the PCN, NAFDAC, the National Institute for Pharmaceutical Research and Development and the PSN.

The conference called for greater involvement of pharmacists in humanitarian operations, particularly in emergencies and situations involving displacement.

It noted that humanitarian crises frequently disrupt access to essential medicines and healthcare services, leaving displaced persons, especially those living with chronic conditions, vulnerable to interruptions in treatment.

The conference urged the development of a stronger humanitarian pharmacy workforce equipped to support medicine supply systems, maintain access to essential medicines, assist in chronic disease management and provide pharmaceutical care in emergency settings.

It said pharmacists’ expertise in medicine selection, storage, supply, dispensing and appropriate use should be better integrated into national humanitarian preparedness and response plans.

On the broader health sector, the pharmacists warned that Nigeria could not achieve meaningful national development while citizens remained frequently ill, essential medicines were inaccessible and health institutions operated in isolation.

They identified five strategic bridges needed to transform the country’s health system: implementation, financing, medicine sovereignty, integration and accountability.

The conference stressed the need for connected knowledge, coordinated professional practice, coherent policies and accountable leadership, urging government to translate policy commitments into measurable outcomes and lasting health impact.

It also applauded the collaboration between the PSN and the West African Society of Parenteral and Enteral Nutrition (WASPEN), calling for a standardised framework to improve workforce planning and integrate advanced pharmacists into multidisciplinary clinical teams.

The conference welcomed the harmonisation of the PSN-WASPEN initiative with the Pharmacy Council of Nigeria’s mandatory continuing professional development training modules.

On workers’ welfare, the PSN commended the Nigeria Labour Congress, Trade Union Congress and the Joint Health Sector Unions/Assembly of Healthcare Professional Associations for sustaining the struggle for justice and equity in the health sector.

It appealed to the labour centres to conclude negotiations on the adjustment of the Consolidated Health Salary Structure (CONHESS), which it said had lingered for about 13 years, while ensuring that JOHESU/AHPA members were not shortchanged in ongoing collective bargaining negotiations.

The conference also called for speedy construction of the Pharmacy House at Victoria Island through a developer under a well-structured timeline, while directing the PSN leadership to address outstanding entitlements of debenture subscribers and regularise the documentation of its properties.

It further endorsed a one-time support contribution proposed by the PSN President to facilitate the society’s centenary celebrations scheduled for March 2027, challenging the planning committee to deliver what it described as the biggest professional event ever hosted in Nigeria.

At the end of the conference, Pharm. Ibrahim Tanko Ayuba emerged as PSN President for the 2026/2027 year.

Other members elected into the National Executive Committee include Pharm. Aisha Tukur Isiaku, Deputy President (North); Pharm. (Prof.) Henri A. Okeri, Deputy President (South); Pharm. Ndukwe Uma Ndukwe, National Secretary; and Pharm. Ehitare Patrick Omoarebu, Assistant National Secretary.

Also elected were Pharm. Jelili Kilani Adewale, Treasurer; Pharm. Sani Ali Yusuf, Financial Secretary; Pharm. Lizette Njideka Ezenekwe, Publicity Secretary; and Pharm. (Prof.) Sunday A. Adesegun, Editor-in-Chief.

The conference expressed appreciation to the Anambra State Government and residents for their hospitality and support throughout the five-day gathering.

The post Drug insecurity threatens national security, pharmacists warn FG appeared first on Vanguard News.

description:

Iheme made the call in a post on his Instagram page on Monday, whe
content:
Nollywood actor Osita Iheme, popularly known as Pawpaw, has urged Nigerian politicians to stop turning campaign rallies into entertainment shows, insisting that Nigerians need competent leaders who can deliver good governance.

Iheme made the call in a post on his Instagram page on Monday, where he criticised the practice of politicians dancing on stage during campaign rallies.

He urged political office seekers to use campaign platforms to showcase their achievements, demonstrate their capacity to lead and explain their plans to Nigerians, rather than engaging in choreography to entertain supporters.

The actor said Nigerians needed competence, good governance and purposeful leadership, not political hype and entertainment.

“We don’t need choreography. We need competence. We don’t need hype men. We need good governance. We don’t need entertainers. We need leaders,” he wrote.

He challenged politicians to tell Nigerians what they had achieved and what they intended to do if elected.

“Show us what you have done. Tell Nigerians what you will do. You are not going for Grammy,” he said.

Iheme also warned politicians against dancing on campaign stages, declaring: “I don’t want to see you guys’ dance on stage again. Be careful.”

content:
Nollywood actress Linda Osifo has announced her engagement to her partner, Mr Ose, expressing gratitude to God for what she described as an answered prayer.

The actress made the announcement in a video shared on her Instagram page on Monday. Osifo has been off social media for months.

In an accompanying post, she revealed that she had taken a break from social media before receiving what she described as a blessing she had once prayed for privately.

“Not in my timing, not in the way I imagined, but in a way only He could have written,” she wrote.

She said the experience was too beautiful to put into words, noting that some love stories were worth the patience and waiting.

Reflecting on her relationship with her partner, the actress wrote, “Today, I look at the man God has blessed me with and all I can say is… God, You did this for me.”

Osifo also expressed her commitment to her partner, saying, “To the man I get to call my forever, Mr Ose, I would choose you in every lifetime.”

Announcing her acceptance of the marriage proposal, she declared, “I SAID YES TO FOREVER!”

The actress further noted that when God authors a love story, every chapter is worth waiting for.

title: Opposition Sets A Signing Date, But The Parties Still Want Different Things
description: Nigeria’s opposition coalition has announced a concrete next step: a summit on 23 November at the NAF Conference Centre, Abuja, where participating parties are expected to sign cooperation documents. The announcement moves the process beyond an unspecified promise of further consultations. It
content:
Nigeria’s opposition coalition has announced a concrete next step: a summit on 23 November at the NAF Conference Centre, Abuja, where participating parties are expected to sign cooperation documents. The announcement moves the process beyond an unspecified promise of further consultations. It does not establish that the parties have settled their competing presidential ambitions.

The Coalition for Democracy, formerly G100, says participants will sign a National Covenant for Democratic Renewal and Framework for Opposition Unity, and adopt a National Reform Programme. Its proposed first common undertaking is protecting votes at polling units. These remain announced intentions: the documents have not yet been adopted at the forthcoming summit, and operational arrangements have not been demonstrated publicly.

The latest reports identify ADC, APM, NDC, PDP, PRP and SDP as participants. Earlier coverage listed nine parties, adding DLA, NRM and YPP, and specified factional PDP participation. The shorter list does not prove that the omitted parties have withdrawn. Establishing who is represented and who can authorise commitments remains part of the verification required before describing the coalition as a settled electoral alliance.

NDC: Cooperation Around The Obi-Kwankwaso Ticket Remains Its Preference.

In a telephone interview on 15 November, national publicity secretary Osa Director said other opposition figures could coalesce around Peter Obi and Rabiu Kwankwaso. He could not confirm a formal proposal or NDC participation in the reported bilateral Atiku-Makinde negotiations. This is support for cooperation on the NDC’s preferred terms, rather than acceptance of an open selection process. Electoral implication: The party’s participation in a common framework should not be interpreted as willingness to surrender its presidential ticket.

ADC: Talks Continue, Without A Confirmed Concession On Atiku

Party spokesman Bolaji Abdullahi and Atiku aide Phrank Shaibu have confirmed opposition engagement, but neither confirmed a specific agreement with Makinde. Reports of compromises between the two camps relied on unnamed sources and disclosed no terms. Assessment: The ADC remains engaged in negotiations while pursuing its own presidential campaign. Its leadership litigation also leaves an unresolved question about the authority through which any arrangement would be implemented.

APM: No Agreed Concessions, Alongside A Southern-Presidency Argument

Oyo APM publicity secretary Michael Ogunsina says the Atiku-Makinde alliance remains unfinished. Separately, Makinde’s campaign has reaffirmed that he is contesting to win and would serve one term, allowing the South to retain the presidency until 2031. These positions leave negotiations open but establish no withdrawal or endorsement. Assessment: Any arrangement around Atiku would require an explanation of how it reconciles with Makinde’s stated position on rotation.

PRP: Conditional Flexibility, With Party Identity Preserved

Donald Duke’s latest substantive offer, made on 10 November, was to respect a democratically agreed opposition choice, provided participants first established a common national vision. Chairman Hakeem Baba-Ahmed rejected collapsing the PRP’s structures into another party. There is no verified subsequent withdrawal or endorsement. Assessment: This leaves room for electoral support across party lines, but the selection process and reciprocal obligations remain unresolved.

SDP: Coalition Participation Alongside Its Own Campaign Preparations

The Adebayo-Bugaje campaign council has been developing a mobilisation framework covering states, local governments, wards and polling units. That is evidence of preparations for its own ticket, not deployment of a shared opposition organisation. No fresh commitment to withdraw Adewole Adebayo or endorse another candidate was verified.

PDP Participants: Authority Matters As Much As Inclusion

The Turaki-led faction’s spokesman, Ini Ememobong, has said candidates remain committed to the cooperation process. That is a factional account of continuing engagement, rather than proof that the entire PDP or every participating candidate has accepted a binding agreement. The summit needs to clarify which PDP representatives are signing and what structures they can commit.

What matters electorally: Joint vote protection offers a possible area of cooperation even if presidential candidates remain rivals. Its effectiveness will depend on shared training, resources, reporting procedures and local implementation. No fresh evidence of functioning joint state committees, pooled funding or shared polling-agent deployment was located. No completed zoning, power-sharing, merger or common-ticket agreement was verified.

Watch next: Attendance and authorised signatures on 23 November; publication of the documents; clarification of membership; and concrete instructions reaching state and constituency organisations. Candidates appearing together would demonstrate engagement. Signed obligations and implementation would establish how far that engagement has become an electoral alliance.

title: Germany thrash Netherlands to top Nations League group
description:
Florian Wirtz scored twice and Brajan Gruda contributed a goal and two assists as Germany cruised to a 5-0 win over the Netherlands in Berlin to reach the Nations League quarter-finals on Monday.



Derry Scherhant and Nico Schlotterbeck also got on the scoresheet as the Germans cut the visitors to
content:
Florian Wirtz scored twice and Brajan Gruda contributed a goal and two assists as Germany cruised to a 5-0 win over the Netherlands in Berlin to reach the Nations League quarter-finals on Monday.

Derry Scherhant and Nico Schlotterbeck also got on the scoresheet as the Germans cut the visitors to shreds in the most impressive match of Jurgen Klopp’s six-game stint as coach.

It was Germany’s biggest win over their neighbours since a 7-0 victory in 1959.

“We hope that we can make it fun for the fans. It was definitely fun for us, especially in the second-half,” Wirtz told German broadcaster ARD.

The Dutch defeat was the first since their coach Xavi Hernandez took charge but, despite Greece’s 1-0 win over Serbia on Monday, they also qualified for the final eight, although the last German goal dropped them to second in the group.

The Netherlands offered little in attack after Germany’s second and missed injured captain Virgil van Dijk at the back, with the hosts cutting through a flimsy defence at will.

So often criticised for a lack of end product since his big-money move to Liverpool in 2025, Wirtz has scored in four in his past four games for Germany.

Germany knew only a victory would give them a realistic chance of reaching the quarters, with coach Klopp describing the match as a “final.”

The game, a rematch of the 1974 World Cup final won by Germany in Munich, began with both sides risk averse and reluctant to move forward.

The Dutch had the first good chance when Jurrien Timber found Crysencio Summerville unmarked on the penalty spot, but the winger lost his footing before getting a shot away.

Just after the half hour, the Berlin-born-and-raised Scherhant latched onto a cross from Freiburg teammate Philipp Treu but hit the far post.

Nine minutes later, Scherhant had another chance from the same blade of grass and this time curled a lovely effort across the face of goal and inside the post.

The Germans continued their assault on the Dutch penalty area after the break, Wirtz adding another with a solo effort on the hour. The Liverpool winger dribbled from left to right and back centrally before lifting a shot in off the left post from the penalty arc.

Schlotterbeck headed in from a Gruda free-kick with 65 minutes gone.

The RB Leipzig winger laid on another goal six minutes later when he tore down the right and found Wirtz, who hammered in off the bottom of the crossbar.

In his first Germany match on home soil, Gruda then added one of his own, tapping in a Scherhant shot which rebounded off the post.

“We don’t mind who we play. We want to play attacking football. We want to score goals and dominate the opponent. And I think we did that perfectly,” said Wirtz.

“We want to keep going next year. We want to get better. I think we’ve taken some great steps in our development as a team.”

title: US Judge Blocks Trump Policy On Foreign Students, Journalists
description: A US federal judge on Monday struck down a Trump administration policy that would impose stricter limits on how long foreign students and journalists can study or work in the United States.District Judge Dennis Saylor, in his order dismissing the case, said the policy was “arbitrary, capriciou
content:
A US federal judge on Monday struck down a Trump administration policy that would impose stricter limits on how long foreign students and journalists can study or work in the United States.

District Judge Dennis Saylor, in his order dismissing the case, said the policy was “arbitrary, capricious, an abuse of discretion, and otherwise not in accordance with law.”

The new visa regulations had been scheduled to take effect in September but were temporarily put on hold by Saylor, a move the Trump administration has already appealed to a higher court.

The judge’s ruling stems from a lawsuit contesting the visa restrictions filed against the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) by a coalition of unions representing universities, teachers and journalists.

In his order, Saylor focused mainly on the impact the new visa policy would have had on international students.

“Put bluntly, DHS is seeking to prevent or discourage the very activity — providing educational opportunities for foreign students in the United States — that Congress sought to permit and encourage,” the judge said.

He said the policy would “prohibit foreign students from engaging in extended periods of study, such as those required for Ph.D. programs; prohibit them from obtaining joint degrees (and) prohibit them from changing their academic concentration.”

Under the proposed new rules, foreigners on student visas would be admitted for a maximum of up to four years after which they would have to apply for an extension.

International students were previously allowed to remain for the duration of their studies.

Foreign journalists would be limited to stays of just 240 days, or around eight months, but could apply for extensions of similar duration.

Until now, they could stay up to five years.

Chinese journalists would get just 90 days, with extensions of 90 days.

The visa restrictions are part of a broader immigration crackdown by President Donald Trump that includes aggressive deportation operations as well as new restrictions on legal pathways to citizenship.

The United States welcomed more than 1.1 million international students in the 2023-24 academic year, more than any other country, according to official data.

AFP

The presidential candidate of the Young Peoples Party (YPP) for the 2027 general election, Peter Agada, has said that a former Anambra State governor, Peter Obi, will not secure up to 30 per cent of the six million votes he got in the 2023 presidential election.

Agada stated this on Monday during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today.

He said that the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) presidential candidate, who was of the Labour Party (LP) in 2023, won in Lagos due to the support received from different groups, including members of the #EndSARS group, youths, and workers.

While assessing the administration of President Bola Tinubu, Agada said that though he supports Tinubu’s removal of the fuel subsidy, he has a problem with the President not targeting the real end users and subsidising the product.

He also said that Nigeria is losing about 70 per cent of its revenue to overbloated contracts.

He also described the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway ₦1trn budget as overbloated, saying that he would construct one kilometre of the road for ₦750 million or ₦800 million.

Asked whether he was part of the proposed coalition to unseat President Tinubu, Agada said no one had approached him.
