title: Stop turning campaigns into entertainment shows, Nollywood actor tells politicians
description:
Nollywood actor, Osita Iheme, popularly known as Pawpaw, has cautioned Nigerian politicians against turning campaign rallies into entertainment shows, saying the country needs leaders who can demonstrate competence and deliver good governance.
Iheme made the remarks in a post shared on his Instagram
content:
Nollywood actor, Osita Iheme, popularly known as Pawpaw, has cautioned Nigerian politicians against turning campaign rallies into entertainment shows, saying the country needs leaders who can demonstrate competence and deliver good governance.

Iheme made the remarks in a post shared on his Instagram page on Monday, where he expressed displeasure over politicians dancing on stage during political campaigns.

The actor urged politicians to focus on presenting their achievements, demonstrating their competence and explaining their plans for Nigerians rather than engaging in choreography and seeking applause from supporters.

He listed some of the expectations of Nigerians from political leaders, stressing that the country needed competence rather than choreography, good governance rather than hype men, and leadership rather than entertainment.

“We don’t need choreography. We need competence. We don’t need hype men. We need good governance. We don’t need entertainers. We need leaders,” he wrote.

Iheme further challenged politicians to tell Nigerians what they had achieved and what they intended to do if elected.

“Show us what you have done. Tell Nigerians what you will do. You are not going for Grammy,” he said.

He also warned politicians against dancing on campaign stages, adding, “I don’t want to see you guys’ dance on stage again. Be careful.”

title: US court strikes down Trump’s four-year limit on foreign students
description:
A federal judge in the United States has overturned a Trump administration regulation that sought to limit how long foreign students and exchange visitors could remain in the country, Bloomberg Law reports on Monday.
Judge F. Dennis Saylor of the US District Court for the District of Massachusetts r
content:
A federal judge in the United States has overturned a Trump administration regulation that sought to limit how long foreign students and exchange visitors could remain in the country, Bloomberg Law reports on Monday.

Judge F. Dennis Saylor of the US District Court for the District of Massachusetts ruled on Monday that the Department of Homeland Security regulation exceeded its statutory authority and failed to consider less restrictive ways of achieving its objectives.

The regulation sought to end the long-standing “duration of status” arrangement, which allows international students to remain in the US while making progress towards completing their academic programmes.

Under the proposed changes, holders of F-1 student visas and J-1 exchange visitor visas would have been limited to four years in the country. Those needing more time would have had to apply to the DHS for extensions.

The judge said the agency had not explained how imposing “an unreviewable, completely discretionary renewal system—after a foreign student has already been in the country for four years—meaningfully enhances the ability of DHS to root out cases of fraud, or how the benefits of such a system outweigh the immense costs of abandoning the existing system.”

Saylor said the department had not adequately explained how replacing the existing arrangement with a discretionary renewal system would help prevent immigration fraud or justify the additional burden on foreign students.

The judge also found that the government had failed to establish a rational link between the restrictions and the objectives it claimed they would achieve.

The case was brought by a coalition of higher education and labour organisations, including the United Auto Workers, which argued that the regulation would disrupt students’ education and make it more difficult for them to complete their degrees.

Saylor had earlier blocked the regulation from taking effect in September. Monday’s order set aside the rule.

The ruling means the proposed four-year limit and the requirement for students and exchange visitors to seek extensions under the new system cannot take effect.

In July, PUNCH Online reported that the Trump administration had introduced a four-year limit on the stay of foreign students and exchange visitors in the US, ending the long-standing “duration of status” arrangement that allowed them to remain in the country for as long as they continued making progress towards completing their academic programmes.

Under the proposed policy, F-1 and J-1 visa holders who needed more than four years would have been required to apply to the Department of Homeland Security for extensions.

content:
Nollywood actress Linda Osifo has announced her engagement to her partner, Mr Ose.

She shared the news in a video posted on her Instagram page on Monday.

In her post, Osifo said she had been away from social media for a while before God answered a prayer she once made in silence.

“Not in my timing, not in the way I imagined, but in a way only He could have written,” she wrote.

She described the blessing as too beautiful to explain, adding that some love stories were worth every season of waiting.

“Today, I look at the man God has blessed me with and all I can say is… God, You did this for me,” she wrote.

Addressing her partner, she said, “To the man I get to call my forever, Mr Ose, I would choose you in every lifetime.”

She announced, “I SAID YES TO FOREVER!” and added that when God writes a love story, every chapter is worth the wait.

title: 2027 Elections: ‘Nigerians Have Been Rejecting Him,’ Segun Sowunmi Faults Atiku’s Candidacy
description: A Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) chieftain, Segun Sowunmi, has criticised African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate Atiku Abubakar’s repeated bids for Nigeria’s presidency, claiming that Nigerians have consistently rejected his ambition at the polls.Sowunmi, who is also a
content:
A Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) chieftain, Segun Sowunmi, has criticised African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate Atiku Abubakar’s repeated bids for Nigeria’s presidency, claiming that Nigerians have consistently rejected his ambition at the polls.

Sowunmi, who is also a member of the All Progressives Congress (APC) campaign council, made the remarks on Monday during an appearance on Channels Television’s Politics Today.

Responding to a question about Atiku’s belief that he is better positioned than President Bola Tinubu to govern Nigeria, Sowunmi said the former vice president should reconsider his ambition.

“Well, he’s been saying that for a while, and Nigerians have been rejecting him,” he said.

“If you have done elections the number of times Waziri (Atiku) has done, there is something he himself must consider. At what point in time does he expect younger, sharper northern people to get tired or be fatigued at running around with him?” he asked.

North Presidency Calculations

The PDP chieftain, who was a spokesperson for the Atiku Abubakar Presidential Campaign Organisation in 2023, also questioned the former vice president’s political calculations, noting that the North had already produced a president who governed for eight years under former President Muhammadu Buhari.

He further questioned Atiku’s candidacy under the African Democratic Congress (ADC), following a Federal High Court judgment nullifying the leadership of the caretaker committee led by former Senate President David Mark.

The November 5 judgment, delivered by Justice Peter Lifu in Abuja, followed a suit filed by Nafiu Bala Gombe, a former deputy national chairman of the ADC, challenging the emergence of the Mark-led leadership.

The ruling affected decisions taken by the committee, including the process that produced Atiku as the party’s 2027 presidential candidate.

The ADC group has rejected the judgment and appealed.

Sowunmi, however, maintained that Atiku’s candidacy remained uncertain.

“As at today, he is not on the ballot. Because you appeal a case you lost in the lower court, does that mean you are going to win it? The bottom line is that, as at today, he is not their candidate,” he said.

He also accused Atiku of mishandling the dispute involving Gombe, describing his approach as an “emir complex”.

“Emirs don’t beg, emirs don’t visit people, call others. Emirs sit at home, and everybody comes to meet them. Yes, you can be an emir, but you can’t be an emir if you are looking for a ticket in another man’s party,” he added.

title: [VIDEO] Bamayi: I’m Extremely Disappointed Security Agencies Allow That Joke To Go On — Sowunmi
description: A chieftain of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), Segun Sowunmi, has condemned the recent ‘Bamayi’ protest in Abuja, expressing disappointment with security agencies over their handling of the incident.Sowunmi, who is also a member of the All Progressives Congress (APC) campaign council
content:
A chieftain of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), Segun Sowunmi, has condemned the recent ‘Bamayi’ protest in Abuja, expressing disappointment with security agencies over their handling of the incident.

Sowunmi, who is also a member of the All Progressives Congress (APC) campaign council, made the remarks on Monday during an appearance on Channels Television’s Politics Today.

He criticised the destruction of campaign posters and the use of violence by protesters who chanted ‘Bamayi’ at President Bola Tinubu’s motorcade, describing such actions as undemocratic.

“I am disappointed, extremely disappointed that security is allowing that kind of joke to go on under the guise of people who are running democracy,” he said.

Sowunmi argued that Nigerians dissatisfied with a political candidate or campaign should express their opposition through the ballot box rather than resorting to violence.

“I expect people who have a point of view different from that of a campaign to wait until the day of election to exercise their franchise. But to be destroying people’s posters, to be carrying sticks and running up and down, that’s for barbarians, and I don’t expect any sane leader to do that,” he added.

The ‘Bamayi’ chants, which translate to ‘we don’t want’ in Hausa, were heard on November 13 after President Tinubu attended Friday prayers at the Shehu Shagari Mosque in the Garki area of Abuja.

Some protesters reportedly threw stones at the President’s convoy and destroyed APC campaign posters, prompting security operatives to intervene.

title: Gunmen ambush, kill Operation Rainbow commander, one other in Plateau
description:
Suspected gunmen have killed a newly graduated unit commander of Operation Rainbow, a Plateau State-owned civilian security outfit, alongside another resident in an ambush in Bokkos Local Government Area of the state.
The victims were reportedly attacked at about 3pm on Monday while returning from a
content:
Suspected gunmen have killed a newly graduated unit commander of Operation Rainbow, a Plateau State-owned civilian security outfit, alongside another resident in an ambush in Bokkos Local Government Area of the state.

The victims were reportedly attacked at about 3pm on Monday while returning from a condolence visit to Hurti village to their community in Tadai, Manguna District, Bokkos LGA.

The community leader, Machief Paul, who confirmed the incident to newsmen, said the two victims were members of his community.

The attack has raised fresh concerns over the security situation in Bokkos, which has witnessed several incidents of violence.

He said, “They are all members of my community. They went to Hurti village for a condolence visit and were returning to Tadai when suspected gunmen ambushed and killed them.

“They were killed in broad daylight this afternoon. It is very sad and unfortunate.”

Paul disclosed that one of the deceased was a newly graduated commander of Operation Rainbow, adding that the killing had thrown the community into mourning.

He said, “The commander had just graduated. We are deeply saddened by this incident, especially given the security challenges our people have continued to face.”

Also confirming the incident, an award-winning Nigerian conflict reporter from Bokkos, Masara Kim, said the two men were killed in the ambush while returning from the condolence visit.

The deceased Operation Rainbow commander was said to have recently completed a refresher training programme for unit commanders in Jos, Kim added.

Efforts to obtain further details from security authorities were unsuccessful as of the time of filing this report.

title: ‘Couldn’t Get Worse,’ Klopp Calls For Change In FIFA leadership
description: Germany coach Jurgen Klopp has called for an end to Gianni Infantino’s time as FIFA president, saying he “did not think things could get worse after Sepp Blatter.”Speaking in Berlin ahead of Monday’s Nations League clash with the Netherlands, Klopp said the next candidate for
content:
Germany coach Jurgen Klopp has called for an end to Gianni Infantino’s time as FIFA president, saying he “did not think things could get worse after Sepp Blatter.”

Speaking in Berlin ahead of Monday’s Nations League clash with the Netherlands, Klopp said the next candidate for football’s global governing body should have the game’s interests at heart.

“I’ve been following football for many years. There are people who are much more knowledgeable about this than I am. But I think most people now agree a change would make a lot of sense,” Klopp said on Sunday.

“I didn’t think things could get worse after Sepp Blatter, but someone has managed to do just that.”

President of FIFA from 1998, Blatter resigned in disgrace in 2015 amid corruption allegations.

Charges were brought against Blatter, who was eventually cleared in two trials, but was banned from football by FIFA’s ethics committee.

“Regarding Gianni Infantino, surely the next person to come along can do a better job,” Klopp added.

Swiss Infantino succeeded Blatter as FIFA president in 2016.

He has come under heavy criticism for a series of decisions and proposals, including his plan to sell off part of the commercial rights of the World Cup and creating and then awarding the inaugural FIFA Peace Prize to US President Donald Trump.

“There are people who truly care about the future of football — people who aren’t driven by financial interests,” said Klopp.

“If someone like that were to step up — if someone like that were to become president — I think that would be a significant improvement.

“There are surely people who care deeply about the future of football and have no financial interests in it.”

The next election for FIFA president takes place in March 2027. Only former Swiss footballer Ramon Vega and Japan’s Kozo Tashima have announced their intention to run against Infantino.

AFP

title: Vanguard loses Online Editor, Femi Ajasa
description:
The Management of Vanguard Media Limited announces with profound sorrow, the death of its Online Editor, Mr Olufemi Finayon Ajasa, who passed away on Sunday at the Lagos University Teaching Hospital, LUTH, after a brief illness. He was aged 44.



A statement from the Editor, Mr. Eze Anaba said his
content:
The Management of Vanguard Media Limited announces with profound sorrow, the death of its Online Editor, Mr Olufemi Finayon Ajasa, who passed away on Sunday at the Lagos University Teaching Hospital, LUTH, after a brief illness. He was aged 44.

A statement from the Editor, Mr. Eze Anaba said his death is a massive loss to the entire Vanguard family, the journalism profession and all those who knew and worked with him

Mr Ajasa was a valued member of the Vanguard family, who made significant contributions to the growth of the company’s digital operations and online journalism.

Born into the Ajasa family of Ajido, in Badagry Local Government Area of Lagos State, Olufemi Ajasa obtained a Bachelor of Science degree in Mass Communication, specialising in Journalism, from Lagos State University, LASU, between 2004 and 2009. He further honed his professional skills with a certification in Advanced Writing and Reporting Skills from the School of Media and Communication, Pan-Atlantic University, in 2015.

He began his journalism career as a photojournalist with National Mirror Newspaper in February 2012, where he worked until November 2013. He joined Vanguard Media Limited in December 2013 as an online reporter and content developer, serving until September 2016.

He subsequently moved to TheNewsGuru.com, where he worked from 2016 to 2021, first as Online Editor and later as Team Lead and Head of Digital Operations. In December 2021, he joined Pulse as Editorial Quality Assurance Manager.

Ajasa returned to Vanguard in June 2022 as Online Editor, a position he held until his death.
His return marked the continuation of a relationship with the organisation that began early in his professional career.

The management of Vanguard Media Limited deeply regrets this irreparable loss and extends its heartfelt condolences to his immediate family, friends, professional associates and all members of the Vanguard family.

At this difficult time, our thoughts and prayers are with his family. We pray that God grants them the strength and fortitude to bear this painful loss, and that the soul of our departed colleague finds eternal rest.

The Service of Songs/Wake-Keep in honour of the deceased will hold at 14 Sylvia Crescent, Anthony Village, Lagos, on Thursday, November 19, at 5 p.m.

Other funeral arrangements will be announced by the family

May his gentle soul rest in perfect peace.

title: ‘This is what real crowd looks like,not the AI you posted’ — Atiku mocks APC after ADC rally in Yobe
description:
Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar has accused the All Progressives Congress (APC) of using artificial intelligence (AI) to create misleading impressions of large crowds at its political rallies.
Atiku, the presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), made the allegation while
content:
Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar has accused the All Progressives Congress (APC) of using artificial intelligence (AI) to create misleading impressions of large crowds at its political rallies.

Atiku, the presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), made the allegation while expressing appreciation to residents of Potiskum and other parts of Yobe State for the reception he received during the party’s campaign rally.

In a statement issued on Monday by Phrank Shaibu, Director of Strategic Communication of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, Atiku also commended Yobe State Governor, Mai Mala Buni, for providing what he described as a level playing field for opposition parties to conduct their campaign activities.

Atiku described the reception he received in Potiskum as overwhelming, saying the turnout and enthusiasm of residents had left a lasting impression on him.

“The welcome from the moment we entered Potiskum from Azare was simply breathtaking. The sea of heads, the joyful faces, the chants and the warmth of the people will remain in my heart,” he said.

He thanked residents of Potiskum and other parts of the state for welcoming the ADC campaign team, adding that the governor’s conduct had strengthened democratic participation by allowing political parties to meet voters and present their messages.

Atiku, however, used the occasion to take a swipe at the APC, alleging that the party relied on AI-generated images to create the impression of massive attendance at its rallies.

“The Presidency may need artificial intelligence to conjure a crowd, but in Potiskum the people came out in flesh and blood, unfiltered, unedited and impossible to fabricate,” he said.

“Our Affordable Life campaign needs no artificial crowd; the people’s presence and their voices speak for themselves.”

The former vice-president further mocked what he alleged was the use of AI-generated images to depict supporters at political gatherings.

“The Presidency’s AI must have forgotten that crowds need seats and that people do not fly. Perhaps in Tinubu’s imaginary rally, the supporters were expected to hover through the speech,” he added.

Atiku also said chants of “Tinubu Must Go” at ADC rallies reflected what he described as Nigerians’ desire for improved living conditions and a change in leadership.

He maintained that the party’s Affordable Life campaign was intended to address the economic difficulties facing Nigerians, rather than serve as a political slogan.

The ADC candidate pledged to take immediate steps to improve living conditions if elected president, saying he would begin implementing his promises after the end of President Bola Tinubu’s tenure on May 29, 2027.

“When President Tinubu leaves office on 29 May 2027, good governance and an affordable life must follow. I solemnly pledge to take immediate steps to make life affordable again when elected president at the January 16 presidential election. That is my promise to our teeming supporters,” he said.

Atiku added that the reception in Yobe had reinforced his belief that Nigerians would respond to political messages addressing their economic challenges and aspirations.

The post ‘This is what real crowd looks like,not the AI you posted’ — Atiku mocks APC after ADC rally in Yobe appeared first on Very Nigerian.

title: NNPP disowns Onu, threatens legal action over alleged impersonation
description:
By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta



The New Nigeria People’s Party (NNPP) has disowned Prince Nweze Onu, who allegedly parades himself as the party’s Deputy National Chairman, describing him as an impostor who has no authority to speak or act on behalf of the party.



The party also warned that Onu cou
content:
By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta

The New Nigeria People’s Party (NNPP) has disowned Prince Nweze Onu, who allegedly parades himself as the party’s Deputy National Chairman, describing him as an impostor who has no authority to speak or act on behalf of the party.

The party also warned that Onu could face arrest over alleged impersonation, insisting that he had long been expelled from its fold alongside Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso.

The NNPP’s position was contained in a statement issued by its National Secretary, Comrade Oginni Olaposi Sunday, and made available to Vanguard in Abeokuta.

He accused Onu of misrepresenting his political affiliation and attempting to create confusion about the party’s leadership.

According to Oginni, Onu is not a recognised official of the NNPP and should not be regarded as its spokesperson or representative.

“Prince Onu is not qualified to speak on behalf of our great party. He is, at the last count, a member of Kwankwasiya in NDC,” the National Secretary stated.

Oginni further called on media organisations to exercise caution and verify the political affiliations and official positions of individuals before publishing statements attributed to them as representatives of political parties.

“We are using this opportunity to call on all media houses to ensure that due diligence is done on verification of the status of individuals before publication,” he said.

The party also condemned what it described as an attack on President Bola Ahmed Tinubu by Onu, dismissing his remarks as politically motivated and an attempt to attract attention from the Presidency.

Oginni described Onu as an expired politician and rabble-rouser, arguing that his comments should not be taken seriously.

“Onu is an expired politician and a rabble-rouser trying to get the attention of the Presidency. Nobody should take him seriously,” he said.

The NNPP reiterated that Onu had no mandate to speak for the party, warning that individuals who falsely claim official positions within its leadership structure could face legal consequences.

title: Lekki residents protest four-month power outage, demand substation
description:
Accuse Eko Power, TCN of shifting blame; say businesses losing billions



By Cynthia Alo



Residents of more than 200 estates along the Orchid Road axis of Lekki, Lagos State, have staged a protest over prolonged electricity outages, accusing Eko Power Limited and the Transmission Company of Niger
content:
Accuse Eko Power, TCN of shifting blame; say businesses losing billions

By Cynthia Alo

Residents of more than 200 estates along the Orchid Road axis of Lekki, Lagos State, have staged a protest over prolonged electricity outages, accusing Eko Power Limited and the Transmission Company of Nigeria (TCN) of shifting blame for the persistent disruption.

The residents, under the aegis of the Lekki Conservation Estates Community Development Association (LECECODA), demanded the immediate restoration of electricity supply, provision of individual prepaid meters and construction of a dedicated injection substation to serve the Orchid Road corridor.

They also called for a technical audit of the Maroko 33kV feeder, through which the community receives electricity, and urged the Nigerian Electricity Regulatory Commission (NERC) to investigate the quality of service being delivered to the area.

The protest, which took place at the weekend, followed what the residents described as five years of engagements and unfulfilled commitments by the electricity distribution company.

It also came barely a week after the Minister of Power, Mr Joseph Tegbe, reportedly assured residents of Lekki and Ajah communities of improved electricity supply.

The protesters, comprising landlords, tenants and business owners, carried placards with inscriptions such as: “Orchid Road Deserves a Substation”, “Orchid Road Band B = Band Nothing”, “We Pay Premium Rates But Get Zero Reliability”, “Eko Power Failed Promise” and “Constant Power Outages Are Killing Businesses on Orchid Road.”

Addressing journalists during the protest, LECECODA President, Bode Akinwande, said the community had received virtually no electricity for more than four months despite continuing to receive electricity bills running into millions of naira.

Akinwande described Orchid Road as a 7.5-kilometre corridor housing approximately 200 residential estates, alongside schools, restaurants, shopping malls, supermarkets, clubs, churches and mosques.

He said the community’s size and contribution to Eko Power’s revenue made the absence of a dedicated injection substation particularly concerning.

He said: “For the past four months, we have received virtually no supply. In the month of October, we did not receive two hours of supply cumulatively. And unfortunately, members of this community, various estates, have received bills in millions. And this is not acceptable to us at all.

“For five years, the leadership of this community has engaged directly with Eko Power, and before it, the former management known as EKEDC. Several meetings have been held, and several commitments have been made. None of them have been implemented.”

The LECECODA president said the current management of Eko Power also met with community stakeholders at Orchid Hotel and made further assurances, but residents had yet to witness any significant improvement.

He said the association formally wrote to the acting Managing Director of Eko Power in October, outlining its concerns and requesting a meeting.

According to him, the company subsequently appealed to the community to suspend its planned protest and allow more time for the situation to be addressed, but the residents rejected the request.

Akinwande said the Maroko 33kV feeder experienced frequent trips, resulting in repeated interruptions, particularly whenever rain threatened.

He added that electricity supply was sometimes restored for barely two minutes after four or five days without power.

“We are paying for a service level we do not receive. The Maroko 33kV feeder trips on a daily basis. At the slightest threat of rain, supply is lost within minutes. In recent weeks, supply has been restored for as little as two minutes after intervals of four to five days without power,” he said.

He demanded that Eko Power either restore electricity supply in line with the community’s Band B classification or review its bills to reflect the actual service delivered.

He also called for a time-bound plan to address the persistent feeder failures and a commitment to construct a dedicated injection substation for the area.

“If they are sure of their service delivery, they should be ready to give all the individual houses within Orchid Road, whether gated or not, prepaid meters. Then we know that it is pay as you use,” he added.

Akinwande further urged TCN’s Ajah Transmission Station to explain the prolonged outages and work with Eko Power to restore stable electricity supply.

He warned that the residents would sustain the protest until there was a noticeable improvement.

“The people of Orchid Road have shown patience and goodwill over many years. That patience has now been exhausted. We remain open to constructive engagement, but we will continue to pursue every legitimate avenue available to us until our community receives the reliable power supply it pays for and deserves.

“If we do not see a stable power supply next month, we are going to gather again. It will be monthly until we receive an appreciable improvement on power supply to us,” he said.

Also speaking, the immediate past president of LECECODA, Osas Airen, said his estate, Buena Vista, spent about N56 million monthly on diesel despite operating a blended electricity arrangement that provided only about 12 hours of power daily.

“As we speak, we owe our diesel supplier. That’s how bad it is,” Airen said.

The association’s Public Relations Officer, Faith Oliver, said more than 200,000 residents and businesses in the community had suffered losses running into billions of naira.

She said businesses dependent on refrigeration, including restaurants, supermarkets and frozen-food outlets, were particularly affected, as alternative sources of electricity could not adequately sustain their operations.

Oliver added that the outages had also disrupted water supply because electricity was needed to pump water into residential estates, forcing some households to purchase water from suppliers.

Similarly, Chairman of DPK District Estates, Adeyinka Adetukasi, said the existing electricity infrastructure was inadequate for the size and power demand of the Orchid Road corridor.

He said the facilities frequently tripped whenever electricity supply was restored, questioning the continued billing of residents for electricity they did not receive.

Eko Power reacts

In response to an October 20 letter from LECECODA, Eko Power Limited said its management had reviewed the issues raised by the community and engaged its technical and operational teams to identify immediate and long-term solutions.

The company attributed the supply constraints to a combination of factors, including limited power generation availability, gas supply challenges affecting generating companies, disruptions on critical TCN infrastructure serving Lagos and operational challenges within sections of the Maroko 33kV network.

Eko Power said it would undertake a comprehensive technical audit and network patrol of the Maroko 33kV feeder and associated infrastructure, covering feeder routes, distribution transformers, protection systems and other critical network assets.

It also said its technical teams had intensified feeder patrols, fault detection, sectionalisation and restoration interventions to reduce the frequency and duration of outages.

The company added that further measures were being evaluated to improve fault isolation, minimise the impact of network disturbances and enhance service reliability.

It also proposed a virtual stakeholder engagement involving its management and technical personnel to discuss the community’s concerns, ongoing interventions, the proposed technical audit and a practical way forward.

However, residents told Vanguard that although the virtual meeting was subsequently held, there had been no improvement in electricity supply.

They said the situation had deteriorated further, with the community recording fewer than 10 hours of electricity supply throughout October.

The residents also alleged that Eko Power’s response to their October 20 letter came only after the company became aware of the planned protest.

The post Lekki residents protest four-month power outage, demand substation appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Sowore petitions police over Ekiti attack, demands arrest
description:
The 2027 presidential candidate of the African Action Congress, Omoyele Sowore, has petitioned the Ekiti State Police Command, demanding the immediate arrest, interrogation and prosecution of an alleged participant in the October 30 attack on him and members of his campaign team in Ado-Ekiti.
In the
content:
The 2027 presidential candidate of the African Action Congress, Omoyele Sowore, has petitioned the Ekiti State Police Command, demanding the immediate arrest, interrogation and prosecution of an alleged participant in the October 30 attack on him and members of his campaign team in Ado-Ekiti.

In the petition dated November 16, 2026 which sighted by PUNCH Online on Monday and addressed to the Commissioner of Police, Sowore, through his lawyer, Damilare Adenola, accused the individual of direct involvement in the attack at Tawakalitu Restaurant and Catering Services in the Dalimore area of the state capital.

The petition alleged that Sowore and his team were attacked shortly after he concluded a radio interview at MIDAS FM 90.5 by “a group of more than twenty armed men” who allegedly used “guns, machetes and bottles”.

It further alleged that the attackers threatened to kill Sowore if he returned to Ekiti State and stole mobile phones, wristwatches and other personal belongings from members of his team.

“Members of the team sustained injuries that required hospital treatment,” the petition stated, adding that photographs of the injured persons and video footage of the attack were attached as evidence.

The lawyer said Sowore had identified the individual as one of those who participated in the attack, while urging the police to examine the footage and verify the identification.

The petition stated that despite the circulation of video footage and identifying details linking the individual to the scene, he had neither been invited, arrested nor questioned.

It added, “The purpose of this petition is to bring these facts directly to your office and to request swift and decisive police action without further delay.”

The lawyers also expressed concern about the continued freedom of the individual, saying, “The Suspect’s continued liberty, several days after an attack of this gravity was reported and filmed, creates a real risk that evidence will be destroyed, witnesses and victims will be intimidated, and the Suspect will evade the law.”

They asked the police commissioner to “cause the immediate arrest and interrogation” of the individual, examine the video footage, identify other participants and establish those who allegedly “planned, sponsored, facilitated or protected the attackers”.

The petition also requested the preservation of evidence, including video footage and recording devices at the restaurant, as well as call and location records of the stolen mobile phones.

It further urged the police to obtain statements from Sowore, eyewitnesses and medical personnel and secure relevant medical records.

The lawyers asked the command to “charge and prosecute every person found culpable, without regard to office, rank or political connection”.

They also requested adequate police protection for Sowore, members of his team and witnesses against possible reprisals.

The petition asked the command to acknowledge receipt, designate a contact person and provide an update on the investigation within 14 days.

The lawyers said their clients and the firm would cooperate with investigators, adding, “Our Clients and this firm will make themselves available to your investigators and will supply the annexed photographs and video, and any further evidence in their possession, as required.”

The latest development comes about two weeks after the attack, which sparked disagreement between Sowore and the police over the circumstances surrounding the incident.

The Ekiti State Police Command had initially described the incident as an altercation between Sowore and some individuals at a restaurant, confirming that the activist sustained injuries and was taken to the Police Hospital in Ado-Ekiti.

However, Sowore rejected the police account, insisting that there was no altercation but an attack by armed men.

The police subsequently announced the arrest of 11 suspects in connection with the incident. The suspects were arrested by operatives of the Rapid Response Squad at their hideouts in the Atikankan area of Ado-Ekiti on October 30.

The command said investigations were ongoing to establish their individual roles, determine their possible connections with the attack and identify other persons involved.

title: Jackson scores as Senegal move closer to 2027 AFCON
description:
Premier League duo Nicolas Jackson and El Hadji Malick Diouf scored on Monday as Senegal beat Sudan 4-2 to virtually clinch a place at the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations tournament.



Cameroon trounced Namibia 3-0 and Benin snatched a late 1-0 win over the Central African Republic to move close to qual
content:
Premier League duo Nicolas Jackson and El Hadji Malick Diouf scored on Monday as Senegal beat Sudan 4-2 to virtually clinch a place at the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations tournament.

Cameroon trounced Namibia 3-0 and Benin snatched a late 1-0 win over the Central African Republic to move close to qualification for the marquee African competition.

Senegal, Cameroon and Benin have 10 points each from four matches and could all be confirmed as qualifiers on Tuesday depending on the other result in their groups.

Cameroon and Senegal are former AFCON champions while the furthest Benin have progressed is the round of 16 at the 2025 tournament.

Jackson came to Africa last week, having scored nine goals in all competitions for Aston Villa this season. He opened the scoring in a 4-1 home win over Sudan last Thursday.

He also broke the deadlock with a fourth-minute goal away to Sudan, who hosted the match in South Sudan because of a civil war in their homeland.

Defender Diouf, who moved from relegated West Ham United to Brentford during the close season, doubled the lead midway through the first half.

Sudan staged a second-half comeback to draw level after 75 minutes through goals from substitute Al Gozoli Nooh and Salaheldin Adil.

But a late Senegalese rally saw Pathe Mboup restore the lead, then set up Paul Mendy to score in added time.

– Cameroon romp –

Senegal won the final of previous edition of the AFCON 1-0 in extra time over hosts Morocco last February.

But CAF declared Morocco champions because most of the Senegalese team temporarily left the field to protest a penalty, which Morocco missed when play resumed.

Senegal have asked the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) in Switzerland to overturn the CAF ruling and a decision is expected this month.

It took Cameroon 12 minutes to score away to Namibia through Mahamadou Nagida. Goals from Ryan Fosso and Saidou Alioum in the second half completed the victory.

Benin left it late to secure maximum points with debutant Ede Oloko netting in added time. The goal condemned the Central African Republic to a fourth straight loss.

Elsewhere, Zimbabwe outplayed Equatorial Guinea 3-0 in Harare, Guinea beat Eritrea 3-1 in Cairo and a Jordan Ayew penalty earned Ghana an unimpressive 1-0 win over Somalia in Essipong.

In the six matches on Monday, Zimbabwe were the only host nation to actually play at home. Central African Republic, Eritrea and Namibia do not have international-standard stadiums.

A civil war that erupted in April 2023 prevents Sudan from playing in Khartoum and Somalia cannot stage AFCON qualifiers due to security concerns in the Horn of Africa.

AFP

title: Bandits Kill 37-Year-Old Chinese Miner, Police Inspector In Bauchi
description: Suspected bandits have killed a 37-year-old Chinese national, Wang Tingjian, who worked with Zurfi Mining Company, and his police escort, Inspector Abba Ya’u, attached to MOPOL 34, Gombe State, in an ambush in Bauchi State.The incident occurred on Saturday at about 1:30 p.m. in Ruga Village, G
content:
Suspected bandits have killed a 37-year-old Chinese national, Wang Tingjian, who worked with Zurfi Mining Company, and his police escort, Inspector Abba Ya’u, attached to MOPOL 34, Gombe State, in an ambush in Bauchi State.

The incident occurred on Saturday at about 1:30 p.m. in Ruga Village, Gwana District, Alkaleri Local Government Area of the state.

Confirming the incident to Channels Television in a telephone interview on Monday, the Police Public Relations Officer (PPRO), SP Nafiu Habib, said the Chinese miner was conducting a survey at a mining site when he and his escort were attacked by suspected gunmen.

He explained that the attack triggered an exchange of gunfire between the security operatives and the assailants.

“During the survey, they were ambushed by unknown gunmen. The Chinese national had even run towards the vehicle conveying them for safety, but they were overwhelmed,” Habib said.

According to the PPRO, the victims were rushed to the Federal Teaching Hospital, Gombe, where they were confirmed dead and their bodies deposited in the hospital’s mortuary.

Habib further disclosed that the anti-kidnapping unit and the Violent Crime Response Unit, in collaboration with the military and local vigilantes, were conducting a manhunt for the attackers.

He added that security agencies were also working to unravel the circumstances surrounding the incident.

title: 2027: Bauchi NDC governorship candidate dumps party for APC
description:
The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) governorship candidate in Bauchi State, Ibrahim Kashim, has defected to the All Progressives Congress (APC) ahead of the 2027 general elections.
Kashim announced his defection on Monday at the APC secretariat in Bauchi, saying the ruling party offered the state
content:
The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) governorship candidate in Bauchi State, Ibrahim Kashim, has defected to the All Progressives Congress (APC) ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Kashim announced his defection on Monday at the APC secretariat in Bauchi, saying the ruling party offered the state a stronger platform to participate in national governance and attract development.

A former Secretary to the Bauchi State Government, he said his decision was informed by the APC’s position as the governing party at the federal level, its political strength in northern Nigeria and its national reach.

“I believe that Bauchi must be strategically positioned within this political reality,” he said.

“We cannot afford to gamble with the future of our state by placing our developmental aspirations on a platform that lacks comparable national reach and institutional influence.

“Our decision must be guided by the interests of Bauchi, not sentiment, political nostalgia or the convenience of individuals.”

Kashim argued that remaining outside the party at the centre could limit Bauchi’s access to federal projects, influence on national policy, investment opportunities and adequate representation in key political circles.

He said he was convinced that the APC had the organisational strength and institutional capacity to advance the state’s interests.

The former governorship candidate urged his supporters, political associates and other stakeholders to join him in the APC, insisting that his commitment to improving Bauchi remained unchanged.

He listed youth employment, women’s empowerment, improved agricultural productivity, quality education and stronger healthcare delivery among his priorities.

“Our ultimate objective is not the triumph of one political party over another,” he said.

“It is the triumph of good governance over poor governance, development over stagnation, opportunity over deprivation and hope over despair.

“I have chosen strategic engagement over political isolation. I have chosen a broader national platform over limited political reach.

“Above all, I have chosen what I sincerely believe offers Bauchi State a better opportunity for development and prosperity.”

Kashim appealed to residents to support his decision, saying the state should not be left out of opportunities available through the federation.

The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) had listed him as the NDC governorship candidate in Bauchi.

He had earlier resigned from the NDC on October 16, although the report of his defection to the APC was announced on Monday.

title: Budget 2027: FG moves to slash overhead costs, directs MDAs to share facilities
description:
By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief



As the Federal Government prepares its 2027 budget, it is stepping up efforts to cut overhead expenditure by directing Ministries, Departments and Agencies (MDAs) to maximise the use of existing government-owned facilities instead of spending public funds on hotel
content:
By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief

As the Federal Government prepares its 2027 budget, it is stepping up efforts to cut overhead expenditure by directing Ministries, Departments and Agencies (MDAs) to maximise the use of existing government-owned facilities instead of spending public funds on hotels and other privately owned venues for official meetings.

The move is part of a broader cost-saving initiative by the Federal Ministry of Finance, through its Efficiency Office (E-Office), to eliminate avoidable expenditure, improve the utilisation of public assets and ensure value for money in government operations.

According to Efe Ovuakporie, Head, Information and Public Relations Unit of the Federal Ministry of Finance, in a statement in Abuja on Monday evening, under the initiative, “The Office is working towards establishing a coordinated system that will enable MDAs to identify and access available meeting and conference facilities across government institutions, thereby reducing the need to hire commercial venues for official engagements.”

She added, “A major component of the programme is the compilation of a comprehensive directory of meeting facilities owned by MDAs nationwide. The directory, which will be published on the Federal Ministry of Finance’s website upon completion, is expected to provide government institutions with information on available facilities and make it easier to locate suitable venues.

“The arrangement will also enable MDAs with under-utilised conference facilities to generate revenue by making them available to other government institutions, while reducing pressure on government overhead budgets.”

Ovuakporie said the initiative aligns with the Efficiency Office’s mandate to promote value for money, reduce overhead expenditure, monitor the utilisation of public assets and identify areas of waste across government institutions.

In a related development, the Office recently inspected shared government facilities across the five South-Eastern states of Abia, Anambra, Ebonyi, Enugu and Imo, as part of efforts to identify underutilised public infrastructure and opportunities for cost savings.

The inspection covered selected Federal Secretariats, Federal Polytechnics, Federal Medical Centres and Federal Universities.

The exercise assessed the condition, availability, utilisation and maintenance of the facilities, with particular attention to areas where improved management could enhance productivity and reduce unnecessary government spending.

Among the findings were under-utilised office spaces and facilities, deteriorating furniture, fittings and equipment, as well as inadequate maintenance of some offices and common areas.

The inspection teams also identified opportunities to improve the utilisation of conference facilities and strengthen the organisation, storage and preservation of official records.

The Efficiency Office engaged the management of the institutions visited on measures to address the identified shortcomings, including regular maintenance schedules, proper asset inventories, improved records management and more effective arrangements for sharing available facilities.

The findings are expected to inform recommendations for strengthening the management of government assets, promoting cooperation among institutions and ensuring that infrastructure acquired with public funds delivers maximum value.

The office emphasised that the inspections were not intended to apportion blame but to identify areas requiring improvement and encourage more responsible management of public resources.

The Federal Ministry of Finance said the interventions underscore the need for government institutions to look inward, make better use of existing infrastructure and eliminate avoidable costs through improved planning, coordination and resource sharing.

The initiative is expected to strengthen the Federal Government’s drive to rein in overhead expenditure by ensuring that public institutions utilise available resources before committing additional funds to facilities and services that the government already possesses.

The post Budget 2027: FG moves to slash overhead costs, directs MDAs to share facilities appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: 45 Traders Affected By Gwagwalada International Market Fire Outbreak, Says FEMD
description: The FCT Emergency Management Department (FEMD) has confirmed that about 45 traders operating 28 open stalls and two lock-up shops were affected by a fire outbreak at the Gwagwalada International Market in Gwagwalada Area Council.The FEMD said the incident, which occurred last Saturday, prompted a po
content:
The FCT Emergency Management Department (FEMD) has confirmed that about 45 traders operating 28 open stalls and two lock-up shops were affected by a fire outbreak at the Gwagwalada International Market in Gwagwalada Area Council.

The FEMD said the incident, which occurred last Saturday, prompted a post-disaster assessment visit to the market by the Director, Muhammad Dikko, accompanied by officials of the National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA).

“During the assessment, the Chairman of the Market Association, Mr. Aminu Lawal Bakinruwa, informed the delegation that security personnel on duty noticed smoke emanating from one of the shops at about 8:00 p.m., approximately 20 minutes after electricity supply was restored by the Abuja Electricity Distribution Company (AEDC),” a statement by the Head of Public Affairs at FEMD, Nkechi Isa, disclosed this in a statement on Monday,” partly read.

It explained that some of the affected traders, who spoke with the FEMD delegation, expressed deep distress over the losses incurred, describing the incident as a major setback to their businesses and livelihoods.

“One of the traders, Mrs. Salome Israel, who was visibly emotional, disclosed that she lost goods worth approximately ₦400,000, including yams, tomatoes and peppers. Other items destroyed by the fire included clothing, herbal medicines and beverages,” it stated.

“Addressing the affected traders, the FEMD Director, Muhammad Dikko, urged market operators to prioritise fire safety by ensuring that all electrical appliances are switched off before leaving their shops.

“He also emphasised the importance of insurance coverage for businesses, noting that insured traders would be in a better position to recover their losses in the event of disasters.”

It further said that Dikko stressed the need for the market to be equipped with adequate firefighting equipment to facilitate prompt intervention during emergencies, and appealed to the Market Board of Trustees and the leadership of the traders’ union to explore ways of providing support to the affected traders and easing their hardship.

“Speaking on behalf of NEMA, Mrs. Mariam Dantanko clarified that the Agency’s disaster response support is primarily provided through relief materials rather than direct cash payments,” the statement added. “She explained that such assistance, which may include food and building materials, is subject to assessment and approval by the agency’s headquarters.”

Meanwhile, the Relief and Rehabilitation Division of FEMD was also present at the scene to conduct a needs assessment to determine the immediate requirements of the affected traders.

The department reiterated the importance of fire safety consciousness, regular inspection of electrical installations, and the provision of functional firefighting equipment in markets and other public facilities to prevent avoidable fire incidents.

title: Man detained for ‘witchcraft’ regains freedom after 5 months
description:
…AFAW commends bail, demands charges be dropped
A man remanded since June for alleged ‘witchcraft and juju’ by an Upper Sharia Court in Zamfara State, Samaila Bala, has been freed on bail.
The release was confirmed on Monday by contacts in Zamfara and by the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) o
content:
…AFAW commends bail, demands charges be dropped

A man remanded since June for alleged ‘witchcraft and juju’ by an Upper Sharia Court in Zamfara State, Samaila Bala, has been freed on bail.

The release was confirmed on Monday by contacts in Zamfara and by the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) office in Gusau.

In a WhatsApp message to the Advocacy for Alleged Witches (AfAW), the NHRC said: “Congratulations! Samaila Bala has been freed and is out.”

AfAW, which has been campaigning for Bala’s release, confirmed the development in a statement signed by its Director, Leo Igwe and made available to Journalists in Owerri.

According to Igwe, Bala has been remanded several times since 2020 for the same alleged offence. He said letters had been written to the Governor, the Grand Khadi, the Attorney General, and the Director of Public Prosecution urging his release.

He said over a week ago, the Registrar of the Sharia Court of Appeal called AfAW and asked the organisation to send someone to complete the bail formalities, which it did.

Igwe said local sources informed AfAW that some elements in the judiciary had been frustrating the process, with some officials not answering calls or their numbers not reachable.

He said he was advised to contact the Grand Khadi, and on Saturday, November 14, 2026, he sent him a message appealing for intervention.

“Dear Grand Khadi, my name is Leo Igwe. I live in Oyo State. I am in Malawi. I finished attending an international conference on witchcraft accusations and ritual attacks. One case highlighted was Bala’s. I got a call over a week ago. The registrar of the Sharia Court of Appeal called and said that I should send someone to formalize the bail. We sent someone to finalize bail formalities, but nothing has happened. Please, I urge you again to intervene and release him. Bala is innocent . ”

AfAW welcomed Bala’s release on bail and commended the Grand Khadi and other judicial officers for yielding to its appeal.

“Nobody should be prosecuted or jailed for witchcraft and juju in this 21st century because these offences do not exist under Nigerian law. The imprisonment of Bala is illegal, unconstitutional, and a violation of his human rights. Bala’s case is a case of sharia state witch hunt,” Igwe said.

AfAW said it was not yet clear whether the prosecution would continue, and urged a discontinuation of what it described as a legal charade.

“The prosecution should enter a nolle prosequi, drop the charges, and compensate Bala. End witch hunts in Zamfara. End witch hunts in Nigeria. End witch hunts in Africa.”

The post Man detained for ‘witchcraft’ regains freedom after 5 months appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Gombe CP decorates nine promoted senior police officers
description:
The Commissioner of Police, Gombe State Command, Umar Chuso, has decorated nine senior officers recently promoted in the Nigeria Police Force.
The ceremony, held on Monday at the command headquarters in Gombe, was conducted on behalf of the Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Rilwan Disu, with mem
content:
The Commissioner of Police, Gombe State Command, Umar Chuso, has decorated nine senior officers recently promoted in the Nigeria Police Force.

The ceremony, held on Monday at the command headquarters in Gombe, was conducted on behalf of the Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Rilwan Disu, with members of the command’s management team in attendance.

According to a statement signed by the command’s Public Relations Officer, Buhari Abdullahi, the promotion saw two Chief Superintendents of Police elevated to Assistant Commissioners of Police, two Superintendents promoted to Chief Superintendents, one Deputy Superintendent elevated to Superintendent, and four Assistant Superintendents promoted to Deputy Superintendents.

The officers promoted to Assistant Commissioners of Police are Garga Ibrahim Audu, Officer-in-Charge of Research and Planning at the state headquarters, and Mapindi Yusuf, Divisional Police Officer, Shongom.

Also promoted from Superintendent to Chief Superintendent of Police were Abubakar Kabiru, DPO, Tumfure, and Ibrahim Tukur, Second-in-Command of the Violent Crime Response Unit.

Congratulating the officers, Chuso described their elevation as recognition of their dedication, professionalism, discipline, loyalty and years of meritorious service to the police force.

“This promotion is a recognition of your dedication, professionalism, discipline, loyalty and years of meritorious service to the Nigeria Police Force,” he said.

The commissioner urged the newly promoted officers to justify the confidence reposed in them by maintaining high standards of discipline, integrity and professionalism.

“Promotion comes with greater responsibilities. I therefore charge you to uphold the highest standards of discipline, integrity, leadership and professionalism in the discharge of your duties,” he added.

Speaking on behalf of the promotees, Mapindi expressed appreciation to the Inspector-General of Police and the Gombe Commissioner for finding them worthy of the promotions.

“We sincerely appreciate the Inspector-General of Police and the Commissioner of Police for finding us worthy of these elevations. We reaffirm our commitment to professionalism and effective service delivery,” he said.

He also acknowledged the contributions of their families, friends, colleagues and well-wishers, saying their support and encouragement had been instrumental to their achievements.

The decoration comes amid other promotion exercises in the Nigeria Police Force.

On November 11, the Inspector-General of Police decorated 29 senior officers promoted to the ranks of Deputy Inspector-General of Police, Assistant Inspector-General of Police and Commissioner of Police.

The IG urged them to demonstrate integrity, accountability and professionalism in their new positions.

title: Tinubu orders immediate release of 3m fertiliser bags for dry-season farming
description:
• Directs NSA to track stocks, protect supply to insecurity-hit communities

President Bola Tinubu has ordered the immediate mobilisation and release of more than three million bags of fertiliser for farmers ahead of the forthcoming dry-season farming season, in a major intervention aimed at reducin
content:
• Directs NSA to track stocks, protect supply to insecurity-hit communities

President Bola Tinubu has ordered the immediate mobilisation and release of more than three million bags of fertiliser for farmers ahead of the forthcoming dry-season farming season, in a major intervention aimed at reducing input costs and boosting food production.

The directive, announced by Vice President Kashim Shettima on Monday, also mandates the Office of the National Security Adviser (ONSA) to verify fertiliser stocks declared by industry operators and ensure that farmers in security-challenged communities are not excluded from the distribution exercise.

According to a issues by his media aide, Stanley Nkwocha, the Vice President gave the directive at a meeting with stakeholders in the fertiliser industry at the Presidential Villa, Abuja, following the President’s approval of funding under the Renewed Hope Agricultural Stabilisation and Productivity Initiative.

The move comes amid concerns over the high cost of agricultural inputs and the underutilisation of Nigeria’s fertiliser blending plants, which the government says have limited domestic production and increased the burden on farmers.

The Vice President said the intervention would stimulate local production, restore jobs and make fertiliser more affordable, while strengthening the country’s food security drive.

He said the Federal Government was determined to revive the country’s fertiliser blending capacity by ensuring that factories resumed production and workers, transporters, warehouse operators and agro-dealers returned to business.

“Today, many of our fertilizer blending plants are operating below capacity at the same time the high cost of fertilizer continues to increase the cost of production for our farmers,” he said.

Shettima stressed that Nigerian farmers remained the primary beneficiaries of the initiative, explaining that the government would purchase fertiliser produced by local blending companies and make it available to them at affordable prices.

“But ultimately the Nigerian farmer is at the centre of this initiative. Under the Renewed Hope Agricultural Stabilisation and Productivity Initiative, government intends to purchase fertilizers produced by Nigerian blenders and make it available to our farmers at affordable prices,” he said.

He charged stakeholders to ensure timely production and efficient distribution ahead of the dry-season farming window.

The Vice President specifically tasked the Office of the National Security Adviser with verifying and tracking fertiliser stocks declared by stakeholders to guarantee transparency and accountability.

He also insisted that farmers in areas affected by insecurity must benefit from the programme, warning against leaving vulnerable and hard-to-reach farming communities behind.

Earlier, the Minister of Budget and Economic Planning, Atiku Bagudu, disclosed that stakeholders had identified approximately 496,000 metric tonnes of fertiliser-related stocks as a starting point for implementing the intervention.

Bagudu said the government would explore additional funding opportunities through existing programmes to sustain the initiative beyond the immediate presidential directive.

President of the Fertiliser Producers and Suppliers Association of Nigeria (FEPSAN), Abubakar Kassim, said the industry had the capacity to make about 3.5 million bags of fertiliser available within the stipulated period.

He disclosed that raw materials already available to FEPSAN members could support the production of approximately 148,000 metric tonnes of NPK 20-10-10 fertiliser, equivalent to about three million bags, within the next few weeks.

Kassim added that members also had about 29,000 metric tonnes of finished NPK fertiliser ready for immediate purchase and distribution.

He said Nigeria had invested considerably in blending plants, warehouses, distribution infrastructure and agro-dealer networks, but many of the facilities were operating below installed capacity.

According to him, reviving the industry would boost fertiliser availability and restore economic activities across production, transportation, storage and distribution.

In a related presentation, a representative of the Ministry of Finance Incorporated (MOFI) disclosed that the organisation had about 90,000 metric tonnes of materials available, with additional supplies in transit bringing the combined volume to approximately 248,000 metric tonnes.

As part of the implementation framework, Tinubu approved the Bank of Agriculture and the Bank of Industry as fund administrators and financial intermediaries for the initiative.

The intervention is part of the administration’s broader agricultural productivity and food security agenda, aimed at strengthening domestic fertiliser production, improving access to essential farm inputs and supporting rural livelihoods.

The post Tinubu orders immediate release of 3m fertiliser bags for dry-season farming appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Delta police, vigilantes storm Edo-Ogwashi forest, kill 2 suspected kidnappers after 3-day hunt
description:
Two suspected kidnappers have met their Waterloo following a fierce gun duel with operatives of the Delta State Police Command in Edo-Ogwashi forest, in Aniocha South Local Government Area of the state.
The operation was carried out on Sunday, 15th November 2026, at about 7:00am by operatives of the
content:
Two suspected kidnappers have met their Waterloo following a fierce gun duel with operatives of the Delta State Police Command in Edo-Ogwashi forest, in Aniocha South Local Government Area of the state.

The operation was carried out on Sunday, 15th November 2026, at about 7:00am by operatives of the Special Anti-Kidnapping Unit (SAKU), Sector III, Ubulu-Uku, in collaboration with a human rights activist and members of the Ubulu-Uku Community Vigilante.

Police Public Relations Officer, SP Edafe Bright in a statement on Monday, said they acted on intelligence after the abduction of a 30-year-old man on 12th November 2026 in Edo-Ogwashi.

Edafe said that the police team trailed the suspects to their hideout in the forest, but on sighting the operatives, the hoodlums reportedly opened fire, leading to a gun duel.

Two of the suspected kidnappers sustained gunshot injuries, while others escaped into the forest. He said that the injured suspects were taken to the hospital where they were confirmed dead by a doctor.

One locally fabricated single-barrel gun, three live cartridges and part of the ransom paid were recovered.

A manhunt for the fleeing suspects is ongoing.

In a separate operation same day at about 3:30pm, operatives of Agbor Division, while conducting a stop-and-search along Baleke Street, Agbor, intercepted one Lucky Rechard, aged 31.

A search of the suspect led to the recovery of one English pistol, one locally made cut-to-size gun and three live cartridges.

The suspect is in custody while investigations continue.

The Commissioner of Police, Delta State Command, CP Samuel E. Erale, commended members of the public for volunteering credible information and appreciated the collaboration of community vigilante groups, civil society organisations and other stakeholders.

He reiterated the importance of community policing and urged citizens to sustain the partnership with the Police for peace and security across the state.

The post Delta police, vigilantes storm Edo-Ogwashi forest, kill 2 suspected kidnappers after 3-day hunt appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Governor Oyebanji Signs Three New Laws
description: Ekiti State Governor, Mr Biodun Oyebanji, on Monday signed three new laws following their passage by the State House of Assembly.The three laws presented to the Governor for assent in his office in Ado-Ekiti by the Speaker of the Ekiti State House of Assembly, Adeoye Aribasoye, are the 2026 Revised
content:
Ekiti State Governor, Mr Biodun Oyebanji, on Monday signed three new laws following their passage by the State House of Assembly.

The three laws presented to the Governor for assent in his office in Ado-Ekiti by the Speaker of the Ekiti State House of Assembly, Adeoye Aribasoye, are the 2026 Revised Appropriation Law; Ekiti State Pension Reform (Second Amendment) Law, 2026 (No. 4 of 2026); and Ekiti State Right of Way Law, 2026 (No. 5 of 2026).

The legislation on the 2026 Revised Appropriation Law retains the state’s total budget size at ₦415,572,070,139.44, while adjusting the allocation between recurrent and capital expenditure.

Under the revised budget, recurrent expenditure increases from ₦221,872,839,071.84 to ₦268,765,546,864.66, while capital expenditure decreases from ₦193,699,231,067.60 to ₦146,806,523,274.78.

The adjustment represents a reallocation of resources from capital expenditure to recurrent expenditure to accommodate the state’s financial and operational obligations without increasing the overall budget size originally approved in December 2025.

The revised appropriation is expected to sustain government operations while maintaining funding for infrastructure, social development, economic growth, and institutional efficiency.

The Ekiti State Pension Reform (Second Amendment) Law, 2026 is an amendment of the existing Pension Reform Law No. 3 of 2022 to formally accommodate the designation of a Director-General alongside the Permanent Secretary in the administrative and governance structure of the Commission responsible for the Contributory Pension Scheme in the state.

The amendment also makes consequential adjustments to relevant provisions of the principal law, including the composition of the Commission’s Board, staff administration, remuneration and allowances, among others.

The Ekiti State Right of Way Law, 2026, establishes a regulatory framework for the approval and administration of permits for the installation and maintenance of telecommunications infrastructure in the state.

The legislation fixes the maximum Right of Way fee at ₦145 per linear metre for ducts and cables and ₦700,000 per site for a Base Transceiver Station.

It also requires telecommunications operators to comply with approved engineering standards, protect public safety and the environment, minimise damage to roads and public utilities, and restore affected infrastructure after installation.

The three laws are aimed at strengthening public institutions, improving the regulatory environment for infrastructure development, and ensuring effective management of public resources in the interest of the people.

The governorship candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement in Oyo State, Bimbo Adekanmbi, has promised to sustain the development of Ladoke Akintola University of Technology, Ogbomoso, if elected governor.
Adekanmbi gave the assurance on Monday during his campaign visit to the institution, where he a
content:
The governorship candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement in Oyo State, Bimbo Adekanmbi, has promised to sustain the development of Ladoke Akintola University of Technology, Ogbomoso, if elected governor.

Adekanmbi gave the assurance on Monday during his campaign visit to the institution, where he addressed students and urged them to support candidates of the party in the forthcoming elections.

In a statement issued by the Director of Communication and Spokesperson of the APM Campaign Council, Yinka Oladoyinbo, the candidate said his administration would implement policies and programmes to support students and make their aspirations achievable.

He said the development recorded by the university under the administration of Governor Seyi Makinde would be sustained by an APM government.

“All the demands that you have put forward will be looked into and implemented because the present administration and the one we plan to run believe in your ability to contribute to the development of the state.

“As undergraduates, you have a future that can be looked forward to, and we, as a government, will support you to achieve your dreams and make your plans for the future achievable.

“However, if you say you love us and love our party, you have to love us with your votes; you have to vote for us to sustain the development that this institution has been witnessing in the last seven years,” he said.

Also addressing the students, the party’s deputy governorship candidate, Muftau Salawu, who is from Ogbomoso, appealed to them to vote for Adekanmbi and other APM candidates.

The party’s Oyo North senatorial candidate, Shina Abiola Peller, an alumnus of the university, said the forthcoming election offered students an opportunity to have one of their own represent them in the Senate.

Peller urged the students to mobilise support for Adekanmbi, saying an APM administration would sustain the development recorded under Makinde’s Omituntun 1.0 and 2.0 programmes.

He also called for collective efforts to address the country’s challenges and shape a better future for coming generations.

title: Gunmen kill Operation Rainbow commander, one other in Plateau
description:
By Golok Nanmwa



Suspected gunmen have killed a newly graduated unit commander of the Plateau State-owned civilian security outfit, Operation Rainbow, and another person in an ambush in Bokkos Local Government Area of Plateau State.



The victims were reportedly killed at about 3pm on Monday whil
content:
By Golok Nanmwa

Suspected gunmen have killed a newly graduated unit commander of the Plateau State-owned civilian security outfit, Operation Rainbow, and another person in an ambush in Bokkos Local Government Area of Plateau State.

The victims were reportedly killed at about 3pm on Monday while returning from a condolence visit to Hurti village to their community in Tadai, Manguna District of Bokkos Local Government Area.

The community leader, Machief Paul, who confirmed the incident to newsmen, said both victims were members of his community.

He said, “They are all members of my community. They went to Hurti village for a condolence visit and were returning to Tadai when suspected gunmen ambushed and killed them.

“They were killed in broad daylight this afternoon. It is very sad and unfortunate.”

Paul disclosed that one of the deceased was a newly graduated commander of Operation Rainbow, adding that the killing had thrown the community into mourning.

He said, “The commander had just graduated. We are deeply saddened by this incident, especially given the security challenges our people have continued to face.”

Also confirming the incident, an award-winning Nigerian conflict reporter from Bokkos, Masara Kim, said the two men were killed in the ambush while returning from the condolence visit.

The deceased Operation Rainbow commander was said to have recently completed a refresher training programme for unit commanders in Jos, Kim added.

Efforts to obtain further details from security authorities were unsuccessful as of the time of filing this report.

The post Gunmen kill Operation Rainbow commander, one other in Plateau appeared first on Vanguard News.
