title: Seven things to know about the next James Bond film
description:
British actor Robert Pattinson has been announced as the next James Bond, taking over the iconic role previously played by Daniel Craig in the long-running film franchise.
Amazon MGM Studios announced Pattinson’s casting on Monday, November 16, 2026, in a statement published on its official website.
content:
British actor Robert Pattinson has been announced as the next James Bond, taking over the iconic role previously played by Daniel Craig in the long-running film franchise.

Amazon MGM Studios announced Pattinson’s casting on Monday, November 16, 2026, in a statement published on its official website.

The announcement was also confirmed on the official James Bond social media accounts on Instagram and X, as verified by our correspondent.

The upcoming film will be directed by Denis Villeneuve, with Steven Knight writing the screenplay. Amy Pascal and David Heyman will serve as producers, while Tanya Lapointe will be executive producer.

Pattinson described his appointment as the honour of a lifetime, while the studio said his casting marked a new chapter for the franchise.

Following the announcement, here are seven things to know about the upcoming James Bond film, as curated in a separate release on the MGM website on Monday.

1. Robert Pattinson takes over as James Bond

Pattinson has been officially cast as the next actor to portray James Bond, the fictional British secret agent also known as 007.

The actor, whose career spans more than two decades, has appeared in independent films and major studio productions, including The Twilight Saga, Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire, Tenet, The Lighthouse, Mickey 17 and The Batman.

He also starred in A24’s The Drama and Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey in 2026.

Reacting to his appointment, Pattinson said, “James Bond is one of the most legendary characters in cinema, and to be entrusted with 007 is the honour of a lifetime. I’m deeply grateful to Denis, Amy, David, Tanya, and everyone at Amazon MGM Studios for their belief in me. To say this role is a dream come true is an understatement. I couldn’t be more excited about this partnership and the work ahead with this fantastic team.”

2. Denis Villeneuve to direct the film

Canadian filmmaker Denis Villeneuve will direct the upcoming James Bond production.

Villeneuve is known for directing films including Dune, Blade Runner 2049, Arrival, Sicario, Prisoners, Enemy and Incendies.

Amazon MGM Studios announced his appointment as director on June 25, 2025, alongside the announcement that Tanya Lapointe would serve as executive producer.

Speaking about taking on the project, Villeneuve said: “Some of my earliest movie-going memories are connected to 007. I grew up watching James Bond films with my father, ever since Dr. No with Sean Connery. I’m a die-hard Bond fan. To me, he’s sacred territory. I intend to honor the tradition and open the path for many new missions to come.

“This is a massive responsibility, but also incredibly exciting for me and a huge honor. Amy, David, and I are absolutely thrilled to bring him back to the screen. Thank you to Amazon MGM Studios for their trust.”

3. Peaky Blinders creator Steven Knight writes the screenplay

Steven Knight, the creator of the television series Peaky Blinders, is writing the screenplay for the upcoming James Bond film.

Amazon MGM Studios announced his appointment on July 31, 2025.

The British screenwriter, producer and director is also known for creating Taboo, SAS: Rogue Heroes, See and A Thousand Blows.

His film credits include Dirty Pretty Things, Eastern Promises, Spencer, Hummingbird, Locke and Serenity.

Knight also co-created the international television game show Who Wants to Be a Millionaire?

4. Spider-Man and Harry Potter producers join the project

Amy Pascal and David Heyman will produce the upcoming film through their respective production companies, Pascal Pictures and Heyday Films.

Amazon MGM Studios announced their appointment on March 25, 2025.

Pascal is known for her work on the Spider-Man franchise, including the four films starring Tom Holland and the three animated Spider-Verse productions.

Her other production credits include Project Hail Mary, Challengers and Spider-Noir.

Heyman, on the other hand, produced all eight film adaptations of J.K. Rowling’s Harry Potter books, as well as the three Fantastic Beasts films.

His other credits include Once Upon a Time… in Hollywood, Marriage Story, Gravity and Barbie.

5. Tanya Lapointe named executive producer

Tanya Lapointe will serve as executive producer of the upcoming James Bond film.

Her appointment was announced by Amazon MGM Studios on June 25, 2025, alongside Villeneuve’s selection as director.

Lapointe is known for her work with Villeneuve, including their collaboration on the Dune films.

Amazon MGM Studios also named her as executive producer in its November 16, 2026 announcement confirming Pattinson’s casting.

6. Amazon MGM Studios has creative control of James Bond

Amazon MGM Studios’ involvement in the franchise follows its acquisition of MGM in 2022, which brought a catalogue of more than 4,000 films and 17,000 television shows under its ownership.

In March 2025, Amazon MGM Studios concluded a new joint venture with Barbara Broccoli and Michael G. Wilson, under which the studio gained creative control of the James Bond intellectual property rights.

The arrangement gave Amazon MGM Studios control over the creative direction of the franchise.

7. All 25 previous James Bond films are on Prime Video

Amazon says all 25 previous official James Bond films are streaming on Prime Video worldwide.

The collection features the different actors who have portrayed the British secret agent over the decades, including Sean Connery, George Lazenby, Roger Moore, Timothy Dalton, Pierce Brosnan and Daniel Craig.

Pattinson’s appointment makes him the next actor to take on the role in the official film series, following Craig’s final appearance in No Time to Die, released in 2021.

The post Seven things to know about the next James Bond film appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: GTA 6 hacker pleads guilty to cybercrimes after hospital release
description:
A hacker who stole dozens of unfinished clips of Grand Theft Auto 6 and attempted to extort the game’s developers has pleaded guilty to a series of cybercrimes after being released from a secure hospital.
Arion Kurtaj, 21, from Oxford, United Kingdom, pleaded guilty on Monday at Woolwich Crown Court
content:
A hacker who stole dozens of unfinished clips of Grand Theft Auto 6 and attempted to extort the game’s developers has pleaded guilty to a series of cybercrimes after being released from a secure hospital.

Arion Kurtaj, 21, from Oxford, United Kingdom, pleaded guilty on Monday at Woolwich Crown Court to hacking Rockstar Games in 2022 and several other offences committed when he was 16 and 17 years old as a member of the hacking group Lapsus$`.

According to the BBC on Monday, Kurtaj was initially sentenced to an indefinite stay in a secure hospital because of the severity of his autism. However, following a routine assessment late last year, he was deemed fit to stand trial and transferred to a normal prison in January.

Kurtaj hacked Rockstar Games while on bail for multiple other hacking offences and under police protection.

He was staying at a Travelodge hotel in Bicester, where he had been accommodated to protect him from rival hackers who had threatened to attack him over his stolen Bitcoin holdings.

With his computer confiscated, Kurtaj carried out the attack using an Amazon Fire Stick connected to his hotel television, alongside a Bluetooth keyboard and mouse.

He stole internal company data, including 90 clips showing nearly 60 minutes of gameplay from the unfinished Grand Theft Auto 6.

He subsequently accessed the company’s internal Slack messaging system and issued an ultimatum, declaring: “If Rockstar does not contact me on Telegram within 24 hours I will start releasing the source code.”

When the company refused to cooperate, he published the clips and source code on an online forum using the username TeaPotUberHacker.

Rockstar Games said the breach cost the company `$5m (£3.79m) to recover from, in addition to thousands of hours of staff time.

The company also said the hack exposed for the first time that one of the game’s playable characters was a woman, a detail it had been closely guarding for marketing purposes.

Kurtaj was initially considered unfit to stand a traditional trial because of the severity of his autism and was instead subjected to what is known as a trial of the facts.

Under the procedure, the jury was required to determine whether he committed the alleged acts rather than whether he did so with criminal intent.

In December 2023, the court ruled that he would remain in a secure hospital indefinitely unless doctors determined that he was no longer a danger.

However, a routine assessment late last year found him fit to face a criminal trial, which was scheduled to take place at Woolwich Crown Court.

Kurtaj subsequently pleaded guilty to all the offences.

The BBC reported that he appeared in court with short hair and an unkempt beard, wearing a suit and buttoned-up white shirt without a tie.

He reportedly blinked frequently during the hearing and stood to confirm his identity before entering his guilty pleas without visible emotion.

Other companies targeted

The offences to which Kurtaj pleaded guilty also included cyberattacks on BT/EE, Revolut and Uber, where he used social engineering techniques to gain access to internal systems.

The court heard that during his attack on Uber, he posted a picture of a penis as part of his attempts to force the company to pay a ransom.

His attacks on the companies were estimated to have caused about £10m in damage.

Using data stolen from the firms, Kurtaj and other members of Lapsus$` also targeted cryptocurrency investors.

The prosecution argued that the group stole at least `$300,000 from individual victims.

Kurtaj also admitted physically assaulting workers while in custody, including multiple biting incidents.

While in prison, he was caught with a mobile phone after sending a taunting text message to police and posting updates on Snapchat.

He will be sentenced at a later date.

The prosecution described Kurtaj as a “leading light” in the teenage hacking group Lapsus$`.

Lapsus`$ member jailed for five years

Another member of the group, who was 17 at the time, was found guilty at Southwark Crown Court during Kurtaj’s original trial in 2023.

The teenager, whose identity could not be disclosed at the time because of his age, received an 18-month Youth Rehabilitation Order, including intensive supervision and a ban on using virtual private networks online.

Earlier in 2026, the same hacker, identified as Thalha Jubair, was sentenced to five years and six months in prison after continuing his cybercrime activities with another group known as Scattered Spider.

Among the victims of the group’s subsequent activities was Transport for London, which suffered a disruptive cyberattack that caused an estimated £39m in damage and significant disruption within the organisation.

The post GTA 6 hacker pleads guilty to cybercrimes after hospital release appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Agbara Nla hits N513m, sets faith-based film record
description:
Faith-based film, ‘Agbara Nla: The Return,’ has grossed over N513.4m at the Nigerian box office, becoming the second highest-grossing Nollywood title of 2026.
The film also emerged as the highest-grossing faith-based title of all time and the ninth highest-grossing Nollywood title ever.
The distribu
content:
Faith-based film, ‘Agbara Nla: The Return,’ has grossed over N513.4m at the Nigerian box office, becoming the second highest-grossing Nollywood title of 2026.

The film also emerged as the highest-grossing faith-based title of all time and the ninth highest-grossing Nollywood title ever.

The distributor, Nile Entertainment, announced the milestone on Monday in an Instagram post, stating that the film had grossed over N513.4m in Nigeria.

“Agbara Nla: The Return is now the second highest-grossing Nollywood title of 2026, the highest-grossing faith-based film of all time and the 9th highest-grossing Nollywood title ever,” the distributor said.

The distributor added, “We’re proud to celebrate this moment with everyone who made it happen.”

The distributor had earlier described the film’s opening as the biggest non-December Nollywood opening weekend, the biggest October opening weekend and the biggest opening weekend for a faith-based film.

The film, a remake of the 1993 Christian production created by filmmaker Mike Bamiloye, returned to cinemas on October 1, 2026, more than three decades after the original was released.

The new production was directed by Bamiloye’s sons, Damilola Mike-Bamiloye and Joshua “Jay Mikee” Mike-Bamiloye.

The distributor also said the film’s single-day preview earnings had surpassed N71m.

Agbara Nla: The Return is a modern reimagining of the original film, which was later released in English as The Ultimate Power in 1994.

The story follows Muwonleru, a village controlled by a powerful herbalist, Isawuru, as two believers, Olaboye and Olatomi, leave their city lives to take the Christian message to the community, leading to a conflict between their faith and Isawuru’s spiritual power.

Mike Bamiloye reprises his role as Isawuru, while the cast also includes Aanu Kolade Abiodun, Remilekun Mosiko, Philip Olubakin, Gloria Mike-Bamiloye and David Kola Okeowo.

title: Beyoncé becomes first artiste to earn 100 Grammy nominations
description:
Beyoncé has become the first artist in Grammy history to receive 100 career nominations after earning a nod at the 2027 Grammy Awards.
The singer reached the milestone on Monday following the announcement of nominees for the 69th Annual Grammy Awards, with her song, “Morning Dew (Donk),” nominated i
content:
Beyoncé has become the first artist in Grammy history to receive 100 career nominations after earning a nod at the 2027 Grammy Awards.

The singer reached the milestone on Monday following the announcement of nominees for the 69th Annual Grammy Awards, with her song, “Morning Dew (Donk),” nominated in the Best R&B Solo Performance category.

The latest nomination takes her career tally to 100, extending her record as the most-nominated artist in the history of the awards.

Despite receiving only one nomination for the 2027 edition, Beyoncé remains the most-awarded artist in Grammy history, with 35 wins.

“Morning Dew (Donk)” is among the nominees alongside “Out the Window” by Kehlani, “Let Me” by Victoria Monét, “Pressha” by Jill Scott and “What You Need” by Nigerian singer Tems.

The nomination adds another milestone to Beyoncé’s Grammy record, having previously received 11 nominations for her album, Cowboy Carter, at the 2025 ceremony.

The 69th Annual Grammy Awards will hold on February 7, 2027, at the Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles, United States.

title: Ekiti gov signs revised N415.6bn budget, pension, telecoms laws
description:
Ekiti State Governor, Mr Biodun Oyebanji, on Monday signed three new laws following their passage by the State House of Assembly.
The three laws presented to the governor for assent in his office in Ado-Ekiti by the Speaker, Ekiti State House of Assembly, Adeoye Aribasoye, are the 2026 Revised Appro
content:
Ekiti State Governor, Mr Biodun Oyebanji, on Monday signed three new laws following their passage by the State House of Assembly.

The three laws presented to the governor for assent in his office in Ado-Ekiti by the Speaker, Ekiti State House of Assembly, Adeoye Aribasoye, are the 2026 Revised Appropriation Law; Ekiti State Pension Reform (Second Amendment) Law, 2026 (No. 4 of 2026); and Ekiti State Right of Way Law, 2026 (No. 5 of 2026).

The Special Adviser to the Governor on Media, Yinka Oyebode, said in a statement in Ado Ekiti, “The signing of the three laws underscores the Oyebanji administration’s commitment to strengthening public institutions, improving the regulatory environment for infrastructure development and ensuring effective management of public resources in the interest of the people”.

According to the statement, the legislation on the 2026 Revised Appropriation Law retains the state’s total budget size at ₦415,572,070,139.44, while adjusting the allocation between recurrent and capital expenditure. Under the revised budget, recurrent expenditure increases from ₦221,872,839,071.84 to ₦268,765,546,864.66, while capital expenditure decreases from ₦193,699,231,067.60 to ₦146,806,523,274.78.

It stated, “The adjustment represents a reallocation of resources from capital expenditure to recurrent expenditure to accommodate the state’s financial and operational obligations without increasing the overall budget size originally approved in December 2025.

“The revised appropriation is expected to sustain government operations while maintaining funding for infrastructure, social development, economic growth and institutional efficiency,” Oyebode stated.

He added that the Ekiti State Pension Reform (Second Amendment) Law, 2026 “is an amendment of the existing Pension Reform Law No. 3 of 2022 to formally accommodate the designation of a Director-General alongside the Permanent Secretary in the administrative and governance structure of the Commission responsible for the Contributory Pension Scheme in the state.

“The amendment also makes consequential adjustments to relevant provisions of the principal law, including the composition of the Commission’s Board, staff administration, remuneration and allowances among others,” he said.

He added that the Ekiti State Right of Way Law, 2026, established a regulatory framework for the approval and administration of permits for the installation and maintenance of telecommunications infrastructure in the state.

Oyebode stated, “The legislation fixes the maximum Right of Way fee at ₦145 per linear metre for ducts and cables and ₦700,000 per site for a Base Transceiver Station.

“It also requires telecommunications operators to comply with approved engineering standards, protect public safety and the environment, minimise damage to roads and public utilities, and restore affected infrastructure after installation.”

title: Two mass shootings claim 17 lives in South Africa
description:
By Juliet Umeh, Agency Report



At least 17 people have been killed in two separate mass shootings in South Africa, with police yet to establish the motives behind the attacks, which occurred about 530 kilometres apart on Sunday.



Eight people were found dead inside a bullet-riddled vehicle in Sw
content:
By Juliet Umeh, Agency Report

At least 17 people have been killed in two separate mass shootings in South Africa, with police yet to establish the motives behind the attacks, which occurred about 530 kilometres apart on Sunday.

Eight people were found dead inside a bullet-riddled vehicle in Sweetwaters, outside Pietermaritzburg, while nine others were killed in a shack in Jeffsville, near the capital, Pretoria.

Police spokesperson, Robert Netshiunda, said the identities of the eight victims in Sweetwaters were yet to be confirmed, although some families had approached authorities to assist.

“It’s still too early to tell what the motive could have been and who could be behind the shooting because we are yet to identify the victims,” he said.

In Jeffsville, six males and three females were found with gunshot wounds inside a four-room shack. Police spokesperson, Brenda Muridili, said officers were alerted at about 7:30 a.m. on Monday, although the shooting reportedly occurred between 10 p.m. and 11 p.m. on Sunday.

No arrests had been made as investigations continued.

Gauteng Police Commissioner, Tommy Mthombeni, said the killings could be linked to a shooting in nearby Saulsville last year, which claimed 12 lives and left 13 others injured.

He disclosed that one of Sunday’s victims was a person of interest in the previous attack, adding that police could not rule out retaliation.

South Africa has recorded several deadly mass shootings in the past year. In September, 11 people, including a pregnant woman, were killed in an attack on a house near Durban, while another shooting at a tavern claimed 17 lives.

Two separate shootings in Johannesburg in June also left 24 people dead, with police linking one to rival illegal mining gangs.

Two other mass shootings in December last year claimed 21 lives.

Police investigations into Sunday’s attacks are ongoing.

The post Two mass shootings claim 17 lives in South Africa appeared first on Vanguard News.

content:
By Elizabeth Adegbesan

Nigeria’s headline inflation rate declined to 14.06 per cent in October 2026 from 14.63 per cent recorded in September, the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) has said.

The NBS disclosed this in its latest Consumer Price Index (CPI) report released on Monday, also showing a decline in food inflation to 19.13 per cent in October from 19.59 per cent in the preceding month.

According to the report, headline inflation stood at 18.97 per cent in October 2025, indicating a 4.91 percentage-point decline in the annual rate between October 2025 and October 2026.

The statistics agency, however, reported an increase in the month-on-month headline inflation rate, which rose to 0.43 per cent in October from 0.06 per cent in September.

It explained that the development indicated that the average price level increased at a faster rate in October than in the preceding month.

“In October 2026, the Headline inflation rate stood at 14.06%, down from 14.63% in September 2026 and stood at 18.97% in the same month of the preceding year (October 2025),” the NBS stated.

The report added that the October 2026 headline inflation rate represented a 4.91 percentage-point decline compared with the corresponding period of the previous year.

“On a month-on-month basis, the Headline inflation rate in October 2026 was 0.43%, which was 0.38% higher than the rate recorded in September 2026 (0.06%).

“This means that in October 2026, the rate of increase in the average price level was higher than the rate of increase in the average price level in September 2026,” the agency said.

title: INEC disowns ‘staff’ behind report of partisan recruitment in Edo
description:
The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) in Edo has disowned the author of a viral video, claiming to have recruited ad-hoc personnel for the commission and directing them to work for a particular political interest.



In a statement issued on Monday in Benin by the commission’s Head of
content:
The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) in Edo has disowned the author of a viral video, claiming to have recruited ad-hoc personnel for the commission and directing them to work for a particular political interest.

In a statement issued on Monday in Benin by the commission’s Head of Voter Education and Publicity, Mr Samuel Sunday, on behalf of the Resident Electoral Commissioner, the commission stated that the man was not its staff member.

“INEC Edo declares that no one named Osayi Israel Omoroduwa is among its staff in Edo, and that no one has the power or access to recruit ad-hoc staff for the commission,” Sunday explained.

He further explained that the recruitment of ad-hoc personnel was conducted exclusively through the online INECPRES platform, administered by INEC Headquarters.

“The path to being an ad-hoc staff of INEC is by online application through the INECPRES platform and whoever has internet access can do so by themselves or support others so qualified to apply,” he added.

He emphasised that staff members in its state offices could not influence the recruitment process, adding that the person named in the video had no special access to the platform.

According to Sunday, successful applicants will undergo scrutiny by the commission and receive training on the conduct and ethics of elections.

The INEC Spokesman described the online video as “an irresponsible and targeted attack” on the commission and its processes.

He argued that the video was intended to undermine public confidence in the electoral process through misinformation.

He, however, reaffirmed the commitment of the commission to conducting credible elections and urged the public to disregard what it described as “falsehood contained in the video”. (NAN)

title: Two killed, 30 inmates escape from Chad prison break
description:
Two people have been killed and 30 inmates escaped after a prison break at a correctional facility in Mongo, the capital of Chad’s Guéra Province.
The Agence de Presse Africaine (APA) reported on Monday, November 16, 2026, that the incident also left three people seriously injured, destroyed several
content:
Two people have been killed and 30 inmates escaped after a prison break at a correctional facility in Mongo, the capital of Chad’s Guéra Province.

The Agence de Presse Africaine (APA) reported on Monday, November 16, 2026, that the incident also left three people seriously injured, destroyed several prison offices and resulted in the loss of inmates’ records and other facilities.

According to APA, which cited the provincial government delegate and the prosecutor general of the Mongo Court of Appeal, Djouma Mahamadene, six offices were set ablaze during the incident.

The affected offices included the prison director’s office, secretariat and security offices.

The prison pharmacy and storage facilities were also ransacked, leading to the destruction of medicines.

Other items reportedly lost included 25 cartons of utensils, 100 mosquito nets recently donated by UNICEF and sewing machines.

The destruction of the prison’s admission and release registers was also reported, raising concerns about the loss of official records.

A headcount conducted after the incident found 476 inmates out of the prison’s recorded population of 510, while authorities confirmed that 30 prisoners had escaped.

The government delegate in Guéra Province, Abdoulaye Ibrahim Siam, confirmed the escape to Agence France-Presse (AFP), saying security forces were searching for the fleeing inmates.

“We count 30 prisoners who escaped. The forces of order and justice are on their tail,” he told AFP.

The sub-prefect of Mongo, Ahmat Tagal, also told AFP that security operatives had recaptured about 22 other inmates who attempted to escape.

The latest incident is the second major prison break at the facility in less than two years.

In April 2025, more than 100 inmates escaped from the same prison during a deadly shoot-out that left three people dead and three others injured, including the provincial governor, according to a PUNCH report published on April 20, 2025.

The report, based on an AFP account, said the breakout followed an uprising at the high-security penitentiary, located about five kilometres from Mongo.

A local official told AFP that some inmates broke into a manager’s office to steal firearms, triggering a shoot-out with prison guards.

“A shootout with guards ensued, at the same time the governor arrived. He was wounded,” the official said.

Hassan Souleymane Adam, the secretary-general of Guéra Province, had put the number of escapees at about 100, while another Mongo official estimated that 132 inmates fled.

The local official also said the prisoners revolted over complaints about a lack of food.

The November 15 incident marks another deadly security breach at the correctional facility, which had a recorded population of 510 inmates before the latest escape.

title: 2027: Showunmi urges Ribadu to check inflammatory political statements
description:
A chieftain of The Alternative, Otunba Segun Showunmi, has called on the National Security Adviser, Nuhu Ribadu, to establish clear standards for political conduct and ensure that anyone whose actions threaten national security is held accountable, regardless of political affiliation.
Showunmi made
content:
A chieftain of The Alternative, Otunba Segun Showunmi, has called on the National Security Adviser, Nuhu Ribadu, to establish clear standards for political conduct and ensure that anyone whose actions threaten national security is held accountable, regardless of political affiliation.

Showunmi made the appeal in an open letter to Ribadu, warning that inflammatory remarks, ethnic and religious insinuations, threats and the use of sensitive national issues for political gains could aggravate Nigeria’s security challenges.

He argued that the country was already dealing with several security concerns and should not allow political rivalries, personal ambitions and partisan disagreements to create further instability.

“There is a difference between robust political engagement and conduct that deliberately or recklessly threatens public peace. There is a difference between criticising government and deliberately inciting citizens against one another,” he wrote.

The political figure expressed concern over what he described as the increasing acceptance of provocative statements and irresponsible communication by politicians, their supporters and other influential individuals.

He maintained that holding public office, having political influence or maintaining close relationships with powerful figures should not protect anyone from the consequences of unlawful conduct.

“National security cannot be held hostage to political ambition,” he said, stressing that democratic participation did not give anyone the right to incite violence, threaten citizens or encourage lawlessness.

Showunmi urged the NSA to collaborate with security and law-enforcement agencies to develop and communicate clear guidelines for political communication, particularly as political activities intensify ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Among the measures he proposed were impartial enforcement of the law, a coordinated approach to political misinformation and incitement, and greater accountability within political parties.

He also recommended establishing a rapid-response mechanism to document incidents, verify information, counter false narratives and investigate fabricated reports deliberately circulated to provoke violence.

On the responsibility of political parties, Showunmi said their leadership should be held accountable for the conduct of individuals operating under their platforms or acting on their behalf.

He further called on security agencies to respond promptly when credible threats, organised intimidation or incitement pose identifiable risks to public safety rather than waiting for violence to occur.

He insisted that investigations and prosecutions must be based on credible evidence, due process and established legal standards, irrespective of the political status of those involved.

Showunmi clarified that his appeal was not aimed at restricting opposition activities, legitimate criticism or peaceful protests, maintaining that democracy must allow dissent and competing political opinions.

However, he warned against individuals exploiting democratic freedoms to undermine national stability.

“We cannot continue to behave as though national security is the exclusive responsibility of soldiers, policemen, intelligence officers and other security operatives.

“Political actors also have a responsibility to preserve the environment in which democracy can function,” he said.

He urged Ribadu to make it clear that political position, financial influence or personal connections would not shield anyone from legitimate investigation.

“We must not wait for an avoidable national tragedy before demonstrating the seriousness of our institutions. We must not allow reckless political behaviour to become the trigger for security emergencies that could have been prevented,” he added.

Showunmi also copied President Bola Tinubu, Minister of Defence Christopher Musa, the President’s Special Adviser on Homeland Security, Adeyinka Famadewa, Inspector-General of Police Tunji Disu, Director-General of the Department of State Services Oluwatosin Ajayi, and Minister of State for Defence Bello Matawalle in the letter.

title: NASS Announces Approval Of 36 Houses Of Assembly For State Police Bill
description: All 36 State Houses of Assembly have approved the proposed constitutional amendment to establish state police, clearing the way for the bill to be transmitted to President Bola Tinubu for assent.The Clerk to the National Assembly, Kamoru Ogunlana, announced the endorsement in a statement on Monday,
content:
All 36 State Houses of Assembly have approved the proposed constitutional amendment to establish state police, clearing the way for the bill to be transmitted to President Bola Tinubu for assent.

The Clerk to the National Assembly, Kamoru Ogunlana, announced the endorsement in a statement on Monday, describing it as 100 per cent approval by the state legislatures.

The approval exceeds the constitutional requirement of at least 24 state assemblies under Section 9(2) of the 1999 Constitution, as amended.

“The Clerk to the National Assembly wishes to announce that all the thirty-six (36) State Houses of Assembly have approved ‘A Bill for an Act to Alter the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 to Provide for the Establishment of State Police Services and for related Matters’.

“This represents one hundred percent (100%) endorsement by the State Houses of Assembly which exceeds the threshold of twenty-four (24), provided under Section 9(2) of the Constitution (as amended),” said Ogunlana.

The development marks the completion of the state assemblies’ consideration of the proposed amendment, following weeks of legislative engagement over the establishment of state police.

The National Assembly had, on November 3, announced that 28 state assemblies had approved the bill, exceeding the required two-thirds threshold.

The Clerk had said the legislative process would continue to receive approvals from the remaining states before the bill was transmitted to the President.

A day later, the Senate gave the six outstanding state assemblies until November 15 to communicate their decisions, after Senate Leader Opeyemi Bamidele disclosed that 30 states had endorsed the proposal.

In the latest statement, Ogunlana explained that although the bill had already met the constitutional and administrative requirements for transmission, the National Assembly leadership delayed the process to allow for broader consultations and consensus among the states.

“It is important to note that the Bill had long satisfied all the constitutional and administrative requirements for transmission as prescribed by the Constitution and the Acts Authentication Act Cap. A2, Laws of the Federation of Nigeria, 2004, but the Leadership of the National Assembly directed a brief delay of transmission to allow for broader national consensus and engagement of all the States of the Federation,” he said.

He described the “unanimous endorsement” as an unprecedented demonstration of cooperation among the different levels of government.

“The unanimous endorsement of the Bill is an unprecedented demonstration of synergy between the National Assembly and the State Houses of Assembly, as well as constructive cooperation between Executive Arms of government at both Federal and State levels,” he added.

The Clerk further said his office had completed the verification process and that the bill was now ready for transmission to the President for assent.

“Following the completion of the verification process by my Office, the Bill is set for transmission to the President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, for His Excellency’s assent,” he said.

Ogunlana added that the development would provide a foundation for the National Assembly to advance other proposed constitutional amendments.

“This achievement serves as a foundation for the National Assembly to complete and transmit the other Sixth Constitution Alteration Bills to the State Houses of Assembly for their consideration as soon as possible.”

The National Assembly had earlier transmitted the state police amendment to the 36 state legislatures for consideration as part of the ongoing review of the 1999 Constitution.

The proposed amendment seeks to provide the constitutional basis for the establishment of state police services alongside the existing federal policing structure.

The Clerk commended the 36 state governors, speakers and members of the state assemblies, as well as other stakeholders, for their cooperation in the process.

The post NASS Announces Approval Of 36 Houses Of Assembly For State Police Bill appeared first on Channels Television.

title: We blocked channels used to siphon Abia funds — Otti
description:
Governor attributes poor roads, dirty environment to alleged diversion of public resources



By Steve Oko



UMUAHIA — Abia State Governor, Dr Alex Otti, has attributed the infrastructural and environmental challenges inherited by his administration to the alleged diversion of public resources by s
content:
Governor attributes poor roads, dirty environment to alleged diversion of public resources

By Steve Oko

UMUAHIA — Abia State Governor, Dr Alex Otti, has attributed the infrastructural and environmental challenges inherited by his administration to the alleged diversion of public resources by some politicians in the state.

Otti said his administration had blocked entrenched channels through which public funds were allegedly siphoned, describing the former system as a political feeding bottle.

The governor, who spoke at a two-day crusade organised by the Lord’s Chosen Charismatic Renewal Ministries at Ogbonnaya Onu Polytechnic, Aba, said those criticising his administration were unhappy because they could no longer access public resources through the alleged channels.

“Why they are murmuring is that we removed the feeding bottle from their mouths. And that feeding bottle was what they used to siphon all our resources. That was why there were no good roads and everywhere was dirty,” he said.

Otti maintained that his administration would not reverse course despite criticisms, insisting that blocking access to public resources by vested interests was necessary to redirect government funds towards development.

He cited road rehabilitation, improved environmental sanitation and drainage infrastructure in Aba as evidence of the changes recorded under his administration.

According to him, the city has witnessed significant improvement in flood control, with floodwaters no longer lingering after heavy rainfall as they reportedly did in previous years.

“Before now, there were no good roads, everywhere was dirty, the gutters were blocked, and whenever it rained, the entire place became flooded.

“But I am sure that those of you living in Aba can testify that, despite the heavy rains this year, floodwaters no longer remain for long after the rains,” he said.

Promises consolidation after rescue phase

Looking ahead, Otti said the achievements recorded in the past three and a half years represented only the beginning of his administration’s efforts to reposition the state.

He promised that the next four and a half years would focus on consolidating the gains already recorded.

“What we have done in three and a half years is just the beginning of the rescue. The next four and a half years will be serious consolidation,” he declared.

The governor also announced plans to improve facilities for future large-scale crusades organised by the ministry following concerns over the exposure of worshippers to the scorching sun at the polytechnic venue.

He disclosed that he had directed the Commissioner for Youth and Sports Development to ensure that subsequent major gatherings by the ministry were held at the stadium.

Otti also offered to personally bear the cost of hiring the facility as his contribution to the ministry.

“I have instructed the Honourable Commissioner for Youth and Sports Development that whenever you are having an event like this again, it should be held at the stadium. I know that using the stadium costs money, but I will pay. That will be my own contribution to the ministry,” he said.

He added that the stadium could accommodate about 15,000 worshippers and promised to liaise with the General Overseer ahead of future programmes to ensure adequate arrangements.

‘I didn’t come here to campaign’

Otti explained that his presence at the crusade was not politically motivated but was to fulfil a promise he made to the General Overseer, Pastor Lazarus Muoka, during their recent meeting in Lagos.

He, however, made a light-hearted political remark, saying there was no need to campaign at the gathering because the worshippers would naturally support him.

“Why we can’t campaign here is that we already have all your votes,” the governor said.

He thanked Muoka for his visit, prayers and spiritual support, assuring him of his administration’s continued partnership with the ministry.

Otti also prayed for the growth of the church and God’s continued strengthening of its leadership and members.

Earlier, Muoka had charged Christians to demonstrate genuine obedience to God by doing what He commands and refraining from whatever He forbids.

He described obedience as fundamental to victorious Christian living, urging believers to guard their hearts, exercise self-discipline and resist temptations capable of compromising their faith.

Muoka called on Christians to remain steadfast in God’s word and take divine instructions seriously.

Top government officials accompanied the governor to the crusade.

title: Amosun, Ndume decry leadership failure, hail founding fathers
description: Former Ogun State Governor, Senator Ibikunle Amosun, and former Senate Chief Whip, Senator Ali Ndume, have paid glowing tributes to Nigeria’s founding fathers, describing the late Dr Nnamdi Azikiwe, Chief Obafemi Awolowo and Sir Ahmadu Bello as selfless leaders whose legacies remain a benchmark for
content:
Former Ogun State Governor, Senator Ibikunle Amosun, and former Senate Chief Whip, Senator Ali Ndume, have paid glowing tributes to Nigeria’s founding fathers, describing the late Dr Nnamdi Azikiwe, Chief Obafemi Awolowo and Sir Ahmadu Bello as selfless leaders whose legacies remain a benchmark for good governance and democracy.

They lamented the country’s leadership challenges, saying Nigeria had failed to sustain the vision, patriotism and selflessness demonstrated by the nation’s founding fathers.

The former governors and other political figures spoke on Monday at the 7th Dr Nnamdi Azikiwe Annual Award Lecture held in Abuja.

Amosun said Nigerians enjoyed considerable respect internationally during the era of the country’s founding fathers but had lost that standing because successive leaders failed to sustain their ideals.

The former lawmaker said the problem was not a shortage of ideas but a lack of purposeful leadership.

“Nigerians are who we are. A person will treat you the way you present yourself. When you look at the formation of Nigeria, those giants- yes, we mentioned the three of them, because they represent all three major tribes,” he said.

The former governor, who disclosed that he was pursuing a PhD in leadership at King’s College London, expressed optimism that Nigeria could overcome its challenges with the emergence of selfless leaders.

He described Azikiwe, Awolowo and Bello as statesmen who prioritised national development over personal wealth.

“They are statesmen, not businessmen. As some persons said today, we cannot remember Zik, Pa Awolowo or Ahmadu Bello leaving behind huge amount of money for this or that.

“No, what they did was that they served diligently and selflessly. They were not thinking about making money or anything like that. You can’t be both businessman and statesman at the same time. No, you must pick one. And they chose to be statesmen,” Amosun said.

He added that the three leaders remained reference points for good governance because of their commitment to public service.

Similarly, Ndume described Azikiwe as a visionary, intellectual patriot and Pan-Africanist whose contributions to Nigeria and Africa went beyond political leadership.

The senator said Azikiwe, Bello and Awolowo had left enduring legacies despite not amassing enormous personal wealth while in office.

He said their names continued to command respect decades after their deaths because of their contributions to nation-building.

“Let us take these three that I mentioned as a reward for good leadership. All of us believe in God, and this is how God does his things. After all these years, and after so many leadership changes that we have in this country, these three names still shine,” he said.

Ndume lamented what he described as the declining international reputation of Nigeria, recalling how he travelled to the United Kingdom as a student without obtaining a visa but was subjected to a search at the airport during a recent official visit despite holding a diplomatic passport.

He said the founding fathers had laid a solid foundation for Nigeria, adding that the country could have been competing with China, India and Hong Kong if their leadership ideals had been sustained.

The former Senate Chief Whip also urged African leaders to build on the political independence secured by the founding generation through economic transformation, democratic stability and technological advancement.

He warned against the personalisation of government, saying Nigeria’s democracy was increasingly serving the interests of a few rather than the wider population.

“Our democracy has been turned into government of some people, by some people, and for some people. It is getting to a level whereby government is being personalised and privatised, and that is where we got it wrong,” Ndume said.

He called for stronger constitutional democracy, respect for the rule of law, protection of human rights and accountability in the management of public resources.

Also speaking, the Action Democratic Party presidential candidate, Aliyu Bin Abbas, described Nigeria as a country in distress, urging political leaders to draw inspiration from the lives and sacrifices of the founding fathers.

“As a Nigerian, I must say that right now, my country is bleeding. Our country is collapsing and sinking. I am speaking like this because I am here to participate in the lecture in honour of a man who played a great role in making Nigeria what it is today,” he said.

Abbas accused political leaders of prioritising personal interests over national development, saying younger politicians must take responsibility for defending the country’s future.

He said his presidential ambition was driven by the desire to challenge the existing political system, which he argued had failed Nigerians.

“We are only against the system because it has not been favourable to anybody,” he added.

In his remarks, the Chairman of the Code of Conduct Tribunal and Secretary to the Board of Trustees of the foundation, Dr Mainasara Kogo, called for national unity, warning against ethnic and religious divisions.

Kogo said the country’s present situation was inconsistent with the ideals Azikiwe stood for, stressing that Nigerians must recognise their common humanity and work towards national cohesion.

He urged citizens to reflect on Section 15(1) of the Constitution, which identifies national unity, faith, peace and progress as the country’s motto.

He said Nigerians must reject ethnic and religious chauvinism if the country was to achieve meaningful development.

Azikiwe, popularly known as Zik of Africa, was Nigeria’s first President, serving from 1963 to 1966, after becoming the country’s first indigenous Governor-General in 1960.

Born on November 16, 1904, in Zungeru, present-day Niger State, he was a leading nationalist whose political activities and advocacy contributed to Nigeria’s struggle for independence.

He died on May 11, 1996.

The post Amosun, Ndume decry leadership failure, hail founding fathers appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Okpe leaders demand restoration of distinct ethnic status in Delta
description: Leaders in Okpe Kingdom have urged their indigenous people to work towards restoring the recognition of the Okpe as a distinct ethnic nationality, saying this would pave the way for the kingdom to regain its rightful status under the DESOPADEC Law, as was the case in the defunct Midwest Region and B
content:
Leaders in Okpe Kingdom have urged their indigenous people to work towards restoring the recognition of the Okpe as a distinct ethnic nationality, saying this would pave the way for the kingdom to regain its rightful status under the DESOPADEC Law, as was the case in the defunct Midwest Region and Bendel State.

The elders, while reflecting on the historical position of the Okpe Union, said it would continue to push for the recognition of the Okpe as a distinct ethnic nationality in Nigeria and Delta State.

They made this known in a statement signed by Professor Igho Natufe, President-General, Okpe Union (Worldwide); Kingsley Akpederin, General Secretary, Okpe Union (Worldwide); and Victor Oruno, National Publicity Secretary, Okpe Union (Worldwide).

The statement read: “Since the restoration of the Okpe Monarchy on January 1, 1945, after an interregnum of over 150 years, the Orodje institution has gradually re-established itself as one of the most important centres of administrative stability in Nigeria, contributing to the socio-economic and political evolution of the country and, most importantly, to inter-ethnic relations in the then Midwest Region (later known as Bendel State) and now Delta State.

“At the creation of Delta State, the then Orodje of Okpe Kingdom, HRM Orhoro I, became the pioneer chairman of the Delta State Council of Traditional Rulers. In furtherance of the legacy of the Okpe Nation as a rallying centre for the unity of the various ethnic nationalities in the Delta area, it is heartwarming that the Delta State Government recognised and appointed HRM Orhue I as Chairman of the Delta State Council of Traditional Rulers. In this position, HRM Orhue I has contributed to the peaceful coexistence and security of our dear Delta State.”

They also congratulated His Royal Majesty, Orhue I, the Orodje of Okpe Kingdom, and all Okpe nationals on the 20th anniversary of his coronation, being commemorated from November 13 to 22, 2026.

The leaders praised the traditional ruler for his leadership and initiatives aimed at uplifting the people of Okpe Kingdom.

“Back home in the Okpe Nation, there has been notable and sustained improvement in the infrastructural landscape of the Okpe Kingdom since 2006, when HRM Orhue I ascended the throne of the forefathers of the Okpe Nation. The Okpe Nation has moved from the highest political position of Deputy Governorship it ever attained in the Second Republic to the Governorship of Delta State currently, after the position of Speaker of the House of Assembly had been occupied consecutively by two Okpe sons during the reign of HRM Orhue I.”

They also commended Orhue I for ensuring that the Okpe language was officially recognised by the Nigerian Educational Research and Development Council, NERDC.

The statement added: “This paved the way for the official recognition by the Delta State Ministry of Basic Education of the Okpe language as the local language to be taught in primary and junior secondary schools in the two local government areas of Okpe Kingdom.

“This has short-changed the Okpe people, preventing them from receiving a fair share of infrastructural projects, bursary allocations for Okpe students and positions such as exclusive DESOPADEC commissioner, executive director in DESOPADEC and other development agencies, despite the distinctiveness and size of the Okpe Nation.”

While welcoming the restoration of Sapele Constituency 2 and Okpe Constituency 2 for the House of Assembly during the reign of HRM Orhue I, the leaders called for the restoration of Sapele Federal Constituency, which, they said, would enable the Okpe Nation to be represented by two members in the House of Representatives at the federal level, as was the case with the Sapele and Okpe Federal Constituencies between 1979 and 1993.

The post Okpe leaders demand restoration of distinct ethnic status in Delta appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: NUJ Lagos hails Sanwo-Ou over mandatory health insurance policy, seeks journalists’ inclusion
description: The Nigeria Union of Journalists (NUJ), Lagos State Council, has applauded Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu for introducing mandatory health insurance coverage for residents, describing the policy as a timely intervention that will improve access to healthcare and reduce the financial burden of medical e
content:
The Nigeria Union of Journalists (NUJ), Lagos State Council, has applauded Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu for introducing mandatory health insurance coverage for residents, describing the policy as a timely intervention that will improve access to healthcare and reduce the financial burden of medical expenses.

The Council, however, called for the inclusion of journalists across the state’s media industry in the implementation of the policy, announcing the constitution of a five-man committee to develop strategies for securing affordable and accessible health insurance coverage for media practitioners.

In a statement signed by the Council Chairman, Comrade Adewale Akodu, and Secretary, Olayide Awosanya, the NUJ said the initiative represents an important step towards strengthening healthcare delivery, promoting preventive healthcare and ensuring that access to medical services is not determined solely by financial capacity.

The policy requires residents, employers and workers in Lagos State to obtain health insurance coverage on or before December 31, 2026, ahead of full enforcement scheduled to begin on January 1, 2027.

While commending the governor for the initiative, the Council stressed that its implementation must take into account the peculiar working conditions of journalists, including those in print, broadcast, online and other media platforms.

To this end, the Akodu-led administration has constituted a five-member committee as part of its healthcare support agenda to prepare a comprehensive position paper on the implementation of the policy within the media industry.

Members of the committee are Vivian Ihechu of the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN), Julie Ekong of Radio Nigeria, Aminat Elegushi of Lagos Television (LTV), Aderayo Idowu-Olaiya of Lagos Traffic Radio and Olawale Afolabi of the Lagos State Ministry of Information and Strategy.

The committee is expected to examine the financial realities of journalists, the welfare needs of freelance practitioners and other categories of media professionals, as well as the respective responsibilities of employers and employees under the new policy.

It will also explore areas of collaboration among the NUJ, Lagos State Government, Lagos State Health Management Agency (LASHMA), accredited Health Maintenance Organisations (HMOs) and media organisations to facilitate sustainable healthcare coverage for journalists.

According to the Council, the proposed position paper will provide a framework for constructive engagement with government agencies, media owners and other stakeholders to ensure that journalists are not left out of the policy’s implementation.

The NUJ maintained that journalists, who work tirelessly to inform, educate and hold society accountable, deserve access to quality and affordable healthcare, noting that their well-being is critical to professional productivity and the sustainability of the media industry.

The Council therefore urged media organisations, employers, journalists and other stakeholders to begin preparations towards securing appropriate health insurance coverage before the December 31 deadline.

Reaffirming its commitment to journalists’ welfare, the Akodu-led administration said it would continue to pursue purposeful policies, strategic partnerships and initiatives aimed at improving the professional and personal well-being of media practitioners.

The Council emphasised that a healthy journalist is a productive journalist and that a healthy media workforce remains indispensable to a vibrant and sustainable media industry.

title: Plateau Council imposes curfew after gunmen burn seven houses
description:
Residents flee Qua’an-Pan communities as tension mounts



By Golok Nanmwa



JOS — The Qua’an-Pan Local Government Council of Plateau State has imposed a dusk-to-dawn curfew on Doemak District following heightened tension after suspected gunmen set seven houses ablaze in Bong community.







The
content:
Residents flee Qua’an-Pan communities as tension mounts

By Golok Nanmwa

JOS — The Qua’an-Pan Local Government Council of Plateau State has imposed a dusk-to-dawn curfew on Doemak District following heightened tension after suspected gunmen set seven houses ablaze in Bong community.

The curfew, which runs from 6pm to 6am daily, was imposed amid reports of residents fleeing their homes, shops shutting down and commercial activities grinding to a halt over fears of further attacks.

The Director of Press and Publicity to the Executive Chairman of the council, Danaan Cletus Sylvanus, announced the restriction in a public notice issued on Monday, November 16, 2026.

He said the curfew was necessary in view of the prevailing security situation in the district, warning that anyone found moving around during the restricted hours would be treated as a security threat by security agencies.

The council urged residents to comply strictly with the directive and cooperate with security agencies to maintain peace and prevent further breakdown of law and order.

The development followed Sunday’s attack on Bong community in Doemak District, where suspected gunmen reportedly stormed the village at about 9pm and set seven houses on fire.

A community source, Mr Silas Bishop, who confirmed the incident, lamented the destruction and called on security operatives to intensify efforts to track down and arrest those responsible.

He also urged security agencies to strengthen surveillance and deploy additional personnel to vulnerable communities to prevent further attacks.

Meanwhile, tension has reportedly gripped Doemak, the headquarters of Qua’an-Pan Local Government Area, with residents said to be packing their belongings and relocating to safer locations over fears for their lives and property.

As of Monday evening, shops were reportedly closed, while commercial activities remained disrupted amid growing concerns over the security situation.

Confirming the attack, the Executive Chairman of Qua’an-Pan Local Government Council, Hon. (Dr.) Christopher Audu Manship, condemned the incident and assured residents that the government would not abandon them.

Manship, who visited Bong community to assess the destruction, pledged government support for efforts to rebuild the houses destroyed by the attackers.

He said, “Government will not abandon the people of Bong community. We will support efforts towards the restoration of the houses destroyed and sustain measures to secure the community against further attacks.”

The chairman urged youths in the affected communities to remain vigilant and promptly report suspicious movements to security agencies.

The attack on Bong occurred around the same time suspected terrorists invaded Zwagal community in Jipal District of neighbouring Mangu Local Government Area, where several residents were reportedly killed.

Manship, who visited Zwagal alongside the Executive Chairman of Mangu Local Government Council, Hon. Emmanuel Bala Mwolpun, described the attack as barbaric and inhuman.

He said the government would intensify efforts to protect lives and property, which he described as its primary responsibility.

The Qua’an-Pan chairman also conveyed Governor Caleb Mutfwang’s condolences to the bereaved families in Zwagal, assuring them that the governor remained committed to addressing insecurity in the state.

Also speaking, Mwolpun said efforts were being made to improve network services in the affected communities to strengthen security surveillance and communication.

Earlier, the Long Zwagal, Miskagam Jonathan Wadong, thanked the two council chairmen for their prompt response and mobilisation of security personnel following the attack.

He said gunshots suddenly rang out in the community at about 8pm before the attackers invaded, throwing residents into panic.

Wadong appealed to the government to deploy more security personnel to the area to prevent a recurrence of the attacks.

title: Abia APC kicks off Presidential Campaign, promises massive votes for Tinubu
description:
Abia State chapter of the All Progressives Congress (APC), has kicked off its presidential campaign rally with assurance to galvanize massive votes for President Bola Tinubu in the 2027 election.
Speaking at the rally held at Umuahia Township stadium, deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives,
content:
Abia State chapter of the All Progressives Congress (APC), has kicked off its presidential campaign rally with assurance to galvanize massive votes for President Bola Tinubu in the 2027 election.

Speaking at the rally held at Umuahia Township stadium, deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Rt. Hon Benjamin Kalu while assuring Tinubu of massive votes from Abia in 2027, was emphatic they were not going to negotiate with anybody for the president to get 25 percent votes in Abia as APC in the state has the capacity to give him over 75 percent votes.

Rt. Hon Kalu commended President Tinubu for choosing a tough path in his quest to revamp the nation’s economy.

Kalu said in the last three years, the President chose the tough path of removal of fuel subsidy so Nigeria could continue to exist as a nation.

He stated that the moment of hardship was over and that now is the moment of joy as the people will start to reap from their sacrifices.

He told the mammoth crowd at the stadium of some other things the president has done that should make him to be re-elected for a second term in office.

Kalu mentioned the stabilization of the currency, stoppage of strike by the Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU), and tax reform he said has brought stability to the fiscal policy, among others as some of the things Tinubu has done to strengthen the country.

The deputy Speaker applauded the President for the creation and funding of the the State East Development Commission (SEDC), and his efforts to fight insecurity in different parts of the country.

The State Chairman of the party, Hon Chijioke Chukwu commended President Tinubu for what he has been doing for the state.

Apart from the infrastructural development he said are going on in South East under the Tinubu administration, he equally mentioned Benjamin Kalu becoming the deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives as the handiwork of Tinubu.

“Tinubu has ensured the provision of some critical infrastructure in the state and these include the ongoing reconstruction of the Umuahia/Ikot Ekpene, Omenuko Bridge and others.

He equally mentioned the approval by the National Assembly, for the establishment of some tertiary institutions in the state which he said has the backing of the President.

He said Tinubu was doing all these despite the fact that the state gave him merger vote in 2023 and said 2027 will be the time to reciprocate the President’s goodness to the state by support and voting him for a second term.

He thanked the President for not only establishing the South East Development Commission (SEDC), but also adequately funding it for the good of the people.

The former Governor of the state and current Nigerian Ambassador to Spain, Dr. Okezie Ikpeazu said they would all work together to ensure Tinubu is re-elected in 2027.

Represented by the deputy Governorship candidate of the People’s Democratic Party (PDP), Amah Abraham, Ikpeazu recalled that the nation was in a critical condition before Tinubu and the President for his efforts to revive the country.

The Abia Governorship candidate of APC, Dr. Eric Opah said Abia will not only vote massively for Tinubu in the coming election, but also sweep other seats at the polls.

Other speakers including Mike Okoye (jnr), Managing Director of the SEDC, Cosmos Ndukwe, Henry Ikoh, Donatus Nwamara, among others, all spoke glowingly of the President and promised of massive votes for him in 2027.

title: Mining marshals: Reps gives NSCDC boss 24 hrs ultimatum over alleged extortion
description:
The House of Representatives Committee on Solid Minerals has directed the Commandant-General of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), Ahmed Audi, to appear before it over allegation of extortion and harassment of licensed mining operators by mining marshals.
The panel issued the dire
content:
The House of Representatives Committee on Solid Minerals has directed the Commandant-General of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), Ahmed Audi, to appear before it over allegation of extortion and harassment of licensed mining operators by mining marshals.

The panel issued the directive, on Tuesday, at at investigative hearing on the operations and funding of mining marshals, following
allegations bordering on abuse of power, extortion, unlawful detention, financial irregularities and alleged misconduct by personnel of the special security unit established to combat illegal mining across the country.

The Chairman of the committee, Gaza Gbefwi, while speaking at investigative hearing, explained that the probe was aimed at establishing the facts surrounding allegations of unlawful arrests and harassment of licensed mining operators, and alleged ₦2 billion transaction linked to the bank account of a former state commandant of the NSCDC.

According to him, “We see this inquiry as essential to confidence in Nigeria’s solid minerals sector. We want our mineral wealth to sustain livelihoods, attract responsible investment and strengthen national revenue. We must therefore protect mining communities and lawful enterprise, while ensuring that security powers serve the public interest.

“Our nation’s mineral wealth must translate into opportunity and security for its people.
Our investigation arises from the House’s resolution to examine serious concerns about the Mining Marshals’ performance, legal status, funding and alleged compromise.

“We must determine whether the unit’s conduct, structure and funding fulfil that purpose and comply with Section 3 of the NSCDC Act and the Nigerian Minerals and Mining Act 2007.

“We will examine allegations of unlawful arrests and harassment of licensed mineral title holders; the alleged ₦2 billion linkage to a former State Commander’s bank account and his reported redeployment to Enugu State; alleged syndicate compromise across the 36 states and the FCT; and vehicle procurements for which verifiable legislative appropriation has been questioned.

“We will establish the sources and legal authority for the unit’s funding, including external inflows. We have serious reservations about the initial response of the head of the Mining Marshals to the Speaker, imputing ulterior motives to the mover of the motion and, by implication, casting doubt upon the House’s purpose.

“We respect the right to respond and disagree. A resolution adopted by the House, however, engages the responsibility of the institution, and its questions deserve substantive answers. We will assess every explanation on its merits; speculation about motives cannot settle the issues before us.”

title: Kunle Afolayan’s son opens up on suicide attempts, sexual assault
description:
Dieko Afolayan, son of Nollywood filmmaker Kunle Afolayan, has spoken about his experiences with bullying, sexual assault and repeated suicide attempts, describing how he has been working towards healing and discovering his purpose.
He shared his experiences during an interview on The Morayo Show on
content:
Dieko Afolayan, son of Nollywood filmmaker Kunle Afolayan, has spoken about his experiences with bullying, sexual assault and repeated suicide attempts, describing how he has been working towards healing and discovering his purpose.

He shared his experiences during an interview on The Morayo Show on Monday, where he reflected on the emotional challenges he had faced and how they influenced his journey through life.

According to him, overcoming the trauma has been difficult, but he has come to understand that his past does not determine his identity or future.

“I have tried so many times to commit suicide, and I am also a victim of sexual assault. However, I have realised that these experiences do not define who I am, where I get to or what I do with myself,” he said.

Recounting how deeply he struggled with feelings of rejection, Dieko disclosed that he once attempted to ingest broken glass because he felt he did not belong.

“There were so many times I would cry. I remember a time I tried to ingest broken glass because I felt I did not belong here,” he added.

He described his journey from pain to purpose as challenging, noting that his traumatic experiences had made the process of rebuilding his life particularly difficult.

“Moving from pain to purpose has not been easy, especially knowing that you are going to be doing a lot of difficult things, having been through difficult experiences,” he said.

Dieko, however, identified his discovery of a passion for hosting and programme presentation while in school as a major turning point.

He explained that the positive feedback he received after making presentations helped him recognise his ability to communicate effectively and use his voice to make a difference.

“I realised that I came into this world for something. I have a mission on earth, and that is to make people feel something and use my voice for the voiceless,” he said.

He also encouraged people going through difficult experiences to practise self-compassion, saying a change in how he viewed himself and his circumstances had helped him develop a more positive outlook.

“I feel like if there is anything anyone should practise, it is self-compassion,” he added.

title: Kashim dumps NDC for APC ahead of Bauchi 2027
description:
Former SSG defects days after emerging as opposition governorship candidate



By Christopher Ameh, Bauchi



The political landscape in Bauchi State ahead of the 2027 governorship election has witnessed a significant development following the defection of former Secretary to the State Government (S
content:
Former SSG defects days after emerging as opposition governorship candidate

By Christopher Ameh, Bauchi

The political landscape in Bauchi State ahead of the 2027 governorship election has witnessed a significant development following the defection of former Secretary to the State Government (SSG), Ibrahim Kashim, from the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) to the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC).

Kashim, who was recently listed by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) as the NDC governorship candidate for the 2027 election, announced his defection on Monday at a ceremony held at the APC State Secretariat in Bauchi.

His move comes days after his emergence as the opposition party’s standard-bearer, raising questions about the future of its governorship campaign in the state.

Explaining his decision, Kashim said he joined the APC because of its national political influence, institutional strength and capacity to attract development opportunities to Bauchi State.

He said the APC’s control of the Federal Government and its strong political presence across Northern Nigeria made it a strategic platform for advancing the interests of the state.

“The APC is currently the governing party at the Federal level and has an overwhelming presence across Northern Nigeria. It is also the party with the political structure, national reach and institutional capacity to provide a viable platform for the political and developmental aspirations we seek for Bauchi,” he said.

The defection comes as political parties intensify consultations and mobilise support ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Kashim’s departure could prompt fresh political calculations among stakeholders, particularly within the NDC, where his name had already featured on INEC’s published list of governorship candidates.

For the APC, his entry brings into its fold a former senior official in the administration of Governor Bala Mohammed, although the extent to which his political supporters and grassroots structures will follow him remains unclear.

The development has also drawn attention to the implications of high-profile defections for opposition parties as preparations for the 2027 governorship election gather pace.

title: AI could destroy world if left unregulated, Izunaso warns
description:
• raises alarm over fake content, social media attacks on politicians

Senator Osita Izunaso has warned that artificial intelligence (AI) could become a global calamity if left unregulated, citing the growing use of the technology to generate fake content, manipulate public opinion and undermine tru
content:
• raises alarm over fake content, social media attacks on politicians

Senator Osita Izunaso has warned that artificial intelligence (AI) could become a global calamity if left unregulated, citing the growing use of the technology to generate fake content, manipulate public opinion and undermine trust in information.

Izunaso, Chairman of the Senate Committee on Capital Market, said AI-generated images and digital content had become so realistic that it was increasingly difficult to distinguish fabricated materials from genuine ones.

He also raised the alarm over the weaponisation of social media against politicians, alleging that some individuals resorted to online harassment, falsehoods and coordinated negative campaigns against public office holders when their personal demands were not met.

The senator spoke on Monday in Abuja at the World Public Relations Forum, themed, “Responsible Communication: The Voice of the World”.

He said urgent regulatory measures were needed to prevent the potential dangers of AI from overshadowing its benefits.

“AI is a medical issue right now. And globally, AI is not regulated in most countries.

“Just like when new media started, most politicians did not find it necessary to regulate the new media. We started late as parliamentarians and I am also of the opinion that AI must be regulated before AI will destroy the world,” he said.

Izunaso observed that the sophistication of AI-generated images had made it increasingly difficult for people to establish the authenticity of materials circulated online.

“Now, when you see AI images, they look so real that sometimes you might not be able to decipher which is AI and which is real. Don’t get me wrong. AI is good, but it has to be regulated before the goodness of AI will become the calamity of the world,” he said.

The lawmaker also decried what he described as the growing use of social media to intimidate and malign politicians, particularly by individuals unhappy with their inability to secure personal favours from public office holders.

He said some people who approached politicians with requests they could not fulfil subsequently resorted to publishing damaging comments about them online.

“When people ask you for something and you are unable to do that thing, they will say okay, don’t worry. Then, within one week, you will see what they post about you. All manner of negativity,” he said.

He cited the case of a political appointee who, instead of receiving congratulatory messages following his appointment to a campaign council of the ruling party, became the subject of negative online comments because of perceived personal or political differences.

Izunaso called for greater responsibility and accountability in digital communication, stressing that truth, empathy and accountability must guide interactions on social media.

Earlier, the Vice-Chancellor of Chukwuemeka Odumegwu Ojukwu University, Anambra State, Kate Omenugha, called for the integration of communication ethics into university curricula across disciplines.

She said the widespread use of social media and AI without adequate training and ethical guidelines had heightened the risks of misinformation and irresponsible communication.

Also speaking, the President and Chief Executive Officer of the Global Alliance for Public Relations and Communication Management, Justin Green, highlighted Africa’s growing representation in the organisation’s leadership.

He disclosed that Africa, which previously had no representative on its board, now had six members, the highest representation from any continent.

Green described the development as a significant achievement for the continent and invited the six African board members to the stage in recognition of their contributions to the global public relations community.

The Chief Executive Officer of the Chartered Institute of Public Relations (CIPR), United Kingdom, Alastair McCapra, said public relations professionals must address their own credibility challenges before assuming the responsibility of rebuilding public trust in institutions and society.

The post AI could destroy world if left unregulated, Izunaso warns appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

The Ukrainian Embassy said
content:
…Introduces newly appointed honorary consul

The Ukrainian Ambassador to Nigeria, Ivan Kholostenko, at the weekend, held a meeting with members of the Ukrainian community in Lagos.

The Embassy of Ukraine in Nigeria, disclosed the details of the meeting in a Facebook post.

The Ukrainian Embassy said that during the meeting, the ambassador introduced the newly appointed Honorary Consul of Ukraine in Lagos, Fadi Michel Issa, whose key responsibilities will include the protection of the rights and interests of Ukrainian citizens.

The participants, the embassy stated, discussed current issues affecting the Ukrainian community, as well as opportunities to improve consular services and strengthen cooperation with the embassy.

“The Embassy expresses its appreciation to all participants for the constructive dialogue,” the Embassy of Ukraine in Nigeria said.

Speaking about the meeting, Kholostenko said he had the pleasure of meeting with the Ukrainian community in Lagos.

The envoy also said that during the meeting, he was pleased to introduce to his fellow Ukrainians, the new Honorary Consul of Ukraine in Lagos, Fadi Michel Issa.

“One of his key responsibilities will be to protect the rights and interests of Ukrainian citizens in Lagos.

“In a warm and friendly atmosphere, we discussed current issues and challenges facing Ukrainians, as well as proposals for improving consular services.

“My sincere thanks to everyone who joined us for the open dialogue, trust, and constructive suggestions!

“I congratulate Mr. Fadi Michael Issa on taking up this important responsibility and wish him every success in serving Ukraine and our fellow citizens!

“I would also like to thank Ms. Olena Nedryhailo, Representative of the Ukrainian Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Nigeria, for her assistance in organizing the meeting.

“And a very special thanks to Ms. Tetiana Buchak and TOP BEANS – Coffee and More for the warm welcome and genuine Ukrainian hospitality!” Kholostenko said.
