title: ‎Tinubu hails Nigeria’s re-election into ITU council
description: ‎‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru‎‎ABUJA –PRESIDENT Bola Tinubu has applauded Nigeria’s re-election to the Council of the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) for another four-year term, which begins in 2027.‎‎The President described Nigeria’s re-election at the ongoing ITU conference in Doha, Qatar,
content:
‎
‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru
‎
‎ABUJA –PRESIDENT Bola Tinubu has applauded Nigeria’s re-election to the Council of the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) for another four-year term, which begins in 2027.
‎
‎The President described Nigeria’s re-election at the ongoing ITU conference in Doha, Qatar, as a significant diplomatic and strategic achievement that underscores the country’s growing influence in global telecommunications, digital innovation and ICT governance.
‎
‎He urged the Nigerian representatives to use the renewed mandate to strengthen the country’s leadership in digital innovation, telecommunications development and international ICT cooperation.
‎
‎President Tinubu commended the Minister of Foreign Affairs, Ambassador Bianca Odumegwu-Ojukwu, for coordinating Nigeria’s diplomatic engagement and providing the leadership needed to secure this important victory.
‎
‎He also applauded the Minister of Communications, Innovation and Digital Economy, Dr Bosun Tijani, who led the Nigerian delegation, for his commitment and effective representation of the country’s interests.
‎
‎A statement by the presidential spokesman, Bayo Onanuga, quoted the President as saying: “I equally recognise the invaluable contributions of Nigeria’s Ambassador to Qatar, Prof. Mahmood Yakubu, who served as Deputy Head of Delegation; the Executive Vice Chairman of the Nigerian Communications Commission (NCC), Dr Aminu Maida; Nigeria’s Permanent Representative to the United Nations Office in Geneva, Ambassador Innocent Imejuo; and the officials of the Federal Ministry of Communications, the NCC, the Permanent Mission in Geneva and the Nigerian Embassy in Doha.
‎
‎”I appreciate the dedication, teamwork and professionalism of all members of the Nigerian delegation and diplomatic personnel whose collective efforts contributed to this successful outcome.”
‎
‎The ITU, established in 1865 as the United Nations specialised agency for information and communication technologies, plays a critical role in shaping global telecommunications standards, expanding digital connectivity and promoting international cooperation in the digital economy.
‎
‎Nigeria’s continued presence on the ITU Council provides an important platform for the country to contribute to global policy decisions, champion the interests of developing nations, promote inclusive digital transformation and advance its aspirations in the rapidly evolving global digital landscape.

title: 2027: Osun Senator Fadahunsi begins re-election campaign
description:
The Senator representing Osun East in the Senate, Francis Fadahunsi, has expressed confidence that voters in the 10 local government areas in the district will re-elect him for another term in the 2027 general elections.
Fadahunsi, a retired officer of the Nigeria Customs Service, was first elected
content:
The Senator representing Osun East in the Senate, Francis Fadahunsi, has expressed confidence that voters in the 10 local government areas in the district will re-elect him for another term in the 2027 general elections.

Fadahunsi, a retired officer of the Nigeria Customs Service, was first elected to the Senate in 2019 and re-elected in 2023 on the platform of the Peoples Democratic Party.

The lawmaker, who will contest the 2027 election on the platform of the All Progressives Congress, said his record of service had placed him in a good position to win the poll.

He made this known in a statement signed by Akinyele Akintola on behalf of the Fadahunsi Campaign Organisation. A copy of the statement was obtained in Osogbo on Monday.

“We are confident that the electorate across the 10 local government areas in Osun East have seen what we are capable of doing, and they will trust us again in 2027 to do more for humanity.

“We have done lots of developmental projects and empowerment in our constituency; this we will be building upon if re-elected,” Fadahunsi said.

Unveiling the lawmaker’s campaign activities, the statement said Fadahunsi would soon begin a working tour of the 10 local government areas in Osun East Senatorial District.

During the tour, the campaign council said the lawmaker would inspect ongoing projects and officially inaugurate completed ones, which were carefully selected to accelerate development in communities across the district.

“The tour, which will start at Ife North, underscores the senator’s achievements and commitment to delivering tangible dividends of democracy, improving rural-urban connectivity and enhancing the socio-economic wellness of Osun East residents.

“During the tour, Senator Fadahunsi will hold meetings with stakeholders, commission key infrastructural and social intervention projects, including transformers, solar power lights, road infrastructure, water projects, school classroom projects, ICT and health care facilities, and so on.

“He will use the opportunity to unveil his manifesto and diligent readiness to further uplift Osun East Senatorial District if re-elected in the January election,” the statement read.

title: Tinubu’s debt interest gulped 124% of revenue in six months, NDC alleges
description:
The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) National Campaign Council has raised the alarm over the country’s debt burden, saying the Federal Government spent N7.7 trillion on debt interest payments in the first half of 2026, exceeding its total revenue of N6.2 trillion within the period.
According to the
content:
The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) National Campaign Council has raised the alarm over the country’s debt burden, saying the Federal Government spent N7.7 trillion on debt interest payments in the first half of 2026, exceeding its total revenue of N6.2 trillion within the period.

According to the party, the development is a fiscal suicide which exposed the growing pressure of debt servicing on government finances at the expense of infrastructure and human development.

Spokesperson of the council, Dr. Chiogo Ikokwu, in a statement on Monday, cited the World Bank’s 2026 Nigeria Development Update, saying debt interest payments consumed 124.19 per cent of federal revenue in the first six months of the year.

She furthee said the situation raised serious questions about the direction of the country’s economy, particularly against the backdrop of increased borrowing, fuel subsidy removal and the economic hardship confronting Nigerians.

“The grim reality for every suffering family in our nation today is that under the President Bola Tinubu administration, Nigeria is no longer borrowing to build roads, equip hospitals, or fund schools. It is borrowing recklessly to pay interest on past debts, thereby mortgaging the survival of today’s citizens and the destiny of unborn generations,” the party said.

According to the statement, debt interest payments rose from N5.6 trillion in the first half of 2025 to N7.7 trillion in the corresponding period of 2026, accounting for 3.1 per cent of the country’s Gross Domestic Product (GDP).

It contrasted this with capital expenditure, which it said fell to N700 billion, representing 0.3 per cent of GDP, from one per cent in the corresponding period of the previous year.

Ikokwu said the Federal Government was spending about 11 times more on debt interest than on critical infrastructure, describing the trend as unsustainable.

The spokesperson also faulted the administration’s revenue performance, noting that although federal revenue increased from N3.6 trillion in the first half of 2025 to N6.2 trillion in the corresponding period of 2026, Nigerians had little to show for the additional collections.

She argued that the increase came amid heavier taxation and mounting pressure on households and businesses, while a significant portion of government revenue went into servicing expensive domestic debts.

According to the council, the figures reinforced the question repeatedly raised by its presidential candidate, Peter Obi, over the management of public resources.

“Fellow Nigerians, you can see part of why Mr. Peter Gregory Obi has been asking: Despite the removal of the fuel subsidy and the massive borrowing, ‘Where is our money?'” the statement said.

The party called for an immediate halt to what it described as reckless domestic borrowing, warning that excessive government borrowing could crowd out private sector access to credit.

It also demanded a comprehensive audit and restructuring of the country’s debts to reduce debt servicing to sustainable levels, alongside a review of government spending priorities.

The NDC urged the administration to redirect resources from overheads to infrastructure, healthcare, education and productive sectors of the economy.

Looking ahead to the 2027 elections, the party said the Obi-Kwankwaso ticket would pursue a different economic direction anchored on productivity, fiscal discipline and sustainable growth.

It said the objective would be to ensure that public resources were deployed towards improving the living conditions of Nigerians rather than being consumed by debt obligations.

title: APC flags off 2027 campaign in Abia, Kalu targets 75% for Tinubu
description:
…SEDC unveils 100,000-hectare agro-project, gas pipeline, industrial parks



By Steve Oko



UMUAHIA – The All Progressives Congress (APC) on Monday formally flagged off its 2027 general election campaign in Abia State with a rally in Umuahia, where party leaders pledged massive votes for President
content:
…SEDC unveils 100,000-hectare agro-project, gas pipeline, industrial parks

By Steve Oko

UMUAHIA – The All Progressives Congress (APC) on Monday formally flagged off its 2027 general election campaign in Abia State with a rally in Umuahia, where party leaders pledged massive votes for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election.

The rally, held at the Umuahia Township Stadium, attracted party leaders, candidates and supporters from across the state, with thousands of people filling the venue and causing heavy vehicular and human traffic around adjoining streets.

Leading the campaign, Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Rt. Hon. Benjamin Kalu, declared that Abia would deliver 75 per cent of its votes to Tinubu in 2027, insisting that the President would not need to struggle to secure the constitutionally required 25 per cent in the state.

Kalu, who described the turnout as evidence of the APC’s growing political strength in Abia, said the party had about 162,000 registered members and had challenged each member to mobilise 10 additional voters for Tinubu.

According to him, the strategy could translate into more than 1.6 million votes for the President.

“Don’t beg for 25 per cent. Your sons and daughters in Abia State will give you 75 per cent. We have about 2.3 million voters in Abia State. We are mobilising. We are not sleeping,” he declared.

He said the party’s mobilisation efforts extended beyond rallies to house-to-house, village-to-village and community-to-community campaigns.

The Deputy Speaker challenged those questioning the APC’s electoral strength in Abia to await the party’s proposed rally at Enyimba Stadium, Aba, on December 7, describing the Umuahia gathering, organised within one week, as a foretaste of what was to come.

Kalu also appealed to Tinubu to reconsider his earlier decision to attend only the Enugu rally during his South-East campaign engagements and attend the proposed Aba rally.

Tinubu has remembered South-East — Kalu

Explaining why the South-East should support Tinubu’s second-term ambition, Kalu listed the establishment of the South-East Development Commission (SEDC), stabilisation of the foreign exchange market, student loans under NELFUND, tax reforms and increased security funding among the administration’s interventions.

He said the President had demonstrated commitment to the region by addressing longstanding grievances dating back to the Nigerian Civil War.

Kalu also credited the administration with expanding access to higher education through student loans and supporting efforts to prevent recurrent industrial actions in public universities.

He commended Tinubu for supporting his emergence as Deputy Speaker, describing the position as an opportunity to advance the interests of the South-East.

SEDC unveils 100,000-hectare agro-project, gas pipeline

Earlier, the Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of the SEDC, Mr Mark Okoye, made a case for Tinubu’s re-election, describing the establishment of the commission as a significant intervention in the development of the South-East.

Okoye said successive military and civilian administrations had failed to meet the region’s longstanding demand for a dedicated development commission since the end of the Civil War in 1970.

He disclosed that the commission was working on a 25-year development blueprint, known as the South-East 2050 Vision, to provide a coordinated roadmap for the region’s economic transformation.

According to him, the last comprehensive development plan for the region dated back to 1962, under the late Premier of Eastern Nigeria, Dr Michael Okpara.

Unveiling some of the commission’s interventions, Okoye said the SEDC had commenced its South-East Agro-Development Programme, targeting more than 100,000 hectares of farmland for food production, processing and agricultural development.

He said the programme had commenced in Enugu State, with Abia expected to benefit within two weeks, followed by Ebonyi State.

On industrialisation, he said the commission was developing industrial platforms across the five South-East states, including the Abia Integrated Industrial Platform, Anambra Industrial City, Ebonyi Business Park and industrial facilities in Enugu and Imo states.

He explained that the commission was prioritising access roads, water supply and other critical infrastructure to attract investors and make the industrial estates operational.

Okoye also disclosed that Tinubu had approved a South-East Gas Pipeline Project to supply gas across the five states and support industrial development.

He said the project was expected to begin delivering gas from February or March 2027, with the network eventually extending across the region.

The SEDC boss further disclosed that the commission was pursuing rail development to facilitate the movement of goods from industrial centres to ports and markets.

He announced the South-East Venture Capital Programme to provide funding for young technology entrepreneurs and innovative businesses.

On sports development, Okoye said the commission was introducing a grassroots sports programme to provide modern facilities across the region.

He specifically announced that Ibeku in Umuahia and Bende would benefit from new football pitches within two weeks.

Making a political appeal, he urged the South-East to support Tinubu, arguing that the region should acknowledge the President’s role in establishing the SEDC.

He recalled that the South-East collectively gave the APC about 127,000 votes in the 2023 presidential election, but Tinubu subsequently appointed prominent people from the region to strategic federal positions, including the Deputy Speaker and Minister of Works.

“Since 1970, we have had about six military presidents and five democratically elected presidents. The only man who broke that jinx and gave us what we had been begging for for 55 years was Asiwaju Bola Ahmed Tinubu,” he said.

Okoye challenged opposition parties to present their records in government and explain their contributions to the development of the South-East.

Opiah, Ikoh, Nwoye rally support for Tinubu

The APC governorship candidate in Abia, Chief Eric Opiah, said the turnout had demonstrated the party’s growing presence in the state.

He urged Abians to support Tinubu and other APC candidates, arguing that the benefits of the President’s economic reforms should translate into improved living conditions for Nigerians.

Opiah said the party had expanded its membership and mobilisation capacity, urging supporters to take the campaign to their respective wards and polling units.

Former Minister of Science and Technology and Abia Renewed Hope Ambassador, Chief Henry Ikoh, also called for Tinubu’s re-election, saying the President had taken bold decisions to reposition the country.

Ikoh cited increased federal allocations to states and the ability of state governments to meet salary obligations as some of the benefits of the administration’s economic policies.

The APC Deputy National Chairman (South), Chief Ben Nwoye, who represented the party’s National Chairman, commended Abia APC leaders for the mobilisation, describing the gathering as the mother of all rallies.

He expressed satisfaction with the party’s organisational strength in the state.

APC leaders pledge victory

Speaking for Abia North Senatorial District, former Deputy Speaker of the Abia State House of Assembly, Hon. Cosmos Ndukwe, assured the party of an overwhelming victory.

He pledged 99.9 per cent of the votes in the district, citing Tinubu’s appointment of Kalu as Deputy Speaker and federal interventions in roads, education and other sectors.

Former Abia South lawmaker, Hon. Emeka Stanley, commended Kalu for uniting APC members and mobilising them ahead of the elections.

The APC Abia Central Senatorial candidate, Hon. Emeka Atuma, also endorsed Tinubu’s second-term ambition, saying the President’s interventions had provided additional resources for development at the state and grassroots levels.

Similarly, the General Manager of the Niger Delta Power Holding Company, Mrs Jennifer Adighije, represented by Alexander Chukwu Ifaka, said Tinubu deserved the support of the electorate.

The APC South-East Zonal Youth Leader, Chimankpam Ogbonna, also urged support for the President, citing what he described as new development opportunities created by the administration.

Ikpeazu, PDP leaders endorse Tinubu

In a political development at the rally, the immediate past Abia State Governor and Nigeria’s Ambassador to Spain, Dr Okezie Ikpeazu, was represented by the PDP Deputy Governorship candidate, Abraham Amah, who publicly endorsed Tinubu’s re-election.

Amah, who said he spoke on behalf of Ikpeazu and the PDP leadership in Abia, described the removal of fuel subsidy as a courageous decision that had helped reposition the economy.

He argued that the increased resources available to state governments following the reforms had strengthened their capacity to meet financial obligations, including payment of workers’ salaries.

He consequently declared support for Tinubu’s second term.

Onyejeocha predicts 90% victory for Tinubu

Former Minister of State for Labour, Chief Nkeiruka Onyejeocha, predicted that Tinubu would secure 90 per cent of the votes in Abia State in 2027.

Onyejeocha, who is contesting the Isuikwuato/Umunneochi Federal Constituency seat, said the turnout at the Umuahia Township Stadium demonstrated the party’s growing presence in the state.

She urged Abians to translate their participation in the rally into votes for Tinubu and other APC candidates.

The APC National Organising Secretary, Hon. Donatus Nwankpa, called for total victory for the party’s candidates, urging members to adopt a “bottom-to-top” voting strategy.

Nwankpa dismissed suggestions of an alliance between the APC and other political parties, insisting that the party was contesting independently and should receive the votes of its supporters across all elective positions.

Speaking on behalf of Abia women, Hon. Blessing Nwagba assured Tinubu of their support, citing the programmes of the First Lady, Senator Oluremi Tinubu, aimed at improving women’s welfare and economic empowerment.

In an interview with Vanguard, the APC Director of Organising in Abia State and member of the Security and Intelligence Directorate of the party’s Presidential Campaign Council, Chief Chinasa Iheanyi, expressed confidence that Tinubu would secure between 65 and 70 per cent of the votes in the state.

Iheanyi, a former Abia Chief Liaison Officer in Abuja, estimated that between 15,000 and 17,000 supporters attended the rally, adding that thousands more were reportedly stranded across local government areas due to transportation and other logistical challenges.

He described the turnout as evidence of the party’s growing political strength in Abia and declared that the APC was prepared for the 2027 elections.

“Abia State is indeed APC. We are excited and ready for the coming elections. APC in Abia has come to stay. That talk about 25 per cent should be forgotten because that is not going to happen. We are giving Mr President a minimum of 65 to 70 per cent of the votes, and from there, we will ramp it up,” he said.

title: WHO issues first guidelines on adult type 1 diabetes, warns millions lack insulin
description:
More than 100 years after the discovery of insulin, millions of people living with type 1 diabetes still lack access to the lifesaving medicine, prompting the World Health Organisation (WHO) to issue its first-ever guidelines on the diagnosis and management of the condition in adults.
The guidelines
content:
More than 100 years after the discovery of insulin, millions of people living with type 1 diabetes still lack access to the lifesaving medicine, prompting the World Health Organisation (WHO) to issue its first-ever guidelines on the diagnosis and management of the condition in adults.

The guidelines, released to mark World Diabetes Day 2026, provide evidence-based recommendations to improve diabetes care and ensure access to affordable insulin, including in low-resource, emergency and humanitarian settings.

WHO said an estimated 9.5 million people were living with type 1 diabetes globally in 2025, with another 500,000 diagnosed within the year, warning that the condition, often associated with childhood, is increasingly affecting adults.

Type 1 diabetes is a lifelong condition in which the body produces little or no insulin, leaving affected persons dependent on daily insulin treatment to survive.

The new guidelines outline recommendations on diagnosis and classification, insulin regimens and delivery methods, monitoring of blood glucose levels and self-management of the condition.

WHO strongly recommends intensified insulin therapy involving multiple daily injections, with doses adjusted according to blood glucose levels, to help patients achieve better control of the disease.

It, however, recognises that treatment approaches may need to be adapted to local realities, particularly in emergencies and humanitarian settings where access to healthcare services and essential medicines may be disrupted.

The global health agency also recommends human insulin as an effective and generally cheaper treatment option, while noting that insulin analogues can be used when necessary.

On monitoring, WHO recommends regular blood glucose checks, including laboratory tests to assess average blood sugar levels over several months and home monitoring through finger-prick tests or continuous glucose monitors.

Where blood glucose testing is unavailable, urine glucose testing may be considered.

According to WHO, the recommendations are intended primarily for healthcare providers but will also guide policymakers, programme managers and humanitarian organisations in strengthening equitable and person-centred diabetes care.

Speaking on the guidelines, Director, Noncommunicable Diseases and Mental Health, WHO, Dr. Soren Brostrom, lamented that despite the discovery of insulin more than a century ago, many patients with type 1 diabetes still struggle to obtain affordable, quality treatment.

“Insulin is a lifesaving treatment, discovered more than 100 years ago. Yet many people with type 1 diabetes do not have access to affordable and high-quality insulin,” he said.

Brostrom said the guidelines would help countries deliver effective treatment, including in settings where resources were limited and health services disrupted.

WHO said it would support countries with practical tools and guidance to translate the recommendations into action and monitor progress, urging governments to involve people living with type 1 diabetes in designing, implementing and evaluating diabetes programmes.

The initiative is also expected to advance WHO’s global diabetes coverage target of ensuring universal access to affordable insulin treatment and blood glucose self-monitoring by 2030.

The 2026 World Diabetes Day is themed, “Early action on diabetes,” amid growing concerns over the rising global burden of the disease and its potentially devastating complications.

Diabetes can cause blindness, kidney failure, heart attacks, stroke and lower-limb amputation when not properly managed.

WHO said the global burden of diabetes had more than quadrupled since 1990, with an estimated 830 million people living with the condition worldwide in 2022, the majority of them having type 2 diabetes.

It added that more than 40 per cent of people living with diabetes globally were unaware they had the condition, leaving many undiagnosed and at risk of complications.

title: 20 make first class as ESUT graduates 7,149 students
description:
From Jude Chinedu, Enugu
The Enugu State University of Science and Technology (ESUT), Enugu, will graduate 7,149 students at its 22nd convocation ceremonies for the 2024/2025 academic session, with 20 of the graduands making First Class Honours.
The graduands comprise 5,635 first-degree recipients,
content:
From Jude Chinedu, Enugu

The Enugu State University of Science and Technology (ESUT), Enugu, will graduate 7,149 students at its 22nd convocation ceremonies for the 2024/2025 academic session, with 20 of the graduands making First Class Honours.

The graduands comprise 5,635 first-degree recipients, 298 Postgraduate Diploma holders, 811 master’s degree recipients and 405 doctoral degree candidates.

Of the first-degree graduands, 1,248 obtained Second Class Upper Division, 3,956 made Second Class Lower Division, while 177 graduated with Third Class and 237 fell into the pass or unclassified category.

The Vice-Chancellor, Professor Aloysius-Michaels Okolie, disclosed this on Monday during a press briefing ahead of the convocation ceremonies at the Peter Mbah Auditorium, ESUT.

He also announced Miss Marycynthia Cheluchi Ona of the Department of Medical Laboratory Sciences, Faculty of Allied Health Sciences, as the overall best graduand, with a Cumulative Grade Point Average (CGPA) of 4.85.

Anthony Judith Chisom of the Department of Psychology came second with 4.74 CGPA, while Nwobodo Chukwunonso of the Faculty of Pharmaceutical Sciences emerged third with 4.70 CGPA.

Okolie said the outstanding graduands would receive special recognition during the ceremonies.

He described the 2026 convocation as the fifth consecutive annual convocation organised by the present management since assuming office in April 2022.

He said the university had fulfilled its commitment to restoring the tradition of annual convocation as part of efforts to reposition the institution and improve its academic standing.

The Vice-Chancellor also disclosed that six ESUT Law graduates who attended the last Nigerian Law School recorded First Class results in their respective examinations.

On the institution’s academic expansion, he said the National Universities Commission (NUC) had approved eight new programmes, including Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, Software Engineering, Cyber Security, Intelligence and Security Studies, International Relations and Diplomacy, Religious Studies and Philosophy.

He added that the university had commenced admission into the programmes for the 2026/2027 academic session, while the Senate had approved the establishment of a Faculty of Computing.

Okolie further announced that the Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria had increased the admission quota for the university’s College of Medicine from 120 to 350, making it the second-highest in the country.

He said 19 of the 20 undergraduate programmes assessed by the NUC during its October/November 2025 accreditation exercise secured full accreditation, while Surveying and Geo-Informatics received interim accreditation.

The Vice-Chancellor also disclosed that the university had been selected to host a Tertiary Education Trust Fund (TETFund)/NUC Centre for Artificial Intelligence and Robotics.

The convocation lecture, scheduled for Thursday, November 19, will be delivered by the founder and former Governor of old Anambra State, Chief Jim Nwobodo.

Three eminent Nigerians, including Nwobodo, Robert Anwatu and Lady Betty Granville Akuvue, will also receive honorary doctorate degrees during the convocation.

title: One dies as herders clash with campaign convoy in Jigawa
description:
No fewer than two people have sustained injuries, and one person has died, following a clash between herders and a convoy of unidentified political campaign vehicles in Guri Local Government Area of Jigawa State.
Findings by our correspondent showed that the fatal incident occurred along the Abunabo
content:
No fewer than two people have sustained injuries, and one person has died, following a clash between herders and a convoy of unidentified political campaign vehicles in Guri Local Government Area of Jigawa State.

Findings by our correspondent showed that the fatal incident occurred along the Abunabo–Jangon Fulani Road, Kadira District, Guri LGA on Saturday, November 14, 2026, at about 1840 hours.

The incident comes amid increasing movement of campaign convoys and supporters of political parties across the state as campaign activities intensify by all political parties and their candidates ahead of the forthcoming 2027 general elections in the country.

It was gathered that the altercation broke out when the campaign convoy was passing through the area and encountered the herders, leading to an exchange that left three persons injured with arrows.

Confirming the incident in a statement made available to journalists in Dutse, the state capital, on Monday, the Public Relations Officer of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps, Jigawa State Command, Badaruddeen Tijjani, said the command received a distress call over the incident.

“One of the victims, identified as Ja’o Alh. Bura, a 25-year-old male from Gaduwa Settlement, later died from his injuries,” the Jigawa NSCDC PRO revealed.

He said the distress call was received from the Miyetti Allah Chairman of Musari Ward, Wakili Haruna, who reported the altercation involving the two parties.

Tijjani said that upon receipt of the report, a joint security patrol team promptly proceeded to the scene, adding that the affected persons were evacuated to Guri General Hospital for medical attention.

“Preliminary information revealed that three persons sustained injuries, reportedly inflicted with arrows, during the incident.

“Unfortunately, Ja’o Alh. Bura was subsequently confirmed dead by a medical doctor,” Tijjani said.

According to him, the corpse was photographed and released to his relatives for burial in accordance with Islamic rites.

Highlighting further, the PRO said the other two injured persons also received medical attention, with one treated and discharged.

“The other two were referred to the Federal Medical Centre, FMC, Nguru, for further medical attention,” Tijjani stated.

Accordingly, the NSCDC Jigawa PRO said the state Commandant, Kabiru Ingawa, expressed concern over the unfortunate incident.

He revealed that the commandant extended his condolences to the family of the deceased.

“The commandant called on all parties involved to remain calm, exercise restraint, and refrain from any action capable of escalating tensions or threatening public peace.

“The command wishes to assure members of the public that investigations are ongoing to establish the circumstances surrounding the altercation and the events that led to the fatality,” he added.

Moreover, the NSCDC Jigawa spokesperson disclosed that appropriate measures would be taken in collaboration with relevant security agencies to ensure the maintenance of peace and security in the area.

Efforts by our correspondent to identify the political party whose convoy was involved in the altercation proved abortive, as enquiries made to the Jigawa NSCDC spokesperson yielded no specific details, with the PRO maintaining that the investigation is still ongoing to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident.

The post One dies as herders clash with campaign convoy in Jigawa appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Oyebanji signs three laws, revises Ekiti ₦415.5bn budget
description:
By Rotimi Ojomoyela



ADO-EKITI – Ekiti State Governor, Biodun Oyebanji, has signed three new laws, including the 2026 Revised Appropriation Law, the Pension Reform (Second Amendment) Law and the Right of Way Law.







The laws were presented to the governor for assent in his office in Ado-Ekiti
content:
By Rotimi Ojomoyela

ADO-EKITI – Ekiti State Governor, Biodun Oyebanji, has signed three new laws, including the 2026 Revised Appropriation Law, the Pension Reform (Second Amendment) Law and the Right of Way Law.

The laws were presented to the governor for assent in his office in Ado-Ekiti by the Speaker of the State House of Assembly, Rt. Hon. Adeoye Aribasoye, following their passage by the legislature.

The 2026 Revised Appropriation Law retains the state’s total budget at ₦415.57 billion but adjusts the allocation between recurrent and capital expenditure.

Under the revised budget, recurrent expenditure increases from ₦221.87 billion to ₦268.76 billion, while capital expenditure decreases from ₦193.69 billion to ₦146.80 billion.

The adjustment represents a reallocation of funds from capital to recurrent expenditure to accommodate the state’s financial and operational obligations without increasing the overall budget approved in December 2025.

The revised appropriation is expected to sustain government operations while maintaining funding for infrastructure, social development, economic growth and institutional efficiency.

The second legislation, the Ekiti State Pension Reform (Second Amendment) Law, 2026 (No. 4 of 2026), amends the existing Pension Reform Law No. 3 of 2022 to formally accommodate the designation of a Director-General alongside the Permanent Secretary in the administrative and governance structure of the commission responsible for the Contributory Pension Scheme in the state.

The amendment also makes consequential adjustments to relevant provisions of the principal law, including the composition of the commission’s board, staff administration, remuneration and allowances.

The third legislation, the Ekiti State Right of Way Law, 2026 (No. 5 of 2026), establishes a regulatory framework for approving and administering permits for the installation and maintenance of telecommunications infrastructure in the state.

The law fixes the maximum Right of Way fee at ₦145 per linear metre for ducts and cables and ₦700,000 per site for a Base Transceiver Station.

It also requires telecommunications operators to comply with approved engineering standards, protect public safety and the environment, minimise damage to roads and public utilities, and restore affected infrastructure after installation.

The signing of the three laws underscores the Oyebanji administration’s efforts to strengthen public institutions, improve the regulatory environment for infrastructure development and ensure effective management of public resources.

title: Count me out of Awka kingship, says Jeff Nweke
description:
…Declares interest in governing Anambra State



By Vincent Ujumadu



AWKA – Former governorship candidate of the Action Alliance (AA) in the last Anambra State governorship election, Ozo Jeff Nweke, has dismissed speculation that he is interested in becoming the next traditional ruler of Awka King
content:
…Declares interest in governing Anambra State

By Vincent Ujumadu

AWKA – Former governorship candidate of the Action Alliance (AA) in the last Anambra State governorship election, Ozo Jeff Nweke, has dismissed speculation that he is interested in becoming the next traditional ruler of Awka Kingdom, declaring that he has no ambition to occupy the throne.

Nweke, a prominent indigene of Awka, said he was neither interested in becoming the traditional ruler nor a kingmaker, stressing that his political ambition was to govern Anambra State.

Addressing reporters in Awka, he said aspiring to become the traditional ruler would not serve his political interests or his desire to contribute to the development of his people.

He explained that speculations about his interest in the Eze Uzu Awka stool might have been fuelled by the construction of a large mansion, insisting that the size of his family informed the size of the property.

“I want to make it clear that I am not interested in Awka kingship. Some people are insinuating that because I am building a mansion in a very large compound, that I am planning to become Eze Uzu Awka. This is not true.

“I have a very large family. I am married to five wives and therefore someone who has up to 18 children should need a very large compound. It does not in any way mean that I am building a palace for Awka Kingdom,” he said.

On the lingering crisis surrounding the Awka traditional institution, Nweke said the community was in an unusual situation with two individuals claiming the traditional stool.

He identified the two as Eze Uzu II, whom he said was legitimately installed and recognised by the state government, and Eze Uzu III, who he said was also installed by the same kingmakers.

“We have Eze Uzu II, who was legitimately installed as the traditional ruler of Awka Kingdom, and we also have Eze Uzu III. Eze Uzu II is there and nobody will take it away from him, especially as he is recognised by the state government.

“Then we have Eze Uzu III, who was also legitimately installed by the same kingmakers who installed Eze Uzu II. However, since he is not recognised by government, what it means is that we have two kings in Awka,” he said.

Nweke argued that if Eze Uzu II, being the older of the two, died, Eze Uzu III would assume the position, adding that speculation about his own succession to the throne was unfounded.

He also pointed out that he came from the same village as the incumbent Eze Uzu II, saying there was no basis for him to aspire to succeed the traditional ruler.

“My ambition is to become the gubernatorial candidate of my party in the next political dispensation. I am a politician and I want to do something for my people, and being a traditional ruler won’t serve that purpose,” he stated.

Nweke, however, acknowledged that it was unusual for a community to have two traditional rulers at the same time.

“But if Awka people decide to have two kings, maybe they want one to be on standby,” he said.

He added that the installation of two traditional rulers suggested that there were issues that needed to be resolved within the traditional institution.

Nweke said the leadership of the Awka Development Union was trying to establish the circumstances that led to the situation, expressing hope that the matter would be resolved.

“I think that the leadership of Awka Development Union is trying to find out what really led to this abnormal situation. Until they unravel what really happened, we will continue with this abnormal situation,” he said.

title: 2027: Gwamna unveils manifesto, targets 100,000 jobs in Gombe
description:
…Promises 110 Agricultural Clusters, 50,000 SME Support, 10,000 Affordable Homes



…Targets 400,000 Out-of-School Children, 90% Digital Literacy by 2031



By Ben Ngwakwe, Gombe



The All Progressives Congress (APC) governorship candidate in Gombe State, Dr Jamilu Isyaku Gwamna, has unveiled a sev
content:
…Promises 110 Agricultural Clusters, 50,000 SME Support, 10,000 Affordable Homes

…Targets 400,000 Out-of-School Children, 90% Digital Literacy by 2031

By Ben Ngwakwe, Gombe

The All Progressives Congress (APC) governorship candidate in Gombe State, Dr Jamilu Isyaku Gwamna, has unveiled a seven-pillar development manifesto, promising to create 100,000 net new jobs, establish 110 agricultural clusters and support 50,000 small and medium-scale enterprises (SMEs) if elected governor in 2027.

Gwamna unveiled the manifesto, which he described as a covenant with the people of Gombe State, on Monday at the APC Square, Gombe, outlining an ambitious development agenda focused on economic transformation, human capital development, industrialisation, agriculture, technology and security.

The manifesto, tagged IMPACTS, covers seven key areas: infrastructure and essential services; manufacturing and industrialisation; people and human capital development; agriculture and rural transformation; commerce and trade; technology and digital inclusion; and security and environmental protection.

According to the APC candidate, each pillar contains specific commitments, measurable targets, implementation timelines and public accountability mechanisms to ensure that the proposed programmes translate into tangible benefits for residents.

He said his vision was to transform Gombe into Northern Nigeria’s leading agro-industrial and logistics hub, as well as a destination for conferences, tourism, hospitality and cultural activities, while positioning the state as a youth-driven centre for digital innovation.

Gwamna also promised to ensure that every child had access to quality education in a safe learning environment, while improving access to water, sanitation, drainage and erosion control.

Job creation and economic transformation

Outlining the economic targets, Gwamna said his administration would create 100,000 net new jobs within its proposed four-year tenure ending in 2031, alongside 50,000 indirect jobs in manufacturing and value chains.

He also pledged to generate 20,000 direct and indirect employment opportunities across the livestock value chain, with sector-based reporting mechanisms to ensure accurate documentation and avoid double counting.

In agriculture, he promised to establish 110 agricultural clusters, facilitate the creation of 100 dairy cooperatives and support 50,000 SMEs to stimulate production, entrepreneurship and wealth creation.

The APC candidate further pledged to deliver or facilitate 10,000 affordable housing units or serviced residential plots.

He also promised to ensure that every ward in the state had at least two fully functional and adequately equipped primary healthcare facilities.

To promote transparency, Gwamna said his administration would introduce quarterly public performance scorecards to enable citizens to monitor the implementation of government programmes and commitments.

Education and human capital development

On education, the governorship candidate identified teacher recruitment, professional development, school infrastructure and the reintegration of out-of-school children as major priorities.

He promised to recruit 1,000 new teachers within the first two years and provide training opportunities for 10,000 existing teachers to improve teaching standards and learning outcomes.

He also pledged to return 100,000 out-of-school children to the education system annually, targeting 400,000 over four years.

He said the programme would operate with an annual reporting framework to distinguish newly enrolled children from those retained from previous years.

Within two to three years of assuming office, Gwamna promised to construct an additional mega secondary school in each of the state’s three senatorial districts, alongside a new mega college in each zone.

He said technical and vocational colleges would be revived to equip young people with practical skills, while digital literacy programmes would be introduced across primary and secondary schools.

The initiative, he said, was designed to achieve at least 90 per cent digital literacy across the state by 2031.

He further pledged to upgrade at least 60 per cent of public basic schools and ensure that a minimum of 10,000 teachers benefited from training, mentorship or certification programmes.

According to him, the initiative would cover at least 80 per cent of the verified 2027 basic education teaching workforce, with a target of improving numeracy outcomes by at least 35 per cent from the 2027 baseline.

The manifesto also provides for tertiary education scholarships for at least 10,000 students from indigent households and support for 3,000 bonded students pursuing critical professional courses.

Additionally, Gwamna promised to introduce school feeding programmes for at least 25,000 children from disadvantaged households and extend education, healthcare, skills acquisition, feeding and livelihood-related social protection interventions to at least 200,000 vulnerable households.

APC leaders rally support

Speaking at the event, Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, represented by his Deputy, Dr Manassah Daniel Jatau, urged party members to complement prayers and political mobilisation with practical actions to secure victory for all APC candidates in the forthcoming general elections.

Jatau called on party faithful to intensify grassroots mobilisation and work collectively towards delivering the party at all levels, stressing the need to translate political support into electoral results.

Similarly, the APC State Chairman, Mohammed Dantata Ndu, charged party members to take responsibility for securing victory in their respective wards.

He urged them to mobilise voters and sustain the party’s political strength, arguing that the developmental achievements of the Inuwa Yahaya administration provided a basis for the APC to seek another mandate.

Also speaking, the Director-General of the Gwamna Campaign Council, Sa’ad Hassan, challenged opposition governorship candidates not to copy the manifesto unveiled by the APC candidate.

Hassan described Gwamna’s development blueprint as a continuation of the achievements and policy direction of the Inuwa Yahaya administration, saying the candidate’s programme was designed to consolidate existing gains while introducing additional development initiatives.

He expressed confidence that the manifesto would provide a framework for sustaining development and accelerating economic transformation in Gombe State.

title: Gas explosion rocks NNPC station in Lagos, damages school
description:
By Esther Onyegbula & Olasunkanmi Akoni







A gas explosion at a Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation (NNPC) filling station at Savannah Bus Stop, Command, Ejigbo, Lagos State, triggered a fire that spread to an adjoining school, damaging parts of its premises.







No casualty was recorded
content:
By Esther Onyegbula & Olasunkanmi Akoni

A gas explosion at a Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation (NNPC) filling station at Savannah Bus Stop, Command, Ejigbo, Lagos State, triggered a fire that spread to an adjoining school, damaging parts of its premises.

No casualty was recorded in the incident, which occurred at about 1 p.m., as the school, Saint Lawrence Greater Height School, was closed for the weekend.

The Controller-General of the Lagos State Fire and Rescue Service, Margaret Adeseye, confirmed the incident, saying the prompt intervention of firefighters prevented the fire from spreading to other sections of the school and causing further damage.

Adeseye said the agency received a distress call at 12:50 p.m. and arrived at the scene at 1:13 p.m. following reports of an explosion and an ensuing fire at the filling station.

She said firefighters from the Ejigbo, Ikeja and Bolade fire stations were immediately deployed to the scene to contain the blaze and prevent it from spreading to neighbouring buildings.

According to her, the intensity of the explosion caused the fire to spread rapidly from the filling station to the adjoining school, affecting parts of the institution’s premises.

She, however, said the firefighters worked collaboratively to bring the situation under control and prevented the fire from engulfing other sections of the school.

“No casualty was recorded in the incident,” Adeseye stated.

She added that preliminary investigations had commenced to establish the circumstances surrounding the explosion.

The incident has renewed concerns over the safety risks associated with gas-related operations at filling stations, particularly facilities located close to schools and other public institutions.

The fire service urged members of the public to remain safety-conscious as investigations into the cause of the explosion continue.

title: Gunmen burn seven houses in Plateau community
description:
…Council chairman condemns attack, promises support for victims



By Golok Nanmwa



JOS – Gunmen have burnt down seven houses in Bong community, Doemak District of Qua’an-Pan Local Government Area of Plateau State, in a fresh attack that has heightened concerns over insecurity in the state.
content:
…Council chairman condemns attack, promises support for victims

By Golok Nanmwa

JOS – Gunmen have burnt down seven houses in Bong community, Doemak District of Qua’an-Pan Local Government Area of Plateau State, in a fresh attack that has heightened concerns over insecurity in the state.

The attack, which occurred at about 9 p.m. on Sunday, November 15, 2026, reportedly coincided with an assault by suspected terrorists on Zwagal community in Jipal District of neighbouring Mangu Local Government Area, where several people were killed.

A community source, Mr Silas Bishop, who confirmed the incident, said the attackers stormed Bong community and set seven houses ablaze.

Bishop described the attack as unfortunate and called on security agencies to intensify efforts to track down and arrest those responsible.

He also urged the authorities to strengthen surveillance and deploy more security personnel to the community to prevent further attacks.

Confirming the incident, the Executive Chairman of Qua’an-Pan Local Government Council, Hon. (Dr.) Christopher Audu Manship, condemned the attack and assured residents that the government would not abandon them.

Manship, in a statement signed by his Director of Press and Publicity, Danaan Cletus Sylvanus, on Monday, gave the assurance during an on-the-spot assessment of the destruction in Bong community.

He said the government was committed to protecting lives and property across the state.

“Government will not abandon the people of Bong community. We will support efforts towards the restoration of the houses destroyed and sustain measures to secure the community against further attacks,” he said.

The council chairman also visited Zwagal community in Mangu Local Government Area alongside his Mangu counterpart, Hon. Emmanuel Bala Mwolpun, where he condemned the killing of residents.

Describing the attack as barbaric and inhuman, Manship said every human life was precious and that the loss of lives had left lasting pain on the affected families.

“The government will intensify efforts to secure lives and property, which remains the primary responsibility of every government,” he said.

He urged youths in the affected communities to remain vigilant and promptly report suspicious movements to security agencies for necessary action.

Manship also said Governor Caleb Mutfwang remained determined to tackle insecurity in Plateau State, adding that the state government was committed to strengthening security measures.

He conveyed the governor’s condolences to the bereaved families and residents of Zwagal, while praying for the repose of the souls of those killed.

Also speaking, the Mangu Local Government Chairman, Hon. Emmanuel Bala Mwolpun, assured residents that efforts were being made to improve network services in the affected communities to enhance security surveillance and communication.

Earlier, the Long Zwagal, Miskagam Jonathan Wadong, thanked the two council chairmen for their prompt response and mobilisation of security personnel following the attack.

Wadong said the attackers struck at about 8 p.m., adding that residents heard gunshots before the assailants invaded the community.

title: Atiku mocks presidency over alleged AI-generated rally crowds
description:
By Luminous Jannamike



ABUJA – Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has taken a swipe at President Bola Tinubu over allegations of using artificial intelligence (AI) to create images of campaign crowds, insisting that the massive reception he received in Potiskum, Yobe State, was genuine.







A
content:
By Luminous Jannamike

ABUJA – Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has taken a swipe at President Bola Tinubu over allegations of using artificial intelligence (AI) to create images of campaign crowds, insisting that the massive reception he received in Potiskum, Yobe State, was genuine.

Atiku said the reception reflected growing public interest in the African Democratic Congress (ADC)’s Affordable Life campaign, while commending the Yobe State governor for allowing the opposition party to campaign freely in the state.

In a statement on Monday by his Director of Strategic Communication, Phrank Shaibu, the former vice president expressed gratitude to residents of Potiskum and Yobe State for the warm reception that greeted his arrival from Azare, Bauchi State.

He described the reception as overwhelming, saying the turnout and enthusiasm of residents would remain memorable.

“The welcome from the moment we entered Potiskum from Azare was simply breathtaking. The sea of heads, the joyful faces, the chants and the warmth of the people will remain in my heart,” he said.

Commending the governor for providing an opportunity for the ADC to engage voters, Atiku said equal access to the electorate was essential to democratic competition.

“Democracy is strengthened when every party can meet the people freely and present its message. We appreciate the opportunity to bring our vision to Yobe,” he said.

However, taking a swipe at Tinubu, Atiku suggested that the Presidency needed artificial intelligence to create the impression of large campaign crowds, insisting that the supporters who welcomed him in Potiskum were physically present.

“The Presidency may need artificial intelligence to conjure a crowd, but in Potiskum the people came out in flesh and blood, unfiltered, unedited and impossible to fabricate.

“Our Affordable Life campaign needs no artificial crowd; the people’s presence and their voices speak for themselves,” he said.

He further mocked the alleged use of AI-generated images, saying: “The Presidency’s AI must have forgotten that crowds need seats and that people do not fly. Perhaps in Tinubu’s imaginary rally, the supporters were expected to hover through the speech.”

On the significance of the “Tinubu Must Go” chants at ADC rallies, Atiku described them as expressions of the people’s desire for change and a reminder of the responsibility that comes with securing their mandate.

“The ADC’s Affordable Life campaign is not mere sloganeering. When I hear the crowd chanting ‘Tinubu Must Go’ at our rallies, I take those words personally.

“They are a call for change and a reminder of the responsibility that will come with the people’s mandate,” he said.

Atiku pledged to prioritise making life affordable for Nigerians if elected president in the January 16, 2027 presidential election.

He said his administration would take immediate steps to address the cost-of-living challenges facing Nigerians after Tinubu leaves office on May 29, 2027.

“When President Tinubu leaves office on 29 May 2027, good governance and an affordable life must follow.

“I solemnly pledge to take immediate steps to make life affordable again when elected president at the January 16 presidential election. That is my promise to our teeming supporters,” he said.

The post Atiku mocks presidency over alleged AI-generated rally crowds appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: UEFA backs France’s Diallo to stand against Infantino in FIFA election
description:
European football’s governing body UEFA has given its “unanimous” backing to French Football Federation chief Philippe Diallo to stand against incumbent Gianni Infantino in March’s FIFA presidential election, it said in a statement Monday.



The body said that Diallo had been “invited…to stand as a
content:
European football’s governing body UEFA has given its “unanimous” backing to French Football Federation chief Philippe Diallo to stand against incumbent Gianni Infantino in March’s FIFA presidential election, it said in a statement Monday.

The body said that Diallo had been “invited…to stand as a candidate in the FIFA presidential election in March 2027” and that European national associations had “unanimously pledged their full support”.

The deadline for rival candidates to declare themselves is this Wednesday, November 18.

UEFA, which boasts 55 member associations, said Diallo “has accepted the invitation to stand” and that his candidature is set to be confirmed at a meeting of the French federation (FFF) on Tuesday.

Under its Slovenian president Aleksander Ceferin, UEFA has led the opposition to Infantino since his announcement in late July of a project to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors.

Infantino quickly abandoned the proposal in the face of widespread uproar, but UEFA has since gone to a court in Florida in an attempt to gather evidence for a potential complaint of “criminal mismanagement” against the FIFA president in Switzerland.

UEFA had been struggling to find a credible candidate to stand against Infantino in the election, which will take place at the FIFA Congress on March 18 next year in the Moroccan capital, Rabat.

– Wenger not in running –

Arsene Wenger, the French former Arsenal manager and FIFA’s current chief of global football development, had been seen as a potential candidate that could get Europe’s backing.

One source within football governance said that Wenger had been UEFA’s “Plan A” and that Diallo had never been seen as a solution before it became clear the ex-Arsenal boss would not be a candidate.

CONCACAF chief Victor Montagliani had previously been mooted as a candidate, but the Canadian later announced his desire to stand for a new term as the head of his confederation, which covers North and Central America and the Caribbean.

The Asian Football Confederation, which consists of 47 member associations, announced last month that it was backing Infantino for re-election.

Diallo said in September that the FFF was withdrawing its backing for Infantino in the election, following similar announcements from other European associations.

“We believe that the trust placed in the FIFA president has been betrayed, and that the way in which the governance of world football is envisaged no longer reflects us,” he said at the time.

Diallo, the 63-year-old son of a Senegalese boxing champion, has been president of the FFF since January 2023.

He was initially appointed to the post on an interim basis when previous chief Noel Le Graet was forced to stand down following a series of controversies.

Diallo, from Saint-Nazaire on France’s Atlantic coast, was then elected to the role by a large majority in June of that year, before being re-elected in December 2024 for a new four-year term.

Kozo Tashima, honorary president of the Japan Football Association and a member of the FIFA Council, said at the start of this month that he also intended to stand against Infantino.

Swiss former Tottenham Hotspur defender Ramon Vega has also stated his intention to run for the top job at world football’s governing body.

Infantino, a former UEFA secretary general, has been in charge of FIFA since 2016.

At the weekend Germany coach Jurgen Klopp added his voice to the calls for a new leader at the helm of FIFA.

“I’ve been following football for many years. There are people who are much more knowledgeable about this than I am. But I think most people now agree a change would make a lot of sense,” said the former Liverpool manager.

title: Tinubu’s reforms painful but necessary – Abbas
description:
The Speaker of the House of Representatives, Tajudeen Abbas, has acknowledged the economic hardship confronting Nigerians, describing the ongoing reforms of President Bola Tinubu’s administration as difficult but necessary to address longstanding structural weaknesses in the economy.
Abbas, however,
content:
The Speaker of the House of Representatives, Tajudeen Abbas, has acknowledged the economic hardship confronting Nigerians, describing the ongoing reforms of President Bola Tinubu’s administration as difficult but necessary to address longstanding structural weaknesses in the economy.

Abbas, however, said the Federal Government must ensure that the benefits of the reforms translate into tangible improvements in the living conditions of ordinary Nigerians.

The Speaker spoke on Monday during a panel session titled “Misinformation and Social Cohesion: Rebuilding Trust through Responsible Public Relations” at the Global Alliance World Public Relations Forum in Abuja.

He was represented at the event by the House Majority Leader, Prof. Julius Ihonvbere.

The forum brought together communication experts, public relations practitioners and global industry leaders to examine the changing responsibilities of the profession amid the growing influence of digital technology and the spread of misinformation.

Acknowledging the economic difficulties facing the country, Abbas said the challenges confronting households and businesses were real and deserved serious attention.

According to him, the economic situation should also be understood against the backdrop of global economic pressures and longstanding structural weaknesses in Nigeria’s economy.

He said, “The difficulties confronting households and businesses are real and deserve serious attention. These difficulties must also be understood within the wider context of global economic pressures and long-standing structural weaknesses in our national economy.

“The reforms being pursued by the administration of President Bola Tinubu are aimed at addressing some of these weaknesses, restoring economic stability, and laying the foundation for sustainable growth.

“These reforms are neither easy nor without immediate costs. The challenge before government is to ensure that their benefits translate into tangible improvements in the lives of ordinary Nigerians.”

Tinubu announced the removal of the petrol subsidy in his inaugural address on May 29, 2023, shortly after taking office.

The government subsequently harmonised and floated the foreign exchange market, triggering significant adjustments in petrol prices and exchange rates, with consequential effects on the cost of living and doing business.

Abbas said the government must also address the country’s security challenges through sustained action, accountability and stronger security institutions.

“Our security challenges equally demand decisive and sustained action. Every innocent life lost today is a tragedy that calls for justice and accountability.

“We must remain resolute in confronting those responsible, strengthening our security institutions, and protecting every Nigerian, irrespective of religion, ethnicity, or place of origin,” he said.

The Speaker also highlighted the role of the National Assembly in strengthening democratic institutions, promoting accountability and addressing the country’s developmental challenges.

He said the House of Representatives, through its 360 members, had a responsibility to ensure that the interests and concerns of Nigerians were reflected in national decision-making.

Abbas said the House had pursued an eight-point legislative agenda covering good governance, national security, economic growth and development, education, healthcare, social inclusion, institutional strengthening and an open Parliament.

He listed the proposed establishment of state police and the Reserved Seats for Women Bill among the constitutional and legislative initiatives being pursued by the House.

Earlier in his speech, the Chairman, Senate Committee on Capital Market, Senator Osita Isiguzo, called for the regulation of artificial intelligence, warning that the technology could become dangerous if its misuse was left unchecked.

Isiguzo said although AI offered significant opportunities, its capacity to generate convincing images and other forms of manipulated content posed a threat to information integrity.

“AI is a major issue right now, and you know, globally, AI is not regulated in most climes just like when new media started, most jurisdictions did not find it necessary to regulate the new media except now that we are now saying, no, we cannot allow our children to have access to all manner of social media platforms. But we started late.

“As a parliamentarian, I’m also of the opinion that AI must be regulated before AI will destroy the world,” he said.

He added, “Now, when you see AI images, they look so real that sometimes you might not be able to discover which is AI and which is real. Don’t get me wrong, AI is good, but it has to be regulated before the goodness of AI becomes the calamity of the world.”

Also speaking, the President and Chief Executive Officer, Global Alliance for Public Relations and Communication Management, Prof. Justin Green, highlighted the growing representation of Africa in the organisation’s leadership.

The post Tinubu’s reforms painful but necessary – Abbas appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Police arrest 8 over APC, NDC clash in Kano
description:
The Kano State Police Command has arrested eight suspects following a clash between supporters of the All Progressives Congress (APC) and the New Democratic Congress (NDC) in Bichi Local Government Area of the state.







The command’s spokesman, CSP Abdullahi Kiyawa, disclosed this in a statement
content:
The Kano State Police Command has arrested eight suspects following a clash between supporters of the All Progressives Congress (APC) and the New Democratic Congress (NDC) in Bichi Local Government Area of the state.

The command’s spokesman, CSP Abdullahi Kiyawa, disclosed this in a statement on Monday in Kano, saying the incident occurred at about 4:45 p.m. on Sunday.

He said the clash resulted in the destruction of campaign banners, billboards and vehicles, while some persons sustained injuries.

According to him, police operatives were immediately deployed to the area after receiving reports of the incident and successfully restored normalcy.

Kiyawa disclosed that 13 vehicles were vandalised during the clash, while five injured persons were taken to hospital for treatment.

Items recovered by the police included one Gariyo, two cutlasses, two hard sticks, a bottle of solution and a substance locally known as “Suck and Die”.

He quoted the Commissioner of Police, Ibrahim Bakori, as condemning the violence and destruction of campaign materials by political supporters.

Bakori warned that the command would not tolerate any act capable of disrupting public peace before, during or after the political season.

He urged political leaders and their supporters to conduct their activities peacefully and in accordance with the law.

The police spokesman said the eight suspects had been transferred to the State Criminal Investigation Department (SCID) for discreet investigation.

He added that the suspects would be charged to court upon completion of the investigation.

Kiyawa urged political leaders, party supporters and members of the public to shun violence and report suspicious activities to the nearest police station.

He said the area remained relatively calm, while police monitoring continued.

title: Abaribe urges leaders to embrace Azikiwe’s ideals
description:
The Senator representing Abia South Senatorial Zone, Enyinnaya Abaribe, has said towering leadership, radical change of mindset backed by a clear philosophy and re-orientation can lead to sustainable development in Nigeria and across Africa.
Abaribe said 30 years after the death of Nigeria’s first P
content:
The Senator representing Abia South Senatorial Zone, Enyinnaya Abaribe, has said towering leadership, radical change of mindset backed by a clear philosophy and re-orientation can lead to sustainable development in Nigeria and across Africa.

Abaribe said 30 years after the death of Nigeria’s first President and nationalist, Dr Nnamdi Azikiwe, many countries in Africa, especially Nigeria, were still in an unending search for leadership anchored on firm principles which Azikiwe had championed over 50 years ago.

He stated this on Monday at the 14th Annual Zik Lecture Series with the theme, ‘Zik’s vision for Renaissance: Lessons from emerging economies in Africa’, held at the Secretariat Complex of the Academic Staff Union of Universities, Nnamdi Azikiwe University, Awka, Anambra State.

The annual Zik’s lecture series is in honour of Nigeria’s first President and nationalist, the late Dr Nnamdi Azikiwe.

In the series, Zik’s virtues, leadership, legacies and love for the development of Nigeria and Africa are highlighted.

Abaribe, who gave the keynote address at the event, noted that the greatest problem facing Nigeria was leadership, adding that the late Azikiwe was a great nationalist, whose virtues, leadership and legacies should be imbibed for sustainable growth in the country.

He also listed uncensored exposure to social media, breakdown of family structure, unilateral focus of schools on grades and glorification of ill-gotten wealth as some of the key factors responsible for moral decadence in the country today.

He said, “For many people from my generation, Zik represents what towering leadership backed by a clear philosophy is about.

“For Zik, leadership was not just about political power, but mainly about using every available arsenal such as education, re-orientation, call for freedom, infrastructural development and precocious vision to direct the trajectory of the people.

“This, for me, is what leadership should be about. It is to our disadvantage that decades after the great Zik left this world, many countries in Africa, especially Nigeria, are still in an unending search for leadership anchored on the firm principles which Zik had championed over half a century ago.

“One critical thing which framed Zik’s vision and which became the motto of his West Africa Pilot was Dante Alighieri’s ‘show the light, and the people will find the way.

“Some of the things that have led us to where we are today are uncensored exposure to social media, breakdown of family structure, unilateral focus of schools on grades and glorification of ill-gotten wealth. Today, we glorify ill-gotten wealth.

“A society that applauds sudden wealth without questioning is losing its moral values. This is the greatest danger that Nigeria is facing today. If you reward integrity, you will produce statesmen.”

Addressing the students, the Senator advised them that the purpose of education is for them to have the value so that when they are given their certificate, they would be found to be worthy in character and learning.

“This was what the great Zik propounded many years ago, but today, education doesn’t seem to translate into moral values. We can lament how our young ones are drifting away, but we ought to know that what is happening today is a manner by which the young ones are learning from their leaders.

“State capture is a systematic capture of the institution of the state, not towards a public interest, but the interest of a few. The Nigerian state is gradually becoming an enterprise for a few. Policies, justice and interventions cannot be for a few, it must be for all.

“If we continue as we are doing, we would have entrenched immorality as a part of government, and we may no longer be able to correct it, when immorality will be the norm.

“Azikiwe understood that values make a man and therefore, he insisted that we must at all times put education and moral values first in making Nigeria get to that position it aspires to be. We must ensure that we imbibe the virtues of discipline, morality, and character. We must follow Zik’s footsteps to ensure that,” Abaribe added.

Also speaking, the Benefactor, Zik Lecture Series, Senator Ben Obi, said he took the initiative to establish the lecture series as a modest but purposeful contribution to the preservation and promotion of the ideals of Dr Nnamdi Azikiwe.

Obi said Zik was not merely a political leader, but a nationalist and advocate of African emancipation who understood that the liberation of a people must begin with the liberation of their minds through education, critical thinking, civic consciousness and responsible leadership in building a strong and prosperous nation.

He eulogised the late Azikiwe, saying he fought to ensure Nigeria remained one.

Earlier, in his welcome address, the Vice Chancellor, UNIZIK, Prof. Ugochukwu Anyaehie, said over the years, the Zik lecture series has established itself as a premier intellectual forum for interrogating critical socio-political, economic, and developmental issues affecting Nigeria and the African continent.

According to the VC, the 14th edition, alongside the school’s convocation ceremonies, is a reminder that a university is not merely a centre for the award of degrees, but a crucible of ideas designed to illuminate the path toward societal transformation.

“The theme chosen for this year’s lecture is both timely and deeply resonant. Long before the modern discourse on African economic integration and self-reliance gained global traction, Dr Nnamdi Azikiwe articulated a bold philosophy of Renascent Africa.

“He envisioned a continent liberated not only from political subjugation, but also from economic dependency, intellectual stagnation and social fragmentation.

“Zik believed firmly in the capacity of the African mind to innovate, to build resilient institutions and to harness indigenous resources for collective prosperity.

“Today, several emerging economies across Africa are demonstrating what is possible when visionary leadership, institutional discipline, investment in human capital, and strategic economic diversification converge.

\”From rapid strides in digital innovation and renewable energy to infrastructural renewal and regional trade integration, these economies offer practical lessons that align remarkably with Zik’s foundational ideals,” the VC added.

The post Abaribe urges leaders to embrace Azikiwe’s ideals appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Infantino worse than Blatter, says Klopp
description:
Former Liverpool manager Jurgen Klopp has launched a strong criticism of FIFA president Gianni Infantino, claiming that football’s governing body needs new leadership and suggesting that things have become worse under him than during Sepp Blatter’s tenure.
Blatter resigned as FIFA president in 2015
content:
Former Liverpool manager Jurgen Klopp has launched a strong criticism of FIFA president Gianni Infantino, claiming that football’s governing body needs new leadership and suggesting that things have become worse under him than during Sepp Blatter’s tenure.

Blatter resigned as FIFA president in 2015 amid a corruption scandal and was succeeded by Infantino in February 2016.

However, Infantino has recently faced growing criticism over his proposed FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) plan, which included selling stakes in the World Cup and other FIFA competitions to private investors.

As reported by BBC Sport on Monday, speaking about the controversy, Klopp said he believed a change of leadership at FIFA would be beneficial to world football.

“I’ve been following football for many years. There are people who are much more knowledgeable about this than I am. But I think most people now agree a change would make a lot of sense.

“I didn’t think things could get worse after Sepp Blatter, but someone has managed to do just that,” Klopp said.

The former Borussia Dortmund and Liverpool manager added that FIFA needed someone new to take charge.

“Regarding Gianni Infantino, surely the next person to come along can do a better job,” he said.

Infantino has apologised to the FIFA Council over the FFE proposal but has faced calls to release all relevant documents and answer questions surrounding the plan.

Meanwhile, UEFA has backed French Football Federation president Philippe Diallo as its candidate to challenge Infantino in the upcoming FIFA presidential election.

Diallo received unanimous support from UEFA’s executive committee, with formal ratification from the French Football Federation expected on Tuesday.

UEFA has repeatedly criticised Infantino’s leadership and called for renewed unity and trust within the global football community.

Former Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger, who serves as FIFA’s head of global development, had reportedly considered challenging Infantino but has decided against entering the race.

Former Tottenham defender Ramon Vega and Japan Football Association honorary president Kozo Tashima have also expressed interest in contesting the presidency.

Klopp believes FIFA needs a leader whose priorities go beyond financial interests.

“There are people who truly care about the future of football – people who aren’t driven by financial interests,” he said.

“If someone like that were to step up – if someone like that were to become president – I think that would be a significant improvement.

“There are surely people who care deeply about the future of football and have no financial interests in it.”
