title: Tinubu: 1,000 terrorists convicted, 2,000 prosecuted
description:
By Kingsley Omonobi



President Bola Tinubu has disclosed that more than 1,000 terrorists have been convicted, while over 2,000 suspected terrorists are currently undergoing prosecution as part of his administration’s efforts to dismantle terrorist networks across the country.







The President
content:
By Kingsley Omonobi

President Bola Tinubu has disclosed that more than 1,000 terrorists have been convicted, while over 2,000 suspected terrorists are currently undergoing prosecution as part of his administration’s efforts to dismantle terrorist networks across the country.

The President also said Nigerian security forces had killed or arrested four of eight identified senior global terrorist leaders, describing the development as evidence of the country’s growing capacity to dismantle terrorist command structures.

Tinubu, who was represented by the National Security Adviser, Mallam Nuhu Ribadu, made the disclosures on Monday at the opening of the 2026 Chief of Defence Intelligence (CDI) Annual Conference in Abuja.

He said the number of convictions and ongoing prosecutions placed Nigeria among countries with high rates of terrorism-related prosecutions globally.

Highlighting the operational successes recorded by security agencies, the President cited the elimination of senior Islamic State leader, Abu Bilal al-Minuki, in May 2026, as well as the arrests of other prominent terrorist figures.

According to him, the operations also targeted Ahmed Ohida’s ISWAP southern expansion network, while Abu Barra of Ansaru and Mamuda of Mahmudawa were arrested in 2025.

“Recent operational successes demonstrate our growing capacity to dismantle terrorist leadership, disrupt expansion networks and deny violent groups freedom of action.

“Under this administration, four of eight identified senior terrorist leaders have been killed or arrested. These gains include action against Ahmed Ohida’s ISWAP southern expansion network, the elimination of senior Islamic State leader Abu Bilal al-Minuki in May 2026, and the arrests of Abu Barra of Ansaru and Mamuda of Mahmudawa in 2025,” he said.

Tinubu, however, identified the remaining four senior terrorist figures as Ba Shuwa of ISWAP, Abdullahi Oro of IS-Sahel, Sadiku of JAS in the North-Central region and Bakura Doro in the Lake Chad Basin.

He said security agencies were sustaining operations against the remaining leaders and their networks, adding that senior bandit leaders, including Halilu Sububu, had also been killed alongside several of their fighters.

On developments in the Niger Delta, the President disclosed that incidents of illegal oil bunkering and vandalism of critical oil and gas installations declined from 32 in the first quarter of 2026 to 21 in the second quarter and 17 in the third quarter.

He said the figures represented a 46.88 per cent reduction between the first and third quarters.

Tinubu added that crude oil and condensate production averaged approximately 1.68 million barrels per day in August 2026, stressing the need to sustain the protection of the country’s energy assets and revenue sources.

He attributed the security gains to improved intelligence sharing and coordinated operations among the Department of State Services (DSS), Armed Forces, Police and other security agencies.

The President said the administration would consolidate the gains and sustain pressure on criminal and terrorist networks, particularly ahead of the 2027 general elections.

“Every Nigerian must be able to live, work and exercise their democratic rights in safety,” he said.

On the changing nature of security threats, Tinubu said technological advancements, particularly artificial intelligence, machine learning, cyber capabilities and unmanned systems, were creating new opportunities for intelligence gathering and security operations.

He said such technologies could help security agencies detect patterns, map criminal networks and generate early warnings of potential threats.

The President called for the integration of AI-assisted analysis, geospatial intelligence and unmanned surveillance through secure and interoperable systems capable of translating information into timely operational decisions.

He, however, cautioned that artificial intelligence outputs must be verified through accountable human judgement, while data protection and cybersecurity safeguards must be incorporated into the systems.

“Technology must strengthen the trusted human intelligence on which effective security depends,” he said.

Tinubu further disclosed that he had directed the Special Adviser on Homeland Security, Major General A.A. Famadewa (rtd), to coordinate the preparation of a Comprehensive National Threat Assessment and a Five-Year Rolling Strategic Defence Operations Plan.

He said the initiative was aimed at placing accurate, integrated and forward-looking intelligence at the centre of Nigeria’s defence planning.

The President also emphasised the importance of collaboration among the Armed Forces, Defence Intelligence Agency, DSS, National Intelligence Agency, Nigeria Police Force, Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps and other relevant institutions.

He said intelligence cooperation must extend to regional and international partners, subnational entities, technology companies and research institutions.

Tinubu listed the United States, France, the United Kingdom, China, the United Arab Emirates, Türkiye and Nigeria’s African neighbours among countries with which his administration had strengthened security partnerships.

He pledged to deepen intelligence sharing, training and technological cooperation while safeguarding Nigeria’s sovereignty and national interest.

The President also urged Nigeria’s Defence Advisers and Attachés abroad to strengthen strategic intelligence and defence relationships with their host countries and international partners.

He called on State Office Coordinators to intensify collaboration with local security agencies to improve intelligence gathering and coordination.

Tinubu commended the Chief of Defence Intelligence, Lieutenant General Emmanuel Akomaye Parker Undiandeye, and his team for their leadership and contributions to strengthening defence intelligence and strategic cooperation.

In his remarks, the Minister of Defence, retired General Christopher Musa, commended intelligence personnel for their professionalism and contributions to national security.

Musa urged them to remain proactive, stressing that credible, timely and actionable intelligence was critical to successful military operations.

He also reaffirmed the Federal Government’s commitment to indigenous defence production, describing local manufacturing as essential to developing sustainable military capabilities.

Similarly, the Chief of Defence Staff, General Olufemi Oluyede, described intelligence as fundamental to operational planning, strategic decision-making and effective military responses.

Oluyede called for increased investment in artificial intelligence, advanced data analytics, geospatial intelligence and unmanned systems.

He said the Armed Forces would continue to prioritise intelligence integration, capacity development and technological innovation.

The CDS stressed the need to shift security operations from largely reactive responses to proactive, intelligence-led engagements capable of anticipating and disrupting threats before they materialise.

The conference, organised by the Defence Intelligence Agency, is themed, “Optimising Intelligence through Technological Innovations for Effective Strategic Operations in a Complex Security Environment.”

Vanguard Newspaper

title: UniAbuja land cut approved by Wike’s predecessor – FCTA
description:
The Federal Capital Territory Administration has defended its decision to reduce the land allocated to the University of Abuja, saying the action was based on recommendations made by a joint committee established in 2016 by the administration of former FCT Minister Mohammed Bello.
The FCTA said the
content:
The Federal Capital Territory Administration has defended its decision to reduce the land allocated to the University of Abuja, saying the action was based on recommendations made by a joint committee established in 2016 by the administration of former FCT Minister Mohammed Bello.

The FCTA said the committee, comprising representatives of the administration and the university, had recommended that the institution’s landholding of over 11,000 hectares be reduced to 100 hectares in line with the National Universities Commission’s recommended size for universities.

The administration’s position followed a protest by the university’s academic and non-academic staff, students and alumni on Monday over the reduction of its original 11,824.04 hectares of land to 4,685 hectares by the administration of the incumbent FCT Minister, Nyesom Wike.

In a statement issued on Monday by the minister’s Senior Special Assistant on Public Communications and Social Media, Lere Olayinka, the FCTA described the protest as misplaced, insisting that Wike merely implemented a decision taken by his predecessor.

According to the statement, the joint committee was inaugurated on November 10, 2016, to examine the university’s land size, encroachment by indigenous settlers, illegal developments around its Gwagwalada mini-campus and the issuance of title documents for the institution’s two campuses.

Olayinka disclosed that five of the committee’s 12 members were representatives of the university, namely Prof Otaki Alanana, Prof A. Mallam, Mohamed Kassim, A.E. Ripite and Sadiq O. Shuaibu.

He said the committee subsequently recommended that the university’s landholding of over 11,000 hectares was far beyond the size recommended by the NUC, adding that the 100-hectare recommendation was approved by Bello.

“It is on record that on November 10, 2016, the then FCT Minister inaugurated a Joint Committee of FCTA and UNIABUJA on Land and Sundry Issues. The committee was to look into the UNIABUJA land size vis encroachment by indigenous settlers, encroachment on the Gwagwalada Mini Campus land by illegal developers and issuance of titles for the two campuses of the university with their actual land size.

“The committee recommended, amongst others, that the land area of over 11,000 hectares of the main campus was far beyond the recommended size by the National University Commission (NUC), and that the recommended size of 100 hectares by the NUC be given to the university.

“Report of the committee was approved by the immediate past FCT Minister, Mohammed Musa Bello, and going by the committee’s recommendation, only 100 hectares of land ought to be given to UNIABUJA,” the statement partly read.

Olayinka, however, said Wike approved 4,519.80 hectares for the university, rather than the 100 hectares recommended by the committee.

It added that the retained land could accommodate more than 80,000 buildings, using a plot size of 500 square metres.

The FCTA also accused the university of allocating portions of its land to individuals and corporate organisations without consulting the administration, citing the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission as one of the beneficiaries.

The statement questioned the rationale behind the university’s insistence on retaining more than 11,000 hectares, asking what significant expansion the institution had undertaken in its 38 years of existence to justify such a land requirement.

“Questions to ask the protesters, particularly the Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU), Senior Staff Association of Nigerian Universities (SSANU), Non-Academic Staff Union of Educational and Associated Institutions (NASU), Students’ Union Government (SUG) and the university’s alumni association are; were they unaware that the university had representatives in the committee that recommended the reduction of the UNIABUJA land to 100 hectares in line with the NUC recommendation?

“Where in the civilised world is a university built on over 11,000 hectares of land, on which over 220,000 houses can be built at 500 square meters per plot?

“If the government that owns a university chooses to reduce the size of its land on which no structure has been built in the school’s 38 years of existence, what effect will that have on ASUU, SSANU and NASU? Will that affect the payment of their salaries? Will it affect the students in terms of their studies?,” Olayinka asked.

The media aide urged the academic unions to be honest and clarify their interest in a land dispute between the administration and the management.

The FCTA’s defence comes amid an escalating dispute between the administration and the university community over the ownership, control and proposed redistribution of portions of the institution’s land in Giri District, Abuja.

The controversy dates back to June 2025, when Wike announced that the administration had reclaimed about 7,000 hectares of land from the university, accusing the institution of laying claim to an extensive portion of government land without adequate documentation.

At the inauguration of access roads in Giri District, the minister directed relevant agencies to carve out about 4,000 hectares for the university, while the remaining portions would be made available for other developments.

Wike had argued that the university could not retain such an extensive landholding without developing it, particularly as the FCTA sought to open up the district for infrastructure and institutional development.

However, the university’s management and ASUU have maintained that the original land allocation was legitimate and necessary for the institution’s long-term development, including academic expansion, agricultural research and other infrastructure.

The university’s Pro-Chancellor, Senator Olanrewaju Tejuoso, had also argued that much of the land left for the institution comprised rocky hills, raising questions about the actual amount of land available for development.

The dispute has also taken a legal dimension, with the university instituting Suit No. FCT/HC/CV/3500/2026 before the High Court of the Federal Capital Territory, Maitama.

In the suit, Justice F.E. Messiri, on August 18, 2026, reportedly ordered parties to maintain the status quo ante bellum concerning Plot No. 1, Giri District, pending the determination of the substantive matter.

ASUU has subsequently accused the FCTA of violating the court order through alleged allocations of portions of the disputed land to private individuals and companies on September 26, 2026.

The post UniAbuja land cut approved by Wike’s predecessor – FCTA appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: INEC debunks claim of remote BVAS log-out before voting ends
description:
The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has dismissed as false and misleading a viral social media video alleging that the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) would be remotely logged out before the end of voting.







The commission clarified that only the poll official operati
content:
The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has dismissed as false and misleading a viral social media video alleging that the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) would be remotely logged out before the end of voting.

The commission clarified that only the poll official operating the device has the authority to log in or log out of the BVAS during voter accreditation and the subsequent result upload process.

INEC disclosed this in a statement posted on its official X platform on Monday, following the circulation of a video on Instagram alleging that voters would be logged out of the system before the conclusion of voting.

Describing the claim as fabricated, the commission said each polling unit was assigned unique login credentials, which were issued to the Presiding Officer on the eve of an election.

According to INEC, the credentials enable the poll official to log into the BVAS for voter accreditation on election day and subsequently upload the polling unit result sheet at the close of polls.

“The claim that the BVAS can be remotely logged out before the conclusion of accreditation and voting is false,” the commission stated.

It stressed that there was no provision for any external individual or authority to remotely log out the device.

The commission also dismissed claims that election results uploaded offline could be lost, explaining that the IReV application had been upgraded to accommodate offline uploads.

INEC said the enhancement followed experiences during the 2023 general election, when some poll officials were held hostage at their polling units because they could not upload results due to poor or non-existent network connectivity.

It explained that the offline upload feature allows poll officials in areas with poor or no network coverage to upload polling unit result sheets in the presence of stakeholders at the polling unit.

According to the commission, such results remain securely stored on the BVAS pending successful transmission to the INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV).

” As Poll Officials proceed from the polling unit to the Ward Collation Centre and the device reconnects to the internet, the result sheet is automatically transmitted to the IReV portal without requiring any further manual intervention,” it said.

INEC assured Nigerians that the BVAS and IReV systems operate in accordance with established procedures designed to protect the integrity, transparency and credibility of the electoral process.

The commission urged members of the public to disregard the video, refrain from creating or sharing unverified information and rely on its official communication channels for accurate information.

It reaffirmed its commitment to transparency, accountability and the conduct of free, fair and credible elections.

title: Correctional service decorates 6,207 promoted officers, pledges to end backlogs
description:
The Civil Defence, Correctional, Fire and Immigration Services Board has assured personnel of the Nigerian Correctional Service that promotion backlogs will not recur, following the promotion of 6,207 officers in the 2026 exercise.
The Secretary of the board, retired Major General Abdulmalik Jibrin,
content:
The Civil Defence, Correctional, Fire and Immigration Services Board has assured personnel of the Nigerian Correctional Service that promotion backlogs will not recur, following the promotion of 6,207 officers in the 2026 exercise.

The Secretary of the board, retired Major General Abdulmalik Jibrin, gave the assurance at the decoration ceremony for the promoted officers in Abuja on Monday.

Jibrin said accumulated promotion backlogs had previously affected personnel morale and contributed to the exit of some officers from the correctional service.

He said President Bola Tinubu, following the intervention of the Minister of Interior, Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo, had approved the clearance of outstanding promotion backlogs.

“I want to assure you that I will not allow that to happen again. Officers who give their best, and are tested and fulfil the requirements will certainly be given their due promotion,” he said.

The Controller-General of Corrections, Sylvester Nwakuche, said the exercise involved 6,207 personnel, comprising 4,924 senior and 1,283 junior officers.

He said the promotions included three medical professionals elevated from Controller of Corrections to Assistant Controller-General, alongside other senior officers across nine rank categories.

Nwakuche added that 743 Chief Correctional Assistants were converted to Inspectors of Corrections after completing the required conversion course, while 129 personnel were upgraded to the Inspector cadre upon acquiring relevant qualifications.

He described promotion as recognition of service, competence and experience, urging the officers to justify their elevation through discipline, integrity and professionalism.

“Promotion is not merely an administrative exercise or a change in designation. It is an important recognition of service, competence, experience and demonstrated capacity,” he said.

Representing the Minister of Interior, the Permanent Secretary, Magdalene Ajani, said the promotion of more than 6,000 personnel in one exercise reflected the Federal Government’s commitment to personnel welfare and career progression.

Tunji-Ojo described the exercise as a demonstration of ongoing reforms in the ministry, saying the reforms were repositioning the NCoS as a centre for transformation, reformation and rehabilitation rather than a mere facility for imprisoning offenders.

He urged the newly promoted officers, particularly those assuming management positions, to demonstrate leadership, take initiatives and address challenges promptly.

“You must play the managerial role of the positions you now occupy. You are not going to be waiting for directives while things are going bad because you will now be held responsible,” he said.

The minister also urged the officers to share the service’s vision with their subordinates and ensure younger personnel were carried along in implementing reforms.

Nwakuche further directed the officers to embrace the Performance Management System, saying future career progression would depend partly on performance records, competencies and measurable contributions to the service.

He said the service mandate extended beyond secure custody to reformation, rehabilitation, reintegration and the administration of non-custodial measures.

Also speaking, the Commandant-General of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps, Prof. Abubakar Audi, urged the newly promoted officers to embrace discipline and mentorship.

Audi particularly advised officers elevated to the rank of Controller of Corrections to prepare for greater command responsibilities and mentorship of younger personnel.

The ceremony was attended by retired Controllers-General of Corrections, heads of other paramilitary agencies, traditional rulers, correctional service management officials, families and other dignitaries.

title: Plateau records 5,457 suspected diabetes cases in nine months
description:
By Golok Nanmwa



JOS — The Plateau State Government has raised concerns over the growing burden of diabetes in the state, following the record of 5,457 suspected new cases between January and September 2026.







The Commissioner for Health, Dr Nicholas Ba’amlong, disclosed this on Monday during
content:
By Golok Nanmwa

JOS — The Plateau State Government has raised concerns over the growing burden of diabetes in the state, following the record of 5,457 suspected new cases between January and September 2026.

The Commissioner for Health, Dr Nicholas Ba’amlong, disclosed this on Monday during a press briefing in Jos to commemorate the 2026 World Diabetes Day.

Ba’amlong said the figure followed 5,546 suspected cases recorded in 2025, but clarified that the numbers represented suspected cases and not confirmed diagnoses.

He said diabetes remained a major public health concern because many people were living with the condition without knowing their status.

The commissioner also disclosed that findings from the 2024 nationwide Know Your Number, Control Your Number screening campaign showed that 14,359 people were screened in Plateau State, with 2,610, representing approximately 18 per cent, recording elevated blood glucose levels.

He, however, cautioned that the findings did not represent the prevalence of diabetes in the state.

According to him, the figures underscore the need to expand access to screening, diagnosis and treatment services.

As part of activities marking this year’s World Diabetes Day, the Ministry of Health, in collaboration with the Plateau State chapters of the Diabetes Association of Nigeria and the Endocrine and Metabolic Society of Nigeria, conducted a free workplace screening exercise at the Joseph Gomwalk Secretariat Complex, Jos.

Ba’amlong said the exercise targeted 1,000 civil servants and provided blood glucose and blood pressure checks, weight and body mass index assessments, health education, counselling and referrals for further medical attention where necessary.

Speaking on government interventions, the commissioner said the administration of Governor Caleb Mutfwang was working towards extending diabetes education and screening services to underserved communities across the state’s 17 local government areas through existing primary healthcare facilities and community outreach programmes.

He added that the government was exploring partnerships and appropriate medical technologies to improve access to diagnostic services, particularly at the primary healthcare level, while strengthening follow-up and referral systems for people with elevated blood glucose levels.

“Screening is only the beginning. Early detection must lead to appropriate diagnosis and treatment,” he said.

The commissioner urged residents, particularly those with a family history of diabetes, excess weight or high blood pressure, to check their blood glucose levels regularly and seek medical attention when necessary.

He also advised residents to adopt healthy lifestyles through balanced diets, regular physical activity and weight management, while avoiding tobacco and limiting alcohol consumption.

Ba’amlong identified excessive thirst, frequent urination, unexplained weight loss and persistent fatigue as some of the symptoms that could indicate diabetes.

He further urged people living with the condition to adhere to prescribed treatment and attend regular medical reviews to prevent complications.

World Diabetes Day is observed annually on November 14 to raise awareness about diabetes, promote prevention and encourage access to quality healthcare for people living with the condition.

The Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, has said that scheduled domestic carriers have until the end of December to connect to the Airport Passenger Verification System (vPASS) platfo
content:
…Says NIN-linked boarding to end ticket touting, use of false identities on local flights

The Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, has said that scheduled domestic carriers have until the end of December to connect to the Airport Passenger Verification System (vPASS) platform, and that from January 1, no airline will be allowed to board passengers who have not been checked through it.

Speaking during the launch of the biometric system at the General Aviation Terminal of the Murtala Muhammed Airport on Monday, Keyamo said the vPASS, is a biometric identity system developed with a technology firm is meant to speed up passenger processing, tighten airport security and improve the travel experience.

To use it, he said, a passenger completes a one-time registration with their National Identification Number (NIN) and a facial scan. The details are checked against the national identity database and after that, the passenger can pass through designated entry points fitted with electronic gates, using facial recognition in place of paper identification.

Keyamo said no one can board a local flight without a verified NIN and tthat the system would end ticket touting, stop people from buying tickets in bulk and reselling them, and prevent the use of false identities to board aircraft. He also said it would give airlines clean passenger manifests. Asked whether passengers would pay more, Keyamo said any additional cost would be very minimal. He also said the project is being funded by private investment, rather than the public purse.

“We are here to launch what we call the vPAS and to break it down for people to understand. The vPAS is simply a system that is linked to all our NINs, all Nigerians, and therefore you cannot board any aircraft now locally without your NIN. Now this is what this has achieved in one fell swoop. Let me be very, very clear about it, this is for local flights not for international flights.

“We have actually done that for international flights in collaboration with the Ministry of Interior. Because for international you must work with the Ministry of Interior because of other agencies that will claim you to travel abroad. This was approved by the Federal Executive Council sometime early this year, I guess, or last year, no, last year and we have just been in the process of implementing the decision of the Federal Executive Council,” he said.

On the deadline for the airlines, Keyamo said the Nigerian Civil Aviation Authority (NCAA) has been directed to give airlines until the end of December to comply. From January 1, scheduled flights must be keyed into vPASS before passengers can board. He said the operational steps for connecting airlines would be worked out with FAAN. The first phase starts at the domestic terminals of MMA in Lagos and Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport (NAIA) in Abuja. Keyamo said the system would eventually cover every local airport in the country.

Speaking on the roll out, the Managing Director of the Federal Airport Authority of Nigeria (FAAN), Olubunmi Kuku, said the application is available on iOS and Android, so passengers can register before they travel or enrol at the airport.

Kuku explained how the process works on the day of travel. She said ppassengers enter the last four digits of their NIN at the security gate to open it. At the airline boarding gate, they can use a facial or iris scan, or the QR code on their boarding pass, rather than showing several forms of identification. She said this single sign-on approach would make operations faster and more secure.

“We’ve promised you smart airports, improved passenger experience, and you’re seeing it live. The Minister and I just onboarded ourselves into the vPASS technology. You watched us as we used our NIN data to enrol.

“And what this means is a single sign-on, unique identifier that improves the experience for us, but also helps us in terms of securing and allowing us to be a bit more efficient in our operations. So you come in, before you get into the security gates, you’re basically just entering the last four digits of your NIN after you have registered that is, and it opens the gates for you. You go through security, when you get to the airline boarding gates, as opposed to someone looking at your different forms of identity, you can actually just use biometrics.

“So in this case, you can use your iris, so the facial biometrics, or potentially use the QR code on your boarding pass. It’s swift, it is smart, it is efficient, it is quick, and it secures our airports. What I do want to tell Nigerians is, as the Minister has said, we’re giving all of the airlines till end of December. This application is also available. You can onboard at the airport. We’re rolling out with Lagos and Abuja,” Kuku said.

The post FG gives domestic airlines Jan 1 deadline to connect to vPASS appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Ejiofor hails DSS DG over evacuation of Igbo youths from Wawa facility
description:
By Nwabueze Okonkwo



ONITSHA — Human rights lawyer, Sir Ifeanyi Ejiofor, has commended the Director-General of the Department of State Services (DSS), Oluwatosin Adeola Ajayi, for reforms at the Wawa detention facility and the evacuation of a significant number of Igbo youths from the facility.
content:
By Nwabueze Okonkwo

ONITSHA — Human rights lawyer, Sir Ifeanyi Ejiofor, has commended the Director-General of the Department of State Services (DSS), Oluwatosin Adeola Ajayi, for reforms at the Wawa detention facility and the evacuation of a significant number of Igbo youths from the facility.

Ejiofor also praised Ajayi for what he described as an end to the alleged arbitrary arrest and abduction of Igbo youths, which he claimed had become frequent under the previous leadership of the Service.

The lawyer made the commendation in a statement on Monday titled, “Wawa Barracks: The horrifying testimonies of survivors of enforced disappearances under the Buhari regime — a time for Igbos to introspect”.

He expressed concern over alleged abuses at the detention facility, including arbitrary arrests, torture, deprivation of medical attention and deaths, based on accounts he attributed to former detainees.

According to him, the situation had at some point deteriorated to the extent that some individuals of Igbo extraction allegedly exploited security agencies to settle personal scores.

He said the reported reforms under Ajayi had helped restore confidence and a measure of security in the South-East.

“Happily, that dark chapter has been brought to an end, restoring confidence, peace and a measure of security in the South-East geopolitical zone,” he said.

Ejiofor described the alleged experiences of detainees as disturbing, claiming that many Igbo youths had suffered under the previous DSS leadership.

He, however, stressed that his criticism of alleged security abuses should not be interpreted as support for criminal activities by non-state actors operating in the region.

” No grievance, however genuine, confers a licence for criminality; equally, no allegation of criminality confers a licence for lawlessness by the State,” he said.

The lawyer appealed to the DSS Director-General to facilitate the release of more detainees who, according to him, had no involvement in criminal activities and against whom there was no credible evidence of wrongdoing.

He also urged the Service to withdraw charges allegedly founded on ethnic profiling, arguing that addressing the underlying causes of agitation was more important than sustaining what he described as prejudicial ethnic categorisation.

Ejiofor further commended Ajayi for what he called commendable reforms within the Service, saying the intervention demonstrated the importance of professionalism and institutional changes in rebuilding public confidence.

He called for an end to the use of propaganda as a security strategy, arguing that public trust could only be restored through justice, accountability and respect for citizens’ rights.

The lawyer also urged the Igbo people to reflect on the crisis, warning against internal divisions and the exploitation of collective grievances by individuals seeking personal benefits.

He said the community should not allow the alleged misconduct of others to become an excuse for internal wrongdoing or personal vendettas.

Ejiofor also accused the administration of former President Muhammadu Buhari of overseeing a pattern of abuses against Igbo youths, alleging that the former Attorney-General of the Federation, Abubakar Malami, and former DSS Director-General, Yusuf Magaji Bichi, played significant roles.

He said recent testimonies by alleged survivors of detention at Wawa Barracks had brought to light claims of physical torture, psychological trauma, denial of medical care and deaths in custody.

According to him, some detainees reportedly survived on inadequate food and water, with conditions worsening before the change in DSS leadership under the Tinubu administration.

He further claimed that the new leadership had initiated changes, including the release of some detainees against whom no indictments were sustained, the payment of compensation without court orders and the transfer of some detainees to conventional custodial facilities.

Ejiofor maintained that the reforms should be sustained, while calling for the release of other detainees against whom no credible evidence of criminal wrongdoing existed.

The post Ejiofor hails DSS DG over evacuation of Igbo youths from Wawa facility appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Kano belongs to all, not those in power, Kwankwasiyya tells govt
description:
By Hadiza Yusuf



The Kwankwasiyya Movement has accused the Kano State Government of politicising the reported attack on the convoy of its leader, Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, insisting that the state belongs to all residents, irrespective of their political affiliations.







The movement said
content:
By Hadiza Yusuf

The Kwankwasiyya Movement has accused the Kano State Government of politicising the reported attack on the convoy of its leader, Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, insisting that the state belongs to all residents, irrespective of their political affiliations.

The movement said the government had a responsibility to protect all citizens and should not allow political differences to undermine their safety and fundamental rights.

Its spokesperson, Dr Habibu Sale Mohammed, stated this in a statement on Monday while reacting to the reported attack on Kwankwaso’s convoy during a political engagement in Bichi Local Government Area on Sunday.

The movement also criticised the state government for dismissing the incident as fictitious and accusing the Kwankwasiyya Movement of fabricating the allegation to attract public sympathy.

It specifically faulted the Commissioner for Information, Sanusi Bature Dawakin Tofa, for demanding pictures and videos of the incident rather than allowing security agencies to investigate the allegation.

The group questioned why victims should be expected to provide evidence before the government could express concern about their safety.

“Kano belongs to all its people, not exclusively to those occupying government offices. Its security, peace and democratic freedoms are collective responsibilities that must never be sacrificed on the altar of partisan politics,” the statement said.

The movement maintained that investigating allegations of criminal activities was the responsibility of security agencies, not the victims.

It also accused the commissioner of reaching conclusions on the incident without presenting the outcome of any police investigation.

The group called on the Kano State Police Command to investigate the reported attack, establish what transpired in Bichi and ensure that anyone found culpable was brought to justice.

It further demanded an investigation into the alleged destruction of vehicles and injuries reportedly sustained by members of Kwankwaso’s delegation.

The movement urged Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf to rise above political considerations and guarantee the safety of all political parties, candidates, campaign officials and supporters across the state.

It warned against political intimidation, insisting that opposition members must be allowed to participate in lawful political activities without fear of harassment or violence.

“Political competition is not warfare, and opposition politics is not a criminal offence,” the statement added.

The Kwankwasiyya Movement said it remained committed to peaceful political participation but warned that its commitment to peace should not be mistaken for acceptance of intimidation or impunity.

It urged the state government to allow security agencies to establish the facts surrounding the reported incident before making public statements on the matter.

title: 2027: Shehu Buba inaugurates 1,000-member campaign council
description:
By Christopher Ameh, Bauchi



The governorship candidate of the Peoples Redemption Party (PRP) in Bauchi State, Senator Shehu Buba Umar, has inaugurated a 1,000-member campaign council ahead of the 2027 general elections, urging members to embrace unity, peaceful political engagement and issue-base
content:
By Christopher Ameh, Bauchi

The governorship candidate of the Peoples Redemption Party (PRP) in Bauchi State, Senator Shehu Buba Umar, has inaugurated a 1,000-member campaign council ahead of the 2027 general elections, urging members to embrace unity, peaceful political engagement and issue-based campaigns.

Buba, who represents Bauchi South Senatorial District in the National Assembly, inaugurated the council on Sunday, with members drawn from the 20 local government areas of the state.

He described the inauguration as a major step towards strengthening the party’s grassroots mobilisation, coordinating its political activities and improving its chances in the 2027 governorship election.

The senator said the council comprised experienced party stakeholders and directors representing the various senatorial districts and local government areas, with the responsibility of developing strategies and coordinating campaign activities.

He urged members to set aside personal differences and work collectively towards the party’s victory, stressing that political disagreements should be resolved through dialogue, persuasion and mutual understanding.

Buba warned against violence, slander and character assassination, insisting that electoral victory could only be achieved through constructive engagement with voters and the presentation of credible alternatives.

He said his ambition to govern Bauchi State was driven by the desire to address what he described as challenges of misgovernance and redirect the state towards sustainable development and prosperity.

According to him, his development agenda will focus on economic stability and growth, improved security, urban and rural infrastructure, people-oriented reforms and the general welfare of residents.

The PRP candidate also emphasised the importance of grassroots mobilisation, adequate electoral preparation and voter education, particularly on the need for voters to protect their votes after casting their ballots.

He noted that effective governance would require cooperation between the executive and legislative arms of government, expressing the need for the PRP to secure representation in the State House of Assembly and National Assembly to facilitate the implementation of its manifesto.

Describing the 2027 contest as challenging, Buba charged members of the campaign council to develop a workable programme and adopt strategies capable of securing victory for the party.

He urged them to take the campaign to communities, wards and polling units, listen to residents’ concerns and communicate the party’s programmes and policies to the electorate.

He further insisted that the PRP’s campaign should be guided by respect for voters and issue-based engagement rather than unnecessary attacks on political opponents.

Expressing confidence in the party’s chances, Buba identified unity, commitment, hard work and popular support as critical factors for victory.

He subsequently declared the campaign council inaugurated and directed members to commence immediate grassroots mobilisation through door-to-door campaigns and engagements across the state.

Earlier, the Bauchi State Chairman of the PRP, Abdulrahman Yusuf Muazu, said the campaign council was carefully constituted to reflect the political composition and diversity of the state.

He urged members to regard their appointments as a privilege rather than a mark of superiority over other party faithful, warning against complacency, indiscipline and arrogance.

Muazu charged them to work diligently towards attracting more members and supporters to the party ahead of the elections.

Also speaking, the Director-General of the campaign council, Hon. Ibrahim Makama, assured that the council was ready to commence mobilisation and campaign activities to build support for the PRP and its governorship candidate.

Makama described his appointment and those of other members as a privilege, pledging their loyalty and commitment to the party’s objectives and Buba’s governorship ambition.

He also urged party members and supporters to conduct issue-based campaigns, shunning character assassination, calumny and violence.

description:
By Precious Enaike



The Zonal Director, South-South Election Planning, Coordination, Monitoring and Mobilisation of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council, Dr. Ngozi Olejeme, has expressed confidence that President Bola Tinubu, Delta State Governor Sheriff Oborevwori and
content:
By Precious Enaike

The Zonal Director, South-South Election Planning, Coordination, Monitoring and Mobilisation of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council, Dr. Ngozi Olejeme, has expressed confidence that President Bola Tinubu, Delta State Governor Sheriff Oborevwori and other APC candidates will win the 2027 general elections.

Olejeme attributed her optimism to what she described as the growing strength of grassroots mobilisation within the party’s campaign structure, particularly in Oshimili South Local Government Area of Delta State.

She spoke at the Oshimili South Arcade, Asaba, where she joined other party leaders in welcoming Oborevwori, his deputy, Sir Monday Onyeme, former Governor Ifeanyi Okowa and other members of the State Campaign Council to the local government.

The former boss of the Nigeria Social Insurance Trust Fund (NSITF) assured the governor that her council was prepared to mobilise support for all APC candidates in the area.

Addressing party supporters, traders, youths and other residents at the rally, Olejeme expressed confidence that sustained grassroots engagement would translate into overwhelming electoral support for the APC.

She said, “My Governor, we are here to tell you that Tinubu has already won. All APC candidates have already won. Mr. Governor, Oshimili South is the capital of government, and we trust and believe in you.

“Based on the work we have done so far at the grassroots, I can assure you that we have already delivered President Tinubu and you, our confirmed Governor.”

Olejeme, however, urged residents and party supporters to collect their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs), stressing that grassroots mobilisation must be backed by active participation in the electoral process.

“I have only one request to make: Go and make sure you collect your PVC. Your PVC is what will give us this victory. Collect your PVC; it is very important because we are already set for victory. We have reached our promised land, and your PVC is of immense importance at this point,” she said.

She described Oborevwori as a performing governor who had exceeded expectations, while applauding Tinubu for what she called his achievements in office.

Olejeme urged Nigerians to give the President another mandate in 2027, arguing that his performance deserved a second term.

“Our Governor has performed very well. Governor Oborevwori is the best in Africa. President Tinubu has done so much that the people are not talking about. For the good work he has done, we have to give him more work to do by re-electing him in the 2027 general election,” she said.

She expressed confidence that Tinubu, Oborevwori, senators and other APC candidates would emerge victorious in the 2027 elections.

title: Tinubu’s debt interest exceeds revenue, NDC alleges
description:
By Henry Umoru



ABUJA — The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) has accused President Bola Tinubu’s administration of plunging the country into what it described as “fiscal suicide”, alleging that interest payments on public debt have exceeded the Federal Government’s total revenue.







The party
content:
By Henry Umoru

ABUJA — The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) has accused President Bola Tinubu’s administration of plunging the country into what it described as “fiscal suicide”, alleging that interest payments on public debt have exceeded the Federal Government’s total revenue.

The party claimed that Nigeria spent N7.7 trillion on debt interest payments in the first half of 2026, compared with total federal revenue of N6.2 trillion, representing 124.19 per cent of revenue generated within the period.

The NDC Spokesperson for the National Campaign Council, Dr. Chiogo Constance Ikokwu, made the allegations in a statement issued on Monday ahead of the 2027 general elections.

According to the party, the figures, which it attributed to the World Bank’s 2026 Nigeria Development Update, indicate that the country is increasingly borrowing to service existing debts rather than investing in critical infrastructure and social services.

It said the development had placed an additional burden on Nigerians and threatened the economic prospects of future generations.

The statement read, “The grim reality for every suffering family in our nation today is that under the President Bola Tinubu administration, Nigeria is no longer borrowing to build roads, equip hospitals, or fund schools. It is borrowing recklessly to pay interest on past debts, thereby mortgaging the survival of today’s citizens and the destiny of unborn generations.”

The party further claimed that debt interest payments rose from N5.6 trillion in the first half of 2025 to N7.7 trillion in the corresponding period of 2026, consuming 3.1 per cent of the country’s Gross Domestic Product (GDP).

It contrasted the figure with capital expenditure, which it said fell to N700 billion, representing 0.3 per cent of GDP, from one per cent in the corresponding period of the previous year.

Describing the disparity as alarming, the NDC said the government was spending about 11 times more on debt interest than on critical infrastructure.

The party also faulted the administration’s revenue performance, arguing that the increase in federal revenue from N3.6 trillion to N6.2 trillion had not translated into improved living conditions for Nigerians.

It attributed the revenue growth to increased taxation and pressure on businesses and ordinary citizens, alleging that much of the money was being channelled into servicing high-cost domestic borrowing.

The NDC also referenced the recurring question raised by its presidential candidate, Peter Obi, over the utilisation of funds accruing to the country following the removal of petrol subsidy and increased borrowing.

“This reckless trajectory is unsustainable,” the party declared.

It consequently called for an immediate halt to what it described as reckless domestic borrowing, a comprehensive audit and restructuring of the country’s debts, and a review of government spending priorities.

The party also advocated increased investment in infrastructure, healthcare, education and productive sectors, alongside a reduction in government overheads.

Looking ahead to the 2027 elections, Ikokwu expressed confidence that the Obi/Kwankwaso presidential ticket would offer Nigerians an alternative built on productivity, fiscal discipline and sustainable economic growth.

She said an NDC-led government would prioritise the responsible management of public resources and redirect spending towards areas capable of improving citizens’ welfare and strengthening the economy.

The post Tinubu’s debt interest exceeds revenue, NDC alleges appeared first on Vanguard News.

content:
By Muhammad Inuwa, Dutse

The governorship candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Jigawa State, Mustapha Sule Lamido, has urged women to reject monetary inducements from politicians ahead of the 2027 general elections, warning against sacrificing their children’s future for temporary financial gains.

Lamido made the appeal while addressing PDP stakeholders during meetings in Gumel and Hadejia, where he urged women to consider the long-term implications of their electoral choices.

He cautioned against accepting money and other material gifts from politicians at the expense of the future of their children, urging voters to critically assess the performance of the incumbent administration before deciding which party to support.

The PDP candidate said the All Progressives Congress (APC)-led government should be judged by its record in office rather than campaign promises, propaganda or alleged attempts to influence voters through the distribution of money and other items.

Lamido maintained that the PDP had a record of achievements from its previous administrations to present to the electorate, insisting that the party was better positioned to offer the state an alternative direction.

He urged voters to evaluate whether the APC-led administration had met their expectations, adding that those dissatisfied with its performance should consider the PDP as an alternative in 2027.

He stressed that the future of Jigawa State and the well-being of the next generation should take precedence over temporary political benefits.

title: No casualty as gas explosion rocks Lagos NNPC station, spreads to school
description:
By Olasunkanmi Akoni



A gas explosion on Sunday rocked a Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation (NNPC) filling station at Savannah Bus Stop, Command, Ejigbo, Lagos State, triggering a fire that spread to the adjoining Saint Lawrence Greater Height School.







No casualty was recorded in the in
content:
By Olasunkanmi Akoni

A gas explosion on Sunday rocked a Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation (NNPC) filling station at Savannah Bus Stop, Command, Ejigbo, Lagos State, triggering a fire that spread to the adjoining Saint Lawrence Greater Height School.

No casualty was recorded in the incident, which occurred at about 1pm, as the school was closed for the weekend.

The Controller-General of the Lagos State Fire and Rescue Service, Margaret Adeseye, who confirmed the incident, said the fire was successfully contained through the prompt intervention of firefighters.

Adeseye said the agency received a distress call at 12:50pm and arrived at the scene at 1:13pm.

She disclosed that firefighters from Ejigbo, Ikeja and Bolade fire stations were deployed to the scene to combat the fire, prevent further damage and bring the situation under control.

According to her, the intensity of the explosion caused the fire to spread rapidly to the adjoining school, affecting parts of its premises.

She, however, said the firefighters prevented the fire from spreading to other sections of the school.

“No casualty was recorded in the incident,” Adeseye stated.

She added that preliminary investigations into the cause of the explosion were ongoing.

title: INEC debunks claims of remote BVAS logout, missing offline results
description:
The Independent National Electoral Commission has dismissed claims that officials can remotely log out of the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System before the end of voting, insisting that only the presiding officer operating the device has the authority to log in or out.
The commission also clarified
content:
The Independent National Electoral Commission has dismissed claims that officials can remotely log out of the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System before the end of voting, insisting that only the presiding officer operating the device has the authority to log in or out.

The commission also clarified that election results uploaded offline are securely stored on the device and automatically transmitted to its Result Viewing Portal once internet connectivity is restored.

INEC was reacting to a viral Instagram video in which a man claiming to have worked as a presiding officer alleged that officials could log voters out of BVAS before the close of polls and that results uploaded offline could be lost.

In the video, the man warned prospective poll workers ahead of the 2027 elections against uploading results offline, advising them to take screenshots of the results and wait for network connectivity before uploading them.

However, INEC, in a statement on Monday shared on its official X account, described the claims as “false, fabricated and misleading”, urging Nigerians to disregard the video.

The commission explained that each polling unit was assigned unique login credentials, which were issued to the presiding officer on the eve of an election.

It said the credentials enabled the presiding officer to log into BVAS for voter accreditation on election day and subsequently upload the polling unit result sheet after the close of polls.

“The claim that the BVAS can be remotely logged out before the conclusion of accreditation and voting is false. Only the Poll Official operating the device has the authority to log in or log out of the BVAS, whether during voter accreditation or the result upload process,” the commission stated.

It added that there was no provision for any external individual or authority to remotely log out the device.

On the allegation that results uploaded offline could disappear, INEC said the offline upload feature was introduced following challenges experienced during the 2023 general election.

According to the commission, some presiding officers were held hostage at polling units because they could not upload results due to poor or non-existent network connectivity.

It said the IReV application was subsequently upgraded to allow presiding officers in areas with poor or no network coverage to upload polling unit result sheets offline in the presence of stakeholders.

“The uploaded result sheet remains securely stored on the BVAS pending successful transmission,” INEC stated.

The commission explained that as presiding officers moved from their polling units to ward collation centres and their devices reconnected to the internet, the results were automatically transmitted to the IReV portal without further manual intervention.

INEC assured Nigerians that the BVAS and IReV systems operated in line with established procedures designed to protect the integrity, transparency and credibility of the electoral process.

It urged members of the public to refrain from creating or sharing unverified information and rely on its official communication channels for accurate information.

The post INEC debunks claims of remote BVAS logout, missing offline results appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

content:
…As Bishop Timothy Kume celebrates 57th birthday, 19th anniversary of church

A renowned cleric and Founder of Faith Hill Prophetic Assembly (FHPA), Archbishop Emmanuel Jatau, has called on Christian clerics to take up political and traditional leadership positions, saying the involvement of righteous people in governance is essential to addressing the moral challenges confronting society.

Jatau said the growing presence of men of God in positions of traditional authority and political leadership would help promote righteousness, integrity and responsible leadership in the country.

He made the call during activities marking the 57th birthday celebration of the Presiding Bishop of FHPA, Makurdi, Bishop Timothy Kume, as well as the church’s 19th anniversary and 2026 annual convention.

According to him, evil thrives in society when people with good values shy away from leadership responsibilities, thereby allowing individuals without the fear of God to occupy positions of authority.

He said, “Evil reigns in the land because righteous people stay away from taking up responsibilities. If you allow unrighteous and unholy people to occupy positions of kingship and political authority, you will get what you see.”

The Archbishop expressed delight that more people were beginning to recognise the importance of godly leadership, citing the Tor Tiv and the Och’Idoma as examples of traditional rulers who are also pastors.

He also referenced other traditional rulers across the country who are men of God, expressing the hope that more Christian leaders would accept chieftaincy titles and contribute to the development of their communities.

Jatau further urged Nigerians to pay greater attention to their health, expressing concern over increasing cases of kidney failure and other health challenges.

He attributed some of the health concerns to the consumption of adulterated food and fake drinks, urging members of the public to be more careful about what they eat and drink.

Speaking on the 57th birthday of Bishop Kume, Jatau declared God’s abundant blessings, divine favour, good health and continued progress upon the celebrant. He prayed God to reward Kume for his service in the ministry, preserve his life and grant him greater joy, honour and promotion as he marks another year.

The Archbishop also declared that the celebrant’s life and ministry would continue to experience multiplication, restoration and testimonies, praying that God’s grace would sustain him and enable him to fulfil greater assignments in His vineyard. He described the occasion as an opportunity to celebrate God’s faithfulness and prayed for lasting blessings upon Kume and his household.

Earlier, the celebrant and presiding Bishop of Faith Hill Prophetic Assembly, Dr Timothy Kume expressed gratitude to God for His faithfulness upon his life and the achievements recorded by the church in its 19 years of existence.

He described the 2026 annual convention, which held from November 11 to 15, under the theme, “Abundant Life”, as a divine opportunity for spiritual renewal and positive transformation in the lives of participants.

Kume, who appreciated Archbishop Jatau for his love, support and care for him and the Benue church, also commended other ministers of God who contributed to the success of the convention.

He said the convention was designed to bring positive changes in the spiritual lives, marriages, finances, health and general circumstances of participants.

The cleric also identified the graduation of students of the Faith Bible Institute, the training arm of the church, and the ordination of deserving ministers as major highlights of the programme.

He explained that the ordination was in recognition of those found worthy of greater responsibilities in the service of God, while urging all Christians to remain committed to spreading the gospel.

Kume called on believers not to leave the responsibility of evangelism to ordained ministers alone, stressing that every Christian had a role to play in the Great Commission.

He further appreciated his family, friends and well wishers for gathering to celebrate his birthday, praying God to uplift them and meet them all at the point of their needs.

Those ordained include Aondoakaa Msendoo, Tindi ANDREW, Ieren Sunday Jacob, Alabi Bilikisu, Harry Benedicta, Comfort Orpin, Ejigbo Doris, Bernard Moses, Asawa Udende, And Iorshe Mercy.

Others are Evang. Iorundu Mathias, Mnyamchier Isaac, Beatrice Terngu, Lawrence Lydia, Franca Enenche, Terveshima Dorcas, Abe Nathie, Onuminya Enenche, Thomas Kor, Sandra Pila, Terfa Evelyn and Hyacinth Ahua.

The post Cleric urges men of God to take up political, traditional leadership positions appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Showunmi urges Ribadu to sanction politicians threatening security
description:
By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta



The Convener of The Alternative Movement, Otunba Segun Showunmi, has urged the National Security Adviser, Mallam Nuhu Ribadu, to establish clear standards for political conduct and ensure that politicians whose actions threaten Nigeria’s peace and security are held ac
content:
By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta

The Convener of The Alternative Movement, Otunba Segun Showunmi, has urged the National Security Adviser, Mallam Nuhu Ribadu, to establish clear standards for political conduct and ensure that politicians whose actions threaten Nigeria’s peace and security are held accountable, irrespective of their status or political affiliation.

Showunmi made the call in an open letter to Ribadu, expressing concern over what he described as the growing toxicity of political engagement, reckless public communication and the increasing use of inflammatory rhetoric by politicians, their supporters and other influential individuals.

In the letter, titled, “An Open Letter to the National Security Adviser: On the Urgent Need to Establish Firm Boundaries for Political Conduct and Hold Those Who Threaten National Security Accountable,” he warned that Nigeria’s already precarious security situation could worsen if political actors continued to exploit sensitive national issues for partisan advantage.

The letter was also copied to President Bola Tinubu; the Minister of Defence, General Christopher Gwabin Musa (rtd.); the President’s Special Adviser on Homeland Security, Major General Adeyinka A. Famadewa (rtd.); the Inspector-General of Police, Mr Olatunji Rilwan Disu; the Director-General of the Department of State Services, Mr Oluwatosin Ajayi; and the Minister of State for Defence, Alhaji Bello Muhammad Matawalle.

Showunmi argued that political competition, personal ambition and partisan disagreements should not become additional threats to national stability.

He noted that Nigeria was already grappling with multiple security challenges requiring vigilance, effective intelligence gathering, institutional coordination and responsible leadership. He urged political actors to recognise the far-reaching consequences of their words and actions.

“There is a difference between robust political engagement and conduct that deliberately or recklessly threatens public peace. There is a difference between criticising government and deliberately inciting citizens against one another,” he stated.

He cautioned against the abuse of freedom of expression to promote hostility, circulate inflammatory narratives and undermine national cohesion.

According to him, the apparent normalisation of provocative statements, ethnic and religious insinuations, threats and inflammatory public performances had become a worrying development requiring urgent institutional attention.

“Some individuals seem to believe that because they are politicians, party loyalists, public commentators or influential supporters of powerful political interests, they can say virtually anything, mobilise others irresponsibly and walk away without consequences. That assumption must be firmly challenged,” he said.

Showunmi maintained that national security must not be sacrificed for political ambition, stressing that democratic participation did not confer the right to incite violence, threaten citizens, encourage lawlessness or create conditions capable of triggering communal tensions.

He urged the Office of the National Security Adviser to collaborate with relevant security and law-enforcement agencies to develop and publicly communicate clear standards governing political communication and conduct, particularly as political activities and competition intensify across the country.

Among the measures he proposed was the establishment of clearly defined boundaries for political communication, with politicians, political parties, spokespersons, campaign organisations and supporters expected to exercise responsibility in their public engagements.

He insisted that political platforms must not be used to promote violence, ethnic hostility, religious antagonism, intimidation or threats to public peace.

The Alternative Movement convener also called for the impartial application of the law, insisting that public office holders, former office holders, party leaders, political financiers, campaign spokespersons, social media influencers and ordinary supporters should be treated equally whenever credible evidence of criminal conduct emerges.

“There must be no sacred cows, no political exemptions and no selective enforcement,” he declared.

He advocated a coordinated rapid-response mechanism to address political misinformation and incitement. Such a mechanism, he said, should provide for the documentation of incidents, verification of information, correction of false narratives and responsible public communication.

He cautioned public institutions against amplifying unverified allegations, while urging that deliberately fabricated information intended to provoke violence should be investigated in accordance with the law.

Showunmi further called on political parties and their leadership structures to take responsibility for maintaining discipline among their members, spokespersons and supporters.

He argued that political parties should not enjoy the benefits of democratic participation while distancing themselves from misconduct committed under their banners or on their behalf.

He also urged security agencies to develop clear early-intervention protocols to enable them to respond promptly to credible threats, organised intimidation and incitement before they escalate into violence.

“Security institutions should not wait until inflammatory rhetoric has translated into violence before responding. Credible threats, organised intimidation, incitement and conduct presenting an identifiable risk to public safety should attract timely, proportionate and lawful intervention,” he stated.

He added that prevention remained preferable to crisis management, particularly given the complex security challenges confronting the country.

Emphasising the need for accountability irrespective of political influence, Showunmi insisted that no individual should be shielded from legitimate investigation or prosecution on account of political position, financial influence, personal relationships or proximity to government.

He, however, clarified that his intervention was not intended to encourage the suppression of opposition voices, silence critical opinions or criminalise legitimate political disagreements.

According to him, democracy must provide sufficient room for dissent, criticism, peaceful protests and competing political visions, while protecting the country against individuals who exploit democratic freedoms to threaten public safety and national stability.

“The government must be able to distinguish between legitimate political expression and conduct that crosses the threshold into criminality. That distinction must be made through established legal standards, credible evidence, due process and respect for fundamental rights,” he stressed.

Showunmi also argued that responsibility for national security should not be left exclusively to soldiers, police officers, intelligence personnel and other security operatives.

He maintained that political actors had an equally important responsibility to preserve the conditions necessary for democratic governance and peaceful coexistence.

“We cannot continue to behave as though national security is the exclusive responsibility of soldiers, policemen, intelligence officers and other security operatives. Political actors also have a responsibility to preserve the environment in which democracy can function. Their words matter. Their conduct matters. Their influence carries consequences,” he said.

He appealed to Ribadu to send an unequivocal message that political relevance, public office and personal influence would not confer immunity on anyone whose actions violated the law.

Warning against waiting for an avoidable national tragedy before taking decisive action, Showunmi urged relevant institutions to demonstrate their commitment to preventing security crises arising from irresponsible political conduct.

“The time has come to draw the line, establish the boundaries and enforce the law impartially,” he declared.

title: Actor Robert Pattinson Lands Role As New James Bond
description: British actor Robert Pattinson was Monday named as the new James Bond, stepping into the coveted role of the world’s most famous fictional spy.“Amazon MGM Studios have announced that Robert Pattinson will take on the iconic role of James Bond,” the studio said on the official 007.c
content:
British actor Robert Pattinson was Monday named as the new James Bond, stepping into the coveted role of the world’s most famous fictional spy.

“Amazon MGM Studios have announced that Robert Pattinson will take on the iconic role of James Bond,” the studio said on the official 007.com website.

Pattinson would succeed Daniel Craig as the super-suave MI6 agent, “ushering in a new era for one of cinema’s most celebrated characters”, the studios added.

It will be the first Bond film since long-term Bond producers Barbara Broccoli and Michael Wilson stepped back and Amazon took creative control of the franchise, after acquiring the series’ parent company MGM.

“James Bond is one of the most legendary characters in cinema, and to be entrusted with 007 is the honour of a lifetime,” Pattinson said.

“To say this role is a dream come true is an understatement,” he added in a statement.

Amazon MGM also announced that Oscar-nominated Canadian director Denis Villeneuve, behind such box-office hits as the “Dune” films, would be directing the next Bond movie from a script by “Peaky Blinders” creator Steven Knight.

Knight said in May that Amazon has given him a licence to play with the legendary secret agent created by author Ian Fleming.

“Bond has been bulletproof. People have been able to make mistakes and variations and the character has survived,” Knight told Screen magazine at the Cannes Film Festival.

“Because the core of it is like a diamond. You can’t touch it,” he added.

Knight also told reporters that he has done research with “the SAS and even more secret outfits” for his reinvention of the next 007 movie.

Pattinson, 40, started out in amateur dramatics before getting his break in “Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire” (2005) as Cedric Diggory, a champion for Hogwarts.

But he rocketed to global fame for his part as brooding teen heartthrob in the romantic vampire saga “Twilight”.

‘Extremely Inventive’

He was paid a reported $2 million for his lead in “Twilight” (2008), but by the time the saga wrapped up with the two parts of “Breaking Dawn” in 2011 and 2012, he was reportedly on $12.5 million plus 7.5 percent of the box office take.

One of his first forays into edgier cinema came with 2012 drama “Cosmopolis”, in which he portrayed a self-destructive currency speculator as his life falls apart.

The film was directed by legendary US auteur David Cronenberg, who described the actor as “extremely inventive”.

He received critical acclaim after later switching to more independent films and was nominated for best actor at the Cannes festival in 2017 for neo-grindhouse crime caper “Good Time” by New York-based brothers Josh and Ben Safdie.

In 2022, Amazon bought storied Hollywood studio MGM, which held distribution rights to Bond’s extensive back catalogue.

But it was not until early 2025 that the company struck a deal with longtime Bond producers Wilson and Broccoli to obtain full creative control.

The franchise had been closely guarded by the Broccoli family since 1962’s “Dr. No”.

They famously insisted on preserving the integrity of the Bond character and brand, resisting spin-offs and licensing that many industry experts expect to see following Amazon’s takeover.

title: 2027: Oluremi Tinubu empowers 5,000 Zamfara women, bags traditional title
description:
Nigeria’s First Lady, Oluremi Tinubu, has empowered over 5,000 women in Zamfara State, as her visit also marked the historic moment of the first First Lady’s official visit to the North-Western state.
The empowerment was held at the APC North-West Women’s Mega Rally and Empowerment Programme, which
content:
Nigeria’s First Lady, Oluremi Tinubu, has empowered over 5,000 women in Zamfara State, as her visit also marked the historic moment of the first First Lady’s official visit to the North-Western state.

The empowerment was held at the APC North-West Women’s Mega Rally and Empowerment Programme, which she hosted in person at the Trade Fair Complex on Thursday in Gusau, the state capital.

According to a statement made available to PUNCH Online on Monday, the First Lady was welcomed by thousands of residents and supporters at the venue.

Ahead of the rally, the Co-Director, All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council Women Mobilisation Directorate, Betta Edu, and the other leaders of the directorate, on behalf of the First Lady, empowered women at a town hall stakeholders engagement meeting and supported businesses at the market with a humanitarian outreach for women and children at the hospitals.

Tinubu said that the empowerment has been part of the Renewed Hope Initiative since its inception, adding that it was borne out of love for the people and not politically motivated.

She was also conferred with the title of ‘Jagaban Matan Arewa’ by the Zamfara State Council of Chiefs.

The event was led by Zamfara State Governor, Dauda Lawal; his wife, Huriyya Lawal; former governors; First Ladies from the North-West; among others.

“Before the rally, Senator Tinubu met with traditional rulers in the state to seek their blessings. She was subsequently conferred with the title of ‘Jagaban Matan Arewa’ by the Chairman of the Zamfara State Council of Chiefs and Emir of Anka, Alhaji Attahiru Muhammad Ahmad,” the statement partly read.

She expressed her delight at visiting the state as she described her visit as a demonstration of solidarity and compassion, particularly towards women affected by insecurity, poverty and limited economic opportunities.

“This is the happiest day of my life. Except for Zamfara, I have been in all 36 states of Nigeria, including the FCT. I have always wanted to come to Zamfara, and today I have fulfilled that,” she said.

Tinubu also expressed condolences to families who had lost loved ones to insecurity in the state, praying for the repose of the deceased.

The statement continued, “She said the Renewed Hope Initiative had continued to empower women since its inception, insisting that its interventions went beyond political campaigns.

“The only party that empowers during the campaign, and it is not about the campaign; we have been empowering from day one. And that is why it is not politics but love for our people.”

The First Lady also conveyed President Bola Tinubu’s commitment to the state, assuring residents that the President would continue working for their benefit.

She also commended the airport and other infrastructure built by the governor, saying, ” With this airport in place, I and my husband, the President, will come to Zamfara again and again.”

Earlier, Lawal thanked the First Lady for her support through the Renewed Hope Initiative, particularly its food outreach programme.

He described her visit as historic, saying her presence represented more than an official engagement.

He said empowering women remained central to the state’s efforts to strengthen families, improve economic prosperity, and promote sustainable peace.

The governor also declared the support of his administration and the people of Zamfara for the President’s re-election bid.

“I assure Your Excellency that Zamfara’s government and people unwaveringly support Mr President’s second term. With the women here and the men supporting them, Zamfara and the North-West will deliver for Mr President come January 2027,” he said.

The post 2027: Oluremi Tinubu empowers 5,000 Zamfara women, bags traditional title appeared first on Punch Newspapers.
