title: Reps give NSCDC CG 24 hours over ₦2bn transactions, extortion allegations
description:
By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja



The House of Representatives Committee on Solid Minerals has given the Commandant-General of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) 24 hours to appear before it over allegations of financial impropriety, extortion, unlawful arrests and human rights violat
content:
By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja

The House of Representatives Committee on Solid Minerals has given the Commandant-General of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) 24 hours to appear before it over allegations of financial impropriety, extortion, unlawful arrests and human rights violations involving the Mining Marshals.

The committee is also seeking explanations over the alleged killing of a serving NSCDC officer, Deputy Superintendent Agada Levi Agada, reportedly by fellow officers while on duty at a mining site.

The ultimatum followed a motion moved by Hon. Ali Amburura, representing Sokoto State, and seconded by Hon. Majidi from Katsina State during an investigative hearing into the activities, funding and operations of the Mining Marshals.

The committee’s Chairman, Hon. Gaza Gbefwi, said the investigation was prompted by allegations of abuse of power, extortion, unlawful detention of licensed mining operators and financial irregularities within the special security unit established to combat illegal mining.

Gbefwi said the lawmakers were particularly concerned about an alleged transaction of over ₦2bn linked to the bank account of a former state commander, suspected compromise among Mining Marshals personnel across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory, as well as questions surrounding vehicle procurement and the unit’s sources of funding.

He said the investigation was being conducted in accordance with the National Assembly’s constitutional oversight powers under Sections 88 and 89 of the 1999 Constitution, as amended.

The lawmaker recalled that more than 2,200 Mining Marshals were inaugurated in March 2024 to strengthen the fight against illegal mining, protect the country’s mineral resources and improve security at mining locations.

He also called for the protection of the family of the deceased officer and other witnesses, alleging that some had been subjected to threats and intimidation.

According to him, Agada left behind a widow and two children aged 10 and seven.

Gbefwi expressed condolences to the deceased officer’s family and assured them that their petition would be forwarded to the appropriate authorities for necessary action.

He also requested an executive summary of the family’s submissions to assist the committee in documenting the allegations and determining appropriate interventions.

Meanwhile, the Director of Communications at Stone Rockers Nigeria Limited, Rachel Ogbonna, accused the Mining Marshals of subjecting licensed mining operators to arbitrary arrests, prolonged detention and harassment.

Ogbonna told the committee that the company’s quarry site had remained sealed for over one year despite its possession of valid mining licences and other relevant operational documents.

She alleged that 12 employees of the company were arrested and taken to an NSCDC detention facility along Airport Road.

According to her, the company’s chairman and director were also detained after visiting the facility with relevant documents to establish the reasons for their employees’ arrest and secure their release.

She further alleged that the detainees were denied access to their lawyers, while the company’s director was prevented from receiving essential medication during detention.

Describing the alleged treatment as a violation of fundamental human rights, Ogbonna said the Mining Marshals should not use their enforcement responsibilities as justification for disregarding the law.

She urged the committee to investigate the unit’s budgetary allocations, special intervention funds and other sources of financing, including expenditure on publications, publicity materials and operational activities.

In a separate submission, a security operative, Odey Cosmas Polycarp, accused the Mining Marshals, allegedly led by one Onoja Attah, of unlawfully arresting and detaining members of his workforce while demanding ₦100m for their release.

Polycarp alleged that the workers were arrested in a residential neighbourhood where no quarrying or mining activities were taking place, questioning the justification for their arrest and detention.

He further claimed that the detainees were repeatedly beaten while in custody, leaving them traumatised and fearful for their safety.

He urged the lawmakers to investigate the allegations of extortion, unlawful detention and assault, and ensure that any officers found culpable were held accountable.

The allegations have raised concerns about the operational conduct, funding and accountability mechanisms of the Mining Marshals, particularly their enforcement activities involving licensed mining operators.

The committee is expected to hear from the NSCDC leadership and other relevant stakeholders as it examines the unit’s financial and operational framework and determines whether its personnel have acted within their statutory mandate.

The investigation is also expected to address the protection of legitimate mining businesses, respect for fundamental rights and measures to prevent the enforcement of laws against illegal mining from being abused.

The post Reps give NSCDC CG 24 hours over ₦2bn transactions, extortion allegations appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Ishow Pepper, Iya Efunsetan’s daughter dies
description:
Dr Olatunde Ogunsola-Oluyemi, daughter of the late veteran Yoruba theatre practitioner, Ishola Ogunsola, popularly known as Ishow Pepper, and veteran actress Evangelist Iyabo Ogunsola, popularly known as Iya Efunsetan, is dead.
The news of her death was confirmed on Monday, with tributes pouring in
content:
Dr Olatunde Ogunsola-Oluyemi, daughter of the late veteran Yoruba theatre practitioner, Ishola Ogunsola, popularly known as Ishow Pepper, and veteran actress Evangelist Iyabo Ogunsola, popularly known as Iya Efunsetan, is dead.

The news of her death was confirmed on Monday, with tributes pouring in from people in the Yoruba film and theatre industry.

PUNCH Online gathered that Oluyemi was one of the daughters of the late theatre icon.

Her death was also announced by her friend and colleague, Wumi Olabimtan, in an Instagram post on Monday, in which she described the deceased as one of the closest people in her life.

Olabimtan fondly recalled calling her “Aunty Tunde” and “Mummy Iwa”, describing her as a talented woman whose laughter, wisdom and kindness made a lasting impression on those around her.

She wrote, “The incredibly beautiful and talented Aunty Tunde. You were one of the dearest, closest souls to me. Your laughter was a sanctuary, your talent was effortless, and your heart was completely pure.”

Olabimtan added, “The stage of this world feels so empty without you Dr Olatunde Oluyemi (Nee Ishowpepper).”

She also prayed for the repose of Oluyemi’s soul, saying she would “forever remain the leading lady” of her heart.

She was married to filmmaker and theatre practitioner Ayo Oluyemi, who is associated with the Ibadan Metropolitan College of Theatre Arts and Cinematography.

The cause of her death was not disclosed.

title: Tinubu orders release of 78 suspects arrested over Abuja convoy attack
description:
The Federal Capital Territory (FCT) Police Command has announced plans to release 78 suspects arrested in connection with the attack on President Bola Tinubu’s motorcade in Abuja following the President’s decision to grant them clemency.
The command’s spokesperson, Josephine Adeh, disclosed this in
content:
The Federal Capital Territory (FCT) Police Command has announced plans to release 78 suspects arrested in connection with the attack on President Bola Tinubu’s motorcade in Abuja following the President’s decision to grant them clemency.

The command’s spokesperson, Josephine Adeh, disclosed this in a statement issued on Monday.

According to the statement, the suspects were arrested following an attack on the President’s convoy on Friday, November 13, at a mosque in the Garki District of Abuja.

The incident reportedly occurred shortly after Tinubu observed Jumu’ah prayers at the mosque.

“The FCT Police Command wishes to inform the public that 78 suspects were arrested following the attack on the motorcade of President Bola Tinubu, GCFR, on Friday, November 13, 2026, at a mosque in Garki District, Abuja.

“The incident occurred shortly after the President observed Jumu’ah prayers at a mosque in Garki, when some individuals attacked the departing convoy with stones and other dangerous objects, damaging several vehicles and causing injuries to some security operatives,” the statement partly read.

She said a joint security team led by the Police responded to the incident, adding that intelligence-led raids in the area subsequently led to more arrests, bringing the total number of suspects to 78.

“A joint security team, led by the Police, swiftly responded to the incident, while subsequent intelligence-led raids within the area led to further arrests, bringing the total number of suspects arrested in connection with the incident to seventy-eight, ” she said.

Adeh added that following the clemency, the Presidency directed that the suspects be warned and released.

“Following the extension of presidential clemency to the individuals involved in the attack, the Presidency directed that the suspects arrested in connection with the incident be warned and released. In compliance with the directive, the Command wishes to inform the public that the suspects are currently undergoing the necessary release processes.,” the statement said.

She also said the CP Ahmed Sanusi warned against violence ahead of the 2027 General Elections.

“The CP warns against acts of violence, public disorder and destruction of property. As preparations for the 2027 General Elections intensify, the Command urges all political parties, political actors and their supporters to embrace peaceful political engagement and shun violence, intimidation, inflammatory statements and incitement, ” Adeh said.

She said the CP has directed all Area Commanders, Divisional Police Officers and heads of tactical units to remain vigilant and intensify security operations to ensure the safety of residents and visitors, the statement added.

The police statement is the first official acknowledgment of the attack.

On the day of the incident, it was disputed by the Presidency.

Tinubu’s Senior Special Assistant on Digital Engagement, Strategy and New media, O’tega Ogra rejected claims that the convoy was stoned by youths at the Shehu Shagari Central Mosque in Area 1, Garki.

“Contrary to the narrative being pushed by the opposition, with videos of their alleged paid thugs at the National Mosque today, here is footage of Mr President leaving the mosque after Friday prayers this afternoon,” Ogra wrote in a post accompanying a video of the President leaving the mosque.

A chieftain of the African Democratic Congress, Dino Melaye later posted a video showing youths throwing stones at a convoy that appeared to be the President’s.

The clip, which went viral, also captured some of the youths chanting “Ba ma yi, ba ma so,” a Hausa expression meaning “we don’t want you; we don’t support you.

The post Tinubu orders release of 78 suspects arrested over Abuja convoy attack appeared first on Very Nigerian.

title: FCTA: Wike gave UNIABUJA 4,519 hectares, above 100-hectare limit approved by predecessor
description:
• Says protesters ignored 2016 committee report involving varsity reps
• Accuses institution of allocating 100 hectares to EFCC without FCTA approval

Federal Capital Territory Administration (FCTA) has disclosed that Minister Nyesom Wike approved 4,519.8 hectares of land for the University of Abuja
content:
• Says protesters ignored 2016 committee report involving varsity reps

• Accuses institution of allocating 100 hectares to EFCC without FCTA approval

Federal Capital Territory Administration (FCTA) has disclosed that Minister Nyesom Wike approved 4,519.8 hectares of land for the University of Abuja (UNIABUJA), far above the 100 hectares recommended by a joint committee and approved by the immediate past FCT Minister, Mohammed Bello.

The administration said this disclosure exposed what it described as the misplaced nature of Monday’s protest by the university’s Joint Action Committee (JAC) over the reduction of its landmass from 11,824.04 hectares to 4,685 hectares.

According to the FCTA, Wike did not arbitrarily reduce the university’s land but acted on the recommendations of a committee established in 2016 to address land-related issues involving the institution and the administration.

The FCTA’s position was contained in a statement issued on Monday by the Senior Special Assistant to the FCT Minister on Public Communications and Social Media, Lere Olayinka.

Olayinka said the committee, inaugurated on November 10, 2016, by the then FCT Minister, was mandated to examine the university’s land size, encroachment by indigenous settlers, illegal development on its Gwagwalada Mini Campus and the issuance of title documents for the two campuses.

He noted that five of the committee’s 12 members were representatives of UNIABUJA, including Prof. Otaki Alanana, Prof. A. Mallam, Mohamed Kassim, A.E. Ripite and Sadiq O. Shuaibu.

The committee, he said, concluded that the university’s over 11,000 hectares of land was far beyond the size recommended by the National Universities Commission (NUC), which it put at 100 hectares.

Olayinka said the report was subsequently approved by Bello, adding that Wike, rather than restrict the university to the 100 hectares recommended, approved 4,519.8 hectares.

He argued that the allocation was sufficient to accommodate more than 80,000 buildings on plots measuring 500 square metres each.

The minister’s aide also questioned the rationale behind the protest by members of the Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU), Senior Staff Association of Nigerian Universities (SSANU), Non-Academic Staff Union of Educational and Associated Institutions (NASU), the Students’ Union Government and the university’s alumni association.

He challenged the protesters to explain whether they were unaware that university representatives participated in the committee that recommended the reduction of the institution’s landholding.

Olayinka further alleged that the university had been allocating portions of the disputed land to individuals and corporate organisations, including the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC), to which it allegedly allocated 100 hectares without recourse to the FCTA.

He questioned the justification for retaining more than 11,000 hectares when, according to him, the university had not demonstrated the need for such an expansive landholding in its 38 years of existence.

The FCTA spokesman also dismissed concerns that the land reduction would negatively affect the university’s academic and administrative operations, challenging the unions to explain how the decision would affect staff salaries or students’ education.

He urged the protesting unions to be transparent about their interests in the land dispute, insisting that the land was originally allocated to the university by the government.

The post FCTA: Wike gave UNIABUJA 4,519 hectares, above 100-hectare limit approved by predecessor appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: NIN VERIFICATION: Keyamo gives domestic airlines December deadline
description:
By Dickson Omobola



Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, Monday, directed the Nigeria Civil Aviation Authority, NCAA, to enforce full compliance with the Airport Passenger Verification System, vPASS, among all scheduled domestic airlines by December 31, saying passengers
content:
By Dickson Omobola

Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, Monday, directed the Nigeria Civil Aviation Authority, NCAA, to enforce full compliance with the Airport Passenger Verification System, vPASS, among all scheduled domestic airlines by December 31, saying passengers without a valid National Identification Number, NIN, will be barred from boarding domestic flights from January 1, 2027.

Keyamo said the initiative, approved by the Federal Executive Council, FEC, under President Bola Tinubu’s airport modernisation drive, was designed to eliminate airport touting, bulk ticket racketeering and identity fraud.

He spoke during the official unveiling of the vPASS at the Murtala Muhammed Airport, MMA, Domestic Terminal in Lagos.

He said: “I am giving the airlines till the end of December. I repeat it again: from January 1, no airline will be allowed to board their passengers if they don’t key into vPASS. All airlines, irrespective of whom, irrespective of whatever, must key into vPASS for scheduled flights.

“The vPASS is simply a system that is linked to all our NINs, so you cannot board any aircraft locally without your NIN. In one fell swoop, it has eliminated touting at the airport where people who have no business boarding aircraft get access to the departure lounge, or buy tickets in bulk and sell to people in other names. We now have clean manifests for all aircraft, and we know the clear identity of those who board.”

vPASS, developed by the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria, FAAN, in partnership with private-sector technology firm VERXID Technologies Limited, would be replacing the traditional physical identity checks and boarding-gate bottlenecks with contactless facial and iris biometric recognition.

Under the new protocol, Nigerian travellers must link their NIN and date of birth to their biometric profiles, either through the vPASS mobile application, available on the Google Play Store and Apple App Store, or at designated airport onboarding kiosks. Foreign nationals travelling on domestic routes will complete the onboarding process using their international passports.

Keyamo said the system would apply strictly to domestic operations, adding that a separate border-control framework had already been deployed at international terminals in collaboration with the Ministry of Interior.

On concerns that the public-private partnership could lead to additional costs for passengers, the minister assured travellers that any associated charge would be “very, very minimal.”

Speaking after demonstrating live registration alongside the minister, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of FAAN, Olubunmi Kuku, said the platform introduced a seamless “single sign-on” experience that strengthened terminal access control while accelerating passenger processing.

Kuku said: “Once you register, before you get into the security gates, you simply enter the last four digits of your NIN and it opens the gates for you. When you get to the airline boarding gates, instead of someone checking different forms of physical ID, you just use your facial biometrics or the QR code on your boarding pass. It is swift, smart, and efficient.”

Kuku confirmed that the infrastructure was already operational in Lagos and Abuja ahead of its nationwide expansion to all domestic airports.

She added that the remainder of November and the December Yuletide travel period would serve as an onboarding and pilot window for travellers before mandatory enforcement takes effect on January 1.

Highlighting the technical architecture behind the deployment, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of VERXID Technologies Limited, Adebayo Bankole, said the platform was built to meet strict data governance and operational standards.

Bankole said: “Our sole responsibility is to ensure the implementation is seamlessly put together, that passenger data security is well protected in full alignment with Nigeria’s data protection laws, and that travellers enjoy a frictionless experience across the airport ecosystem.”

title: Otti assures of his continuous provision of enabling environment for talented youths to thrive
description:
Governor Alex Otti has assured that his administration would continue to create an enabling environment for talented individuals to develop their abilities and contribute meaningfully to society.
Governor Otti gave the assurance while speaking during the 13th edition of the Vision Africa Icons Music
content:
Governor Alex Otti has assured that his administration would continue to create an enabling environment for talented individuals to develop their abilities and contribute meaningfully to society.

Governor Otti gave the assurance while speaking during the 13th edition of the Vision Africa Icons Music Talent Show held in Umuahia, Abia State.

The Governor, represented by his Chief of Staff (CoS), Caleb Ajagba, observed that the event demonstrated what could be achieved when the right leadership and supportive institutions provided opportunities for people to realise their potential.

According to him, Abia possesses enormous human resources which, if properly identified, encouraged and supported, could produce individuals capable of achieving recognition beyond the state.

“Abia is blessed, and we shall continue to identify, encourage and support the talents that God has deposited in our people,” the governor stated.

Otti also expressed his administration’s readiness to partner with Vision Africa in advancing talent discovery and development, commending the organisation’s founder, Archbishop Dr Sunday Ndukwo Onuoha, whom he described as his personal friend, for sustaining the initiative.

The governor described the performances as evidence of the diverse gifts with which God had endowed the people of Abia, noting that the different voices, musical expressions and artistic styles displayed by the contestants reflected the richness of the state’s human resources.

“What you are seeing today shows that we are many parts. Looking at all the contestants, you will know that God has blessed them with different voices. They have all demonstrated their uniqueness,” he said.

Otti commended the contestants for demonstrating the depth of musical talent and creative abilities within the state.

The governor further assured that the eventual winner would receive the necessary support and exposure to pursue opportunities on the international music stage.

The founder and President of Vision Africa, Archbishop Dr Sunday Ndukwo Onuoha, called for greater tolerance, justice, equity and peaceful coexistence among Nigerians, irrespective of their ethnic, religious, linguistic and cultural differences.

He noted that Nigeria’s diversity made it unrealistic to expect citizens to speak the same language, exhibit identical cultural practices or approach life from the same background.

He however maintained that these differences should not constitute barriers to national unity, insisting that Nigerians could preserve their individual identities while working together towards a common national destiny.

Onuoha emphasised the importance of allowing individuals and communities to express themselves freely within their respective capacities, arguing that mutual respect and acceptance were essential ingredients for sustainable peace.

The Chairman of the occasion, Dr Noah Nuhu Dallaji, represented by Chief Theo Ubani, commended Onuoha for his contributions to human development and humanitarian causes, describing the Vision Africa initiative as an important platform for identifying and nurturing emerging talents.

He expressed appreciation for the organisation’s consistency and progressive development, noting that the competition was helping young Nigerians discover their abilities and prepare for opportunities that could contribute to the country’s future growth.

Dallaji also applauded Vision Africa for providing a platform through which Nigerian talents could gain wider exposure and potentially take their creative abilities to international audiences.

In her remarks, Nollywood actress and film producer, Sophia Williams, described the competition as a distinctive initiative deserving of commendation, particularly for its commitment to discovering and developing emerging musical talents.

She praised Onuoha for his confidence in African creativity and his determination to create opportunities for gifted young people to showcase their abilities.

Mr Antia Elvis Ifeanyichukwu, contestant number eight, has emerged winner of the 13th edition of the Vision Africa Icons Music Talent Show.

title: State assemblies approve state police bill, await Tinubu’s assent
description:
By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja



All 36 State Houses of Assembly have approved the proposed constitutional amendment seeking to establish state police services in Nigeria, paving the way for the bill to be transmitted to President Bola Tinubu for assent.







The Clerk to the National Assembly, Kamo
content:
By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja

All 36 State Houses of Assembly have approved the proposed constitutional amendment seeking to establish state police services in Nigeria, paving the way for the bill to be transmitted to President Bola Tinubu for assent.

The Clerk to the National Assembly, Kamoru Ogunlana, disclosed this in a statement issued on Monday, November 16, 2026.

According to the statement, the unanimous approval represents 100 per cent endorsement by the state legislatures, exceeding the constitutional requirement of at least 24 state assemblies under Section 9(2) of the 1999 Constitution, as amended.

The bill, titled, “A Bill for an Act to Alter the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 to Provide for the Establishment of State Police Services and for Related Matters,” seeks to provide the constitutional framework for establishing state police across the country.

Ogunlana explained that the bill had earlier fulfilled all constitutional and administrative requirements for transmission, but the leadership of the National Assembly directed a brief delay to allow for broader national consensus and engagement with all the states.

He described the unanimous endorsement as an unprecedented demonstration of cooperation between the National Assembly and state legislatures.

According to him, the development also reflects constructive collaboration between the executive arms of government at the federal and state levels.

“Following the completion of the verification process by my Office, the Bill is set for transmission to the President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, for His Excellency’s assent,” the statement read.

The Clerk described the development as a major milestone in the ongoing efforts to reform Nigeria’s policing system.

He added that the achievement would provide a foundation for the National Assembly to complete and transmit other Sixth Constitution Alteration Bills to the State Houses of Assembly for consideration.

The leadership of the National Assembly also commended the 36 state governors, Speakers and members of the State Houses of Assembly, as well as other stakeholders, for their cooperation and commitment to reforming the country’s policing system.

title: Tinubu Grants Clemency To 78 Suspects Arrested Over Attack On Presidential Convoy
description: The Federal Capital Territory (FCT) Police Command has said it is processing the release of 78 suspects arrested over the attack on President Bola Tinubu’s convoy in Abuja, following a presidential clemency directive.In a statement on Monday, the FCT Police Public Relations Officer, Josephine
content:
The Federal Capital Territory (FCT) Police Command has said it is processing the release of 78 suspects arrested over the attack on President Bola Tinubu’s convoy in Abuja, following a presidential clemency directive.

In a statement on Monday, the FCT Police Public Relations Officer, Josephine Adeh, said the Presidency had directed that the suspects be warned and released after extending presidential clemency to those involved in the incident.

Adeh said the suspects were currently undergoing the necessary release processes.

The suspects were arrested after the President’s motorcade was reportedly attacked on Friday, November 13, shortly after he observed Jumu’ah prayers at a mosque in the Garki District of the Federal Capital Territory.

Some individuals were said to have attacked the departing presidential convoy with stones and other dangerous objects, damaging several vehicles and injuring some security operatives.

According to the police, a joint security team led by the Force responded swiftly, while subsequent intelligence-led raids in the area led to additional arrests, bringing the total number of suspects to 78.

“Following the extension of presidential clemency to the individuals involved in the attack, the Presidency directed that the suspects arrested in connection with the incident be warned and released,” the statement partly read. “In compliance with the directive, the Command wishes to inform the public that the suspects are currently undergoing the necessary release processes.”

The Commissioner of Police, FCT Command, Ahmed Sanusi, warned against violence, public disorder and destruction of property.

He also urged political parties, political actors and their supporters to embrace peaceful engagement as preparations for the 2027 general elections intensify.

The police commissioner directed area commanders, divisional police officers and heads of tactical units to remain vigilant and intensify security operations to protect residents and visitors.

Residents were also urged to report suspicious people and activities to the nearest police station or through the Command’s emergency lines.

title: Lagos retrains sanitation workers on safety, efficiency
description:
By Olasunkanmi Akoni



The Lagos State Government has reaffirmed its commitment to improving the capacity, safety and efficiency of sanitation workers through continuous training and professional development to promote a cleaner and healthier environment.







The commitment was reiterated on Mon
content:
By Olasunkanmi Akoni

The Lagos State Government has reaffirmed its commitment to improving the capacity, safety and efficiency of sanitation workers through continuous training and professional development to promote a cleaner and healthier environment.

The commitment was reiterated on Monday at a capacity-building workshop for selected sanitation workers held at the Lagos Chamber of Commerce and Industry (LCCI) building, Alausa, Ikeja.

The Permanent Secretary, Office of Environmental Services, Omobolaji Gaji, represented by the Director of Sanitation Services, Dr Hassan Sanuth, said the workshop was designed to equip participants with the knowledge, practical skills and safety measures required to improve sanitation operations across the state.

He described sanitation workers as indispensable partners in the government’s efforts to maintain a clean, healthy and liveable environment, noting that their daily activities, including street sweeping, drainage clearing and waste collection, were critical to protecting public health and preventing flooding.

Gaji commended the workers for their dedication, observing that many of them begin their duties early in the morning, long before most residents commence their daily activities.

He said their contributions remained essential to maintaining environmental orderliness and ensuring that Lagos remained a city residents could be proud of.

According to him, the selected participants were identified in recognition of their commitment and dedication to duty, adding that the training represented a deliberate investment by the government in improving their welfare, competence and productivity.

He explained that the programme would expose participants to safer working practices, appropriate use of personal protective equipment (PPE), modern waste-handling techniques and improved approaches to sanitation service delivery.

The Permanent Secretary added that the workshop would also provide an opportunity for participants to exchange experiences, discuss operational challenges and share practical ideas for improving environmental sanitation.

He urged the workers to actively participate in the sessions, engage the facilitators and apply the knowledge acquired to their daily responsibilities.

“This capacity-building programme underscores the Lagos State Government’s commitment to developing a more skilled, safety-conscious and efficient sanitation workforce capable of responding effectively to the environmental challenges of a rapidly growing metropolis,” Gaji said.

He also appreciated the facilitators, partners and other stakeholders whose contributions supported the organisation of the programme, calling for sustained collaboration to improve environmental sanitation and public health.

He said a clean and sustainable Lagos required collective responsibility, stressing that sanitation workers remained central to the state’s environmental management efforts.

Gaji assured the workers that the government valued their contributions, respected their dignity and remained committed to their professional development.

In a lecture titled, “Safety Culture: A Need to Prevent Occupational Accidents,” the guest speaker, Mr Adeyinka Adebiyi, urged sanitation workers to prioritise workplace safety while carrying out their daily assignments.

He noted that their duties exposed them to various occupational hazards capable of causing injuries, illnesses and, in severe cases, loss of lives.

Adebiyi emphasised the need for strict compliance with safety procedures, proper use of personal protective equipment, effective risk assessment and responsible handling of waste materials.

He also advised the workers to remain vigilant, avoid unsafe practices and promptly report potential hazards to prevent avoidable accidents and health complications.

The capacity-building initiative is expected to improve sanitation service delivery, promote safer working conditions and contribute to a cleaner and healthier environment for residents across Lagos State.

title: NDC condemns attack on Kwankwaso, demands arrest of perpetrators
description:
By Henry Umoru



ABUJA — The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) has condemned the reported attack on its 2027 vice-presidential candidate and former Kano State Governor, Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, in Bichi, Kano State, calling on the police and other security agencies to investigate the incident
content:
By Henry Umoru

ABUJA — The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) has condemned the reported attack on its 2027 vice-presidential candidate and former Kano State Governor, Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, in Bichi, Kano State, calling on the police and other security agencies to investigate the incident and arrest those responsible.

The party also demanded the arrest of anyone found to have sponsored the attack, while urging security agencies to guarantee the safety of political candidates and their supporters, irrespective of party affiliation.

The NDC made its position known in a statement on Monday by its National Publicity Secretary, Osa Director, describing the incident as an attack on its candidate, supporters and democratic values.

The party alleged that the attackers were thugs loyal to the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC), although it did not provide evidence to substantiate the allegation.

According to the statement, the incident was not a mere disruption but a deliberate assault that should be thoroughly investigated.

The party expressed concern over what it described as a growing pattern of violence against opposition candidates and supporters across the country.

It alleged that such incidents were attempts to intimidate political opponents and undermine democratic participation.

“The spate of violent attacks on opposition candidates and supporters across the country is a clear sign that the APC has lost the argument, lost the people, and has now resorted to thuggery and intimidation to cling to power,” the statement said.

The NDC, however, declared that it would not be intimidated or discouraged from participating in the political process.

“The NDC will not be intimidated. We will not be silenced. We will not retreat,” Director said.

The party called on the Nigeria Police Force, the Department of State Services (DSS) and other security agencies to immediately investigate the Bichi incident, identify and arrest those responsible, including any alleged sponsors, and prevent further attacks on political actors.

It stressed that Nigeria deserved free, fair and peaceful elections rather than political violence and intimidation.

The statement added: “Nigeria deserves a free, fair, and peaceful election — not a reign of terror. A New Nigeria is possible with the NDC.”

title: Robert Pattinson unveiled as new James Bond star
description:
British actor Robert Pattinson has been unveiled as the new James Bond, bringing an end to years of speculation over who will succeed Daniel Craig as the iconic British secret agent.
Pattinson, best known for his roles in the Twilight franchise and The Batman, described his appointment as an “honour
content:
British actor Robert Pattinson has been unveiled as the new James Bond, bringing an end to years of speculation over who will succeed Daniel Craig as the iconic British secret agent.

Pattinson, best known for his roles in the Twilight franchise and The Batman, described his appointment as an “honour of a lifetime” and a “dream come true”.

“I couldn’t be more excited about this partnership and the work ahead with this fantastic team,” he said.

The announcement by Amazon MGM Studios on Monday confirmed Pattinson as the latest actor to take on the role of 007, following Craig’s departure after starring in five Bond films, with his final appearance in No Time to Die in 2021.

Several actors had been linked with the coveted role over the years, including Henry Cavill, Idris Elba, Aaron Taylor-Johnson, Jack Lowden, Theo James, Paul Mescal, James Norton, Callum Turner and Jacob Elordi.

Pattinson’s appointment also marks a major development for the franchise, with acclaimed filmmaker Denis Villeneuve set to direct the new Bond film from a screenplay by Steven Knight, creator of the hit television series Peaky Blinders.

Villeneuve, whose film credits include Prisoners and the Dune trilogy, will lead the next chapter of the long-running spy franchise.

The new production will be the first James Bond film under Amazon MGM Studios, following the reported $1bn sale of the franchise in 2025 by its long-time producers, Barbara Broccoli and Michael G. Wilson.

The deal gave Amazon full creative control of the franchise, ending the decades-long involvement of the Broccoli family, which had overseen the series since the era of its original producer, Albert ‘Cubby’ Broccoli.

Pattinson faces the challenge of succeeding Craig, whose five outings as Bond earned about $3.5bn worldwide and helped restore the franchise’s commercial and critical appeal.

Craig’s casting in 2005 initially attracted criticism from some fans and sections of the British press, but his portrayal of the spy went on to become one of the most successful periods in the franchise’s history.

Pattinson’s selection followed a series of screen tests conducted in October by Villeneuve, casting director Nina Gold and Amazon executives. Other actors reportedly considered for the role included Callum Turner, Jack Lowden, Josh O’Connor and Nicholas Hoult.

Reports before the announcement suggested Pattinson had emerged as the favourite after being offered a three-film commitment, compared with the four-film requirement reportedly presented to other contenders.

The actor, whose recent film credits include The Drama and Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey, is also expected to appear in Dune: Part Three, scheduled for release in December.

title: Two Killed In Chad Prison Break
description: Two people died in a jailbreak that saw 30 detainees escape from the Mongo prison in central Chad at the weekend, local authorities told AFP on Monday.Three other people were wounded in the chaos on Sunday, Abdoulaye Ibrahim Siam, the government’s delegate in Guera province, told AFP.“We
content:
Two people died in a jailbreak that saw 30 detainees escape from the Mongo prison in central Chad at the weekend, local authorities told AFP on Monday.

Three other people were wounded in the chaos on Sunday, Abdoulaye Ibrahim Siam, the government’s delegate in Guera province, told AFP.

“We count 30 prisoners who escaped. The forces of order and justice are on their tail,” he added.

Around 22 other inmates who attempted to abscond were “recaptured by law enforcement”, the sub-prefect of Mongo, Ahmat Tagal, told AFP.

Several of the prison’s offices were set on fire in the breakout, the authorities said.

The establishment housed 510 inmates before the escape.

In April 2025, a violent mutiny broke out at the same prison, leaving four dead.

Three others were wounded, including the provincial governor, who was hit as he tried to bring the situation back under control.

Some inmates had managed to get hold of the prison guards’ weapons, triggering a mass breakout in which more than 100 prisoners managed to flee.

title: Plateau Records Over 5,400 Suspected Diabetes Cases In Nine Months
description: The Plateau State Government says 5,457 suspected new cases of diabetes were recorded across health facilities in the state between January and September 2026, raising concerns over the need for increased screening, early diagnosis and proper management of the disease.The Commissioner for Health, Dr
content:
The Plateau State Government says 5,457 suspected new cases of diabetes were recorded across health facilities in the state between January and September 2026, raising concerns over the need for increased screening, early diagnosis and proper management of the disease.

The Commissioner for Health, Dr. Nicholas Ba’amlong, disclosed this on Monday during a press briefing in Jos to commemorate the 2026 World Diabetes Day, noting that the figure followed 5,546 suspected cases recorded in 2025.

Ba’amlong, however, clarified that the figures represented suspected cases and not confirmed diagnoses, stressing that diabetes remained a major public health concern because many people were living with the condition without knowing their status.

He also disclosed that findings from the 2024 nationwide Know Your Number, Control Your Number screening campaign showed that 14,359 people were screened in Plateau State, with 2,610, representing approximately 18 per cent, recording elevated blood glucose levels.

According to him, the findings highlight the need to expand access to screening, diagnosis and treatment, but do not represent the prevalence of diabetes in the state.

As part of activities marking this year’s World Diabetes Day, the Ministry of Health, in collaboration with the Plateau State chapters of the Diabetes Association of Nigeria and the Endocrine and Metabolic Society of Nigeria, conducted a free workplace screening exercise at the Joseph Gomwalk Secretariat Complex, Jos.

The exercise, which targeted 1,000 civil servants, provided blood glucose and blood pressure checks, weight and body mass index assessments, health education, counselling and referrals for further medical attention where necessary.

The commissioner said the state government, under Governor Caleb Mutfwang, was also working towards extending diabetes education and screening services to underserved communities across the 17 local government areas through existing primary healthcare facilities and community outreach programmes.

He added that the government was exploring partnerships and appropriate medical technologies to improve access to diagnostic services, particularly at the primary healthcare level, while strengthening follow-up and referral systems for individuals with elevated blood glucose levels.

“Screening is only the beginning. Early detection must lead to appropriate diagnosis and treatment,” Ba’amlong said.

He urged residents, particularly those with a family history of diabetes, excess weight or high blood pressure, to regularly check their blood glucose levels and seek medical attention when necessary.

The commissioner also advised residents to maintain healthy lifestyles through balanced diets, regular physical activity and weight management, while avoiding tobacco and limiting alcohol consumption.

He identified excessive thirst, frequent urination, unexplained weight loss and persistent fatigue as some of the symptoms that could indicate diabetes, urging people living with the condition to adhere to prescribed treatment and attend regular medical reviews.

World Diabetes Day is observed annually on November 14 to raise awareness about diabetes, promote prevention and encourage access to quality care for people living with the condition.

title: Abbas urges fairer global narrative on Nigeria, says country is more than its challenges
description:
• Insists call for balanced reporting not an attempt to shield government from scrutiny

Speaker of the House of Representatives, Tajudeen Abbas, has urged the international community to adopt a fairer and more balanced narrative about Nigeria, warning against portraying the country exclusively thro
content:
• Insists call for balanced reporting not an attempt to shield government from scrutiny

Speaker of the House of Representatives, Tajudeen Abbas, has urged the international community to adopt a fairer and more balanced narrative about Nigeria, warning against portraying the country exclusively through its economic difficulties, insecurity and other challenges.

Abbas said while the hardship confronting Nigerians was real and demanded urgent attention from governments, Nigeria should not be defined solely by its problems at the expense of its human capital, economic potential and development progress.

He spoke on Monday at the ongoing Global Alliance World Public Relations Forum in Abuja, where he addressed issues bordering on responsible communication, democratic accountability, governance and institutional reforms.

The Speaker, who was represented by the House Majority Leader, Prof. Julius Ihonvbere, said there was a distinction between reporting Nigeria’s challenges and reducing the country’s identity to those difficulties.

“The difficulties confronting households and businesses are real and deserve serious attention,” he said.

He added: “There is a difference between reporting a country’s difficulties and reducing the country to those difficulties. There is also a difference between legitimate scrutiny and the construction of narratives that oversimplify complex realities.

“We do not seek immunity from scrutiny. We seek fairness in the exercise of scrutiny. This is not an argument for managing Nigeria’s image at the expense of truth.”

Abbas urged public relations practitioners and other communication professionals to promote fairness, accuracy and balance in their work, noting that the narratives they shaped could influence public understanding of countries, institutions and democratic processes.

He said the government must, however, match its demand for fair international representation with concrete action to improve the living conditions of citizens.

According to him, Nigerians expect improved security, more employment opportunities, efficient public services and better governance, while the benefits of ongoing economic reforms must begin to reflect in their daily lives.

He said the reforms being implemented by the President Bola Tinubu-led administration were intended to address structural weaknesses, restore economic stability and lay the foundation for sustainable growth.

Acknowledging the immediate costs of the reforms, Abbas said government had a responsibility to ensure that their eventual benefits translated into tangible improvements in the lives of ordinary Nigerians.

On insecurity, he called for decisive and sustained action against perpetrators of violence, describing every innocent life lost as a tragedy requiring justice and accountability.

“Every innocent life lost is a tragedy that calls for justice and accountability,” he said.

He urged the country to strengthen its security institutions and protect every citizen, irrespective of religion, ethnicity or place of origin.

Reflecting on Nigeria’s democratic journey since 1999, Abbas said the country had sustained constitutional governance through successive elections, changes in leadership and the continued operation of democratic institutions.

He, however, acknowledged that the democratic process remained a work in progress, identifying institutional capacity, electoral confidence, public accountability and political intolerance as challenges requiring attention.

According to him, democracy depends not only on strong institutions but also on the space it provides for disagreement, representation, negotiation and peaceful political competition.

“Democracy cannot thrive on institutions alone. It also depends on the quality of public discourse,” he said.

The Speaker called for access to reliable information to enable citizens to make informed decisions, urging political actors to focus debates on ideas, policies and evidence rather than insults, intimidation and deliberate falsehoods.

He also called for the protection of press freedom, saying journalists must be allowed to scrutinise those in authority while maintaining professional standards. Public institutions, he added, must embrace transparency and accountability.

Abbas described parliament as the constitutional platform for representation, deliberation and accountability, saying its legitimacy depended not only on the laws it enacted but also on public confidence in its processes.

He said the House of Representatives, with 360 members representing constituencies across the federation, had a responsibility to accommodate the diverse interests and aspirations of Nigerians.

He listed national security, economic growth, education, healthcare, social inclusion, institutional strengthening and an open parliament among the legislature’s priorities.

The Speaker said legislative performance should ultimately be measured by its impact on citizens’ welfare, security and opportunities.

He also disclosed that the National Assembly had advanced constitutional reforms aimed at strengthening the country’s security architecture, including a proposal for the establishment of state police.

The post Abbas urges fairer global narrative on Nigeria, says country is more than its challenges appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: FCTA accuses UniAbuja of selling land to individuals, corporate bodies, EFCC
description:
By Omeiza Ajayi



ABUJA: The Federal Capital Territory Administration FCTA has accused the University of Abuja of selling its land to individuals and corporate organisations, including the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission EFCC, to which it allocated 100 hectares without recourse to the Admi
content:
By Omeiza Ajayi

ABUJA: The Federal Capital Territory Administration FCTA has accused the University of Abuja of selling its land to individuals and corporate organisations, including the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission EFCC, to which it allocated 100 hectares without recourse to the Administration.

Lere Olayinka, Senior Special Assistant on Public Communications and Social Media to the Federal Capital Territory FCT minister, Nyesom Wike, made the disclosure in a statement on Monday.

He spoke as the Joint Action Committee (JAC) of UniAbuja protested the reduction of the university’s land from 11,824.04 hectares to 4,685 hectares.

The FCTA described the protest as misplaced, saying Wike only acted on an approval granted by the previous administration.

Olayinka challenged the protesters to name public universities anywhere in the world that sit on over 11,000 hectares. He also asked what expansion UniAbuja has not carried out in 38 years of its establishment that would now require 11,824.04 hectares.

He said Wike acted on the 2016 recommendation of a Joint Committee of the FCTA and UNIABUJA on Land and Sundry Issues. What that committee recommended for the university, and what the immediate past FCT Minister, Mohamed Musa Bello, approved, was 100 hectares.

“It is on record that on November 10, 2016, the then FCT Minister inaugurated a Joint Committee of FCTA and UNIABUJA on Land and Sundry Issues.

“The committee was to look into the UNIABUJA land size vis encroachment by indigenous settlers, encroachment on the Gwagwalada Mini Campus land by illegal developers and issuance of titles for the two campuses of the university with their actual land size”, the statement added.

The statement said the university was well represented on the panel. “Five out of the 12 members of the committee were from UNIABUJA. They were Prof Otaki Alanana, Prof A. Mallam, Mohamed Kassim, A.E. Ripite and Sadiq O. Shuaibu.

“The committee recommended amongst others that the land area of over 11,000 hectares of the main campus was far beyond the recommended size by the National University Commission (NUC), and that the recommended size of 100 hectares by the NUC be given to the university.

“Report of the committee was approved by the immediate past FCT Minister, Mohammed Musa Bello, and going by the committee’s recommendation, only 100 hectares of land ought to be given to UNIABUJA.

“However, instead of the 100 hectares recommended by the committee and approved by the immediate past Minister, Wike approved the allocation of 4,519.80 hectares to the university, which should accommodate over 80,000 buildings at 500 square meters per plotx, the FCTA said.

Olayinka directed his questions at the Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU), the Senior Staff Association of Nigerian Universities (SSANU), the Non-Academic Staff Union of Educational and Associated Institutions (NASU), the Students’ Union Government (SUG) and the university’s alumni association.

“Questions to ask the protesters, particularly the Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU), Senior Staff Association of Nigerian Universities (SSANU), Non-Academic Staff Union of Educational and Associated Institutions (NASU), Students’ Union Government (SUG) and the university’s alumni association are; were they unaware that the university had representatives in the committee that recommended the reduction of the UNIABUJA land to 100 hectares in line with the NUC recommendation?

“Where in the civilised world is a university built on over 11,000 hectares of land, on which over 220,000 houses can be built at 500 square meters per plot?”, he queried.

On the effect of the reduction, the statement asked: “If the government that owns a university chooses to reduce the size of its land on which no structure has been built in the school’s 38 years of existence, what effect will that have on ASUU, SSANU and NASU? Will that affect the payment of their salaries? Will it affect the students in terms of their studies?

“Therefore, ASUU, SSANU and NASU should be honest enough to tell Nigerians what their real interests are in a land matter between a university and the government from which it got the land allocation in the first place”, he added.

The post FCTA accuses UniAbuja of selling land to individuals, corporate bodies, EFCC appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Tinubu Approves Recruitment Of 28,000 Soldiers, 50,000 Police Officers - Check Below For Full Details
description: President Tinubu has approved the recruitment of 28,000 additional soldiers and 50,000 police officers under a proposed Five-Year Strategic Defence Operations Plan, the APC Presidential Campaign Council announces.
content:
President Bola Tinubu has approved the recruitment of an additional 28,000 soldiers and 50,000 police officers as part of efforts to strengthen Nigeria’s security architecture and address rising insecurity across the country.

The approval forms part of the administration’s proposed Five-Year Strategic Defence Operations Plan, designed to improve military effectiveness, expand operational capacity and strengthen the country’s response to terrorism, banditry, kidnapping and other criminal activities.

The All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council disclosed this in a statement issued on Sunday by its spokesperson, Dele Alake.

According to the statement, the recruitment of additional soldiers is intended to increase the military’s presence on the ground and improve its operational capacity. “To further the manpower expansion drive, President Tinubu also approved recruiting an additional 28,000 soldiers to strengthen the military’s presence on the ground and enhance its operational effectiveness,” the statement said.

The council added that the President had also approved the recruitment of 50,000 additional police officers to reinforce internal security, expand policing capacity and improve the country’s response to criminal activities.

It further disclosed that the President had created four new Army divisions and restructured existing military formations to expand operational coverage and improve responses to security threats.

The statement also said the administration had approved the establishment of two additional Army depots in Osogbo, Osun State, and Amasiri-Edda, Ebonyi State, to increase military training capacity and accelerate the recruitment of soldiers. Each depot can accommodate 6,000 recruits at a time, giving the two facilities a combined training capacity of 12,000 soldiers. It added that 5,210 recruits were already undergoing training at the Osogbo facility.

The campaign council also highlighted investments in military accommodation and operational infrastructure, including a 700-unit military barracks project in Ikere-Ekiti, Ekiti State.

On the fight against insurgency, the council claimed that military operations across the country had resulted in the killing of more than 15,000 Boko Haram terrorists and bandits over the past three years, and that more than 130,000 Boko Haram fighters and their dependents had surrendered through Operation Safe Corridor, the Federal Government’s rehabilitation programme for repentant insurgents.

The council said the proposed Five-Year Strategic Defence Operations Plan would provide a long-term framework for aligning defence priorities, operational requirements, capability development and expenditure with the country’s security challenges — “toward a more coordinated, intelligence-led, technology-enabled, and prevention-oriented system capable of addressing terrorism, banditry, kidnapping, and other forms of criminality.”

The figures and claims in this report are as stated by the APC Presidential Campaign Council; independent confirmation from the Defence Headquarters and the Nigeria Police Force is yet to be published at the time of this report.

title: Tinubu convoy attack: FCT police to release 78 arrested suspects after presidential clemency
description:
From Molly Kilete, Abuja
The Federal Capital Territory (FCT) Police Command said it is set to release all 78 suspects arrested last Friday over the attack on the motorcade of President Bola Tinubu at a mosque in Garki District of Abuja.
The Police Public Relations Officer, Josephine Adeh, who made t
content:
From Molly Kilete, Abuja

The Federal Capital Territory (FCT) Police Command said it is set to release all 78 suspects arrested last Friday over the attack on the motorcade of President Bola Tinubu at a mosque in Garki District of Abuja.

The Police Public Relations Officer, Josephine Adeh, who made this known, said their release followed the extension of presidential clemency to the individuals involved in the attack.

Adeh, in a statement, said the Presidency had directed that the suspects arrested in connection with the incident be warned and released.

The statement reads: “The FCT Police Command wishes to inform the public that seventy-eight (78) suspects were arrested following the attack on the motorcade of the President and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces, His Excellency, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, GCFR, on Friday, 13th November 2026, at a mosque in Garki District, Abuja.

“The incident occurred shortly after the President observed Jumu’ah prayers at a mosque in Garki, when some individuals attacked the departing convoy with stones and other dangerous objects, damaging several vehicles and causing injuries to some security operatives.

“A joint security team, led by the Police, swiftly responded to the incident, while subsequent intelligence-led raids within the area led to further arrests, bringing the total number of suspects arrested in connection with the incident to seventy-eight (78).

“Following the extension of presidential clemency to the individuals involved in the attack, the Presidency directed that the suspects arrested in connection with the incident be warned and released. In compliance with the directive, the Command wishes to inform the public that the suspects are currently undergoing the necessary release processes.

“The Commissioner of Police, FCT Command, CP Ahmed Mohammed Sanusi, PhD, warns against acts of violence, public disorder and destruction of property. As preparations for the 2027 General Elections intensify, the Command urges all political parties, political actors and their supporters to embrace peaceful political engagement and shun violence, intimidation, inflammatory statements and incitement.

“The CP has consequently directed all Area Commanders, Divisional Police Officers and heads of tactical units to remain vigilant and intensify security operations to ensure the safety of residents and visitors. Residents are also urged to remain security conscious and promptly report suspicious persons and activities to the nearest Police station or through the Command’s emergency lines: 08032003913, 08061581938.”

The post Tinubu convoy attack: FCT police to release 78 arrested suspects after presidential clemency appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Inflation in October 2026 dips to 14.06% from 14.63% in September, says NBS
description:
From Isaac Anumihe, Abuja
The Statistician General of the Federation (SG) and Chief Executive Officer of the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS), Prince Adeyemi Adeniran, has said that inflation for October 2026 has dipped further to 14.06 per cent, compared with the August and September 2026 rates
content:
From Isaac Anumihe, Abuja

The Statistician General of the Federation (SG) and Chief Executive Officer of the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS), Prince Adeyemi Adeniran, has said that inflation for October 2026 has dipped further to 14.06 per cent, compared with the August and September 2026 rates of 15.39 per cent and 14.63 per cent respectively.

In a statement, Adeniran maintained that the month-on-month headline inflation rate in October 2026 was 0.43 per cent, which was 0.38 per cent higher than the rate recorded in September 2026 (0.06 per cent).

Adeniran explained that at the divisional level, the three major contributors to the headline inflation were food and non-alcoholic beverages (5.63 per cent), restaurants and accommodation services (1.82 per cent) and transport (1.50 per cent).

Meanwhile, the least contributors were recreation, sport and culture (0.04 per cent); alcoholic beverages, tobacco and narcotics (0.05 per cent); and insurance and financial services (0.07 per cent).

The food inflation rate in October 2026, the SG said, was 19.13 per cent on a year-on-year basis, lower than the 16.30 per cent recorded in October 2025. Also, on a month-on-month basis, the food inflation rate in October 2026 was -0.75 per cent, up by 0.80 percentage points from September 2026 (-1.55 per cent).

“This can be attributed to the rate of change in the average prices of the following products: Vegetable oil (75cl), titus sardines (125g), green peas (prepacked), mackerel frozen, croakers (apo), rice local, catfish fresh, beef tripes, palm oil (75cl), millet flour (sold loose), among others.

“Core Inflation, which excludes the prices of volatile agricultural produce and energy, stood at 10.78 per cent in October 2026 on a year-on-year basis. On a month-on-month basis, the core inflation rate was -0.53 per cent in October 2026, down by 1.64 per cent compared to September 2026 (1.11 per cent),” the NBS said.

Regarding the newly introduced indices, the inflation rate of the sub-indices for October 2026 shows that the monthly changes recorded were farm produce (-0.40 per cent), energy (1.74 per cent), services (-0.94 per cent), goods (-0.01 per cent) and imported food (-0.38 per cent).

Meanwhile, the inflation rate on a year-on-year basis recorded farm produce (18.38 per cent), energy (12.30 per cent), services (11.73 per cent), goods (13.58 per cent) and imported food (8.39 per cent).

“On a year-on-year basis, the urban inflation rate in October 2026 was 14.84 per cent. On a month-on-month basis, the urban inflation rate was 0.43 per cent in October 2026, down by 0.10 per cent compared to September 2026 (0.53 per cent). The rural inflation rate in October 2026 was 12.17 per cent on a year-on-year basis. On a month-on-month basis, the rural inflation rate in October 2026 was 0.18 per cent, up by 1.07 per cent compared to September 2026,” the SG noted.

The post Inflation in October 2026 dips to 14.06% from 14.63% in September, says NBS appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: The Rise Of Natural-Light Beauty Editorials Using AI
description: Beauty photography has been quietly moving away from heavy retouching and studio gloss. Readers now respond to freckles, soft skin texture, and the warm, slightly uneven glow of real daylight. It is a harder look to fake than it seems, because natural light is subtle and unforgiving. An AI image cre
content:
Beauty photography has been quietly moving away from heavy retouching and studio gloss. Readers now respond to freckles, soft skin texture, and the warm, slightly uneven glow of real daylight. It is a harder look to fake than it seems, because natural light is subtle and unforgiving.

An AI image creator can now explore this style quickly, helping art directors test looks before a single model sits in a chair. Dreamina, with its advanced image generation models, is a natural home for this work. Seedream 5.0 Pro, Nano Banana and GPT Image 2 each interpret light a little differently, so you can compare approaches in one workspace. Here is how to build a natural-light beauty editorial that feels genuinely lived-in.

Why softness is replacing gloss

Audiences have seen enough airbrushed perfection. A face with texture reads as trustworthy, and trust sells skincare, fragrance and wellness more effectively than flawless surfaces. Natural-light editorials position a brand as honest, which is a powerful place to stand.

Understanding daylight’s moods

Not all daylight is the same, and each time of day gives a different emotional tone:

  • Early morning: cool, clean and calm
  • Midday shade: even, neutral and fresh
  • Golden hour: warm, glowing, and romantic
  • Overcast afternoon: soft, wrapped and quiet

Skin that looks like skin

The most common giveaway of a synthetic beauty image is skin that is too smooth. Ask for “visible pores,” “fine facial hair catching light,” and “natural variation in tone.” These cues pull the image toward photographic realism rather than plastic finish.

Makeup that looks like no makeup

Editorial beauty now favours subtlety: a flush of colour on the cheeks, brushed-up brows, a balm-glossed lip. Describe the finish rather than the product: “skin-like base, soft peach blush, barely-there mascara,” and the result keeps its quiet, fresh quality.

Where the light comes from

Direction matters as much as softness. Side light from a window sculpts cheekbones gently, while front light flattens. A white reflector or pale wall bouncing fill into the shadow side lifts the face without ever feeling lit. Mention the window’s side in your prompt to keep the modelling intentional.

Backgrounds that stay out of the way

Beauty needs a calm stage. Plain plaster, linen, a bare wall or softly blurred greenery keep attention on the face. Avoid busy patterns, and keep colours in harmony with the product’s packaging if the image will promote it.

Dreamina’s image models for realistic skin and light

Seedream 5.0 Pro, Dreamina’s latest and most advanced model, handles fine texture with real care. Its 2K output preserves pores and individual hairs, and its deep reasoning generation weighs light, expression and styling together so the whole portrait feels consistent. Pinpoint precision editing lets you correct a single strand or highlight without touching the rest of the face, and multi-layer control keeps background and subject separate.

Nano Banana is useful when you want to test many light directions fast, and GPT Image 2 brings a different tonal sensibility, handy for comparing how soft or contrasty each engine renders the same brief. Together they give an art director a real range of options without leaving Dreamina.

Your 3-step daylight shoot with Dreamina

Step 1: Write a text prompt

Navigate to Dreamina and write a detailed text prompt describing the subject, skin, makeup finish, light direction, and backdrop. You can also add a reference image for a particular look or pose.

Example: Three-quarter portrait of a woman in her thirties with natural freckles and fine skin texture, soft peach blush and a balm-glossed lip, gentle side light from a window on the left, pale plaster wall behind her, calm direct gaze, natural-light beauty editorial photography.

Specifying the window side and the skin texture together is what delivers the honest, unretouched feel.

Step 2: Adjust parameters and generate

Choose your model, Image 5.0 Pro by Seedream 5.0 Pro, then set the aspect ratio, size, and resolution. Use 1K when you are exploring light directions and 2K for the final portrait where texture needs to hold up. Click Dreamina’s icon to generate.

Step 3: Customize and download

Polish the portrait with Dreamina’s AI customization options. Use inpaint to adjust a catchlight or flyaway, expand to make room for editorial text, remove to clear a distracting highlight, and retouch gently to even tone without erasing texture. When it feels like a real morning, click the Download icon to save it.

Pairing the portrait with editorial layout

A beautiful frame becomes an editorial when it sits within a layout. Leave calm space for a headline, choose a typeface that echoes the softness of the image, and keep colour in the same family as the skin tones. The image and the typography should feel like a single quiet voice.

Where natural-light beauty imagery works best

This look has strong uses across the industry:

  • Skincare and clean-beauty campaigns
  • Magazine and newsletter features
  • Salon and spa branding
  • Social content that favours authenticity over gloss

Final thoughts

The beauty industry’s move toward honesty rewards photography that looks observed rather than manufactured. An AI image creator like Dreamina, with Seedream 5.0 Pro, Nano Banana and GPT Image 2 working side by side, lets you explore that honesty before production begins.

Describe the light’s direction, keep skin textured, stay subtle with makeup, and let Dreamina help your next editorial glow naturally.

title: COP31: Customs officers’ wives plant 14,882 trees, seek N402m funding
description:
The Customs Officers’ Wives Association says it has planted 14,882 economic trees and empowered more than 8,000 people in communities along Nigeria’s borders in one year, as it seeks additional funding to expand its climate resilience programme and set a Guinness World Record.
The association also a
content:
The Customs Officers’ Wives Association says it has planted 14,882 economic trees and empowered more than 8,000 people in communities along Nigeria’s borders in one year, as it seeks additional funding to expand its climate resilience programme and set a Guinness World Record.

The association also announced plans to collaborate with the Office of the President’s Special Assistant on Climate Change Matters to organise what it described as one of the largest gatherings of environmental activists and green workers in Abuja on December 5, 2026.

The initiative, which is expected to attract Guinness World Records recognition, is part of efforts to increase public participation in environmental protection and strengthen community-led responses to climate change.

National President of COWA, Kikelomo Adeniyi, disclosed these at a side event organised by the association at the ongoing COP31 climate conference on Monday in Antalya, Turkiye.

She said the association returned to the United Nations climate conference with evidence of the achievements it promised at COP30 in Belém, Brazil, last year, including tree planting, women’s economic empowerment and climate education for children.

Adeniyi said, “Last year, when we came to Belém, Brazil, we made so many promises that we were going to plant trees, empower women in green areas and sensitise our children on climate change. We have achieved all of these and more.

“Here in Antalya, Turkey, we have come to show evidence of all these things that we have achieved. So far, we have planted over 14,800 economic trees. These are trees that will be beneficial to our women in the near future. They will harvest them, take them to the market and sell them to make money.”

She explained that the tree-planting programme was deliberately designed around economic benefits to ensure that environmental restoration also provided sustainable livelihoods for women in border communities.

According to her, COWA has also trained women in recycling, farming and other green economic activities, while introducing solar energy solutions to help communities maximise their resources.

The association has mobilised 682 Green Ambassadors, while its community education programme has reached 6,093 beneficiaries. Another 4,041 people have benefited from health outreaches, while 1,138 have received skills acquisition support.

Adeniyi said the wider intervention had reached more than 8,000 people across border communities, including Seme, Idiroko and Illela.

She explained that the programme was also intended to address the economic vulnerability that could push residents, particularly young people, into smuggling and other illicit activities.

“The plan is to empower them because we believe that in the border areas, when people do not have something legal to do, they will go into illicit business, and that is where smuggling comes in. The children will begin to go into smuggling, and the mothers will encourage them to do so.

“We are giving them jobs and creating opportunities for the children and their mothers so that they can have something sustainable to do instead of going into illicit businesses,” she said.

The COWA president, however, said the association needed additional investment to scale up the programme, disclosing that it was seeking about N402 million to complete its innovation centre in Abuja.

She said the centre, for which the association had already invested about N415m, would serve as a national hub for training, research and the development of green skills, including solar installation.

“We have started already. It is already at the finishing level. Now, we are seeking over N400m just to bring it to completion. This is a place where people will come for training and research, and women will have a space where they can learn even how to fix solar systems.

“We want to have a place where everybody can come from the North, South, East and West as a hub for COWA,” she said, appealing to development partners and investors to support the project and its proposed expansion across Nigeria’s geopolitical zones.

Speaking during a panel session at the event, the Director-General, National Environmental Standards and Regulations Enforcement Agency, Innocent Barikor, commended COWA for directing attention to border communities, which he said were often overlooked in environmental interventions.

Barikor said NESREA could support the association through environmental governance advice, technical guidance and monitoring to ensure that its interventions produced verifiable and lasting results.

He stressed that the success of the tree-planting campaign should not be measured by the number of seedlings planted but by how many survived over time.

The NESREA chief also cautioned against introducing inappropriate or invasive tree species, urging the association to ensure that the trees planted were suitable for their locations and did not threaten existing vegetation.

Also speaking, the Special Assistant to the President on Climate Change Matters, Yussuf Kelani, described COWA’s initiative as an important contribution to climate prevention and community resilience.

He said the association was demonstrating how non-traditional environmental actors could contribute to climate action, noting that security agencies were usually called upon to respond to disasters after they occurred.

“Whenever we have climate crises around the world, we have the paramilitaries and the military coming in whenever there is a bush fire, extreme weather conditions or storms in different communities. We call on the military to salvage the situation.

“But now, the fact that we are preaching that there is no way forward without prevention, that we must participate in prevention, and the Customs Officers’ Wives Association has come up with this initiative, where they are actually participating in prevention, is a very good one,” he said.

Kelani disclosed that the National Council on Climate Change and the Ministry of Environment were working with the association to support the implementation of climate policies and community-based interventions.

The event also featured the presentation of an award to the COWA President by the President of the Nigeria Community in Türkiye, Emre Magboh, on behalf of Nigerians living in Türkiye, in recognition of the association’s contributions to environmental sustainability and community development.
