title: 2027 Grammys: Davido, Asake, Tems, Burna Boy, Ayra Starr, Wizkid Earn Nominations
description: Afrobeats stars Davido, Asake, Tems, Burna Boy, Ayra Starr and Wizkid have earned nominations for the 69th Annual Grammy Awards, with Nigerian artistes featuring prominently across several categories.The Recording Academy announced the nominations on Monday, with Nigerian artistes securing multiple
content:
Afrobeats stars Davido, Asake, Tems, Burna Boy, Ayra Starr and Wizkid have earned nominations for the 69th Annual Grammy Awards, with Nigerian artistes featuring prominently across several categories.

The Recording Academy announced the nominations on Monday, with Nigerian artistes securing multiple nods in the Best African Music Performance and Best Global Music categories.

Tems leads the Nigerian contingent with four nominations, while Asake earned two nominations in the Best African Music Performance category.

Other Nigerian artistes recognised include Davido, Ayra Starr, Burna Boy and Wizkid, who shares a nomination with Asake.

In the Best African Music Performance category, Nigerian artistes account for four of the five nominated entries.

Asake earned nominations for his songs ‘Gratitude’ and ‘Jogodo’, his collaboration with Wizkid.

Tems was nominated for ‘Big Daddy’, while Ayra Starr received a nod alongside Beninese singer Angélique Kidjo for their collaboration, ‘Aye Kan (Are You Coming Back?)’.

The fifth nominee is Ghanaian musician King Ayisoba, whose song ‘No Tradition, No Africa’ features Rocky Dawuni.

Tems also received nominations in three other categories. She was recognised in the Best R&B Solo Performance and Best R&B Song categories for ‘What You Need’, as well as Best Global Music Album for her project, Love Is a Kingdom.

Ayra Starr earned another nomination in the Best Global Music Album category for Starrgirl, while Davido’s Oriadé was also nominated in the category.

Burna Boy received a nomination in the Best Global Music Performance category for ‘Dìá Dìá’, his collaboration with Colombian singer Shakira.

Other International Stars

British singer-songwriter RAYE emerged as the biggest winner among international artistes at the 69th Annual Grammy Awards, leading all nominees with 11 nominations. Her recognition includes Album of the Year for ‘This Music May Contain Hope’, as well as Record and Song of the Year for ‘Where Is My Husband!’ and Songwriter of the Year. Spanish singer Rosalía followed with nine nominations, including Album of the Year for ‘Lux (Complete Works)’ and Record and Song of the Year for ‘Berghain’, her collaboration with Björk and Yves Tumor.

Other major international contenders include American singer Olivia Rodrigo and country star Ella Langley, who each earned seven nominations, while British singer Olivia Dean secured six.

Phoebe Bridgers and Miranda Lambert also received seven nominations each, while Bruno Mars and Leon Thomas earned six apiece. Taylor Swift received five nominations, including recognition in the major categories for her album ‘The Life of a Showgirl’ and songs ‘The Fate of Ophelia’ and ‘I Knew It, I Knew You’.

Beyond the major categories, the nominations also highlighted the Grammy Awards’ growing international reach, with Tame Impala and South Korean singer JENNIE recognised for ‘Dracula’, while Thailand’s LISA and South Korea’s IVE earned nominations in the newly introduced Best Asian Pop Music Performance category.

Filipino groups BINI and SB19 also secured nominations, alongside Colombian star Karol G, who featured among the contenders in the inaugural Best Latin Song category.

title: 2027: Kebbi backs Tinubu, rallies LGAs for presidential rally
description:
The Kebbi State Government has intensified mobilisation across its 21 local government areas ahead of President Bola Tinubu’s forthcoming visit for the All Progressives Congress presidential rally, reaffirming its support for his second-term ambition.
The state Commissioner for Information and Cultu
content:
The Kebbi State Government has intensified mobilisation across its 21 local government areas ahead of President Bola Tinubu’s forthcoming visit for the All Progressives Congress presidential rally, reaffirming its support for his second-term ambition.

The state Commissioner for Information and Culture, Yakubu Ahmed-BK, said the government, APC leadership and various support groups were working together to ensure a massive turnout and a memorable reception for the President.

Ahmed-BK disclosed this on Monday during a press briefing in Birnin Kebbi, where he said Governor Nasir Idris had inaugurated several sub-committees to coordinate arrangements for the visit.

He described the forthcoming rally as an opportunity for Kebbi to demonstrate its political loyalty to Tinubu and support for the Federal Government’s Renewed Hope Agenda.

“Kebbi State is fully prepared to receive Mr President. Under the purposeful leadership of Governor Nasir Idris, the government, APC leadership and various support groups have continued to mobilise stakeholders across the state to ensure a successful and historic rally,” he said.

The commissioner said the mobilisation had extended to party leaders, elected representatives, women, youths, farmers, labour unions and grassroots supporters.

He linked Kebbi’s support for Tinubu’s re-election bid to the expected economic benefits of ongoing federal infrastructure projects, particularly the Sokoto-Badagry Superhighway.

According to him, the project would improve transportation, facilitate trade and strengthen economic activities, particularly in Kebbi, where agriculture remains a major economic activity.

He said improved road connectivity would enable farmers to transport their produce to markets more easily, reduce transportation difficulties and expand commercial opportunities.

Ahmed-BK also identified the Bachaka Road, Malando-Ngaski Road and other federal and state infrastructure projects as critical interventions capable of connecting rural communities and stimulating economic development.

On the political front, the commissioner recalled that Kebbi was among the first states to openly endorse Tinubu for a second term, describing the decision as a reflection of confidence in his leadership and ongoing reforms.

“Our position remains that Nigeria needs sustained leadership, strong partnerships and a government capable of translating policies into tangible benefits for its citizens,” he said.

He attributed the APC’s political strength in Kebbi to what he described as the cordial relationship between Governor Idris’s administration and the people, citing achievements in education, healthcare, agriculture, infrastructure, workers’ welfare and social development.

The commissioner said the administration’s inclusive governance and people-oriented policies had helped strengthen public confidence in the ruling party.

He challenged opposition parties to present credible alternatives, clear policy directions and verifiable records of service rather than relying on political promises.

Ahmed-BK expressed confidence that the APC would maintain its dominance across the state’s 21 local government areas, attributing its strength to party unity, consultation and grassroots engagement.

He urged party members, supporters and residents to participate peacefully in the rally and give the President a rousing welcome.

“Our message is clear: Kebbi is ready, Kebbi is united, and Kebbi stands firmly with President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and the All Progressives Congress,” he declared.

The post 2027: Kebbi backs Tinubu, rallies LGAs for presidential rally appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

description:
By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo



Suspected bandits have abducted 12 residents of Kurmin Wali community in Afogo Ward, Kajuru Local Government Area of Kaduna State, in a fresh attack that has left 14 people in captivity.







The attack reportedly occurred on Sunday, November 15, 2026, when armed men inva
content:
By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo

Suspected bandits have abducted 12 residents of Kurmin Wali community in Afogo Ward, Kajuru Local Government Area of Kaduna State, in a fresh attack that has left 14 people in captivity.

The attack reportedly occurred on Sunday, November 15, 2026, when armed men invaded the community at about 9:14am and abducted 12 residents.

The village head, Isiaku Danazumi, who confirmed the incident on Monday, said three of the abducted residents had escaped and returned to the community, while nine others remained in the custody of their abductors.

He explained that the nine victims, alongside five other residents abducted in two separate attacks in October, brought the total number of people still being held by the bandits to 14.

“Yes, the incident happened on Sunday around 9:14am. Twelve people were abducted by the bandits, but three returned, while the remaining nine are still with them.

“But on October 2, 2026, two people were also abducted during the rainy season. Again, on October 10, three other people were abducted. So, in total, 14 of our people are with the bandits in the bush,” he said.

The traditional ruler expressed concern over the recurring abductions, saying that although the relevant authorities had been notified, no concrete action had been taken to secure the victims’ release.

He further disclosed that some security personnel visited the community on Sunday after the attackers had fled but reportedly left less than an hour after arriving.

The latest attack has heightened concerns over the security situation in Kurmin Wali, which attracted national attention in January 2026 when suspected bandits abducted more than 80 residents during a church service.

The mass abduction sparked widespread outrage and renewed calls for urgent government intervention to protect vulnerable communities in Kaduna State.

As of the time of filing this report, the Kaduna State Police Command and the Ministry of Internal Security and Home Affairs had yet to issue official statements on Sunday’s attack.

title: Oyo proposes N1.115trn 2027 budget, targets jobs, infrastructure
description:
By Adeola Badru



The Oyo State Government has proposed a N1.115 trillion budget for 2027, prioritising infrastructure development, job creation, entrepreneurship and the growth of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) to accelerate economic expansion and improve residents’ living standards.
content:
By Adeola Badru

The Oyo State Government has proposed a N1.115 trillion budget for 2027, prioritising infrastructure development, job creation, entrepreneurship and the growth of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) to accelerate economic expansion and improve residents’ living standards.

The proposed budget, tagged “Budget of Sustained Progress,” is designed to consolidate gains recorded across critical sectors while strengthening the state’s economic competitiveness through investments in infrastructure, agriculture, human capital development and public-private partnerships.

Governor Seyi Makinde presented the proposal to the Oyo State House of Assembly last week, with capital expenditure accounting for 60.1 per cent of the total spending plan.

Speaking during the presentation of the budget breakdown and analysis at the Ministry of Budget and Economic Planning in Ibadan on Monday, the Permanent Secretary, Julius Ayanleke, said the proposal aligned with the administration’s vision of making Oyo State the fastest-growing economy in Nigeria.

He said the government’s spending priorities would focus on completing ongoing projects, strengthening Internally Generated Revenue (IGR), attracting public and private investments, supporting MSMEs, expanding infrastructure and ensuring efficient utilisation of resources through Public-Private Partnerships (PPPs).

According to Ayanleke, the proposed budget comprises N670.03 billion for capital expenditure, representing 60.1 per cent, and N445.31 billion for recurrent expenditure, accounting for the remaining 39.9 per cent.

He explained that the substantial allocation to capital projects was intended to sustain the state’s development drive, particularly through the completion of ongoing projects and execution of critical infrastructure programmes.

Among the projects earmarked for priority funding are the Ibadan Circular Road, Ido-Eruwa Road and several rural road projects, which he said had received adequate provisions to facilitate their timely completion.

Providing an update on the state’s fiscal performance, Ayanleke disclosed that Oyo generated N618.72 billion between January and September 2026.

He said the revenue comprised N401.44 billion in recurrent revenue and N217.28 billion in capital receipts.

The permanent secretary explained that the 2027 budget was developed through the Medium-Term Expenditure Framework (MTEF), sectoral planning processes and consultations with stakeholders across the state’s seven geopolitical zones to ensure that the spending priorities reflected residents’ development needs.

Outlining the government’s fiscal targets, he said the administration would prioritise the completion of ongoing projects, reduce non-essential overhead costs and improve efficiency in personnel and recurrent expenditure.

He added that the government was targeting a minimum annual growth of 10 per cent in IGR between 2027 and 2029, while ensuring that recurrent expenditure was financed through sustainable revenue sources.

Other priorities, according to him, include diversifying the state’s revenue base, accelerating critical capital projects and expanding access to grants, development funding and public-private partnership arrangements.

Ayanleke said maintaining the 60:40 capital-to-recurrent expenditure ratio demonstrated the government’s commitment to development-focused investments and long-term economic growth.

He added that the spending approach would enable the state to channel more resources into productive investments capable of stimulating economic activities, supporting businesses, creating employment opportunities and improving residents’ welfare.

Also speaking, the Executive Assistant to the Governor on Finance, Budget and Economic Planning, Gafar Bello, commended the state’s budget performance since 2019, attributing the progress to transparency, fiscal discipline, efficiency and effective deployment of fiscal management tools.

Bello said the administration’s approach to fiscal management had contributed to improved budget implementation and strengthened the state’s capacity to pursue its development objectives.

In his remarks, the President of the Multi-disciplinary Finance Professionals (MFP), Dr Oyedepo Oyebade, praised the state government and the Ministry of Budget and Economic Planning for what he described as the transparent presentation of the 2027 budget and impressive implementation of the 2026 fiscal proposal.

Oyebade particularly highlighted the state’s 103 per cent performance on statutory allocation on a pro-rata basis, saying it reflected the adoption of prudent and realistic revenue projections.

He also commended the government for sustaining transparency, accountability and the January-to-December budget cycle, describing the consistency as an important feature of sound fiscal management.

According to him, allocating about 60 per cent of the proposed budget to capital projects underscored the administration’s commitment to completing ongoing projects, expanding infrastructure and driving development across the state.

The post Oyo proposes N1.115trn 2027 budget, targets jobs, infrastructure appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: 2027: Tinubu’ll get over 80% votes in Ebonyi, Nwifuru vows
description:
By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki



Governor Francis Nwifuru of Ebonyi State has vowed to deliver more than 80 per cent of the state’s votes to President Bola Tinubu in the 2027 general election, citing what he described as the President’s contributions to the state and its people.







Nwifuru said Tinu
content:
By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki

Governor Francis Nwifuru of Ebonyi State has vowed to deliver more than 80 per cent of the state’s votes to President Bola Tinubu in the 2027 general election, citing what he described as the President’s contributions to the state and its people.

Nwifuru said Tinubu had demonstrated commitment to Ebonyi through key appointments, particularly the appointment of former Governor David Umahi as Minister of Works.

The governor spoke during the inauguration of the President Bola Ahmed Tinubu (PBAT) Door-to-Door Campaign Movement at Unity Square, Abakaliki, where he also commended the group’s initiator, Government Ekpemupolo, popularly known as Tompolo, for mobilising support for the President’s re-election.

He described Umahi’s appointment as a significant recognition of the South-East, noting that the region had not previously occupied the position of Minister of Works.

“Most importantly, like we said during the presidential campaign inauguration here, he has appointed our son, our brother, our ally, our father, the Minister of Works of the Federal Republic of Nigeria. And he is a true supporter of our dear President.

“I am feeling very, very grateful to our dear brother, Tompolo, for this show of love and show of gratitude,” he said.

Nwifuru described Tinubu as an exceptional leader who had supported youths and other Nigerians, adding that his administration’s actions had strengthened the state’s commitment to the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC).

He said the President’s appointments and other interventions had convinced the people of Ebonyi to support his re-election bid.

“We do not want anybody to embarrass us because what the President has done to us has convinced us. And we are ready to vote for him beyond 80 per cent.

“Our people are well educated. They are well enlightened. They are aware of the sacrifices Mr President has made,” the governor said.

He also urged residents to vote massively for APC candidates in the 2027 elections, describing the party’s performance in the state as deserving of electoral support.

“And the party has done tremendously well for our people here. We are indebted to the party. And to pay the party back is to vote for APC party massively from top to bottom,” he added.

Speaking at the event, the National Coordinator of the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement, Government Tompolo, who was represented by the Managing Director of Tantita Security Services, Kestin Pondi, said the movement was established to take the President’s re-election campaign directly to households across the country.

Pondi described Tinubu as a courageous leader who had embarked on economic reforms from the beginning of his administration and sustained them despite the challenges.

He said the movement’s slogan, “Every Door Matters”, reflected its commitment to reaching Nigerians at the grassroots and mobilising support for the President.

According to him, Tinubu’s policies, including the removal of petrol subsidy, had helped state governments meet their salary obligations and address economic challenges.

He also claimed that the naira was strengthening, the economy was stabilising and fuel queues had eased under the administration.

“Today, we are not having fuel queues, though we are almost in December, because President Tinubu knows what he is doing. And we need to give him another four years for him to consolidate on what he has started,” Pondi said.

He disclosed that the movement had visited 26 states, including the Federal Capital Territory, as part of its nationwide mobilisation campaign.

Pondi said the group had brought 25 campaign vehicles fitted with speakers, microphones, amplifiers and generators to Ebonyi State to facilitate its grassroots mobilisation.

He said the vehicles would be deployed to take the movement’s message to communities across the state.

title: All 36 state assemblies approve state police bill
description:
All 36 state Houses of Assembly have approved the proposed constitutional amendment to establish state police, clearing the way for the National Assembly to transmit the bill to President Bola Tinubu for assent.
The Clerk to the National Assembly, Kamoru Ogunlana, disclosed this in a statement issue
content:
All 36 state Houses of Assembly have approved the proposed constitutional amendment to establish state police, clearing the way for the National Assembly to transmit the bill to President Bola Tinubu for assent.

The Clerk to the National Assembly, Kamoru Ogunlana, disclosed this in a statement issued on Monday, describing the unanimous endorsement as an unprecedented demonstration of cooperation between the federal and state legislatures.

The development means the bill has secured 100 per cent approval from the state assemblies, exceeding the constitutional requirement of at least 24 states under Section 9(2) of the 1999 Constitution.

Ogunlana said the bill had satisfied all constitutional and administrative requirements for transmission but that the National Assembly leadership delayed the process briefly to allow for broader national consensus and engagement with all states.

He said, “Following the completion of the verification process by my Office, the Bill is set for transmission to the President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, for His Excellency’s assent.”

The bill, known as the Constitution (Sixth Alteration) Bill to provide for the establishment of State Police Services and related matters, is designed to amend the 1999 Constitution to provide a legal framework for the establishment of state-controlled police formations.

Ogunlana said the unanimous approval reflected cooperation between the National Assembly and state legislatures, as well as constructive engagement between the executive arms of government at both federal and state levels.

He commended the 36 state governors, speakers and members of the state assemblies, as well as other stakeholders, for their contributions to the process.

The Clerk added that the development would provide a foundation for the National Assembly to transmit other Sixth Constitution Alteration Bills to the state assemblies for consideration.

The approval came barely 24 hours after the Senate Leader, Opeyemi Bamidele, disclosed that 32 state assemblies had endorsed the proposed state police legislation, with reports from the remaining four still being awaited.

(https://punchng.com/state-police-senate-sets-november-17-deadline-for-four-states/)

Bamidele had said the four outstanding assemblies were expected to submit their reports by Tuesday ahead of the National Assembly’s resumption.

He had also indicated that the National Assembly was preparing to proceed with the next stage of the constitutional amendment process once the outstanding reports were received.

With all 36 assemblies now having approved the bill, attention has shifted to its formal transmission to Tinubu for his assent, which would pave the way for the implementation of the constitutional framework for state police.

title: N100m damages: Appeal Court reserves SERAP’s case for judgment
description:
By Ikechukwu Nnochiri



ABUJA – A special panel of the Court of Appeal in Abuja on Monday reserved its judgment on two separate appeals seeking to set aside a verdict that ordered the Socio-Economic Rights and Accountability Project (SERAP) to pay N100 million in damages for defaming two Department
content:
By Ikechukwu Nnochiri

ABUJA – A special panel of the Court of Appeal in Abuja on Monday reserved its judgment on two separate appeals seeking to set aside a verdict that ordered the Socio-Economic Rights and Accountability Project (SERAP) to pay N100 million in damages for defaming two Department of State Services (DSS) officials.

The three-member panel, led by Justice Danlami Senchi, reserved the matter for judgment after all the parties adopted their final briefs of argument.

The two appeals, marked CA/ABJ/CV/1114/2026 and CA/ABJ/CV/1105/2026, were filed by SERAP and its Deputy Director, Mr. Kolawole Oluwadare, respectively.

While the appellants, represented by Mr. Paul Mgbenwa and Mr. Oluwatosin Adesioye, prayed for the appeals to be upheld and the High Court’s order set aside, the respondents’ legal team, led by Mr. Akinolu Kehinde, SAN, sought the dismissal of the appeals for want of merit.

The Justice Senchi-led panel said it would communicate the judgment date to the parties.

It will be recalled that a High Court of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), in a judgment delivered on May 5, awarded damages against SERAP and Mr. Oluwadare, who were sued as the 1st and 2nd defendants.

The trial judge, Justice Yusuf Halilu, held that he was satisfied that the non-governmental organisation had, on September 9, 2024, tarnished the reputations of two DSS personnel, Sarah John and Gabriel Ogundele, when it falsely alleged that they had invaded its office in Abuja.

The court held that the defendants had unjustly defamed the operatives when they published on SERAP’s website and X (formerly Twitter) handle that the operatives had invaded the office and harassed a staff member.

According to the court, the publication was in bad taste.

Therefore, in addition to the N100m damages, the court ordered SERAP to tender public apologies to the defamed DSS operatives in two national newspapers, on two television stations and on its website.

It also ordered the defendants to pay the two operatives N1m to cover the cost of the litigation, as well as 10 per cent annual interest on the judgment sum until it is fully liquidated.

The judgment followed Suit No. CV/4547/2024, which the two operatives filed before the court to challenge what they regarded as SERAP’s false claim, which had negatively affected both their reputations and the corporate image of the DSS.

The appellants are asking the court to set aside the judgment in its entirety, insisting that the trial judge erred in law and occasioned a miscarriage of justice against them.

In processes filed through its lawyers, led by Mr. Tayo Oyetibo, SAN, SERAP anchored its appeal on 24 grounds.

It raised questions concerning the essential elements of defamation, the evidential burden of establishing identification, the competence of the evidence relied upon by the trial court, and the protection of freedom of expression and public-interest advocacy.

“The central issue in this appeal is whether the respondents established by credible evidence that the publications complained of referred to them. The publications did not name the respondents, and the descriptions relied upon were general physical descriptions which did not, without more, identify the particular individuals who brought the action.

“The alleged suspension of the 1st and 2nd Respondents was likewise not supported by independent documentary evidence. The award against SERAP was therefore not only excessive but also arbitrary and ought to be set aside.

“The award of liability cannot stand where the essential findings on falsity and justification were not supported by the evidence. We respectfully submit that the finding of liability and consequential award of damages cannot stand once the findings upon which they were founded are shown to be erroneous.

“Where a claimant is not expressly named in a publication, the burden remains on the claimant to establish by evidence the circumstances from which a reasonable reader would understand the publication to refer specifically to that claimant. That essential link was not established in this case.

“Neither publication identified the respondents by name, rank, designation, office or photograph. The descriptions relied upon were physical descriptions which, on the evidence before the trial court, were not unique to the respondents.

“The respondents pleaded that members of the public and persons within the SSS understood the publications to refer to them, but no member of the public was called to testify that they had read the publications and understood them to refer to the respondents.

“No independent witness was called to establish the alleged identification, while the social-media reactions relied upon by the respondents were not tendered in evidence.

“The law is settled that the words complained of in an action for defamation must be considered from the standpoint of the ordinary reasonable reader. The question is whether a reasonable person reading the publication would associate the words complained of with the claimant.

“The significance of this principle in the present appeal is considerable. The two SSS/DSS officers were not named in either publication. Their case therefore depended upon establishing by evidence the factual circumstances connecting the descriptions contained in the publications to their particular identities.

“The trial court consequently supplied the missing identifying link by relying, among other things, on its own observation of the physical appearance of the respondents in court.

“The trial court could not properly supply by its own observation the essential identifying link which the respondents were required to establish by evidence.

“The issue was whether the publications identified the respondents when they were published, not whether the respondents happened to fit the descriptions when they appeared before the court,” SERAP argued.

The post N100m damages: Appeal Court reserves SERAP’s case for judgment appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: 2027: LP factional presidential candidate quits race, backs Tinubu
description:
A factional presidential candidate of the Labour Party, Kennedy Ahanotu, has withdrawn from the 2027 presidential race and declared support for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election, citing the lingering leadership crisis in the opposition party.
Ahanotu announced this at a press briefing in Abuja on
content:
A factional presidential candidate of the Labour Party, Kennedy Ahanotu, has withdrawn from the 2027 presidential race and declared support for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election, citing the lingering leadership crisis in the opposition party.

Ahanotu announced this at a press briefing in Abuja on Monday.

The former National Youth Leader of the party and an ally of LP’s 2023 presidential candidate, Peter Obi, said he has agreed to work with the City Boy Movement to mobilise support for Tinubu ahead of the 2027 general election.

In May 2026, The PUNCH reported that Ahanotu emerged as the consensus presidential candidate of the Julius Abure-led faction of the Labour Party at its presidential, governorship and House of Representatives primaries held in Abuja.

The faction adopted the 42-year-old party stalwart amid the protracted leadership crisis that had divided the opposition party.

However, he disclosed his withdrawal from the race on Monday, explaining that his decision followed a meeting with youth leaders across the country, who mandated him to engage with the President’s support group and galvanise support for his re-election because of the lingering crisis in the party.

He said, “I took the decision to withdraw my presidential ambition after a meeting with the Labour Party youth structure we deployed in 2023 across the country, where all the state leaders, having witnessed and seen what the party has become, urged me to align with City Boy Movement to back President Bola Tinubu’s re-election.

“Nobody is happy with what the party has become. It has spent the last few years in crisis. So, when your followers mandate you as a leader to make a bold move, you have to do it. So I heeded that call.

“Of course, Seyi Tinubu has been my friend since 2022, and we have a good relationship. Most people don’t know this. He’s a great guy, very intelligent and brilliant.”

Ahanotu said the youth leaders, who represented structures across the 774 local government areas, believed the persistent crisis in the Labour Party had made it necessary to explore alternative political alignments.

He added, “We are currently partnering to support the re-election of President Bola Tinubu in 2027.”

Defending his decision against allegations of betraying the Labour Party, Ahanotu said he had invested 10 years in the party, having joined in 2016 after studying the manifestos of several political parties.

He said he actively campaigned for Obi during the 2023 presidential election, mobilising young Nigerians to support the Labour Party candidate.

However, he accused politicians who joined the party shortly before the 2023 elections of sidelining its longstanding members after gaining political prominence, alleging that the party’s legacy members were eventually pushed out of its leadership structure.

Asked whether his support for Tinubu would be regarded as a betrayal by Labour Party stakeholders, Ahanotu said the party had betrayed him instead.

He said, “I can’t say I have betrayed anybody. I’d rather say that the party has betrayed me because the party I’ve worked for, the party I gave all, I gave 10 years to the Labour Party.”

But the Labour Party dismissed Ahanotu’s claim to its membership and presidential candidacy, insisting that neither was recognised by the Senator Nenadi Usman-led leadership.

The party’s National Publicity Secretary, Ken Asogwa, said Ahanotu was free to support any presidential candidate but accused him of dragging the party’s name into his political realignment.

He said, “The young man, who used to be a member of the Labour Party, is free to root for any candidate of his choice. After all, the Constitution guarantees him that freedom to make his choice. However, the Labour Party feels particularly embarrassed that its name is being dragged into his new undertaking.

“First, the fellow was expelled by the Party as far back as 14th March 2026 and is, therefore, no longer a member of the Labour Party. He is only dragging the Party’s name along because he knows that his faceless name cannot land him a job in the APC.

“Secondly, it is a crime and an offence against the Electoral Act for anyone to refer to this individual as a former or factional presidential candidate of the Labour Party. He was not even a member of the Labour Party when the Party commenced the sale of its presidential nomination forms and, therefore, could not have laid claim to being a presidential candidate of the Party, or a factional one.”

Asogwa also dismissed Ahanotu’s claim that the party’s internal crisis informed his decision, describing the alleged factionalisation as imaginary.

He said, “There is no crisis in the Party to warrant the mention of an imaginary faction as an excuse for his defection to the APC.

“Finally, the Labour Party notes with enthusiasm the recent upsurge in the penchant for dropping the name of the Labour Party by politicians seeking refuge in other political platforms. It evidently demonstrates that the soaring image of the Party remains unmatched.

“However, as much as the party recognises that these pockets of name-dropping are a testament to its towering image, the Labour Party wishes to enjoin displaced politicians to desist from needlessly dragging the name of the Party into their political activities. The party will soon begin to take legal action against some of these acts of impersonation.”

The post 2027: LP factional presidential candidate quits race, backs Tinubu appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Iyovwaye challenges Oborevwori over Adeda’s death, Asaba rally violence
description:
By Egufe Yafugborhi



ASABA — Governorship candidate of the New Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in Delta State, Chris Iyovwaye, has challenged Governor Sheriff Oborevwori to provide an update on the investigation into the death of late Deputy Director, Unity Adeda, before demanding the prosecutio
content:
By Egufe Yafugborhi

ASABA — Governorship candidate of the New Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in Delta State, Chris Iyovwaye, has challenged Governor Sheriff Oborevwori to provide an update on the investigation into the death of late Deputy Director, Unity Adeda, before demanding the prosecution of suspects involved in the November 7 violence at an NDC rally in Asaba.

Iyovwaye, in a statement, questioned what he described as differing levels of urgency by the state government in addressing the two incidents, insisting that Deltans deserved accountability in both cases.

He said the government’s call for the prosecution of those involved in the Asaba rally violence should also extend to anyone who might have acted under government authority.

“The Delta State Government has called for prosecution over the violence at the NDC rally in Asaba. We expect that investigation to examine the conduct of anyone who may have acted under government authority.

“Governor, you must also speak to Deltans about the death of Mr Unity Adeda. What has the investigation established about the circumstances of his death?

“What is the status of those arrested, including your Commissioner for Secondary Education? Have charges been filed?

“We demand a public update and the prosecution of anyone against whom the evidence supports charges, regardless of office,” he said.

The NDC candidate also questioned reported remarks by the Commissioner for Information, Charles Aniagwu, concerning a tricycle task force allegedly linked to the Asaba incident.

He urged Oborevwori to clarify the identities of the task force members, who appointed and deployed them, the instructions they received and those responsible for supervising their activities.

“Commissioner Charles Aniagwu’s reported remarks about a tricycle task force raise questions that Governor Sheriff Oborevwori must answer publicly.

“What are the names of the task force members that were involved? Who appointed them, who deployed them, what instructions did they receive, and who supervised them?” he asked.

Iyovwaye said the investigation should establish whether public authority or resources were deployed against NDC supporters, stressing that membership of a government-appointed task force did not confer the right to assault citizens or intimidate political supporters.

Citing Sections 33 and 40 of the Nigerian Constitution, he said the rights to life, peaceful assembly and association must be protected irrespective of political affiliation.

He also alleged that NDC banners, posters and other campaign materials had been destroyed across the state, calling on the police to investigate possible involvement of public officials or government-appointed agents.

“Governor Oborevwori should publicly direct every state task force to stay within its mandate and stop any interference with lawful political activity,” he said.

Warning public employees and political appointees against carrying out unlawful directives, Iyovwaye said that instructions from superiors could not excuse illegal actions.

“A superior’s order cannot make an unlawful act lawful,” he declared.

He maintained that the NDC would not be intimidated, claiming that residents dissatisfied with APC leadership at different levels were supporting his party.

“The NDC will not be intimidated. Across Delta State, people who are tired of APC leadership at every level are standing with us.

“We will continue to organise peacefully and defend the right of every Deltan to support the party of their choice,” he said.

Iyovwaye urged residents to hold the governor and his administration accountable, insisting that the government’s condemnation of the Asaba rally violence must be followed by concrete measures to protect citizens participating in political gatherings.

content:
By Adegboyega Adeleye

Nigerian music star Tems leads the Nigerian nominees with four nominations for the 2027 Grammy Awards, while Asake, Wizkid, Burna Boy, Davido and Ayra Starr also earned nods across African music, global music and R&B categories.

The nominations were announced on Monday during a live YouTube programme, as the Recording Academy unveiled nominees across 100 categories ahead of the awards ceremony.

Tems leads the Nigerian nominees with four nominations. She is nominated for Best R&B Song and Best R&B Solo Performance for “What You Need.” In the solo performance category, she will compete against Beyoncé for “Morning Dew (Donk),” Kehlani for “Out the Window,” Victoria Monét for “Let Me” and Jill Scott for “Pressha.”

Tems is also nominated for Best African Music Performance for “Big Daddy” and Best Global Music Album for Love Is a Kingdom. “What You Need” was released on 21 November 2025 as a single from her EP Love Is a Kingdom.

Asake is nominated for Best African Music Performance for “Gratitude” and shares another nomination in the category with Wizkid for their collaboration “Jogodo.” Other nominees include Tems for “Big Daddy,” and Ayra Starr and Angélique Kidjo for “Aye Kan (Are You Coming Back?),” as well as King Ayisoba featuring Rocky Dawuni for “No Tradition, No Africa.”

Wizkid’s nomination comes through “Jogodo,” his collaboration with Asake, in the Best African Music Performance category.

Burna Boy is nominated alongside Shakira for “Dai Dai” in the Best Global Music Performance category. Davido is nominated for Best Global Music Album for Oriadé. The category also features Anitta’s Equilibrivm, Angélique Kidjo’s Hope!!, Ayra Starr’s Starrgirl and Tems’ Love Is a Kingdom.

Ayra Starr has two nominations: Best African Music Performance with Angélique Kidjo for “Aye Kan (Are You Coming Back?)” and Best Global Music Album for Starrgirl.

The 69th Grammy Awards are scheduled to hold on 7 February 2027 at the Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles, California.

title: Create waste ministry, group urges next Lagos govt
description:
An advocacy group, the Lagos Waste Forum, has called on the next administration in Lagos State to establish a dedicated Ministry of Waste Resources to provide “strategic leadership and effective oversight” of the state’s waste management sector.
The forum said the proposed ministry would coordinate
content:
An advocacy group, the Lagos Waste Forum, has called on the next administration in Lagos State to establish a dedicated Ministry of Waste Resources to provide “strategic leadership and effective oversight” of the state’s waste management sector.

The forum said the proposed ministry would coordinate waste management activities, strengthen accountability and provide long-term policy direction for the sector.

According to a statement made available to our correspondent, the call was made during a virtual policy dialogue titled The Governor’s Brief: Setting a Waste Policy Agenda for the Next Lagos, organised by the Lagos Waste Forum in collaboration with the SWEEP Foundation NG last Thursday.

The dialogue brought together stakeholders from the media, private sector, civil society, environmental advocacy groups and the informal waste economy, including waste pickers, recyclers, waste operators and policy experts.

The stakeholders said Lagos’ waste management challenges had become structural and could no longer be addressed through periodic changes in agencies, contractors and operational arrangements.

They noted that the state’s population had increased from about 5.7 million in 1991 to more than 22 million, putting increasing pressure on its waste management infrastructure.

The forum also cited an acknowledgement by the state Deputy Governor, Obafemi Hamzat, that Lagos generates about 17,000 tonnes of waste daily, compared with the previously cited 13,000 tonnes.

It said only about 60 per cent of the waste generated was collected, while approximately 13 per cent was recycled, leaving substantial quantities inadequately managed.

According to the stakeholders, the situation contributes to environmental pollution, blocked drainage channels, flooding and public health risks.

They called for a comprehensive waste governance framework that would integrate waste management with public health, flood prevention, infrastructure development and economic planning.

The forum also urged the incoming administration to improve waste data collection and public reporting, maintain waste infrastructure, increase disposal capacity and reduce dependence on the monthly environmental sanitation exercise by promoting everyday environmental responsibility.

The Convener of the Lagos Waste Forum, Obuesi Phillips, said the policy dialogue was aimed at moving beyond recurring complaints about waste management failures to developing a coordinated reform agenda.

Phillips said the recommendations from the engagement would be consolidated into a policy compendium to be presented to the incoming governor and other relevant government stakeholders.

The panel at the dialogue included the Publisher of Prime Business Africa, Dr Marcel Mbamalu; Metro Editor of PUNCH Newspapers, Joel Nwokeoma; Phillips; BBC Senior Journalist, Esther Omopariola; and City Scope Africa’s John Fatanmi.

title: Atiku says Plateau will not forget Tinubu’s absence during killings
description:
Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar has criticised President Bola Tinubu over his handling of insecurity in Plateau State, saying the people may forgive him for failing to visit them during periods of deadly attacks but would not forget his absence when they needed presidential reassurance.
Atiku,
content:
Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar has criticised President Bola Tinubu over his handling of insecurity in Plateau State, saying the people may forgive him for failing to visit them during periods of deadly attacks but would not forget his absence when they needed presidential reassurance.

Atiku, the presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress, said Tinubu’s recent visit to the state to seek forgiveness and solicit support ahead of the 2027 general elections could not erase what he described as the president’s failure to stand with victims of killings and kidnappings.

The former Vice-President stated this in a statement issued on Monday by his Director of Strategic Communication, Phrank Shaibu, from Potiskum, Yobe State, where he was taking his Affordable Life campaign message to residents.

He argued that Plateau residents needed the President’s presence when communities were under attack and families were mourning their loved ones, rather than during an electioneering campaign.

“The people of Plateau needed their president when they were grieving, when their communities were under attack and when families desperately needed reassurance.

“President Tinubu promised to end the killings and protect them, but he failed to keep those promises. He did not visit to stand with them in their darkest hour,” Atiku said.

The former Vice-President maintained that the president’s belated appeal for forgiveness during his Plateau visit would not erase the memories of lives lost and communities devastated by insecurity.

“Now he has gone to Plateau to campaign and ask for forgiveness. The people may forgive him, but they will never forget the lives lost, the communities left in fear and the absence of their President when they needed him most.

“President Tinubu cannot abandon Plateau in its hour of agony, then return when he needs its votes and expect a warm welcome. The people are not props for his campaign, and their grief is not a slogan to be used when politically convenient,” he said.

He further argued that the security challenges confronting Plateau reflected what he described as the broader failure of the Tinubu administration to address the country’s worsening economic and security conditions.

According to him, the president’s record in office had weakened his moral standing to seek another mandate in 2027.

“Atiku noted that a president who looks away while Nigerians endure the worst cost-of-living crisis in recent memory has forfeited the ground to ask them for another term. He has failed the 36 per cent of Nigerians who gave him the opportunity to lead in 2023,” the statement added.

The ADC presidential campaign candidate also used the opportunity to promote his party’s Affordable Life campaign, which he said was designed to tackle the economic difficulties facing Nigerian households and restore their purchasing power.

He said Nigerians deserved a government that would respond to their suffering with practical interventions, compassion and responsible leadership.

Plateau State has witnessed recurring attacks on rural communities, resulting in deaths, displacement and destruction of property. The persistent violence has remained a major security concern, with affected communities repeatedly calling for stronger protection and decisive government action.

Tinubu’s recent visit to the state, during which he appealed for forgiveness, has provided fresh political ammunition for the opposition as parties intensify their campaigns ahead of the 2027 presidential election.

The exchange also underscores the growing attempt by opposition parties to make insecurity and the rising cost of living central issues in the contest for the presidency.

title: China, Russia, US to have in-depth exchange of views on safeguarding world peace as Xi Jinping hosts China-Russia-US summit
description:
From Aidoghie Paulinus, Abuja
China, Russia and the United States will meet in Shenzhen, China, on 19 November 2026 to have an in-depth exchange of views on safeguarding world peace and enabling strategic stability in major-country relations.
This follows an announcement by the Chinese Foreign Minis
content:
From Aidoghie Paulinus, Abuja

China, Russia and the United States will meet in Shenzhen, China, on 19 November 2026 to have an in-depth exchange of views on safeguarding world peace and enabling strategic stability in major-country relations.

This follows an announcement by the Chinese Foreign Ministry that the Chinese President, Xi Jinping, will hold the China-Russia-United States Summit with President Vladimir Putin and President Donald J. Trump in Shenzhen on 19 November.

Briefing journalists in Beijing, the Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson, Mao Ning, said the summit would be the first-ever face-to-face meeting between the Chinese, Russian and United States heads of state.

“The three presidents will have an in-depth exchange of views on safeguarding world peace and enabling strategic stability in major-country relations. The summit is of ground-breaking significance,” Mao said.

The spokesperson also said China, Russia and the United States were founding members of the United Nations and permanent members of the Security Council.

She added that, in history, the three countries had fought side by side to win the World Anti-Fascist War.

Mao further said that, under the current circumstances, the three countries shoulder important responsibilities to work together in addressing global challenges and promoting world peace and stability.

“It is in the interest of the three countries to strengthen communication, manage differences and maintain stable relations. This is also the expectation of the international community and is conducive to global stability and dialogue and cooperation,” the spokesperson stated.

title: Kano: Police arrest 8 as Kwankwaso’s, Gwarzo’s convoys come under attack
description:
From Desmond Mgboh, Kano
The convoy of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) vice presidential candidate, Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, was attacked on Sunday by opposition political thugs in Bichi LGA of Kano State.
The attack also affected the convoy of the party’s governorship candidate in the state, Ami
content:
From Desmond Mgboh, Kano

The convoy of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) vice presidential candidate, Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, was attacked on Sunday by opposition political thugs in Bichi LGA of Kano State.

The attack also affected the convoy of the party’s governorship candidate in the state, Aminu Abdussalam Gwarzo.

The incident occurred while the party was returning from a political tour of Tofa, Rimin Gado, Kabo, Gwarzo, Shanono and Bagwai LGAs.

Confirming the attack, the spokesperson for the NDC governorship candidate, Ibrahim Garba Shuaibu, said that while approaching Bichi they had received intelligence reports that some people had blocked the road to prevent them from holding a political rally in the town.

According to Shuaibu, upon arriving in the town, they noticed signs of stone-throwing, and shortly after passing the local government secretariat, a group of youths armed with dangerous weapons emerged and attacked their convoy.

He said the attack left some supporters injured and damaged several vehicles, adding that he personally saw about seven vehicles with smashed windscreens at the scene.

Kwankwaso and Gwarzo were said to have escaped unhurt, he disclosed.

In a statement, the police in Kano said the Command had received a report at about 4.45pm on Sunday, 15 November 2026, of a clash within Bichi township, which led to the destruction of campaign banners, billboards and motor vehicles, and injuries to several persons.

The statement, signed by the police spokesman, Abdullahi Haruna Kiyawa, said that eight suspects had been arrested in connection with the incident.

It added that items recovered as exhibits included one gariyo, two cutlasses, two hard sticks, one bottle of solution, and a substance locally referred to as “Suck and Die”.

It explained that thirteen vehicles were vandalised during the clash, while five persons who sustained injuries were rushed to hospital, where they are currently receiving treatment.

The Commissioner of Police, Kano State Command, strongly condemned the resort to violence and the destruction of campaign materials by political supporters, warning that the Command would not tolerate any act capable of breaching public peace before, during and after the political season.

He urged political leaders, supporters and the general public to shun violence, remain law-abiding and report any suspicious activity to the nearest police station.

Meanwhile, the suspects have been conveyed to the State Criminal Investigation Department (SCID), Bompai, for discreet investigation and will be charged to court upon completion of investigation.

The post Kano: Police arrest 8 as Kwankwaso’s, Gwarzo’s convoys come under attack appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Nigeria retains seat on ITU Council for 2027–2030
description:
By Omeiza Ajayi



ABUJA — Nigeria has been re-elected to the Council of the International Telecommunication Union (ITU), securing its seat for the 2027–2030 term at the ongoing conference in Doha, Qatar.







The re-election guarantees Nigeria continued representation on the council of the United
content:
By Omeiza Ajayi

ABUJA — Nigeria has been re-elected to the Council of the International Telecommunication Union (ITU), securing its seat for the 2027–2030 term at the ongoing conference in Doha, Qatar.

The re-election guarantees Nigeria continued representation on the council of the United Nations specialised agency responsible for information and communication technologies (ICTs).

Established in 1865 and headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland, the ITU brings together 194 member states and more than 1,000 sector members, including companies, universities and international organisations.

Nigeria joined the union in 1961.

Nigeria’s participation in the conference was coordinated by the Minister of Foreign Affairs, Ambassador Bianca Odumegwu-Ojukwu, while the delegation was led by the Minister of Communications, Innovation and Digital Economy, Dr Bosun Tijani.

Nigeria’s Ambassador to the State of Qatar, Prof. Mahmood Yakubu, served as Deputy Head of Delegation.

He was supported by the Executive Vice Chairman of the Nigerian Communications Commission (NCC), Dr Aminu Maida, and the Nigerian Permanent Mission to Geneva, led by Ambassador Innocent Imejuo.

Officials of the Ministry of Communications, Innovation and Digital Economy, the NCC and staff of the Nigerian Embassy in Doha were also part of the Nigerian delegation.

title: MSF: Shortage of diphtheria drugs fuelling outbreak in Northern Nigeria
description:
By Ndahi Marama, Maiduguri







MAIDUGURI — Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) has warned that shortages of diphtheria antitoxin (DAT), a critical drug for treating the disease, coupled with low immunisation coverage, are fuelling transmission and undermining efforts to contain the outbreak in norther
content:
By Ndahi Marama, Maiduguri

MAIDUGURI — Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) has warned that shortages of diphtheria antitoxin (DAT), a critical drug for treating the disease, coupled with low immunisation coverage, are fuelling transmission and undermining efforts to contain the outbreak in northern Nigeria.

The international medical humanitarian organisation said the situation was putting thousands of children at risk of severe illness and death, calling on the Federal and state governments, donors and international partners to urgently address shortages of essential medicines and vaccines.

MSF Medical Coordinator in Nigeria, Dr David Kizito, raised the alarm in a statement made available to our correspondent in Maiduguri on Monday.

He urged relevant authorities and international partners to secure available supplies of diphtheria antitoxin, vaccines and other essential medicines, ensure their timely clearance at ports of entry and facilitate rapid distribution to affected communities across northern Nigeria.

Diphtheria is a life-threatening but vaccine-preventable bacterial disease transmitted mainly through respiratory droplets and contact with infected wounds.

Kizito described the global shortage of diphtheria antitoxin as a serious threat to the treatment of patients, warning that dwindling stocks could leave medical teams unable to save lives as the outbreak persists.

“The global shortage of diphtheria antitoxin is becoming a matter of life and death. Our stocks are dangerously low, and we risk being unable to treat children and save lives as the outbreak continues.

“Diphtheria is a preventable disease, yet children continue to arrive at health facilities with life-threatening complications because they are not fully vaccinated or cannot access care in time,” he said.

He explained that diphtheria antitoxin was the only specific treatment capable of neutralising the toxin produced by the disease.

Although included in the World Health Organisation’s Model List of Essential Medicines, he said its global availability remained inconsistent.

According to him, the drug is most effective when administered within 48 hours of the onset of symptoms, but inadequate supplies have repeatedly forced MSF medical teams to ration treatment, potentially compromising patients’ outcomes.

The statement said Nigeria had been battling a major diphtheria outbreak since late 2022, with the cumulative toll exceeding 41,000 suspected cases, more than 24,000 confirmed infections and over 1,260 deaths nationwide.

It identified Bauchi, Borno, Kaduna, Katsina, Kano, Plateau, Sokoto and Zamfara as among the northern states particularly affected by the outbreak, with several areas recording recent increases in cases.

In 2026 alone, as of August 9, Nigeria had recorded 12,977 suspected cases, 10,476 confirmed infections and 406 deaths, according to the organisation.

MSF said it had been supporting state health authorities through patient treatment, infection prevention and control, disease surveillance, community engagement, health promotion, referral systems, vaccination support and the provision of medical supplies.

It said its teams were treating patients and supporting isolation and treatment facilities in Kano, Sokoto and Zamfara states, while providing additional assistance in Bauchi, Katsina and Kebbi states.

Since the beginning of its response this year, the organisation said it had treated more than 9,000 diphtheria patients through facility-based and community-based care, while scaling up emergency interventions in areas with high infection rates.

In partnership with the Kano State Ministry of Health, MSF also supported a two-round vaccination campaign in April and June, during which more than 835,000 vaccine doses were administered to children across the state.

The organisation disclosed that following Zamfara State’s declaration of an outbreak in September, MSF-supported facilities in Gusau recorded more than 671 admissions within a month, beginning October 6.

It said most of the patients were children, while four out of every five admitted had not been vaccinated against the disease.

In Sokoto State, MSF also supported two rounds of vaccination between February and April, reaching 49,018 children under the age of 15.

The organisation, however, expressed concern over inadequate vaccine supplies in Zamfara, noting that only 25,000 of the 90,000 doses required for a reactive vaccination campaign had been supplied, leaving a significant number of children unreached.

MSF said it was working with government health authorities to secure additional doses and implement a large-scale vaccination campaign.

The statement stressed that routine immunisation remained critical to preventing diphtheria, but coverage in northern Nigeria, particularly in rural communities, remained low.

It also included the account of a mother, Shafa’atu, whose three children were treated for diphtheria at an MSF-supported hospital in Sokoto.

“We were very worried when our first child became sick because we knew very little about diphtheria at the time,” she said.

“My child struggled to eat, and whenever he ate, he vomited. Diphtheria is a dangerous disease.”

MSF called for sustained, long-term investment in routine immunisation to build community immunity and prevent future outbreaks.

It also urged manufacturers and global health partners to urgently expand production of diphtheria antitoxin and establish reliable supply chains to meet critical treatment needs in Nigeria and other countries experiencing rising cases.

LAGOS, NIGERIA — A community-driven startup pitching and funding platform, ChipInHere, has concluded the inaugural edition of its entrepreneurship initiative, Pitch & Fund
content:
….. BuildConnect CEO Mamah Bonaventure emerges grand winner of ₦250,000 as registration for Pitch & Fund 2.0 opens November 20.

LAGOS, NIGERIA — A community-driven startup pitching and funding platform, ChipInHere, has concluded the inaugural edition of its entrepreneurship initiative, Pitch & Fund 1.0, empowering 29 emerging Nigerian founders and awarding ₦500,000 in cash prizes to top-performing innovators.

Built on the belief that promising ideas deserve accessible support to grow, Pitch & Fund provides a platform where aspiring founders, creators, and small business owners can showcase their ventures, attract public backing, and raise funds to scale their operations.

Unlike conventional pitching competitions decided solely by a judging panel, Pitch & Fund 1.0 adopted a community-backed funding model that enabled contestants to rally financial support and public engagement directly from friends, family members, customers, and the wider public via ChipInHere and its official social media channels.

Commenting on the initiative, Founder of ChipInHere, Oyin Osundina, said the platform was created to bridge the early-stage funding and visibility gap facing everyday entrepreneurs across the country.

“Across Nigeria, brilliant entrepreneurs are building real solutions every day, yet many stall simply because they lack early backing or visibility. With ChipInHere and Pitch & Fund, we wanted to prove that when you give founders a simple tool to rally their own communities, ordinary people can become the earliest investors in extraordinary businesses,” Osundina stated.

Also speaking on the outcome of the maiden edition, Co-Founder of ChipInHere, Fadah Oyinkuro, noted that the enthusiastic response across social channels validated the power of collective support.

“Pitch & Fund 1.0 showed us what happens when technology meets African communal spirit. Watching 29 founders turn 60-second pitches and WhatsApp links into real capital, new customers, and massive social engagement across Instagram and Facebook reinforces why we built ChipInHere — to make collective support effortless for everyone,” Oyinkuro said.

WINNERS OF PITCH & FUND 1.0

The competition, which commenced on October 10, 2026, and closed at 11:59 pm West Africa Time on October 31, 2026, culminated in the emergence of three winners who shared the ₦500,000 prize pool:

• Grand Winner (₦250,000): Mamah Bonaventure, Chief Executive Officer, BuildConnect

• First Runner-Up (₦150,000): Okon Christiana Ufon, Chief Executive Officer, Elegant Bead NG

• Second Runner-Up (₦100,000): Oyinpreye Rachel Omemu, Chief Executive Officer, Creative Playground

Beyond the financial rewards, organisers noted that the initiative provided all 29 participants with national visibility, networking opportunities, customer acquisition, and practical exposure to community-driven fundraising.

HOW THE COMPETITION OPERATED

According to the organisers, Pitch & Fund 1.0 was structured around a three-step process to make pitching, visibility, and grassroots fundraising accessible to entrepreneurs nationwide:

  1. Creation of Funding Links: Each contestant generated a personalised fundraising link on the official ChipInHere platform to serve as a dedicated collection page for supporters.
  2. Short Video Pitches: Participants submitted 30-to-60-second video pitches introducing their enterprises, outlining the problems they solve, and presenting their growth plans.
  3. Social Amplification and Community Mobilisation: Organisers published the contestants’ pitch videos across ChipInHere’s official Instagram and Facebook pages, allowing their communities to watch, engage, and vote, while founders shared their unique links across WhatsApp and other social media platforms to receive direct contributions and monitor their fundraising progress in real time.

SUSTAINING GRASSROOTS BUSINESS FUNDING

While Pitch & Fund 1.0 has officially concluded, ChipInHere stated that its digital infrastructure remains open year-round for entrepreneurs, creators, and community organisers seeking collective financial support.

Through https://www.chipinhere.co, users can create personalised fundraising or collection links, invite co-hosts to manage campaigns, share links seamlessly across WhatsApp communities, and track contributions without complex administrative bottlenecks.

PITCH & FUND 2.0 REGISTRATION OPENS NOVEMBER 20

Following the strong participation recorded in the maiden edition, ChipInHere has announced that registration for Pitch & Fund 2.0 will officially open on November 20, 2026.

Prospective applicants are expected to submit their entries via the competition’s official portal at https://www.pitchandfund.co, while business owners seeking immediate funding can launch independent campaigns at https://www.chipinhere.co.

The post ChipInHere Empowers 29 Nigerian Founders With Community-Backed Funding, Announces Edition 2.0 appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

content:
Lagos State Governor, Babajide Sanwo-Olu, hosted Nigeria’s history-making Flamingos at a grand dinner reception at Lagos House, Marina, on Sunday, where he announced a N300 million reward package for the team.

‎Each of the 21 players and nine members of the coaching and backroom staff will receive N10 million.

‎The U-17 players also received an iPhone 18 Pro Max and customised headphones, while members of the technical crew received bespoke outfits and other gifts.

‎The reception drew government officials, sports administrators, family members and supporters, all of whom turned out to celebrate the newly-minted world champions.

‎Sanwo-Olu congratulated the team for putting Nigeria on the world map, describing their victory as a product of hard work, discipline and belief. NigerianNewspaper Access.

‎He urged the young players not to rest on their laurels but to remain focused on their education and football careers, assuring them that Lagos would continue to support sports development and reward excellence.

‎The governor also praised head coach Akeem Ishola Busari and his technical crew for guiding the team to glory.

‎The Flamingos became the first African team to win the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup after defeating Japan 2-1 in the final in Rabat, Morocco, on November 7.

‎Awawu Bashiru and Oluebube Umejiaku scored the goals that secured Nigeria’s maiden title in the competition.

‎One of the evening’s emotional moments came when captain Harmony Chidi knelt before the governor to express gratitude on behalf of the team.

‎Five members of the squad are from Robo Queens of Mushin, Lagos, highlighting the state’s contribution to the team’s success.

‎The Lagos reward follows the Federal Government’s reception for the team in Abuja, where President Bola Tinubu approved a N100 million Federal Government Savings Bond for each player.

‎The head coach received N100 million in cash, while other members of the technical and administrative crew received N50 million each.

Soludo gave the
content:
By Vincent Ujumadu

AWKA — Anambra State Governor, Prof. Chukwuma Soludo, has cautioned politicians against turning churches and other places of worship into campaign arenas, insisting that sacred spaces must remain neutral grounds for people of different political persuasions.

Soludo gave the warning on Sunday during the 30th anniversary celebration of the Mountain of Holy Ghost Intervention and Deliverance Ministry, founded by Prophet Chukwuemeka Ohanaemere, popularly known as Odumeje.

Addressing the congregation, the governor urged religious leaders to maintain a clear distinction between politics and worship, stressing that places of worship should provide an atmosphere where everyone could freely seek God without political interference.

According to him, churches should remain holy places where people of different political affiliations can worship peacefully.

“It should not be a place for politics. There is a venue for politics. If you want to worship God, you have to go to the house of God. We must separate the two things clearly,” Soludo said.

The governor recalled that about six months before his election, he deliberately resolved not to use any church platform to solicit votes or campaign for political support.

He said he maintained the decision by worshipping at the Government House chapel throughout the period leading to the election and after.

“It was a deliberate decision. I worshipped in the Government House chapel until the election day and afterwards,” he stated.

Soludo reiterated his opposition to the politicisation of religious institutions, urging politicians to keep campaign activities away from churches and other places of worship.

“We must never politicise the church. We must never politicise the place of worship. Politicians, keep off churches. Keep off places of worship. That’s a deliberate message and it is my kind of consistency of character,” he added.

title: ‘Blackmail is not politics’: Jijiwa cautions opposition ahead of 2027
description:
The Director-General of the Presidential Support Organisation (PSO), Comrade Umar Jijiwa, has urged opposition parties to abandon blackmail and personal attacks as political activities gather momentum ahead of the 2027 general elections.
Jijiwa, also known as Youth Jagaban, coordinates support group
content:
The Director-General of the Presidential Support Organisation (PSO), Comrade Umar Jijiwa, has urged opposition parties to abandon blackmail and personal attacks as political activities gather momentum ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Jijiwa, also known as Youth Jagaban, coordinates support group structures for President Bola Tinubu ahead of the next general election.

He made the remarks during an appearance on PoliticsOnSunday on TVC, where he discussed the state of opposition politics and preparations for the 2027 polls.

He criticised what he described as the use of old political tactics, arguing that blackmail and personal attacks would not help political parties present credible alternatives to Nigerians.

“But you have to understand, blackmail is not politics. We need to move on from this kind of politics. For God’s sake. We are having people that are trying to use the same old ideas, the same old tactics, thinking that it will work in a new world,” he said.

The presidential support group director-general also argued that opposition parties needed to present workable ideas rather than focus their efforts on criticising the ruling All Progressives Congress.

He said he had no objection to opposition figures holding the government accountable but challenged them to offer practical solutions to the country’s problems.

“As opposition, I have no issue with them pointing fingers. But for God’s sake, can you please give me a better idea?” Jijiwa asked.

He also dismissed suggestions that the APC was responsible for the difficulties confronting opposition parties, maintaining that their challenges largely stemmed from internal disagreements and organisational problems.

According to him, several opposition groups had initially appeared united by a shared desire to remove President Bola Tinubu from office but later struggled to agree on how to work together.

Jijiwa cited disagreements within the African Democratic Congress (ADC) as an example, claiming that rival groups had clashed over control of the party.

He added that he was still trying to understand the political approach of the newly established Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC).

Speaking about the 2023 general elections, Jijiwa also accused supporters of Labour Party’s 2023 presidential candidate, Peter Obi, popularly known as Obidients, of insulting and disrespecting others during the election period.

“In the last election, I know how disrespectful and insulting the Obidients have been to everybody. That I know for sure,” he said.

Jijiwa further said he had experienced disagreements within the APC himself, recalling his dissatisfaction after contesting for the party’s national leadership position.

However, he said he remained in the party and worked through the disagreements because of what he described as their shared objective of winning elections and continuing to govern.
