title: Hardship real, but Nigeria is more than its challenges — Abbas
description:
By John Alechenu



ABUJA — Speaker of the House of Representatives, Tajudeen Abbas, has acknowledged the hardship confronting Nigerians, saying governments at all levels must urgently address the difficulties facing households and businesses.







Abbas, however, cautioned the international commu
content:
By John Alechenu

ABUJA — Speaker of the House of Representatives, Tajudeen Abbas, has acknowledged the hardship confronting Nigerians, saying governments at all levels must urgently address the difficulties facing households and businesses.

Abbas, however, cautioned the international community against defining Nigeria solely by its challenges, insisting that the country’s economic potential, human capital and development progress should also be recognised.

He spoke on Monday at the ongoing Global Alliance World Public Relations Forum in Abuja, where he addressed issues bordering on responsible communication, democratic accountability, governance and institutional reforms.

The Speaker, who was represented by the House Majority Leader, Prof. Julius Ihonvbere, said the economic difficulties confronting Nigerians could no longer be ignored or dismissed.

“The difficulties confronting households and businesses are real and deserve serious attention,” he said.

Abbas noted that Nigerians expected improved security, employment opportunities, efficient public services and better governance, adding that the benefits of ongoing economic reforms must begin to reflect in their daily lives.

He said the reforms being implemented by the President Bola Tinubu-led administration were designed to address structural weaknesses, restore economic stability and lay the foundation for sustainable growth.

However, he acknowledged that the reforms had come with immediate costs, stressing that government had a responsibility to ensure that their eventual benefits translated into tangible improvements in citizens’ living conditions.

“The challenge before government is to ensure that their benefits translate into tangible improvements in the lives of ordinary Nigerians,” he said.

On insecurity, the Speaker called for decisive and sustained action against those responsible for violence across the country.

He described every innocent life lost to insecurity as a tragedy that demanded justice and accountability.

“Every innocent life lost is a tragedy that calls for justice and accountability,” he said.

Abbas urged the country to remain resolute in confronting perpetrators of violence, strengthening security institutions and protecting every citizen, irrespective of religion, ethnicity or place of origin.

Turning to Nigeria’s international image, the Speaker warned against narratives that portray the country exclusively through its difficulties, arguing that such representations could overshadow its achievements and development potential.

“There is a difference between reporting a country’s difficulties and reducing the country to those difficulties. There is also a difference between legitimate scrutiny and the construction of narratives that oversimplify complex realities.

“We do not seek immunity from scrutiny. We seek fairness in the exercise of scrutiny. This is not an argument for managing Nigeria’s image at the expense of truth,” he said.

He urged public relations practitioners and other communication professionals to uphold fairness, accuracy and balance, noting that their work played an important role in shaping public understanding and sustaining democracy.

Reflecting on Nigeria’s democratic journey since 1999, Abbas said the country had maintained constitutional governance through successive elections, changes in leadership and the continued operation of democratic institutions.

He, however, acknowledged that the democratic process remained a work in progress, identifying institutional capacity, electoral confidence, public accountability and political intolerance as some of the challenges requiring attention.

According to him, democracy thrives not only through institutions but also through the space it provides for disagreement, representation, negotiation and peaceful political competition.

“Democracy cannot thrive on institutions alone. It also depends on the quality of public discourse,” he said.

Abbas stressed the need for citizens to have access to reliable information to make informed decisions, urging political actors to engage in debates based on ideas, policies and evidence rather than insults, intimidation and deliberate falsehoods.

He also called for the protection of press freedom, saying journalists must be allowed to scrutinise those in authority while adhering to professional standards.

Public institutions, he added, must equally embrace transparency and accountability.

Describing parliament as the constitutional platform for representation, deliberation and accountability, Abbas said its legitimacy depended not only on the laws it enacted but also on public confidence in its processes.

He noted that the House of Representatives, with 360 members representing constituencies across the federation, had a special responsibility to accommodate the diverse interests and aspirations of Nigerians.

He listed national security, economic growth and development, education, healthcare, social inclusion, institutional strengthening and an open parliament among the legislature’s priorities.

The Speaker maintained that legislative performance should ultimately be measured by its impact on the welfare, security and opportunities available to Nigerians.

He also disclosed that the National Assembly had advanced constitutional reforms aimed at strengthening the country’s security architecture, including a proposal for the establishment of state police.

The post Hardship real, but Nigeria is more than its challenges — Abbas appeared first on Vanguard News.

content:
Romelu Lukaku has disclosed his retirement from the Belgium men’s national team, calling an end to an international career that spanned 16 years.

Lukaku, popularly called ‘Big Rom,’ revealed this on his Instagram page on Monday.

The 33-year-old striker made his international debut in 2010 and became Belgium’s all-time leading men’s goalscorer with 94 goals in 135 appearances. He represented the country in four World Cups and three European Championships.

According to BBC Sport, Lukaku is the fifth-highest men’s international goalscorer of all time, behind leader Cristiano Ronaldo with 146, Lionel Messi, Sunil Chhetri and Ali Daei.

The Fenerbahçe striker retires from international football as Belgium’s third-most-capped player, behind Jan Vertonghen (157) and Axel Witsel (140).

Lukaku, who played for top clubs in Europe, including Chelsea, Manchester United and Inter Milan, expressed appreciation to his teammates, the coaches for “pushing and trusting me to help the team” and the Belgian fans for their support.

In his retirement post, Lukaku noted that he was at “peace” with himself to call the final shot on his international career, as he vowed to remember the moments he had on the team.

“These 16 years, I gave all I had for the national team. I went through every emotion possible. I played with amazing teammates that I will always be grateful for.

“I want to thank them all. I want to thank all the coaches as well for pushing and trusting me to help the team. It was a nice ride, and I enjoyed every single moment.

“To the Belgian fans, thank you for the support you gave our team. I am proud to have represented my country in four World Cups and three European Championships.

“I will never forget those moments. I’m at peace with my decision to stop here. It was amazing and enjoyable. I’m grateful.”

Lukaku scored eight goals across four World Cups, including in the run to the quarter-finals at this summer’s tournament, and a total of six goals at three European Championships.

He missed Belgium’s Nations League win over Turkey last week with a hip injury and was an unused substitute on Sunday as they qualified for the last eight of the competition by beating Italy 4-1, BBC Sport reports.

In 2023, Lukaku scored 14 times in eight Euro 2024 qualifying appearances, breaking the record for goals scored by a player in a European Championship qualifying campaign.

The post Lukaku retires from Belgium as all-time leading goalscorer appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: 2027: A-Court warns officials against using election cases to make money
description:
…trains 655 to serve in tribunal registries



By Ikechukwu Nnochiri



ABUJA – The President of the Court of Appeal, Justice Monica Dongban-Mensem, on Monday read the riot act to 655 staff members and Deputy Chief Registrars of the Court who have been selected to serve on the various tribunals that
content:
…trains 655 to serve in tribunal registries

By Ikechukwu Nnochiri

ABUJA – The President of the Court of Appeal, Justice Monica Dongban-Mensem, on Monday read the riot act to 655 staff members and Deputy Chief Registrars of the Court who have been selected to serve on the various tribunals that will hear disputes arising from the 2027 general elections.

Emphasising that the integrity of the judiciary was on the line, Justice Dongban-Mensem cautioned the court’s registry staff against exploiting their election tribunal assignments for financial gain.

She warned that anyone found culpable would be handed over to the relevant security agencies for prosecution.

“It is part of your obligation to discharge your duties with utmost good faith and not be carried away by little advances.

“Your integrity and that of the Tribunal and its members are in the public searchlight, you must therefore ensure you are not used as weapons to truncate the process.

“Ensure to live above board so that you will not put the Judiciary into disrepute. Do not see it as an opportunity to enrich yourselves but rather go there to build your name and your future as it is said that a good name is better than silver and gold.

“The Court will not hesitate to deal with anyone found wanting in this regard,” Justice Dongban-Mensem added.

She spoke at the opening session of a two-day capacity-building workshop for election petition tribunal registry staff, organised at the Body of Benchers Complex in Abuja.

The PCA said the workshop with the theme: “Modern Registry Practices for Effective Election Petition Tribunal Administration,” was designed as a platform to equip the participants with hands-on knowledge on the use of technology in case management, best practices in records keeping, and the ethical standards expected of Tribunal staff.

“As you are well aware, elections play a very vital role in a democratic system of government as it gives the citizens the chance to choose their leaders.

“The Registry is a very important organ of an Election Petition Tribunal and its administrative duties include the receipt of the petition and other court processes for filing, service of court processes timeously on parties, issuance of hearing notices, preparation of court proceedings and orders, custody and safekeeping of the Tribunals’ documents, compilation of records among various other duties and responsibilities.

“The effectiveness, quality, efficiency, transparency and speed of the Registry has direct impact on the performance and justice delivery of the Election Tribunal.

“Modern registry practices therefore demand more than manual filing and routine administrative work. They demand a new mindset. They demand the adoption of electronic filing and case management systems that allow for easy tracking and retrieval of cases.

“They demand proper documentation, accurate and systematic archiving. They demand timely service of processes and effective scheduling that respects the strict timelines prescribed by law for election petitions. They demand confidentiality, integrity and professionalism,” the PCA added.

In his remarks, the Chief Registrar of the Court of Appeal, Mr. Umar Bangari, urged the participants to be conscious of the fact that after the elections, “the spotlight of the entire nation will now turn on the Judiciary.”

“While Honourable Judges, among others, sit on the bench of the Tribunals to adjudicate disputes arising from the conduct of the said elections, the success, efficiency, and credibility of every Tribunal really rest heavily on your shoulders.

“You should be aware that you are the custodians of all the processes filed at the Tribunal, the managers of strict statutory timelines, and the primary administrative interface between parties on one hand, and the Bench on the other hand.

“Accordingly, you are hereby placed on strict notice against engaging in any form of misconduct, including but not limited to collusion, conspiracy, conniving with any party, to manipulate court processes, alter records, or confer an unfair advantage upon one party to the detriment of another.

“You must also avoid file tampering, leaking confidential internal communications, draft rulings, panel deliberations, or privileged case information to unauthorized persons, among so many other acts of misconduct.

“We shall entertain zero tolerance towards any breach of neutrality or ethical standards. Any secretary or staff member found to be conniving with any party or counsel to subvert the course of justice will face severe consequences,” he added.

The Deputy Chief Registrar of the Court in charge of the election petition tribunals, Mrs. Maitumbi Altine, disclosed that a total of 223 of the participants had previously served in tribunals while 432 of them were first-timers.

She said it was the first time in the annals of the court that such training was organised for staff members who will serve the various election tribunals.

The post 2027: A-Court warns officials against using election cases to make money appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Toluwanisings: Defendant fails to meet bail conditions, spends weekend in correctional centre
description:
Joshua Oladipupo, a defendant, facing trial over alleged posting of fake news on the death of gospel singer, Bayonile Olayemi, popularly called Toluwanisings, failed to perfect his bail and spent the weekend at Agodi Correctional Centre, Ibadan.



Investigation by the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) o
content:
Joshua Oladipupo, a defendant, facing trial over alleged posting of fake news on the death of gospel singer, Bayonile Olayemi, popularly called Toluwanisings, failed to perfect his bail and spent the weekend at Agodi Correctional Centre, Ibadan.

Investigation by the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) on Monday revealed that Oladipupo, arraigned at the Iyaganku Magistrates’ Court in Ibadan on Friday, was yet to meet his bail conditions.

The defendant, who was arraigned on a three-count charge of publication of fake news and conduct likely to cause breach of the peace, spent the weekend at the Agodi Correctional Centre.

He had pleaded not guilty to the charges, and the magistrate, Mrs Oluwabusayo Osho, granted him N2 million bail with two sureties.

Osho had also directed that the two sureties must be of close blood relations and must have landed properties within the jurisdiction of the court.

She further held that the lands must possess Certificates of Occupancy (C of O) and survey documents.

The magistrate subsequently ordered that the defendant be remanded at Agodi Correctional centre pending the perfection of the bail and adjourned the case until Dec. 17 for hearing.

Earlier, the prosecutor, Insp Adeshina Folaranmi, had told the court that the defendant committed the offences in October 2026 in the Dugbe area of Ibadan.

Folaranmi alleged that the defendant published fake news on Facebook and other social media handles about the death of a gospel singer, Bayonile Olayemi, popularly called Toluwanisings.

He alleged that the defendant falsely published that the late singer’s personal assistant, Babadunni Gbolabo; wife, Damilola; and members of the deceased’s mother’s family were responsible for his death.

The prosecutor alleged that the defendant’s intent was to cause fear and alarm to the public.

Folaranmi said the offences contravened provisions of Sections 59 and 249(d) of the Criminal Laws of Oyo State, 2000.

A NAN correspondent in court on Monday learnt that the defendant was still in custody because he had yet to meet the bail conditions.

A reliable source, who preferred to speak on condition of anonymity, said that Oladipupo remained in custody pending meeting bail conditions set by the court. (NAN)

title: Visually Impaired Persons protest exclusion in Ondo, demand recognition
description:
By Dayo Johnson



AKURE — Members of the Association of Technology Inclined Visually Impaired Persons of Nigeria (ATIVIPN), Ondo State chapter, on Monday staged a peaceful protest, demanding official recognition and inclusion in government programmes and interventions.







The protesters accused
content:
By Dayo Johnson

AKURE — Members of the Association of Technology Inclined Visually Impaired Persons of Nigeria (ATIVIPN), Ondo State chapter, on Monday staged a peaceful protest, demanding official recognition and inclusion in government programmes and interventions.

The protesters accused the Ondo State Ministry of Women Affairs of neglecting their association despite submitting relevant registration documents and several letters seeking official recognition.

They alleged that the state government recognises only the Nigeria Association of the Blind (NAB), thereby excluding other groups of visually impaired persons from government interventions and benefits.

Speaking during the protest, the state chairman of ATIVIPN, Comrade Omiyale Babatunde, said members had been excluded from government intervention programmes since the beginning of the year.

Babatunde said the association had submitted its Corporate Affairs Commission (CAC) certificate and other relevant registration documents to the ministry but expressed disappointment over the alleged failure of the authorities to act on their request.

He said several members of the association were educated but remained unemployed, appealing to the state government to provide them with opportunities to become economically productive.

“We have to be included. We need jobs. Some of us are educated, we need something doing, we need palliatives,” he said.

Babatunde, who disclosed that he was formerly a member of the NAB from 2018, alleged that the association’s leadership had failed to adequately address the concerns of visually impaired persons in both rural and urban communities.

Also speaking, the youth leader of ATIVIPN, Bello Yusuf, said the association was seeking independent recognition and inclusion in government activities and programmes designed for persons with disabilities.

Yusuf said the association was established in April 2026 following disagreements with the NAB, whose leadership he accused of bias, alleged diversion of palliatives and failure to cater adequately for visually impaired persons at the grassroots.

“We need inclusion and recognition. That is our main point here. We are no more part of NAB because of the bias they actually bear, the cheating and diversion of palliatives,” he said.

He explained that the association had submitted its registration documents and other necessary papers to the Ministry of Women Affairs but was yet to receive official recognition.

Yusuf said the group had written several letters to the ministry and formally notified it of its intention to protest before staging Monday’s demonstration.

Responding to the protesters, the Permanent Secretary of the Ministry of Women Affairs, Kolawole Kayode, assured them that their complaints would be addressed within seven days.

Kayode, who acknowledged receiving two letters from the association, urged the protesters not to lose confidence in the ministry, promising that its executives would receive a positive response before the expiration of the seven-day ultimatum.

“We are working on it. I want to assure you that before the end of the seven days of the ultimatum you gave us to address your issue of inclusion, your executives will definitely hear from us,” he said.

However, Yusuf warned that the association would stage another mass protest if the government failed to address its demands within the stipulated seven days.

He said the group would intensify its peaceful demonstration and block access to government offices to press home its demands.

content:
By Emmanuel Okogba

Nigerian singer Temilade Openiyi, popularly known as Tems, has secured a nomination for Best R&B Solo Performance at the 69th Annual Grammy Awards for her song, ‘What You Need’.

The singer will compete against Beyoncé, nominated for ‘Morning Dew (Donk)’; Kehlani, with ‘Out the Window’; Victoria Monét, nominated for ‘Let Me’; and Jill Scott, with ‘Pressha’.

‘What You Need’ was released on November 21, 2025, as a single from Tems’ extended play, Love Is a Kingdom.

The Recording Academy announced the nominees on Monday during a live YouTube programme, unveiling contenders across 100 categories ahead of the 2027 ceremony.

The 69th Grammy Awards are scheduled to take place on February 7, 2027, at the Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles, California.

Tems remains one of Nigeria’s most celebrated Grammy-winning artistes. She won Best Melodic Rap Performance in 2023 for her contribution to Future’s ‘Wait for U’, featuring Drake, and Best African Music Performance in 2025 for her song ‘Love Me JeJe’.

title: Kaduna court fixes December 14 for ruling in cleric’s case
description:
By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo



KADUNA — An Upper Sharia Court sitting along Daura Road, Kaduna State, has fixed December 14, 2026, for ruling in a case involving Islamic cleric, Sheikh Sunusi Khalil, over allegations of sexual relations outside marriage and threats against a woman who accused him of fath
content:
By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo

KADUNA — An Upper Sharia Court sitting along Daura Road, Kaduna State, has fixed December 14, 2026, for ruling in a case involving Islamic cleric, Sheikh Sunusi Khalil, over allegations of sexual relations outside marriage and threats against a woman who accused him of fathering her pregnancy.

The court fixed the date on Monday, November 16, after the presiding judge, Justice Auwal Abdullahi, said the ruling had not been brought to his attention and was not on his schedule.

“The ruling was not brought to my notice. It is not in my diary,” the judge said.

The new date was subsequently secured by the defendant’s lead counsel, Abass Machika. Counsel to the complainant, Hafsat Uwa Usman, was reportedly absent when the date was fixed.

The case followed a direct criminal complaint filed by Usman on September 21, 2026, in which she accused the cleric of engaging in sexual relations with her outside marriage, resulting in pregnancy, and subsequently threatening her life when she declined to terminate it.

In her complaint, Usman alleged that she first met the defendant in 2024 around Kawo Bus Stop, Kaduna, where he reportedly approached her through one of his aides and introduced himself as an Islamic cleric.

She claimed their initial discussions centred on religion, dressing and general conduct before the relationship allegedly developed into a romantic and intimate one.

The complainant, who said she was formerly known as Faith Usman and practised Christianity, alleged that the cleric encouraged her to embrace Islam and promised to provide for her needs if she agreed to an intimate relationship.

She said she converted to Islam in early 2025 at Juma’at Mosque, Rigachikun, Kaduna, where she adopted the name Hafsat Uwa Usman.

According to her, the defendant’s religious standing and the circumstances surrounding her conversion contributed to the trust she placed in him.

She further alleged that their relationship became intimate and resulted in sexual intercourse without a valid Islamic marriage.

Usman maintained that no wali, mahr, marriage witnesses or formal solemnisation of nikah took place between them.

She also claimed that she had no sexual relationship with another man during the period the pregnancy was conceived and attributed the pregnancy to the cleric.

On the alleged threat, the complainant stated that Khalil visited her residence in Millennium City, Kaduna, sometime in August 2026, ostensibly to discuss the pregnancy.

She alleged that during the visit, he asked her to terminate the pregnancy and threatened to kill her when she refused.

Usman said the alleged threat made her fear for her life and the safety of her unborn child.

She further accused the cleric of subsequently withdrawing from the relationship, avoiding her telephone calls and failing to provide financial, medical or other assistance during the pregnancy.

In her complaint, she expressed readiness to present telephone records, messages and other available evidence in support of her allegations. She also indicated willingness to undergo a lawful DNA examination with the child after birth to establish paternity.

The complainant urged the court to take cognisance of the allegations and issue a criminal summons against the defendant.

She cited alleged offences of zina under Section 121 of the Sharia Penal Code Law of Kaduna State, 2002, and criminal intimidation under Sections 232 and 233 of the same law.

The court is expected to deliver its ruling on December 14.

However, the allegations against Sheikh Sunusi Khalil remain unproven, and the court has yet to determine the merits of the complaint.

title: EU showcases Ukrainian art, digital innovation at Lagos Biennial 2026
description:
From Fred Ezeh, Abuja
The European Union (EU) has unveiled two immersive digital exhibitions at the 2026 Lagos Biennial, showcasing Ukrainian artistic perspectives and emerging forms of digital creativity as part of efforts to strengthen cultural cooperation between Europe and Africa.
The exhibition
content:
From Fred Ezeh, Abuja

The European Union (EU) has unveiled two immersive digital exhibitions at the 2026 Lagos Biennial, showcasing Ukrainian artistic perspectives and emerging forms of digital creativity as part of efforts to strengthen cultural cooperation between Europe and Africa.

The exhibitions, presented at the EU pavilion, titled “Together”, opened at the weekend, with the EU Ambassador to Nigeria and ECOWAS, Gautier Mignot, describing the initiative as a demonstration of the growing partnership between European and African creative communities.

Mignot said the EU’s participation followed several years of planning and reflected its determination to move beyond sponsoring cultural events to participating directly in major international exhibitions.

He cited previous engagements at the Guadalajara International Book Fair in Mexico and Expo 2025 in Osaka, Japan, noting that Nigeria had become a natural choice when the EU considered expanding its cultural engagement in Africa.

According to him, Lagos’ position as a major global cultural centre and its reputation for artistic innovation made the Lagos Biennial an important platform for the initiative.

The ambassador recalled meeting the Biennial’s founder and director, Folakunle Oshun, in Paris about two years ago, shortly after assuming his diplomatic responsibilities in Nigeria, saying the encounter had laid the foundation for the partnership.

Describing the outcome as exceeding expectations, Mignot commended the organisers for transforming the initial idea into a major international cultural gathering.

“The first exhibition, Home Beyond the Dawn, focused on the human cost of Russia’s war against Ukraine, presenting the experiences of Ukrainian artists and civilians whose lives, homes and communities have been devastated by the conflict.

“Through immersive digital artworks, it explored displacement, destruction of homes, family separation, human rights abuses and the suffering of civilians in Russian-occupied territories,” he said.

He said the exhibition also highlighted the role of art in preserving cultural identity, memory and collective resistance despite the devastation caused by war.

Mignot said the exhibition demonstrated how art and the concept of home could become instruments of identity and resistance in the face of aggression.

“The second exhibition, The Future is Shared, by Italian digital artist Stefano Fake, explores the possibilities of immersive technology in contemporary artistic expression.

“Combining images, light, sound and digital environments, the installation encourages visitors to become active participants in the creative process rather than passive observers.

“Fake is also engaging students, designers and artists in collaborative activities, with their contributions expected to form part of an evolving digital installation,” he said.

Both exhibitions feature in the fifth edition of the Lagos Biennial, themed “The Museum of Things Unseen”, which seeks to bring overlooked experiences and perspectives into public attention.

Mignot also drew attention to the Africa-Europe Partnerships for Culture programme, through which the EU supports collaboration between artists and cultural institutions across both continents.

He encouraged Nigerian creative institutions, museums and other stakeholders to take advantage of available funding opportunities under the programme.

In his remarks, Oshun thanked the EU for its support, describing the partnership as an important contribution to the development of the Biennial.

He also acknowledged the participating artists, sponsors and cultural professionals whose contributions had sustained the exhibition over the past nine years.

The post EU showcases Ukrainian art, digital innovation at Lagos Biennial 2026 appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Newlywed couple die after fire engulfs Plateau residence
description:
By Golok Nanmwa



JOS — A newly married couple, identified as Sikiru Habib and his wife, Ramlat Lawan, have died following a fire outbreak at their residence in Anguwan Miyango, Bukuru, Jos South Local Government Area of Plateau State.







The couple reportedly sustained severe injuries after fi
content:
By Golok Nanmwa

JOS — A newly married couple, identified as Sikiru Habib and his wife, Ramlat Lawan, have died following a fire outbreak at their residence in Anguwan Miyango, Bukuru, Jos South Local Government Area of Plateau State.

The couple reportedly sustained severe injuries after fire engulfed their room at about 2:30 a.m. on Saturday while they were asleep.

A neighbour, Engineer Lawal Suleiman, said the fire was suspected to have been triggered by a high-voltage power surge, although the cause had yet to be officially established.

He described the incident as tragic, explaining that the couple became trapped inside the room after the door reportedly failed to open as the fire spread.

According to him, youths in the neighbourhood rushed to the scene and made frantic efforts to rescue the victims.

He said the rescuers eventually broke through a window and brought the couple out before firefighters arrived to provide emergency assistance.

The victims were subsequently rushed to the Jos University Teaching Hospital (JUTH) for medical treatment.

However, Suleiman said the husband died on Sunday, while his wife succumbed to her injuries on Monday, despite efforts to save their lives.

The deaths have thrown the couple’s families, friends and residents of Anguwan Miyango into mourning, particularly as the tragedy occurred shortly after their wedding.

content:
Nigerian music stars Asake, Burna Boy, Tems, Wizkid, Davido and Ayra Starr have earned nominations at the 69th Annual Grammy Awards, with Asake securing two nominations in the Best African Music Performance category.

In a live announcement on the Recording Academy’s YouTube channel on Monday, Asake earned two nominations in the category for his songs, ‘Gratitude’ and ‘Jogodo’, his collaboration with fellow Nigerian singer Wizkid.

Tems also earned a nomination for ‘Big Daddy’, while Ayra Starr was recognised alongside Beninese singer Angélique Kidjo for their collaboration, ‘Aye Kan (Are You Coming Back?)’.

The other nominee in the category is ‘No Tradition, No Africa’ by King Ayisoba featuring Rocky Dawuni.

Burna Boy also earned a nomination in the Best Global Music Performance category for ‘Dìá Dìá’, his collaboration with Colombian singer Shakira.

Nigerian artistes also featured in the Best Global Music Album category, with Davido nominated for ‘Oriadé’, Ayra Starr for ‘Starrgirl’ and Tems for ‘Love Is a Kingdom’.

Tems also secured a nomination in the Best R&B Solo Performance category for her song, ‘What You Need’.

The 69th Annual Grammy Awards will hold on February 7, 2027, at the Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles, California.

title: Gov Radda Welcomes Zamfara ADC Defectors To APC
description: Katsina State Governor, Malam Dikko Umaru Radda, has expressed confidence that the All Progressives Congress (APC) will significantly surpass its 2023 electoral performance in the 2027 general elections, citing the party’s growing acceptance and expanding grassroots support across the state.Go
content:
Katsina State Governor, Malam Dikko Umaru Radda, has expressed confidence that the All Progressives Congress (APC) will significantly surpass its 2023 electoral performance in the 2027 general elections, citing the party’s growing acceptance and expanding grassroots support across the state.

Governor Radda made the declaration on Monday during the Tinubu/Dikko 2027 Campaign Council rally held at the Lazio Football Ground in Zango Local Government Area as the campaign tour continued across the Daura Senatorial Zone.

The rally attracted thousands of party supporters and witnessed the defection of members of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) to the APC, further strengthening the ruling party’s campaign drive ahead of the elections.

Addressing the crowd, Governor Radda urged residents to remain steadfast in their support for the APC and cautioned them against what he described as “business politicians” whose objective, he said, was to undermine the achievements of the ruling party for personal interests.

He called on the electorate to vote for APC candidates at all levels to sustain the administration’s development agenda.

According to the governor, his administration has made significant investments in healthcare, education, agriculture, youth employment, economic development and security, while also providing subsidised fertiliser to farmers across the state to boost food production and improve livelihoods.

“Beware of business politicians. APC will not disappoint you. We will continue to do more for our people. We have constructed hospitals, employed youths, strengthened education, agriculture, the economy and security. We have also distributed subsidised fertiliser to farmers across the state and remain committed to improving the living standards of our citizens,” Governor Radda said.

“Ensure that you vote APC from top to bottom so that we can continue the good work we have started.”

Also speaking, the Katsina State APC Deputy Chairman, Bala Abu Musawa, described the APC as a youth-focused party committed to creating greater opportunities for young people.

He urged voters to support the party in the 2027 elections to consolidate ongoing development initiatives and deliver improved governance.

Former Secretary to the Katsina State Government and former APC governorship aspirant, Dr. Mustapha Muhammad Inuwa, maintained that no opposition party could match the APC’s popularity and performance in the state.

He alleged that critics of the ruling party were being dishonest and claimed that the ADC was facing internal legal and leadership challenges.

Dr. Inuwa further urged residents to align themselves with the APC, saying the party remained the strongest political platform in Katsina State ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The Tinubu/Dikko 2027 Campaign Council has continued its grassroots mobilisation across the Daura Senatorial District, with party leaders expressing optimism that the growing wave of defections and public support will translate into an overwhelming victory for the APC in the forthcoming elections.

The post Gov Radda Welcomes Zamfara ADC Defectors To APC appeared first on Channels Television.

title: Police release 78 suspects over attack on Tinubu’s convoy
description:
By Kingsley Omonobi



The Federal Capital Territory (FCT) Police Command has commenced the release of 78 suspects arrested in connection with the attack on President Bola Tinubu’s motorcade in Abuja, following a presidential directive granting them clemency.







The suspects were arrested after
content:
By Kingsley Omonobi

The Federal Capital Territory (FCT) Police Command has commenced the release of 78 suspects arrested in connection with the attack on President Bola Tinubu’s motorcade in Abuja, following a presidential directive granting them clemency.

The suspects were arrested after the President’s convoy was attacked on Friday, November 13, 2026, shortly after he observed Jumu’ah prayers at a mosque in the Garki District of Abuja.

The attack, according to the police, involved individuals who allegedly hurled stones and other dangerous objects at the departing convoy, damaging several vehicles and injuring some security operatives.

The FCT Police Public Relations Officer, CSP Josephine Adeh, disclosed the development in a statement on Monday, saying a joint security team led by the police responded to the incident, while subsequent intelligence-led operations in the area led to additional arrests.

She said the number of suspects arrested in connection with the incident eventually rose to 78.

Adeh explained that the Presidency subsequently directed the police to warn and release the suspects following the extension of presidential clemency to those involved in the attack.

“In compliance with the directive, the Command wishes to inform the public that the suspects are currently undergoing the necessary release processes,” she said.

Meanwhile, the Commissioner of Police, FCT Command, CP Ahmed Mohammed Sanusi, warned against violence, public disorder and destruction of property.

He urged political parties, political actors and their supporters to embrace peaceful engagement and shun violence, intimidation, inflammatory statements and incitement as preparations for the 2027 general elections gather momentum.

The police commissioner also directed Area Commanders, Divisional Police Officers and heads of tactical units to remain vigilant and intensify security operations to protect residents and visitors in the FCT.

Adeh urged residents to remain security-conscious and promptly report suspicious persons or activities to the nearest police station.

She also provided the command’s emergency contact numbers as 08032003913 and 08061581938.

title: Wike tasks APC campaign council to stop ADC, NDC from winning 25% FCT votes
description:
• Says Tinubu’s achievements, infrastructure projects enough to secure victory
___________________________________________________________________
From Juliana Taiwo-Obalonye, Abuja
The Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, has challenged the All Progressives Congress (APC) P
content:
• Says Tinubu’s achievements, infrastructure projects enough to secure victory

___________________________________________________________________

From Juliana Taiwo-Obalonye, Abuja

The Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, has challenged the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council and the Rainbow Coalition to ensure that opposition parties, particularly the African Democratic Congress (ADC) and the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), fail to secure 25 per cent of the votes in the territory in the January 16, 2027 general election.

Wike, who is the coordinator of the FCT Presidential Campaign Council, gave the charge on Monday during the inauguration of the APC Presidential Campaign Council and Rainbow Coalition at the Bola Ahmed Tinubu International Conference Centre, Abuja.

He urged members of the campaign council to intensify grassroots mobilisation across the six area councils, insisting that the achievements of President Bola Tinubu’s administration provided sufficient evidence to convince voters to support the APC.

The minister, however, cautioned party members against taking electoral victory for granted, stressing that they must demonstrate the administration’s achievements to residents rather than rely on political rhetoric.

“You don’t need to go and see a prophet. You don’t need to go and see any doctor or anybody to tell you what to do. It is obvious; it is factual. Look at what Mr President has done for the people of the FCT. These are the tools you need to campaign,” he said.

Wike argued that Tinubu had demonstrated an unprecedented commitment to the development and political inclusion of the FCT, particularly through institutional reforms and infrastructure projects.

He said that, 50 years after the creation of Abuja in 1976, Tinubu had become the first president to ensure that the FCT was represented at the Federal Executive Council, giving the territory a voice in national decision-making.

He also listed the establishment of the FCT Civil Service Commission, the appointment of a Head of Service and the elevation of FCT civil servants to permanent secretary positions as major achievements of the administration.

The minister further cited the creation of the Mandate Secretariats for Women Affairs and Youth Development, saying they had provided opportunities for women and young people to participate more actively in governance.

On financial autonomy, Wike said the removal of the FCT from the Treasury Single Account arrangement had given the territory greater financial independence and enabled it to access loans for critical infrastructure development.

He challenged opposition politicians to compare the infrastructure projects executed under previous administrations with those delivered since Tinubu assumed office in 2023.

Wike particularly highlighted the administration’s record in the issuance of Certificates of Occupancy (C of O), claiming that previous administrations between 1999 and 2023 had issued only about 7,000 to 8,000 certificates, compared with more than 20,000 issued by the Tinubu administration within three years.

“How can governments from 1999 to 2023 sign only about 8,000 C of Os, while the government of 2023 to 2026, in three years, has signed over 20,000? How?” he queried.

He urged campaign council members to take the administration’s record to communities, wards and polling units, particularly in satellite towns, where residents could assess the impact of government projects.

Earlier, the FCT APC Chairman, Ishaku Yamawo, expressed confidence that the party would secure an overwhelming victory for Tinubu and its National Assembly candidates in the forthcoming elections.

Yamawo described the infrastructure transformation under Wike as a major campaign advantage, saying the projects had strengthened public confidence in the APC-led administration.

“Your projects have already become our strongest campaign message. The goodwill and confidence you have earned among our people, both indigenes and residents of the FCT, are exceptional,” he told the minister.

He assured the party leadership that the APC and the Rainbow Coalition were fully mobilised to deliver victory on January 16, 2027.

Yamawo also described the political cooperation among stakeholders in the FCT as unprecedented, urging members of the campaign council to sustain the unity and take the party’s message to every ward and polling unit.

He said the inauguration should serve as a call to greater responsibility, adding that the campaign must be inclusive, disciplined and firmly connected to the grassroots.

Also speaking, the FCT PDP Chairman, Ismaila Mohammed Dogara, expressed confidence that political leaders and stakeholders in the territory would mobilise support for Tinubu and other endorsed candidates, even in Wike’s absence.

Dogara commended the minister for building a political structure capable of sustaining mobilisation and coordinating electoral activities without his physical presence.

He described the cooperation between APC and PDP leaders under the Rainbow Coalition as a significant political development, expressing confidence that the alliance would translate into electoral victory.

“Even if you are not in the FCT, our executive chairman does not allow any space, not even for one minute, before taking it from where you stopped. That shows that on the faithful day of the election, if the Honourable Minister is not in the FCT, those leaders are ready and capable of delivering Mr President, Senator Philip Aduda, Tanimu and others,” Dogara said.

He expressed optimism that members of the coalition would return to the conference centre on January 17, a day after the election, to celebrate their anticipated victory.

“The big day is January 16, and the return day is January 17. By the special grace of God, we are going to return to this hall to celebrate,” he declared.

The Federal Capital Territory Police Command has said 78 suspects arrested over the attack on President Bola Tinubu’s motorcade in Abuja are to be released following the President’s extension of clemency to them.

In a statement released on Monday by the command spokesperson, Josephine Adeh, the suspects were arrested after the attack on the President’s convoy on Friday, November 13, at a mosque in Garki District.

The incident happened shortly after Tinubu observed Jumu’ah prayers.

“The FCT Police Command wishes to inform the public that 78 suspects were arrested following the attack on the motorcade of President Bola Tinubu, GCFR, on Friday, November 13, 2026, at a mosque in Garki District, Abuja.

“The incident occurred shortly after the President observed Jumu’ah prayers at a mosque in Garki, when some individuals attacked the departing convoy with stones and other dangerous objects, damaging several vehicles and causing injuries to some security operatives,” the statement partly read.

She said a joint security team led by the Police responded to the incident, adding that intelligence-led raids in the area subsequently led to more arrests, bringing the total number of suspects to 78.

“A joint security team, led by the Police, swiftly responded to the incident, while subsequent intelligence-led raids within the area led to further arrests, bringing the total number of suspects arrested in connection with the incident to seventy-eight, ” she said.

Adeh added that following the clemency, the Presidency directed that the suspects be warned and released.

“Following the extension of presidential clemency to the individuals involved in the attack, the Presidency directed that the suspects arrested in connection with the incident be warned and released. In compliance with the directive, the Command wishes to inform the public that the suspects are currently undergoing the necessary release processes.,” the statement said.

She also said the CP Ahmed Sanusi warned against violence ahead of the 2027 General Elections.

“The CP warns against acts of violence, public disorder and destruction of property. As preparations for the 2027 General Elections intensify, the Command urges all political parties, political actors and their supporters to embrace peaceful political engagement and shun violence, intimidation, inflammatory statements and incitement, ” Adeh said.

She said the CP has directed all Area Commanders, Divisional Police Officers and heads of tactical units to remain vigilant and intensify security operations to ensure the safety of residents and visitors, the statement added.

The police statement is the first official acknowledgment of the attack.

On the day of the incident, it was disputed by the Presidency.

Tinubu’s Senior Special Assistant on Digital Engagement, Strategy and New media, O’tega Ogra rejected claims that the convoy was stoned by youths at the Shehu Shagari Central Mosque in Area 1, Garki.

“Contrary to the narrative being pushed by the opposition, with videos of their alleged paid thugs at the National Mosque today, here is footage of Mr President leaving the mosque after Friday prayers this afternoon,” Ogra wrote in a post accompanying a video of the President leaving the mosque.

A chieftain of the African Democratic Congress, Dino Melaye later posted a video showing youths throwing stones at a convoy that appeared to be the President’s.

The clip, which went viral, also captured some of the youths chanting “Ba ma yi, ba ma so,” a Hausa expression meaning “we don’t want you; we don’t support you.

title: Showunmi urges NSA to act against politicians threatening national security
description:
A chieftain of the Peoples Democratic Party in Ogun State and convener of The Alternative Movement, Segun Showunmi, has urged the National Security Adviser, Nuhu Ribadu, to take action against politicians whose conduct threatens national security and unity.
In an open letter addressed to Ribadu in A
content:
A chieftain of the Peoples Democratic Party in Ogun State and convener of The Alternative Movement, Segun Showunmi, has urged the National Security Adviser, Nuhu Ribadu, to take action against politicians whose conduct threatens national security and unity.

In an open letter addressed to Ribadu in Abuja and made available to journalists on Monday, Showunmi expressed concern over what he described as the growing toxicity of political conduct, reckless political communication and the increasingly dangerous behaviour of politicians, their supporters and influential individuals.

Titled “An Open Letter to the National Security Adviser: On the Urgent Need to Establish Firm Boundaries for Political Conduct and Hold Those Who Threaten National Security Accountable,” the letter urged the Office of the National Security Adviser to work with relevant security and law enforcement agencies to address political behaviour capable of undermining public peace and national stability.

Showunmi also copied President Bola Tinubu; the Minister of Defence, General Christopher Gwabin Musa (retd.); the Special Adviser to the President on Homeland Security, Major General Adeyinka A. Famadewa (retd.); the Inspector-General of Police, Mr Olatunji Rilwan Disu; the Director-General of the Department of State Services, Mr Oluwatosin Ajayi; and the Minister of State for Defence, Alhaji Bello Muhammad Matawalle.

He argued that Nigeria’s existing security challenges should not be compounded by political competition, personal ambition and partisan disagreements.

“The country is navigating a delicate security environment requiring vigilance, institutional coordination, intelligence gathering and responsible leadership.

“At such a time, it is difficult to understand why we should allow political competition, personal ambition and partisan disagreements to become additional threats to our national stability.

“There is a difference between robust political engagement and conduct that deliberately or recklessly threatens public peace. There is a difference between criticising government and deliberately inciting citizens against one another”.

He further warned against what he described as the apparent normalisation of provocative statements, ethnic and religious insinuations, threats, inflammatory public performances and the manipulation of sensitive national issues for political advantage.

According to him, some politicians, political loyalists and influential supporters appeared to believe that their positions or connections conferred immunity from the consequences of their public statements and actions.

“That assumption must be firmly challenged,” he declared, adding that “National security cannot be held hostage to political ambition.

As part of his recommendations, Showunmi urged Ribadu to establish and publicly communicate clear standards for political communication, particularly as Nigeria enters an increasingly competitive political period.

He argued that politicians, political parties, spokespersons, campaign organisations and their supporters must recognise that freedom of expression carries corresponding responsibilities.

The PDP chieftain, who was recently appointed a member of the Communication and Strategy Committee of the All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council, specifically called for public communication to be kept free from the promotion of violence, ethnic hostility, religious antagonism, intimidation and threats to national peace.

Showunmi also called on political parties and their leadership structures to accept greater responsibility for the conduct of individuals operating under their platforms or acting on their behalf.

He argued that political parties should not enjoy the benefits of democratic participation while distancing themselves from the irresponsible conduct of their supporters, spokespersons and other affiliated individuals.

The PDP chieftain said that “Going forward, decisive lawful action must follow credible evidence of offences, irrespective of how highly placed the individual involved may be.

“No political position, personal relationship, financial influence or proximity to government should provide protection against legitimate investigation and prosecution.”

According to him, the responsibility for protecting national security should not be left exclusively to soldiers, police officers, intelligence operatives and other security personnel.

Political actors, he argued, also had an obligation to preserve the conditions necessary for democratic governance and national stability.

“We cannot continue to behave as though national security is the exclusive responsibility of soldiers, policemen, intelligence officers and other security operatives. Political actors also have a responsibility to preserve the environment in which democracy can function. Their words matter. Their conduct matters. Their influence carries consequences,” he wrote.

Showunmi, however, warned that his call for responsibility and accountability should not be taken as an attempt to suppress opposition, restrict legitimate criticism or criminalise political disagreement.

He acknowledged that dissent, protest, criticism and competing political visions were essential elements of democratic governance.

The Egba-born politician therefore urged the government and security institutions to distinguish legitimate political expression from conduct that crossed the threshold into criminality.

He cautioned that public institutions must avoid amplifying unverified allegations, while deliberately fabricated information intended to provoke violence should be investigated in accordance with the law.

The post Showunmi urges NSA to act against politicians threatening national security appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Tems earns 2027 Grammy nomination for ‘what you need’
description:
Nigerian singer Temilade Openiyi, popularly known as Tems, has been nominated for Best R&B Solo Performance at the 69th Annual Grammy Awards for her song, ‘What You Need’.
Tems will compete in the category with Beyoncé, nominated for ‘Morning Dew (Donk)’; Kehlani, nominated for ‘Out the Window’; Vic
content:
Nigerian singer Temilade Openiyi, popularly known as Tems, has been nominated for Best R&B Solo Performance at the 69th Annual Grammy Awards for her song, ‘What You Need’.

Tems will compete in the category with Beyoncé, nominated for ‘Morning Dew (Donk)’; Kehlani, nominated for ‘Out the Window’; Victoria Monét, nominated for ‘Let Me’; and Jill Scott, nominated for ‘Pressha’.

‘What You Need’ was released on 21 November 2025 as a single from Tems’ extended play, Love Is a Kingdom.

The nomination was announced on Monday during a live YouTube program as the Recording Academy unveiled nominees across 100 categories ahead of the 2027 awards ceremony.

The 69th Grammy Awards will hold on 7 February 2027 at the Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles, California.

Tems is among Nigeria’s most successful Grammy-winning artistes, having won the Best Melodic Rap Performance award in 2023 for her contribution to Future’s ‘Wait for U’, featuring Drake, and Best African Music Performance in 2025 for ‘Love Me JeJe’.

title: China says Xi, Trump, Putin to discuss ‘world peace’ in trilateral
description:
China said on Monday that President Xi Jinping and his US and Russian counterparts Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin would discuss “world peace” when they hold their first trilateral summit in Shenzhen this week.



The three leaders will hold “in-depth exchanges on safeguarding world peace and promot
content:
China said on Monday that President Xi Jinping and his US and Russian counterparts Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin would discuss “world peace” when they hold their first trilateral summit in Shenzhen this week.

The three leaders will hold “in-depth exchanges on safeguarding world peace and promoting strategic stability in major-power relations”, foreign ministry spokeswoman Mao Ning told a news briefing, hours after Beijing confirmed the meeting.

“It will be of ground-breaking significance,” she said.

The trilateral is expected to happen on Thursday on the sidelines of a summit of Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) leaders in the southern Chinese city.

The Kremlin and the White House both previously confirmed the three-way meeting.

Trump wants to talk about reducing nuclear arsenals and is also set to bring up his war in Iran — but he is not expected to discuss Russia’s war in Ukraine, US officials said.

German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier said Xi showed “irritation” in a recent meeting when the idea of the trilateral talks covering Ukraine came up.

“He explicitly pointed out that this is a European conflict, in which the Europeans must also be at the table,” Steinmeier told ARD.

On nuclear disarmament, China has long insisted that the United States and Russia reduce their own giant nuclear arsenals before it agrees to talks on its own stockpile.

title: Oborevwori presents N1.23trn 2027 budget, earmarks 65% for capital projects
description:
From Enweliku Kent, Asaba
Delta State Governor Sheriff Oborevwori, on Monday, presented a proposed N1.23 trillion budget for 2027, with 65 per cent allocated to capital projects.
Tagged “Budget of Sustained Prosperity and Enhanced Growth”, the proposal earmarks N806.8 billion for capital expenditure
content:
From Enweliku Kent, Asaba

Delta State Governor Sheriff Oborevwori, on Monday, presented a proposed N1.23 trillion budget for 2027, with 65 per cent allocated to capital projects.

Tagged “Budget of Sustained Prosperity and Enhanced Growth”, the proposal earmarks N806.8 billion for capital expenditure and N430 billion for recurrent spending.

Presenting the estimates to the State House of Assembly in Asaba, Oborevwori said the budget would consolidate ongoing projects, stimulate economic growth and improve living conditions.

He explained that the proposal was N493.01 billion, or 28.5 per cent, lower than the N1.729 trillion approved for 2026.

The governor said the reduction reflected a deliberate decision to adopt realistic spending projections and strengthen fiscal discipline.

He identified completing ongoing projects, initiating new investments, consolidating achievements and expanding social interventions as the administration’s priorities.

On infrastructure, Oborevwori disclosed that his administration had embarked on 872 road projects and 20 bridges and flyovers since assuming office, adding that the projects covered 2,348 kilometres of roads, alongside 1,871 kilometres of drainage infrastructure across the state.

He said community consultations showed that roads, bridges and jetties remained the most pressing demands, particularly in rural and riverine communities.

Consequently, N320 billion was proposed for the two Ministries of Works to sustain infrastructure development and complete ongoing projects.

On revenue generation, the governor said Delta’s Internally Generated Revenue had grown from N83 billion in 2023 to a projected N283 billion by December 2026.

He attributed the improvement to technology-driven collection, an expanded revenue base and efforts to eliminate leakages without imposing additional tax burdens.

Oborevwori also disclosed that N400 billion of the N463 billion legacy debt had been repaid, leaving N63 billion outstanding. He expressed confidence that the remaining legacy debt would be cleared by the end of the first quarter of 2027.

In the education sector, N74 billion was proposed, comprising N10 billion for primary, N12 billion for technical, N12 billion for secondary and N40 billion for higher education.

The governor said the government would sustain investments in school rehabilitation, teacher development, digital learning, laboratories and accreditation of academic programmes.

He also disclosed that N10.8 billion had been approved for the rehabilitation and renovation of primary and secondary schools.

For healthcare, the proposed N50 billion allocation will support hospital upgrades, medical supplies, recruitment and welfare of health personnel.

Oborevwori highlighted the College of Health Technology, Ovrode, which has enrolled more than 800 pioneer students, as part of efforts to address manpower shortages in the health sector.

Other allocations include N50 billion for the 25 local government areas, N20 billion for the Delta State Capital Territory Development Agency and N20 billion for the Warri-Uvwie and Environs Development Agency.

The budget also provides N12 billion for energy, N10 billion for urban and physical planning, N5 billion for agriculture and N5 billion for social interventions.

On economic diversification, Oborevwori said his administration was attracting private investment into agriculture, industrialisation, entertainment and small and medium-scale enterprises.

He cited the $70 million Olam Agri feed mill project at Ogwashi-Uku as one of the outcomes of the 2026 Delta State Economic and Investment Summit.

The governor said the project would create employment opportunities and provide a ready market for locally produced agricultural commodities.

He further disclosed that Delta’s Gross Domestic Product had risen from N14.5 trillion in 2024 to approximately N17.9 trillion in 2025, making it Nigeria’s fifth-largest state economy.

On electricity, he said the administration had executed 2,155 energy projects, including 90 transformers, 2,003 solar street-lighting projects and 23 power-grid extensions.

The governor also said he had assented to the 13th-month salary bill for public servants, commencing in December 2026, saying the initiative was in recognition of workers’ contributions and an effort to ease their financial responsibilities during the festive season.

On security, Oborevwori said his administration was strengthening collaboration with security agencies to tackle kidnapping, cultism, pipeline vandalism and other criminal activities.

He disclosed that approval had been given for the construction of 25 police divisional headquarters for state police, alongside an application to recruit 1,000 forest guards.

The governor said the 2027 budget would prioritise infrastructure, economic diversification, human capital development, peace and security, while ensuring that ordinary Deltans benefited from economic growth.

He subsequently presented the Appropriation Bill to the lawmakers for consideration and approval. The motion was moved by the House Leader, Hon. Emeka Nwaobi, and seconded by Hon. Marilyn Okowa-Daramola.

Earlier, the Speaker of the House, Rt. Hon. Emomotimi Guwor, commended Oborevwori for his administration’s achievements in infrastructure, healthcare, education, social welfare and human capital development.

Guwor particularly praised the approval of the 13th-month salary, describing it as evidence of the governor’s concern for workers’ welfare.

He reaffirmed the legislature’s commitment to a cordial working relationship with the executive, saying that the House would take the second reading of the bill on Tuesday, November 17, 2026.

The Speaker noted that the cooperation between both arms had contributed to Delta’s development and assured the governor of the Assembly’s support for the budget.

The post Oborevwori presents N1.23trn 2027 budget, earmarks 65% for capital projects appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: FG warns newly promoted correctional officers against inmates’ abuse
description:
….Entrenches performance management system



By Omeiza Ajayi



ABUJA: The Federal Government has warned officers of the Nigerian Correctional Service against abuse of authority and inmates’ rights, insisting that the powers vested in them must be exercised “within the confines of the law, respect
content:
….Entrenches performance management system

By Omeiza Ajayi

ABUJA: The Federal Government has warned officers of the Nigerian Correctional Service against abuse of authority and inmates’ rights, insisting that the powers vested in them must be exercised “within the confines of the law, respect for human dignity and the highest standards of professional conduct.”

Minister of Interior, Hon. Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo, gave the charge on Monday in Abuja at the decoration of 6,207 newly promoted personnel at the service’s National Headquarters in Abuja

Represented by the Permanent Secretary in the ministry, Dr Magdalene Ajani, the minister told the newly promoted controllers that they would now be held responsible for failures in their commands.

“You are not going to be waiting for directives while things are going bad, because you will now be held responsible squarely because you are now management staff.

“We do not imprison people anymore. We bring you in for corrections, we try to reform you and rehabilitate you, and send you back to the society much better than you were when you approached or came to our institution,” she said.

Ajani urged the officers to “play the managerial role of the positions you now occupy,” take initiatives “based on extant rules” and “make sure that problems are solved immediately, you see them.”

Controller General of Corrections, Mr Sylvester Ndidi Nwakuche, announced that the Performance Management System PMS is being institutionalised as the yardstick for future promotions.

Nwakuche said the promotion covered 4,924 senior officers and 1,283 junior officers. Among them, 1,281 Inspectors of Corrections moved to Assistant Superintendents of Corrections II, and 743 Chief Correctional Assistants were converted to Inspector of Corrections after completing the prescribed conversion course.

He said the PMS would change the basis on which officers are judged. “It is a framework that will help us move from merely assessing the time officers have spent in service to objectively evaluating what they have contributed to the achievement of our institutional objectives.

“Let me emphasise that going forward, your performance records, demonstrated competencies, achievement of assigned targets and measurable contributions to the objectives of the Service will constitute major considerations in assessing your suitability for future career progression, in accordance with extant regulations and guidelines. Promotion must increasingly reflect not just how long an officer has served, but also how well that officer has performed,” he said.

The Controller General told the officers to own their appraisals, adding that the PMS should not be regarded as an annual paperwork exercise or something to be attended to only when an appraisal is due. It must become part of our everyday work culture, he said.

On conduct, Nwakuche said: “Never allow your new rank to become a licence for arrogance, intimidation or abuse of authority. Rank should deepen your sense of responsibility, not diminish your respect for others. Our uniform must inspire confidence, our conduct must command respect, and our institutions must reflect the values and aspirations of a modern correctional system.”

Nwakuche thanked President Bola Tinubu for the administration’s support for the service and the Civil Defence, Correctional, Fire and Immigration Services Board (CDCFIB) for facilitating the exercise.

title: Britain’s Prince William In India For Earthshot Prize
description: Britain’s Prince William played street cricket and took a metro ride in India’s financial capital, Mumbai, on Monday ahead of hosting his environmental Earthshot Prize, on a visit that will also include a meeting with Prime Minister Narendra Modi.The future king, accompanied by his wife
content:
Britain’s Prince William played street cricket and took a metro ride in India’s financial capital, Mumbai, on Monday ahead of hosting his environmental Earthshot Prize, on a visit that will also include a meeting with Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

The future king, accompanied by his wife Princess Catherine, took part in India’s beloved game of “gully” cricket with batting legend Sachin Tendulkar in the Ballard Estate area of the city.

The princess, dressed in a lime-green blazer and white trousers, tried her hand at batting before posing for photographs with young local players.

The three-day visit is the first official overseas trip undertaken together by the couple in four years, with Catherine’s cancer diagnosis and treatment limiting international travel.

The royal couple also hopped on for a ride in the city’s metro train to highlight sustainable travel.

“Catherine and I are delighted to be in India for this year’s Earthshot Prize,” the Prince of Wales said in a social media post.

The prize, which supports innovative solutions to the world’s most pressing environmental challenges, selects five winners from 15 finalists in categories covering nature conservation, ocean protection, waste reduction, climate action and clean air.

Each winner will receive £1 million ($1.3 million) at Tuesday night’s ceremony to expand their work.

Hosted by filmmaker Karan Johar, the event is expected to draw Oscar-winning actor Rami Malek and Bollywood stars Alia Bhatt and Sonam Kapoor.

William said that India had “become one of the most exciting places in the world for environmental innovation, with people across the country developing practical solutions to some of the greatest challenges we all share”.

“I am very appreciative that the royal family has taken up such a noble cause,” Tendulkar, international cricket’s all-time leading run-scorer, told reporters.

‘Great challenges’

The clean-air category includes Indian vehicle manufacturer Mahindra Last Mile Mobility, which is expanding its electric three-wheeler business. Other finalists include Uganda’s AirQo, which uses artificial intelligence and pollution monitors to track air quality, and Argentina’s Satellites on Fire, which uses satellite data and artificial intelligence to detect wildfires.

“We know that there are still great challenges but we cannot wait for everyone to agree before we act,” William said at a ceremony where the Earthshot finalists were introduced.

“We all want clean air to breathe, a chance to build good lives… these are not ambitions that divide us, they are ambitions that unite us.”

The seaside city of Mumbai faces persistent air pollution, although it is spared the choking winter smog that engulfs northern India.

New Delhi, where the royal couple will travel on Wednesday, was shrouded in toxic smog on Monday, as vehicle emissions, farm fires and industrial pollution choke the capital.

Readings of cancer-causing PM2.5 fine particles hit 556 micrograms per cubic metre in New Delhi on Monday, according to monitoring organisation IQAir, more than 37 times the World Health Organization’s recommended daily limit.

A 2024 study in The Lancet Planetary Health estimated that fine-particle air pollution was linked to 3.8 million deaths in India between 2009 and 2019, equivalent to five percent of all deaths over that period.

AFP

title: FIFA: Infantino is worse than Blatter — Klopp
description:
By Adegboyega Adeleye



Germany manager Jurgen Klopp has said FIFA president Gianni Infantino is worse than his predecessor, Sepp Blatter, and called for a change in leadership at world football’s governing body.



According to the BBC, Klopp said he had not expected FIFA’s leadership to worsen af
content:
By Adegboyega Adeleye

Germany manager Jurgen Klopp has said FIFA president Gianni Infantino is worse than his predecessor, Sepp Blatter, and called for a change in leadership at world football’s governing body.

According to the BBC, Klopp said he had not expected FIFA’s leadership to worsen after Blatter, but believed Infantino had made it worse.

“I didn’t think things could get worse after Sepp Blatter, but someone has managed to do just that,” Klopp said.

Blatter resigned as FIFA president in 2015 amid a corruption scandal. Infantino succeeded him in February 2016 and plans to seek re-election in March.

Infantino has faced pressure since scrapping his FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal, which included selling stakes in the World Cup and other FIFA competitions to private investors. He apologised to the FIFA Council over the plan, but was told he was not fit to lead the organisation unless he released all the documents and answered key questions.

Klopp said there was broad support for a change at the top of FIFA, adding that the next person to take over could do a better job.

“I’ve been following football for many years. There are people who are much more knowledgeable about this than I am. But I think most people now agree a change would make a lot of sense,” he said.

“Regarding Gianni Infantino, surely the next person to come along can do a better job.”

UEFA has repeatedly called on Infantino to stand down. It has prepared criminal legal proceedings against him and lodged claims in three US courts seeking the release of documents related to the FFE proposal.

Candidates have until Wednesday to confirm they are standing against Infantino in FIFA’s presidential election. Former Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger, FIFA’s head of global development, has ruled himself out, sources told BBC Sport. UEFA is still hoping to find an alternative candidate before the deadline.

Former Tottenham defender Ramon Vega was the first to declare his candidacy in October. Japan Football Association honorary president Kozo Tashima has also announced plans to stand.

Klopp said a candidate without financial interests in football could bring significant improvement to FIFA.

“There are people who truly care about the future of football – people who aren’t driven by financial interests,” he said.

“If someone like that were to step up – if someone like that were to become president – I think that would be a significant improvement.

“There are surely people who care deeply about the future of football and have no financial interests in it.”

title: UPDATED: 2027 opposition parties move to sign pact for democratic renewal
description:
From Ndubuisi Orji, Abuja
A coalition of opposition political parties has said it will sign a Covenant for Democratic Renewal, as part of efforts to unite the opposition ahead of the 2027 general election.
The opposition parties, under the aegis of the Coalition for Democracy, according to a stateme
content:
From Ndubuisi Orji, Abuja

A coalition of opposition political parties has said it will sign a Covenant for Democratic Renewal, as part of efforts to unite the opposition ahead of the 2027 general election.

The opposition parties, under the aegis of the Coalition for Democracy, according to a statement by Salihu Lukman, will sign the pact at the Second Summit of Nigeria’s Opposition Political Parties on November 23 in Abuja.

The coalition, which consists of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Allied Peoples Movement (APM), Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), Peoples Redemption Party (PRP) and Social Democratic Party (SDP), is exploring the possibility of fielding a single opposition presidential candidate in the 2027 polls.

The statement noted that the summit represents the next phase in the collective effort of the participating political parties to build an opposition capable of defending Nigeria’s democracy, restoring public confidence in its institutions and presenting citizens with a credible alternative for national leadership.

“The Summit builds on the foundation laid at the First Summit of Opposition Leaders, convened by the G100 in collaboration with the House of Representatives Minority Caucus at the Yar’Adua Centre, Abuja, on August 31, 2026.

“Since then, Working Groups drawn from the participating political parties have worked diligently to translate our shared convictions into three foundational documents: the National Covenant for Democratic Renewal, the Framework for Opposition Unity, and the National Reform Programme.

“On November 23, the parties will formally receive these documents, adopt them and append their signatures to them. What began as a shared recognition of the challenges confronting our democracy will become a collective commitment to addressing them.

“The Summit comes at a defining moment for Nigeria’s democracy, when the gains of electoral transparency are increasingly under threat and the democratic space continues to narrow under the deliberate actions of the ruling party.

“Democracy cannot thrive where the ruling party seeks to determine not only the outcome of elections, but also the character and composition of the opposition. Nigeria needs a strong, independent and competitive opposition, not as a concession from those in power, but as a fundamental requirement of constitutional democracy,” the coalition stated.

Furthermore, it noted that “in the past, opposition cooperation has too often rested on personal understandings that did not survive the political circumstances that brought them about. This time, we have chosen to build on a different foundation. Opposition parties are putting their commitments in writing, institutionalising our cooperation, and establishing principles that must outlive both the moment and the personalities.

“Our objective is not simply to unite against a ruling party. It is to unite around a vision of the country we want to build and the democratic principles by which we intend to govern. At the Summit, all participating political parties will jointly sign the National Covenant for Democratic Renewal, the Framework for Opposition Unity as a shared commitment to the Nigerian people.”
