title: Police arrest eight after APC, NDC clash in Kano
description:
The Kano State Police Command has arrested eight suspects following a clash between supporters of the All Progressives Congress and the National Democratic Congress in Bichi Local Government Area of the state.
The police said five people sustained injuries while 13 vehicles were vandalised during th
content:
The Kano State Police Command has arrested eight suspects following a clash between supporters of the All Progressives Congress and the National Democratic Congress in Bichi Local Government Area of the state.

The police said five people sustained injuries while 13 vehicles were vandalised during the violence, which occurred at about 4:45 pm on Sunday.

The command disclosed this in a statement issued on Monday by its Public Relations Officer, CSP Abdullahi Haruna Kiyawa.

“The clash also led to the destruction of campaign banners and billboards belonging to the political parties,” the statement said.

It said police teams were immediately deployed to the area after receiving a report of the incident, adding that their intervention restored calm.

“Items recovered from the suspects included one Gariyo, two cutlasses, two hard sticks, a bottle of solution and a substance locally known as ‘Suck and Die’,” the police said.

The five injured persons were taken to hospital, where they were receiving treatment, the statement added.

The Commissioner of Police, Ibrahim Adamu Bakori, condemned the violence and destruction of campaign materials by political supporters, warning that the command would not tolerate activities capable of threatening public peace.

“I’m urging political parties and their supporters to conduct their activities peacefully and in accordance with the law,” the commissioner said.

The statement said the suspects had been transferred to the State Criminal Investigation Department, Bompai, Kano, for investigation and would be charged in court upon its conclusion.

The command urged political leaders, party supporters and residents to shun violence and report suspicious activities to the nearest police station.

It added that the area remained relatively calm, while security monitoring continued.

PUNCH Online earlier on Monday reported that suspected thugs had attacked the convoy of former Kano State Governor, Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, in Bichi Local Government Area of Kano State.

In a post on his verified X account on Monday, the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, Peter Obi, confirmed the incident and said several members of Kwankwaso’s entourage sustained injuries, while about seven vehicles were vandalised.

He described Kwankwaso as his brother and running mate in the 2027 presidential election under the Nigeria Democratic Congress.

“I am deeply saddened by reports of the attack on the convoy of my brother and running mate, Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, and members of his entourage in Bichi Local Government Area of Kano State.

“I strongly condemn this unfortunate incident. Reports indicate that several members of the entourage sustained injuries, while about seven vehicles were vandalised. This is unacceptable and must not be allowed to become part of our political culture,” Obi said.

The former Anambra State governor warned against using political differences as justification for violence, intimidation and destruction of property.

He stressed that every Nigerian had the constitutional right to participate in the democratic process without fear of attack, regardless of political affiliation.

Obi urged the Nigeria Police Force and other security agencies to investigate the incident, identify those responsible, including alleged sponsors, and ensure they were brought to justice.

He also expressed solidarity with Kwankwaso, the Kano State leadership of the NDC, and others affected by the incident, while wishing the injured a speedy recovery.

“Our commitment to building a new Nigeria remains unwavering. We believe that change must come through peaceful engagement, persuasion, ideas and the ballot, not violence.

“Nigeria belongs to all of us. We may belong to different political parties, but we remain one people with a common destiny. No political ambition is worth the life of any Nigerian,” he added.

The post Police arrest eight after APC, NDC clash in Kano appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: FG captures 34m pupils, 700,000 teachers in digitalisation drive
description:
…Deploys technology to track enrolment, tackle out-of-school children



…Unveils digital teacher portal, AI assistant, targets full implementation by 2030



By Joseph Erunke, Abuja



The Federal Government has enrolled more than 34 million learners and 700,000 teachers on its Nigerian Education D
content:
…Deploys technology to track enrolment, tackle out-of-school children

…Unveils digital teacher portal, AI assistant, targets full implementation by 2030

By Joseph Erunke, Abuja

The Federal Government has enrolled more than 34 million learners and 700,000 teachers on its Nigerian Education Data Infrastructure (NEDI), as part of efforts to digitalise the country’s education system, improve planning and tackle the challenge of out-of-school children.

The initiative, which has also captured 340 schools on its database, is expected to strengthen the government’s capacity to monitor school enrolment, track teachers, identify communities with high numbers of out-of-school children and ensure effective distribution of educational resources.

The National Project Coordinator, Special Programmes Operations and Implementation Unit, Office of the Minister of Education, Mr Adebayo Onigbanjo, disclosed this on Monday in Abuja at a news conference ahead of the launch of the National Educational Technology (EdTech) Strategy.

Onigbanjo described NEDI as the data backbone of Nigeria’s education system, saying it would provide reliable and up-to-date information to guide policy decisions, resource allocation and accountability.

He said the initiative was designed to address the country’s longstanding dependence on manual data collection, which often resulted in delayed, fragmented and outdated information, thereby undermining effective education planning.

Under the new arrangement, data will be collected directly from schools through digital devices and uploaded to a central platform, enabling government to access more accurate information on learners, teachers and educational institutions.

Beyond data collection, he said the infrastructure would help identify communities with significant numbers of out-of-school children, monitor enrolment trends and direct government interventions to areas and learners with the greatest needs.

Onigbanjo said the National EdTech Strategy would provide a unified framework for integrating technology into teaching, learning, teacher development, education management, digital infrastructure and governance.

According to him, the strategy reflects the Federal Government’s determination to reposition the education sector and move Nigeria from a resource-based economy towards a knowledge-driven economy through technology-enabled learning.

“The Nigerian National EdTech Strategy represents the Federal Government of Nigeria’s commitment to building a unified, data-driven, and future-ready education system.

“It provides a coherent national framework for integrating technology across teaching, learning, education management, teacher development, digital infrastructure, and governance.

“It ensures that investments in education technology translate into improved learning outcomes and greater equity across the country,” he said.

He identified five major pillars of the strategy as data and interoperability, digital infrastructure, technology and procurement, teacher transformation, and governance and coordination.

He explained that the data and interoperability component would establish common standards to enable existing education technology platforms to exchange information seamlessly, while ensuring the protection of personal records in line with the Nigerian Data Protection Act.

On digital infrastructure, he said the government would prioritise reliable electricity, broadband connectivity and access to digital devices, particularly in rural and underserved communities where inadequate facilities continue to widen the digital divide.

The strategy, he added, would also strengthen teacher development through standards for digital competencies, certification and career progression under the National Teachers Digital Competency Framework (NTDCF).

To drive the process, Onigbanjo disclosed plans to establish a National Teacher Professional Development Portal, which would provide teachers with online, offline and blended learning opportunities to improve their digital skills and classroom delivery.

He also announced the introduction of AskFM, a digital assistant designed to provide parents, students, teachers, educational institutions and members of the public with information on the Ministry of Education’s policies, programmes and services.

On the deployment of artificial intelligence, the coordinator said the government would adopt a responsible approach, focusing on digital literacy, teacher development and controlled pilot programmes rather than unrestricted use of emerging technologies.

He stressed that data privacy, child protection and human oversight would remain non-negotiable in implementing the strategy.

Onigbanjo said implementation would be phased, beginning with mobilisation in late 2026 and 2027, followed by expansion, optimisation and sustainability measures up to 2030.

He listed the immediate priorities to include strengthening NEDI and expanding its interfaces, identifying infrastructure gaps in schools, commencing implementation of the teachers’ digital competency framework, establishing governance structures and formalising implementation arrangements with participating states.

“Our immediate priorities are clear: put the governance arrangements in place, strengthen NEDI and extend its priority interfaces, map school infrastructure gaps, launch NTDCF implementation, formalise arrangements with participating States, and mobilise our partners.

“Implementation will be phased. We will mobilise in late 2026 and 2027, scale up thereafter, and focus on optimisation and sustainability through 2030,” he said.

He said the strategy was developed through collaboration involving the Federal Ministry of Communications, Innovation and Digital Economy, state governments, development partners, the private sector, academia and civil society.

He acknowledged the contributions of the Mastercard Foundation and the World Bank to the development of the initiative.

The Federal Government expressed optimism that the coordinated deployment of digital infrastructure, reliable education data, teacher capacity development and emerging technologies would improve learning outcomes, strengthen accountability and expand access to quality education across the country.

The post FG captures 34m pupils, 700,000 teachers in digitalisation drive appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Onanuga accuses Kwankwaso of urging weapon-making
description:
Bayo Onanuga, Special Adviser to President Bola Tinubu on Information and Strategy, has accused former Kano State Governor, Rabiu Kwankwaso, of allegedly urging his supporters to improvise weapons ahead of the 2027 general elections.







Onanuga made the allegation in a post on his X platform on
content:
Bayo Onanuga, Special Adviser to President Bola Tinubu on Information and Strategy, has accused former Kano State Governor, Rabiu Kwankwaso, of allegedly urging his supporters to improvise weapons ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Onanuga made the allegation in a post on his X platform on Monday, following Kwankwaso’s address at a rally in Bichi, Kano State, on Sunday.

According to Onanuga, Kwankwaso told supporters: “Continue to stay prepared; do not go easy on these shameless people.”

He further alleged that the former governor encouraged his supporters to improvise dangerous weapons, describing the reported remarks as a cause for concern ahead of the 2027 elections.

Onanuga said political leaders should use their influence to promote restraint, tolerance and peaceful engagement rather than make statements that could be interpreted as encouraging confrontation among supporters.

He noted that Kano was politically sensitive, warning that inflammatory political rhetoric could heighten tensions between rival camps.

Reacting to the alleged remarks, a human rights activist, Comrade Musa Bala Gaye, called on security agencies to intervene and address what he described as a threat to peace in the state.

Gaye said the 2027 general elections were expected to attract intense political competition but insisted that campaigns should focus on policies, ideas and alternative visions of governance rather than preparations for violence.

He also raised concerns about the responsibility of political leaders to discourage thuggery and protect residents from possible clashes involving rival supporters.

The activist maintained that political disagreements were part of democratic competition but said any encouragement of supporters to improvise dangerous weapons would undermine peaceful political participation.

He urged political leaders to clarify controversial statements and demonstrate commitment to peaceful campaigns ahead of the elections.

The allegations have drawn attention to the need for restraint in political mobilisation, particularly as parties and their supporters begin preparations for the 2027 polls.

title: French Actor Depardieu Drops Appeal For Sexual Assault Conviction
description: French screen icon Gerard Depardieu on Monday formally dropped his appeal against a conviction for sexually assaulting two women during the filming of a movie in 2021.A court last year handed the 77-year-old an 18-month suspended sentence and ordered him to register as a sex offender, marking a spec
content:
French screen icon Gerard Depardieu on Monday formally dropped his appeal against a conviction for sexually assaulting two women during the filming of a movie in 2021.

A court last year handed the 77-year-old an 18-month suspended sentence and ordered him to register as a sex offender, marking a spectacular fall from grace for an actor who dominated French cinema for half a century.

Depardieu, who has acted in more than 200 films and television series, is the highest-profile figure caught up in France’s response to the #MeToo movement.

The trial related to charges of sexual assault during the filming in 2021 of “Les Volets Verts” (“The Green Shutters”) by director Jean Becker.

Depardieu’s withdrawal was lodged at the start of the appeal trial on Monday, bringing it to an end and rendering the original judgment final.

“Justice has spoken. I was found guilty. I hear it, and I accept this conviction,” Depardieu said in a statement sent to AFP shortly before the hearing began.

At the start of the hearing, the prosecutor and the civil parties also withdrew their appeals.

“For a long time on film sets, I hid behind provocation and ribald humour,” Depardieu said, acknowledging that his remarks and “some of my gestures” were not “without consequences.”

He offered his “deep and sincere apologies” to those who “may have suffered as a result.”

The actor said he had never intended to hurt the women he encountered, but added that he had “come to understand that intention changes nothing about the harm caused.”

“Court proceedings damage us,” added the actor.

The plaintiffs were a set dresser and an assistant director. Depardieu has denied the allegations.

In another case, a French investigating judge in 2025 ordered Depardieu to stand trial on charges of raping actor Charlotte Arnould in 2018. He has denied those charges and is appealing.

title: NANS tells NDLEA to halt N10,000 drug test fee
description:
…Warns against turning students into revenue sources



By Adeola Badru



The National Association of Nigerian Students (NANS) has urged the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) to immediately suspend the alleged N10,000 drug testing fee imposed on students, describing the charge as exploit
content:
…Warns against turning students into revenue sources

By Adeola Badru

The National Association of Nigerian Students (NANS) has urged the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) to immediately suspend the alleged N10,000 drug testing fee imposed on students, describing the charge as exploitative and an additional burden on families struggling with economic hardship.

The association specifically called on the NDLEA Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, Brigadier-General Mohamed Buba Marwa (retd.), to stop the enforcement and collection of the fee, arguing that students should not bear the financial cost of an initiative introduced by a government agency.

NANS, in a statement issued on Monday and signed by its President, Akinteye Babatunde Afeez, said it was unacceptable for a government agency to turn students into revenue sources through a programme purportedly designed to promote drug-free educational institutions.

While expressing support for genuine efforts to combat drug abuse and promote safer campuses, the association insisted that such initiatives must not come at the expense of students’ welfare.

“While we are not opposed to drug testing, the promotion of drug-free institutions or any genuine effort aimed at addressing drug abuse among students, we stand fiercely opposed to any attempt to transfer the financial burden of such exercises to Nigerian students, particularly when the initiative is being driven by the Agency itself and students have not independently requested these tests,” the statement said.

The student body expressed concern that the proposed charge would worsen the financial difficulties confronting students, who are already grappling with rising tuition fees, increasing living costs and other economic pressures.

“It is disheartening to see government agencies turn students into business ventures, exploit them and impose additional financial burdens on Nigerian students despite the government’s various interventions and policies aimed at making education accessible and improving students’ welfare,” it added.

NANS maintained that government agencies should fund programmes initiated in the discharge of their statutory responsibilities rather than transfer the financial burden to students.

It urged Marwa to intervene without delay and direct an immediate halt to the collection of the N10,000 fee, warning that it would resist any policy capable of subjecting students to avoidable financial exploitation.

“If the Agency must carry out its official responsibilities, it must do so without imposing any financial burden on Nigerian students.

“Charging students for an exercise initiated by the Agency itself is utterly unacceptable, and we therefore demand that the Chairman and Chief Executive Officer immediately halt this practice,” the association declared.

NANS further argued that students’ welfare should not become a revenue-generating opportunity for government institutions, particularly when many Nigerian families are struggling to meet the cost of education.

Reaffirming its support for initiatives aimed at creating safer learning environments and discouraging substance abuse among young people, the association said its objection was to the financial implications of the alleged policy and not the broader objective of tackling drug abuse.

It vowed to continue defending students’ interests and opposing measures that could impose additional financial pressure on them.

“As the apex student representative body, we stand firmly for affordable education and the protection of students’ welfare. We shall not fold our arms and watch students being subjected to avoidable financial exploitation,” it said.

The association urged the NDLEA leadership to prioritise students’ welfare and ensure that efforts to promote drug-free educational institutions did not become another source of financial hardship for Nigerian students.

title: Photos: Don’t allow ADC, NDC score 25% in FCT, Wike tells Rainbow Coalition
description:
By Omeiza Ajayi – ABUJA 



Minister of the Federal Capital Territory FCT, Nyesom Wike, has told members of the Rainbow Coalition to make sure the African Democratic Congress ADC and the Nigeria Democratic Congress NDC do not get 25 per cent of the votes in the FCT in the January 16, 2027 general el
content:
By Omeiza Ajayi – ABUJA

Minister of the Federal Capital Territory FCT, Nyesom Wike, has told members of the Rainbow Coalition to make sure the African Democratic Congress ADC and the Nigeria Democratic Congress NDC do not get 25 per cent of the votes in the FCT in the January 16, 2027 general election.

Wike, coordinator of the FCT Presidential Campaign Council, spoke on Monday in Abuja at the inauguration of the All Progressives Congress APC Presidential Campaign Council/Rainbow Coalition FCT.

He warned the members against assuming the contest was already won, saying the election was a chance for the APC to show its political strength in the territory.

On how to sell the president’s record, he said;”You don’t need to go and see a prophet. You don’t need to go and see any doctor or anybody to tell you what to do. It is obvious; it is factual. Look at what Mr President has done for the people of the FCT. These are the tools you need to campaign”.

The minister disclosed that between 1999 and 2023, successive governments issued only about 7,000 to 8,000 Certificates of Occupancy (C of O), against more than 20,000 under President Bola Tinubu in three years.

“How can governments from 1999 to 2023 sign only about 8,000 C of Os, while the government of 2023 to 2026, in three years, has signed over 20,000? How?” he queried.

Wike also dared opposition politicians to set projects built before 2023 beside those delivered since Tinubu took office, arguing that the work going on in the city centre and the satellite towns spoke for itself.

On political inclusion, he said 50 years after Abuja was created in 1976, Tinubu is the first president to give the FCT a seat at the Federal Executive Council, so that the territory is no longer only the nation’s administrative capital but has a say in national decisions.

He listed the FCT Civil Service Commission, the appointment of a Head of Service, the promotion of FCT civil servants to permanent secretary rank, and the Mandate Secretariats for Women Affairs and Youth Development among the gains. He added that taking the FCT out of the Treasury Single Account arrangement now allows it to borrow for major infrastructure.

The minister urged council members to carry this record to wards, communities and polling units, especially in the satellite towns, where residents can see the projects for themselves.

The FCT APC Chairman, Ishaku Tanko Yamawo, said the party was set for an overwhelming win for Tinubu and its National Assembly candidates, and called the minister’s projects the party’s best asset.

“Your projects have already become our strongest campaign message. The goodwill and confidence you have earned among our people, both indigenes and residents of the FCT, are exceptional,” Yamawo told Wike.

He praised the Rainbow Coalition for bringing different political interests under one roof and urged members to work as a team so that the APC’s message reaches every ward and polling unit.

The FCT Peoples Democratic Party PDP Chairman, Ismaila Mohammed Dogara, said the structure Wike built could keep mobilising voters even if the minister is not in the territory on election day.

“Even if you are not in the FCT, our executive chairman does not allow any space, not even for one minute, before taking it from where you stopped. That shows that on the faithful day of the election, if the Honourable Minister is not in the FCT, those leaders are ready and capable of delivering Mr President, Senator Philip Aduda, Tanimu and others,” Dogara said.

He described the working relationship between APC and PDP leaders in the coalition as a significant political development.

“The big day is January 16, and the return day is January 17. By the special grace of God, we are going to return to this hall to celebrate,” he declared.

The post Photos: Don’t allow ADC, NDC score 25% in FCT, Wike tells Rainbow Coalition appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Obi highlights ANIDS, development initiatives in 10-day record of service
description:
Former Anambra State Governor and Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) presidential candidate, Peter Obi, has highlighted the development initiatives and governance framework introduced by his administration, as he begins a 10-day presentation of his achievements in office.







Obi, in a post on his
content:
Former Anambra State Governor and Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) presidential candidate, Peter Obi, has highlighted the development initiatives and governance framework introduced by his administration, as he begins a 10-day presentation of his achievements in office.

Obi, in a post on his X platform on Monday titled Nigerians, Go and Verify (1), said his administration was built on transparency, prudence, accountability and measurable results.

In the first instalment of the series, tagged Introduction: Governance as a Public Trust, the former governor said Anambra was at a critical point when he assumed office, with weak public institutions and governance that had become increasingly disconnected from the people.

He said his administration recognised the need to move away from established practices and redefine governance as a public trust dedicated to improving the living conditions of ordinary citizens.

According to him, the administration’s governing philosophy was anchored on four principles: character, competence, capacity and compassion.

Obi said leadership, in his view, was not about personal recognition, political slogans or self-promotion but about translating public resources into tangible benefits for the people.

He explained that one of the first challenges identified by his administration was the absence of a unified development plan to guide government priorities and resource allocation.

To address this, he said his administration established the Ministry of Economic Planning to provide an institutional framework for coordinated and sustainable development.

Following groundwork and consultations, his government introduced the Anambra Integrated Development Strategy (ANIDS), which became the overarching framework for its development agenda.

Obi said ANIDS was designed to adapt the eight Millennium Development Goals (MDGs) to the peculiar circumstances and development needs of Anambra State.

The goals included eradicating extreme poverty and hunger, achieving universal primary education, promoting gender equality, reducing child mortality, improving maternal health, combating HIV/AIDS and other diseases, ensuring environmental sustainability and strengthening global partnerships for development.

He said his administration sought to translate the international development objectives into practical policies, programmes and measurable outcomes that would improve the lives of residents.

The former governor also recalled that his administration redefined the state’s public identity, changing its slogan from “Home for All” to “The Light of the Nation”.

He explained that the change was intended to restore public confidence in government, strengthen civic pride and position Anambra as a model of purposeful leadership and development.

Under a section titled The ANIDS Blueprint: A Comprehensive Framework for Development, Obi said his administration rejected an approach that prioritised one sector at the expense of others.

He argued that education, healthcare, infrastructure, security, agriculture and effective public institutions were interconnected and required balanced attention to achieve sustainable development.

According to him, progress in one sector could not be sustained without corresponding improvements in other areas, making comprehensive planning and prudent management of public resources essential.

Obi added that restoring the dignity of the Anambra person was central to his administration’s vision.

He said such dignity could be measured not by political rhetoric but by the condition of roads and other infrastructure, access to healthcare, quality of education, performance of public institutions and the treatment of workers, pensioners and traditional institutions.

The former governor’s latest publication is the first in the 10-day Record of Service series he announced on Monday, through which he said he would present his administration’s interventions and accomplishments for public scrutiny.

title: JUST IN: Headline inflation falls to 14.06% in October
description:

The NBS disclosed this on Monday in its latest Consumer Price Index (CPI) report.

content:
Nigeria’s headline inflation rate declined to 14.06 per cent in October 2026, down from 14.63 per cent recorded in September, according to the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS).

The NBS disclosed this on Monday in its latest Consumer Price Index (CPI) report.

The report also showed that food inflation dropped to 19.13 per cent in October from 19.59 per cent in the previous month.

“In October 2026, the headline inflation rate stood at 14.06%, down from 14.63% in September 2026, and stood at 18.97% in the same month of the preceding year (October 2025).

“Looking at the movement, the October 2026 headline inflation rate showed a decrease of 4.9% compared to the October 2025 (18.97%) headline inflation rate.

“On a month-on-month basis, the headline inflation rate in October 2026 was 0.43%, which was 0.38% higher than the rate recorded in September 2026 (0.06%).

“This means that in October 2026, the rate of increase in the average price level was higher than the rate of increase

in the average price level in September 2026.”

Details later

title: ADC, NDC Must Not Secure 25% Votes In FCT, Wike Charges APC FCT Campaign Council
description: The Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Barr. Nyesom Wike, has charged members of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council and the Rainbow Coalition to ensure that opposition parties, particularly the African Democratic Congress (ADC) and the Nigeria Democratic
content:
The Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Barr. Nyesom Wike, has charged members of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council and the Rainbow Coalition to ensure that opposition parties, particularly the African Democratic Congress (ADC) and the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), do not secure 25 per cent of the votes in the FCT during the January 16, 2027 general election.

Wike gave the charge on Monday in Abuja during the inauguration of the APC Presidential Campaign Council/Rainbow Coalition FCT at the Bola Ahmed Tinubu International Conference Centre, where he urged members to intensify grassroots mobilisation and take the achievements of President Bola Tinubu’s administration to voters across the six area councils.

The minister, who is the coordinator of the FCT Presidential Campaign Council, said the forthcoming election presented an opportunity for the APC to demonstrate its political strength in the territory, insisting that members must not take victory for granted.

He challenged campaign council members to move beyond political rhetoric and present verifiable evidence of the achievements of the Tinubu administration, particularly in infrastructure, institutional reforms and policies designed to improve governance in the FCT.

“You don’t need to go and see a prophet. You don’t need to go and see any doctor or anybody to tell you what to do. It is obvious; it is factual. Look at what Mr President has done for the people of the FCT. These are the tools you need to campaign,” Wike said.

The minister argued that President Tinubu had demonstrated an unprecedented commitment to the development and political inclusion of the FCT, noting that several institutional reforms introduced by the administration had addressed longstanding demands of residents and indigenous communities.

According to him, 50 years after the creation of Abuja in 1976, Tinubu became the first president to ensure that the FCT was represented at the Federal Executive Council, where major national policies and decisions affecting the country are made.

He said the decision reflected a recognition that the FCT should not merely serve as the nation’s administrative capital but should also have a voice in national governance.

Wike further listed the establishment of the FCT Civil Service Commission, the appointment of a Head of Service and the elevation of FCT civil servants to permanent secretary positions as major milestones under the Tinubu administration.

He also highlighted the creation of the Mandate Secretariats for Women Affairs and Youth Development, saying the initiative had provided platforms for women and young people to participate more meaningfully in governance and channel their concerns to government.

The minister said the administration had also granted the FCT greater financial independence through its removal from the Treasury Single Account arrangement, enabling it to access loans to finance critical infrastructure projects.

On infrastructure, Wike challenged opposition politicians to compare projects executed under previous administrations with those delivered since Tinubu assumed office in 2023.

He maintained that the scale of ongoing projects across the city centre and satellite communities provided sufficient evidence of the president’s commitment to the territory.

Wike particularly cited the administration’s record in the issuance of Certificates of Occupancy (C of O), claiming that while previous administrations between 1999 and 2023 issued about 7,000 to 8,000 certificates, the Tinubu administration had issued more than 20,000 within three years.

“How can governments from 1999 to 2023 sign only about 8,000 C of Os, while the government of 2023 to 2026, in three years, has signed over 20,000? How?” he queried.

He urged campaign council members to take the message of the administration’s achievements to communities, wards and polling units, particularly in the satellite towns, where residents could assess the impact of government projects.

Earlier, the FCT APC Chairman, Ishaku Tanko Yamawo, expressed confidence that the party would secure an overwhelming victory for Tinubu and its National Assembly candidates in the forthcoming elections.

Yamawo described the infrastructure transformation under Wike as a major campaign advantage, saying the projects had strengthened public confidence in the APC-led administration.

“Your projects have already become our strongest campaign message. The goodwill and confidence you have earned among our people, both indigenes and residents of the FCT, are exceptional,” he told the minister.

He also commended the Rainbow Coalition for bringing political interests together, stressing that the alliance would strengthen the party’s mobilisation capacity across the six area councils.

Yamawo urged members of the campaign council to work as a united team, maintain effective coordination and ensure that the APC’s message reached every ward and polling unit.

Also speaking, the FCT PDP Chairman, Ismaila Mohammed Dogara, expressed confidence in the capacity of political leaders and stakeholders in the territory to mobilise support for Tinubu and other endorsed candidates, even in Wike’s absence.

Dogara commended the minister for building a strong political structure capable of sustaining mobilisation and coordinating electoral activities without his physical presence.

He described the cooperation between APC and PDP leaders under the Rainbow Coalition as a significant political development, expressing optimism that the alliance would translate into victory at the polls.

“Even if you are not in the FCT, our executive chairman does not allow any space, not even for one minute, before taking it from where you stopped. That shows that on the faithful day of the election, if the Honourable Minister is not in the FCT, those leaders are ready and capable of delivering Mr President, Senator Philip Aduda, Tanimu and others,” Dogara said.

He expressed confidence that members of the coalition would return to the conference centre on January 17, a day after the election, to celebrate their anticipated victory.

“The big day is January 16, and the return day is January 17. By the special grace of God, we are going to return to this hall to celebrate,” he declared.

The post ADC, NDC Must Not Secure 25% Votes In FCT, Wike Charges APC FCT Campaign Council appeared first on Channels Television.

title: 2027: Court dismisses suit seeking to bar Aondoakaa from Benue governorship race
description:
From Godwin Tsa, Abuja
A Federal High Court in Abuja on Monday dismissed a suit by four Benue State indigenes seeking to stop former Attorney-General of the Federation, Michael Aondoakaa, from contesting the 2027 governorship election in the state.
Delivering judgment, Justice Joyce Abdulmalik held
content:
From Godwin Tsa, Abuja

A Federal High Court in Abuja on Monday dismissed a suit by four Benue State indigenes seeking to stop former Attorney-General of the Federation, Michael Aondoakaa, from contesting the 2027 governorship election in the state.

Delivering judgment, Justice Joyce Abdulmalik held that the plaintiffs lacked the locus standi to institute the action.

She upheld the preliminary objection raised by the defendants and ruled that the suit was statute-barred and was, in substance, a pre-election matter dressed up as a judgment enforcement action.

The judge said the suit was filed outside the mandatory 14-day window. She rejected the plaintiffs’ argument that they only became aware of Mr Aondoakaa’s nomination by the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) on August 30, 2026.

“The evidence before the court clearly showed that the third defendant was declared winner on June 24, 2026, and presented with a certificate of return on June 26, 2026,” she said. “This suit, having been filed outside the mandatory 14 days, is statute-barred and is dismissed in its entirety.”

On locus standi, Justice Abdulmalik held that the plaintiffs, who described themselves as registered voters in Benue, could not import themselves into matters of public interest litigation.

She also agreed with the defence that, given the nature of the reliefs sought, the suit was a pre-election matter. Since the plaintiffs were not candidates in the PDP governorship primary, she said, they had no standing to challenge its outcome.

The judge further held that the plaintiffs were not parties to Aondoakaa v. Obot, the case whose judgment they sought to enforce, and had failed to place material evidence before the court to justify the reliefs sought.

The plaintiffs, David Ejembi, Aondoaver Teryila, Joseph Okpanachi and Benedict Orkume, filed the suit, marked FHC/ABJ/CS/2152/2026, against the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), the PDP and Mr Aondoakaa, the party’s governorship candidate.

Led by Fredricks Itula, SAN, they relied on the Supreme Court judgment in Aondoakaa v. Obot (2022) 5 NWLR (Pt. 1824) 523, which they argued bars Mr Aondoakaa from holding any public office. They contended that, under sections 235 and 287(1) of the Constitution, read with the definition of “public office of a state” in Section 318(1), INEC and the PDP were constitutionally bound to comply with that judgment.

They asked the court to:

* declare that INEC is obliged to obey the Supreme Court judgment by preventing the PDP from sponsoring Mr Aondoakaa in the 2027 poll;
* declare that the PDP is obliged to comply by withdrawing his candidature;
* issue a perpetual injunction restraining INEC from allowing the PDP to sponsor him; and
* issue a perpetual injunction restraining Mr Aondoakaa from contesting the election.

The defence

Mr Aondoakaa’s legal team, led by Prof. Anthony Ijohor, SAN, urged the court to dismiss the suit in limine as incompetent, on the following grounds:

* Defective counter-affidavit: The plaintiffs’ counter-affidavit to the objection was documentary hearsay, based on information from a lawyer in the same firm. Neither deponent had first-hand knowledge of the facts or was a party to the suit. The defence argued that the offending paragraphs should be struck out or discountenanced, citing Salini Nig. Ltd v. Lifewire Industries (2019) and Andrew v. INEC (2018).

* Disguised pre-election matter: The defence rejected the claim that the PDP was approbating and reprobating, insisting that the plaintiffs’ own label did not determine the true nature of the suit. It added that a fresh action could not be used to enforce a final judgment (AMCON v. Capital Oil & Gas, 2019), and that the suit was an abuse of process.

* No locus standi or cause of action: The suit challenged an election yet to hold and was therefore premature, hypothetical and speculative (Wabara v. Nnadede, 2009). The plaintiffs were neither aspirants in the primary nor judgment creditors in Aondoakaa v. Obot, and had shown no special interest or injury.

* Constitutional limits: Section 182 of the Constitution exhaustively lists the grounds for disqualification, so the court could not direct INEC to restrain the PDP from sponsoring a candidate. Sponsorship, the defence added, is the party’s internal affair.

* No right to enforce the judgment: Only a judgment creditor may enforce a judgment against a judgment debtor (Oviawe v. Igiebor, 2021; Access Bank v. Ikpon, 2025). A non-party would need leave of court and substitution under Order IV Rule 2 of the Judgment (Enforcement) Rules. The plaintiffs held no certificate of judgment (sections 104 and 107, Sheriffs and Civil Process Act), had no leave, and had no privity, since Aondoakaa v. Obot is a judgment in personam. The defence described them as “busybodies and meddlesome interlopers”.

The post 2027: Court dismisses suit seeking to bar Aondoakaa from Benue governorship race appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: 2027: Bayelsa West APC leaders unite, back Tinubu
description:
By Samuel Oyadongha, Yenagoa



Political leaders and key stakeholders of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Sagbama and Ekeremor Local Government Areas of Bayelsa West Senatorial District have resolved to set aside internal differences and work together to secure victory for President Bola Tinu
content:
By Samuel Oyadongha, Yenagoa

Political leaders and key stakeholders of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Sagbama and Ekeremor Local Government Areas of Bayelsa West Senatorial District have resolved to set aside internal differences and work together to secure victory for President Bola Tinubu and other party candidates in the 2027 general elections.

The resolution was reached at an expanded stakeholders’ meeting convened by the Deputy Governor of Bayelsa State, Dr Peter Akpe, and the Minister of State for Petroleum Resources (Oil), Senator Heineken Lokpobiri.

The meeting, attended by party leaders and members across the senatorial district, ended with a unanimous commitment to abandon internal acrimony and present a united front in the forthcoming elections.

Addressing the gathering, Akpe urged APC members to put aside grievances arising from the emergence of party candidates and concentrate on strengthening the party ahead of the elections.

He warned that opposition parties were strategising to secure simple majorities across states and urged APC members to remain vigilant and committed to the party’s electoral objectives.

“No political parties should be allowed to score 25 per cent,” the deputy governor declared.

Also speaking, Lokpobiri urged APC members in Bayelsa West to mobilise massive support for Tinubu and other party candidates, recalling that Sagbama had historically delivered substantial votes during the days of the old Rivers State.

He challenged the people of the senatorial district to replicate that voting pattern in 2027 by turning out massively for the APC.

The minister also called for unity among party members, warning against alleged double allegiance and political disloyalty.

“If you are in APC by the day and be in the NDC at night, you will be caught in the middle. No one will trust you,” he warned.

Lokpobiri expressed confidence in the APC’s electoral prospects, arguing that the party was more actively engaged in political campaigns than its opponents.

“If you are a good observer, you will know that APC will win. The only party campaigning is the APC. The opposition are holding town hall meetings. The issue of the APC winning is not in doubt,” he said.

The minister also revisited the power rotation arrangement between Ekeremor and Sagbama in the representation of Bayelsa West Senatorial District, insisting that political agreements should be respected.

He recalled that in 2015, he declined to seek a third term in the Senate in deference to the rotation arrangement.

“Due to the issue of power rotation, I did not bother to seek a third term in the Senate,” he said, recalling that former Governor Seriake Dickson had appealed to him to step aside in the interest of unity.

Lokpobiri further recalled that the APC did not support Peremobowei Ebebi’s senatorial ambition in the subsequent election because the arrangement between the two local government areas was still in force, but backed him for a second term in 2023.

He accused Ebebi of reneging on the understanding, questioning his credibility over the alleged failure to honour the agreement.

“For him to insist on going for second term, he is a man that lacks credibility. How can he be a man of credibility? He agreed and reneged,” Lokpobiri stated.

The post 2027: Bayelsa West APC leaders unite, back Tinubu appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: 2027: Atiku, Obi, Makinde set for second meeting in unified move against APC
description: Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, former Anambra State Governor Peter Obi and Oyo State Governor Seyi Makinde are among opposition leaders expected to meet in Abuja on November 23 to sign a pact aimed at strengthening opposition unity and defending Nigeria’s democracy ahead of the 2027 general e
content:
Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, former Anambra State Governor Peter Obi and Oyo State Governor Seyi Makinde are among opposition leaders expected to meet in Abuja on November 23 to sign a pact aimed at strengthening opposition unity and defending Nigeria’s democracy ahead of the 2027 general election.

The Coalition for Democracy disclosed this on Monday in a statement signed by Salihu Moh. Lukman on behalf of the coalition parties.

The meeting, which will be the Second Summit of Nigeria’s Opposition Political Parties, is expected to culminate in the adoption and signing of a Covenant for Democratic Renewal by participating political parties.

Atiku represents the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Obi is the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), while Makinde is associated with the Allied Peoples Movement (APM).

According to the coalition, the summit will mark a major step towards building a united, credible and purposeful opposition capable of providing an alternative to the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC).

The meeting follows the First Summit of Opposition Leaders, organised by the G100 in collaboration with the House of Representatives Minority Caucus at the Yar’Adua Centre, Abuja, on August 31, 2026.

The coalition said working groups established after the first summit had prepared three documents to guide the proposed alliance: the National Covenant for Democratic Renewal, the Framework for Opposition Unity and the National Reform Programme.

“On November 23, the parties will formally receive these documents, adopt them and append their signatures to them. What began as a shared recognition of the challenges confronting our democracy will become a collective commitment to addressing them,” the statement said.

The coalition expressed concern over what it described as growing threats to electoral transparency and shrinking democratic space, accusing the ruling party of actions that could weaken opposition politics.

It argued that Nigeria needed a strong and independent opposition, insisting that a competitive multiparty system was essential to constitutional democracy.

Explaining why the latest initiative would be different from previous opposition alliances, the coalition said its members had chosen to formalise their commitments rather than rely on personal agreements.

“In the past, opposition cooperation has too often rested on personal understandings that did not survive the political circumstances that brought them about. This time, we have chosen to build on a different foundation.

“Opposition parties are putting their commitments in writing, institutionalising our cooperation, and establishing principles that must outlive both the moment and the personalities,” it said.

The coalition identified the protection of votes at polling units nationwide as its first common national undertaking, stressing that all Nigerians must be allowed to choose their leaders freely.

It also placed emphasis on the physical attendance of presidential candidates and their running mates at the summit, saying they would be expected to publicly affirm their commitment to democratic principles.

A special session will feature goodwill remarks by the candidates, providing an opportunity for them to demonstrate their willingness to work together in the national interest.

The summit is expected to attract national chairmen and secretaries of participating parties, members of their National Working Committees and Presidential Campaign Councils, as well as members of the National Assembly, civil society organisations, diplomats and media representatives.

The Alaago of Kajola Alago, Ileshan, Oba Oladipo Olaitan, and Professor Ango Abdullahi are among the statesmen invited to deliver addresses on the theme, “The Doctrine of a Necessary Democratic Opposition”.

The Coalition for Democracy is a multiparty platform involving the ADC, APM, NDC, Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), Peoples Redemption Party (PRP) and Social Democratic Party (SDP).

The coalition said its doors remained open to other political parties willing to commit to democratic renewal, constitutional governance, electoral integrity and national reform.

It added that the summit would end with a group photograph of opposition leaders, describing the gathering as a transition from consultations to a formal commitment to collective action.

The post 2027: Atiku, Obi, Makinde set for second meeting in unified move against APC appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: 2027: Trouble for Tinubu as Atiku, Obi, Makinde, other opposition leaders holds fresh unity summit November 23
description: Opposition presidential candidates, including Atiku Abubakar of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Peter Obi of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) and Seyi Makinde of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), are expected to converge in Abuja on Monday, November 23, for the signing of a Covenant for
content:
Opposition presidential candidates, including Atiku Abubakar of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Peter Obi of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) and Seyi Makinde of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), are expected to converge in Abuja on Monday, November 23, for the signing of a Covenant for Democratic Renewal.

The Coalition for Democracy announced this on Monday in Abuja in a statement signed by Salihu Moh. Lukman on behalf of the coalition parties.

According to the statement, the Second Summit of Nigeria’s Opposition Political Parties will provide an opportunity for participating parties to formally adopt and sign the proposed agreement.

The coalition described the move as “a decisive step towards a united, credible and purposeful democratic opposition.”

The summit follows the First Summit of Opposition Leaders, convened by the G100 in collaboration with the House of Representatives Minority Caucus at the Yar’Adua Centre, Abuja, on August 31, 2026.

The coalition said working groups drawn from the participating parties had since “worked diligently to translate our shared convictions into three foundational documents: the National Covenant for Democratic Renewal, the Framework for Opposition Unity, and the National Reform Programme.”

“On November 23, the parties will formally receive these documents, adopt them and append their signatures to them. What began as a shared recognition of the challenges confronting our democracy will become a collective commitment to addressing them,” the statement said.

The coalition said the summit was coming “at a defining moment for Nigeria’s democracy, when the gains of electoral transparency are increasingly under threat and the democratic space continues to narrow under the deliberate actions of the ruling party.

“Democracy cannot thrive where the ruling party seeks to determine not only the outcome of elections, but also the character and composition of the opposition. Nigeria needs a strong, independent and competitive opposition, not as a concession from those in power, but as a fundamental requirement of constitutional democracy,” it said.

On why this effort should be different, the statement said: “In the past, opposition cooperation has too often rested on personal understandings that did not survive the political circumstances that brought them about. This time, we have chosen to build on a different foundation.

“Opposition parties are putting their commitments in writing, institutionalising our cooperation, and establishing principles that must outlive both the moment and the personalities,” it added.

The coalition said its first common national undertaking would be “the protection of the integrity of the vote at every polling unit across the country.”

“Whatever differences may exist among our parties, there can be no disagreement on the right of Nigerians to freely choose their leaders and have their votes count. Defending that right is the irreducible minimum of our cooperation,” the statement said.

The coalition laid particular stress on the candidates’ presence. “The Coalition attaches particular importance to the attendance, in person, of every presidential candidate and their running mates of the participating political parties,” it said.

According to the statement, a dedicated session will feature goodwill remarks from the presidential candidates and give them “an opportunity to affirm, before the Nigerian people, their collective commitment to the democratic principles that must guide the contest for national leadership.”

“The strength of this Coalition will be measured not only by the commitments made by our parties, but also by the willingness of those who aspire to lead our country to work together. Leadership begins with the willingness to stand together when the national interest demands it. That is a message no one can deliver by proxy,” it said.

The summit will bring together the National Chairmen and National Secretaries of the participating parties, members of their National Working Committees and Presidential Campaign Councils, presidential candidates and their running mates, and representatives of the G100 and the House of Representatives Minority Caucus.

Other party leaders, members of the National Assembly, civil society representatives, the diplomatic community and the media have also been invited to witness the proceedings.

The Alaago of Kajola Alago, Ileshan, Oba Oladipo Olaitan and Prof. Ango Abdullahi are among the statesmen invited to deliver addresses of encouragement on “The Doctrine of a Necessary Democratic Opposition.”

The Coalition for Democracy is a multiparty platform pioneered by the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Allied Peoples Movement (APM), Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), Peoples Redemption Party (PRP) and Social Democratic Party (SDP).

It said the door “remains open to all political parties willing to commit to the principles of democratic renewal, constitutional governance, electoral integrity and national reform.”

On the traditional group picture, the statement said: “The family photograph of Nigeria’s democratic opposition will be taken at the close of proceedings. Nigerians will expect it to be complete.

“Nigeria’s democratic opposition has made a choice: to move from consultation to commitment, and from fragmented efforts to collective action. We will stand together. We will defend democracy. And we will work together to build a Nigeria worthy of the hopes and aspirations of its people,” the statement added.

title: Mayweather Meets Sanwo-Olu, Plans Grassroots Boxing Initiative In Nigeria
description: American boxing champion Floyd Mayweather Jr. has met Lagos State Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu as part of plans to develop grassroots boxing talent and attract international boxing events to Nigeria.Mayweather met the governor on Sunday at Lagos House, Marina, during his ongoing visit to the country.
content:
American boxing champion Floyd Mayweather Jr. has met Lagos State Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu as part of plans to develop grassroots boxing talent and attract international boxing events to Nigeria.

Mayweather met the governor on Sunday at Lagos House, Marina, during his ongoing visit to the country.

The visit is part of efforts by the former world champion to establish the TMT Frontrow Fight Series Nigeria, an initiative aimed at discovering, training and promoting emerging boxers across the country.

The programme is expected to provide young talents with professional coaching, mentorship and competitive opportunities, while creating pathways for them to pursue careers in professional boxing.

It also includes plans to establish boxing academies and grassroots development programmes in several Nigerian cities, including Lagos, Abuja, Enugu and Calabar.

The first event under the initiative is scheduled to be held in 2027. Mayweather is also expected to participate in a boxing contest in Nigeria that year, although details of the proposed bout have yet to be announced.

Sanwo-Olu disclosed the meeting in a post on his official X account on Sunday, describing it as a pleasure to receive the American boxer.

He said Mayweather’s vision of inspiring grassroots boxing talent across Africa, beginning in Nigeria, and bringing international boxing events to Lagos presented opportunities for young people and the state’s sports industry.

“Lagos is ready to welcome major sporting events. We have continued to invest in sports infrastructure, and we are focused on creating an environment where talent can grow and succeed,” the governor wrote.

He added that the state looked forward to exploring the opportunities and strengthening Lagos’s position as a leading destination for sports and entertainment in Africa.

Mayweather also met the Director-General of the Lagos State Sports Commission, Lekan Fatodu, during his visit.

The former five-division world champion arrived in Nigeria earlier in November, with Abuja as his first stop, where he announced plans for the grassroots boxing development initiative.

His latest visit also builds on a pledge made during an earlier trip to Nigeria in May 2022 to support the development of boxing through an academy.

Mayweather, widely regarded as one of the greatest boxers of his generation, retired from professional boxing with an unbeaten record of 50 wins, including 27 knockouts.

His visit to Nigeria comes ahead of a scheduled exhibition bout against Australian boxer Matt “The Jedi” Floyd in Bangkok, Thailand, on December 19, 2026.

The post Mayweather Meets Sanwo-Olu, Plans Grassroots Boxing Initiative In Nigeria appeared first on Channels Television.

title: Nigeria’s security crisis complex, varies across regions — Bishop Anagbe

Anagbe, who spoke in Owerri while gi
content:
By Chidi Nkwopara

OWERRI — The Catholic Bishop of Makurdi Diocese, Most Rev. Wilfred Chikpa Anagbe, has described Nigeria’s security situation as troubling and complex, saying the nature and causes of violence vary across different parts of the country.

Anagbe, who spoke in Owerri while giving an account of the peculiar circumstances of displaced persons in parts of Nigeria, said insecurity in the country was driven by several factors, including religiously targeted violence, criminal banditry, land and resource disputes, communal tensions and failures of protection.

He cautioned against generalising security incidents or making unverified claims, insisting that religiously motivated attacks should be identified where evidence supports such conclusions.

“The security situation in Nigeria is complex and varies from place to place. In some incidents, the religious identity of victims is central to the violence; in others, insecurity is also connected with criminal banditry, land and resource disputes, communal tensions and failures of protection,” he said.

The cleric added: “We must be courageous enough to name religiously targeted violence where the evidence supports that conclusion, and responsible enough to verify claims before repeating them.

“Accuracy does not weaken our advocacy. It gives it credibility, protects vulnerable people and makes it harder for those responsible for injustice to dismiss the truth.”

The bishop urged public office holders and other Nigerians to place the safety and dignity of citizens above political interests, ethnic loyalties and social standing.

He challenged Nigerians to examine whether political affiliations or ethnic differences had prevented them from speaking out against injustice and supporting victims of violence.

“Standing with persecuted Christians does not require us to turn away from the suffering of others. It asks us to stand firmly with those who are targeted while treating every person with the respect the Gospel demands,” he said.

Anagbe warned against allowing political affiliation, ethnic background, wealth or social position to determine whose suffering deserved attention.

He said Nigerians should see their different backgrounds and responsibilities as resources for a common mission of protecting lives, pursuing justice, helping displaced families rebuild and defending freedom of worship.

The bishop further observed that behind every reported attack were individuals and families grappling with fear, displacement, loss and uncertainty.

He cited parents worried about the safety of their children, families forced out of their homes, communities struggling to rebuild and worshippers uncertain whether their plight was receiving adequate attention.

Anagbe recalled that he had taken the plight of affected communities in his Makurdi Diocese to national and international platforms, stressing that drawing attention to their suffering should translate into concrete interventions.

On the way forward, he called for credible and practical action to address persecution, insecurity, banditry and violence across the country.

He urged Nigerians to listen to displaced families, grieving widows, children whose education had been disrupted, threatened parish communities and people who had lost their means of livelihood.

The cleric cautioned against allowing repeated reports of violence to normalise human suffering or reducing the experiences of affected communities to statistics and political arguments driven by vested interests in security votes.

“Every human life has a dignity that demands our attention and every credible account of suffering calls for a response marked by compassion, truth and responsible action,” he said.

The post Nigeria’s security crisis complex, varies across regions — Bishop Anagbe appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Dike to Amaechi: Tinubu not weak, you lack leadership knowledge
description:
From Tony John, Port Harcourt
A member of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential/Rivers Rainbow Coalition Candidates Campaign Council, Barrister Princewill Dike, has faulted the former Minister of Transportation and African Democratic Congress (ADC) Vice-Presidential candidate, Chibuike Am
content:
From Tony John, Port Harcourt

A member of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential/Rivers Rainbow Coalition Candidates Campaign Council, Barrister Princewill Dike, has faulted the former Minister of Transportation and African Democratic Congress (ADC) Vice-Presidential candidate, Chibuike Amaechi, over his comments on President Bola Tinubu’s leadership style.

Dike described Amaechi’s position as a misunderstanding of the principles of leadership.

Reacting to Amaechi’s account of working closely with Tinubu during the 2015 presidential campaign, Dike said the former Rivers State governor was bereft of the realities of leadership by interpreting the delegation of responsibilities as a sign of ineptitude.

He argued that the ability to identify competent individuals, assign responsibilities and harness their intellectual capacities remained one of the defining attributes of effective leadership.

“No successful leader can personally undertake every responsibility,” Dike said.

According to him, great leaders distinguish themselves by surrounding themselves with brilliant and resourceful people whose expertise and contributions strengthen decision-making and promote result-oriented governance.

“Leadership is not about being a jack of all trades or attempting to control every aspect of administration, but about building a competent team, providing direction and ensuring accountability in the discharge of assigned duties,” he said.

To buttress his position, Dike cited the biblical account of Moses and his father-in-law, Jethro, in Exodus 18:14-26, where Jethro advised Moses to appoint capable men to handle the disputes of the Israelites instead of shouldering the entire responsibility alone.

“Moses accepted the advice and appointed leaders over thousands, hundreds, fifties and tens, thereby establishing a system of shared responsibility that made administration more effective and reduced his burden,” he said.

The political commentator also cited Jesus Christ’s delegation of responsibilities to His disciples, as recorded in Luke 9:1-2 and 6, as well as the appointment of Stephen, Philip and five others by the early Apostles to handle specific administrative responsibilities in Acts 6:1-7.

“See also Luke 9:1-2 and 6, as well as the appointment of Stephen, Philip and five others by the early Apostles to handle specific administrative responsibilities in Acts 6:1-7. There you will know that delegation of duties is key in governance,” Dike said.

He said the biblical examples demonstrated that delegation was a time-tested principle of effective leadership and should not be misconstrued as weakness or inability to perform.

Dike further referenced the renowned neurosurgeon Ben Carson’s 2008 book, Take the Risk, which highlighted the Bible as an inexhaustible source of practical wisdom for everyday living.

On the political implications of Amaechi’s comments, Dike challenged opposition politicians to provide Nigerians with credible alternative economic policies rather than resorting to personal attacks against Tinubu.

He argued that those seeking to take over the leadership of the country in 2027 should demonstrate their preparedness through concrete policy proposals capable of addressing Nigeria’s economic and developmental challenges.

Dike expressed confidence in Tinubu’s political prospects ahead of the 2027 general election, warning opposition politicians against underestimating the president’s political experience and mobilisation capacity.

He also pointed to the political influence of the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, describing him as a significant factor in the political calculations ahead of the 2027 presidential election.

The political commentator maintained that the forthcoming electoral contest would require more than political rhetoric and personal criticism, insisting that opposition candidates must demonstrate a clear understanding of contemporary political realities and present convincing alternatives to Nigerians.

title: Obi unveils 10-day record of service as governor
description:
Former Anambra State Governor and the presidential candidate of Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, Peter Obi, has announced plans to publish a 10-day account of his achievements while in office, saying he wants his record to speak amid renewed scrutiny of his administration.







Obi, who disclosed
content:
Former Anambra State Governor and the presidential candidate of Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, Peter Obi, has announced plans to publish a 10-day account of his achievements while in office, saying he wants his record to speak amid renewed scrutiny of his administration.

Obi, who disclosed this in a post on his X platform on Monday, said the series, titled Record of Service, would highlight his interventions, accomplishments and responsibilities during his tenure as governor.

The announcement came as he disclosed that he had arrived in the United States to honour an invitation and participate in a series of engagements scheduled to begin at 9am on Tuesday in Washington DC.

Obi said he had consistently focused on policies, ideas and practical solutions capable of addressing Nigeria’s challenges, rather than allowing political debates to revolve around personal attacks.

He, however, said he had decided to present facts about his past administration following what he described as repeated scrutiny of his record by individuals who appeared uncomfortable with their own records.

“Starting today and running for ten days, I will present some of the accomplishments recorded during my tenure as Governor of Anambra State. This series will outline my interventions, achievements and the responsibilities entrusted to me. I have titled it my Record of Service,” he said.

The former governor maintained that he had always given his best in every public office he held, insisting that although not all intended objectives could be achieved, he had never lacked commitment or dedication to his responsibilities.

He also specifically addressed allegations that he abandoned Anambra State during the erosion crisis, saying he considered it necessary to make the facts available to the public.

“In particular, in light of allegations that I abandoned Anambra State during the erosion crisis, among other assertions, I consider it necessary to present the facts to the public,” he said.

Obi insisted that he had never evaded any responsibility entrusted to him and would not shy away from contributing to efforts to address Nigeria’s challenges.

He added that he would continue to update Nigerians on his daily engagements and other significant developments as political activities ahead of the 2027 general elections gather momentum.

” I am confident that, ultimately, facts outlast allegations, while records carry greater weight than rhetoric.

“Let my record speak for itself!” he added.

title: NGX Group acquires 10% strategic stake in Nairobi Securities Exchange
description:
By Peter Egwuatu



Nigerian Exchange Group Plc (NGX Group) has acquired a 10% equity stake in the Nairobi Securities Exchange (NSE), a strategic investment that extends the Group’s participation in East Africa and advances its pan-African growth strategy.



The NGX, in a statement stressed that th
content:
By Peter Egwuatu

Nigerian Exchange Group Plc (NGX Group) has acquired a 10% equity stake in the Nairobi Securities Exchange (NSE), a strategic investment that extends the Group’s participation in East Africa and advances its pan-African growth strategy.

The NGX, in a statement stressed that the strategic investment aligns with its priority of building regional leadership through partnerships and African market integration, strengthening its investment presence across West and East Africa.

“This latest development builds on NGX Group’s strategic investment in the Ethiopian Securities Exchange (ESX), further demonstrating the Group’s long-term commitment to participating in the development and growth of African capital market infrastructure” the statement added.

On the strategic rationale, the NGX explained that the acquisition provides it with exposure to one of East Africa’s most established capital markets, broadening its investment portfolio beyond Nigeria and positioning the Group to benefit from the long-term growth of the region’s capital markets and increasing financial integration across the continent.
It also reflects NGX Group’s disciplined approach to capital allocation, balancing strategic growth opportunities with its commitment to sustainable shareholder returns. The investment supports three key strategic priorities: Regional Integration- Strengthening connections between African capital markets and supporting cross-border investment opportunities; portfolio diversification -Expanding NGX Group’s investment exposure beyond Nigeria, complementing its existing investments; Shareholder Value – pursuing long-term growth opportunities through disciplined capital allocation, while maintaining a commitment to sustainable shareholder returns” the statement noted.

Commenting on the investment, Alhaji Umaru Kwairanga, Group Chairman, NGX Group, said: “African capital markets are at an inflection point, where integration is moving from aspiration to architecture. Exchange groups that commit patient capital to market infrastructure will help shape how capital flows across the continent. Our investment in the Nairobi Securities Exchange is a disciplined, long-term step in that direction, strengthening the financial linkages between West and East Africa while creating opportunities for sustainable shareholder value.”

Temi Popoola, Group Managing Director/Chief Executive Officer, NGX Group, said: “This investment reflects our strategy to build a more diversified and resilient exchange group with a stronger presence across African markets. Kenya is a cornerstone of East Africa’s financial ecosystem, and our investment in NSE provides exposure to its long-term growth potential while broadening our sources of investment returns beyond Nigeria.

“Both markets have already shown what closer collaboration can achieve for issuers and investors and a shareholding relationship gives that collaboration permanence. We remain focused on disciplined capital allocation and investments that deliver sustainable value to our shareholders over the long term.”

The post NGX Group acquires 10% strategic stake in Nairobi Securities Exchange appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: NANS rejects N10,000 drug test fee for students
description:
The National Association of Nigerian Students has opposed the proposed N10,000 drug test fee for students, calling on the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency to immediately halt its enforcement and collection.
The students’ body made the demand in a statement on Monday, signed by its President, Aki
content:
The National Association of Nigerian Students has opposed the proposed N10,000 drug test fee for students, calling on the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency to immediately halt its enforcement and collection.

The students’ body made the demand in a statement on Monday, signed by its President, Akinteye Afeez.

NANS said it was concerned that the NDLEA was demanding N10,000 from Nigerian students for drug tests, describing the move as an additional financial burden on students already grappling with economic challenges.

The association said it was not opposed to drug testing, the promotion of drug-free institutions or efforts to address substance abuse among students, but rejected the decision to make students pay for tests initiated by the agency.

“While we are not opposed to drug testing, the promotion of drug-free institutions or any genuine effort aimed at addressing drug abuse among students, we stand fiercely opposed to any attempt to transfer the financial burden of such exercises to Nigerian students, particularly when the initiative is being driven by the Agency itself and students have not independently requested these tests,” the statement read.

It said students were already facing rising tuition fees and the increasing cost of living, adding that imposing further charges under the guise of drug testing was unacceptable.

“It is disheartening to see government agencies turn students into business ventures, exploit them and impose additional financial burdens on Nigerian students despite the government’s various interventions and policies aimed at making education accessible and improving students’ welfare,” NANS said.

The association called on the NDLEA Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, Brig. Gen. Mohamed Buba Marwa (retd.), to immediately stop the enforcement and collection of the fee.

“If the Agency must carry out its official responsibilities, it must do so without imposing any financial burden on Nigerian students. Charging students for an exercise initiated by the Agency itself is utterly unacceptable, and we therefore demand that the Chairman and Chief Executive Officer immediately halt this practice,” it said.

NANS maintained that the welfare of students should not be turned into a source of revenue for government agencies, warning that it would not remain silent over what it described as financial exploitation.

“The welfare of Nigerian students must not become a revenue-generating venture for government agencies.

“We remain committed to supporting every initiative that advances the welfare, safety and development of Nigerian students. However, we shall not fold our arms and watch students being subjected to avoidable financial exploitation,” the statement added.

The association reaffirmed its commitment to affordable education and the protection of students’ welfare.

The post NANS rejects N10,000 drug test fee for students appeared first on Punch Newspapers.
