title: Ondo Air Crash: NAF recovers black box, fixes memorial for Nov 26
description:
The Nigerian Air Force (NAF) has confirmed the recovery of the Cockpit Voice Recorder (CVR), commonly referred to as the black box, from the site of the October 5 aircraft crash in Igbokoda, Ondo State.
The Service also announced plans to hold a memorial service and wreath-laying ceremony on Novembe
content:
The Nigerian Air Force (NAF) has confirmed the recovery of the Cockpit Voice Recorder (CVR), commonly referred to as the black box, from the site of the October 5 aircraft crash in Igbokoda, Ondo State.

The Service also announced plans to hold a memorial service and wreath-laying ceremony on November 26, 2026, in honour of personnel and other victims who lost their lives in the NAF 931 aircraft accident.

The ceremony will take place at the National Military Cemetery in Abuja, providing an opportunity for bereaved families, colleagues, friends and members of the Air Force community to pay their last respects.

The Director of Public Relations and Information, Air Commodore Ehimen Ejodame, disclosed the developments in a statement on Sunday.

He said the memorial would serve as a formal expression of the Service’s respect and remembrance for those who died in the crash.

On the recovery operation, Ejodame confirmed that the Cockpit Voice Recorder, alongside other aircraft fragments and relevant evidence, had been retrieved from the crash site.

He explained that data recovered from the recorder was being analysed and was expected to contribute significantly to the ongoing investigation into the circumstances surrounding the accident.

According to him, the investigation is being conducted in collaboration with the Nigerian Safety Investigation Bureau (NSIB) and the Nigerian Civil Aviation Authority (NCAA).

The Air Force spokesman reaffirmed the Service’s commitment to ensuring that the investigation meets the highest standards of professionalism, transparency and accountability, while supporting the independent technical processes required to establish the cause of the crash.

Ejodame also disclosed that recovery operations had yielded several human remains and aircraft fragments, while efforts to identify the recovered remains were still ongoing.

He said the exercise had been particularly challenging due to the swampy nature of the terrain and the depth at which some of the aircraft wreckage had become embedded in the ground.

The NAF spokesman added that the Service was working with relevant agencies to address environmental concerns arising from the recovery operation and ensure appropriate remediation after the exercise.

He said the Air Force remained mindful of the grief experienced by bereaved families and was committed to providing them with sustained support.

The Service also acknowledged the cooperation of relevant agencies, host communities and other stakeholders who had assisted with the recovery and investigation efforts.

The Nigerian Air Force assured the public that it would continue to pursue a thorough investigation, responsible environmental management and a dignified remembrance of all those who lost their lives in the October 5 accident.

The post Ondo Air Crash: NAF recovers black box, fixes memorial for Nov 26 appeared first on Very Nigerian.

title: Why Atiku? The Answer is in The Solutions: by Paul Ibe
description:
Thank you for your open letter. Your central question—why Nigerians should expect an Atiku Abubakar presidency to deliver better outcomes—is legitimate. It deserves an answer grounded in policies and accountability.
You are right that Nigeria owes nobody the presidency. Neither longevity in politics
content:
Thank you for your open letter. Your central question—why Nigerians should expect an Atiku Abubakar presidency to deliver better outcomes—is legitimate. It deserves an answer grounded in policies and accountability.

You are right that Nigeria owes nobody the presidency. Neither longevity in politics nor persistence in seeking office creates an entitlement to lead. Atiku must earn the confidence of Nigerians.

Where I respectfully disagree is with the suggestion that familiarity with the same political establishment makes Atiku and President Bola Tinubu equivalent. Shared acquaintances do not establish identical convictions, competence or approaches to government. Treating them as interchangeable is like comparing apples and oranges while overlooking the differences that matter.

The useful comparison concerns what each proposes, how those proposals would work, and what they would mean for ordinary Nigerians.

That is where #AtikuSolutions—affordability, security and economic revival—should become the centre of this conversation.

Affordability: economic policy must make life liveable

For a mother deciding between food and medicine, the most meaningful economic indicator is what her income can buy. For a small business owner, it is whether electricity, transport and financing costs leave enough to remain in business.

Atiku’s proposed production subsidy addresses a major source of these pressures: energy costs.

His published proposal would provide preferentially priced domestic crude to qualifying Nigerian refineries, subject to verified production, domestic supply and conditions requiring the benefit to reach consumers. It envisages a budget ceiling, independent audits and sanctions for abuse. It also acknowledges that discounted crude carries a real cost to public revenue.

The intended connection is practical: lower the cost of producing fuel locally, ensure consumers receive the benefit, and ease the energy burden on households and businesses.

You ask how this would be financed. That question deserves precision. The crude discount represents revenue forgone; it must therefore be explicitly costed and accommodated within the budget. Published reporting also identifies details still requiring disclosure, including the discount rate, eligible volumes and annual ceiling. Those are proper subjects for scrutiny. We strengthen the proposal by answering them.

But a proposal with identifiable mechanisms and costs deserves examination on its merits. Dismissing it as an absence of ideas prevents precisely the policy debate you seek.

Security: protect lives and restore livelihoods

Your description of northern deprivation raises an essential point: a leader’s geographical origin does not guarantee development for people from that region.

A northern presidency is no substitute for effective government. Neither is a southern presidency. Nigerians everywhere need protection, functioning schools, accessible healthcare and opportunities to earn a living.

Atiku’s published security agenda includes decentralising security institutions, strengthening intelligence and border control, improving regional cooperation and addressing the conditions that sustain conflict. His longstanding economic programme also emphasises private investment, infrastructure and education.

The practical test of security policy is whether farmers can return to their land, children can attend school and traders can travel without fear.

Security and affordability are connected. When violence drives farmers away, food supply suffers. When transport routes become dangerous, distribution becomes more expensive. When businesses cannot protect their workers and investments, employment suffers.

Restoring security is therefore part of restoring the economy.

Economic revival: give enterprise room to grow

You ask where the new ideas are. An idea should be judged by whether it addresses the problem and can be implemented successfully.

Atiku’s economic approach places private enterprise at the centre of investment and job creation, with government providing security, infrastructure and credible rules. His published programme advocates wider private participation in infrastructure and stronger education and skills development. These are proposals against which his candidacy can be assessed.

For Nigerians, the questions are concrete: Can a manufacturer obtain dependable power? Can a farmer reach a market? Can a young entrepreneur access finance? Can an investor trust that the rules will remain predictable?

Economic revival requires answers across these areas. Affordable energy helps businesses survive. Security allows production to resume. Investment expands employment. Education equips people to participate.

That is the connection between priorities of #AtikuSolutions.

Accountability must accompany the programme

Your questions about wealth, allegations and public integrity should not be dismissed. Equally, allegations must be distinguished from findings established through due process. Neither political loyalty nor political hostility should determine the standard of evidence.

No candidate should receive immunity from scrutiny.

Your demand for clarity about implementation, financing and accountability is particularly valuable. Nigerians should insist on costed programmes, clear responsibilities, published milestones, transparent procurement and independent scrutiny. Supporting Atiku should strengthen those demands.

Nor should the lifestyle of an associate replace examination of the candidate’s programme. Concerns about political ostentation deserve to be heard, especially amid hardship. But the decisive questions concern who would exercise public responsibility, their competence and the standards governing their conduct.

Inclusion deserves a serious answer

Your concern about rotation also merits respect. Political balance matters in a diverse federation, and apprehensions about exclusion cannot simply be waved away.

Atiku must earn trust across regions through the substance of his commitments to inclusion, equitable appointments, development and devolution of power. Every Nigerian deserves a meaningful stake in the country, whoever occupies the presidency.

Your letter ends with a proposition I share: the presidency belongs to the Nigerian people.

They deserve a choice informed by evidence. They deserve to compare programmes, interrogate costs, examine records and demand measurable results.

Atiku’s experience gives Nigerians a record to scrutinise. His proposals give them an alternative to examine. Neither asks them to surrender their judgment.

The case for Atiku is that his approach to affordability, security and economic revival offers a credible direction that deserves serious consideration.

Let us debate that case with the rigour Nigeria’s circumstances demand.

The post Why Atiku? The Answer is in The Solutions: by Paul Ibe appeared first on Very Nigerian.

title: Obi to publish Anambra achievements in 10-day series
description:
The 2027 presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, Peter Obi, has announced plans to publish a 10-day account of his achievements as governor of Anambra State amid allegations that he abandoned the state during an erosion crisis.
Obi said the series, titled ‘Record of Service’, woul
content:
The 2027 presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, Peter Obi, has announced plans to publish a 10-day account of his achievements as governor of Anambra State amid allegations that he abandoned the state during an erosion crisis.

Obi said the series, titled ‘Record of Service’, would highlight his interventions, achievements and responsibilities during his tenure as governor.

The former Anambra governor disclosed this in a post on his X handle on Monday, shortly after arriving in the United States for a series of engagements in Washington, DC.

He said the presentation would begin on Tuesday and run for 10 days, explaining that he decided to make his record public in response to repeated scrutiny of his past.

“Nevertheless, because certain individuals have repeatedly scrutinised my past, even as they appear uneasy about their own records, I have chosen to allow the facts to speak for themselves.

“Starting today and running for ten days, I will present some of the accomplishments recorded during my tenure as Governor of Anambra State.

“This series will outline my interventions, achievements and the responsibilities entrusted to me. I have titled it my Record of Service,” he said.

Obi also specifically addressed allegations that he abandoned Anambra State during the erosion crisis, insisting that he had never evaded any responsibility entrusted to him.

“In particular, in light of allegations that I abandoned Anambra State during the erosion crisis, among other assertions, I consider it necessary to present the facts to the public.

“I have never evaded any responsibility entrusted to me, and I will certainly not shirk my responsibility to help address Nigeria’s challenges,” he said.

Recall that on November 6 during the APC rally in Akwa Ibom, Tinubu took a swipe at Obi, accusing him of failing to tackle erosion in his state while contrasting his record with efforts to confront the Atlantic Ocean in Lagos.

However, Obi, on Monday, maintained that his political campaigns had focused on policies, ideas and practical solutions to Nigeria’s challenges rather than personal criticisms.

“Throughout my election campaigns, I have sought to emphasise policies, ideas, and practical solutions that can deliver the change Nigeria urgently requires and help our nation overcome its current challenges,” he added.

The former governor said he had always given his best in every position he had occupied, although he acknowledged that not all intended results could always be achieved.

“In every position I have held, I have consistently given my utmost effort in fulfilling my responsibilities. Although no one can always attain every intended result, I have never been found lacking in dedication or effort. I have always given the task my full commitment,” he said.

Obi added that he would continue to update supporters on his daily engagements and other significant developments as campaign activities gathered momentum.

He expressed confidence that facts would ultimately outlast allegations, adding, “I am confident that, ultimately, facts outlast allegations, while records carry greater weight than rhetoric.”

The post Obi to publish Anambra achievements in 10-day series appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Sanwo-Olu gifts Flamingos N10m, iPhones each
description:
Lagos State Governor, Babajide Sanwo-Olu, has rewarded Nigeria’s victorious U-17 women’s national team, the Flamingos, with ₦10 million each, iPhone 17 Pro Max devices and other gifts following their historic triumph at the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco.
Sanwo-Olu announced the reward
content:
Lagos State Governor, Babajide Sanwo-Olu, has rewarded Nigeria’s victorious U-17 women’s national team, the Flamingos, with ₦10 million each, iPhone 17 Pro Max devices and other gifts following their historic triumph at the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco.

Sanwo-Olu announced the reward package on Sunday at a special dinner reception held in honour of the team at Lagos House, Marina, where he hosted the players and their technical crew to celebrate their achievement.

Under the package, each player and member of the technical crew will receive ₦10 million, bringing the total cash reward to ₦300 million. The beneficiaries also received iPhones, headphones and bespoke outfits.

The Lagos State Government’s gesture adds to the growing list of rewards and recognition announced for the team since it made history in Morocco.

The Flamingos became the first African team to win the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup after defeating Japan 2-1 in the final on November 7 at the Mohammed VI Football Complex in Rabat.

Awawu Bashiru gave Nigeria the lead in the 39th minute before tournament Most Valuable Player, Oluebube Umejiaku, doubled the advantage shortly after the restart.

Japan pulled one back through Fuki Ito in the 80th minute, but the Flamingos held on to secure the title.

The victory capped a remarkable campaign for the Nigerian side, which recovered from a 2-1 opening defeat to Poland to win six consecutive matches and claim the trophy.

They responded to the setback with a 2-0 victory over Puerto Rico before defeating defending champions Korea DPR 3-1 to strengthen their chances of progressing in the competition.

Nigeria subsequently overcame Mexico in the Round of 16 and edged Venezuela 1-0 in the quarter-finals, with Azeezat Oduntan scoring a decisive 89th-minute penalty.

The team then defeated Brazil 3-1 in the semi-finals to reach their first-ever final before completing their historic run with victory over Japan.

The triumph made Nigeria the first African country to win the women’s U-17 World Cup and the first African nation to claim both the men’s and women’s U-17 World Cup titles.

The country’s previous best finish in the women’s competition was third place at the 2022 edition in India.

Sanwo-Olu’s announcement follows the Federal Government’s reward package for the team at a presidential reception in Abuja on November 11.

President Bola Tinubu approved a ₦100 million Federal Government Savings Bond for each player, with the investment expected to generate monthly returns and remain intact after five years.

Head coach Akeem Ishola Busari was awarded ₦100 million in cash, while assistant coaches and other members of the technical and administrative crew were allocated ₦50 million each.

The First Lady, Senator Oluremi Tinubu, announced the package on behalf of the President, commending the players for their resilience in recovering from their opening defeat to win their remaining six matches.

The Senate also announced a ₦100 million reward for the team following a special reception hosted by Senate President Godswill Akpabio.

The reward followed a motion moved by Senator Abdul Ningi, Chairman of the Senate Committee on Sports, congratulating the Flamingos on their historic achievement.

Earlier, the team received a $50,000 cash gift from sports stakeholder and commission sponsor Saleh Ahmadu during a reception organised in Rabat by the Chairman of the National Sports Commission, Shehu Dikko, and its Director General, Bukola Olopade.

The Presidency also directed the National Sports Commission to facilitate the payment of outstanding bonuses and allowances owed to the players and officials from the preliminary qualifying rounds through to the World Cup final.

Beyond the team’s collective achievement, Umejiaku earned individual recognition after winning the adidas Golden Ball as the tournament’s best player.

title: UK expands six-month paid jobs scheme for 90,000 youths
description:
A young person in the United Kingdom has said a government-backed employment scheme helped rebuild their confidence after a prolonged period of unemployment left them uncertain about returning to work.
The participant, who secured a placement at Kenny Waste through the Jobs Guarantee scheme, said th
content:
A young person in the United Kingdom has said a government-backed employment scheme helped rebuild their confidence after a prolonged period of unemployment left them uncertain about returning to work.

The participant, who secured a placement at Kenny Waste through the Jobs Guarantee scheme, said the experience had improved their confidence in handling workplace responsibilities and preparing for career progression.

“Taking part in the Jobs Guarantee scheme has had a really positive impact on my confidence with finding and being in work,” the participant said.

“Before starting my placement at Kenny Waste, being out of work made me feel uncertain about my abilities in settling into a workplace and being able to handle the job role after being out of one for so long.

“Working in a supportive team and having reassurance from my brilliant co-workers helped me overcome this. I now feel much more confident in my abilities to handle the workload and progress more in the workplace.

“Even though I have only been in the role for 6 weeks, I feel like it was the perfect placement for me and have gained so much from it already.

“I have the Jobs Guarantee scheme to thank for this, as the support I had there was amazing and they really do find the right role for each person,” he added.

The account comes as the UK Government announced plans to expand the Jobs Guarantee scheme nationwide, offering fully funded six-month paid employment to more than 90,000 young people aged 18 to 24 who are claiming Universal Credit and looking for work.

Our correspondent on Monday retrieved this from the Department for Work and Pensions in a statement published on its website on November 14, saying the programme would be extended across England, Scotland and Wales from the end of November.

Under the scheme, the government will fund up to 25 hours of paid work weekly for six months at the applicable minimum wage. Jobs will be matched to participants’ skills, with tailored support provided before and during their employment.

The department said the expansion followed a successful rollout in six areas with some of the highest levels of youth unemployment and was expected to help more than 90,000 young people into work by March 2029.

It also announced that from April 2027, eligible young people who have been claiming Universal Credit and looking for work will be able to access the scheme after 12 months rather than the current 18 months.

Work and Pensions Secretary Pat McFadden said the expansion was intended to ensure young people did not remain unemployed for extended periods without opportunities.

“The longer someone is out of work, the harder it is to get back in, and no young person should be left waiting on a scrapheap for an opportunity.

“That is why we are expanding our guaranteed jobs scheme across Great Britain and bringing it forward, so that help arrives when it matters most.

“Employers are crying out for talent, and there is a generation of talent ready to be unleashed. We are backing them with the support they need to build a fulfilling future,” he said.

More than 400 employers have supported the scheme, including Lidl, Leonardo Hotels and Boots.

Lidl GB’s Chief People Officer, Stephanie Rogers, said the company had already welcomed its first employees through the programme and planned to expand recruitment.

“Young people have huge ambition to offer, but too often struggle to find the right door to open – which is why initiatives such as the Youth Guarantee Scheme are so important.

“At Lidl GB, young people are a key part of our workforce and we believe in giving our colleagues a fair chance to build meaningful careers. We have already welcomed our first colleagues through the scheme, with plans already to expand recruitment further.

“Through this scheme, we are not just offering a placement, but industry-leading training and a supportive environment where young people develop transferable skills to secure their future. Alongside our fast-track interview pathways for the long-term unemployed and our apprenticeship programmes, we’re proud to offer a strong launching pad into stable, long-term careers in retail,” she said.

The government also said young people receiving the health element of Universal Credit would be able to participate in the scheme voluntarily from April 2027.

The Jobs Guarantee is part of a wider £2.5bn government investment aimed at supporting almost one million young people and creating 500,000 opportunities.

The expansion comes ahead of a review by Alan Milburn into the causes of rising youth inactivity, with the final report expected the following week.

The government said the scheme was part of its wider effort to ensure young people had access to employment, education and training opportunities.

title: NGX Group acquires 10% stake in Nairobi securities exchange
description:
Nigerian Exchange Group Plc has acquired a 10 per cent equity stake in the Nairobi Securities Exchange, Kenya, in a move aimed at expanding its presence in East Africa and advancing its pan-African growth strategy.
The group disclosed this in a statement by its Team Lead, Public Relations and Intern
content:
Nigerian Exchange Group Plc has acquired a 10 per cent equity stake in the Nairobi Securities Exchange, Kenya, in a move aimed at expanding its presence in East Africa and advancing its pan-African growth strategy.

The group disclosed this in a statement by its Team Lead, Public Relations and Internal Engagement, Joseph Kadiri on Monday, saying the investment would strengthen its participation in African capital markets and support greater financial integration across the continent.

It said the acquisition would give it exposure to one of East Africa’s established capital markets, broaden its investment portfolio beyond Nigeria and position it to benefit from the long-term growth of the region’s financial markets.

The investment also builds on NGX Group’s earlier strategic investment in the Ethiopian Securities Exchange, further demonstrating its commitment to the development of capital market infrastructure across Africa.

According to the group, the acquisition supports three strategic priorities: regional integration, portfolio diversification and shareholder value.

It said the investment would strengthen connections between African capital markets, support cross-border investment opportunities and expand its exposure beyond Nigeria while pursuing sustainable returns for shareholders.

Commenting on the development, the Group Chairman, NGX Group, Umaru Kwairanga, said the investment was a long-term step towards strengthening financial connections between West and East Africa.

He said, “African capital markets are at an inflection point, where integration is moving from aspiration to architecture. Exchange groups that commit patient capital to market infrastructure will help shape how capital flows across the continent.

“Our investment in the Nairobi Securities Exchange is a disciplined, long-term step in that direction, strengthening the financial linkages between West and East Africa while creating opportunities for sustainable shareholder value.”

The Group Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer, Temi Popoola, said the investment aligned with the group’s strategy to build a diversified and resilient exchange group with a stronger presence across African markets.

“Kenya is a cornerstone of East Africa’s financial ecosystem, and our investment in NSE provides exposure to its long-term growth potential while broadening our sources of investment returns beyond Nigeria,” Popoola said.

He added that the investment would strengthen collaboration between the two markets and provide a more permanent basis for cooperation.

“Both markets have already shown what closer collaboration can achieve for issuers and investors and a shareholding relationship gives that collaboration permanence,” he said.

Popoola said the group remained committed to disciplined capital allocation and investments capable of delivering sustainable value to shareholders over the long term.

NGX Group said it would continue to pursue opportunities to expand its regional participation, diversify its investment returns and support the development of more connected and competitive African capital markets.

title: 2027 poll: Showunmi writes Ribadu, urges him to set firm boundaries for political conduct
description:
Says Nigeria navigating delicate security environment
_______________________________________________________________________
From Laide Raheem, Abeokuta
Convener of The Alternative Movement, Segun Showunmi, has called on the National Security Adviser, Mallam Nuhu Ribadu, to set firm boundaries for
content:
Says Nigeria navigating delicate security environment

_______________________________________________________________________

From Laide Raheem, Abeokuta

Convener of The Alternative Movement, Segun Showunmi, has called on the National Security Adviser, Mallam Nuhu Ribadu, to set firm boundaries for political conduct and initiate decisive action against politicians and their supporters whose words and actions threaten national security.

Showunmi, who made the call in an open letter addressed to the National Security Adviser, a copy of which was made available to Daily Sun on Monday, said Nigeria was navigating a particularly delicate security environment that demanded vigilance, institutional coordination and responsible leadership.

In the open letter, titled “On the Urgent Need to Establish Firm Boundaries for Political Conduct and Hold Those Who Threaten National Security Accountable”, he warned that political competition, personal ambition and partisan disagreements must not be allowed to become additional threats to national stability.

“There is a difference between robust political engagement and conduct that deliberately or recklessly threatens public peace. There is a difference between criticising the government and deliberately inciting citizens against one another,” he said.

Showunmi expressed concern over what he described as the normalisation of provocative statements, ethnic and religious insinuations, threats, inflammatory public performances and the deliberate manipulation of sensitive national issues for political advantage.

He said some individuals seemed to believe that because they were politicians, party loyalists, public commentators or influential supporters of powerful political interests, they could say virtually anything, mobilise others irresponsibly and walk away without consequences.

“That assumption must be firmly challenged. National security cannot be held hostage to political ambition,” he added.

He stressed that the right to participate in democratic politics did not include the right to endanger the Republic, adding that political disagreements must never become a licence to incite violence, threaten citizens, encourage lawlessness or create conditions that could trigger communal tensions.

Showunmi urged Ribadu’s office, working with relevant security and law-enforcement institutions, to establish and publicly communicate clear boundaries for political conduct, particularly as the country moved deeper into an increasingly competitive political period.

He proposed six urgent measures to the Office of the NSA: the establishment of clear national boundaries for political communication; application of the law without regard to political status; development of a coordinated rapid-response mechanism against political misinformation and incitement; holding political parties and their leadership structures accountable for the conduct of individuals acting under their banners or on their behalf; establishment of a clear protocol for early intervention; and making accountability independent of political hierarchy, to curb the political menace.

Showunmi, however, clarified that his letter was not a call to suppress legitimate opposition, silence critical voices or criminalise political disagreement, noting that dissent, criticism, protest and competing political visions were essential ingredients of democratic governance.

“But democracy must also protect the Republic from those who would exploit its freedoms to threaten its existence and security,” he said.

He added that the government must be able to distinguish between legitimate political expression and conduct that crossed the threshold into criminality, through established legal standards, credible evidence, due process and respect for fundamental rights.

“We cannot continue to behave as though national security is the exclusive responsibility of soldiers, policemen, intelligence officers and other security operatives. Political actors also have a responsibility to preserve the environment in which democracy can function,” Showunmi emphasised.

He appealed to Ribadu to send an unmistakable message to every political actor who believed political relevance conferred immunity, that the rules applied to everyone.

“We must not wait for an avoidable national tragedy before demonstrating the seriousness of our institutions. Enough is enough. Nigeria must come first, and nobody’s political ambition is worth the peace, stability and security of our country,” he concluded.

The letter was copied to President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, the Minister of Defence, General Christopher Musa (Rtd), the Special Adviser to the President on Homeland Security, Major General Adeyinka A. Famadewa (Rtd), the Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Rilwan Disu, the Director-General of the Department of State Services, Mr Oluwatosin Ajayi, and the Minister of State for Defence, Alhaji Bello Muhammad Matawalle.

title: New York police shoot man dead after suspected abduction sparks chase
description:
New York police officers have shot dead a 26-year-old man, identified as Omatoyo Neverson, after a suspected abduction report triggered a vehicle chase and confrontation on the Belt Parkway in Brooklyn.
The incident occurred shortly before 7:30 pm on Saturday after two people called emergency servic
content:
New York police officers have shot dead a 26-year-old man, identified as Omatoyo Neverson, after a suspected abduction report triggered a vehicle chase and confrontation on the Belt Parkway in Brooklyn.

The incident occurred shortly before 7:30 pm on Saturday after two people called emergency services to report a possible abduction involving a woman inside a white van in the Coney Island neighbourhood.

According to NBC New York, in a now updated report on Monday, the callers alerted nearby police officers after reporting that a woman was screaming and apparently struggling inside the vehicle.

Speaking at a press briefing, NYPD Assistant Chief Charles Minch said the male caller reported seeing the woman inside the van, saying, “There’s a girl kicking and screaming in there.”

The female caller, meanwhile, told emergency operators that she heard the woman repeatedly shouting, “Let me go!”

Minch said the callers subsequently spotted officers in a marked police vehicle and alerted them to the suspected abduction.

When the officers approached the white van, however, the driver allegedly drove onto the sidewalk and sped away.

Police broadcast the vehicle’s description and registration details over their radio channels before officers located it in heavy traffic on the eastbound Belt Parkway in Sheepshead Bay.

According to the police account, officers approached the van, ordered the driver to get out and broke its front passenger-side window when he failed to comply.

Minch said the driver subsequently began moving the vehicle forwards and backwards, striking police and civilian vehicles.

“The driver began to drive forwards and backwards, ramming both police and occupied civilian vehicles indiscriminately on the Belt Parkway,” he said.

He added that officers attempted to subdue the driver using pepper spray and Tasers, but the measures were unsuccessful.

“And the driver continued to ram nearby vehicles. Officers then discharged their firearms and struck the driver,” Minch said.

The officers removed the driver from the van, called an ambulance and performed cardiopulmonary resuscitation before he was taken to NYU Langone Hospital–Brooklyn, where he was pronounced dead.

Police later identified the deceased as Neverson, 26, of Canarsie, Brooklyn.

However, subsequent investigations established that the person initially believed to be a kidnapped girl was an adult woman who had escaped from the van before officers arrived.

“The female is an adult and was not injured,” Minch said, adding that she confirmed she had been inside the van and had been screaming before leaving the vehicle.

“At this point, we believe that the screaming was in relation to a domestic dispute,” he added.

Minch also disclosed that Neverson was wanted in connection with an unlawful imprisonment case reported the previous month and a domestic assault earlier in November. Police said the woman found in the van was the victim in both cases.

The fatal shooting was captured on police body-worn cameras and is being investigated by the NYPD’s Force Investigation Unit. The New York State Attorney General’s Office of Special Investigation is also expected to review the incident, in line with its responsibility to investigate deaths involving police officers.

The shooting forced the temporary closure of parts of the Belt Parkway as investigators examined the scene.

title: England’s 3-2 win over Spain our best yet – Tuchel
description:
England manager Thomas Tuchel has described his side’s 3-2 victory over world champions Spain in Madrid as the best performance since he took charge of the Three Lions, praising their resilience, energy and football quality.
PUNCH Online had earlier reported Sunday that 10-man England beat the Spani
content:
England manager Thomas Tuchel has described his side’s 3-2 victory over world champions Spain in Madrid as the best performance since he took charge of the Three Lions, praising their resilience, energy and football quality.

PUNCH Online had earlier reported Sunday that 10-man England beat the Spanish team at their turf.

Tuchel’s side produced an impressive display at the Metropolitano Stadium on Saturday, taking a 3-0 lead before Elliot Anderson’s red card and a subsequent penalty allowed Spain to fight back to 3-2.

England travelled to Madrid for their final UEFA Nations League group game knowing that only a victory would guarantee them top spot ahead of next March’s quarter-finals.

The Three Lions delivered the performance demanded by their manager, going toe-to-toe with the world champions and establishing a three-goal advantage midway through the second half.

However, the game took a dramatic turn after Anderson was sent off for fouling Lamine Yamal, with Spain converting the resulting penalty before Neco Williams scored again to reduce the deficit to 3-2 with 15 minutes remaining.

England held on despite the pressure, with goalkeeper James Trafford making important saves to help secure the victory.

Speaking after the match, in a release on the team’s website on Sunday, Tuchel said, “It was a brilliant performance and a well-deserved win.”

He added, “Overall, we were the better team and we put out a fantastic performance from start to finish.

“The red card and the penalty, it’s always a big decision and I need to understand why it’s a double punishment.

“From then it was a long, long 30 minutes, but I don’t want to focus on that. There were so, so many positive things and the performance and the result over the 60 minutes was well deserved.

“You need a complete performance when you come here and we brought everything to the table.

“We were brave on the ball, we were impatient off the ball, we were hungry, and in our own half we were patient and closed the gaps.

“A fantastic team performance, spirit-wise, energy-wise, but also in terms of football quality. That was the highest level.”

Trafford started in goal in place of Jordan Pickford, who featured in England’s first match of the international window against Croatia.

Asked whether the two goalkeepers were competing for the number one position, Tuchel said, “No, there’s no number one. It’s a group. The double save was exactly what we wanted and he had a brilliant match, because it only works if you’re top from number one to eleven.”

He added, “We showed what we’re made of and what we can do, and that we trust the process, and that we’re hungry enough to develop, and that we’re always ready to push our limits.

“We had our best result in 60 years [at the World Cup] and we were not happy with it. We wanted to get better and we bridged the gap in the things that we wanted to improve.

“It is impressive what we did in the last two camps, so full credit to the team.

“Given the circumstances, against whom and where we played, it was the best I’ve seen.”

The post England’s 3-2 win over Spain our best yet – Tuchel appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: 2027: NDC will resist attacks with equal force – Aisha Yesufu
description:
A chieftain of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, Aisha Yesufu, has warned that members of the party will no longer tolerate attacks on them, declaring that anyone who attacks them will be met with “equal force” as political tensions rise ahead of the 2027 general elections.
Yesufu made the declaratio
content:
A chieftain of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, Aisha Yesufu, has warned that members of the party will no longer tolerate attacks on them, declaring that anyone who attacks them will be met with “equal force” as political tensions rise ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Yesufu made the declaration during an interview on Channels Television’s Sunday Politics, days after suspected political thugs disrupted the party’s town hall meeting for its presidential candidate, Peter Obi, in Oregun, Lagos State.

“I am prepared for war because I want peace. And they are coming out protecting… to try to defend myself, right to defend my life. It’s a fundamental right, it’s a human right, it’s a natural right, and I will protect myself,” she said.

She accused President Bola Tinubu and members of the All Progressives Congress of failing to speak out against previous attacks on opposition supporters, while questioning why the President had condemned the recent incident involving the NDC.

Recalling attacks and threats allegedly made against opposition supporters in different parts of the country, Yesufu cited the killing of an NDC supporter in Enugu, whom she said was the only son of his mother.

She also referred to alleged threats against Obi in Benue State, in Edo State and in Abuja, questioning why Tinubu had not publicly condemned such incidents.

According to her, the President’s position that all was fair in politics had emboldened political violence, adding that opposition supporters had previously chosen not to retaliate because they wanted to maintain peace.

“The fact that some people think they have the monopoly of violence and they will unleash their thugs and their thugs will kill, they will maim, they will destroy, and they will not say anything, it has passed. We will no longer accept that,” she said.

The NDC chieftain, however, denied threatening to initiate violence, insisting that her comments were about defending herself and other party members against attacks.

“I am not threatening violence, but anybody that comes to attack us will be met with force, equal force. I am not threatening violence. I am threatening that I am going to defend my life,” she added.

The comments followed the November 12 attack on the NDC’s town hall meeting at Classique Event Centre in Oregun, Ikeja, where suspected political thugs reportedly disrupted preparations for the gathering involving Obi, his running mate, Rabiu Kwankwaso, and the party’s Lagos governorship candidate, Funso Doherty.

Several attendees were injured during the incident, while vehicles were damaged and some journalists reportedly lost equipment. The meeting was later held after Obi arrived at the venue.

The Lagos State chapter of the APC and the party’s presidential campaign council denied involvement in the attack and called for the perpetrators to be arrested.

 Tinubu also condemned violence at political events and directed security agencies to tackle political thuggery, stressing that all candidates and political parties should be allowed to campaign without intimidation.

Speaking on the 2027 elections, Yesufu said the NDC was more confident of its chances than it was during the 2023 general election, adding that its members would not be intimidated.

“I will tell you something, this 2027 election, we have more hope than we even did in that 2023, and we will continue to go on that. We are peace-loving people, but we are also people that are not going to take nonsense from anybody,” she said.

She added that the party’s major concern was ensuring that its votes were protected and that its victory, if secured, was not overturned through electoral malpractice.

“Winning is not our problem. The main issue is ensuring that when we win, nobody, born of man or woman, will rig our election,” Yesufu said.

title: Saudi Arabia Publishes Allowances For Foreign Workers Including Housing And Transport - Check Below For Full Details
description: Saudi Arabia detailed the full allowances package for foreign contract workers: air tickets, housing allowance of at least SAR 8,000, furnishing support of 50% of monthly salary and SAR 300-400 monthly transport.
content:
Saudi Arabia has outlined the full package of allowances available to non-citizen contract workers in the country, covering air travel, housing, furnishing and monthly transportation.

Under Article 17 of the contract regulations, the Ministry covers the cost of air tickets for non-citizen workers at two specific points: once at the start of the contract when the worker travels from their home country to the Kingdom, and again at the end of the contract when they return home.

Workers already residing in Saudi Arabia at the time of their appointment are not eligible for the first ticket. The Ministry also provides a return air ticket to the worker's home country once a year during the contract period when the worker takes their regular annual leave.

On accommodation, the Ministry pays a housing allowance worth three months of the worker's salary, with a minimum value of SAR 8,000. This amount is paid in a single lump sum at the start of the contract and at the beginning of each renewal year.

Where a female worker is accompanied by a male non-marriageable relative, known as a Mahram, only one housing allowance is paid, going to whichever of the two earns the higher salary. Workers provided with Ministry-arranged housing do not receive this allowance.

A one-off furnishing allowance, equal to 50% of the worker's monthly salary, is also paid at the start of the contract.

The Ministry pays a monthly transportation allowance to cover workers' commutes to their duty stations. Workers earning less than SAR 2,000 receive SAR 300 per month; those earning between SAR 2,001 and SAR 3,500 receive SAR 350; and workers earning above SAR 3,500 receive SAR 400 per month.

In some cases, instead of paying the monthly allowance, the Ministry may arrange and provide suitable means of transportation directly to the worker.

The allowance details are drawn from Saudi Arabia's published contract regulations as reported by Legit.ng. Workers should confirm current terms with their employers or the relevant Saudi authorities.

title: NIS Deploys Mobile Passport Enrolment Unit To Nigerian Embassy In Madrid - Check Below For Full Details
description: Nigerians in provinces far from Madrid will no longer need to travel long distances for passport enrolment as the Nigeria Immigration Service deploys a Mobile Enrolment Unit to the embassy in Spain.
content:
Nigerians living outside Madrid will soon have easier access to passport enrolment services following the deployment of a Mobile Enrolment Unit (MEU) by the Nigeria Immigration Service (NIS) to the Nigerian Embassy in Madrid, Spain.

Nigeria's Ambassador to Spain, Dr Okezie Victor Ikpeazu, said the initiative would reduce the burden of long-distance travel for passport applicants residing in provinces far from the Spanish capital.

According to a statement issued by the Embassy on Friday, Ikpeazu said this when the Head of the Immigration Section at the Nigerian Embassy in Madrid, Mr Ayotunde Adigun, formally presented the mobile enrolment equipment to him alongside other embassy officials.

"The deployment of the MEU will significantly ease the enrolment process for Nigerian passport applicants residing in provinces far from Madrid," the ambassador said.

He described the initiative as "a practical and citizen-centred intervention that will reduce the burden of long-distance travel, save time and resources for applicants, and bring essential consular services closer to Nigerians living across Spain."

The ambassador commended the Comptroller-General of the Nigeria Immigration Service, Kemi Nandap, for approving the deployment, and urged eligible passport applicants to take advantage of the facility once the operational schedules are announced.

He reaffirmed the embassy's commitment to improving the accessibility and efficiency of consular services for Nigerians within its jurisdiction.

title: WHO Sounds Alarm On Antimicrobial Resistance Threat
description: The spread of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is threatening modern medicine despite progress in combating drug-resistant bacteria, senior World Health Organization officials said Monday.WHO officials said countries had expanded efforts to tackle AMR, but warned that progress in prevention, diagnosis
content:
The spread of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is threatening modern medicine despite progress in combating drug-resistant bacteria, senior World Health Organization officials said Monday.

WHO officials said countries had expanded efforts to tackle AMR, but warned that progress in prevention, diagnosis and the appropriate use of antibiotics remained too slow to meet global targets.

Bacteria have long evolved resistance to medicines designed to kill them.

The widespread use of antibiotics in human health, animal husbandry and food production has accelerated the problem, making AMR one of the leading causes of infectious-disease deaths worldwide.

“Antimicrobial resistance is widespread and threatening the future of modern medicine,” said Jean-Pierre Nyemazi, interim head of antimicrobial resistance at the WHO.

“Unlike COVID-19, which was very visible, drug-resistant infections have been taking people’s lives for years without us noticing it and raising the alarm as we should,” said Nyemazi.

In 2021 alone, AMR was directly responsible for more than one million deaths and linked to some 4.7 million others, said the agency.

A WHO investigation in 183 countries into the progress of the fight against antimicrobial resistance this year revealed that nearly nine in 10 countries had a national action plan against the phenomenon. In 2017, the figure was only around four in 10.

But only 42 countries — less than one in five — said they had a plan that was financed, implemented and monitored, said Pravasha Prakash, an AMR technical officer with the global health agency.

“Countries are moving forward in every step but progress still needs to be speeded up to reach the 2030 targets,” she added.

Poor Access To Diagnostics

One of the main weaknesses remains access to diagnostics. Only 36 percent of countries had a national reference laboratory capable of testing for resistance in all bacteria and fungi monitored by the WHO — well short of the 80 percent target set for 2030.

“Without testing, clinicians must treat without knowing the cause of infection or which antibiotic will work,” said Sylvia Bertagnolo, head of surveillance for AMR at the WHO.

The latest global surveillance data show that in 2023, one in every six laboratory-confirmed bacterial infections flagged to the WHO was resistant to antibiotics used to treat it.

As a result, the WHO has announced the release of two new tools designed to help countries strengthen their diagnostic capacities.

The first defines the tests that should be available at every level of the healthcare system, from primary care centres to referral hospitals.

The second compiles 73 laboratory procedures, from sample collection to the identification of pathogens and antibiotic susceptibility testing.

The WHO has estimated that AMR could cause some 39 million deaths between now and 2050.

There needs to be improved use of existing antibiotics, at a time when the development of new treatments is failing to keep pace with the rise of resistance, it said.

Infection prevention, vaccination, improved access to water and sanitation, and the appropriate use of antimicrobials are the main levers to combat the issue, it added.

AFP

The post WHO Sounds Alarm On Antimicrobial Resistance Threat appeared first on Channels Television.

title: UK pardons women convicted of abortion offences
description:
Women previously convicted of, or cautioned for, abortion offences relating to their own pregnancies in the United Kingdom have been automatically pardoned, with details of their convictions, arrests and investigations set to be removed from criminal records.
The pardon takes effect on Monday, Novem
content:
Women previously convicted of, or cautioned for, abortion offences relating to their own pregnancies in the United Kingdom have been automatically pardoned, with details of their convictions, arrests and investigations set to be removed from criminal records.

The pardon takes effect on Monday, November 16, following the commencement of provisions in the Crime and Policing Act 2026, according to a statement by the UK Ministry of Justice published on Sunday.

The measure also covers women who were arrested or investigated over such offences, including those who ended their pregnancies or attempted to do so beyond the 24-week time limit provided for under the Abortion Act 1967.

The ministry said some women had ordered abortion medication online, including during the COVID-19 pandemic, with some later saying they did not realise they were beyond the 24-week limit or had been victims of domestic abuse or coercive control.

Under the new provisions, relevant details of convictions, cautions, arrests and investigations will be deleted from criminal records. Where complete deletion is not reasonably practicable, the records will be annotated and treated as though they had been deleted.

Minister for Victims and Tackling Violence Against Women and Girls, Alex Davies-Jones, said the pardons had been a priority and welcomed the commencement of the changes approved by Parliament.

“Pardoning women for abortion offences related to their own pregnancy has been a priority and I’m pleased to be able to commence the change that Parliament voted for,” she said.

Davies-Jones said affected women would not need to apply for a pardon or take any direct action, adding that they could obtain further information online or contact the ministry’s dedicated casework team.

She said police forces and courts would begin updating their records in line with the new requirements.

The Chief Executive Officer of the British Pregnancy Advisory Service, Heidi Stewart, described the development as a historic change, saying women had faced investigations, prosecutions and convictions under abortion laws at vulnerable moments in their lives.

“For too long, women have faced the devastating consequences of outdated abortion laws – including police investigations, prosecutions and criminal convictions, often at moments of unimaginable vulnerability,” she said.

Stewart added that although the pardon could not undo the distress experienced by affected women, it recognised the harm caused by their criminalisation.

“Today marks an important milestone in ensuring that no woman faces criminal punishment or lifelong stigma because of the circumstances surrounding the end of her pregnancy,” she said.

The ministry clarified that the reform does not change the Abortion Act 1967, which remains the legal framework governing access to abortion services.

It said it would remain an offence for medical professionals or other people to act outside the provisions of the Act, but women acting in relation to their own pregnancies would no longer face criminal charges for abortion offences.

Sections 241 and 242 of the Crime and Policing Act 2026 provide for the decriminalisation and automatic pardon arrangements, with the latter provision coming into force on November 16.

The post UK pardons women convicted of abortion offences appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Japan’s economy stalls as inflation bites
description:
The Japanese economy stalled in the third quarter, official data showed on Monday, as it was hit by Iran war-fuelled inflation, bad weather and an earthquake.
The zero quarter-on-quarter growth in July-September was short of forecasts for 0.1 per cent expansion and was down from the 0.4 per cent rec
content:
The Japanese economy stalled in the third quarter, official data showed on Monday, as it was hit by Iran war-fuelled inflation, bad weather and an earthquake.

The zero quarter-on-quarter growth in July-September was short of forecasts for 0.1 per cent expansion and was down from the 0.4 per cent recorded in the previous three months.

Persistently high inflation triggered by the Middle East conflict was a factor in sluggish consumer spending, while a weak yen pushed up the cost of imported goods.

On an annualised basis, the economy shrank 0.1 per cent, against expectations of 0.2 per cent growth.

Higher oil prices have swollen Japan’s import bill and led to higher prices for consumers.

Inflation excluding fresh food accelerated sharply in September, surpassing the two per cent target set by the Bank of Japan.

That partly helped explain why real private consumption fell 0.3 per cent in the third quarter, extending a similar drop in April-June.

But the weather was likely a factor too, “as typhoons and heavy rain kept consumers away from shops,” according to Taro Kimura of Bloomberg Economics.

Net exports were also down — acting as another drag on growth — in part because of an earthquake that struck the southwestern island of Kyushu in July, leading to factory closures.

Government support measures and a rebound in corporate investment were not enough to keep economic growth in positive territory.

“The stagnation in real GDP (Gross Domestic Product) in the third quarter was a touch weaker than the analyst consensus… the details were rather discouraging, said Marcel Thieliant of Capital Economics.

However, chief researcher at Mitsubishi UFJ Research and Consulting, Shumpei Fujita, said prior to the data release that “considering the headwinds from the worsening situation in Iran, the domestic economy is maintaining its resilience.”

The latest growth figure is unlikely to dissuade the Bank of Japan from raising interest rates again in December as inflationary pressure builds, analysts say.

“In fact, it looks increasingly likely that the Bank will have to tighten policy more aggressively than we’ve been anticipating as inflation is about to surge,” Thieliant said.

The central bank last month said inflation had hit its two per cent target, more than 13 years after it adopted the goal in a bid to pull the economy out of deflation.

Japan is expected to fall to sixth place among the world’s largest economies in 2027, with India and Germany overtaking it, according to projections from the International Monetary Fund.

AFP

title: COP31: Nigeria won’t sacrifice development for energy transition – FG
description:
The Federal Government has reaffirmed Nigeria’s commitment to achieving net-zero emissions, insisting that the country’s transition from fossil fuels must reflect its national development priorities and should not be dictated by international partners.
The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, Sola
content:
The Federal Government has reaffirmed Nigeria’s commitment to achieving net-zero emissions, insisting that the country’s transition from fossil fuels must reflect its national development priorities and should not be dictated by international partners.

The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, Sola Enikanolaiye, said Nigeria was making progress towards cleaner energy but would not abandon its petroleum resources without adequate alternatives to protect government revenue, industrialisation, energy security and economic growth.

He spoke in an exclusive interview with The PUNCH on Sunday, on the sidelines of the ongoing 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference in Antalya, Türkiye, after Nigeria and the United Kingdom announced a new energy transition partnership.

Enikanolaiye said the agreement allowed Nigeria to present its position on the global shift away from fossil fuels and negotiate international support to advance its development objectives.

“Our position is very clear. We need fossil fuels to even fund the transition to other alternative sources of energy. So we cannot jump into a transition plan that does not address our national development aspirations and objectives.

“This is why we are calling for a just transition plan, an equitable transition plan and a plan that is also sustainable that would not inflict any damage on our own national development aspirations as contained in our NDC 3.0,” he said.

The minister stressed that Nigeria must participate in decisions affecting its energy future, warning against transition policies that ignored the different economic realities and development stages of countries.

“We have to be part of that conversation to ensure that nothing is imposed on us. You cannot impose an energy transition plan on us without us being at the table to negotiate and agree on what we know will promote our own national interests,” he said.

He explained that the non-binding Memorandum of Understanding signed with the UK was intended to promote cooperation at different levels, including government-to-government engagements, private sector investments and partnerships with civil society organisations and host communities.

The minister said Nigeria was already diversifying its economy to reduce excessive dependence on petroleum revenues, citing developments in agriculture, technology, digital trade, financial technology and services.

He said the administration of President Bola Tinubu was pursuing a broader economic restructuring that would create additional sources of growth and revenue beyond oil and gas.

Addressing concerns that Nigeria was caught between the effects of climate change and international pressure to reduce fossil fuel production, Enikanolaiye said diplomacy remained essential to balancing competing global interests.

He cited the Russia-Ukraine war and tensions involving Iran and the United States in the Middle East as examples of geopolitical developments affecting global energy supplies and petroleum prices.

The minister also highlighted the contribution of the Dangote Petroleum Refinery to stabilising petroleum supply, saying its impact extended beyond Nigeria to the wider African market.

“So, I believe we are on course, and we are heading towards zero emissions ultimately. But it has to be gradual. It must take into consideration the different levels of development, like I stressed, development and national development aspirations,” he added.

Enikanolaiye dismissed suggestions that Nigeria was being pressured into accepting the energy transition agenda of developed countries, insisting that the country had the diplomatic capacity to defend its interests.

“I don’t think we are under any pressure. And even if we do, we have the capacity to remain focused on our national interest. The Nigerian Foreign Ministry and diplomacy have demonstrated that over the years. So pressure is not a point. We are into partnership of equals, of sovereignty. You know where our national interest, in the spirit of strategic autonomy, guides what we do,” he said.

He challenged international partners to demonstrate their commitment through climate financing, infrastructure development and technology transfer rather than merely advocating the abandonment of fossil fuels.

The minister also cited the Federal Government’s compressed natural gas bus programme as part of efforts to expand cleaner transportation options and reduce the pressure of energy costs on Nigerians following economic reforms.

Under the UK-Nigeria Energy Security and Transition Partnership, both countries are expected to strengthen cooperation on methane reduction, particularly in the oil and gas, agricultural and waste sectors.

Enikanolaiye said the partnership would support improved methane measurement, reporting and verification, leak detection and repair, as well as the reduction of gas flaring and venting.

The post COP31: Nigeria won’t sacrifice development for energy transition – FG appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: ‘You’ve been rejected’ – Dino Melaye mocks Tinubu after Atiku’s triumphant entry into To be State
description:
Former Kogi West Senator, Dino Melaye, has claimed that residents of Yobe State have rejected President Bola Tinubu, following the massive turnout that welcomed African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate Atiku Abubakar during his campaign visit to the state.
Melaye made the assertion i
content:
Former Kogi West Senator, Dino Melaye, has claimed that residents of Yobe State have rejected President Bola Tinubu, following the massive turnout that welcomed African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate Atiku Abubakar during his campaign visit to the state.

Melaye made the assertion in a post on his X handle shortly after Atiku’s campaign rally in Potiskum on Sunday.

Atiku visited the town for his presidential campaign rally at Dabo Aliyu Stadium, where a large crowd of supporters gathered to welcome him.

Videos and photographs from the visit showed men, women and youths lining the streets, walking alongside the campaign motorcade and waving ADC flags, banners and posters.

Reacting to the turnout, Melaye argued that it reflected the people’s rejection of Tinubu ahead of the 2027 presidential election.

“It is very clear that the people of Yobe have rejected Tinubu,” he wrote.

At the rally, Atiku promised to restore fuel and electricity subsidies if elected president in 2027, while also pledging to address insecurity and youth unemployment in Yobe State and other parts of the country.

“Let me assure you that once I am elected president in 2027, I will bring back the fuel subsidy. I swear I will also bring back the subsidy on electricity,” Atiku said.

The rally was held in Potiskum following reports that the ADC had been denied access to a venue in Damaturu, the Yobe State capital, prompting the party to move the event to the town.

However, Melaye’s claim about the political position of Yobe residents was based on the crowd that attended Atiku’s rally and does not, by itself, establish the voting preferences of the entire state.

The post ‘You’ve been rejected’ – Dino Melaye mocks Tinubu after Atiku’s triumphant entry into To be State appeared first on Very Nigerian.

title: England knew Spain were beatable – Declan Rice
description:
England midfielder Declan Rice has revealed that the Three Lions were confident of beating world champions Spain ahead of their 3-2 victory in the UEFA Nations League in Madrid.
England ended Spain’s 43-match unbeaten run with an impressive performance at the Metropolitano Stadium, where a Harry Kan
content:
England midfielder Declan Rice has revealed that the Three Lions were confident of beating world champions Spain ahead of their 3-2 victory in the UEFA Nations League in Madrid.

England ended Spain’s 43-match unbeaten run with an impressive performance at the Metropolitano Stadium, where a Harry Kane penalty and goals from Ezri Konsa and Ben White gave the visitors a 3-0 lead inside an hour.

However, Elliot Anderson’s sending off for a foul on Lamine Yamal allowed Spain back into the contest, with Mikel Oyarzabal converting the resulting penalty before Nico Williams scored at the far post to reduce the deficit to 3-2.

England eventually held on for the victory, with Rice saying the players had believed they could secure the result before the encounter.

“We knew we were going to beat them tonight,” he said afterwards, in a release on the team’s website on Sunday.

“The messaging from the manager after the Croatia game has been so positive, and the message from the boys; everyone has been pushing together, knowing that we were going to come here and not just sit back and try to hit on the counter.

“The red card changes the course of the game because it could have been a couple more, if I’m being honest.

“If we don’t go down to 10 men, I think we see more of the ball. We start to see them jump more, we start to see more space, and we get to see our attacking players thrive doing what they did in the second half,” he added.

England were forced to defend their advantage in the closing stages after Williams reduced the deficit to one goal with 15 minutes remaining.

Spain mounted sustained pressure, but goalkeeper James Trafford produced an impressive double save to preserve England’s lead.

Rice praised the goalkeeper’s intervention, describing it as crucial to the visitors’ victory.

“For him to make two saves in the space of two of seconds was massive,” he added.

“For a second, when they got their second [goal], you might have thought it was going to go the other way [with] the amount of pressure they were putting on us.

“But that resilience, that defending, keep looking up at the clock, realising there wasn’t long left, and everyone kept emptying the tank, doing anything for this badge, for this team, for our players, for the manager,” the Arsenal star concluded.

The post England knew Spain were beatable – Declan Rice appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Israeli Opposition Chiefs Denounce Netanyahu Over ‘Attempted Coup’
description: Two Israeli opposition leaders denounced Monday an “attempted coup” following press reports that outgoing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s office tried to frame members of an Arab-Israeli party ahead of last month’s election.“As more and more details come to light, i
content:
Two Israeli opposition leaders denounced Monday an “attempted coup” following press reports that outgoing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s office tried to frame members of an Arab-Israeli party ahead of last month’s election.

“As more and more details come to light, it becomes clear: This wasn’t an attempt to disrupt the elections. It was an attempted coup,” wrote Yair Lapid on X, who headed the opposition in the previous legislature and co-chairs the Beyachad list.

Israel’s Channel 12 reported Sunday that on the eve of the October 27 election, Netanyahu’s chief of staff Ido Norden had phoned in a complaint to the police about members of the Arab-Israeli Raam party.

Norden reportedly pointed the police to a purported intelligence source — a former employee of Netanyahu’s office — who provided information that led to the arrest of three Raam members.

The three men were later released when the police determined that the information was unfounded.

Netanyahu subsequently accused Arab parties of electoral fraud after they gained a record number of seats. His Likud party issued a statement denying the latest allegations.

The Israeli newspaper Haaretz also reported that David Zini, head of the Shin Bet domestic security service, sought to wiretap leaders of the other Arab slate, the Joint List, but the attorney general turned down his request due to lack of evidence.

Following the report, Joint List leader Yousef Jabareen also denounced an “attempted coup by Netanyahu”.

“If the findings are confirmed, this is a criminal mechanism that operated from the heart of government to rig the election results. Everyone found responsible must be held accountable, including Netanyahu,” he wrote on X.

Raam’s number two, former police chief Yoav Segalovitz, called for an urgent investigation.

“These suspicions require an immediate, independent and thorough criminal investigation that reaches everyone involved, at every level and in every role,” he wrote on X.

“Netanyahu cried out that his election was being stolen, while he himself tried to steal the country and is still trying to do so now,” he added.

Netanyahu’s main rival, former army chief of staff Gadi Eisenkot, wrote on Sunday that the caretaker prime minister “cannot remain at the head of the government for a minute longer”.

Neither Netanyahu’s bloc nor Eisenkot’s opposition secured the 61 seats required to form a government following last month’s election.

The two Arab parties, the Joint List and Raam, have indicated support for Eisenkot.

AFP

title: I’m scared of marriage, relationships – Mr Macaroni
description:
Nigerian actor and comedian Debo Adedayo, popularly known as Mr Macaroni, has said he is scared of marriage and romantic relationships, admitting that he is uncertain about his ability to meet the demands of commitment.
The comedian said his prolonged period of being single had made it difficult for
content:
Nigerian actor and comedian Debo Adedayo, popularly known as Mr Macaroni, has said he is scared of marriage and romantic relationships, admitting that he is uncertain about his ability to meet the demands of commitment.

The comedian said his prolonged period of being single had made it difficult for him to adjust to the expectations of a relationship, particularly the need for constant communication and attention.

Mr Macaroni made this known during an appearance on the In My Opinion podcast on Sunday, where he spoke about his personal life and challenges with romantic relationships.

He disclosed that he had been having conversations with a woman he genuinely loved but was unsure whether he could commit fully to the relationship.

“I’m so scared of marriage, relationships. I’ve been single for so long. But the truth is, I don’t know how to do it anymore.

“I’m not sure. And when I say do it, I mean the constant calls. A part of me wants it. A part of me knows that I care for this person, but some days I just want to be left alone,” he said.

The actor described it as unfair to tell someone that you love them when you are not willing to commit fully to the relationship.

He said being in a relationship came with responsibilities that he was not certain he could fulfil.

“I always think that it is totally unfair to say to someone that you love them, but you’re not willing to commit all the way through.

“If you say you want to be with someone, you have responsibility,” he added.

Explaining his struggles with communication, Mr Macaroni said he sometimes found it difficult to keep up with the expectation of regular contact.

He recalled an occasion when he promised to call the woman after a conversation but became engrossed in playing FIFA after returning home.

He said although he remembered his promise, he continued playing the game instead of making the call.

The comedian also disclosed that he could go for one or two weeks without communicating with someone, adding that he sometimes preferred to be alone, play video games and have his personal space.

He, however, clarified that his reluctance to embrace relationships was not necessarily connected to his career but to how long he had been accustomed to being single.

“I think it’s not because of my career. I think it’s just because it’s been so long,” he said.

Mr Macaroni, who is known for his comedy skits and the character Daddy Waidi, began his acting career with minor roles before venturing into content creation.

During the interview, he said frustration with waiting for bigger acting opportunities partly pushed him to create his own content.

The actor announced on November 3 that he had earned a Master of Arts degree with distinction in Performance (Acting) from the Mountview Academy of Theatre Arts in London.

He announced the achievement in a video shared on his Instagram page, describing the programme as challenging.

He added that completing the degree had tested him in several ways but contributed to his personal and professional development.

The post I’m scared of marriage, relationships – Mr Macaroni appeared first on Punch Newspapers.
