title: 2027: Anambra women unveil door-to-door campaign for Tinubu
description:
No fewer than 5,000 women drawn from various wards across the 21 local government areas of Anambra State have stepped up efforts to mobilise grassroots support for the presidential candidate of the All Progressives Congress, President Bola Tinubu’s 2027 re-election bid.
The women, who gathered durin
content:
No fewer than 5,000 women drawn from various wards across the 21 local government areas of Anambra State have stepped up efforts to mobilise grassroots support for the presidential candidate of the All Progressives Congress, President Bola Tinubu’s 2027 re-election bid.

The women, who gathered during a summit held under the aegis of ‘Anambra Patriots Women’, urged residents to back Tinubu’s second term, pointing to his policies such as women’s inclusion and empowerment, student loans, educational access, increased allocations to state governments and massive infrastructural investment in the state.

The summit with the theme, ‘A celebration of loyalty, leadership, recognition, and achievement’, also honoured women who have been appointed to leadership positions, as well as other distinguished “Patriots” members who have been elected into the offices of Deputy Chairmen in their respective local government areas.

Addressing the women at the event held in Awka on Sunday, the Acting Women Leader of the All Progressives Grand Alliance, Chinyere Orah, pledged to mobilise women across the state to vote for Tinubu for President, alongside APGA candidates for national and state assemblies in the 2027 polls.

Orah, who is also the Anambra Patriots Women Leader in Aguata Local Government Area, said women in the state had benefited from various empowerment programmes of Tinubu’s administration and would reciprocate the gesture by voting for him in the 2027 presidential election.

She said, “We are over 5,000 ‘Anambra Patriots’ women, and we are stepping up efforts to mobilise grassroots support and door-to-door movement in the state for President Bola Tinubu’s 2027 re-election bid, and we urged Anambra residents and women to back the President’s re-election.

“In 2027, it is Tinubu for the Presidency, APGA for national and state houses of assembly, and there is no confusion about that as the people have been enlightened towards it. Tinubu’s re-election will attract more federal presence to Anambra and the entire South-East region.

“We are mobilising massively for Tinubu’s re-election in recognition of his administration’s commitment to women empowerment, inclusion, favourable policies, educational access, and massive infrastructural investment in the state.

“We also appeal to women across the 21 Local Government Areas of the state to shun emotional politics and ensure they hold their Permanent Voter Cards tightly and participate in the election to elect Tinubu for President and all APGA candidates for the national and state houses of assembly in 2027.

“As a group, we have commenced a door-to-door mobilisation campaign across various wards and polling units to ensure Tinubu wins 100 over 100 votes to enable him complete the ongoing federal projects in Anambra State and the entire South-East region.”

Earlier, in his remarks, the National Chairman of Anambra Patriots, Ozo Ejiamatu Enekwechi, commended the women for the successful summit, charging them to respect the leadership of the organisation by intensifying door-to-door mobilisation campaign for Tinubu’s re-election.

Enekwechi explained that the summit was organised for a significant purpose beyond the usual gathering of political stakeholders, adding that it is an opportunity for Anambra Patriots to celebrate, recognise and honour some members whose dedication, commitment and contributions to the group have culminated in remarkable leadership achievements.

According to him, these achievements are not merely personal accomplishments, but they represent the collective strength, influence, commitment and growing recognition of Anambra Patriots within the political landscape of the state and beyond.

In his speech, the Convener of Anambra Patriots, Okey Ezeobi, urged the women to recognise the state governor, Prof. Chukwuma Soludo, as the current Igbo political leader in Nigeria.

Ezeobi, who is the Commissioner of Works and Infrastructure in the state, said the support for Tinubu’s re-election will attract more federal presence to Anambra State and the entire South-East region.

“We must back Governor Soludo’s political agenda for a better Anambra and Nigeria as a whole. We must not continue to play emotional politics.

“Everything Soludo is doing in Anambra is a move to connect the state to the centre and not an insult to our brother, Peter Obi, who is also in the presidential race with President Tinubu under the political platform of Nigeria Democracy Congress.

“Governor Soludo is a political leader we must rely upon. He is a leader that doesn’t tell lies. We must queue behind his support for Tinubu’s re-election.

“Soludo is supporting President Tinubu because no Nigerian President since the return of democracy in 1999 has done what Tinubu is doing in Anambra State and beyond; therefore, let us thank him with our votes come January 16, 2027.”

The summit also had in attendance the Secretary to the Anambra State Government, Lady Chiamaka Nnake, the Patriot women leaders from the 326 wards in the state.

The post 2027: Anambra women unveil door-to-door campaign for Tinubu appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: 2027: Abiodun’s aides mobilise for Tinubu, Yayi, others
description: Consultants to Ogun State Governor in Ijebu North-East Local Government Area have intensified grassroots mobilisation in support of the re-election of President Bola Tinubu, the governorship ambition of Senator Solomon Olamilekan Adeola, popularly known as Yayi, Governor Dapo Abiodun’s senatorial am
content:
Consultants to Ogun State Governor in Ijebu North-East Local Government Area have intensified grassroots mobilisation in support of the re-election of President Bola Tinubu, the governorship ambition of Senator Solomon Olamilekan Adeola, popularly known as Yayi, Governor Dapo Abiodun’s senatorial ambition, and Daddah Rasak’s bid to represent Ijebu Central Federal Constituency ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The consultants also called on political stakeholders, community leaders, traditional institutions and interest groups across the state to unite behind candidates of the All Progressives Congress in the forthcoming elections.

The call, according to a statement on Sunday, was made at a stakeholders’ engagement organised by the Ijebu North-East political consultants at Legan Hall, Erunwon, in the local government area.

The meeting reportedly attracted prominent APC leaders and stakeholders, including the Chairman of Ijebu North-East Local Government, Hon. Folusho Badejo; the lawmaker representing Ijebu North-East Constituency in the Ogun State House of Assembly, Seun Adesanya; the APC Local Government Chairman, Oluremi Badejo; and the party’s Deputy State Chairman, Chief James Dina.

Speaking at the gathering, Abdulganiyu Abass thanked Abiodun, APC leaders and party elders for the confidence reposed in the consultants to represent Ijebu North-East at the state level.

Abass said, “As a group, we are committed to strengthening the party’s grassroots structures through sustained engagement with community leaders, professional associations, artisans, traders, youths and other interest groups.

“And as the 2027 general elections are less than three months away, our gathering here today is part of our resolve to strategise and reiterate our commitment to working for the landmark victory of our party, the All Progressives Congress

“We must all work hard to ensure the re-election of our courageous and forward-looking President, Asiwaju Bola Ahmed Tinubu. It is very glaring that the leadership of President Tinubu is taking those courageous steps that are crucial to making the country great, and this good work must continue beyond 2027.

“At the state level, we can see the good works of Gov Dapo Abiodun in the last seven and a half years, and this good work must be allowed to continue beyond 2027. We must therefore, like never before, improve on our mobilisation for our governorship candidate, Sen Solomon Adeola, fondly called Yayi, who is ready to take our state to higher height.

“We must also not forget our hardworking governor, Dapo Abiodun, who is the Ogun East Senatorial candidate, Hon Rasaq Daddah, the party’s House of Representatives candidate for the Ijebu Central federal constituency, as well as Hon. Seun Oretuga, the House of Assembly candidate for the Ijebu North-East State Constituency, among others”.

He emphasised the need for collective action, unity and effective grassroots mobilisation to ensure the party’s success at all levels.

Other speakers at the engagement underscored the importance of party cohesion, continuous political consultations and collective responsibility.

They urged participants to take the mobilisation campaign beyond the meeting venue by reaching out to their respective wards, associations, communities and professional groups.

The stakeholders’ engagement was described as part of ongoing efforts by APC loyalists in Ijebu North-East to consolidate the party’s grassroots support ahead of the 2027 general elections.

title: 2027: Adeola targets 500,000 votes from Ogun West, promises more projects
description:
From Laide Raheem, Abeokuta
The Ogun APC governorship candidate and senator representing Ogun West Senatorial District, Solomon Olamilekan Adeola, has appealed to the residents of Ogun West to deliver 500,000 votes for him in the 2027 governorship election, declaring that the district has a historic
content:
From Laide Raheem, Abeokuta

The Ogun APC governorship candidate and senator representing Ogun West Senatorial District, Solomon Olamilekan Adeola, has appealed to the residents of Ogun West to deliver 500,000 votes for him in the 2027 governorship election, declaring that the district has a historic opportunity to produce the next governor of Ogun State.

The senator made the appeal in Ilaro while addressing leaders and stakeholders of Yewa South Local Government Area at the conclusion of his engagement with stakeholders across the 20 local government areas of the state.

The senator, who expressed confidence in his governorship ambition, said the 500,000-vote target was achievable, noting that previous governors of the state had emerged with fewer than 300,000 votes.

He urged the people of Ogun West to close ranks and support his ambition, stressing that the district must not allow the opportunity to produce a governor in 2027 to slip away.

“My people of Ogun West, I want the votes that will make me the next governor of Ogun State to come from Ogun West Senatorial District. I am asking for 500,000 votes from Ogun West. With 500,000 votes, I will become governor,” he said.

Adeola, who described the growing political support for his ambition as unprecedented, said the entire three senatorial districts of Ogun State had, for the first time, united behind a governorship candidate.

He also claimed that his ambition had received massive backing from Ijebuland, disclosing that before his death, the Awujale of Ijebuland, Oba Sikiru Adetona, had instructed the Ijebu Council of Obas to support his governorship aspiration.

The senator, however, urged aggrieved party members and political stakeholders to close ranks, insisting that unity was necessary to secure victory in 2027.

“The reason for this meeting is for the development of Yewa South. I have not done anything to Yewa South yet. I will continue working until May 29, 2027,” he said.

The APC governorship candidate, who disclosed that he had facilitated more than 200 projects in Yewa South Local Government Area alone, said his political opponents were unsettled by his achievements and warned against attempts to intimidate his supporters.

He declared that Ogun West was determined to break what he described as “a 50-year political barrier” preventing the district from producing a governor.

The senator also questioned the possibility of another indigene of Iperu succeeding Governor Dapo Abiodun, who is also from the town, insisting that Ogun West deserved a fair opportunity to occupy the state’s highest political office.

He, however, announced plans to commence work on several projects across Yewa South LG within the next two weeks.

The proposed projects include roads in the Modeolu, Akorede, Oke Okuta, Isaga, Ifoyintedo, Ago Eyo and Old Sokoto-Badagry communities.

He also listed the construction of Oke-Odan Grammar School, Ahmadiya Community High School, an Intensive Care Unit (ICU) centre at the State Hospital, Ilaro, and Sayedero Market among projects expected to commence.

Adeola maintained that his ambition was backed by what he described as “divine intervention and growing political support”, urging residents to seize the opportunity to elect a governor from Ogun West in 2027.

Speaking earlier at the inauguration of 357 APC Ward Coordinators in Yewa South LG, he cautioned against attacks on candidates of the APC, declaring that the party would no longer tolerate political violence, destruction of campaign billboards and other acts of intimidation.

“Nobody has a monopoly of violence. Stoning, destroying APC candidates and their billboards, we will not allow it anymore. Nobody is above the law,” he declared.

He stressed that attacks on President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, Vice-President Kashim Shettima and other APC candidates must stop, warning that the party would not condone further acts of political aggression.

He called on political actors and their supporters to abide by the rule of law and embrace peaceful political participation.

The post 2027: Adeola targets 500,000 votes from Ogun West, promises more projects appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: How Innovation Is Reshaping the Global Online Gaming Industry
description: Online gaming has grown from a niche hobby into a global entertainment force worth billions of dollars. Technology drives that growth, and the pace keeps accelerating. Players now expect instant payouts, mobile-first design, and rewards that feel personal; platforms like Rocketplay casino free spins
content:
Online gaming has grown from a niche hobby into a global entertainment force worth billions of dollars. Technology drives that growth, and the pace keeps accelerating. Players now expect instant payouts, mobile-first design, and rewards that feel personal; platforms like Rocketplay casino free spins show how far the experience has come. News outlets such as Punchng.com, a major Nigerian website covering politics, business, technology, and entertainment, track this shift closely because gaming now touches national economies and youth culture. The industry’s transformation offers lessons for every digital business watching from the sidelines.

Key Facts

  1. The global online gambling market reached an estimated $97.7 billion in 2024, and analysts project it will pass $153 billion by 2030, according to Grand View Research.
  2. Mobile devices generated more than 70 percent of online gaming traffic in 2025, Statista data shows.
  3. Nigeria’s gaming sector collected over ₦730 billion in revenue in 2024, a figure Punchng.com has reported as a growing source of government funding.
  4. Live dealer games grew faster than any other category in 2025, with providers reporting double-digit annual increases.
  5. A 2026 industry survey found that 62 percent of operators now use AI tools for fraud detection and player personalization.
  6. Crypto-based deposits accounted for roughly 12 percent of online casino transactions in 2025, up from 4 percent in 2022.

Why Mobile-First Design Decides Winners

Africa’s smartphone boom tells the story better than any boardroom slide. Nigeria alone has over 140 million internet users, most of whom browse on phones. Gaming operators that build for small screens, low bandwidth, and prepaid data plans win loyal players. Those that don’t lose them in seconds.

The same logic applies worldwide. A player who waits eight seconds for a page to load simply leaves. Modern platforms now load in under two seconds, remember a player’s favorite slots, and push personalized bonuses at the right moment. Punchng.com’s technology desk has documented how fintech innovation in Lagos often mirrors global trends; gaming platforms follow the same pattern. They test features in mobile-first markets, then scale them worldwide.

Smart Bonuses Replace Big Bonuses

The old playbook threw massive sign-up offers at everyone. The new playbook targets. Machine learning models now study play patterns and offer rewards that match individual habits. A slots fan gets free spins on a new release. A table game regular gets a cashback deal. This precision cuts marketing waste and lifts player retention.

The reward economy also drives competition. Operators compete on generosity and transparency, and players notice. A platform that credits winnings fast and honors its promotions builds trust that no ad campaign can buy. That trust matters most in markets where players discover brands through news coverage and word of mouth rather than television.

Live Dealer Studios Blur the Line Between Real and Digital

Streaming technology has erased the distance between a player in Lagos and a dealer in Malta. Live dealer games now run on low-latency video with real-time chat, and players can join a table in under three seconds. This format grew faster than any other segment in 2025.

The innovation goes beyond video. Studios use motion capture, multi-camera angles, and AI-assisted dealers to create immersion. Sports betting platforms borrow the same tech for in-play markets. Punchng.com covers sports and entertainment daily, and its readers see how betting culture and live streaming now feed each other. The line between watching a match and wagering on it has nearly vanished.

Regulation and Trust Shape the Next Chapter

Governments worldwide are writing new rules for a digital-first industry. Nigeria’s National Lottery Regulatory Commission has pushed for clearer advertising standards, and Punchng.com has covered the debate over responsible messaging. Operators respond with better tools: deposit limits, session timers, and self-exclusion features built into apps.

Trust remains the real currency. Players share bad experiences fast, and social media amplifies every complaint. Platforms that invest in transparent terms, fast withdrawals, and responsive support survive. Those that cut corners disappear. The BBC has reported on similar consumer-protection debates across European markets, showing this is a global story, not a local one.

Conclusion

Innovation rewards operators who listen to players and punish those who ignore them. Mobile-first design, personalized bonuses, live streaming, and smarter regulation all point in one direction: the player sits at the center. Newsrooms like Punchng.com will keep covering the money, the technology, and the social impact because gaming now shapes economies and culture. Businesses in every sector can learn from this industry’s speed, its data obsession, and its relentless focus on the user. The winners of 2026 and beyond will be the platforms that treat innovation as a daily habit, not a one-time project.

title: Firearms training in Kogi not politically motivated – Police
description:
The Kogi State Police Command has refuted claims that the firearms training going on in Ankpa Local Government Area of the state has a political undertone, describing it as legitimate.
A statement issued on Sunday by the command’s spokesperson, Salisu Afusat, stated that the clarification became nec
content:
The Kogi State Police Command has refuted claims that the firearms training going on in Ankpa Local Government Area of the state has a political undertone, describing it as legitimate.

A statement issued on Sunday by the command’s spokesperson, Salisu Afusat, stated that the clarification became necessary due to a viral video circulating on social media alleging the claim.

“The command wishes to clarify that the allegation is false and does not reflect the true nature or purpose of the exercise,” she stated.

The command’s spokesperson said that preliminary investigations have established that the activity is a legitimate training programme organised by the Kogi State Vigilante Service, involving members of its Mining and Boundary Vigilante Group.

“The training, which has been ongoing for the past four days, is aimed at ensuring the proper handling and utilisation of newly acquired firearms by its personnel as part of efforts to strengthen the state’s security architecture,” the command noted.

It also confirmed that the exercise was duly communicated to the relevant security authorities before its commencement, including details of the exercise and the names and photographs of personnel selected for the training.

Afusat said, “During preliminary interviews, the originator of the viral video explained that his intention was to draw the attention of security agencies to the exercise to ascertain its legitimacy, in keeping with the security advocacy principle of ‘See Something, Say Something.'”

She said that while encouraging public cooperation and vigilance, the command urges residents to exercise caution when sharing information on social media and refrain from circulating unverified claims capable of causing unnecessary panic, tension or public unrest.

“Members of the public are advised to channel security concerns to the appropriate authorities for verification and necessary action. The command acknowledges the importance of public vigilance and encourages citizens to report activities that raise security concerns.”

She said that the command recognises the significant contributions of the KSVS to security operations across the state, as well as its collaborative operations with the police and other security agencies.

She noted that the command remains committed to ensuring that these activities are properly monitored and conducted within the ambit of the law.

The post Firearms training in Kogi not politically motivated – Police appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

content:
From Taiwo Oluwadare, Ibadan

The National Union of Road Transport Workers (NURTW), Oyo State chapter, has issued a seven-day ultimatum to Governor Seyi Makinde, declaring that its members will resume full operations at motor parks across the state on November 23, 2026, irrespective of government approval.

The union said the decision followed what it described as seven and a half years of illegal proscription, injustice, hunger, humiliation and the alleged loss of several members since the state government suspended its activities.

In a statement jointly signed by its Chairman, Alhaji Abideen Olajide, popularly known as Ejiogbe, and Secretary, Comrade Lekan Alesinloye, on Sunday, the union described the ultimatum, which runs from November 16 to November 23, as its final warning to the state government.

The union also said it had alerted the Federal Government, the General Officer Commanding (GOC), the Department of State Services (DSS), the Oyo State Commissioner of Police and the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) of its intention to enforce a court judgment restoring its operations.

“We are alerting the Federal Government; GOC; Director of DSS and the Commissioner of Police that we will implement the court judgment by ourselves because the State Governor has failed us,” the statement read.

The union added that it was prepared for any eventuality, including the possible declaration of a state of emergency, insisting that it had suffered enough under the present administration.

“We don’t mind if the State of Emergency is declared. We are ready. Enough is enough. We are putting the State NLC on notice too,” the leaders said.

The NURTW said its decision was anchored on the unanimous judgment of the Court of Appeal, Ibadan Division, delivered on September 26, 2025, in Appeal No. CA/IB/263/2022.

In the judgment, Justice Kenneth Amadi held that the state government had failed to justify the suspension of the union’s activities on the grounds of breach of peace, law and order.

The appellate court consequently allowed the appeal, set aside the suspension of the union’s operations in Oyo State and overturned the judgment of the lower court.

The union said it had obtained the Certified True Copy of the judgment, dated October 3, 2025, but accused the Makinde administration of failing to implement the court’s decision.

It also cited a Notice of Preliminary Objection dated April 23, 2026, filed by the Attorney-General and Commissioner for Justice, Mr Abiodun Aikomo, in which the state government reportedly stated that it had not done anything to prevent the NURTW from operating in the state.

“With the Attorney-General now on record that government is not preventing NURTW from operating, we expect full compliance without further delay, victimisation or harassment of our members at motor parks,” the union said.

However, the NURTW accused the Attorney-General of misrepresenting the appellate court’s judgment during a recent multi-stakeholder meeting convened by the Commissioner of Police following the union’s request for security protection ahead of its planned return to the parks.

The union said it had earlier written to the Attorney-General through Falana & Falana’s Chambers in a letter dated June 26, 2026, describing his interpretation of the judgment as a calculated misrepresentation of a binding court decision.

It maintained that the appellate court’s decision setting aside the suspension of its operations was sufficient to restore its operational status without requiring another court order.

Citing Section 287(2) of the 1999 Constitution, the union argued that all authorities in the country were constitutionally bound to enforce decisions of the Court of Appeal.

It warned that any continued obstruction of its members’ activities would amount to deliberate and continuing contempt of court.

The union consequently demanded that the Attorney-General withdraw his interpretation of the judgment, advise the state government and persons acting as park managers to vacate the motor parks, and publicly acknowledge the binding nature of the appellate court’s decision.

It also called on the Commissioner of Police to provide immediate security for its members, direct Area Commanders and Divisional Police Officers to ensure compliance with the judgment, and arrest anyone found obstructing its activities.

Meanwhile, the union raised concerns over an alleged acquisition of firearms and ammunition by the Park Management System (PMS) to confront its members during their planned resumption.

“We have it on good authority that the PMS in the state have acquired guns to fight our union members. We are ready for them,” the union leaders alleged.

The NURTW insisted that its planned return to the motor parks was not an attempt to foment violence but an effort to resume lawful activities following the appellate court’s decision.

It described its members as breadwinners who deserved dignity and the opportunity to earn a living, rather than continued exclusion from their means of livelihood.

“An injustice to one is an injustice to all,” the union leaders declared, adding that “enough is enough.”

The post Oyo NURTW gives Makinde seven-day ultimatum, threatens to reclaim motor parks appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: 2027: Peter Obi condemns attack on Kwankwaso’s convoy in Kano
description:
Former Anambra State Governor and presidential candidate of the National Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has condemned the reported attack on the convoy of former Kano State Governor, Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, in Bichi Local Government Area of Kano State.
The attack reportedly left several members
content:
Former Anambra State Governor and presidential candidate of the National Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has condemned the reported attack on the convoy of former Kano State Governor, Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, in Bichi Local Government Area of Kano State.

The attack reportedly left several members of Kwankwaso’s entourage injured, while about seven vehicles were vandalised.

Obi, who disclosed the incident in a statement posted on his X handle on Monday, described Kwankwaso as his brother and running mate, expressing sadness over the attack.

He said political differences should not be used to justify violence, intimidation or destruction of property, warning that such incidents should not become part of Nigeria’s political culture.

“Democracy is not warfare. Political differences should never be a reason to resort to violence, intimidation or the destruction of property.

“Every Nigerian, regardless of political affiliation, has the constitutional right to participate in the democratic process without fear of attack,” Obi said.

He called on the Nigeria Police Force and other security agencies to investigate the incident, identify those responsible, including anyone suspected of sponsoring the attack, and ensure they are brought to justice.

The former governor also expressed solidarity with Kwankwaso, the Kano State leadership of the NDC and others affected by the incident, while wishing those injured a speedy recovery.

Obi reiterated his commitment to peaceful political engagement ahead of the 2027 general elections, insisting that political change should be pursued through persuasion, ideas and the ballot rather than violence.

The post 2027: Peter Obi condemns attack on Kwankwaso’s convoy in Kano appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Yobe NASU Issues Fresh 14-Day Ultimatum Over Unresolved Members’ Welfare
description: The Non-Academic Staff Union of Educational and Associated Institutions (NASU), Yobe State Council, has issued an additional 14-day ultimatum to the Yobe State Government over the unresolved welfare package of its members or face possible industrial action.The Chairman of the Council, Ali Usman, in
content:
The Non-Academic Staff Union of Educational and Associated Institutions (NASU), Yobe State Council, has issued an additional 14-day ultimatum to the Yobe State Government over the unresolved welfare package of its members or face possible industrial action.

The Chairman of the Council, Ali Usman, in a press statement on Monday, revealed the additional 14-day ultimatum was in the spirit of constructive engagement with the government, having received its response.

“NASU wishes to inform its members, the general public and relevant stakeholders that it has resolved to grant the Yobe State Government an additional fourteen (14) day ultimatum to address the outstanding welfare demands affecting Non-Academic Staff in State-Owned Tertiary Institutions”

“This decision followed the receipt of the Government’s response dated 10th November, 2026, indicating that the issues raised by the Union are receiving attention”

“After carefully considering the Government’s response at its meeting held on 12th November, 2026, the State Council resolved, in the spirit of constructive engagement and industrial harmony, to extend the initial ultimatum by another fourteen (14) days, effective from 12th November, 2026, and expiring on 26th November, 2026,” the statement reads in part.

The Union emphasised that the extension granted is in good faith and should not be misconstrued as a withdrawal, abandonment, or compromise of its legitimate demands; rather, it reflected.

NASU’s commitment to peaceful engagement and its willingness to give the Government another opportunity to address the longstanding concerns.

The outstanding demands include Implementation of the 65-Year Retirement Age, Implementation of the Reviewed 2024 Salary Table (CONTEDISS), Implementation of the Consolidated Non-Teaching Tools Allowance (CONTTA) and Earned Allowance (EA).

NASU therefore calls on the Yobe State Government and the relevant authorities to utilise the additional period to expedite the necessary approvals and take concrete steps towards implementing the outstanding demands of the workers’ welfare, dignity and legitimate entitlements it deserves.

The post Yobe NASU Issues Fresh 14-Day Ultimatum Over Unresolved Members’ Welfare appeared first on Channels Television.

title: 17 Killed In Two Mass Shootings In South Africa — Police
description: Seventeen people have been killed in two separate shootings in South Africa, police said on Monday, as the crime-weary country battles persistently high murder rates.Roughly 60 people are killed in the country on average a day, according to police statistics, with motives ranging from the drugs trad
content:
Seventeen people have been killed in two separate shootings in South Africa, police said on Monday, as the crime-weary country battles persistently high murder rates.

Roughly 60 people are killed in the country on average a day, according to police statistics, with motives ranging from the drugs trade and illegal mining to competition over minibus taxi routes.

In one incident, nine bodies were found early Monday in an informal settlement outside the capital Pretoria, police said.

“All nine were found in a shack with gunshot wounds this morning,” a spokeswoman said.

The dead were six men and three women.

The second killing occurred in a semi-rural area outside the eastern city of Pietermaritzburg, where police found a bullet-riddled vehicle after responding to reports of a shooting late Sunday.

“Inside the vehicle police found eight men who had multiple gunshot wounds and were certified dead at the scene,” a police statement said.

The men had not yet been identified, and it was too early to speculate on a motive, KwaZulu-Natal province police spokesman Colonel Robert Netshiunda told the Newzroom Afrika broadcaster.

“We have seen these kinds of shootings before and there have been different motives from stock theft-related, to drugs-related to taxi violence,” he said.

AFP

title: 2027: NDC will defeat Tinubu’s government, Babachir Lawal declares
description:
A chieftain of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Babachir Lawal, has expressed confidence that the party will defeat President Bola Tinubu’s administration in the 2027 general elections.
Lawal said the party had established structures across the country and was preparing to challenge the ruling
content:
A chieftain of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Babachir Lawal, has expressed confidence that the party will defeat President Bola Tinubu’s administration in the 2027 general elections.

Lawal said the party had established structures across the country and was preparing to challenge the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) at the polls.

He made the remarks during an interview on ARISE News, where he also cited his experience in opposition politics under former President Muhammadu Buhari and the current administration as an advantage in understanding the political landscape.

“The NDC will defeat this government. We have put structures in place, and having been in the opposition under both Buhari and Tinubu, I understand the political terrain, recognise the signs and know the loopholes we need to address,” he said.

Lawal also expressed confidence in the popularity of the party’s prominent figures, Peter Obi and Rabiu Kwankwaso, saying they enjoyed considerable public support.

According to him, the crowds attending their political rallies without financial inducement reflect the genuine backing they receive from Nigerians.

“Peter Obi and Kwankwaso also enjoy the grace of God and genuine support from the people, as seen in the large crowds that turn up at their rallies without being paid,” the NDC chieftain said.

title: 2027: APC started political violence, Babachir Lawal alleges
description:
A chieftain of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Babachir Lawal, has accused the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) of being responsible for the outbreak of political violence in the country ahead of the 2027 general elections.
Lawal made the allegation during an interview on ARISE News, wh
content:
A chieftain of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Babachir Lawal, has accused the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) of being responsible for the outbreak of political violence in the country ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Lawal made the allegation during an interview on ARISE News, where he discussed the attacks on opposition members and the need for them to prepare to defend themselves.

He argued that when opposition politicians lose confidence in the ability of the government and the law to guarantee a fair political environment, they are compelled to prepare for possible threats.

“Once you lose faith in the ability of the law or the government to provide a free and fair environment for you to operate, you begin to prepare for whatever may come your way. After all, who started the violence? It was the APC, the party in government,” he said.

The former Secretary to the Government of the Federation questioned whether opposition members should remain vulnerable to attacks without taking steps to protect themselves.

He further suggested that the incidents of political violence in Lagos were linked to the experiences of previous elections.

“What is happening in Lagos, in particular, appears to be a reaction to the experiences of previous elections,” Lawal added.

title: Kenyan, Ivorian Cinema Take Spotlight As 2026 AMAA Delivers Stunning, Historic Sweeps
description: The Africa Movie Academy Awards (AMAA) delivered a night of stunning upsets and historic sweeps, with Kenyan and Ivorian cinema firmly taking the spotlight at this year’s ceremony.​While the night was a celebration of cinematic excellence across the continent and the diaspora, two films emerge
content:
The Africa Movie Academy Awards (AMAA) delivered a night of stunning upsets and historic sweeps, with Kenyan and Ivorian cinema firmly taking the spotlight at this year’s ceremony.

​While the night was a celebration of cinematic excellence across the continent and the diaspora, two films emerged as the undeniable titans of the evening: Kenya’s One Woman, One Bra and Côte d’Ivoire’s Colours of Exile.

In terms of qualitative prestige, the night belonged to Kenya. One Woman, One Bra was crowned the biggest winner in quality, taking home the highly coveted Best Film award. The cinematic masterpiece didn’t stop there; it also captured Best Film in an African Language, while its visionary creator, Vincho Nchogu, was honored with the award for Best Debut Feature Film by a Director. The triple victory cemented the film’s status as a critical darling and a landmark achievement in contemporary East African cinema.

If Kenya took the night’s biggest prize, Côte d’Ivoire dominated the sheer volume of accolades. Colours of Exile proved to be an unstoppable force, securing a leading four awards to become the biggest winner in numbers. The Ivorian powerhouse swept major categories, with Azlorabe Alaoui winning Best Director and Naku Sy Savane taking home Best Actress in a Leading Role. The film’s immersive technical execution was also recognized with wins for Achievement in Cinematography and Achievement in Sound.

Nigeria maintained a formidable presence throughout the ceremony, demonstrating its continued technical and narrative prowess with a total of eight wins. The Herd was a standout, securing three awards: Achievement in Production Design, Achievement in Make-up, and a Best Actress in a Supporting Role win for Linda Ejiofor.

​Wale Ojo delivered a major acting victory for Nigeria, winning Best Actor in a Leading Role for Light Out.

title: From Mini LED pioneer to display inventor: how TCL built the technology others are still trying to reach
description:
TCL’s launch of SQD-Mini LED TV is not the beginning of a story. It is the result of a decade of manufacturing investment, panel science and a strategic decision to own the entire display chain, from the quantum dot lab to the living room wall.
Attributed to TCL MEABG SPOKESPERSON / REGIONAL DIRECTO
content:
TCL’s launch of SQD-Mini LED TV is not the beginning of a story. It is the result of a decade of manufacturing investment, panel science and a strategic decision to own the entire display chain, from the quantum dot lab to the living room wall.

Attributed to TCL MEABG SPOKESPERSON / REGIONAL DIRECTOR: Mr. Daniel Ray, Director of Sales / General Manager of West Africa

In Nigeria, as in every major market across the Middle East and Africa, televisions have become one of the most consequential purchase decisions a household makes. Not because the price is high (though it often is) but because the screen at the centre of the living room is now expected to replace the cinema, host the football match, enable competitive gaming, and do all of this without compromising when the afternoon sun floods the room.

Meeting that expectation requires more than a product launch. It requires a foundation that most television brands simply do not have. TCL does.The company’s introduction of SQD-Mini LED TV to Nigeria in 2026 is the sixth generation of a display technology journey that began in 2019, when TCL launched its first QD-Mini LED television, two years before the term “Mini LED TV” had entered mainstream media coverage. That head start was not accidental. TCL CSOT, the company’s display panel manufacturing division, had been developing quantum dot and Mini LED integration for years before the first commercial product reached a showroom.

Today, TCL CSOT is the world’s number one manufacturer of televisions at 85 inches and above, holding a 28.8 percent global market share in that segment. It operates twelve panel production lines with cumulative investment exceeding 300 billion RMB. When TCL says it has invented a new display technology, the claim comes from a company that owns the factory, the quantum dot chemistry, the backlight engineering and the panel itself.

That distinction matters in a market where premium television claims are abundant but engineering credentials are rarely scrutinised. Most television brands do not manufacture their own panels. They design products around components sourced from a small number of suppliers, including, in many cases, TCL CSOT itself. When TCL develops SQD-Mini LED TV, competitors are buying panels from the same ecosystem TCL helped build.

SQD-Mini LED TV combines three core advances: Super QLED, which improves quantum dot particle purity to eliminate colour imprecision at the conversion stage; Precise Dimming Series, which enables one dimming zone to perform with the efficacy of multiple, eliminating blooming and halo effects; and Ultra Color Filter, which reduces colour impurities at the filter layer for accurate colour reproduction across the entire screen. Together, they address brightness, colour and contrast at the panel level, not through software correction after the fact. The result: 10,000 nits peak brightness, more than 20,000 local dimming zones, zero colour crosstalk, and a 60,000-hour lifespan, twice that of OLED.

In Nigeria, where household entertainment investment is on the rise, the timing of this launch reflects TCL’s understanding that the premium display conversation has permanently changed. In 2026, that conversation belongs to SQD-Mini LED TV.

title: N220bn solar push: ECN boss rallies youths behind Tinubu
description:
From Charity Nwakaudu, Abuja
The Director-General of the Energy Commission of Nigeria (ECN), Dr Mustapha Abdullahi, has urged Nigerian youths to support President Bola Tinubu’s second-term ambition, citing the administration’s investments in solar energy and renewable power development.
Abdullahi sa
content:
From Charity Nwakaudu, Abuja

The Director-General of the Energy Commission of Nigeria (ECN), Dr Mustapha Abdullahi, has urged Nigerian youths to support President Bola Tinubu’s second-term ambition, citing the administration’s investments in solar energy and renewable power development.

Abdullahi said continuity in leadership would enable the Federal Government to consolidate ongoing reforms, expand renewable energy projects and accelerate Nigeria’s quest for energy security.

The ECN boss, who highlighted the administration’s achievements in the energy sector, said the government had made significant investments in solar power as part of efforts to reduce dependence on the national grid and expensive diesel-powered generators.

He identified the National Public Sector Solarisation Initiative, backed by a reported N220 billion commitment, as one of the major interventions designed to provide alternative electricity to public institutions.

The programme targets the delivery of more than 100 megawatts of alternative energy to 72 primary healthcare centres and tertiary institutions nationwide.

The Energy Commission, he said, had provided technical support through energy audits, load assessments, project designs and coordination.

Among the flagship projects is the 4MWp solar photovoltaic mini-grid at Aminu Kano Teaching Hospital, Kano, which had reached 85 per cent completion as of May 2026.

Other beneficiary institutions include the University of Abuja, Bayero University Kano, Enugu Research Centre and Aliko Dangote University of Science and Technology, Wudil.

Abdullahi said the projects would reduce electricity costs and guarantee more reliable power for healthcare delivery, teaching and research.

He also listed the $750 million Distributed Access through Renewable Energy Scale-up (DARES) programme, supported by the World Bank, as another major intervention to expand electricity access in underserved and off-grid communities.

On the achievements of the Commission, the ECN boss highlighted its strategic partnership with LONGi, an international solar technology company, to promote local solar manufacturing, technology transfer and the development of Nigeria’s renewable energy value chain.

He said the partnership would reduce dependence on imported solar technologies while creating opportunities for local engineers, technicians and entrepreneurs.

The Commission has also strengthened collaboration with China Energy on renewable energy development, grid modernisation and technical cooperation.

Another major initiative is the establishment of the Barefoot Renewable Energy College at Osara, Kogi State, to train young Nigerians in solar installation, maintenance and other clean energy technologies.

Abdullahi said the initiative would equip youths with practical skills to benefit from emerging employment opportunities in the renewable energy industry.

The Commission has equally advanced the country’s clean mobility agenda with the commissioning of an electric vehicle charging station at its Abuja headquarters.

It has also established the National Committee on Renewable Energy, Energy Efficiency, Innovation and Certification to strengthen research, technical standards and collaboration among stakeholders.

Abdullahi further identified the promotion of Minimum Energy Performance Standards for cooling and refrigeration equipment as part of efforts to reduce energy consumption and electricity costs.

He maintained that renewable energy development offered enormous opportunities for Nigerian youths to become manufacturers, installers, researchers, engineers and entrepreneurs.

He urged young Nigerians to support the Tinubu administration’s second-term bid, insisting that policy consistency and sustained investment were necessary to deepen ongoing reforms and transform the country’s energy sector.

According to him, sustaining the momentum would help deliver affordable electricity, create jobs and strengthen Nigeria’s industrial capacity.

title: Manufacturing growth doubles to 3.2% amid easing cost pressures
description:
By Yinka Kolawole



Nigeria’s manufacturing sector recorded a 3.2 per cent year-on-year (YoY) growth in the second quarter of 2026, up from 1.6 per cent in the corresponding period of 2025, reflecting improved industrial activity amid gradual easing of operating pressures.



The performance, accor
content:
By Yinka Kolawole

Nigeria’s manufacturing sector recorded a 3.2 per cent year-on-year (YoY) growth in the second quarter of 2026, up from 1.6 per cent in the corresponding period of 2025, reflecting improved industrial activity amid gradual easing of operating pressures.

The performance, according to data from the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS), indicates a gradual recovery in the sector, supported by stronger activities across food and beverages, chemicals, pharmaceuticals, cement and refining subsectors.

The improvement was also driven by relative stability in the foreign exchange market, which enhanced manufacturers’ access to imported raw materials and other production inputs, allowing businesses to improve procurement and inventory planning.

Similarly, easing inflationary pressures helped reduce uncertainty around input costs, providing some relief to manufacturers and supporting production and business planning.

The growth underscores manufacturing’s continued importance to Nigeria’s economic diversification efforts, particularly its role in expanding non-oil production, creating jobs and strengthening domestic value chains.

However, despite the improved performance, manufacturers continue to contend with structural challenges, including high energy costs, inadequate infrastructure, logistics bottlenecks and elevated financing costs.

These constraints have continued to undermine competitiveness, limit investment capacity and slow production expansion across several industrial segments.

The moderation in inflation is expected to provide further relief to businesses and households, potentially supporting consumer demand and enabling manufacturers to plan production more effectively.

Nevertheless, persistent geopolitical tensions in the Middle East remain a source of concern for the sector, given their potential implications for global energy prices and supply chains.

Any escalation could trigger higher crude oil and gas prices, increase transportation and production costs, and reverse some of the gains from easing domestic inflationary pressures.

For Nigerian manufacturers, sustaining the growth momentum will therefore depend not only on macroeconomic stability but also on addressing persistent structural constraints, particularly energy supply, infrastructure deficits and access to affordable financing.

title: 2027: Kaduna students rally behind Tinubu, Uba Sani
description:
From Charity Nwakaudu, Abuja
The Kaduna State chapter of JAGABA/UBA Students’ Mandate 2027 has unveiled campus ambassadors to mobilise students across tertiary institutions for the re-election of President Bola Tinubu and Governor Uba Sani in 2027.
The group said its support for the two leaders was
content:
From Charity Nwakaudu, Abuja

The Kaduna State chapter of JAGABA/UBA Students’ Mandate 2027 has unveiled campus ambassadors to mobilise students across tertiary institutions for the re-election of President Bola Tinubu and Governor Uba Sani in 2027.

The group said its support for the two leaders was driven by their investments in education, skills acquisition and youth empowerment.

Speaking at the inauguration, the convener of the group, Comrade Munzali Abubakar, described the Campus Ambassadors initiative as a strategic platform to mobilise students and promote awareness of government policies and interventions in the education sector.

He said the ambassadors would establish a strong network across tertiary institutions to educate students on the achievements of the Tinubu and Uba Sani administrations.

Abubakar said the Federal Government’s Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND) scheme had expanded access to tertiary education, benefiting over 1.6 million students, with more than ₦322 billion disbursed.

He also cited the government’s Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) programme, which targets over one million youths across 1,600 centres, offering free tuition, monthly stipends and starter packs.

The convener further highlighted the Federal Government’s agreement with the Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU), which he said had improved university operations, salaries, research funding and staff welfare.

On Kaduna State, Abubakar commended Uba Sani for allocating 25 per cent of the state’s budget to education in 2024 and increasing it to 26.14 per cent in 2025.

He said the governor had constructed 62 secondary schools, comprising 39 junior and 23 senior schools, while approving 50 additional schools.

According to him, the administration has also delivered 2,326 classrooms and renovated 707 others across the state.

He listed the $62.8 million Reaching Out-of-School Children (ROOSC) project, being implemented with the Kuwait Fund and other development partners, as another major intervention.

The project is expected to provide 102 climate-resilient schools and rehabilitate 170 learning centres across the state’s 23 local government areas.

Abubakar also disclosed that over ₦1 billion had been invested in scholarships, student loans and other educational support programmes.

On teachers’ development, he said 33,137 teachers, head teachers and school support officers had benefited from professional development programmes covering modern teaching methods, computer literacy and classroom management.

He further highlighted the establishment of three Vocational and Technology Skills Acquisition Cities across the state’s three senatorial zones, targeting 12,000 trainees in the first year and 24,000 in the second.

The centres will provide training in 13 vocational areas, including welding, solar panel installation, fashion design and aluminium fabrication.

The group also cited the transformation of Panteka Market into an industrial and vocational skills development hub, noting that the market accommodates more than 38,000 artisans.

Other initiatives highlighted included the Kaduna Youth Economic Empowerment Programme (K-YEEP), which has supported over 6,000 startups, and the Kaduna TechHUBs, where young people receive training in artificial intelligence, cybersecurity and robotics.

Abubakar also commended the AREWA LADIES-4-TECH initiative for equipping 5,100 women with ICT skills, as well as career fairs that reportedly facilitated over 300 job placements.

He said the inauguration of the Kaduna State Skills Development Council had further strengthened the state’s framework for coordinating skills development programmes.

The newly inaugurated ambassadors were charged with taking the mobilisation campaign to campuses and engaging students on government policies and programmes.

Abubakar said: “We cannot afford to return to a past where young people were denied opportunities, schools lacked basic facilities and students struggled to access quality education.”

The post 2027: Kaduna students rally behind Tinubu, Uba Sani appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: ‘Democracy is not warfare’ – Peter Obi condemns Kwankwaso convoy attack
description:
…Kano govt dismisses attack claims
Presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi has condemned a reported attack on the convoy of his running mate, Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, in Bichi Local Government Area of Kano State.
Some political thugs allegedly attacked Kwankwa
content:
…Kano govt dismisses attack claims

Presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi has condemned a reported attack on the convoy of his running mate, Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, in Bichi Local Government Area of Kano State.

Some political thugs allegedly attacked Kwankwaso and members of his entourage on Sunday evening as they were leaving the area after a series of political engagements across parts of the state.

However, the Kano State Government has dismissed the reported attack as a fabrication by the Kwankwasiyya Movement to curry public sympathy.

In a Monday statement, Obi said he was deeply saddened by reports of the attack on Kwankwaso and members of his entourage.

“I strongly condemn this unfortunate incident. Reports indicate that several members of the entourage sustained injuries, while about seven vehicles were vandalised. This is unacceptable and must not be allowed to become part of our political culture,” he stated.

Obi said democracy is not warfare and political differences should never lead to violence.

The former Anambra governor stated, “Democracy is not warfare. Political differences should never be a reason to resort to violence, intimidation or the destruction of property. Every Nigerian, regardless of political affiliation, has the constitutional right to participate in the democratic process without fear of attack.

“We must not allow violence to take the place of dialogue, nor intimidation to silence those who hold different political opinions. Our democracy can only grow when we respect one another, uphold the rule of law and recognise that political competition is not a battle against fellow Nigerians.”

He called on the Nigeria Police Force and all relevant security agencies to immediately investigate the incident, identify those responsible, including anyone found to have sponsored the attack, and ensure they are brought to justice.

“No individual should be above the law, regardless of political position or influence,” Obi said.

He expressed solidarity with Kwankwaso, the Kano State NDC leadership and everyone affected by the incident, and wished those injured a speedy recovery.

“Our commitment to building a new Nigeria remains unwavering. We believe that change must come through peaceful engagement, persuasion, ideas and the ballot, not violence.

“Nigeria belongs to all of us. We may belong to different political parties, but we remain one people with a common destiny. No political ambition is worth the life of any Nigerian,” Obi said.

Meanwhile, the Kano State Government dismissed the reported attack as a fabrication.

In a Sunday post on Facebook, the state Commissioner for Information, Sanusi Bature Dawakin Tofa, accused the Kwankwasiyya movement of inventing the alleged incident in Bichi and challenged its members to provide evidence to substantiate the claim.

He said, “In an attempt to generate public sympathy, the Kwankwasiyya team has framed themselves a fictitious attack in Bichi, no pictures, no videos.”

The post ‘Democracy is not warfare’ – Peter Obi condemns Kwankwaso convoy attack appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Amazon Loses 40 Satellites In Failed Rocket Launch
description: Amazon lost 40 satellites from its internet constellation on Sunday after a rocket failed during the first of several dozen flights the tech giant has purchased, marking a setback in Jeff Bezos’ race against Elon Musk’s Starlink.The Vulcan rocket operated by United Launch Alliance (ULA)
content:
Amazon lost 40 satellites from its internet constellation on Sunday after a rocket failed during the first of several dozen flights the tech giant has purchased, marking a setback in Jeff Bezos’ race against Elon Musk’s Starlink.

The Vulcan rocket operated by United Launch Alliance (ULA) lifted off at 12:40 pm local time (1740 GMT) from Cape Canaveral, Florida, and “suffered an anomaly 10 minutes into the flight and failed to deliver the Amazon mission to orbit,” ULA said in a statement.

ULA is a joint venture between Boeing and Lockheed Martin, and the company said on X it “exists to provide assured access to space for our nation and for the customers who depend on us” by taking on “some of the hardest missions in spaceflight.”

Amazon has purchased 38 launches from ULA, and over the long term, Vulcan is supposed to launch nearly half of the first generation of Amazon Leo, which is to comprise 3,232 satellites.

The e-commerce giant founded by Bezos has launched around 400 satellites since April 2025.

Sunday’s failed launch was going to send up the largest batch of satellites ever attempted for Amazon, which has not carried out any launches since July.

Amazon had announced plans to use the satellites to open its commercial internet service Amazon Leo in 2026.

“There is risk with any launch, and that’s especially true for inaugural missions,” Amazon Leo posted to X, adding it believes ULA will “learn from this mission and deliver on their long-term plans for Vulcan.”

The setback came a day after Musk’s SpaceX deployed 26 large Starlink satellites during a test flight of its Starship mega-rocket, pulling off the first-ever “catch” of a spaceship to demonstrate the feasibility of reusable rockets.

Bezos-founded Blue Origin’s New Glenn rocket, which Amazon is also relying on for launches, has been grounded since an explosion during a test in May.

The billionaire is also the main commercial customer of French company Arianespace, which is scheduled to launch 36 Amazon satellites aboard its Ariane 6 rocket “no earlier than” November 23 from Kourou in French Guiana.

AFP

title: Tinubu govt eliminated 15,000 terrorists in 3yrs, 130,000 Boko Haram fighters surrendered – APC Campaign Council
description: The All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council (APC-PCC) has disclosed that the military has killed more than 15,000 Boko Haram terrorists and bandits in the past three years, while over 130,000 Boko Haram fighters and their dependents have surrendered under the Federal Government’s reh
content:
The All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council (APC-PCC) has disclosed that the military has killed more than 15,000 Boko Haram terrorists and bandits in the past three years, while over 130,000 Boko Haram fighters and their dependents have surrendered under the Federal Government’s rehabilitation programme.

The council’s spokesperson, Dele Alake, made this known in a statement on Sunday, attributing the figures to the scale of military operations under President Bola Tinubu’s administration.

According to Alake, Tinubu is determined to end the 17-year insurgency and other security challenges through a Five-Year Strategic Defence Operations Plan.

He said the more than 130,000 Boko Haram fighters and dependents surrendered through Operation Safe Corridor, the Federal Government’s programme for rehabilitating repentant insurgents.

The statement said the figures reflected the administration’s two-pronged approach to tackling insecurity through sustained military operations and non-kinetic interventions.

It described the Five-Year Strategic Defence Operations Plan as a long-term framework designed to align defence priorities, operational requirements, military capabilities and expenditure with Nigeria’s present and anticipated security challenges.

The council said the plan was intended to reposition the country’s security architecture towards a more coordinated, intelligence-driven and technology-enabled system capable of tackling terrorism, banditry, kidnapping and other forms of criminality.

On military restructuring, Alake said Tinubu had established four new Army divisions and restructured existing formations to expand operational coverage, decentralise military operations and enable troops to respond more quickly to security threats.

He also disclosed that the president had approved the establishment of two additional Army depots in Osogbo, Osun State, and Amasiri-Edda, Ebonyi State.

According to the statement, each facility has the capacity to train 6,000 recruits at a time, bringing their combined training capacity to 12,000.

The Osogbo facility is already training 5,210 recruits, a development the council said would help reduce recruitment turnaround time and increase the number of soldiers available for deployment.

As part of efforts to strengthen military operations, Tinubu has also approved the recruitment of an additional 28,000 soldiers, alongside 50,000 police officers to boost internal security and improve policing capacity.

The statement further highlighted investments in military accommodation and operational infrastructure, including a 700-unit barracks project in Ikere-Ekiti, Ekiti State.

The project, according to the council, is designed to provide military personnel with improved living conditions and essential facilities.

Alake said the Federal Government was ensuring that investments in the security sector were guided by identified threats, operational requirements and national priorities.

He added that the strategic plan was expected to improve combat readiness, address critical capability gaps, optimise available resources and reduce unnecessary expenditure.

“The plan is expected to strengthen combat readiness, address critical capability gaps, optimise available resources and minimise unnecessary expenditure and wastage,” the statement said.
