title: Uganda woos Dangote for oil refinery, fertiliser projects
description:
Uganda has approached the Dangote Group to invest in its proposed billion-dollar oil refinery, fertiliser and salt production projects as the East African country seeks to transform its natural resources into finished products, create jobs and reduce dependence on imports.
 The country made the inve
content:
Uganda has approached the Dangote Group to invest in its proposed billion-dollar oil refinery, fertiliser and salt production projects as the East African country seeks to transform its natural resources into finished products, create jobs and reduce dependence on imports.

 The country made the investment pitch during a visit to the Dangote Petroleum Refinery & Petrochemicals and Dangote Fertiliser Limited in Lagos by a delegation led by its Minister of Energy and Mineral Development, Dr Monica Musenero Masanza, and Minister of State for Finance, Planning and Economic Development (Privatisation and Investment), Hajjat Amina Mukalazi.

According to a statement on Sunday, the ministers called on Africa’s richest industrialist, Aliko Dangote, to partner with Uganda in developing its petroleum and mineral resources, particularly through the proposed 60,000-barrel-per-day refinery in the Hoima area.

They also identified opportunities in fertiliser blending, phosphate processing and salt manufacturing, expressing the government’s readiness to support the proposed investments and remove obstacles to their implementation.

President and Chief Executive of Dangote Industries Limited, Dangote, received the delegation alongside senior executives of the group, including the Group Vice President, Devakumar Edwin.

Presenting Uganda’s proposals, Mukalazi invited Dangote to take a leading role in the planned refinery, describing the project as a major industrial priority for the country.

She said the group’s experience in engineering, construction and operating large industrial facilities would be valuable to the project.

“You have shown that an African company can build world-scale industry in Africa and run it by Africans themselves,” she said.

Mukalazi noted that the refinery could complement the Dangote Group’s proposed refinery in Lamu, Kenya, with the Ugandan facility serving inland markets while the coastal project supplied maritime and coastal markets.

She, however, acknowledged that the estimates presented by the delegation would require technical assessment by Dangote’s team.

The minister stated that Uganda’s crude oil, phosphate and salt deposits offered opportunities for investments that can be connected through shared infrastructure and distribution networks.

“Our crude, our phosphate, our salt are waiting to be turned into fuel, fertilisers and chemicals here in Africa and in Uganda by Africans,” Mukalazi said.

She also invited Dangote to visit Uganda for further discussions, assuring him that the government would support the proposed partnership and address investment bottlenecks.

“Uganda needs Dangote, and now is the right time. Our country is ready and moving rapidly towards industrialisation.

“He (Dangote) would bring investment, technology and opportunities for local participation, as we have seen here today. He has demonstrated what is possible elsewhere, and we believe he can do the same in Uganda,“ she noted.

Mukalazi said the proposed investments would create opportunities for skills development, employment and local businesses, particularly among young people.

Also speaking, Uganda’s Minister of Energy and Mineral Development, Dr Musenero, said the delegation visited the facilities to learn from Dangote’s industrial experience and explore practical areas of collaboration in the country’s petroleum and fertiliser industries.

She identified fertiliser production as a major investment opportunity, explaining that Uganda had mineral resources suitable for manufacturing fertilisers but had not been successful in converting them into finished products.

In his remarks, the Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Dangote Petroleum Refinery & Petrochemicals, David Bird, said the presence of the two ministers demonstrated Uganda’s commitment to exploring an industrial partnership with the group.

He said the country had significant natural resources and human capital, alongside the political commitment required to pursue industrialisation.

“Uganda has incredible natural resources and human capital. As both ministers have expressed during this visit, there is also no shortage of ambition or political will to pursue industrialisation,” he said.

The post Uganda woos Dangote for oil refinery, fertiliser projects appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: FCMB finances 60,000-tonne plastic recycling plant
description:
First City Monument Bank has provided N40bn in machinery and working-capital financing to Polysmart Packaging Limited for a plastic recycling plant with an annual production capacity of 60,000 tonnes in Ileke town, Ogun State.
A statement from the bank on Sunday said that the facility, commissioned
content:
First City Monument Bank has provided N40bn in machinery and working-capital financing to Polysmart Packaging Limited for a plastic recycling plant with an annual production capacity of 60,000 tonnes in Ileke town, Ogun State.

A statement from the bank on Sunday said that the facility, commissioned on 29 October, will convert recovered post-consumer plastic waste into food-grade recycled polyethylene terephthalate materials for manufacturers.

Described by Polysmart as Africa’s largest plastic recycling plant, the investment is expected to strengthen local packaging production, support plastic-waste recovery and reduce Nigeria’s dependence on imported raw materials.

Speaking at the commissioning ceremony, Minister of Environment, Balarabe Lawal, said the facility would improve Nigeria’s capacity to recover and recycle plastic waste while supporting the country’s environmental sustainability objectives.

Ogun State Governor, Dapo Abiodun, described the investment as a demonstration of Nigerian enterprise, innovation and the opportunities created by a supportive investment environment.

FCMB Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer, Yemisi Edun, said the bank’s support reflected its commitment to financing businesses that combine industrial development with environmental responsibility and economic opportunities.

“At FCMB, we believe that financing sustainable businesses is essential to building a resilient economy and securing long-term shared prosperity. By converting recovered plastic into new products, this plant shows how manufacturing and environmental responsibility can work together,” Edun said.

“Polysmart embodies our commitment to sustainable manufacturing practices, environmental sustainability and wealth creation, reflected in our ₦40 billion in funding for machinery and working capital.”

Polysmart Group Managing Director, Wasiu Balogun, said the investment demonstrated the capacity of Nigerian businesses to develop recycling infrastructure that serves local industries and creates opportunities across the waste-recovery chain.

“This is climate action made in Nigeria. The investment demonstrates the capacity of Nigerian businesses to develop world-class recycling infrastructure,” Balogun said.

He said the facility would process up to 100,000 tonnes of mixed plastics annually at full capacity, equivalent to about 6.5 billion bottles.

Balogun added that the operation was expected to generate about 1,000 direct jobs and more than 50,000 indirect jobs across plastic collection, aggregation, transportation and processing.

He also acknowledged FCMB’s longstanding support, saying the bank’s financing and partnership had been instrumental in Polysmart’s growth and expansion.

Polysmart estimates that Nigeria consumes about 600,000 tonnes of virgin PET annually, creating opportunities for locally produced recycled materials to replace some imported resin.

The company projects that the facility could save Nigeria about $72m annually in foreign exchange by reducing imports of virgin resin. Founded in 2013, Polysmart Packaging Limited produces food-grade recycled PET resin and flakes from post-consumer plastic waste.

The post FCMB finances 60,000-tonne plastic recycling plant appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: NEM Insurance appoints former SEC DG to board
description:
NEM Insurance Plc has appointed former Director-General of the Securities and Exchange Commission, Mounir Gwarzo, and Adejoke Teluwo as Non-Executive Directors to its board, effective 28 October, 2026.
 The company disclosed the appointments in a notice filed with the Nigerian Exchange Limited on 9
content:
NEM Insurance Plc has appointed former Director-General of the Securities and Exchange Commission, Mounir Gwarzo, and Adejoke Teluwo as Non-Executive Directors to its board, effective 28 October, 2026.

 The company disclosed the appointments in a notice filed with the Nigerian Exchange Limited on 9 November, 2026.

 Gwarzo was appointed as an Independent Non-Executive Director, while Teluwo joined the board as a Non-Executive Director.

 Gwarzo brings more than 30 years of experience spanning capital market regulation, banking, securities, trade and commerce.

 He previously served as Executive Commissioner in charge of Operations at the SEC before becoming its Director-General.

 His career also includes stints at the Ministry of Trade and Commerce, the Nigerian Stock Exchange, the Federal Mortgage Bank of Nigeria and the SEC.

 At the Federal Mortgage Bank, he served as General Manager and Regional Executive overseeing the bank’s northern operations.

 Gwarzo is currently the Chief Executive Officer of Prime Capital and Investment Limited.

 He holds a bachelor’s degree from Bayero University, Kano, and a master’s degree in Management and Leadership from Robert Kennedy College, in collaboration with York St John University, United Kingdom. He is also a fellow of the Chartered Institute of Stockbrokers.

 Teluwo, on her part, has more than 15 years of experience across regulated businesses and entrepreneurial environments, with expertise in governance, regulatory compliance, enterprise risk management and legal matters.

 She holds an LLB degree from Coventry University, United Kingdom, and previously served as Compliance Lead at Exso Focus Group in London between 2016 and 2019.

 She is currently the Founder and Managing Director of Kintsu, a professional services and workspace enterprise providing operational infrastructure and business solutions.

 NEM Insurance said the appointments would strengthen the board’s collective expertise and effectiveness, adding that it expected the new directors to contribute to the company’s strategic objectives and corporate governance standards.

 The appointments come as the insurer continues to pursue its business objectives in Nigeria’s insurance industry.

The post NEM Insurance appoints former SEC DG to board appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Sovereign Trust Insurance’s assets rise 48% to N41.78bn
description:
Sovereign Trust Insurance Plc increased its total assets by 48 per cent to N41.78bn as of September 2026, from N28.31bn at the end of December 2025, supported by growth in cash holdings, financial investments and reinsurance contract assets.
 The insurer disclosed this in its unaudited financial sta
content:
Sovereign Trust Insurance Plc increased its total assets by 48 per cent to N41.78bn as of September 2026, from N28.31bn at the end of December 2025, supported by growth in cash holdings, financial investments and reinsurance contract assets.

 The insurer disclosed this in its unaudited financial statements for the nine months ended 30 September, 2026, filed with the Nigerian Exchange.

 Cash and cash equivalents rose by 36.3 per cent to N15.94bn from N11.69bn, while investments in financial assets measured at fair value through profit or loss increased to N4.99bn from N2.07bn.

 Reinsurance contract assets recorded one of the largest increases, rising to N9.90bn from N3.95bn, representing a 150.7 per cent increase.

 The company’s statutory deposit also rose to N1.5bn from N315m, while property, plant and equipment increased to N3.08bn from N2.70bn.

 The balance sheet expansion coincided with a return to profitability, as the insurer posted a profit after tax of N1.04bn in the nine months ended September 2026, compared with a N100.53m in the corresponding period of 2025.

 Profit before tax increased to N1.23bn from N171.67m a year earlier.

 The improvement in earnings came despite a decline in insurance revenue, which fell by 21.4 per cent to N31.53bn from N40.13bn in the corresponding period of 2025.

 Insurance service expenses declined by 24.9 per cent to N13.75bn from N18.31bn, while the insurance service result stood at N1.69bn from N1.70bn.

 However, net expenses from reinsurance contracts held remained high at N16.09bn, although they declined from N20.12bn in the previous year.

 Investment returns increased to N3.64bn from N1.53bn, supported by higher investment income and fair value gains on financial assets.

 Shareholders’ funds rose to N21.71bn from N15.66bn at the end of December 2025, partly supported by N5.02bn raised through the issuance of share capital during the period.

 Insurance contract liabilities also increased to N14.09bn from N6.50bn, reflecting higher obligations associated with the company’s insurance business.

 Sovereign Trust Insurance provides general insurance and risk management services to individual and corporate customers.

The post Sovereign Trust Insurance’s assets rise 48% to N41.78bn appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: GOXI combines high claims payments with community development drive
description: GOXI Microinsurance Company Limited is combining insurance claims settlement with community development initiatives, having paid N160.65m to policyholders between January and July 2026 while stepping up interventions in environmental sustainability, women’s empowerment and support for vulnerable gro
content:
GOXI Microinsurance Company Limited is combining insurance claims settlement with community development initiatives, having paid N160.65m to policyholders between January and July 2026 while stepping up interventions in environmental sustainability, women’s empowerment and support for vulnerable groups.

 The company said the claims payments provided financial relief to individuals and businesses affected by unexpected losses, reflecting the role of microinsurance in helping low-income households and small business owners protect their livelihoods.

 The latest payout adds to more than N821m in claims the insurer had previously reported paying to traders, low-income households and small business owners over six years.

 Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of GOXI Microinsurance, Shina Gbadegesin, said claims settlement remained central to the company’s mission of protecting customers against financial shocks.

 He said the value of insurance became evident when policyholders experienced losses and received financial support to recover.

 “The N160.65m paid in claims between January and July 2026 reflects our commitment to honouring our promises and providing timely relief to our policyholders. We will continue to make insurance affordable, accessible and relevant to individuals, families and small businesses,” Gbadegesin said.

 Beyond its claims obligations, the insurer has expanded its corporate social responsibility activities to address social and environmental challenges in its host communities.

 In June 2026, the company organised an environmental clean-up and waste-management awareness campaign at Alade Market in Ikeja, Lagos.

 The exercise brought together employees, traders and other community members to promote responsible waste disposal and improve environmental cleanliness in the market.

 The company also marked International Women’s Day on 9 March, 2026, by visiting three female clients and presenting them with gift items in recognition of women’s contributions to families, businesses and economic development.

 The engagement aligned with the United Nations’ 2026 International Women’s Day theme, ‘Rights. Justice. Action. For ALL Women and Girls.’

 Earlier, in October 2025, GOXI had extended its community intervention to Modupe Cole Memorial Child Care and Treatment Home in Akoka, Lagos, where it supported children and other vulnerable individuals through donations and direct engagement.

 Gbadegesin said the company’s community programmes complemented its core insurance business by addressing broader social and environmental needs.

 “For us, microinsurance and corporate social responsibility are connected by one purpose — protecting people and strengthening communities,” he said.

 He added that while claims payments helped customers recover from unexpected losses, community initiatives enabled the company to contribute to the wellbeing of vulnerable groups and the sustainability of local communities.

 The company said its interventions had helped strengthen stakeholder confidence, improve employee engagement and deepen relationships with host communities.

 GOXI Microinsurance, Nigeria’s first licensed standalone microinsurance company, provides life and non-life insurance products to low-income individuals, households, microenterprises and small businesses under the regulation of the National Insurance Commission.

The post GOXI combines high claims payments with community development drive appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Fortis Global Insurance cuts loss to N1.40bn as revenue rises
description:
Fortis Global Insurance Plc reduced its loss after tax by 35.5 per cent to N1.40bn in the nine months ended September 2026, as a sharp increase in investment income helped cushion rising insurance service expenses.
 The insurer reported a loss after tax of N1.40bn, compared with N2.17bn in the corre
content:
Fortis Global Insurance Plc reduced its loss after tax by 35.5 per cent to N1.40bn in the nine months ended September 2026, as a sharp increase in investment income helped cushion rising insurance service expenses.

 The insurer reported a loss after tax of N1.40bn, compared with N2.17bn in the corresponding period of 2025, according to its unaudited financial statements filed with the Nigerian Exchange.

 Insurance revenue surged by 1,588 per cent to N2.06bn from N122.26m a year earlier, reflecting increased underwriting activity following the company’s recapitalisation.

 However, insurance service expenses rose even faster, increasing by 626 per cent to N3.96bn from N545.77m, leaving the company with an insurance service deficit of N1.90bn.

 The deficit widened by 338 per cent from N434.47m recorded in the corresponding period of 2025, indicating that the growth in premium-related revenue has yet to translate into profitable underwriting operations.

 Investment income provided some relief, rising by 324 per cent to N2.24bn from N527.57m in the previous year.

 Despite the improvement in investment returns, Fortis recorded a loss before tax of N1.38bn, compared with N2.17bn in the corresponding period of 2025.

 The company’s other operating expenses increased sharply to N2.01bn from N285.26m, while other finance costs declined to N71.81m from N1.28bn.

 The insurer’s balance sheet expanded following its recapitalisation, with total assets rising to N48.83bn as of 30 September, 2026, from N25.39bn a year earlier.

 Cash and cash equivalents increased by 134 per cent to N27.45bn from N11.75bn, while financial assets rose to N5.36bn from N907.66m.

 Shareholders’ funds also increased to N37.64bn from N10.01bn, reflecting fresh capital and the conversion of debt into equity.

 The company’s liabilities declined to N11.18bn from N15.38bn, while its outstanding borrowings fell from N6.51bn to zero.

 Fortis said its recapitalisation had strengthened liquidity and solvency and positioned it to meet regulatory obligations under the Nigerian Insurance Industry Reform Act 2025.

 The insurer said its immediate priority was to translate the improved capital position into sustainable profitability, adding that the resolution of legacy issues and stronger balance sheet would support its return to profitability.

 “The Company is now financially stable and fully capitalised. Management’s priority is to translate this stability into sustainable profitability. With the balance sheet repaired and legacy issues resolved, the Company is well-positioned to return to profitability in the coming periods,” the insurer noted.

The post Fortis Global Insurance cuts loss to N1.40bn as revenue rises appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Rainbow coalition for civic education in Berlin
description:
“We pay a price when we deprive children of the exposure to the values, principles, and education they need to make them good citizens.” ~ Justice Sandra Day O’Connor
 It was a rainbow coalition of sorts! From the North, East, West and South of the world, delegates from 23 countries, including mysel
content:
“We pay a price when we deprive children of the exposure to the values, principles, and education they need to make them good citizens.” ~ Justice Sandra Day O’Connor

 It was a rainbow coalition of sorts! From the North, East, West and South of the world, delegates from 23 countries, including myself, gathered in the German capital, Berlin, to commemorate the 2026 International Civic Education Summit. From November 1–5, the Konrad-Adenauer-Stiftung, in collaboration with the Heinrich-Böll-Stiftung and Arolsen Archives, brought together educators, researchers, practitioners, and civil society actors from around the world to explore how participation can be strengthened through civic education. Through the exchange of experiences and innovative approaches, participants examined how democratic engagement can be fostered in diverse political, social, and cultural contexts.

 Delegates from Africa, Asia, Europe, Latin America, North America, and the Middle East engaged in bilateral meetings, institutional visits, and discussions with Berlin-based partners from educational institutions, public authorities, foundations, museums, memorial sites, and civil society organisations. The programme focused on how to promote mutual learning, highlight successful practices, and strengthen international networks dedicated to democratic engagement and civic learning.

 Before taking a deep dive into the programmes of the event, what exactly is civic education and why is it very important to democratic consolidation? An independent international expert and researcher on environment and development, Jennifer Rietbergen-McCracken wrote in a paper on CIVICUS Global Alliance online that “Civic education (also known as citizen education or democracy education) can be broadly defined as the provision of information and learning experiences to equip and empower citizens to participate in democratic processes. Civic education can take many forms, including classroom-based learning, informal training, experiential learning, and mass media campaigns. Civic education can be targeted at children or adults, in developed or developing countries and at the local, national or international level. As such, civic education is an approach that employs a range of different methods, and is often used in combination with other participatory governance tools.”

 According to her, the overall goal of civic education is to promote civic engagement and support democratic and participatory governance. Civic education has been used to address a wide variety of political and governance issues (e.g. corruption, civic apathy or post-conflict reconciliation) as well as important social issues (e.g. domestic violence, drug abuse, and HIV/AIDS).

 Whenever I facilitate training on civic education and voter education, I use the analogy: “All accidents are incidents, but not all incidents are accidents.”

” That is to say, “All voter education is civic education, but not all civic education is voter education.

” This is because voter education is just a subset of civic education. In Civics for Life by Sandra Day O’Connor, the author establishes the nexus between civic education and democratic consolidation. It says, “The success of our democracy and society depends on civic education. It equips us with the knowledge, skills, and values necessary to become informed citizens actively participating in our democratic process. Civic education helps us understand our rights and responsibilities as citizens, promotes critical thinking, problem-solving, and responsible action.”

 Another soundbite from Civics for Life says, “The success of a democracy relies heavily on its citizens having the necessary knowledge and skills to participate in the political process. The ability of citizens to make informed decisions, including electing their representatives and understanding the laws that govern them, is the foundation for any functioning democracy. Without an informed citizenry, a democracy cannot endure.”. I couldn’t agree more with that submission.

 Now, back to Berlin, one of the outstanding presentations for me was at the Bundestag, the German Parliament Building, where we met with a Member of Parliament, CDU/CSU parliamentary group, Member of the Internal Affairs Committee, David Gregosz, who, along with the Head of the Domestic Affairs Department, Heinrich Böll Foundation, Bastian Hermisson, walked us through a presentation on “Polarisation and Populism – Democracy under Pressure”. It was very insightful and participatory as we learnt about Germany’s political development.   I also recall the memorable visit to the headquarters of the Heinrich Böll Foundation, where we learnt about the HBS work in the field of civic education and democracy strengthening, with a particular focus on political participation. This session also offers insight into the Foundation’s work on memory culture and its international programming.

 My key takeaway from the engagement at HBS was learning about cultural memory: the constructed understanding of the past passed from one generation to the next through text, oral traditions, monuments, rites, and other symbols. Prof. Gernot Wolfram of the Department of Cultural Management and Cultural Studies at Macromedia University, Berlin, made a presentation on “Innovative Solutions – Participation in Times of AI and Societal Polarisation”. From this presentation, I learnt about the interactive “Wahl-O-Mat,” which informs voters about party policies and helps them decide which party is right for them.

 The actual International Civic Education Summit 2026 was held on Wednesday, November 4, at the KAS Academy. On this day, all 23 delegates had the opportunity to present their projects. I participated in the panel with the theme: “Seats at the Table: Empowering Participation in Democratic Institutions.” The moderator was Shelly Kupferberg. Other members of the panel included: Melanie Walker of Canadian International Council, Canada; Adam Kądziela of Department of Public Policy Coordination, Chancellery of the Prime Minister of Poland; and Beatriz Kipnis of Center for Studies and Debates at Fundação Fernando Henrique Cardoso, Brazil.

  I presented my anti-corruption work, which was done with funding support from the MacArthur Foundation, which culminated in the publication of my third book titled “Nigeria: Corruption and Opacity in Governance”. I also referenced my engagement as a resource person to train the new generation of youth leaders by HBS under the Nigeria Green Academy Program from the 2023 edition to date, as well as the hosting of a television talk show, Development Focus with Jide Ojo on ITV, Abuja, from January 2021 to December 2022. Lastly, I spoke about my ubiquitous media advocacy initiatives, which I am using to mobilize Nigerians to participate in the country’s democratic activities.

  I learnt a lot from the keynote presentation by Christiana Bukalo titled “Who Gets to Participate? Citizenship, Statelessness and the Preconditions of Democracy”.  I learnt that there are approximately 30 million stateless people around the world. You may ask what statelessness is. According to UNHCR, the international legal definition of a stateless person is “a person who is not considered as a national by any State under the operation of its law”. In simple terms, this means that a stateless person does not have the nationality of any country. Some people are born stateless, but others become stateless.

 Statelessness often has a severe and lifelong impact on those it affects. The millions of people around the world who are denied a nationality often fight for the same basic human rights that most of us take for granted. Often, they are excluded from cradle to grave – being denied a legal identity when they are born, access to education, health care, marriage and job opportunities during their lifetime and even the dignity of an official burial and a death certificate when they die. Many pass on statelessness to their children, who then pass it on to the next generation. South African Grammy Award winner, Miriam Makeba (Mama Africa), was said to be stateless for about 30 years when she was exiled by the apartheid government of South Africa.

 I.G: @jideojong

The post Rainbow coalition for civic education in Berlin appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: On election campaigns and election manifestos
description: Governance should focus on sustainable economic development, improving people’s living conditions day by day. If in doubt, ask President Donald Trump. The global rising cost of living or declining standard of living led, invariably, to demonstrations in countries like Germany and France, while Unite
content:
Governance should focus on sustainable economic development, improving people’s living conditions day by day. If in doubt, ask President Donald Trump. The global rising cost of living or declining standard of living led, invariably, to demonstrations in countries like Germany and France, while United States citizens used the Mid-Term elections in November to demonstrate their displeasure with President Trump and the Republican Party, with the loss of a majority in both the Senate and House of Representatives. With 55 seats in the Senate, the Democrats gained eight more seats lost by the Republicans. In the House, Democrats won 256 seats to the Republicans’ 169.

 According to available research records, the loss by the Republican Party has been attributed to five main causes, namely soaring cost of living, the unpopular Iran war, a disciplined message from the democrats, unpopularity of President Trump in connection to his policies generally and economic policies in particular, and shifts in the position of Hispanic and black voters as related to Trump’s immigration policy. What matters here is the soaring cost of living, a global phenomenon. The state of an economy, specifically citizens’ economic condition, has a way of helping or destroying candidates participating in elections. The rising cost of living phenomenon is the necklace being worn by every country’s leader today!

 When we talk about the macroeconomic goals every country wants to achieve, price stability is central. It seems to be the central point around which achieving other macroeconomic goals revolves. The macro goals or objectives are full employment of resources, economic growth, price stability, balance of payments equilibrium, equitable income distribution and sustainable development. We need stable prices to achieve full employment, yet we need some moderate inflation to achieve economic growth. If the law of supply is to hold, upward adjustment of prices serves to encourage higher supply. That is, the higher the price, the higher the supply.

 And higher supply means growth. Growth, encouraged by higher prices, makes external trade possible, improving the balance of payments and moving it toward equilibrium. Higher economic growth implies higher national income, for which equitable distribution is essential for peace to reign in the country. Sustainable economic growth moves the economy toward rising employment and incomes or the full-employment goal and eventually results in economic development. While moderate price rises necessarily achieve those stated macroeconomic objectives, the kind of rapid inflation being witnessed today creates a disastrous situation, particularly with respect to citizens’ welfare. The fact that this second wave of inflation came from external shocks provides a lesson in policymaking.

 We witnessed the first wave of inflation when the subsidy on fuel was removed and petroleum prices were deregulated, in addition to the massive devaluation of the naira by about 300 per cent. That was a domestic shock and did require some reforms. External shocks require policy revolution to prevent, in the future, the magnitude of the effects that we are having presently. That is why the current political campaign should centre around economic revolution rather than economic reform.

 Many African leaders are afraid of using revolution but prefer reforms, the language of the World Bank and IMF. Whereas the economic policies are necessary to take Africa out of the economic doldrum, it finds itself in a revolutionary adjustment. There is a need to overhaul the economic system of production whereby we produce to satisfy the industrial needs of advanced economies. We remain producers of raw materials in human and non-human resources. Our physical products feed industries in the Western world, and human resources are attracted by improved working environments and higher wages and salaries.

 A revolution does not mean chaotic changes like the French Revolution, but drastic, radical, or fundamental changes like the First Industrial Revolution in 18th- and 19th-century Great Britain. The revolution transformed global production, labour, and trade through mechanised factories and steam power. What we require in Nigeria and the whole of Africa is revolutionary production in agriculture, factories or industries generally, whereby we export finished products like the rest of the world. The present campaign for election in Nigeria and the manifestos of principal actors should reflect a revolutionary departure from the present situation.

 Such revolutionary changes will minimise the depth of external shocks that we are witnessing now. Politicians should tell us how many megawatts of electricity will be generated yearly and how they will do it. President Tinubu was promising a growth rate of six per cent per year for the next four years. That is not ambitious. He should be proposing a minimum growth of 10 per cent. China did take over 900 million Chinese out of poverty in three decades by growing at 10 per cent per year for more than a decade. According to the World Bank Poverty and Equity Report, an estimated 496 million Indians moved out of poverty between 2011 and 2023, driven by increased employment opportunities. This was linked to sustained growth of about 10 per cent over the decade. Specific government schemes were credited with the massive decline.

 Every presidential candidate should be specific about what to do with agriculture, education, industry, science and technology and medicine. Manifestos must be clear, just like the campaign. Every specific promise must be backed by data and a timeline. We cannot continue to run Nigeria on handouts to consumers; we must run it on jobs and enhanced productivity. A conducive production environment must be promised and fulfilled. This will include reliable electricity or power infrastructure. Without electricity, neither China nor India would have achieved the feats reported. China has long achieved 100 per cent electricity, while India is almost there, with an achievement of over 90 per cent in the last five years. The Nigerian government, like other African governments, must declare revolutionary development rather than unending reforms and transformation.

title: Weep not for Nigeria

Some months ago, I was travelling late in the evening with a very senior colleague along the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway, Mowe outbound.
My boss, as I fondly called him, a deep lover of Nigeria as most of us, wer
content:
“A child that is not well trained will sell the house that is well built.” – Yoruba proverb

Some months ago, I was travelling late in the evening with a very senior colleague along the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway, Mowe outbound.

My boss, as I fondly called him, a deep lover of Nigeria as most of us, were, was quick to notify me of the recent developments on the Long Bridge (the bridge along Berger (Lagos) and Warewa/Arepo, Ogun State): an array of glistering solar-powered streetlights that brighten the entire stretch of the bridge.

People conversant with this route will understand that this new facility is just not an afterthought embellishment; it’s a much-needed infrastructure for night travellers along the bridge due to the occasional thefts and robberies whenever there’s heavy traffic along the corridor.

The news was a signal of hope that good things still happen in my country, and I could remember discussing this good initiative for many minutes during the journey.

Just recently, seven months after this first encounter, I was privileged to travel again with the same boss along the same route, at approximately the same time.

With his index fingers slightly raised and in a discordant tone, he called my attention to the once-glittering streetlights that dazzled the entire bridge – almost 80 per cent of them had vanished; the stumps of the clean-cut pipes and the resurrected darkness on the bridge were there as witnesses.

It was like an eyesore. We all shook our heads in disbelief, and I must confess the grief was so heavy that our words were few, unlike other days.

Recently too, a friend shared a video of how some people were mining the iron rods that were used to reinforce a popular bridge in Lagos. The harvesting was so professionally executed that one needs to zoom in closer to see the unimaginable damage to the bridge.

Who is responsible for these evil acts? Your guess is as good as mine.

Albeit, because of the nature of their jobs, I have heard some people point fingers at bowlers and scavengers, but if you want to know how deplorable our country has descended, just drop any valuable iron around your house and monitor it; you will discover that our situation is beyond what you think.

But as we approached the middle of the bridge, still in bewilderment, I gently nudged my boss with some pertinent questions: “Sir, irrespective of whatever economic challenges or situation you may find yourself in, can you do this? Can I do it?”

It happens that one of the main reasons we could not do this is not because we are rich or poor, nor because of the level of education or status; it is not even just the fear of God; it’s based on the perceived advantages and privileges—how we feel the nation has fared with us.

Besides the inherent greediness and wickedness of men, there’s another foul side of us that can be triggered by the feeling of unfairness or being cheated.

That’s why it doesn’t matter how much you are being paid; you still want to know if you are being treated unfairly, and it doesn’t matter how much you score in an exam; you are likely to be comforted by the marks of others.

Our nation is currently on the cusp of inequality, with citizens who are a million miles away from their rulers. The gaps continue to widen every day, and the trust in the leadership or the nation itself has reached a palpable ebb. It is now a fight for self-survival, not a spirit of patrimony about our land; the cohesive spirit of a nation is in a silo.

Leaders seek positions to amass wealth and secure the future of their children, including the next generations and the unborn, not for the nation; citizens seek any opportunity to have their own bites of the national cake.

Everyone is making a demand of what the nation can offer, not what we can give, and any attempt to build anything meaningful without first building the people will end in futility, like the streetlights on the long bridge.

Why you should not weep for Nigeria!

 A nation that left the building of her people to frivolities is not a serious type—I – I have studied the projects and focus of our successive governments over 20 years; none of them has been able to address the teeming youth unemployment and underemployment that have plagued our nation.

It’s unprofitable to waste your tears on a nation where it is more profitable to become a politician than to work, and the citizens know this.

You should refrain from weeping because those who should really wail for the nation are wining, those that should be tearing are toasting, and those that should groan are gallivanting.

Solomon the wise said it is not wise to declare that the past is better than the present, but probably Nigeria’s case is a bit unique, for I have heard many elders telling me, while shaking their heads, that we, the current generation, do not really enjoy Nigeria; how do you say the best of a nation is in the past?

I believe in Nigeria and pray for her salvation, but please spare me my tears.

  • Charles is a pharmacist

title: We’ll complete job in Zanzibar – Adams
description:
Super Eagles forward, Akor Adams, has said the team will complete the job against Tanzania in Zanzibar, after the 3-1 win in Uyo gave the squad confidence and motivation for the return leg.
Adams told Footy-Africa that Tanzania were a difficult test, but he was pleased that Nigeria got the job done.
content:
Super Eagles forward, Akor Adams, has said the team will complete the job against Tanzania in Zanzibar, after the 3-1 win in Uyo gave the squad confidence and motivation for the return leg.

Adams told Footy-Africa that Tanzania were a difficult test, but he was pleased that Nigeria got the job done.

“It was a very tough game against a good opponent, but I am happy our aim was achieved as we got all three points against a very tough side. All games are difficult, and this was no different. We had to find a way to break them down, and I am glad it worked out well,” he said.

He said the squad was determined to qualify for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations. “We have to look at the positives and take them into the next game. I was a bit unlucky with the end result, but there are a lot of good things to take from the game. The team is committed to qualifying for the Africa Cup of Nations. We must make the AFCON. It is what I want and what the entire team wants.”

“This result is a morale booster, and we will now travel to Tanzania to complete the job. We must be at the next AFCON,” he added.

The Venezia forward started on Friday and had a few chances to score, but could not convert them.

Nigeria made a bright start at the Godswill Akpabio International Stadium, with Alhassan Yusuf finishing a swift counter-attack after Ademola Lookman found him in the box. Tanzania levelled in the 32nd minute when Alphonce Msanga punished a mistake in midfield involving Wilfred Ndidi.

The Super Eagles returned from the break with more intensity. Substitute Tolu Arokodare restored the lead in the 52nd minute, flicking home a pass from captain Ndidi. The Ajax forward made it 3-1 eight minutes later, slotting past the goalkeeper after a defender failed to deal with a pull-back from fellow substitute Moses Usor.

The Super Eagles face Tanzania again in Zanzibar on Tuesday, November 17, knowing another win will strengthen their bid to qualify.

title: Linkage Assurance targets profitable growth, digital expansion
description:
Linkage Assurance Plc plans to deepen its presence in profitable insurance segments and expand digital services as it seeks to strengthen its market position in an increasingly competitive industry.
 Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Linkage Assurance, Daniel Braie, said the company’s
content:
Linkage Assurance Plc plans to deepen its presence in profitable insurance segments and expand digital services as it seeks to strengthen its market position in an increasingly competitive industry.

 Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Linkage Assurance, Daniel Braie, said the company’s 2026 strategy was focused on consolidation, business growth, operational and financial excellence, as well as customer and people development.

 He said the insurer would pursue opportunities in profitable business segments while improving customer experience and developing products that respond to changing market needs.

 Technology and digital transformation would also feature prominently in the company’s growth plans, particularly in improving products and services for direct and personal insurance customers.

 Braie said Linkage Assurance would introduce different motor insurance options to accommodate customers’ varying risk exposures and financial capacities.

 The company also plans to sustain initiatives aimed at strengthening brand awareness and delivering greater value to customers.

 The strategic priorities come against the backdrop of the company’s improved financial performance in the nine months ended September 2026.

 Linkage Assurance recorded a 31 per cent increase in profit after tax to N4.09bn from N3.12bn in the corresponding period of 2025. Profit before tax also rose by 29 per cent to N4.32bn from N3.34bn.

 Investment and other income increased by 27 per cent to N7.71bn from N6.05bn, supporting earnings growth, while insurance revenue rose six per cent to N20.55bn from N19.30bn.

The insurer’s total assets expanded by 31 per cent to N100.83bn as of 30 September, 2026, compared with N76.90bn at the end of December 2025.

 However, gross claims paid increased to N5.59bn from N4.02bn in the corresponding period, reflecting higher claims obligations during the review period.

 The company’s strategy comes as Nigeria’s insurance industry adjusts to a new regulatory and competitive environment following the recapitalisation exercise, which has raised expectations for stronger underwriting capacity, improved customer service and sustainable growth.

title: Chelle gets double boost ahead return leg
description:
Super Eagles coach Eric Chelle has received a fitness boost ahead of Nigeria’s return fixture against Tanzania, with defenders Calvin Bassey and Benjamin Fredrick recovering from the cramps they suffered during Friday’s 3-1 victory in Uyo.
The pair experienced discomfort during the opening-leg encou
content:
Super Eagles coach Eric Chelle has received a fitness boost ahead of Nigeria’s return fixture against Tanzania, with defenders Calvin Bassey and Benjamin Fredrick recovering from the cramps they suffered during Friday’s 3-1 victory in Uyo.

The pair experienced discomfort during the opening-leg encounter at the Godswill Akpabio International Stadium, raising concerns over their availability for the return meeting.

However, Chelle confirmed that both defenders were in good physical condition after the match, offering Nigeria encouragement as they prepare for the second leg.

The update comes at an important time for the Super Eagles, who will be seeking to protect their two-goal advantage and complete the job against the Taifa Stars.

While the defensive situation appears more encouraging, Nigeria still have concerns over Ademola Lookman, who was forced off before half-time after suffering a knee problem.

“Ademola, his knee, he has a little problem. He took a shock, and we don’t know if it was a shock,” Chelle said.

The coach explained that the Atletico Madrid forward first felt discomfort while attempting to score before taking another knock to the same knee.

“When he tried to score the goal with his left foot, his knee started to feel bad. After that, he took a knock on his knee. This is why he went off the pitch,” he added.

Lookman’s condition remains a concern, particularly after he was replaced by Moses Simon in the first half.

Nigeria will hope Bassey and Fredrick remain available as Chelle considers his defensive options for the return encounter.

The post Chelle gets double boost ahead return leg appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Poch retains Bassey on United transfer list
description:
Nigeria international Calvin Bassey is expected to feature prominently on Mauricio Pochettino’s list of potential Manchester United targets ahead of the January transfer window.
According to The Telegraph, the Fulham defender is among the options being considered as the new United head coach prepare
content:
Nigeria international Calvin Bassey is expected to feature prominently on Mauricio Pochettino’s list of potential Manchester United targets ahead of the January transfer window.

According to The Telegraph, the Fulham defender is among the options being considered as the new United head coach prepares to strengthen his side’s defence.

Pochettino, who is expected to begin work at Old Trafford later this week, faces the task of improving a backline that has struggled this season.

United have conceded 19 goals in their opening 10 Premier League matches, with their defensive problems making reinforcements a priority ahead of the winter transfer window.

Bassey’s pace, physical presence and versatility are understood to make him an attractive option. The 26-year-old can operate at centre-back and left-back, potentially offering cover in both positions.

The Nigerian has also impressed since joining Fulham from Ajax in 2023 and has captained the club under head coach Alvaro Arbeloa this season.

Arbeloa has praised the defender’s performances and expressed his desire to secure him on a new contract.

However, Bassey’s current deal runs until next summer, although Fulham have an option to extend it by another 12 months. The situation could leave the London club facing a decision if United make a substantial offer in January.

Bassey previously played for Rangers and Ajax before returning to the Premier League with Fulham, where he has established himself as a regular.

The post Poch retains Bassey on United transfer list appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Okolie predicts Joshua knockout win over Fury
description:
Former world champion, Lawrence Okolie, has predicted that British-Nigerian heavyweight, Anthony Joshua, will knock out Tyson Fury when the two meet in their long-awaited Battle of Britain on December 11.
Okolie, who has shared rounds with both fighters, gave a tactical breakdown of the fight to Box
content:
Former world champion, Lawrence Okolie, has predicted that British-Nigerian heavyweight, Anthony Joshua, will knock out Tyson Fury when the two meet in their long-awaited Battle of Britain on December 11.

Okolie, who has shared rounds with both fighters, gave a tactical breakdown of the fight to Boxing News magazine. He believes the contest will be won and lost on tactics.

The two Britons will meet at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff for the WBA “super” title. Each man has the chance to become a three-time world champion, and the fight will finally settle a rivalry that has simmered for about 10 years.

Okolie said Joshua can end the fight if he is aggressive.

“If Fury is allowed to get into a rhythm, he makes it a one-sided boxing match. However, if AJ comes in like the landlord and punches aggressively at middle distance, he has every chance of ending it. AJ has explosive speed and power at middle range, and we have seen Fury get hurt a good few times,” he said.

The contender’s view is that Joshua has the edge in power, having sparred both men. The 36-year-old Joshua remains a potent puncher, but recent form shows that neither fighter is near his best.

Fury’s speed and elusiveness appeared less pronounced than usual in his points, and stoppage wins over Arslanbek Makhmudov and Mariusz Wach. Joshua, for his part, showed a worrying lack of punch resistance against Kristian Prenga in July.

The British-Nigerian was knocked down twice before he stopped the Albanian in the second round.

title: Why we are building Nigeria’s healthcare economy
description: Nigeria should be producing far more of the medicines and medical equipment our people need. We have an established pharmaceutical industry base, highly skilled health professionals, and a substantial domestic market. Yet our dependence on imported health products remains unacceptably high, and many
content:
Nigeria should be producing far more of the medicines and medical equipment our people need. We have an established pharmaceutical industry base, highly skilled health professionals, and a substantial domestic market. Yet our dependence on imported health products remains unacceptably high, and many Nigerians still travel abroad for treatment. A country with our demographic strength should secure a greater share of production, employment, and specialist services supported by what our people spend on their health.

This dependence has broad consequences for families and for the economy. Exchange rate changes can put essential medicines beyond a household’s reach. Disruptions far from our shores can affect supplies in our hospitals. Money spent on treatment abroad sustains expertise and facilities elsewhere that we must also develop within Nigeria.

I established the Presidential Initiative for Unlocking the Healthcare Value Chain in October 2023 to address these problems. Through PVAC, we are bringing Nigerian and international investment into domestic manufacturing and healthcare services. Our objectives are to produce more essential health products, improve the care available within our country, and create quality employment across the sector.

This work forms part of the Nigeria Health Sector Renewal Investment Initiative, which I launched in December 2023 to give effect to the health commitments of the Renewed Hope Agenda. Its purpose is to save lives and reduce the physical and financial hardship caused by illness. We are pursuing this through stronger governance, better health services, domestic production, and greater preparedness for health emergencies. Through the accompanying compact, the Federal Government, states, and development partners committed to a common reform programme. Under this framework, investment in industry must serve the same national purpose as investment in clinics and hospitals.

Healthcare as an economic priority:

Nigeria needs more enterprises that produce, employ, and compete. Healthcare offers an opportunity to build such enterprises around substantial, enduring demand. As we expand access to treatment, more of the expenditure involved should support businesses and skilled work within our economy.

Good health is fundamental to the prosperity we seek. It is both a cause and consequence of human capital accumulation. When illness keeps a worker at home, a child out of school, or a small business owner away from work, the cost extends beyond the clinic. A serious illness can consume years of a family’s savings.

Protecting Nigerians from those losses is part of building a more productive economy.

The government has a direct role in making that possible. Ill health undermines productivity. Outbreaks can disrupt economies. A presidential initiative enables us to bring decisions on health, finance, industry and investment into a common programme. Manufacturers should be able to plan with confidence in the rules under which they operate. Investors should find government institutions working towards the same objectives. That coordination is essential when a project requires substantial capital and several years to reach commercial scale.

We have acted on production costs:

The Executive Order I signed in June 2024 provided tax and tariff relief for specified machinery, equipment, and inputs used in local healthcare manufacturing. Between January 2025 and June 2026, the government approved more than N24 billion in waivers for 75 manufacturers. The purpose is to make investment and expansion more viable, with benefits that carry through to the availability and cost of essential products.

Investment in production and skills:

The manufacturing base is expanding. Ten factories producing priority health products are being established, including six in 2026. These investments cover products as varied as medicines, diagnostic tests, medical oxygen and mosquito nets. They represent productive assets around which further skills, suppliers, and investment can develop.

The mosquito-net industry provides a clear example. Following its 2024 agreement with PVAC, Vestergaard announced it will start operations at Health Textiles Nigeria from September 2026. Similarly, Harvestfield, an indigenous firm, is producing dual-ingredient nets. Production of advanced insecticide-treated nets is now underway, with Nigerian employees receiving further technical training. At full scale, the companies will produce more than ten million nets annually and employ more than 600 people.

For a country carrying a heavy malaria burden, the significance is immediate. The benefit must reach families through wider access to effective malaria protection. Resources devoted to preventing disease can also support manufacturing employment within Nigeria. As production expands, the opportunity extends to suppliers and service businesses, and the knowledge Nigerian workers acquire becomes an asset for the country. We should be able to meet more of our own needs and supply markets elsewhere in Africa.

The same ambition applies to diagnostics. Codix Bio’s agreement with the Medicines Patent Pool, supported by the World Health Organisation, enables the transfer of technology from SD Biosensor to manufacture rapid diagnostic tests in Nigeria. Partnerships like this bring technical knowledge to Nigerian enterprises and strengthen their ability to produce to international standards.

International cooperation is central to this effort. Nigeria welcomes investors who bring capital, expertise, and a long-term commitment to production here. Our market offers commercial opportunity with a strong, youthful demographic, and successful partnerships should leave the country with stronger businesses and deeper technical competence. That is how investment can contribute to economic diversification and, over time, greater export earnings. NASENI-Troment is another manufacturer using world-class technology to produce diagnostic kits locally.

Better care and greater opportunity:

From the outset, our ambition has also been to improve the care available within Nigeria. We must develop services that give Nigerians greater confidence in seeking treatment at home. Investments in advanced diagnostics, cancer care, and other specialist services can keep more healthcare expenditure within the country while creating opportunities for our clinicians and researchers. For a family facing cancer, access to treatment within Nigeria can spare them the added cost of travel abroad and long separation from loved ones.

I recognise that Nigerians will judge these reforms by the care they can obtain and afford today. New capacity takes time to reach its full effect. Domestic manufacturers still face costs that we must address, and local production must meet demanding standards of quality and competitiveness. Government support must result in better products and affordable services for Nigerians.

Our national health reform framework, pursued through a sector-wide approach, connects this industrial investment to the expansion of healthcare. As we strengthen primary care through the Basic Health Care Provision Fund and expand health insurance, we must ensure that facilities can obtain the medicines and diagnostic tests patients need. Better purchasing arrangements can turn this growing demand into predictable orders for manufacturers, supporting investment while helping public funds go further.

The benefit must reach Nigerians through reliable supplies and affordable treatment, including in rural communities. Medipool, Nigeria’s first nationally approved group purchasing organisation, was established to pool demand for quality medicines and other health commodities, negotiate better prices, and provide a more dependable market for local manufacturers.

The next stage requires sustained attention to financing, reliable demand, and the practical conditions under which enterprises operate. Announced investments must progress into production, and production must reach the facilities where Nigerians receive care. I expect the Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare to sustain this work with the relevant institutions and private partners.

Nigeria’s healthcare needs should support a growing source of national prosperity. We can build businesses that serve our people, develop expertise that stays within our country and create products that compete beyond our borders. The progress already made gives us a basis to pursue that ambition with confidence. Nigerians should expect these investments to deliver dependable care, more affordable treatment and opportunities to earn a decent living.

President Tinubu is the Commander-in-Chief of the Federal Republic of Nigeria

title: Giving traditional pottery new purpose
description: For generations, clay has been part of everyday African life. Shaped into cooking pots, water vessels, storage containers and objects that carry the knowledge and craftsmanship of communities across generations. For many of us growing up in African homes, clay was never just mud shaped into a pot; i
content:
For generations, clay has been part of everyday African life. Shaped into cooking pots, water vessels, storage containers and objects that carry the knowledge and craftsmanship of communities across generations. For many of us growing up in African homes, clay was never just mud shaped into a pot; it was part of the rhythm of everyday life. We remember our grandmothers’ clay water pots, holding cool, refreshing water that seemed to taste better simply because it had rested in the earth’s embrace. There was something familiar about its earthy taste, the coolness against a parched throat, and the feeling of finally being home. Beyond these familiar comforts, clay also served practical purposes. In some traditional water-settling practices, water was left undisturbed so suspended particles could settle, making the clearer water above easier to draw off. These memories remind us that long before modern materials and technologies became widespread, our communities had developed everyday ways of working with the natural properties of clay. Today, that inherited knowledge offers more than nostalgia; it invites us to rediscover what this humble material can contribute to modern living.

Clay was also a faithful companion in our grandmothers’ kitchens. It was there when ewedu soup was stirred to its silky perfection, when rich stews simmered slowly, and when the aroma of a home-cooked meal filled the air. There was something special about food prepared and served in traditional clay pots, the earthy character of the vessel, the deep flavours of the soup, and the warmth that seemed to linger long after the fire had gone out. Even minutes after a pot had been taken off the fire, its heat remained, gently holding the meal warm as family members gathered to eat. Our grandmothers understood the value of materials that worked with the rhythms of everyday life. Today, those memories invite us to look at clay again, not merely as a relic of the past, but as a material whose practical value and cultural significance still deserve a place in our homes. But what happens when this age-old material is brought into conversations about today’s most pressing challenges?

For a Nigerian creative enterprise, The Lightning Artz, the answer is to rethink what traditional pottery can do. The Founder believes creativity should go beyond aesthetics to solve real-world problems, combining indigenous ceramic knowledge with modern innovation to develop practical products for healthier living and a more sustainable future. Its work reflects a simple but powerful idea: materials and knowledge passed down through generations can still help address present-day needs.

One of its clearest expressions is AquaMax, an electricity-free ceramic water-purification and dispensing solution that helps households access safer drinking water. By applying their expertise in clay, enhanced by technology to create a locally workable product, the product offers a solution for households seeking practical ways to treat drinking water, particularly where reliable access to safe water remains a challenge. For the founder, Obanijesu Francis, the work is personal. Growing up in an underserved community in Ifo Local Government Area of Ogun State, he experienced the difficulties of accessing safe drinking water. He and his siblings travelled long distances to fetch water, and the family experienced recurring bouts of typhoid that disrupted their schooling and daily lives.

Those experiences helped shape his conviction that creativity should not be reserved for decoration, luxury or the interests of the privileged. It can also be used to respond to needs that affect people’s health, dignity and quality of life. These possibilities are central to their mission.

By developing products locally and building pathways to reach underserved households, the enterprise connects creative innovation with practical community needs. Its approach suggests that cultural heritage and social progress need not exist in separate spaces; they can strengthen one another.

Esther Temilade, a communications and M&E manager, writes via temiladeest@gmail.com

title: England End Spain’s 44-Game Unbeaten Run With Nations League Win
description: England snapped world champions Spain’s unbeaten run with a 3-2 victory in Madrid on Sunday to clinch the top spot in Nations League group A3.Goals from Harry Kane, Ezri Konsa and Ben White inflicted La Roja’s first loss in a competitive game since March 2023, after 44 without defeat.Eng
content:
England snapped world champions Spain’s unbeaten run with a 3-2 victory in Madrid on Sunday to clinch the top spot in Nations League group A3.

Goals from Harry Kane, Ezri Konsa and Ben White inflicted La Roja’s first loss in a competitive game since March 2023, after 44 without defeat.

England’s Elliot Anderson was sent off in the second half as Spain fought back from three goals down with strikes from Mikel Oyarzabal and Nico Williams, but Luis de la Fuente’s World Cup winners could not find the equaliser.

Both sides were already sure to progress, but as group winners England will be seeded for the quarter-finals in March.

England coach Thomas Tuchel selected James Trafford in goal over Jordan Pickford and also brought White and Konsa into the side.

Teenage star Lamine Yamal was fit to start for Spain at Atletico Madrid’s Metropolitano stadium after missing their midweek win over the Czech Republic.

However the youngster did not see much of the ball in the first half as England came out strongly.

Spain goalkeeper Unai Simon produced a strong reaction save to deny Jude Bellingham, while Anthony Gordon had a dangerous shot blocked.

Ballon d’Or winner Kane, who beat Yamal to the award, sent an effort narrowly wide.

Barcelona defender Pau Cubarsi handed England the advantage when he clumsily felled Kane in the area on the stroke of half time.

The Bayern Munich hitman powered a perfect penalty past Simon, who dived the right way but to no avail.

De la Fuente tried to react at half-time with a triple change, including throwing on Barcelona duo Fermin Lopez and Pedri, but England quickly found more joy.

Konsa headed home the second from Declan Rice’s corner in the 53rd minute after the Arsenal defender was left unmarked by Spain’s defence.

Four minutes later England sliced open Spain’s defence with Kane and Bellingham combining to set up White for the third.

La Roja clawed their way back into the game when Elliot Anderson fouled Yamal in the area as the Spain striker ran in on goal.

The Manchester City midfielder was dismissed and Mikel Oyarzabal slotted home the penalty.

Spain found a second when Gordon gave the ball away and Yamal fed Nico Williams, whose shot hit the post and bounced in.

Williams curled over and Trafford denied Yamal and Marc Cucurella as Spain looked fruitlessly for the goal they needed to preserve their unbeaten record.

The post England End Spain’s 44-Game Unbeaten Run With Nations League Win appeared first on Channels Television.
author: Donatus Anichukwueze

title: England end Spain’s 43-Game unbeaten run with thrilling 3-2 victory in Nations League
description:
England produced a commanding performance to secure a landmark 3-2 victory over Spain in Madrid, handing the reigning world champions a rare defeat in regulation time and recording what could be regarded as their finest display under head coach Thomas Tuchel.
The Three Lions raced into a three-goal
content:
England produced a commanding performance to secure a landmark 3-2 victory over Spain in Madrid, handing the reigning world champions a rare defeat in regulation time and recording what could be regarded as their finest display under head coach Thomas Tuchel.

The Three Lions raced into a three-goal lead before the hour mark but were forced to withstand intense pressure in the closing stages after midfielder Elliot Anderson was sent off, allowing Spain to mount a spirited comeback.

England stunned the home supporters at the Metropolitano Stadium with their dominance from the opening whistle, overpowering a Spanish side that had gone 43 matches without a defeat in regulation time. Spain’s last such loss came in March 2024, although they were beaten by Portugal on penalties in the Nations League final.

Despite wasting several opportunities in the first half, England eventually broke the deadlock just before the interval when captain Harry Kane converted a penalty. The striker, who was fouled by Pau Cubarsi, registered his 93rd international goal from the spot.

Tuchel’s men continued their impressive display after the restart, doubling their advantage in the 53rd minute through Ezri Konsa, who headed home Declan Rice’s corner.

Arsenal defender Ben White made it 3-0 four minutes later, finishing off a sweeping attacking move with a powerful angled effort to leave Spain facing a difficult task.

However, England’s comfortable advantage was put under threat in the 65th minute following a defensive error by Jarell Quansah. The mistake allowed Spain to launch an attack, forcing Anderson to pull back Lamine Yamal.

The midfielder was shown a straight red card, while Mikel Oyarzabal converted the resulting penalty to give Spain hope.

The hosts, who had struggled to make an impact for much of the contest, suddenly found renewed confidence, with Yamal playing a key role in their revival.

Spain reduced the deficit further in the 75th minute when Yamal delivered an excellent cross for substitute Nico Williams, who beat England goalkeeper James Trafford.

With momentum shifting towards the home side, Trafford became increasingly important, producing a series of outstanding saves to deny Spain an equaliser and preserve England’s advantage.

England eventually held on to secure a memorable 3-2 victory, a result that also confirmed their position at the top of their UEFA Nations League group.

title: Insecurity: Tinubu’s Five-Year Defence Plan Ready, Says APC Campaign Council
description: The APC Presidential Campaign Council says President Bola Tinubu’s administration is preparing a five-year defence strategy, alongside plans to recruit 78,000 additional military and police personnel, as part of efforts to tackle insecurity.The council disclosed this in a statement on Sunday b
content:
The APC Presidential Campaign Council says President Bola Tinubu’s administration is preparing a five-year defence strategy, alongside plans to recruit 78,000 additional military and police personnel, as part of efforts to tackle insecurity.

The council disclosed this in a statement on Sunday by its spokesperson, Dele Alake, outlining measures the administration says are aimed at strengthening the country’s security architecture and improving the capacity of security agencies.

According to the statement, the proposed Five-Year Strategic Defence Operations Plan will provide a framework for aligning military operations, training, equipment and expenditure with Nigeria’s security challenges.

The council said the strategy would adopt a coordinated, intelligence-led and technology-driven approach to tackling terrorism, banditry, kidnapping and other forms of criminality.

It also highlighted the outcome of military operations under the Tinubu administration, claiming that more than 15,000 terrorists and bandits had been eliminated in the last three years.

The statement further claimed that over 130,000 Boko Haram fighters and their dependants had surrendered through Operation Safe Corridor, the Federal Government’s rehabilitation programme for repentant insurgents.

The council described the figures as evidence of the administration’s combination of military operations and non-kinetic measures in addressing insecurity.

On efforts to increase the number of personnel available to security agencies, the statement said Tinubu had approved the recruitment of 28,000 additional soldiers and 50,000 police officers.

It also disclosed that four new Army divisions had been created, while existing military formations had been restructured to expand operational coverage and improve responses to security threats.

The administration, according to the council, has also approved two additional Army depots in Osogbo, Osun State, and Amasiri-Edda, Ebonyi State, to increase the capacity for training new soldiers.

Each facility is designed to accommodate 6,000 recruits at a time. The council said 5,210 recruits were already undergoing training at the Osogbo depot.

It added that the new facilities would shorten the time required to train recruits and increase the number of soldiers available for deployment.

The statement also cited investments in military accommodation and operational infrastructure, including a 700-unit barracks project in Ikere-Ekiti, Ekiti State.

The council said the project was intended to improve the living and working conditions of military personnel, while providing infrastructure to support their operations.

It maintained that the proposed defence plan would guide government spending according to identified security threats and operational needs, improve combat readiness and address gaps in the capabilities of security agencies.

The statement did not give a timeline for the implementation of the five-year plan.

title: Massive crowd welcomes Atiku’s campaign motorcade in Yobe ahead of presidential rally
description:
A large crowd of supporters on Sunday lined the streets of Potiskum, Yobe State, as the campaign motorcade of former Vice-President and African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, moved through the town.
Photographs and videos obtained by VERY NIGERIAN showed men, women
content:
A large crowd of supporters on Sunday lined the streets of Potiskum, Yobe State, as the campaign motorcade of former Vice-President and African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, moved through the town.

Photographs and videos obtained by VERY NIGERIAN showed men, women and youths walking alongside a branded campaign truck conveying party leaders and supporters, with many waving flags, banners and posters.

Security personnel were also seen escorting the procession as supporters gathered along the roads. Vehicles, motorcycles and tricycles equally joined the motorcade during the campaign activity.

The campaign truck carried the inscriptions “Dokaji 2027” and “A Wajen Allah Muke Nema”, while supporters cheered and chanted as the procession moved through the town.

The turnout attracted reactions on social media, with some supporters describing the crowd as a sign of growing support for the ADC ahead of the 2027 general election.

Meanwhile, reports indicated that the ADC had been denied access to a venue in Damaturu, the Yobe State capital, forcing the party to relocate its rally to Potiskum.

However, Our Journalist said it could not independently verify the claim about the alleged denial of a venue as of the time of filing the report.

Atiku’s campaign activity in Yobe also came amid a legal dispute over his emergence as the ADC presidential candidate. A Federal High Court in Abuja had reportedly nullified his emergence and removed the David Mark-led national executive of the party.

The court ruling has introduced further uncertainty into the party’s preparations for the 2027 general election.
